r1-ATR-NK-2026-001.s: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported, as an example, that from 12 to 15 January in several localities of Rutshuru territory, North Kivu, at least 10 children, nine women and eight men suspected of collaborating with Wazalendo groups were killed by AFC/M23 combatants.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-001.x: BCNUDH: at least 10 children, nine women, eight men killed
r1-ATR-NK-2026-001.n: Publication date of the monthly report not printed in the extracted text; 2026-01-31 is the date shown in the search listing and the file sits under a 2026-04 upload path. Localities not named in the excerpt. 17 plus 10 = 27 victims by the sum of the categories printed (10+9+8); the report does not print a total in the excerpt.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-001.vn: Excerpt verified in the retained PDF (section on non-State armed groups, 'A titre d'exemple'). UN body's documented monitoring: grade A. Researcher's note arithmetic ('17 plus 10 = 27') is muddled; the categories sum to 27 but no total is printed, so none is stated. The report gives the example by category only (10 children, nine women, eight men); it prints no total and does not name the localities.
src: du 12 au 15 janvier, dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Rutshuru, province du Nord Kivu, au moins 10 enfants, neuf femmes et huit hommes soupçonnés de collaborer avec les groupes Wazalendo ont été tués par des combattants de l’AFC/M23.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-002.s: BCNUDH reported that on 2 January 2026 the FARDC used armed drones in Masisi territory, North Kivu, against AFC/M23 positions, and that several strikes hit densely populated areas in Masisi-centre, injuring 42 people and killing seven others, including two women, a girl and a boy, and destroying houses.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-002.x: BCNUDH: 42 injured, 7 killed (two women, one girl, one boy among the dead)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-002.n: Described by BCNUDH as 'dommages collatéraux' (collateral damage) of drone use. No FARDC or government statement on this strike was found in these searches.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-002.vn: Verified in the retained PDF; 'sept' is spelled out (flag on '7' is a format false positive). UN body documentation: grade A. BCNUDH lists this under 'Dommages collatéraux résultant de l'utilisation de drones'.
src: Le 2 janvier 2026, les FARDC ont utilisé des drones armés dans le territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu) pour frapper des positions de l’AFC/M23. Plusieurs de ces frappes ont touché des zones densément peuplées à Masisi-centre, blessant 42 personnes et tuant sept autres dont deux femmes, une fille, un garçon et détruisant des maisons.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.s: UN News, citing a MONUSCO press release, reported that a French UNICEF employee was killed on Wednesday 11 March 2026 in a drone attack on a building housing humanitarian workers in Goma, and that the attack also killed two civilians and damaged civilian homes.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.l: Goma (Himbi quarter per UN Group of Experts), North Kivu
r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.a: not attributed by UN News (attribution contested)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.x: MONUSCO via UN News: 1 UNICEF employee and 2 civilians killed
r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.n: Goma is described by UN News as under M23 control for over a year. Perpetrator not stated by UN News; see the separate claim on the Group of Experts. Victim not named in this source.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-003.vn: Verified on the page. The researcher's note that the victim is unnamed is wrong; the page names her (see note). Both sources are the same page and origin (MONUSCO via UN News): grade B, not A. The same UN News page names the victim as Karine Buisset (UNICEF statement: 'notre collègue Karine Buisset'); the stored excerpts do not, so the name is not yet on this claim (lead: add_excerpt). UN News does not attribute the strike. MONUSCO's acting head Bruno Lemarquis said attacks on UN personnel 'pourraient constituer des crimes de guerre' and called for an independent inquiry.
src: Une employée française de l’UNICEF a été tuée mercredi lors d’une attaque de drone contre un bâtiment abritant des travailleurs humanitaires à Goma

L’attaque de drone a également entraîné la mort de deux civils et causé des dégâts à des habitations civiles, a précisé le Mission de paix des Nations Unies en RDC, la MONUSCO , dans un communiqué de presse.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-004.s: Beto.cd, in an article credited to AFP summarising the UN Group of Experts report S/2026/466, reported that the experts reconstructed the strike that killed UNICEF worker Karine Buisset in Goma on 11 March as an aerial fragmentation munition fired by a drone coming from Lake Kivu, and that attribution remains contested.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-004.n: Page carries an AFP credit; cited as relayed by Beto.cd. The report S/2026/466 itself was not opened. Earlier lead (not cited): Goma strikes were reported by local social media as attributed to the FARDC; no party statement on responsibility was fetched.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-004.vn: Byline 'AFP La Rédaction': credited to AFP. Single wire relay of a UN report not opened: B. Party accounts on the same AFP page (not in the stored excerpt; lead for add_excerpt): 'L’AFC/M23 a accusé l’armée congolaise d’avoir lancé les drones ; Kinshasa a présenté ses condoléances et ouvert une enquête sans désigner de coupable, tout en pointant une « agression technologique » rwandaise.' The page places the strike in the Himbi quarter around 4 a.m. The Group of Experts report itself was not opened. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: article credited to AFP 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-009: Checked the AFP summary against the retained GoE report: its annex supports it ('high-explosive fragmentation', platform 'approaching from over Lake Kivu', per witness accounts and damage analysis) and the Group names no perpetrator. Amended only to show the relay: the page is Beto.cd's, credited to AFP.; excerpt-support: added the headline and byline ('AFP La Rédaction', 2 July 2026) as an excerpt for the AFP credit
src: Le groupe d'experts de l'ONU (S/2026/466) reconstitue la frappe qui a tué l'humanitaire française de l'Unicef Karine Buisset à Goma le 11 mars : une munition aérienne de fragmentation, tirée par un drone venu du lac Kivu. L'attribution, elle, reste contestée.
Frappe de drone à Goma : les vérités du Groupe d’experts de l’ONU AFP La Rédaction Kinshasa - 2 JUILLET 2026

r1-ATR-NK-2026-005.s: 7sur7.cd reported that AFC/M23 military spokesperson Willy Ngoma was killed on Tuesday in a drone strike attributed to the FARDC near Rubaya, Masisi territory, according to concordant sources and movement officials.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-005.n: Date computed from weekday and the page's dateline (Tuesday 24 February 2026). A search listing (Africanews) reported at least nine dead in the same strike; that page was not opened, so no figure is given. Ngoma is a combatant; recorded as a military event, not as a civilian atrocity.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-005.vn: Verified on the page (byline David Lupemba, no wire credit). Flag on '7' comes from the outlet name 7sur7. Single local outlet: grade C (lowered from B). Who attributes the strike to the FARDC is not specified by the outlet. Tuesday = 24 February 2026 from the article date.
src: Le porte-parole militaire du mouvement rebelle AFC/M23, Willy Ngoma, a été tué mardi dans une frappe de drone attribuée aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), ont indiqué des sources concordantes ainsi que des responsables du mouvement.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-006.s: Radio Okapi reported on Monday 25 May that aerial strikes attributed to military drones, whose origin remained undetermined and which no party had claimed, hit Rubaya (Masisi) and Rumangabo (Rutshuru) the day before; a strike on Sunday around 07:30 hit a training centre for the women and widows of ICCN rangers in the Virunga National Park compound at Rumangabo, with no loss of life confirmed, and an earlier strike around 00:15 targeted a guest house in Rubaya.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-006.a: unidentified; not claimed by any party (source)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-006.x: Radio Okapi: no official human toll communicated; no loss of life confirmed at Rumangabo
r1-ATR-NK-2026-006.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Monday 25 May 2026; strikes 'au lendemain'). The AFC/M23 accused the FARDC of the strikes (Kivu Morning Post headline of 24 May 2026, in search results, page not opened); no FARDC statement found. No official toll at the time of the report.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-006.vn: All clauses verified on the retained page. Radio Okapi (UN-run) as a single credible non-partisan origin: B. No official human toll at the time of the report; the Rubaya guest house reportedly housed several people ('hébergerait').
src: Les frappes, dont l’origine reste indéterminée, n’ont été revendiquées par aucune des parties impliquées dans le conflit.

À Rumangabo, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, une frappe survenue dimanche vers 7h30 a touché un bâtiment abritant un centre de formation destiné aux femmes et aux veuves d’écogardes de l’ICCN, situé dans l’enceinte du parc national des Virunga.
Quelques heures plus tôt, vers 00h15, une autre frappe avait ciblé une maison d’accueil dans la cité minière de Rubaya, dans le territoire de Masisi.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Ihula, Katobo and Mukohwa in Kisimba groupement, Walikale territory, were retaken by AFC/M23 rebels on Tuesday 26 May after intense fighting against the FARDC and allied Wazalendo; according to its sources, the rebels used drones to bomb loyalist positions.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-007.l: Ihula, Katobo, Mukohwa (Kisimba groupement), Walikale territory
r1-ATR-NK-2026-007.n: Single local outlet citing unnamed sources; no AFC/M23 or FARDC statement found. Source says the clashes caused mass displacement towards Kalinga and Mpombi.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-007.vn: The retake is the outlet's own narration; only the drone use is attributed to its sources. Attribution re-ordered accordingly. Same page: loyalist forces held Ngambi and Buhimba; households fled towards Kalinga and Mpombi.
src: Les villages d'Ihula, Katobo et Mukohwa, situés dans le groupement Kisimba, dans le territoire de Walikale au Nord-Kivu, ont été repris par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 mardi 26 mai après des combats intenses contre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et leurs alliés wazalendo.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that fighting between Wazalendo armed groups and AFC/M23 rebels was reported on Wednesday 10 June in Masisi territory, notably at Kishanja and Kasenyi, with heavy and light weapons heard.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-008.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (Maï-Maï Lamuka coalition and Groupe Armé des Volontaires per local sources)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-008.n: Frontline context only. The same page reports local civil society saying the escalation caused population displacement.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-008.vn: Verified on the retained page. Single report citing unnamed local sources: C. Same page: local sources say Maï-Maï Lamuka and GAV elements responded to an AFC/M23 attack from 5 a.m. at Kashovu (Ufamandu groupement); fighting also on Tuesday at Kazinga (Nyamaboko groupement). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Jun 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt lacks the date and the heavy and light weapons, added here.
src: Selon plusieurs sources locales, des affrontements opposent les groupes armés Wazalendo aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23. Les combats ont notamment été signalés dans les localités de Kishanja et Kasenyi, où la situation reste tendue.
Des détonations d’armes lourdes et légères ont été entendues jusqu’à la matinée de ce mercredi 10 juin dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Masisi, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué that 10 civilians were summarily killed by the M23 in the locality of Kiseguru, near Virunga National Park, Bwito chiefdom, North Kivu, on Tuesday 02 June 2026, and that the FARDC condemned this as a new violation of international humanitarian law; the same communiqué said several other citizens were arrested and transferred to Kanyangambi central prison in Rutshuru on the pretext that they were FDLR.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.l: Kiseguru, Bwito chiefdom, near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru territory
r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.a: M23 (as alleged by the FARDC communiqué)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.x: FARDC communiqué via 7sur7.cd: 10 civilians killed; 'plusieurs' others arrested
r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.n: Single account relaying a party communiqué (FARDC); victims not named; the communiqué itself was not found. An AFC/M23 response to this allegation was searched for and not found (see gaps). Arrests are as described in the same communiqué (an allegation against M23).
r1-ATR-NK-2026-009.vn: Verified on the page (byline Alphonse Muderwa). Partisan communiqué relayed by one outlet: C. Flag '7' is from the outlet name. Party allegation (FARDC); the legal characterisation is the FARDC's own. 'Rutshuru' for Kiseguru rests on the prison clause and Bwito chiefdom (which is in Rutshuru territory); the page does not print 'Rutshuru' beside Kiseguru. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: FARDC condemnation as quoted 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Legal label must sit inside an attributed quote: the page prints 'condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' in the sentence that continues source 0 (add_excerpt needed). Fresh search found only relays of the same FARDC communiqué (MediaCongo, Enquete.cd), no independent account and no M23 response. Place lead: other reporting places Kiseguru in Binza groupement (Bwisha chiefdom, near Nyamilima), not Bwito; keep 'Bwito' as printed and flag it.; excerpt-support: added the communiqué sentence with 'condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' as an excerpt 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 4 Jun 2026 (Alphonse Muderwa). The phrase 'cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire' is the outlet's paraphrase of the FARDC condemnation, not a quotation from the communiqué, so it should not be presented as 'what it called'. Otherwise all clauses are on the page.
src: 10 civils ont été sommairement tués par le M23 dans la localité de Kiseguru, près du parc national de Virunga, en chefferie de Bwito au Nord-Kivu, mardi 02 juin 2026. Les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l'annoncent dans un communiqué
Le même communiqué indique que plusieurs autres citoyens ont été arrêtés et transférés dans la prison centrale de Kanyangambi à Rutshuru sous prétexte qu'ils seraient des FDLR.
Les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l'annoncent dans un communiqué et condamnent cette nouvelle violation du droit international humanitaire.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-010.s: The Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 54 people were killed in attacks by ADF-MTM since January 2026 in the Baswagha chiefdom and the Bapere sector of Lubero territory, according to a provisional toll compiled on Thursday by the Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC), whose president Vianney Kitsamba cited 33 deaths in Baswagha and 21 civilians in the Bapere sector.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-010.l: Baswagha chiefdom and Bapere sector, Lubero territory
r1-ATR-NK-2026-010.x: CLPC via Kivu Morning Post: at least 54 killed (33 Baswagha, 21 Bapere)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-010.n: Local civil-society tally, provisional. Differs from the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination tally reported by Radio Okapi on 6 February (62 in Beni and Lubero, of which 52 in Lubero, as of a statement of 3 February): different compilers and cut-off dates; figures are not merged. The Thursday is 22 January per the page date.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-010.vn: Verified on the page. Local civil-society tally via one local outlet: C. Kept separate from the North Kivu civil society coordination tally (52 in Lubero as of 3 February, Radio Okapi): different compiler, area and cut-off; not merged. 'Terroristes' is the outlet's wording.
src: Au moins 54 personnes ont été tuées dans les attaques des terroristes des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF-MTM) depuis janvier 2026, dans la chefferie des Baswagha et le secteur des Bapere, dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Ce bilan provisoire a été dressé ce jeudi par le Comité local de protection communautaire (CLPC)

« Comment comprendre que les ADF tuent ainsi les civils : 33 morts à Baswagha et 21 civils dans le secteur des Bapere depuis janvier 2026 ? » , s’interroge Vianney Kitsamba, président de cette structure citoyenne.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that in a statement published on Tuesday 3 February 2026, the provincial coordination of North Kivu civil society said at least 62 civilians had been killed since the start of the year by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero territories, 52 of them in Lubero and 10 in Beni.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-011.x: Civil society via Radio Okapi: at least 62 killed (52 Lubero, 10 Beni)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-011.n: Civil-society tally; see the Kivu Morning Post claim for the differing 22 January figure. Same page lists one health post burned (see separate claim).
r1-ATR-NK-2026-011.vn: Verified on the page. Civil-society tally: C. Differs from the CLPC figure of 54 (Baswagha and Bapere only, 22 January); the two tallies are kept separate.
src: Dans une déclaration publiée, mardi 3 février 2026, la coordination provinciale de la société civile du Nord-Kivu dresse un bilan alarmant : au moins 62 civils ont été tués depuis le début de l'année par des rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) dans les territoires de Beni et Lubero.
Selon les données compilées par la société civile, le territoire de Lubero est le plus durement touché, avec 52 personnes tuées, contre 10 autres en territoire de Beni.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu civil society tally of violence by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero since January 2026 included one health post burned, 67 shops and 10 houses burned, 23 motorcycles burned and the destruction of a local chief's 'barza' meeting place.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-012.l: Beni and Lubero territories (health post not located by the source)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-012.x: Civil society via Radio Okapi: 1 health post, 67 shops, 10 houses, 23 motorbikes
r1-ATR-NK-2026-012.n: Excerpt reproduces the page's typo ('Le ban fait état de d'un'). The health post is not named or located by the source.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-012.vn: Verified on the page; 'un poste de santé' carries 'one' (flag is a format false positive). The health post is not named or located. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: suspected ADF rebels 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: The statement calls it a tally 'of ADF violence', firmer than the source's 'rebelles presumes des ADF' in the same article; restored 'suspected'. Health post still unlocated.; excerpt-support: added the article's opening sentence ('rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF)') as an excerpt 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le ban fait état de d'un poste de santé incendié, 67 boutiques et 10 maisons brûlées ; 23 motos calcinées ; et la destruction du le « barza » (lieu de réunion) d'un chef de localité.
au moins 62 civils ont été tués depuis le début de l'année par des rebelles présumés des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) dans les territoires de Beni et Lubero
Un poste de santé, vingt-trois motos, soixante-sept boutiques, dix maisons d’habitation ainsi que le barza du chef de localité ont été incendiés

r1-ATR-NK-2026-013.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing health sources, that the health centres of Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya and Musenge and the reference health centre (CSR) of Masoy had ceased activities in the Mwenye groupement of Lubero territory, along with several health posts, following persistent insecurity marked by killings of civilians attributed to suspected ADF rebels; the reference health centre of Masoya, chief town of the groupement, had closed about a week earlier.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-013.a: ADF (suspected; killings of civilians cited as the cause of insecurity)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-013.n: Closures attributed to insecurity, not a direct attack on the facilities. The same page quotes a civil society president saying pressure on the Biambwe health centre pushed nurses to close; that passage is not relied on here. Spelling 'Masoy'/'Masoya' as printed on the page.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-013.vn: Statement used 'Masoya' where the cited passage prints 'Masoy'; aligned to each passage and added the 'several health posts' and the one-week closure the page states. The page spells the reference centre both 'Masoy' and 'Masoya'. Closures are attributed to insecurity, not to a direct attack on the facilities. A civil society leader on the same page also cites pressure on the Biambwe health centre (armed group members and their wives treated without paying).
src: Des sources sanitaires indiquent à ACTUALITÉ.CD que les centres de santé de Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, ainsi que le centre de santé de référence (CSR) de Masoy, ont cessé leurs activités.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, an ADF incursion in the night of 21 to 22 July 2026 in the Bapere sector of Lubero territory cost the lives of at least seven civilians and several homes were burned, forcing many households to flee.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-014.x: Local sources via Actualite.cd: at least 7 civilians killed
r1-ATR-NK-2026-014.n: Zone named by the article title as the Bapere sector. A search listing (Instagram, not opened) mentions at least seven civilians killed on Thursday 23 July at Kazaroho; not cited.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-014.vn: Verified on the page; 'sept' spelled out (flag false positive). Village of the attack not named; the alert concerns villages of Bapakombe groupement (Mambau, Maakele, Makumo, Souma).
src: Cette alerte intervient au lendemain d'une attaque des ADF dans la nuit du 21 au 22 juillet 2026 dans cette zone. Selon des sources locales, l'incursion a coûté la vie à au moins sept civils. Plusieurs habitations ont également été incendiées, contraignant de nombreux ménages à fuir leurs villages pour se mettre à l'abri.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that five civilians were killed and about ten houses burned in a new attack attributed to ADF combatants in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January at the village of Mavwe-Mavwe, in the Mandelya locality, and that four women were among the victims.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-015.l: Mavwe-Mavwe, Mandelya locality, Mwenye groupement, Lubero territory
r1-ATR-NK-2026-015.x: Actualite.cd: 5 civilians killed (4 women among victims), about 10 houses burned
r1-ATR-NK-2026-015.n: Date given as 'Tuesday to Wednesday 21 January'; recorded as the range 20-21 January. Reported in passing in an article about health centre closures.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-015.vn: Verified on the page; figures spelled out (flag false positive). 21 January 2026 was a Wednesday, so the 20-21 range is consistent.
src: Pour rappel, cinq civils ont été tués et une dizaine de maisons incendiées lors d'une nouvelle attaque attribuée aux combattants ADF dans la nuit du mardi au mercredi 21 janvier dernier. L'incident s'est produit au village de Mavwe-Mavwe, dans la localité de Mandelya. Parmi les victimes figuraient quatre femmes.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.s: MediaCongo, carrying a report credited 'Gloire Kamandi/Butembo, Actu30 / MCP', reported that the Karisimbi communal youth council alerted on Wednesday 8 July 2026 to the abduction of more than 50 young people by armed men in the Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters of Goma, and that the council fears their possible forced enrolment into the March 23 movement (M23/AFC).
r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.l: Kasika and Mabanga Nord quarters, Goma
r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.a: armed men; youth council alleges vehicles belonging to M23/AFC elements
r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.x: Youth council via Actu30/MediaCongo: more than 50 young people abducted
r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.n: Single claim by a youth council relayed by Actu30/MCP. Search listings (Ouragan.cd, Instagram, not opened) place the abduction in the night of 7 July and attribute it to the AFC/M23, one saying 'police de l'AFC/M23'; no AFC/M23 statement found. Council president named in the page as Claude Rugo. Youth include boys, girls and children according to the council president (page text); not quoted here.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-016.vn: Added the council's stated fear of forced enrolment (excerpt 1). The conditional vehicle attribution stays in the note because the stored excerpts do not carry it. Origin is Actu30.cd. Single unverified account: C. The page (Actu30 / MCP relay) also quotes the council president, Claude Rugo, saying the youths were forced into more than four vehicles 'qui appartiendraient aux éléments du mouvement du 23 mars (M23/AFC)', and that they include boys, girls and children. That attribution is conditional and not in the stored excerpts (lead for add_excerpt). 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: MediaCongo, 8 Jul 2026, credited 'Gloire Kamandi/Butembo, Actu30 / MCP'; the council president Claude Rugo spoke to Actu30.cd and said the youths were taken in vehicles that 'appartiendraient' to M23/AFC elements. All clauses are on the page; the statement should credit Actu30's copy.
src: Le conseil communal de la jeunesse de Karisimbi a alerté ce mercredi 8 juillet 2026 sur l’enlèvement de plus de 50 jeunes par des hommes armés dans les quartiers Kasika et Mabanga Nord, en ville de Goma, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.

Le conseil communal de la jeunesse de la commune de Karisimbi, qui craint un éventuel enrôlement forcé de ces jeunes au sein du mouvement du 23 mars (M23/AFC), plaide pour l’intervention de l’opinion nationale et internationale afin que ces civils recouvrent leur liberté.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-017.s: Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 announced six members of one family, a woman and her five children, were killed in an attack it said was carried out by the FDLR in Rutshuru territory, and that, according to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attack took place in the night of 2 July 2026 in the Kabizo/Butare area of Bwito chiefdom.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-017.x: AFC/M23 via Umuryango.rw: six killed (a woman and five children)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-017.n: Single-party account (AFC/M23) relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the page itself notes that the information comes from one side and no independent confirmation or DRC government response was found. The page also says a UN experts' report of late June 2026 found the FDLR still active in North Kivu, in places cooperating with Congolese forces and Wazalendo (not relied on). The children are described as 'abana' (children); ages not given. Treat as partisan_afc_m23 for the claim.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-017.vn: Verified on the retained Kinyarwanda page; all six names printed. Partisan origin: C. Single-party account (AFC/M23). The outlet itself notes the information comes from one side. Kanyuka also accused the DRC government of working with the FDLR. Names of the dead are as the outlet prints them (source 1).
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 ryatangaje ko abantu batandatu bo mu muryango umwe, barimo umugore n’abana be batanu, bishwe mu gitero rivuga ko cyagabwe n’umutwe wa FDLR mu Teritwari ya Rutshuru, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru.
Abo bivugwa ko bahasize ubuzima ni Tuombe Maniragaba wari umugore wa Rugamba, hamwe n’abana babo batanu ari bo Sifiwe Rugamba, Dorika Rugamba, Emery Rugamba, Mariam Rugamba na Divine Rugamba.
Nk’uko byatangajwe n’umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, icyo gitero cyabaye mu ijoro ryo ku wa 2 Nyakanga 2026 mu gace ka Kabizo/Butare, gaherereye muri Sheferi ya Bwito.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-018.s: Actualite.cd, relaying Reporters sans frontières (RSF), reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was held in a container at the North Kivu Provincial Assembly in Goma by the AFC/M23, forced to film an interview of the M23 spokesperson and then released, according to RSF on Friday 24 April.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-018.n: RSF accusation relayed by Actualite.cd; exact detention date not given ('quelques jours' after RSF's earlier report); recorded as April 2026. No AFC/M23 response found in these searches. RSF's earlier report is said to concern at least two journalists held incommunicado in containers in eastern DRC (not detailed here).
r1-ATR-NK-2026-018.vn: Excerpts verified. The detention ran from 29 March to 3 April per the page, so the date is widened from April to March-April; exact dates are in the note pending add_excerpt. RSF investigation through one relay: B. Per RSF as relayed on the same page (not in the stored excerpts; lead for add_excerpt): Mbata, based in Minova, was arrested on 29 March at his radio's premises by three individuals presenting as M23, transferred to Goma the next day, held four days in a container, and on 3 April taken to the offices of M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka and filmed interviewing him before release. The page says M23 had earlier denied RSF's container revelations as 'des informations totalement infondées'.
src: le directeur de la radio communautaire Top Buzi FM, Espoir Mbata a, à son tour, été séquestré. Il a ensuite été contraint de réaliser une interview filmée du porte-parole du M23, le groupe armé qui le détenait, avant d’être finalement libéré. C’est ce qu’a révélé ce vendredi 24 avril RSF.

Quelques jours seulement après les révélations de RSF sur l’utilisation de conteneurs comme lieu de détention, l’AFC/M23 a de nouveau enfermé un journaliste dans l’un de ceux situés dans l’Assemblée provinciale du Nord-Kivu, à Goma.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.s: Amnesty International reported in a September 2026 briefing that it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators in mines in North and South Kivu, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.l: M23-controlled artisanal mines incl. Rubaya and Lomera (North and South Kivu)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.a: M23 or their collaborators (as alleged by Amnesty International)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.x: Amnesty: 18 artisanal miners summarily killed, at least 9 beaten and died at health centres or before reaching hospital
r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.n: The briefing does not give incident dates in the passage; interviews were January-April 2026 and a miner mentions events 'last year'. Some incidents may predate 2026. The Rubaya mine is in Masisi territory (North Kivu); Lomera is in South Kivu. Amnesty wrote to the M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on 11 August 2026 and reported no response from M23 at publication (passage in the same document).
r1-ATR-NK-2026-019.vn: Verified in the retained PDF. Dropped '26 interviews' and 'between January and April', which the stored excerpt does not print (they are in the note). Documented major-NGO investigation: A. Date not stated: the briefing gives no date range for the 18 killings. The cases it does date all fall in the window (a Rubaya miner beaten to death in February 2025; two Lomera detainees shot after a June 2025 detention; a pit-boss killing in December 2025; seven miners who died at a health centre after beatings between January and March 2026). Not all 18 are dated, so some may fall outside these dates. Interviews ran January-April 2026. Amnesty wrote to M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on 11 August 2026 and had no response at publication.
src: Amnesty International documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-020.s: Amnesty International reported that more than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-020.a: M23 fighters (as alleged by Amnesty International)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-020.x: Amnesty: more than 20 miners from Rubaya held in a pit
r1-ATR-NK-2026-020.n: Incident date not stated in the passage (interviews January-April 2026). Same briefing describes forced recruitment threats of transfer to the Rumangabo and Tchanzou training sites in Rutshuru.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-020.vn: Narrowed to what the stored excerpt prints: the ndake depth figures are not in the excerpt (they are in the note). The undated summary and the February 2026 testimony are surfaced, not merged. Major-NGO investigation: A. Date not stated for this summary figure. Amnesty says M23 uses underground cells known as ndake, roughly 1.5 to 2 m deep. In the body, a Rubaya miner says M23 detained and beat him in February 2026 in a pit inside a wooden house at Kanyenzuki, west of Rubaya, and that 'There were 20 of us in the pit'; he was released the next day after paying about US$32. Discrepancy: the summary says 'more than 20', the witness says 20, and Amnesty does not say they are the same case.
src: More than 20 miners from Rubaya were kept in a pit and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.

r1-ATR-NK-2026-021.s: Health Policy Watch reported that UN experts, in a statement the previous week, called for an end to what they described as a 'reign of terror' by the Rwanda-backed M23, citing a growing volume of civilian testimony, and said rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi, adding that 'while these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end'.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-021.l: M23-controlled areas of eastern DRC (North and South Kivu; place not specified in the excerpt)
r1-ATR-NK-2026-021.n: Secondary relay of an OHCHR press release listed in the search results as dated 21 July 2026 ('M23's reign of terror by torture in eastern DR Congo must end'); the OHCHR page could not be fetched, so the original wording is unverified. An earlier OHCHR experts' release of 26 February 2026 on M23 violence against human rights defenders in North and South Kivu was also found in listing only. Experts' statement is general and not tied to a single territory.
r1-ATR-NK-2026-021.vn: Verified on the page (Stefan Anderson, 30/07/2026). Relay of a UN statement whose original was not opened: B. Secondary relay; the OHCHR original was not fetched. The same page says the experts described arbitrary detention, 'torture including sexual torture', forced labour and forced recruitment, with detainees held in unofficial sites 'with little or no medical access' (not in the stored excerpt; lead for add_excerpt). The experts also said the crimes 'are not exclusive to M23'. Not tied to a specific place. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 'these crimes are not exclusive to M23' 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-028: Read the retained page: the experts' very next sentence qualifies the attribution ('not exclusive to M23'), which the claim omitted. Added it; still a relay of the OHCHR statement (original not fetched), so B stands.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): 'these crimes are not exclusive to M23' 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: In a separate statement last week, UN experts called for an end to what they described as a “reign of terror” by the Rwanda-backed M23 armed group, citing a growing volume of testimony from civilian victims. “Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23's modus operandi,” the experts said.
While these crimes are not exclusive to M23, the number of individuals affected is staggering and must end.
“Rapes, gang rapes, violent assaults and killings of civilians are a common feature of M23’s modus operandi,” the experts said in a press release.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-001.s: Witnesses and relatives told Human Rights Watch that drone attacks in the highlands killed at least two Banyamulenge people in March 2026: an 86-year-old man near Minembwe on 23 March and a 14-year-old boy near his village in Fizi territory on 30 March. HRW said it was unclear if the attacks intended to target military objectives.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-001.l: Minembwe and Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-001.a: drones, operator not established by the source
r1-ATR-SK-2026-001.n: Victims unnamed in source. Minor (14) unnamed.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-001.vn: Excerpt verified on retained HRW page; same event, same figures. Operator of the drones not established by HRW for these two deaths; victims unnamed.
src: Witnesses and relatives told Human Rights Watch that drone attacks in the highlands killed at least two Banyamulenge people in March 2026. On March 23, an 86-year-old man was killed while tending his cattle near Minembwe. On March 30, a 14-year-old boy was killed in a field near his village in Fizi territory. It is unclear if the attacks intended to target military objectives.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-002.s: Human Rights Watch reported that a community radio station in Madegu, near Minembwe, was damaged in an apparent drone attack on 9 March 2026, and that an apparent drone attack was carried out on a church in Ilundu village at night, also in March. Human Rights Watch said it could not establish responsibility with certainty but that the targets suggest the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled the drones; Human Rights Watch said it had asked the Congolese army's regional commander for information on the strikes and had not received a response.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-002.l: Madegu and Ilundu, near Minembwe, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-002.a: drones; operator not established; HRW infers from the targets that the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled them (HRW's inference)
r1-ATR-SK-2026-002.n: Church attack dated only 'in March'. Two excerpts from one page.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-002.vn: Removed the '4 April' figure no excerpt prints (date kept in note); 'contacted' changed to HRW's wording; drone-control inference kept attributed to HRW. Responsibility is HRW's inference from the targets, not an established finding. HRW spoke to the commander on 4 April (page text).
src: A community radio station in Madegu, near Minembwe, was damaged in an apparent drone attack on March 9, disrupting access to information in an area where the phone network has been disrupted for over a year.

While Human Rights Watch could not establish with certainty responsibility for these strikes, the targets suggest that the Congolese army or allied fighters controlled the drones, Human Rights Watch said.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-003.s: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to Minembwe residents and UN and diplomatic sources, the Twirwaneho had forced families to provide a fighter or financially compensate the armed group and retaliated if they refused, and that, according to the same sources, the Twirwaneho had also blocked civilians from leaving Minembwe.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-003.n: Undated ongoing practice as of HRW's April 2026 report.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-003.vn: Blocking clause is on the page in the next sentence, not the excerpt; attribution to 'the sources' made explicit.
src: Minembwe residents and UN and diplomatic sources said that the Twirwaneho had forced families to provide a fighter or financially compensate the armed group, and retaliated if they refused.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-004.s: Human Rights Watch reported, citing security sources, that the Burundian army had about 4,000 troops deployed to Fizi and Mwenga territories to fight alongside Congolese armed forces.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-004.l: Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-004.n: Figure is from unnamed security sources per HRW; Burundian authorities per SOS Médias Burundi gave no casualty figures.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-004.vn: Removed 'against Twirwaneho and M23 armed groups', which the excerpt does not state; the irrelevant SOS Medias note is not supported here. Figure from unnamed security sources as relayed by HRW.
src: The Burundian army currently has about 4,000 troops deployed to Fizi and Mwenga territories to fight alongside Congolese armed forces, according to security sources.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-005.s: Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga reported that Rwandan air force fighter jets had once again bombed Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili and Mikenge on Wednesday 8 July 2026, causing enormous material and human damage; the territorial authority said several civilians were wounded in these bombings.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-005.l: Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili, Mikenge, Fizi, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-005.a: Rwandan air force (as alleged by DRC authority)
r1-ATR-SK-2026-005.n: Government-side claim; attribution to Rwanda is the official's. Rwanda/Twirwaneho account not found in this unit.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-005.vn: Wounded clause rests on a page passage, not the excerpt; 'heavy' changed to 'enormous' per the source; discrepancy in the article surfaced. Discrepancy: the same Radio Okapi article later says 'Ces bombardements attribués aux Twirwaneho et à leurs alliés'. Attribution to Rwanda is the administrator's; no Rwandan or Twirwaneho response found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 9 Jul 2026, quotes Badibanga on the Rwandan air force bombing and reports his statement of several civilian wounded; the stored excerpt lacks the wounded clause, added here. Discrepancy on the page: a later sentence says 'Ces bombardements attribués aux Twirwaneho et à leurs alliés'.
src: « Les avions de chasse de l’armée de l’air du Rwanda ont une fois de plus bombardé les agglomérations de Rugezi, Mulima, Point Zéro, Kazaroho, Bilalo Mbili et Mikenge, causant d’énormes dégâts matériels et humains, ce mercredi 8 juillet 2026 » , a rapporté l’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Samy Badibanga.
L’autorité territoriale indique que plusieurs blessés civils ont été enregistrés à la suite de ces bombardements.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the 'nouvelle dynamique de la société civile', Fizi branch, about 16 civilians were killed and 12 others wounded in a bombing reported at Mulima the previous weekend, and that the victims included women and children.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-006.a: not stated by the source for the Mulima bombing
r1-ATR-SK-2026-006.x: Civil society (Fizi): about 16 civilians killed, 12 wounded
r1-ATR-SK-2026-006.n: Date computed from 'le week-end dernier' and publication date 9 July (weekend of 4-5 July). Conflicting figure from a different framing (troops, 3 July) should be checked in a later round. Critical Threats (digest, lead only) says local sources claimed a drone attack on Mulima on 3 July killed 19 FARDC/Burundian troops; not cited.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-006.vn: Statement supported; actor field corrected (the article's Twirwaneho attribution refers to the 8 July bombings, not the Mulima one); excerpt_en flag recorded. Date derived from 'le week-end dernier' in an article published Thursday 9 July 2026 (weekend of 4-5 July). Lead for a later round: other reports describe a 3 July drone strike at Mulima killing troops, not civilians; not checked here. The stored excerpt_en is a mistranslation (it translates the Badibanga quote, not this excerpt) and needs fixing via source_edits.py: correct translation is 'According to the new dynamic of civil society, Fizi branch, about 16 civilians were killed and 12 others wounded. Among the victims are women and children.'
src: Selon la nouvelle dynamique de la société civile, antenne de Fizi, environ 16 civils ont été tués et 12 autres blessés. Parmi les victimes figurent des femmes et des enfants.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that residents of several villages in Fizi and Mwenga had fled into the bush; according to local sources the displacement was caused by bombings attributed to kamikaze drones from Rwanda. Fizi's elected national deputy, Nyamangyoku Ishibwela, raised the alert and said that even civilians wounded in these strikes struggle to receive medical care.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-007.l: Mulima, Point Zéro, Rugezi (Fizi); Kipupu, Mikenge, Kiseke (Mwenga), South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-007.a: kamikaze drones attributed to Rwanda by local sources (as reported by Radio Okapi)
r1-ATR-SK-2026-007.n: Statement by a Congolese MP; displacement start date from the article's lead paragraph, not in the excerpt. No independent confirmation of the drones' origin.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-007.vn: Drone attribution moved from the deputy to 'local sources' as the page states; '24 July' removed from statement because no excerpt prints it (kept in date field and note). Village names kept in location/note because the stored excerpt does not print them. The page dates the flight and the bombings from 24 July ('depuis le 24 juillet'). The drone attribution is from unnamed local sources, not the deputy. The deputy is also quoted: 'les blessés n’ont aucun endroit pour se soigner'. Villages named on the page: Mulima, Point Zéro and Rugezi (Fizi); Kipupu, Mikenge and Kiseke (Mwenga). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-28: source 2 publisher edited: verify:r3-G-CTR read the page: 'AFP' is the credit on the header photo (span ahero__credit), not a wire credit for the text 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L'alerte est lancée par le député national élu de Fizi, le professeur Nyamangyoku Ishibwela. Il dénonce une crise humanitaire majeure où même les civils blessés lors de ces frappes peinent à recevoir des soins médicaux.
L’alerte a été lancée par le député national élu de Fizi, le professeur Nyamangyoku Ishibwela.

Le 29 juillet 2026, le député national élu de Fizi, Nyamangyoku Ishibwela, alerte sur le sort de milliers de personnes déplacées depuis le 24 juillet par des bombardements qu’il attribue à des drones kamikazes venus du Rwanda.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Mikenge, in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory, was retaken on Sunday by the FARDC, supported by the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo militia, after remaining for over a year under the control of Twirwaneho fighters and allied rebels.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-008.l: Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-008.n: Date computed from weekday and dateline 2 March 2026. Burundi-based outlet; single source; M23/AFC and Burundian accounts not found.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-008.vn: 'Citing local sources' removed: the recapture passage is the outlet's own narration (local sources are cited only for the hospital detail). Dateline 'Mikenge, March 2, 2026'; 'Sunday' is therefore 1 March 2026 (derived). Single outlet. The page names the rebels as M23 ('Twirwaneho fighters from the Banyamulenge minority and M23 rebels'); the name is left out of the statement only because the stored excerpt does not print it.
src: The town of Mikenge, located in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory in South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, was retaken on Sunday by the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), supported by the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo militia.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, according to local sources, that the FARDC, the FDNB and the Wazalendo militia now controlled strategic points in the centre of Mikenge, including the general hospital.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-009.n: Military presence at a hospital; the source alleges no harm to it. Source writes 'National Democratic Forces of Burundi' for FDNB.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-009.vn: Verified on retained page. Military control of a hospital; the source alleges no harm to the facility or patients.
src: the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo), the FDNB (National Democratic Forces of Burundi), and the Wazalendo militia now control strategic points in the center of Mikenge, including the general hospital.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-010.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing concordant sources, that after AFC/M23-Wazalendo clashes the previous Sunday, Kasika in Lwindi chiefdom (Mwenga territory) remained under AFC/M23 control while the Wazalendo were positioned at Kalambi, about 20 km away.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-010.l: Kasika and Kalambi, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga, South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-010.n: Date computed from 'dimanche' / 'le week-end dernier' and publication 4 Sept 2026 (Sunday 30 August). Casualty/displacement details are in neighbouring passages of the same page, not in the excerpt, so the statement should be narrowed by the verifier if needed.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-010.vn: Verified; date derivation checked against the page. Sunday = 30 August 2026, derived from the article ('la rentrée était prévue mardi 1er septembre 2026').
src: La cité de Kasika reste sous le contrôle de l’AFC/M23, tandis que les Wazalendo sont positionnés à Kalambi, à environ 20 kilomètres de Kasika, toujours dans la chefferie de Lwindi.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-011.s: Rwandan outlet Umuryango reported that AFC/M23 spokesman Kanyuka said in a post on X on 21 August 2026 that civilians, including women and children, were killed in attacks at Luntukulu on the Nzibira road in South Kivu.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-011.a: Wazalendo and Kinshasa allies (as AFC/M23 alleges)
r1-ATR-SK-2026-011.n: Party claim only; X post URL not located. Territory (Walungu) inferred from Nzibira, not stated in excerpt; verifier may blank it. Outlet is Rwanda-based and sympathetic; treat as partisan relay.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-011.vn: Excerpt verified; 'baguye mu bitero' = died in the attacks; partisan relay, kept as 'party says'. Party claim (AFC/M23) relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet; not independently verified. The article's lead says Kanyuka blamed Wazalendo and others allied with Kinshasa. Territory not stated by the source.
src: Mu butumwa yashyize kuri X ku wa 21 Kanama 2026, Kanyuka yavuze ko mu gace ka Luntukulu, ku muhanda wa Nzibira, abasivili barimo abagore n’abana baguye mu bitero.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-012.s: Umuryango reported that Kanyuka, the rebel coalition's spokesman, also said the armed forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo were continuing to launch bomb attacks in the Minembwe area, and that kamikaze drones and TK-6 weapons were being used in these operations.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-012.a: Congolese armed forces (as alleged by AFC/M23 spokesman Kanyuka)
r1-ATR-SK-2026-012.n: Party claim; counter to Kinshasa claims (e.g. Badibanga) of Rwandan drone strikes at Minembwe area.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-012.vn: Narrowed 'continued shelling' to the source's 'bomb attacks' and kept the weapons as Kanyuka's statement. Party claim (AFC/M23) via a Rwanda-based outlet; not independently verified.
src: Kanyuka kandi yavuze ko ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo zikomeje kugaba ibitero by’ibisasu mu gace ka Minembwe. Yavuze ko muri ibyo bikorwa hakoreshwa drones za kamikaze ndetse n’intwaro za TK-6

r1-ATR-SK-2026-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to independent UN experts, the AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and that the experts' statement reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-013.l: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
r1-ATR-SK-2026-013.n: Region-wide; not specific to South Kivu. Excerpt does not mention abductions/arson/investigations/21 July/Geneva (those are in adjacent sentences), so the verifier should narrow. Territory field is a placeholder.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-013.vn: Narrowed to the excerpt as instructed; conditional 'aurait' kept as 'reportedly'. Region-wide (the article frames North and South Kivu), not South Kivu-specific. The page also says the statement was published on 21 July in Geneva and that the experts reported abductions and arson and called for independent investigations; those details are not in the stored excerpt. The UN statement itself should be retrieved as the primary source.
src: Selon les experts onusiens, l’AFC/M23 aurait mis en place un véritable système de contrôle fondé sur la peur dans les zones qu’il administre. Le communiqué fait état d’arrestations et de détentions arbitraires, d’actes de torture, y compris de violences sexuelles, ainsi que de cas de travail forcé et de recrutement forcé de civils.

r1-ATR-SK-2026-014.s: MSF reported that between January and April 2026 its support to Baraka general referral hospital (Fizi territory, South Kivu), through medical and logistical supplies and staff training, helped treat 426 war-wounded patients arriving in the influx of violence-related injuries.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-014.x: MSF: 426 war-wounded patients treated with MSF support, January-April 2026
r1-ATR-SK-2026-014.n: Article date taken from search result (20 May 2026); msf.fr copy dated 4 June. Context of care capacity, not an attack.
r1-ATR-SK-2026-014.vn: Verified on retained MSF page. Page dated 20 Mai 2026. Care-capacity context, not an attack.
src: Entre janvier et avril 2026, MSF a appuyé l’hôpital général de référence de Baraka en renforçant ses capacités à travers des approvisionnements médicaux et logistiques, ainsi que des sessions de formation au personnel soignant, afin de mieux répondre à l’afflux de blessés liés aux violences. Cet appui a permis de prendre en charge 426 patients blessés de guerre.

r1-GOE-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, in the days preceding the signature of the Washington Agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025.
r1-GOE-001.n: Final report S/2026/466 para. 40 (sources cited in its footnote 44: United Nations, civil society, intelligence sources, researchers). Dates of the offensive differ elsewhere: para. 72 says the offensive began at the end of November 2025.
r1-GOE-001.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The same report (para. 72) dates the start of the offensive to the end of November 2025. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc2: S/2026/466 para. 40 carries every clause, but the stored excerpt says only 'its signature'; the referent (Washington Agreement signed by the DRC and Rwanda on 4 December 2025) is in the preceding sentence, added as one contiguous passage.
src: However, in the days preceding its signature, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025

On 4 December 2025, the Governments of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda signed the Washington Agreement, 42 aimed at de-escalation and cessation of hostilities. 43 However, in the days preceding its signature, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and AFC/M23 launched a coordinated military offensive in South Kivu, taking control of Uvira on 10 December 2025

r1-GOE-002.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 after sustained international diplomatic pressure, and that the withdrawal, presented as a goodwill gesture, was followed by consolidation of AFC/M23 and RDF positions as they redeployed to adjacent areas.
r1-GOE-002.n: S/2026/466 paras. 77-78. First anchor fixed below if the PDF text has no space after 'AFC/'.
r1-GOE-002.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/ M23 and RDF troops eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, following sustained international diplomatic pressure
Presented as a goodwill gesture, the withdrawal was a strategic move followed by the consolidation of AFC/M23 and RDF positions, as they redeployed to adjacent areas

r1-GOE-003.s: The Group of Experts reported that at the end of November 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF launched a major offensive along the Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor and adjacent axes, aiming to seize the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira, to compel Burundi's disengagement from the conflict.
r1-GOE-003.l: Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor, Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
r1-GOE-003.n: S/2026/466 para. 72 (sources: military and intelligence sources, UN, diplomatic sources, civil society, researchers, AFC/M23 members and officers). The same paragraph lists further stated aims (Lemera, Moyens Plateaux, Minembwe, Mwenga, Kalemie).
r1-GOE-003.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: At the end of November 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF launched a major offensive along the Bukavu-Uvira (RN5) corridor and adjacent axes, aiming to seize the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira, to compel Burundi’s disengagement from the conflict

r1-GOE-004.s: The Group of Experts reported that the offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu, and that AFC/M23 and RDF sources had signaled since early October the intent of taking Uvira, pointing at a carefully planned operation by AFC/M23 and Rwanda.
r1-GOE-004.n: S/2026/466 para. 75 (sources: military/intelligence; intelligence, diplomatic and former RDF sources). Mr. Makenga is 'General' Sultani Makenga per para. 61; Mr. Byamungu is 'General' Byamungu per para. 64.
r1-GOE-004.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: The offensive on Uvira was conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu.
AFC/M23 and RDF sources signaled since early October the intent of taking Uvira, pointing at a carefully planned operation by AFC/M23 and Rwanda.

r1-GOE-005.s: The Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and heavy equipment to the Ruzizi Plain frontlines, and that BM21 rockets were fired from Kamanyola on 4 and 5 December, with cross-border shelling on 5 December causing civilian casualties in Cibitoke, Burundi.
r1-GOE-005.l: Ruzizi Plain; Kamanyola, South Kivu; Cibitoke, Burundi
r1-GOE-005.x: Group of Experts: over 8,000 RDF troops
r1-GOE-005.n: S/2026/466 para. 76. Excerpt is long; trimmed if over 60 words.
r1-GOE-005.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain

Heavy artillery and shelling were employed, including firing BM21 rockets from Kamanyola on 4 and 5 December. Cross-border shelling on 5 December has also caused civilian casualties in Cibitoke, Burundi.

r1-GOE-006.s: The Group of Experts reported that heavy artillery fire and shelling in the Uvira offensive caused civilian casualties and displacement from the Ruzizi Plain towards Burundi, and that after AFC/M23 and RDF consolidated control of Uvira in early December they conducted cordon-and-search operations that led to the killing of those suspected of affiliation with FARDC or Wazalendo.
r1-GOE-006.l: Uvira (city) and Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
r1-GOE-006.n: S/2026/466 para. 80 (sources: UN, humanitarian, civil society, human rights defenders, NGOs, researchers, diplomatic and intelligence). No victim counts given in this paragraph. See HRW report of 14 May 2026 on Uvira for case detail (separate unit).
r1-GOE-006.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Heavy artillery fire and shelling resulted in civilian casualties and significant population displacement from the Ruzizi Plain towards Burundi

As clashes subsided and AFC/M23 and RDF consolidated control throughout Uvira in early December, they conducted cordon -and-search operations that led to the killing of those suspected of affiliation with FARDC or Wazalendo.

r1-GOE-007.s: The Group of Experts reported that before their January 2026 withdrawal AFC/M23 instructed the Banyamulenge community to leave Uvira, claiming returning Wazalendo and FARDC forces would target them, and that some members of the Banyamulenge community alleged this movement was coerced to justify claims of a genocidal threat.
r1-GOE-007.n: S/2026/466 para. 81. The Group reports the coercion claim as an allegation 'including from some members of the Banyamulenge community'; it does not itself conclude. AFC/M23's stated reason is recorded as stated.
r1-GOE-007.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The coercion claim is an allegation the Group reports; the Group does not itself conclude on it.
src: Prior to their withdrawal in January 2026, AFC/M23 instructed the Banyamulenge community to leave Uvira, claiming that returning Wazalendo and FARDC forces would target them. This led to allegations, including from some
members of the Banyamulenge community, that their movement was coerced with the aim of justifying claims of a genocidal threat on the community.

r1-GOE-008.s: The Group of Experts reported that when Wazalendo groups re-entered Uvira on 18 January they triggered widespread disorder, including looting, destruction of civilian, humanitarian and State properties and the killing of individuals accused of collaborating with AFC/M23, and that Banyamulenge churches and homes were looted or destroyed in several neighbourhoods; it did not document any targeted killings of Banyamulenge civilians.
r1-GOE-008.n: S/2026/466 para. 82; the Group states investigations into reported incidents remain ongoing. Excerpt may exceed 60 words; adjusted by builder warning.
r1-GOE-008.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: When Wazalendo groups re-entered Uvira on 18 January, they triggered widespread disorder, including looting, the destruction of civilian, humanitarian and State properties and the killing of individuals accused of collaborating with AFC/M23.

Violence also affected members and properties of the Banyamulenge community, with churches and homes looted or destroyed across several neighbourhoods. 89 The Group of Experts did not document any targeted killings of Banyamulenge civilians.

r1-GOE-009.s: The Group of Experts reported that, according to multiple sources, government authorities including DRC President Félix Tshisekedi instructed Wazalendo elements not to target civilians, particularly the Banyamulenge, and that FARDC placed 31 Banyamulenge families remaining in Uvira under its protection.
r1-GOE-009.x: Group of Experts: 31 Banyamulenge families under FARDC protection
r1-GOE-009.n: S/2026/466 para. 82. Reported by the Group from sources (footnote 90: diplomatic and military sources, intelligence, Congolese authorities, Banyamulenge civilians, civil society, researchers); no direct quote from President Tshisekedi is given.
r1-GOE-009.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Reported by the Group from multiple sources; no direct quotation of President Tshisekedi.
src: Multiple sources indicated that government authorities, including the President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, instructed Wazalendo elements not to target civilians, particularly the Banyamulenge. FARDC placed 31 Banyamulenge families remaining in Uvira under its protection.

r1-GOE-010.s: The Group of Experts reported that after the Wazalendo return to Uvira in January 2026 the South Kivu Governor convened all Wazalendo leaders, banned unauthorized armed elements, roadblocks and any substitution for government functions, and arrested recalcitrant combatants, and that provincial authorities began a registration process with payment of $325 to each registered combatant.
r1-GOE-010.a: South Kivu provincial government; FARDC; Wazalendo
r1-GOE-010.x: Group of Experts: $325 per registered combatant
r1-GOE-010.n: S/2026/466 paras. 114-115. Group notes payment became regular after February 2026 and led to a sharp increase in self-declared Wazalendo.
r1-GOE-010.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: The Governor convened all Wazalendo leaders and banned the presence of unauthorized armed elements, prohibited roadblocks or any substitution for government functions and arrested recalcitrant combatants
the provincial government implemented a formal registration process and the payment of $325 to each registered

r1-GOE-011.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones': a first zone covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories led by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye, a second covering Masisi and Walikale led by 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga, and a third covering South Kivu led by 'General' Byamungu.
r1-GOE-011.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (AFC/M23-held areas)
r1-GOE-011.n: S/2026/466 para. 64; report covers investigations to 15 April 2026 so the date is approximate. Sources: military and intelligence sources, UN, diplomatic sources, civil society, researchers, AFC/M23 officers and combatants, Wazalendo combatants. Ranks are in quotation marks as in the report.
r1-GOE-011.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three “defense zones”, led respectively by “General” Baudoin Ngaruye (first zone, covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories), “Brigadier-General” Justin Gacheri Musanga (second zone, covering Masisi and Walikale) and “General” Byamungu (third zone, covering South Kivu).

r1-GOE-012.s: The Group of Experts reported that overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with 'General' Makenga, although his position was increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda, and that Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders, all receiving instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.
r1-GOE-012.l: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
r1-GOE-012.n: S/2026/466 paras. 61-62. First anchor may need adjusting.
r1-GOE-012.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with “General” Makenga, although his position became increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda

Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa remained the political leaders. Both the military and political leadership continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services

r1-GOE-013.s: The Group of Experts reported that the estimated combat strength of AFC/M23 was around 30,000 elements, and that the figure included thousands of recently graduated FARDC, Congolese national police and Wazalendo elements who were either captured or volunteered following the fall of Goma.
r1-GOE-013.l: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
r1-GOE-013.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: The estimated combat strength of AFC/M23 was around 30,000 elements.
They also included thousands of recently graduated FARDC, Congolese national police and Wazalendo elements who were either captured or who volunteered following the fall of Goma

r1-GOE-014.s: The Group of Experts reported that the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025; special forces units under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi supported both, and the RDF Army Chief of Staff, General Vincent Nyakarundi, oversaw operations.
r1-GOE-014.n: S/2026/466 para. 99. The report notes Gatama was referenced in late 2025 as RSF Joint Task Force Commander in Mozambique (footnote). Excerpt was fixed by the builder; footnote markers appear inside the page text.
r1-GOE-014.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: General Vincent Nyakarundi, the RDF Army Chief of Staff who was sanctioned by the United States in March 2026, 111 oversaw operations in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.

the 3rd Division, under command of Major General Eugene Nkubito, 114 operated predominantly in North Kivu; and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu, under the command of Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late-2025.
Both divisions were supported by special forces units, under the command of Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi.

r1-GOE-015.s: The Group of Experts reported that in December 2025 RDF deployment in eastern DRC was conservatively estimated at 8,000 to 10,000 elements in South Kivu and 6,000 to 8,000 in North Kivu, with no evidence of significant withdrawals thereafter.
r1-GOE-015.n: S/2026/466 para. 96. Rwanda's government has publicly denied that its troops operate in the DRC in other sources (not collected in this unit).
r1-GOE-015.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: In December 2025, RDF deployment in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo was conservatively estimated at 8,000 to 10,000 elements in South Kivu and 6,000 to 8,000 in North Kivu, with no evidence of significant withdrawals

r1-GOE-016.s: The Group of Experts reported that President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as Senior Defence and Security Advisor on 1 December 2025 and Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy on 29 January 2026, and that Mr. Nyirabutama was directly involved in operational matters in eastern DRC including communication channels with AFC/M23.
r1-GOE-016.n: S/2026/466 para. 98 (spelling 'Kaberebe' in that sentence; 'Kabarebe' elsewhere in the report). Excerpt anchors fixed below.
r1-GOE-016.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The report spells the name both 'Kaberebe' and 'Kabarebe'.
src: On 1 December 2025, President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as his Senior Defence and Security Advisor. On 29 January 2026, he appointed Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama 106 as deputy to Mr. Kabarebe.
Mr. Nyirabutama was directly involved in operational matters in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, including handling communication channels with AFC/M23

r1-GOE-017.s: The Group of Experts reported that withdrawals by RDF and AFC/M23 from frontlines in North Kivu began on 23 March 2026 but fell short of agreed terms, barely exceeding 15 to 20 km, and amounted to tactical repositioning; RDF personnel and equipment were redeployed from Lubero to the Masisi-Walikale axis.
r1-GOE-017.l: Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
r1-GOE-017.n: S/2026/466 para. 47, following the 17-18 March 2026 Washington 'initial steps plan' (paras. 43-45). AFC/M23 representatives said no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations (para. 50).
r1-GOE-017.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Withdrawals by RDF and AFC/M23 from frontlines in North Kivu began on 23 March but fell short of agreed terms and deadlines. Withdrawals – barely exceeding 15 to 20 km – represented limited strategic and territorial concessions. Movements amounted to tactical repositioning
RDF personnel, heavy artillery and sophisticated equipment (jamming, spoofing and other air defence systems) were redeployed from Lubero to the Masisi-Walikale axis

r1-GOE-018.s: The Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing RDF and AFC/M23 retained control over most withdrawal-designated localities and kept their operational focus on Pinga and Walikale, with intense clashes persisting in April 2026 along the Walikale-Masisi border against FARDC, VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR.
r1-GOE-018.a: AFC/M23 and RDF; FARDC; VDP/Wazalendo; FDLR
r1-GOE-018.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: At the time of writing, RDF and AFC/M23 had retained control over most withdrawal-designated localities and maintained operational focus on Pinga and Walikale. In April, intense clashes over territorial control persisted along the Walikale-Masisi border, between AFC/M23 and RDF on the one side and FARDC, Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP)/Wazalendo and FDLR

r1-GOE-019.s: The Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 FARDC, with Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors, launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, and that on 31 March FARDC launched a major offensive on Minembwe to which RDF responded with drone strikes and aerial resupply for MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23.
r1-GOE-019.a: FARDC; Wazalendo; FDNB; MRDP/Twirwaneho; AFC/M23; RDF
r1-GOE-019.n: S/2026/466 paras. 83, 85. The report says drone strikes in early to mid-April forced FARDC to withdraw from key positions including Muranvia, temporarily halting their advance.
r1-GOE-019.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: In late January 2026, FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors (see paras. 143–144), launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who reinforced MRDP/ Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.

On 31 March, FARDC launched a major offensive on Minembwe following sustained gains across the Hauts Plateaux. 93 In response, RDF supported MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 through drone strikes and aerial resupply.

r1-GOE-020.s: The Group of Experts reported that Minembwe had effectively been encircled by FARDC and allied forces since mid-2025, with severe obstacles to population movements and entry of essential goods and humanitarian assistance, and that since February 2026 access was limited to air supply only.
r1-GOE-020.n: S/2026/466 para. 86 (sources: military and intelligence, UN, Banyamulenge, humanitarian sources). Members of the Banyamulenge community denounced both parties for trapping civilians (para. 88).
r1-GOE-020.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Since mid-2025, Minembwe has effectively been encircled by FARDC and allied forces (see S/2025/858, para. 53), resulting in severe obstacles for population movements, the entry of essential goods and humanitarian assistance. Since February 2026, access has been limited to air supply only.

r1-GOE-021.s: The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe through coercion and threats of violence, and that, as previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat.
r1-GOE-021.x: Group of Experts: boys 10 to 12 years old and all able-bodied men
r1-GOE-021.n: S/2026/466 para. 87 (sources: military and intelligence, UN, Banyamulenge sources, researchers, humanitarian sources, human rights defenders).
r1-GOE-021.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks. 97 As previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat

r1-GOE-022.s: The Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting and that Banyamulenge community members reported three civilian deaths.
r1-GOE-022.x: Group of Experts: three civilian deaths reported by Banyamulenge community members
r1-GOE-022.n: S/2026/466 para. 89 and footnote 99 (statements on X including by Lawrence Kanyuka on 13 December 2025). Excerpt may exceed 60 words; builder will flag.
r1-GOE-022.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments of densely populated areas.

the Group of Experts did not substantiate their intentional targeting. In the context of frequent aerial operations since mid-2025, members of the Banyamulenge community, including human rights organizations, have reported three civilian deaths, including one teenage boy and two elderly individuals.
Statements on X, including by Lawrence Kanyuka on 13 December 2025.

r1-GOE-023.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 14 January 2026 a FARDC drone strike targeted the 'Blue Cat' bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties.
r1-GOE-023.n: S/2026/466 para. 165 (sources: military, intelligence, civil society). The excerpt text gives the strike as a FARDC drone operation targeting AFC/M23 leadership. No casualty figure given.
r1-GOE-023.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership. On 14 January 2026, a drone strike targeted the “Blue Cat” bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira, during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties.

r1-GOE-024.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 February 2026 a FARDC drone strike in Rubaya killed sanctioned individual 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Willy Ngoma, the military spokesperson of AFC/M23, and that on 7 March 2026 a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.
r1-GOE-024.l: Rubaya and Mushaki, Masisi, North Kivu
r1-GOE-024.n: S/2026/466 para. 165 and Summary. Willy Ngoma listed by the UN sanctions committee as CDi.044 per the report.
r1-GOE-024.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On 24 February 2026, a FARDC drone strike in Rubaya killed sanctioned individual “Lieutenant-Colonel” Willy Ngoma (CDi.044), the military spokesperson of AFC/M23. 195 On 7 March 2026, a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.

r1-GOE-025.s: The Group of Experts reported that several FARDC drone operations affected civilian objects and populations: strikes in late October 2025 in Shoa and the Nyabiondo hills (Masisi) killed at least three civilians and caused displacement, and a drone strike on 2 January 2026 in Masisi centre damaged civilian and administrative buildings and the sub-base of War Child, causing at least seven fatalities.
r1-GOE-025.l: Masisi centre, Shoa and Nyabiondo hills, North Kivu
r1-GOE-025.x: Group of Experts: at least three civilians killed (late Oct 2025); at least seven fatalities (2 Jan 2026)
