r1-GOE-025.n: S/2026/466 para. 163 (sources: UN, humanitarian, military, civil society, intelligence, diplomatic). Late-October 2025 strikes have no exact day.
r1-GOE-025.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Several FARDC drone operations affected civilian objects and populations. In Masisi territory, strikes in late October 2025 in Shoa and the Nyabiondo hills killed at least three civilians and caused displacement. On 2 January 2026, a drone strike in
Masisi centre damaged civilian and administrative buildings and the sub -base of the international humanitarian organization War Child, causing at least seven fatalities.

r1-GOE-026.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 11 March 2026 two successive detonations were reported near a residential compound in the Himbi neighbourhood of Goma, the second causing the death of a UNICEF staff member; M23 military personnel deployed to the scene shortly after the strike and removed all ballistic remnants; AFC/M23 attributed the strike to FARDC while Congolese authorities announced an investigation, and the Group's investigations continue.
r1-GOE-026.a: not attributed by the Group of Experts; AFC/M23 attributed to FARDC
r1-GOE-026.n: S/2026/466 paras. 171-172 (M23 personnel removed ballistic remnants per para. 171; acoustic signature of at least one UAV detected before the explosions). Perpetrator not determined by the Group.
r1-GOE-026.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-009: Attribution is correctly left open (party accounts only). Strongest true version adds the Group's own finding, in stored excerpt 1, that M23 personnel removed all ballistic remnants, which bears on why attribution is unresolved.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; the ballistic-remnants sentence is in source 1
src: On 11 March 2026, two successive detonations were reported near a residential compound located in the Himbi neighbourhood in Goma. The second detonation impacted a residential compound resulting in the death of a United Nations Children’s
Fund (UNICEF) staff member. M23 military personnel deployed to the scene shortly after the strike and removed all ballistic remnants
AFC/M23 attributed the strike to FARDC, while Congolese authorities announced an investigation. 201 The Group of Experts’ investigations into this incident continue.

r1-GOE-027.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued to forcibly or voluntarily recruit adults and minors, and that former recruits denounced systematic torture and executions in training camps, notably in Rumangabo.
r1-GOE-027.n: S/2026/466 para. 66 (sources: AFC/M23 recruits, UN, military intelligence, researchers, civil society; interviews with former recruits). Leon Kanyamibwa identified as the AFC/M23 commander responsible for all training centres (same paragraph).
r1-GOE-027.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/M23 continued to forcibly or voluntarily recruit adults and minors (see S/2025/858, para. 22). 70 Former recruits denounced systematic torture and executions in training camps, notably in Rumangabo.
Leon Kanyamibwa continued to be identified as AFC/M23 commander responsible for all training centres

r1-GOE-028.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.
r1-GOE-028.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (eastern DRC)
r1-GOE-028.n: S/2026/466 para. 11 (cross-referring to S/2025/858 para. 80 and annex 37). The paragraph does not name provinces; the report as a whole covers eastern DRC. Date is the report's period (2025 into 2026).
r1-GOE-028.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations (see S/2025/858, para. 80 and annex 37). Humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, with cases disproportionately affecting women and girls

r1-GOE-029.s: The Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 the UN in the DRC verified at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, with North Kivu the most affected province (33 victims: 22 women and 11 girls), followed by South Kivu (22 victims: 13 women and nine girls) and Ituri (six victims).
r1-GOE-029.a: not attributed in this passage (see next claim)
r1-GOE-029.x: UN (as cited by the Group): 46 cases, 61 victims; North Kivu 33 victims; South Kivu 22 victims

src: In January 2026, the UN in DRC verified at least 46 cases of CRSV affecting 61 victims in conflict-affected provinces in eastern DRC.

North Kivu was the most affected province with 33 victims (22 women and 11 girls), followed by South Kivu with 22 victims (13 women and nine girls) and Ituri with six victims (four women, one girl and one man).

r1-GOE-030.s: The Group of Experts reported, citing a UN source, that for the January 2026 verified cases armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims (M23 most, with 21 victims, then Nyatura four, Raïa Mutomboki three and ADF two), while State agents were responsible for 46 per cent of the cases, with FARDC soldiers ranking first, followed by the PNC and one official from the Ministry of Mines and Energy.
r1-GOE-030.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
r1-GOE-030.a: M23; Nyatura; Raïa Mutomboki; ADF; FARDC; PNC
r1-GOE-030.x: UN (as cited by the Group): armed groups 52 per cent of victims; State agents 46 per cent of cases
r1-GOE-030.n: S/2026/466 annex 4. The cited figures cover all conflict-affected provinces in the data (includes Ituri). Excerpt may need tightening.
r1-GOE-030.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Armed groups continued to bear the main responsibility for CRSV and were responsible for cases affecting 52 per cent of victims. M23 committed most cases with 21 victims (13 women and eight girls)
the Nyatura with four victims (two women and two girls), the Raïa Mutomboki with three victims (two women and one girl), and the ADF with two victims, (both women).
State agents were responsible for 46 percent of the cases. FARDC soldiers ranked first followed by the PNC and one official from Ministry of Mines and Energy.

r1-GOE-031.s: The Group of Experts reported that IPS inspectors of the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department inspected the premises of humanitarian actors after an 11 February 2026 AFC/M23 'Note Explicative', requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits to curb what AFC/M23 alleged were 'fake' victims.
r1-GOE-031.n: S/2026/466 annex 5 (confidential sources; 'Note Explicative' dated 11 February 2026 on file with the Secretariat). The Group notes AFC/M23's stated intention not to impede access to assistance (annex 5 para. 6) and that its actions may deter victims from seeking assistance (para. 8).
r1-GOE-031.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: The Group reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026 that the AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in the provision of health care

Following the distribution of this note, the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (Inspection Provinciale de la Santé or IPS) initiated a series of inspections of the premises of humanitarian actors. IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims and other personal information
Some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease the distribution of dignity kits to curb the number of what they alleged to be “fake” victims seeking humanitarian assistance.

r1-GOE-032.s: The Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 AFC/M23 officials reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data about sexual violence, affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence, and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; the officials present included Colonel John Imani Nzenze and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete.
r1-GOE-032.n: S/2026/466 annex 5 para. 6 (confidential sources). The same paragraph reports a later agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared, and AFC/M23's stated intention to increase oversight of humanitarian actors but not to impede access or provision of assistance. Meeting venue not stated.
r1-GOE-032.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: A joint meeting was held in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23 at which the issue of sexual violence data was discussed. AFC/M23 officials present at the meeting included Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and the AFC/M23 liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete

At the meeting, the AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data. It affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files as this made it more difficult for it to punish perpetrators

r1-GOE-033.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 15 November 2025 ADF elements entered the village of Byambwe, Lubero territory, killing 23 civilians including women admitted to the maternity ward inside a Catholic Church-run health center, setting four hospital pavilions housing patients on fire, and looting and burning the medical facility, from which equipment and medicines were taken.
r1-GOE-033.l: Byambwe (Biambwe), Manzya groupement, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-GOE-033.x: Group of Experts: 23 civilians killed (13 women and 10 men)
r1-GOE-033.n: S/2026/466 annex 9 (ADF attacks since June 2025), para. 8 (sources: UN, civil society, local authorities, military, police, intelligence, judicial authorities, researchers). Radio Okapi (next claim) gave a provisional toll of 20 civilians, 18 of them patients. Names of villages spelled as the report prints them.
r1-GOE-033.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Radio Okapi gave a provisional toll of 20 civilians, 18 of them patients (separate claim); the figures are not merged.
src: On 15 November 2025, between approximately 19:00 and 23:00 hours, ADF elements carried out an incursion into the village of Byambwe, in Manzya groupement, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, killing 23 civilians, including 13 women and 10 men. Among the victims were women admitted to the maternity ward who were killed inside a Catholic Church–run health center.

During the attack, four hospital pavilions housing patients were set on fire. The assailants looted and burned 27 houses, including the medical facility, from which equipment and medicines were taken.

r1-GOE-034.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, that ADF fighters targeted the health centre in Byambwe (night of Friday to Saturday 15 November), where they killed people, looted medicines and set neighbouring houses on fire; the provisional toll, not yet confirmed by official sources, was 20 civilians killed, including 18 patients receiving care in the facility.
r1-GOE-034.l: Centre de santé de Byambwe, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-GOE-034.a: ADF (as Radio Okapi reports, attributed to ADF rebels)
r1-GOE-034.x: Radio Okapi: provisional toll of 20 civilians killed, including 18 patients
r1-GOE-034.n: Radio Okapi, 15 Nov 2025. Provisional toll (20, incl. 18 patients) differs from the Group of Experts' 23; figures are per source and unmerged.
r1-GOE-034.vn: Figures field carried the Group's 23, which this source does not print; narrowed to Radio Okapi's own figures. Date and place are in the article's lead paragraph. Provisional toll per Radio Okapi; the Group of Experts gives 23 killed (separate claim). Figures not merged. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon des sources locales concordantes, les ADF ont ciblé le Centre, où ils ont tué, pillé des médicaments et incendié des maisons voisines. Le bilan provisoire, pas encore confirmé par des sources officielles, est de 20 civils tués, dont 18 malades qui recevaient des soins dans cette structure sanitaire

Le bilan de la récente attaque meurtrière des islamistes ADF à Byambwe, dans le territoire de Lubero, dans la nuit du vendredi 14 novembre, a été revu à la hausse, passant de 20 à 28 personnes tuées, dont 17 patients exécutés au centre de santé de référence de la localité.

r1-GOE-035.s: The Group of Experts reported in an annex that an attack attributed to Abwakasi's elements on the night of 8 to 9 September 2025 on civilians attending a funeral in Ntuyo village, east of Manguredjipa in Lubero territory, killed 71 civilians, including men, women and children, and that at least 36 houses were looted and set on fire; the main text of the same report dates the massacre of 71 civilians at a funeral in 'Nturo village' to November 2025.
r1-GOE-035.l: Ntuyo / Nturo village, Manguredjipa, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-GOE-035.x: Group of Experts: 71 civilians killed; at least 36 houses looted and burned
r1-GOE-035.n: DISCREPANCY inside S/2026/466: annex 9 para. 7 gives the night of 8-9 September 2025 and the village as 'Ntuyo'; main text para. 20 says 'Nturo village in November 2025'. Not resolved here. Lubero is in North Kivu. Excerpt 1 may exceed 60 words; trim if flagged.
r1-GOE-035.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. DISCREPANCY within S/2026/466: annex 9 gives the night of 8-9 September 2025 and 'Ntuyo'; the main text (para. 20) gives November 2025 and 'Nturo'. Neither date is preferred here.
src: Among the most significant incidents attributed to Abwakasi’s elements was the massacre of civilians attending a funeral in Ntuyo village, located approximately 6 kilometers east of Manguredjipa town, in Bapere sector, Lubero territory. The attack was carried out on the night of 8 to 9 September 2025
A total of 71 civilians, including men, women, and children, were killed. At least 36 houses were looted and set on fire
Abwakasi’s group massacred 71 civilians attending a funeral in Nturo village in November 2025.

r1-GOE-036.s: The Group of Experts reported that between January and December 2025 the UN in the DRC verified at least 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 1,534 victims in conflict-affected provinces of eastern DRC, a 59 per cent increase on 2024 (364 cases); North Kivu was the most affected province (676 victims), followed by South Kivu (537) and Ituri (300).
r1-GOE-036.a: not attributed in this passage (see next claim)
r1-GOE-036.x: UN (as cited by the Group): 887 cases, 1,534 victims; North Kivu 676; South Kivu 537; Ituri 300
r1-GOE-036.n: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 3 (UN-verified data; figures as printed, verified cases only; Group notes elsewhere that CRSV is under-reported). Victim breakdown: 854 women, 672 girls, four men, four boys.
r1-GOE-036.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. UN-verified cases only, as cited by the Group.
src: Between January and December 2025, the UN in DRC verified at least 887 cases of CRSV affecting a total of 1,534 victims in conflict-affected provinces in eastern DRC. This represented an increase of 59 per cent in comparison to 2024 when 364 cases were verified.
Among the victims were 854 women, 672 girls, four men, and four boys. North Kivu was the most affected province with 676 victims, followed by South Kivu with 537 victims and Ituri with 300 victims.

r1-GOE-037.s: The Group of Experts reported, for the 2025 cases verified by the UN, that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of victims (M23 ranked first, followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions) and State agents for 19 per cent (FARDC soldiers first, followed by the PNC), and that the UPDF, the FNDB and RED-Tabara were also responsible for CRSV cases.
r1-GOE-037.a: M23; CODECO; Wazalendo; Mai-Mai factions; FARDC; PNC; UPDF; FNDB; RED-Tabara
r1-GOE-037.x: UN (as cited by the Group): armed groups 75 per cent of victims; State agents 19 per cent
r1-GOE-037.n: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 3. 'FNDB' is the spelling printed in the annex (Burundi National Defence Force is elsewhere abbreviated FDNB). Counts by province are not broken down by perpetrator in the passage.
r1-GOE-037.vn: Year 2025 is printed in the same annex paragraph (para. 3) that opens with the January-December 2025 figures; all other clauses in the excerpts.
src: The UN identified that DRC armed groups were responsible for cases affecting 75 per cent of CRSV victims. M23 ranked first followed by CODECO, Wazalendo and Mai-Mai factions. State agents were responsible for cases affecting 19 per cent of CRSV victims. FARDC soldiers ranked first followed by the PNC.
Foreign armed forces – the UPDF and the FNDB – as well as foreign armed groups – RED-Tabara – were also responsible for CRSV cases.

r1-GOE-038.s: The Group of Experts reported, citing its earlier report (S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38), that it had verified a sharp escalation of conflict-related sexual violence cases in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups.
r1-GOE-038.a: Wazalendo armed groups (areas under DRC Government and Wazalendo control)
r1-GOE-038.n: S/2026/466 annex 4 para. 1, referring to S/2025/858 para. 82 and annex 38. The Group also says it received information about but could not investigate new CRSV cases in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements (same paragraph).

The Group has verified a sharp escalation of cases of CRSV in South Kivu in areas under the control of the DRC Government and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups (S/2025/858, para. 82, annex 38)

r1-GOE-039.s: The Group of Experts reported that mining activity at AFC/M23-controlled Rubaya increased substantially compared with a year earlier according to its March 2026 satellite imagery model, with production assessed to exceed 2024 estimates of approximately 120 tons monthly, and that AFC/M23 taxed all actors, with a per-kilogram tax at commercialization of $4 for coltan and $2 for cassiterite.
r1-GOE-039.x: Group of Experts: above approx. 120 tons monthly (2024 estimate); $4/kg coltan, $2/kg cassiterite
r1-GOE-039.n: S/2026/466 paras. 213-214 and annexes 67-68 (satellite model from high resolution imagery of March 2026). Category chosen as resource exploitation; no atrocity alleged in the passage.
r1-GOE-039.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Comparison with activity observed one year earlier indicated a substantial increase in mining activity. Production levels are assessed to exceed 2024 estimates of approximately 120 tons monthly

AFC/M23 continued to tax all actors involved in the production and supply chains. The most significant revenue was generated through a per-kilogram tax imposed at the point of commercialization, 239 notably $4 for coltan and $2 for cassiterite.

r1-GOE-040.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 issued per-kilogram tax invoices in Rubaya and Mubambiro, and that once shipments were delivered in Rwanda the transporter settled AFC/M23 tax payments by depositing the amounts in an Equity Bank account held by Patient Haba, the AFC/M23 provincial financial coordinator.
r1-GOE-040.n: S/2026/466 para. 217; Group also names Bazimazika Kabano Bazinga as AFC/M23-appointed coordinator for artisanal mining in Rubaya (para. 215) and Patrice Biraira as overseeing transport coordination (para. 216).
r1-GOE-040.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/M23 issued per-kilogram tax invoices in Rubaya and Mubambiro, which were paid after delivery in Rwanda. Once shipments were delivered in Rwanda, the transporter settled AFC/M23 tax payments by depositing the amounts in an Equity Bank account held by Patient Haba, the AFC/M23 provincial financial coordinator

r1-GOE-041.s: The Group of Experts reported that in early December 2025 AFC/M23 introduced a codified list of taxes mirroring Congolese State tax structures, and that the national water and electricity companies (SNEL and REGIDESO) were placed under the administrative authority of the AFC/M23-appointed governor and the financial oversight of the AFC/M23 finance department.
r1-GOE-041.l: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
r1-GOE-041.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

the national water and electricity companies (SNEL and REGIDESO) were placed under the administrative authority of the AFC/M23 -appointed governor and the financial oversight of the AFC/M23 finance department

r1-GOE-042.s: The Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups established new geographically organized coalitions called 'synergies': the 'Synergie Front Grand Nord' (24 armed groups in Lubero and Beni, commanded by UPLC leader 'General' Mayani), the 'Synergie Petit Nord' (14 groups in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo, commanded by Jonas Bigabo), and the 'Synergie Masisi-Walikale' (17 groups, led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa).
r1-GOE-042.l: Lubero, Beni, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
r1-GOE-042.x: Group of Experts: 24, 14 and 17 armed groups respectively
r1-GOE-042.n: S/2026/466 paras. 107-108 (Wazalendo commanders, combatants, FARDC and official authorities). FDLR-FOCA combatants were integrated into the Masisi-Walikale and Petit Nord synergies (same paragraph).

r1-GOE-043.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 80 and 150 Wazalendo groups were reported active across South Kivu, with at least 70 self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'Generals' operating in Uvira and its surroundings, and that by December 2025 Uvira had become the epicentre of tensions and clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo and among Wazalendo fighting over revenue from illegal taxation.
r1-GOE-043.x: Group of Experts: 80-150 groups; at least 70 self-proclaimed generals
r1-GOE-043.n: S/2026/466 paras. 109 and 112. Excerpts adjusted by builder.
r1-GOE-043.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Between 80 and 150 Wazalendo groups were reported active across South Kivu, with at least 70 self proclaimed Wazalendo “Generals” operating in Uvira and its surroundings 127 (see annex 35). Mobilization and recruitment increased.
By December 2025, Uvira had become the epicentre of tensions and clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo and among Wazalendo fighting over revenue from illegal taxation.

r1-GOE-044.s: The Group of Experts reported that at the time of drafting Wazalendo factions in South Kivu remained divided into at least three coordinations, one led by Yakutumba, another by Alexis Mwamba Dunya (the RAD-appointed coordinator in South Kivu) and a third by Ngomanzito, and that renewed efforts to establish a unified command had failed.
r1-GOE-044.n: S/2026/466 para. 117. Footnote: in late December 2025 in Baraka William Yakutumba was elected overall Wazalendo coordinator but several Wazalendo leaders rejected his appointment. Spelling 'Ngomanzito' as printed in para. 117 ('Ngomazito' appears in para. 121).
r1-GOE-044.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: renewed efforts to establish a unified command had failed and the Wazalendo factions remained divided into at least three distinct coordinations: 136 one led by Yakutumba; 137 another by Alexis Mwamba Dunya, the RAD-appointed coordinator in South Kivu; and a third by Ngomanzito, who attempted to establish a “special unit” mobilized along ethnic lines, notably from the Bafuliro community.

r1-GOE-045.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 22 August 2025 Brigadier-General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, Commander of the Sokola 2 operational sector in South Kivu, met the main Wazalendo groups to define a counteroffensive strategy against AFC/M23 and RDF, and that FARDC subsequently transferred truckloads of weapons and ammunition to Wazalendo at several front lines, including Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika and Walungu.
r1-GOE-045.l: Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika, Walungu, South Kivu
r1-GOE-045.n: S/2026/466 para. 120 (intelligence, armed groups sources, civil society, UN, researchers). The transfers' dates after 22 August 2025 are not given.
r1-GOE-045.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: FARDC continued to supply war materiel to Wazalendo. On 22 August 2025, Brigadier-General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, Commander of Sokola 2 operational

sector in South Kivu, met with the main Wazalendo groups to define a counteroffensive strategy against AFC/M23 and RDF. Subsequently, FARDC transferred truckloads of weapons and ammunition to Wazalendo at several front lines, including Kiliba, Songe, Luvungi, Lubarika and Walungu.

r1-GOE-046.s: The Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with the FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain: FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover, and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.
r1-GOE-046.l: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu

r1-GOE-047.s: The Group of Experts reported that the Coalition nationale du peuple pour la souveraineté du Congo (CNPSC), led by Yakutumba, maintained a parallel administration in areas it controlled, particularly in Fizi territory, that in January 2026 its 'finance bureau' published a list of taxes across multiple sectors, and that since 2023 it had operated a parallel judicial system with detention facilities, former detainees reporting release conditioned on payment of fines of 2,000,000 to 5,000,000 Congolese francs.
r1-GOE-047.x: Group of Experts: fines 2,000,000-5,000,000 Congolese francs
r1-GOE-047.n: S/2026/466 paras. 123-125 and annexes 37-38. Excerpt anchors adjusted by builder.

Former detainees reported that release was conditioned on the payment of fines ranging between 2,000,000 and 5,000,000 Congolese francs

r1-GOE-048.s: The Group of Experts reported that FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions (FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-FPP), that 'Major-General' Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and 'General' Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA's military commander and political leader, and that UN and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.
r1-GOE-048.l: North Kivu (Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale) and South Kivu
r1-GOE-048.x: Group of Experts (UN and intelligence sources): 3,500 to 4,500 FDLR combatants
r1-GOE-048.n: S/2026/466 paras. 126-127 and 130. FDLR sources claimed over 10,000 combatants (para. 130); the Washington Agreement estimated 3,000 to 3,500. Anchors adjusted by builder.
r1-GOE-048.vn: Figures field carried FDLR-claimed and Washington Agreement estimates that no excerpt prints; narrowed to the excerpted estimate.
src: At the time of writing, FDLR (Cde.005) was fragmented into three principal factions: FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP)

“Major-General” Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) (CDi.024) and “General” Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) (CDi.003) remained, respectively, FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader.
United Nations and intelligence sources estimated that the total FDLR strength was between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants

r1-GOE-049.s: The Group of Experts reported that in late March 2026 a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by 'Major-General' Uzabakiriho Cyprien that had been fighting AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory, and that on 7 April a confidential encounter between a Kinshasa delegation including FARDC generals and the FDLR-FOCA high command in Pinga decided that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.
r1-GOE-049.n: S/2026/466 paras. 136-137 (FDLR-FOCA, intelligence and UN sources; Wazalendo commanders, FDLR, FARDC, intelligence sources). This is the Group's account from FDLR/FARDC/intelligence sources; no Kinshasa reply on this point is recorded in the report.

src: On 7 April, a confidential encounter between a high -level delegation from Kinshasa, including FARDC generals, and representatives of the FDLR -FOCA high command in Pinga decided, inter alia, that FDLR-FARDC cooperation would continue.

In late March 2026, a FARDC helicopter landed in Pinga to deliver weapons to FDLR-FOCA units led by “Major-General” Uzabakiriho Cyprien (alias Kolomboka Niyo Tedium Mugisha) that had been engaged in fighting against AFC/M23 and RDF in Masisi territory

r1-GOE-050.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 29 March 2026 FARDC announced the launch of an operation to neutralize FDLR around Pinga-Walikale and deployed additional troops from Kisangani to Walikale, but that at the time of writing no anti-FDLR operations had taken place.
r1-GOE-050.n: S/2026/466 para. 51 (FARDC sources); the Group's assessment that commitment 'remained questionable' is its own and not the FARDC's.
r1-GOE-050.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.

r1-GOE-051.s: The Group of Experts reported that private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered Uvira in January 2026, that multiple drone strikes conducted with their support targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe on 1 February 2026, and that between 2 and 8 February 2026 they airdropped FARDC 'Hiboux' special forces units at Point Zero.
r1-GOE-051.l: Uvira, Minembwe and Point Zero, South Kivu
r1-GOE-051.n: S/2026/466 para. 144; see also paras. 143 (Jan-Mar 2026 contractors in South Kivu) and 145-148 (Quantum Global / Vectus Global; Vectus told the Group in Feb 2026 that the DRC Government had requested support in planning operations to retake Uvira). Mr. Sirot denied involvement in the contract's military aspects (para. 148).
r1-GOE-051.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: private military contractors accompanied FARDC when they entered in Uvira in January 2026 (see para. 40). 178 On 1 February 2026, multiple drone strikes conducted with the support of private military contractors targeted AFC/M23 positions around Minembwe. 179 Between 2 and 8 February 2026, private military contractors airdropped FARDC “Hiboux” special forces units at Point Zero

r1-GOE-052.s: The Group of Experts reported that a meeting in Washington, D.C. on 17 and 18 March 2026 between representatives of the Governments of the DRC, Rwanda and the United States resulted in an 'initial steps plan' that foresaw withdrawal of RDF and AFC/M23 'personnel and equipment', Rwanda's disengagement from defined areas, efforts by the DRC to neutralize the FDLR, and restrictions on drone strikes.
r1-GOE-052.l: Washington, D.C.; areas of interest in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale (North Kivu) and South Kivu
r1-GOE-052.a: DRC government; Rwandan government; United States
r1-GOE-052.n: S/2026/466 paras. 43-45 (a copy of the plan was consulted by the Group; annex 18). Statement is about a political agreement, not a communiqué; recorded as reported by the Group.
r1-GOE-052.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: a meeting in Washington, D.C. on 17 and 18 March 2026 between representatives of the Governments of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Rwanda and the United States resulted in commitments defined in an “initial steps plan

The plan included coordinated steps to de-escalate tensions, commitments to sovereignty and territorial integrity, Rwanda’s disengagement from defined areas in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, efforts by the Democratic Republic of the Congo to neutralize the Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR), restrictions on drone strikes
The plan foresaw the withdrawal of both RDF and AFC/M23 “personnel and equipment

r1-GOE-053.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 representatives announced that no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations.
r1-GOE-053.n: S/2026/466 para. 50 (footnote 50 cites an X post by Lawrence Kanyuka). Date approximate: after the 23 March 2026 start of reported withdrawals and before 15 April 2026.
r1-GOE-053.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: AFC/M23 representatives announced that no withdrawal was taking place, describing movements as routine troop rotations

r1-GOE-054.s: The Group of Experts reported public statements by the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, that 'defensive measures' also included troop deployment in the DRC.
r1-GOE-054.n: S/2026/466 para. 50; annex 19 is a Kagame interview published in Jeune Afrique (date not stated in the excerpt). The same sentence goes on to give the Group's own inference about Rwanda's intent, which is not part of this claim.
r1-GOE-054.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: as well as public statements by the President of Rwanda, Paul Kagame, that “defensive measures” also included troop deployment in the Democratic Republic of the Congo

r1-GOE-055.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals on 1 and 3 March respectively as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, that male caregivers were briefly detained and released, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted (48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho), some undergoing treatment and others who had refused to leave for fear of forced recruitment. It reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, saying they acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law to secure the hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants' who were 'endangering' patients and staff, and that, contrary to those assertions, witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals and the arrested individuals had not endangered patients or staff.
r1-GOE-055.l: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-055.x: Group of Experts: 164 patients abducted (48 from Heal Africa, 116 from CBCA Ndosho)
r1-GOE-055.n: S/2025/446 paras. 105 and 107. Date given as the report's 1 March (Heal Africa) and 3 March (CBCA Ndosho). A lead from the OHCHR press release of 3 March 2025 (not fetched here) gives the night of 28 February for the raids: possible date discrepancy for a verifier. The report calls the individuals taken 'patients' and also describes them as people hors de combat; AFC/M23's own account is in the denial claims.
r1-GOE-055.vn: Date was the second raid only; set to the 1-3 March range the paragraph gives. Figures field carried the AFC/M23 figure of 130, which no excerpt of this claim prints. AFC/M23's communiqué figure (130 FARDC elements taken) is a separate claim. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: AFC/M23 leaders' denials (para. 107) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: The claim quotes 'contrary to those assertions' without saying what was asserted, so it leaves out AFC/M23's denial (check 8). Para. 107 of the retained report gives it. Dates and counts differ from OHCHR/Reuters (night of 28 Feb; 116 and 15) and Amnesty (more than 130); keep the discrepancy surfaced.; excerpt-support: added para. 107 (AFC/M23 leaders' public denials) as an excerpt; 'operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants' is already in source 0
src: AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma. Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals were targeted, on 1 and 3 March, respectively, as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered (see para. 21 above). Male caregivers were briefly detained and released.
A total of 164 patients were abducted – 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho – some of whom had been undergoing treatment, others who had refused to leave for fear of forced recruitment
Contrary to those assertions, witnesses confirmed that no weapons were found in the hospitals and the arrested individuals had not endangered patients or staff

Following the incidents in March, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and “General” Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming they had acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and with the aim of securing the hospitals from “infiltrated rogue combatants” who had been “endangering” patients and medical staff

r1-GOE-056.s: The Group of Experts reported in an annex that on 3 March 2025 Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital amongst other sick and wounded patients, and that he subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23.
r1-GOE-056.l: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-056.n: S/2025/446, annex on AFC/M23 parallel administration and customary chiefs (page 86 of the report). Cross-refers to paras. 105-108. Cause of death is stated as 'reportedly'.
r1-GOE-056.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On 3 March 2025, Fikiri Mwishuko, the Chef de groupement of Shanga, was abducted by AFC/M23 from the CBCA Ndosho hospital (paras. 105-108), amongst others sick and wounded patients. Fikiri Mwishuko subsequently died, reportedly after having been tortured by AFC/M23.

r1-GOE-057.s: The Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed treatment but stayed for fear of being recruited, opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members; the soldiers did not enter the ward but bullets struck treatment areas.
r1-GOE-057.x: Group of Experts: one person killed, three injured, two staff assaulted
r1-GOE-057.n: S/2025/446 para. 106 (protection sources; footnote cites MSF statement).
r1-GOE-057.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On the night of 4 to 5 April 2025, armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed medical treatment but remained at the hospital for fear of being recruited. The AFC/M23 elements opened fire within the facility grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.
Although the soldiers did not enter the hospital ward, bullets struck the treatment areas.

r1-GOE-058.s: The Group of Experts reported that an official AFC/M23 communiqué of 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denied responsibility for the raids on Goma hospitals and accused MONUSCO officials of erroneous interpretation of the facts; the communiqué acknowledged that 130 FARDC elements were taken but claimed the operation was peaceful and in full compliance with international humanitarian law because the elements had 'infiltrated' the medical facilities.
r1-GOE-058.n: S/2025/446 annex 52 (AFC/M23 leadership denials of responsibility for attacks on hospitals in Goma). The Group reports the communiqué's content; it is a partisan statement recorded as what AFC/M23 said. See also para. 107 (Bisimwa, Kanyuka and Makenga denials).
r1-GOE-058.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. AFC/M23's account as reported by the Group; the Group states witnesses confirmed no weapons were found (separate claim).
src: An official AFC/M23 communiqué was published on 5 March 2025, signed by Lawrence Kanyuka, denying responsibility for the raids on the hospitals, accusing MONUSCO officials of erroneous interpretation of the facts

The communiqué acknowledges that 130 FARDC elements were taken, but claims that the operation was carried out in in a peaceful manner and in full compliance with IHL, because the FARDC elements had “infiltrated” the medical facilities

r1-GOE-059.s: The Group of Experts reported that in an interview excerpt published on X on 13 March 2025, 'General' Sultani Makenga, asked about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, repeated that the men arrested were former FARDC pretending to be patients or hospital staff.
r1-GOE-059.l: Heal Africa hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-059.n: S/2025/446 annex 52. The annex also gives the English translation of Makenga's reply: 'Former FARDC soldiers were pretending to be patients or hospital attendants. Fourteen weapons were found there.' The Group's finding that no weapons were found is in para. 107.
r1-GOE-059.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On 13 March 2025, the excerpt from an interview by Alain Destexhe, a Belgian national, with “General” Sultani Makenga was published on “X”. Responding to a question about the raid on the Heal Africa hospital, Makenga repeated the claims that the men who were “arrested” were former FARDC who were pretending to be patients or hospital staff

r1-GOE-060.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 19 January and 14 February 2025 multiple incidents harmed medical facilities and personnel: on 20 January bullets and several rockets landed near the MSF-supported hospital in Masisi town, killing one MSF worker and injuring another; on 27 January firing and shelling affected two Goma hospitals, injuring a medical practitioner and a newborn at Goma Provincial Hospital; and humanitarian actors reported at least 27 health structures in and around Goma were impacted between 25 January and 14 February.
r1-GOE-060.l: Masisi town and Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-060.x: Group of Experts: one MSF worker killed and one injured (Masisi, 20 Jan); at least 27 health structures impacted around Goma (25 Jan-14 Feb)
r1-GOE-060.n: S/2025/446 paras. 81-83. The Group attributes the context to warring parties generally ('Indiscriminate shelling in populated areas'); no single perpetrator is named for these incidents.
r1-GOE-060.vn: Date range set to the paragraph's own 19 January-14 February 2025 window (printed on the page, para. 83). Statement unchanged.
src: On 20 January, bullets and several rockets landed near the Médecins sans frontières (MSF) -supported hospital in Masisi town, killing one MSF worker and injuring another.
On 27 January, intense firing and shelling affected two hospitals in Goma, injuring a medical practitioner and a newborn at Goma Provincial Hospital.
Humanitarian actors reported that, between 25 January and 14 February, at least 27 health structures in and around Goma had been impacted by attacks.

r1-GOE-061.s: The Group of Experts reported that human rights defenders said survivors of sexual violence faced significant barriers in accessing medical care, primarily due to fear of reprisals by AFC/M23 elements, and that a further alarming surge in sexual violence cases had been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict.
r1-GOE-061.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (Goma and surrounding areas)
r1-GOE-061.a: AFC/M23 (reprisal fear); all armed actors party to the conflict (surge)
r1-GOE-061.n: S/2025/446 humanitarian-impact annex on Goma ('Increasing sexual violence'); footnote cites MSF reporting of massive figures of sexual violence admissions. Date approximate (aftermath of the January-February 2025 fighting).
r1-GOE-061.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: A further alarming surge in cases has been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict, both in the immediate aftermath of the fighting and during the subsequent
consolidation of AFC/M23’s control. Human rights defenders reported that survivors faced significant barriers in accessing medical care, primarily due to fear of reprisals by AFC/M23 elements.

De nombreux autres cas de violence restent non documentés en raison de divers facteurs, tels que la crainte de représailles de la part des auteurs, la stigmatisation au sein de la communauté et l’inaccessibilité et l’absence de services spécialisés.

r1-GOE-062.s: The Group of Experts reported that reports on the mass escape of prisoners from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January 2025 indicated that over 160 women perished in a fire, with a significant number of women reportedly raped by escaping male prisoners, and that it had not been able to independently verify the figures.
r1-GOE-062.x: reported: over 160 women perished; Group of Experts has not verified
r1-GOE-062.n: S/2025/446 humanitarian-impact annex. The Group states it 'has not yet been able to independently verify the reported figures and continues to investigate the incident'.
r1-GOE-062.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. Unverified reports, as the Group itself states. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded C->B on independent, non-partisan corroboration.
src: Reports on the mass escape of prisoners from Muzenze prison in Goma on 27 January 2025 indicated that over 160 women perished in a fire that engulfed the facility, with a significant number of women reportedly raped by escaping male prisoners.284 The Group has not yet been able to independently verify the reported figures
Hours later, inside the compound, there was a fire - apparently set by male prisoners as they tried to escape.
A total of 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.
The BBC cannot verify how many women were raped that night,

r1-GOE-063.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 6 and 8 February 2025, in South Kivu between Kalehe and Kavumu, retreating FARDC forces looted civilian property and a health centre, forcibly enlisted civilians to transport stolen goods, deliberately killed at least 15 civilians and engaged in widespread sexual violence; in the same paragraph it reported that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, without stating where, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.
r1-GOE-063.l: between Kalehe and Kavumu, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r1-GOE-063.x: Group of Experts: at least 15 civilians killed; three girls aged 13 to 17 raped
r1-GOE-063.n: S/2025/446 para. 88 (civil society, FARDC, UN, audiovisual sources). The same passage reports FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported arrests, and that on 10 February at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu.
r1-GOE-063.vn: Original wording joined the MONUSCO-documented rapes to the Kalehe-Kavumu events; the source gives different dates and no place for them. The paragraph gives no place for the three rapes documented by MONUSCO; their dates (31 January-2 February) precede the Kalehe-Kavumu events. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: The excerpt carries the FARDC authorities' response (confirmation and arrests), which the statement left out; it is a party's account investigators need. Also restored the omitted forced-enlistment clause. No search run.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: Between 6 and 8 February, similar patterns were recorded in South Kivu, between Kalehe and Kavumu, as retreating FARDC forces looted civilian property and a health centre, forcibly enlisted civilians to transport stolen goods, deliberately killed at least 15 civilians 87 and engaged in widespread sexual violence.

MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February. FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.

r1-GOE-064.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 15 February 2025 the withdrawal of FARDC forces from Bukavu led to the escape of over 2,800 detainees and widespread looting, and that on 27 February two explosions at a public meeting hosted by Nangaa in Bukavu killed 17 civilians and wounded 68.
r1-GOE-064.x: Group of Experts: over 2,800 detainees escaped; 27 Feb explosions: 17 civilians killed, 68 wounded
r1-GOE-064.n: S/2025/446 para. 88 (end) and footnote 195 to para. 171. The footnote does not attribute the 27 February explosions. Two incidents on different days are combined in one claim as the same source's account of Bukavu in February 2025.
r1-GOE-064.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The Group does not attribute the 27 February explosions in this passage.
src: On 15 February, the withdrawal of FARDC forces from Bukavu led to the escape of over 2,800 detainees and widespread looting
At a public meeting hosted by Nangaa in Bukavu on 27 February, two explosions resulted in 17 civilians killed and 68 wounded.

r1-GOE-065.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 26 January 2025 several bombs launched from positions on the Bulenga peninsula, controlled by RDF, struck the Rusayo 1 and 2 internally displaced persons camps on the outskirts of Goma, killing at least 12 people including children and injuring many others.
r1-GOE-065.l: Rusayo 1 and 2 IDP camps, Goma outskirts, North Kivu
r1-GOE-065.a: bombs launched from RDF-controlled positions on the Bulenga peninsula (as the Group of Experts reports)
r1-GOE-065.x: Group of Experts: at least 12 killed
r1-GOE-065.n: S/2025/446 para. 84 (UN sources, local authorities, civil society). Excerpt includes footnote markers as printed.
r1-GOE-065.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On 26 January 2025, several bombs launched from positions on the Bulenga peninsula, controlled by RDF (see para. 53 above), 79 struck the Rusayo 1 and 2 internally displaced persons camps on the outskirts of Goma, killing at least 12 people, including children, and injuring many others.

r1-GOE-066.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 28 January and 9 April 2025 it recorded at least 70 distinct incidents of targeted killings in Goma attributable to AFC/M23, resulting in over 200 fatalities, with adult men the majority of victims but also women and children.
r1-GOE-066.x: Group of Experts: at least 70 incidents; over 200 fatalities
r1-GOE-066.n: S/2025/446 para. 100 (community-based confidential sources, residents, witnesses, UN and other sources). The Group lists motives in para. 101 (alleged collaboration with FARDC, FDLR or Wazalendo; refusal to join; dissent; civil society activity). Excerpt reproduces the PDF text spacing.
r1-GOE-066.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Between 28 January and 9 April, the Group recorded at least 70 distinct incidents of targeted kill ings in Goma attributable to AFC/M23, resulting in over 200 fatalities. Adult men comprised the majority of the victims, but which also included women and children.

r1-GOE-067.s: The Group of Experts reported that musician and activist Delcat Idengo (real name Delphin Katembo Vinywasiki) was shot and killed by AFC/M23 elements on 13 February 2025 in Goma shortly after publicly criticizing AFC/M23, and that eyewitnesses identified AFC/M23 fighters as responsible. The Group also reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka publicly denied any involvement the same evening, calling the killing a 'score-settling between different factions of the Wazalendo and the FARDC', and reiterated the denial on 12 March 2025.
r1-GOE-067.n: S/2025/446 annex 49 (local community leaders, civil society, researchers, audio-video testimonies on file with the Secretariat). First anchor to be finalised by the builder.
r1-GOE-067.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: killing took place in Goma 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kanyuka denial the same evening 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: denial reiterated on 12 March 2025 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Attribution matches the Group's annex, but the same annex records an AFC/M23 denial that the claim leaves out (counter-account, check 8). Read in the retained S/2025/446 text, annex on the killing of Delcat Idengo, under 'Denial of responsibility by AFC/M23'.; excerpt-support: added three excerpts from the annex: 'assassination in Goma' (caption), Kanyuka's denial of 13 February, and the reiteration of 12 March 2025
src: On 13 February 2025, Delcat Idengo – by his real name Delphin Katembo Vinywasiki – a well-known “revolutionary” activist musician, famous for his politically charged songs, was shot and killed by AFC/M23 elements shortly after publicly criticizing AFC/M23
Eyewitnesses who were at the scene identified AFC/M23 fighters as responsible for his assassination.
Screenshot from the video of Idengo’s recorded speech, two days prior to his assassination in Goma.

The same evening, on 13 February, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka publicly denied any involvement in the killing of Idengo, condemning it as a “score-settling between different factions of the Wazalendo and the FARDC”
A month later, on 12 March 2025, Lawrence Kanyuka reiterated his denial of AFC/M23’s responsibility for the killing of Idengo

r1-GOE-068.s: The Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths in the fighting for Goma, claiming that all fatalities were combatants, and that the Group stated these claims were contradicted by consistent reports of civilian casualties from residents, humanitarian and medical actors, UN sources, public reporting and photographic and video evidence.
r1-GOE-068.n: S/2025/446 para. 79 (see annex 44). Date approximate: refers to the January 2025 Goma hostilities; exact date of Bisimwa's statement not in the excerpt.
r1-GOE-068.vn: Checked against para. 79; the excerpt carries the denial and the contradiction.
src: Bertrand Bisimwa publicly denied civilian deaths, claiming that all fatalities were combatants (see annex 44). These claims were contradicted by consistent reports on civilian casualties from residents, humanitarian and medical actors

r1-GOE-069.s: The Group of Experts reported that after the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued by AFC/M23 on 11 February 2025, demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR and urging civilians to denounce them, AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC.
r1-GOE-069.n: S/2025/446 para. 102 (UN sources and protection actors). Ultimatum content as described by the Group.
r1-GOE-069.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: After the expiration of a seven-day ultimatum issued on 11 February by AFC/M23 – demanding the surrender of members of the FARDC, PNC, Wazalendo and FDLR, urging civilians to denounce them

and warning that failure to comply would result in being treated as enemies – AFC/M23 intensified house-to-house searches and targeted operations against individuals suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo, FDLR or FARDC

r1-GOE-070.s: The Group of Experts reported that after taking control of Goma, AFC/M23 forcibly displaced internally displaced persons camps west of the city, ordering civilians to vacate within 72 hours, without ensuring that returns were safe, and that tens of thousands were displaced again.
r1-GOE-070.l: IDP camps west of Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-070.n: S/2025/446 para. 93 (annex 48). The Group's legal characterisation in the paragraph is not reproduced. Date approximate: after the 27 January capture of Goma.
r1-GOE-070.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: After taking control of Goma, AFC/M23 forcibly displaced internally displaced persons camps west of the city, ordering civilians to vacate within 72 hours, without ensuring that returns were safe

r1-GOE-071.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and retained control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it, and that two weeks later they captured Minova town in Kalehe territory, South Kivu.
r1-GOE-071.l: Masisi centre (North Kivu) and Minova (Kalehe, South Kivu)
r1-GOE-071.n: S/2025/446 para. 14. 'Two weeks later' places Minova's capture at about 18 January 2025 (approximate). The report says the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before the arrival of AFC/M23 and RDF.
r1-GOE-071.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: On 4 January 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and managed to retain control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it. Two weeks later, AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu

r1-GOE-072.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 21 and 27 January 2025 several columns of RDF troops, each comprising hundreds of well-equipped soldiers, advanced into and seized control of Sake, Mubambiro and Goma town following a coordinated encirclement of each locality, and that Goma was fully conquered on 27 January.
r1-GOE-072.l: Sake, Mubambiro and Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-GOE-072.n: S/2025/446 paras. 35 and 16. Para. 15 adds that on 22 January RDF occupied the Bulenga peninsula. Group states Rwandan officials had confidentially informed it a week before that President Kagame had decided to take control of Goma and Bukavu (para. 34).
r1-GOE-072.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Between 21 and 27 January 2025, several columns of RDF troops, each comprising hundreds of well-equipped soldiers, advanced into and seized control of Sake, Mubambiro and Goma town, following a coordinated encirclement of each locality.
After several days of intense fighting, significant casualties were reported among combatants, including RDF, and among civilians (see paras. 65 –67 below). Goma was fully conquered on 27 January.

r1-GOE-073.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 January 2025 the Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami, known for his long-standing ties with FDLR-FOCA, was shot dead in Sake; in its annex 6 the Group says he was shot on 24 January while visiting FARDC and Wazalendo forces in Sake and succumbed to his injuries the following day.
r1-GOE-073.a: not attributed by the source in this passage
r1-GOE-073.n: S/2025/446 para. 15 (see annex 6). The excerpt says only that he 'was shot dead in Sake'; the perpetrator is not stated in the passage.
r1-GOE-073.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. The Military Governor of North Kivu, Major-General Peter Cirimwami, was shot on 24 January while visiting FARDC and Wazalendo forces in Sake to encourage them and request them to continue fighting. He succumbed to his injuries the following day.

r1-GOE-074.s: The Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF broke through the joint FARDC-FDNB positions in Nyabibwe on 6 February 2025, seized the strategic airport of Kavumu on 14 February, and that Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu, was taken on 16 February without combat.

r1-GOE-074.n: S/2025/446 para. 17; para. 170 says retreating FARDC units systematically committed abuses and that AFC/M23 announced the capture of Bukavu to protect the population from FARDC/Wazalendo atrocities.

src: AFC/M23 and RDF broke through the joint FARDC-FDNB positions in Nyabibwe on 6 February and managed to seize the strategic airport of Kavumu on 14 February. Bukavu, the provincial capital of South Kivu, was taken on 16 February without combat

r1-GOE-075.s: The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF forces withdrew from Walikale following sustained FARDC airstrikes targeting critical infrastructure including the Kigoma airstrip and mounting international pressure, and that, according to corroborated information, the withdrawal followed a direct instruction from the Government of Rwanda.
r1-GOE-075.n: S/2025/446 para. 18 ('wit hdraw' is a PDF text-extraction split). The same paragraph gives mid-March 2025 as when AFC/M23 and RDF advanced deep into Walikale territory. Para. 19: by early April 2025 the controlled area was the largest ever recorded, a 100 per cent increase compared with November 2024.
r1-GOE-075.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: In early April, AFC/M23 and RDF forces withdrew from Walikale following sustained FARDC airstrikes targeting critical infrastructure, including the Kigoma airstrip (see para. 38 below), alongside mounting international pressure.
According to corroborated information obtained by the Group, the decision to wit hdraw was taken following direct instruction from the Government of Rwanda

r1-GOE-076.s: The Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu, with a footnote citing former RDF and Rwandan intelligence reporting at least 10,000 RDF troops deployed in eastern DRC, and that by the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23-controlled territories.
r1-GOE-076.l: North Kivu and northern South Kivu
r1-GOE-076.x: Group of Experts: 6,000 (Jan-Feb 2025, conservative); former RDF/Rwandan intelligence: at least 10,000; Group (at time of writing): 1,000-1,500
r1-GOE-076.n: S/2025/446 paras. 36-37 and footnote 25. Figures are as stated by the Group per source and not merged.
r1-GOE-076.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: In January and February 2025, a conservative estimate of 6,000 25 RDF troops, including RDF special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu.
Former RDF and Rwandan intelligence reported that at least 10,000 RDF troops were deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo.
At the time of writing, an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.

r1-GOE-077.s: The Group of Experts reported that since 17 February 2025 Uvira experienced a severe breakdown in law and order as the AFC/M23 advance loomed and security forces retreated or lost control, with criminal elements and undisciplined FARDC and Wazalendo engaging in widespread killings, looting and attacks on civilian and humanitarian infrastructure, and that residents reported bodies strewn all over the city.
r1-GOE-077.n: S/2025/446 para. 89 (civilian, humanitarian and UN sources). The paragraph adds that for weeks the city was paralysed, with mass displacement of civilians to Burundi, and that until early April Wazalendo elements controlled the city 'operating with full impunity'.
r1-GOE-077.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: Similarly, since 17 February, Uvira experienced a severe breakdown in law and order, as the AFC/M23 advance loomed and security forces either retreated (see paras. 169–170 below) or lost control of key areas. Criminal elements and undisciplined FARDC and Wazalendo engaged in widespread killings, looting and attacks on civilian and humanitarian infrastructure. Residents reported bodies strewn all over the city.

r1-GOE-078.s: The Group of Experts reported that from February 2025, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups de facto controlled Uvira town and surroundings, using disproportionate force and committing widespread abuses, in particular targeting Banyamulenge communities, and that FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu Governorate were reinstalled in Uvira in early March.
r1-GOE-078.n: S/2025/446 paras. 173-174. Early April: the Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and RAD ex-coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to pacify Wazalendo groups (para. 174).
r1-GOE-078.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: From February, as the Democratic Republic of the Congo authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups de facto controlled
Uvira town and surroundings, where they resorted to the disproportionate use of force and widespread abuses, in particular targeting Banyamulenge communities.
FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu Governorate were reinstalled in Uvira in early March.

r1-GOE-080.s: The Group of Experts reported that Twirwaneho's sanctioned military leader, 'General' Michel Rukunda, was killed by a FARDC CH-4 drone strike on 15 February 2025, and that the following day, after heavy clashes with FARDC, Twirwaneho took control of the Minembwe airstrip, effectively cutting off FARDC resupply in the Hauts Plateaux.
r1-GOE-080.n: S/2025/446 para. 175 (security, FARDC and Banyamulenge sources, per footnote). The report says a second FARDC drone strike on 25 February killed four Twirwaneho leaders (para. 177). Rukunda's place of death not stated.

r1-GOE-082.s: The Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB supported by FARDC and Wazalendo, and AFC/M23 supported by RDF, resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.
r1-GOE-082.l: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux (Minembwe), South Kivu
r1-GOE-082.x: Group of Experts: 7,000-9,000 Burundian troops; several hundreds of FDNB casualties
r1-GOE-082.n: S/2025/446 para. 179 (annex 72). The report also states the troop build-up fuelled Rwanda-Burundi tensions.

Heavy clashes between FDNB supported by FARDC and Wazalendo, and AFC/M23 supported by RDF, resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.

r1-GOE-083.s: The Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back, and that Rwanda in turn signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the DRC.
r1-GOE-083.a: Government of Burundi; Government of Rwanda
r1-GOE-083.n: S/2025/446 para. 180 (annex 73). The Group's wording on Rwanda ('signalled a commitment to regime change') is its own characterisation and no Rwandan statement is quoted in the paragraph. In mid-March the two countries reportedly agreed verbal and military de-escalation (para. 181).
r1-GOE-083.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts. 'Signalled a commitment to regime change' is the Group's characterisation; no Rwandan statement is quoted.

Rwanda, in turn, signalled a commitment to regime change in both Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

r1-GOE-084.s: The Group of Experts reported that in Lubero town on 20 February 2025, after AFC/M23 advances led to heavy clashes and FARDC withdrawals, FARDC elements engaged in systematic looting of civilian homes and shops, and that the next day FARDC issued a public apology, attributing the acts to fleeing, undisciplined soldiers acting in violation of orders and assuring they would face justice.
r1-GOE-084.n: S/2025/446 para. 90. The report adds that on 15 March 55 FARDC elements convicted for the lootings were among 260 soldiers enrolled in a refresher training programme at Nyaleke, Beni. Excerpt includes footnote markers as printed.
r1-GOE-084.vn: Every clause checked against the retained report text; attributed to the Group of Experts.
src: In Lubero town, North Kivu, on 20 February 2025, after AFC/M23 advances had led to heavy clashes and FARDC withdrawals, FARDC elements engaged in systematic looting of civilian homes and shops. 93 The next day, FARDC issued a public apology, attributing the acts to fleeing, undisciplined soldiers acting in violation of orders, and giving assurances that they would face justice.

r1-GOE-085.s: The Group of Experts reported that, during operations by RDF and AFC/M23 in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, targeting FDLR and associated armed groups and civilians accused of collaborating with them, RDF and AFC/M23 forces carried out summary executions, arbitrary arrests and detentions, and the deliberate destruction and burning of civilian infrastructure, including homes and villages; and that since operations began in April 2025 UN and humanitarian sources reported over 300 civilians killed in Bwito chiefdom alone, both as collateral casualties and through targeted executions.

r1-GOE-085.x: UN and humanitarian sources (as cited by the Group): over 300 civilians killed in Bwito chiefdom alone since April 2025
r1-GOE-085.n: S/2025/858 para. 38. Footnote: UN and humanitarian actors reported the overall civilian death toll surpassed 500 throughout Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms since April 2025; the Group could not independently establish verified casualty figures. The Group also says the Bwito/Bwisha operations fall under the AFC/M23 'First Defence Zone' led by 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye (para. 44). The report's own legal characterisation (para. 43) is not reproduced.

r1-GOE-086.s: The Group of Experts reported that between 9 and 27 July 2025 over 300 civilian casualties were reported across Binza, notably in Nyamilima, Kisharo, Burambo, Kiseguro, Katwiguro, Musinga and Kigarigari, and that witness accounts, confirmed by photographic and video evidence, indicated civilians were summarily executed following arbitrary accusations of collaboration with FDLR or other Wazalendo armed groups, bodies were frequently disposed of in rivers, and burials were prohibited by local AFC/M23 authorities.

Bodies were frequently disposed of in rivers, and burials were prohibited by local AFC/M23 authorities.

r1-GOE-088.s: The Group of Experts reported that in mid-September 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF launched operations across northern Masisi, seizing Bibwe and several surrounding localities (an estimated 100 km²) while advancing towards Lukweti, and that on 21 September AFC/M23 captured Nzibira in Walungu territory, South Kivu, a strategic mineral trading hub.

r1-GOE-090.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force', named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer, and deployed primarily in Goma and Bukavu.

src: On 24 August 2025, “General” Sultani Makenga (CDi.008) unveiled the AFC/M23 “elite police force” operating under the movement’s internal security structure. 26 Named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC) (see annex 11), it was placed under the command of “Colonel” Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.
The new police units were deployed primarily in Goma and Bukavu, allowing military troops to focus on the front lines.

r1-GOE-091.s: The Group of Experts reported that systematic forced recruitment intensified in all areas under AFC/M23 occupation, with men and underage boys rounded up, often under the pretext of identity verification or security operations, and that attempted desertion or refusal of orders at training sites such as Rumangabo and Tchanzu led to inhumane punishments and summary executions.
r1-GOE-091.l: Rumangabo and Tchanzu, North Kivu; AFC/M23-held areas
r1-GOE-091.n: S/2025/858 paras. 22 and 25. AFC/M23 publicized the pass-out of 7,437 'commandos' at Rumangabo on 14 September and 9,350 at Tchanzu on 1 October 2025 (para. 23); the Group could not corroborate those figures.

r1-GOE-092.s: The Group of Experts reported that on 12 May 2025 AFC/M23 rounded up over 2,000 civilians, mostly Hutu, from collective shelters around Goma and Sake and transferred them under coercive conditions to the UNHCR transit centre in Goma, that 1,798 were subsequently transferred to Rwanda between 17 and 22 May, and that the AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs, Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba, threatened UNHCR staff to abort screenings. The Group reports that, despite AFC/M23's framing of the operation as a 'voluntary return' of Rwandan nationals, the conditions for voluntary returns were not met.

r1-GOE-092.x: Group of Experts: over 2,000 rounded up; 1,798 transferred to Rwanda

Attribution otherwise matches.; excerpt-support: added para. 85 as an excerpt; cut 'publicly' (the report says only 'the framing of the operation by AFC/M23') and kept the Group's rejection of that framing beside it
src: On 12 May 2025, AFC/M23 rounded up over 2,000 civilians from collective shelters around Goma and Sake – mostly Hutu civilians forcibly displaced by AFC/M23 in February from villages near Virunga National Park – and transferred them, under coercive conditions, to the transit centre for refugees managed by UNHCR in Goma.
Of these, 1,798 individuals were subsequently transferred to Rwanda between 17 and 22 May.
The AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs, Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba, threatened UNHCR staff to abort screenings and proceed with the transfer.
Despite the framing of the operation by AFC/M23 as a “voluntary return” of Rwandan nationals, the conditions for voluntary returns were not met.

r1-GOE-093.s: The Group of Experts reported, in an annex, that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories 'the recent months' were marked by a sharp escalation in human rights violations including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; separately, citing verified reports from field inquiries by UN-supported national NGOs, it said that between January and June 2025 at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu province alone, exceeding the total recorded in all other provinces combined, with incidents peaking in March.
r1-GOE-093.a: Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups; Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba

Reuters said M23 spokespersons Willy Ngoma and Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
