src: M23 fighters raided CBCA Ndosho Hospital and Heal Africa Hospital during the night of Feb. 28, taking 116 and 15 patients respectively, U.N. Human Rights Office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said in a statement.
The abducted men were suspected of being Democratic Republic of Congo soldiers or members of a pro-government militia known as Wazalendo.
East Congo rebels abduct at least 130 hospital patients, UN says By Reuters March 03, 2025
M23 rebels launching an offensive in east Congo abducted at least 130 sick and wounded men from two hospitals in the city of Goma last week, the United Nations said Monday.
M23 spokespersons Willy Ngoma and Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
Au moins 112 personnes ont été emmenées à une destination inconnue, dans la nuit du dimanche 2 mars, lors d'une opération des rebelles du M23 à l’Hôpital CBCA/Ndosho, à Goma (Nord-Kivu).

Les combattants du groupe M23, soutenu par le Rwanda, ont attaqué l’hôpital CBCA Ndosho et l’hôpital Heal Africa dans la nuit du 28 février, enlevant 116 patients de l’hôpital CBCA et 15 autres de Heal Africa, accusés d’être des militaires de l’armée congolaise ou des membres de la milice pro-gouvernementale Wazalendo.

r1-HC-2025-002.s: Lawrence Kanyuka, political spokesperson of AFC/M23, said the UN statement was false because those arrested in the hospitals were FARDC soldiers who had gone there to hide.
r1-HC-2025-002.n: Partisan account (AFC/M23 spokesperson), as relayed by Rwandan outlet Umuseke; the page says the UN statement was on Monday 3 March 2025.
r1-HC-2025-002.vn: Excerpt exact and the translation is faithful ('Umuryango w’Abibumbye' = United Nations). Shamdasani is printed on the page; passage given. Party account (AFC/M23). Umuseke is a Rwandan outlet. Date is the article date (6 March 2025); the page does not date Kanyuka's statement. The page also quotes him saying the operation to find '130 FARDC soldiers' hiding in hospitals was carried out peacefully and in line with international humanitarian law.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, umuvugizi mu bya Politiki wa AFC/M23, yavuze ko ibyo Umuryango w’Abibumbye uvuga ari ibinyoma, kuko abafatiwe muri biriya bitaro ari abasirikare ba FARDC bagiye kuhihisha.

r1-HC-2025-003.s: Amnesty International reported that Sultani Makenga, M23's military chief, said in an interview that Congolese army members in hospitals posed as patients or carers, that M23 found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff alerted them.
r1-HC-2025-003.x: Makenga as relayed by Amnesty: 14 weapons found in hospitals
r1-HC-2025-003.n: Makenga's own interview not located; relayed by Amnesty (undated 'recently'; Amnesty release is 18 March 2025). Date is report date.
r1-HC-2025-003.vn: Excerpt exact; attribution chain preserved. Party account relayed by Amnesty; the interview itself and its date were not located. Amnesty adds that Makenga said M23 arrested those who were not part of the hospital.
src: Sultani Makenga, le chef militaire du M23, a récemment déclaré dans une interview que les membres de l’armée congolaise présents dans les hôpitaux se faisaient passer pour des patients ou des soignants. Il a ajouté que le M23 avait trouvé 14 armes dans des hôpitaux et que le personnel hospitalier les avait alertés de la situation.

r1-HC-2025-004.s: Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that, since taking Goma in January, the Rwanda-backed M23 had raided hospitals, abducted patients from their beds (civilians and hospitalised Congolese soldiers) and subjected them to torture.
r1-HC-2025-004.n: Amnesty documented the allegation; M23 denies (see counterclaims). Amnesty's wording 'Rwanda-backed' is Amnesty's.
r1-HC-2025-004.vn: Excerpt exact; documented by a major NGO. Amnesty interviewed 25 victims, witnesses and others. It dates hospital raids to the night of 28 February and morning of 3 March (more than 130 taken to a stadium, some tortured). 'Rwanda-backed' is Amnesty's wording. M23 disputes (see counterclaims).
src: Depuis qu’il s’est emparé de la ville de Goma, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), en janvier, le groupe armé M23 soutenu par le Rwanda a effectué des descentes dans des hôpitaux, enlevé des patient·e·s dans leurs lits, dont des civil·e·s et des soldats congolais hospitalisés, et les a soumis à des actes de torture, a déclaré Amnesty International le 18 mars 2025.

r1-HC-2025-005.s: The WHO reported that, since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, and 65 injuries from 3 hospitals in South Kivu.
r1-HC-2025-005.l: Goma and surroundings, North Kivu; South Kivu hospitals
r1-HC-2025-005.x: WHO: 3082 injured and 843 dead from 31 health facilities in and around Goma; 65 injuries from 3 hospitals in South Kivu
r1-HC-2025-005.n: Report date used; figures are as reported by facilities to WHO, cumulative from 26 January.
r1-HC-2025-005.vn: WHO's own press release; excerpt exact. WHO is the publisher, so naming it is supported by the page. Cumulative figures reported by facilities to WHO, 26 January to 7 February 2025; WHO said they were expected to rise.
src: Since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead have been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu. With the alarming expansion of violence further south, 65 injuries were reported from 3 hospitals in South Kivu.

r1-HC-2025-006.s: Dr Sidibe Abdurahman, emergency physician at CBCA Ndosho hospital, said, as quoted by DW, that since January the hospital had received more than 1,000 patients against a capacity of 146 beds and was totally overwhelmed.
r1-HC-2025-006.x: more than 1.000 patients since January; capacity 146 beds
r1-HC-2025-006.n: Capacity context for hospital overload after the fall of Goma.
r1-HC-2025-006.vn: 'told DW' narrowed to 'as quoted by DW' (page uses 'explique'); '1000' flag is only number formatting. Single hospital physician quoted by DW (byline Ruth Alonga, 3 February 2025). The figure is printed '1.000' (French thousands separator).
src: Le docteur Sidibe Abdurahman, médecin urgentiste à l'hôpital CBCA Ndosho, explique que "d epuis janvier, nous avons reçu plus de 1.000 patients. Notre capacité est de 146 lits, nous sommes totalement débordés.

r1-HC-2025-007.s: The ICRC reported, from a study of health facilities in the Kivus, that three fifths of the facilities surveyed had experienced looting since the intensification of the conflicts.

src: Selon l’étude réalisée par le CICR, trois cinquièmes des structures interrogées ont connu des pillages depuis l’intensification des conflits.

r1-HC-2025-008.s: The ICRC reported that the majority of medical facilities noted a halving of consultations of children under five in the first quarter of 2025 compared with the same period in 2024, and quoted an observed increase of more than 4 times in the number of stillbirths in the facilities covered by the assessment, particularly in North Kivu.

r1-HC-2025-008.vn: Stillbirth figure is a quote from Etienne Penlap, now attributed; halving was 'noted by the majority of facilities', narrowed accordingly. Au 1er trimestre 2025, la majorité des établissements médicaux ont noté une diminution de moitié du nombre de consultations chez les enfants de moins de cinq ans, comparé à la même période en 2024.

src: Human Rights Watch also documented eight cases of rape by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira.

r1-HC-2026-002.s: Human Rights Watch reported that survivors of sexual violence in Uvira spoke of a near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, in particular the absence of timely HIV post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) and of adequate care for injuries and infections resulting from sexual violence.

src: Survivors spoke of the near-total lack of accessible healthcare services during the occupation, particularly the absence of timely post-exposure prophylactic (PEP) treatment to prevent contracting HIV, and of adequate care for injuries and infections resulting from sexual violence.

r1-HC-2026-003.s: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented the summary execution of 53 civilians by the M23 and Rwandan forces in Uvira, most on December 10, 2025, and that the forces went door-to-door seeking men and boys accused of ties to the Wazalendo.
r1-HC-2026-003.a: M23 and Rwandan forces, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
r1-HC-2026-003.x: HRW: 53 civilians summarily executed (documented), most on 10 December 2025; headline says "more than 50"

src: Human Rights Watch documented the summary execution of 53 civilians by the M23 and Rwandan forces, most on December 10.
Once M23 and Rwandan forces had control of Uvira, they began seeking out men and boys in door-to-door operations, accusing them of ties to the Wazalendo and executing many on the spot.

r1-HC-2026-004.s: Human Rights Watch reported that the M23 abducted civilians into their forces during the Uvira occupation and that, in at least 12 documented cases, their whereabouts remain unknown.
r1-HC-2026-004.a: M23, as alleged by Human Rights Watch

src: The M23 also abducted civilians into their forces during the Uvira occupation. In at least 12 documented cases, their whereabouts remain unknown.

r1-HC-2026-005.s: AFPDE reported in a humanitarian alert, citing reports from partner structures, that the territories of Uvira and Fizi faced a wave of violence marked by the systematic looting of health infrastructure from 5 December 2025. It said that more than 8 health centres, including KATOGOTA, LUBERIZI, NAZARENO, KILIBA CBCA, I’AMBA/MAKOBOLA, KABIMBA, MUNENE and ABEKA, and 1 hospital (Centre hospitalier d’ABEKA) were vandalised by unknown persons, depriving about 145003 people of all access to care. Elsewhere the same alert gives a total of 7 health structures neutralised, and it dates the Kabimba incident '15/01' with no year.
r1-HC-2026-005.l: Uvira and Fizi territories (health zones Lemera, Ruzizi, Nundu), South Kivu

r1-HC-2026-006.s: Opinion-info.cd reported on 30 January 2026 that, according to AFPDE, more than 145 000 people in Uvira and Fizi territories were deprived of access to care following the systematic looting of 'eleven' health structures in the region; the list it prints names twelve (Katogota, Luberizi, Nazareno, Kiliba CBCA, Kigoma, Mutarule, Nyakabere, Iamba/Makobola, Kabimba, Munene, Abeka and the Abeka hospital centre). The article does not name the looters; it says the situation worsened from early December 2025, after military positions at Katogota and Lubarika broke, and that health centres were looted as residents were fleeing.
r1-HC-2026-006.x: Opinion-info/AFPDE: more than 145 000 people; eleven structures (AFPDE alert text: more than 8 centres and 1 hospital, about 145003 people)
r1-HC-2026-006.n: Relays the same AFPDE assessment (not independent of the AFPDE alert); counts differ (eleven structures vs 8 centres plus 1 hospital).
r1-HC-2026-006.vn: Replacement quote extends the exact excerpt with the contiguous sentence naming the facilities; 'South Kivu' replaced with 'the region' as the excerpt says 'cette région' (the title prints Sud-Kivu). Relay of AFPDE, so corroborates but not independent. Relays the AFPDE alert (not independent of it). Counts differ from the alert itself: eleven structures here vs 'Plus de 8 centres de santé' and 1 hospital (and '7 structures' elsewhere) in the alert; this article adds Kigoma, Mutarule and Nyakabere. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Uvira and Fizi territories 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: list of twelve names 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: worsening from early December 2025 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: looting while residents were fleeing 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-022: Count discrepancy surfaced: 'onze structures' but twelve names listed on the retained page (and the AFPDE alert itself gives 8 centres and 1 hospital). src: Plus de 145 000 personnes sont privées d’accès aux soins, suite au pillage systématique de onze structures sanitaires dans cette région, a révélé ce vendredi l’Association des Femmes pour la Promotion et le Développement Endogène (AFPDE).
Une crise sanitaire majeure frappe actuellement les territoires d’Uvira et Fizi, dans la province du Sud-kivu

Parmi les structures affectées figurent des centres clés tels que Katogota, Luberizi, Nazareno, Kiliba CBCA, Kigoma, Mutarule, Nyakabere, Iamba/Makobola, Kabimba, Munene, Abeka ainsi que le Centre hospitalier d’Abeka.
Le rapport rendu public ce jour souligne que la situation s’est aggravée dès le début décembre 2025, à la suite de la rupture des positions militaires à Katogota et Lubarika.
Alors que les habitants fuyaient, certains centres de santé, déjà fragiles, ont été pillés
Selon des sources locales et humanitaires, au moins sept structures de santé dans les zones de santé de Ruzizi (territoire d’Uvira) et de Fizi (territoire de Fizi) ont été pillées et vandalisées
des sources sanitaires rapportent que plus de huit structures de santé ont été pillées dans les ZS de Ruzizi et d’Uvira, réduisant drastiquement, voire totalement, leurs capacités opérationnelles
Lors des désordres cette nuit-là, ces militaires et wazalendo ont dépouillé et saccagé le centre de santé Iàmba, situé dans le sous-village de Bangwe, dans la zone de santé Nundu.
Selon les estimations de l’AFPDE, environ 145 003 personnes sont aujourd’hui privées d’accès aux soins de santé

r1-HC-2026-007.s: LeJour reported that the military hospital of Uvira began refurbishment after damage and equipment losses suffered during the occupation and withdrawal of the M23-RDF coalition, and that, according to hospital officials, looting affected beds, mattresses, pharmaceutical cabinets and consumables as well as water and electricity networks.
r1-HC-2026-007.a: M23-RDF coalition, as characterised by LeJour; hospital officials describe "le pillage" without naming perpetrators
r1-HC-2026-007.x: LeJour: 54 new beds delivered on 25 February; 35 tonnes of medicines delivered the previous Friday; prior capacity about 50 beds
r1-HC-2026-007.n: Pro-Kinshasa framing: the delivery was made by presidential advisers on behalf of the Head of State (Kinshasa-side account). The perpetrator attribution is the outlet's own wording; officials quoted say only "le pillage". M23/Rwanda response not found.
r1-HC-2026-007.vn: Both excerpts exact in the retained page (byline 'Avec D. Michombero'). Figures 54/35/50 printed on page: 'Vendredi dernier, l’équipe présidentielle avait déjà livré 35 tonnes de médicaments' and 'dont la capacité antérieure était d’environ 50 lits'. Date 2026-02-25 is the delivery date, not the date of the looting. Kinshasa-aligned outlet; the M23-RDF attribution is the outlet's narration, while the hospital officials quoted describe 'le pillage' without naming who carried it out. The delivery was made by presidential advisers 'au nom du Chef de l’État'.
src: L’hôpital militaire d’Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, entame sa remise à niveau après des dégradations et pertes d’équipements subies lors de l’occupation et du retrait de la coalition rebelle M23–RDF.
Selon les responsables hospitaliers, le pillage a touché lits, matelas, armoires pharmaceutiques et consommables, ainsi que les réseaux d’eau et d’électricité, compromettant la continuité des soins.

r1-HC-2026-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) announced it had treated about twenty patients wounded in clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen at the Bitale hospital centre, Kalehe territory, South Kivu.
r1-HC-2026-008.l: Bitale, Kalehe territory (Bunyakiri health zone), South Kivu
r1-HC-2026-008.a: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo (clash parties), per Actualite.cd
r1-HC-2026-008.x: MSF (via Actualite.cd): about twenty wounded patients
r1-HC-2026-008.n: Access to care context (wounded treated), not an attack on a facility. Also a territorial-control lead: Bitale reported taken by AFC/M23 on 15 June 2026 (Actualite.cd).
r1-HC-2026-008.vn: Replacement extends the exact excerpt with the contiguous sentence that carries the clash parties (byline Josué Mutanava, Goma). The original MSF statement was not opened. Source 1 (Bitale taken by AFC/M23 on 15 June 2026) is context; the article places the wounded in the Bunyakiri health zone.
src: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) annonce avoir pris en charge une vingtaine de patients blessés au centre hospitalier de Bitale, situé dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu.

l’agglomération de Bitale est passée sous le contrôle des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans la matinée du lundi 15 juin 2026, après deux jours d’intenses affrontements contre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et les miliciens Wazalendo.

r1-HC-2026-009.s: Insecurity Insight reported, citing Actualite, that on 23-24 July 2026 in Masisi rural commune, Masisi territory, North Kivu, pharmacies were forced to close due to clashes between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo fighters, and reopened on 25 July 2026 after security conditions improved.
r1-HC-2026-009.l: Masisi rural commune, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-2026-009.a: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo (clash parties), per Insecurity Insight
r1-HC-2026-009.x: Insecurity Insight: an unspecified number of pharmacies
r1-HC-2026-009.n: Secondary compilation; the underlying Actualite article was not opened.
r1-HC-2026-009.vn: Exact on the retained ReliefWeb page. Secondary compilation of a media report; the underlying Actualite article was not opened.
src: 23-24 July 2026: In Masisi rural commune, Masisi territory, North Kivu province, pharmacies were forced to close due to clashes between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo fighters. They reopened on 25 July 2026 after security conditions improved. Source: Actualite

r1-HC-2026-010.s: Insecurity Insight reported, citing Actualite, that on 02 August 2026 in Buleusa, Ikobo groupment, Walikale territory, North Kivu, an unspecified number of pharmacies were looted of medicines by Wazalendo fighters during a raid at around 2300hrs.
r1-HC-2026-010.l: Buleusa, Ikobo groupment, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-2026-010.x: Insecurity Insight: unspecified number of pharmacies
r1-HC-2026-010.n: Secondary compilation; the underlying Actualite article was not opened. Also categorisable as health_care_access / supplies_looted.
r1-HC-2026-010.vn: Exact; the originating Actualite credit follows the entry on the page. Secondary compilation; the underlying Actualite article was not opened.
src: 02 August 2026: In Buleusa rural locality, Ikobo groupment, Walikale territory, North Kivu province, an unspecified number of pharmacies were looted of medicines by Wazalendo fighters during a raid on the area around 2300hrs. Actualite

r1-HC-2026-011.s: Insecurity Insight reported that on 27 July 2026 in Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu, Zawadi Mapendo Health Post was set on fire by unidentified men following rumours that a health worker was deliberately infecting patients or falsely diagnosing them with Ebola.
r1-HC-2026-011.l: Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu
r1-HC-2026-011.x: Insecurity Insight (since the outbreak on 21 May to 04 August 2026): 35 attacks on Ebola response measures in the DRC; 11 treatment centres attacked and damaged
r1-HC-2026-011.n: Ebola-outbreak context; not conflict-party violence. Recorded because it is an attack on a health facility in North Kivu in the window.
r1-HC-2026-011.vn: Exact; figures in figures field printed on the same page (Insecurity Insight data note). Ebola-related community violence, not attributed to a conflict party. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: 27 July 2026: In Bulengera commune, Butembo city, North Kivu province, Zawadi Mapendo Health Post was set on fire by unidentified men following rumours that a health worker was deliberately infecting patients or falsely diagnosing them with Ebola before transferring them to Katwa Ebola Treatment Centre.
Cette attaque survient seulement deux jours après l’incendie du poste de santé Zawadi, connu localement sous le nom de Mapendo, dans la cellule Kyaghala, commune de Bulengera.

Deux des huit incendies ne figurent dans aucun rapport de situation congolais, ni avant ni après : celui du poste de santé Zawadi Mapendo, le 27 juillet, et celui du centre hospitalier Crinovic, dans la nuit du 28 au 29 juillet, tous deux à Butembo.
Ce poste de santé mieux connu localement sous le nom de Mapendo a été incendié dans la nuit du dimanche à lundi 27 juillet dernier par des hommes également non identifiés

r1-HC-2026-012.s: Insecurity Insight reported that on 28-29 July 2026 in Kavikene locality, Butembo city, North Kivu, Crinovic Hospital Centre was set on fire and destroyed by unidentified perpetrators overnight after its director was accused by local residents of killing patients under the pretext of Ebola.
r1-HC-2026-012.l: Kavikene locality, Congo ya Sika district, Butembo city, North Kivu
r1-HC-2026-012.x: Insecurity Insight: one hospital centre destroyed

src: 28-29 July 2026: In Kavikene locality, Congo ya Sika district, Butembo city, North Kivu province, Crinovic Hospital Centre was set on fire and destroyed by unidentified perpetrators overnight after its director was accused by local residents of killing patients under the pretext of Ebola.
Le dernier incident a visé le Centre hospitalier Crinovic, situé à Kavikene, dans le quartier Congo ya Sika, commune de Vulamba.
Le dernier incident s’est produit dans la nuit du mardi 28 au mercredi 29 juillet au Centre hospitalier Crinovic, situé à Kavikene, dans le quartier Congo ya Sika, en commune de Vulamba.

Deux des huit incendies ne figurent dans aucun rapport de situation congolais, ni avant ni après : celui du poste de santé Zawadi Mapendo, le 27 juillet, et celui du centre hospitalier Crinovic, dans la nuit du 28 au 29 juillet, tous deux à Butembo.

r1-HC-2026-013.s: Physicians for Human Rights, citing a Mercy Corps analysis, reported that 68 security incidents targeting the Ebola response were recorded in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu between May 15 and June 30, 2026, including 51 attacks on personnel, health facilities, vehicles or equipment.
r1-HC-2026-013.l: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu (combined figure)
r1-HC-2026-013.x: PHR citing Mercy Corps: 68 incidents; 51 attacks; 14 threats or intimidation; 3 abductions or unlawful confinements; at least 11 Ebola health facilities or treatment centres damaged; 30 humanitarian workers and 11 government officials injured
r1-HC-2026-013.n: Figure is not broken down by province, so it cannot be attributed to North or South Kivu alone. Ebola context.
r1-HC-2026-013.vn: Exact; figure-field numbers printed on the page in the next sentence. Combined three-province figure; not broken down by province. The page prints 'three' abductions in words. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: According to a recent analysis by Mercy Corps, 68 security incidents targeting the Ebola response were recorded in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu between May 15 and June 30, 2026. These included 51 attacks on personnel, health facilities, vehicles, or equipment
recorded over 30 days, compared with 68 over the 47 days of the previous period.
These dynamics, combined with attacks against health personnel and limited access, have reduced operational reach in certain areas

r1-HC-2026-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that a 32-year-old woman was raped and then killed by armed men on a date it gives as 'mardi le 13 juillet' in Kamituga, South Kivu, and that, according to civil-society sources, her body was found in the morning in the Kalinga quarter. The Association des femmes journalistes engagées pour la paix (AFJEP) said the rape was committed by unidentified persons and called for an investigation. Actualite.cd described Kamituga as controlled by Wazalendo militiamen allied to the national army ('alliés à l’armée congolaise').
r1-HC-2026-014.l: Kalinga quarter, Kamituga, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-HC-2026-014.a: armed men; AFJEP wrote of "personnes non identifiées"; Actualite.cd noted Kamituga is controlled by Wazalendo and that rights violations attributed to the Wazalendo are denounced by the population
r1-HC-2026-014.n: Single outlet relaying civil-society sources. 13 July 2026 is a Monday (not Tuesday) in the calendar; the article says "mardi le 13 juillet", so the date is as printed but flagged as inconsistent. Victim not named.
r1-HC-2026-014.vn: Corrected attribution: the rape/killing sentence is Actualite.cd's own narration; only the finding of the body is credited to civil-society sources. Added AFJEP's 'personnes non identifiées' (on the page). The outlet also writes that rights violations attributed to the Wazalendo have been denounced by the population for several weeks. Date inconsistency: 13 July 2026 was a Monday, but the article says 'mardi le 13 juillet'. Perpetrators unidentified; the Wazalendo control of Kamituga is the outlet's context, not an attribution of this act.
src: Une femme âgée de 32 ans a été violée et puis tuée par des hommes armés mardi le 13 juillet à Kamituga, dans la province du Sud-Kivu. Selon les sources de la société civile, le corps de la victime a été retrouvé dans la matinée précisément au quartier Kalinga.
Kamituga, ville aurifère du territoire de Mwenga est contrôlée par les miliciens wazalendo, alliés à l’armée congolaise.

r1-HC-2026-015.s: Human Rights Watch reported that in North Kivu M23 armed group fighters raped a 42-year-old woman who reached a hospital within 72 hours, but the hospital had no kits; HRW wrote that the Rwanda-backed M23 controls the area.
r1-HC-2026-015.a: M23 armed group fighters, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
r1-HC-2026-015.n: Date of the incident is not stated by HRW (report dated 2026-01-12, covering 2025 events); date field is the report date. HRW says survivor names are pseudonyms and this case gives none. Health aspect: absence of PEP kits.
r1-HC-2026-015.vn: Exact. The page also says she later fled to Uganda and was diagnosed with HIV. Incident date unknown; kept as a lead with the window caveat. HRW does not give the date or place of this rape; interviews were conducted in November 2025, and other cases in the same release date from 2024, so this incident may predate the 1 January 2025 window. The date field is the report date only.
src: In neighboring North Kivu province, M23 armed group fighters raped a 42-year-old woman. She reached a hospital within 72 hours, but the hospital had no kits. The Rwanda-backed M23, which controls the area, continued to threaten her

r1-HC-NK-2025-001.s: MSF reported that on Sunday 19 January two MSF employees were slightly injured when a rocket hit the MSF garage next to the Masisi general referral hospital (HGR) in North Kivu, that another rocket hit a latrine close to the hospital, and that the hospital and the MSF staff living base were also hit by bullets.
r1-HC-NK-2025-001.l: Masisi Centre, Masisi hospital (HGR), North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-001.a: not attributed by the source for this incident (MSF described fighting for Masisi Centre between M23/AFC and the Congolese army)
r1-HC-NK-2025-001.x: MSF: two employees slightly injured; two rockets (garage; latrine)
r1-HC-NK-2025-001.n: Single NGO origin (the facility operator). MSF's page calls this the second incident in four days to directly affect Masisi hospital; the first (about 15-16 January) is not detailed in the passage cited here. MSF does not name who fired.
r1-HC-NK-2025-001.vn: Excerpts carry every clause; page checked. MSF does not say who fired; it calls this the second incident in four days to affect Masisi hospital amid fighting for Masisi Centre between M23/AFC and the Congolese army. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Ce dimanche 19 janvier, deux employés de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) ont été légèrement blessés lors d’un tir de roquette ayant touché le garage MSF adossé à l’Hôpital Général de Référence (HGR) de Masisi, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.
Le même jour, une autre roquette a touché une latrine située à proximité immédiate de l’hôpital. L’hôpital et la base de vie du personnel de MSF ont également subi des impacts de balles.
On January 19, two Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders or MSF) workers were slightly injured when two rockets struck near the General Reference Hospital in Masisi.
slightly injured when a rocket hit the MSF garage next to the Masisi General Referral hospital [and] ... on the same day, another rocket hit a latrine near the hospital.

r1-HC-NK-2025-002.s: MSF reported that on a Thursday an MSF employee was very gravely wounded by gunfire that again hit the MSF base at Masisi Centre, and that a child sheltering with his family in the base was also wounded. MSF said fighting between VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters had occurred in and around Masisi Centre almost daily since early January.
r1-HC-NK-2025-002.l: MSF base, Masisi Centre, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-002.a: VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters were fighting in the area (MSF); shooter not identified
r1-HC-NK-2025-002.x: MSF: one employee very gravely wounded; one child wounded
r1-HC-NK-2025-002.n: Date: the page says 'ce jeudi'; the date 2025-02-20 is taken from MSF's later release (see next claim) which states 'Le 20 février', and from the page's publication date. The employee later died (next claim).
r1-HC-NK-2025-002.vn: Release dated 20 February 2025 on the page ('ce jeudi'), so the date holds. Shooter not identified by MSF. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Un employé de l’organisation médicale internationale Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a été très grièvement blessé ce jeudi lors de tirs ayant à nouveau touché la base de MSF à Masisi Centre, au Nord-Kivu. Un enfant qui avait trouvé refuge avec sa famille dans la base de MSF a également été blessé par ces tirs.
Depuis début janvier, la cité de Masisi Centre et ses environs sont le théâtre d’affrontements quasi quotidiens entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo (alliés à l’armée congolaise) et le M23/AFC.
Depuis début janvier, la cité de Masisi-Centre et ses environs sont le théâtre d’affrontements quasi quotidiens entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo (alliés à l’armée congolaise) et le M23/AFC.

est décédé ce samedi des suites d’une blessure par balle reçue lors des affrontements du 20 février entre les combattants VDP/Wazalendo et ceux du M23/AFC à Masisi Centre, dans la province du Nord-Kivu

r1-HC-NK-2025-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that MSF announced on Saturday 22 February the death of one of its employees, who had been shot the previous Thursday during violent clashes between M23/AFC rebels and VDP/Wazalendo near the Masisi general referral hospital; a statement by MSF quoted by Radio Okapi named him as Jerry Muhindo Kavali, and Radio Okapi said he died aged 49 after more than ten years with MSF. In a later release MSF said a radio operator at its Masisi Centre base was mortally hit on 20 February by gunfire between VDP/Wazalendo and M23/AFC fighters close to the MSF building.
r1-HC-NK-2025-003.l: Masisi Centre, near Masisi general referral hospital, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-003.a: M23/AFC and VDP/Wazalendo (clashes near the hospital, per MSF and Radio Okapi); shooter not identified
r1-HC-NK-2025-003.n: Two MSF-origin accounts (Radio Okapi relaying the MSF announcement; MSF's April release) agree on the 20 February shooting. MSF's April release does not name the employee; Radio Okapi names him in a quote from MSF. The injury date ('jeudi dernier') in Radio Okapi is a weekday; date 2025-02-20 is supported by MSF's April release.
r1-HC-NK-2025-003.vn: The age and length of service are Radio Okapi's narration, not MSF's words; attribution split. Both sources go back to MSF, so this is one origin plus the operator's own release.
src: Médecins sans frontières (MSF) a annoncé samedi 22 février le décès de l’un de ses employés qui avait été blessé par balle jeudi dernier, lors de violents affrontements entre les rebelles du M23/AFC et les VDP/Wazalendo, près de l’hôpital général de référence de Masisi (Nord-Kivu).

La disparition tragique de Jerry Muhindo Kavali s’inscrit en effet dans un contexte de violences de plus en plus marquées affectant les installations sanitaires et humanitaires dans l’est de la RDC ». Décédé à 49 ans, Jerry a travaillé avec Médecins sans frontières durant plus de dix ans.

Le 20 février, un radio-opérateur de MSF, alors en poste dans la base de l’ONG à Masisi centre, a été mortellement touché par des tirs entre combattants VDP/Wazalendo et du M23/AFC à proximité du bâtiment de MSF.

r1-HC-NK-2025-004.s: MSF reported that on the evening of 18 April an MSF employee, a nurse at the Masisi general referral hospital, was shot dead at his home in Masisi centre by an armed man in uniform, the second MSF employee shot dead in Masisi centre in two months. MSF said two men in military uniform armed with assault rifles assaulted and extorted civilians in Masisi town before bursting into the MSF employee's home, and reminded all weapon carriers, whom it named, that protecting civilians in conflict is an obligation.
r1-HC-NK-2025-004.a: an armed man in uniform / two men in military uniform armed with assault rifles (MSF); no unit identified
r1-HC-NK-2025-004.x: MSF: second MSF employee shot dead in Masisi centre in two months
r1-HC-NK-2025-004.n: Single NGO origin (employer). The employee is not named in the MSF release. The release itself says 'le troisième dans la région du Nord-Kivu depuis le début de l'année', adding an MSF employee shot dead at home in Goma 'quelques jours' after 20 February (not otherwise detailed). Actualite.cd (2025-04-24) relayed the release.
r1-HC-NK-2025-004.vn: 'rappelle' is 'reminded', not 'called on'; 'robbed' narrowed to the source's 'agressé et racketté'. The uniformed men are not tied to any unit or party by MSF. MSF named the weapon carriers it addressed as M23/AFC, VDP/Wazalendos and FARDC; it does not attribute the killing to any of them. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Dans la soirée du 18 avril, un employé de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a été tué par balle à son domicile de Masisi centre (Nord-Kivu) par un homme armé en uniforme. Infirmier à l’hôpital général de référence de la ville, il est le second employé MSF à être tué par balle à Masisi centre en deux mois

Le 18 avril, deux hommes en uniforme militaire armés de fusils d’assauts ont agressé et racketté des civils dans la ville de Masisi avant de faire irruption au domicile d’un employé de MSF afin d’y extorquer les biens des résidents.

On the evening of April 18, a Doctors Without Borders/Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) health worker was shot dead in his home in Masisi town, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) by a gunman in a military uniform.

r1-HC-NK-2025-005.s: MSF said that since January about fifteen incidents had directly affected teams, ambulances, offices and structures run or supported by MSF.
r1-HC-NK-2025-005.a: not attributed by the source (MSF addressed all weapon carriers: M23/AFC, VDP/Wazalendo, FARDC)
r1-HC-NK-2025-005.x: MSF: about fifteen incidents since January
r1-HC-NK-2025-005.n: Aggregate NGO figure, not broken down by place or perpetrator.
r1-HC-NK-2025-005.vn: Publication date removed from the statement (shown with the source). Aggregate, not broken down by place or perpetrator; the release concerns North Kivu. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Depuis janvier, une quinzaine d’incidents ont directement touché les équipes, ambulances, bureaux et structures gérées ou soutenues par MSF.
Since early 2025, MSF teams have witnessed violent incidents on an almost daily basis – and on several occasions have been injured or lost their lives.

r1-HC-NK-2025-006.s: MSF reported that fighting between the FARDC and the M23/AFC and their respective allies reached Walikale town on 19 March, trapping MSF staff at its base and at the hospital, and that violence severely affected access to health care as 80% of the population fled the town and more than 700 displaced people took refuge in Walikale general hospital. MSF's North Kivu programme manager said MSF teams must suspend medical activities when fighting breaks out and cannot move safely.
r1-HC-NK-2025-006.l: Walikale town and Walikale general hospital, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-006.a: FARDC and M23/AFC and their respective allies (MSF)
r1-HC-NK-2025-006.x: MSF: 80% of the population fled the town; more than 700 displaced people sheltering in the hospital
r1-HC-NK-2025-006.n: Single NGO origin (the operator of the hospital's support). Page is dated '2 Avril 2025' in its text; 'ce 19 mars' as printed. The M23 withdrew from Walikale town in early April (see next claims); this MSF page describes the situation before that.
r1-HC-NK-2025-006.vn: All clauses in excerpts; page dated 2 April 2025. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L'escalade de la violence entre les FARDC et le M23/AFC, et leurs alliés respectifs, dans le Nord-Kivu, en République démocratique du Congo, a atteint la ville de Walikale le 19 mars, piégeant le personnel de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) à notre base et à l'hôpital.

La violence a gravement affecté l'accès aux soins de santé, car 80 % de la population a fui la ville en entendant les tirs d'artillerie et en craignant les hostilités. Plus de 700 personnes déplacées se sont réfugiées à l'hôpital général de Walikale, ce qui accroît la pression sur des ressources médicales déjà limitées.

Nos équipes doivent suspendre leurs activités médicales lorsque des combats éclatent et ne peuvent pas se déplacer en toute sécurité. La sécurité de notre personnel et de nos patients est notre priorité absolue », déclare Natalia Torrent, responsable des programmes de MSF au Nord-Kivu.

passé sous occupation rebelle la veille, ont provoqué des déplacements massifs de populations. Certains civils ont pris la direction de Hombo dans la province du Sud-Kivu, d’autres sont allés sur l’axe Mubi-Lubutu-Kisangani, tandis que d'autres encore se sont réfugiés près de l'hôpital de Walikale alors que quelques-uns sont restés dans leurs maisons, rapportent des sources locales. Cet hôpital général et une base logistique d'une ONG ont été endommagés lors des combats, entraînant des morts et des blessés, selon des témoins.

r1-HC-NK-2025-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that Walikale civil society denounced the systematic looting of several hospitals and health centres by alleged M23 elements between 3 and 4 April 2025, particularly in the Kibua health zone, where the general referral hospital and the Mungazi health centre were stripped of biomedical, administrative and medical equipment, and that Fiston Misona, president of the territorial civil-society coordination, said the rebels dismantled solar panels, took essential medicines and destroyed administrative documents.
r1-HC-NK-2025-007.l: Kibua health zone (Kibua general referral hospital; Mungazi and Kishanga health centres), Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-007.a: 'éléments présumés de la rébellion M23' per Walikale civil society (Radio Okapi); M23 withdrawing from Walikale-centre
r1-HC-NK-2025-007.x: Radio Okapi (civil society): Kibua general referral hospital and Mungazi health centre stripped; Kishanga health centre also looted
r1-HC-NK-2025-007.n: Civil-society allegation relayed by Radio Okapi; beto.cd (7 April) also reported the Kibua hospital looted on Saturday 5 April by retreating M23 per residents, but that page could not be retrieved reliably by the checker and is not cited. Dates differ slightly (3-4 April vs 5 April). No M23 response found. Radio Okapi (2025-10-02) separately says four Walikale-area referral hospitals suffered massive looting 'en janvier'; see later claim.
r1-HC-NK-2025-007.vn: Civil-society allegation relayed by one outlet; attribution kept ('alleged M23 elements'). DATE CONFLICT: Radio Okapi (7 April 2025) dates this looting to 3-4 April 2025, as the M23 withdrew from Walikale-centre; a later Radio Okapi article (2 October 2025) says the four Walikale-area referral hospitals, including Kibua, were massively looted 'en janvier dernier'. Both are kept as separate claims; the conflict is unresolved.
src: La société civile de Walikale au Nord-Kivu, dénonce le pillage systématique de plusieurs hôpitaux et centres de santé par des éléments présumés de la rébellion M23 entre le 3 et le 4 avril 2025.

Ces actes ont particulièrement touché la zone de santé de Kibua, où l’hôpital général de référence et le centre de santé de Mungazi ont été dépouillés de leurs équipements biomédicaux, administratifs et médicaux.

Selon Fiston Misona, président de la coordination territoriale de la société civile, les rebelles ont démantelé les panneaux solaires, emporté les médicaments essentiels et détruit des documents administratifs. Le centre de santé de Kishanga, situé à une dizaine de kilomètres, a subi le même sort, avec le vol d’équipements énergétiques et de stocks pharmaceutiques.

r1-HC-NK-2025-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that 9 of 18 health structures in the Walikale health zone had already been ransacked between 17 and 23 March, during the initial M23 advance.
r1-HC-NK-2025-008.l: Walikale health zone, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-008.a: the M23 ('lors de l'avancée initiale du M23', per civil society as relayed by Radio Okapi)
r1-HC-NK-2025-008.x: Walikale civil society via Radio Okapi: 9 of 18 health structures in the Walikale health zone ransacked, 17-23 March
r1-HC-NK-2025-008.n: Figure is the civil-society count as stated by Radio Okapi without a named source for the 9/18; not independently verified. The facilities are not named. Counter-reporting: Actualite.cd (2025-04-21): Dates the looting to the AFC/M23 withdrawal in early April and counts four structures, not 9 of 18 on 17-23 March.
r1-HC-NK-2025-008.vn: The 9/18 sentence is Radio Okapi's own narration, not attributed to civil society; 'per Walikale civil society' removed. 'During' the M23 advance is not 'by' the M23. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Ces pillages interviennent dans un contexte où 9 structures sanitaires sur 18 dans la zone de santé de Walikale avaient déjà été saccagées entre le 17 et le 23 mars lors de l’avancée initiale du M23.

Lors du retrait de leur retrait de la commune rurale de Walikale au début du mois d'avril, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont pillé systématiquement les structures sanitaires dans la région. Dans la zone de santé rurale de Walikale, quatre structures sanitaires ont été dépouillées de tout et peinent à se relancer.

r1-HC-NK-2025-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that the four referral hospitals of the Walikale, Itebero, Pinga and Kibua health zones in North Kivu had suffered 'un pillage massif en janvier dernier' during fighting between the FARDC and the M23 rebels, paralysing many services and causing the loss of essential medical equipment.
r1-HC-NK-2025-009.l: Referral hospitals of Walikale, Itebero, Pinga and Kibua health zones, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-009.a: fighting between the FARDC and the M23 rebels (Radio Okapi); looters not identified
r1-HC-NK-2025-009.n: DISCREPANCY: Radio Okapi says 'janvier' but other sources (MSF, Radio Okapi 7 April, beto.cd) put M23 fighting at Walikale from 19 March and looting of Kibua hospital on 3-5 April 2025. M23 held no Walikale positions in January 2025 per the other claims in this unit; treat 'janvier' as likely an error or a reference to a different looting, unverified. Kept as a separate claim, not merged. Contradicting reporting: Actualite.cd (2025-09-26): Headline places the Kibua hospital pillage about six months before 26 Sept 2025 (about March), not January.
r1-HC-NK-2025-009.vn: Publication date removed from the statement; stray punctuation fixed; the four zones are on the page (replacement quote). Looters not identified by the source. DATE CONFLICT: this article (2 October 2025) says 'janvier dernier' (January 2025), but Radio Okapi on 7 April 2025 dated the looting of the Kibua hospital to 3-4 April 2025, and MSF dated the arrival of fighting in Walikale town to 19 March 2025. The January date is unverified and may be an error or a different looting; kept as a separate claim. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Ces hôpitaux avaient été victimes d’un pillage massif en janvier dernier lors des combats entre les Forces armées de la RDC et les rebelles du M23, causant la paralysie de nombreux services et la perte du matériel médical essentiel.
l'hôpital général de Kibua appuyé en médicaments six mois après son pillage par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23

r1-HC-NK-2025-010.s: MSF reported that patients from Binza treated at Rutshuru hospital described massacres and summary executions of civilians in the fields east of Virunga National Park, and that 124 intentionally wounded people were treated at Rutshuru general referral hospital in July and August, mostly from the Binza and Bambo health zones. MSF said all survivors name armed men as the perpetrators, some citing the M23 armed group, and that it could not verify the exact number of victims.
r1-HC-NK-2025-010.l: Binza and Bambo health zones; Kiseguru village; Rutshuru general referral hospital, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-010.a: 'hommes armés', some patients citing the M23 armed group (MSF)
r1-HC-NK-2025-010.x: MSF: 124 intentionally wounded treated at Rutshuru hospital, July-August 2025; on average 59 victims of violence per month January-August 2025 (+15% on the same period of the previous year)
r1-HC-NK-2025-010.n: Perpetrators are not identified by MSF beyond 'armed men' (some patients cite M23); MSF also says abuses by CMC, Wazalendo or FDLR are reported. Individual patients are pseudonymised (asterisk) in the page and are not listed. Massacre-level detail (counts of dead) is in other units' sources; this claim records the health-care angle (patients and caseload).
r1-HC-NK-2025-010.vn: Narrowed to the page's wording on the patients' accounts ('patients from Binza', not 'around Binza'); the massacre-description clause rests on a page passage (replacement quote).
src: Tous les survivants désignent des hommes armés comme auteurs des massacres, certains citant le groupe armé M23.

Bien que MSF ne soit pas en mesure de vérifier le nombre exact de victimes, 124 personnes blessées intentionnellement ont été soignées à l'hôpital général de référence de Rutshuru en juillet et août, provenant pour la plupart des zones de santé de Binza et Bambo.

Entre janvier et aout 2025, dans l'hôpital général de Rutshuru, où MSF fournit des soins médicaux et chirurgicaux, a été traité en moyenne 59 victimes de violence par mois. Cela représente une augmentation de 15 % par rapport à la même période l'année précédente

r1-HC-NK-2025-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to civil society, fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms (Rutshuru and Masisi territories) between 28 September and 8 October 2025 caused at least 4 deaths, 13 disappearances and the rape of 8 women; Radio Okapi also reported that the Muliki health centre was looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle. The source does not say who carried out the rapes or the looting.
r1-HC-NK-2025-011.l: Muliki health centre, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) and Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi territory), North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-011.a: AFC-M23 and FARDC fighting (Radio Okapi); looters of the health centre not identified
r1-HC-NK-2025-011.x: Civil society via Radio Okapi: at least 4 killed, 13 missing, 8 women raped, several dozen houses burned
r1-HC-NK-2025-011.n: Single local outlet citing civil society; perpetrators of the rapes and of the looting are not attributed in the passage. The rapes are recorded here only as part of the civil-society tally; no survivor is named. Muliki is placed in Bwito chiefdom by inference from the article's list of affected groupings only in the sense that it is in the affected area; the page does not state the territory of Muliki explicitly.
r1-HC-NK-2025-011.vn: All clauses in excerpts; perpetrators left unattributed as in the source. The source does not attribute the rapes or the looting of the Muliki health centre to either party, and does not say in which chiefdom Muliki lies. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The draft put the Muliki looting under 'according to civil society', but the page narrates the damage itself (see the verifier note on sibling claim r1-SV-NK-2025-004); separated, and the absence of attribution for rapes and looting made explicit. No search.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; checked the retained page, which names no perpetrator for the rapes or the looting
src: Selon la société civile, ce conflit a provoqué la mort d’au moins 4 personnes et la disparition de 13 autres, ainsi que le viol de 8 femmes.
Le centre de santé de Muliki a également été pillé, avec en prime le vol d’une vingtaine de bovins.

Des combats violents ont opposé les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) dans les chefferies de Bwito et Bahunde, situées respectivement dans les territoires de Rutshuru et Masisi au Nord-Kivu entre le 28 septembre et le 8 octobre 2025.

r1-HC-NK-2025-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that the toll of the ADF attack in Byambwe/Biambwe, Lubero territory, on the night of Friday 14 November was revised from 20 to 28 killed, including 17 patients executed at the reference health centre, per Lubero territory administrator colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, who called the figures provisional. A caregiver quoted by Actualite.cd said the maternity ward and operating theatre were burned and medicines looted, and that 17 people including four breastfeeding women were executed in their hospital beds.
r1-HC-NK-2025-012.l: Biambwe/Byambwe health centre, Lubero territory (Biena health zone), North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-012.a: ADF (Allied Democratic Forces, called islamistes ADF by Actualite.cd)
r1-HC-NK-2025-012.x: Actualite.cd (territory administrator, provisional): 28 killed, including 17 patients at the health centre (revised from 20); health worker: 17 executed in hospital beds incl. four breastfeeding women
r1-HC-NK-2025-012.n: Headline of the page says 'une dizaine de patients' while the body says 17 patients; the body text is cited. Initial reports gave 18 (AFP via TV5Monde/La Libre) and later ~29-30 (AA, Congo Rassure); figures vary by source and are provisional. Place is spelled Byambwe in the body text and Biambwe in the headline/URL. See also UN News (next claim) and Vatican News.
r1-HC-NK-2025-012.vn: Single outlet (one credible origin with an official and a health worker); graded B on its own sources rather than A. Figures provisional and vary across sources (Vatican News: 15 in the clinic and 5 nearby; UN News/MONUSCO: 17 shot in the health centre). The page headline says 'une dizaine de patients'.
src: Le bilan de la récente attaque meurtrière des islamistes ADF à Byambwe, dans le territoire de Lubero, dans la nuit du vendredi 14 novembre, a été revu à la hausse, passant de 20 à 28 personnes tuées, dont 17 patients exécutés au centre de santé de référence de la localité.

Selon le colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, administrateur du territoire de Lubero, joint par ACTUALITÉ.CD, ce nouveau bilan découle des fouilles menées à Biambwe et dans ses environs au lendemain de l’attaque. Il précise toutefois que ces chiffres demeurent provisoires.

La zone de santé de Biena confirme l’attaque. Un membre du personnel soignant évoque l’incendie du pavillon de maternité et du bloc opératoire, ainsi que le pillage des médicaments. Il affirme que 17 personnes, dont quatre femmes allaitantes, ont été exécutées sur leur lit d’hôpital.

r1-HC-NK-2025-013.s: UN News reported that, according to information gathered by MONUSCO, at Byambwe 17 people were shot dead in a health centre, including women patients who had come to give birth, and that in other localities (Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa) homes were burned, civilians abducted and medical supplies looted, in a wave of ADF attacks that killed at least 89 civilians in Lubero territory between 13 and 19 November.
r1-HC-NK-2025-013.l: Byambwe health centre; Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa; Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-013.x: UN News (citing MONUSCO): at least 89 civilians killed between 13 and 19 November in Lubero territory, including 20 women; 17 shot dead in the health centre at Byambwe
r1-HC-NK-2025-013.n: UN News relays MONUSCO information; the 89 figure is stated in the page's lead-in text (the same sentence appears as the article's standfirst). Independent of Actualite.cd's local sources, though both may derive from local health staff.
r1-HC-NK-2025-013.vn: Supported. Graded B: UN News relaying MONUSCO information, not a published investigation.
src: Selon les informations recueillies par la Mission des Nations unies en République démocratique du Congo ( MONUSCO ), à Byambwe, 17 personnes ont été abattues dans un centre de santé, dont des patientes venues accoucher ; ailleurs, dans les localités de Mabiango, Tunarudi ou Sambalysa, des habitations ont été incendiées, des civils enlevés, des fournitures médicales pillées.
Entre le 13 et le 19 novembre, les ADF ont tué au moins 89 civils, dont 20 femmes et un nombre encore inconnu d’enfants dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu.

r1-HC-NK-2025-014.s: UN News reported that UN Secretary-General António Guterres, in a press release, 'fermement condamné' (strongly condemned) the attacks attributed to the ADF in North Kivu and expressed his condolences to bereaved families, and that the UN Security Council, in a statement, reaffirmed its 'détermination' to support the peace process and demanded humanitarian access that is 'total, sûr et sans entrave'.
r1-HC-NK-2025-014.l: North Kivu (statement issued at UN headquarters)
r1-HC-NK-2025-014.n: The article (24 November, Monday) says the statements came 'samedi'; that implies Saturday 22 November, computed from the weekday and the publication date. Context statement by a mediator-side body; recorded because the Lubero toll includes the health-centre killings.
r1-HC-NK-2025-014.vn: Grammar fixed; the Security Council clause rested only on the page, now given as a replacement quote. The page says both statements came 'samedi'; 22 November 2025 is computed from the weekday and the 24 November publication date.
src: Dans un communiqué de presse, António Guterres a « fermement condamné » ces attaques attribuées aux Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF), une milice originaire de l'Ouganda voisin, et exprimé ses « plus sincères condoléances aux familles et communautés endeuillées ».

r1-HC-NK-2025-015.s: Vatican News reported that at around 10:00 PM on Friday ADF militants entered the town of Byambwe and attacked a diocesan health centre run by the Sisters of the Presentation, massacred patients and set the facility ablaze, killing several women in the maternity ward. Italian missionary Fr Giovanni Piumatti, who confirmed the attack to Vatican News, was quoted as saying fifteen people were killed in the clinic and another five in the surrounding area, that the attackers set fire to the facility and twenty-seven nearby homes, and that they looted all the medical supplies.
r1-HC-NK-2025-015.l: Byambwe diocesan health centre (Diocese of Butembo-Beni), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-015.x: Vatican News (Fr Piumatti): fifteen killed in the clinic and five in the surrounding area; twenty-seven nearby homes burned
r1-HC-NK-2025-015.n: Second-hand account: the missionary is in Italy and relays information; figures differ from Actualite.cd (28, incl. 17 patients) and UN News (17 shot in the health centre). Kept as a separate claim because the figures conflict. 'Friday' = 14 November computed from the 16 November publication date and the other sources.
r1-HC-NK-2025-015.vn: The narrative of the attack is Vatican News's own; only the toll, the burning of homes and the looting are Piumatti's words. Attribution split. Graded C: a relayed, second-hand account. Second-hand account from a missionary now in Italy; figures differ from Actualite.cd (28 killed incl. 17 patients) and UN News/MONUSCO (17 shot in the health centre).
src: At around 10:00 PM local time on Friday, militants from the ADF (Allied Democratic Forces)—aligned with the so-called Islamic State since 2009—entered the town of Byambwe, in the Diocese of Butembo-Beni. They attacked a diocesan health center run by the Sisters of the Presentation, massacred patients, and then set the entire facility ablaze, killing several women in the maternity ward.
“Fifteen people were killed in the clinic and another five in the surrounding area. They set fire to the entire facility and twenty-seven nearby homes.

r1-HC-NK-2025-016.s: UN News reported, citing OCHA's health cluster, a worsening cholera outbreak in and around Goma, with at least 420 cases and 1 death over two consecutive weeks (3 to 15 February), more than a third of the 1,280 cholera cases recorded in North Kivu since the start of the year, and suspected cholera cases in the MONUSCO camp in Goma where disarmed FARDC members had taken refuge, with one death and 24 suspected cases under treatment.
r1-HC-NK-2025-016.l: Goma and surroundings; MONUSCO camp in Goma, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-016.a: not applicable (epidemic context following M23/AFC capture of Goma)
r1-HC-NK-2025-016.x: OCHA via UN News: 420 cases and 1 death 3-15 February around Goma; 1,280 cholera cases in North Kivu since the start of 2025; MONUSCO camp: 1 death, 24 suspected cases
r1-HC-NK-2025-016.n: Figures are OCHA/health-cluster reporting relayed by UN News; Actualite.cd (2025-02-24) gives a different, more cautious count for the MONUSCO camp ('une vingtaine de cas dont un décès'); not merged. The article does not attribute the outbreak to a cause.
r1-HC-NK-2025-016.vn: '1,280' is the page's '1.280'. Graded B: UN News relaying cluster data, one origin. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon le Bureau de la coordination des affaires humanitaires de l’ONU ( OCHA ), le groupe sectoriel Santé alerte sur une aggravation de l’épidémie de choléra dans et autour de Goma.

Au moins 420 cas et 1 décès ont été signalés sur deux semaines consécutives (du 3 au 15 février), soit plus d’un tiers des 1.280 cas de choléra enregistrés dans toute la province du Nord-Kivu depuis le début de l’année.

des cas suspects de choléra ont été signalés au sein du camp de la Mission de paix des Nations Unies ( MONUSCO ) à Goma, où de nombreux membres des Forces armées de RDC (FARDC) désarmés se sont réfugiés.
À ce jour, un décès dû au choléra a été enregistré, tandis que 24 cas suspects sont en cours de traitement.

r1-HC-NK-2025-017.s: UN News reported that the health cluster said three mpox treatment centres had been destroyed at Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa as a result of bombings.
r1-HC-NK-2025-017.l: Kalehe, Minova and Miti Murhesa (Kalehe territory), South Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-017.x: UN News (health cluster): three mpox treatment centres destroyed
r1-HC-NK-2025-017.n: Outside North Kivu (South Kivu, Kalehe territory); recorded here as an epidemic-response effect found while researching the North Kivu cholera claim.
r1-HC-NK-2025-017.vn: The 2-8 February range came from an unrelated mpox caseload sentence; the source dates only the report. Marked as a related event outside the unit's province. The source gives no date for the destruction or the bombings, and no perpetrator; the date is the report date. r1-HC-NK-2025-018.s: UN News quoted Dr Boureima Hama Sambo, WHO Representative in DRC, as saying that WHO aid teams 'cannot move freely to support the hospitals, even ambulances cannot run', calling it a public-health nightmare, and he warned that mpox patients had fled at least one camp's treatment centre and were living in host communities.
r1-HC-NK-2025-018.a: not applicable (M23 advance on Goma; M23 fighters in control of a significant portion of the city per UN agencies)
r1-HC-NK-2025-018.n: Statement of a WHO official, 29 January (Wednesday per the article); the quote is not a finding of who blocked access. The page spells 'Representive' and 'living now in'.
r1-HC-NK-2025-018.vn: Quoted statement; not a finding on who blocked access. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Aid teams from the UN World Health Organization ( WHO ) “cannot move freely to support the hospitals, even ambulances cannot run. It’s a situation that in public health is a nightmare,” said Dr Boureima Hama Sambo, WHO Representive in DRC.
Dr Sambo warned that mpox patients had fled at least one camp’s treatment centre and were now living now in host communities and with families.
Ninety percent of the mpox patients (128 of 143) in isolation units in Goma had fled for safety

r1-HC-NK-2025-019.s: Insecurity Insight reported, in an attacks-on-health-care news brief, that since late January reports had increased in North Kivu as M23 rebels expanded control, attacking ambulances and looting vital medical supplies, and that in one incident a baby in an incubator at Virunga General Hospital in Goma was injured by an M23-fired bullet that pierced the ceiling of the neonatal unit during clashes between M23 and the Congolese army.
r1-HC-NK-2025-019.l: North Kivu; Virunga General Hospital, Goma
r1-HC-NK-2025-019.x: Insecurity Insight (all countries, 1 January-17 March 2025): 247 incidents in 20 countries and territories; 29 health workers killed, 59 injured, 10 kidnapped, 19 arrested; not specific to North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-019.n: Monitor summary built from open-source reports; the page gives no dates, places or sources for the ambulance and looting incidents (the event-level data sits in the HDX dataset, which no longer carries descriptions). The global figures are not North Kivu figures. ReliefWeb page, original published 1 Apr 2025.
r1-HC-NK-2025-019.vn: Brief's date range removed from the statement (it is in the source title). Insecurity Insight is a compiler; its attribution of the bullet to M23 is its own and stays attributed. Monitor summary of open-source reports; the brief gives no date, place or source for the ambulance and looting incidents. Its global figures (247 incidents in 20 countries, 1 January-17 March 2025) are not North Kivu figures. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-002: The 'M23 fired bullet' attribution rests only on a compiler's brief (Insecurity Insight) that gives no source. A search for the incident found contemporaneous reports (UNICEF DRC Facebook post about an 18-day-old baby, Faraja; social posts from about 27 January 2025) that describe a bullet piercing the ceiling onto an incubator in a Goma hospital, some calling it a stray bullet ('balle perdue'), without naming who fired it. Keep the attribution strictly as Insecurity Insight's; the ambulance and looting clause is also undated and unsourced.
src: Since late January, reports increased in North Kivu, DRC, as M23 rebels expanded control, attacking ambulances and looting vital medical supplies. During one incident, a baby in an incubator at Virunga General Hospital in Goma city was injured by an M23 fired bullet that pierced the ceiling of the neonatal unit during clashes between M23 and the Congolese army.

Insecurity Insight identified 247 incidents of violence against or obstruction of health care in 20 countries and territories between 01 January and 17 March. In these incidents, 29 health workers were killed, 59 injured, 10 kidnapped and 19 arrested.

r1-HC-NK-2025-020.s: The EastAfrican reported that the AFC (Congo River Alliance) 'strongly denies' the UN human rights office's allegations of attacks on hospitals, saying it never targeted civilian establishments, that the UN mission MONUSCO had manipulated the details, and that its raid was aimed at securing medical infrastructure it said had been infiltrated by fighters; the AFC claimed the heads of the hospitals corroborated in the operation.
r1-HC-NK-2025-020.l: Goma, North Kivu (CBCA Ndosho and Heal Africa hospitals)
r1-HC-NK-2025-020.x: UN human rights office (as quoted by The EastAfrican): 116 patients taken from CBCA Hospital and 15 from Heal Africa; the AFC statement gives no figure
r1-HC-NK-2025-020.n: Party statement reported by a Nation Media Group correspondent in Kigali; recorded as what the AFC said, not as fact. The headline says M23 'admit attacks on hospitals', but the text has the AFC denying the allegations while describing a 'raid' to secure the infrastructure; the article does not clarify the fate of the abducted patients. Existing claim r1-HC-2025-002 records the AFC spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka's version via Umuseke; this is an additional outlet. The OHCHR statement itself (3 March) could not be fetched by the retrieval helper (via=none), so only the EastAfrican's quote of it is used.
r1-HC-NK-2025-020.vn: All clauses on the page; the 'never targeted ... manipulated' clause added as a replacement quote. Graded B for the fact of the statement, from a credible outlet. Party statement (AFC/M23): what the AFC said, not a finding. The OHCHR said on 3 March that M23 fighters took 116 patients from CBCA Ndosho and 15 from Heal Africa in the night of 28 February (quoted by the same article).
ent: Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights
src: “The Congo River Alliance (AFC) strongly denies allegations by the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights regarding attacks allegedly perpetrated against hospitals,” they said, referring to their umbrella coalition name.
The M23 said their raid was aimed at securing the medical infrastructure, which had been infiltrated by fighters. They claimed that the heads of the hospitals corroborated in the operation.

“Fighters of the Rwandan-backed group raided CBCA Ndosho Hospital and Heal Africa Hospital in the night of 28 February, taking 116 patients from CBCA Hospital and 15 others from Heal Africa, on allegations of being DRC army soldiers or members of the pro-government Wazalendo militia,” the office said on March 3.

r1-HC-NK-2025-021.s: Radio Télévision Communautaire la Référence (RTCR) reported that in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 25 June 2025 presumed armed bandits visited several homes and the Centre hospitalier La Providence in the Kamesimbonzo quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo, and that, according to John Kameta, president of the Bulengera communal civil-society core, two of the bandits came into the hospital around midnight and took one hundred thousand Congolese francs belonging to patients, as well as telephones.
r1-HC-NK-2025-021.l: Centre hospitalier La Providence, Vukonderya cell, Bulengera commune, Butembo, North Kivu
r1-HC-NK-2025-021.a: 'présumés bandits armés' (RTCR); not linked to any armed group by the source
r1-HC-NK-2025-021.x: RTCR (civil society): one hundred thousand Congolese francs belonging to patients, plus telephones
r1-HC-NK-2025-021.n: Criminal incident in an M23-free area (Butembo), not linked to the armed conflict by the source; recorded for completeness on obstruction of health care. Radio Okapi, Radio Moto and Congo Quotidien also reported it on 26 June (seen in search results, not fetched/cited). Local community radio, one civil-society source.
r1-HC-NK-2025-021.vn: Kameta's title corrected to the page's wording ('président de la société civile noyau communal de Bulengera', not 'coordinator'); his name was on the page only, now in a replacement quote. Criminal incident; the source does not link it to any party to the conflict.
src: Dans la nuit de mardi au mercredi 25 juin 2025, les présumés bandits armés ont choisi le quartier Kamesimbonzo, commune de Bulengera en ville de Butembo au Nord-Kivu. Surplace, ils ont visité plusieurs maisons d'habitations ainsique que le centre hospitalier La providence.
Deux de ces bandits se sont pointés dans le centre hospitalier La providence autour de zéro heures. A part cent mille franc congolais appartenant aux malades, ces malfrats ont emporté des téléphones

r1-HC-SK-2025-001.a: armed men (not further identified by the source)

src: 10-11 August 2025: In Ludaha village, Cirunga group, Kabare territory, South Kivu province, the Ludaha Health Centre was looted overnight by armed men, taking medical equipment, including a microscope, a printer, telephones, money, and other valuables. r1-HC-SK-2025-014.s: Kivu Morning Post, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that the health system in the Minembwe area was on the verge of collapse with a prolonged shortage of medicines, and that at Minembwe General Reference Hospital between July and September 2025 more than 60% of deaths concerned children.
r1-HC-SK-2025-014.l: Minembwe General Reference Hospital, Minembwe, South Kivu
r1-HC-SK-2025-014.a: not applicable (access restriction; armed presence on roads per OCHA)
r1-HC-SK-2025-014.x: OCHA (via Kivu Morning Post): more than 60% of deaths at the hospital in July-September 2025 were children
r1-HC-SK-2025-014.n: Relay of the OCHA communiqué; the OCHA original was not fetched. The article also says that since January 2025 these areas saw armed clashes, attacks on civilians and looting of health structures by armed groups, and that since May the region has been almost wholly isolated.
r1-HC-SK-2025-014.vn: Page attributes to an OCHA communiqué; excerpt verbatim. The excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (Hôpital Général de Référence rendered in English); translation covers the excerpt only. Actualite.cd, relaying the same OCHA bulletin, gives the count as 25 of 40 deaths. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 source_type edited: variant spelling of the existing key partisan_afc_m23 (party account of AFC/M23 vice-governor Gaddy Mukiza, relayed by Radio Maendeleo) 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le système de santé est au bord de l’effondrement, avec une rupture prolongée de médicaments. À l’Hôpital Général de Référence de Minembwe, la situation est alarmante : entre juillet et septembre 2025, plus de 60 % des décès concernaient des enfants.

Plusieurs structures dans les villages des hauts plateaux de Fizi, particulièrement à Minembwe au sud de la province du Sud-Kivu et ses environs, font face à un manque criant de médicaments depuis l’avènement de la guerre. Cette situation met en danger des vies humaines dans cette partie de la province du Sud-Kivu. C’est ce qu’indique Gaddy MUKIZA, vice-gouverneur du Sud-Kivu en charge de l’économie et des finances sous l’AFC M23, au terme d’une descente d’itinérance effectuée mercredi dernier au bureau central de la zone de santé et à l’hôpital général de Minembwe. Gaddy MUKIZA indique que cette situation est causée par l’enclavement de cette zone de santé et de tous les villages voisins dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi, des entités où la voie routière et celle aérienne restent fermées. À cela s’ajoute le désengagement des partenaires humanitaires
Entre juillet et septembre 2025, plus de 25 enfants sont décédés à l’hôpital général de référence de Minembwe suite à la rupture des médicaments et intrants médicaux.

r1-HC-SK-2025-015.s: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) reported that heavy violence and clashes broke out in Uvira in February 2025 between the Congolese army (FARDC) and their presumed allies, the Wazalendo fighters, and quoted a mother who said they heard gunshots inside the hospital where her 10-month-old son was admitted at the mpox treatment centre of Uvira General Hospital.
r1-HC-SK-2025-015.l: Uvira General Hospital, Uvira, South Kivu
r1-HC-SK-2025-015.a: clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo (as described by MSF); who fired inside the hospital is not stated
r1-HC-SK-2025-015.n: The mother is quoted under a pseudonym ('Aisha*'; MSF states names were changed), so she is not listed as a named person. MSF does not say who fired. The MSF 9 December 2025 article ('gunfire was reported inside the hospital in Uvira') repeats the point without a date; related draft SV-2025#25.
r1-HC-SK-2025-015.vn: Both passages on the MSF page in the Uvira section; pseudonym confirmed by MSF's note that names were changed. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact. MSF also writes 'Les installations médicales n'ont pas été épargnées par les tirs' but does not say who fired. The mother is quoted under a pseudonym (MSF says names were changed), so no name is recorded. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: En février 2025, de fortes violences et des affrontements avaient éclaté dans Uvira, entre l'armée congolaise (FARDC) et leurs alliés présumés, les combattants Wazalendo

Nous avons entendu des coups de feu à l'intérieur de l'hôpital. Quand les tirs ont cessé, je suis partie avec mon fils, même s’il était encore malade ; je ne me sentais pas en sécurité », raconte Aisha*, son fils de 10 mois était hospitalisé au centre de traitement mpox à l’hôpital général d’Uvira.
Au moins 17 personnes ont été tuées ces mardi et mercredi dans la ville d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu) où des affrontements spontanés ont éclaté entre des militaires congolais et des miliciens wazalendo.

Des échanges de tirs à balles réelles secouent la ville d’Uvira, ce dimanche 16 février 2025, plus précisément au port de Kalundu, où des affrontements violents opposent les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) à leurs alliés de circonstance, les Wazalendo.

r1-HC-SK-2025-016.s: MSF reported that persistent insecurity on the road linking Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira made it practically impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the front line, and that humanitarian aid now had to transit through several countries to reach the populations on each side.
r1-HC-SK-2025-016.a: not attributed by the source (front line between M23/AFC-held Kamanyola and government-held Uvira)
r1-HC-SK-2025-016.n: Published 30 May 2025 (updated 2 June 2025); describes a situation at that date, not a single event.
r1-HC-SK-2025-016.vn: Both sentences on the MSF page under 'Accès humanitaire entravé entre Kamanyola et Uvira'. Describes the situation at the article's publication (May-June 2025), not a single event. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L’insécurité persistante sur la route reliant Bukavu, Kamanyola et Uvira, rend pratiquement impossible la circulation des organisations humanitaires entre les deux côtés de la ligne de front.
L’aide humanitaire doit désormais transiter par plusieurs pays, pour atteindre les populations de chaque côté de la ligne de front.

Les voyageurs, notamment ceux de Bukavu, passent désormais par quatre pays pour rejoindre Uvira : la RDC, le Rwanda, la Tanzanie et le Burundi. Ce détour prolongé est causé par la présence du groupe armé M23 dans certaines zones de la région, notamment dans la Plaine de la Rusizi à Katogota et Kamanyola, ce qui rend la route principale dangereuse.

Le trafic Bukavu-Uvira a timidement repris depuis dimanche 14 décembre 2025. Coupé depuis plus de 7 mois suite aux affrontements des rebelles du M23 et des militaires FARDC appuyés par des Wazalendo et l'armée burundaise dans la plaine de la Ruzizi.

r1-HC-SK-2025-017.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing a nurse it contacted, that in the Kamisimbi grouping (Walungu territory, South Kivu), where AFC/M23 troops and Wazalendo fought repeatedly, only Kamisimbi hospital remained functional while Muku hospital, Mulambi health centre and several other structures had closed.
r1-HC-SK-2025-017.l: Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu (Muku, Mulambi)
r1-HC-SK-2025-017.a: clashes between AFC/M23 troops and Wazalendo (per the headline); no single perpetrator for the closures
r1-HC-SK-2025-017.x: Radio Maendeleo: one hospital functioning; Muku hospital, Mulambi health centre and other structures closed
r1-HC-SK-2025-017.n: Single local outlet with an anonymous nurse source; the second excerpt says providers left 'after looting and the torture suffered in recent months' without saying who did it. Date is the page date.
r1-HC-SK-2025-017.vn: Article dated 2025/09/19 prints the headline and the nurse passage verbatim; single local outlet, anonymous nurse, so C. Figure flag is a false positive (M23 name). The '23' flagged is from the name AFC/M23, printed in the page title.
