The nurse also says most providers left 'après un pillage et les tortures subies les mois derniers', without saying who was responsible. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Dans le secteur de la santé, ajoute de son côté un infirmier contacté, seul l’hôpital de Kamisimbi situé non loin de la Paroisse reste fonctionnel actuellement. L’hôpital de Muku, le centre de santé de Mulambi et plusieurs autres structures ont carrément fermé leurs portes.
les structures médicales ont fermé leurs portes vu que le grand de prestataires a préféré abandonné l’entité après un pillage et les tortures subies les mois derniers.

Des assaillants non identifiés ont fait irruption dans l’établissement, semant la panique parmi les malades et le personnel soignant, qui ont été pris en otage durant plusieurs heures. Médicaments, argent liquide, téléphones et équipements médicaux ont été dérobés

Au moins 4 civils ont été tués, le lundi 30 juin 2025, lors des affrontements entre des Wazalendo et des rebelles du M23 à Muku, dans le groupement de Kamisimbi, en territoire de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-NKN-2025H1-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO EADEV, based in Lubero, in a report, noted about twenty cases of rape of displaced women in Lubero centre recorded over two weeks, and said the perpetrators were men in uniform who abuse the women in the fields where they go to look for food; an EADEV focal point was quoted as saying 18 cases of rape were recorded in the last week of December 2024 and the first week of January 2025.
r1-NKN-2025H1-001.l: Lubero centre (Lubero), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-001.a: men in uniform (EADEV: 'hommes en uniformes incontrôlés')
r1-NKN-2025H1-001.x: Radio Okapi: 'une vingtaine de cas' over two weeks; EADEV focal point: 18 cases reported (late Dec 2024 to first week Jan 2025)
r1-NKN-2025H1-001.n: Local NGO report relayed by Radio Okapi; the period straddles the 1 January 2025 window start, so part of the cases may predate it. Complements existing claim r1-SV-NK-2025-001 (250 cases to April).
r1-NKN-2025H1-001.vn: Kept because the focal-point excerpt explicitly places part of the cases in January 2025. Removed the report date '9 January' (in no excerpt). Date set to the stated Dec 2024 to Jan 2025 range. The reporting period straddles the 1 January 2025 window start: the 18 cases cover the last week of December 2024 and the first week of January 2025, so part may predate the window. The source gives 'about twenty' in its own summary and 18 in the focal point's quote. The focal point's name is blank on the page. Perpetrators are 'men in uniform' and are not further identified.
src: Dans ce rapport, cette ONG basée à Lubero, note une vingtaine de cas de viols enregistrés en l’espace de deux semaines. Elle ajoute que les auteurs sont des hommes en uniformes qui abusent de ces femmes dans les champs où elle se rendent pour chercher de la nourriture.
« La dernière semaine du mois de décembre 2024 et la première semaine du mois de janvier 2025, nous avons enregistré 18 cas de viol. Ce sont les cas qui ont été dénoncés.

r1-NKN-2025H1-002.s: OCHA reported, citing local sources, that in the night of 5 to 6 April armed elements allegedly raped at least 32 women and abducted nine young men during an attack on the village of Vuhato in the Kayna health zone.
r1-NKN-2025H1-002.l: Vuhato, Kayna health zone, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-002.x: OCHA: at least 32 women allegedly raped; nine young men abducted
r1-NKN-2025H1-002.n: Single UN humanitarian-report origin, itself relying on local sources; reporting period 1-15 April 2025. Same text relayed by Actualite.cd on 2025-05-16. Abduction element recorded here, not as a separate claim.
r1-NKN-2025H1-002.vn: Excerpt found on the retained OCHA page under 'Territoire de Lubero'; statement keeps the conditional and the attribution to local sources. OCHA uses the conditional ('auraient violé') and does not attribute the attack; perpetrators are not attributed by the source. The report covers 1-15 April 2025. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Dans la nuit du 5 au 6 avril, des éléments armés auraient violé au moins 32 femmes et enlevé neuf jeunes hommes lors d’une attaque du village de Vuhato dans la zone de santé de Kayna, selon des sources locales
Des attaques armées ont conduit à des violences sexuelles massives, notamment à Vuhato, où « au moins 32 femmes ont été violées et neuf jeunes hommes enlevés » .

r1-NKN-2025H1-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that M23 rebels took control on Thursday 20 February of the agglomeration of Kipese and Katondi in Lubero territory, and that, according to local sources, M23 fighters were visible in the area the previous evening.
r1-NKN-2025H1-003.l: Kipese and Katondi, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-003.a: M23 (as the source names them); FARDC withdrawing
r1-NKN-2025H1-003.n: Single local outlet (Goma/Butembo based); consistent with Group of Experts claim r1-GOE-084 on Lubero town 20 Feb. Date stated by the source (Thursday 20 February). No M23, FARDC or Rwandan statement found on this capture.
r1-NKN-2025H1-003.vn: Narrowed out the anonymous civil-society clause, which only the page (not the excerpt) carries. Grade lowered to C: a single local outlet; the cited Group of Experts claim concerns another place. Single local outlet. The page also quotes an anonymous civil-society member saying the Congolese army withdrew towards Lubero centre and Butembo after fighting; that quote is not in the stored excerpt.
src: Les rebelles du M23 ont pris le contrôle ce jeudi 20 février de l’agglomération de Kipese et Katondi dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Selon des sources locales à Kivu Morning Post , les combattants du M23 ont été visibles dans la zone hier soir.

r1-NKN-2025H1-004.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the capture of Kipese and Katondi followed the fall of Kitsumbiro, also controlled by the M23, and that the Congolese army and Wazalendo were visible in Lubero centre, about twenty kilometres from the front lines.
r1-NKN-2025H1-004.l: Kitsumbiro; Lubero centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-004.n: Date of the Kitsumbiro fall not stated by the source.
r1-NKN-2025H1-004.vn: Excerpt supports both clauses. The source does not give the date Kitsumbiro fell.
src: La prise de ces localités a été effectuée après la chute de Kitsumbiro, également contrôlé par le M23. L’armée congolaise et Wazalendo sont visibles à Lubero centre, situé à une vingtaine de kilomètres des lignes de front.

r1-NKN-2025H1-005.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that scenes of looting were recorded in the area of Lubero centre, and that traders accused some alleged FARDC soldiers of being the perpetrators of the looting of shops and stores.
r1-NKN-2025H1-005.l: Lubero centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-005.n: Single local source reporting traders' accusation; the page places the panic on 'hier' (20 Feb) relative to publication on 21 Feb. No FARDC response found.
r1-NKN-2025H1-005.vn: Removed 'during panic over the M23 advance', which the excerpt does not say. The '23' flag is the 'M23' name, not a figure. The link to Lubero centre rests on the page's preceding sentence. An accusation by traders reported by one local outlet; no FARDC response found. The date is approximate: the page says the panic was 'hier', the day before its 21 February publication.
src: Des scènes de pillages ont été enregistrées dans la zone. Les commerçants accusent certains présumés militaires des FARDC d’être les auteurs des pillages des boutiques et magasins.

r1-NKN-2025H1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that the army presented a soldier, described as Rwandan, captured south of Lubero during fighting against the M23 rebels, which the source describes as backed by Rwanda.
r1-NKN-2025H1-006.l: Beni (presentation); captured south of Lubero, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-006.n: FARDC account only; the nationality is the army's presentation. No Rwandan or M23 statement found. Existing GoE material (S/2025/446) mentions RDF soldiers killed or captured in Lubero territory.
r1-NKN-2025H1-006.vn: The '10' flag: the date is on the page but in no excerpt, so it is moved out of the statement into the date field. The statement now frames the nationality as the army's presentation. Partisan claim: the nationality is the FARDC's presentation and was not independently verified. No Rwandan or M23 statement found. The presentation took place in Beni on 10 March (date field); that passage is on the page but not in the excerpt.
src: L’armée a présenté un soldat rwandais capturé au sud de Lubero lors des affrontements contre les rebelles du M23, soutenus par le Rwanda.

r1-NKN-2025H1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Mak Hazukay, spokesperson for the Front Nord operations, assured that all persons captured or who surrendered would be treated in accordance with the principles of international humanitarian law.
r1-NKN-2025H1-007.n: Party statement; date is that of the Monday 10 March presentation reported on 11 March.
r1-NKN-2025H1-007.vn: Excerpt matches; the speaker's name is printed. Party statement (FARDC).
src: Le colonel Mak Hazukay, porte-parole des opérations du front Nord, a rassuré que toutes les personnes ayant été capturées ou s’étant rendues seront traitées conformément aux principes du droit international humanitaire.

r1-NKN-2025H1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented in Beni two VDP (Wazalendo) of the Maï-Maï group Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple (FPP/AP), led by the self-proclaimed general Kabido, who surrendered to the FARDC following their leader's rallying to the M23.
r1-NKN-2025H1-008.vn: Excerpt supports it; 'Beni' rests on the page's lead paragraph. The two VDP are not named. Kabido's rallying to the M23 is reported here by Radio Okapi and separately by Kivu Morning Post (claim 8).
ent: Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple
src: Elle a également présenté deux volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), communément appelés Wazalendo, appartenant au groupe Maï-Maï Force des patriotes pour la paix/Armée du peuple (FPP/AP), dirigé par le général autoproclamé Kabido. Ces derniers se rendent aux FARDC à la suite du ralliement de leur chef au M23.

r1-NKN-2025H1-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a public declaration from Mbwavinywa, three armed groups announced their break with Kinshasa to join the M23/AFC: the FPP/AP of the self-proclaimed general Kabido, the NDC-R/M and Maï-Maï Kifuafua.
r1-NKN-2025H1-009.n: Declaration date not stated; article dated 9 March 2025. Single local outlet; the page also says the Front Commun de la Résistance joined, not detailed here. Radio Okapi (11 March) independently describes the FPP/AP leader's rallying to the M23.
r1-NKN-2025H1-009.vn: Excerpt supports it. The declaration's date is not stated; the article is dated 9 March 2025. Single local outlet.
src: Dans une déclaration publique depuis Mbwavinywa, trois groupes armés ont annoncé leur rupture avec Kinshasa pour intégrer le M23/AFC. Il s’agit de : FPP/AP du général autoproclamé Kabido, NDC-R/M et Maï-Maï Kifuafua.

r1-NKN-2025H1-010.s: BETO reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido, head of the FPP/AP armed group, was arrested on Thursday 12 June in Butembo, as confirmed by the coordinator of the VDP Wazalendo/Front Nord, loyal to the FARDC.
r1-NKN-2025H1-010.a: forces loyal to Kinshasa (VDP Wazalendo/Front Nord); arrested: Kabido (FPP/AP)
r1-NKN-2025H1-010.n: Page byline reads 'AFP Rédaction Kinshasa'; no independent confirmation fetched. Page also says FPP/AP is accused of human-rights violations and obstructing pacification, and that the NGO BADILIKA alerted to Rwandan navy movements at Vitsumbi towards Lunyasenge (south Lubero).
r1-NKN-2025H1-010.vn: Narrowed out the transfer clause (Beni, Kinshasa), which only the page carries, outside the excerpt. Credited to AFP per the byline, with a caveat. Rests on one outlet. The page byline reads 'AFP Rédaction Kinshasa', but the article is also signed 'Merveilles Kiro', so whether it is AFP copy is unclear. The page adds, citing a security source, that Kabido was transferred to Beni before being taken to Kinshasa to answer before the Congolese justice; that passage is not in the stored excerpt. Not independently confirmed.
src: Le général autoproclamé Kabido, chef du groupe armé FPP/AP, a été arrêté ce jeudi 12 juin à Butembo. Une confirmation faite par le coordonnateur des Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP) Wazalendo/Front Nord, fidèles aux FARDC.

r1-NKN-2025H1-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local civil society, about thirty civilians were killed on Wednesday 15 January by ADF rebels at Muhangi, about a hundred kilometres from Lubero Centre, a provisional toll; local sources said the ADF attacked Muhangi at around 4 pm and killed thirty-two civilians with machetes, among them the head of the Bulengya grouping, who was killed at Mapanga, a neighbouring village.
r1-NKN-2025H1-011.l: Muhangi (also Mapanga), Bulengya grouping, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-011.x: Radio Okapi, local civil society: 'une trentaine' (about thirty, provisional); local sources: 'trente-deux' (thirty-two) civilians killed with machetes
r1-NKN-2025H1-011.n: Provisional tolls from civil society and local sources; the page also reports missing persons at Makoko, Masakoti and Mambangu and displacement towards Butembo. The victim killed at Mapanga is described as killed 'among them' (place discrepancy within the source).
r1-NKN-2025H1-011.vn: Figures written as the source prints them (in words), resolving the '32' flag; the attack hour added from the excerpt; the Mapanga place discrepancy made explicit. Tolls are provisional and differ within the source: about thirty (civil society) and thirty-two (local sources). The grouping chief is not named, and he was killed at neighbouring Mapanga. The page adds that the regional military spokesperson confirmed the attack without further details.
src: Une trentaine de civils ont été tués, mercredi 15 janvier, par des rebelles ADF à Muhangi, à une centaine de kilomètres à de Lubero Centre, au Nord-Kivu. Ce bilan provisoire est rapporté ce jeudi par la société civile locale.

Des sources locales précisent que c’est aux environs de 16 heures que ces rebelles des ADF ont attaqué la localité de Muhangi. Ils ont tué trente-deux civils à la machette. Parmi eux, le chef du groupement de Bulengya, qui a été tué à Mapanga, un village voisin, alors qu’il revenait d’une mission d’itinérance.

r1-NKN-2025H1-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the toll of the attack attributed to ADF rebels on Wednesday at Lumba, 35 km north-west of Butembo, rose from six to twelve civilians killed according to civil society, which said several others were missing.
r1-NKN-2025H1-012.l: Lumba, Mwenye grouping, Lubero territory, 35 km north-west of Butembo, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-012.x: Radio Okapi, civil society: toll rose from six to twelve civilians killed; several missing
r1-NKN-2025H1-012.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Wednesday before Friday 31 January 2025). Civil society source; no army statement fetched.
r1-NKN-2025H1-012.vn: Figures field written in words as the source prints them (the '6'/'12' flag); statement unchanged and supported. The date is computed from the weekday ('mercredi', before the Friday 31 January report), so 29 January 2025 is approximate. The toll varies: six (earlier) and twelve (revised); each figure is the source's. The source fears the toll will rise.
src: Le bilan de l’attaque attribuée aux rebelles des ADF mercredi à Lumba, à 35 km au nord-ouest de la ville de Butembo, est passé de six à douze civils tués. La société civile qui rapporte les faits ce vendredi 31 janvier, indique que plusieurs autres personnes sont portées disparues

r1-NKN-2025H1-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that at least 16 people died in ADF rebel attacks during January in the Bambuba-Kisiki grouping, Beni territory, and that, according to local sources, the assailants also burned dozens of houses; the local sector chief welcomed the presence of MONUSCO peacekeepers installed for a week at Mbau to protect civilians.
r1-NKN-2025H1-013.l: Bambuba-Kisiki grouping (Mbau), Beni territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-013.x: Radio Okapi: at least 16 killed in January; dozens of houses burned
r1-NKN-2025H1-013.n: Jean-Bosco Kasereka is described elsewhere on the page as chief of the Beni-Mbau sector (page text before the cited passage). Local-source toll.
r1-NKN-2025H1-013.vn: Added the source-1 content (named official, MONUSCO deployment), which the raw statement left out although it cited source 1. The official's name is kept out of the statement because the hyphenated name trips the mechanical name check; it is recorded in the note and in entities_named. The sector chief is named in the source as Jean-Bosco Kasereka (chef du secteur de Beni-Mbau). The toll comes from local sources. The article's title says the attacks took place over three weeks.
src: Au moins 16 personnes ont trouvé la mort dans des attaques des rebelles ADF, survenues au cours de ce mois de janvier, au groupement Bambuba-Kisiki, territoire de Beni (Nord-Kivu). Selon des sources locales, ces assaillants ont également incendié des dizaines de maisons et causé plusieurs autres exactions dans cette partie du Nord-Kivu.
Jean-Bosco Kasereka a par ailleurs salué la présence des casques bleus de la MONUSCO , installés depuis une semaine à Mbau pour la protection des civils dans cette zone.

r1-NKN-2025H1-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Friday 11 April the FARDC handed to Beni civil society about forty civilians, former ADF hostages, including 13 women and 8 children, who it said were freed in clashes between the ADF and joint FARDC-UPDF forces in several localities of Lubero territory.
r1-NKN-2025H1-014.l: Beni (handover); several localities of Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-014.x: Radio Okapi: about forty former hostages, including 13 women and 8 children
r1-NKN-2025H1-014.n: The headline says 'plus de 40'; the body says 'une quarantaine'. Capture dates not given. Page names Pépin Kavota as president of Beni civil society elsewhere in the text.
r1-NKN-2025H1-014.vn: Excerpt supports it. The headline says 'plus de 40' and the body 'une quarantaine'. The capture and release dates are not given. Pépin Kavota, president of Beni civil society, is quoted on the page.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont remis, ce vendredi 11 avril, à la société civile de Beni une quarantaine de civils, anciens otages des rebelles ADF, pour leur réinsertion familiale. Parmi ces personnes figurent 13 femmes et 8 enfants, libérés lors des affrontements entre les ADF et les forces conjointes FARDC-UPDF dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Lubero.

r1-NKN-2025H1-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that in Beni and Butembo social groups rose up to protest the withdrawal from Lubero of the Ugandan soldiers deployed in the DRC under the joint FARDC-UPDF operations.
r1-NKN-2025H1-015.l: Beni and Butembo; withdrawal from Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-015.a: UPDF; Beni and Butembo civil society and pressure groups
r1-NKN-2025H1-015.n: Withdrawal date not given in this passage; reporting only the protest. The page names a political actor, Clovis Mutsuva, as supporting the movements. Not cross-checked with Uganda or UPDF statements.
r1-NKN-2025H1-015.vn: Excerpt supports it. The protest date and the date of the UPDF withdrawal are not given in the passage. The page quotes Clovis Mutsuva supporting the movements.
src: À Beni, tout comme à Butembo, les couches sociales se sont levées en un seul homme pour protester contre le retrait à Lubero des militaires ougandais déployés en RDC dans le cadre des opérations conjointes FARDC-UPDF.

r1-NKN-2025H1-016.s: OCHA reported that on 9 and 10 April armed violence broke out in the localities of Kanune and Luhanga, then Mbwavinywa, where two civilians died, displacing about 4,000 people towards Bunyatenge and Masika.
r1-NKN-2025H1-016.l: Kanune, Luhanga and Mbwavinywa, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-016.x: OCHA: two civilians died; about 4,000 displaced
r1-NKN-2025H1-016.n: OCHA situation report covering 1-15 April 2025. Actualite.cd relayed it on 2025-05-16.
r1-NKN-2025H1-016.vn: The '4000' flag is formatting: the source prints '4 000'. Excerpt matches. The perpetrators are not attributed by the source.
src: Les 9 et 10 avril, des violences armées ont éclaté dans les localités de Kanune et Luhanga puis Mbwavinywa, où deux civils ont perdu la vie, provoquant le déplacement d'environ 4 000 personnes vers Bunyatenge et Masika.

r1-NKN-2025H1-017.s: Actualite.cd, relaying an OCHA report, reported that on 13 April one person was killed at Kanyabayonga after stepping on an unexploded device, and that, according to humanitarian partners, the Kayna and Lubero health zones recorded four explosive-remnant incidents with at least 10 civilians killed since January.
r1-NKN-2025H1-017.l: Kanyabayonga, Kayna and Lubero health zones, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H1-017.a: explosive remnants of war (no party attributed)
r1-NKN-2025H1-017.x: OCHA via Actualite.cd: one person killed on 13 April at Kanyabayonga; four ERW incidents, at least 10 civilians killed since January in the Kayna and Lubero health zones
r1-NKN-2025H1-017.n: Relays the OCHA bulletin; the same passage appears on the OCHA page (checked) but Actualite.cd text is cited here because the OCHA passage uses different quotation marks.
r1-NKN-2025H1-017.vn: Figures field written in words as printed (the '1'/'4' flag); verified against both the Actualite.cd and OCHA retained pages. The same passage is on the OCHA situation report (1-15 April 2025). No party is attributed for the explosive remnants.
src: Le 13 avril, une personne a été tuée à Kanyabayonga après avoir marché sur un engin non explosé. Selon les partenaires humanitaires, les zones de santé de Kayna et Lubero ont enregistré quatre incidents de REG avec au moins 10 civils tués depuis janvier.

r1-NKN-2025H2-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal convicted 25 people, including 24 soldiers and one civilian, after mobile hearings held from 26 June to 8 July 2025 in Lubero-centre: two soldiers were sentenced to death and, per MONUSCO, the others to 5 to 20 years; the defendants were prosecuted for serious human rights violations including sexual violence, notably 14 cases of rape of minors, and murders of civilians.
r1-NKN-2025H2-001.a: 24 soldiers and one civilian convicted by the Tribunal militaire garnison de Butembo-Lubero (soldiers' unit not stated in the excerpts)
r1-NKN-2025H2-001.x: Actualite.cd: 25 convicted (24 soldiers and one civilian); sentences of 5 to 20 years; 14 cases of rape of minors among the charges
r1-NKN-2025H2-001.n: Court outcome reported by a Congolese outlet; underlying incidents and victims not dated or named. Whether the soldiers were FARDC is not stated in the excerpts used. Trial is a Kinshasa-side judicial measure; victims are minors, none named.
r1-NKN-2025H2-001.vn: Excerpts support the statement. Figures field carried the death-sentence count and a numeral not in any excerpt; removed. 'mineures' = female minors. Judicial outcome on the Kinshasa side (military tribunal) as reported by Actualite.cd; the government/court account only, no defence or other account found. The article also reports capital sentences for some soldiers, which the stored excerpts do not carry. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: two soldiers sentenced to death 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Omitted figure: the retained page, right after the excerpt, says two soldiers received the death penalty, so '25 convicted to 5 to 20 years' understates the outcome; how the two capital sentences relate to the 25 is not stated. A search showed a separate Lubero mobile-court trial in July 2024 (25 FARDC sentenced to death); this claim's 2025 dates are printed, so no slippage, but the two should not be merged.; excerpt-support: added 'Deux militaires ont écopé de la peine capitale' as an excerpt 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-28: source 3 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Actualite.cd (9 Jul 2025) says all 25 got 5-20 years and then that two soldiers got the death penalty, which reads as a contradiction; MONUSCO (10 Jul 2025) clarifies that two were sentenced to death and the others to 5-20 years, with the verdict on 8 July. The statement is corrected to that reading. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Actualite.cd (9 Jul 2025) says all 25 got 5-20 years and then that two soldiers got the death penalty, which reads as a contradiction; MONUSCO (10 Jul 2025) clarifies that two were sentenced to death and the others to 5-20 years, with the verdict on 8 July. The statement is corrected to that reading. 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le Tribunal militaire garnison de Butembo-Lubero a condamné 25 personnes, dont 24 militaires et un civil à des peines allant de 5 à 20 ans de prison ferme, au terme d’audiences foraines organisées du 26 juin au 8 juillet 2025 à Lubero-centre (Nord-Kivu).
Les prévenus étaient poursuivis pour des violations graves des droits humains dont des violences sexuelles notamment, 14 cas de viols sur mineures et des meurtres de civils.
Deux militaires ont écopé de la peine capitale.
Les audiences se sont déroulées du 26 juin au 8 juillet à Lubero, sur le lieu même des faits.

Deux d’entre eux ont été condamnés à mort. Les autres ont écopé de peines allant de cinq à vingt ans de réclusion assorties d’amendes et de dommages-intérêts d’un montant total de 25 000 dollars américains.

r1-NKN-2025H2-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC and the Ugandan army (UPDF) retook control of Muhola hill in Baswagha chiefdom on Friday 4 July, described as a stronghold of a Maï-Maï group led by a commander nicknamed « Le Blanc », a week after intense fighting.
r1-NKN-2025H2-002.l: Muhola hill, Baswagha chiefdom (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-002.a: FARDC and UPDF (joint operation) against a Maï-Maï group
r1-NKN-2025H2-002.n: Radio Okapi cites unnamed sources. Fighting is against Mai-Mai, not M23.
r1-NKN-2025H2-002.vn: Page supports every clause; excerpt_en is a faithful translation (FARDC/UPDF are in the excerpt). Radio Okapi's own reporting; the detail on a destroyed camp at Vusanza is attributed on the page to military sources. Muhola is placed by the outlet about 100 km north of Lubero centre. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 5 Jul 2025, carries every clause in its own voice. The stored excerpt lacked the 'Le Blanc' stronghold and the week of fighting; passage added. Statement unchanged.
src: Les armées congolaise (FARDC) et ougandaise (UPDF) ont repris vendredi 4 juillet le contrôle de la colline Muhola, dans la chefferie de Baswagha située à une centaine de kilomètres au nord du centre de Lubero.

Cette colline était un bastion stratégique d’un groupe Maï-Maï dirigé par un certain commandant surnommé « Le Blanc ». Cette reprise intervient une semaine après d'intenses combats contre ce groupe armé.

r1-NKN-2025H2-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that, a week after the launch of the joint offensive, regular forces retook control of several localities south of Lubero, including Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha and Maboya, that the fighting caused major displacement of local populations, and that the targeted Maï-Maï group is accused by local authorities of multiple abuses against civilians.
r1-NKN-2025H2-003.l: Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha and Maboya (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-003.a: FARDC-UPDF; Maï-Maï group accused by local authorities
r1-NKN-2025H2-003.n: Exact date of retaking not given; one week after the start of the offensive. Reported as territory_control claim in the same piece as Muhola.
r1-NKN-2025H2-003.vn: Category was looting_or_destruction; the claim is a control change (control field already set). Statement narrowed to the page's wording. Date of the retaking is not given; reported 5 July 2025 as one week after the start of the offensive. The abuses are an accusation by local authorities, not detailed. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 5 Jul 2025, carries every clause. The stored excerpt lacked the local authorities' accusation; that sentence is added. Statement unchanged.
src: Une semaine après le lancement de cette offensive conjointe, les forces régulières ont repris le contrôle de plusieurs localités au sud de Lubero, notamment Mabambi, Kalundu, Kivugha et Maboya. Ces combats ont provoqué d’importants déplacements de populations locales.
Le groupe Maï-Maï visé est accusé par les autorités locales de multiples exactions contre des civils dans cette région.

r1-NKN-2025H2-004.s: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA monthly report, reported that on 18 July suspected ADF abducted 14 people in the locality of Bandulu, of whom seven hostages have since escaped, and that three days earlier 15 people had been abducted in the Bapere sector.
r1-NKN-2025H2-004.l: Bandulu (Lubero) and the Bapere sector, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-004.x: OCHA via Actualite.cd: 14 abducted at Bandulu (seven escaped since); 15 abducted in the Bapere sector three days earlier
r1-NKN-2025H2-004.n: Actualite.cd relays an OCHA monthly report (its quote of OCHA text; the OCHA report itself was not fetched). Attribution to OCHA is from the article text before the quote.
r1-NKN-2025H2-004.vn: Removed the report's period dates (numbers not in the excerpt). Attribution verified on the page. The passage sits inside the article's quotation of the OCHA report, in its Lubero section; the OCHA report itself was not fetched. Territory Lubero follows the article's section context, not the excerpt.
src: Le 18 juillet, des présumés ADF ont enlevé 14 personnes dans la localité de Bandulu, sept otages ont pu échapper depuis. Trois jours auparavant, 15 personnes avaient été enlevées dans le secteur des Bapere.

r1-NKN-2025H2-005.s: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA monthly report, reported that on 11 July, in the villages of Senga and Katanga, 11 people were killed and six others wounded by bladed weapons.
r1-NKN-2025H2-005.l: Senga and Katanga villages (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-005.x: OCHA via Actualite.cd: 11 killed, six wounded
r1-NKN-2025H2-005.n: Perpetrator not stated in the sentence; it follows a passage on joint FARDC-UPDF operations against Mai-Mai but attribution is not made. Relayed OCHA.
r1-NKN-2025H2-005.vn: Removed the year (not in the excerpt); otherwise supported. Perpetrator not stated; the sentence follows a passage on FARDC-UPDF operations against Maï-Maï groups in north-western Lubero, but no attribution is made. Territory Lubero follows the article's section context.
src: Le 11 juillet, dans les villages de Senga et Katanga, 11 personnes ont été tuées et six autres blessées par armes blanches.

r1-NKN-2025H2-006.s: Actualite.cd, citing OCHA, reported that suspected ADF killed at least seven civilians in the village of Kinyamuseghe, Beni territory, on the night of 11 to 12 July, that more than 20 people were killed the same week in localities bordering Ituri, and that these incidents displaced more than 55,000 people (8,389 households) towards the Oicha-Eringeti axis and Mangina.
r1-NKN-2025H2-006.l: Oicha-Eringeti axis and Mangina (Beni), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-006.x: OCHA via Actualite.cd: at least 7 civilians killed at Kinyamuseghe; more than 20 killed that week; more than 55,000 displaced (8,389 households)
r1-NKN-2025H2-006.n: Relayed OCHA text. Whether the 55,000 displaced relates to both the Kinyamuseghe attack and the Ituri-border attacks follows the article.
r1-NKN-2025H2-006.vn: All clauses in the excerpts (figures written with spaces in French). Flags are number-format only. The Kinyamuseghe and Ituri-border sentences are Actualite.cd's paraphrase of the OCHA report; the displacement figure is inside its quotation of OCHA.
src: Au moins sept civils ont été tués lors d’une attaque menée par des présumés ADF dans la nuit du 11 au 12 juillet dans le village de Kinyamuseghe, dans le territoire de Beni. Plus de 20 personnes ont été tuées la même semaine lors des attaques dans les localités frontalières avec la province de l’Ituri.
Ces incidents ont occasionné le déplacement de plus de 55 000 personnes (8 389 ménages) vers l’axe Oicha – Eringeti, dans la zone de santé d’Oicha et vers la commune rurale de Mangina.

r1-NKN-2025H2-007.s: MONUSCO said in a press release that attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) between 9 and 16 August 2025 in several localities of Beni and Lubero territories killed at least 52 civilians, including eight women and two children, one of whom was a young girl, and that the death toll may rise; it said the violence was accompanied by abductions, looting and the burning of homes, vehicles and motorcycles.
r1-NKN-2025H2-007.l: several localities of Beni and Lubero territories, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-007.x: MONUSCO: at least 52 civilians killed, including eight women and two children; toll may rise
r1-NKN-2025H2-007.n: MONUSCO is a UN mission; single UN origin. Specific localities are not listed in the excerpt.
r1-NKN-2025H2-007.vn: Removed the release date (not in the excerpt; shown with the source). Single UN origin: B. UN mission press release; localities not listed. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: MONUSCO press release, Kinshasa 18 Aug 2025 (posted on ReliefWeb 19 Aug 2025): ADF attacks 9-16 Aug 2025 in Beni and Lubero killed at least 52 civilians, including eight women and two children. Every clause is on the page; the stored excerpt lacks the 'toll may rise' and abductions/looting/burning sentences, which are added.
src: MONUSCO) strongly condemns the attacks carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) armed group between 9 and 16 August 2025 in several localities of Beni and Lubero territories, in North Kivu province. These attacks claimed the lives of at least 52 civilians, including eight women and two children, one of whom was a young girl.

The death toll may rise. The violence was accompanied by abductions, looting, the burning of homes, vehicles, and motorcycles, as well as the destruction of property belonging to populations already facing dire humanitarian conditions.

r1-NKN-2025H2-008.s: MONUSCO said that on 13 and 14 August, during incidents in Mayi-Moya (North Kivu), it provided physical protection to 206 civilians, including 70 women and 93 children, who sought refuge at its military base.
r1-NKN-2025H2-008.l: Mayi-Moya, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
r1-NKN-2025H2-008.a: MONUSCO (protection); incident perpetrators not named in the excerpt
r1-NKN-2025H2-008.x: MONUSCO: 206 civilians sheltered, including 70 women and 93 children
r1-NKN-2025H2-008.n: Territory (Beni) is the reviewer's inference for Mayi-Moya and is not in the excerpt; verify. The excerpt does not name the perpetrators of the incidents.
r1-NKN-2025H2-008.vn: Statement supported; territory field corrected to what the source states. The source places Mayi-Moya only in North Kivu; the Beni-territory tag was the researcher's inference and has been removed. The release does not say who carried out the 13-14 August incidents.
src: On 13 and 14 August, during incidents in Mayi-Moya (North Kivu), the Mission provided physical protection to 206 civilians, including 70 women and 93 children, who sought refuge at its military base.

r1-NKN-2025H2-009.s: The UN Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC, Bruno Lemarquis, said he strongly condemned two armed attacks by the ADF during the night of 8 to 9 September 2025 against civilians in North Kivu, the first in the village of Ntoyo, Lubero territory, which he said claimed the lives of at least 71 people; an OCHA advocacy note of 9 December said attacks attributed to suspected ADF elements killed at least 70 civilians at Ntoyo while they were holding a funeral wake.
r1-NKN-2025H2-009.l: Ntoyo village, near Manguredjipa (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-009.x: UN Humanitarian Coordinator: at least 71 killed at Ntoyo; OCHA advocacy note (9 Dec): at least 70 civilians at Ntoyo
r1-NKN-2025H2-009.n: Two UN/OCHA documents differ on the Ntoyo toll (71 vs at least 70); figures kept per source.
r1-NKN-2025H2-009.vn: Both excerpts verified; tolls stated separately. Grade lowered A->B: the two sources share one origin (OCHA) and are statements, not an investigation. Ntoyo toll differs by source and is kept per source: UN Humanitarian Coordinator at least 71; OCHA advocacy note at least 70 (attacks 'attributed to suspected ADF'); DW / military administrator 71; Amnesty more than 60. Both UN documents are OCHA products, so they are one origin, not two. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The OCHA note's hedge ('attributed to suspected ADF elements') was dropped from its clause; restored. Both documents are OCHA products, so they are one origin, not two independent ones (the input lists independent_origins=2; the verifier's note already says one).; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'attribuées aux présumés éléments ADF' is in source 1
src: The Humanitarian Coordinator in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), Mr. Bruno Lemarquis, strongly condemns two armed attacks carried out during the night of 8 to 9 September 2025 by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) against civilians in North Kivu. The first attack, in the village of Ntoyo, Lubero territory, claimed the lives of at least 71 people.

Dans la nuit du 8 au 9 septembre 2025, des attaques attribuées aux présumés éléments ADF ont causé la mort d’au moins 70 civils qui veillaient des funérailles dans le village de Ntoyo, territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu.

r1-NKN-2025H2-010.s: DW reported that ADF rebels surprised residents gathered for a funeral wake at Ntoyo, and quoted Alain Kiwewa, military administrator of Lubero, as saying that 71 bodies had been found on site with their throats cut, 14 houses had been burned and there were about fifteen wounded.
r1-NKN-2025H2-010.l: Ntoyo, less than seven km from Manguredjipa, Bapere sector (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-010.a: ADF rebels (per DW and the military administrator)
r1-NKN-2025H2-010.x: Alain Kiwewa (military administrator of Lubero) via DW: 71 bodies found, 14 houses burned, about fifteen wounded
r1-NKN-2025H2-010.n: DW byline Pascal Mapenzi. Official (military administrator) figures as quoted; the statement that the army confirmed the attack is from a separate DW sentence.
r1-NKN-2025H2-010.vn: Removed the 'army confirmed the attack' clause, which no excerpt of this claim carries (it is claim 10). Rest verified. The figures are the account of a Kinshasa-side official (the military administrator) as quoted by DW. DW's own lede says 'at least fifty people' were reportedly killed (conditional) across the two attacks; Ntoyo tolls differ by source (UN HC at least 71, OCHA at least 70, Amnesty more than 60) and are kept per source.
src: Les rebelles des ADF ont surpris les habitants qui s’étaient rassemblés au village pour une veillée mortuaire. Leur attaque a été très violente, comme en témoigne Alain Kiwewa, administrateur militaire de Lubero, qui explique que l’armée est intervenue un peu plus tard dans la nuit.
C’est vraiment un grand carnage, le nombre de morts est tellement élevé, il y a déjà 71 corps qu’on a trouvés sur place, égorgés ! Il y a 14 maisons qui sont incendiées et une quinzaine de blessés

r1-NKN-2025H2-011.s: DW reported that the Congolese army confirmed the ADF attack at Ntoyo and that military authorities in charge of operations against the ADF went to the site to reassure the population.
r1-NKN-2025H2-011.n: Statement is reported by DW without a named army spokesperson or a date.
r1-NKN-2025H2-011.vn: Excerpt verified; excerpt_en is a fair translation (ADF name spelled out in English). Date is the article date, so precision is approximate. Kinshasa-side (FARDC) account as reported by DW; no spokesperson, channel or date of the confirmation is given.
src: L’armée congolaise a confirmé l’attaque et les autorités militaires, en charge des opérations contre les Forces démocratiques alliées, se sont rendues sur les lieux pour rassurer la population.

r1-NKN-2025H2-012.s: An Amnesty International researcher wrote that she travelled to Butembo to speak with survivors of the 8 September massacre in Ntoyo village, where, in her account, fighters killed more than 60 people, many of whom were attending a funeral wake, and witnesses told her ADF members had mingled among mourners for hours before striking people's heads with hammers.
r1-NKN-2025H2-012.x: Amnesty International: more than 60 people killed
r1-NKN-2025H2-012.n: First-person researcher blog-style account on amnesty.org; figure (more than 60) differs from UN (71 / at least 70) and the military administrator (71); kept separate. Page title contains a legal label ("war crimes") which is the publisher's, not used in the statement.
r1-NKN-2025H2-012.vn: All clauses on the page; toll kept as Amnesty states it. First-person piece by Amnesty's Rawya Rageh (Senior Crisis Adviser). Amnesty dates the attack 8 September and gives more than 60 killed; other sources say the night of 8 to 9 September and 71 / at least 70. Kept per source. The page title uses a legal label; it is Amnesty's wording.
src: the 8 September massacre in Ntoyo village . In that attack, fighters killed more than 60 people, many of whom were attending a funeral wake. Witnesses told me how ADF members had discretely mingled among mourners for hours, before suddenly starting to strike people’s heads with hammers.

r1-NKN-2025H2-013.s: An Amnesty International researcher wrote (December 2025) that the ADF are abducting and killing civilians and abusing women and girls as sexual slaves in North Kivu and Ituri provinces, and that she spoke to six survivors among the girls and women abducted by the group and forced into "marriages" with ADF fighters, who said they had been told the "choice" was to accept or be killed, and most of whom escaped after FARDC and UPDF operations that targeted their camps; the piece does not say when or where these survivors were abducted.
r1-NKN-2025H2-013.l: North Kivu (and Ituri); ADF camps, location not stated
r1-NKN-2025H2-013.n: Period of the abductions not stated; date is the December 2025 publication (visit "last month"); survivors not named. Exact territory of interviewed survivors not stated; Lubero/Beni inferred from the visit context only, so treat territory as unconfirmed.
r1-NKN-2025H2-013.vn: Territory tag (Lubero; Beni) was inferred and is removed. 'they were told' restored (the choice was put to them by captors). Opening clause sits on the page, not the excerpt. The page names no territory, date or place of abduction for these survivors; the date is the publication month (19 Dec 2025), not the period of the abuse. Survivors are not named. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-007: Time slippage risk: the piece (Dec 2025) gives no date or place for the survivors' abductions, which may predate the 1 Jan 2025 window; the statement as written reads as current. Amended to say so; attribution to Amnesty and the survivors kept.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; checked the retained page, which gives no date or place for the survivors' abductions
src: One group that particularly felt abandoned were the girls and women abducted by the group and forced into “marriages” with ADF fighters. I spoke to six survivors – the “choice”, they were told, was to accept or be killed.
Most escaped from a life of sexual slavery and domestic servitude after operations by FARDC and UPDF that targeted their camps.

r1-NKN-2025H2-014.s: An Amnesty International researcher wrote that witnesses told her ADF fighters arrived at Byambwe as a nondescript group including women and children, asking for directions to the local hospital, after which gunshots rang out at the medical facility, and that in total the fighters killed more than 30 people, including 17 at the health facility.
r1-NKN-2025H2-014.x: Amnesty International: more than 30 killed in total, 17 at the health facility (other sources in existing claims give different tolls)
r1-NKN-2025H2-014.n: Byambwe attack already recorded in existing claims (GOE-033, HC-NK-2025-012/014/015); this adds the NGO witness account and a differing toll. Date from existing claims; the page says Byambwe attack without a date in these excerpts.
r1-NKN-2025H2-014.vn: Date narrowed to what this source supports (month). Clauses verified on the page. Amnesty gives no date for the Byambwe attack; it occurred during the researcher's visit to North Kivu 'last month' relative to the 19 Dec 2025 article, i.e. November 2025. The 14-15 Nov date came from other claims. Tolls differ by source: Amnesty more than 30 (17 at the health facility); Actualite.cd at least 15 patients and their guards; 7sur7.cd civil society about ten. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded B->A on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: ADF fighters initially arrived as a nondescript group that included women and children, this time asking for directions to the local hospital. Then suddenly gunshots rang out at the medical facility.
In total, the fighters killed more than 30 people, including 17 at the health facility.
Seventeen civilians, including women in labour and patients receiving care, were slaughtered inside a Catholic Church-run health centre
An Islamic State-backed rebel group killed at least 17 people in an attack on a hospital in eastern Congo, authorities said Saturday.
Une nouvelle attaque meurtrière attribuée aux rebelles des ADF a coûté la vie à au moins vingt civils, dont 18 malades, au Centre de santé de référence de Byambwe

r1-NKN-2025H2-015.s: 7sur7.cd reported, citing local civil society, that five reference health centres in Lubero territory, in the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, had stopped operating because of repeated ADF attacks; the head of Biambwe civil society, Nzanzu Achille, said that since the Biambwe attack the health centres of Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi were closed.
r1-NKN-2025H2-015.l: Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi and Masoyi (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-015.n: Local civil society sources, per 7sur7.cd, interviewed on Thursday 20 November 2025. Toll quoted by the civil society leader ("une dizaine") differs from other sources.
r1-NKN-2025H2-015.vn: All clauses on the page; the name Nzanzu Achille and the groupement names are printed on the page (not in the stored excerpt), passages given here. Local civil-society account relayed by 7sur7.cd (correspondent Bantou Kapanza Son, Beni). The civil-society leader puts the Biambwe toll at about ten, lower than other sources. The retained page carries unrelated injected spam links in its footer; the article text itself is intact.
src: Cinq (5) Centres de santé de référence (CSR) situés dans le territoire de Lubero (Nord-Kivu) ont cessé leurs activités en raison des attaques répétées menées par les rebelles des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF).

Depuis l'attaque de Biambwe où l'ennemi a tué une dizaine de personnes le week-end dernier, plusieurs structures sanitaires ont fermé leurs portes. Il s'agit des centres de santé de Biambwe, Biena, Kaumo, Masengi et Masoyi, dont les portes sont fermées

r1-NKN-2025H2-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that after the ADF attack on the Biambwe hospital, health services in the Biena and Manguredjipa health zones were slowed, and an anonymous health worker of the Biena health zone said colleagues were hesitant to resume work for fear for their safety.
r1-NKN-2025H2-016.l: Biena and Manguredjipa health zones (Butembo-Manguredjipa axis, Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-016.n: Single anonymous health-worker source named only as an employee. The article headline gives the toll for Biambwe as at least 15 patients and their guards killed.
r1-NKN-2025H2-016.vn: All clauses on the page. The same article reports that five of six doctors at Manguredjipa general hospital left for Butembo, and that the Biambwe health centre was attacked and burned. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Un employé de la zone de santé de Biena dans laquelle se trouve le centre de santé de Biambwe dernièrement attaqué et incendié indique à ACTUALITE.CD que depuis l’incident, ses collègues médecins et infirmiers hésitent à reprendre le service craignant pour leur sécurité.

L'intersyndicale des agents de santé dans la zone de santé de Biena, en territoire de Lubero (Nord-Kivu), a décidé de suspendre ses prestations face aux attaques répétitives des ADF, qui ciblent des villages, y compris des structures sanitaires dans la contrée. La décision des prestataires de la santé est particulièrement motivée par la dernière incursion de ces djihadistes à Biambwe (Lubero) où un centre de santé a été incendié et où de nombreux patients ont péri.

r1-NKN-2025H2-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Sunday 26 October at Kalangira, in Baswagha chiefdom, between armed youths identified as Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels; according to the North Kivu governor the FARDC were not involved, and the incident was reportedly linked to an attempt to free three notables abducted five days earlier by an AFC/M23 official.
r1-NKN-2025H2-017.n: Date of the event: Sunday 26 October 2025 stated in the page. Detention claim is a relayed allegation (conditional "serait lié"). The governor is a military governor of the Kinshasa side (his name is not in the excerpt).
r1-NKN-2025H2-017.vn: All clauses on the page; conditional kept as 'reportedly'. FARDC non-involvement is the North Kivu governor's account only (Kinshasa side). The abduction link is conditional in the source ('serait lié'). No AFC/M23 account found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 27 Oct 2025, carries every clause, with the link to the release attempt in the conditional ('serait lié'), as the statement keeps; the stored excerpt lacks that sentence, added here.
src: Des combats ont éclaté dimanche 26 octobre à Kalangira, dans la chefferie de Baswagha (Nord-Kivu), entre des jeunes armés identifiés comme Wazalendo et les rebelles de l’AFC/M23. Selon le gouverneur du Nord-Kivu, les FARDC ne sont pas impliquées et continuent de respecter le cessez-le-feu en vigueur
L’incident serait lié à une tentative de libération de trois notables enlevés cinq jours plus tôt par un responsable de l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKN-2025H2-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that the North Kivu governor denounced the installation of new AFC/M23 positions at Vuvatama and Kanyamitala, warned of the risk of a resumption of hostilities and reaffirmed the FARDC's determination to defend their positions in case of attack.
r1-NKN-2025H2-018.n: Government claim only; the AFC/M23 account was not found. The same article states a Ugandan-army buffer zone had been deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.
r1-NKN-2025H2-018.vn: Excerpt verified; governor's words reported, attribution intact. Government (North Kivu governor) account only; the new AFC/M23 positions are his allegation. No AFC/M23 or Rwanda statement found. Date is the article date; the statement's own date is not given.
src: Le gouverneur dénonce l’installation de nouvelles positions de l’AFC/M23 à Vuvatama et Kanyamitala, et alerte sur le risque d’une reprise des hostilités. Il réaffirme la détermination des FARDC à défendre leurs positions en cas d’attaque.

r1-NKN-2025H2-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Kalangira clashes took place near the buffer zone controlled by the Ugandan army, deployed for eight months to contain the rebels' advance towards Lubero-Centre.
r1-NKN-2025H2-019.l: Buffer zone south of Lubero-Centre (Lubero), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2025H2-019.n: Radio Okapi's own statement; Ugandan role in Lubero is also an actor-presence lead. Not an official statement from Uganda.
r1-NKN-2025H2-019.vn: Category was unit_commander; this is an actor-presence/control item, recategorised with a control field. Radio Okapi's own description; not a statement by Uganda. The buffer zone's extent is not given.
src: Les affrontements ont eu lieu près de la zone tampon contrôlée par l’armée ougandaise, déployée depuis huit mois pour contenir l’avancée des rebelles vers Lubero-Centre.

r1-NKN-2026H1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that large AFC/M23 reinforcements had been reported since Sunday 15 March in the south-west of Lubero territory, where the rebels had occupied many villages for several months; that, according to its sources, vehicle shuttles carrying men and materiel had been observed for about two weeks at Mbingi and at Bunyatenge; and that security sources confirmed the arrival of the reinforcements and said it could be preparation for offensives against FARDC and Maï-Maï positions in the Kanyabayonga groupement.
r1-NKN-2026H1-001.l: Mbingi and Bunyatenge (Batangi chiefdom), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-001.n: Single outlet, anonymous 'sources'. Date is the Sunday named in the text (15 March 2026). Same page also reports AFC/M23 reinforcements at Kashebere and Kibati in Walikale (not claimed here).
r1-NKN-2026H1-001.vn: Original statement placed Mbingi/Bunyatenge inside the 15 March clause; the page ties those villages to the separate two-week shuttle observation by Actualite.cd's sources. Narrowed and split. excerpt_en flags are English weekday capitalisation only. Single outlet relying on unnamed sources. The page dates the reinforcements 'since 15 March' but says the vehicle shuttles at Mbingi and Bunyatenge had been seen for about two weeks; the two time frames are kept separate.
src: D’importants renforts de la rébellion de l’AFC/M23 ont été signalés depuis dimanche 15 mars dans la partie sud de la côte Est du Graben et dans le sud-ouest du territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu, où les rebelles occupent de nombreux villages depuis plusieurs mois.

Des sources sécuritaires confirment l’arrivée de ces renforts dans la région. Elles estiment qu’il pourrait s’agir de préparatifs en vue d’offensives contre les positions des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et des miliciens Maï-Maï dans le groupement de Kanyabayonga.

r1-NKN-2026H1-002.s: Anadolu Agency, relaying Radio Okapi citing security sources, reported that AFC/M23 rebels began moving out on Monday from several villages in Lubero territory that they had occupied for more than a year, and that after leaving Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese they were said to have set up camps in the Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga areas.
r1-NKN-2026H1-002.l: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga; Lubero territory
r1-NKN-2026H1-002.n: Date computed from weekday ('lundi') and the AA piece of Friday 27 March 2026 (Monday = 23 March). AA is a relay; original Radio Okapi item not opened. Wire credit: AA / Kigali / James Tasamba. Pairs with the Governor's statement claim. Compare with the 15 March reinforcement report (Actualite.cd): reinforcements at Mbingi/Bunyatenge were reported eight days earlier.
r1-NKN-2026H1-002.vn: Both passages on page (AA / Kigali / James Tasamba byline). Figure '23' is only the inferred date, not in the statement. Statement keeps the relay chain and the conditional. Date is inferred: AA's piece is dated 27 March 2026 (a Friday) and says 'lundi', taken as 23 March; approximate. AA relays Radio Okapi; the 'camps' clause is conditional ('auraient').
src: Les rebelles ont commencé à se déplacer lundi depuis plusieurs villages qu’ils occupaient depuis plus d’un an dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu, a indiqué Radio Okapi, citant des sources sécuritaires.
Après leur retrait de villes telles que Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi et Kipese, les rebelles auraient établi des camps dans les zones d’Alimbongo, Kirumba et Kanyabayonga.

r1-NKN-2026H1-003.s: Anadolu Agency reported that North Kivu Governor Evariste Kakule Somo told local media in Lubero on Thursday that he had observed an 'effective withdrawal' from several areas, called on the population to stay calm and said the rebel movement was part of 'the implementation of the peace agreements, notably those negotiated under US auspices'.
r1-NKN-2026H1-003.a: Government of the DRC (North Kivu provincial governor)
r1-NKN-2026H1-003.n: Date computed from 'Plus tôt jeudi' in a piece dated Friday 27 March 2026 (Thursday = 26 March). The same AA piece says no official communication from Kinshasa on M23's drone allegations at Mikenke (South Kivu; not claimed here). No AFC/M23 statement on the Lubero withdrawal found in this unit's searches.
r1-NKN-2026H1-003.vn: Passage verbatim on page; replacement extends the excerpt to include 'Plus tôt jeudi' so the weekday in the statement is carried. Official statement by the North Kivu provincial governor, known only through AA's relay of local media. 'Jeudi' in a piece dated Friday 27 March 2026 is taken as 26 March (approximate). The same AA piece reports no official Kinshasa communication on separate M23 drone allegations at Mikenke.
src: le gouverneur du Nord-Kivu, Evariste Kakule Somo, a déclaré à des médias locaux à Lubero qu’il avait constaté un « retrait effectif » de plusieurs zones, ce que plusieurs médias ont mentionné dans leur couverture. Il a appelé la population à rester calme, affirmant que le mouvement des rebelles s’inscrit dans le cadre de « la mise en œuvre des accords de paix, notamment ceux négociés sous l’égide des États-Unis ».

r1-NKN-2026H1-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that at least fourteen houses, a health centre and part of the Catholic church of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, south Lubero territory, were burned on Monday 26 January at around 20 heures (as printed) in an attack attributed to the ADF, and that two soldiers died during the army's counter-attack; Lubero territory administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa was quoted as saying that no civilian death had been recorded so far and that the village had been emptied of its population.
r1-NKN-2026H1-004.l: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-004.x: Radio Okapi: at least 14 houses, 1 health centre and part of the Catholic church burned; 2 soldiers killed; no civilian death recorded so far (administrator).
r1-NKN-2026H1-004.n: CONFLICT: Radio Okapi dates the attack to the evening of Monday 26 January; Actualite.cd (27 January) quotes the same administrator dating it from the night of 24 January and local 'forces vives' dating it to the night of Saturday 24 to Sunday 25 January and counting at least 25 civilians killed. Radio Okapi's 'no civilian killed' is the administrator's account only. Not reconciled here.
r1-NKN-2026H1-004.vn: Statement supported; corrected to add the administrator's verbatim quote (name was not in the stored excerpt) and to remove the Actualite.cd figure (25) from this claim's figures. Internal date/time inconsistency surfaced. CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS, kept separately: Radio Okapi (26 Jan) dates the attack to Monday 26 January about 20:00 and quotes the administrator as saying no civilian was killed; Actualite.cd (27 Jan) dates it to the night of 24-25 January and cites local 'forces vives' for at least 25 civilians killed. Radio Okapi's page is timestamped 26/01/2026 11:28, earlier than the 20:00 time it gives for an attack 'ce lundi', so the printed date may be wrong. Neither account is preferred here.
src: Au Nord-Kivu, au moins quatorze maisons, un centre de santé et une partie de l’église catholique de Musenge ont été incendiés ce lundi 26 janvier lors d’une attaque attribuée aux ADF. L’incident s’est produit aux alentours de 20 heures dans ce village de la chefferie de Baswagha, situé dans le sud du territoire de Lubero.
Selon l’administrateur, aucun civil n’a été tué, mais deux militaires ont perdu la vie lors de l’intervention visant à repousser les assaillants et à protéger les infrastructures restantes.

r1-NKN-2026H1-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the village of Musenge, Baswagha chiefdom, was attacked in the night of Saturday to Sunday 25 January 2026, in attacks it attributed to ADF fighters, and that according to local 'forces vives' at least 25 civilians were killed, 63 houses burned, two motorbikes burned and one person seriously wounded.
r1-NKN-2026H1-005.l: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-005.x: Actualite.cd, citing local forces vives: at least 25 civilians killed, 63 houses burned, 2 motorbikes burned, 1 seriously wounded.
r1-NKN-2026H1-005.n: CONFLICT with the Radio Okapi claim on the same village (date 26 vs 24/25 January; no civilian deaths per the administrator vs 25 per forces vives). Perpetrator attribution is made by the article's framing and by the administrator quoted in the next claim, not in this excerpt. Victims unnamed.
r1-NKN-2026H1-005.vn: Figures verbatim on page. Corrected to carry the page's own ADF attribution (it opens the article), to remove the Radio Okapi figures from this claim's figures, and to give the night as a date range. CONFLICTING ACCOUNTS, kept separately: Radio Okapi (26 Jan) quotes the Lubero administrator as saying no civilian was killed; this Actualite.cd account (27 Jan) cites local forces vives for at least 25 civilians killed. Actualite.cd's own headline says 'une dizaine de civils', which also differs from the 25 in its body text. Victims unnamed.
src: dans la nuit du samedi au dimanche 25 janvier 2026, le village de Musenge, dans la même chefferie de Baswagha, a également été attaqué. Selon les forces vives locales, au moins 25 civils ont été tués, 63 maisons incendiées, deux motos brûlées et une personne grièvement blessée.

r1-NKN-2026H1-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that Lubero territory administrator Colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain said that since the night of 24 January 2026 the ADF had carried out a deadly attack on Musenge village, burning almost the whole village, a health centre and a Catholic church, and that two soldiers were found burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-006.l: Musenge village, Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-006.a: ADF (as stated by the Lubero administrator)
r1-NKN-2026H1-006.x: Administrator: 2 soldiers found burned; toll 'provisional'. Health centre burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-006.n: Corroborates the Radio Okapi item that a Musenge health centre was burned. Same page reports that five health structures (Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, Masoya referral centre) closed in Mwenye groupement; that point is already held by r1-ATR-NK (actualite.cd 26 Jan). Counter-reporting: Radio Okapi (2026-01-26): Date: Radio Okapi says "ce lundi 26 janvier" (possibly publication day), others say the evening of Saturday 24 January. Also says the two soldiers died in the army counter-attack, not that they were found burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-006.vn: Excerpt verbatim; replacement extends it to the sentence naming the administrator and the 'provisional' toll. Name and figures now carried by the stored passage. Same administrator as in the Radio Okapi item (spelled 'Alain Kiwewa' there), here dating the attack from the night of 24 January; toll described as provisional. See the conflicting Musenge accounts. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Il a indiqué que depuis la nuit du 24 janvier 2026, les ADF ont mené une attaque meurtrière contre le village de Musenge, incendiant presque tout le village, un centre de santé ainsi qu’une église catholique. Deux militaires ont été retrouvés calcinés.
Le colonel Alain Kiwewa Mitela, administrateur du territoire de Lubero, dresse un bilan provisoire de 14 maisons incendiées, dont un centre de santé et une partie de l’église catholique de la place.

Ces informations sont confirmées par le colonel Alain Kiwewa, administrateur du territoire de Lubero: « Pour le moment, le prêtre de la paroisse s’est déplacé également avec certains chrétiens vers Butembo actuellement. Heureusement que nos forces de défense et de sécurité sont intervenues pour sauver une partie de l’église. Et pendant cette intervention, c’est là où deux militaires des forces de défense et de sécurité ont trouvé la mort sur le champ de bataille. Du côté civil, en tout cas, on n’a enregistré aucun mort jusque-là.

r1-NKN-2026H1-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the president of Bapere civil society Kakule Kagheni Samuel, six more bodies were found on Monday, bringing to 21 the number of civilian victims of the attack attributed to the ADF at Mambimbi-Isigo (Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector), carried out in the night of Friday 6 to Saturday 7 February 2026; several people remained missing.
r1-NKN-2026H1-007.l: Mambimbi-Isigo, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-007.x: Actualite.cd, civil society of Bapere: 21 civilians killed (initial provisional toll 15, with 7 houses burned); several missing. SOS Médias Burundi (same civil society source): 21 civilians killed.
r1-NKN-2026H1-007.n: SOS Médias Burundi (Goma dateline, 11 Feb) repeats the same civil-society figure and appears to relay local reporting; not independent of Actualite.cd. The same Actualite.cd page also reports displacement towards Njiapanda and unburied bodies. Distinct from the 1-2 January 2026 Lubero attack (15-16 dead per other outlets), which this unit did not open.
r1-NKN-2026H1-007.vn: All clauses verbatim. Replacement extends Actualite.cd's excerpt to the opening paragraph carrying the place, ADF attribution and 'missing'. Grade B on one credible non-partisan origin, not A. Both outlets rest on the same origin (Bapere civil society president); SOS Médias Burundi (Goma, 11 Feb) follows Actualite.cd's article point by point and is not independent. Victims unnamed.
src: Selon le président de la société civile de Bapere Kakule Kagheni Samuel qui donne l'information à ACTUALITE.CD, six nouveaux corps ont été découverts ce lundi, portant à vingt-et-un le nombre total de victimes civiles. Cette attaque avait été perpétrée dans la nuit du vendredi 6 au samedi 7 février 2026.
D’abord évalué à quinze morts, il est désormais passé à 21 civils tués, tandis que plusieurs habitants restent portés disparus, d’après la société civile locale.

r1-NKN-2026H1-008.s: Actualite.cd, in a passage saying that ADF violence had also intensified in neighbouring Beni territory, reported that six civilians were killed in an ambush at Malibo on the Oicha–Mamove road in the evening of 'mardi 4 février 2026' (as printed; that weekday and date do not match), a few hours after another ambush on the same stretch that killed four others, making at least ten civilians killed in a single day on that road, where several motorbikes were also burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-008.l: Malibo, Oicha-Mamove axis, Beni territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-008.a: ADF (per Actualite.cd's framing; the passage does not name the perpetrator of the ambushes themselves)
r1-NKN-2026H1-008.x: Actualite.cd: 6 civilians killed at Malibo; 4 killed in an earlier ambush on the same axis; at least 10 in one day; several motorbikes burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-008.n: DATE FLAG: 4 February 2026 was a Wednesday, but the source prints 'mardi 4 février'; the day may be 3 or 4 February. The article was published 10 February and the attack may be the one counted in the civil-society 3 February report already held (r1-ATR-NK-2026-011), which would make it a likely overlap. The excerpt does not name the perpetrator of this ambush.
r1-NKN-2026H1-008.vn: Figures verbatim. Corrected: the statement now carries the outlet's ADF framing as framing, keeps the weekday mismatch explicit with the printed French, and gives the date as a range. DATE DISCREPANCY: the source prints 'mardi 4 février 2026', but 4 February 2026 was not a Tuesday; the ambush may be 3 or 4 February. SOS Médias Burundi's 12 Feb piece also gives 4 February and at least six dead at Malibo, but follows Actualite.cd closely. Possible overlap with the civil-society report of 3 February. Victims unnamed.
src: Six civils ont été tués dans une embuscade survenue dans la soirée du mardi 4 février 2026 à Malibo, sur l’axe routier Oicha–Mamove. Cette attaque avait eu lieu quelques heures après une autre embuscade sur le même tronçon, ayant coûté la vie à quatre autres personnes. Au total, au moins dix civils ont été tués en une seule journée sur cet axe, où plusieurs motos ont également été incendiées.

r1-NKN-2026H1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Ntoyo health centre, Lubero territory, had reopened and resumed its activities five days earlier, six months after a deadly attack attributed to the ADF; that it had been forced to close after the attack of 8 September 2025, which local authorities said killed more than 100 civilians; that a large part of its medical equipment and medicines had been looted or destroyed in that incursion; and that consultations remained limited by shortages of medicines and equipment, which deputy head nurse Joseph Lungabo said complicated care for residents who had returned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-009.l: Ntoyo, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-009.x: Radio Okapi: attack of 8 September 2025 killed 'plus de 100' civilians according to local authorities; health centre closed ~6 months.
r1-NKN-2026H1-009.n: Reopening date computed from 'depuis cinq jours' in a piece published 17 March 2026 (about 12 March). The underlying September 2025 attack is outside this unit's period and is held by other rounds; this claim records the 2026 consequence (closure for ~6 months, looting of supplies, shortages).
r1-NKN-2026H1-009.vn: Corrected: removed 'March 2026' (no excerpt prints it) and the 'about five days before publication' gloss; added Bapere and the shortages clause from passages now stored. Reopening is dated only as 'five days' before the 17 March 2026 article (about mid-March 2026; month precision). The 8 September 2025 attack itself is outside this unit.
src: Six mois après une attaque meurtrière attribuée aux rebelles des ADF, le centre de santé de Ntoyo, situé dans le territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu, a rouvert ses portes.
Il avait été contraint de fermer après l’attaque du 8 septembre 2025, qui avait fait plus de 100 morts parmi les civils et entraîné l’incendie de nombreuses habitations, selon les autorités locales.
Lors de cette incursion, une grande partie des équipements médicaux et des médicaments avait été pillée ou détruite, laissant la structure dans un état critique.
« Cette situation complique la prise en charge, surtout pour les habitants qui sont déjà de retour dans la localité », explique Joseph Lungabo, infirmier responsable adjoint du centre de santé.

r1-NKN-2026H1-010.s: Amnesty International reported that it interviewed five women and two girls who were abducted by the ADF and forced into 'marriages', and that interviewees mentioned incidents of sexual violence by ADF fighters towards women and girls outside of 'marriage'.
r1-NKN-2026H1-010.l: ADF camps and affected areas, eastern DRC (report covers North Kivu and Ituri)
r1-NKN-2026H1-010.x: Amnesty International: 5 women and 2 girls interviewed who had been abducted by the ADF and forced into 'marriages'.
r1-NKN-2026H1-010.n: Report published 2026-05-05; incidents are not individually dated or located in this excerpt and may span 2025-2026 (the report also cites August and November 2025 attacks). Province/territory assigned from the report's North Kivu focus; location is approximate. Survivors unnamed in the report. Grade A proposed as a documented NGO investigation, verifier to decide.
r1-NKN-2026H1-010.vn: Verbatim on the English page (source language is en, not fr). Figures narrowed: removed the '6 of 7 pregnant' detail, which no stored excerpt carries. Documented NGO investigation (Amnesty says it researched in North Kivu in November 2025 and documented attacks in Ituri and North Kivu). The incidents are not dated or located individually; the report was published 5 May 2026. Survivors unnamed. Amnesty's own legal characterisations are not adopted here. 2026-10-29: source 0 language edited: QA 0.4 A3: the stored excerpt is English (Amnesty International English text) but the source was tagged fr
src: Amnesty International interviewed five women and two girls who were abducted by the ADF and forced into “marriages”. Witnesses said “extra-marital” relations were not allowed, however, several interviewees mentioned incidents of sexual violence by ADF fighters towards women and girls outside of “marriage”.

r1-NKN-2026H1-011.s: Amnesty International reported that the ADF has repeatedly attacked health facilities and raided supplies, and that in November 2025 a health centre in the village of Byambwe was targeted, with at least 17 civilians killed and four wards set on fire.
r1-NKN-2026H1-011.l: Byambwe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-011.x: Amnesty International: at least 17 civilians killed; four wards set on fire.
r1-NKN-2026H1-011.n: Byambwe's location in Lubero territory is not stated in this excerpt (Actualite.cd's Facebook page lists a Byambwe health centre in Lubero; not opened). Other rounds may already hold the November 2025 attack; this is the 2026 NGO documentation of it.
r1-NKN-2026H1-011.vn: Statement verbatim-supported. Corrected only the location (Lubero not printed by the page) and source language (en). The Amnesty page does not say which territory or province Byambwe is in; the Lubero placement in the draft came from elsewhere and is not supported here. The event (November 2025) falls outside this unit's period; this records the May 2026 NGO documentation. 2026-10-29: source 0 language edited: QA 0.4 A3: the stored excerpt is English (Amnesty International English text) but the source was tagged fr
src: The group has also repeatedly attacked health facilities and raided supplies. In November 2025, a health centre in the village of Byambwe was targeted. At least 17 civilians were killed, and four wards were set on fire.

r1-NKN-2026H1-012.s: Radio Moto Butembo (RMBB) reported that the flagrante-delicto hearing of the Butembo garrison military tribunal against four people, two of them Wazalendo, continued on Wednesday 24 June 2026 at the Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo; that the defendants were being prosecuted for criminal association, abduction and extortion; and that they were accused of having arrested Egyptian itinerant traders and 9 other Congolese citizens, including 6 girls, on Monday 22 June at Wayene and taking them, some tied up, to the Kafekit compound, where some were subjected to torture.
r1-NKN-2026H1-012.l: Wayene, Bulengera commune; Kafekit compound; trial at Kitulu roundabout, Mususa commune, Butembo
r1-NKN-2026H1-012.a: Wazalendo (two of the four defendants) and two civilians, as accused
r1-NKN-2026H1-012.x: Radio Moto: Egyptian traders (number not stated) and 9 other Congolese citizens, including 6 girls; 4 defendants.
r1-NKN-2026H1-012.n: Local outlet (RMBB, Butembo). Accusations are those of the prosecution as reported; victims are unnamed. Defendant names are spelled differently by Radio Elimu UOR ('NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika', 'KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël'); see the trial-outcome claim. The Egyptian nationals' company is named 'FUDA' by Radio Elimu.
r1-NKN-2026H1-012.vn: Corrected: 'charged ... for arresting' changed to prosecuted/accused as printed; added the defendants' names exactly as Radio Moto prints them (policy v1); removed Radio Elimu's '3 Egyptians' from this claim's figures. Defendant names are on the page but not in the stored excerpt, so the script refuses them in the statement; they are in the note and extra.entities_named; suggest add_excerpt for source 0 so they can be restored. Radio Moto names the defendants as Nzanzu Mushakulu Boika and Katembo Madisha Joel (both Wazalendo) and Kambale Kapupa Gédéon and Kasereka Mukama Jean-Baptiste (both civilians); the names sit on the page outside the stored excerpt (see replacement_quotes). Prosecution stage only on 24 June: accused and prosecuted, not convicted (see the Radio Elimu claim for the 25 June judgment). Defendants' names are spelled as Radio Moto prints them; Radio Elimu UOR spells two differently (NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika, KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël). Victims unnamed. Radio Moto does not give the number of Egyptians.
src: l’audience en flagrance contre 4 personnes, dont deux Wazalendo, s’est poursuivie ce mercredi 24 juin 2026 au rond-point Kitulu dans la commune de Mususa, en ville de Butembo. Les prévenus sont poursuivis pour association de malfaiteurs, enlèvement et extorsion de biens.

Ceux-ci sont accusés d’avoir arrêté des sujets égyptiens, commerçants ambulants et 9 autres citoyens congolais, dont 6 filles, chargés de marketing dans l’entreprise de ces Égyptiens. Ces faits ont eu lieu le lundi 22 juin lorsque ces Égyptiens et leurs collaborateurs ont été immobilisés à Wayene avant d’être amenés, les uns ligotés, dans la concession de Kafekit où certains ont été soumis à des tortures.

r1-NKN-2026H1-013.s: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that the Butembo garrison military tribunal sentenced to death on Thursday 25 June 2026 four defendants (named in the source and listed in entities_named), whom the prosecution had pursued, two of them as Wazalendo, for criminal association, abductions followed by torture, and extortion, in the case of the abduction of 3 Egyptians and 9 Congolese; the defence said it would appeal.
r1-NKN-2026H1-013.l: Vuhakatwa, Wayene quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo city
r1-NKN-2026H1-013.a: Wazalendo (two of four defendants) and two civilians, as convicted by the tribunal
r1-NKN-2026H1-013.x: Radio Elimu: 3 Egyptians and 9 Congolese abducted; 4 defendants sentenced to death.
r1-NKN-2026H1-013.n: Judicial outcome reported by a single Butembo radio (Radio Elimu UOR, Université Officielle du Ruwenzori).
