Spelling of two defendants' names differs from Radio Moto's 24 June report. The wider article states the defence will appeal; no statement from FARDC or Wazalendo leadership on the case was found.
r1-NKN-2026H1-013.vn: Corrected 'the defence was appealing' to the stated intent to appeal; the 22 June date and Vuhakatwa place are not in the stored excerpt, so they moved to the note and location; suggest add_excerpt for source 1 so they can return to the statement. Defendants as Radio Elimu prints them: NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika, KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël, KAMBALE KAPUPA Gédéon, KASEREKA MUKAMA Jean-Baptiste. Radio Elimu places the events on Monday 22 June 2026 at Vuhakatwa, Wayene quarter, Bulengera commune, Butembo (page passage in replacement_quotes, outside the stored excerpt). First-instance judgment of a military garrison tribunal; the defence 'promet d’interjeter appel' (has said it will appeal to the North Kivu Military Court), not an appeal already lodged. Names spelled as Radio Elimu prints them; Radio Moto spells two differently (Nzanzu Mushakulu Boika, Katembo Madisha Joel). The page does not say which two defendants were Wazalendo.
src: le Tribunal Militaire, garnison de Butembo, a condamné à la peine de mort 4 prévenus le jeudi 25 juin 2026. C’est le contenu du jugement rendu après l’instruction de l’affaire autour de l’enlèvement de 3 égyptiens et 9 congolais.

Le ministère public poursuivait quatre personnes deux wazalendo pour association des malfaiteurs, enlèvements suivi des tortures et extorsion. Les prévenus sont NZANZU MUSYAKULU Boika, KATEMBO MADIRISHA Joël, KAMBALE KAPUPA Gédéon et KASEREKA MUKAMA Jean-Baptiste.

r1-NKN-2026H1-014.s: Radio Moto Butembo reported that the World Food Programme launched a food distribution at Lubero-centre on Tuesday 26 May for displaced people and host families affected by the M23 advance in the south of the territory and by massacres attributed to alleged ADF, and that Lubero-centre had for months received displaced people from Kanyabayonga, Kirumba, Mathembe, Vutsorovya, Hutwe and Alimbongo.
r1-NKN-2026H1-014.x: Radio Moto: more than 10,000 households had already flowed to Kitsombiro, Kipese and Lubero-centre during the latest M23 advances (local authorities); WFP's 4th humanitarian shipment to the area since the M23 resurgence.
r1-NKN-2026H1-014.n: Local outlet (RMBB, Butembo). The year 2026 is inferred from the URL date path (2026/05/27) and the publication context; the excerpt gives only 'mardi 26 mai'. Residents also complain of exclusion from final distribution lists (not cited).
r1-NKN-2026H1-014.vn: Verbatim. Replacement extends source 1 to carry the 10,000-households figure; the '4th WFP shipment' detail is dropped from figures as no stored passage carries it. The year is not printed in the text; 2026 comes from the article's dated URL (2026/05/27), and 26 May 2026 was a Tuesday, consistent with 'mardi 26 mai'.
src: Le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM) a lancé ce mardi 26 mai une distribution de vivres à Lubero-centre, chef-lieu du territoire de Lubero, au profit des déplacés et des familles d’accueil. Un soulagement pour des milliers de bénéficiaires victimes à la fois de l’avancée du M23 au sud du territoire et des massacres attribués aux présumés ADF.

Lubero-Centre accueille depuis plusieurs mois de nouvelles vagues de déplacés venus de Kanyabayonga, Kirumba, Mathembe, Vutsorovya, Hutwe et Alimbongo, arrivés souvent sans rien après avoir fui les combats depuis plusieurs mois.

r1-NKN-2026H1-015.s: Grands Lacs News reported that between 1 and 4 January 2026, armed clashes broke out between Wazalendo factions in the Bashu chiefdom and north of Butembo city, pitting the group of self-proclaimed general Tango Fort against the Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL led by Baraka Lolwako, with a certain Fiston Nzoli reportedly involved, and that according to local sources several Tango Fort camps at Kitovo, Misugho and Rwamiso were burned.
r1-NKN-2026H1-015.l: Bashu chiefdom (Kitovo, Misugho, Rwamiso) and north of Butembo, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-015.a: Wazalendo factions: Tango Fort group vs Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL (Baraka Lolwako); Fiston Nzoli
r1-NKN-2026H1-015.n: Single outlet (Grands Lacs News, Fred Mastaki), partly citing anonymous local and security sources. Chiefdom of Bashu is in Beni territory. A reported death of an armed chief is not named. The article attributes the fighting to competition over mining and taxation, which is the outlet's interpretation.
r1-NKN-2026H1-015.vn: Verbatim; replacement extends the excerpt to carry the burned-camps clause. Single outlet relying partly on anonymous local and security sources. The page spells the camp both 'Rwamiso' and 'Lwamiso'. An unnamed armed chief's death is reported 'in this context'. The economic motive is the outlet's and its sources' interpretation. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Grands Lacs News (7 Jan 2026, Fred Mastaki) supports every clause; the burned-camps clause is in the sentence after the stored excerpt and is added. The same sentence also reports the death of an armed leader presented as a warlord.
src: Entre le 1 er et le 4 janvier 2026, des affrontements armés ont éclaté entre factions Wazalendo dans la chefferie des Bashu et au nord de la ville de Butembo. Les combats ont opposé le groupe du général autoproclamé Tango Fort aux Maï-maï Wazalendo RNL, dirigés par Baraka Lolwako, avec l’implication signalée d’un certain Fiston Nzoli.
Selon des sources locales, plusieurs camps de Tango Fort, notamment à Kitovo, Misugho et Rwamiso, ont été incendiés

r1-NKN-2026H1-016.s: Grands Lacs News reported that the Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord claimed the January 2026 operations against Tango Fort, saying it wanted to neutralise him and his supporters, accused of illegal detentions, torture, killings and arbitrary taxation, and that it welcomed the release of at least 11 illegally detained people, including minors, during the attack on the Lwamiso camp.
r1-NKN-2026H1-016.l: Lwamiso camp, Bashu chiefdom, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H1-016.a: Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord (claim); Tango Fort group (accused)
r1-NKN-2026H1-016.x: Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord: at least 11 illegally detained people released, including minors.
r1-NKN-2026H1-016.n: Party claim by a Wazalendo coalition about a rival faction; the outlet itself says the real stakes were economic. The detainees are unnamed. No statement from Tango Fort's group found.
r1-NKN-2026H1-016.vn: Verbatim; attribution to the party kept throughout. Partisan: a claim by a Wazalendo coalition about a rival faction, usable only as 'Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord says'. The accusations against Tango Fort and the release figure are the coalition's, not established. No statement from Tango Fort's group found.
src: La Synergie Wazalendo Front Grand Nord a revendiqué ces opérations, affirmant vouloir neutraliser Tango Fort et ses partisans, accusés de détentions illégales, tortures, assassinats et perception de taxes arbitraires. Elle a également salué la libération d’au moins 11 personnes détenues illégalement dont des mineurs lors de l’attaque du camp de Lwamiso.

r1-NKN-2026H2-001.s: Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reported, in a dispatch from Lubero, that three large agglomerations of Lubero territory (Kanyabayonga, Kayina and Kirumba) are occupied by M23 rebels supported by Rwanda.
r1-NKN-2026H2-001.l: Kanyabayonga, Kayina, Kirumba (Lubero territory), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-001.a: M23 rebels, described by ACP as supported by Rwanda
r1-NKN-2026H2-001.n: Incidental sentence at the end of an ACP (state news agency) dispatch about a health walk in Lubero-centre; Lubero-centre itself not described as M23-held. Frontline claim only for the three named places; consistent with the Radio Okapi/ACP pattern since June 2024. Speaker framing 'rebelles du M23 soutenus par le Rwanda' is ACP's own wording.
r1-NKN-2026H2-001.vn: Excerpt supports the attributed statement; state-media source on a contested fact, so partisan and C. ACP is Congolese state media; the occupation of the three places and Rwandan support are ACP's own wording, recorded as the DRC government side's account.
src: La cité de Lubero est réputée pour son hospitalité car devenue presque la base de tous les projets de développement exécutés dans cette entité dont trois grandes agglomérations (Kanyabayonga, Kayina et Kirumba) sont occupées par les rebelles du M23 soutenus par le Rwanda.

r1-NKN-2026H2-002.s: Bwiza reported that, in Lubero where the AFC/M23 permanent secretary was visiting development projects, he told residents of Kanyabayonga that they would not be abandoned and said: 'we are still here, we are going nowhere', rejecting social-media claims that the group would leave.
r1-NKN-2026H2-002.n: Partisan statement relayed by a Rwanda-focused outlet; page dated 19 July per search listing (page body gives no explicit date). Earlier part of the article places a speech in Lubero on 11 July; the Kanyabayonga remarks are not dated on the page. The speaker is named elsewhere in the article as Benjamin Mbonimpa but the excerpt does not tie the name to the title, so not listed. Responds to rumours (e.g. Congoforum/Afroinfos 19 July) of an M23 pull-back from Lubero towards Kanyabayonga that the page itself does not describe; those rumours were not opened.
r1-NKN-2026H2-002.vn: Removed 'Kigali-based' (not in the excerpt). Party statement, C. Party statement (AFC/M23) relayed by Bwiza (by Denis Nsengiyumva, dated 19 Nyakanga 2026); the Kanyabayonga remarks are not dated on the page. The page names the permanent secretary as Benjamin Mbonimpa ('Umunyabanga Uhoraho, Benjamin Mbonimpa'), outside the stored excerpt: extend the excerpt to add the name.
src: I Lubero, aho Umunyamabanga Uhoraho wa AFC/ M23 yasuraga ibikorwa by'iterambere biri gushyirwa mu bikorwa n'ihuriro, yaboneyeho kuganira n'abaturage ba Kanyabayonga abizeza ko batazabatererana. Ati: "Kuva imbuga nkoranyambaga zabeshya abaturage ko tuzagenda turi he? Turacyari hano, ntaho tuzajya, kandi nijeje abaturage ko tutari hano ngo tuzahave, ahubwo turi hano ngo dushimangire amahoro bafite

r1-NKN-2026H2-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that the local rights organisation Le Cri des victimes du Congo (CVC), in a statement on Sunday 19 July, expressed concern at a resurgence of armed attacks, killings of civilians and incursions attributed notably to ADF rebels in and around Beni city, and called for an independent investigation; Radio Okapi had not obtained a reaction from FARDC.
r1-NKN-2026H2-003.l: Beni city and surroundings, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-003.n: Statement by one local NGO; the article gives no casualty figures or dates for the incidents. Existing claims cover individual ADF attacks near Beni; this is the NGO's call plus a FARDC no-response note (party_statements: FARDC reaction not obtained by Radio Okapi as of 20 July).
r1-NKN-2026H2-003.vn: All clauses on the page; single local NGO statement via Radio Okapi. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-011: The excerpt attributes the attacks 'notamment' (notably, among others) to the ADF; the statement drops that qualifier and reads as if all were ADF. Restored it.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'attribuées notamment aux rebelles' is in source 0 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Jul 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts do not carry the call for an independent investigation, added here. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: Le Cri des victimes du Congo (CVC)
src: Le Cri des victimes du Congo (CVC), une organisation locale de défense des droits humains, a exprimé, dimanche 19 juillet, sa profonde préoccupation face à la recrudescence des attaques armées, des tueries de civils et des incursions attribuées notamment aux rebelles des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) dans la ville de Beni et ses environs, au Nord-Kivu.
Le coordonnateur du CVC, Espoir Sadiki Shemukobya, estime que les allégations évoquant d'éventuelles défaillances dans le système de sécurité doivent être examinées avec rigueur.

Jusqu'à ce lundi après-midi, Radio Okapi n'avait pas encore obtenu la réaction des responsables des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) dans la région de Beni au sujet des préoccupations soulevées par le CVC.
L'organisation demande ainsi l'ouverture immédiate d'une enquête indépendante sur les attaques et incursions armées enregistrées ces derniers jours dans la ville de Beni et ses alentours.

r1-NKN-2026H2-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that local civil society said on Tuesday 18 August that more than 2 400 people had been killed in two years in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, attributing the killings to the ADF.
r1-NKN-2026H2-004.l: Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-004.x: Local civil society (president Samuel Kaheni): more than 2 400 killed in two years in Bapere
r1-NKN-2026H2-004.n: Cumulative figure by one civil-society source covering roughly Aug 2024-Aug 2026, partly outside the window; not an independent count. Same source credits FARDC-UPDF joint operations and Wazalendo for a relative lull in recent months.
r1-NKN-2026H2-004.vn: Supported; attributed civil-society toll. Civil-society figure, not an independent count; the two-year period begins before the 1 January 2025 window. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Plus de 2 400 personnes ont été tuées en l'espace de deux ans dans le secteur de Bapere, situé dans le territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu. Ce bilan était dressé mardi 18 août par la société civile locale , qui pointe la responsabilité des rebelles des ADF (Forces démocratiques alliées).

Une accalmie fragile attribuée aux opérations FARDC-UPDF et aux Wazalendo La société civile note toutefois une accalmie relative au cours des derniers mois. Samuel Kaheni attribue cette légère amélioration aux opérations conjointes menées par les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et l'armée ougandaise (UPDF), ainsi qu'à l'engagement des combattants locaux Wazalendo.

r1-NKN-2026H2-005.s: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that Wazalendo/VDP and AFC/M23 fighters clashed at Vyanze, Lubero territory, on Wednesday 30 September 2026 from 4 am to about 10 am; according to concordant sources, Wazalendo temporarily dislodged M23 from the Kirivu hill position before advancing to the centre of Vyanze, then withdrew for lack of ammunition after M23 returned. No casualty figure was communicated.
r1-NKN-2026H2-005.l: Vyanze (Kirivu hill), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-005.n: Local radio (Butembo-Beni), unnamed concordant sources; no M23 or FARDC account found. Wazalendo origin villages named in the page: Mutondi, Ngolwe, Kitakandya, Kiribata.
r1-NKN-2026H2-005.vn: Supported clause by clause; single local radio with unnamed sources, so C rather than B. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie/Wazalendo (VDP) et les combattants du M23-AFC se sont affrontés ce mercredi 30 septembre 2026 à Vyanze, dans le territoire de Lubero. Les combats ont été lancés à 4 heures jusqu’aux environs 10 heures locales.

Des sources concordantes contactées par RADIOMOTO.NET l’après-midi indiquent que des éléments Wazalendo venus de Mutondi, Ngolwe, Kitakandya et Kiribata ont réussi à déloger temporairement et incendier la position de la partie adverse sur la colline Kirivu avant d’avancer au centre de Vyanze.
Cependant, les Wazalendo, faute de munitions, se sont repliés après le retour du M23, qui se sont réinstallés par la suite dans leurs campements.
Pas de bilan humain communiqué de part et d’autre pour l’instant.

r1-NKN-2026H2-006.s: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that fighting between Wazalendu and M23-AFC continued on Thursday 1 October 2026 in the groupements of Musundi and Hutwe (Batangi and Bamate chiefdoms, Lubero territory); sources said Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie had reportedly recovered Kandole and Kirivu, and that a large rebel reinforcement had reportedly come from Kitsombiro via Kasusa and Luvererya towards Vyanze.
r1-NKN-2026H2-006.l: Musundi and Hutwe groupements (Kandole, Kirivu, Vyanze), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-006.a: Wazalendu / Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie; M23-AFC
r1-NKN-2026H2-006.n: Single local radio source, claims of recapture attributed to unnamed sources; not independently confirmed. Continuation of the 30 September Vyanze fighting.
r1-NKN-2026H2-006.vn: Source uses the conditional ('auraient récupéré', 'serait venu'); restored the hedge. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie
src: Les combats entre les Wazalendu et les éléments du M23-AFC se sont poursuivis dans deux groupements du territoire de Lubero, notamment Musundi et Hutwe dans les chefferies des Batangi et Bamate en territoire de Lubero, ce jeudi 1ᵉʳ octobre 2026.

Elles signalent que les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie auraient récupéré Kandole, Kirivu en se rapprochant de Mutondi et qu’un important renfort rebelle serait venu de Kitsombiro passant par Kasusa, Luvererya en destination de Vyanze.

r1-NKN-2026H2-007.s: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that, according to sources contacted on the spot, residents moved towards Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa and Vungulo, and that more than a thousand households had already been recorded in these reception areas since Wednesday 30 September.
r1-NKN-2026H2-007.l: Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa, Vungulo (Lubero territory), North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-007.x: Radio Moto: more than a thousand households ('mille ménages') recorded in the reception areas since 30 September
r1-NKN-2026H2-007.n: Same page as the preceding claim; figure is from unnamed sources.
r1-NKN-2026H2-007.vn: The flagged '23' came from 'M23-AFC' in a clause about fighting that the excerpt does not carry; dropped that clause so the statement rests on the excerpt alone. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des sources contactées sur place font état de mouvements des habitants vers Kalimba, Kiribata, Vusesa ainsi que Vungulo. Plus de mille ménages répartis dans ces coins d’accueil sont déjà recensés depuis mercredi 30 septembre dernier.

src: Cinq présumés combattants du M23 se sont rendus aux Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie, Wazalendu, dans le territoire de Lubero au cours de la semaine. Ils ont été remis ce 1ᵉʳ octobre aux services de sécurité basés à Kasugho, à 45 km de Lubero-Centre, après avoir rejoint une position Wazalendo à Majengo-Musigha, au sud-ouest du territoire.

Munis de deux armes AK-47, ils disent avoir quitté leur position située dans la zone de Muhungama-Mitoto pour regagner le camp loyaliste, a fait savoir John Mahangaiko, porte-parole de la synergie des VDP Front Grand-Nord dans une déclaration publiée ce 1ᵉʳ octobre.

r1-NKN-2026H2-009.s: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that the five presumed M23 fighters who surrendered in Lubero territory said, in their testimony, that they were former soldiers captured and forcibly enrolled during the fall of Goma to the M23.

r1-NKN-2026H2-009.n: Allegation by surrendered fighters, relayed by the VDP spokesperson, no M23 response found; treat as unverified.

src: Le « kapita » Kombi Lwayivweka, âgé de 38 ans, a été arrêté par des présumés Wazalendu du groupe MDPC du général Kaganga, basés sur place. Il lui était reproché de n’avoir pas apporté des denrées alimentaires à ces combattants. Le « kapita » a été conduit dans le campement des Wazalendu, où il a été torturé et fouetté.
C’est ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 que Kombi Lwayivweka a été libéré, à la suite de l’intervention des autorités locales.
Selon nos sources, sa libération a été obtenue moyennant le paiement d’une somme de 50 dollars américains et d’une poule.
Kasenye se situe à une dizaine de kilomètres de Manguredjipa, dans le groupement Bapakombe, secteur de Bapere, en territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu.

src: Maître Muhindo Wasivinywa, coordonnateur du REDHO. @Kakule Kilumbiro/Novembre 2023 Les organisations de défense des droits de l’homme œuvrant en ville de Butembo réitèrent leur soutien au nouveau commandant de la Police Nationale Congolaise, PNC-ville. Elles lui demandent cependant de combattre les cas de violation de droits humains dont sont auteurs certains OPJ et commandants. Maître Muhindo Wasivinywa, coordonnateur du Réseau de droits de l’homme, REDHO, et responsable de la branche Droit de l’homme au sein de la société civile forces vives, coordination urbaine de Butembo, a, au cours d’une interview avec Radio Moto Butembo-Beni ce samedi 24 octobre 2026

Actuellement, il y a des cas d’incursions dans la ville, surtout dans les communes de Kimemi et Vulamba. Nous avons fait des monitorings, nous n’avons pas trouvé du sérieux dans le travail de la police face à l’ampleur des faits

src: Le Barreau des avocats du Nord-Kivu a déposé une plainte officielle ce mardi 20 octobre 2026 à l’Auditorat militaire supérieur du Nord-Kivu à Beni contre le commissaire supérieur Georges Ngonzila, commandant de la Police Nationale Congolaise en ville de Butembo.
Elle fait suite à des faits graves reprochés à l’officier : arrestations arbitraires, tortures, coups et blessures à l’encontre de leur confrère, Me Papy Wakilongo, le samedi 17 octobre 2026.
C’est le bâtonnier César Fazila Paluku qui a conduit la délégation d’avocats venue déposer la plainte.
Du côté de la hiérarchie de l’incriminé, on assure s’être saisi du dossier et l’on promet de se confier à la justice.

ent: Société Civile Forces Vives de Bulengera
src: Trois personnes blessées par balles et à la machette, plusieurs autres tabassées et ligotées. Plus de 1 400 dollars américains et plusieurs biens de valeur ont été emportés

Ce lourd bilan est livré par la société civile communale, qui parle d’une série d’incursions de bandits armés survenues dans la nuit du samedi 26 au dimanche 27 septembre, vers une heure du matin, dans le quartier Wayene, en commune de Bulengera.

Selon une déclaration de la Société Civile Forces Vives de Bulengera rendue publique ce lundi 28 septembre, les cellules Kyambya et Bulengera ont été la cible de ces hors-la-loi armés d’armes à feu et d’armes blanches, vêtus en tenue civile, qui ont opéré pendant plusieurs heures sans aucune intervention des forces de l’ordre.

« En cellule Kyambya, bloc Mughemero, Mumbere Tutemo Fabrice a été atteint par balle aux deux cuisses et à la main droite. Son épouse, Kavira Germaine, et son fils, Kakule Kitseme Musa, ont été sérieusement tabassés à la machette.

src: Dans un communiqué rendu public ce lundi, la SOCICO dénonce une « résistance violente » de la part d’un groupe de personnes contre les agents de santé.
Selon Célestin Thasihalia, coordonnateur urbain de la SOCICO Butembo, à l’arrivée de l’équipe sur terrain, deux membres ont été bloqués.
Un agent de l’équipe EDS a été grièvement blessé à la main et au genou par machette. Le véhicule de la riposte a également été caillassé.
Cet incident a entraîné l’interruption des activités de prélèvement SWAB ainsi que du service de sécurisation du corps testé positif.
Face à cette situation, la structure citoyenne lance d’abord un appel vibrant à la population du quartier Kyaghala et de la commune Bulengera à adhérer sans condition à la politique sanitaire.

src: Dans le territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu, le système de santé local peine à se relever de la guerre. Plus d'un an après les violents affrontements qui ont secoué la localité d'Alimbongo, les structures médicales portent encore les stigmates profonds des combats, a constaté mercredi 8 juillet le reporter de Radio Okapi.

Le visage actuel du centre de santé d’Alimbongo témoigne de la violence des bombardements passés : des toitures arrachées, des murs troués par des éclats d'obus et des décombres envahis par la végétation.
Le Bureau central de la zone de santé (BCZ) a lui aussi été lourdement touché par les frappes, obligeant l'administration sanitaire locale à se délocaliser vers des locaux de fortune.

r1-NKN-2026H2-020.l: Makumo, Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-NKN-2026H2-020.a: presumed ADF fighters under Abou Wakas; FARDC-Wazalendu coalition
r1-NKN-2026H2-020.n: Single local radio source, unnamed sources. The page adds that ADF settled at Magbutua since the previous weekend and that Kambau hosts displaced people from Bilulu, Nzibe, Kenge, Zangalo and other places without support (not recorded as a claim).
r1-NKN-2026H2-020.vn: Supported. 'No toll was available' is not in the excerpts but is a negative, not a figure; kept as the drafter read it. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des coups de feu ont été audibles à Makumo, un village minier situé dans le groupement Bapakombe, dans le secteur de Bapere, en territoire de Lubero (Nord-Kivu), dans la soirée de ce mardi 27 octobre 2026.

Des sources sur place indiquent que ce sont des combattants présumés ADF, sous la houlette de leur chef rebelle Abou Wakas, qui ont tenté d’attaquer ce village, mais ils ont été repoussés par la coalition FARDC-Wazalendu.

r1-NKN-2026H2-021.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a 'ville morte' (general stay-at-home strike) was observed on Tuesday 11 August in Butembo after a call by youth of citizen movements and pressure groups, who denounced insecurity and the desecration of the tomb of the artist Delcat Idinco and demanded the release of activist Clovis Mutsuva, detained in Beni; the page adds that the call was launched by youths claiming to be of LUCHA to denounce killings of civilians attributed to the ADF.
r1-NKN-2026H2-021.n: Context for Butembo civic reaction to ADF killings and a detention in Beni; the page says no law-enforcement intervention was reported by midday. No official account of Mutsuva's detention found in this unit.
r1-NKN-2026H2-021.vn: Supported by the outlet's report of an observed strike. That Clovis Mutsuva is held in Beni is not in the excerpts; his detention is the protesters' demand. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Une journée « ville morte » est observée ce mardi 11 août dans la ville commerciale de Butembo, à la suite de l’appel des jeunes des mouvements citoyens et groupes de pression. Ils dénoncent l’insécurité dans la région et la profanation de la tombe de l’artiste révolutionnaire Delcat Idinco.

Pour rappel, cet appel à la « ville morte » a été lancé par des jeunes se réclamant de la LUCHA pour dénoncer les tueries de civils attribuées aux ADF et exiger la libération de l’activiste Clovis Mutsuva.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-001.s: AFP reported, citing several UN and security sources, that M23 fighters and more than 3,500 Rwandan soldiers (according to the UN) entered Goma on Sunday, which they had been besieging for several days.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-001.a: M23 and Rwandan soldiers, as AFP describes them
r1-NKS-2025Q1-001.x: AFP: more than 3,500 Rwandan soldiers, according to the UN
r1-NKS-2025Q1-001.n: Weekday only ('dimanche'); date computed from weekday and publication date (published Monday 2025-01-27) = Sunday 2025-01-26. VOA Afrique republishes AFP ('VOA (avec AFP)'). M23 claimed to hold the city on 27 January; fighting continued that day per this page.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-001.vn: Excerpt exact; 3,500 printed as '3.500'. Page credits 'VOA (avec AFP)', so AFP is the origin. Sunday = 26 Jan from the 27 Jan dateline (lede: 'l'entrée dimanche soir').
src: Les combattants du M23 ("Mouvement du 23 mars") et plus de 3.500 soldats rwandais, selon l'ONU, ont pénétré dimanche dans Goma qu'ils assiégeaient depuis plusieurs jours, selon plusieurs sources onusiennes et sécuritaires.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-002.s: Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said on Monday in a statement posted on X that the government continued to work to avoid carnage and loss of life, as reported by AFP.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-002.n: Post on X relayed by AFP; original post not opened. Post date taken as article date (Monday 27 January 2025).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-002.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (brief rule); 'lundi' in the lede carries the day; page dateline 27 janvier 2025 (VOA avec AFP).
src: " Le gouvernement continue de travailler pour éviter le carnage et les pertes en vies humaines ", a assuré Patrick Muyaya dans une déclaration postée sur X.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-003.s: BBC News Afrique reported that the Minister of Rural Development, Muhindo Nzangi, said the DRC army controlled 80% of the city of Goma on Monday evening while M23 had taken only a few areas on the outskirts.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-003.x: BBC: army controlled 80% of Goma (government claim)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-003.n: Live page first published 24 Jan, updated 28 Jan 2025; 'lundi soir' computed as Monday 27 January. Government claim; contradicted by AFP/UN accounts of M23 entering Goma (see other claims). Not independently verified.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-003.vn: Exact on live page (published 24 Jan, updated 28 Jan 2025). Party claim, graded C. Government claim during the fall of Goma; contradicted by other accounts of M23 control.
src: Le ministre du développement rural, Muhindo Nzangi, a déclaré que l'armée de la RDC contrôlait 80 % de la ville de Goma lundi soir, tandis que le M23 ne s'était emparé que de quelques zones dans la périphérie de la ville.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-004.s: Congolese newspaper L'Avenir reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a live address on RTNC on Wednesday 29 January 2025, called on Congolese to show resistance and resilience in the face of an unprecedented worsening of the security situation in the east, which it said he attributed to Rwandan defence forces supporting the M23.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-004.n: Pro-government daily; the attribution to Rwanda is the paper's reading of the speech ('Félix Tshisekedi attribue'); speech text itself not opened. Page date taken from search result (30 Jan 2025). Page is a very large (700k chars) archive listing; excerpt checker must locate by text.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-004.vn: Both excerpts found on the (very large) archive page; statement keeps the paper's attribution. Pro-government daily's account of the speech; speech text not consulted.
src: Au cours d’un discours à la nation en direct sur la chaine de télévision nationale, RTNC, mercredi 29 janvier2025, le Chef de l’Etat Felix-Antoine Tshisekedi a invité les Congolais à faire preuve de résistance et surtout de résilience face à l’aggravation sans précédent de la situation sécuritaire dans l’Est du pays.
Une situation que Félix Tshisekedi attribue aux forces de défense du Rwanda qui, en soutien à leurs marionnettes du M23, continuent leur entreprise terroriste sur notre territoire

r1-NKS-2025Q1-005.s: DW reported that the military governor of North Kivu, général major Peter Cirimwami, was shot during a field visit on Thursday, and that different sources disagreed on whether he was dead or alive; Jeune Afrique reported that the army spokesperson confirmed his death on 24 January.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-005.l: North Kivu (place not stated in these excerpts; Kasengezi per M23 and Sake per Rwanda in other claims)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-005.a: Peter Cirimwami (military governor of North Kivu, FARDC); attacker not stated in these excerpts
r1-NKS-2025Q1-005.n: Two independent outlets. Jeune Afrique is paywalled after the lede; excerpt is from the visible lede. DW says field visit 'ce jeudi' (23 Jan 2025 per DW's own dateline '23.01.2025'). Name 'Peter Cirimwami' printed in the DW excerpt only. Place of the shooting is given by M23 (Kasengezi) and by Rwanda (around Sake) in other claims; not stated in these excerpts.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-005.vn: Both pages support their clauses. Graded B, not A: each fact (shooting; death confirmation) rests on one outlet; the two do not corroborate the same fact. DW's 'jeudi (23.01.2025)' is for the Sake fighting, so 'Thursday' = 23 Jan is inferred.
src: Le gouverneur militaire du Nord-Kivu, général major Peter Cirimwami a été atteint par balle lors d'une descente sur le terrain ce jeudi. Différentes sources s'affrontaient sur son état réel, mort ou encore vivant.
En fin d’après-midi, le 24 janvier, le porte-parole de l’armée congolaise a finalement confirmé le décès du gouverneur militaire

r1-NKS-2025Q1-006.s: DW reported that, according to the M23, military governor Peter Cirimwami had been seriously wounded at Kasengezi while on his way to the front line, which DW said was difficult to verify; DW added that the Congolese government had still not communicated on the matter.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-006.n: 'celui-ci' refers to the governor Peter Cirimwami (preceding sentence). Account of M23 as relayed by DW; later contradicted/superseded by the army's confirmation of death (see previous claim).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-006.vn: Exact; 'celui-ci' refers to Peter Cirimwami in the preceding sentence. M23 account kept attributed and conditional ('aurait').
src: Selon le M23, celui-ci aurait été grièvement blessé à Kasengezi alors qu'il se rendait sur la ligne de front. Une information qu'il était difficile à vérifier. Le gouvernement congolais n'avait en tout cas toujours pas communiqué sur cette situation.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-007.s: The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement dated 26 January 2025 that the recent heavy fighting around Goma was triggered by constant ceasefire violations by the FARDC in coalition with the FDLR, European mercenaries, Wazalendo, Burundian armed forces, SAMIDRC forces and MONUSCO troops.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-007.n: Partisan: cited only for what Rwanda said. The statement does not mention Rwandan troops in Goma; Rwanda's account of its own role is not in this excerpt.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-007.vn: Primary source on the ministry site; dateline prints 26 January 2025. Graded C under the partisan-source rule (the statement's existence is primary-sourced). Party statement: records what Rwanda said, not that it is true.
src: The ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, particularly the recent heavy fighting around Goma, was triggered by constant violations of the ceasefire by the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) in coalition with UN-sanctioned genocidal militia FDLR, European mercenaries, ethnic militias (Wazalendo), Burundian armed forces, SAMIDRC forces as well as MONUSCO troops.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-008.s: The Rwandan foreign ministry said in a statement that the late Maj Gen Peter Cirimwami, Military Governor of North Kivu, who it said was killed during fighting around Sake, served as liaison with the FDLR, citing UN reports.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-008.n: Partisan Rwandan characterisation; the UN report referenced is not identified in the excerpt and was not checked here. Jeune Afrique's lede also says he was 'réputé proche des FDLR' (reputation, unsourced in lede).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-008.vn: Exact, partisan, attributed. Rwandan characterisation; the UN reports it cites are not identified.
src: The United Nations confirmed in their reports that the late Maj Gen Peter Cirimwami, the Military Governor of North Kivu who was killed during fighting around Sake, served as liaison with the FDLR and was responsible for sabotaging planned operations by the FARDC to neutralize the leaders of the FDLR.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-009.s: Rwanda's foreign ministry said on 2 February 2025 that it rejected the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force made in the statement of the SADC extraordinary summit of 31 January 2025, and said the RDF does not attack civilians.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-009.l: Goma, North Kivu (context: SADC summit statement)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-009.n: Partisan: cited only for what Rwanda said. Excerpt is a single contiguous passage; check word count.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-009.vn: Exact primary statement; C under partisan-source rule.
src: Kigali, 2 February 2025 - Rwanda rejects the accusations against the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) made in the statement of the Extraordinary Summit of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) held on 31 January 2025. The RDF defends Rwanda's borders from threats and protects civilians, it does not attack civilians.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-010.s: UN News (Swahili) reported that Mr Lacroix, speaking to journalists, confirmed the deaths of three MONUSCO peacekeepers (one from Uruguay, two from South Africa) and wished a quick recovery to 12 other peacekeepers wounded during clashes with M23 rebels.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-010.a: M23 (as described by the source: 'waasi wa M23')
r1-NKS-2025Q1-010.x: UN News: 3 MONUSCO peacekeepers killed, 12 wounded (as of 27 January 2025)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-010.n: Context event (MONUSCO). Figures as of 27 January 2025 briefing; later totals may differ. Excerpt is 50-60 words; translation provided.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-010.vn: The page names him in full as Jean-Pierre Lacroix, head of UN peacekeeping operations (replacement quote), but the stored excerpt prints only 'Bwana Lacroix'; extend the excerpt to name him in full. 'watatu' = three. Narrowed 'said 12 were wounded' to the source's wording (wished recovery to 12 wounded). The page links the wounding, not explicitly the three deaths, to clashes with M23.
src: Bwana Lacroix ametumia kikao hicho kuthibitisha vifo vya walinda amani watatu wa MONUSCO; mmoja kutoka Uruguay na wawili kutoka Afrika Kusini. Ametuma salamu za rambirambi kwa serikali za Uruguay na Afrika Kusini pamoja na familia za walinda amani hao waliouawa huku akitakia ahueni ya haraka walinda amani wengine 12 waliojeruhiwa wakati wa makabiliano na waasi wa M23.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-011.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that at least 19 soldiers from South Africa, Malawi and Tanzania were killed when the M23 took the city of Goma in January.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-011.a: M23 (as the capture's actor per the source)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-011.x: BBC Gahuza: at least 19 soldiers from South Africa, Malawi and Tanzania killed
r1-NKS-2025Q1-011.n: Publication date taken from search result (2025-03-29, approximate); verify. The page also lists a SADC-M23 meeting attended by Sultani Makenga; names not cited here. SAMIDRC are SADC troops (context).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-011.vn: Exact; publication date 29 March 2025 confirmed on page. Mubambiro appears on the page only as a location of SADC bases, not of the deaths.
src: Abasirikare nibura 19 bo muri Afurika y'Epfo, Malawi na Tanzania barishwe ubwo M23 yafataga umujyi wa Goma, umurwa mukuru w'intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru, muri Mutarama (1) uyu mwaka.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-012.s: Studio Hirondelle reported that Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a briefing in Kinshasa on 3 February, speaking of the massacre and carnage committed in Goma, said that his colleague the Health Minister had been told by his services that morning that there were more than 2,000 bodies to bury.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-012.x: Muyaya (3 Feb): more than 2,000 bodies to bury
r1-NKS-2025Q1-012.n: The page also prints provisional figures of nearly 3,000 dead and about 2,880 wounded (not attributed in that sentence; not recorded here). Excerpt begins mid-quotation. Figures conflict with BBC English (at least 700 killed per UN and government) - see next claims.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-012.vn: Clarified who was informed (the Health Minister, by his services), per the full quotation. Page ends 'Studio Hirondelle RDC, avec AFP' - credited accordingly. Removed year (not printed in the passage).
src: du massacre et du carnage qui a été commis à Goma, ce matin ses services lui ont renseigné qu’il y a plus de 2 000 corps à enterrer », a déclaré Patrick Muyaya, ministre de la Communication et des Médias, porte-parole du gouvernement, au cours d’un briefing le 3 février à Kinshasa.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-013.s: BBC News Afrique reported that the UN said at least 2,900 people were killed in the fighting, that 2,000 bodies had been buried and that 900 others were still in the city's morgues.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-013.a: Fighting between M23 and FARDC and allies, as described by the source
r1-NKS-2025Q1-013.x: BBC Afrique citing UN: at least 2,900 killed; 2,000 buried; 900 in morgues
r1-NKS-2025Q1-013.n: Conflicts with the BBC English figure (700 killed per UN and government) and with the Rwandan government's later characterisation of '3,000 casualties' as exaggerated (not collected here). Unclear whether the 2,900 figure includes combatants.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-013.vn: Exact ('2 900' with a space). Figures conflict across sources (BBC English: at least 700; Muyaya: more than 2,000 bodies); unclear whether combatants are included.
src: L'ONU affirme qu'au moins 2 900 personnes ont été tuées au cours des combats, que 2 000 corps ont été enterrés et que 900 autres se trouvent encore dans les morgues de la ville.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-014.s: BBC News reported that at least 700 people in Goma were killed and close to 3,000 injured as the rebels clashed with the DR Congo army and its allies, according to the UN and the Congolese government.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-014.a: Fighting between M23 and the DRC army and allies, as described by the source
r1-NKS-2025Q1-014.x: BBC: at least 700 killed and close to 3,000 injured (UN and Congolese government)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-014.n: Published date from search result (3 Feb 2025). Figure is lower than the BBC Afrique / Muyaya figures: report all three.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-014.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (brief rule; page date 3 February 2025 shown with the source). Lower than other contemporaneous figures (2,900 per UN in BBC Afrique of 6 Feb).
src: At least 700 people in the city were killed and close to 3,000 injured as the rebels clashed with DR Congo's army and its allies, according to the UN and the Congolese government.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.s: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to an internal UN document it consulted, between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male detainees during the escape from Munzenze prison in Goma, and that most of the women were killed after detainees set fire to the prison; the BBC said it could not verify the information.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.l: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.a: male detainees per an internal UN document, as reported by BBC
r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.x: BBC (internal UN document): 165 to 167 women assaulted
r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.n: BBC (published Thursday 6 Feb 2025) says the escape was 'lundi dernier'; this is either Monday 27 January or Monday 3 February, so the date is given as a range (AFP of 27 Jan reported the prison 'totalement incendiée' after a mass escape, which points to 27 Jan; verify). Survivors are not named by the source. Headline attributes the figures to the UN; body says an internal UN document seen by the BBC.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-015.vn: All clauses on page; caveat kept. BBC could not verify the UN document. 'Lundi dernier' plus 'after M23 began to seize the city' points to 27 January, but the range is kept.
src: Selon un document interne de l'ONU consulté par la BBC, entre 165 et 167 femmes ont été agressées par des détenus masculins lors de l'évasion. Le rapport précise que la plupart des femmes ont été tuées après que les détenus ont mis le feu à la prison.
La BBC n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.s: Belga, in La Libre, reported that a local official told the German news agency DPA that at least 160 female detainees were raped during an escape from the Goma prison; Belga added that it was not yet known whether the rapists were escaped prisoners, M23 rebels or members of other local militias.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.l: Munzenze central prison, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.a: not established: escaped prisoners, M23 or other local militias (source says unknown)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.x: Belga/La Libre (local official to DPA): at least 160 female detainees raped
r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.n: Wire/relay: page carries a Belga credit and says the BBC saw the UN document and DPA quoted a local official (originating sources DPA and BBC). Restricted to single-origin. The page calls M23 a 'milice'.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-016.vn: The 'not yet known' sentence is the agency's own narration, not the official's; reworded so it is not attributed to the official. Origin of source 1 set to Belga (not BBC). Anonymous local official via DPA: C.
src: Au moins 160 détenues ont été violées lors d'une évasion de la prison de Goma, en RDC, a rapporté un fonctionnaire local à l'agence de presse allemande DPA.
On ne sait pas encore si les violeurs étaient des prisonniers évadés, des rebelles de la milice M23 ou des membres d'autres milices locales.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-017.s: UN News reported that the destruction of prisons caused by the offensive led to the escape of many prisoners from the central prisons of Goma and Bukavu, and also in Kabare in South Kivu; Patrice Vahard, director of the BCNUDH, said in an interview with UN News on Wednesday evening that escapees may include people imprisoned for atrocities, notably rape and gender-based violence.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-017.l: Goma (city), North Kivu; Bukavu and Kabare, South Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-017.a: M23 offensive (as described by the source)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-017.n: Interview on the Wednesday before 20 Feb (Wed 19 Feb); date computed from weekday and publication date. Covers both provinces; Bukavu/Kabare belong to South Kivu units.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-017.vn: Misattribution fixed: the prison-destruction sentence is UN News narration, not Vahard's words; Vahard's quote is the escapee risk. The escapes themselves date from late January (Goma) and mid-February (Bukavu); 2025-02-19 is the interview date.
src: les destructions de prisons causées par l’offensive ont conduit à l'évasion de nombreux prisonnier des établissements pénitentiaires centraux dans les deux métropoles, mais également dans la ville de Kabare, au Sud-Kivu.
a déclaré mercredi soir le Directeur du Bureau conjoint des Nations Unies aux droits de l’Homme (BCNUDH), Patrice Vahard, dans un entretien accordé à ONU Info

r1-NKS-2025Q1-018.s: MSF's emergency coordinator in Goma said that on Wednesday 29 January, the first day the fighting had eased, the team received nearly 140 wounded at the hospital triage, many of whom were hospitalised, and that wounded people who had stayed at home had been unable to access care until then.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-018.a: fighting in Goma (M23, Congolese army and respective allies, per MSF)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-018.x: MSF: nearly 140 wounded at triage on 29 January
r1-NKS-2025Q1-018.n: Interview-style statement of MSF's emergency coordinator (MSF is named in the page title, not in the excerpt; 'we' in the excerpt is MSF per the page). Hospital is Kyeshero (stated in the page's preceding text, not in this excerpt).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-018.vn: All on page; hospital is Kyeshero per page context ('MSF teams were working in Kyeshero hospital').
src: In one day alone, Wednesday, 29 January, we received nearly 140 wounded at the hospital triage, many of whom were hospitalised. This was the first day that the fighting had eased. This allowed the wounded, who had stayed at home and could not access care, to go to a hospital.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-019.s: The Guardian reported that Chadrack Kabumba, 20, was treated at Virunga hospital for bullet wounds to his knee and shoulders after being shot four times on his way to check whether his property had been vandalised, the day after M23 entered Goma.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-019.n: 'The day after M23 entered Goma' - date computed from the Guardian's own framing (entry 26/27 Jan per other sources) so approximate. Named victim aged 20 (adult).
r1-NKS-2025Q1-019.vn: Date corrected from 28 to 27 January: the same Guardian page says M23 entered the city on 26 January, so 'the day after' = 27 January (approximate). The page also names another patient, Mamy Esther, 40 (pelvic injury in a bombing; lost her six-year-old son) - not part of this claim; lead for victim names. Shooter not identified by the source. Date approximate.
src: At Virunga hospital, Chadrack Kabumba, 20, nursed bullet wounds to his knee and shoulders after he was shot four times on his way to check if his property had been vandalised, the day after M23 entered Goma.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-020.s: Amnesty International said on 18 March 2025 that armed M23 fighters stormed the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March and abducted more than 130 people, including Congolese soldiers (some wounded) and health workers, who were taken to a stadium where some were tortured. Amnesty also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga had said in an interview that Congolese army members in the hospitals were posing as patients or carers, that M23 had found 14 weapons in hospitals and that hospital staff had alerted them, and that M23 had arrested those who were not part of the hospital.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-020.l: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-020.x: Amnesty: more than 130 people abducted; (OHCHR/Reuters/AP figure of 'at least 130 sick and wounded men' seen in search results, pages not retrievable)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-020.n: Amnesty's own research (25 interviews). OHCHR press release of 3 March and Reuters/AP exist (search results) but their pages could not be retrieved by the page helper, so they are not cited; the UN figure is 'at least 130 sick and wounded men'. Check for an independent second origin (OHCHR) in the verification round. health category: patients_removed / health_worker_harmed.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-020.vn: Amnesty documented research (25 interviews stated on page): A. More specific than existing r1-HC-2025-004 (same page), not a duplicate. OHCHR second origin not retrieved. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Makenga's justification 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Attribution is right, but Amnesty's own page carries M23's justification (Makenga), which the claim leaves out (check 8). The Group of Experts later reports witnesses saying no weapons were found (r1-GOE-055), so the two accounts should sit side by side.; excerpt-support: added Amnesty's passage on Sultani Makenga's interview as an excerpt
src: Dans la nuit du 28 février et dans la matinée du 3 mars, des combattants armés du M23 ont fait irruption dans les hôpitaux Heal Africa et CBCA Ndosho à Goma, où ils ont enlevé plus de 130 personnes. Parmi elles se trouvaient des soldats de l’armée congolaise, dont certains avaient été blessés, ainsi que des soignants.
Tous ont été emmenés dans un stade de la ville, où certains ont été torturés.

Sultani Makenga, le chef militaire du M23, a récemment déclaré dans une interview que les membres de l’armée congolaise présents dans les hôpitaux se faisaient passer pour des patients ou des soignants. Il a ajouté que le M23 avait trouvé 14 armes dans des hôpitaux et que le personnel hospitalier les avait alertés de la situation. Il a conclu que le M23 avait arrêté ceux qui ne faisaient pas partie de l’hôpital.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-021.s: Actualite.cd, relaying Amnesty International, reported that armed M23 fighters burst into the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals in Goma on the night of 28 February and the morning of 3 March, abducting more than 130 people including wounded Congolese soldiers and health workers who, according to Amnesty, were taken by force to a stadium where some were tortured. Actualite.cd also reported that M23 military chief Sultani Makenga said some of the abducted soldiers had posed as patients or carers, that his group had found 14 weapons in the hospitals, and justified the abductions by saying medical staff had reported the presence of Congolese soldiers.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-021.l: Heal Africa hospital and CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma (city), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-021.n: Relay of the Amnesty release (not independent); health-care angle of the same event as the preceding claim. 'a dénoncé Amnesty International mardi' = Tuesday 18 March.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-021.vn: Stadium/torture clause is on the page but not in the stored excerpt; supplied as replacement quote. Not independent of r1-HC-2025-004 (same Amnesty origin). The same page carries Makenga's justification, which the claim omits (check 8). src: Des combattants armés du M23 ont fait irruption dans les hôpitaux Heal Africa et CBCA Ndosho à Goma dans la nuit du 28 février et la matinée du 3 mars, enlevant plus de 130 personnes, dont des militaires congolais blessés et des soignants, a dénoncé Amnesty International mardi.
Selon l’organisation, ces personnes ont été emmenées de force dans un stade de la ville où certaines ont été torturées.

Le chef militaire du M23, Sultani Makenga, a affirmé que certains des militaires enlevés s’étaient fait passer pour des patients ou des soignants et a déclaré que son groupe avait découvert 14 armes dans ces hôpitaux. Il a justifié ces enlèvements en affirmant que des membres du personnel médical avaient signalé la présence de militaires congolais.

M23 fighters raided CBCA Ndosho Hospital and Heal Africa Hospital during the night of Feb. 28, taking 116 and 15 patients respectively, U.N. Human Rights Office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said in a statement.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.s: Amnesty International said humanitarian organisations had reported a sharp rise in rape and sexual violence in North Kivu and South Kivu, and that victims told it they were raped by M23 fighters and threatened with death; in one account, a woman said M23 fighters suspected her of being a spy and five armed fighters in military uniforms raped her collectively; in another case, two men in Congolese military uniform raped a pregnant woman and abducted her husband.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (places of individual cases not stated in the excerpts)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.a: M23 fighters; two men in Congolese military uniform (per Amnesty)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.x: Amnesty: individual cases (one gang rape by five fighters; one rape of a pregnant woman by two men)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.n: Report date 2025-03-18; incident dates and places not given. Survivors are unnamed in the source. Amnesty's line 'Le M23 et l'armée congolaise... doivent répondre de ces viols' appears on the page. The preceding sentence of the page places the humanitarian reporting of rises in North Kivu and South Kivu.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-023.vn: The draft placed the victims' accounts 'in North Kivu and South Kivu'; the page gives the two provinces only for the humanitarian reports of a rise, so the geography is now attributed to that sentence. B (testimonies without place/date) rather than A. Places and dates of the individual incidents are not given; survivors unnamed. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Des victimes ont raconté à Amnesty International qu’elles ont été violées par des combattants du M23 et menacées de mort.

Cinq combattants, portant des uniformes militaires et équipés d’armes, l’ont violée collectivement. Dans un autre cas, deux hommes en uniforme militaire congolais ont violé une femme enceinte et enlevé son mari.

Conflict-related sexual violence in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo has escalated, while support to survivors has significantly dropped. The Rwanda-backed M23 and other armed groups and military forces are using sexual violence as a weapon of war

r1-NKS-2025Q1-024.s: UN News reported that UNFPA's country representative Mady Biaye said that the 895 rape cases reported by UNHCR for the first half of February concerned only survivors who received medical care at the 23 UNFPA-supported sites in Goma.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-024.x: UNHCR (via UN News): 895 rape cases in the first fortnight of February; per Biaye, only survivors treated at 23 UNFPA-supported sites in Goma; UN News headline: nearly 900 rapes in two weeks, average 60 per day
r1-NKS-2025Q1-024.n: Original data from UNHCR (announced Monday 3 March per the page) and UNFPA. UN News translation-neutral; no perpetrators attributed in these passages; counts are of survivors reaching care and are a floor. Excerpt 1 is 57 words. Survivors unnamed.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-024.vn: Name 'Mady' and 'first half of February' are on the page (supplied). Graded B: UN-reported data in a news interview, not a documented UN investigation. Counts are of survivors reaching care at supported sites; a floor, not a total. No perpetrator attributed.
src: les 895 cas de viol rapportés en début de semaine par le HCR. Et M. Biaye de préciser que les cas en question concernent uniquement les survivantes ayant bénéficié de soins médicaux dans les 23 sites soutenus par l’UNFPA à Goma, la principale ville du Nord-Kivu tombée, fin janvier, sous le contrôle du M23.
Près de 900 viols dans l’est de la RDC en l’espace de deux semaines - soit une moyenne de 60 par jour.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-025.s: UN News reported looting of contraceptives, damaged health centres and depleted aid stocks as sexual violence proliferated in eastern DRC, with tens of thousands of women and girls struggling to access emergency care; UNFPA's DRC representative Mady Biaye said UNFPA health infrastructure in Goma had been damaged by the fighting and its Goma warehouse looted (no perpetrator named). The article set the US decision in January to suspend almost all foreign aid programmes for three months against these difficulties; Biaye said the US had been due to contribute 10 million dollars in 2025 for contraceptives in the DRC, 'Mais tout ça c'est arrêté', and the article notes that contraceptive stock-outs were already being felt.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-025.l: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu; places not itemised in the excerpt)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-025.x: UN News: tens of thousands of women and girls struggling to access emergency care
r1-NKS-2025Q1-025.n: Standfirst of the article; geography is 'eastern DRC'; the text identifies Goma-based sites later. Dates of the looting are not given. Consider the UNFPA claim as the basis; look for the underlying UNFPA/OCHA report for place and date.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-025.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (brief rule). The 'meant' causal link is the standfirst's juxtaposition; kept as UN News framing. Standfirst-level summary; places and dates of looting not given. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Mady Biaye, UNFPA DRC representative 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Goma infrastructure damaged; warehouse looted 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: US aid suspension; contraceptive funding stopped 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: contraceptive stock-outs 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-027: The standfirst juxtaposes looting/damage and the access problem; the retained page (UN News, 8 March 2025) gives the concrete basis: UNFPA representative Mady Biaye said UNFPA health infrastructure in Goma was damaged by fighting and its Goma warehouse 'littéralement pillé' (no perpetrator named), and links contraceptive stock-outs in part to the US aid suspension.
