src: Pillages de contraceptifs, centres de santé endommagés et rupture des stocks d’aide.
des dizaines de milliers de femmes et filles peinent à accéder aux soins d’urgence dont elles ont désespérément besoin.
précise Mady Biaye, le principal représentant en RDC de l’agence des Nations Unies pour la santé sexuelle et reproductive ( UNFPA )

M. Biaye indique que les infrastructures sanitaires de l’UNFPA dans la métropole du Nord-Kivu ont été endommagées par les combats, sans parler des stocks de produits de l’agence, qui ont complètement disparu. « Notre entrepôt, dans un seul endroit, à Goma, a été littéralement pillé », déplore-t-il.

C’est à l’aune de ces difficultés qu’il faut analyser l’impact de la décision des Etats-Unis, en janvier dernier, de suspendre presque tous les programmes d’aide étrangère du pays pour une durée de trois mois. Selon M. Biaye, l'administration américaine devait initialement contribuer à hauteur de 10 millions de dollars en 2025 pour l’achat de contraceptifs en RDC. « Mais tout ça c'est arrêté », constate le représentant de l’UNFPA.
Alors que des ruptures de stocks de contraceptifs se font déjà sentir

r1-NKS-2025Q1-026.s: Studio Hirondelle reported that on 3 February 2025 the rebels unilaterally declared a ceasefire 'because of the humanitarian crisis caused by the Kinshasa regime', to take effect on 4 February, and said in a communiqué circulated notably on X that they had 'no intention of taking control of Bukavu or other localities'.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-026.n: Communiqué relayed by the outlet; original post on X not opened. The same page reports fighting resumed in South Kivu on 5 February (Nyabibwe) - South Kivu unit.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-026.vn: Exact; page credited 'Studio Hirondelle RDC, avec AFP'. 'Les rebelles' = AFC/M23 in page context. Fighting resumed in South Kivu on 5 February per the same page.
src: Le 3 février, les rebelles ont décrété unilatéralement un cessez-le-feu « en raison de la crise humanitaire provoquée par le régime de Kinshasa » , censé entrer en vigueur le 4 février. « Nous n’avons aucune intention de prendre le contrôle de Bukavu ou d’autres localités » , avaient-ils déclaré dans un communiqué diffusé notamment sur X.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-027.s: Studio Hirondelle, citing AFP, reported that Patrick Muyaya told AFP that this was proof that the unilateral ceasefire decreed was, as usual, a decoy.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-027.l: Eastern DRC (reaction to ceasefire declared 3 February)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-027.n: Muyaya's reaction followed the 5 February fighting in South Kivu (Nyabibwe), described in the preceding sentences of the page; place of fighting is in a South Kivu unit.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-027.vn: Fixed a stray ',.' and kept the quote's context (5 February fighting) in the note, since the stored excerpt does not print it. 'M23's' removed (the excerpt says only 'the unilateral ceasefire decreed'); the decreeing party is the rebels per the page. Per the same page, Muyaya was reacting to fighting launched in South Kivu at dawn on 5 February by the armed group and the Rwandan soldiers supporting it (replacement quote).
src: « C’est bien la preuve que le cessez-le-feu unilatéral décrété était, comme d’habitude, un leurre » , a réagi auprès de l’AFP Patrick Muyaya.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.s: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that M23 deputy spokesperson Dr Oscar Balinda said the group issued a communiqué calling on FARDC soldiers hiding in houses to gather at the Goma unity stadium, and that Balinda said more than 1,500 were then taken to the military camp at Rumangabo; the outlet said the soldiers were taken there on Thursday 30 January 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.l: Rumangabo military camp, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.a: AFC/M23 (per M23 deputy spokesperson Oscar Balinda)
r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.x: Balinda (via Imvaho Nshya): more than 1,500 FARDC soldiers taken to Rumangabo
r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.n: Partisan Rwandan state-owned paper relaying M23; treat as 'M23 says'. The page frames the soldiers as having surrendered ('zishyikirije') and being taken for M23/AFC political training; coercion is neither stated nor ruled out. Needs corroboration (UN, HRW). Excerpt 3 begins inside Balinda's quotation.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-028.vn: All exact; kept attributed to Balinda. M23 account via a Rwandan state-owned paper; the page frames it as surrender and political training. Not independently corroborated.
src: Aba basirikare bagejejwe i Rumangabo ku wa Kane tariki 30 Mutarama 2025.

Ikiganiro cyihariye Imvaho Nshya yagiranye na Dr Oscar Balinda, umuvugizi wungirije wa M23, yavuze ko batanze itangazo rihamagarira ingabo za FARDC zikihishe mu nzu guhurira ku kibuga cy’ubumwe cya Goma
Twarababwiye ngo baze, baje ari benshi none twahabakuye, barengaga 1 500 tubajyana mu kigo cya Gisirikare cya Rumangabo.

r1-NKS-2025Q1-029.s: Umuseke, a Rwandan outlet, reported that FARDC soldiers began fleeing to Rubavu via the Grande Barrière border crossing on Monday 27 January 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-029.l: Grande Barrière border crossing, Goma, North Kivu / Rubavu, Rwanda
r1-NKS-2025Q1-029.n: Single Rwandan outlet's report from Rubavu; the page adds that the soldiers surrendered to Rwandan security services and were disarmed (not claimed here; see page). Corroboration from wires or UN needed. 'Rubavu' is the Rwandan town opposite Goma.
r1-NKS-2025Q1-029.vn: Exact. The page adds that the soldiers surrendered to Rwandan security services and were searched and disarmed. Single Rwandan outlet. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, FARDC, kuri uyu wa mbere tariki ya 27 Mutarama 2025,zatangiye guhungira i Rubavu zinyuze ku Mupaka Munini, Grande Barrière.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-001.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels retook the localities of Kishishe and Bambo in Rutshuru territory from Wednesday 14 May 2025 after fighting Wazalendo fighters, whom they dislodged from the area.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-001.l: Kishishe and Bambo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-001.n: Single outlet citing local sources; Radio Okapi says M23 had left both places voluntarily over a year earlier (outside window). Actualite.cd (18 May) corroborates 'since 14 May'.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-001.vn: Excerpt carries every clause; excerpt_en's 'Radio Okapi reported that' is framing, not translation (excerpt itself is exact). Radio Okapi says M23 had voluntarily left both places more than a year earlier. Actualite.cd (18 May) repeats the 14 May retaking, likely not independent.
src: Les rebelles du M23 ont repris le contrôle des localités de Kishishe et Bambo, situées en territoire de Rutshuru, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, depuis le mercredi 14 mai 2025. Selon des sources locales, cette reconquête fait suite à des combats menés contre les combattants Wazalendo, qu’ils ont réussi à déloger de la zone.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that a notable of the region said two people were wounded the day before at Kishishe and that several shops were looted at Bambo; it said a large part of the population stayed confined at home during the heavy-weapon fighting.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-002.n: Date: article of 16 May says 'la veille' for Kishishe wounding (15 May); the looting date is not given. Anonymous notable.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-002.vn: Supported; date approximate. 'La veille' is relative to an article dated 16 May; the article also mislabels 16 May as Thursday, so the wounding date (about 15 May) is approximate.
src: Un notable de la région rapporte que deux personnes ont été blessées la veille à Kishishe et que plusieurs boutiques ont été pillées à Bambo. Une grande partie de la population est restée confinée chez elle pendant ces affrontements à l’arme lourde.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-003.s: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) said it treated about twenty wounded people, including six serious cases and one death, after violent clashes on Thursday 15 May in and around Bambo, Rutshuru territory, between M23/AFC and Wazalendo fighters of the CMC group.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-003.x: MSF: about twenty wounded treated, including six serious cases and one death
r1-NKS-2025Q2-003.n: MSF communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd. See next claim for the hospital-related statement.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-003.vn: Statement supported (figures are printed in words); figures field rewritten in words to match the excerpt. Actualite.cd's 4 June article dates this MSF figure differently ('une semaine plus tôt' than 14 May), an internal inconsistency in the outlet's reporting. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) annonce avoir pris en charge une vingtaine de blessés, dont six cas graves et un décès, à la suite de violents affrontements qui ont éclaté ce jeudi 15 mai dans et autour de la cité de Bambo, en territoire de Rutshuru, entre les groupes armés M23/AFC et les combattants Wazalendo du groupe CMC.
L’ensemble des blessés a été pris en charge à l’hôpital général de Bambo. Des combats à l’arme lourde entre les Wazalendo et les rebelles M23 ont provoqué d’importants déplacements de population.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that MSF condemned the holding of clashes in populated areas close to care centres, regretting that gunfire hit a hospital service; the outlet said the fighting at Bambo took place close to the MSF-supported hospital and that the use of heavy weapons forced medical teams to take temporary shelter, limiting their capacity to provide emergency care.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-004.n: Source says 'hôpital appuyer par l'organisation MSF' in the preceding sentence; the statement is the outlet's report of MSF's communiqué.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-004.vn: Hospital proximity is on the page (preceding sentence), not in the excerpt; added the shelter/limited-care clause the excerpt carries.
src: L’usage d’armes lourdes a mis en danger direct les structures de santé, poussant les équipes médicales à se mettre temporairement à l’abri, ce qui a limité leur capacité à fournir des soins d’urgence. « Malgré la dangerosité de la situation, nous avons pu soigner environ vingt blessés, dont six cas graves. Malheureusement, une personne n’a pas survécu à ses blessures », indique MSF dans un communiqué. L’organisation humanitaire condamne fermement la tenue d’affrontements en zones peuplées et proches des centres de soins, déplorant que des tirs aient touché un service hospitalier.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-005.s: Actualite.cd reported, in an article on an MSF appeal, that since 15 May Bambo had been the scene of intense clashes between AFC/AFC rebels (as printed) and Wazalendo militiamen of the CMC group, which had caused more than 900 families from Bwito chiefdom to flee to the town.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-005.n: Reported 4 June; the source text says 'AFC/AFC' (typo for AFC/M23). Displacement count is MSF's per Actualite.cd.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-005.vn: Raw said the figure came 'from an MSF document'; the page does not attribute it to MSF. 'M23' removed because the excerpt prints 'AFC/AFC'. The 900-families figure is the outlet's narration, not attributed to MSF on the page; the same outlet gave the same figure on 25 May ('depuis trois semaines'). The page's lead names the rebels AFC/M23.
src: Depuis le 15 mai, Bambo est le théâtre d’intenses affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC/AFC et les miliciens wazalendo du groupe CMC. Ces combats ont entraîné la fuite de plus de 900 familles de la chefferie de Bwito, venues se réfugier dans cette cité aujourd’hui au bord de l’asphyxie.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least 29 civilians, described as collateral victims of clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo over the previous six days, were buried on Tuesday 27 May in Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano and Kagando villages in Rutshuru territory; six more bodies were buried at Runzenze the same day.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-006.l: Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano, Kagando, Runzenze (Tongo and Bambo groupings), Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-006.x: Radio Okapi (local sources): at least 29 civilians buried on 27 May in four villages; six more bodies buried at Runzenze the same day
r1-NKS-2025Q2-006.n: Radio Okapi (27 May) gave 'at least 14 civilians killed up to Sunday 25 May'; Radio Okapi 10 June gave 'at least 75 killed' for 18 May to 10 June from regional sources. Figures differ by source and period; not merged. Perpetrator not attributed (collateral victims of clashes).
r1-NKS-2025Q2-006.vn: Statement supported; figures field carried other articles' numbers, now limited to this source. Tolls differ by source and period and are kept separate: Radio Okapi 27 May (at least 14 civilians killed to 25 May, claim 8), Radio Okapi 10 June (at least 75 killed 18 May-10 June, claim 10), Bwiza.com (about 38 killed in Mutanda 26-31 May, claim 20). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Attribution matches (collateral victims of clashes, no side blamed; local sources). Amend only corrects 'civils' to 'civilians'. The URL is dated 2025/05/29 while the source date is 2025-05-28; check the page date.; excerpt-support: nothing to add
src: Au moins 29 civils, victimes collatérales des affrontements entre les rebelles du M23 et les combattants Wazalendo au cours des six derniers jours, ont été inhumés mardi 27 mai dans les villages de Kirumba, Lukarara, Rukano et Kagando, situés dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu, selon des sources locales. Ces sources indiquent que six autres corps ont été enterrés à Runzenze ce même jour.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen villagers' houses were burned and that goats and other goods were reportedly looted, while young villagers were reportedly taken hostage by M23 rebels to carry these goods, in villages of the Tongo and Bambo groupings in Rutshuru territory.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-007.l: Tongo and Bambo groupings, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-007.a: M23 (as to hostage-taking; burning not attributed)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-007.n: Conditional wording in source ('auraient été', 'seraient'); local sources unnamed. Also records a detention/abduction element (porters). Dates approximate: report of 28 May about the preceding days.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-007.vn: Removed the report date (no excerpt prints 28); kept conditional wording. Looting and hostage-taking are conditional in the source; burning is not attributed to any party.
src: Plusieurs dizaines de maisons et de petites habitations appartenant à des villageois ont également été incendiées. Des chèvres et d’autres biens auraient été pillés, tandis que de jeunes villageois seraient pris en otage par les rebelles du M23 pour transporter ces biens.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May AFC/M23 elements had been conducting an operation to hunt presumed Rwandan FDLR rebels in several villages of the Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings in Bwito chiefdom, in particular at the edge of Virunga National Park.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-008.l: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-008.n: The framing 'presumed FDLR' is Radio Okapi's wording; other outlets describe the same fighting as M23 against Wazalendo CMC. 'Depuis' = start date, operation ongoing at publication (28 May).
r1-NKS-2025Q2-008.vn: Single clause carried verbatim by the excerpt. 'Presumed FDLR' is Radio Okapi's framing; the same outlet and Actualite.cd describe the fighting as M23 against Wazalendo.
src: Depuis le jeudi 22 mai, les éléments AFC/M23 mènent une opération de traque des présumés rebelles rwandais FDLR dans plusieurs villages des groupements de Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo et Mutanda, dans la chefferie de Bwito, en particulier à la lisière du parc national des Virunga.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that since Thursday 22 May near-daily clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups had occurred in Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo and Mutanda groupings of Bwito, and that sources reported at least 14 civilians killed, dozens wounded and several houses burned up to Sunday 25 May.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-009.l: Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo, Mutanda groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-009.x: Radio Okapi (sources): at least 14 civilians killed, dozens wounded, several houses burned, up to 25 May
r1-NKS-2025Q2-009.n: Lower toll than the 29 buried (Radio Okapi 28 May) for a slightly longer period; shown separately.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-009.vn: Statement supported; figures field no longer carries the article date. Lower toll than the 29 burials Radio Okapi reported on 28 May for a slightly longer period; tolls kept separate.
src: Depuis jeudi 22 mai, des combats quasi quotidiens opposent les rebelles du M23 aux groupes Wazalendo dans les groupements de Bambo, Tongo, Bukombo et Mutanda, situés dans la chefferie de Bwito. Jusqu’au dimanche 25 mai, des sources rapportent un bilan d’au moins 14 civils tués, des dizaines de blessés et plusieurs maisons incendiées.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-010.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that after violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 on the previous day, at Nyamilima in Rutshuru territory a girl of about 10 years was killed and houses were burned at Mulema (Walikale), as of Tuesday 10 June.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-010.n: Date computed: article of Tuesday 10 June says clashes began 'la veille' (9 June). Actualite.cd (9 June) also reports Nyamilima fighting. Perpetrator of the child's death not attributed. Mulema is in Walikale territory.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-010.vn: Supported; 'citing local sources' rests on the article's later 'Selon des sources locales'. The source does not say who killed the girl.
src: La situation sécuritaire reste préoccupante ce mardi 10 juin dans les territoires de Rutshuru et Walikale (Nord-Kivu), où de violents combats ont éclaté, la veille, entre les Wazalendo et les rebelles du M23 dans plusieurs localités. À Mulema, plusieurs maisons d’habitation ont été incendiées, tandis qu’à Nyamilima, une fillette d’environ 10 ans a été tuée.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to sources in the region, between 18 May and 10 June more than 600 houses were burned, at least 75 people killed and 42 wounded, with more than 26 villages affected in the Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-011.l: Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-011.x: Radio Okapi 10 June: >600 houses burned, >=75 killed, 42 wounded, >26 villages (18 May-10 June)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-011.n: Aggregate figures from unnamed regional sources; not split by perpetrator or by civilian/combatant status. Bwiza.com separately reports 543 houses burned and 38 killed in Mutanda grouping 26–31 May.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-011.vn: Excerpt carries the claim verbatim. Aggregate from unnamed sources; not split by perpetrator or civilian/combatant status.
src: D’après des sources dans la région, entre le 18 mai et le 10 juin, plus de 600 maisons ont été incendiées, au moins 75 personnes tuées et 42 autres blessées. Les affrontements ont affecté plus de 26 villages, notamment dans les groupements Bukombo, Tongo et Bambo.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-012.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that in fighting in Rutshuru territory about ten houses were hit by bomb fragments and several civilians were arrested ('interpellés') by M23/AFC rebels after the Wazalendo withdrawal.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-012.l: Rutshuru territory (place of the arrests not specified in the excerpt)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-012.n: The exact village is not given in this sentence (context: Nyamilima fighting, 9-10 June). Names, number and fate of detainees not stated.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-012.vn: Removed the date (no excerpt prints 10); added the bomb-fragment clause the excerpt carries. The page places this in the Nyamilima fighting (Rutshuru), which it dates to the day before its 10 June article. Number, names and fate of those arrested not stated.
src: Selon des sources locales, une dizaine de maisons ont été touchées par des éclats de bombes, et plusieurs civils ont été interpellés par les rebelles du M23/AFC, après le retrait des Wazalendo.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several concurring sources, M23 elements attacked FARDC positions supported by the Volunteers for the Defence of the Homeland (VDP, commonly called Wazalendo) at Lushebere in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; a local youth parliament president quoted by the outlet placed Lushebere between Kishishe and Kirima and said M23 had just progressed on the Lushebere-Kishishe-Bambo axis.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-013.l: Lushebere, between Kishishe and Kirima, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-013.n: The second excerpt is part of a quoted testimony by Chirac Mafula (president of the youth parliament of Bwito, then in Lubero), who calls M23 'terroristes' and alleges RDF support in the sentence before it; that allegation is not reproduced as fact. Casualties 'à vérifier'.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-013.vn: Source 1 is inside the Mafula quote, not the outlet's narration; reattributed. Day number removed from the statement (no excerpt prints 25). Discrepancy: the outlet's lead places Lushebere between Kishishe and Bambo; the quoted youth leader says between Kishishe and Kirima. The same speaker calls M23 'terroristes' and says it was supported by the RDF (his claim). Date (25 May) is printed in the article lead and the testimony, not in the stored excerpts. Toll 'à vérifier'.
src: Plusieurs sources concordantes dans la région annoncent que ce sont les éléments du M23 qui ont attaqué les différentes positions des FARDC appuyées par les Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP), communément appelés Wazalendo.
Lushebere, c’est une localité située entre Kishishe et Kirima dans la chefferie de Bwito, en territoire de Rutshuru. Notons que le M23 venait de progresser sur l’axe Lushebere-Kishishe-Bambo.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to a communiqué of the DRC Interior Ministry published on Saturday 12 April 2025, at least 52 people were killed in an attack described as 'organised and simulated' and attributed to AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-014.a: Government of the DRC (Ministry of the Interior)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-014.n: Government claim reported by Radio Okapi. Radio Okapi's same article states that local sources spoke of an attempted Wazalendo incursion to retake the city, a thesis the government rejects; the AFC/M23 account is not in this article. Clashes in the night of 11-12 April.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-014.vn: Excerpt carries the claim; attribution to the ministry retained. Government claim. Radio Okapi reports that local sources spoke of an attempted Wazalendo incursion, which the government rejects (claim 14). No AFC/M23 or Rwanda reply in this article.
src: Selon un communiqué du ministère de l’Intérieur publié le samedi 12 avril 2025, au moins 52 personnes ont été tuées lors d’une attaque qualifiée d’« organisée et simulée » attribuée aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23, soutenus par l’armée rwandaise.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of an attempted incursion by Wazalendo to retake Goma, while the government rejected that thesis and instead accused M23 of having orchestrated a premeditated attack against civilians.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-015.n: Two competing accounts in one article; neither independently verified there. No AFC/M23 reaction in this article.
src: Si des sources locales évoquent une tentative d’incursion des Wazalendo pour reprendre la ville, le gouvernement rejette cette thèse, accusant plutôt le M23 d’avoir orchestré une attaque préméditée contre les civils.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that the official document (the Interior Ministry communiqué) listed 297 assassinations and summary executions, 72 rapes, hundreds of disappearances, more than 146 cases of bodily torture and the looting of more than 2 000 head of cattle and vehicles between 6 and 11 April 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-016.l: Goma area (not specified in this sentence)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-016.x: DRC Interior Ministry (via Radio Okapi): 72 rapes, 297 killings/summary executions, >146 torture cases, 6-11 April 2025
r1-NKS-2025Q2-016.n: Government figures only; place not stated in this sentence and perpetrators are not named in it (the preceding sentence attributes the 'attack' to AFC/M23). No survivors named; no independent verification. Do not merge with BCNUDH figures.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-016.vn: Removed the communiqué date (no excerpt of this claim prints 12). Government figures only, unverified; place and perpetrator not stated in the figures sentence.
src: Le document officiel recense également 297 assassinats et exécutions sommaires, 72 viols, des centaines de disparitions, plus de 146 cas de tortures corporelles, ainsi que le pillage de plus de 2 000 têtes de bétail et de véhicules entre le 6 et le 11 avril 2025.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government, by an official communiqué of 8 May, denounced violence perpetrated by the AFC/M23 supported by the Rwandan army, citing more than 308 assassinations, 124 cases of rape, 315 cases of torture and hundreds of forced recruitments between April and May 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-017.l: Goma and surrounding areas (not specified in excerpt)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-017.x: DRC government communiqué of 8 May (via Actualite.cd): >308 killings, 124 rapes, 315 torture, hundreds of forced recruitments (April-May 2025)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-017.n: Government figures only; the legal label 'crimes de guerre' is the government's wording as reported. Place not in excerpt. No AFC/M23 reply found in this source. Compare with the 12 April Interior Ministry communiqué (72 rapes for 6-11 April).
r1-NKS-2025Q2-017.vn: Supported as government statement. Government figures only. The page attributes the 'crimes de guerre' label to the government and quotes Interior Minister Jacquemin Shabani Lukoo Bihango.
src: Le gouvernement congolais, par un communiqué officiel du 8 mai, a dénoncé les violences perpétrées par l’AFC/M23 soutenus par l’armée rwandaise. Il évoque des crimes de guerre : plus de 308 assassinats, 124 cas de viols, 315 cas de tortures, des centaines de recrutements forcés et plusieurs cas de spoliations et de destructions d’immeubles publics entre avril et mai 2025.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that MSF said, in a communiqué published Friday 11 April, that about twenty armed men affiliated with M23/AFC entered the compound of the Kyeshero hospital in Goma looking for people who had taken refuge there; one person died, three were injured and two hospital staff were violently assaulted.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-018.x: MSF: one dead, three wounded, two staff assaulted; about twenty armed men
r1-NKS-2025Q2-018.n: MSF's own communiqué via Radio Okapi; the UN Group of Experts already reports the same incident (existing claim r1-UC-M23-021). Independent of the GoE text.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-018.vn: Removed the day numbers 4 and 5 from the statement (no excerpt prints them); figures in words. Grade A not justified on this claim's own single source (no existing claims in packet): B. Incident dates (4-5 April) and the hospital name are on the page, not in the stored excerpt.
src: Selon un communiqué publié vendredi 11 avril, une vingtaine d’hommes armés affiliés au groupe M23/AFC ont pénétré dans l’enceinte de cet établissement médical, cherchant des personnes qui y avaient trouvé refuge. Cet assaut a entraîné la mort d’une personne, blessé trois autres et agressé violemment deux membres du personnel hospitalier.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that MSF warned of an alarming increase in violence targeting medical facilities and staff in eastern DRC since the start of 2025, saying it had faced about fifteen violent incidents directly affecting hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-019.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (MSF-supported hospitals)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-019.x: MSF: about fifteen ('une quinzaine') violent incidents directly affecting MSF-supported hospitals in North and South Kivu since the start of 2025
r1-NKS-2025Q2-019.n: MSF statement of 11 April as relayed; covers both provinces, individual incidents not listed here.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-019.vn: Statement supported; figures field in words as printed.
src: MSF a également alerté sur une augmentation alarmante des violences ciblant les structures et le personnel médical dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) depuis le début de l’année 2025. L’organisation rapporte avoir été confrontée à une quinzaine d’incidents violents affectant directement les hôpitaux qu’elle soutient dans les provinces du Nord et du Sud-Kivu.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-020.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing OCHA, that violent clashes took place on 9 April in the localities of Mutaho, Mujoga and Karungu in Nyiragongo territory and reached Goma two days later; OCHA also reported a clear rise in crime around Goma and Nyiragongo since the advance of the AFC/M23.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-020.l: Mutaho, Mujoga, Karungu (Nyiragongo territory) and Goma
r1-NKS-2025Q2-020.n: Relays an OCHA report (original not retrieved); the clash parties are not named in this excerpt. Links to the 11-12 April Goma fighting. 'Supported by Rwanda' is Actualite.cd's wording of OCHA's report.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-020.vn: Supported. OCHA report not retrieved directly; clash parties not named in the passage.
src: Selon un rapport du Bureau de coordination des affaires humanitaires (OCHA), la criminalité dans la région de Goma et Nyiragongo a connu une nette hausse depuis la progression de la rébellion l’AFC/ M23, soutenue par le Rwanda. OCHA signale notamment de violents affrontements le 9 avril dans les localités de Mutaho, Mujoga et Karungu (territoire de Nyiragongo), qui ont atteint Goma deux jours plus tard.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-021.s: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported, without citing a source for the figure, that about 38 people, including women and children, were killed between 26 and 31 May 2025 in Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory, an area it described as controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-021.l: Mutanda grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-021.n: Single outlet (Bwiza.com, Rwanda-based, Kinyarwanda); no named source for the toll; perpetrators not attributed. Compare Radio Okapi 27-28 May (14 killed to 25 May; 29 buried 27 May) in overlapping areas.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-021.vn: Excerpt supports; source_type set to partisan given the outlet's Rwanda base. Bwiza.com is a Kigali-based outlet (page footer: 'Kigali, Rwanda'); treat as a Rwanda-aligned source. No named source for the toll; perpetrators not attributed. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kigali-based outlet 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Partisan-only support: the single source is Rwanda-aligned and unsourced, and 'Kinyarwanda-language outlet' alone does not signal that. Amend adds the outlet's alignment and makes 'controlled by AFC/M23' the outlet's description. No perpetrator named, as in the source; grade C stays.; excerpt-support: added the page's masthead line (Kigali, Rwanda) as an excerpt for 'Kigali-based'; changed 'without naming its sources' to 'without citing a source for the figure', because the next sentence on the page attributes the 30 May killing at Kashalira to local residents ('Amakuru yaturutse mu baturage baho'); the page calls itself 'kigenga' (independent)
src: Abantu bagera kuri 38 barimo abagore n’abana bishwe hagati ya tariki ya 26 kugeza kuya 31 Gicurasi 2025 muri Gurupema ya Mutanda, iherereye muri Teritwari ya Rutshuru mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, hagenzurwa n’inyeshyamba za AFC/M23.
BWIZA.COM ni ikinyamakuru kigenga cyandika amakuru yibanda ku Rwanda, Akarere k'Ibiyaga Bigari n'Isi yose mu ndimi zitandukanye zirimo Ikinyarwanda, Icyongereza, n'Igifaransa. Kigali, Rwanda

r1-NKS-2025Q2-022.s: Bwiza.com reported, citing local residents, that Muhindo Sabuni Philémon, head of Kirima village, was killed at Kashalira market on Friday 30 May by unidentified armed men; the outlet said he had reportedly been recently appointed by the M23 administration.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-022.l: Kashalira market, Kirima village, Mutanda grouping, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-022.n: Single Kinyarwanda outlet; appointment by M23 is 'bivugwa' (said). Name printed as 'Muhindo Sabuni Philémon'.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-022.vn: Name printed exactly as in the excerpt; both clauses carried. Single Rwanda-based outlet; the M23 appointment is 'bivugwa' (it is said).
src: Amakuru yaturutse mu baturage baho avuga ko ubwicanyi buheruka bwabaye ku wa Gatanu tariki ya 30 Gicurasi, ubwo Muhindo Sabuni Philémon, wari umuyobozi w’umudugudu wa Kirima, yicirwaga ku isoko rya Kashalira n’abantu bitwaje intwaro bataramenyekana.
Uyu muyobozi bivugwa ko yari aherutse gushyirwaho n’ubuyobozi bwa M23, bwafashe aka gace kuva mu mezi makeya ashize.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.s: Bwiza.com, a Kigali-based Kinyarwanda-language outlet treated here as Rwanda-aligned, reported that 'other information' it did not source confirmed about 543 houses were burned, notably in Marangara, Runzenze, Butare, Kanyangiri, Kasali, Kanyatsi, Mashango, Kibwe, Nyenyeri and Buhambi hamlets in North Kivu, and that at the end of May Wazalendo fighters burned about ten houses in Butare village where they suspected the owners of working with M23.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.l: Marangara, Runzenze, Butare and other hamlets, Mutanda/Bwito, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.a: Wazalendo (for the ten houses at Butare); not attributed for the 543 houses
r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.x: Bwiza.com: about 543 houses burned (undated, unattributed); about ten ('icumi') houses burned at Butare by Wazalendo at the end of May
r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.n: Unattributed 'other information' for 543; the source does not date the burning. Grade C.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-023.vn: Statement supported; figures field in words as printed. Rwanda-based outlet; compare Radio Okapi's 'more than 600 houses' for 18 May-10 June (claim 10). Tolls kept separate. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Kigali-based outlet 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-004: Partisan-only support: the sole source is a Rwanda-aligned outlet, and the burning by Wazalendo rests on it alone, yet the statement does not tell the reader that. Amend flags the outlet's alignment and that the 543 figure is unsourced; grade C stays.; excerpt-support: added the page's masthead line (Kigali, Rwanda) as an excerpt for 'Kigali-based'; 'other information' unsourced is in source 0 ('Hari kandi n'andi makuru yemeza'); the page calls itself 'kigenga' (independent)
src: Hari kandi n’andi makuru yemeza ko amazu agera kuri 543 yatwitswe, cyane nko munsisiro za Marangara, Runzenze, Butare, Kanyangiri, Kasali, Kanyatsi, Mashango, Kibwe, Nyenyeri na Buhambi, aho hose akaba ari muri Kivu y’Amajyaruguru. Mu mpera z’ukwezi kwa 5 dushoje nabwo abarwanyi ba Wazalendo batwitse amazu agera ku icumi mu mudugudu wa Butare, aho bakekaga ko ba nyirayo bakorana na M23.
BWIZA.COM ni ikinyamakuru kigenga cyandika amakuru yibanda ku Rwanda, Akarere k'Ibiyaga Bigari n'Isi yose mu ndimi zitandukanye zirimo Ikinyarwanda, Icyongereza, n'Igifaransa. Kigali, Rwanda

r1-NKS-2025Q2-024.s: Actualite.cd reported that the NGO TRIAL International, in a communiqué, said that several escaped prisoners, convicted or prosecuted for international crimes, had quickly joined armed groups including M23 and Wazalendo militias and were taking part in the fighting, and that it denounced killings, death threats, torture, rapes and extortion targeting those who contributed to their indictment or conviction.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-024.l: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu prisons escapes)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-024.a: escaped prisoners now in M23 and Wazalendo (per TRIAL International)
r1-NKS-2025Q2-024.n: NGO statement as relayed; no individual incidents, places or victims given in this excerpt. Scope region-wide; assigned North Kivu because Goma's Munzenze prison escape is cited in the article.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-024.vn: Removed the communiqué date (no excerpt prints 18). The outlet's headline frames the escapees as AFC/M23 fighters; TRIAL's own words name both M23 and Wazalendo.
src: « Plusieurs évadés, condamnés ou poursuivis pour crimes internationaux, ont rapidement rejoint des groupes armés, notamment le M23 et les milices Wazalendo, et participent activement aux affrontements. Nous dénonçons les meurtres, menaces de mort, tortures, viols et extorsions qui visent celles et ceux ayant contribué à leur mise en accusation ou condamnation », indique TRIAL International.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-025.s: Radio Okapi reported that, at a meeting of North Kivu civil-society coordinations, participant Pepin Kavota said that between January and May 2025 more than 200 civilians were killed by the M23/AFC/RDF in Rutshuru, 76 in Masisi, and '9600 à Goma' (figure as printed), alongside 3500 people wounded by weapons in Nyiragongo territory and Goma city.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-025.x: Pepin Kavota (civil society, via Radio Okapi): >200 killed Rutshuru; 76 Masisi; 9600 Goma; 3500 wounded Nyiragongo/Goma
r1-NKS-2025Q2-025.n: Civil-society figures with no stated method; the '9600' for Goma is printed so and looks implausible next to the other figures (possible typo or different measure) - reported as printed. Attribution to RDF is the speaker's.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-025.vn: Supported as attributed figures. Civil-society figures with no stated method; '9600' for Goma is printed so and is out of scale with the other figures (possible typo or different measure). RDF attribution is the speaker's. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Figures check: '9600 à Goma' is out of scale with the other figures and may be a typo or a different measure; amended to mark it as printed so it is not read as a verified toll. The RDF attribution is the speaker's; single civil-society origin at C.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; '9600 à Goma' is printed in source 0
src: Entre janvier et mai 2025, plus de 200 civils tués par le M23/AFC/RDF à Rutshuru, 76 à Masisi, 9600 à Goma aux cotés de 3500 blessés par armes dans le territoire de Nyiragongo et la ville de Gom a », a détaillé Pepin Kavota, l’un des participants, faisant la synthèse de ces recommandations.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-026.s: Radio Okapi reported that Pepin Kavota, a participant in the North Kivu civil-society meeting, also mentioned kidnappings and forced recruitment within the rebel armed groups.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-026.n: Generic statement; no dates, places or numbers. Date is report date (15 June 2025).
src: a détaillé Pepin Kavota, l’un des participants, faisant la synthèse de ces recommandations. Il a également évoqué des kidnappings et recrutements forcés au sein des groupes armés rebelles.

r1-NKS-2025Q2-027.s: Jeune Afrique reported that AFC/M23 was multiplying sweeping operations in the North Kivu capital to flush out soldiers and militiamen who refused to surrender, and that, amid arbitrary arrests, forced disappearances and sometimes killings, Goma residents were bearing the full brunt of an explosion of insecurity denounced by NGOs and citizen movements.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-027.n: Only the paywall-free teaser/lede was retrievable; the rest of the article is paywalled and was not read. AFC/M23 response not in the visible text.
r1-NKS-2025Q2-027.vn: Removed the publication date, byline and dateline (no excerpt prints them). Only the free lede was readable; the article is paywalled. The byline (Yassin Kombi) and publication date are on the page, not in the excerpt. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Attribution drift, minor: in the excerpt AFC/M23 is the subject only of the sweep operations; the arrests, disappearances and killings are listed as part of an 'explosion de l'insécurité' that residents suffer, without a stated perpetrator. The amended wording follows the excerpt's structure; the perpetrator field 'AFC/M23' should read 'not stated for the arrests, disappearances and killings; context of AFC/M23 sweeps'. 'Forced disappearances' stays as Jeune Afrique's wording. No search (paywalled single source).; excerpt-support: nothing to add; the wording follows source 0
src: Dans la capitale du Nord-Kivu, l’AFC/M23 multiplie les opérations de ratissage pour débusquer les militaires et les miliciens qui ont refusé de se rendre. Entre arrestations arbitraires, disparitions forcées et parfois assassinats, les habitants de Goma subissent de plein fouet cette explosion de l’insécurité que dénoncent ONG et mouvements citoyens.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-001.s: Human Rights Watch said that between 10 and 30 July 2025 M23 fighters summarily executed local residents and farmers, including women and children, in villages, fields and near the Rutshuru River across the Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that witness accounts, the UN and military sources indicate the Rwanda Defence Force were also involved in the M23 operations.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-001.l: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q3-001.x: HRW: over 140 civilians summarily executed in July 2025 in at least 14 villages and farming areas; HRW compiled a list of 141 people killed or missing and feared dead; HRW: credible reports indicate the number killed in Rutshuru territory since July may exceed 300
r1-NKS-2025Q3-001.n: HRW did not independently verify all killings per Rwanda's response; HRW says it interviewed 36 people by telephone. Contested: see AFC/M23 and Rwanda statements below. Existing claims cover the UN GoE and MSF accounts; this adds HRW's own documentation.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-001.vn: Excerpts exact; figures 140/141/300 are printed on the page (quotes supplied); figures field narrowed to HRW's wording, incl. the hedge on 300. Documented NGO investigation -> A, attributed to HRW. All figures and the RDF involvement are Human Rights Watch's findings; the 'may exceed 300' figure is HRW citing unnamed credible reports. Rwanda and AFC/M23 deny (separate claims).
src: Between July 10 and 30, M23 fighters summarily executed local residents and farmers, including women and children, in their villages, fields, and near the Rutshuru River across the Binza administrative subdivision ( groupement ) in Rutshuru territory, North Kivu province.
Witness accounts, the UN, and military sources indicate that the Rwandan military, the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), were also involved in the M23 operations.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-002.s: Human Rights Watch said its research indicates the M23 military operations in Binza in July 2025 were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. Samuel Mushagara and Brig. Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively, and noted General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-002.n: Attribution of command responsibility is HRW's research finding, not an adjudicated finding. Excerpt contains HRW's own legal label in a sentence about sanctions; the statement does not repeat it.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-002.vn: Exact excerpt; attribution kept to HRW. Graded B (single origin for a command attribution) conservatively. Unit and commander attribution is Human Rights Watch's ('research indicates'); not independently corroborated. Being named is not a finding of individual responsibility.
src: Human Rights Watch’s research indicates the M23’s military operations were carried out by the 1st Battalion of the 1st Brigade, commanded by Col. Samuel Mushagara and Brig. Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, respectively. General Ngaruye is under UN sanctions for his role in M23 war crimes .

r1-NKS-2025Q3-003.s: UN News reported that the UN human rights office (OHCHR) said it had received first-hand accounts indicating that at least 319 civilians were killed by M23 fighters, aided by members of the Rwanda Defence Force, between 9 and 21 July in North Kivu province, and that Rwanda has repeatedly denied its forces support the M23.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-003.a: M23, aided by members of the RDF (as OHCHR says)
r1-NKS-2025Q3-003.n: Place named as Rutshuru in HRW's quote of the OHCHR statement; UN News excerpt says North Kivu province. Compare GoE figure of over 300 casualties for 9-27 July in existing claim.

src: The UN human rights office ( OHCHR ) said it had received first-hand accounts indicating that at least 319 civilians were killed by M23 fighters, aided by members of the Rwanda Defence Force, between 9 and 21 July in North Kivu province. Rwanda has repeatedly denied that its forces have been lending support to M23 militia.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa, at a press conference in Goma on 7 August 2025, called the UN report on the alleged massacre of more than 300 civilians in Rutshuru in July 'non factuel'; according to Bisimwa, the villages named as massacre sites would lie in the protected zone of Virunga National Park and therefore be uninhabited, and he said there is no family in mourning in Rutshuru and that the figure of 300 dead is implausible.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-004.l: Goma, North Kivu (press conference); Rutshuru territory (subject)
r1-NKS-2025Q3-004.n: Party statement reported by a Congolese outlet; cited for what AFC/M23 said only. Article also calls Bisimwa 'président du M23'.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-004.vn: Kept Bisimwa's conditional ('seraient') and quoted the 300 figure as he did; the 'over 300 civilians' report description is the outlet's narration (quote supplied). Source 1 excerpt_en is a faithful translation ('Virunga National Park' renders 'parc national des Virunga'); flag resolved. Partisan denial: AFC/M23's account only, kept separate from the HRW, OHCHR and Rwanda claims. The 'over 300' description of the UN report is Actualite.cd's.
src: Lors d’une conférence de presse ce jeudi 7 août 2025 à Goma, Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur adjoint de l’AFC a qualifié ce rapport de « non factuel » et dénoncé ce qu’il considère comme une tentative de « diabolisation » du mouvement armé par certains acteurs humanitaires et politiques.

Selon lui, les villages mentionnés comme lieux du massacre seraient situés en pleine zone protégée du parc national des Virunga, donc inhabités. « Il n’y a aucune famille en deuil à Rutshuru. Ce chiffre de 300 morts est invraisemblable.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-005.s: The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it rejects the false accusations in the recent OHCHR statement, that OHCHR alleges 'without any evidence' that the Rwanda Defence Force 'aided' in the killing of '319 civilians' in farms in eastern DRC, and that the gratuitous inclusion of the RDF in these allegations is 'unacceptable'.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-005.n: Partisan party statement. HRW (20 Aug) says that on 11 August Rwanda also claimed an armed group opposed to the M23 carried out the killings; that detail is not in this communiqué's text and is not recorded here.

Date left to the date field (2025-08-11) and source date, as the stored excerpt does not print it. Partisan statement: Rwanda's position only. This statement does not name any other perpetrator; Human Rights Watch reports that on 11 August the Rwandan government claimed an armed group opposed to the M23 carried out the killings, which must be recorded as HRW reporting Rwanda's position, not from this page.
src: Rwanda rejects the false accusations made in the recent statement of the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR). OHCHR alleges, without any evidence, corroboration or reported motives, that the Rwanda Defence Force “aided” in the killing of “319 civilians” in farms in eastern DRC. The gratuitous inclusion of the RDF in these allegations is unacceptable

r1-NKS-2025Q3-006.s: The Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs) said in a statement that it firmly rejects the findings of Human Rights Watch, OHCHR and UNJHRO alleging mass killing of civilians in Binza, that 'Human Rights Watch itself admits that it did not independently verify the alleged killings', and that only an independent investigation will shed light on these allegations.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-006.n: Partisan party statement. The page's first paragraph (rejection of HRW, OHCHR and UNJHRO findings) is quoted from a second part of the page and is not in this excerpt.

src: Human Rights Watch itself admits that it did not independently verify the alleged killings of Hutu civilians over a period of almost two weeks.
Only an independent investigation will shed light on these allegations.

The Government of Rwanda firmly rejects the findings of Human Rights Watch, Office of the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights (OHCHR) and the UN Joint Human Rights Office (UNJHRO), alleging mass killing of civilians in Binza

r1-NKS-2025Q3-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that eight bodies were buried over the weekend after deadly attacks on 8 August in the fields of Kihito and at Nyamilima (Binza, Rutshuru); it said seven victims, five wood-sawyers and two farmers from one family, were killed by gunfire or bladed weapon and, according to local sources, were reportedly targeted during an operation by AFC-M23 rebels to hunt alleged FDLR; the eighth victim, a local official of Kiheka neighbourhood, was found dead at home after a night incursion by unidentified armed men.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-007.l: Kihito fields and Nyamilima, Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-007.x: Radio Okapi: 8 bodies buried, 7 killed in the attacks plus a local official found dead at home
r1-NKS-2025Q3-007.n: Local sources. Victims not named. Date of attacks is stated by the article as 8 August.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-007.vn: 'Sept' printed (7). excerpt_en of source 1 faithful ('Kiheka' etc. in original); flag resolved. Perpetrator attribution is local sources' and conditional ('auraient'); the eighth victim was killed by unidentified armed men. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-006: The source's attribution is conditional ('reportedly'), which the statement dropped; restored, and the eighth victim's unidentified attackers added so the AFC-M23 attribution is not read as covering all eight. Search (Kihito/Nyamilima M23 FDLR août 2025) found consistent reporting (Critical Threats, HRW on the wider July-August Binza killings) and no AFC/M23 denial for this incident.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'auraient été' and the eighth victim are in source 1
src: Huit corps sans vie ont été enterrés ce week-end, après une série d’attaques meurtrières survenues le 8 août dans les champs de Kihito et à Nyamilima. Sept des victimes, dont cinq scieurs de bois et deux cultivateurs issus d’une même famille, ont été tuées par balles ou à l’arme blanche.

Selon des sources locales, elles auraient été prises pour cibles lors d’une opération de traque des présumés FDLR menée par les rebelles de l’AFC-M23. La huitième victime est un cadre de base du quartier Kiheka, retrouvé mort à son domicile après une incursion nocturne d’hommes armés non identifiés.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that a fragile calm prevailed on Wednesday 16 July in Binza groupement (Rutshuru) after several days of intense fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and various local armed groups along the Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, and that, according to local sources, the most recent clashes took place on Tuesday in Nyabanira and Kasave.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-008.l: Binza groupement; Nyabanira, Kasave; Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha axis, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-008.n: 'Tuesday' = 15 July (date computed from weekday and publication date). Nyabanira and Kasave are among the localities HRW lists for July killings.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-008.vn: Date 16 July printed on page (quote supplied).
src: Ce répit intervient après plusieurs jours de combats intenses ayant opposé les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 à divers groupes armés locaux, le long de l’axe Kiwanja–Nyamilima–Ishasha. Selon des sources locales, les affrontements les plus récents ont eu lieu mardi dans les localités de Nyabanira et Kasave.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, the disappearance of about a hundred farmers, notably in the Kongo-paysannat area west of Nyamilima, and said about twenty farmers had been missing since Monday 21 July; it linked the loss of access to farmland to fighting between AFC/M23 and alleged FDLR fighters near Virunga park.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-009.l: Kongo-paysannat, west of Nyamilima, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-009.x: Radio Okapi (local sources): about a hundred farmers disappeared; Radio Okapi: about twenty farmers missing since Monday 21 July (both figures in the same article)
r1-NKS-2025Q3-009.n: The two figures in one article differ (about 100 vs about 20) and are not reconciled by the source. Fate unknown. Weekday 21 July is as printed in the article.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-009.vn: Raw statement matches the page: figures in the excerpt; the link to AFC/M23 vs alleged FDLR fighting near Virunga park is in the lead paragraph (quote in clause_support; extend excerpt with add_excerpt). '23' flag is the 'M23' in 'AFC/M23', printed in the lead paragraph. The article prints two figures, about a hundred and about twenty missing farmers; both stand as printed and the article does not reconcile them. No perpetrator is named for the disappearances.
src: Des sources locales signalent la disparition d’une centaine de cultivateurs, notamment dans la zone de Kongo-paysannat, à l’ouest de Nyamilima. À ce jour, une vingtaine d’agriculteurs sont portés disparus depuis le lundi 21 juillet.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that after three months of prohibition the M23 again allowed residents of the Katwiguru–Nyamilima axis (Bwisha chiefdom, Binza, Rutshuru) to access their fields from Monday 25 August, for an expected two weeks according to local sources, and that the restriction had been imposed by the M23 to avoid confusion between civilians and alleged FDLR rebels.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-010.l: Katwiguru to Nyamilima axis, Binza, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-010.n: The reason for the restriction is as stated by Radio Okapi's article, not attributed to the M23 itself. The article also states that the M23 and the Rwandan government contested the HRW accusations in a communiqué of 22 August.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-010.vn: Exact excerpts support all clauses. The stated purpose of the restriction is as Radio Okapi reports it, not an M23 statement.
src: Après trois mois d'interdiction, les rebelles du M23 ont de nouveau permis aux populations de l’axe Katwiguru jusqu’à Nyamilima, dans la chefferie de Bwisha à Binza, territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu), d'accéder à leurs champs. Cette mesure, entrée en vigueur lundi 25 août, ne devrait toutefois durer que deux semaines, selon des sources locales.
Cette restriction d’accès avait été imposée par le M23 afin d’éviter toute confusion entre civils et rebelles présumés des FDLR.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that Kahumiro, near Kibirizi in Rutshuru territory within the Virunga park zone, had been the scene of violent clashes since 20 August 2025 between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters and alleged FDLR elements.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-011.l: Kahumiro, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-011.vn: Single exact excerpt carries the whole statement. excerpt_en faithful ('Virunga National Park' renders 'parc national des Virunga'); flag resolved.
src: La localité de Kahumiro, située dans la zone du parc national des Virunga près de Kibirizi, territoire de Rutshuru, est le théâtre de violents affrontements depuis le 20 août 2025, opposant les rebelles AFC-M23 aux combattants Wazalendo et à des présumés éléments des FDLR.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-012.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that M23 rebels 'under the command of Makenga' launched an operation to hunt alleged FDLR rebels at Kahumiro, while community leaders said there was no longer an active FDLR presence in the area.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-012.a: M23 under the command of Makenga (per local sources)
r1-NKS-2025Q3-012.n: 'Makenga' as printed; the source gives no first name or rank.

src: Selon plusieurs sources locales, les rebelles du M23, sous le commandement de Makenga, ont lancé une opération de traque contre des présumés rebelles FDLR. Toutefois, des leaders communautaires affirment qu’il n’y aurait plus de présence active des FDLR dans cette zone.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that local sources spoke of about ten deaths among residents, mainly Hutu and other local ethnic groups of Bwito chiefdom, in the Kahumiro clashes, and that hundreds of households fled to Kibirizi and neighbouring villages.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-013.x: Radio Okapi (local sources): about ten residents killed; 'hundreds' of households displaced
r1-NKS-2025Q3-013.vn: Exact; excerpt_en faithful; flag resolved. Toll from unnamed local sources; the article does not say who killed the residents.
src: Des sources locales évoquent une dizaine de morts parmi les habitants, principalement des Hutus et autres ethnies locales de la chefferie de Bwito. Environ des centaines de ménages ont fui vers Kibirizi et d’autres villages voisins.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that the chief of Kimoka locality (Kamuronza groupement), named as Kibihira Bauma, was shot dead at his home in Sake in the night of Saturday to Sunday 3 August 2025, in a zone it described as totally under M23 control according to testimonies; the authors were not identified and no official report had been issued.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-014.l: Sake, Masisi territory (about 20 km north-west of Goma), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2025Q3-014.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (3 August 2025 is a Sunday). Same article recalls the killing of Charles Kilibiri, chief of Malehe village, on 21 March (outside this unit's period; not recorded here).
r1-NKS-2025Q3-014.vn: Date 3 August 2025 and Kamuronza/Kimoka printed on page (quote supplied); name spelled as printed. Perpetrators not identified by the source; the M23 control of the area is context, not an attribution.
src: Ce crime a été commis dans la nuit de samedi à dimanche, dans une zone totalement sous contrôle des rebelles du M23, selon les témoignages recueillis. Le chef Kibihira Bauma a été froidement abattu à son domicile, situé dans la cité de Sake. Les auteurs de ce meurtre n’ont pas été identifiés, et aucun signalement officiel n’a été communiqué jusqu’à présent.

src: Cette série d’attaques survient après un rapport du conseil provincial de la jeunesse du Nord-Kivu qui a documenté 47 morts, 75 cas de violences sexuelles, 14 enlèvements, 66 braquages et 63 cas d’incendies entre le 7 juin et le 3 juillet 2025 dans les territoires de Nyiragongo et Rutshuru mais aussi dans la ville de Goma.
Dans un rapport publié début juillet, ces jeunes Gomatraciens affirment avoir recensé, en un mois, 47 morts, 75 viols, 14 enlèvements et 66 braquages.
Cette explosion de violence généralisée est confirmée par une étude menée par Epicentre du 23 avril au 11 juin 2025 à Goma.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that two people were killed by armed bandits on the evening of Wednesday 9 July 2025 in Goma; according to local sources, the first was a motorcycle taxi driver killed in Kasika quarter and the second a woman killed in Katoyi quarter, Karisimbi commune; it described Goma and Nyiragongo territory as under AFC/M23 control since late January 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-016.l: Kasika and Katoyi quarters, Karisimbi commune, Goma; Nyiragongo territory
r1-NKS-2025Q3-016.a: armed bandits (as described by the source); not attributed to a group

Selon les sources locales, la première victime est un taximan de moto, tué au quartier Kasika et la seconde est femme assassinée au quartier Katoyi, dans la commune de Karisimbi.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that, to secure Goma, the AFC/M23 administration installed infrared surveillance cameras in some quarters of Goma on Wednesday 9 July 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-017.vn: Exact excerpt carries the statement; date 9 July printed (year from the article's own 9 July 2025 date line in the same paragraph sequence).
src: Pour sécuriser la ville, l’administration de l’AFC/M23 a procédé ce mercredi 9 juillet, à l’installation des caméras de surveillance dotée de l’infrarouge dans certains quartiers de Goma.

r1-NKS-2025Q3-018.s: Actualite.cd, citing an OCHA report on June 2025, reported that since 5 June more than 3,600 people (about 720 households) fled Bukombo, south of Rutshuru, after intensified fighting between armed groups, and that most of the displaced found refuge at Birambizo General Reference Hospital, the local Catholic parish and host families.
r1-NKS-2025Q3-018.a: armed groups (not named in the excerpt)
r1-NKS-2025Q3-018.x: OCHA (via Actualite.cd): more than 3,600 people, about 720 households

src: Depuis le 5 juin, plus de 3 600 personnes (environ 720 ménages) ont fui Bukombo (au sud de Rutshuru) à la suite de l'intensification des combats entre des groupes armés. La grande majorité de ces personnes déplacées a trouvé refuge à l'Hôpital Général de Référence de Birambizo, à la paroisse catholique locale et auprès de familles d'accueil à Bukombo.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC accused armed men likened to M23 fighters of abducting at least 42 women in Bukombo centre grouping, Rutshuru territory; according to the communication officer of the 34th military region, Dieudonné Kasereka, the events took place on Sunday 28 December in Bwito chiefdom, and the 42 victims reportedly underwent torture before being abducted, according to the army citing testimony from inhabitants.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-001.x: Radio Okapi: at least 42 women (per army)

Later follow-up exists (Actualite.cd Facebook post: three women still in captivity), not fetched.

src: Selon le chargé de communication de la 34e région militaire,Dieudonné Kasereka, les faits se sont déroulés dimanche 28 décembre dans la chefferie de Bwito. Les victimes, au nombre de 42, auraient subi des actes de torture avant leur enlèvement, selon l’armée, citant les témoignages recueillis auprès des habitants.
Le chargé de communication de la 34e région militaire, Dieudonné Kasereka, a confirmé ces informations, s’appuyant sur des témoignages recueillis auprès des habitants terrorisés.
Les FARDC accusent les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 d’enlèvement d’au moins 42 femmes à Rutshuru
Des hommes armés, assimilés à des combattants du M23, sont accusés de l’enlèvement d’au moins 42 femmes dans le groupement Bukombo centre, territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-002.s: Radio Okapi reported on 15 October 2025 that civilian sources gave a toll of at least seven people killed, including two women, in the tenth day of fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC-Nyatura Wazalendo in Bwito chiefdom, with nearly ten other women reportedly raped and more than a quarter of the houses of Mashango village burned.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-002.vn: Excerpt exact; raw statement accurate (page dated and describing fighting on 15 October 2025). Rapes not attributed to any party by the source. Local civilian sources via Radio Okapi; rapes reported conditionally ('auraient été violées') and not attributed to any party.

Search ('"Chirumba" OR "Kagango" M23 tués Bwito 2025') found only relays of the same Radio Okapi text, no independent account and no AFC/M23 denial.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'auraient été perpétrées' is in source 0
src: Ce bilan vient s’ajouter à au moins 39 personnes tuées, il y a plus d’une semaine dans les groupements voisins de Tongo et Bambo, respectivement dans les villages Chirumba et Kagango. Selon les sources civiles dans la zone, ces tueries et exactions auraient été perpétrées lors des opérations de représailles des rebelles AFC/M23.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-004.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on 7 November 2025, that at least four people were killed and seven wounded in successive incursions by armed men over the previous two nights in Katsiru, Bwito chiefdom; per local notables, unidentified armed men attacked local defence units set up by AFC-M23, which occupies the area.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-004.a: unidentified armed men attacking local defence units set up by AFC-M23
r1-NKS-2025Q4-004.x: Radio Okapi: at least 4 killed, 7 wounded
r1-NKS-2025Q4-004.n: Single local-source report. Page adds the night of Wed-Thu had 5 dead incl. 4 civilians and one local-defence fighter, and wounded admitted to the Katsiru reference health centre; those details are not in the excerpts above and are not claimed. The same page names Katsiru as a long-running AFC-M23 vs CMC/Nyatura front.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-004.vn: Both excerpts exact, same page. 'four' is spelled in words in the excerpt (flag spurious). excerpt_en flag: 'Katsiru agglomeration' wording is fine. Discrepancy between 4 dead (lead) and 5 dead incl. 4 civilians (body) noted, not hidden. The page also says several wounded were admitted to the Katsiru reference health centre; the body gives five dead (four civilians) on the night of Wednesday to Thursday, differing from the headline's four.
src: Au moins quatre personnes ont été tuées et sept autres blessées lors d’incursions successives d’hommes armés au cours des deux dernières nuits, dans l’agglomération de Katsiru, située dans la chefferie de Bwito, territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu), rapportent des sources locales ce vendredi 7 novembre 2025.
Selon les sources des notabilités locales, des hommes armés non identifiés ont attaqué les unités de défense locale mises en place par les rebelles du mouvement AFC-M23, qui occupent la zone.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that, after clashes on Tuesday and Wednesday between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo in the villages of Muko, Karambi and Mashango (Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory), one person was killed, several others wounded and about ten houses burned, according to its sources; several local sources said AFC/M23 rebels searching for CMC-FDP wazalendo initiated the fighting, causing displacement, and burned houses in the three villages.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-005.l: Muko, Karambi and Mashango, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q4-005.x: Actualite.cd: 1 killed, several wounded, about 10 houses burned
r1-NKS-2025Q4-005.n: Date computed from weekday (Tuesday/Wednesday) and publication date Friday 19 Dec 2025. Local-source report; AFC/M23 account not found.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-005.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '19 December 2025', which no excerpt prints; numbers otherwise in words. Added displacement, which the excerpt prints. Dates 16-17 December 2025 are computed from 'Tuesday and Wednesday' and the 19 December publication date. No AFC/M23 account found.
src: Un calme précaire s'observe dans les villages de Muko, Karambi et Mashango, dans le groupement Bukombo (territoire de Rutshuru) au Nord-Kivu, après des affrontements mardi et mercredi entre les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 et les wazalendo. Selon nos sources, une personne a perdu la vie, plusieurs autres blessés et une dizaine de maisons ont été incendiées lors des combats

Plusieurs sources locales rapportent que les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 qui étaient à la recherche des wazalendo du groupe CMC-FDP ont été à l’initiative des combats occasionnant un déplacement de la population. Plusieurs maisons de la population ont été incendiées par les rebelles dans ces trois villages, selon les mêmes sources.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that an AFC/M23 unit on patrol on the Goma-Rutshuru road inside Virunga National Park fell into an ambush set by Wazalendo near Rumangabo on Wednesday 24 December; several sources said a vehicle of the rebels was burned, and one anonymous source spoke of rebel casualties.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-006.l: Rumangabo, Goma-Rutshuru road (Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2025Q4-006.n: Local-source report. Casualty remark by one anonymous source on the page is not claimed.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-006.vn: Excerpt exact; casualty clause placed by a replacement quote from the same page. excerpt_en flag concerns 'National Park' capitalisation only.
src: Une unité des rebelles denl'AFC/M23 en pleine patrouille sur la route Goma-Rutshuru en plein parc national des Virunga est tombée dans une embuscade mercredi 24 décembre, tendue par Wazalendo près de Rumangabo. D'après plusieurs sources dans la zone, il s'en est suivi un échange de tirs entre les deux camps, qui s'est soldé par l’incendie d’un véhicule des rebelles de l'AFC/M23 après avoir été dispersé par les wazalendo.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-007.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, a series of robberies attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru and Masisi over two days; in Rutshuru, three women fish sellers returning from Vitshumbi by motorbike were attacked on Friday 19 December on the Rwindi-Kibirizi road in Virunga park and lost their goods, money and phones.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-007.a: armed groups (the source says identifying the perpetrators is difficult in an AFC-M23-occupied zone where Wazalendo and FDLR also operate)
r1-NKS-2025Q4-007.n: Single local-source report. Same page notes a similar ambush on choristers from two Vitshumbi churches the day before. Actualite.cd (20 Dec) separately reported a double robbery on Kiwanja-Kanyabayonga road (not fetched for excerpt).
r1-NKS-2025Q4-007.vn: Excerpt exact and supports the statement. Radio Okapi says the perpetrators are hard to identify in an AFC-M23-occupied zone where Wazalendo and FDLR also operate.
src: Une série de braquages attribués à des groupes armés ont été enregistrés, ces deux derniers jours, les territoires de Rutshuru et Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Plusieurs civils, notamment des commerçants, des choristes et des responsables d’écoles, ont été victimes de ces attaques, selon des sources locales. À Rutshuru, trois femmes vendeuses de poissons revenant de Vitshumbi, et voyageant à moto, ont été attaquées vendredi 19 décembre sur l’axe Rwindi–Kibirizi, en plein parc des Virunga. Elles ont perdu leurs marchandises, leur argent et leurs téléphones.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué issued on Saturday, accused the rebel coalition, which it said is backed by Rwanda, of intensifying attacks in the east of the country in violation of commitments made in the Washington and Doha peace processes; according to the text signed by army spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekeng Bomusa Efomi, the rebels attacked several military positions in South Kivu and North Kivu over the previous 72 hours.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-008.n: Page says 'samedi' and was published Sunday 9 Nov, so date computed from weekday and publication date. Page also reports that wounded from Katsiru (Rutshuru) were being treated at Mweso hospital (medical sources, Masisi). No AFC/M23 reply found in this unit.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-008.vn: Excerpt exact; '8' not printed (page says 'samedi'), removed from statement and kept in date field as computed. Accusation framing added from page lead. Party statement (FARDC). Date 8 November 2025 is computed from 'samedi' and the 9 November publication date. The page names Bulambula, Kibanda Mangobo, the Mudugwe bridge and Tuwetuwe (South Kivu) and Kasopo, Kajinga and Mont Irimwi (North Kivu) as positions attacked. The coalition accused is the AFC/M23, as the article's headline and lead state.
src: Selon le texte signé par le général-major Sylvain Ekeng Bomusa Efomi, porte-parole de l’Armée les rebelles ont attaqué plusieurs positions militaires au Sud-Kivu et au Nord-Kivu au cours des 72 dernières heures.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Monday 15 December 2025 vehicles carrying support troops were seen crossing Kirumba towards the north of Lubero territory, coming from the PENA centre in Rutshuru territory; the article attributes the positions in Lubero to AFC/M23 and cites Lubero civil society.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-009.l: Kirumba, Lubero territory (from PENA centre, Rutshuru)
r1-NKS-2025Q4-009.a: AFC/M23 (per Lubero civil society and local sources)
r1-NKS-2025Q4-009.n: Excerpt does not name AFC/M23 in itself; page headline and body attribute these movements to AFC/M23 positions. The Lubero military administrator, Lt Col Kiwewa Mitela Alain, neither confirmed nor denied. Lubero is outside this unit's geography; kept as reinforcement movement from Rutshuru.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-009.vn: Excerpt exact; raw statement correctly says the article (not the excerpt) attributes the Lubero positions to AFC/M23 and cites Lubero civil society; clause support from the page. The page does not explicitly say whose troops the 15 December vehicles carried; it reports them in the context of AFC/M23 reinforcements. The FARDC-appointed military administrator called the reports rumours. Lubero military administrator Lt Col Kiwewa Mitela Alain neither confirmed nor denied, calling the reports rumours.
src: Ce lundi 15 décembre 2025, en milieu de journée, des véhicules transportant des troupes d’appui ont été aperçus traversant l’agglomération de Kirumba en direction du nord du territoire de Lubero, en provenance du centre PENA, situé dans le territoire de Rutshuru.

r1-NKS-2025Q4-010.s: MSF reported that in October two health centres supported by MSF were hit by stray bullets in Masisi and Rutshuru territories in the same week, and that in total three MSF staff have been killed in North Kivu in 2025.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-010.l: Health centres in Masisi and Rutshuru territories (not named by the source)
r1-NKS-2025Q4-010.a: not attributed by the source (stray bullets)
r1-NKS-2025Q4-010.n: Facility names, dates and the party responsible are not given in the excerpt. Only the October stray-bullet incident is claimed; the 'three MSF staff killed in North Kivu in 2025' sentence is in a separate passage and is not claimed here.
r1-NKS-2025Q4-010.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '9 December 2025' from the statement. The staff-deaths sentence is on the page (replacement quote), so kept with its own clause support rather than left unsupported. MSF does not name the facilities, give exact dates or say who fired. The October date is October 2025 by context (project update of 9 December 2025).
src: In October, two health centres supported by MSF were hit by stray bullets in Masisi and Rutshuru territories in the same week

r1-NKS-2026Q1-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters, allies of the FARDC, continued on Thursday 15 January in the Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory, around the town of Mweso, and that according to local sources the fighting involved Wazalendo of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC).
r1-NKS-2026Q1-001.l: Bukombo grouping, around Mweso (Bumbasha, Mubirubiru), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q1-001.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (CMC), allies of the FARDC, as named by the source
r1-NKS-2026Q1-001.n: Local sources via Radio Okapi. Overlaps in time with BCNUDH r1-ATR-NK-2026-001 (12-15 Jan, Rutshuru); this is the fighting narrative, no casualty total.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-001.vn: Both excerpts on the retained page; translation flag is only the expansion of FARDC, which the excerpt prints. Radio Okapi narration plus local sources.
ent: Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC)
src: De violents combats qui opposent les rebelles AFC/M23 aux combattants Wazalendo, alliés des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC), se sont poursuivis ce jeudi 15 janvier dans le groupement de Bukombo, territoire de Rutshuru, autour de la cité de Mweso, au Nord-Kivu.

Elles confirment que les combats, opposant l’AFC/M23 aux Wazalendo du Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC), se sont étendus vers le Jardin Théicole de Ngeri, dans la localité de Mubirubiru.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that several civilians, including displaced people, were wounded in the villages of Bumbasha, Kivuma and Kanyangohe during fighting in Rutshuru territory, and that a local customary source said a precise toll was hard to establish.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-002.l: Bumbasha, Kivuma, Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-002.a: not attributed by the source (fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-002.x: Radio Okapi: 'plusieurs civils' wounded, no number
r1-NKS-2026Q1-002.vn: Removed '15 January' from the statement (not in this claim's excerpt); the date stays in the date field and is carried by the page lead. No perpetrator is named by the source.
src: Plusieurs civils, dont des personnes déplacées, ont été blessés dans les villages de Bumbasha, Kivuma et Kanyangohe. Une source coutumière locale indique qu’il est difficile d’établir un bilan précis, mais déplore que de nombreuses familles déplacées soient dispersées

r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that several dozen civilians mobilised by AFC/M23 fighters for community work were targeted by CMC militiamen ambushed in the locality of Kiyeye, in the Kihondo grouping; separately, according to MSF as relayed by Radio Okapi, at least 32 wounded, mostly civilians, victims of shell fragments and direct fire, were evacuated and treated at the Nyanzale health centre (the source does not say all were wounded in the Kiyeye ambush).
r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.l: Kiyeye, Kihondo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Nyanzale health centre
r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.a: CMC militiamen (as named by Radio Okapi)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.x: MSF via Radio Okapi: at least 32 wounded, mostly civilians
r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.n: The 19 January date and attribution are in Radio Okapi's own narrative; the 32-wounded figure is attributed to an MSF communiqué of 23 January. Not seen on MSF's own site. 'Travaux communautaires' may be forced labour; the source does not say so.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-003.vn: Removed '19 January 2026' from the statement (excerpt says 'Ce jour-là'); the page prints the date, kept in the date field. Wording kept to 'community work' without implying forced labour. The source says the civilians were 'mobilisés ... pour des travaux communautaires'; it does not say whether this was forced. MSF's figure (at least 32 treated at Nyanzale over three days) is not explicitly limited to the Kiyeye ambush. MSF's own communiqué was not fetched. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: The excerpts place the CMC attribution on Radio Okapi and the 32-wounded figure on MSF, but MSF's figure is not limited to the Kiyeye ambush; the statement joined them. Amended to separate them. Fresh search: Radio Okapi (20 Jan) first reported 'au moins vingt civils' seriously wounded at Kiyeye on 19 January (search snippet, not retained), a different early toll.; excerpt-support: nothing to add
src: Ce jour-là, plusieurs dizaines de civils mobilisés par les combattants de l’AFC/M23 pour des travaux communautaires ont été pris pour cible par des miliciens du CMC, embusqués dans la localité de Kiyeye, dans le groupement de Kihondo.
Au moins 32 blessés, pour la plupart des civils, ont été évacués et soignés au centre de santé de Nyanzale. Ils ont été victimes d’éclats d’obus et de tirs directs, indique MSF.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that the humanitarian organisation MSF, in a communiqué, also reported that several civilian houses were burned in the area after the attack in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-004.n: Weekday 'vendredi' = 23 January per the page's own text ('publié vendredi 23 janvier').
r1-NKS-2026Q1-004.vn: Removed '19 January' and 'Friday 23 January' from the statement (not in the excerpt); the page carries them, and the date range stays in the date field.
