src: Dans un communiqué publié ce vendredi, l'organisation humanitaire rapporte également que plusieurs maisons de civils ont été incendiées dans la zone après l’attaque.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.s: Actualite.cd, summarising an OCHA report for January, reported that between 12 and 16 January fighting occurred in more than ten villages of the Bukombo, Kihondo and Mutanda groupings, as well as Bambo and Tongo, in Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, where about fifty civilians were killed, and that the report noted the displacement of several hundred people.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.l: Bukombo, Kihondo, Mutanda, Bambo and Tongo groupings, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.a: not named in the excerpt; the article's lead says the fighting notably opposed AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo militiamen affiliated with the Congolese army
r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.x: OCHA via Actualite.cd: about fifty civilians killed ('une cinquantaine' in the body; the headline says 'plus d’une cinquantaine'); several hundred people displaced
r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.n: Corroborates BCNUDH r1-ATR-NK-2026-001 (12-15 January, Rutshuru). Headline says 'plus d’une cinquantaine', body says 'une cinquantaine': both recorded in figures. Original OCHA report not fetched.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-005.vn: Statement narrowed to the excerpt's wording (no '2026' in the report title clause; 'groupings' list as printed). Figures field dropped the 'close to one hundred across three territories' total, which is page-only; actor marked as from the lead. Attributed to OCHA via Actualite.cd. Figure is OCHA's as relayed by Actualite.cd; OCHA's own report was not fetched. Headline ('plus d’une cinquantaine') and body ('une cinquantaine') differ slightly.
src: Entre le 12 et 16 janvier dernier, des combats sont survenus dans plus d’une dizaine de villages des groupements Bukombo, Kihondo, Mutanda, ainsi que Bambo et Tongo dans la chefferie de Bwito (territoire de Rutshuru) où une cinquantaine de civils ont été tués.

Le rapport souligne des déplacements de plusieurs centaines de personnes, dont la majorité a pris la direction de Bukombo-centre, Ihula, Nyanzale, Kikuku-centre et Katsiru tandis que d’autres ménages se sont repliés vers Mweso et Kitchanga, dans le territoire de Masisi.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that fighting pitted AFC/M23 rebels against wazalendo early on the morning of Tuesday 3 February at Kivuma and Kanyangohe, two localities of Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that after several hours of violent clashes the AFC/M23 rebels were forced to fall back to Mweso, their starting base; Radio Okapi also reported that AFC/M23 rebels launched an attack on Wazalendo positions in Kivuma and Kanyangohe, in the Bukombo grouping.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-006.l: Kivuma and Kanyangohe, Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (about 5 km from Mweso)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-006.n: Two Congolese outlets agree on the attack; the 'repelled' outcome is Actualite.cd's sources only. Both outlets are Kinshasa-leaning-neutral national media; no AFC/M23 account found.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-006.vn: Removed the Radio Okapi '4 February ... fragile calm' clause: neither the date nor the calm is in the excerpt. Category set to military_operation: the source reports a repelled attack, not a change of control. The outcome (AFC/M23 forced to fall back) rests on Actualite.cd's sources only; no AFC/M23 account found.
src: Des combats ont opposé tôt le matin de ce mardi 3 février, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 aux wazalendo à Kivuma et Kanyangohe, deux localités de la chefferie de Bwito (territoire de Rutshuru) au Nord-Kivu.
Après plusieurs heures de violents affrontements, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont été contraints de se replier vers Mweso, leur base de départ.
Dans le territoire de Rutshuru : Les rebelles de l'AFC-M23 ont lancé une attaque contre les positions des Wazalendo dans les localités de Kivuma et Kanyangohe, situées dans le groupement de Bukombo.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-007.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing concordant local sources, that a convoy of travellers from Rutshuru territory heading to Butembo was ambushed by unidentified armed men on Sunday 1 February on the Rwindi-Kanyabayonga stretch, in an area under AFC/M23 control, with several wounded and no deaths, and that travellers' valuables were looted.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-007.l: Rwindi-Kanyabayonga road, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q1-007.n: Single local report; victims taken to health facilities at Kanyabayonga.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-007.vn: All excerpts on the page; 'no deaths' and 'concordant local sources' are on the page next to the excerpts.
src: Un convoi de voyageurs en provenance du territoire de Rutshuru à destination de la ville de Butembo a été la cible d’une attaque armée ce dimanche 1er février, sur le tronçon Rwindi–Kanyabayonga.

L’attaque a eu lieu dans une zone actuellement sous contrôle des rebelles de l’AFC/M23. Les assaillants ont ouvert le feu et utilisé des armes blanches contre les passagers, provoquant plusieurs blessés.

Outre les violences physiques, tous les biens de valeur des voyageurs ont été systématiquement pillés, laissant plusieurs passagers dépouillés de leurs effets personnels dont argent, téléphones portables et marchandises.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that in the village of Kabanda, near Kibirizi (Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), an incursion by unidentified armed men was reported between 3 and 4 a.m.; the attackers looted the population's belongings, a young boy known by the name Jade was killed, and three civilians were wounded and admitted to the Kibirizi reference health centre.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-008.l: Kabanda, near Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-008.x: Radio Okapi (whole night in Bambo and Kibirizi): one dead, three wounded, one truck burned
r1-NKS-2026Q1-008.n: Date is the night of Sunday to Monday 16 February (date computed from the page's own text). Single local report.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-008.vn: Removed 'night of Sunday to Monday 16 February' from the statement (not in the excerpt and, on the page, tied to Kibirizi/Bambo rather than explicitly to Kabanda). Jade is printed in the excerpt. The page dates the night of violence in Kibirizi and Bambo to the night of Sunday to Monday 16 February; the Kabanda incursion is reported in the same article without its own date.
src: dans le village de Kabanda, une incursion d’hommes armés non identifiés a été signalée entre 3 h et 4 h du matin. Les assaillants ont pillé les biens de la population. Un jeune garçon, connu sous le nom de Jade, a été tué, tandis que trois civils ont été blessés.
Les blessés ont été admis au centre de santé de référence de Kibirizi pour recevoir des soins.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, the instability in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) is notably linked to a hunt operation led by the AFC/M23 against the Rwandan Hutu FDLR rebels and their local allies, including fighters of the Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement (CMC/Nyatura).
r1-NKS-2026Q1-009.l: Bambo and Kibirizi, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-009.a: AFC/M23 against FDLR and CMC/Nyatura (as named by local sources)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-009.n: 'Rebelles hutu rwandais FDLR' is the outlet's wording. Single local-sources report.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-009.vn: Removed 'in February 2026' and the '1 a.m. on 16 February' Bambo clause: neither number is in the excerpt. 'Rwandan Hutu FDLR' is the outlet's wording.
ent: Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement (CMC/Nyatura)
src: Selon des sources locales, cette instabilité est notamment liée à une opération de traque menée par l’AFC/M23 contre les rebelles hutu rwandais FDLR et leurs alliés locaux, dont les combattants du Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement (CMC/Nyatura).

r1-NKS-2026Q1-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that despite a ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, fighting continued between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said that since early Friday 20 February AFC/M23 had been fighting Wazalendo of PARECO at Mitimingi, Kaunda and Mbiso in Masisi territory, and that other clashes were reported in some areas of Rutshuru territory.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-010.l: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu (Mitimingi, Kaunda, Mbiso named for Masisi; no Rutshuru places named)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-010.n: Context: the same article says the truce was proposed 11 February by Angola after a Luanda meeting. Rutshuru clashes are not located by the source.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-010.vn: Both excerpts exact and cover the statement; translation flag is only the FARDC expansion.
src: En dépit du cessez-le-feu annoncé pour le 18 février à midi, les affrontements se poursuivent dans l’est de la RDC entre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et la rébellion de l’AFC/M23.

Depuis tôt ce vendredi 20 février, des combats opposent l’AFC/M23 aux Wazalendo du PARECO dans les localités de Mitimingi, Kaunda et Mbiso, dans le territoire de Masisi. D’autres affrontements sont signalés dans certaines zones du territoire de Rutshuru.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources reached from Mweso, that two civilians (a young girl and a cattle guard) were killed by stray bullets on Thursday 26 February in an exchange of fire between AFC/M23 elements on patrol and an unidentified armed group in the JTN concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso; twelve cows were also shot dead, and no official toll was communicated by the parties.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.l: JTN agro-pastoral concession, Bwito chiefdom, near Mweso
r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.a: AFC/M23 and an unidentified armed group
r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.x: Actualite.cd: two civilians killed; twelve cows shot
r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.n: Headline places the event in Rutshuru; the body places Mwesso in Masisi territory and the concession in Bwito chiefdom. Location discrepancy within the source.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-011.vn: All clauses on the page; 'twelve cows' and 'on patrol' are page-only, next to the excerpts. Location discrepancy within the source: the headline says Rutshuru; the body places Mwesso in Masisi territory and the JTN concession in Bwito chiefdom.
src: Deux civils ont perdu la vie jeudi 26 février 2026 à la suite d’un échange de tirs entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et un groupe armé non encore identifié dans la concession JTN, située dans la chefferie de Bwito, à proximité de Mwesso (territoire de Masisi).
Le bilan humain fait état de deux victimes civiles : une jeune fille et un gardien de bétail, mortellement atteints par des balles perdues au cours des échanges.
Aucun bilan officiel n’a été communiqué par les parties impliquées, et aucune information précise n’a filtré sur d’éventuelles pertes parmi les combattants.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-012.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on Wednesday 18 March armed men fired on and stopped a vehicle on the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road inside Virunga park, Rutshuru territory, wounding two passengers, a woman and her son, who were evacuated to the Kanyabayonga reference health centre; the assailants' identity remained unknown, though several security sources said this part of the territory is under AFC/M23 influence.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-012.l: Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road, Virunga park, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-012.n: Single local report. Complements the 1 February ambush on the neighbouring Rwindi-Kanyabayonga stretch.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-012.vn: All clauses on the page; 'under influence' is not attribution of the attack, and the statement keeps it that way.
src: Un nouveau cas de braquage de véhicule a été signalé ce mercredi 18 mars sur l’axe routier reliant Kanyabayonga à Kiwanja, dans le territoire de Rutshuru au Nord-Kivu.
Lors de cette attaque, deux passagers, une femme et son fils ont été blessés. Les victimes ont été évacuées au centre de santé de référence de Kanyabayonga (CSR CEPROMI).
L’identité des assaillants demeure inconnue. Toutefois, plusieurs sources sécuritaires indiquent que cette partie du territoire de Rutshuru est sous influence des rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the head nurse of the Kalembe health centre (Mweso health zone, Masisi territory), identified as Kapita Lucien, was shot in the hand after being violently beaten, and that the local Red Cross coordinator, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, also suffered physical abuse on the same occasion; the outlet attributed the incident to armed elements of the AFC/M23 and reported that the two men were reportedly accused, without formal proof, of links with the wazalendo and were taken away by motorbike by their abductors to an unknown destination. The article said AFC/M23 officials had not yet reacted.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-013.l: Kalembe, Mweso health zone, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q1-013.a: AFC/M23 elements, as named by the source
r1-NKS-2026Q1-013.n: Masisi territory (edge of the NKS unit). Single local report; the page states an AFC/M23 non-reaction as of publication. Source also relays a call for ICRC/MSF to intervene.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-013.vn: Removed 'Monday 30 March' from the statement (not in any excerpt; the page lead carries it and the date field keeps it). Both names are printed in excerpts 0 and 1, spelled as printed. The headline calls the second man a Red Cross volunteer ('volontaire') and says both were 'arrêtés'; the body calls him the local Red Cross coordinator and their captors 'ravisseurs'. The accusation of wazalendo links is reported in the conditional ('seraient accusés').
src: Selon des sources locales, l’infirmier titulaire du centre de santé de Kalembe, identifié comme Kapita Lucien, a été blessé par balle à la main après avoir été violemment battu.
Le coordinateur local de la Croix-Rouge, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, a également subi des sévices physiques à la même occasion.

Les deux hommes seraient accusés, sans preuves formelles, d’entretenir des liens avec les wazalendo. Après leur passage à tabac, ils ont été embarqués à moto par leurs ravisseurs vers une destination inconnue.
Les responsables de l’AFC/M23 n’ont pas encore réagi à cet incident.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that Bruno Lemarquis, Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator in the DRC, on a mission in Goma since Monday 16 March, called on the leaders of the AFC/M23 rebellion to guarantee absolute respect for humanitarian space, in a statement made during a meeting with the de facto authorities of Goma and its surroundings, led by Corneille Nangaa.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-014.l: Goma (city), Sake and Nyiragongo territory visited
r1-NKS-2026Q1-014.a: UN (Bruno Lemarquis); AFC/M23 de facto authorities led by Corneille Nangaa
r1-NKS-2026Q1-014.n: Page published 18 March, modified 23 March. The statement is generic, no incident named.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-014.vn: Removed 'left Goma on Wednesday 18 March' from the statement (not in the excerpts); the date is now the mission range 16-18 March, since the page does not give the meeting's exact day.
src: En mission à Goma depuis lundi 16 mars, Bruno Lemarquis, Coordonnateur résident et humanitaire en RDC, a lancé un appel aux responsables de la rébellion AFC/M23 pour garantir le respect absolu de l’espace humanitaire.
Cette déclaration a été faite lors d’une rencontre avec les autorités de fait de Goma et de ses environs, conduites par Corneille Nangaa.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, in an exchange with the diplomatic corps accredited in Kinshasa on Wednesday 25 March 2026, called the situation 'préoccupante', said the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian flights had not happened, and accused the AFC/M23 of lacking political will.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-015.n: Government account; the AFC/M23 reply on the same page is in the next claim. The 21 February AFC/M23 airport statement is already in POL-2026.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-015.vn: All clauses on the page; the airport clause is a direct quote on the page outside the excerpts.
src: Au cours d’un échange avec l’ensemble du corps diplomatique accrédité à Kinshasa, mercredi 25 mars 2026, la cheffe de la diplomatie congolaise, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, a présenté une situation qu’elle qualifie de « préoccupante ».
Elle accuse l’AFC/M23 de manquer de volonté politique sur une question pourtant réalisable, en vue de soulager les populations civiles.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 maintains that the humanitarian situation is improving in the zones it controls and alarming in the zones controlled by Kinshasa, in the context of the dispute over reopening Goma airport.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-016.n: Paraphrase by Actualite.cd, not a verbatim M23 quote; the outlet then cites Corneille Nangaa speaking in Goma on 20 February.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-016.vn: Flag '23' is the '23' in 'AFC/M23', which the excerpt context prints. Paraphrase correctly attributed. Actualite.cd's paraphrase of the AFC/M23 position, undated on the page; not a verbatim AFC/M23 statement.
src: Celle-ci affirme plutôt qu’il y a une amélioration de la situation humanitaire dans les zones sous son contrôle, soutenant en revanche que la situation est alarmante dans les zones contrôlées par le gouvernement de Kinshasa.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the North Kivu governor under AFC/M23 administration, Bahati Musanga Erasto, began a tour of Bwito collectivity, Rutshuru territory, on 12 February 2026, visiting Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe) and Nyanzale, and that at the end of the tour more than twenty young people were recruited into the ARC.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-017.l: Tongo, Butare, Kabizo, Bambo (Kishishe), Nyanzale, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q1-017.a: AFC/M23 de facto governor Bahati Musanga Erasto; ARC (as printed; the page does not expand the abbreviation)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-017.n: Goma-based outlet; the page does not say whether recruitment was voluntary or forced. Should be read against the Bwito fighting and the MSF/OCHA reports for the same weeks. 'ARC' is the printed abbreviation; the page does not expand it.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-017.vn: Statement unchanged; actor corrected: the page prints only 'ARC' and does not expand it, so the expansion is removed. No implication about forced recruitment. The page does not say whether the recruitment into the ARC was voluntary or forced, or who carried it out. Goma-based outlet operating under AFC/M23 administration.
src: Le gouverneur du Nord-Kivu sous administration de l’AFC/M23, Bahati Musanga Erasto, a entamé une tournée dans la collectivité de Bwito, territoire de Rutshuru, le 12 février 2026.
À l’issue de la tournée, plus d’une vingtaine de jeunes ont été recrutés au sein de l’ARC.
Il a appelé à se désolidariser des groupes armés, notamment les FDLR et les Nyatura.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-018.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Kisangani airport (Tshopo) as a 'warning' to Kinshasa, as its leader said, and that the movement said its drones destroyed a military drone base at the airport 'where attacks killing civilians were prepared' in Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe and elsewhere; BBC said it could not independently verify either side's claims.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-018.l: Kisangani (Bangoka) airport, Tshopo (statement concerns attacks on Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe)
r1-NKS-2026Q1-018.n: Kinyarwanda article published 4 February 2026 (page header 'Yatangajwe 4 Ukwa kabiri 2026'). The strike was on 'Ku Cyumweru' (Sunday) per the Tshopo provincial account; date computed from weekday and publication date = 1 February 2026. Outside North/South Kivu; recorded because M23's stated rationale concerns Rutshuru and Masisi.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-018.vn: Excerpts exact; the BBC caveat sits on the page directly after excerpt 1. Party claim ('AFC/M23 says'); BBC says it could not independently verify either side. Strike date computed from 'ku Cyumweru' and the 4 February publication date.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 wemeje ko ari wo wagabye igitero cya 'drones' ku kibuga cy'indege cyo mu mujyi wa Kisangani mu ntara ya Tshopo mu buryo bwo "kuburira" Kinshasa, nk'uko umukuru w'uyu mutwe abivuga.

M23 yo ivuga ko muri icyo gitero 'drones' zayo zashenye ikigo cya 'drones' za gisirikare kuri icyo kibuga cy'indege "ahategurirwaga ibitero by'ubwicanyi ku basivile" i Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Minembwe n'ahandi.

r1-NKS-2026Q1-019.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Tshopo provincial government said eight bomb-carrying drones tried to attack Bangoka airport at Kisangani on Sunday but were all shot down before reaching their target, and that the government side condemned the attack on a civilian airport and blamed the M23 and Rwandan forces.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-019.a: Tshopo provincial government; DRC government side
r1-NKS-2026Q1-019.n: Counter-account to the AFC/M23 claim. Date computed from weekday and publication date. The 'blamed M23 and Rwandan forces' element comes from a separate sentence on the page and is not in the excerpt, so it is not claimed here beyond what the excerpt supports; reviewers may narrow the statement.
r1-NKS-2026Q1-019.vn: The blame clause is on the page (one sentence after the BBC caveat), not in the excerpt; kept with that page quote. Flag '23' is 'M23'.
src: Leta y'intara ya Tshopo yatangaje ko ku Cyumweru indege umunani za 'drones' zitwaye ibisasu zagerageje igitero ku kibuga cy'indege kizwi nka Bangoka cy'umujyi wa Kisangani, ariko ko zose zarashwe "zitaragere ku mugambi mubisha wazo".

r1-NKS-2026Q2-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that clashes between wazalendo and AFC/M23 were reported from the morning of Friday 10 April 2026 in the locality of Rwankuba (Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory), with heavy gunfire heard in the villages of Kiringa and Bwuma.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-001.l: Rwankuba, Kiringa and Bwuma (Bwito chiefdom), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-001.a: wazalendo and AFC/M23, as named by Actualite.cd
r1-NKS-2026Q2-001.n: Single outlet citing its own sources; no control change reported. Place names as printed. Weekday and date both stated by the source.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-001.vn: Both excerpts exact on the retained page (Actualite.cd, 10/04/2026 11:26); statement matches, attribution to the outlet's sources kept. No control change reported.
src: Des affrontements ont été signalés depuis les premières heures de la matinée de ce vendredi 10 avril dans le territoire de Rutshuru, précisément dans la localité de Rwankuba (groupement Kihondo), dans la chefferie de Bwito.
Selon des sources d’ACTUALITE.CD, des tirs nourris sont entendus dans les villages de Kiringa et Bwuma, où les wazalendo s’opposent aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that six civilians were killed on 23 April 2026 in their fields at Bushenge, Gisigari groupement (Rutshuru territory), and that, according to several local sources, the killings were attributed to the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) operating through the AFC/M23 rebels. The outlet said the circumstances were not clearly established and the motive was unknown.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-002.l: Bushenge, Gisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-002.a: Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) operating through AFC/M23, according to local sources cited by Actualite.cd
r1-NKS-2026Q2-002.n: Single local-sourced report; attribution rests on unnamed local sources and the outlet says circumstances are not established. No RDF or AFC/M23 response found.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-002.vn: All six names printed in the source 1 excerpt, spelled as printed. excerpt_en flag is benign ('Rwandan Defence Forces' renders 'Forces de défense rwandaises'). The 'circumstances not established' hedge is on the page (page-only clause), kept because it limits the claim. Perpetrator attribution rests on unnamed local sources; the outlet says the circumstances are not established.
src: Six civils ont été sauvagement assassinés le 23 avril à Bushenge, dans le groupement de Gisigari, alors qu’ils se trouvaient dans leurs champs. Selon plusieurs sources locales, ces tueries sont attribuées aux Forces de défense rwandaises (RDF), opérant à travers les rebelles de l’AFC/M23.
Les victimes ont été identifiées comme étant Ndibaganira Bikiga, Matata Ruchumika, Bienvenu Goliyo, Gamira Busimba, Made Barayata et Nganyirende Biloloena.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-003.s: Human Rights Watch said, in a report, that Rwandan military forces and the M23 armed group carried out a campaign of forced recruitment and abusive detention of thousands of captured combatants and civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo; the report documents large-scale roundups and arrests in North and South Kivu and grave abuses against detainees at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps in North Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025. HRW said its researchers found that M23 fighters, backed by Rwandan military personnel, committed murder, torture and corporal punishment and used forced labor and child soldiers.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-003.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps, North Kivu (Rutshuru territory per Actualite.cd's account of the report)
r1-NKS-2026Q2-003.a: M23 backed by Rwandan military forces / Rwanda Defence Force, as alleged by Human Rights Watch
r1-NKS-2026Q2-003.n: Report published in the window but the abuses it documents run mid-2024 to December 2025 (largely before the window). Entered as the report's publication event, not as events of the quarter. HRW interviewed former detainees; the report also uses geolocated video and satellite imagery. Rwandan and M23 response: none found in this unit (Actualite.cd and HRW both state they have long rejected such allegations without investigating). Overlaps existing r1 claims citing hrw.org; check for duplicates.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-003.vn: Removed '10 June 2026' from the statement: it comes from the page's 'released today', not from an excerpt (the date stays in the claim's date field and source date). Rest exact; legal labels on the page ('war crimes') left out per vocabulary rule. Publication event of the report (source dated 10 June 2026); the abuses documented run mid-2024 to December 2025. HRW states Rwandan government and M23 officials have long denied, but failed to investigate, allegations of abuse.
src: Rwandan military forces and the M23 armed group carried out a campaign of forced recruitment and abusive detention of thousands of captured combatants and civilians in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo , Human Rights Watch said in a report released today.

documents large-scale roundups and arrests in North and South Kivu provinces in eastern Congo, as well as grave abuses against detainees at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training camps in North Kivu, between mid-2024 and December 2025.
M23 fighters, backed by Rwandan military personnel, have committed murder, torture, corporal punishment, and used forced labor and child soldiers, researchers found.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that a communiqué published on Thursday 4 June 2026 by the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, said that 204 AFC-M23 rebels had surrendered to the FARDC and their allies in Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi (North Kivu) in waves during April and May.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-004.l: Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi territories (North Kivu), and Kalehe (South Kivu)
r1-NKS-2026Q2-004.n: Party claim (FARDC) reported by Radio Okapi; AFC/M23 reaction not found. The same spokesperson also said the recruits were 'recruited by force'.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-004.vn: Exact; figure stays attributed to the FARDC communiqué. excerpt_en flag benign (expanded 'Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo'). Party claim relayed by a credible outlet: C kept for the unverified figure. FARDC figures, not independently verified; the page body adds Kalehe (South Kivu) as a further surrender zone and quotes Kasereka saying the recruits were 'recrutés par force'.
src: Au total, 204 rebelles de l’AFC-M23 se rendent aux Forces armée de la République démocratique du Congo et leurs alliés à Lubero, Rutshuru et Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Ces redditions volontaires se sont effectuées par vagues successives aux mois d’avril et mai derniers, explique un communiqué publié jeudi 4 juin 2026 par le porte-parole de la 34ᵉ région militaire, le major Dieudonné Kasereka.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 8 April 2026 the command of the 34th military region of North Kivu confirmed the voluntary surrender of 263 elements from the ranks of the AFC/M23 between February and March 2026.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-005.l: North Kivu (Lubero, Rutshuru and Masisi) and Kalehe, South Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-005.n: FARDC claim; surrenders themselves dated Feb-Mar 2026, statement dated 8 April. Territories named in the page body: Lubero, Rutshuru, Masisi, Kalehe.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-005.vn: Exact; 'confirmed' is Radio Okapi's verb for the command's statement; figure stays attributed. FARDC figure, not independently verified. Page body: four officers among them; surrenders in Lubero, Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe per Major Dieudonné Kasereka.
src: Le commandement de la 34ᵉ région militaire du Nord-Kivu, a confirmé, ce mercredi 8 avril, la reddition volontaire de 263 éléments issus des rangs de l'AFC/M23 entre février et mars 2026.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that a kamikaze drone hit the headquarters of the Congolese Institute for Nature Conservation (ICCN) at Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, on the morning of Sunday 24 May 2026; Virunga National Park public-relations officer Méthode Uhoze confirmed the facts to the outlet and said the attack came around 8 a.m. The outlet reported that the building was burned and the frame destroyed, that no toll was yet available and that the author of the attack had not been identified.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-006.l: Rumangabo (ICCN headquarters, Virunga National Park), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-006.n: Complements existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi, 24-25 May) with the ICCN/Virunga confirmation. Rumangabo is also named by HRW as an M23 training camp; the AFC/M23 account (KMP claim below) says the strike hit a densely populated area and the eco-guards camp. Time: Actualite.cd ~8:00, Kanyuka 07:35.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-006.vn: All excerpts exact; 'no toll' clause is page-only but verbatim. excerpt_en flags benign (expanded ICCN name). Times differ: about 8 a.m. per Virunga (Actualite.cd); 07h35 per AFC/M23 (Kivu Morning Post). Author unidentified per Actualite.cd; AFC/M23 blames Kinshasa's forces (claim 6).
src: Un drone kamikaze a touché, dans la matinée de ce dimanche 24 mai, le quartier général de l’Institut congolais pour la conservation de la nature (ICCN). La position visée est située à Rumangabo, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu.

Contacté par ACTUALITÉ.CD, Méthode Uhoze, chargé des relations publiques au sein du Parc national des Virunga, a confirmé les faits. Il a indiqué que l’attaque est intervenue aux environs de 8 heures.

Le bâtiment a été incendié et la charpente détruite. Il reste à vérifier si des membres du personnel se trouvaient à l’intérieur au moment de l’attaque. L’auteur de cette attaque n’a pas encore été identifié.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a statement on X, accused government forces of 'un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé' on Rumangabo; he said it took place on Sunday 24 May 2026 at 07h35 against the densely populated area of Rumangabo and the eco-guards camp of Virunga National Park, using CH-4 combat drones.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-007.a: AFC/M23 accuses 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa' (partisan account)
r1-NKS-2026Q2-007.n: Partisan claim (AFC/M23), cited only for what it said. The page also reports Kanyuka claiming 'pertes en vies humaines' without a figure. FARDC statement on Rumangabo: none found.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-007.vn: Statement unchanged and exact; corrected source_type: Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based media outlet (labelled 'media' in claim 7), the partisan origin is Kanyuka's X statement, recorded in originating_source. Second quote is Kanyuka's words ('a-t-il déclaré' on the page). Partisan account (AFC/M23), cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Kanyuka also claimed loss of life without a figure. The page says Congolese authorities had not reacted.
src: Dans une déclaration publiée sur son compte X, le porte-parole de l’AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, a accusé les forces gouvernementales d’avoir mené « un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé » contre Rumangabo.

Ce dimanche 24 mai 2026 à 07h35, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont procédé à un bombardement criminel et indiscriminé contre la zone densément peuplée de Rumangabo ainsi que le camp des éco-gardes du Parc national des Virunga, au moyen de drones de combat CH-4

r1-NKS-2026Q2-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that from Saturday 23 May 2026 the North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration suspended passenger transport between Goma and Butembo until further notice, announced in a communiqué of Friday 22 May 2026 as a preventive measure against Ebola (Bundibugyo strain). Kivu Morning Post reported the same communiqué.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-008.l: Goma–Butembo road (Goma city; Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories on the route), North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-008.a: North Kivu governorate under AFC/M23 administration
r1-NKS-2026Q2-008.n: Two Congolese outlets agree. Goods transport stays allowed with driver and assistant only (per both pages). Related Ebola-in-Goma announcement is in existing r1-POL-2026-009. Reaction of the Kinshasa government: not searched in depth.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-008.vn: Both excerpts exact; Ebola/Bundibugyo clause is on the Actualite.cd page (page-only). Both outlets relay one communiqué, so B for an authority announcement. excerpt_en flags benign. Kivu Morning Post does not itself name AFC/M23 as the administration; the date and content match the same communiqué.
ent: Gouvernorat de la province du Nord-Kivu
src: À dater de ce samedi 23 mai 2026, le transport des passagers entre les villes de Goma et Butembo est suspendu jusqu’à nouvel ordre par le Gouvernorat de la province du Nord-Kivu, sous l’administration de l’AFC/M23. La décision a été annoncée dans un communiqué ce vendredi 22 mai 2026

Dans un communiqué officiel publié le 22 mai 2026, le gouvernorat de la province du Nord-Kivu annonce la suspension, à partir du samedi 23 mai 2026, de tout transport de personnes entre les villes de Goma et Butembo.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Rwanda's foreign minister (printed 'Oliver Nduhungirehe'), in a statement the day after the Mushaki drone attack, deplored the silence of the international community and of the UN mission in the DRC regarding 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo'; he said that on 11 March 2026 FARDC attack drones struck Goma, killing UNICEF humanitarian Karine Buisset and two other civilians.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-009.l: Goma (the 11 March 2026 strike alleged); statement made from Rwanda
r1-NKS-2026Q2-009.a: Government of Rwanda (Olivier Nduhungirehe) accusing FARDC
r1-NKS-2026Q2-009.n: Rwandan government allegation, cited only for what Rwanda said; the 11 March strike itself predates the quarter. Date computed: page says he spoke 'le lendemain' of the Mushaki attack (8 May, per same page) and also 'le week-end dernier' (publication 11 May); date approximate. FARDC/Kinshasa response to this statement: none found. Same page also cites Mushaki (Masisi) 8 May strike, outside this unit.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-009.vn: Statement exact and attributed (the page frames the 11 March passage with 'Il ajoute que'). Corrected source_type: Kivu Morning Post is a media outlet; the partisan origin (Rwandan government, via X) is in originating_source. Karine Buisset printed in source 2 excerpt. Rwandan government allegation, cited only for what Rwanda said; the page spells the minister both 'Oliver' and 'Olivier' Nduhungirehe. Statement date approximate (page: 'le lendemain' of the Mushaki attack, which he dates 8 May 2026, and 'le week-end dernier').
src: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères de la République du Rwanda a déploré, le week-end dernier, dans une déclaration, le silence de la communauté internationale et de la Mission onusienne en RDC face aux « crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo »
Oliver Nduhungirehe l’a dit le lendemain de l’attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise à Mushaki

le 11 mars 2026, des drones d’attaque des FARDC ont encore frappé, cette fois-ci à Goma (aux mains de l’AFC/M23), tuant l’humanitaire française Karine Buisset de l’UNICEF, ainsi que deux autres civils.

r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said FDLR fighters infiltrated the Kabuye and Kabanda areas in the night of 18 May 2026 (time given as 'saa Saba z’igicuku'), killing a 77-year-old named Nzirorera Nsekuye at Kabanda and abducting Munenge Samuel and Karuhije Innocent at Kabuye; the outlet placed the incident in Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.l: Kabanda and Kabuye, Bambo centre, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.a: FDLR, per AFC/M23 spokesperson (partisan account relayed by Rwandan state-aligned outlet)
r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.x: Umuryango.rw / Kanyuka: one killed, two abducted
r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.n: Single partisan claim: AFC/M23 spokesperson relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media (Umuryango.rw, Kigali), which itself adopts the FDLR attribution in its own voice ('terrorist group'); treat as 'AFC/M23 says'. Time given as 'saa Saba z'igicuku' (not converted). FDLR/FARDC response: none found.
r1-NKS-2026Q2-010.vn: 'around midnight' was a mistranslation of 'saa Saba z’igicuku' (seventh hour of the night, about 1 a.m.); replaced with the source's own phrase rather than adding an unprinted number. All three names and the age printed in source 0 excerpt. Partisan, grade C. Single partisan claim: AFC/M23 spokesperson relayed by a Kigali outlet that adopts the FDLR attribution in its own voice. 'saa Saba z’igicuku' is the seventh hour of the night in Swahili/Kinyarwanda time-reckoning (about 1 a.m.), not midnight.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko FDLR yacengeye mu gace ka Kabuye na Kabanda ahagana saa Saba z’igicuku cyo ku wa 18 Gicurasi 2026. Kanyuka yasobanuye ko muri Kabanda ari ho FDLR yiciye umusaza w’imyaka 77 witwa Nzirorera Nsekuye, igeze muri Kabuye ishimuta uwitwa Munenge Samuel na Karuhije Innocent.
Umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR wishe umusivili muri Santere ya Bambo, Teritwari ya Rutshuru, Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi

r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that local sources, including notables, said at least nine civilians were killed on Thursday 17 July in the village of Hohé, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory, and attributed the attack to AFC/M23 fighters on patrol.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.l: Hohé, near Rushege, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.a: AFC/M23 fighters on patrol (as attributed by local sources)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.x: Radio Okapi: at least nine civilians killed (provisional)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.n: Local sources only; no AFC/M23 or FARDC response found. 'Thursday 17 July' stated by the source. Same page says the area sees AFC/M23 operations against FDLR and alleged collaborators.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-001.vn: Page supports every clause; single outlet relaying local notables, no party response found. Toll is provisional per Radio Okapi; attribution to AFC/M23 rests on local sources only.
src: Au moins neuf civils ont été tués lors d’une attaque survenue jeudi 17 juillet dans le village de Hohé, situé dans le groupement de Tongo, en territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu). L’information a été confirmée ce samedi par plusieurs sources locales, notamment des notables de la région, qui attribuent cette attaque à des combattants de l’AFC/M23 en patrouille dans la zone.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people were killed, one wounded and two missing in the last six days in the north of Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory. It said these incidents came a few days after the killing of five people on 28 July in the same area; among the victims were Justin Kahiti, chief of the village of Kirima recently appointed by the AFC/M23, his motorcycle driver and two of his bodyguards, who were killed in an ambush at Kasesero.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.l: Kibirizi, Kasesero, Kilambo; Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.a: not identified; local sources attribute some acts to M23 elements and others to reprisals by presumed Wazalendo combatants (unconfirmed)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.x: Radio Okapi: at least five dead, one wounded, two missing in six days; five killed on 28 July, of whom four (Kahiti, his driver, two bodyguards) in the Kasesero ambush
r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.n: Local sources. The page describes mixed attributions (some acts attributed by local sources to M23 elements, others to reprisals by combatants); the excerpts support only the toll and the ambush. Date range runs to the article date.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-002.vn: Draft said five were killed in the ambush; the page lists four ambush victims. Draft's actor read 'combatants' where the page says presumed Wazalendo. The page does not say all five 28 July victims died in the Kasesero ambush: it names four killed there (Kahiti, his driver, two bodyguards) and separately reports a notable of Kinyatsi shot the same day. Whether the 28 July deaths are inside the 'six days' toll is unclear on the page. The page also says that, according to local sources, some of these acts are attributed to M23 elements and others to reprisals by presumed Wazalendo combatants, accusations not confirmed by official sources (page text, not in the stored excerpt).
src: Ces nouveaux incidents interviennent quelques jours après le meurtre de cinq personnes, le 28 juillet, dans la même zone. Parmi les victimes figurent Justin Kahiti, chef du village de Kirima récemment nommé par l’AFC/M23, son conducteur de moto ainsi que deux de ses gardes du corps. Ils ont été tués dans une embuscade à Kasesero.

Au moins cinq personnes ont été tuées, une autre blessée et deux autres restent portées disparues au cours des six derniers jours dans le nord de la chefferie de Bwito, en territoire de Rutshuru, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that, the day before Sunday 2 August, two people were abducted in their fields around the village of Kilambo, Kanyabayonga groupement, and that their families said they were still without news; on the evening of Sunday 2 August unidentified armed men burst into a civilian's home in Kibirizi, Mutanda groupement, and shot him.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-003.l: Kilambo (Kanyabayonga groupement) and Kibirizi (Mutanda groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q3-003.x: Radio Okapi: two abducted; one shot
r1-NKS-2026Q3-003.n: 'La veille' = day before Sunday 2 August, i.e. 1 August (computed). Victim not named. Single local-source report.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-003.vn: Both passages verbatim on the page; date of abduction (1 August) is computed from 'la veille'. The Kibirizi victim survived the shooting and was taken to a local health facility, per the page.
src: Le dernier incident rapporté remonte dans la soirée du dimanche 2 août dans la localité de Kibirizi, groupement Mutanda. Des hommes armés non identifiés ont fait irruption au domicile d’un civil avant de lui tirer dessus.

La veille, deux personnes ont également été enlevées dans leurs champs aux environs du village de Kilambo, dans le groupement voisin de Kanyabayonga. Leurs familles indiquent être toujours sans nouvelles de leurs proches.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least about fifty young people were arrested on Tuesday 7 July during an operation by AFC/M23 police elements near the disused Katindo military camp in Goma, and that no official information was given on their place of detention or the reasons for their arrest.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-004.l: Avenues Salongo 3 and Katoyi 1 (per the article), near Katindo camp, Goma
r1-NKS-2026Q3-004.x: Actualite.cd: at least about fifty (« au moins une cinquantaine ») young people
r1-NKS-2026Q3-004.n: Corroborates existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-016 (MediaCongo/Radio Okapi 8 July) from an independent Congolese outlet. The page says residents had reported the youths for thefts and alleged cannabis use (alleged grounds, not an official reason). Radio Okapi 2026-07-08 also carries it (headline seen in search, not fetched).
r1-NKS-2026Q3-004.vn: Statement is supported; figures field normalised to the source's 'une cinquantaine' (no '50' is printed). The cited existing claim was not in the packet, so independence from it is not checked here. Residents said the youths had been denounced over thefts and alleged cannabis use; these are residents' allegations, not an official reason.
src: Au moins une cinquantaine de jeunes ont été interpellés mardi 7 juillet lors d'une opération menée par des éléments de la police de l'AFC/M23 aux abords du camp militaire désaffecté de Katindo, dans la ville de Goma.
Aucune information officielle n'a été communiquée sur leur lieu de détention ni sur les motifs de leur interpellation.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-005.s: The outlet reported that a teacher died in detention in Goma after his arrest by AFC/M23 elements, according to several sources close to his family, who accused elements of the movement and their allies of responsibility for his death. According to these sources, he had been arrested after demanding the return of his plot, which he believed had been occupied since the AFC/M23 took control of the city, and was reportedly taken to a place of detention known as 'Chien méchant', where, the family sources said, he reportedly suffered violence before succumbing to his injuries.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-005.a: AFC/M23 elements (as alleged by the family)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-005.x: one teacher died in detention (number not otherwise given)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-005.n: Date of death not stated in the cited excerpts; date is the article date (6 September 2026). Victim not named. Anonymous family sources; no AFC/M23 comment found.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-005.vn: Draft said the family accused 'the movement and its allies'; page says 'elements of the movement and their allies'. Restored the source's conditionals; removed stray punctuation. Anonymous family sources; the page uses the conditional for the detention site and the violence. Victim not named. The page adds that his body was reportedly transferred to the Hôpital général de Goma morgue and the family had difficulty recovering it.
src: Un enseignant est mort en détention en ville de Goma après son arrestation par des éléments de l’AFC/M23, selon plusieurs sources proches de sa famille.
Les mêmes sources familiales affirment que la victime y aurait subi des violences avant de succomber à ses blessures.
Après avoir saisi des responsables du mouvement pour faire valoir ses droits, il aurait été conduit dans un lieu de détention connu sous le nom de « Chien méchant ».
D’après ces sources, l’enseignant a été interpellé après avoir réclamé la restitution de sa parcelle, qu’il estimait avoir été occupée depuis la prise de contrôle de la ville par l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-006.s: Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd reported an explosive-device explosion on Saturday in Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, with differing accounts. Radio Okapi, citing concordant sources, placed it at Nyirubara village, said it happened while children were handling an explosive device they had just picked up, and gave seven dead (five children and two women) and about ten seriously injured taken to health facilities. Actualite.cd placed it at Gikoro, gave at least seven dead and more than ten seriously injured, said according to several sources that the device had reportedly been abandoned by persons not yet identified, and that the victims were reportedly mainly farmers; it called the toll provisional.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-006.l: Nyirubara (Radio Okapi) / Gikoro (Actualite.cd), Jomba groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q3-006.x: Radio Okapi: seven dead (five children, two women), about ten seriously injured; Actualite.cd: at least seven dead (six on the spot, one during evacuation), more than ten seriously injured, provisional
r1-NKS-2026Q3-006.n: Discrepancy to surface: place (Nyirubara vs Gikoro) and victim profile (5 children + 2 women vs mainly farmers). Both agree on 7 dead, 12 September, Jomba groupement. Igihe (Kinyarwanda) also headlined 7 killed by a buried device; its page could not be fetched. Context, not a clash-related attack by a named party.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-006.vn: Draft said both outlets gave 'seven' dead; Actualite.cd says 'at least seven' and calls the toll provisional. The 12 September date is printed in each article's lead but not in the stored excerpts, so the statement says 'Saturday' and the date sits in the date field. Discrepancy kept visible: place (Nyirubara vs Gikoro), circumstances (children handling a picked-up device vs a device abandoned by unidentified persons) and victim profile (five children and two women vs mainly farmers). Both agree on at least seven dead on 12 September in Jomba groupement. Neither attributes the device to a party.
src: Selon des sources concordantes, l’explosion est survenue, samedi vers 11 heures locales au village Nyirubara situé dans le groupement de Jomba, chefferie de Bwisha, pendant que les enfants manipulaient un engin explosif qu'ils venaient de ramasser.

Une fois l'engin explosé, sept personnes en sont mortes (cinq enfants et deux femmes). Une dizaine des personnes grièvement blessées ont été acheminées dans des structures sanitaires de la zone pour des soins appropriés, affirment ces sources.

Selon plusieurs sources, l’engin explosif aurait été abandonné par des personnes non encore identifiées. D’après les premières informations recueillies sur place, les victimes seraient principalement des cultivateurs qui se trouvaient dans la zone au moment de l’explosion.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Tuesday 28 July a so-called peaceful march organised by a platform presenting itself as the Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu paralysed several sectors in Goma between 7 and 11 a.m. and ended at the MONUSCO headquarters, where the organisers handed a memorandum to the mission's representatives. The call had been widely relayed the day before by neighbourhood authorities, who said the initiative was part of a decision taken by the de facto AFC/M23 authorities in the zones under their control; some residents interviewed by Radio Okapi said the mobilisation was coercive.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-007.a: Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu; de facto AFC/M23 authorities
r1-NKS-2026Q3-007.n: Related to the UN sanctions listing of 14 July (existing claims r1-UC-M23-033/035). Page also says protesters opposed the DRC constitutional reform project and denounced the sanctions.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-007.vn: Attribution tightened: the link to an AFC/M23 decision is the neighbourhood authorities' account, not Radio Okapi's finding. Per the memorandum, the protesters denounced sanctions against some AFC and M23 leaders and opposed the constitutional reform project.
ent: Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu
src: L’appel à la mobilisation avait été largement relayé la veille par les autorités de différents quartiers. D’après ces derniers, cette initiative s’inscrivait dans le cadre d’une décision prise par les autorités de fait de l’AFC/M23 dans les zones sous leur contrôle.

Si les initiateurs ont présenté l’événement comme une manifestation pacifique, certains habitants interrogés par Radio Okapi ont toutefois exprimé leur mécontentement, estimant que la mobilisation revêtait un caractère contraignant.

Les activités socioéconomiques ont été fortement perturbées ce mardi matin 28 juillet dans la ville de Goma, où une marche dite pacifique, organisée par une plateforme se présentant comme la Société civile plurielle et Forces vives du Nord-Kivu, a entraîné la paralysie de plusieurs secteurs entre 7 heures et 11 heures locales.

La marche a pris fin au quartier général de la Mission de l’organisation des Nations unies pour la stabilisation en République démocratique du Congo (MONUSCO), où les organisateurs ont remis un mémorandum aux représentants de la mission onusienne.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 10 August 2026 the deputy permanent secretary of the AFC-M23, Delion Kimbulungu, accompanied by the deputy governor of North Kivu Bahati Shadrack, toured higher-education institutions in Goma, including the ISTM, ISTA, ISP and ISC, where he chaired handover ceremonies between the old and new management teams. It said the decision designating the new management committees concerns ten institutions in Goma and Bukavu, and was signed by Bertrand Bisimwa and submitted for approval to Corneille Nangaa.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-008.l: Goma (ISTM, ISTA, ISP, ISC); also Bukavu
r1-NKS-2026Q3-008.n: Adds Goma detail to existing r1-POL-2026-008 (Kinshasa's rejection of the appointments, Radio Okapi 10 Aug). The page attributes the purpose of the tour to AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X (not cited here).
r1-NKS-2026Q3-008.vn: Draft said he 'installed new management teams at' the four institutes; the page says he toured and chaired handover ceremonies, the four being named as places visited. The 'ten institutions' clause needed the page passage. Bahati Shadrack is the AFC/M23-appointed deputy governor ('vice-gouverneur du Nord-Kivu' as the page puts it). The purpose of the tour is given by AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X, per the page.
src: Le secrétaire permanent adjoint de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo-Mouvement du 23 Mars (AFC-M23), Delion Kimbulungu, a effectué lundi 10 août 2026 une tournée dans plusieurs établissements d’enseignement supérieur et universitaire de Goma, où il a présidé des cérémonies de remise et reprise entre les anciennes et les nouvelles équipes dirigeantes.

La décision portant désignation des nouveaux comités de gestion est signée par Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur adjoint de l’AFC-M23 chargé des questions politiques, administratives, juridiques et diplomatiques, et soumise à l’approbation de Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur politique de l’AFC-M23.

Accompagné du vice-gouverneur du Nord-Kivu, Bahati Shadrack, M. Kimbulungu s’est notamment rendu à l’Institut supérieur des techniques médicales (ISTM), à l’Institut supérieur des techniques appliquées (ISTA), à l’Institut supérieur pédagogique (ISP) et à l’Institut supérieur de commerce (ISC).

r1-NKS-2026Q3-009.s: La Prunelle Verte reported that the AFC-M23 administration announced stricter movement restrictions: people coming from Beni, Butembo and Oïcha were no longer allowed to enter the territories under AFC-M23 control until further notice, and vehicles from those areas must be checked, as a measure it presented as preventive against Ebola.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-009.l: Territories under AFC-M23 control (entry from Beni, Butembo, Oïcha)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-009.n: Epidemic context (Ebola) for access to care; no finding that care was denied to patients. Zonebourse (20 Aug, seen in search only) carries a similar item.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-009.vn: Every clause on the page. A de facto authority's announcement as relayed by one outlet; no finding on its effect on access to care.
src: Selon cette administration, les personnes en provenance notamment de Beni, Butembo et Oïcha ne sont désormais plus autorisées à entrer dans les territoires sous contrôle de l’AFC-M23, et ce, jusqu’à nouvel ordre.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-010.s: Enquête.cd reported that the health crisis cell set up by the rebel administration announced on Thursday 3 September a new confirmed Ebola case in the Kayna health zone, a 21-year-old man from Butembo identified at a health checkpoint in the Itsu health area and transferred to the Kirumba quarantine site; it said Reuters also reported on 4 September a new case in an AFC/M23-controlled zone after the epidemic had been declared over in the territories under its control.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-010.l: Kayna health zone (Itsu health area; Kirumba quarantine site)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-010.a: AFC/M23 health crisis cell (de facto authority)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-010.n: Outside strict unit geography (Lubero territory, rebel-held) but relevant to the de facto health administration in North Kivu. Epidemic context only.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-010.vn: All clauses on the page; the Reuters clause is Enquête.cd's own citation of Reuters, kept attributed. Kayna is outside the unit's core territories (rebel-held Lubero); de facto health administration context. The Reuters report was not opened.
src: Un nouveau cas de maladie à virus Ebola a été confirmé dans la zone de santé de Kayna, au Nord-Kivu, une région sous contrôle de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo/Mouvement du 23 Mars (AFC/M23). L’annonce a été faite jeudi 3 septembre par la Cellule de crise sanitaire mise en place par l’administration rebelle.

Selon les informations communiquées, le patient est un jeune homme âgé de 21 ans, en provenance de Butembo. Il avait été identifié comme un cas suspect lors de son passage à un point de contrôle sanitaire installé dans l’aire de santé d’Itsu.
Après son identification, le jeune homme a été transféré vers le site de quarantaine de Kirumba, où des analyses ont finalement confirmé son infection par le virus Ebola.

Reuters a également rapporté, vendredi 4 septembre, la confirmation d’un nouveau cas dans une zone contrôlée par l’AFC/M23, après une période durant laquelle l’épidémie avait été déclarée terminée dans les territoires sous son contrôle.

r1-NKS-2026Q3-011.s: Bwiza (Kigali) reported that the AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said FDLR fighters attacked civilians at Mulala in Rutshuru territory on the night of Monday 31 August, killing four and wounding ten, and that two women going to their fields were abducted; the movement accused Kinshasa of failing to stop FDLR activities.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-011.l: Mulala, about 20 km from Vitshumbi, Rutshuru territory
r1-NKS-2026Q3-011.x: AFC/M23 via Bwiza: 4 killed, 10 wounded, 2 women abducted
r1-NKS-2026Q3-011.n: Party account only (AFC/M23 claim carried by a Rwandan private outlet; the article's own voice asserts the FDLR attack as fact, but the confirmation it cites is the AFC/M23's; no independent source). No Kinshasa/FDLR response found in searches. Kinyarwanda source. Cite 'AFC/M23 says'. Possibly same series as umuryango.rw existing claims on FDLR in Rutshuru.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-011.vn: Every clause is on the page and stays attributed to the AFC/M23; partisan source, grade C. Party account only: Bwiza (Kigali) states the FDLR attack in its own voice, but the confirmation it cites is the AFC/M23's. No independent source and no FDLR or Kinshasa response found. Time given as about 21:45 ('saa tatu n'iminota 45 z'ijoro').
src: Amakuru y'ubu bwicanyi yemejwe n'umutwe wa AFC/M23, biciye mu muvugizi wawo, Lawrence Kanyuka. Yavuze ko icyo gitero cyabaye mu ijoro ryo ku wa Mbere tariki ya 31 Kanama, ahagana saa tatu n’iminota 45 z’ijoro.
AFC-M23 ivuga ko uretse abantu bane bishwe n’abandi 10 bagakomereka, abagore babiri bashimuswe, ubwo bari bagiye gukora mu mirima.
Abarwanyi b'umutwe wa FDLR bagabye igitero ku baturage bo mu gace ka Mulala ho muri Teritwari ya Rutshuru mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, kigahitana abantu bane abandi 10 barabakomeretsa.
Ni igitero cyabereye bilometero bibarirwa muri 20 uvuye i Vitshumbi.
Uyu mutwe washinje ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa gukomeza kwanga gufata ingamba zo guhagarika ibikorwa bya FDLR

r1-NKS-2026Q3-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a declaration on Tuesday 21 July in Mangina, Beni territory, the coordination of North Kivu civil society implicated the ADF in the north and the AFC/M23 coalition in the south in the worsening security situation; its coordinator John Banyene said: 'Le M23 continue de massacrer, torturer, violer, piller les ressources naturelles et les biens de la population'. Radio Okapi, summarising the declaration, said the rebels were deploying recently trained troops at Tchanzu with logistical support from the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF).
r1-NKS-2026Q3-012.a: coordination of North Kivu civil society (speaker); M23, ADF and RDF (as alleged)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-012.n: Civil-society allegation, general, not an incident. The page does not state where Tchanzu is. General allegation including 'violer' without incident detail.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-012.vn: Attribution of the Tchanzu sentence made precise: it is the outlet's summary of the declaration, not a quoted line of the declaration. General civil-society allegations (including rape) with no incident detail. The Tchanzu/RDF sentence is Radio Okapi's narration of the civil society's assessment, not a quotation. Banyene's quote continues on the page (illegal occupation of homes and fields, illegal taxes, forced recruitment of youths, targeted killings).
src: John Banyene, coordonnateur de la société civile du Nord-Kivu, dénonce les exactions commises dans les zones sous contrôle des rebelles : « Le M23 continue de massacrer, torturer, violer, piller les ressources naturelles et les biens de la population
Les rebelles déploient des troupes récemment formées à Tchanzu avec l’appui logistique des Forces de défense rwandaises (RDF), démontrant une volonté manifeste d’escalade.

Dans une déclaration solennelle faite mardi 21 juillet à Mangina, dans le territoire de Beni, l’organisation dresse un constat accablant des exactions commises contre les civils. Mettant directement en cause la nébuleuse terroriste des ADF au nord et la coalition AFC/M23 au sud

r1-NKS-2026Q3-013.s: Congovirtuel reported, citing Africa Intelligence, that Théo Binamungu, described as a close political adviser to Nangaa, was arrested at the end of August by loyalists of Makenga, interrogated by the military intelligence of the Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) and then by the Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), and transferred to Munzenze central prison on 8 September.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-013.a: loyalists of Sultani Makenga; ARC military intelligence; DSR (as reported by Africa Intelligence)
r1-NKS-2026Q3-013.n: Single, paywalled-origin report relayed by Congovirtuel (analysis outlet; editorialised). Not verified independently; reported by Africa Intelligence per the page. The ARC is the AFC/M23 army wing as the page uses the name. Unit/commander lead: Sultani Makenga.
r1-NKS-2026Q3-013.vn: Draft wrote 'AFC/M23 military intelligence'; the page names the ARC's military intelligence. Origin credited to Africa Intelligence. Single paywalled origin (Africa Intelligence) relayed by an editorialising analysis site; not independently verified. No AFC/M23 comment found.
ent: Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR)
src: L’arrestation de Théo Binamungu fin août, suivie de ses interrogatoires par les renseignements militaires de l’Armée de la révolution congolaise (ARC) puis par la Direction pour la sécurité et les renseignements (DSR), illustre de manière implacable de la guerre des Chefs au sein du Mouvement rebelle . Son transfert à la prison centrale de Munzenze le 8 septembre scelle l’échec de de la tentative d’émancipation.

L’arrestation de Théo Binamungu, proche conseiller politique de Nangaa, par des fidèles de Makenga démontre que toute tentative des responsables politiques d’affirmer une autorité indépendante ou de réclamer une part plus importante des revenus miniers se heurte à une répression militaire immédiate, a rapporté Africa Intelligence.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that fighting was reported on the morning of Tuesday 13 October around Kiseguro, Rutshuru territory, between presumed Wazalendo fighters and those of the AFC/M23, described as recently renamed the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN). Local sources said the attack on an AFC/M23 (FRN) position began around 5 a.m. and no toll was available.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-001.l: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-001.n: Local sources, no toll. Kiseguro said to be about twenty km north-east of Kiwanja. Sibling reports: Actualite.cd 14 Oct, Les Volcans News 13 Oct.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-001.vn: Both excerpts on the retained page and about this event; 'Tuesday' translates 'mardi' (flag spurious). Toll clause is on the page. Radio Okapi does not say who held Kiseguro after the fighting; Actualite.cd and Les Volcans News give differing accounts (separate claims).
ent: Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN)
src: Des combats ont été signalés dans la matinée de ce mardi 13 octobre autour de Kiseguro, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu, entre des combattants présumés Wazalendo et ceux de l’AFC/M23, récemment rebaptisée Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN).
D’après ces sources, l’attaque contre une position de l’AFC/M23 (FRN) à Kiseguro, dans le groupement de Binza, a débuté vers 5 heures (heure locale).

r1-NKS-2026Q4-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the Wazalendo launched the attack on a Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) position at Kiseguro on Tuesday morning and, after several hours of fighting, withdrew from the area, leaving the positions in the hands of the FRN rebels.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-002.l: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-002.n: Date computed from weekday ('mardi') and publication date 2026-10-14. Conflicts in emphasis with Les Volcans News (control 'not clearly established'), see next claim.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-002.vn: Supported; date is computed from a weekday so date_precision set to approximate. Actualite.cd's account of control; Les Volcans News said control was not clearly established. Keep the accounts separate. The article dates the attack only as 'mardi' (date computed from the 14 Oct publication).
src: D’après les mêmes sources, les wazalendo se sont finalement retirés de la zone après plusieurs heures de combats, laissant les positions aux mains des rebelles du FRN.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-003.s: Les Volcans News reported, citing local sources, that clashes broke out on Tuesday 13 October 2026 at about 5 a.m. at Kiseguro, and that control of Kiseguro by either side was not clearly established when the article was written.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-003.l: Kiseguro (Binza groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-003.x: Les Volcans News: no human or material toll available
r1-NKS-2026Q4-003.n: Same morning's event as Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd; accounts differ on who held the place afterwards.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-003.vn: Both excerpts verbatim on page; flagged capitalised word is a translation of 'RDC'/'mardi'. Differs from Actualite.cd (FRN kept positions). Both accounts recorded separately.
src: Le contrôle de Kiseguro par l’un ou l’autre des camps n’était pas clairement établi au moment de la rédaction de cet article.

Des affrontements entre les Wazalendo et le M23 ont éclaté mardi 13 octobre 2026, vers 5 heures, à Kiseguro, dans le groupement de Binza, en territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), selon des sources locales.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-004.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that around 22:00 the night before the 13 October clashes, explosions were heard at Kalengera, Kisigari groupement, Rutshuru territory, and that a military drone strike was said to have targeted a rebel position there; no toll was communicated.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-004.l: Kalengera (Kisigari groupement), Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-004.a: military drone, unattributed by the source; targeted a 'rebel position'
r1-NKS-2026Q4-004.n: Night before 13 Oct, so approx 12 Oct. Actualite.cd 14 Oct and Les Volcans News speak of 'combats' at Kalengera the day before, not a drone strike.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-004.vn: Supported; flagged figures 13 and 22h are on the page (22 heures = 10 p.m.). Drone strike is conditional ('aurait visé') and unattributed. Actualite.cd and Les Volcans News describe 'combats' at Kalengera the day before, not a drone strike.
src: La nuit précédant ces combats, vers 22 heures, des explosions ont été entendues à Kalengera, dans le groupement de Kisigari, toujours dans le territoire de Rutshuru. Selon des sources locales, une frappe de drone militaire aurait visé une position rebelle dans cette localité.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-005.s: FNTV reported, citing a family source quoted by the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP), that Martin Dushime, 27, a final-year medical student said to have been forcibly enrolled in the AFC/M23, surrendered to the FARDC; the article states he had been abducted in Goma on 6 July 2025. The accusation of abduction and forced recruitment comes from the family source and the outlet and is not confirmed by AFC/M23 in the article.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-005.n: Single anonymous family source via ACP. 'jeudi' = day before publication on 9 Oct (date computed from weekday and publication date). Abduction itself dates to 2025-07-06 (within window); consider a separate record. No AFC/M23 response found.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-005.vn: All clauses on the page; flagged '23' is from 'AFC/M23'. Replacement adds the family quote that carries the forced-recruitment allegation. The surrender date is not stated; 8 Oct is the day ('jeudi') ACP cited the family source, computed from the 9 Oct publication. Anonymous family source; no AFC/M23 response found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: FNTV (9 Oct 2026, Lionel Kibuluku) supports the statement; the 'final-year medical student', 'forcibly enrolled' and 'surrendered' clauses are in the outlet's lead paragraph, not in the stored excerpts, so it is added. The body later calls the forced enrolment 'présumé' (alleged), which matches the statement's caveat.
src: Martin Dushime, 27 ans, a été récupéré par les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), selon une source familiale citée jeudi par l’Agence congolaise de presse (ACP).
Le jeune étudiant avait été enlevé le 6 juillet 2025 à Goma, chef-lieu du Nord-Kivu.

Enlevé en pleine rue à Goma, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, puis enrôlé de force dans les rangs de l’AFC/M23, un étudiant en dernière année de médecine a fini par se rendre à l’armée congolaise.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) provided care to more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence at Sake, Masisi territory, over 13 months of intervention, and announced the transfer of its medical activities at Sake to Première Urgence Internationale (PUI).
r1-NKS-2026Q4-006.x: Actualite.cd (MSF figure): more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence in 13 months; more than 10 400 people given psychological support
r1-NKS-2026Q4-006.n: Care-provision count, not an incident count; the article gives no perpetrators or dates of assaults. Article says MSF began in February 2025 and rehabilitated the Sake reference health centre 'lourdement endommagé par les combats'. MSF says it will refocus on Katoyi. MSF country coordinator Christine Januel quoted in the article.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-006.vn: Supported; the 10 400 psychological-support figure is on the page and now in the replacement excerpt. A care-provision count reported by MSF, not an incident count; no perpetrators or assault dates given. The article says MSF rehabilitated the Sake reference health centre, 'lourdement endommagé par les combats'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Plus de 10 300 survivantes de violences sexuelles ont bénéficié d’une prise en charge de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) à Sake, dans le territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu, au cours de 13 mois d’intervention.

Médecins sans frontières a annoncé le transfert de ses activités médicales à Sake à l’organisation Première Urgence Internationale (PUI), afin d’assurer la continuité des soins dans cette partie du Nord-Kivu.

Les équipes ont également soigné plus de 10 300 survivantes de violences sexuelles et apporté un soutien psychologique à plus de 10 400 autres. Suite à l’évolution du contexte, MSF passe le relais à PUI, qui assurera la continuité des soins à Sake.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.s: Enquete.cd reported that the 33rd Military Region spokesperson, Captain Dieudonné Kasereka, as cited by several Congolese media, confirmed on Sunday 4 October that twenty-nine fighters presented as belonging to the AFC-M23 laid down arms and surrendered to the FARDC and Wazalendo groups between 1 and 4 October 2026 in Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories; according to the military authorities, several of them were reportedly young recruits enrolled by force.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.l: Lubero, Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.a: FARDC and Wazalendo (recipients); AFC-M23 fighters (surrendering), as the FARDC says
r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.x: Enquete.cd: 29 surrendered; ten others captured with weapons at Remeka, Mohololo, Biriko and Miko
r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.n: FARDC account only; party claim, not independently verified (Top Africa News says independent verification remains limited). Radio Okapi 8 Oct credits the '34e région militaire' communication service for related statement: unit number differs between outlets. No AFC/M23 response found.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-007.vn: Forced-recruitment clause was attributed to Kasereka but the page attributes it to 'les autorités militaires' and in the conditional; narrowed. The page also reports ten further captures at Remeka, Mohololo, Biriko and Miko (in figures; not in any stored excerpt, so left out of the statement). FARDC account only, not independently verified; no AFC/M23 response found. Discrepancy: Enquete.cd names the 33rd Military Region, while Radio Okapi (8 Oct) credits the communication service of the 34th military region for the 4 October announcement of the 29 surrenders. Both stated as printed. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Enquete.cd (5 Oct 2026, Josué Kid, Kinshasa dateline) supports every clause, but says the spokesperson's confirmation was relayed 'cité par plusieurs médias congolais'; the statement dropped that second-hand sourcing, which is restored. 4 October 2026 is a Sunday.
src: L’information a été confirmée dimanche 4 octobre par le capitaine Dieudonné Kasereka, porte-parole de la 33ᵉ Région militaire, cité par plusieurs médias congolais.

vingt-neuf combattants présentés comme appartenant à l’AFC-M23 ont déposé les armes et se sont rendus aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ainsi qu’aux groupes Wazalendo entre le 1er et le 4 octobre 2026, dans les territoires de Lubero, Masisi et Walikale
D’après les autorités militaires, plusieurs des personnes concernées seraient de jeunes recrues enrôlées de force dans les rangs de l’AFC-M23.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-008.s: Top Africa News reported that African Union facilitators held closed-door talks with AFC/M23 leaders in Goma on Monday, meeting political coordinator Corneille Nangaa and his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict, and no joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-008.n: Page says 'on Monday' and is dated 6 Oct (published '3 weeks ago' as scraped); date computed from weekday and publication date: Monday 5 October. Search results also carried AFC/M23 posts dating the reception to 5 October 2026 (leads only). Delegation per Top Africa News: Kenyatta, Masisi, Zewde. Digest-style outlet; corroborate with Reuters/AFP or AU.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-008.vn: Supported; added the AFC/M23 leaders named in source 1 and moved the opening sentence into source 1's excerpt. Graded C: one digest outlet of uncertain independence, partisan quote. Single digest-style outlet ('We Digest News'); the page prints no date, only 'on Monday' and '3 weeks ago', so 5 Oct is computed from the URL date 2026/10/06 (approximate). Kanyuka's words are AFC/M23's account. Corroboration from AU or wire copy not found.
src: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the movement received the mission in the framework of efforts toward a political, durable and African-led resolution of the conflict. No joint communiqué or concrete agreements were announced after the meeting.

A delegation of former heads of state arrived in the North Kivu provincial capital, which has remained under AFC/M23 control since early 2025, and met the movement’s political coordinator, Corneille Nangaa, together with his deputies Bertrand Bisimwa and Freddy Kaniki.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-009.s: Tic-Tac Hebdo reported that AFC/M23 North Kivu governor Bahati Musanga Erasto signed communiqué n°01/007/CAB/GP-NK/2026 of 2 October, setting the Grande Barrière border post at Goma to open daily from 5 a.m. to 2 a.m. the following day; the document was circulated by Lawrence Kanyuka.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-009.l: Goma, North Kivu (Grande Barrière, Goma-Rubavu crossing)
r1-NKS-2026Q4-009.a: AFC/M23 provincial governorate of North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-009.n: Reported by a local outlet from a communiqué it says was circulated by Kanyuka; the document itself was not seen. Source type: media reporting a partisan (AFC/M23) document, cite for what the de facto authority decided only.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-009.vn: All clauses on the page; flagged '23' is from 'AFC/M23'. De facto authority's decision as reported by a local outlet; the communiqué itself was not retained.
src: À Goma, le communiqué officiel n°01/007/CAB/GP-NK/2026, daté du 2 octobre et signé par le gouverneur Bahati Musanga Erasto , fixe les nouveaux horaires de la Grande Barrière. La mesure entre en vigueur à compter de sa signature et prévoit une ouverture quotidienne de 5 h à 2 h du matin le lendemain, soit une plage de fonctionnement de 21 heures sur 24.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-010.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing several military sources, that the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition was said to have retaken the centre of Katoyi on Tuesday, but was said still to be struggling to retake Kasake, which was reportedly still occupied by AFC/M23 rebels.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-010.l: Katoyi and Kasake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-010.n: Masisi edge of the unit. Date computed from weekday (Tuesday) and publication date 2026-10-07 (article says 'depuis l'aube de ce mercredi'). Military-source claim only; no AFC/M23 account found.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-010.vn: Supported verbatim; Tuesday date computed (approximate already set). Military-source claim in the conditional. The same article says fighting was still concentrated around the centre of Katoyi from dawn on Wednesday 7 October, so control remained contested. No AFC/M23 account found.
src: Selon plusieurs sources militaires, la coalition FARDC-Wazalendo aurait repris mardi le centre de Katoyi. Toutefois, elle éprouverait encore des difficultés à reprendre l’agglomération de Kasake, qui serait toujours sous occupation des rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-011.s: Les Volcans News reported, according to local sources, that families displaced by armed clashes had taken refuge in Ngungu, Masisi territory, and that they said they had received no food aid since arrival and lacked sufficient means for medical care of their family members.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-011.l: Ngungu (Ufamandu 1er groupement), Masisi territory, North Kivu
