r1-NKS-2026Q4-011.n: Displaced people's self-report via a local outlet; health obstacle is lack of means, no actor blocking access is alleged. Category kept as displacement_humanitarian.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-011.vn: health 'access_denied' implied a denying actor the source does not allege, and the field applies only to health_care_access claims: cleared. Date is the publication date of an ongoing situation: approximate. Added the Ngungu refuge sentence to the excerpt. Self-reported situation; no actor is alleged to block access to care. The article also says several health facilities in the area were reportedly closed for lack of medicines (not in this claim). Date is the report date.
src: Depuis leur arrivée, elles déclarent n’avoir reçu aucune aide alimentaire et ne disposent pas de moyens suffisants pour assurer la prise en charge médicale des membres de leurs familles.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.s: Enquete.cd reported, citing journalist Daniel Michombero who cited the group's spokesperson, that three fighters of the 'FRN-M23-RDF coalition' were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement in Rutshuru territory (the article goes on to quote Me Héritier Gashegu); two bodyguards of the new commander were also killed and another fighter wounded; according to the same sources, a woman presented as the presumed wife of the commander, and her infant, reportedly also died, hit by gunfire during the attack.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.l: Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (exact place not stated)
r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.a: Wazalendo CMC/FDP (alleged by their own spokesperson)
r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.x: Enquete.cd (per CMC/FDP spokesperson via journalist): three coalition fighters killed; two bodyguards of the new commander also killed (the article does not say whether they are among the three); one fighter wounded; a woman and her infant reportedly killed
r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.n: Source is the Wazalendo's own spokesperson relayed by a journalist; the attack date is not stated in the article (reported 27 Oct; Kabizo named only in a reference to the Ruza killing). The coalition label 'FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's. Civilian deaths are unverified and no other party's account (FRN/AFC-M23, Rwanda) was found. Separate Rwandan outlets (Igihe, others in search results) reported five people killed at Kabizo on the night of 25-26 October, attributed to FDLR and Nyatura: page could not be fetched, so not cited; possible competing account of related events, lead only.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-012.vn: 'Were also killed' upgraded the source's conditional; figures 'incl. two bodyguards' was an inference; 'Kabizo area' is not where the article places the attack. Date set to month. Rests on the attacking group's own spokesperson relayed by a journalist; civilian deaths are in the conditional and unverified. Attack date and exact place not stated (reported 27 Oct). 'FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's label. No FRN/AFC-M23 or Rwandan account found; Rwandan outlets reportedly described killings at Kabizo on 25-26 Oct attributed to FDLR/Nyatura (not fetched; lead only). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: two bodyguards killed, another fighter wounded 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Me Héritier Gashegu quoted after the spokesperson reference 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-011: Search found a retained counter-account: the FRN-appointed administrator (a party) describes a CMC FDP/FDLR attack at Kabizo on 25-26 Oct as killing five civilians, whereas Enquete.cd, via the attacking group's spokesperson, describes coalition fighters killed. Re-reading the Enquete.cd page also gives the spokesperson's name. Both accounts are partisan; the amendment sets them side by side without merging them.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): two bodyguards killed, another fighter wounded; Me Héritier Gashegu quoted after the spokesperson reference | cut the Kivu Morning Post / Euphrem Kabasha counter-account of a Kabizo attack (25-26 Oct, five civilians killed) and the sentence on whether the two reports describe the same attack, because the claim cites no Kivu Morning Post page; the counter-account needs its own claim from that page. Softened 'Me Héritier Gashegu, per the article' as spokesperson: the page names the spokesperson and then quotes Gashegu but does not say in one passage that Gashegu is the spokesperson
src: D’après les mêmes sources, une femme, présentée comme l’épouse présumée du responsable, ainsi que son nourrisson auraient également perdu la vie, atteints par des tirs lors de l’attaque.

Trois combattants de la coalition FRN-M23-RDF ont été tués lors d’une attaque attribuée aux Wazalendo du mouvement CMC/FDP, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu. L’information a été rapportée par le journaliste Daniel Michombero, citant le porte-parole du groupe.
Deux gardes du corps du nouveau responsable ont également été tués au cours de l’attaque, tandis qu’un autre combattant a été blessé.
citant le porte-parole du groupe. Selon Me Héritier Gashegu

r1-NKS-2026Q4-013.s: Enquete.cd, relaying journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson, reported that three fighters of the FRN-M23-RDF coalition were killed in an attack attributed to the Wazalendo of the CMC/FDP movement; according to Me Héritier Gashegu, quoted in the article, one of the fighters killed had just been deployed to replace Nshimiye Kabo, described as head of the coalition's operations in that part of Rutshuru territory, who had been killed on 16 October at Ruza, about six kilometres from Kabizo.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-013.l: Ruza, about six km from Kabizo, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-013.a: not attributed by the source (killing of Nshimiye Kabo); speaker Me Héritier Gashegu
r1-NKS-2026Q4-013.n: Single partisan-sourced (Wazalendo spokesperson) report; no independent confirmation found. Not clear from the article whether Gashegu speaks for the CMC/FDP.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-013.vn: Actor field implied the Wazalendo killed Kabo; the source does not attribute that killing. Statement itself is supported. Single partisan-side source; the article does not say who killed Nshimiye Kabo, nor state Gashegu's role. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: relay via journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson; attack attributed to the CMC/FDP; FRN-M23-RDF coalition 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: The page does state Gashegu's role: he is the spokesperson of the CMC/FDP group that carried out the attack, relayed via a journalist, so this is a party-says account (the attacking side) and should read as such. 'Coalition FRN-M23-RDF' is the outlet's/speaker's label. A search for "Nshimiye Kabo" found nothing independent; who killed Kabo remains unstated. Grade C appropriate.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): relay via journalist Daniel Michombero citing the group's spokesperson; attack attributed to the CMC/FDP; FRN-M23-RDF coalition | cut the identification of Me Héritier Gashegu as the spokesperson (the page does not print it in one passage; it names 'le porte-parole du groupe' and then quotes Gashegu)
src: Selon Me Héritier Gashegu, l’un des combattants tués venait d’être déployé dans cette zone pour remplacer Nshimiye Kabo, responsable des opérations de la coalition dans cette partie du territoire. Ce dernier avait été tué le 16 octobre dernier à Ruza, à environ six kilomètres de Kabizo.

Trois combattants de la coalition FRN-M23-RDF ont été tués lors d’une attaque attribuée aux Wazalendo du mouvement CMC/FDP, dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu. L’information a été rapportée par le journaliste Daniel Michombero, citant le porte-parole du groupe.

r1-NKS-2026Q4-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced the surrender of seventeen fighters of the AFC-M23/Twirwaneho coalition in Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that operation Sokola 2 Sud-Kivu spokesperson Sub-Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi said one of them was a young civilian who had been kidnapped and forcibly recruited in Goma, North Kivu, by the M23; the army also said several children aged 14 to 16 were among the 17.
r1-NKS-2026Q4-014.l: Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja, Fizi territory, South Kivu (abduction in Goma, North Kivu)
r1-NKS-2026Q4-014.x: Radio Okapi (FARDC): 17 surrendered, children aged 14 to 16 among them; one more captured in fighting
r1-NKS-2026Q4-014.n: Event in Fizi (South Kivu), kept here because the alleged abduction/recruitment took place in Goma; Fizi unit should integrate. FARDC account only; no AFC-M23/Twirwaneho response found. Page labelled 'Publié le mer, 07/10/2026'; title in the page differs slightly (AFC-M23/Twiraneho).
r1-NKS-2026Q4-014.vn: Supported; dates and places of surrender are on the page but not in the stored excerpts, so moved to the note; date field 2026-10-06 is printed on the page. FARDC account only; no AFC-M23/Twirwaneho response found. The article says the FARDC announced on Wednesday 7 October surrenders on Tuesday 6 October at Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja in the Fizi highlands; its body spells 'Twiraneho' (title and tag 'Twirwaneho'). Event is in Fizi (South Kivu); the Fizi unit should integrate it. The same article credits the 34th military region for the 4 Oct announcement of 29 surrenders (cf. Enquete.cd's '33rd'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 7 Oct 2026 (modified 8 Oct): FARDC announced on 7 Oct the surrender on 6 Oct of 17 AFC-M23/Twirwaneho fighters in the Fizi highlands (at Abala, Nyaruhinga and Kabanja); spokesperson Reagan Mbuyi's account of the kidnapped civilian and the army's mention of children aged 14-16 match. The stored excerpts did not carry the announcement or Fizi, so the lead sentence is added.
src: Le sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, porte-parole de l’opération Sokola 2 Sud-Kivu, affirme que parmi les combattants qui se sont rendus figure un jeune civil qui avait été kidnappé puis recruté de force à Goma, au Nord-Kivu, par le M23.
L’armée déplore également la présence de plusieurs enfants âgés de 14 à 16 ans parmi les 17 combattants qui se sont rendus.

Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé, mercredi 7 octobre, la reddition de dix-sept combattants de la coalition AFC-M23/Twiraneho mardi 6 octobre dans les Hauts Plateaux du territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-NKW-2025H1-001.s: The news site reported that FARDC-Wazalendo coalition elements recovered Masisi-Centre from the M23/RDF rebels on Wednesday 8 January 2025 after a counter-offensive; the president of the Masisi territory civil society confirmed this to the outlet and said fighting continued around the town.
r1-NKW-2025H1-001.n: Conflicts with the UN Group of Experts claim (draft r1/GOE#70, r1/UC-BI-FDLR#18) that AFC/M23 and RDF took Masisi centre on 4 January 2025 and retained it despite repeated Wazalendo/FARDC attempts. 7sur7 relays civil society and unnamed official confirmation; Radio Okapi 3 April 2025 says M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu for months. Surfaced, not resolved.
r1-NKW-2025H1-001.vn: Excerpt real and on-event; statement narrowed to name the civil-society speaker the page prints and to place the 'fighting continues' clause with him. 7sur7 says unnamed official sources confirmed but gave no comment; not used. Single local outlet, contradicted by other sources: C. The civil-society president is named on the page as Voltaire Batundi Sadiki. Contested: the UN Group of Experts and BBC Afrique (4 January) report M23 capture of Masisi, and Radio Okapi (3 April) says M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu for several months. Accounts recorded separately, not resolved.
src: Les éléments de la coalition FARDC-Wazalendo ont récupéré Masisi-Centre des mains des rebelles du M23/RDF dans le territoire de Masisi en province du Nord-Kivu, le mercredi 08 janvier 2025.

r1-NKW-2025H1-002.s: The news site reported that Guillaume Ndjike Kaiko, spokesperson of the military governor of North Kivu, announced on his X account on Tuesday evening that the Tuesday counter-offensive had allowed FARDC-Wazalendo to recover several localities from the enemy, which suffered heavy losses, without naming the localities.
r1-NKW-2025H1-002.l: North Kivu (Masisi territory localities, not named)
r1-NKW-2025H1-002.n: Statement was reported as posted on X by the spokesperson (per 7sur7); post not independently opened. Localities not named. Date: the Tuesday before 9 Jan 2025 = 7 Jan.
r1-NKW-2025H1-002.vn: Excerpt real; added the page's own framing (X post, Tuesday evening, localities not named). Date computed from weekday, so precision set to approximate. Party claim of enemy losses stays attributed. Party statement (FARDC) as relayed by 7sur7.cd; the X post itself was not opened. Date 7 January computed from 'mardi dernier' relative to the 9 January article.
src: « La contre-offensive de mardi a permis aux FARDC-Wazalendo de récupérer plusieurs localités de l'ennemi qui a enregistré plusieurs pertes importantes », a mentionné Guillaume Ndjike Kaiko, porte-parole du gouverneur militaire de la province du Nord-Kivu.

r1-NKW-2025H1-003.s: The news site reported that, according to first accounts, a bomb reportedly came from the rebel zone during fighting in the heights of Sake, where FARDC and presumed rebels had been clashing since the morning, and that its sources on the spot said the explosion killed three civilians; the local civil society said the bomb struck them in their house.
r1-NKW-2025H1-003.a: Bomb attributed by witnesses to the rebel (M23) zone; not otherwise attributed
r1-NKW-2025H1-003.n: Single local outlet; victims not named; perpetrator attribution is 'according to first accounts', 'would have come'.
r1-NKW-2025H1-003.vn: Split the attributions as the page does: origin of the bomb = first accounts (conditional), deaths = sources on the spot, 'in their house' = local civil society quote. Victims not named. Single local outlet: C.
src: Selon les premiers témoignages, cette bombe serait venue de la zone rebelle alors que des combats se concentrent dans les hauteurs de la cité de Sake, faisant craindre une escalade de la violence. Nos sources sur place affirment que l'explosion a malheureusement coûté la vie à trois civils.

r1-NKW-2025H1-004.s: BBC News Afrique reported that the M23 rebellion took control of Masisi, about 80 km north of Goma, on Saturday, and, citing Radio Okapi, that the army and its Wazalendo allies had retaken the town of Ngungu in Masisi territory.
r1-NKW-2025H1-004.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (Saturday before 6 Jan 2025 = 4 Jan). Page text mixes a Reuters-attributed passage; not relied on. Consistent with UN GoE 4 Jan claim; 7sur7 reports FARDC recapture 8 Jan (see separate claim).
r1-NKW-2025H1-004.vn: Dropped the 'a few days earlier' timing: the page says Okapi reported it 'yesterday' in an article updated later, so the relative order is not fixed. Parts of the page quote Reuters; the Masisi sentence carries no credit, so credited to BBC. Date approximate as flagged. The page is a running explainer published 6 January and updated 23 January 2025; 'samedi' is read as 4 January from the publication date (approximate). The Ngungu passage says Okapi reported it 'hier' without a fixed reference date, so its timing is not given. Contested with 7sur7's 8 January FARDC-Wazalendo recapture claim.
src: La rébellion du M23, le groupe armé soutenu par le Rwanda qui dément ce soutien , a pris le contrôle samedi de Masisi, Masisi est située à environ 80 km au nord de Goma, la capitale de la province du Nord-Kivu

r1-NKW-2025H1-005.s: Human Rights Watch reported that, after it captured Masisi in January, the M23 ordered two displacement sites dismantled, according to a humanitarian source.
r1-NKW-2025H1-005.n: Single anonymous humanitarian source relayed by HRW; sites not named.
r1-NKW-2025H1-005.vn: Verbatim on the HRW page; attribution to a humanitarian source kept. Single credible NGO relaying one anonymous source: B.
src: After it captured Masisi in January, the M23 ordered two displacement sites dismantled, a humanitarian source said.

r1-NKW-2025H1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing witnesses, that Walikale's general hospital and an NGO logistics base were damaged during the fighting, causing deaths and injuries, after the Walikale area passed under rebel occupation.
r1-NKW-2025H1-006.n: Corroborates MSF's account (existing r1-HC-NK-2025-006) that crossfire hit its base on 19 March; Radio Okapi does not name the NGO. Perpetrator not attributed.
r1-NKW-2025H1-006.vn: Excerpt real and on-event (hospital = Walikale hospital named in the prior sentence). Perpetrator unattributed as in the source. The MSF corroboration cited in the draft notes is not in this packet, so graded on its own source: single outlet relaying witnesses, C. The source does not say who caused the damage, nor name the NGO. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Cet hôpital général et une base logistique d'une ONG ont été endommagés lors des combats, entraînant des morts et des blessés, selon des témoins.

Fiston Misona, a civil society activist in Walikale, told the Reuters news agency: “The rebels are now visible in the centre of the city. There are at least seven people wounded who are at the general hospital.”

r1-NKW-2025H1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that on the same Thursday scenes of looting were reported in the mining centres of Mubi and Ndjingala, while gunfire continued to be heard.
r1-NKW-2025H1-007.l: Mubi and Ndjingala mining centres, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-007.n: Single local outlet; perpetrator not named.
r1-NKW-2025H1-007.vn: The page does not say who reported the looting ('ont été signalées'); removed 'citing local sources'. Perpetrator not named by the source.
src: Par ailleurs, ce même jeudi, des scènes de pillage ont été signalées dans les centres miniers de Mubi et Ndjingala, tandis que des crépitements de balles continuaient d'être entendus.

r1-NKW-2025H1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that FARDC soldiers and their Wazalendo allies were reported to have fallen back toward Mubi-Lubutu on the road to Kisangani.
r1-NKW-2025H1-008.a: M23 (supported by the Rwandan army, per Radio Okapi)
r1-NKW-2025H1-008.n: Hedged ('se seraient repliés'). The page also says M23 had a few days earlier attacked Kashebere and Kibati before the final assault.
r1-NKW-2025H1-008.vn: Verbatim; hedge ('se seraient repliés') kept as 'were reported to have'. Single outlet, conditional: C (draft B lowered).
src: Les militaires des FARDC et leurs alliés les Wazalendo, se seraient repliés vers Mubi-Lubutu, sur la route menant à Kisangani (Tshopo).

r1-NKW-2025H1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the population, armed men in military uniform carried out systematic looting in several villages, including Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana and Kangama in Walikale territory.
r1-NKW-2025H1-009.l: Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana, Kangama, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-009.a: armed men in military uniform (not further attributed by the source)
r1-NKW-2025H1-009.n: Single local outlet; no unit attributed. Complements existing Radio Okapi hospital-looting claims (r1-HC-NK-2025-007/008).
r1-NKW-2025H1-009.vn: Verbatim, attributed to the population. The page gives no date for the looting, so precision set to approximate. The source does not date the looting; 2025-03-21 is the report date.
src: Parallèlement, la population dénonce des pillages systématiques perpétrés par des hommes armés en tenue militaire dans plusieurs villages et agglomérations de la région, notamment à Mubi, Ndjingala, Logu, Biruwe, Makana et Kangama, jusqu'à la limite entre le Nord-Kivu et la province du Maniema.

r1-NKW-2025H1-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that six days after its announced withdrawal, the AFC/M23 was still present in Walikale's chef-lieu.
r1-NKW-2025H1-010.l: Walikale chef-lieu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-010.n: Consistent with Kanyuka's 24 March communiqué (existing claims) that withdrawal was blocked by FARDC drones and aircraft; GoE places withdrawal in early April. Note Okapi's page says the announcement was 'six days' earlier (22 March).
r1-NKW-2025H1-010.vn: Verbatim outlet narration; page dates the withdrawal announcement to Saturday 22 March 2025.
src: Au sixième jour après l'annonce de son retrait, l'AFC/M23 est toujours présent dans le chef-lieu du territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2025H1-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the compound of Walikale general referral hospital, which already held more than 600 displaced households, recorded an influx of new households, and that hospital sources said the assistance of MSF Holland could not cover needs.
r1-NKW-2025H1-011.l: Walikale general referral hospital, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-011.x: Radio Okapi: more than 600 displaced households already in the hospital compound
r1-NKW-2025H1-011.n: Figure is the outlet's, from hospital sources. A second passage on the page attributes the MSF shortfall to 'certaines sources de l'hôpital'.
r1-NKW-2025H1-011.vn: Both clauses on the page; MSF shortfall attributed to hospital sources as stated.
src: L'enceinte de l'hôpital général de référence de Walikale, qui comptait déjà plus de 600 ménages de personnes déplacées, enregistre un afflux de nouveaux ménages fuyant vers la brousse autour de la cité.

r1-NKW-2025H1-012.s: A statement from the office of the government spokesperson of Rwanda said Rwanda welcomed M23's announcement on the repositioning of its forces from Walikale in support of peace initiatives underway, as well as the DRC's announcement that all offensive operations by FARDC and Wazalendo would be halted.
r1-NKW-2025H1-012.l: Walikale, North Kivu (statement issued from Kigali)
r1-NKW-2025H1-012.n: Rwandan state source cited only for what Rwanda said; Xinhua (Chinese state agency) confirms the Sunday (23 March) statement. Date 23 March from the gov.rw listing and Xinhua 'Sunday'. Note Rwanda denies supporting M23 in other statements; this statement does not address it.
r1-NKW-2025H1-012.vn: Removed the date from the statement (the English page prints none; the date is in the date field). Speaker attribution rests on Xinhua. Xinhua is a relay of the Rwandan statement, not independent of it. Partisan source: recorded only as what the Government of Rwanda said. The English post carries no date; 23 March comes from Xinhua's 'on Sunday' (article of Tuesday 25 March) and the dated French and Kinyarwanda versions listed on gov.rw.
src: Rwanda welcomes M23's announcement on the repositioning of its forces from Walikale in support of peace initiatives underway, as well as DRC's announcement that all offensive operations by FARDC and Wazalendo will be halted.

Rwanda on Sunday welcomed the March 23 Movement (M23) rebel group's decision to withdraw from Walikale town, which it seized earlier in the week, as well as the Congolese government's decision to de-escalate hostilities in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).

r1-NKW-2025H1-013.s: Xinhua reported that, in response to the AFC announcement, the Congolese military urged Congolese self-defence forces to de-escalate the same day, stressing the need to prioritise peace talks and advance the Luanda and Nairobi dialogue processes.
r1-NKW-2025H1-013.n: Relays the FARDC statement without naming the speaker; existing KMP claim (r1-ST-M23-2025-018) records the FARDC 24 March position. Xinhua is a state agency.
r1-NKW-2025H1-013.vn: Verbatim; date computed from 'Saturday' relative to the 25 March article, so approximate. Xinhua does not name the speaker or quote the FARDC text; 'the same day' refers to the Saturday (22 March) AFC announcement.
src: In response, the Congolese military urged Congolese self-defense forces to de-escalate on the same day, emphasizing the need to prioritize peace talks and advance the Luanda and Nairobi dialogue processes.

r1-NKW-2025H1-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in villages around the Masisi chef-lieu, near Kanii on Thursday, left residents hiding; some sources said Wazalendo launched an offensive to dislodge the M23, others a M23 counter-offensive against Wazalendo coming from the Nyabiondo axis.
r1-NKW-2025H1-014.l: Kanii and Masisi-centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-014.a: M23 and Wazalendo (as the source says)
r1-NKW-2025H1-014.n: Contested account of who attacked; no toll available per the source. Also states M23 had occupied the Masisi chef-lieu 'for several months', which conflicts with the 7sur7 8 Jan claim of an FARDC recapture.
r1-NKW-2025H1-014.vn: All clauses on the page; competing accounts kept separate. Who attacked is contested between sources on the page; no toll was available.
src: Certaines sources indiquent que les combattants Wazalendo ont lancé une offensive contre les rebelles du M23 pour tenter de les déloger du chef-lieu du territoire de Masisi, qu’ils occupent depuis plusieurs mois.
D’autres sources parlent d’une contre-offensive des rebelles du M23 contre les Wazalendo venus de l’axe Nyabiondo, menaçant leurs positions à Masisi-centre depuis lundi.

r1-NKW-2025H1-015.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that M23 rebels took Kilambo (Buabo grouping, south of Masisi chef-lieu) at the end of the previous week and were attacked by Wazalendo on Tuesday 15 April, and reported that on the morning of Wednesday 16 April the rebels were counter-attacking to reoccupy the whole area.
r1-NKW-2025H1-015.l: Kilambo, Buabo grouping, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-015.n: Local outlet only. Capture date is 'end of last week' (about 11-13 April). Residents fled toward Nyamaboko.
r1-NKW-2025H1-015.vn: All clauses on the page; capture date approximate as the draft says. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 16 Apr 2025. The capture and the 15 April Wazalendo attack are attributed to local sources; the Wednesday-morning counter-offensive is in Radio Okapi's own voice and was not in the stored excerpt. Passage added and attribution separated. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 16 Apr 2025. The capture and the 15 April Wazalendo attack are attributed to local sources; the Wednesday-morning counter-offensive is in Radio Okapi's own voice and was not in the stored excerpt. Passage added and attribution separated.
src: Selon des sources locales, les rebelles du M23 se sont emparés de Kilambo à la fin de la semaine dernière. Mardi 15 avril, ils ont été attaqués par les Wazalendo, provoquant une riposte violente.
Ce mercredi matin, les rebelles mènent une contre-offensive dans le but de réoccuper entièrement la zone.

r1-NKW-2025H1-016.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) attacked M23 positions at Buleusa, Walikale territory, around 6 a.m. on Thursday 17 April, a locality occupied by the M23 for several months.
r1-NKW-2025H1-016.n: The page adds that about half the population had fled toward Pinga and southern Lubero. Local outlet only; no toll.
r1-NKW-2025H1-016.vn: Removed the year, which the passage does not print (it is the page's publication date). Otherwise verbatim.
ent: Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC)
src: De violents affrontements ont opposé, ce jeudi 17 avril au matin, les rebelles du M23 aux combattants Wazalendo du groupe Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) à Buleusa, dans le territoire de Walikale au Nord-Kivu. Selon des sources locales, les combattants du CMC ont attaqué les positions des rebelles du M23 aux alentours de 6 heures locales, dans cette localité occupée par ces derniers depuis plusieurs mois.

r1-NKW-2025H1-017.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the villages of Bibatama, Luke and Mungote in Masisi territory were the scene of violent clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters for almost all of Sunday, and that hundreds of residents fled.
r1-NKW-2025H1-017.l: Bibatama, Luke, Mungote, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-017.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (published 21 April, Monday; Sunday = 20 April). No toll available per the source.
r1-NKW-2025H1-017.vn: All clauses on the page; date approximate as in draft. Article published Monday 21 April 2025 (modified 22 April); 'dimanche' = 20 April, computed.
src: Selon des sources locales, les villages Bibatama (groupement Kibabi 2), Luke (groupement Nyamaboko 2) et Mungote (groupement Kibabi 2) ont été, presque toute la journée de dimanche, le théâtre de violents combats.
Les affrontements y ont opposé les rebelles du M23 aux combattants Wazalendo.
Selon plusieurs sources, des centaines d’habitants ont fui leurs villages.

r1-NKW-2025H1-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that local sources denounced extortion of residents of Ufamandu 2 by fighters of the group Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, 'd'un certain Noah Maachano', who were said to be imposing since the previous week a parallel tax of 10 000 Congolese francs (3.5 USD) per household.
r1-NKW-2025H1-018.a: Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, of 'un certain Noah Maachano' (as the source prints it)
r1-NKW-2025H1-018.x: Radio Okapi: 10 000 Congolese francs (3.5 USD) per household
r1-NKW-2025H1-018.n: Single local outlet; hedged ('imposeraient'). The source does not label the group Wazalendo. Date: published 21-22 April, 'since last week'.
r1-NKW-2025H1-018.vn: Verbatim; conditional kept. Name spelled as the source prints it; being named is not a finding of responsibility. Allegation is conditional ('imposeraient'). 2026-10-28: source 0 date edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi page carries the statement verbatim, conditional kept ('imposeraient'). The page is dated 'Publié le lun, 21/04/2025 - 23:01' although the URL path says 2025/04/22; source date corrected to 2025-04-21.
ent: Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo
src: Pendant ce temps, ces sources dénoncent le rançonnement des habitants d’Ufamandu 2 par les combattants du groupe Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo, d’un certain Noah Maachano. Ces derniers imposeraient, depuis la semaine dernière, une taxe parallèle de 10 000 francs congolais (3.5 USD) par ménage.

r1-NKW-2025H1-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out on Friday 25 April between M23 rebels and APCLS Wazalendo fighters in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory despite the truce declared at Doha; sources at Nyabiondo-Centre said the rebels reportedly launched simultaneous attacks on Wazalendo positions around 5 a.m., while other sources said APCLS fighters were the first to open fire on M23 positions.
r1-NKW-2025H1-019.l: Kinyumba, Burubi, Kibanda, Kikomo, Kasopo (Osso Banyungu sector), Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-019.n: Contested account of who opened fire. The page spells the group 'APCLC' once and 'APCLS' elsewhere. Families sheltered at the MSF base and Nyabiondo hospital per the page. Local outlet only.
r1-NKW-2025H1-019.vn: Nyabiondo sources say the rebels 'auraient lancé simultanément leurs attaques', not that they attacked first; reworded with the conditional. Removed the year the passages do not print. The page spells the group 'APCLC' in its lead and 'APCLS' later. Who fired first is contested between sources.
src: Des combats ont éclaté ce vendredi 25 avril entre les rebelles du M23 et les combattants Wazalendo de l'APCLC dans le secteur d'Osso Banyungu, territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu, malgré la trêve déclarée à Doha entre Kinshasa et le M23/AFC
Selon des sources à Nyabiondo-Centre, les rebelles auraient lancé simultanément leurs attaques sur les positions des Wazalendo vers 5 heures du matin, ce vendredi.
D'autres sources affirment que les combattants de l'APCLS ont été les premiers à ouvrir le feu sur les positions du M23.

r1-NKW-2025H1-020.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to other sources, the rebels were also said to have repositioned at Kibati, Walikale territory, where they set up forward positions after withdrawing from Walikale, and that a local notable said their objective would be to conquer all of Masisi and retake control of the chef-lieu of Walikale territory.
r1-NKW-2025H1-020.l: Kibati, Walikale territory, and Nyabiondo, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-020.n: Hedged ('se seraient'). Page continues: a local notable says their aim is to conquer all of Masisi and retake Walikale chef-lieu (opinion, not cited). Complements the 26 April claim that M23 pulled back from Kibati.
r1-NKW-2025H1-020.vn: Added the page's attribution ('d'après d'autres sources') carried into the Kibati sentence ('Ils se seraient également'). The '23' flag is from 'M23'. The notable's statement is an opinion about intent, not an observed fact. A 26 April Okapi report says M23 withdrew from Kibati on the night of 25 April.
src: Ils se seraient également repositionnés à Kibati, en territoire de Walikale, où ils ont installé des positions avancées après s'être retirés de Walikale.
Un notable local indique que leur objectif serait de conquérir tout le Masisi et de reprendre le contrôle du chef-lieu du territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2025H1-021.s: Radio Okapi reported that Wazalendo fighters of the Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS) retook the villages of Kasopo, Lushali and Burubi in Masisi territory after violent clashes with the M23 on Friday 25 April; that, according to local sources at Nyabiondo, Kinyumba remained under rebel occupation; and that the same sources said M23 withdrew from its forward position at Kibati (Walikale territory) on the night of Friday 25 April, falling back toward Kashebere, 15 km away.
r1-NKW-2025H1-021.l: Kasopo, Lushali, Burubi, Kinyumba (Masisi); Kibati, Kashebere (Walikale)
r1-NKW-2025H1-021.n: Local sources at Nyabiondo only; no M23 or FARDC account found.
r1-NKW-2025H1-021.vn: Draft dated the recapture to 25 April 2025; the page only says it followed the 25 April clashes. Narrowed; removed the year the passages do not print. The page does not give the exact day the villages were retaken; it follows the 25 April clashes and was reported on 26 April. No M23 or FARDC account found.
ent: Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS)
src: Les combattants Wazalendo de l’Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS) ont repris le contrôle des villages de Kasopo, Lushali et Burubi dans le territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu.

Les mêmes sources rapportent également que les rebelles du M23 se sont retirés de leur position avancée à Kibati, en territoire de Walikale, dans la nuit du vendredi 25 avril. Ils se sont repliés vers Kashebere, à 15 km de Kibati, laissant ce dernier village vide de toute présence armée.

r1-NKW-2025H1-022.s: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 19 March 2025 the M23 took control of Walikale town and withdrew from it shortly afterwards, while peace-negotiation initiatives were under way in Qatar and Washington.
r1-NKW-2025H1-022.l: Walikale town, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-022.n: The report does not date the withdrawal; GoE (existing claim) puts it in early April after FARDC airstrikes, and Radio Okapi on 27 March says M23 was still in the chef-lieu.
r1-NKW-2025H1-022.vn: Verbatim in paragraph 19 of S/2025/403 (the PDF text has a stray space in 's ’est'). UN report: A. The report does not date the withdrawal.
src: Le 19 mars, le M23 a pris le contrôle de la ville de Walikale et s’est retiré de la localité peu de temps après, alors que des initiatives de négociations de paix avaient lieu au Qatar et à Washington.

r1-NKW-2025H1-023.s: The UN Secretary-General reported that on 2 May 2025 the M23 clashed with the FARDC as it expanded west into Lubero, toward the shores of Lake Edward, and that in mid-May the group resumed its expansion in the northern part of Walikale territory.
r1-NKW-2025H1-023.l: Northern Walikale territory and Lubero, North Kivu
r1-NKW-2025H1-023.n: Lubero lies outside this unit; recorded for context. The report adds in its following sentence that the northward expansion was halted by increased FARDC and UPDF deployments around Lubero under Operation Shujaa.
r1-NKW-2025H1-023.vn: Verbatim in paragraph 19 of S/2025/403. UN report: A. The report adds that the northward expansion was then halted by increased FARDC and UPDF deployments around Lubero under Operation Shujaa.
src: Le 2 mai, le M23 a affronté les FARDC alors qu’il s’étendait vers l’ouest à Lubero, en direction des rives du lac Édouard, et à la mi-mai, le groupe a repris son expansion dans la partie nord du territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2025H2-001.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil sources, that between 200 and 400 young people, including some secondary pupils, were seized by the AFC-M23 rebels in a cordon operation on Wednesday 5 November and taken to the Materdei parish compound in Masisi; the local sources described it as forced recruitment, while the report said there had been no communication about the operation on the movement's digital platforms.
r1-NKW-2025H2-001.n: Single local-source report; mentions AFC-M23 had not communicated on the operation. Date: 'mercredi 5 novembre' stated in page.
r1-NKW-2025H2-001.vn: Excerpt real and on-event. Day number and 'M23' removed from the statement because the stored excerpt does not print them; date 2025-11-05 and actor AFC-M23 rest on page passages in clause_support. The page also says those rounded up included minors ('jeunes mineurs et adultes confondus'). Allegation by local sources; no AFC-M23 account found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Nov 2025: civil sources report the cordon operation of Wednesday 5 Nov and 200-400 youths taken to Materdei parish; the page says only that there was no communication about the operation on the AFC-M23's digital platforms, which the statement widens. Excerpts for the cordon and no-communication clauses added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Nov 2025: civil sources report the cordon operation of Wednesday 5 Nov and 200-400 youths taken to Materdei parish; the page says only that there was no communication about the operation on the AFC-M23's digital platforms, which the statement widens. Excerpts for the cordon and no-communication clauses added. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Nov 2025: civil sources report the cordon operation of Wednesday 5 Nov and 200-400 youths taken to Materdei parish; the page says only that there was no communication about the operation on the AFC-M23's digital platforms, which the statement widens. Excerpts for the cordon and no-communication clauses added.
src: Entre 200 et 400 jeunes, parmi lesquels quelques élèves du secondaire, ont été saisis et conduits dans l’enceinte de la paroisse Materdei de Masisi. Alors que les raisons de ces interpellations en masse restent non élucidées, ces sources locales crient au recrutement forcé.
Selon des sources locales, ces jeunes ont été capturés lors d’une opération de bouclage, mercredi 5 novembre, dans différents quartiers et villages autour de Masisi-Centre.
Il n’y a jusqu’à présent aucune communication concernant cette opération sur différentes plateformes numériques du mouvement AFC-M23, qui contrôle la région.

r1-NKW-2025H2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Wednesday the wazalendo, withdrawing from Ihula and Ibuga (Kisimba grouping, Walikale) after clashes with AFC/M23, took away five people they accuse of collaborating with the AFC/M23 rebels; the fate of these hostages remained unknown.
r1-NKW-2025H2-002.n: Single outlet citing its sources; the page's own typo 'les ils' kept verbatim. Same page: residents fleeing to the bush, villages still held by AFC/M23.
r1-NKW-2025H2-002.vn: Supported; day number removed from statement (not in excerpt), date kept in date field from page passage. The five people are not named on the page.
src: Après ces affrontements, les wazalendo se sont retirés de ces entités. Mais au cours de leur retrait, les ils ont emporté cinq personnes qu'ils accusent de collaborer avec les rebelles de l'AFC/M23. Le sort de ces otages demeure inconnu jusqu'à présent.

r1-NKW-2025H2-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Tuesday the rebels and wazalendo clashed at Mpombi (Banakindi locality, Kisimba grouping, Walikale); after a tense day the wazalendo pushed the rebels back towards Mpety, their main stronghold around Pinga, and Mpombi and its surroundings remained in wazalendo hands.
r1-NKW-2025H2-003.l: Mpombi, Banakindi, Kisimba grouping (Walikale); Mpety; Pinga
r1-NKW-2025H2-003.n: Single outlet. Context: rebels from Mpety tried to bypass FARDC/wazalendo positions on Mpety-Pinga axis towards Pinga.
r1-NKW-2025H2-003.vn: Supported; day number and 'M23' removed from statement (not printed by the stored excerpt); both on the page (clause_support).
src: Après une journée tendue, les wazalendo ont repoussé les rebelles vers Mpety, leur principal bastion dans la zone autour de Pinga. Mpombi et ses environs restent toujours entre les mains des wazalendo.

r1-NKW-2025H2-004.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that during fighting in Nyamaboko (Osso-Banyungu, Masisi), in which Ngululu and Kataandwa were particularly affected, the Wazalendo occupied the village of Mulema while AFC/M23 took control of the village of Karere, about 3 km from the centre of Kazinga.
r1-NKW-2025H2-004.l: Mulema and Karere, near Kazinga, Osso-Banyungu (Masisi)
r1-NKW-2025H2-004.n: Single outlet. Same page: at Mwesso AFC/M23 fired in the air after the death of one of their officers in a Wazalendo ambush on the Mokoto–Kibarizo axis; a civil was wounded by a stray bullet at Mbuhi (separate claim).
r1-NKW-2025H2-004.vn: Supported; day number removed (date field carries it from the page). The page calls Nyamaboko a sector and Osso-Banyungu a grouping; kept as printed.
src: Selon des sources locales, les localités de Ngululu et Kataandwa ont particulièrement subi les affrontements, avec des avancées signalées des deux camps : les Wazalendo ont occupé le village de Mulema, tandis que l’AFC/M23 a pris le contrôle du village de Karere, situé à environ 3 kilomètres du centre de Kazinga.

r1-NKW-2025H2-005.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that at Mwesso, during an agitated night before Wednesday morning, AFC/M23 rebels fired in the air after learning of the death of one of their officers, killed in an ambush set by the Wazalendo on the Mokoto–Kibarizo axis, and that during this firing a civilian was wounded by a stray bullet at Mbuhi.
r1-NKW-2025H2-005.n: Single outlet; stray bullet, not targeted.
r1-NKW-2025H2-005.vn: Draft dated the firing 12 November; page places it in the night before the Wednesday morning, so date widened to a range and day number removed. Stray bullet, not reported as a targeted attack. The firing took place during the night before Wednesday 12 November. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 12 Nov 2025: the Mwesso firing and the stray-bullet wounding end with 'selon des sources concordantes'; the statement drops that attribution, restored here.
src: Des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont tiré en l’air après avoir appris le décès de l’un de leurs officiers, tué lors d’une embuscade tendue par les Wazalendo sur l’axe Mokoto–Kibarizo. Lors de ces tirs, un civil a été blessé par une balle perdue à Mbuhi

r1-NKW-2025H2-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that clashes broke out early on Monday between the rebels and Wazalendo in Masisi, beginning around 5:30 at Ngululu (Osso Banyungu sector, Nyamaboko grouping); according to local sources the rebels allegedly attacked positions of Wazalendo elements, notably the APCLS led by Janvier Karairi, and fighting spread to Mikeno (Mufuni-Shanga grouping), with residents fleeing towards Walikale territory. No official toll was communicated.
r1-NKW-2025H2-006.l: Ngululu and Mikeno, Osso Banyungu / Mufuni-Shanga (Masisi)
r1-NKW-2025H2-006.n: Single outlet; no casualty figure communicated per the page.
r1-NKW-2025H2-006.vn: Supported; 'M23' and day number removed from statement because the stored excerpt lacks them (clause_support carries them). Conditional 'auraient attaqué' kept as 'allegedly'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Oct 2025, carries every clause; the stored excerpt lacks the spread to Mikeno, the flight to Walikale and the no-toll clause, added here.
ent: Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS)
src: Selon des sources locales, les hostilités ont débuté vers 5h30 dans le village de Ngululu, situé dans le secteur Osso Banyungu, groupement Nyamaboko. Les rebelles auraient attaqué les positions tenues par des éléments Wazalendo, notamment ceux de l’Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS), dirigée par Janvier Karairi.

Les combats se sont rapidement étendus au village de Mikeno, dans le groupement voisin de Mufuni-Shanga, en chefferie des Bahunde. Cette reprise des violences provoque de nouveaux déplacements de population, plusieurs habitants fuyant vers le territoire de Walikale, jugé plus sûr. Pour l’heure, aucun bilan officiel n’a été communiqué

r1-NKW-2025H2-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to concordant sources, AFC-M23 rebels, described as supported by Rwanda, were fighting the VDP/Wazalendo of the group PARECO/FF in Ufamandu 2 (Katoyi sector, Masisi) on Saturday; the fighting began around 07 hours local time when M23 rebels attacked Wazalendo positions at Kahunda and Mitimingi, and residents fled towards Walikale territory or into the forest.
r1-NKW-2025H2-007.l: Kahunda and Mitimingi, Ufamandu 2, Katoyi sector (Masisi)
r1-NKW-2025H2-007.n: Title truncated in search snippet; title as inferred from URL slug and page. Casualties unknown per page. 'supported by Rwanda' is the outlet's wording.
r1-NKW-2025H2-007.vn: Supported; day number and '07:00' removed (not printed as such). excerpt_en flag is a false positive (sentence-initial 'According'). Toll unknown as of midday per the page. 'Supported by Rwanda' is in the sources' sentence as relayed by Radio Okapi.
src: Selon des sources concordantes, les rebelles de l’AFC-M23, soutenus par le Rwanda, affrontent les VDP/Wazalendo du groupe PARECO/FF. Les affrontements ont commencé vers 07 heures locales, lorsque les rebelles du M23 ont attaqué les positions des Wazalendo à Kahunda et Mitimingi, dans la zone d’Ufamandu 2.

r1-NKW-2025H2-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Kasopo locality (Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi) was deserted after two days of fighting from Wednesday 10 September between M23 rebels and a coalition of Wazalendo groups made up of elements of the MAC, the APCLS and Uhuru.
r1-NKW-2025H2-008.n: Single outlet. Page also says Wazalendo retook two of four localities previously held by M23 and that this back-and-forth continued since April 2025 (not used as claim).
r1-NKW-2025H2-008.vn: Every clause on the page and in the excerpt. Page also reports the Wazalendo retook two of four localities held by M23 on the Wednesday.
src: Depuis mercredi 10 septembre 2025, la localité de Kasopo connaît une crise humanitaire majeure, la population fuyant massivement les combats entre les rebelles du M23 et les milices Wazalendo, composées d’éléments du Mouvement d’action congolais (MAC), de l’APCLS et d’Uhuru.

r1-NKW-2025H2-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Friday AFC/M23 rebels, according to several local sources, initiated fighting by attacking positions of the wazalendo of the APCLS armed group of Janvier Karairi on Changara hill and at Showa near Bukombo (Osso Banyungu, Masisi), and that the wazalendo pushed the attack back to Bukombo, disrupting traffic between Masisi centre and Nyabiondo.
r1-NKW-2025H2-009.n: Single outlet; casualty toll not established per page.
r1-NKW-2025H2-009.vn: Supported; day number removed (date from dateline + 'ce vendredi'). Toll not established per the page.
src: Plusieurs sources locales indiquent que les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 ont été à l’initiative de combats en lançant l’attaque contre les positions des wazalendo sur la colline de Changara et Showa non loin de Bukombo. Cette attaque a été repoussée par les wazalendo jusqu'à Bukombo, ce qui a perturbé la circulation entre Masisi centre et Nyabiondo.

r1-NKW-2025H2-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources, at around 17 hours local time a FARDC Sukhoi aircraft dropped bombs on rebel positions at Kibanda, near Kasopo (Osso Banyungu, Masisi), in support of FARDC soldiers and wazalendo fighting the rebels on the ground since the morning, and that the bombing let them repel the rebels who had attacked wazalendo positions at Kibanda.
r1-NKW-2025H2-010.n: URL fetched at actualite.cd/2025/11/22/... resolves the same page (index.php variant used in search). Single outlet; no casualty figure. Page says fighting was in violation of the Doha framework agreement (outlet wording).
r1-NKW-2025H2-010.vn: Supported; day number and 'M23' removed from statement (stored excerpt prints only 17); date and actor on the page. No casualty figure on the page. The outlet itself describes the fighting as in violation of the Doha framework agreement.
src: Selon les sources d’ ACTUALITE.CD dans la région, c'est aux environs de 17 heures locales que l’avion Sukhoï des FARDC a survolé cet espace aérien avant de larguer des bombes sur les positions rebelles.

r1-NKW-2025H2-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in an official communiqué dated Saturday 20 September, the spokesperson of the 3rd defence zone, Major Nestor Mavudisa, denounced 'attaques et provocations intolérables' attributed to the rebels since Thursday 18 September; the army said it reserved the 'droit de riposter avec rigueur'.
r1-NKW-2025H2-011.l: Mpeti and Malemo, Walikale and Masisi
r1-NKW-2025H2-011.n: Radio Okapi relaying FARDC communiqué; partisan on the fact.
r1-NKW-2025H2-011.vn: Supported; the right-to-retaliate line is the army's, not explicitly the spokesperson's, and is on the page only (clause_support). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 22 Sept 2025, carries the communiqué clause and the riposte clause; the stored excerpt lacks the 'droit de riposter avec rigueur' sentence, added here. The riposte sentence is in the outlet's voice ('L'armée congolaise affirme'), not quoted from the communiqué.
src: Dans un communiqué officiel daté du samedi 20 septembre, le porte-parole de la 3e zone de défense, le major Nestor Mavudisa, dénonce des « attaques et provocations intolérables » attribuées aux rebelles depuis le jeudi 18 septembre.
L’armée congolaise affirme se réserver le « droit de riposter avec rigueur ».

r1-NKW-2025H2-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that AFC-M23 accused the FARDC on Friday 19 September of bombing the villages of Bibwe, Nyange and Hembe (Bashali Mokoto grouping, Masisi) with drones and Sukhoi-25 fighter jets; the same day, sources close to the FARDC accused the rebellion of killing about twenty civilians in the village of Chanjikiro, Kisimba grouping, Walikale.
r1-NKW-2025H2-012.a: AFC-M23 (accusing FARDC); sources close to FARDC (accusing AFC-M23)
r1-NKW-2025H2-012.x: Sources close to FARDC via Radio Okapi: about twenty civilians killed at Chanjikiro
r1-NKW-2025H2-012.n: Both accusations are partisan and unverified; no independent confirmation found. Contested event with both parties' accounts in one page.
r1-NKW-2025H2-012.vn: Both accounts printed as stated and kept separately attributed; excerpt_en flag is a false positive (Sukhoi spelling / 'For'). Two opposing partisan accusations, each attributed; neither independently confirmed. Radio Okapi says 'Chaque camp rejette la responsabilité'.
src: De son côté, le mouvement AFC-M23 a accusé, vendredi 19 septembre, les FARDC d’avoir bombardé les villages de Bibwe, Nyange et Hembe — situés dans le groupement Bashali Mokoto, territoire de Masisi — à l’aide de drones et d’avions de chasse Sukhoï-25.
Le même jour, des sources proches des FARDC ont, quant à elles, accusé la rébellion d’avoir tué une vingtaine de civils dans le village de Chanjikiro, groupement Kisimba, territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2025H2-013.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Wazalendo, in a communiqué denouncing attacks against them, stated that on 15 November 2025 the positions of the ANCDH/AFDP at Kashanje (Masisi), of the UPLC/EPLC at Mikenge (Mwenga) and of the CMC/FDP at Kitunda (Rutshuru) were attacked.
r1-NKW-2025H2-013.n: Wazalendo own account relayed by outlet; the page says the attacks came from AFC-M23 the same day a Doha framework agreement was signed. Further Wazalendo claims on the page (16 Nov Ikobo, 17 Nov Kivuye and Mpati) not recorded. No M23 response found.
r1-NKW-2025H2-013.vn: Supported; statement narrowed to the groups' own wording and attacker attributed as in the communiqué. Party account (Wazalendo) only; no AFC-M23 response found. Mikenge (Mwenga) is in South Kivu.
src: Ils affirment que le 15 novembre 2025, les positions de l’ANCDH/AFDP à Kashanje (Masisi), de l’UPLC/EPLC à Mikenge (Mwenga) et du CMC/FDP à Kitunda (Rutshuru) ont été attaquées.

r1-NKW-2025H2-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Friday 17 October 18 AFC/M23 fighters surrendered with their weapons to government forces at Munsanga (Kisimba grouping, Walikale), coming from Rusamambu in Ikobo grouping according to the grouping's administrative secretary, and were later escorted by wazalendo to Pinga and handed to FARDC military authorities there; military sources confirmed the surrender.
r1-NKW-2025H2-014.n: Single outlet; page also says Wazalendo control that part of the Wanianga sector and escorted the surrendered fighters to Pinga. Category territorial_control used loosely; no place changed hands.
r1-NKW-2025H2-014.vn: Supported; added the Wazalendo escort and the source of the Rusamambu detail; arrival-day inconsistency surfaced in note. Discrepancy on the page: the surrender is dated Friday 17 October but the arrival at Pinga is dated 'ce même samedi dans la soirée'. The page names the grouping's administrative secretary as Lavie Changwi.
src: Dix-huit (18) combattants de la rébellion de l'AFC/M23 se sont rendus avec leurs armes aux forces gouvernementales ce vendredi 17 octobre à Munsanga dans le groupement Kisimba (territoire de Walikale) au Nord-Kivu.

r1-NKW-2026H1-001.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources and confirmed by a source in the North Kivu 3 education sector, that three schoolgirls were allegedly victims of sexual violence when about thirty final-year pupils were intercepted by unidentified armed men on Friday 19 June on the Kiseya-Kilambo road in Bafuna groupement, Walikale territory; the pupils were robbed of their belongings and then released.
r1-NKW-2026H1-001.l: Kiseya–Kilambo axis, near Kimua, Bafuna groupement, Walikale
r1-NKW-2026H1-001.n: Date given as 'vendredi 19 juin' with no year in the sentence; article dated 2026-06-23. Victims are minors/pupils, not named. Perpetrators unidentified; the page does not attribute to a party. Sexual violence is hedged ('auraient été').
r1-NKW-2026H1-001.vn: All clauses on the retained Radio Okapi page; hedge and perpetrator attribution preserved; excerpt_en flags are only weekday capitalisation. Perpetrators are 'unidentified armed men' (hommes armés non identifiés) as the source states; no party is named. The sexual violence is reported in the conditional ('auraient été'). The page places the interception near Kimua, in the neighbouring Waloa Yungu groupement, while the road is described as in Bafuna groupement. The sentence prints no year; the article is dated 23/06/2026. Survivors not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Une trentaine d’élèves finalistes ont été victimes d’une attaque menée par des hommes armés non identifiés, vendredi 19 juin, sur l’axe routier Kiseya–Kilambo, dans le groupement Bafuna (territoire de Walikale), au Nord-Kivu.

Les sources locales indiquent également que trois élèves filles auraient été victimes de violences sexuelles avant que les assaillants ne relâchent le groupe. Une information confirmée par une source du secteur éducatif du Nord-Kivu 3.
Trois élèves filles auraient subi des violences sexuelles avant que les assaillants ne relâchent le groupe, une information rapportée par une source du secteur éducatif du Nord-Kivu 3.

r1-NKW-2026H1-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that Wazalendo attacked AFC/M23 positions in Kalembe, Masisi territory, on the night of Sunday 24 to Monday 25 May 2026; residents said a provisional toll was five people killed and nine injured, all civilians, and that houses and shops were also pillaged. The outlet said no official communication had been made, and that Kalembe remained under AFC/M23 control.
r1-NKW-2026H1-002.a: Wazalendo (attacking AFC/M23 positions) per local sources
r1-NKW-2026H1-002.n: Single local-source outlet; toll provisional. Not who killed the civilians: the page does not attribute the deaths. Includes pillage (looting) during the operation.
r1-NKW-2026H1-002.vn: Dates 24/25 May 2026 printed on the page (flag resolved by clause_support); all clauses verified. The source does not say who killed the civilians or who carried out the pillage. Toll provisional, from residents. Single outlet.
src: Le bilan provisoire fait état de cinq personnes tuées et neuf autres blessées. Les victimes sont toutes des civils, renseignent des habitants contactés dans la zone. Plusieurs maisons et commerces ont également été pillés au cours de cette opération
Selon des sources locales, des Wazalendo ont attaqué les positions des rebelles de l'AFC/M23 dans cette agglomération.

r1-NKW-2026H1-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that dozens of residents of Kihuma village, Buabo groupement, Masisi territory, were victims of pillaging during an incursion by armed men on the night of Sunday to Monday 27 April; local notable sources also reported the abduction of two young boys, whose whereabouts were unknown.
r1-NKW-2026H1-003.n: Perpetrators 'hommes armés non identifiés'. Boys are minors, not named. Same article carries a Buabo civil society claim of 15 civilians shot dead in a month (separate claim).
r1-NKW-2026H1-003.vn: Verified on retained page. Perpetrators unidentified per the source. 27 April 2026 was a Monday, consistent with the source. Abducted boys not named.
src: Des dizaines d’habitants du village de Kihuma, dans le groupement de Buabo en territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu), ont été victimes de pillages lors d’une incursion d’hommes armés survenue dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi 27 avril.
Les sources de la notabilité locale rapportent également l’enlèvement de deux jeunes garçons au cours de cette attaque. Jusqu’à présent, leur destination demeure inconnue.

r1-NKW-2026H1-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that local civil society of Buabo said at least fifteen civilians had been shot dead in one month in attacks by armed men in several localities of the Buabo entity, Masisi territory, an area it described as under AFC/M23 occupation where several other armed groups also operate; it said an attack on Friday 25 April in Ndete and Mashaki killed five civilians, including a teacher, an infant and its mother.
r1-NKW-2026H1-004.a: armed men, not attributed by the source
r1-NKW-2026H1-004.x: Buabo civil society (via Radio Okapi): at least 15 civilians shot dead in a month; 5 killed in attack at Ndete/Mashaki
r1-NKW-2026H1-004.n: Civil-society claim relayed by Radio Okapi; 'vendredi 25 avril' stated by source (25 April 2026 was a Saturday, so the weekday/date pairing in the source is inconsistent; reviewer should note). Not attributed to a party.
r1-NKW-2026H1-004.vn: Verified on page; weekday mismatch kept stated in note. Weekday/date mismatch in the source: it prints 'Vendredi 25 avril', but 25 April 2026 was a Saturday (Friday was 24 April). The exact day of the Ndete/Mashaki attack is therefore uncertain. Figures are Buabo civil society's, relayed by Radio Okapi; the killings are attributed only to 'armed men', not to a party.
src: Elle affirme qu’au moins quinze civils ont été tués par balles en l’espace d’un mois lors de différentes attaques menées par des hommes armés dans plusieurs localités de l’entité coutumière.
Vendredi 25 avril, une nouvelle attaque y avait coûté la vie à cinq civils, dont un enseignant, un nourrisson et sa mère.

La société civile dénonce des violations répétées des droits humains et du droit international humanitaire dans cette zone sous occupation de l’AFC/M23, où opèrent également plusieurs autres groupes armés.

r1-NKW-2026H1-005.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that violent fighting had opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militiamen since early Friday 27 February on the Kinyumba axis, about ten kilometres north of Nyabiondo (Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi); according to the same sources it was reportedly an attack launched by AFC/M23 against positions held by Wazalendo. The sources also said at least three civilians were wounded on the Thursday evening when a military device exploded in the Isiro quarter, in the centre of Nyabiondo.
r1-NKW-2026H1-005.l: Kinyumba and Nyabiondo (Isiro quarter), Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-005.x: Radio Okapi: at least 3 civilians wounded
r1-NKW-2026H1-005.n: The excerpt prints 'l’ax e' with a stray space (page rendering). Cause of the explosion not stated. Weekday dates: Friday = 27 February per the page itself; Thursday = 26 February computed.

The page was first published 27/02/2026 (modified 02/03/2026). The AFC/M23-initiated attack is in the conditional ('il s'agirait').
