src: Selon plusieurs sources locales, de violents combats opposent depuis tôt ce vendredi 27 février les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 aux miliciens Wazalendo sur l’ax e Kinyumba.
Vers 18 heures, jeudi, un engin militaire a explosé dans le quartier Isiro, au centre de Nyabiondo, blessant trois civils.

Depuis l’aube, des détonations d’armes lourdes et légères sont entendues autour du village de Kinyumba, situé à une dizaine de kilomètres au nord de Nyabiondo, dans le secteur Osso-Banyungu. D’après ces mêmes sources, il s’agirait d’une attaque lancée par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 contre des positions tenues par les miliciens Wazalendo.

r1-NKW-2026H1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that after violent fighting on Sunday 5 April between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo at Lukweti, about ten kilometres east of Nyabiondo (Masisi), the M23 assailants were repelled and fell back to Nyabiondo, their starting position; the locality, described as a Wazalendo stronghold, remained under Wazalendo control with an uneasy calm from Monday afternoon. No toll had been communicated.
r1-NKW-2026H1-006.vn: All clauses on the page; graded C as a control claim resting on a single outlet's unnamed local sources. Control reported by one outlet citing unnamed local sources; no party statement found. 'No toll' means no official toll by authorities or the parties. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 8 Apr 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the uneasy calm since Monday afternoon at Lukweti (with its location and the Sunday 5 April fighting), the stronghold description and the no-toll clause, added here. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 8 Apr 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the uneasy calm since Monday afternoon at Lukweti (with its location and the Sunday 5 April fighting), the stronghold description and the no-toll clause, added here.
src: Selon des sources locales, les assaillants du M23 ont été repoussés et se sont repliés vers Nyabiondo, leur position de départ
un mouvement de retour progressif est signalé dans la localité, qui reste sous le contrôle des Wazalendo.

Un calme précaire est observé depuis lundi après-midi dans la localité de Lukweti, située à une dizaine de kilomètres à l’est de Nyabiondo, dans le territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Ce répit fait suite à une journée de dimanche 5 avril, marquée par de violents affrontements à l’arme lourde et légère entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et les éléments Wazalendo.
À ce jour, aucun bilan officiel des affrontements n'a été communiqué par les autorités ou les parties en présence.

r1-NKW-2026H1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the Wazalendo briefly retook control of Nyabiondo (Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi) on Wednesday before being dislodged again; it also reported that clashes had continued for several days in the Bahunde chiefdom, affecting the localities of Kasenyi, Kinigi, Runigi, Kanyaru, Nyakigano, Nyamyamba and Kasaki, around Rubaya.
r1-NKW-2026H1-007.l: Nyabiondo; Bahunde chiefdom villages around Rubaya, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-007.n: Wednesday computed from publication date (Saturday 30 May): 27 May. The page does not name who dislodged the Wazalendo (context implies AFC/M23, which is not stated in the excerpt).
r1-NKW-2026H1-007.vn: Raw statement tied the 28 May resumption to Rubaya/Bahunde, which the page does not; narrowed to what the excerpts carry (28 May not printed in any excerpt, so kept in the note and date field). The page says fighting between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 resumed on Thursday 28 May (generally, on the Walikale-Goma axis via Masisi), not specifically around Rubaya. It does not say who dislodged the Wazalendo from Nyabiondo. Wednesday is 27 May only by computation from the publication date (30/05/2026).
src: À Nyabiondo, par exemple, les Wazalendo ont brièvement repris le contrôle de la localité mercredi, avant d’en être à nouveau délogés.
Ces affrontements touchent les localités de Kasenyi, Kinigi, Runigi, Kanyaru, Nyakigano, Nyamyamba et Kasaki, autour de Rubaya.

r1-NKW-2026H1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that amid the fighting around Nyabiondo, Katoyi and the Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi), health structures faced a shortage of medicines, the Ngungu–Ufamandu road had been cut for more than ten days and prices of basic goods were rising.
r1-NKW-2026H1-008.l: Ngungu–Ufamandu axis, Nyabiondo, Katoyi, Bahunde chiefdom, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-008.n: Shortage is not attributed to any party's action by the source; recorded as access context, not as an attack.
r1-NKW-2026H1-008.vn: Verified on page. Access context, not an attack: the source does not attribute the medicine shortage or the road cut to any party, and does not name the health facilities. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les mêmes sources rapportent que la route reliant Ngungu à Ufamandu est coupée depuis plus de dix jours. Sur place, les structures de santé font face à une rupture de médicaments
Les mêmes sources signalent que la route reliant Ngungu à Ufamandu demeure coupée depuis plus de dix jours, compliquant l’acheminement des biens et de l’aide humanitaire vers les localités affectées.

r1-NKW-2026H1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, mass displacement and villages nearly emptied of inhabitants since Sunday 31 May in Walikale and Masisi territories after new clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo groups allied to the FARDC; it named villages affected in Masisi (Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo).
r1-NKW-2026H1-009.l: Walikale and Masisi territories (Yaki, Kasopo, Ndete, Mulema, Luke, Kasenyi, Mbizo)
r1-NKW-2026H1-009.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo allied to the FARDC
r1-NKW-2026H1-009.x: No figure given by the source
r1-NKW-2026H1-009.vn: Verified; flags are 'M23' digits and capitalisation only. No displacement figure given. Kasenyi and Mbizo are named on the page as sites of clashes in Kibabi groupement, Bahunde chiefdom (not in the stored excerpts). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, carries every clause (Ndete, Mulema and Luke per witnesses; Kasenyi and Mbizo in the outlet's voice); the stored excerpts stop before 'allied to the FARDC' and omit Kasenyi and Mbizo, so the full sentences are added. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, carries every clause (Ndete, Mulema and Luke per witnesses; Kasenyi and Mbizo in the outlet's voice); the stored excerpts stop before 'allied to the FARDC' and omit Kasenyi and Mbizo, so the full sentences are added.
src: Des déplacements massifs de populations et des villages presque entièrement vidés de leurs habitants sont signalés depuis dimanche 31 mai dans les territoires de Walikale et de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu
notamment Ndete, Mulema et Luke, dans le groupement Nyamaboko I, secteur Osso-Banyungu.

Des déplacements massifs de populations et des villages presque entièrement vidés de leurs habitants sont signalés depuis dimanche 31 mai dans les territoires de Walikale et de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu, à la suite de nouveaux affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et les groupes Wazalendo alliés aux FARDC.
Toujours ce weekend, d’autres accrochages ont concerné les localités de Kasenyi et Mbizo, dans le groupement Kibabi, en chefferie des Bahunde, à proximité du secteur de Katoyi.

r1-NKW-2026H1-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes on Sunday 31 May at Yaki, between Kashebere and Miba in Luberike groupement (Walikale), opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the NDC-Rénové group led by Guidon Shimiray.
r1-NKW-2026H1-010.l: Yaki, between Kashebere and Miba, Luberike groupement, Walikale
r1-NKW-2026H1-010.a: NDC-Rénové (Wazalendo), led by Guidon Shimiray; AFC/M23
r1-NKW-2026H1-010.vn: Name and group printed on page; date derivation stated. 'Sunday 31 May' derives from 'la veille' of Monday 1 June as printed on the page. Concordant local sources per Radio Okapi. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, states the Yaki clash of the day before in its own voice; 'des sources locales concordantes' on that page refers to the separate Kasopo detonations, so the attribution is corrected. Excerpt for Yaki's location added. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 1 Jun 2026, states the Yaki clash of the day before in its own voice; 'des sources locales concordantes' on that page refers to the separate Kasopo detonations, so the attribution is corrected. Excerpt for Yaki's location added.
src: La localité a toutefois été le théâtre, la veille, de violents affrontements opposant les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 aux combattants Wazalendo du groupe NDC-Rénové dirigé par Guidon Shimiray.
Cependant, un calme relatif était observé ce lundi 1er juin dans la matinée dans le village de Yaki, situé entre Kashebere et Miba, dans le groupement Luberike, en territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2026H1-011.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that after fighting on Sunday 1 March the two sides were said to share control of Kibati (Luberike groupement, Walikale): FARDC and allied Wazalendo reportedly held the centre of Kibati and two former rebel positions, while AFC/M23 still held two positions on the axis to Kashebere; fighting resumed on Monday 2 March, the third consecutive day, after rebel reinforcements arrived from Kashebere.
r1-NKW-2026H1-011.l: Kibati, Luberike groupement, Mungazi–Kashebere axis, Walikale
r1-NKW-2026H1-011.n: Conditional tense ('se seraient partagé', 'auraient réussi'). Kinshasa and AFC/M23 accounts not found in this source.
r1-NKW-2026H1-011.vn: Wording keeps the source's hedges; graded C (single outlet, unnamed local sources, conditional). Shared control reported in the conditional ('se seraient partagé') by one outlet citing local sources; no FARDC or AFC/M23 account found. The outlet says fighting began Saturday 28 February with a government offensive to retake Kibati.
src: À l’issue des affrontements de dimanche 1er mars, les deux camps se seraient partagé le contrôle du village. Les FARDC et leurs alliés wazalendo occupent le centre de Kibati ainsi que deux positions précédemment tenues par les rebelles, qu’ils auraient réussi à déloger.
les combats ont débuté samedi 28 février, lorsque les forces gouvernementales ont lancé une offensive pour reprendre le contrôle de Kibati.

r1-NKW-2026H1-012.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that after two days of intense fighting begun Sunday 31 May with an offensive by regular forces against rebel positions, a precarious calm held on Tuesday 2 June at Kibati (Walikale), where FARDC and Wazalendo occupied the centre and the rebels the surrounding hills; traffic between Mungazi and Kashebere was suspended.
r1-NKW-2026H1-012.n: Toll unknown per source. Second round of fighting at Kibati after 28 Feb-2 Mar.
r1-NKW-2026H1-012.vn: Verified; graded C as a control claim on one outlet's unnamed sources. Single outlet citing its own sources; toll unknown; sources in Kashebere said rebels were reinforcing toward Kibati.
src: Selon ces dernières, les FARDC et les wazalendo occupent le centre de Kibati pendant que les rebelles occupent les collines surplombant cette entité.
Les combats ont éclaté le dimanche 31 mai après le lancement de l'offensive des forces régulières contre les positions rebelles.

r1-NKW-2026H1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo began on Saturday 13 June 2026 at Buhimba (Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale), after Wazalendo positions there were bombed around 15:00 local time; the outlet said Buhimba had been under Wazalendo control for a week after they dislodged AFC/M23 following intense fighting.
r1-NKW-2026H1-013.l: Buhimba, Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale/Masisi boundary
r1-NKW-2026H1-013.n: Who carried out the bombing is not stated. Rwandan outlet IGIHE (partisan-aligned) reported AFC/M23 'reclaims Buhimba' (en.igihe.com/news-40/article/walikale-afc-m23-reclaims-buhimba-after-intense-clashes); page could not be fetched here (via=none), so not cited. Date of the reclaim not verified.
r1-NKW-2026H1-013.vn: Verified; '15:00' renders the page's '15 heures'; graded C (single outlet, customary/administrative sources). The source does not say who bombed the Wazalendo positions. Single outlet; its sources are local administrative and customary sources. A Rwandan outlet (IGIHE) reportedly said AFC/M23 later reclaimed Buhimba; that page was not retained and is not cited.
src: Depuis une semaine, l'agglomération de Buhimba est sous contrôle des wazalendo après y avoir délogé les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 à l'issue d'intenses combats.
Ces affrontements interviennent après le bombardement de positions des wazalendo à Buhimba ce même samedi aux environs de 15 heures locales.

r1-NKW-2026H1-014.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing customary sources in Waloa Yungu groupement, that on Thursday 1 January AFC/M23 rebels coming from Kasopo (Masisi) tried to retake Buhimba, on the Walikale-Masisi boundary, which they had lost about two months earlier, and that, according to its sources, the FARDC supported by Wazalendo repelled them back to Kasopo and about ten AFC/M23 fighters were captured by the army. The outlet added that FARDC officials in Walikale had promised to comment within hours.
r1-NKW-2026H1-014.l: Buhimba, Waloa Yungu groupement, Walikale (rebels from Kasopo, Masisi)
r1-NKW-2026H1-014.n: Customary sources only; capture of ten fighters unconfirmed; 'ce jeudi 1er janvier' as printed. Detainees' fate not stated. Buhimba held by FARDC/Wazalendo as of this date, lost by AFC/M23 'about two months' earlier per source.
r1-NKW-2026H1-014.vn: Verified on page; C. Customary sources only; the capture of about ten fighters is unconfirmed and their fate is not stated. 1 January 2026 was a Thursday, consistent with the source. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Actualite.cd, 2 Jan 2026. The page states in its own voice, not via its sources, that FARDC officials in Walikale promised to comment; the corrected wording attributes that clause to the outlet. Other clauses match. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Actualite.cd, 2 Jan 2026. The page states in its own voice, not via its sources, that FARDC officials in Walikale promised to comment; the corrected wording attributes that clause to the outlet. Other clauses match.
src: L'armée congolaise appuyée par les wazalendo a repoussé les rebelles qui sont rentrés jusqu'à Kasopo d'après nos sources. Le bilan de ces affrontements n'est pas encore connu mais nos sources parlent d'une dizaine de combattants de l’AFC/M23 capturés par l'armée.
afin de reconquérir cette agglomération qu'ils ont perdu il y a environ deux mois.

Le bilan de ces affrontements n'est pas encore connu mais nos sources parlent d'une dizaine de combattants de l’AFC/M23 capturés par l'armée. Les responsables des FARDC à Walikale ont promis de s'exprimer à ce sujet dans les heures qui suivent.

r1-NKW-2026H1-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a witness, that on the morning of Tuesday 27 January 2026 six armed men in military uniform intercepted a motorcycle taxi rider and two passengers about two kilometres from Kashuga on the Kashuga-Kalembe road (Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi); the outlet reported the victims were beaten and tortured and taken to an unknown destination, and that one escaped.
r1-NKW-2026H1-015.l: Kashuga–Kalembe road, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-015.a: six armed men in military uniform, described as 'bandits armés'/'coupeurs de route'
r1-NKW-2026H1-015.x: Kivu Morning Post: headline 'two people abducted'; text: three victims, one escaped
r1-NKW-2026H1-015.n: Headline says two abducted; text says three victims, one escaped. Perpetrators not attributed to a party. Unnamed.
r1-NKW-2026H1-015.vn: Verified on page. Headline says two abducted; text names three victims of whom one escaped (consistent: two remained abducted). Perpetrators described as 'bandits armés' / 'coupeurs de route' in military uniform; the outlet attributes insecurity on this road to unidentified armed men and notes AFC/M23 patrols there, without attributing this incident to any party. Victims unnamed.
src: Ils ont été interceptés par six hommes armés en tenue militaire, à environ deux kilomètres de l’agglomération de Kashuga. Sur place, les trois victimes ont été violemment battues et torturées avant d’être emmenées vers une destination inconnue.

r1-NKW-2026H1-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, whom it described as president of the movement and its deputy coordinator, said on Wednesday that the Kinshasa regime had 'once again trampled the ceasefire' by launching a 'generalised offensive on all front lines and beyond', and that there had been 'no public reprimand, no condemnation' of it; the outlet also reported that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a separate communiqué, reported attacks that day in Minembwe and Kalehe.
r1-NKW-2026H1-016.l: North Kivu / eastern DRC front lines (statement)
r1-NKW-2026H1-016.n: Partisan party statement, cited only for what AFC/M23 said. Location is general; Minembwe/Kalehe are outside this unit.
r1-NKW-2026H1-016.vn: Raw statement said he 'complained of no public condemnation from mediators'; the page names no mediators. Rewritten as quoted. Weekday date and 'M23' digits are not in the stored excerpts, so they are kept in note, date and actor fields. AFC/M23 says: a party statement, cited only for what AFC/M23 said. Bisimwa is president of the M23 and deputy coordinator of AFC/M23 (per the page); statement date 25 February 2026. He did not name mediators: he regretted the absence of any clear initiative to halt the offensive. Minembwe and Kalehe are in South Kivu.
src: « Nous constatons que le régime de Kinshasa a, une fois de plus, foulé aux pieds le cessez-le-feu en déclenchant une offensive généralisée sur l’ensemble des lignes de front et au-delà.
Aucune réprimande publique, aucune condamnation », a-t-il ajouté.

r1-NKW-2026H1-017.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on Wednesday 25 February fighting resumed at Kibanda, about two kilometres from Kasopo (Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Osso Banyungu sector, Masisi), where Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo coming from Buhimba (Walikale) launched an offensive against AFC/M23 positions; the outlet said AFC/M23 had occupied the locality for several months.
r1-NKW-2026H1-017.l: Kibanda, near Kasopo, Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-017.n: Relation tagged counterclaim to pair with the AFC/M23 'generalised offensive' claim above (Kinshasa/FARDC's own account of this offensive not found).
r1-NKW-2026H1-017.vn: Verified. Relation changed from 'counterclaim' to 'new': this is the outlet's field report, not a party's account contradicting the AFC/M23 statement (it is consistent with it). The outlet's own sources, not a Kinshasa or FARDC statement; no FARDC account found.
src: Selon des sources d’Actualite.cd, des militaires congolais et des wazalendo en provenance de Buhimba, dans le territoire voisin de Walikale, ont lancé une offensive contre les positions de l’AFC/M23, qui occupe la localité depuis plusieurs mois.

r1-NKW-2026H1-018.s: Congoprofond.net reported that a violent fire broke out on Monday 19 January 2026 around 23:00 at the logistics base of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) and spread to much of the Masisi General Reference Hospital (HGR) in Masisi-Centre; at publication the fire was still burning, no official source had given a cause and no casualty toll had been communicated.
r1-NKW-2026H1-018.l: Masisi-Centre, Masisi (HGR Masisi and MSF logistics base)
r1-NKW-2026H1-018.a: not attributed; cause not established by the source
r1-NKW-2026H1-018.n: Single local outlet, first-hours report; cause unknown (short circuit, accident or malicious act all open per the source). No claim of deliberate attack. Health relevance: HGR Masisi is MSF-supported. Follow-up on cause and damage not found. Counter-reporting: Actualite.cd (2026-01-20): Claim says no official source had given a cause and no toll was communicated; this later report gives an electrical fault as cause and four patient deaths (three children). Says nothing on the MSF logistics base.
r1-NKW-2026H1-018.vn: Verified on page; health relevance as damage to a facility, not as an attack. Cause unknown: the source lists a short circuit, a domestic accident or a malicious act as open questions. This is a fire, not a reported attack; no party is alleged responsible. Single local outlet, first-hours report; no follow-up found. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. Regraded C->B on independent, non-partisan corroboration. 1 verified counter-reporting source(s) recorded in notes. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Un incendie d’une rare violence s’est déclaré ce lundi 19 janvier 2026 aux alentours de 23 heures, touchant de plein fouet des infrastructures sanitaires vitales pour la région.
Pour le moment, aucune source officielle n’a été en mesure de préciser l’origine du sinistre.
Quatre patients sont morts à l’hôpital général de référence de Masisi (Nord-Kivu) à la suite d’un incendie déclaré dans cet établissement sanitaire, a appris ACTUALITE.CD.

r1-NKW-2026H1-019.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that violent clashes on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo of the CMC group, starting at Bumbasha a few kilometres from Mweso, caused hundreds of residents to flee toward neighbouring villages and to Mweso centre in Masisi, where they took refuge in churches and schools; no toll was communicated.
r1-NKW-2026H1-019.l: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru) and Mweso, Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H1-019.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo of the CMC group
r1-NKW-2026H1-019.n: Fighting itself is in Rutshuru territory (Bukombo); relevant to this unit for displacement into Mweso. Recorded territory Rutshuru.
r1-NKW-2026H1-019.vn: Verified on page; Rutshuru location noted. The fighting itself was in Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru territory (despite the headline 'à Masisi'); the displaced fled into Mweso, Masisi. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 13 Jan 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the date, the CMC group, the no-toll clause and the refuge in churches and schools, added here. The page places the fighting in Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru. 2026-10-28: source 1 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 13 Jan 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpts lack the date, the CMC group, the no-toll clause and the refuge in churches and schools, added here. The page places the fighting in Bukombo grouping, Rutshuru.
src: Selon des sources locales, les affrontements ont débuté à Bumbasha, à quelques kilomètres de Mweso; avant de s’étendre vers Karambi et Chahemba.
Pour ces sources, ces combats ont provoqué la fuite de centaines d’habitants, qui se sont dirigés vers des villages voisins, ainsi que vers le centre de Mweso, dans le territoire voisin de Masisi.

De violents combats ont opposé, toute la matinée du lundi 12 janvier, les rebelles AFC/M23 aux combattants Wazalendo du groupe CMC dans plusieurs villages du groupement de Bukombo, territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu). Aucun bilan n'a été communiqué.
Sur place, ils ont trouvé refuge dans des églises et des écoles.

r1-NKW-2026H2-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing customary and local security sources, that the town of Katoy, seat of Katoy sector in Masisi territory, returned to Wazalendo control on Sunday 12 July after fighting with AFC/M23; the Wazalendo offensive was said to have been launched by fighters from Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale, and AFC/M23 were said to have withdrawn towards the Ngungu axis.
r1-NKW-2026H2-001.n: Actualite.cd says information is hard to verify independently and no casualty figures were available. Katoy is spelled Katoyi in later reports; a later draft claim (NKS-2026Q4#9) has Katoyi centre retaken 6 Oct.
r1-NKW-2026H2-001.vn: Page supports every clause; withdrawal kept conditional ('se seraient repliés'). Single outlet relaying unnamed local sources: C. Actualite.cd says the information is hard to verify independently; no toll given. Katoy is spelled Katoyi in other reports.
src: est repassée sous le contrôle des combattants Wazalendo ce dimanche 12 juillet, à la suite d’affrontements qui les ont opposés aux rebelles de l'AFC/M23, selon des sources coutumières et sécuritaires locales.

r1-NKW-2026H2-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance (GAPE) said, in an interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026, that at least fifty-six children had been recruited by local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions, in Walikale territory during the first two weeks of the school holidays; according to testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator, the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily to join the groups.
r1-NKW-2026H2-002.l: Walikale territory (groupements Waloa Uroba and Bakano)
r1-NKW-2026H2-002.a: local armed militias, notably Wazalendo factions (per GAPE)
r1-NKW-2026H2-002.n: Single NGO account. Page also lists groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo' and says children reportedly left families voluntarily, per GAPE testimonies; see next claim.
r1-NKW-2026H2-002.vn: Flagged '15' and '56' are printed on the page (interview date; coordinator quote '56 enfants au total'); the excerpt prints the figure in words (cinquante-six). Single NGO account: C. excerpt_en flag: 'NGO' renders 'ONG'; translation is faithful. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: interview on Wednesday 15 July 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Walikale territory 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: children reportedly left voluntarily, per testimonies cited by GAPE's coordinator 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Category forced_recruitment overstates the source: GAPE speaks of recruitment/enrolment of children, and on the same page its coordinator says the children reportedly left voluntarily ('auraient quitté volontairement'). Child recruitment stands as GAPE's allegation, but the 'forced' element is not in the source; add the voluntary-departure caveat (add_excerpt needed) and consider category child recruitment rather than forced.; excerpt-support: added three excerpts: the interview of Wednesday 15 July, the Walikale territory survey, and the coordinator's account that the children 'auraient quitté volontairement leurs familles'
ent: Groupe d'action pour la protection de l'enfance
src: l’ONG Groupe d’action pour la protection de l’enfance (GAPE) dénonce le recrutement d’au moins cinquante-six enfants par des milices armées locales, notamment des factions Wazalendo, durant les deux premières semaines des vacances.

Dans une interview mercredi 15 juillet à Radio Okapi, l’ONG Groupe d’action pour la protection de l’enfance (GAPE) dénonce le recrutement d’au moins cinquante-six enfants par des milices armées locales
L’ONG GAPE affirme avoir mené une enquête la semaine dernière qui démontre qu’au moins cinquante-six enfants ont été enrôlés dans des milices actives au territoire de Walikale.

Selon le coordonnateur de GAPE, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, ce phénomène prend une tournure dramatique nourrie par la précarité : « 56 enfants au total ont été identifiés au sein de groupes armés. Selon les témoignages, ces enfants auraient quitté volontairement leurs familles pour rejoindre ces groupes

r1-NKW-2026H2-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that GAPE's inquiries covered several localities of the Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements (Walikale), notably in the ranks of the armed groups 'Uhuru' of 'général Machite' and 'Kalomendo'; GAPE's coordinator, Bayomba Mishiki Bam’s, said that according to testimonies the children had reportedly left their families voluntarily.
r1-NKW-2026H2-003.l: Waloa Uroba and Bakano groupements, Walikale
r1-NKW-2026H2-003.n: Roster lead: 'Uhuru' and 'Kalomendo' Wazalendo-type groups, Walikale. 'général' is a self-style rank as printed.
r1-NKW-2026H2-003.vn: Raw statement attributed the Uhuru/Kalomendo identification to the coordinator; on the page it is Radio Okapi's narration of the NGO's inquiries. The 'left voluntarily' point is conditional ('auraient quitté') and is kept so. The coordinator's name is printed on the page but not in the stored excerpt.
src: groupements Waloa Uroba et Bakano, notamment dans les rangs des groupes armés « Uhuru » du général Machite et « Kalomendo ».

r1-NKW-2026H2-004.s: Actualite.cd reported on 1 August 2026 that violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo self-defence groups began in the early hours of Saturday 1 August at Shango village, Butsike locality, Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi territory; per local sources AFC/M23 attacked Wazalendo positions and gunfire was heard in neighbouring Shoa and Mahanga, with no casualty or damage figures available.
r1-NKW-2026H2-004.n: Reclassify as military_operation if preferred; no civilian harm reported beyond panic and sheltering.
r1-NKW-2026H2-004.vn: Flagged '1' (1 August, Nyamaboko 1) is printed on the page; every clause supported. Page also says it was unclear which force controlled the area afterwards.
src: D’après des sources locales, les éléments de l’AFC/M23 ont lancé une attaque contre des positions occupées par les Wazalendo dans cette partie du secteur d’Osso Banyungu.

r1-NKW-2026H2-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to local sources, clashes on Monday 3 August in the Ikobo and Kisimba groupements (Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a coalition of Wazalendo groups were accompanied by looting; notables reported important looting at Buleusa, seat of Ikobo groupement, and nearby Rusamambu, where kiosks and shops were entirely emptied. Local sources said Wazalendo fighters led by self-proclaimed general Jonas Bigabo launched simultaneous attacks on AFC/M23 positions between midnight and 4 a.m.
r1-NKW-2026H2-005.l: Buleusa, Rusamambu, Kalonge, Kasopo, Kateku (Ikobo and Kisimba groupements), Walikale
r1-NKW-2026H2-005.a: Wazalendo coalition led by self-proclaimed general Jonas Bigabo; AFC/M23
r1-NKW-2026H2-005.n: Radio Okapi; local sources and notables. Looting perpetrators not named. Wazalendo reportedly occupied some localities for a few hours before calm returned; both forces remained present.
r1-NKW-2026H2-005.vn: Flagged '3' and '4' are printed on the page ('lundi 3 août', 'quatre heures du matin'). All clauses supported. Looting perpetrators are not named by the source.
src: Ces mêmes sources rapportent d’importants actes de pillage à Buleusa, chef-lieu du groupement d’Ikobo, ainsi que dans l’agglomération voisine de Rusamambu.
des combattants Wazalendo dirigés par le général autoproclamé Jonas Bigabo ont lancé des attaques simultanées contre plusieurs positions de l’AFC/M23.

r1-NKW-2026H2-006.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant and administrative sources, that AFC-M23 fighters retook Remeka, seat of Ufamando groupement in Masisi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 after intense fighting against FARDC allied with Wazalendo; Kashukano, Kamuobe, Miano and Buuli were also said to have fallen to AFC-M23.
r1-NKW-2026H2-006.n: Local outlet in Goma (M23-held). Remeka changed hands again: FARDC claim reconquest 15 Sept (separate claim).
r1-NKW-2026H2-006.vn: Date 20 Aug matches the excerpt. Flag '23' is the 'M23' in the group name. Single local outlet (Goma-based): graded C, not B. Remeka changed hands again: FARDC say they retook it on 15 Sept (FARDC communiqué); fighting resumed there on 25 Sept (Actualite.cd).
src: La prise de cette localité est intervenue jeudi 20 août 2026, après d’intenses combats contre les FARDC, alliées aux Wazalendo, selon des sources concordantes et administratives à KivuMorningPost.

r1-NKW-2026H2-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a communiqué, accused government coalition forces of summarily executing several civilians at Luntukulu, on the Nzibira axis; according to AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka the victims allegedly included women and children.
r1-NKW-2026H2-007.l: Luntukulu, Nzibira axis (location as printed by the source)
r1-NKW-2026H2-007.n: Partisan allegation, reported date approximate (communiqué date not given; page published 2026-08-21). Location is outside Masisi/Walikale (Nzibira is in South Kivu); kept as related to the unit's news page. Province/territory not established by the source. No FARDC response found.
r1-NKW-2026H2-007.vn: Statement matches page, attributed throughout, conditional kept ('allegedly'). Kanyuka's name is printed on the page (not in the excerpt). Outside the unit's Masisi/Walikale area, so relation new_related_event; province South Kivu. Partisan allegation (AFC/M23 says); not verified. Luntukulu is in South Kivu; the source does not name the territory. No FARDC response found in this unit.
src: Dans un communiqué, l’AFC-M23 accuse les éléments des forces coalisées gouvernementales d’avoir sommairement exécuté plusieurs civils dans la localité de Luntukulu, sur l’axe Nzibira.

r1-NKW-2026H2-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing a notable contacted on the spot, that fighting on Saturday around Buruso (Ufamandu I groupement, Masisi) and Biriko (Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale) between AFC/M23 and a Wazalendo coalition allied to the FARDC caused new displacement toward Walikale-Centre, Hombo and elsewhere; Radio Okapi described the Ufamandu I and II groupements as almost entirely emptied of residents, and military sources said they shot down on Saturday in Nyamaboko I a kamikaze drone attributed to AFC/M23.
r1-NKW-2026H2-008.l: Buruso (Masisi); Biriko, Kilambo, Busurungi (Walikale); Nyamaboko I
r1-NKW-2026H2-008.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo coalition allied to FARDC
r1-NKW-2026H2-008.n: Page also says rebels' advance since 13 August worsens the crisis, and the army accuses rebels of multiplying attacks to extend their zone of occupation (army account, attributed on page).
r1-NKW-2026H2-008.vn: Raw said 'an AFC/M23 kamikaze drone'; the page says a drone 'attribué à l'AFC/M23' by military sources: attribution restored. The emptied-groupements line is Radio Okapi's own narration, not the notable's. Day number dropped from the statement (no excerpt prints it); the date field carries 29 Aug, printed on the page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 30 Aug 2026 (fighting Saturday 29 Aug). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts carry only the emptied-groupements and drone sentences, so the fighting, notable and location passages are added. Statement wording stands. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 30 Aug 2026 (fighting Saturday 29 Aug).
