All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts carry only the emptied-groupements and drone sentences, so the fighting, notable and location passages are added. Statement wording stands.
src: Les groupements d'Ufamandu I et II sont aujourd'hui presque entièrement vidés de leurs populations.
où des sources militaires affirment avoir abattu samedi un drone kamikaze attribué à l'AFC/M23.
Les combats, signalés samedi 29 aout à Buruso et Biriko, ont provoqué de nouveaux déplacements de populations vers Walikale-Centre, Hombo et d'autres zones jugées plus sûres.

Selon un notable contacté sur place par Radio Okapi, ces nouveaux déplacements sont consécutifs aux violents combats qui ont opposé, toute la journée de samedi, l'AFC/M23 à une coalition de combattants Wazalendo alliés aux FARDC.

Les affrontements, d'une forte intensité, se sont concentrés autour du village de Buruso, dans le groupement d'Ufamandu I en territoire de Masisi, ainsi que dans le village voisin de Biriko, situé dans le groupement de Waloa Loanda dans le territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2026H2-009.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on Tuesday 8 September wazalendo dislodged AFC/M23 from Rutoboko and then retook Kibahemula in Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Masisi; the Humura commercial centre was said to remain under AFC/M23 control.
r1-NKW-2026H2-009.n: Conflicts with Kivu Morning Post report of AFC/M23 taking Kazinga and Humura around 7 Sept (separate claim); the two reports describe fluid, contested control. Actualite.cd says no precise toll available.
r1-NKW-2026H2-009.vn: Date 8 Sept and every clause printed on the page. Kept separate from the Kazinga/Humura claim, which is a different account. Separate account from Kivu Morning Post's report (published 8 Sept) of AFC/M23 taking Kazinga and Humura; both describe contested, shifting control in Nyamaboko 1. Actualite.cd on 18 Sept says FARDC and wazalendo had retaken Humura and Rutoboko.
src: Au terme des affrontements, ils sont parvenus à déloger les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 de Rutoboko, avant de reprendre également le contrôle de Kibahemula.

r1-NKW-2026H2-010.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing concordant sources, that AFC/M23 took control of the villages of Kazinga and Humura in Nyamaboko 1 groupement, Masisi, dislodging the Congolese army and Wazalendo militias who had retaken the area; an anonymous health source quoted said AFC/M23 had also retaken Ngomashi, Mwima, Humura and Burinda.
r1-NKW-2026H2-010.l: Kazinga, Humura, Ngomashi, Mwima, Burinda (Nyamaboko 1), Masisi
r1-NKW-2026H2-010.n: Page dated 2026-09-07/08; exact capture day not stated. Same page says AFC/M23 had also taken Katoyi-Centre. Contrasts with Actualite.cd 9 Sept (Humura still AFC/M23-held; Rutoboko/Kibahemula retaken by wazalendo).
r1-NKW-2026H2-010.vn: Statement supported. Date corrected: 7 Sept on the page is a different event (fighting on another axis); the capture is dated only by the report's publication, so 2026-09-08, approximate. Flag '1' is 'Nyamaboko 1', printed. Capture day not stated; dated to the report (8 Sept). The only 7 Sept on the page concerns fighting on the Minjenje-Pinga axis in Walikale. Separate account from Actualite.cd's report of wazalendo retaking Rutoboko and Kibahemula on 8 Sept. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (8 Sep 2026) supports every clause, but the stored excerpt carried only the dislodging sentence; the capture sentence and the health-source quote are added. The page gives no exact date for the capture (8 Sep is the publication date). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (8 Sep 2026) supports every clause, but the stored excerpt carried only the dislodging sentence; the capture sentence and the health-source quote are added. The page gives no exact date for the capture (8 Sep is the publication date).
src: Selon des sources concordantes, les combattants de l’AFC/M23 ont délogé l’armée congolaise et les milices Wazalendo qui avaient repris le contrôle de cette zone.
Les combattants de l’AFC/M23 ont pris le contrôle des villages de Kazinga et Humura, dans le groupement Nyamaboko 1, en territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu.

« Kazinga est sous contrôle de l’AFC/M23. Ils ont repris aussi Ngomashi, Mwima, Humura et Burinda. Il y a des combats loin de nous », a déclaré une source sanitaire à Kivu Morning Post, sous couvert d’anonymat.

r1-NKW-2026H2-011.s: Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'DMK, La Tempête des Tropiques / MCP', reported that, according to certain sources, the army allegedly used air strikes on Tuesday 8 September at around 5 p.m. against rebel positions at Malemo (Bahali Mokoto groupement, Masisi) and Luola (Walikale); local sources said they heard loud detonations.
r1-NKW-2026H2-011.n: Conditional ('aurait fait usage'); unnamed sources; no FARDC confirmation seen.
r1-NKW-2026H2-011.vn: Statement supported and kept conditional. '5 p.m.' renders '17h'. End-of-page credit shows the origin is La Tempête des Tropiques, so originating_source set to it. Republished by Mediacongo from La Tempête des Tropiques; the article is written in the conditional and uses pro-government wording elsewhere ('l'ennemi rwandais'). No toll given; no FARDC confirmation seen. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Mediacongo, 10 Sep 2026, credit line 'Par DMK, La Tempête des Tropiques / MCP, via mediacongo.net' (originating_source already records it). All clauses are on the page, in the conditional; no toll available. The statement should credit La Tempête des Tropiques.
src: A en croire certaines sources, l'armée nationale aurait fait usage de frappes aériennes, le mardi 8 septembre, aux environs de 17h, visant les positions rebelles à Malemo, dans le groupement Bahali Mokoto, territoire de Masisi, ainsi qu'à Luola, dans le territoire de Walikale.

r1-NKW-2026H2-012.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing anonymous local sources, that violent fighting began at about 5 a.m. on Thursday 10 September 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale, when a Wazalendo-FARDC coalition launched an offensive on AFC-M23 positions; it described Kibati as having been under AFC-M23 control for several months, and a resident said no inhabitants remained in Kibati.
r1-NKW-2026H2-012.n: Outcome reported by Actualite.cd on 18 Sept (next claim).
r1-NKW-2026H2-012.vn: Date '10' printed on the page. All clauses supported. Single local outlet relaying anonymous sources: graded C, not B. excerpt_en flags: 'AFC-M23'/'Kibati' renderings, translation faithful.
src: Selon des sources locales, sous couvert d’anonymat, la coalition Wazalendo-FARDC a lancé une offensive contre les positions de l’AFC-M23 vers 5 heures du matin, dans le but de les déloger de la zone.
Considéré comme une zone stratégique, Kibati était sous contrôle des éléments de l’AFC-M23 depuis plusieurs mois.

r1-NKW-2026H2-013.s: Actualite.cd reported on 18 September that the centre of Kibati, in Luberike groupement (Walikale), had returned under AFC/M23 control after the withdrawal of the FARDC and wazalendo, who had briefly occupied Kibati and advanced to Milonge, about five kilometres along the Kibati-Kashebere axis.
r1-NKW-2026H2-013.n: Date is publication date; exact retaking day not given. Page also describes an AFC/M23 push toward Hembe aimed at Pinga via Bushimoo, met by a FARDC counter-offensive.
r1-NKW-2026H2-013.vn: Every clause supported. Flag '18' is the publication date, printed on the page ('ven 18/09/2026'). Day of the retaking not given; dated to the report (18 Sept).
src: Le centre de Kibati dans le groupement Luberike, est repassé sous contrôle de l’AFC/M23 après le retrait des FARDC et des wazalendo.

r1-NKW-2026H2-014.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the FARDC, in a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Marc Elongo, spokesperson of operational sector Sokola 1 Grand-Nord and Front Nord, said on 20 September they observe the ceasefire on all North Kivu front lines while denouncing attacks they attribute to AFC/M23-RDF on the Walikale-Masisi axis, which they said violate the Doha and Washington accords and cause displacement toward Walikale, with villages burned and fields destroyed.
r1-NKW-2026H2-014.n: Partisan statement of the Congolese army. Same page: military governor of North Kivu and operations commander is général-major Somo Kakule Évariste (named as printed 'Somo Kakule Évariste').
r1-NKW-2026H2-014.vn: All clauses printed on the page. Flagged '20', '23', '7' are the receipt date, 'M23' and '7sur7'; all printed. 'said on 20 September' is read as the date the communiqué was made public/received (noted). Party statement (FARDC says). 20 September is the day a copy reached 7sur7.cd; the communiqué's own date is not printed. The communiqué also cites the North Kivu military governor, général-major Somo Kakule Évariste, on the army's right to defend its positions. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 20 Sep 2026 (Bantou Kapanza Son): every clause is on the page (communiqué copy received on Sun 20 Sep). The stored excerpt only carried the displacement clause; added the ceasefire and accords passages. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 20 Sep 2026 (Bantou Kapanza Son): every clause is on the page (communiqué copy received on Sun 20 Sep). The stored excerpt only carried the displacement clause; added the ceasefire and accords passages.
src: Toujours selon ce communiqué signé par le lieutenant Marc Elongo, porte-parole du secteur opérationnel Sokola 1 Grand-Nord et Front Nord, ces attaques provoquent de nouveaux déplacements de populations civiles vers Walikale.
Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) affirment observer le cessez-le-feu sur l’ensemble des lignes de front dans la province du Nord-Kivu, à l'est de la RDC .
Selon les FARDC, ces actions seraient en violation des accords de Doha et de Washington, que la RDC affirme respecter.

r1-NKW-2026H2-015.s: 7sur7.cd reported a communiqué from major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, in which the FARDC, supported by VDP, said they neutralised 14 AFC/M23 elements over three days of fighting in Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru, with thirteen other fighters wounded, three captured and two VDP fighters killed; the FARDC said they retook the Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi) on Tuesday 15 September 2026.
r1-NKW-2026H2-015.l: Masisi, Walikale and Rutshuru territories; Miko hill and Remeka centre (Masisi)
r1-NKW-2026H2-015.x: FARDC: 14 AFC/M23 killed, 13 wounded, 3 captured, 2 VDP killed, 8 weapons recovered
r1-NKW-2026H2-015.n: Army figures, unverified. The 14 'neutralised' figure appears in the page's first sentence ('affirment avoir neutralisé 14 éléments') and two VDP killed in a later sentence. Date range: three days ending around 19 Sept; 15 Sept for the Remeka claim. 34th military region (page spelling).
r1-NKW-2026H2-015.vn: Every figure is printed on the page (14 in the title and lead; two VDP killed and eight weapons, conditional, later in the article). Attribution to FARDC kept throughout. date_precision 'range' with a single date was incoherent: set approximate. Party figures (FARDC says), unverified. The three days of fighting are not dated on the page; only the Remeka/Miko retaking is dated (15 Sept). Actualite.cd (18 Sept) separately reports Miko and Remeka back under government control. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 19 Sep 2026 (Reagan Bin Kakani): every clause is on the page, but the stored excerpts do not carry the headline figure (14 AFC/M23 neutralised) or the two VDP killed; added. The page dates the retaking of Miko and Remeka to Tue 15 Sep 2026; the article itself is dated 19 Sep. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: 7sur7.cd, 19 Sep 2026 (Reagan Bin Kakani): every clause is on the page, but the stored excerpts do not carry the headline figure (14 AFC/M23 neutralised) or the two VDP killed; added. The page dates the retaking of Miko and Remeka to Tue 15 Sep 2026; the article itself is dated 19 Sep.
src: Selon un communiqué du major Dieudonné Kasereka, chargé de communication de la 34ᵉ région militaire, parvenu à 7SUR7.CD, treize autres combattants ont été blessés et trois capturés au cours de ces affrontements.
Les FARDC indiquent, par ailleurs, avoir reconquis, mardi 15 septembre 2026, la colline de Miko ainsi que le centre de Remeka, dans le territoire de Masisi.

Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP), affirment avoir neutralisé 14 éléments de l’AFC/M23 au terme de trois jours de combats dans les territoires de Masisi, Walikale et Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu.
Le même bilan fait état de deux combattants VDP tués au cours des opérations.

r1-NKW-2026H2-016.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting resumed early on Friday 25 September between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by wazalendo at Remeka, Ufamandu 1er groupement (Masisi), about a week after the FARDC and wazalendo retook the centre of Remeka in a counter-offensive; AFC/M23 reportedly attacked with reinforcements from Ngungu.
r1-NKW-2026H2-016.n: Outcome of 25 Sept fighting not stated.
r1-NKW-2026H2-016.vn: Date 25 Sept and every clause printed on the page. Flags '1' (Ufamandu 1er) and '23' (M23) printed. Outcome of the 25 Sept fighting not stated. 'About a week after' is consistent with the FARDC's 15 Sept retaking claim.
src: Cette reprise des combats intervient environ une semaine après la reconquête du centre de Remeka par les FARDC et les wazalendo, lors d’une contre-offensive

r1-NKW-2026H2-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that Médecins Sans Frontières was transferring its medical activities at Sake, Masisi territory, to Première Urgence Internationale after 13 months; in that period MSF teams treated more than 10 300 survivors of sexual violence, and MSF said it was redirecting resources to other areas including Katoyi in Masisi.
r1-NKW-2026H2-017.a: Médecins Sans Frontières; Première Urgence Internationale
r1-NKW-2026H2-017.x: MSF (via Actualite.cd): over 10 300 survivors of sexual violence treated; about 3 500 malnourished children; over 1 740 deliveries; psychological support to over 10 400 people, over 13 months
r1-NKW-2026H2-017.n: Handover of care, not an attack or denial of access; 'health' field set as nearest allowed value is questionable: reviewer may recategorise as displacement_humanitarian. Page says MSF in Feb 2025 rehabilitated the heavily damaged Sake reference health centre. Complements existing draft NKS-2026Q4#5 (Actualite.cd 17 Oct).
r1-NKW-2026H2-017.vn: Statement and figures supported by the page. Recategorised from health_care_access/facility_closed to displacement_humanitarian, since the facility did not close (care handed over to PUI). Handover of care to PUI, not a closure or an attack: PUI continues care at the Sake reference health centre. The sexual-violence figure (survivantes, female survivors) covers 13 months of MSF activity at Sake. Figures are MSF's, relayed by Actualite.cd.
src: Ses équipes ont également soigné plus de 10 300 survivantes de violences sexuelles et apporté un soutien psychologique à plus de 10 400 personnes.
transfère ses activités médicales à Sake, dans le territoire de Masisi, à l’organisation Première Urgence Internationale (PUI), afin d’assurer la continuité des soins.

r1-NKW-2026H2-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Club des Filles Reporters RDC (CFR RDC), after a mission from 25 to 27 September 2026, said nearly 2 350 displaced families lived in precarious conditions at Lukaraba (Walikale) and Hombo Sud (Kalehe, South Kivu); at Lukaraba the families had fled Ziralo, Ufamandu, Remeka, Lurere and Biriko, and at Hombo Sud the hospital was said to be under strain from sick or war-wounded displaced people.
r1-NKW-2026H2-018.n: Page notes needs in food, health care and protection of women, girls and children.
r1-NKW-2026H2-018.vn: Flagged figures (2 350; 25-27 Sept) are printed in the article's first paragraph. All clauses supported. Single NGO account relayed by Radio Okapi; the headline says 'more than 2 000 families', the body 'nearly 2 350'.
src: À Lukaraba, les familles ayant fui les violences dans plusieurs localités, notamment Ziralo, Ufamandu, Remeka, Lurere et Biriko, vivent dans des abris de fortune, rapporte le CFR RDC.

r1-POL-2025-001.s: Jeune Afrique reported that the leaders of SADC and EAC, meeting in a summit in Tanzania, urged an end to fighting between the Congolese army and the M23 and its Rwandan allies, and that the defence chiefs of the two blocs were tasked to meet within five days and give technical guidance on an immediate and unconditional ceasefire, a spokesperson said.
r1-POL-2025-001.l: Dar es Salaam, Tanzania (call on North and South Kivu conflict)
r1-POL-2025-001.a: EAC and SADC heads of state; Rwandan President Paul Kagame and (by videoconference) Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi attended, per Jeune Afrique
r1-POL-2025-001.n: Two independent outlets on the same summit; DW dates the communiqué 8 Feb 2025. The Jeune Afrique excerpt does not itself print the date; date taken from DW.
r1-POL-2025-001.vn: Both pages support the summit; JA copy is credited 'Par Jeune Afrique avec AFP', so origin is AFP; DW is its own reporting (Fréjus Quenum), independent. Statement attributed per source. The actor field's Kagame/videoconference Tshisekedi attendance is printed on the JA page: 'Le sommet, auquel ont participé le président rwandais Paul Kagame et, par vidéoconférence, son homologue congolais Félix Tshisekedi'. 'M23' (flagged '23') printed on JA page. excerpt_en flag: translation fine. Jeune Afrique's copy is credited 'Par Jeune Afrique avec AFP'. DW dates the summit Saturday 8 February 2025 (08.02.2025) in Dar es Salaam and separately reports the leaders demanded de-escalation measures.
src: Les chefs des forces de défense des huit pays membres de la Communauté des États d’Afrique de l’Est (EAC) et des 16 pays membres de la Communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe (SADC) ont été chargés de « se réunir dans les cinq jours et de fournir des directives techniques sur un cessez-le-feu immédiat et inconditionnel », a indiqué un porte-parole.
Réunis en sommet extraordinaire à Dar es Salaam, les leaders de la SADC et de l'EAC ont exigé des mesures de désescalade.

r1-POL-2025-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that Angola's earlier mediation ended after two diplomatic setbacks: it had announced the end of its mediation and said it wanted to concentrate on African Union priorities.
r1-POL-2025-002.l: Luanda, Angola (mediation on eastern DRC conflict)
r1-POL-2025-002.n: The excerpt's 'two setbacks' are described just before it on the page; announcement date not in excerpt (RFI, 24 Mar 2025, could not be fetched).
r1-POL-2025-002.vn: Supported. The two setbacks are the failed Dec 2024 Luanda meeting and the AFC/M23 refusal of the 18 March meeting, both described just before on the page. excerpt_en flag: 'African Union' translates 'Union africaine'; acceptable. The page says the announcement came less than two weeks before 26 March 2025; the exact date of the announcement is not on this page.
src: Ces deux revers diplomatiques avaient conduit l’Angola à annoncer la fin de sa médiation. Luanda a indiqué vouloir désormais concentrer ses efforts sur les priorités de l’Union africaine.

r1-POL-2025-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that a joint summit of SADC and EAC heads of state had resulted on Monday in the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi processes.
r1-POL-2025-003.a: SADC and EAC heads of state
r1-POL-2025-003.n: Weekday only ('lundi') on a page dated Wed 26 Mar 2025; the page text is internally unclear on which Monday (the Feb joint summit was a Saturday, 8 Feb). Reviewer should check; do not draw a date from this claim.
r1-POL-2025-003.vn: Excerpt exact and supports the narrow statement. Weekday-only timing kept as month precision; no date derived. The page (dated Wed 26 March 2025) says only 'lundi'; the exact Monday is not stated on the page and is not asserted here. The DW report on the 8 Feb summit also lists the merger of the Luanda and Nairobi processes as a measure retained then.
src: Dans le même temps, un sommet conjoint des chefs d’État de la SADC et de l’EAC a abouti lundi à la fusion des processus de Luanda et de Nairobi.

r1-POL-2025-004.s: Al Jazeera reported that the US Treasury Department said on Thursday that Rwanda's Minister of State for Regional Integration James Kabarebe was being targeted because he is "central to Rwanda's support" for the M23 armed group.
r1-POL-2025-004.l: Washington, D.C. (sanctions relating to North and South Kivu conflict)
r1-POL-2025-004.a: US Treasury Department; Rwanda (as sanctions target); M23
r1-POL-2025-004.n: Date 2025-02-20 from the page URL and weekday 'Thursday'. Rwanda denies supporting M23 (see next claim). Second sanctioned person (M23 spokesperson) not in this excerpt.
r1-POL-2025-004.vn: Supported; page published 20 Feb 2025 with 'on Thursday' (20 Feb 2025 was a Thursday). Attribution to Treasury preserved. Allegation by the US Treasury; Al Jazeera notes Rwanda denies supporting the M23.
src: The US Treasury Department on Thursday said Rwanda’s Minister of State for Regional Integration James Kabarebe was being targeted because he is “central to Rwanda’s support” for the M23 armed group.

r1-POL-2025-005.s: BBC News reported that, responding to the US sanctions, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict.
r1-POL-2025-005.n: Headline calls the sanctions 'unjustified'; the body's 'unjustified and unfounded' wording sits in a passage with a link artifact so is not quoted. Publication date used.
r1-POL-2025-005.vn: Supported by BBC (Wycliffe Muia). Party statement relayed by BBC. Date is the BBC publication date (21 Feb 2025); the BBC does not give the day of the ministry statement.
src: Responding to the US move, Rwanda's foreign ministry said the sanctions would not resolve the conflict

r1-POL-2025-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that the signing ceremony of the DRC-Rwanda peace agreement in Washington was presided over by US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, in the presence of Congolese Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner and her Rwandan counterpart Olivier Nduhungirehe.
r1-POL-2025-006.l: Washington, D.C. (agreement concerning the conflict in North and South Kivu)
r1-POL-2025-006.n: Page title title_en: 'DRC and Rwanda sign a peace agreement in Washington under US auspices'.
r1-POL-2025-006.vn: Supported. excerpt_en flag: capitalised words (US etc.) are translation of 'américain'; acceptable.
src: La cérémonie de signature de cet accord a été présidée par le secrétaire d’État américain Marco Rubio, en présence de Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, ministre congolaise des Affaires étrangères, et Olivier Nduhungirehe, son homologue rwandais.

r1-POL-2025-007.s: The DRC foreign ministry said in a press release that the comprehensive peace accord with Rwanda was signed in Washington in the presence of US Secretary of State Marco Rubio and described it as a decisive step towards ending the conflict.
r1-POL-2025-007.a: Government of the DRC (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
r1-POL-2025-007.n: Party communiqué, cited for what the party said only.
r1-POL-2025-007.vn: Supported by the communiqué itself. Partisan source, grade C as party statement. Party (DRC government) communiqué; recorded as what Kinshasa said.
src: Signé à Washington, D.C., en présence du Secrétaire d’État américain Marco Rubio, cet Accord historique marque une avancée décisive vers la fin du conflit.

r1-POL-2025-008.s: UN News reported that, in a statement released on 19 July, MONUSCO said the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha under Qatari mediation between the DRC government and AFC/M23 "reflects the parties’ resolve to prioritise peaceful means, establish a ceasefire, and set up a joint mechanism to define its practical implementation."
r1-POL-2025-008.l: Doha, Qatar (DRC government and AFC/M23; North and South Kivu conflict)
r1-POL-2025-008.n: UN News dates the MONUSCO statement 19 July; the page and Doha process pages date signature to 19 July 2025 (page headline-level; signing day itself is in the Qatari/AU texts).
r1-POL-2025-008.vn: Supported; 'AFC/M23' (flagged '23') printed on page. Date is the MONUSCO statement date.
src: In a statement released on 19 July, MONUSCO said that the Declaration of Principles, signed in Doha under the mediation of Qatar, “reflects the parties’ resolve to prioritise peaceful means, establish a ceasefire, and set up a joint mechanism to define its practical implementation.”

r1-POL-2025-009.s: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Minister of State Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the DRC government and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step.
r1-POL-2025-009.n: Mediator's own statement; dateline 15 Nov 2025 (a Saturday).
r1-POL-2025-009.vn: Supported; dateline 15 Nov 2025, which was a Saturday. Mediator's own statement.
ent: Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi
src: Dr. Mohammed bin Abdulaziz bin Saleh Al Khulaifi affirmed that the signing of the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the Congo River Alliance (March 23 Movement), which took place Saturday, represents an important step

r1-POL-2025-010.s: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs said the parties' progress included the signing of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism on October 14, 2025, and the detainee release mechanism on September 14, 2025.
r1-POL-2025-010.n: Two dated mechanisms, as stated by the mediator.
r1-POL-2025-010.vn: Supported verbatim by the release. Dates as stated by the mediator; not independently checked here.
src: including the signing of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism on October 14, 2025, and the detainee release mechanism on September 14, 2025.

r1-POL-2025-011.s: BBC News Afrique reported that the verdict of the Haute Cour militaire in the trial of Joseph Kabila was delivered on a Tuesday after several postponements: the former Congolese president was sentenced to death by the court, which also ordered his immediate arrest.
r1-POL-2025-011.n: Date computed from weekday 'mardi' and the page's 'Mise à jour 30 septembre 2025' (page 'Published 25 juillet 2025'); Le Monde URL also dated 2025-09-30 (page could not be fetched). Verdict was in absentia per Le Monde headline (not fetched).
r1-POL-2025-011.vn: Supported. Not adding in-absentia detail (no fetched source prints it). The page's own 'crimes de guerre' wording is not used in the statement. Date derived from 'ce mardi' and the page update of 30 Sept 2025 (a Tuesday). The BBC page does not state the verdict was in absentia; it says his whereabouts are unknown. Joseph Kabila rejects all charges, per the same page.
src: Reporté à plusieurs reprises, le verdict de la Haute Cour militaire de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) dans le procès contre Joseph Kabila est tombé ce mardi. L'ancien président congolais est condamné à mort par la cour qui ordonne également son arrestation immédiate.

r1-POL-2025-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe told the press on Thursday 30 October 2025 that any decision on reopening Goma airport must be taken within the Doha negotiations, and that Paris could not reopen an airport while those concerned were not present.
r1-POL-2025-012.l: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement made in Kigali/Rwanda)
r1-POL-2025-012.n: Context: French President Macron announced at a Paris conference the planned reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian flights. DW (2025-10-31) independently reports Rwanda's opposition.
r1-POL-2025-012.vn: Statement supported. Location of the remark is inferred in draft location field; flagged in note. The page does not say where Nduhungirehe spoke; the location 'Kigali/Rwanda' in the draft is not supported.
src: Notre position est que toute décision doit être prise dans le cadre des négociations de Doha, où le gouvernement congolais et l’AFC/M23 sont engagés dans un dialogue. Paris ne peut rouvrir un aéroport alors que les principaux concernés ne sont pas présents"a déclaré jeudi 30 octobre 2025, devant la presse, Olivier Nduhungirehe.

r1-POL-2025-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya recalled that the reopening of Goma airport would take place only with the authorisation of the Congolese authorities and exclusively for daytime humanitarian flights.
r1-POL-2025-013.l: Goma airport, North Kivu (statement in Kinshasa)
r1-POL-2025-013.n: Exact date of the remark not stated; publication date used.
r1-POL-2025-013.vn: Excerpt exact, supports statement. Date is the Actualite.cd publication date; the page does not date Muyaya's remark.
src: Le porte-parole du gouvernement, Patrick Muyaya, a rappelé que la réouverture de l’aéroport de Goma se fera uniquement sur autorisation des autorités congolaises, et exclusivement pour des vols humanitaires effectués en journée.

r1-POL-2025-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa asked on X how the reopening of Goma airport for humanitarian reasons could be discussed while Walikale and Masisi in North Kivu and Fizi, Walungu and Mwenga in South Kivu were, in his words, subjected daily to bombardments by the Kinshasa regime targeting civilian sites, factories, bridges, airfields and humanitarian aircraft.
r1-POL-2025-014.l: Walikale, Masisi (North Kivu); Fizi, Walungu, Mwenga (South Kivu)
r1-POL-2025-014.n: Partisan allegation of strikes by Kinshasa; cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Not independently corroborated here (lead for attack/health-access units).
r1-POL-2025-014.vn: Supported as party statement; 'AFC/M23' printed on page. Partisan allegation by AFC/M23; not corroborated. Date is the article's publication date.
src: Comment évoquer la réouverture de l’aéroport de Goma pour des motifs humanitaires alors que les territoires de Walikale et de Masisi au Nord-Kivu, ainsi que ceux de Fizi, Walungu et Mwenga au Sud-Kivu, subissent quotidiennement des bombardements du régime de Kinshasa ciblant des sites civils, usines, ponts, aérodromes et avions humanitaires ? " s’est interrogé Corneille Nangaa sur le réseau social X.

r1-POL-2025-015.s: Jeune Afrique reported that, after several days of pressure from the US administration, the Kigali-backed rebel group announced in the night of 15 to 16 December its intention to withdraw from the city of Uvira, which it had taken the previous week.
r1-POL-2025-015.a: AFC/M23 (the 'groupe rebelle soutenu par Kigali', per Jeune Afrique)
r1-POL-2025-015.n: Capture of Uvira roughly 10 Dec 2025 (BBC page dated 11 Dec); exact day not in excerpt. Announcement only; actual withdrawal not established here (Afrikarabia, 24 Dec, says fighting continued around the city; not fetched).
r1-POL-2025-015.vn: Supported; JA byline 'Par Jeune Afrique' (photo credit AFP only). Announcement only; Anadolu reported no withdrawal movement observed by 07:00 GMT on Tuesday 16 December. 'Kigali-backed' is Jeune Afrique's characterisation.
src: Après plusieurs jours de pression exercée par l’administration américaine, le groupe rebelle soutenu par Kigali a annoncé dans la nuit du 15 au 16 décembre son intention de se retirer de la ville d’Uvira, conquise la semaine dernière.

r1-POL-2025-016.s: BBC News Afrique reported that, in a press release published Tuesday, AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa said the unilateral withdrawal followed a request from the American mediators. Anadolu Agency quoted a communiqué signed by Corneille Nangaa: "The AFC/M23 will unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, as requested by the American mediation".
r1-POL-2025-016.n: BBC page dated 11 Dec, updated 16 Dec; 'mardi' = 16 Dec 2025 computed from weekday and update date; JA says communiqué dated 15 December. Date computed from weekday and publication date.
r1-POL-2025-016.vn: Both sources verified independently (BBC: Makumeno/Chothia/Muia; AA: Pascal Mulegwa, Kinshasa). Statement now says which clause rests on which outlet; date widened to the communiqué date/publication range. Anadolu and Jeune Afrique say the communiqué is dated 15 December; the BBC says it was published Tuesday (16 December). Anadolu reported that no withdrawal movement had been observed by 07:00 GMT Tuesday. The communiqué also sets conditions (demilitarisation, neutral force).
src: Dans un communiqué de presse publié mardi, Corneille Nangaa, le leader de l'AFC /M23, a déclaré que ce retrait unilatéral faisait suite à une demande des médiateurs américains.

« L’AFC/M23 retirera unilatéralement ses forces de la ville d’Uvira, comme l’a demandé la médiation américaine », indique un communiqué signé par Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo et dirigeant de la branche politique du M23.

r1-POL-2025-017.s: The US State Department said, in a release on the signing of the Washington Accords for Peace and Prosperity between the DRC and Rwanda, that the DRC and Rwanda signed the Regional Economic Integration Framework, that President Felix Tshisekedi signed on behalf of the Government of the DRC and President Paul Kagame on behalf of the Government of Rwanda, and that the signing ceremony was attended by, among others, Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye.
r1-POL-2025-017.a: Government of the DRC; Government of Rwanda; United States
r1-POL-2025-017.n: Official US release; mediator's own account. Date from release URL path and search listing (4 Dec 2025).
r1-POL-2025-017.vn: Draft tied the Tshisekedi/Kagame signatures to the REIF only; the release does not say which instrument that sentence refers to, and its main subject is the Washington Accords. Narrowed to the release's own sentences; 'Felix' spelled as printed. The release says the signing on December 4 was hosted by President Donald J. Trump.
src: President Felix Tshisekedi signed on behalf of the Government of the DRC, and President Paul Kagame signed on behalf of the Government of Rwanda. The signing ceremony was attended by Togolese President of the Council of Ministers Faure Gnassingbé, Angolan President João Lourenço, Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, Kenyan President William Ruto

r1-POL-2026-001.s: The US Department of the Treasury announced on 2 March 2026 that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) had imposed sanctions on the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) and four of its senior officials, stating that the RDF is actively supporting, training, and fighting alongside the M23.
r1-POL-2026-001.a: United States Department of the Treasury (OFAC)
r1-POL-2026-001.n: US government is a mediator/party to Washington Accords; statement is its own position. Page dated 2 Mar 2026 per search result; excerpt checked against fetched page. Rwanda's response not yet searched (see gaps).
r1-POL-2026-001.vn: Excerpt exact; the date (March 2, 2026) is printed in the page header next to the title. Statement matches the page. The US government's own position (it is a mediator and party to the Washington Accords). The page names the four designated officers: Vincent Nyakarundi, Ruki Karusisi, Mubarakh Muganga and Stanislas Gashugi (not yet in a claim).
src: Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) imposed sanctions on the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)—the military of Rwanda—and four of its senior officials. The RDF is actively supporting, training, and fighting alongside the March 23 Movement (M23)

r1-POL-2026-002.s: The US Treasury said that, days after the Washington Accords signing, M23 captured Uvira, a strategic city on the border with Burundi, in an offensive that resulted in civilian deaths and forced thousands of residents to flee their homes; it said that despite M23's subsequent exit from Uvira, its continued presence near the border with Burundi, and the RDF's continued support for M23, carried the risk of escalating the conflict into a broader regional war.
r1-POL-2026-002.a: United States Department of the Treasury (OFAC)
r1-POL-2026-002.n: Attribution is the US Treasury's own wording. Overlaps UV-2026Q1 on Uvira withdrawal; adds the US characterisation.
r1-POL-2026-002.vn: The draft said the Uvira events were 'part of its rationale for sanctions'; the page says instead that M23's presence near the border and RDF support 'carries the risk of escalating the conflict into a broader regional war'. Narrowed to the page's own wording. US government characterisation; the Treasury does not give dates for the capture of or exit from Uvira.
src: M23 captured Uvira, a strategic city located along the DRC-Burundi border. This military offensive resulted in civilian deaths and forced thousands of residents to flee their homes. Despite its subsequent exit from Uvira, M23’s continued presence near the border with Burundi

r1-POL-2026-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that representatives of the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, meeting from 17 to 21 August 2026 in Switzerland, agreed new steps for the Doha peace process, including a roadmap for continuing negotiations and strengthened follow-up of their commitments.
r1-POL-2026-003.n: State.gov and France24 results (22-23 Aug 2026) carry the joint statement; not opened.
r1-POL-2026-003.vn: Excerpt exact and matches. excerpt_en flag is only sentence-initial words (The, Meeting); the translation renders the excerpt alone.
src: Les représentants du gouvernement congolais et de l’AFC/M23 ont convenu de nouvelles étapes pour faire avancer le processus de paix engagé à Doha, au Qatar. Réunis du 17 au 21 août 2026 en Suisse, les deux camps ont notamment établi une feuille de route pour la poursuite des négociations et convenu de renforcer le suivi de leurs engagements.

r1-POL-2026-004.s: BBC News Afrique reported that the creation of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), with Joseph Kabila as president, was announced by FRN adviser Claude Ibalanky at a joint press conference at the former president's residence in Goma, a city controlled by the M23; BBC described the FRN as replacing the AFC-M23, and reported that Kabila would have as deputies the rebel leaders Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki and Sultani Makenga.
r1-POL-2026-004.a: FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation); Joseph Kabila; AFC/M23
r1-POL-2026-004.n: Announcement date not stated in excerpts; other results say meeting in Goma 10-11 Oct, declaration dated 12 Oct (Instagram snippets, not opened); BBC published 14 Oct. Date is approximate. Kinshasa's reaction in the next claim.
r1-POL-2026-004.vn: Date 2026-10-13 was not printed in any excerpt; set to a range ending on the publication date. Added the deputies clause, which source 2 prints (resolves the entities flag). excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial words only. The BBC article (published 14 October 2026) does not date the press conference; its sidebar lists a related BBC item dated 13 October 2026 ('L'ancien président nommé chef de la nouvelle coalition rebelle'). Announcement date therefore on or before 14 October 2026; exact day unconfirmed.
src: C'est au cours d'une conférence de presse tenue dans la résidence même de l'ancien président, Joseph Kabila à Goma, cette ville de l'Est de la RDC contrôlée par le mouvement rebelle M23, que la création du FRN, Front pour la refondation de la nation a été annoncée.

"Est créé un mouvement politico-militaire Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN)", et "devient président : Joseph Kabila", a déclaré Claude Ibalanky, conseiller du FRN, lors de la conférence de presse commune tenue dans la résidence de l'ancien président.

Placé désormais à la tête de ce mouvement rebelle, Joseph Kabila, ancien président de la République aura comme adjoints les chefs rebelles Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki et Sultani Makenga.

r1-POL-2026-005.s: Sosoyamboka.net reported that, in a declaration published on Sunday 18 October, Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya denounced the creation of the FRN as a new label masking the actors in the crisis, and said: "Quelle que soit sa dénomination, ce groupe armé relooké est appelé à disparaître au terme du processus de Doha".
r1-POL-2026-005.n: Single local aggregator; the original declaration not located. Spokesperson's full title/channel not verified.
r1-POL-2026-005.vn: Excerpts exact; the spokesperson title is printed in the article lede. excerpt_en flag is sentence-initial only. Single local outlet; the original declaration was not located. The same page reports Muyaya also accused Rwanda of seeking to present the conflict as an internal Congolese crisis (not yet a claim).
src: Dans une déclaration publiée dimanche 18 octobre, Patrick Muyaya a dénoncé la création de ce mouvement qu’il présente comme une nouvelle appellation destinée à masquer la nature des acteurs impliqués dans la crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC).
« Quelle que soit sa dénomination, ce groupe armé relooké est appelé à disparaître au terme du processus de Doha », a-t-il affirmé.

r1-POL-2026-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in Goma, in front of EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib and then the press, that the 'premiers demandeurs' for reopening the Goma international airport were the authorities in Goma, i.e. his movement, and that the AFC/M23 now said it accepted 'the principle' of discussions on the reopening process, 'taking into account the constraints' of the area it controls.
r1-POL-2026-006.n: Partisan statement reported by a Congolese outlet. Airport closed since late January 2025 (same article). Relevant to civilian access to health (humanitarian flights).
r1-POL-2026-006.vn: Name and date are on the page (lede) but not in the stored excerpt, so the date moves to the date field and the statement keeps the name the draft already had; added the 'principle' clause from source 1. Party statement reported by one Congolese outlet. The name Corneille Nangaa and the date 20 February are printed in the article's first sentence, not in the stored excerpt.
src: Devant la commissaire européenne Hadja Lahbib, puis face à la presse, le coordonnateur politique de la rébellion a assuré que les « premiers demandeurs » de la réouverture étaient les autorités présentes à Goma, c’est-à-dire son mouvement.
Signe d’une inflexion, l’AFC/M23 dit désormais accepter « le principe » de discussions sur le processus d’ouverture, « en tenant compte des contraintes » liées à l’espace qu’il contrôle.

r1-POL-2026-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the AFC/M23 made public on 6 June 2026 in Goma decision N°033/COORDO-PR/AFC-M23/2026 appointing new political-administrative authorities in South Kivu, including Kyalangalilwa Mulondani Nicolas as mayor of Bukavu.
r1-POL-2026-007.n: Party decision as reported by local outlet; the decision text itself not seen. Page also names commune and territory appointees (Bagira, Ibanda, Kadutu, Idjwi, Kabare, Kalehe, Walungu, Minova) — available for a names-only follow-up.
r1-POL-2026-007.vn: Excerpts exact; figure 033 is on the page (passage given). Deputy mayor Nyota Luandja Céline is printed in source 1. excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial only. The decision number is printed on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Per the page the decision modifies an earlier decision of April 2025, and also names: Shaka Muhoza and Bahaya Léon (Bagira), Mweze Prisca and Mutunwa Mbulanga (Ibanda), Ruremesha Théo and Cikuru Barhakaziga Pascaline (Kadutu), Ntambuka Pascal and Mwimbirisa Bulikoko René (Idjwi), Elie Rubabura Espoir and Kasindi Kingombe Benjamin (Kabare), Buseyi Jean Bosco and Muhamuka Mweze Amza (Kalehe), Shengamungu Anastasie and Tumusifu Félicien (Walungu), Sengimana Ruhungande Augustin and Mahombi Mutumai (Minova cité). Names-only follow-up needed.
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo/M23 (AFC/M23) a rendu publique, le 6 juin 2026 à Goma, une décision officielle portant nomination de nouvelles autorités politico-administratives dans la province du Sud-Kivu.
Monsieur Kyalangalilwa Mulondani Nicolas est nommé maire de la ville, assisté de Madame Nyota Luandja Céline comme maire adjointe.

r1-POL-2026-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese Ministry of Higher Education (ESU-RSI) firmly condemned on Monday 10 August the AFC/M23's appointments at several public higher-education institutions in Goma and Bukavu, calling the appointments publicised on 7 August 2026 by the de facto authorities a 'grave and unacceptable interference'.
r1-POL-2026-008.a: Government of the DRC (ESU-RSI ministry); AFC/M23
r1-POL-2026-008.n: Both Kinshasa position and AFC/M23 action; the institutions include medical-technique institutes (ISTM Goma/Bukavu).
r1-POL-2026-008.vn: Statement matches the excerpts. Removed 'Lawrence Kanyuka' from entities_named: the page does not print that name. Institutions named on the page include ISTM/Goma and ISTM/Bukavu (medical-technique institutes), ISC/Goma, ISDR/Bukavu, ISP/Goma and the Université Officielle de Bukavu. The ministry warned that anyone acting on the appointments faces sanctions.
src: Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur, universitaire, de la Recherche scientifique et des Innovations (ESU-RSI) a fermement condamné, ce lundi 10 aout, les nominations effectuées par l’AFC/M23 au sein de plusieurs établissements publics d’enseignement supérieur et universitaire de Goma et Bukavu, dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu.
Selon le document, les désignations rendues publiques, vendredi 7 août 2026, par les autorités de facto de Goma et Bukavu constituent une « ingérence grave et inacceptable »

r1-POL-2026-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC-M23 confirmed that a case of Ebola virus disease had been reported in Goma, an announcement made on Sunday 17 May 2026 by its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka.
r1-POL-2026-009.n: Epidemic context: health response in an M23-held area; RFI 21 May 2026 (not opened) reports Mukwege calling on M23 to reopen Goma airport for the response. Possible leads: DW 19 May, IRIS 8 June.
r1-POL-2026-009.vn: Excerpt exact and matches. excerpt_en flag is sentence-initial only. Party statement (AFC/M23 communiqué) reported by one Congolese outlet; the page also reports the AFC/M23 set up a special Ebola response cell. No independent health-authority confirmation in this unit. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-009: Wording aligned with the source ('confirme qu'un cas ... a été signalé'). Searched (fr): no counter-account; the case is independently corroborated (Le Monde 17 May, 'un premier cas confirmé à Goma'; MSF citing North Kivu authorities' confirmation on 16 May), a lead for corroborate.py.; excerpt-support: nothing to add 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L’AFC-M23 confirme qu’un cas de Maladie à virus Ebola a été signalé à Goma, dans la province du Nord-Kivu. L’annonce a été faite ce dimanche 17 mai 2026 par Lawrence Kanyuka, chef du département de la communication et porte-parole de la rébellion AFC/M23.
Les autorités sanitaires ont confirmé, dimanche 17 mai 2026, la détection du premier cas d’Ebola dans la ville de Goma, au Nord-Kivu

r1-POL-2026-010.s: A joint statement by the representatives of the Government of the DRC and of the AFC/M23, published by the African Union Peace and Security Department, said the Parties agreed on the critical importance of ensuring life-saving humanitarian assistance for the people of eastern DRC and made substantial progress toward a protocol on Humanitarian Access and Judicial Protection, agreed to refrain from attacks on objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities, and agreed to respect and protect humanitarian actors.
r1-POL-2026-010.a: Government of the DRC; AFC/M23 (joint statement also released with Qatar, the United States, Togo as AU mediator, the African Union Commission and Switzerland)
r1-POL-2026-010.n: Joint party text hosted by AU; the page lists the title date '18 April 2026' (search snippet showed 19 Apr). Also covers ceasefire verification mechanism and prisoner release; the same page carries a commitment to refrain from attacks on hospital and school facilities.
r1-POL-2026-010.vn: Credited the joint statement to all its authors (not the hosting AU page); removed the '18 April' date from the statement (not printed in an excerpt; it stays in the date field); added the hospital-facilities commitment, relevant to health-care access, from the same page. Joint text of the parties and mediators, hosted by the AU; meetings held 13-17 April in Montreux. It records commitments in negotiation, not implementation. The page title carries the date 18 April 2026.
src: The Government of the DRC and AFC/M23 (the Parties) agreed on the critical importance of ensuring life-saving humanitarian assistance for the people of eastern DRC and made substantial progress toward conclusion of a protocol on Humanitarian Access and Judicial Protection.

The Parties agreed to respect and protect humanitarian actors including local responders and beneficiaries, and their objects used for humanitarian relief operations, and allow them to operate safely.

r1-POL-2026-011.s: Amnesty International said on 25 June 2026 that the Wazalendo member group CMC-FDP, backed by the Congolese army, has killed and tortured civilians, looted property, and abducted women as sexual slaves in Rutshuru territory; Amnesty interviewed 16 victims, survivors and family members about abuses between June and December 2025.
r1-POL-2026-011.l: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-POL-2026-011.a: CMC-FDP (Collective of Movements for Change-People’s Defence Forces), a Wazalendo member group
r1-POL-2026-011.x: Amnesty International: 16 victims, survivors and family members interviewed
r1-POL-2026-011.n: NGO investigation (remote interviews). Perpetrator is as alleged by Amnesty; CMC-FDP denial recorded separately. Area is under M23 control per Amnesty. No individual names recorded here (survivors unnamed).
r1-POL-2026-011.vn: Excerpts exact; the date 25 June 2026 and the Wazalendo membership are printed on the page (passages given). Amnesty's allegations, based on remote interviews; CMC-FDP operates in the Bukombo area of Rutshuru, which Amnesty says is controlled by M23. The page describes two survivors held in conditions Amnesty calls sexual slavery (one abducted in June 2025, held at a base in Mudugudu, Bukombo); survivors are unnamed. Legal characterisations on the page are Amnesty's.
src: An armed group backed by the Congolese army (FARDC) has killed and tortured civilians, looted property, and abducted women as sexual slaves in Rutshuru territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Amnesty International said today.

Between March and April 2026, Amnesty International conducted remote interviews by secure phone applications with 16 victims, survivors, and family members of civilians killed, raped, tortured, abducted, or ill-treated by CMC-FDP fighters between June and December 2025.

r1-POL-2026-012.s: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026 and denied responsibility for the abuses Amnesty documented, asserting that CMC-FDP remains committed to respecting human rights.
r1-POL-2026-012.l: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-POL-2026-012.n: Party denial reported by Amnesty; counter to the claim above.
r1-POL-2026-012.vn: Excerpt exact and matches. Party denial as reported by Amnesty; per the same page CMC-FDP 'categorically rejects' the sexual violence allegations.
src: CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026. CMC-FDP denied responsibility for the abuses documented here and asserted that “CMC-FDP remains committed to respecting human rights and the discipline of its combatants.”

r1-POL-2026-013.s: Human Rights Watch and the Congolese organization SOFEPADI said that conflict-related sexual violence in eastern DRC had escalated, and that HRW had documented sexual violence by members of at least five non-state armed groups and the Congolese army.
r1-POL-2026-013.l: Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu provinces
r1-POL-2026-013.a: M23, other armed groups and Congolese army, as HRW says
r1-POL-2026-013.n: The page's dateline reads 'January 12, 2025' but the URL path and search metadata say 2026; the dateline is probably a typo — verifier to check. Regional (Ituri included); only North and South Kivu relevant to phase 1.
r1-POL-2026-013.vn: Excerpt exact; the 'escalated' clause and SOFEPADI co-authorship are on the page (passage given). Date checked: header 2026, dateline typo 2025. The page header dates the release 'January 12, 2026'; the body dateline reads '(Kinshasa, January 12, 2025)', which is inconsistent with the November 2025 interviews the release describes, so 2026 is taken as correct. HRW's interviews were with SOFEPADI's Beni and Bunia offices (northeastern Congo); the release covers Ituri as well as the Kivus.
src: Human Rights Watch has documented sexual violence by members of at least five non-state armed groups and the Congolese army in eastern Congo.

r1-POL-2026-014.s: Human Rights Watch and SOFEPADI said that expanded fighting in Ituri, North Kivu and South Kivu, funding cuts and limited access to health services made it harder for survivors of sexual violence to get support, and that many clinics offering health care and other support had been forced to close.
r1-POL-2026-014.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (and Ituri)
r1-POL-2026-014.n: See date caveat in the previous claim.
r1-POL-2026-014.vn: Statement matches. Removed 'Évariste Ndayishimiye' from entities_named: a copy error, the HRW page does not name him. See the date note on the companion HRW claim (header 2026, dateline typo 2025). The page links the clinic closures in part to US aid cuts.
src: Expanded fighting in Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu provinces as well as funding cuts and limited access to health services, have made it increasingly difficult for women and girls who survive sexual violence to get the holistic support they need. Many clinics offering health care and other support have been forced to close .

r1-POL-2026-015.s: Beto.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said on France 24 on 23 September 2026, on the margins of the UN General Assembly, that he saw no sign of disengagement of Rwandan forces from eastern DRC and judged that the FDLR were only a pretext.
r1-POL-2026-015.n: Same page notes the UN Group of Experts has not established Burundi army–FDLR collaboration in its last three reports (not cited). Rwanda's reply not searched.
r1-POL-2026-015.vn: Excerpt exact and matches; the year 2026 is in the page's dateline (29 SEPTEMBRE 2026) and the 81st UNGA session reference. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words that are also capitalised in the French (FDLR, DRC equivalents). Relay by a Congolese outlet of a France 24 interview; the France 24 original was not opened. Per the same page Ndayishimiye spoke as a head of state whose army fights in South Kivu and as AU chairperson; it quotes him: 'nous sommes dans l'impasse'.
src: Sur France 24, le 23 septembre, en marge de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies, le président burundais Évariste Ndayishimiye dit ne voir aucun signe de désengagement des forces rwandaises de l’est de la RDC et juge que les FDLR ne sont qu’un prétexte.

r1-POL-2026-016.s: Al Jazeera, citing AFP and Reuters, reported that on Monday the UN and government sources said a ceasefire monitoring team had arrived to track the Qatari-mediated truce, and that the UN said the mission had deployed to Minembwe in South Kivu, where intense fighting had persisted in recent months.
r1-POL-2026-016.a: ceasefire verification mission (Congolese government, M23, ICGLR observers)
r1-POL-2026-016.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date. The same article says the mission will visit Uvira and Kalehe. Caption dates a photo as 12 May 2026 for FARDC in Ruzizi Plains.
r1-POL-2026-016.vn: Excerpts exact (stored excerpt 0 omits the space before the final period; verbatim passage given). Monday = 24 Aug 2026, the publication date. Byline 'Al Jazeera Staff, AFP and Reuters', published 24 Aug 2026 (a Monday). Per the page the mission is composed of members of the Congolese government and M23 plus ICGLR observers, with MONUSCO logistical support reported by local journalists, and will visit Uvira and Kalehe. Lead: the same page reports a DRC statement that day accusing M23 of killing 'more than 300 people' in June and July, rejected by M23.
src: The United Nations and government sources said on Monday that the monitoring team had arrived to track the progress of the Qatari-mediated truce.
The UN said that the mission had deployed to Minembwe, located in the country’s mineral-rich South Kivu province, where intense fighting has persisted in recent months.

r1-SKC-2025H1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that the villages of Muzinzi and Bwahungu in Walungu territory were the scene of fighting between the FARDC supported by the Wazalendo and the M23.
r1-SKC-2025H1-001.vn: Day number came only from the page header (sam 01/03/2025), not the excerpt or body; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. 'Citing several witnesses' dropped: the excerpt is the outlet's narration. Article dated 1 March 2025; witnesses quoted say the fighting had gone on since the morning.
src: Deux villages du territoire de Walungu notamment Muzinzi et Bwahungu sont le théâtre des affrontements entre les FARDC appuyées par les Wazalendo et le M23.

r1-SKC-2025H1-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to several local sources, fighting resumed early on 1 March 2025 in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where the Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to the M23 attacked Wazalendo positions.
r1-SKC-2025H1-002.l: Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Itombwe, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-002.a: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Android (allied to M23); Wazalendo
r1-SKC-2025H1-002.n: Local civil-society sources named elsewhere in the article (Pacifique Kararuka, Parisien Ngini) are not in the excerpt. The article says Twirwaneho and Wazalendo had clashed in Itombwe villages since 23 February.
r1-SKC-2025H1-002.vn: Body prints 'ce 1 mars' (year only in page header); flag resolved by page clause. Excerpt carries attribution to local sources. A civil-society leader quoted in the same article describes the fighting as Twirwaneho against the FARDC, not the Wazalendo.
src: Selon plusieurs sources locales, les éléments de la coalition Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Android alliés au M23 qui ont attaqué les positions des Wazalendo.

r1-SKC-2025H1-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that local civil-society groups denounced the burning of houses in Bilalombili village, which had hosted people displaced from Mikenge and elsewhere, without giving a number.
r1-SKC-2025H1-003.n: Article quotes civil society saying all houses were burned and no toll was yet known; perpetrator not stated in the excerpt; the same article reports the Twirwaneho/M23 attack that morning.
r1-SKC-2025H1-003.vn: Excerpt supports; perpetrator correctly left unattributed.
src: Le village de Bilalombili avait accueilli les déplacés venus de Mikenge et ailleurs, les sociétés civiles locales dénoncent le fait que les maisons ont été incendiées sans donner le nombre.

r1-SKC-2025H1-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that, after fighting with Wazalendo militiamen, the AFC/M23 rebels entered Mwenga territory late on Monday 3 March 2025 via the locality of Kilungutwe.
r1-SKC-2025H1-004.l: Kilungutwe, Mwenga territory (from Walungu across the Kadubo river)
r1-SKC-2025H1-004.vn: Excerpt supports; title names AFC/M23 and Mwenga.
src: après des combats contre les miliciens wazalendo, les rebelles du M23 ont fait leur entrée dans ce territoire tard dans la soirée de ce lundi 3 mars 2025 via par la localité de Kilungutwe.

r1-SKC-2025H1-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that on the Monday (3 March 2025) on which the M23 entered Mwenga, fighting was reported in Walungu, Kaniola, Burhale, Bwahungu and Kamisisi in Walungu territory, and that it counted the AFC/M23 as already present in six South Kivu territories (Mwenga, Kalehe, Kabare, Walungu, Uvira and Fizi), the count resting in part on the Twirweneho group's allegiance to the rebellion, with only Shabunda and Idjwi not yet affected by the war.
r1-SKC-2025H1-005.l: Walungu, Kaniola, Burhale, Bwahungu and Kamisisi, Walungu territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-005.vn: Excerpt says only 'lundi'; the day number is printed elsewhere on the page, so the statement no longer gives it (date field keeps 3 March). Actor narrowed: the excerpt does not say who fought in those places. excerpt_en flag is the translation of 'Sud-Kivu' as 'South Kivu', a faithful translation. The six-territory count is the outlet's own statement and rests on the Twirwaneho's allegiance to the AFC/M23 in Uvira and Fizi. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Actualite.cd, 4 March 2025. The page qualifies the six-territory count 'par le fait de l'allégeance du groupe Twirweneho à cette rébellion'; the statement dropped that qualifier, which overstates direct AFC/M23 presence (notably in Uvira and Fizi). Excerpt is verbatim.
src: Pendant la journée du lundi, des combats ont été signalés à Walungu, Kaniola, Burhale, Bwahungu et Kamisisi (territoire de Walungu). Après avoir atteint le territoire de Mwenga, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 sont déjà présents dans 6 territoires à savoir, Mwenga, Kalehe, Kabare, Walungu, Uvira et Fizi par le fait de l'allégeance du groupe Twirweneho à cette rébellion. Au Sud-Kivu, seuls les territoires de Shabunda et d’Idjwi ne sont pas encore touchés par la guerre

r1-SKC-2025H1-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels seized Kaziba Centre late at night on 10 March 2025 after a full day of fighting against the FARDC supported by Wazalendo militiamen.
r1-SKC-2025H1-006.l: Kaziba Centre, Kaziba chefferie, Walungu territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-006.vn: Excerpt supports exactly. Kaziba later changed hands: Wazalendo control reported from 15 March or 17 March (two Actualite.cd articles disagree); AFC/M23 retook it on 27 April.
src: Les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 se sont emparés de Kaziba Centre tard dans la nuit du 10 mars 2025, après une journée entière de combats contre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) appuyées par les miliciens wazalendo.

r1-SKC-2025H1-007.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that Kaziba in Walungu territory and the localities of Kigarama and Rurambo in the Uvira highlands had been occupied by Wazalendo since Saturday 15 March 2025, and that residents saw no AFC/M23 rebels in Kaziba.
r1-SKC-2025H1-007.l: Kaziba, Walungu territory; Kigarama and Rurambo, Uvira highlands
r1-SKC-2025H1-007.n: Discrepancy to surface: the same outlet's 24 April article says the Wazalendo retook Kaziba on 17 March (a week after 10 March); this article says occupied since 15 March.
r1-SKC-2025H1-007.vn: The '23' flag is the '23' in 'AFC/M23', not a figure. Residents' observation is on the page, not in the excerpt (page-only clause). The article also says Kigatama/Rurambo were retaken by Wazalendo and 'certains éléments de la Task Force dont font partie les troupes burundaises': a lead on Burundian troops for a separate claim. Date conflict: this article says Wazalendo held Kaziba from Saturday 15 March; Actualite.cd's 24 and 28 April articles say they retook it on 17 March, a week after the 10 March capture.
src: La cité de Kaziba, dans le territoire de Walungu, ainsi que les localités de Kigarama et Rurambo dans les hauts plateaux d'Uvira sont occupés par les miliciens Wazalendo depuis samedi 15 mars dernier, selon plusieurs sources locales.

r1-SKC-2025H1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that two people died and many others were wounded in violent clashes on Tuesday 18 March between Wazalendo and the M23 in the Burhale groupement, Walungu territory.
r1-SKC-2025H1-008.vn: Statement unchanged; category changed from attack_on_civilians to military_operation because the source does not say the victims were civilians or name a perpetrator. The '2' flag is 'Deux' in the excerpt. The article does not say whether the dead and wounded were civilians or combatants, or who caused the casualties.
src: Deux personnes ont perdu la vie et de nombreuses autres ont été blessées lors de violents affrontements survenus mardi 18 mars entre les Wazalendo et le M23 dans le groupement de Burhale, situé dans le territoire de Walungu.

r1-SKC-2025H1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that the chef-lieu of Walungu territory was encircled, with the Wazalendo on one side and the M23 on the other, that the local administration was paralysed with its officials forced to live in hiding, and that the police and intelligence services were absent.
r1-SKC-2025H1-009.a: local administration; Wazalendo; M23; PNC and intelligence services
r1-SKC-2025H1-009.n: Report date; condition described as ongoing at publication.
r1-SKC-2025H1-009.vn: Report date (19 March) came only from the page header; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. Condition described as current at the report date.
src: Le chef-lieu du territoire de Walungu est encerclé de toutes parts : les Wazalendo d'un côté, le M23 de l'autre. L'administration locale est paralysée, ses responsables contraints de vivre dans la clandestinité. Les bureaux de l'administrateur de territoire et de la chefferie de Ngweshe sont abandonnés, alimentant les craintes des habitants de cette entité qui abrite les infrastructures administratives. Par ailleurs, la police et les services de renseignement sont désormais absents, accentuant le sentiment d'insécurité.

r1-SKC-2025H1-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Sunday 13 April M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups opened a new front in Butondo village (Luindi chefferie, Ihanga groupement, Mwenga territory), and quoted a local source denouncing the looting of cows, saying the M23 left with 16 cows the first time.
r1-SKC-2025H1-010.l: Butondo village, Ihanga groupement, Luindi chefferie, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-010.n: Alleged livestock looting by M23 rests on one anonymous local source; the quote is attributed in the article to "une source locale" (after the quoted words). The article says more cows were taken later, number not stated. The article calls these the first clashes to reach Luindi chefferie.
r1-SKC-2025H1-010.vn: Both excerpts on the page; locality detail is on the page next to the excerpt; quote correctly attributed to 'une source locale'. The cattle-looting allegation rests on one anonymous local source quoted by the outlet.
src: Les rebelles du M23 et différents groupes des Wazalendo ont ouvert un nouveau front la journée de ce dimanche 13 avril dans le village de Butondo
Cependant nous dénonçons le pillage des vaches. Pour la première fois les M23 sont partis avec 16 vaches

r1-SKC-2025H1-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that clashes on Thursday 17 April between Wazalendo fighters and the AFC-M23 rebels in the Kamanyola groupement, launched by Wazalendo from the hills above Kamanyola against M23 positions in Kamanyola-Centre, began at 8:30 in Kalunga and lasted five hours, with wounded taken to a local medical institution according to sources on the spot.
r1-SKC-2025H1-011.vn: All three excerpts from the same page support their clauses. excerpt_en flags: added 'DRC'/'Walungu'-type capitalisation in translation only; translations are faithful.
src: Le groupement de Kamanyola dans le territoire de Walungu vit dans la psychose à la suite d'affrontements qui ont opposé jeudi 17 avril les combattants Wazalendo aux rebelles AFC-M23

Les attaques sur les positions M23 à Kamanyola-Centre ont été lancées par les Wazalendo à partir des collines qui surplombent Kamanyola dans les escarpements de Ngomo. Les échanges des tirs ont débuté jeudi dans la localité Kalunga à partir de 8h30 et ont duré 5 heures de temps.
Des sources contactées sur place par Radio Okapi affirment avoir vu des blessés qui été conduits dans une institution médicale locale pour des soins appropriés.

r1-SKC-2025H1-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that M23 troop reinforcement was also seen on its positions in the rural areas under its control, a list that included Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre and Muzinzi.
r1-SKC-2025H1-012.l: Nyangezi, Walungu-Centre, Muzinzi and other positions around Bukavu
r1-SKC-2025H1-012.n: Report date; reinforcement described as ongoing.
r1-SKC-2025H1-012.vn: Report date (18 April) came only from the page header; removed from the statement, kept in the date field. Condition described as current at the report date.
src: Ce renforcement des troupes M23 s’observe également sur ses différentes positions dans tous les milieux ruraux sous son contrôle: Panzi, Ciriri, Nyantende, Nyangezi, Mudaka, Katana, Kabamba, Kalehe, Walungu-Centre, Muzinzi

r1-SKC-2025H1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that several residents of Kaziba, Walungu territory, left their homes on Wednesday 23 April because of clashes between the AFC/M23 rebels and various Wazalendo groups.
r1-SKC-2025H1-013.l: Kaziba chefferie (Mushenyi, Cibanda, Nyanfunze), Walungu territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-013.vn: 'Plusieurs' is 'several', not 'many'; 'according to several local sources' attaches on the page to the resumption of fighting, not to the departures, so removed. This article dates the Wazalendo retaking of Kaziba to 17 March; Actualite.cd's 17 March article says 15 March.
src: Plusieurs habitants de Kaziba, dans le territoire de Walungu au Sud-Kivu ont abandonné leurs domiciles la journée de ce mercredi 23 avril à cause des affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et les différents groupes des wazalendo.

r1-SKC-2025H1-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that Kaziba chefferie had been the scene of violent clashes since the evening of Saturday 26 April, that the AFC-M23 was trying to dislodge Wazalendo to reach the Minembwe highlands where its allies Twirwaneho, Androïd and Gumino are based, and that residents said five truckloads of soldiers arrived at Tchofi and Kasheke.
r1-SKC-2025H1-014.n: Internal date inconsistency in the source: the article first says clashes began Saturday 26 April and later says Saturday 27 April around 17:00 (27 April 2025 was a Sunday). The claim of arrivals from Rwanda by speedboat is attributed to witnesses ("certains auraient même emprunté...") and is not repeated here. Radio Okapi 25 April (fetched) also reports FARDC against M23 at Kaziba from Mushenyi.
r1-SKC-2025H1-014.vn: First two clauses in the excerpt; the trucks clause is on the page next to it (page-only). The article is internally inconsistent: it says the clashes began on the evening of Saturday 26 April and later that they began on 'samedi 27 avril' around 17:00 (27 April 2025 was a Sunday). Tchofi and Kasheke are in Kalehe/Kabare, outside Kaziba.
src: La chefferie de Kaziba, dans le territoire de Walungu (province du Sud-Kivu) est le théâtre de violents affrontements depuis la soirée du samedi 26 avril. Des tirs nourris ont poussé les habitants de Kaziba centre à fuir vers les montagnes où ils ont passé une nuit blanche. L'AFC-M23 tente de déloger les combattants Wazalendo pour obtenir l'accès aux hauts plateaux de Minembwe où sont cantonnés ses alliés Twirwaneho, Androïd, Gumino.

r1-SKC-2025H1-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels retook control of Kaziba, Walungu territory, on Sunday 27 April after clashes with the Wazalendo, who were forced to pull back, and that several residents who fled Kaziba took refuge in neighbouring villages and chefferies, notably Luhwinja.
r1-SKC-2025H1-015.n: Article dates M23 capture to 10 March and Wazalendo retaking to 17 March (cf. 15 March in the 17 March article).
r1-SKC-2025H1-015.vn: 'Plusieurs' is 'several', not 'many'; the withdrawal is on the page, not in the excerpt (page-only clause). This article dates the earlier Wazalendo retaking of Kaziba to 17 March; Actualite.cd's 17 March article says 15 March. Radio Okapi (27 April) puts the start of the fighting on 26 April.
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont repris le dimanche 27 avril, le contrôle de Kaziba, dans le territoire de Walungu après des affrontements contre les wazalendo.
Plusieurs habitants qui ont fui Kaziba se sont réfugiés dans les villages et chefferies voisins notamment Luhwinja.

r1-SKC-2025H1-016.s: Amnesty International reported that, after a security incident in Walungu Centre on 9 March, M23 fighters fired heavy weapons in the direction of the General Reference Hospital in Walungu, damaging the main hospital and injuring patients.
r1-SKC-2025H1-016.l: General Reference Hospital, Walungu Centre, Walungu territory
r1-SKC-2025H1-016.n: Independent NGO attribution to M23; existing claims cite the UN fact-finding mission (shell hit paediatric ward, five killed) and Louvain Coopération. Amnesty section 6.8 says M23 fighters reportedly pursued suspected thieves and fired heavy weapons that hit the hospital; it interviewed 13 people about the hospital attacks overall. M23/Rwanda response on this incident not found.
r1-SKC-2025H1-016.vn: Excerpt verbatim in the retained PDF; attribution to M23 is Amnesty's own documented finding. Amnesty International's finding; it says it interviewed 13 people about the hospital incidents and received information from four others.
src: After a security incident in Walungu Centre, a village in Walungu territory in South Kivu, on 9 March, M23 fighters fired heavy weapons in the direction of the General Reference Hospital in Walungu, damaging the main hospital and injuring patients.

r1-SKC-2025H1-017.s: The OHCHR-mandated fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu, as apparent collective punishment.
r1-SKC-2025H1-017.l: Walungu and Kabare territories, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H1-017.n: Range spills past the unit window (July); only June is in scope. Consistent with the FARDC allegation on Munzinzi (22 June) and CNDH claims already recorded.

r1-SKC-2025H1-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that an official FARDC communiqué signed on Monday 23 June by army spokesperson General Sylvain Ekenge denounced a massacre by the RDF/AFC/M23 coalition that cost the lives of 17 civilians on Sunday 22 June around 18:30 at Munzinzi village, Walungu territory.

Selon un communiqué officiel signé ce lundi 23 juin par le porte-parole de l’armée, le général Sylvain Ekenge, les faits se sont déroulés la veille, dimanche 22 juin, vers 18h30 au village de Munzinzi, dans le territoire de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-SKC-2025H1-019.s: Ouragan.cd reported, citing the FARDC communiqué signed by spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge, that seventeen civilians were executed on the evening of Sunday 22 June at Munzinzi and that the army said the assailants acted in reprisal for military failures, accusing residents of collaborating with the regular army.
