r1-SKC-2025H2-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Monday 29 September FARDC supported by Wazalendo launched a counter-offensive to retake Nzibira, Walungu territory, a week after its occupation by AFC-M23 rebels.
r1-SKC-2025H2-017.n: Page also reports FARDC drone strikes on Mulunga, Chirwa, Nyamarhege, Mulamba and Kaniola mountains (not in this excerpt).
r1-SKC-2025H2-017.vn: Supported. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les milices Wazalendo, ont lancé lundi 29 septembre une contre-offensive pour reprendre le contrôle de Nzibira, dans le territoire de Walungu (Sud-Kivu), une semaine après son occupation par les rebelles de l’AFC-M23.

r1-SKC-2025H2-018.s: Actualite.cd reported that fighting resumed on the morning of Sunday 10 August 2025 between AFC/M23 rebels and wazalendo militiamen at Mulamba, Walungu territory, according to its sources.
r1-SKC-2025H2-018.vn: Supported. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les affrontements ont repris l'avant midi de ce dimanche 10 août 2025 entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et les miliciens wazalendo à Mulamba, dans le territoire de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu, selon les sources d’ACTUALITE.CD.

r1-SKC-2025H2-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that a few hours before the fighting resumed on 10 August, Didier Kabi, spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, said FARDC and wazalendo had withdrawn from Mulamba and Kaniola to avoid bloodshed and that these zones were controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels.
r1-SKC-2025H2-019.l: Mulamba and Kaniola, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H2-019.n: Kabi is quoted on the page as speaking to RFI; the same statement lists Kaniola, Muzinzi, Ciruko and part of Mulamba as occupied. AFC/M23 account of the same events not found in this unit.
r1-SKC-2025H2-019.vn: Supported; the date of the resumption is on the same page. Origin credited to RFI, where Kabi's direct quote was given. Partisan statement (South Kivu provincial government): usable only as what the provincial government said. In the direct quote to RFI Kabi names Kaniola, Muzinzi, Ciruko and part of Mulamba as occupied. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Quelques heures avant la reprise des hostilités, Didier Kabi, porte-parole du gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu a indiqué que les FARDC et wazalendo se sont retirés de Mulamba et Kaniola pour éviter le bain de sang. Et que ces zones étaient contrôlées par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r1-SKC-2025H2-020.s: Actualite.cd reported that a precarious calm had prevailed since the afternoon of Wednesday 19 November in several Walungu territory villages after clashes between wazalendo factions and AFC/M23, notably at Mugogo, Walungu Centre and Cagala on the Kaniola road, where heavy and light weapons were heard on Tuesday.
r1-SKC-2025H2-020.l: Mugogo, Walungu Centre, Cagala, Kaniola road, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H2-020.n: Casualties not quantified by notables quoted ('dégâts humains à Cagala et Kaniola').
r1-SKC-2025H2-020.vn: Supported. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Un calme précaire règne depuis l'après-midi de ce mercredi 19 novembre dans plusieurs villages du territoire de Walungu caractérisé par les affrontements entre différentes factions des wazalendo et les rebelles de l'AFC/M23. C’est notamment à Mugogo, Walungu Centre et Cagala sur la route de Kaniola, où des détonations d'armes lourdes et légères ont retenti mardi.

r1-SKC-2025H2-021.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, per independent sources, the rebels were reportedly at Kalimbi, 5 km from Mwenga-centre, while the army and its allies were reportedly at the Lwindi bridge; per local civil society the AFC-M23 was still at Kasika and its surroundings and only patrolling Kalimbi-centre, while on Sunday 30 November 2025 displaced families moved towards Kitutu and Kamituga.
r1-SKC-2025H2-021.l: Kalimbi, Kasika, Lwindi bridge, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H2-021.n: Page dated 30 Nov/1 Dec; two sources give slightly different positions; hedged ('seraient').
r1-SKC-2025H2-021.vn: Supported. Positions are hedged in the source ('seraient'); the two accounts differ slightly. 2026-10-28: source 0 date edited: fact-check fc1: The page uses the conditional ('seraient') for both positions, which the statement dropped. No publication date is printed on the saved text; the URL path is 2025/12/01, so the 30 Nov date is the civil-society event date, not the publication date. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: The page uses the conditional ('seraient') for both positions, which the statement dropped. No publication date is printed on the saved text; the URL path is 2025/12/01, so the 30 Nov date is the civil-society event date, not the publication date. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon des sources indépendantes, les rebelles seraient à Kalimbi, à 5 km de Mwenga-centre, tandis que l’armée et ses alliés seraient au pont Lwindi. « Dimanche 30/11/2025, d’autres familles déplacées venues des villages Itumba, Misebu, Kataraka, Kitale, Ilibo, Mulole, dans les deux groupements Irangi et Kalimbi de la chefferie de Lwindi, se dirigent vers Kitutu et la ville de Kamituga », a alerté la société civile. « L’AFC-M23 est encore à Kasika et ses environs, mais effectue seulement des patrouilles à Kalimbi-centre »

r1-SKC-2025H2-022.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Burundian soldiers positioned on the Kilungu-Kasika axis in Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, reportedly left their positions for Kamituga, with videos on social media on Sunday 19 October 2025 showing hundreds of Burundian soldiers, and local sources and civil society confirmed it.
r1-SKC-2025H2-022.l: Kilungu-Kasika axis, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory; Nyamibungu aerodrome, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H2-022.n: Page says no official reaction from the Congolese army was recorded and the motive was unknown. No Burundian government statement found.
r1-SKC-2025H2-022.vn: Supported; hedge kept. The videos were not verified. The page adds that the soldiers headed for the Nyamibungu aerodrome, 30 km from Kamituga, that the motive is unknown and that the Congolese army had made no official reaction. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les militaires burundais positionnés sur l’axe Kilungu-Kasika, dans le territoire de Mwenga, chefferie de Lwindi, auraient quitté leurs positions pour se diriger vers la ville de Kamituga. Dans des vidéos diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux dimanche 19 octobre 2025, on aperçoit des centaines de militaires burundais portant armes et sacs sur le dos. Des sources locales et la société civile confirment l’information

r1-SKC-2025H2-023.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that two people were killed and several wounded in clashes between the FARDC and Wazalendo combatants in Kamituga on Thursday 9 October 2025, triggered by the killing of a FARDC captain attributed to armed men assimilated to Wazalendo, with combat lasting about four hours.
r1-SKC-2025H2-023.a: FARDC; Wazalendo (armed men assimilated to Wazalendo, per the page)
r1-SKC-2025H2-023.x: Radio Okapi (local civil society): 2 killed, several wounded
r1-SKC-2025H2-023.n: Local civil society is the source of the facts. Independent of the Kivu Morning Post items already drafted for 9-10 Oct in the period packet. Includes pillage by unidentified armed men the same night.
r1-SKC-2025H2-023.vn: Figure is a word in the excerpt (Deux). Supported. The facts are reported by local civil society. The FARDC captain is not named. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Oct 2025, states that local civil society is the source of these facts ('La société civile locale qui rapporte ces faits'); the statement credits them to Radio Okapi alone, so the attribution is added. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Deux personnes ont été tuées et plusieurs autres blessées lors des accrochages survenus entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et les combattants Wazalendo dans la ville de Kamituga, au Sud-Kivu, jeudi 9 octobre 2025. Ces affrontements ont été déclenchés par le meurtre d'un capitaine des FARDC, attribué à des hommes armés assimilés aux Wazalendo. Alertées vers une heure du matin, les FARDC ont réagi, provoquant des combats qui ont duré environ quatre heures. La société civile locale qui rapporte ces faits, déplore en plus les scènes de pillage perpétrées la même nuit par des hommes armés non identifiés.

r1-SKC-2025H2-024.s: Radio Okapi reported that young people of Kamituga demonstrated on Friday 10 October to demand that Wazalendo leave, accusing them of abuses including theft and murder, and that the president of the Espace Lega council, Crispin Mpombo, called on the government to protect civilians.
r1-SKC-2025H2-024.n: Allegations by demonstrators, not independently verified.
r1-SKC-2025H2-024.vn: Supported by the page; the Mpombo clause is page-only (excerpt gap). Allegations by demonstrators, not verified. Crispin Mpombo's appeal is on the page but not in the stored excerpt. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des jeunes de Kamituga (Sud-Kivu) ont manifesté, vendredi 10 octobre, pour exiger le départ des Wazalendo de leurs milieux. Ils accusent ces combattants de diverses exactions dans leurs milieux dont le vol, le meurtre et autres, semant ainsi la terreur au sein de la population.

r1-SKC-2025H2-025.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that a mixed unit of police and FARDC soldiers dispersed a peaceful march in Kamituga on Tuesday 22 July against electricity overbilling by the company CRE SEKO, with live fire and tear gas reported and several arrests; organiser Lucky Mutiki said the movement would continue.
r1-SKC-2025H2-025.a: mixed unit of police and FARDC soldiers (per local sources)
r1-SKC-2025H2-025.n: Number of arrests and any casualties not stated. Kivu Morning Post also covered the repression (see period packet draft UCD-FARDC-WZ). Not an AFC/M23 area event.
r1-SKC-2025H2-025.vn: Flag resolved: 22 July is printed on the page. Supported. Number of arrests not known per the source; no casualties reported. The date, CRE SEKO and Lucky Mutiki are on the page but not in the stored excerpt. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 23 Jul 2025, carries every clause (march on Tuesday 22 July against CRE SEKO overbilling; mixed police-FARDC unit, live fire and tear gas, arrests per local sources). The stored excerpt lacked Lucky Mutiki's statement; passage added. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: D’après des sources locales, une unité mixte composée de policiers et de militaires des FARDC est intervenue pour disperser les manifestants. Des tirs à balles réelles et des jets de gaz lacrymogènes ont été signalés, semant la panique au sein de la population mobilisée. Plusieurs arrestations ont été enregistrées
L’un des organisateurs, Lucky Mutiki, a déclaré que le mouvement se poursuivra jusqu’à ce qu’une solution soit trouvée à la problématique de la tarification électrique.

r1-SKC-2025H2-026.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a young man named as NDINO DONATIEN, accused of having raped, killed and buried a 13-year-old girl on Thursday 31 July, was arrested on Friday 1 August 2025 near the Lupupu mining site; the Mwenga civil society president Hilaire ISOMBYA named the victim as Bitondo Byamungu.
r1-SKC-2025H2-026.l: Kamituga (Bitanga) and Lupupu mining site, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2025H2-026.a: civilian suspect (NDINO DONATIEN), not an armed group per the source
r1-SKC-2025H2-026.n: Civilian crime, recorded as context for sexual violence in Mwenga; no armed actor alleged. Suspect named as accused, not a finding of responsibility. Victim is a minor, named per policy v1.
r1-SKC-2025H2-026.vn: Statement unchanged and supported; victims_named status set to 'minor' per policy v1 (details of the harm stay in the statement and note). The victim is a 13-year-old girl (minor), named per naming policy v1 and censored in the edition; the source says she was raped, killed and buried. The suspect is accused only; no armed actor is alleged. Arrested is not charged. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le jeune présumé criminel NDINO DONATIEN, accusé d’avoir violé, tué et enterré une fillette de 13 ans ce jeudi 31 juillet, a été appréhendé ce vendredi 1ᵉʳ août 2025 vers le site minier de Lupupu. La victime a été violée dans la ville de Kamituga, dans le territoire de Mwenga, en province du Sud-Kivu. Selon Hilaire ISOMBYA, Président de la société civile de Mwenga, “le bureau de coordination urbaine de Kamituga dénonce cette énième homicide dont a été victime la fillette dénommée Bitondo Byamungu, âgée de 13 ans.

r1-SKC-2026H1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that a Médecins Sans Frontières convoy was attacked by Wazalendo militiamen on "vendredi 3 mai" (as printed; 3 May 2026 was a Sunday) at the former hot spot called Kalimoto, a few kilometres from Kalambi in Lwindi chiefdom (Mwenga territory), while heading to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs; it reported that the agents were looted and that MSF staff came out unharmed.
r1-SKC-2026H1-001.l: Kalimoto near Kalambi, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-001.n: The article is dated 05/05/2026 (Tuesday) and says "vendredi 3 mai"; 3 May 2026 was a Sunday, so the weekday/day-number do not match and the exact day is uncertain. Existing claim r1-SV-2026-020 (Kivu Morning Post) dates the incident 2026-05-01. The "attack" is a robbery of staff; no medical supplies are stated looted. Page body also has no byline wire credit. Contradicting reporting: Médecins Sans Frontières (2026-05-08): Date is 1 May, not 3 May ('vendredi 3 mai' is also not a Friday in 2026; 1 May 2026 is). MSF describes armed men firing at each other with the team caught in between and does not mention an attack on or looting of the convoy.
r1-SKC-2026H1-001.vn: All clauses on the page. Single outlet, own reporting; MSF statements are paraphrased. Weekday mismatch kept stated; date_precision approximate. Date uncertain: the article (5 May 2026) says 'vendredi 3 mai', but 3 May 2026 was a Sunday; the weekday and day number do not match. The source states the staff were looted; it does not say medical supplies were taken. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-023: Counter-account and date: MSF's own statement (claim r1-SKS-2026Q2-001) dates the incident to 1 May 2026 (a Friday, so 'vendredi 3 mai' is likely an error), describes a stop at a Wazalendo-controlled checkpoint followed by armed men 'firing among themselves', names no attacker and mentions no looting. A later Actualite.cd article (10 May 2026, found by search) itself dates the incident to 1 May. The Wazalendo attribution and the looting are Actualite.cd's alone and should sit beside MSF's account.; excerpt-support: cut MSF's own account (incident dated Friday 1 May; team stopped at a Wazalendo-controlled checkpoint; armed men firing among themselves): the claim cites no MSF page; it needs its own claim 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review.
src: Un convoi de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) a été attaqué vendredi 3 mai dernier par des miliciens wazalendo au niveau de l’ancien point chaud, communément appelé Kalimoto, à quelques kilomètres de Kalambi, dans la chefferie de Lwindi (territoire de Mwenga).
Selon les informations disponibles, l’équipe de MSF se dirigeait vers Mwenga, Kamituga et Kitutu, au sud-ouest de Bukavu, afin d’évaluer les besoins humanitaires. Les agents ont été pillés.
Les membres du personnel de MSF sont sortis indemnes de l’attaque
On 1 May, an MSF team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga, and Kitutu, in South Kivu, as part of an assessment of humanitarian and medical needs, were involved in a security incident.

In Kalimoto rural locality, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, South Kivu province, an INGO convoy travelling to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs was reportedly attacked and robbed by Wazalendo militiamen during a humanitarian mission.

r1-SKC-2026H1-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least six people were killed and seven others wounded in fighting between two Wazalendo factions on Friday 20 February 2026 in Kisenya village, Shabunda territory, which caused the displacement of more than 1073 households; quoting Shabunda territory civil society, it said Wazalendo elements of the Kiseketi dit Solide group (known as Katabilalo) and of Mukamba Lukabya dit Karuleta clashed with Wazalendo elements of the Ngandu Lundimu group, and that the provisional toll would be six dead, including three men, a woman and two children aged 14 and 17, with seven seriously wounded and about 1073 households displaced into the bush.
r1-SKC-2026H1-002.l: Kisenya village, Bamunguba-Sud groupement, Bakisi chiefdom, Shabunda territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-002.a: Wazalendo factions (Kiseketi dit Solide group "Katabilalo" and Mukamba Lukabya dit Karuleta, against the Ngandu Lundimu group, per civil society)
r1-SKC-2026H1-002.x: Kivu Morning Post: at least six killed and seven wounded; more than 1073 households displaced. Civil society (provisional, conditional): six dead (three men, a woman, two children aged 14 and 17), seven seriously wounded, about 1073 households displaced
r1-SKC-2026H1-002.n: Single local outlet quoting civil society; toll provisional. Victims unnamed. Intra-Wazalendo fighting, civilians among dead per civil society.
r1-SKC-2026H1-002.vn: Figures written as the source prints them; displacement passage added from the page; Bamunguba-Sud/Bakisi kept in location only. The civil society toll is provisional and conditional ('serait'); victims are not named.
src: Au moins six personnes ont été tuées et sept autres blessés dans des combats entre deux factions Wazalendo le vendredi 20 février 2026. Le drame a eu lieu dans le territoire de Shabunda en province du Sud-Kivu dans le village Kisenya. Une situation qui a occasionné un déplacement massif de plus 1073 ménages.

un affrontement s’est produit entre des éléments Wazalendo du groupe armé Kiseketi dit Solide, connus sous le nom de Katabilalo, et ceux de Mukamba Lukabya dit Karuleta. Ils se sont opposés à des éléments Wazalendo du Groupe Armé de Ngandu Lundimu.
Le bilan provisoire serait de six morts, dont trois hommes, une femme 2 enfants âgés de 14 et 17 ans, dont un garçon et une fille.

r1-SKC-2026H1-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing Shabunda civil society, that in the night of 20 to 21 February 2026 Wazalendo elements of the armed group of a self-proclaimed general "BASILA", coming from Lulingu, made incursions at Bubala village, fired shots and looted livestock and valuables, and that Bubala institute teacher Munembwe Samitamba was wounded by bullets in the back.
r1-SKC-2026H1-003.l: Bubala village, Bamunguba-Sud groupement, Bakisi chiefdom, Shabunda territory (about 65 km north-east of Shabunda-centre)
r1-SKC-2026H1-003.a: Wazalendo elements of the group of the self-proclaimed General BASILA
r1-SKC-2026H1-003.n: Single local source quoting civil society.
r1-SKC-2026H1-003.vn: All clauses on the page; name spelled as printed; excerpt_en flags are honorifics/capitalisation only.
src: des éléments Wazalendo du Groupe Armé du Général autoproclamé le Sieur BASILA, en provenance de Lulingu, ont effectué des incursions. Ces inciviques ont tiré plusieurs balles, suivi du pillage de bétails, de volailles et de biens de valeurs de la population
Cette structure citoyenne ajoute dans la nuit du 20 au 21/02/2026, dans le village Bubala, Groupement de Bamunguba-Sud en Chefferie des Bakisi
L’enseignant de l’Institut Bubala, Monsieur Munembwe Samitamba, a été blessé par balles au dos de la part de ces derniers.

r1-SKC-2026H1-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that national deputy Placide Wenda, in an alert launched on Tuesday 3 March in Kinshasa, denounced serious crimes including torture and human mutilations by armed men in Shabunda territory, and noted that inhabitants reportedly had ears cut off or eyes gouged out; Radio Okapi said two people died in one week in clashes between two Wazalendo factions on the Kalole-Masanganjia axis to Mukoloka.
r1-SKC-2026H1-004.l: Kalole-Masanganjia axis to Mukoloka, Shabunda territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-004.a: Wazalendo factions (as named by Radio Okapi)
r1-SKC-2026H1-004.x: Radio Okapi: two people died in a week
r1-SKC-2026H1-004.n: Allegations by a deputy relayed by Radio Okapi; not independently verified. Date is the date of the alert; underlying incidents undated. The deputy used a legal label that is not reproduced here.
r1-SKC-2026H1-004.vn: Supported; allegations attributed; mutilations kept conditional. The deputy's own legal characterisation ('assimilé à des crimes contre l'humanité') is on the page and is not adopted here. The date is the date of the alert; the underlying incidents are undated.
src: Deux personnes ont perdu la vie en une semaine à la suite des accrochages entre deux factions Wazalendo , sur l’axe Kalole-Masanganjia jusqu’à Mukoloka, en territoire de Shabunda (Sud-Kivu). Dans une alerte lancée mardi 3 mars à Kinshasa, le député national Placide Wenda dénonce des crimes graves, notamment des actes de torture et des mutilations humaines que commettent ces hommes armés.
Cet élu note des cas de mutilations barbares. Des habitants auraient eu les oreilles coupées ou les yeux crevés.

r1-SKC-2026H1-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that Wazalendo groups had been officially declared undesirable by the different social strata in Shabunda territory, accused of atrocities against civilians including widespread looting, extortion and mutilations; local sources said on Thursday 5 March that the social climate had become deleterious in Wakabango chiefdom and Bamuguba-Sud groupement; and it reported that the provincial infrastructure minister publicly asked the Wazalendo to withdraw without delay from the territory capital.
r1-SKC-2026H1-005.l: Wakabango chiefdom and Bamuguba-Sud groupement, Shabunda territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-005.n: Local sources, unnamed; the minister is described only as "ministre provincial des Infrastructures". The Forum des nationalistes coordinator Jules Magene Kakumbu is named in the page but not in the excerpts, so he is not listed.
r1-SKC-2026H1-005.vn: Supported; 'declared undesirable' is in the title and body. The page also quotes Jules Magene Kakumbu (national coordinator, ASBL Forum des nationalistes) denouncing Wazalendo abuses; the minister is unnamed and his visit undated ('récente'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Mar 2026: only the 'climat social délétère' clause is attributed to local sources on 5 March; the declaration of the Wazalendo as undesirable is said in the outlet's voice, made 'by the different social strata', and had no excerpt. Attribution untangled and excerpt added. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Mar 2026: only the 'climat social délétère' clause is attributed to local sources on 5 March; the declaration of the Wazalendo as undesirable is said in the outlet's voice, made 'by the different social strata', and had no excerpt. Attribution untangled and excerpt added.
src: Le climat social est devenu délétère, particulièrement dans la chefferie de Wakabango et le groupement de Bamuguba-Sud, ont indiqué jeudi 5 mars des sources locales.
Pillages généralisés, extorsions et, plus grave encore, des mutilations atroces : la liste des méfaits attribués aux Wazalendo ne cesse de s'allonger.
il a dû publiquement demander aux Wazalendo de se désengager sans délai du chef-lieu du territoire de Shabunda.
Accusés de commettre des atrocités contre les civils, ils sont aujourd'hui officiellement déclarés indésirables par les différentes couches sociales.

r1-SKC-2026H1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing the army, that FARDC captured warlord Amisi Sisawa alias "Muswahili", leader of an armed group claiming to be Wazalendo, in an operation on Sunday in the locality of Kitete, Shabunda-Centre, with fire exchanged in the early hours of Sunday 29 March; according to the army the operation ended with the arrest of Amisi Sisawa and thirteen of his fighters, and the toll also reported two dead and two seriously wounded.
r1-SKC-2026H1-006.a: FARDC against the group of Amisi Sisawa alias Muswahili
r1-SKC-2026H1-006.x: Army via Radio Okapi: Amisi Sisawa and thirteen fighters arrested; two dead and two seriously wounded
r1-SKC-2026H1-006.n: Army account relayed by Radio Okapi; the army calls the group "faux Wazalendo".
r1-SKC-2026H1-006.vn: Downgraded to C: the source's own lead says 'rapporte l'armée', so the origin is a party. Figures in words as printed; weapons count removed from figures (not in an excerpt). Army account; the page also says the FARDC reported recovering five AK-47-type weapons. Whose dead and wounded the toll counts is not stated.
src: L’intervention des forces armées est intervenue dimanche dans la localité de Kitete, à Shabunda-Centre.
Le seigneur de guerre Amisi Sisawa, alias « Muswahili », est désormais entre les mains des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo, (FARDC).
L’objectif : neutraliser un groupe armé se réclamant des Wazalendo, mais impliqué dans des activités criminelles.

Selon l’armée, l’opération s’est soldée par l’arrestation d’Amisi Sisawa, ainsi que de treize de ses combattants. Le bilan fait également état de deux morts et de deux blessés graves à l’issue des affrontements.
Les échanges de tirs ont eu lieu aux premières heures de la journée de dimanche 29 mars, aux alentours de 4 heures locales.

r1-SKC-2026H1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Nord-Sud Kivu operational sector, Meya Jérémie, said the group led by "Muswahili" was involved in several serious human rights violations, the alleged acts including looting, extortion, torture and forced labour, notably in mining areas.
r1-SKC-2026H1-007.n: FARDC allegation against the group; not independently verified. Excerpt text ends at "notamment dans les zones minières de la région" (sentence continues).
r1-SKC-2026H1-007.vn: Verbatim; FARDC statement, partisan; allegation not verified.
src: D’après le porte-parole du secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Nord-Sud Kivu, Meya Jérémie, le groupe dirigé par « Muswahili » est impliqué dans plusieurs violations graves des droits humains. Parmi les faits reprochés figurent des pillages, des extorsions, des actes de torture ainsi que des travaux forcés, notamment dans les zones minières de la région.

r1-SKC-2026H1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Shabunda territory, Justin Balegamire Byenda, detained in Maniema for more than nine months, was acquitted by military justice and reinstated on Thursday by provincial justice minister Faustin Mayani Shindano, amid an open conflict with his deputy Konga Konga, each reportedly relying on Wazalendo militiamen to assert power.
r1-SKC-2026H1-008.n: The article lead gives the ceremony as Thursday 26 March 2026; the excerpt itself says only "jeudi".
r1-SKC-2026H1-008.vn: Supported; date from the article lead. Radio Okapi says the ceremony was disrupted by unrest; the minister blamed people 'instrumentalised' by offices in Kinshasa. The acquittal concerned a murder case, per the minister.
src: Son retour aux affaires intervient dans un contexte de conflit ouvert entre lui et son adjoint Konga Konga; chacun d'eux s’appuyant sur les miliciens Wazalendo pour asseoir son pouvoir.

Arrêté et détenu au Maniema depuis plus de neuf mois, l’administrateur Justin Balegamire Byenda a été acquitté par la justice militaire et remis dans ses fonctions jeudi par le ministre provincial de la Justice, Faustin Mayani Shindano.

r1-SKC-2026H1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that Mwenga territory civil society accused some FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo (VDP) of involvement in torture, killings and looting, in an area it described as under central government control.
r1-SKC-2026H1-009.a: FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo/VDP, as alleged by civil society
r1-SKC-2026H1-009.n: Civil society allegation; no incident-level detail in this article.
src: La société civile accuse certains soldats des FARDC ainsi que des Wazalendo (VDP) d’être impliqués dans des actes de torture, de meurtres et de pillages.

r1-SKC-2026H1-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that Mwenga territory administrator Ishikitilo Mao said that on receiving the civil society's letter about some undisciplined soldiers "we convened a meeting with the military authorities", and that the FARDC commander in charge of the Mwenga sector admitted the presence of "brebis galeuses" (black sheep) within his troops and said he had already sanctioned three elements, including one Muzalendo volunteer, transferred to the general staff in Kisangani.
r1-SKC-2026H1-010.n: Commander not named by the source.
r1-SKC-2026H1-010.vn: Ishikitilo Mao was not in the stored excerpt: replaced it with a contiguous passage that prints the name. Category changed: this is an admission, not a denial. FARDC and territorial administration statements (government side). The commander is not named. A later Radio Okapi item (1 April) quotes the sector commander saying suspects were transferred to Kindu.
src: Le commandant FARDC en charge du secteur de Mwenga admet la présence de « brebis galeuses » au sein de ses troupes. Il reconnaît avoir déjà sanctionné trois éléments, dont un volontaire Muzalendo, transférés auprès de l’État-major à Kisangani.

r1-SKC-2026H1-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that Lungele Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society coordination framework, cited an incident on 12 March in which Dodos Ngama, a young man of 30, was "fusillé" (shot) by a "VDP -RAD Wazalendo" element at Ilinda, and said that on 13 March Mukaba Masilia Ndebo, aged 56, was also "fusillé" at "Kibumb a" (spelling as printed).
r1-SKC-2026H1-011.l: Ilinda; Kibumba [as printed "Kibumb a"], Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-011.a: VDP-RAD Wazalendo element (as named by civil society)
r1-SKC-2026H1-011.n: "fusillé" may mean shot dead or shot; the source does not say "killed". Mwenga civil society is the origin of the list. Typo "Kibumb a" kept as printed.
r1-SKC-2026H1-011.vn: Lungele Itebo was not in the stored excerpt: replaced it with the contiguous passage that prints the name and the incidents. 'Fusillé' may mean shot or shot dead; the source does not say the victims were killed. Perpetrator for the 13 March case is not stated separately. The same passage also names Patient Lunanga, former accountant of the Basile chiefdom, robbed at Kalende on 4 March 2026 (3 million Congolese francs, 500 US dollars and other valuables): an uncovered lead.
src: Il évoque aussi l'incident survenu le 12 mars, où un jeune homme de 30 ans, Dodos Ngama, a été " fusillé par un élément VDP -RAD Wazalendo à Ilinda. Le 13 mars Mukaba Masilia Ndebo, âgé de 56 ans, était aussi fusillé à Kibumb a

r1-SKC-2026H1-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that Lungele Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society coordination framework and part of a team documenting abuses attributed to groups presented as "pseudo Wazalendo", listed among recent cases that nurse Bwato Mulungula was stripped of all his belongings at Musika on 03 March 2026.
r1-SKC-2026H1-012.a: not attributed by the source (civil society elsewhere speaks of "pseudo Wazalendo")
r1-SKC-2026H1-012.n: Same incident as existing draft r1/UCD-FARDC-WZ#24 (Kivu Morning Post, citing Mwenga civil society), and the same origin (civil society); adds the nurse name. Not independent corroboration.
r1-SKC-2026H1-012.vn: Name of the civil society president was not in the excerpt; contiguous passage supplied. Same civil-society origin as the Kivu Morning Post report of the case: not independent corroboration. The source does not say who robbed the nurse, nor whether he was on duty or whether medical supplies were taken.
src: Il énumère plusieurs cas récents : "L’infirmier Bwato Mulungula était dépouillé de tous ses biens à Musika le 03 mars 2026.

r1-SKC-2026H1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Tuesday 24 March residents of Mwenga observed a "ville morte" (stay-at-home day) to denounce multiple harassments by some FARDC and Wazalendo elements; Samuel Itebo, president of the Mwenga civil society forces vives, said some FARDC and Wazalendo elements extort the population and threaten to kill those who resist, and denounced the reappearance of paying barriers, the seizure and use of civilians' motorcycles by soldiers without compensation, and the occupation of hotels and civilians' houses without compensation.
r1-SKC-2026H1-013.l: Mwenga centre, Buziba, Kitutu, Lugushwa, Kakemenge, Kibe, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-013.a: Some FARDC and Wazalendo elements, as alleged by civil society
r1-SKC-2026H1-013.n: Civil society president is printed as Samuel Itebo here and Lungele Itebo (also "Lungele Itebo Samuel") in Radio Okapi/KMP: likely same person; not merged.
r1-SKC-2026H1-013.vn: Name not in the stored excerpt: contiguous passage supplied; added the threat clause the page prints. Printed here as 'Samuel Itebo'; Radio Okapi and Kivu Morning Post print 'Lungele Itebo' and 'Lungele Itebo Samuel'. Probably the same person; not merged. The ville morte is reported as fact; the abuses are civil society allegations.
src: Les habitants de Mwenga dans la province du Sud-Kivu ont observé, ce mardi 24 mars, une journée ville morte pour dénoncer les tracasseries multiples dont ils sont victimes de la part de certains éléments FARDC et Wazalendo.
La réapparition des barrières payantes, la saisie et l’utilisation sans compensation des motocyclettes de civils par des militaires, l’occupation sans compensation des hôtels et des maisons de civils

r1-SKC-2026H1-014.s: Actualite.cd reported, quoting the association AFJEP, that on the night of 27 January around 21h a man of about 45, a state agent assigned to the mining service, sexually raped a 3-year-old girl, and that the victim was taken to Kamituga General Referral Hospital (Hôpital Général de Référence de Kamituga) for medical care; according to women's rights defenders the act took place in Sawasa neighbourhood, and the alleged perpetrator was in the hands of law enforcement. The source does not link the incident to the armed conflict.
r1-SKC-2026H1-014.a: state agent of the mining service (not an armed group, as per the source)
r1-SKC-2026H1-014.x: One victim, a girl aged 3; alleged perpetrator a man of about 45
r1-SKC-2026H1-014.n: Child victim not named by source. Not stated to be conflict-related; recorded as a sexual-violence lead and civilian health-care use (referral hospital).
r1-SKC-2026H1-014.vn: Sawasa was not in the stored excerpt: contiguous passage supplied. Time kept as printed (21h); added the source's lack of a conflict link. Not tied to the conflict by the source; recorded as a sexual-violence lead. The source reports an arrest ('aux arrêts'), not a charge or conviction. The victim is not named. The stored English translation of the excerpt renders '21h' as '9 pm'.
ent: Hôpital Général de Référence de Kamituga
src: Dans la nuit de ce 27 Janvier vers 21h un homme d'environ 45 ans, agent de l'état affecté au service des Mines a violé sexuellement une petite fille de 3, la victime a été acheminée à l'hôpital Général de Référence de Kamituga pour une prise en charge médicale", indique l'association des femmes journaliste engagé pour la Paix AFJEP
Actuellement, le présumé auteur de cet acte est dans les mains des services de l'ordre

r1-SKC-2026H1-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that deaths were reported in Ilundu village, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, on Sunday 7 June, and that according to local sources bombardments in the area killed at least two people; local civil society sources said one of the two dead was a young person aged 19. The outlet said the wounded included two children, one of them aged 7 (its headline gives six wounded in all), and said two classrooms of Ilundu primary school were damaged. The article does not say who carried out the bombardments; its headline refers to drone bombardments.
r1-SKC-2026H1-015.l: Ilundu village, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-015.a: not attributed by the source (Kivu Morning Post elsewhere refers to drone strikes)
r1-SKC-2026H1-015.x: Actualite.cd: at least two killed (civil society: one aged 19); wounded include two children, one aged 7 (headline: six wounded); two classrooms damaged
r1-SKC-2026H1-015.n: Single outlet; wounded not named. Attribution not given; see Mikenge claims for the same days.
r1-SKC-2026H1-015.vn: Translation flag: the 19 and 7 figures were in the translation but not the excerpt; they are on the page, so source 1's excerpt is replaced with that passage. Wounded list added from the same passage. No perpetrator named. The stored excerpt of source 1 was the classroom sentence while its translation rendered the 19-year-old/7-year-old passage: resolved by replacing the excerpt with the passage that prints those figures.
src: Des morts sont signalés dans le village d'Ilundu, secteur d'Itombwe, territoire de Mwenga, dans le Sud-Kivu, le dimanche 7 juin. Selon les sources locales, des bombardements ont eu lieu dans cette contrée et ont coûté la vie à au moins deux personnes.
On y ajoute également deux classes de l'école primaire Ilundu qui ont été endommagées.

r1-SKC-2026H1-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Twirwaneho fighters, allies of AFC-M23, retook the locality of Mikenge in the highlands of Mwenga territory after fighting against FARDC supported by Wazalendo and the Burundian army; according to local sources Mikenge fell after Congolese army drone strikes followed by ground fighting on Monday 8 June 2026.
r1-SKC-2026H1-016.a: Twirwaneho (allied to AFC-M23) vs FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian army
r1-SKC-2026H1-016.n: Excerpt is long; check_raw will confirm. Contested: FARDC says it retook the place by 9-10 June (next claims). Existing claims r1-ATR-SK-2026-008 / r1-ST-BI-022 say FARDC retook Mikenge on 1 March 2026.
r1-SKC-2026H1-016.vn: Supported; grade B because the FARDC communiqué (Radio Okapi) independently confirms the localities were occupied on Monday. Contested sequence: Kivu Morning Post (this item) reports capture on 8 June; the FARDC communiqué says retaken on the morning of 10 June; the Fizi administrator says back under FARDC control since 9 June. On the same page a security source is quoted confirming 'la prise de Mikenge par le M23', which the page says civil society confirmed. Drone strikes here are attributed to the Congolese army; the Fizi administrator attributes drones to AFC/M23.
src: Les combattants du Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC-M23, ont repris le contrôle de la localité stratégique de Mikenge, située dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu.
La prise de cette localité est intervenue après des combats contre les FARDC, appuyées par les Wazalendo et l’armée burundaise.
Selon des sources locales, Mikenge est tombée après des frappes de drones de l’armée congolaise, suivies d’intenses combats au sol le lundi 8 juin 2026.

r1-SKC-2026H1-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Congolese army retook the city of Mikenge, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, on Wednesday 10 June 2026; according to local sources the army counter-attacked with attack drones, pushing Twirwaneho fighters to withdraw during the night, and a security source of the Congolese army said it had retaken Kalingi and Mikenge that morning. The same article quoted an administrative source in the area saying violent fighting was still under way at Mikenge and elsewhere that morning.
r1-SKC-2026H1-017.n: The article body also says fighting was still under way at Mikenge, Kilulwe and Kakenge that morning.
r1-SKC-2026H1-017.vn: Attribution adjusted: the lead is the outlet's narration, the counter-attack detail is from local sources; the 'security source' wording and the administrative-source discrepancy are added from a contiguous passage. Within the same article, an army source says Mikenge was retaken while an administrative source says fighting was still under way there that morning.
src: L’armée congolaise a repris, ce mercredi 10 juin 2026, la cité de Mikenge, dans le secteur d’Itombwe, en territoire de Mwenga
Selon des sources locales, l’armée a contre-attaqué dans la zone à l’aide de drones d’attaque, une situation qui a poussé les combattants Twirwaneho à se retirer durant la nuit.
affirme avoir repris ce matin Kalingi et Mikenge.

r1-SKC-2026H1-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced they had retaken, on the morning of Wednesday 10 June, control of Mikenge, Kakenge and Kalingi in the highlands of Fizi and Mwenga territories; according to an army communiqué these localities had been occupied the previous Monday by a coalition of Twirwaneho and M23, whose assailants reportedly used military drones, and the FARDC said the recapture followed a counter-offensive of about 48 hours with Wazalendo support. Fizi territory administrator Samy Kalonji Badibanga confirmed the recapture and gave an earlier date than the communiqué for the return of Mikenge to FARDC control (see note), and said the attack of Monday 8 June was reportedly facilitated by drones attributed to AFC/M23 and by allied armed groups, notably Red Tabara and Twirwaneho.
r1-SKC-2026H1-018.l: Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi (Mwenga and Fizi territories)
r1-SKC-2026H1-018.n: Government/army account (partisan). Fizi administrator places Mikenge back under FARDC control since Tuesday 9 June; the FARDC communiqué says Wednesday 10 June. The excerpt is long: check_raw to confirm.
r1-SKC-2026H1-018.vn: Added the administrator's 9 June date (contiguous passage supplied) so each government account stands separately; communiqué's occupation claim added. Government-side accounts, recorded as such. The communiqué dates the recapture to the morning of 10 June; the Fizi administrator, per Radio Okapi, said Mikenge was back under FARDC control 'depuis mardi 9 juin' (page text, not yet in a stored excerpt). The administrator attributes the drones to AFC/M23, whereas Kivu Morning Post's local sources describe drone strikes by the Congolese army before the fall of Mikenge.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé avoir repris, le matin de ce mercredi 10 juin, le contrôle des localités de Mikenge, Kakenge et Kalingi, dans les hauts plateaux des territoires de Fizi et de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu.

Selon un communiqué de l’armée congolaise, ces localités avaient été occupées lundi dernier par la coalition Twirwaneho-M23 à la suite d’une attaque violente. Les assaillants auraient notamment utilisé des drones militaires lors de l’offensive.
Les FARDC indiquent que la reconquête de ces positions est intervenue après une contre-offensive d’environ 48 heures, menée avec l’appui des combattants Wazalendo.

Samy Kalonji Badibanga précise que l’attaque du lundi 8 juin aurait été facilitée par l’usage de drones attribués à l’AFC/M23, ainsi que par l’intervention de groupes armés alliés, notamment Red Tabara et Twirwaneho.

r1-SKC-2026H1-019.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that on Wednesday 10 June 2026 the "coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime", notably the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and elements of the Burundian national force, launched attacks against the densely populated areas of Gakenke and surroundings in the Minembwe highlands (Lulenge sector, Fizi territory); on X he said the attacks, carried out with kamikaze-type and KT-6 combat drones and heavy artillery, caused heavy loss of life, destroyed many homes and forced civilians to flee. Kivu Morning Post said no communication was possible in the zone, telephone lines and the internet being cut.
r1-SKC-2026H1-019.l: Gakenke and surroundings, Minembwe highlands, Lulenge sector, Fizi territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-019.a: AFC/M23 spokesperson accusing FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and Burundian forces
r1-SKC-2026H1-019.n: Partisan; cited only for what AFC/M23 said. KMP says phone and internet lines in the zone were cut so unverified. Fizi territory event but linked to the Mikenge fighting.
r1-SKC-2026H1-019.vn: Location names and the homes/displacement clause were outside the stored excerpts: contiguous passages supplied. Party statement (AFC/M23), not verified; the outlet says communications in the zone were cut. The second drone type is printed as 'KT-6'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (10 Jun 2026) carries all clauses; the page names the second drone type as KT-6, and the communications-cut sentence was in no stored excerpt, so it is added. The same article reports the FARDC retook Mikenge that day. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Kivu Morning Post (10 Jun 2026) carries all clauses; the page names the second drone type as KT-6, and the communications-cut sentence was in no stored excerpt, so it is added. The same article reports the FARDC retook Mikenge that day.
src: « Ce mercredi 10 juin 2026, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa, notamment les FARDC, les FDLR, les Wazalendo et les éléments de la force nationale burundaise, ont lancé des attaques contre les zones densément peuplées de Gakenke et de ses environs

a déclaré dans un communiqué Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC/M23. Sur son compte X, il précise que ces attaques, menées à l’aide de drones de combat de type kamikaze et KT-6 ainsi que d’artillerie lourde, ont causé de lourdes pertes en vies humaines
Pour l’heure, aucune communication n’est possible dans la zone, les lignes téléphoniques et la connexion internet étant toujours coupées.

r1-SKC-2026H1-020.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to "independent sources" it did not name, at least some thirty ("au moins une trentaine") soldiers of the Burundian army reportedly lost their lives on Tuesday 9 June 2026 in fighting on the Minembwe axis, which continued the next day.
r1-SKC-2026H1-020.a: armée burundaise (Burundian army), as named by the source
r1-SKC-2026H1-020.x: Unnamed 'independent sources' via Kivu Morning Post: at least some thirty ('une trentaine') Burundian soldiers reportedly killed
r1-SKC-2026H1-020.n: Unnamed sources; no Burundian statement found.
r1-SKC-2026H1-020.vn: Hedge and approximate figure kept as printed; 'FDNB' removed from actor (not printed). Unnamed sources; conditional ('auraient'); approximate figure. No Burundian statement found.
src: Selon des sources indépendantes, au moins une trentaine de militaires de l’armée burundaise auraient perdu la vie hier, mardi 9 juin 2026, dans des combats sur l’axe Minembwe qui se sont poursuivis ce mercredi.

r1-SKC-2026H1-021.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least 21 people, including 15 soldiers of the DRC armed forces, were killed in clashes on Wednesday 20 May 2026 between the Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 and the Congolese army, supported by Wazalendo militias and the Burundian army, in Fizi and Mwenga territories; according to concordant sources and civil society, the toll was recorded at FARDC positions in Mikenge (9 dead), Bukunji village (three dead) and Bichumbe village near Point Zéro (three dead). The outlet said the toll remained provisional because the zone was inaccessible to the press, and that a security source disputed it.
r1-SKC-2026H1-021.l: Mikenge, Bukunji, Bichumbe near Point Zéro, Mwenga and Fizi territories
r1-SKC-2026H1-021.a: Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 vs FARDC, Wazalendo, Burundian army
r1-SKC-2026H1-021.x: Kivu Morning Post / concordant sources and civil society: at least 21 dead including 15 FARDC soldiers (9 at Mikenge, three at Bukunji, three at Bichumbe); provisional. Disputed by a security source (separate claim)
r1-SKC-2026H1-021.n: Toll contested by a security source (next claim). Note FARDC held Mikenge on 20 May per this source; AFC/M23-side account not found.
r1-SKC-2026H1-021.vn: Figures written as printed; provisional caveat added from a contiguous passage. Kept separate from the security source's toll. Tolls differ by source: 21 dead incl. 15 FARDC (Kivu Morning Post, concordant sources and civil society) versus 4 dead and six wounded (unnamed security source). The per-place figures add to 15, not 21; the source does not explain the difference.
src: Au moins 21 personnes, dont 15 militaires des Forces armées de la RDC, ont été tuées lors d’affrontements mercredi 20 mai 2026 entre les Twirwaneho alliés à l’AFC-M23 et l’armée congolaise, appuyée par les milices Wazalendo et l’armée burundaise, dans le territoire de Fizi et de Mwenga, en province du Sud-Kivu.

Selon des sources concordantes et la société civile, ce bilan a été enregistré sur les positions des FARDC à Mikenge, où l’on dénombre 9 morts, au village de Bukunji avec trois morts, ainsi que trois autres morts au village de Bichumbe, près du Point Zéro.

r1-SKC-2026H1-022.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a security source contacted in the region refuted the outlet's toll for the clashes (see the related claim) and instead gave a figure of 4 dead and six wounded.
r1-SKC-2026H1-022.l: Mikenge, Bukunji, Bichumbe, Mwenga and Fizi territories
r1-SKC-2026H1-022.x: Unnamed security source: 4 dead and six wounded (versus Kivu Morning Post: at least 21 dead)
r1-SKC-2026H1-022.vn: Numbers 21 and 20 May were not in the stored excerpt: contiguous passage from the lead supplied; 'six' kept in words as printed. The security source is unnamed and its affiliation is not stated.
src: Une source sécuritaire contactée dans la région réfute ce bilan et avance plutôt un chiffre de 4 morts et six blessés.

r1-SKC-2026H1-023.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Lungele Itebo Samuel, president of the Mwenga territory civil society, said that in January 2026 the Kamituga and "Kititu" (as printed) health zones were hit by a measles epidemic causing deaths, especially among children, with no response so far, and that since February 2026 the population of Mwenga health zone had been hit by cholera, with 13 deaths and 34 cases under inappropriate treatment to date in health facilities of Iganda, Sungwe, Kalole, Tuseswa and the Mwenga general referral hospital; the civil society said these facilities lacked pharmaceutical products to eradicate the epidemic.
r1-SKC-2026H1-023.l: Mwenga health zone (Iganda, Sungwe, Kalole, Tuseswa), Kamituga and Kitutu health zones, Mwenga territory
r1-SKC-2026H1-023.a: not applicable (epidemic and lack of supplies)
r1-SKC-2026H1-023.x: Civil society: 13 cholera deaths and 34 cases under inappropriate treatment (since February 2026)
r1-SKC-2026H1-023.n: Civil society claims; context for civilian access to health care, no attack alleged.
r1-SKC-2026H1-023.vn: The measles and 'since February' clauses were not in the stored excerpt: contiguous passage supplied. Draft said 'Kitutu health zones'; the source prints 'Kititu'. Context for civilian access to health care; no attack alleged. The source spells the health zone 'Kititu' (and lists 'Kitutu' as a health area).
src: À ce jour, il y a 13 morts et 34 cas sous traitement inapproprié dans des structures sanitaires d’Iganda, Sungwe, Kalole, Tuseswa, ainsi qu’à l’hôpital général de référence de Mwenga », a ajouté Lungele Itebo Samuel.
La société civile affirme que ces structures sont dépourvues de produits pharmaceutiques destinés à éradiquer cette épidémie.

r1-SKC-2026H2-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that Kaniola civil society said three civilians returning from a Léopards match were summarily executed on 24 September at Kaniola, naming them as Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac and Bizimana Ciraza.
r1-SKC-2026H2-001.n: Spellings differ from Opinion-info's account of the same event (separate claim). Radio Okapi (Oct 21) separately says three youths were killed at Kaniola 'par des éléments du M23' according to locally reported information.
r1-SKC-2026H2-001.vn: Excerpt matches the retained page and carries every clause. Same origin as existing r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011 (same letter, same URL), so not independent. Single civil-society origin: C. r1-SKC-2026H2-003.s: Opinion-info reported that South Kivu civil society said it had received alerts of several murders of civilians at Luntukulu (Mulamba groupement), more than ten cases in September, which the article says were given without documentation allowing independent verification; the article adds that cases of beatings, rapes and forced recruitment of young people are also reported.
r1-SKC-2026H2-003.l: Luntukulu, Mulamba groupement, Walungu territory, South Kivu

src: Dans le groupement de Mulamba, à Luntukulu, la société civile dit également avoir reçu des alertes concernant plusieurs assassinats de civils. Elle avance le chiffre de plus de dix cas enregistrés au cours du mois de septembre, sans fournir dans son communiqué de documentation permettant de vérifier indépendamment ce bilan. Des cas de bastonnades, de viols et d’enrôlement forcé de jeunes sont également rapportés.

r1-SKC-2026H2-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that Kaniola civil society said that on 21 September at Nzibira-Luntukulu two teachers were tortured and subjected to an attempted assassination, and that on 23 September at Kashanja a taxi driver from Kalengera, Zigashane Mashali, was extorted of 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) before being killed by beating.
r1-SKC-2026H2-004.l: Nzibira-Luntukulu and Kashanja, Walungu territory, South Kivu

src: Le 21 septembre à Nzibira‑Luntukulu, deux enseignants ont été torturés et victimes d’une tentative d’assassinat. Le 23 septembre à Kashanja, un taximan de Kalengera, Zigashane Mashali, a été extorqué de 30 000 francs congolais (13 USD) avant d’être tué par bastonnade.

r1-SKC-2026H2-006.l: Nzibira-Shabunda road, Nzibira (Walungu) to Shabunda, South Kivu

src: Elle accuse les combattants de l’AFC/M23, devenu Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), d’exiger le recrutement de 10 jeunes de Nzibira dans leurs rangs, sous peine de maintenir cette voie fermée. Selon cette structure, cette situation perturbe fortement les activités économiques et l’accès aux soins de santé dans la région.
Selon cette structure, les combattants exigent le recrutement de dix jeunes de Nzibira dans leurs rangs pour rouvrir l’axe.
Selon cette organisation, les combattants de l’AFC/M23, également connus sous l’appellation Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), subordonnent la levé

r1-SKC-2026H2-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that the civil society of Kitutu village, Mwenga territory, alerted to the continued presence of soldiers and Wazalendo fighters in mining sites of the area, one month after President Félix Tshisekedi's order for the immediate and definitive withdrawal of forces illegally present in the mines.
r1-SKC-2026H2-010.a: FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters, per local civil society
r1-SKC-2026H2-010.n: Title reconstructed from search snippet plus URL; verify. Radio Okapi says it was unable to reach the FARDC South Kivu spokesperson for a reaction.
r1-SKC-2026H2-010.vn: The order concerned 'forces présentes illégalement dans les mines', not specifically 'their' (soldiers' and Wazalendo's) withdrawal: narrowed to the source's wording. Title on the retained page is 'La société civile de Kitutu (Sud-Kivu) dénonce la présence persistante des militaires dans les sites miniers' (the stored title was reconstructed and is wrong). C. Radio Okapi says it could not obtain a reaction from the FARDC spokesperson in South Kivu.
src: La société civile du village de Kitutu, dans le territoire de Mwenga (Sud-Kivu), alerte sur la présence continue de militaires et de combattants Wazalendo dans les sites miniers de la zone. Cette situation perdure un mois après l’ordre donné par le président Félix Tshisekedi pour le retrait immédiat et définitif des forces présentes illégalement dans les mines.

r1-SKC-2026H2-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that Félicien Myaka, president of the Kitutu civil society, said any dissenting voice is immediately silenced, sometimes by violence, and urged local authorities to apply the head of state's order on forces in mining sites.
r1-SKC-2026H2-011.n: General allegation; no specific incident or perpetrator named.
r1-SKC-2026H2-011.vn: Statement supported. The actor ('soldiers and Wazalendo guarding mining sites, implied') was inferred: replaced with 'not attributed by the source'. Title corrected as for the Kitutu claim. C. General allegation with no incident, victim or perpetrator. Myaka also says all sites 'restent gardés par des militaires et des Wazalendo', but does not say who silences dissent.
src: dénonce Félicien Myaka, président de la société civile de Kitutu. Il affirme que toute voix discordante est immédiatement réduite au silence, parfois par la violence, et exhorte les autorités locales à appliquer l’ordre du chef de l’État.

r1-SKC-2026H2-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that massive population displacements had been recorded for several days in the villages of Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta following clashes of 24 to 27 September 2026 between the AFC/M23 coalition, which it described as backed by Red Tabara and Twirwaheno, and the FARDC/Wazalendo; the local Itombwe youth council said the incidents caused large population movements.
r1-SKC-2026H2-012.l: Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo and Maheta, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2026H2-012.a: AFC/M23 coalition 'appuyée par les Red Tabara et les Twirwaheno' vs FARDC/Wazalendo
r1-SKC-2026H2-012.n: Title reconstructed from search snippet and URL; verify. Source is the local youth council (Mfariji Lewis, president), relayed by Actualite.cd. Placement in Mwenga territory is the source's. 'Twirwaheno' is spelled as printed.
r1-SKC-2026H2-012.vn: The draft attributed the outlet's narration (including the Red Tabara/Twirwaheno backing) to the youth council; the page attributes it to no one. Re-attributed clause by clause; 'Mwenga territory' cut from the statement (only the title prints Mwenga). The youth-council clause is page-only. Title confirmed. C. The displacements and the description of the coalition are Actualite.cd's narration; the youth council (president Mfariji Lewis, per the page) is quoted on the incidents and movements towards Masango, Kigoma and Itombwe forest areas. The headline places the area in Mwenga territory.
src: Des déplacements massifs de populations sont enregistrés depuis plusieurs jours dans les villages de Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo et Maheta, à la suite des affrontements survenus du 24 au 27 septembre 2026 entre la coalition AFC/M23, appuyée par les Red Tabara et les Twirwaheno, et les FARDC/Wazalendo.

r1-SKC-2026H2-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Itombwe local youth council said a significant proportion of displaced households lacked adequate shelter and had difficulty accessing food and drinking water, and that several schools and health structures were reportedly closed, damaged or difficult to reach.
r1-SKC-2026H2-013.l: Itombwe sector (Kashongo, Magunda, Msongyo, Maheta), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2026H2-013.n: No facility named; the cause of closure is not stated.
r1-SKC-2026H2-013.vn: Excerpt exact; 'Le conseil local' is the conseil local de la jeunesse d’Itombwe named earlier on the page. No facility named, no cause given. C.
src: Le conseil local souligne qu’une proportion importante des ménages déplacés est actuellement sans abri adéquat, confrontée à des difficultés d’accès à la nourriture et à l’eau potable. Plusieurs écoles et structures sanitaires seraient fermées, endommagées ou difficilement accessibles

r1-SKC-2026H2-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, violent clashes had been under way since the morning of 28 August between AFC/M23 rebels and their allies and the FARDC backed by Wazalendo groups in the Point Zéro area, which the article places in Mwenga territory, with fighting beginning around 4 a.m. in the Itombwe highlands at Point Zéro Centre.
r1-SKC-2026H2-014.l: Point Zéro Centre, Itombwe sector, South Kivu (the article says Mwenga territory)
r1-SKC-2026H2-014.a: AFC/M23 and allies; FARDC with Wazalendo groups

Kept as the source prints it; territory field flagged for reviewer. Title reconstructed from search snippet; verify. The same article recalls that Twirwaheno took Point Zéro on 4 July (already recorded in existing claims).

Grade lowered from B to C: one outlet relying on unnamed local sources. DISCREPANCY: Actualite.cd places Point Zéro in Mwenga territory; other sources place it in Fizi territory. The same article says Point Zéro lies 74 km from Fizi-Centre and 27 km from Mikenge. Source wording kept; conflict not resolved.
src: De violents affrontements opposent depuis la matinée du 28 août les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et leurs alliés aux FARDC, appuyées par les groupes Wazalendo, dans la zone de Point Zéro, territoire de Mwenga (Sud-Kivu). Selon des sources locales, les combats ont débuté vers 4 heures du matin

r1-SKC-2026H2-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that videos had circulated online a few days earlier showing elements assimilated to the Wazalendo vandalising trucks during construction work at Mwenga; civil society called for legal action against the authors of the vandalism 'à balles réelles' on 31 July 2026 at Ngenga, and demanded the opening of a secured humanitarian corridor for humanitarian NGOs wishing to intervene in the government-held part.
r1-SKC-2026H2-015.l: Mwenga territory (Kamituga, Kitutu, Kibe, Lugushwa, Kibumba, Ngenga), South Kivu
r1-SKC-2026H2-015.a: elements 'assimilés aux Wazalendo' (vandalism at Ngenga, 31 July 2026)

The ville morte statement itself is from the first lines of the page (excerpt 1 covers vandalism; the 'ville morte' fact is in the page's opening sentences, which the reviewer should check against the page or cite separately).
r1-SKC-2026H2-015.vn: The first clause (ville morte on 13 August, RN2) is covered by no excerpt: cut per instructions. The 'after videos circulated' link in the draft is not on the page: rephrased as two facts. Category changed to looting_or_destruction (the remaining substance is the vandalism allegation). Title on the retained page: 'Mwenga : ville morte pour réclamer la réhabilitation de la RN2 et des sanctions contre les Wazalendo, auteurs du vandalisme des engins de construction' (stored title was reconstructed and incomplete). C. The page's opening sentences report a 'ville morte' across Mwenga territory (Kamituga, Kitutu, Kibe, Lugushwa, Kibumba) from the morning of Thursday 13 August to demand rehabilitation of the RN2; no stored excerpt carries this, so it is not in the statement (lead: extend the excerpt with add_excerpt to record it).
src: Il y a à peine quelques jours, des vidéos ont circulé sur la toile où certains éléments assimilés aux Wazalendo étaient en train de vandaliser des camions en pleins travaux de construction à Mwenga. La société civile plaide également pour l'ouverture des actions judiciaires. " Ouvrir une sanction juridique contre les auteurs de ce vandalisme à balles réelles le 31 juillet 2026, à Ngenga ", ajoute la société civile.

Dans leurs revendications, les acteurs de la société civile ont également réclamé l'ouverture d'un couloir humanitaire, et sécurisé aux ONGs humanitaires désireuses d'intervenir dans la partie gouvernementale.

r1-SKC-2026H2-016.s: KazibaOnline reported that the Cirimiro commercial centre, at the boundary of the Kaziba and Luhwindja chiefdoms, was targeted by an armed looting on the evening of Sunday 11 October 2026, in which, per information reported to it, a trader was shot, a motorbike was burned and goods were taken; it named the wounded trader as Mugisho Eraston Gadi Nakahakwa and said the attackers' identity remained to be established.
r1-SKC-2026H2-016.l: Cirimiro, boundary of Kaziba and Luhwindja chiefdoms, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2026H2-016.n: Local community site (KazibaOnline, Kaziba, Walungu), author named on page as Charles Irenge Lwaboshi; single local source. Page says displaced people from Kabembe, Butuzi and Kashozi who had taken refuge at Cirimiro were also reportedly assaulted, and that fighting between Wazalendo and M23 was reported at the same time on Rhanga, Chemba and Kamano hills in Kabembe.
r1-SKC-2026H2-016.vn: Both excerpts exact; the 'identity to be established' clause is page-only. C. Per the same page: more than 30 armed men 'décrits comme portant des uniformes'; displaced people from Kabembe, Butuzi and Kashozi who had sheltered at Cirimiro were reportedly assaulted; the wounded trader is treated at the Hôpital général de référence de Kaziba. Single local community outlet; cover image is AI-generated.
src: Le centre commercial de Cirimiro, situé à la limite des chefferies de Kaziba et de Luhwindja, a été visé par un pillage armé dans la soirée du dimanche 11 octobre 2026. Selon les informations rapportées à Kazibaonline.com, un commerçant a été blessé par balle, une moto incendiée et des biens emportés.

Au cours de l’attaque, M. Mugisho Eraston Gadi Nakahakwa a été atteint par balle à la jambe. Il poursuit sa prise en charge médicale à l’Hôpital général de référence de Kaziba, d’après les informations transmises.

r1-SKC-2026H2-017.l: Mitimbili hills, Ntagereka groupement, eastern Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SKC-2026H2-017.a: M23 elements; FARDC and Wazalendo fighters, per a local source
r1-SKC-2026H2-017.n: Single local source. The lead sentence giving the place and date (Mitimbili, Ntagereka, Monday 12 October) is in the preceding passage of the page. The article's cover image is AI-generated and not evidence.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that M23 rebels conquered the cité of Minova (Kalehe territory) in South Kivu on Monday 20 January, after intense fighting on the last hills of Masisi territory in neighbouring North Kivu.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, quoting a journalist who attended a meeting held by M23 in Minova, that the rebels said schools could reopen within 48 hours and promised that the RN2 Minova-Bweremana-Sake-Goma road would be reopened.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that two people died and two others were wounded after shooting by FARDC soldiers in Kabare territory, 25 km north of Bukavu, on the evening of Monday 20 January; local sources said the victims were hit by bullets fired by a group of FARDC soldiers heading to the front. The deputy commander of the military region in charge of intelligence and operations confirmed the shooting without giving its motive, and did not confirm the toll.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.l: Kavumu and Katana, Kabare, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.a: FARDC soldiers (per Radio Okapi and local sources)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.x: Radio Okapi: 2 killed, 2 wounded (toll not confirmed by FARDC)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.n: Victims not named by the page excerpt.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-003.vn: Original statement attributed the toll to local sources, but the toll is Radio Okapi's own narration; local sources are cited for who fired. Added the FARDC 33rd Military Region response printed on the page (a party statement) and the title, which prints the figures. The page title places the incident in Kavumu and Katana, one death in each. Per local sources the soldiers were heading to the front on the Kalehe axis; the responding officer is the deputy commander of the 33rd Military Region (33e Région militaire), who did not confirm the toll. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Deux personnes sont mortes et deux autres blessées après des tirs des militaires FARDC dans le territoire de Kabare à 25 km au nord de la ville de Bukavu (Sud-Kivu) lundi 20 janvier dans la soirée.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that the citizen movement LUCHA denounced killings in Miti and Kavumu (Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory) during the night of Friday to Saturday 8 February; in a statement signed in Bukavu LUCHA reported that 9 people were killed by what it called undisciplined soldiers of the Congolese armed forces.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-004.l: Miti and Kavumu, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q1-004.a: soldiers of the Congolese armed forces (per LUCHA)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-004.n: Single civil-society account relayed by Radio Okapi; no FARDC response in the excerpt. Search for FARDC reply not found.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-004.vn: Excerpt verbatim and carries all clauses; attribution kept to LUCHA. Later on the page LUCHA's spokesperson places the killings at Mululu in Miti grouping and at Kavumu in Bugorhe grouping. Allegation by LUCHA; no FARDC response on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le mouvement citoyen Lutte pour le changement (LUCHA) dénonce les tueries survenues à Miti et Kavumu, dans le groupement de Bugorhe, au territoire de Kabare dans la province du Sud-Kivu, durant la nuit du vendredi au samedi 8 février. Dans une déclaration signée samedi à Bukavu, LUCHA rapporte que 9 personnes ont été tuées par certains militaires indisciplinés des Forces armées de la RDC.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Kavumu airport in South Kivu passed under the control of M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, on the afternoon of Friday 14 February.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-005.a: M23 supported by Rwanda (per Radio Okapi)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-005.vn: Excerpt verbatim; the date 14 is printed in a later sentence of the same article (supplied). Radio Okapi reports, per concordant local sources, no confrontation between Katana and Kavumu; military authorities at camp Nyamunyunyi could not be reached. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L'aéroport de Kavumu au Sud-Kivu vient de passer en début de ce vendredi après-midi sous le contrôle des rebelles du M23, soutenus par le Rwanda.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that the rebels and their allies, the Rwandan armed forces, entered Kabare territory from the cité of Kabamba in the Irhambi Katana grouping on the morning of Friday 14 February.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-006.l: Kabamba (Irhambi Katana) to Kabare, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q1-006.a: rebels and the Rwandan armed forces (per Radio Okapi)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-006.n: Attribution of 'Rwandan armed forces' is Radio Okapi's; no RDF/Rwanda government statement searched in this unit's excerpt; Rwanda has denied direct involvement elsewhere (not verified here).
r1-SKN-2025Q1-006.vn: Excerpt verbatim and supports the statement; the flagged entity is an English rendering of the printed French name. 'Rwandan armed forces' translates the page's 'forces armées rwandaises'; the description of Rwandan forces as allies is Radio Okapi's own. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: C'est depuis la cité de Kabamba dans le groupement d'Irhambi Katana que les rebelles et leurs alliées, les forces armées rwandaises, sont entrés dans le territoire de Kabare dans la matinée de ce vendredi 14 février.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that M23 fighters, supported by the Rwandan army, appeared in the streets of Bukavu, chef-lieu of South Kivu, on Sunday 16 February.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-007.a: M23, supported by the Rwandan army (per Radio Okapi)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-007.n: Afrikarabia gives 15 February for the entry into Bukavu; see the next claim. Discrepancy to surface.

Radio Okapi says columns arrived from Kazingo (Kabare) from the early morning. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des combattants du groupe rebelle M23, soutenus par l'armée rwandaise, ont fait une apparition remarquée dans les rues de Bukavu, chef-lieu du Sud-Kivu, ce dimanche 16 février.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-008.s: Afrikarabia reported a sequence of M23 captures in South Kivu: Nyabibwe on 5 February, Kalehe on 12 and the Kavumu airport on 14, before entering Bukavu on 15 February.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-008.l: Nyabibwe, Kalehe, Kavumu airport, Bukavu, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q1-008.n: Same page dates Minova and Sake to 24 January (Actualite.cd: Minova 20 January) and Bukavu entry 15 February (Radio Okapi: 16 February). Afrikarabia is an analytic outlet; treat dates as to be reconciled.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-008.vn: Excerpt verbatim; M23 printed in the preceding sentence (supplied). Kavumu 14 Feb matches Radio Okapi; Bukavu 15 Feb differs from Radio Okapi's 16 Feb.
