src: Commence ensuite une descente express vers le Sud-Kivu avec les prises de Nyabibwe le 5 février, de Kalehe le 12 et de l’aéroport de Kavumu le 14, avant d’entrer dans Bukavu le 15 février.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-009.s: UN News (Swahili) reported that the UN Humanitarian Coordinator, Lemarquis, said in a video interview with UN News that Kalehe, which he described as a large town in the province, had fallen that afternoon.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-009.n: Page says the interview was given 'yesterday Wednesday' (computed 2025-02-12, date computed from weekday and publication date). The excerpt does not name the captor.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-009.vn: Removed the publication date (13 is printed only in the page dateline) and named the speaker, who is printed on the page (supplied). The quote does not name who took Kalehe. Date derived from the interview being given 'yesterday Wednesday' relative to a page dated 13 February 2025. The same page wrongly calls Goma the capital of South Kivu, so the Swahili text is not error-free. The page names the coordinator in full as Bruno Lemarquis.
src: Kalehe, ambao ni mji mkubwa katika jimbo hili, umeanguka leo mchana,” Mratibu wa Misaada ya Kibinadamu aliripoti.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-010.s: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 fighters entered the small town of Kamanyola, on the border of DR Congo, Burundi and Rwanda, on Tuesday night, according to residents.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-010.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (19 Feb). Outside the strict unit geography (Walungu) but bears on the Bukavu-Uvira frontline.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-010.vn: Excerpt verbatim; the 'AFP' on the page is a photo credit, not a wire credit. Date computed from 'Tuesday night' on a page dated 19 February 2025. The page also says, as hearsay, that DRC troops from Bukavu and the Kamanyola border had fled days earlier towards Uvira.
src: Abarwanyi ba M23 binjiye mu mujyi muto wa Kamanyola uri ku mupaka wa DR Congo, u Burundi n'u Rwanda mu ijoro ryo ku wa kabiri, nk'uko abahatuye babivuga.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-011.s: BBC Gahuza reported that Radio RFI said there was fighting on Tuesday between M23 and Burundian troops who were camped at Kamanyola, before those troops fled; it also reported that the FARDC did not respond to BBC's request about the capture of Kamanyola.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-011.a: M23 and Burundi troops (per RFI via BBC)
r1-SKN-2025Q1-011.n: Relayed RFI report; original RFI item not fetched. No Burundi government statement found in this unit.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-011.vn: Both clauses printed on the page; FARDC and BBC are named in the supplied passage. The fighting with Burundian troops is RFI's report relayed by BBC Gahuza; the RFI original was not fetched. FARDC: no response to BBC.
src: Radio RFI ivuga ko ku wa kabiri habaye imirwano hagati ya M23 n'ingabo z'u Burundi zari zikambitse i Kamanyola mbere y'uko izo ngabo zihunga.

r1-SKN-2025Q1-012.s: CAJ News Africa reported that the Panzi Foundation, whose headquarters are in Bukavu and which runs a hospital, was wary of the safety of its staff after rebel forces took control of Bukavu, and quoted Panzi as saying its team was unharmed, Panzi Hospital remained open with an on-call staff, and its surgeons were treating an influx of patients with gunshot wounds and severe injuries from explosives.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-012.n: Operating status, not an attack; no health_care harm alleged. Single outlet relaying the foundation.
r1-SKN-2025Q1-012.vn: Original statement's names (Panzi Foundation, Panzi Hospital) were printed in the excerpt only partly; supplied the passage that prints them and M23. Added the trauma-caseload line for the health-care focus. Panzi is a credible non-partisan origin, so B. Health-care operating status during the takeover of Bukavu, per Panzi's own statement; no attack on the facility is alleged. CAJ News names the forces as the March 23 Movement (M23).
src: “At this time, our team remains unharmed, albeit shaken, and Panzi Hospital remains open with an on-call staff,” Panzi stated.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 9 April, on the Kalehe highlands, Wazalendo of COPACO and MCDPN, commanded by self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho, Maike and Bahige, recovered Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 and Nyawaronga after fighting with M23 backed by Rwanda.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-001.l: Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2, Nyawaronga, Kalehe highlands
r1-SKN-2025Q2-001.a: Wazalendo (COPACO, MCDPN) vs M23 supported by Rwanda, as the source names them
r1-SKN-2025Q2-001.n: Headline says 8 localities of Kalehe passed to Wazalendo after 3 days of fighting. Wazalendo accounts via local sources; M23 account not found in this source.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-001.vn: Date '9 April' rests on the article's lead sentence, not the excerpt; added that passage. Highlands sentence itself is 'Le même mercredi'. Radio Okapi's 9 April article says the same coalition recovered these four localities after fighting on 6 and 7 April (per local rights activists), while the 10 April article places the recovery on Wednesday 9 April; the exact day is uncertain. Names are as printed by Radio Okapi. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Apr 2025. The COPACO/MCDPN sentence is written in Radio Okapi's own voice; the article's 'selon plusieurs sources locales' attaches to the separate Raia Mutomboki recapture of eight localities in Mbinga Sud, so 'citing local sources' is dropped from this clause. Otherwise verbatim.
src: Le même mercredi, dans les Hauts plateaux du territoire de Kalehe, les Wazalendo de COPACO et MCDPN, commandés par les généraux autoproclamés Kirikicho, Maike et Bahige, ont récupéré les agglomérations de Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 et Nyawaronga après des affrontements avec les M23 soutenus par le Rwanda.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-002.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local activists, that after fighting on Sunday 6 and Monday 7 April on the hills above Bushushu, Lemera and Ihusi, local sources said most of the population of the Kalehe highlands had displaced toward Bushushu, Mabuka and Ihusi.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-002.n: Same source also reports M23 fighters seen at Kalehe centre (Ihusi) on 9 April.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-002.vn: Supported by the page; dates from the passage preceding the excerpt. On the page, local rights activists are cited for the recovery of localities after the 6-7 April fighting; the displacement is attributed to local sources.
src: Des sources locales indiquent que la majeure partie de la population s'est déplacée vers Bushushu, Mabuka et Ihusi, fuyant la violence des combats.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that M23, supported by Rwandan forces, retook four localities of Kalehe and Kabare territories on Tuesday 15 April after fighting with Wazalendo allied to the FARDC, including Lemera, Bushaku 1 and Bushaku 2 (Kalehe) and Kabamba (Kabare).
r1-SKN-2025Q2-003.a: M23 supported by Rwandan forces, as the source says
r1-SKN-2025Q2-003.n: Body text says hostilities lasted all day 14 April; headline/lead date the retaking 15 April. Actualite.cd (16 April) also reports the retaking (not re-cited here).
r1-SKN-2025Q2-003.vn: Supported; localities list added from the next sentence. The same article says the hostilities lasted all day on 14 April; Kivu Morning Post (16 April) reports the same retaking on 14 and 15 April. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 16 Apr 2025, carries every clause in its own voice. The stored excerpt does not name the localities; the passage that does is added. Statement unchanged.
src: Les rebelles du M23, soutenus par des forces rwandaises, ont reconquis quatre localités des territoires de Kalehe et Kabare (Sud-Kivu) le mardi 15 avril 2025, après de violents affrontements avec les combattants Wazalendo, alliés de l’armée congolaise (FARDC).
Les localités reprises incluent Lemera, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 (Kalehe) et Kabamba (Kabare), où trois civils ont été tués dans le groupement d’Irhambi Katana.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that the localities retaken included Kabamba (Kabare), where three civilians were killed in the Irhambi Katana groupement; the source does not say who killed them.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-004.a: not stated by the source (fighting between M23 and Wazalendo)
r1-SKN-2025Q2-004.n: Perpetrator not stated by the source; fighting was between M23 and Wazalendo with heavy weapons.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-004.vn: 'when M23 retook the locality' implied timing/causation the source does not state; spelling Irhambi Katana as printed; perpetrator not stated. Grade B: credible outlet's own reporting. Kivu Morning Post (16 April) also reports three civilians killed at Irhambi Katana in the 14 April fighting with heavy weapons. Victims not named.
src: Les localités reprises incluent Lemera, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2 (Kalehe) et Kabamba (Kabare), où trois civils ont été tués dans le groupement d’Irhambi Katana.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-005.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that M23 also controlled the Kavumu airport (Kabare territory) after attack attempts on the town the previous weekend.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-005.n: Radio Okapi (16 April) says Wazalendo temporarily retook the airport on 13 April per regional sources; accounts differ on timing and are given separately.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-005.vn: Supported verbatim. Draft source_type held an English translation; corrected to media (the draft's language field also holds a wrong value). Recorded separately. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le M23 contrôle également l'aéroport de Kavumu, suite à des tentatives d'attaque dans la cité le week-end dernier.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to concordant testimonies, M23/AFC reinforcements arrived by Lake Kivu from North Kivu and by road from Bukavu and Kavumu, a redeployment that sources in the region said followed the Wazalendo's temporary recapture of Kavumu airport on 13 April.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-006.a: Wazalendo, per sources in the region
r1-SKN-2025Q2-006.n: Single-source assertion by regional sources; conflicts with or qualifies the Kivu Morning Post claim that M23 controlled the airport.

src: Ce redéploiement fait suite à la reprise temporaire de l’aéroport de Kavumu par les Wazalendo le 13 avril, affirment des sources dans la région.

Selon des témoignages concordants, des renforts du M23/AFC sont arrivés par le lac Kivu en provenance du Nord-Kivu et par voie routière depuis Bukavu et Kavumu, où des accrochages avaient opposé les belligérants le week-end précédent.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that M23 rebels were accused of looting on Sunday 20 April during their withdrawal from the Kalehe highlands, and that witnesses said they systematically ransacked kiosks and shops in the Kasheke commercial centre.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-007.a: M23, as accused in the source
r1-SKN-2025Q2-007.n: Accusation reported via witnesses and local sources; no M23 response in the source.
src: Les rebelles du M23 sont accusés d’avoir commis des actes de pillage, dimanche 20 avril, lors de leur retrait des hauts plateaux de Kalehe, dans le Sud-Kivu. Des témoins rapportent que, lors de leur passage, ils ont systématiquement dévalisé des kiosques et des boutiques du centre commercial de Kasheke.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that during the same M23 movement from the Kalehe highlands passers-by had phones and money stolen and others, in particular young people, were forced to carry the rebels' luggage.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-008.n: Attribution to M23 comes from the article's preceding sentences (movements of M23 fighters, 'les rebelles').
r1-SKN-2025Q2-008.vn: Supported; M23 attribution from the preceding sentences. The article does not give a separate date for these acts; they are placed in the same 20 April withdrawal account.
src: Des passants se sont fait voler leurs téléphones et leur argent, tandis que d’autres, en particulier des jeunes, ont été forcés de transporter les bagages des rebelles.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that Wazalendo fought M23 for at least an hour at Irambo, and that a man of about thirty was shot dead inside the grounds of the Catholic parish of Irambo Kalehe as a result of the violence.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-009.a: not attributed by the source (fighting between Wazalendo and M23)
r1-SKN-2025Q2-009.n: Date is that of the article's account (20 April withdrawal); victim not named.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-009.vn: Supported verbatim. Shooter not identified by the source; victim not named; date inferred from the 20 April withdrawal account.
src: Des sources concordantes indiquent que les combattants Wazalendo ont riposté en engageant des affrontements avec le M23 pendant au moins une heure dans la localité d’Irambo. Un jeune homme d’une trentaine d’années a été tué par balle dans l’enceinte de la paroisse catholique d’Irambo Kalehe à la suite de ces violences.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Wednesday 14 May tension remained high at Tchofi and Kasheke (Kalehe) and Kabamba and Mabingu (Kabare), that M23 was pushed back on Tuesday evening from Katasomwa to the Kasheke and Tchofi ports, and that sources on site said it resumed fighting on Wednesday morning with troops from Bukavu and Goma.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-010.l: Kasheke-Lemera axis; Tchofi, Kasheke (Kalehe); Kabamba, Mabingu (Kabare)
r1-SKN-2025Q2-010.a: Wazalendo vs AFC-M23, as the source says
r1-SKN-2025Q2-010.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (14 May 2025; 'mardi soir' = 13 May). Exact toll said to be unknown; civilians fled to Ihoka and Ishovu islets and Kajuchu.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-010.vn: Supported; date from the lead sentence. Radio Okapi says the exact toll was unknown. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 14 May 2025, carries every clause; the 'tension remained high' clause with its four villages was not in the stored excerpt, so the opening passage is added. src: Ce n’est qu’en début de soirée que les rebelles du M23 ont été repoussés de Katasomwa jusqu’aux ports de Kasheke et de Tchofi. Selon des sources sur place, les rebelles ont relancé les combats dès ce mercredi matin, renforcés par des troupes venues de Bukavu et Goma, avec un nouvel apport en munitions.

La tension restait vive, ce mercredi 14 mai avant midi, dans les villages de Tchofi et Kasheke (territoire de Kalehe), ainsi qu’à Kabamba et Mabingu (territoire de Kabare) au Sud-Kivu, où des affrontements opposent les Wazalendo aux rebelles de l’AFC-M23.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-011.s: Congo Rassure reported that on the morning of Monday 12 May shots caused panic at Mugote market, in the south of Idjwi island, as the population tried to oppose taxes imposed by M23 rebels, which it said now control that part of the territory.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-011.n: Single Congolese online outlet (Kinshasa-aligned wording: 'illégales'); the article says rebels 'auraient tiré' (allegedly fired live rounds). Social-media posts on the same day describe a 10 USD moto tax (leads only, not cited).

r1-SKN-2025Q2-012.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing human rights defenders in Kalehe, that about 18 young people suspected of belonging to the Wazalendo were taken to an unknown destination by the rebels during a 'youth hunt' that began on Friday at Chofi.

src: Selon des témoignages de défenseurs des droits humains à Kalehe, environ 18 jeunes, soupçonnés d'appartenir au mouvement Wazalendo, ont été emmenés vers une destination inconnue par les rebelles lors d'une opération de chasse aux jeunes qui a débuté vendredi à Chofi.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that the same rights defenders said one of the abducted young people was reportedly killed, and that a couple accused of being close to M23 was abducted by Wazalendo at Kamunyerere.

src: Ils précisent que l'un des jeunes enlevés aurait été tué, et qu'un couple accusé d'être proche du M23 a également été enlevé par les Wazalendo dans la localité de Kamunyerere.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-014.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that on the evening of Thursday 5 June Wazalendo attacked M23 positions at Mabingu, on the Kabare-Kalehe boundary, which M23 had held for about ten days, and succeeded in dislodging the rebels.

r1-SKN-2025Q2-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that, while losing ground at Mabingu, M23 rebels carried out round-ups targeting men whom they equate with Wazalendo fighters, and that these arbitrary arrests took place at the edge of Kahuzi-Biega National Park, according to witnesses.
r1-SKN-2025Q2-015.l: Edge of Kahuzi-Biega National Park near Mabingu; Kasheke axis, Kalehe
r1-SKN-2025Q2-015.a: M23 rebels, per witnesses and local sources

r1-SKN-2025Q2-016.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing human rights activists, that the Mabingu fighting caused the death of one civilian and seriously wounded two people, a woman and an 11-year-old girl, and that residents of Mbinga Sud (Tchofi, Kasheke, Luzira) fled toward Idjwi island, Kajuchu and the Ihoka and Ishovu islets.

Des sources locales rapportent que les engins utilisés pour labourer la plantation théière ont été emportés vers une destination inconnue.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-001.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that five civilians were shot dead between 11 and 12 July at Karambi (Kabare territory) by armed men identified as M23-AFC-RDF rebels, in reprisal for the alleged killing of one of their members by the population; it named the victims, and said two of them were teachers returning from an exam centre at EP Chanya.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-001.a: armed men identified as M23-AFC-RDF rebels (as Radio Okapi reports)
r1-SKN-2025Q3-001.n: Single local-source report (Radio Okapi, 'selon des sources locales'). Source gives Friday for the first victim and 'the next day' for the rest; the range follows the article's 11-12 July. Perpetrator attribution is the outlet's report of local sources, not verified.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-001.vn: Excerpts exact; names as printed; Kabare/Karambi and the local-sources attribution carried by an extended source-1 passage. excerpt_en flag is the translation of 'vendredi' as 'Friday' (faithful). Perpetrator attribution is Radio Okapi's ('identifiés comme des rebelles du M23-AFC-RDF'), citing local sources; not independently verified. The source says Balume Mulingwa was killed on the Friday and was suspected of Wazalendo affiliation; the other four were 'exécutés le lendemain'.
src: Cinq civils ont été abattus entre les 11 et 12 juillet courant par des hommes armés identifiés comme des rebelles du M23-AFC-RDF, en représailles à l’assassinat présumé d’un de leurs éléments par la population. Parmi les victimes : Balume Mulingwa, tué vendredi, soupçonné d’être affilié aux Wazalendo, Mibambwe Mukenje, Pétro Bashwira, Bunani Rukozo et Jean Claude Cinamula, exécutés le lendemain.
Deux d’entre eux étaient enseignants revenant d’un centre d’examen à l’EP Chanya.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-002.s: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of terror at Bukavu and Nyantende, that at around 19 heures armed men burst into the local hospital at Nyantende, first neutralising the security guards and then turning on patients; according to local sources the assailants looted goods, extorted phones from patients and violently assaulted an on-duty doctor, then withdrew unhindered to an area reputed to be under rebel control.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-002.a: armed men (not identified by the source); the article's lead speaks of incursions by 'bandits armés'; they withdrew to an area 'réputée sous contrôle rebelle'
r1-SKN-2025Q3-002.n: Single local-source report. Night of 'mardi à mercredi 16 juillet' per the article (published 16 July). A 17 July La Prunelle press review snippet (laprunellerdc.cd) appears to repeat this (doctors assaulted, medical equipment looted in Kabare) but was not opened.

src: À Nyantende, c’est l’hôpital local qui a été la cible d’une attaque particulièrement choquante. Vers 19 heures, des hommes armés ont fait irruption dans l’établissement de santé, neutralisant d’abord les agents de sécurité avant de s’en prendre aux patients.

Selon des sources locales, les assaillants ont pillé des biens, extorqué des téléphones aux malades et violemment agressé un médecin de garde. Après leur forfait, ils se sont repliés sans être inquiétés, dans une zone réputée sous contrôle rebelle.
Selon des sources locales, les assaillants ont pillé des biens, extorqué des téléphones aux malades et violemment agressé un médecin de garde.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-003.s: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on a night of insecurity in Bukavu and Nyantende, that those events came only a few days after a cordon operation carried out by the M23 rebels in the Nyamugo neighbourhood of Kadutu commune, which it said led to the seizure of four AK-47 weapons and the arrest of about thirty young people suspected of criminal activity.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-003.a: M23 rebels (as Radio Okapi calls them)
r1-SKN-2025Q3-003.x: Radio Okapi: four AK-47 seized; about thirty young men arrested
r1-SKN-2025Q3-003.n: Exact date not given ('quelques jours' before 16 July). Fate of the detainees not reported. Operation described only in passing.

src: Ces événements surviennent quelques jours seulement après une opération de bouclage menée dans le quartier Nyamugo, toujours dans la commune de Kadutu par les rebelles du M23. Cette opération avait permis la saisie de quatre armes de type AK-47 et l’interpellation d’une trentaine de jeunes soupçonnés d’activités criminelles.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting broke out on Wednesday 30 July in Kamakombe village (Kabare territory) between M23-AFC rebels, described as allied to the RDF, and a Wazalendo group; it said the clashes had begun on the Tuesday in Mbayo village (Bugorhe groupement) following a reinforcement of M23 troops coming from Kavumu airport, and, according to several local sources, these troops launched an offensive against the Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC), a Wazalendo branch present in the area.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-004.l: Kamakombe and Mbayo, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-004.a: M23-AFC with RDF (per source); Wazalendo MDLC/RRADRDC
r1-SKN-2025Q3-004.n: Single local-source report. The Tuesday is 29 July (date computed from weekday and publication date). Places M23 troops at Kavumu airport (sources' wording) but does not state who controlled the airport.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-004.vn: Narrowed the 'several local sources' attribution to the clause the source attaches it to (the offensive), not the start of fighting at Mbayo. The Tuesday (29 July) is computed from the weekday and the 30 July date. The source does not say who controlled Kavumu airport.
ent: Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC)
src: Des combats violents ont éclaté ce mercredi 30 juillet dans le village de Kamakombe, territoire de Kabare (Sud-Kivu), opposant les rebelles du M23-AFC alliés au RDF à un groupe Wazalendo actif dans la région.
Ces affrontements ont débuté dès mardi dans le village de Mbayo, situé dans le groupement de Bugorhe, à la suite d’un renforcement des troupes du M23 en provenance de l’aéroport de Kavumu.
Selon plusieurs sources locales, ces troupes ont lancé une offensive contre le Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC/RRADRDC), une branche Wazalendo présente dans la zone.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-005.s: Radio Okapi reported, under a headline on fighting between M23 and Wazalendo resuming despite the accord, that at dawn M23-AFC-RDF insurgents launched an offensive in Bugorhe groupement against positions of the Wazalendo of the Mouvement décisif de la Libération du Congo (MDLC) at Kamakombe village (Kabare territory); after a brief M23 occupation of half the village, the Wazalendo pushed the attackers back towards the heights of Kavumu; the same day another attack attributed to the M23 targeted the Muzinzi subgroupement in neighbouring Walungu territory.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-005.l: Kamakombe, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-005.n: Single local-source report. The article's Walungu attack is outside this unit's geography and recorded only as context.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-005.vn: Removed the unprinted date and the Doha clause from the statement (date stays in the date field, carried by the page passage); Muzinzi attack worded as the source does ('attribuée au M23'). Walungu (Muzinzi) attack is context outside the unit's main area; the source attributes it to the M23 ('attribuée au M23'). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, Sat 2 Aug 2025, carries every clause, including Kamakombe in the lead. The Muzinzi attack was on no stored excerpt; that passage is added. Statement unchanged.
ent: Mouvement décisif de la Libération du Congo (MDLC)
src: À l’aube, des tirs ont éclaté dans le groupement de Bugorhe, lorsque les insurgés du M23-AFC-RDF ont lancé une offensive contre les positions des Wazalendos du Mouvement décisif de la Libération du Congo (MDLC).
Après une brève occupation de la moitié du village par le M23, les Wazalendos ont réussi à repousser les assaillants vers les hauteurs de Kavumu dans le même secteur.
Par ailleurs, dans le territoire voisin de Walungu, une autre attaque attribuée au M23 a visé le sous-groupement de Muzinzi ce même jour.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that four civilians were killed on Thursday 7 August in fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and Wazalendo of the MDLC group at Kasheke village, on the border of Kabare and Kalehe territories; according to local sources, the M23 attacked MDLC positions at Kamakombe and opened a second front against the MDLC headquarters at Kasheke, headed by the self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani, and the toll was described as provisional.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.l: Kasheke (and Kamakombe), border of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.a: AFC-M23; Wazalendo MDLC (self-proclaimed general Imani Shabani)
r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.x: Radio Okapi: four civilians killed (provisional), several wounded
r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.n: Single local-source report. Victims not named. Article text says clashes continued around 14:00 at 'Chez Mbayo', 3 km from the centre of 'Kavumo' (as printed).
r1-SKN-2025Q3-006.vn: Kamakombe clause was only on the page; added an extended source-1 passage. The source does not say which side killed the civilians. Imani Shabani is named by the source as the MDLC's self-proclaimed general.
src: Quatre civils ont été tués ce jeudi 7 août lors d’affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les Wazalendo du groupe MDLC dans le village de Kasheke, à la frontière des territoires de Kabare et Kalehe, dans la province du Sud-Kivu.

Pour accentuer la pression, les rebelles ont ouvert un second front contre le quartier général du MDLC à Kasheke, dirigé par le général autoproclamé Imani Shabani. Le bilan provisoire fait état de quatre civils tués et de plusieurs blessés.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-007.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing several local sources, that violent clashes between Wazalendo and M23 since the afternoon of jeudi 10 juillet in the villages of Kasheke and Buzunga (Kalehe territory) caused a mass displacement of civilians; Radio Maendeleo likewise reported that fighting on 10 July caused a mass displacement of the population in the villages of Kasheke, Buzunga and Lemera in Mbinga Sud groupement, Kalehe territory.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-007.l: Kasheke, Buzunga, Lemera (Mbinga Sud groupement), Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-007.x: not given in the excerpts (both outlets report a mass displacement); the Radio Okapi page says hundreds of families fled to the Ihoka islet and Kadjucu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-007.n: Two local outlets (Radio Okapi, Bukavu; Radio Maendeleo, Bukavu community radio) both cite local sources; independence not established. Radio Okapi's 11 July article also says the M23 was trying to retake RN2.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-007.vn: Destinations and the 'hundreds of families' / 'thousands' figures were not in the stored excerpts: removed from the statement; the Radio Okapi figure is noted with its page passage in replacement_quotes. Two Bukavu outlets, each citing local sources; whether their local sources overlap is not known. Radio Maendeleo puts the displaced 'par milliers' (civil-society sources), not recorded in the figures.
src: Depuis l’après-midi du jeudi 10 juillet, de violents affrontements opposent les miliciens Wazalendo aux rebelles du M23 dans les villages de Kasheke et Buzunga, situés dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu. Ces combats ont provoqué un déplacement massif de la population civile, selon plusieurs sources locales.

Les combats qui a opposé jeudi 10 juillet dernier, les éléments du M23 aux combattants WAZALENDO ont causé un déplacement massif des populations dans les villages de Kasheke, Buzunga et Lemera dans groupement Mbinga Sud, chefferie de Bukavu en territoire de Kalehe et ses environs.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, in an article on fighting at Kasheke and Buzunga, that witnesses spoke of generalised panic, looted goods, houses visited and even cases of abduction, notably at Buhama.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-008.n: Witness-based, no numbers, no victims or perpetrator named. Lead only.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-008.vn: Removed '10-11 July' (not in the excerpt); the article title carries Kasheke and Buzunga. The page ties Buhama to new departures on the Friday morning (passage in replacement_quotes). Witness-based; no numbers, victims or perpetrators. The Friday is the article's 'ce vendredi' (article of 11 July). Radio Maendeleo separately reports that 'des éléments incontrôlés' looted and took people to unknown destinations (not cited here).
src: Des témoins évoquent une panique généralisée, des biens pillés, des maisons visitées et même des cas d’enlèvement, notamment à Buhama.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a communiqué of the FARDC Third Defence Zone, signed by Major Nestor Mavudisa Kamba Mayoyo, spokesperson of 'cette zone militaire', said that 'ces ennemis de la paix' attacked FARDC positions at Kamatembe and Kalao (Mubuku groupement, Kalehe territory) on the morning of 12 July 2025, and that, according to the FARDC, another position was attacked at Batanga, Irambi Katana groupement, Kabare territory.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-009.n: Party statement relayed by a Goma-based outlet; evidence of what the FARDC said, not of the attacks. The M23 side's account for these dates was not found in this unit (the article itself mentions an earlier Kanyuka accusation against the army, not opened for this unit). The communiqué's date of 15 July is as reported; the Batanga attack date follows the article's 'same day' reading (14 July).
r1-SKN-2025Q3-009.vn: Removed the communiqué date (15 July, page only; kept in the date field), the 'AFC-M23' and Rwandan-army clauses (headline and page only; the excerpt says only 'ces ennemis de la paix'); the accused party stays in extra.perpetrator_alleged. Graded C as a single partisan statement relayed by one local outlet. Partisan official statement (FARDC): evidence of what the FARDC said, not of the attacks. The article's headline says the FARDC accuse the AFC-M23; the article also says the army accuses the Rwandan army of supporting them (not in the excerpts). The communiqué was published on 15 July per the article. The Batanga date ('en cette même date') is ambiguous (12 or 14 July).
src: Ces ennemis de la paix ont successivement lancé des attaques contre les positions des FARDC dans les localités de KAMATEMBE et KALAO dans le groupement de MUBUKU, en territoire de KALEHE l’avant-midi du 12 juillet 2025 » , indique le communiqué signé par le Major Nestor Mavudisa Kamba Mayoyo, porte-parole de cette zone militaire.

Le même jour, une autre attaque a été signalée dans le territoire de Kabare. Selon les FARDC, « elle attaquera en cette même date une autre position à la localité de BATANGA, dans le groupement d’IRAMBI KATANA, en territoire de KABARE »

r1-SKN-2025Q3-010.s: 7sur7.cd reported that fighting between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 broke out again on Wednesday 16 July 2025 on the hills above Kabulungu village (Bughore, Kabare territory), according to local civil society, and quoted a resident saying 'Des civils ont même été tués'; socio-economic activity had been paralysed there since the previous Monday.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-010.l: Kabulungu, Bughore, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-010.n: Anonymous resident quote; no toll. Walungu part of the article is outside this unit.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-010.vn: Date and 'paralysed since Monday' clauses were only on the page; extended passages added. '23' flag is 'M23'. Killing of civilians rests on one anonymous resident's quote; no toll, place or perpetrator for the deaths.
src: Dans le territoire de Kabare, la société civile locale renseigne que les combats ont eu lieu dans l'avant-midi sur les collines surplombant le village de Kabulungu à Bughore.
« Nous souffrons beaucoup suite aux affrontements de chaque jour dans notre entité. Des civils ont même été tués », a déclaré à 7SUR7.CD, un habitant de la place, ce mercredi.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-011.s: MSF said that an assessment it carried out in March, following violent clashes in the area in early 2025, found that of 24 health facilities evaluated in the Katana and Kalehe health zones, 15 had had to close, 10 had been damaged and 16 had been looted; Radio Okapi, reporting the same assessment, gave about 15 closed, 10 damaged and 'une quinzaine' looted.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-011.l: Katana (Kabare territory) and Kalehe health zones, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-011.x: MSF: 24 facilities assessed, 15 closed, 10 damaged, 16 looted; Radio Okapi: about 15 closed, 10 damaged, about fifteen ('une quinzaine') looted
r1-SKN-2025Q3-011.n: Damage dates to early 2025 (Jan-Feb fighting per MSF) and the assessment to March; the report date is 2025-08-12. Counts differ slightly between MSF (16 looted) and Radio Okapi (about fifteen); MSF is the primary. Perpetrators are not named. Katana health zone lies in Kabare territory.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-011.vn: Removed the unprinted '12 August 2025' from the statement; date changed from the report date to what the excerpt says (early 2025 to March); Radio Okapi credited as a relay of MSF. Dates: the damage followed clashes 'début 2025' and was found by an assessment in March 2025 (date range Jan-Mar 2025 per the excerpt; the MSF page's English summary puts the heavy fighting in January and February). The MSF release of 12 Aug 2025 is the source date, not the event date. Radio Okapi relays MSF and is not independent; its looted count ('une quinzaine') differs slightly from MSF's 16. Perpetrators not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Une évaluation menée par MSF en mars, suite aux affrontements violents dans la zone début 2025, a révélé une situation de crise majeure: sur 24 structures de santé évaluées dans les zones de Santé de Katana et Kalehe, 15 ont dû fermer, 10 ont été endommagées et 16 ont été pillées.
Parmi les structures sanitaires évaluées par Médecins sans frontières, environ 15 ont été contraintes de fermer leurs portes, 10 ont été endommagées et une quinzaine pillée.

A March assessment by MSF revealed the scale of the crisis following violent clashes in the region at the start of the year: of 24 health facilities in Katana and Kalehe, fifteen had to close, ten were damaged and sixteen looted.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-012.s: MSF said that, besides the damage to health facilities, patients faced barriers to care such as economic difficulties and insecurity, and that insecurity and the closure of the Bukavu and Goma airports continued to limit humanitarian access.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-012.l: Katana and Kalehe health zones, and Bukavu airport, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-012.n: General statement by an NGO on a health system, not a discrete incident. Lead for the airport closure's effect on access.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-012.vn: Removed the unprinted '12 August 2025' from the statement. General NGO statement on conditions, not a discrete incident; dated by the MSF release (12 Aug 2025).
src: En plus des dommages subis par les structures de santé, mettant en péril leur opérationnalité, les patients font face eux aussi à des barrières d'accès aux soins telles que les difficultés économiques et l’insécurité.
Malgré ces avancées, l’insécurité et la fermeture des aéroports de Bukavu et Goma continuent de limiter l’accès humanitaire.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that pastor Kelly Bahati Kazibaziba was shot dead on Monday 11 August by armed men on Michombero avenue in Kadutu commune (Bukavu); according to several local sources it was a premeditated murder, with suspicion of a link to the stance of his brother Joseph Kazibaziba, a businessman and president of the South Kivu Chamber of Mines, known for denouncing abuses attributed to the M23 rebellion.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-013.n: Single local-source report; motive is local speculation. No party claimed or denied the killing in the source. Related lead on civilian insecurity in M23-held Bukavu.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-013.vn: Last clause was only on the page; extended source-0 passage added. '23' flag is 'M23'. Motive is local suspicion as reported ('il s’agirait'); perpetrators unidentified.
src: Le pasteur Kelly Bahati Kazibaziba a été abattu lundi 11 août par des hommes armés sur l’avenue Michombero, dans la commune de Kadutu. Selon plusieurs sources locales, il s’agirait d’un meurtre prémédité. Des soupçons pèsent sur un lien avec les prises de position de son frère, Joseph Kazibaziba, homme d’affaires influent et président de la Chambre des mines du Sud-Kivu.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that gunfire spread panic in the Panzi neighbourhood (Ibanda commune, Bukavu); according to the neighbourhood chief, armed individuals appear at nightfall and fire in the air, and on jeudi at around 19 h a fruit seller was fatally hit by a stray bullet as she was walking home; the outlet said rumours placed members of the Wazalendo group in the area but that no proof had been provided.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-014.n: Date computed from weekday ('jeudi') and publication date 15 August. The same night's bullet through the Panzi General Hospital water tank is already recorded (r1-HC-SK-2025-003, citing Radio Okapi / La Prunelle); this claim adds the fatality and the context.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-014.vn: Removed '19:00' format and the unprinted '15 August'; place and date carried by the page passage in replacement_quotes. Victim not named. Thursday = 14 August, computed from the article of 15 August. Shooters not identified; the Wazalendo presence is a rumour the source says is unproven.
src: Selon le chef de quartier, des individus armés surgissent à la tombée de la nuit, tirent en l’air et provoquent des dégâts matériels. Jeudi vers 19 h, une vendeuse de fruits a été mortellement touchée par une balle perdue alors qu’elle rentrait chez elle.
Des rumeurs évoquent la présence de membres du groupe Wazalendo dans cette zone depuis le début de la semaine, mais aucune preuve n’a été apportée à ce jour.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-015.s: CongoRassure, in an article summarising OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that OCHA-RDC said a relative calm was observed across Bukavu during August, but that local sources reported several cases of burglaries, killings and arbitrary arrests attributed to armed men.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-015.n: Secondary relay of an OCHA situation report (the OCHA document itself was not opened). Not an incident-level source.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-015.vn: Excerpt exact; OCHA report attribution carried by an extended passage. Graded C because the OCHA document was not seen and the relay is a small outlet. Second-hand relay of an OCHA situation report that was not itself opened; OCHA in turn cites local sources. Retrieve the OCHA document to confirm and upgrade.
src: OCHA-RDC a déclaré q'un calme relatif a été observé sur l’ensemble de la ville de Bukavu au cours du mois d’août. Néanmoins, des sources locales ont rapporté plusieurs cas de cambriolages, de meurtres et d’arrestations arbitraires attribués aux hommes en armes.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-016.s: CongoRassure, in an article on OCHA-RDC's latest report, reported that persistent clashes that broke out on 17 July in Kabare territory continued throughout August, and that on 13 August at least four civilians were killed by armed men at M'bayo, a locality where about 43 000 people were displaced following armed violence between 17 and 26 July.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-016.x: CongoRassure (relaying OCHA-RDC): at least four civilians killed on 13 August; about 43 000 people displaced (violence of 17-26 July)
r1-SKN-2025Q3-016.n: The attribution to OCHA-RDC comes from the article's opening ('Dans son dernier rapport ... OCHA-RDC'), not from this excerpt. Likely the same place as Mbayo (Bugorhe) in Radio Okapi's 30 July report. Not checked against OCHA's own document.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-016.vn: The 17 July/August clause and the OCHA attribution were not in the stored excerpt; extended passage added. Numbers kept in the source's form. Graded C as an unseen OCHA document relayed by a small outlet. Relay of an OCHA report not itself opened. The source does not say whether the 43 000 were displaced from or into M'bayo. M'bayo is probably the Mbayo (Bugorhe) of Radio Okapi's 30 July report, not confirmed.
src: Dans cette circonstance, le 13 août, au moins quatre civils ont été tués par des hommes armés à M'bayo, une localité où environ 43 000 personnes ont été déplacées à la suite des violences armées survenues entre le 17 et le 26 juillet.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that school activities had been paralysed since Tuesday 9 September in several schools of Kabare territory and at Kamisimbi (Walungu); according to local sources, armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo burst into schools to send pupils home, arrested teachers and forced them to join the armed struggle against the M23 rebels, which the Nouvelle Dynamique de la société civile condemned.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-017.l: Schools in Kabare territory (and Kamisimbi, Walungu), South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-017.a: armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo
r1-SKN-2025Q3-017.n: Single local-source report; no numbers or names of teachers. Armed men 'se présentant comme' Wazalendo, so identity is unverified. Tuesday 9 September 2025 matches the calendar.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-017.vn: All clauses in the excerpts; 9 September 2025 was a Tuesday, matching the source. Identity of the armed men is as they presented themselves ('se présentant comme'); teachers not named or counted.
ent: Nouvelle Dynamique de la société civile
src: Les activités scolaires sont paralysées depuis mardi 9 septembre dans plusieurs écoles du territoire de Kabare et à Kamisimbi, dans le territoire de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu. Un groupe d’hommes armés, se présentant comme des combattants Wazalendo, font irruption dans les écoles pour en renvoyer les élèves.

Selon des sources locales, ces hommes armés arrêtent les enseignants et les contraignent à rejoindre la lutte armée contre les rebelles du M23. Ces agissements sont fermement condamnés par la Nouvelle Dynamique de la société civile.

r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that M23 officials suspended all mining activities at the Lomera site in Luhihi (Kabare territory) from 'lundi 9 septembre' (as printed), for security reasons according to them, and demanded prior identification of all operators; it said thousands of people were affected by the measure of the M23, which it said occupies the region, and that the reopening date was unknown.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.l: Lomera mining site, Luhihi, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.a: M23 officials (as Radio Okapi calls them)
r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.x: Radio Okapi: 'des milliers' of people affected
r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.n: Weekday/date mismatch in source: 9 September 2025 was a Tuesday; the source's 'lundi 9 septembre' is kept as printed (possible error for Monday 8 or Tuesday 9). Single local-source report. Same article says about ten diggers died buried in July (not recorded).
r1-SKN-2025Q3-018.vn: Identification, 'thousands' and reopening clauses were only on the page; extended passage added. 'Thousands of artisanal miners' narrowed to 'thousands of people' as printed. Weekday mismatch kept stated; precision set to approximate. Date discrepancy in the source: it prints 'lundi 9 septembre', but 9 September 2025 was a Tuesday; the suspension began on Monday 8 or Tuesday 9 September. The source says 'des milliers es personnes' (people), not specifically miners. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 10 Sept 2025, carries every clause (it prints 'Des milliers es personnes' and 'lundi 9 septembre'); the stored excerpt lacks the thousands-affected, identification and reopening clauses, added here.
src: Les responsables du M23 ont suspendu, depuis lundi 9 septembre, toutes les activités minières sur le site de Lomera, à Luhihi, dans le territoire de Kabare au Sud-Kivu. Cette décision a été prise pour des raisons sécuritaires, selon eux.

Des milliers es personnes sont touchées par cette mesure du M23 , qui occupe la région. Lomera, réputé pour sa production d’or et de cassitérite, est désormais à l’arrêt. Les dirigeants rebelles exigent l’identification préalable de tous les exploitants, estimant que le site était devenu un foyer d’insécurité. La date de réouverture reste inconnue

r1-SKN-2025Q3-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that continuing clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the highlands of Kalehe territory were preventing parents from preparing their children's 2025-2026 school year and, according to several local sources, were causing massive displacement of the population.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-019.l: Highlands (hauts plateaux) of Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2025Q3-019.n: Qualitative, no figures or specific villages. Shows fighting in Kalehe highlands continuing in late August.
r1-SKN-2025Q3-019.vn: Removed the unprinted '25 August' from the statement. Ongoing situation as of the article of 25 August 2025; no villages or figures.
src: La poursuite des affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 et les combattants Wazalendo dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Kalehe (Sud-Kivu) empêche les parents de préparer la rentrée scolaire 2025-2026 de leurs enfants. Selon plusieurs sources locales, ces combats incessants provoquent des déplacements massifs de la population dans cette région du pays.

r1-SKN-2025Q4-001.s: OCHA reported that on 4 October violent fighting in the localities of Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping (Kabare territory), caused the mass displacement of families to safer areas, that figures for the recently displaced were being verified, and that several victims, including dead and wounded among civilians, were reported.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-001.l: Chulwe and Cishadu, Luhago grouping, Kabare territory
r1-SKN-2025Q4-001.n: Parties to the fighting not named by OCHA. Report dated 17 Nov 2025, published 18 Nov.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-001.vn: Excerpt exact; widened to the contiguous passage that carries 'Kabare'. Year and 'DRC' dropped from statement (not printed in excerpt); the date field carries 2025. OCHA does not name the parties to the fighting or give casualty numbers.
src: Le 4 octobre, de violents combats dans les localités de Chulwe et Cishadu, situées dans le groupement de Luhago, ont entraîné le déplacement massif de familles vers des zones plus sûres. Les chiffres des personnes déplacées récemment sont en cours de vérification. Plusieurs victimes, dont des morts et des blessés parmi les civils, ont été signalées.

r1-SKN-2025Q4-002.s: OCHA DRC reported that on 12 October 2025 about 450 households, close to 2,700 people, fled new fighting between armed groups in the localities of Civanga and Kasirusiru (Kabare territory) and took refuge at Miti and Murhesa, and that humanitarian access remained strongly limited by persistent insecurity.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-002.l: Civanga and Kasirusiru, Kabare territory; refuge at Miti and Murhesa
r1-SKN-2025Q4-002.a: armed groups, not named by the source
r1-SKN-2025Q4-002.x: OCHA: about 450 households, close to 2,700 people
r1-SKN-2025Q4-002.vn: Excerpt exact and matches. '2700' flag is the French thousands separator ('2 700'). 'Kabare' is the section heading on the page directly above this passage.
src: Le 12 octobre, environ 450 ménages – soit près de 2 700 personnes – ont fui de nouveaux affrontements entre groupes armés dans les localités de Civanga et Kasirusiru. Ces familles se sont réfugiées à Miti et Murhesa, dans la Zone de Santé (ZS) de Miti-Murhesa. L’accès humanitaire demeure fortement limité en raison de l’insécurité persistante, ce qui entrave la capacité des acteurs humanitaires à fournir une assistance vitale.

r1-SKN-2025Q4-003.s: OCHA reported that between 12 and 15 October about 27,700 people fled fighting between armed groups in the mountains overlooking Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya and other localities of Kalehe territory, and that the living conditions of the displaced and of host communities were critical, including a rupture of medical inputs and an increased risk of sexual violence.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-003.l: Mountains above Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya, Bwangala, Kilijiwe, Kasasa, Kaitoleya, Bushushu 1 and 2, Kalehe territory; refuge in Kalehe centre, Kasheke, Tchoki, Luzira and others
r1-SKN-2025Q4-003.a: armed groups, not named by the source
r1-SKN-2025Q4-003.n: Caritas Bukavu (below) gives different displacement counts for the 7-12 October fighting: figures are kept separate.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-003.vn: Both excerpts exact; widened to contiguous passages carrying 'Kalehe' and the subject of the second sentence. '27700' flag is the thousands separator. Count is OCHA's. Caritas Bukavu's own figures for the Kalehe fighting differ (see the Caritas claims) and are kept separate; the sources do not reconcile them.
src: Entre le 12 et le 15 octobre, environ 27 700 personnes ont fui les affrontements entre groupes armés dans les montagnes surplombant les localités de Katasomwa, Mbesho, Kashihe, Katoki, Mweya, Bwangala, Kilijiwe, Kasasa, Kaitoleya, Bushushu 1 et 2.
caractérisées par un manque d’abris, de nourriture et d’accès à l’eau potable, une rupture des intrants médicaux et un risque accru de violences sexuelles.

r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.s: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu report on the humanitarian crisis in Kalehe, reported that the fighting of 12 October displaced more than 7,700 people to the areas of Kasheke, Luzira, Bushaku and Kabamba.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.l: Kasheke and Luzira health areas, Kalehe health zone
r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.a: not attributed in the stored excerpt; the page describes clashes between M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups
r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.x: Caritas: more than 7,700 displaced by 12 Oct fighting; table: Kasheke 2,043 households / 10,215 people, Luzira 1,275 / 5,610
r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.n: Caritas is a church humanitarian body; the table gives household and people counts per health area. The 7,700 figure and the table figures (10,215 + 5,610) are not reconciled by the source.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-004.vn: Excerpt exact. Narrowed to what the stored excerpt and title print: the assessment dates, the table figures and the M23/Wazalendo description are on the page but not in the excerpt, so they are in the note pending an excerpt extension. Figures are Caritas's and kept separate from OCHA's. Lead for an excerpt extension (source_edits.py add_excerpt), all on the same page: the assessment ran 'Du 20 au 27 octobre 2025' in the Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone; the crisis is described as 'exacerbée par les affrontements entre les rebelles du M23 et les groupes d’autodéfense Wazalendo'; a table gives 'Kasheke 2 043 10 215 Luzira 1 275 5 610' (displaced households / people), which the source does not reconcile with the 7,700 figure. OCHA, as quoted by Actualite.cd (24 Nov 2025), describes the same Caritas Bukavu assessment as running 20 to 26 October and counting close to 19,900 displaced from fighting of 7 to 12 October: dates and counts differ between the two.
src: Les combats du 12 octobre dernier ont provoqué le déplacement de plus de 7 700 personnes vers les zones de Kasheke, Luzira, Bushaku et Kabamba.

r1-SKN-2025Q4-005.s: Caritasdev.cd, summarising a Caritas Bukavu assessment report on Kalehe, listed under protection and abuse 7 cases of sexual violence documented in October, and reported child enlistment, extortion and cruel treatment.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-005.l: Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone
r1-SKN-2025Q4-005.x: Caritas: 7 cases of sexual violence documented in October
r1-SKN-2025Q4-005.n: No perpetrator, victim details or dates given. Counts documented cases, not prevalence.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-005.vn: Excerpt exact. Statement narrowed to what the excerpt and title print (assessment dates and health-area names were not in this claim's excerpt; they are carried in the related displacement claim). Documented cases from one assessment, not prevalence; no perpetrators, victims, places or dates within October are given. The assessment covered the Luzira and Kasheke health areas, Kalehe health zone, 20-27 October 2025 (see the Caritas displacement claim). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Protection et abus Violences sexuelles : 7 cas documentés en octobre ; Enrôlement d’enfants, extorsions, traitements cruels rapportés
SOURCES D'INFORMATION Principale CARITAS Secondaire OCHA, Comité humanitaire de base de Kalehe

r1-SKN-2025Q4-006.s: Actualite.cd, quoting an OCHA DRC report, reported that between 6 and 12 November two international organisations had to temporarily suspend their movements for monitoring nutrition and health activities in the Chabombo health area because of intensified fighting in Katasomwa, Lumbishi and Chambombo, and that, in addition, four humanitarian workers were arrested by armed actors in the Minova health zone.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-006.l: Minova health zone and Chabombo health area, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2025Q4-006.a: armed actors, not named by the source
r1-SKN-2025Q4-006.n: Relayed from OCHA DRC (report published 18 Nov). Date of the arrests is not stated; the range is the period of the preceding sentence. Place within Minova health zone not given. Detention/health_care_access: access_denied.
r1-SKN-2025Q4-006.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed 'made public on 18 November 2025' (printed on the page, not in the excerpt). Relay of OCHA; the OCHA sitrep retained for this unit does not show this passage in its retained text. The date of the arrests is not stated; the 6-12 November range belongs to the suspension sentence. The armed actors are not named.
src: Entre le 6 et le 12 novembre, deux organisations internationales ont dû suspendre temporairement leurs mouvements pour le suivi des activités de nutrition et santé dans l’aire de santé de Chabombo, en raison de l’intensification des affrontements dans les localités de Katasomwa, Lumbishi et Chambombo.
