The page dates the incursion to midday on Tuesday 24 March 2026 and the man's death to about 16h the same day (not in the stored excerpt). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des sources locales rapportent que c’est aux environs de 12h que cet incident s’est produit dans cette partie du Sud-Kivu sous contrôle de l’AFC-M23. Ces assaillants se sont introduits au domicile d’un homme de la place connu sous le nom de Huit MUCIGA avant de tirer sur le concerné et son épouse au même moment.

r1-SKN-2026Q1-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least seven civilians were killed and fifteen wounded during an incursion by Wazalendo, militiamen allied to the Congolese army, at Shanje, Kalehe territory, on the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026; citing local sources and an anonymous resident, it said the militiamen fired on civilians in the market around 18h30 and looted the population's property.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-009.x: Kivu Morning Post (outlet and anonymous resident): at least 7 civilians killed, 15 wounded
r1-SKN-2026Q1-009.n: Contested attribution/figures: see AFC/M23 claim and 7sur7.cd claim. Shanje is in the area the AFC/M23 was reportedly evacuating around 27-28 March (Minova withdrawal).
r1-SKN-2026Q1-009.vn: Statement supported. Figures field corrected to this source's figures only (the other accounts are separate claims 9 and 10). One of three accounts of the Shanje attack, which differ on perpetrator and toll: Kivu Morning Post (Wazalendo; 7 killed, 15 wounded), 7sur7.cd (armed men of unknown identity; at least 9 killed, 20 wounded) and AFC/M23 (the 'Kinshasa coalition'; 7 executed, more than twenty wounded). Not reconciled. A related KMP headline on the same page reads 'Sud-Kivu : le marché de Shanje incendié par des Wazalendo' (not opened; lead). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon des sources locales, les miliciens ont attaqué la cité et tiré sur des civils présents au marché. « Vers 18h30, les Wazalendo ont fait une incursion ici à Shanje quand les habitants étaient encore dans le marché. Ils ont tiré sur des civils et pillé des biens des populations. Pour l’instant, il y a 7 civils tués et 15 blessés »

r1-SKN-2026Q1-010.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on 29 March 2026 at 18h30 'la coalition de Kinshasa' infiltrated the densely populated centre of Shanje, Kalehe territory, where it 'executed 7 innocent civilians', whom he named; the outlet reported that he also said more than twenty people were wounded, and he alleged that the Kinshasa regime continues to ally itself with FDLR elements and deploy them on various fronts.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-010.x: AFC/M23 (Kanyuka): 7 civilians executed, more than twenty wounded
r1-SKN-2026Q1-010.n: Party account only. The page prints seven names run together without separators (starting 'Shadai Ndagije Bisengi Mpenze Étienne Gitinywa Gashimye Hitimana Daniel Hategeka Ndayambaje Muhire Iradukunda Nzanzumuhire'); name boundaries cannot be determined, so none listed in victims_named. No Kinshasa/FARDC/Wazalendo account found.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-010.vn: Statement narrowed to Kanyuka's words; 'more than twenty' is the outlet's paraphrase of him and is written as a word, as printed. Under policy v1 the names are listed exactly as printed, split on the only even reading, with the uncertainty stated. Party statement (AFC/M23). The page prints the seven names as one run of fourteen words with no separators: 'Shadai Ndagije Bisengi Mpenze Étienne Gitinywa Gashimye Hitimana Daniel Hategeka Ndayambaje Muhire Iradukunda Nzanzumuhire'. The split into seven two-word names is an editorial reading of that run (fourteen words, seven victims), not printed by the source; other splits are possible (e.g. 'Mpenze Étienne', 'Hitimana Daniel'). Verify each identity before relying on it. No Kinshasa, FARDC or Wazalendo account found. The other accounts (claims 8 and 10) give different perpetrators and tolls. 'AFC spokesperson' = spokesperson of the AFC/M23, as the page prints it; the stored excerpt begins after that attribution. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « Le 29 mars 2026 à 18h30, la coalition de Kinshasa a infiltré le centre densément peuplé de Shanje, dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, où elle a exécuté 7 civils innocents

r1-SKN-2026Q1-011.s: The outlet reported that at least 9 people were killed and 20 wounded in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 March 2026 at Shanje village, Kalehe territory, during an incursion of armed men; it cited a local church official, speaking anonymously on Radio Maendeleo, who said the bandits arrived and fired, and said wounded were taken to a medical facility and that the real identity of the armed men was not yet known.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-011.n: Figures differ from Kivu Morning Post (7/15) and AFC/M23 (7/20+). Radio Maendeleo is the underlying source cited on the page.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-011.vn: The draft tied the toll to the church official; on the page the toll is the outlet's own and the official gives the time and a description. Split the attribution accordingly. Signed Alphonse Muderwa. One of three accounts of the Shanje attack (see claims 8 and 9): figures and perpetrator differ and are not reconciled. The toll is given in the outlet's voice, not attributed to the church official; the witness quote comes from Radio Maendeleo. Times differ between accounts (about 19h here, 18h30 in KMP and AFC/M23). The church official dates the incursion to about 19h (not in the stored excerpt). The statement does not name the publisher (7sur7.cd) only because the check reads its digits as figures; the source is shown with its publisher. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Au moins 9 personnes ont été tuées et 20 autres blessées dans la nuit de dimanche à lundi 30 mars 2026 au village Shanje dans le territoire de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu lors d'une incursion d'hommes armés avec une violence indescriptible.

r1-SKN-2026Q1-012.s: BETO reported that AFC fighters left the localities of Pitakongo and Bunyatenge on Saturday 28 March 2026, after having already withdrawn on Thursday and Friday from at least twelve localities of Lubero territory and from the strategic town of Minova; it said the disengagement did not seem to result from a military rout but rather from a planned manoeuvre, citing information relayed by other media and local sources that the move would fit within the ongoing peace processes, and it reported that the rebel mayor of a city under AFC administration described the moves as tactical repositionings.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-012.n: Mediacongo (2026-03-31, 'Le M23 au pied du mur') also says Minova was evacuated on Saturday 28 March, but its excerpt failed the mechanical check so it is not cited. CONFLICT: Actualite.cd reports AFC/M23 arrested a Minova radio director at Minova on 29 March. Weekday dates (Thursday and Friday before Saturday 28 March = 26-27 March) computed from weekday and publication date. Page attributes details to TV5Monde and local sources. No AFC/M23 or FARDC statement on Minova captured: search results showed a social-media post saying AFC/M23 announced withdrawal from Minova, not fetched.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-012.vn: The draft turned BETO's hedge ('ne semble pas') into a firm description; restored the hedge and the conditional on the peace-process link, and added the Goma mayor's characterisation from the page. Dates for Minova are approximate: 'Thursday and Friday' before Saturday 28 March, i.e. about 26-27 March, computed from the weekdays. CONFLICT: Actualite.cd (claim 12) reports AFC/M23 elements arrested a radio director at Minova on Sunday 29 March, which suggests AFC/M23 presence there after the reported withdrawal; both accounts are kept. The BETO byline reads 'AFP Rédaction Kinshasa' while the piece is signed Azarias Mokonzi and is partly commentary; whether it relays AFP copy is unclear. 'AFC fighters' = the AFC/M23 named in the headline (the excerpt says 'ils'). The page names TV5Monde as one of the relaying media. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Ce samedi 28 mars 2026, ils ont quitté les localités de Pitakongo et Bunyatenge, après s’être déjà retirés, jeudi et vendredi, d’au moins douze localités du territoire de Lubero, ainsi que de la cité stratégique de Minova, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-SKN-2026Q1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that Espoir Mbata, director of the community radio Top Buzi FM, was arrested on Sunday 29 March at Minova, Kalehe territory; according to local sources and colleagues at the station he was reportedly detained by AFC/M23 elements, and a journalist close to the radio, speaking anonymously, said the arrest was reportedly linked to an on-air comment by Espoir Mbata about a possible withdrawal of AFC/M23 elements from Minova. The outlet said some journalists had left Minova that morning fearing arrest.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-013.n: Page says some journalists left Minova that morning fearing arrest. This indicates AFC/M23 presence at Minova on 29 March, in tension with reports that Minova was evacuated on 26-28 March. No AFC/M23 comment found; release not found.
r1-SKN-2026Q1-013.vn: Kept the source's conditionals ('reportedly') for both the perpetrators and the motive; the draft stated the motive link without the conditional. Perpetrator attribution is conditional in the source ('aurait été interpellé'), as is the motive ('serait liée'). CONFLICT with claim 11: BETO reports AFC/M23 withdrew from Minova on about 26-27 March; this arrest on 29 March implies AFC/M23 elements were still there. Both kept. Release not found. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le directeur de la radio communautaire Top Buzi FM, Espoir Mbata, a été arrêté ce dimanche 29 mars à Minova, dans le territoire de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu. Selon des sources locales et des collaborateurs de la station, il aurait été interpellé par des éléments de l'AFC/M23.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that around 16:00 on Monday 6 April 2026 several places in the Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory (Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege and Lulamba) had already passed under AFC/M23 control after fighting with wazalendo.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-001.n: Single local-outlet account citing unnamed sources; no AFC/M23 or FARDC account found for this day.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-001.vn: Excerpt and page support each clause; date 'ce lundi 6 avril' and Ziralo/Kalehe printed in the article lede (page, not excerpt). Year from article date 07/04/2026. Single outlet (Actualite.cd, unnamed sources); no AFC/M23 or FARDC account for the day.
src: Vers 16 heures, plusieurs entités, dont Kaziba, Katale, Kafufula, Katanga, Mpanama, Braza, Bushege et Lulamba, étaient déjà passées sous le contrôle de l’AFC/M23.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that on 6 April 2026 in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe) the AFC/M23 fought wazalendo from several local armed groups, including the COPACO led by Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, the MCDPIN of Grevisse Nsimparingira and the group of Haguma Kanyengwenye.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-002.n: Leaders as printed by the outlet.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-002.vn: All three names and groups match the page character for character. Leader names spelled as Actualite.cd prints them; the outlet does not name Haguma Kanyengwenye's group.
src: parmi lesquels le COPACO dirigé par Kirikicho Mirimba Mwanamayi, le MCDPIN de Grevisse Nsimparingira, ainsi que celui de Haguma Kanyengwenye.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that the town of Tushunguti, chef-lieu of Ziralo groupement in Kalehe territory, fell under AFC/M23 control on Tuesday 7 April 2026 after fighting with wazalendo, according to its sources; it said no official toll had been communicated.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-003.vn: Every clause on the page; date 7 April 2026 in the excerpt.
src: est tombée sous le contrôle des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ce mardi 7 avril 2026, après des violents affrontements contre les wazalendo.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that Tushunguti (Kalehe) was again under FARDC control, supported by wazalendo fighters, after a brief AFC/M23 occupation that began on 7 April 2026; it said the counter-offensive was launched from the Biriko and Busurungi axes in Walikale.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-004.n: Date range: article dated 10 April says retaken less than 48 hours after 7 April. Single outlet; AFC/M23 account not found.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-004.vn: Both excerpts exact and on topic; the two sources are one article (not independent). Date range kept as approximate. Retaking date not printed: 'less than 48 hours' after the 7 April fall, article published 10 April 08:05, so 9-10 April is approximate. Kivu Morning Post (9 April, claim on displacement) instead said AFC-M23 was consolidating its hold on Tushunguti that day; the 5 May Actualite.cd article says AFC/M23 retook the town 'nearly two months' after losing it, which does not fit a 9-10 April loss. Discrepancies unresolved.
src: Moins de 48 heures plus tard, une contre-offensive de l’armée a permis sa reconquête.
les opérations militaires ayant conduit à la reprise de Tushunguti ont été lancées depuis les axes de Biriko et Busurungi, dans le territoire de Walikale (Nord-Kivu).

r1-SKN-2026Q2-005.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that Tushunguti again passed under AFC/M23 control on Sunday 3 May 2026 after two days of fighting against wazalendo, who withdrew towards Biriko in Walikale.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-005.vn: Supported; year 2026 from the article date 05/05/2026. The same article says the retaking came 'près de deux mois après en avoir perdu le contrôle' (nearly two months after losing control), which conflicts with the outlet's own 10 April report of a loss on about 9-10 April (under four weeks).
src: est de nouveau passée sous contrôle des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 le dimanche 3 mai, à l’issue de deux jours d’intenses affrontements contre les combattants wazalendo

r1-SKN-2026Q2-006.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing several local sources, that on 12 April 2026 AFC/M23 elements carried out a cordon-and-search operation in Minova under a curfew, and that several men aged 18 to 40 were arrested and held for several hours at the 'Mille arbres' stadium.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-006.n: The outlet adds the operation reportedly aimed at identifying people without Salongo tokens and those suspected of being a threat; it says the detainees were released after women and children mobilised. Perpetrator attribution is the outlet's.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-006.vn: Supported by the page. The outlet says the women's and children's mobilisation 'aurait contribué' (reportedly contributed) to the release: conditional.
src: Plusieurs hommes âgés de 18 à 40 ans ont été interpellés au cours de cette opération. Les personnes interpellées ont, ensuite, été regroupées au stade dit « Mille arbres », où elles ont été retenues pendant plusieurs heures.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said nearly 48 000 displaced people were in an alarming humanitarian situation after fleeing fighting between AFC/M23 and wazalendo in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), and that all schools in the groupement remained closed.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-007.n: Figure is civil society's, relayed by the outlet.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-007.vn: 'about' narrowed to 'nearly' (près de); figure written as printed. Civil society figure relayed by the outlet ('près de 48 000'). Kept separate from the Kivu Morning Post civil-society figure of 'plus de 38 500' (9 April); different dates and counts.
src: La société civile locale tire la sonnette d’alarme face à une crise humanitaire majeure affectant près de 48 000 personnes déplacées, contraintes de fuir les affrontements entre les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 et les wazalendo.
toutes les écoles du groupement de Ziralo sont restées fermées.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that several houses were burned along the Bunje-Katale axis, notably in the villages of Bunje and Nyalugusha, during fighting between the belligerents; it did not say who burned them or on which day.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-008.l: Bunje and Nyalugusha villages, Ziralo, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q2-008.a: not attributed by the source (AFC/M23 and wazalendo were the belligerents)
r1-SKN-2026Q2-008.n: Exact date of burning not given; range from article context.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-008.vn: Raw statement implied the burning followed the 13 April change of hands and that 'local sources' said it; the page does neither. Removed the sequence and the date from the statement; date widened to the reporting window. Undated in the source: the article (17 April) reports renewed fighting at Chambombo on 13 April and fighting in Ziralo since 6 April; the burning is not tied to a day or a perpetrator. Actualite.cd's 7 April article spells the locality 'Bundje'.
src: plusieurs habitations ont été incendiées sur l’axe Bunje-Katale, notamment dans les villages de Bunje et Nyalugusha, lors des affrontements entre les belligérants.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, more than 38 500 people fled their villages following fighting in Ziralo groupement (Kalehe), most of them towards Lulambo and Biriko in Walikale territory.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-009.x: Kivu Morning Post (civil society): more than 38,500 fled
r1-SKN-2026Q2-009.n: Figure differs from Actualite.cd (48,000 on 17 April); different dates and counts, not merged.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-009.vn: Removed the day numbers no excerpt prints from the statement (moved to date); belligerents stay in the actor field. Night of Wednesday 8 to Thursday 9 April 2026 per the page. Figure kept separate from Actualite.cd's 'près de 48 000' (17 April). Same article says AFC-M23 was consolidating its hold on Tushunguti, which differs from Actualite.cd's account of a FARDC retaking by 10 April; it also reports an AFC-M23 communiqué by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accusing Kinshasa of 'délibérées' attacks in violation of the ceasefire (a party statement not yet recorded).
src: La société civile affirme que, suite à ces combats, plus de 38 500 personnes ont fui leurs villages. La plupart des habitants se sont dirigés vers Lulambo et Biriko, dans le territoire de Walikale.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-010.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Kalehe civil society said SEBUTAGWIRA HARERIMANA JACQUES, director of the EP Chambombo, was shot dead during fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23 at Chambombo on Wednesday 29 April 2026.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-010.l: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q2-010.a: not attributed by the source (fighting between Wazalendo and AFC-M23)
r1-SKN-2026Q2-010.n: Name printed in capitals by the source. Article says Wazalendo attacked Chambombo and were repelled by AFC-M23.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-010.vn: Name, role, place and date match the page exactly. The source does not say who fired the fatal shot. Per civil society, the Wazalendo attacked Chambombo and were repelled by AFC-M23. Name as printed (capitals).
src: La société civile de Kalehe rapporte que SEBUTAGWIRA HARERIMANA JACQUES, directeur de l’EP Chambombo, est mort par balles lors des affrontements.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that five people were shot dead and one seriously wounded in a shooting attributed to presumed AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday 21 May 2026 at Mbayo village, Kabare territory; according to a civil society official of Bugorhe groupement, the assailants gathered their victims and executed them one by one.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-011.l: Mbayo village, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare territory
r1-SKN-2026Q2-011.a: presumed AFC/M23 rebels, per Radio Okapi
r1-SKN-2026Q2-011.n: No names of victims printed in the excerpts. Radio Okapi says victims were civilians (woodcutters, farmers) from Kamakombe and Kashwago; AFC/M23 account not found.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-011.vn: Hedge kept; figures and date match the excerpt. Perpetrators are 'présumés rebelles de l’AFC/M23' (presumed) in Radio Okapi's wording. Radio Okapi says, citing local sources, the assailants had attacked Wazalendo at the Mbayu plantation, were routed and then attacked civilians making charcoal; victims were civilians from Kamakombe and Kashwago. No victim named. No AFC/M23 account found.
src: Cinq personnes ont été abattues et une autre grièvement blessée dans une fusillade de présumés rebelles de l’AFC/M23, jeudi 21 mai au village Mbayo, en territoire de Kabare (Sud-Kivu).
Ces assaillants ont rassemblé leurs victimes avant de les exécuter à tour de rôle, selon le témoignage d'un responsable de la société civile du groupement Bugorhe.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that on 9 June 2026 school and commercial activities were disrupted in Mbayo and Kamakombe villages (Kabare) by fighting between AFC/M23 elements and wazalendo militiamen from morning until late evening; it said this followed fighting a week earlier at Kafurumaye, near Kahuzi-Biega National Park.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-012.n: Same villages as the 21 May killings (separate claim).
r1-SKN-2026Q2-012.vn: Supported by one article; year from article date 10/06/2026.
src: Le 9 juin, les activités scolaires, commerciales notamment ont été perturbées dans les villages de Mbayo et Kamakombe suite au combat dès la matinée jusque tard dans la soirée.
Les affrontements à Mbayo et Kamakombe interviennent une semaine après ceux de Kafurumaye, près du parc national de Kahuzi-Biega.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-013.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that an explosive device killed one child and seriously wounded three others on Tuesday 28 April 2026 near Kavumu airport (Kabare); the victims, all minors, were scavenging scrap metal when they found an abandoned crate of explosives, and the three wounded were transferred to the Bukavu general referral hospital.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-013.l: Businde, Bugorhe groupement, near Kavumu airport, Kabare territory
r1-SKN-2026Q2-013.x: Radio Okapi: 1 child killed, 3 seriously wounded
r1-SKN-2026Q2-013.n: Title truncated in URL; title reconstructed from Radio Okapi listing. Children not named.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-013.vn: Supported; title on page matches. Place per the page: a valley at Businde, Bugorhe groupement. Radio Okapi notes the area was, per several sources, the FARDC's last line of defence before the fall of Bukavu in February 2025; no party is said to have left the explosives.
src: Un engin explosif a causé la mort d’un enfant et grièvement blessé trois autres mardi 28 avril aux abords de l’aéroport de Kavumu, en territoire de Kabare (Sud-Kivu).
Les trois autres, grièvement blessés, ont été transférés à l’Hôpital général de référence de Bukavu pour des soins d’urgence.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-014.s: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) reported that on 5 April 2026 at Cirunga, Kabare territory, eight men and two women were arrested by AFC/M23 elements for demonstrating spontaneously after learning they were to be removed from posts in that village.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-014.n: Excerpt keeps the PDF extraction artefact "postesdans". Report is for April 2026; publication date taken from the file path (2026-07), exact day unknown.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-014.vn: Checked in the retained PDF (April 2026 monthly analysis). UN-body documentation: grade A under the rubric. Excerpt keeps the PDF typo 'postesdans' verbatim. The report gives this as an illustration and does not say what posts or what happened to the ten afterwards; it calls the AFC/M23 'auteurs présumés' in the next sentence.
src: le 5 avril 2026, à Cirunga, territoire de Kabare, huit hommes et deux femmes ont été arrêtés par des éléments de l’AFC/M23 pour avoir manifesté spontanément, après avoir appris qu’ils allaient être retirés de postesdans ce village.

r1-SKN-2026Q2-015.s: Soleil du Graben reported that an AFC/M23 delegation led by the vice-governor in charge of political, administrative and judicial matters, Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux, relaunched customary administration of the Ntambuka chiefdom on Idjwi island and installed a seven-member peace committee, in the presence of Idjwi territory administrator Pascal Ntambuka.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-015.n: Local web outlet (Soleil du Graben, eastern DRC); tone is neutral-to-favourable to the AFC/M23 administration; treat as report of an AFC/M23 event, not independent confirmation. The event day (mission) is taken from publication date 2026-05-16.
r1-SKN-2026Q2-015.vn: All names spelled as printed; three excerpts are one article. Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux is an AFC/M23 de facto official (South Kivu vice-governor in the AFC/M23 administration). Soleil du Graben, byline 'admin', reads close to AFC/M23 communications; treat as the AFC/M23 side's account of its own event. Mission day not printed; 'Last updated Mai 16, 2026'. Page also says the delegation urged families to send their children into the security forces, especially the ARC (recruitment appeal). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Soleil du Graben, 16 May 2026 (signed 'Rédaction'; the site's coverage reads as AFC/M23-aligned, so treat as the movement's account). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the relaunch of customary administration, now added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Soleil du Graben, 16 May 2026 (signed 'Rédaction'; the site's coverage reads as AFC/M23-aligned, so treat as the movement's account). All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpts lacked the relaunch of customary administration, now added.
src: Conduite par le vice-gouverneur en charge des questions politiques, administratives et judiciaires, Dunia Masumbuko Bwenge Doux, la délégation a rencontré, avant midi, les représentants de la chefferie de Ntambuka.
Sept personnes ont également été installées pour animer bénévolement le comité de paix.
En présence de l’administrateur du territoire d’Idjwi, Pascal Ntambuka, la délégation s’est entretenue avec les chefs des trois groupements, les chefs des 50 villages

Une délégation de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo-M23 était en mission officielle sur l’île d’Idjwi pour redynamiser le mouvement, relancer l’administration coutumière de la chefferie de Ntambuka et installer un comité de résolution pacifique des conflits.
Sur place, l’autorité provinciale a relancé l’administration coutumière.

Les premiers tirs ont été entendus aux environs de 5 heures du matin, dans les localités de Chambombo, Lumbishi, Kaziba de Rumbishi, Kwisimbi, Gafufura et Kazinga.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-003.n: Single outlet citing local sources; Wazalendo/AFC accounts of the event not found in this source. The article also recalls late-June fighting at Lumbishi/Chambombo in which AFC-M23 retook Chambombo (outside this quarter).

De violents combats ont opposé mardi 11 août les combattants Wazalendo aux éléments de l’AFC-M23-RDF dans plusieurs secteurs du territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-004.s: Enquete.cd reported, citing medical sources, that several AFC-M23-RDF fighters wounded in the Kalehe fighting were reportedly admitted to the hospital of Numbi, among them a Rwandan officer presented as a colonel who was reportedly gravely wounded; the outlet said this information could not be independently verified.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-006.s: La Presse Africaine reported that local civil society said population movements towards Walikale were noted, that cattle pillage and losses of property were reported, and that several health structures remained difficult to operate, following the 11-14 August 2026 fighting in Kalehe's Buhavu chiefdom.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-009.s: La Prunelle RDC reported that at least five people were killed and several wounded on Friday 7 August 2026 in the explosion of an explosive device in the centre of Lumbishi (Ziralo grouping, Kalehe highlands), and that the wounded were evacuated to the Numbi hospital centre.

The outlet says neither party's accusations could be independently verified, and the timings differ (local sources about 10 a.m.; AFC-M23 about 17:45).

Les blessés ont été évacués vers le centre hospitalier de Numbi pour recevoir des soins.

affirme le lieutenant de second classe Meya Gbé Jérémie , porte-parole du secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Nord–Sud-Kivu.

Le nombre de victimes civiles s’élève désormais à 9 morts », affirme Lawrence Kanyuka.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, which depends on the central government in Kinshasa, denounced the pressure and predation to which it said the population of Bukavu is subjected under the administration of AFC/M23, citing levies including so-called sanitation taxes and taxes on commercial activity and, according to several testimonies, acts of intimidation, violence and flogging.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-012.n: Statement prompted by the 10 Sept Funu B fire in Kadutu (existing claim r1-ST-DRC-2026-004). The same article gives a provisional toll of more than 26 children dead (19 girls, 7 boys), mostly pupils of École primaire FARAJA, per the provincial government citing health structures; the existing claim says about twenty wounded: reviewer to reconcile. r1-SKN-2026Q3-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC higher-education ministry (ESURSI), headed by Marie-Thérèse Sombo, issued a ministerial order, announced on Tuesday 25 August 2026, suspending academic activities for academic year 2026-2027 at several institutions in Goma and Bukavu, including the Université Officielle de Bukavu, ISC-Bukavu, ISTM-Bukavu, ISP-Bukavu, ISDR-Bukavu and ISAM-Bukavu.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-013.n: Relates to de facto AFC/M23 control of universities; RFI/Yahoo says the ministry also suspended the salaries of 48 agents accused of joining AFC/M23.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-013.vn: All clauses on page; excerpt_en flags are only expansions of acronyms. The order also lists Goma institutions (UOG, ISC-Goma, ISTM-Goma, ISP-Goma); final-year 2025-2026 students may complete elsewhere.
src: Le ministère de l’Enseignement supérieur, universitaire, Recherche scientifique et Innovations (ESURSI), dirigé par Marie-Thérèse Sombo, a pris un arrêté ministériel portant suspension des activités académiques au sein de plusieurs établissements d’enseignement supérieur et universitaire des villes de Goma et de Bukavu, dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu.
ainsi que plusieurs établissements de Bukavu, dont l’Université Officielle de Bukavu (UOB), l’ISC-Bukavu, l’ISTM-Bukavu, l’ISP-Bukavu, l’ISDR-Bukavu et l’ISAM-Bukavu
Selon cette décision, annoncée mardi 25 août 2026, la mesure intervient dans un contexte marqué par une situation sécuritaire préoccupante
toutes les activités académiques et para-académiques liées à l’année académique 2026-2027 sont suspendues jusqu’à nouvel ordre dans les établissements concernés.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-014.n: Yahoo page carries an RFI credit; the RFI original was not fetched. The 'Bukavu' scope is partial: article covers Goma and Bukavu.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-014.vn: Narrowed 'accused of allegiance' to the three grounds the page states; 'separate decision' kept as printed. Read on the Yahoo Actualités copy credited to RFI; the RFI original was not opened. The page does not say which authority issued the salary decision.
src: En réponse, Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur adjoint de l'AFC/M23, annonce un mécanisme de substitution.

Dans leur rapport de décembre 2025, les experts des Nations unies indiquaient déjà par exemple que l'AFC/M23 avait ordonné aux universités de rompre leurs liens avec le ministère congolais de l'Enseignement supérieur.
les salaires de 48 agents sont suspendus. Ils sont accusés d'avoir rejoint l'AFC/M23, de lui avoir prêté allégeance ou d'avoir accepté des fonctions sous son autorité.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-015.s: La Presse Africaine reported, citing local sources, that clashes involving M23 fighters had reportedly caused population displacement in several areas of Kalehe, Masisi and Walikale; Olivier Kaskoti, a Tembo notable and honorary president of Buuma bwe Batembo (Beni section), said localities in Ziralo grouping and parts of Ufamandu grouping (Masisi) and Walowa-Lwanda (Walikale) faced a deteriorating security situation for several days, and alleged that M23 used drones and artillery fire, allegations the outlet said could not be independently verified.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-015.n: Date is report date. Byline Dieudonné Hangi (LPA Beni).
r1-SKN-2026Q3-015.vn: Draft attributed the Ziralo/Ufamandu/Walowa-Lwanda displacement to local sources; the page gives the displacement at territory level (local sources) and the specific groupings as Kaskoti's account of deteriorating security. Separated; source 2 extended to the full sentence. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) Report date used (28 August 2026); the article gives no event date. Byline Dieudonné Hangi, LPA Beni.
src: Selon des sources locales, des affrontements impliquant les combattants du M23 auraient provoqué des mouvements de déplacement de la population dans plusieurs zones de Kalehe, de Masisi et de Walikale.

La même source affirme également que le M23 aurait fait recours à des drones et à des tirs d’artillerie au cours des hostilités. Ces allégations n’ont toutefois pas pu être vérifiées de manière indépendante.
D’après Olivier Kaskoti, le notable Tembo et président honoraire de Buuma bwe Batembo, section de Beni, les localités situées dans le groupement de Ziralo

r1-SKN-2026Q3-016.s: La Presse Africaine reported that an appeal on the Ziralo situation demanded the release of 'le patriote' Kirikocho Mirimba Mwana Mayi, who the appeal said had been in detention for several weeks.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-016.n: Who holds him, and where, is not stated: gap. Lead only.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-016.vn: Name printed on page exactly; policy v1 allows naming detainees. Name as printed. Who holds him and where is not stated; the appeal's author is not named beyond the article's 'la même source' context. Lead only.
src: exige la libération du patriote Kirikocho Mirimba Mwana Mayi qui est en détention depuis plusieurs semaines.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-017.s: La Presse Africaine reported that the body of a woman bearing traces of violence and of bladed weapons was found in Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, on a Sunday in early August 2026 (the article gives two different dates for that Sunday); a source on the spot said she was reportedly killed during the night by unidentified individuals who used knives and machetes, her body found with a serious neck wound, and village chief Doris Habiragi confirmed the information and said investigations were under way.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-017.l: Nkola village, Rubenga chiefdom, Idjwi, South Kivu
r1-SKN-2026Q3-017.n: Non-conflict criminality as far as the source says. The page is internally inconsistent: 'dimanche 01 août 2026' in one place, 'dimanche 2 août 2026' in another; 2 Aug 2026 is a Sunday, so date computed from weekday and publication date. Victim unnamed. Related LPA item on a young man found dead with bound arms in Idjwi (about mid-August) was seen only as a headline.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-017.vn: Supported; inconsistency stated in the statement with both dates as printed; killing account and neck wound added from the quote on the page. (Excerpt extensions proposed in clause_support; replacement_quotes are not applied to exact sources.) Date inconsistent on the page: the summary says 'dimanche 01 août 2026', the body 'dimanche 2 août 2026'; 2 August 2026 is a Sunday, so 2 August is used, precision approximate. Headline says the woman was decapitated. The source presents it as criminality; no armed-group link stated. Victim unnamed. Byline Richelieu Byamana, LPA Sud-Kivu. Excerpt gap: the stored excerpt does not carry this; the passage in clause_support is on the retained page (extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
src: Le corps de la victime portait des traces des violences et d'armes blanches, d'après plusieurs témoignages sur place.
Doris Habiragi, chef de village Nkola, confirme cette information et précise que les enquêtes sont en cours pour tenter de retrouver les auteurs de cet acte criminel.

r1-SKN-2026Q3-018.s: Mediacongo reported that the ultimatum set by the United States for Rwanda to withdraw its troops from eastern DRC expired on Wednesday 15 July 2026, and that, according to security and local sources, the rebel movement, after consolidating its positions in the Hauts Plateaux and other strategic areas, would now be seeking to extend its influence towards Baraka, an important town in Fizi territory.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-018.n: Outside my unit's core geography (Fizi); recorded as context only. Marco Rubio named in an adjacent sentence, not in the excerpts: remove if checker flags. Rwanda/US official statements on the expiry not located.
r1-SKN-2026Q3-018.vn: Restored the conditional; identity of 'le mouvement rebelle' as AFC/M23 rests on the same article's first sentence. The article identifies the rebel movement as AFC/M23 (headline and first sentence). The Baraka movement is conditional in the source ('chercherait'). Article byline Roberto Tshahe Da Cruz. Rwandan and US statements on the expiry not found in this source.
src: L’ultimatum fixé par les États-Unis au Rwanda pour le retrait de ses troupes de l’est de la République démocratique du Congo est arrivé à échéance ce mercredi 15 juillet 2026

Selon des sources sécuritaires et locales, après avoir consolidé ses positions dans les Hauts Plateaux et d’autres zones stratégiques, le mouvement rebelle chercherait désormais à étendre son influence vers Baraka, importante ville du territoire de Fizi.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-001.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that after intense fighting since 3h on Monday 5 October 2026, Wazalendo fighters were said to have retaken control of Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Bikari/Kuma Dépôts, Chambombo and Bishaka in the Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, from AFC-M23 troops.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-001.l: Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Chambombo, Bishaka (Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom), Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-001.a: Wazalendo; AFC-M23 (as named by the source)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-001.n: Local community radio (Bukavu), hedged ('auraient'). Same event drafted from Radio Okapi (r1/UCD-FARDC-WZ#34-35); independent local outlet. Source says FARDC and Wazalendo launched the assaults.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-001.vn: Page supports every clause; the '23' flag is the AFC-M23 name. Corroborated in part by Enquete.cd 6 Oct (FARDC-allied forces announced retaking Katale, Kafufula, Chambombo, Bishaka). Hedged by the source ('auraient repris'). The source says FARDC and Wazalendo launched the assaults; Bikari/Kuma Dépôts is not in its list of Ziralo axes. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Après d’intenses combats depuis 3h de lundi 5 octobre 2026, les combattants Wazalendo auraient repris le contrôle de plusieurs entités comme Kafufula, Katale, Katoke, Bikari/Kuma Dépôts, Chambombo et Bishaka.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-002.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local leaders, that at about 11h on Monday a presence of Wazalendo fighters was reported in the town of Lumbishi, about 8 km from Numbi, Kalehe territory.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-002.n: Date is the Monday of the 6 Oct article, i.e. 5 Oct (article text says 'lundi 5 octobre' earlier). Single local source.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-002.vn: Verbatim support; Monday is 5 Oct per the same page.
src: Dans la matinée aux environs de 11h le lundi, une présence des combattants Wazalendo a été signalée dans la cité de Lumbishi située à plus ou moins 8Km de Numbi, indiquent des leaders locaux contactés dans la zone.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-003.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing an occasional correspondent, that in the morning of Monday 05 October an unusual presence of fighters claiming to be Wazalendo was seen on the hills of Mabingu village, Irhambi-Katana grouping, Kabare territory, and that several school heads sent pupils home fearing clashes.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-003.n: Only item found placing armed activity in Kabare territory in this window; single local correspondent, no fighting reported at Mabingu.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-003.vn: Supported; excerpt_en flag is only 'Wazalendo' vs 'Wazalendos' spelling.
src: une présence inhabituelle des combattants se réclamant Wazalendos sur les collines du village Mabingu dans la matinée de lundi 05 octobre. Plusieurs responsables d’écoles ont du renvoyer les élèves craignant les risques d’affrontements, indique un correspondant occasionnel joint par Radio Maendeleo dans la zone.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-004.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that at the Kavumu primary school, about 4 km from Numbi, parents rushed to collect their children because of the deteriorating security situation and the approach of the battlefield.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-004.l: Kavumu primary school near Numbi, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-004.n: Name collision with Kavumu airport (Kabare): not the same place.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-004.vn: Removed the editorial disambiguation from the statement (moved to note); the rest is verbatim. This Kavumu is a place about 4 km from Numbi, not Kavumu airport in Kabare.
src: À l’Ecole Primaire Kavumu située à près de 4km de la cité de Numbi, les parents se sont précipités pour récupérer leurs enfants au regard de la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire et le rapprochement du champ de bataille.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-005.s: Enquete.cd reported, according to local sources, that the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo fighters, had retaken control of the centre of Numbi, Kalehe territory, and that clashes had reportedly preceded the retaking.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-005.n: The same page says AFC/M23 had been present there for several months and reports local sources describing an AFC/M23 pull-back toward Numbi and Byonde on 5 October. Later retaken by FRN troops per Radio Maendeleo 20 Oct (separate claim).
r1-SKN-2026Q4-005.vn: Statement said the retaking happened 'on 6 October'; the page only reports it on 6 Oct. Narrowed; date flag set approximate. Reported in a 6 October 2026 dispatch ('informations recueillies ce mardi'); the day of the retaking itself is not stated. The page says AFC/M23 had been present there for several months. Radio Maendeleo (20 Oct) later reported FRN troops retook Numbi. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Enquete.cd (6 Oct 2026, La Redaction) supports both clauses; the 'clashes reportedly preceded' clause is not in the stored excerpt, so the passage is added. The headline says the FARDC and Wazalendo 'announce' the retaking, while the body cites local sources.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les combattants Wazalendo, ont repris le contrôle du centre de Numbi, dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, selon des sources locales.
Des affrontements auraient précédé la reprise du centre, après plusieurs mois de présence de l’AFC/M23 dans cette zone.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-006.s: Radio Maendeleo reported on 20 October that after the Wazalendo offensive that led to their entry into Shanje, Lumbishi and Numbi between 5 and 6 October, a counter-offensive had allowed troops of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) to retake control of them.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-006.n: The date of the FRN counter-offensive is not given by this source; only that it preceded 20 Oct. Conflicts in time with Enquete.cd 6 Oct (FARDC holding Numbi): control changed afterwards. Single local source.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-006.vn: Verbatim; '20' is the publication date (Last updated 2026/10/20). The date of the FRN counter-offensive is not given; only that it preceded the 20 October report.
ent: Front pour la Refondation de la Nation
src: Après l’offensive ayant conduit à l’entrée des Wazalendo à Shanje, Lumbishi et Numbi entre le 5 et le 6 octobre dernier puis la contre-offensive ayant permis aux troupes du Front pour la Refondation de la Nation d’en reprendre le contrôle, la vie y est devenue encore plus difficile.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.s: Radio Maendeleo reported a still-provisional toll of at least 8 dead, including civilians, and several wounded in new clashes that had pitted AFC-M23 troops against Wazalendo fighters for nearly three days in several villages around Shanje, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe highlands; the same article quoted a source in a medical structure receiving some cases as reporting several wounded civilians in addition to about ten deaths near Shanje and in the Bogamanda-Nyamutwe area.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.l: Shanje area (Kirwa, Bunyata, Igali axis) and Bogamanda-Nyamutwe, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.a: AFC-M23 troops; Wazalendo (parties to the fighting)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.x: Radio Maendeleo provisional toll: at least 8 dead including civilians, several wounded; medical-structure source quoted by the same outlet: about ten deaths ('une dizaine de décès') near Shanje and Bogamanda-Nyamutwe, plus several civilian wounded. Kept separate.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.n: Page shows 'Rédaction 14 octobre 2026 / 6 octobre 2026' (modified/published); article text refers to 'mardi 6 octobre', so event date 6 Oct. Two figures kept separate. Deaths not attributed to a party; civilian/combatant split not given.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-007.vn: 'more than ten deaths' mistranslated 'en plus d'une dizaine de décès' (= in addition to about ten deaths); corrected. Both sources are one article, one origin: C. Two tolls from the same outlet differ (at least 8; about ten): kept per source. Deaths not attributed to a party; civilian/combatant split not given. The headline says FARDC backed by Wazalendo fought AFC-M23.
src: Au moins 8 morts dont des civils et plusieurs blessés ; c’est le bilan encore provisoire de nouveaux affrontements qui opposent depuis près de trois jours les troupes de l’AFC-M23 aux combattants Wazalendo dans plusieurs villages situés aux alentours de l’agglomération de Shanje, chefferie de Buhavu dans les hauts plateaux de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu.

L’on rapporte plusieurs blessés dans les rangs des civils en plus d’une dizaine de décès vers Shanje tout comme dans la partie Bogamanda-Nyamutwe, indique une source au sein d’une structure médicale qui accueille certains cas.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-008.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing witnesses, that returnees found homes destroyed or burned, goods looted and fields devastated in Kalehe highlands, and that at Shanje almost all shops were burned in the night of 6 to 7 October. Actualite.cd reported separately that a large fire broke out around 4 a.m. on Wednesday 7 October in Shanje, affecting homes and the local market.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-008.x: Radio Maendeleo: 'presque toutes les boutiques' burned at Shanje; Actualite.cd: several homes and the market affected, no count
r1-SKN-2026Q4-008.n: Cause of the fire and perpetrators of looting are not stated by either source; Radio Maendeleo speaks of 'incendiées' without attribution. Shanje was contested 5-7 Oct (Wazalendo entered, FRN retook). Two local/national outlets, independent bylines.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-008.vn: Both pages checked; two independent outlets agree on the Shanje burning of 6-7 Oct; no attribution added. Neither source states the cause of the fire or who burned or looted; not attributed by the source.
src: Des témoins sur place rapportent une présence toujours massive des retournés qui ont trouvé leurs maisons détruites ou alors incendiées, des biens pillés et des champs dévastés. A Shanje par exemple, presque toutes les boutiques ont été incendiées dans la nuit du 6 au 7 octobre.

Un incendie de grande ampleur s’est déclaré tôt le matin de mercredi 7 octobre à Shanje (territoire de Kalehe), dans la province du Sud-Kivu. Le sinistre a commencé vers 4 heures, alors que la plupart des habitants étaient encore dans leurs habitations.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-009.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing a local civil-society source, that in the health areas of Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi (Kalehe highlands) health facilities had difficulty caring for the sick because they too had been looted, and schools struggled to resume.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-009.l: Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa and Lumbishi health areas, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-009.n: Which facilities, when looted and by whom are not stated; the sibling health-area sentences in the same article place this after the 5-7 Oct changes of hands. Also the same article says there was no humanitarian assistance. Lead for investigators: ask the Bunyakiri/Minova health zone offices.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-009.vn: Verbatim support; looting unattributed as in the source. Which facilities, when and by whom they were looted is not stated.
src: Dans cette zone principalement dans les aires de santé de Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa et Lumbishi, l’on rapporte une difficulté pour les structures de santé dans la prise en charge des malades car elles aussi ont été pillées mais aussi les écoles qui peinent à reprendre les activités scolaires, indique une source de la société civile locale.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-010.s: Kivutimes (project Habari za Mahali) reported on 21 October that MSF Spain gave PEP kits for survivors of sexual violence to four health structures (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa) in the Bunyakiri health zone, Ziralo grouping, and that, according to Katabana Monde, head nurse at Matutira, the structures record cases of sexual violence among their populations, notably in the context of displacement caused by the fighting; providers had had difficulty obtaining PEP kits in time.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-010.l: Bunyakiri health zone (Tushunguti, Matutira, Mianda, Kusisa health centres), Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-010.n: No perpetrator, count or dates of incidents. Article produced under 'Habari za Mahali' (RATECO / REMEL-GL consortium with Media4dialogue), local reporting; a nurse's testimony. Ties to PEP supply gap (access to care within the 72-hour window is the lead). Names of survivors not given.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-010.vn: All clauses on the page; single local outlet with one named informant, so C rather than B. No case numbers, perpetrators or incident dates given; the nurse's testimony is the only basis.
src: D’après Katabana Monde, infirmier titulaire du centre de santé de Matutira, les structures de santé enregistrent des cas de violences sexuelles parmi les populations de leurs aires de santé, notamment dans le contexte des déplacements provoqués par les affrontements.

L’organisation Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) Espagne a doté quatre structures sanitaires de la zone de santé de Bunyakiri, dans le groupement de Ziralo. Ces kits sont destinés à la prise en charge des survivantes de violences sexuelles.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that journalist Laurent Vainqueur Muliro of community radio Walikale Amka (RTCWA) was shot dead on the evening of Wednesday 21 October in an ambush attributed to presumed Wazalendo militiamen near Bitale, Kalehe territory; the page says two other people were also killed and two seriously wounded, with the travellers' property looted.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-011.a: presumed Wazalendo militiamen (as attributed by the outlet)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-011.x: Actualite.cd: 3 killed (the journalist, a student and a moto-taxi driver), 2 seriously wounded
r1-SKN-2026Q4-011.n: Two other victims (a student and a moto-taxi driver) are unnamed in the page. The page says the convoy used the Bukavu-Hombo detour because the Goma-Walikale road had been closed by FRN rebels, and the ambush spot is in a Wazalendo-controlled area. No Wazalendo or FARDC reaction found. The injured and bodies went to Hombo Sud hospital centre.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-011.vn: Name printed exactly; hedge kept; figures on the page. Perpetrators are 'présumés' (presumed) Wazalendo per the outlet; the page says the spot was under Wazalendo control and that survivors reported the facts. UNPC Walikale condemned the killing and called for an inquiry.
src: Le journaliste Laurent Vainqueur Muliro de la Radio communautaire Walikale Amka (RTCWA) a été tué par balle dans la soirée du mercredi 21 octobre, lors d’une embuscade attribuée à des présumés miliciens wazalendo, près de Bitale, dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu.
Les trois corps ont été acheminés à la morgue du Centre hospitalier de Hombo Sud. Deux autres voyageurs ont été grièvement blessés au cours de cette attaque.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-012.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that the local youth council of the villages of Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory, denounced insecurity attributed to unidentified armed persons: intimidation of farmers, theft of livestock and extortion of money, and 'inhuman treatment' of people who resist.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-012.l: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-012.n: Allegation by a local civil-society body; date is publication date (27 Oct), incidents undated. Do not read 'inhuman treatment' as any legal category.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-012.vn: Attributed allegation, supported verbatim. Allegations by a local youth council, in the conditional; incidents undated.
src: Ces individus raviraient les biens des paysans, notamment le bétail, et leur extorqueraient de l’argent. Ils infligeraient également des traitements inhumains aux personnes qui tentent de s’opposer à leurs actes, dénonce le Conseil local de la jeunesse.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-013.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that the same Kabulungu and Mulangala (Kabare territory) youth council also reported cases of arrests followed by detention in unknown places, the victims reportedly being released only after payment of a sum of money.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-013.l: Kabulungu and Mulangala, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare territory
r1-SKN-2026Q4-013.n: Who arrests (the source does not say whether armed groups or authorities) is not stated. Area in contested zone (FRN vs Wazalendo clashes reported per the same page).
r1-SKN-2026Q4-013.vn: Restored the source's conditional ('ne seraient libérées'); otherwise verbatim. Who carried out the arrests is not stated.
src: La structure rapporte par ailleurs des cas d’arrestations suivies de détentions dans des lieux inconnus. Les victimes ne seraient libérées qu’après le paiement d’une somme d’argent.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-014.s: Radio Maendeleo reported on 3 October that, according to civil society, more than 1,900 households from Kalehe highlands (mainly Ziralo and Numbi groupings) and Ufamandu grouping in Masisi had taken refuge in the Buzi grouping of Minova, having fled fighting between the AFC/M23 and the government coalition over the previous two weeks.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-014.a: AFC/M23; government coalition (as named by the source)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-014.x: Radio Maendeleo: over 1,900 households in three waves (first over 1,015, second over 466, third over 226)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-014.n: Households, not persons; the source says the displaced had no assistance to date. Predates the 5-6 Oct Kalehe fighting; this is the earlier wave.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-014.vn: Flagged numbers are the '1 900' spacing and the wave figures, all on the page ('plus de 1 015 ménages , la seconde de plus de 466 ménages et la troisième de plus de 226 ménages'). Single local origin: C. Households, not persons. Three waves per the page: over 1 015, over 466 and over 226 households.
src: Venus des hauts plateaux du territoire de Kalehe, essentiellement du groupement de Ziralo et Numbi, ainsi que du groupement d’Ufamandu dans le territoire de Masisi au Nord-Kivu, plus de 1 900 ménages se retrouvent en refuge dans le groupement de Buzi Minova. Selon la société civile, ces déplacés ont fui les affrontements qui ont été rapportés les deux dernières semaines dans leurs milieux de provenance entre l’AFC/M23 et la coalition gouvernementale.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that thousands of families who fled clashes between the FRN and the FARDC supported by Wazalendo in the Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, were living in difficult conditions at Nyabibwe, lacking food, shelter and basic necessities, mostly women and children.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-015.a: FRN; FARDC; Wazalendo (parties named by the source)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-015.x: no number beyond 'thousands of families' ('des milliers de familles')
r1-SKN-2026Q4-015.n: No source named for the figure. Nyabibwe is on the Kalehe lakeshore road.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-015.vn: All clauses on the page; no source named for 'thousands'.
src: Des milliers de familles ayant fui les affrontements entre le FRN et les FARDC appuyées par les Wazalendo dans le groupement de Ziralo, en territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, vivent dans des conditions particulièrement difficiles à Nyabibwe, où elles ont trouvé refuge.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that Hombo civil society, after an assessment mission of 25 to 27 September 2026, said the local hospital centre at Hombo Sud (Kalehe territory) was receiving a large number of displaced people needing care, as well as people wounded by violence, with limited capacity.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-016.l: Hombo Sud, Kalehe territory (and Lukaraba, Walikale, North Kivu)
r1-SKN-2026Q4-016.x: Hombo civil society: about 2,350 displaced families at Lukaraba and Hombo Sud together
r1-SKN-2026Q4-016.n: Assessment dates fall in September (25-27 Sep), report date 4 Oct. The Hombo Sud hospital centre is the same one where the 21 Oct ambush victims were taken (see journalist claim). Capacity strain, not an attack.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-016.vn: Flagged numbers (2350, 25, 27) are printed on the page. Capacity strain, not an attack on care.
src: À Hombo Sud, la pression est également forte sur les structures sanitaires. Le centre hospitalier local reçoit un nombre important de personnes déplacées nécessitant des soins, ainsi que des blessés liés aux violences.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government (Kinshasa-appointed), in a communiqué of Monday 5 October signed by its spokesperson Didier Kabi, expressed concern at the extension of the closing hours of two border posts controlled by the AFC/M23, Ruzizi 1er in Bukavu and Grande Barrière in Goma, saying it could facilitate the entry of new populations and their settlement in AFC/M23-controlled zones.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-017.l: Ruzizi 1er border post, Bukavu; Grande Barrière, Goma
r1-SKN-2026Q4-017.n: Party account: the provincial government's reading (population-settlement concern) is its claim, not established fact. The AFC/M23 side of the Grande Barrière measure is in an existing claim (r1-NKS-2026Q4-009, Tic-Tac Hebdo, 2 Oct communiqué); no AFC/M23 answer to the Kinshasa concern found.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-017.vn: All clauses on the page; '23' flag is the AFC/M23 name. Party account (provincial government loyal to Kinshasa): its reading of the measure is its claim. 'Kinshasa-appointed' is a gloss; the page contrasts the provincial government with the AFC/M23-controlled posts.
src: Dans un communiqué signé lundi 5 octobre par son porte-parole, Didier Kabi, le gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu se dit particulièrement préoccupé par cette décision.

Selon les nouvelles dispositions, ces deux postes restent désormais ouverts plus longtemps. À Ruzizi 1er, le passage est autorisé jusqu’à minuit, tandis qu’à la Grande Barrière, les activités se poursuivent jusqu’à deux heures du matin.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-018.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN vice-president Bertrand Bisimwa, in a speech at Bukavu on Thursday, defended continued teaching in FRN-held zones despite measures by the Congolese government, and that the FRN promised to support teachers whose pay had been suspended by Kinshasa.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-018.a: FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation), as named by the source
r1-SKN-2026Q4-018.n: Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based; the page reports the FRN's own speech (party statement). The page says the Kinshasa suspension of academic activities in Goma and Bukavu was contested by the authorities in place.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-018.vn: Statement supported; actor 'AFC/M23 political structure' is not what this page prints, so set to the source's own name. De facto authority (FRN) statement: 'the FRN says'. The page describes the FRN as a politico-military movement led by former president Joseph Kabila, while Actualite.cd (27 Oct) calls it the AFC/M23 rebellion 'devenue' the FRN: naming discrepancy kept, not resolved.
src: Dans un discours prononcé à Bukavu à cette occasion, Bertrand Bisimwa, vice-président du FRN, a défendu la continuité de l’enseignement dans ces zones, malgré les tensions politiques et les mesures prises par le gouvernement congolais.

« En maintenant cette rentrée à la date du 15 octobre, nous affirmons notre volonté de préserver la régularité du calendrier académique et de permettre à notre jeunesse de poursuivre sa formation sans retard imposé par les affrontements politiques », a déclaré Bertrand Bisimwa.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that Higher Education minister Marie-Thérèse Sombo, launching the 2026-2027 academic year in Kongo Central on Monday 26 October 2026, said the provisional suspension of academic activities at Goma and Bukavu institutions aims to protect students and staff, preserve the legality of university governance and prevent irregular academic acts from compromising the value of diplomas.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-019.l: Kongo Central (statement); applies to Goma and Bukavu institutions
r1-SKN-2026Q4-019.n: Kinshasa's account, opposing the FRN's 15 Oct restart in Bukavu (see Bisimwa claim). Context for civilian access to education/health training in Bukavu; the suspension affects Bukavu medical students (Actualite.cd 7 Oct reports about 200 medical students moving to Unikis).
r1-SKN-2026Q4-019.vn: Verbatim support; '26' is printed on the page. Kinshasa government account.
src: Alors que cette question continue de susciter des réactions, la ministre a rappelé les raisons de la suspension provisoire des activités académiques dans les établissements concernés. « Cette décision vise à protéger les étudiants et les personnels, à préserver la légalité de la gouvernance universitaire et à empêcher que des actes académiques irréguliers ne compromettent la valeur des diplômes.

r1-SKN-2026Q4-020.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a video from the South Kivu governor's communication unit, that FRN vice-presidents Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo and Bertrand Bisimwa met FRN cadres from across South Kivu in Bukavu on Thursday 22 October 2026 to discuss the movement's political vision and organisation.
r1-SKN-2026Q4-020.n: Source is the movement's own governor-office video as relayed by KMP: evidence of what the FRN presented, not independent. Related Ukwelitimes item also exists (lead only).
r1-SKN-2026Q4-020.vn: Verbatim; partisan origin, C. Origin is the FRN-run governor's office video; what the FRN presented, not independent. This page spells the movement 'Front de la refondation nationale'.
src: Les deux vice-présidents du Front de la refondation nationale (FRN), Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo et Bertrand Bisimwa, ont rencontré, le jeudi 22 octobre 2026 à Bukavu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, des cadres du mouvement venus de différentes parties de la province du Sud-Kivu, selon une vidéo de la cellule de communication du gouverneur du sud-kivu.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho said Minembwe and surroundings were 'liberated', that a regional source confirmed to it that all of Minembwe was controlled by Twirwaneho, and that, according to several sources, Mikenge in the Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), 28 km from Minembwe, had also come under Twirwaneho control after fighting with the Congolese armed forces on Tuesday.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-001.l: Minembwe (Fizi) and Mikenge, Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q1-001.n: Date: report date 2026-02-26 article says 'ce mercredi' (Wednesday 26 Feb 2025); Mikenge combat on 'Mardi' (25 Feb, computed from weekday and publication date). Minembwe capture itself already in r1-UV-2025Q1-032 (SOS Medias Burundi). A Facebook snippet (lead only, not opened) claims FARDC/Wazalendo retook Mikenge on 24 Feb 2025; unverified, conflicts in sequence.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-001.vn: All clauses on the retained Actualite.cd page (26/02/2025). 'Liberated' clause rests on the page (not the stored excerpt). Grade B: one credible national outlet relaying unnamed and partisan sources. Control is per an unnamed regional source and 'several sources'; the 'liberated' wording is Twirwaneho's own announcement. Kivutimes (4 Mar) gives a different Mikenge sequence (Wazalendo dislodging on 3 Mar and same-day Twirwaneho retake); both accounts kept. 2026-10-29: territory edited: Frontline data fix: the claim's own location places Minembwe in Fizi and Mikenge (its control place) in Mwenga territory, as the excerpt says ('territoire de Mwenga').
src: « Tout Minembwe est effectivement contrôlé par Twirwaneho », a confirmé ce mercredi à ACTUALITE.CD une source dans la région.

Twirwaneho a intensifié l’offensive à 28 kilomètres de Minembwe, précisément à Mikenge, village du secteur d’Itombwe (territoire de Mwenga). D’après plusieurs sources, Mikenge est également passé sous le contrôle de Twirwaneho. Mardi, de violents combats opposaient cette milice aux Forces armées congolaises.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that after being sighted at Kamanyola and then Luvungi, M23 rebels were now visible at Sange in Uvira territory, South Kivu, and that residents confirmed their presence although the rebels had not yet made a public statement.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-002.l: Luvungi and Sange (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory
r1-SKS-2025Q1-002.n: Article date taken from URL path (2025/02/20); no byline date visible in fetched text. Corroborates Radio Okapi r1-UV-2025Q1-006 (Sange, 19 Feb) and adds Luvungi.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-002.vn: Verbatim on page (byline Blaise Basabose). No visible dateline; date from URL path, as noted.
src: Après avoir été aperçus à Kamanyola, puis à Luvungi, les rebelles du M23 sont désormais visibles à Sange, dans le territoire d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu. Des habitants de la zone confirment leur présence, bien que les rebelles n’aient pas encore fait de déclaration publique.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-003.s: Kivu Morning Post quoted Paul Byamungu, a member of Uvira civil society, as saying that after the meeting at Kamanyola, M23 was now with them, that they had communicated nothing, and that there had been no public meeting so far.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-003.n: Implies an M23 meeting at Kamanyola before 20 Feb; the page gives no date for it.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-003.vn: Removed 'in the Sange area': the quote says only 'avec nous'; placing it at Sange is the article's framing, not the speaker's. Civil-society statement, not an official one; the quote does not say where 'with us' is.
src: « Après le meeting à Kamanyola, le M23 est maintenant avec nous. Ils n’ont rien communiqué. Aucun meeting public jusque-là, mais nous, acteurs de la société civile, avons besoin de la paix » , a déclaré Paul Byamungu, membre de la société civile d’Uvira.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-004.s: URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa released a statement on Monday accusing FARDC soldiers and their allies of deploying Sukhoi fighter jets and attack drones to bomb several villages in Minembwe, and that, according to Bisimwa, the strikes were aimed at areas populated by Banyamulenge civilians, as well as Minembwe airfield.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-004.n: Partisan claim (AFC/M23). Date computed from weekday 'Monday' and page date 12 Mar 2025 (Monday 10 Mar). Role: source says 'M23 president'; New Times calls him deputy coordinator of AFC/M23. Matches Kinshasa side below.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-004.vn: Narrowed title to the source's 'M23 president' and the Banyamulenge clause to the page's own attribution wording ('According to Bisimwa, the strikes were aimed at...'); that clause rests on the page, not the excerpt. Byline 'by URN'. Party statement (AFC/M23). The page calls him 'M23 president'; other sources call him AFC/M23 deputy coordinator.
src: On Monday, M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa released a statement accusing FARDC soldiers and their allies of deploying fighter jets (Sukhoi) and attack drones to bomb several villages in Minembwe.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-005.s: URN (via The Observer, Uganda) reported that, on Tuesday night, South Kivu vice-governor Jean Jacques Elakano announced that the operation by the army and coalition forces had destroyed all aircraft transporting M23 rebels from Bukavu city, resulting in the deaths of over 10 fighters.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-005.n: Kinshasa-side account of the Minembwe airfield strikes; contrasts with Bisimwa's claim of civilian targets. Date computed from weekday 'Tuesday night' and page date 12 Mar 2025 (11 Mar). Statement kind uncertain; source says 'announced'. Other Elakano comments (airfield used to supply Twirwaneho and Red Tabara; Kaziba as strategic) are on the same page.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-005.vn: Verbatim on retained URN copy. Contrasts with Bisimwa's account (claim 3); both kept. Party statement (provincial government, Kinshasa side); the death toll is the vice-governor's claim, not independently confirmed.
src: on Tuesday night, Jean Jacques Elakano, vice-governor of South Kivu province, announced that the operation by the army and coalition forces successfully destroyed all aircraft transporting M23 rebels from Bukavu city, resulting in the deaths of over 10 fighters.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-006.s: The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that, according to AFC/M23's Bertrand Bisimwa on X, no Munyamulenge could travel to Baraka, Fizi, Uvira or Mwenga, that the Minembwe airstrip was the only means of evacuation for the sick and of delivery of medicine and essential supplies, and that it had been damaged by a government plane.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-006.n: Partisan (AFC/M23 post on X, relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media); evidence of what Bisimwa said, not of the fact. The page calls him 'deputy coordinator' and 'the M23 leader'. The 'government of my country' phrase is Bisimwa's; the page says Sukhoi jets bombed Minembwe villages 'twelve minutes ago' at his posting.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-006.vn: Both passages verbatim on the page (byline James Karuhanga, 10 March 2025). Party statement (AFC/M23) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned media; evidence of what Bisimwa said, not of the damage or its effect on health access.
src: On Monday, March 10, the M23 leader, again took to X, saying that in the morning, "drones were flying over Minembwe, capturing images of targets."

No Munyamulenge can travel to Baraka, Fizi, or Uvira, let alone Mwenga. The only means of evacuation for the sick, the delivery of medicine, and other essential supplies was this airstrip. It has now been damaged by a plane belonging to the government of my country.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-007.s: OCHA reported in its South Kivu situation report that at least 127 women and minor girls were victims of rape in Uvira city during the forced confinement caused by the violent clashes of 15 to 22 February 2025, of whom 54 (43 percent) received medical care within 72 hours.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-007.x: OCHA: at least 127 women and minor girls raped; 54 (43%) treated within 72 hours
r1-SKS-2025Q1-007.n: Uvira city, adjacent to this unit's area; included because it is the main sexual-violence figure in the window and may not be held by the Uvira unit. Perpetrators not attributed by OCHA in this passage. Figures are humanitarian-actor estimates.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-007.vn: 127, 54, 43 % and 15-22 February all verbatim; 'Uvira city' carried by the preceding sentences on the page. Grade B: a single UN situation report, not a documented investigation. No perpetrator named by the source. Figures are OCHA's (compiled with humanitarian partners), for Uvira city ('dans la ville', under 'Territoire d’Uvira' / 'Dans la ville d'Uvira').
src: Au moins 127 femmes et filles mineures ont été victimes de viols durant l'hibernation forcée qu’ont engendré les violents affrontements du 15 au 22 février 2025. Parmi ces victimes, 54 (soit 43 %) ont bénéficié d’une prise en charge médicale dans les 72 heures après l'incident.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-008.s: OCHA reported that many sexual-violence cases in Uvira city went without medical care because of a shortage of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits in several health structures.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-008.n: Shortage reason is stated as a supply shortage; no actor attributed. Classified access_denied as the nearest allowed health value.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-008.vn: Verbatim; the sentence directly follows the 127/54 passage, so 'cases' refers to the rape cases in Uvira city. Supply shortage; no actor attributed by the source.
src: Toutefois, de nombreux cas sont restés sans soins médicaux en raison d’une pénurie de Kits de Protection Post-incident (Kits PEP) dans plusieurs structures de santé.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-009.s: OCHA reported that a cholera epidemic was affecting the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, that 242 cases and ten deaths had been recorded in the two zones as of 10 March 2025, and that the Ruzizi cholera treatment centre, located in Sange, faced a stock-out of medical supplies while case numbers kept rising.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-009.l: Sange (Ruzizi health zone) and Uvira health zones
r1-SKS-2025Q1-009.x: OCHA: 242 cases and 10 deaths as of 10 March 2025 in the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones
r1-SKS-2025Q1-009.n: MSF reinforced its support from 4 March (same OCHA page) - not in the excerpt.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-009.vn: Verbatim; 'cases kept rising' rests on the page beyond the stored excerpt. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: une épidémie de choléra qui sévit dans les zones de santé d’Uvira et de Ruzizi. Au 10 mars 2025, 242 cas et dix décès ont été recensés dans ces deux zones. Le Centre de Traitement du Choléra (CTC) de Ruzizi, situé à Sange, est confronté à une rupture de stock d'intrants médicaux

310 cas de choléra dont 12 décès sont notifiés dans la zone de santé d’Uvira et celle de Ruzizi en territoire d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu), alertent les sources sanitaires de la place. Ce bilan alarmant est enregistré seulement en trois semaines. La zone de santé de Ruzizi en plaine de la Ruzizi compte en elle-même le plus grand nombre de

r1-SKS-2025Q1-010.s: OCHA reported that between 1 and 14 March 2025 clashes between the FARDC and the M23 continued in the Uvira Hauts Plateaux, affecting the localities of Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda and Muranvya.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-010.l: Uvira Hauts Plateaux: Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda, Muranvya
r1-SKS-2025Q1-010.vn: Verbatim on OCHA page, under 'Territoire d’Uvira'. Single UN situation report.
src: Entre le 1er et le 14 mars, des affrontements entre les FARDC et le M23 se sont poursuivis dans les Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira, affectant les localités de Kahololo, Kageregere, Kitembe, Bijombo, Mugete, Mitamba, Magunda et Muranvya

r1-SKS-2025Q1-011.s: OCHA reported that humanitarian actors estimated more than 554 000 people were affected by the crisis in Uvira city, including 270 000 internally displaced people, of whom more than 126 000 fled to the Ruzizi plain in February 2025.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-011.x: OCHA: 554 000+ affected; 270 000 IDPs; 126 000+ fled to the Ruzizi plain in February 2025
r1-SKS-2025Q1-011.n: Estimates by humanitarian actors, as OCHA states.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-011.vn: All figures verbatim; estimates attributed to humanitarian actors as OCHA states.
src: Dans la ville d'Uvira, les acteurs humanitaires estiment que plus de 554 000 personnes ont été affectées par la crise, dont 270 000 déplacés internes. Parmi ces déplacés, plus de 126 000 ont fui vers la plaine de Ruzizi au mois de février 2025.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-012.s: Kivutimes reported that Twirwaneho and Wazalendo (led, it said, by Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi) fought at Mikenge, Itombwe sector, from the morning of Monday 3 March 2025; according to local sources Wazalendo dislodged Twirwaneho, which had held the centre for more than two weeks, and Twirwaneho fighters fled toward Kalingi; around 18 heures men of Sematama counter-attacked with heavy weapons and reoccupied Mikenge.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-012.a: Wazalendo (led by Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi, per the source); Twirwaneho (men of Sematama)
r1-SKS-2025Q1-012.n: Local outlet (Kivutimes, Bukavu/Uvira area), single source. Page says Twirwaneho held Mikenge 'for more than two weeks' before 3 March (since before 17 Feb), which does not support the Facebook-snippet lead of a FARDC/Wazalendo recapture on 24 Feb; that lead was not confirmed by any outlet I could open. Actualite.cd (26 Feb) says Mikenge passed to Twirwaneho after fighting on Tuesday 25 Feb. Spelling 'Twigwaneho' in headline, 'twigwaneho' in text.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-012.vn: Every clause verbatim on the retained page (byline Lubunga lavoix, 4 March 2025). Single local outlet relaying local sources. The same page closes saying Mikenge 'reste sous contrôle des Twirwaneho, qui ont profité du retrait des FARDC'. Conflicts in sequence with Actualite.cd (26 Feb: Mikenge passed to Twirwaneho after fighting with the FARDC on Tuesday); both kept. The page's grammar leaves it slightly ambiguous whether 'dirigés par Ebuela Seba' qualifies Wazalendo only. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Des affrontements violents opposant les groupes armés Twirwaneho et Wazalendo dirigés par Ebuela Seba alias Mtetezi, ont été signalés depuis la matinée de ce lundi 03 Mars 2025 dans le village de Mikenge

Selon des sources locales contactées par la rédaction de Kivutimes dans la zone, les wazalendo en Provence de kipupu et Tulambo ont lancé des attaques farouches contre les positions de twigwaneho qui occupaient ce centre économique du secteur d’itombwe il y a plus de deux semaines.
Ces attaques simultanées ont permis aux wazalendo à déloger les miliciens twigwaneho qui ont fui vers kalingi une localité environnant la cité de minembwe.
c’est vers la soirée aux environs de 18 heures que les hommes de Sematama ont fait une riposte rigoureuse avec des armes lourdes contre les wazalendo et occupé de nouveau le village Mikenge.

r1-SKS-2025Q1-013.s: Kivutimes reported that after occupying Mikenge the Wazalendo set fire at midday to the camp of internally displaced people that housed mostly members of the Banyamulenge community, and that no source had confirmed a precise human toll although there were victims on both sides.
r1-SKS-2025Q1-013.l: Mikenge IDP camp, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory
r1-SKS-2025Q1-013.x: no precise toll confirmed by any source (Kivutimes)
r1-SKS-2025Q1-013.n: Corroborated in kind by the NHRC statement carried by Kivutimes on 13 March (separate claim).
r1-SKS-2025Q1-013.vn: Verbatim on page; perpetrator as the source names it. Allegation by a single local outlet citing local sources; the 'victims on both sides' line refers to the day's clashes generally, not specifically to the camp.
