Selon des sources locales, les combats de ce jeudi 6 novembre 2025, ont été particulièrement violents autour de la localité de Tuwetuwe, où la coalition rebelle a tenté de s’emparer d’une position tenue par les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC).
Appuyés par les Wazalendo du FDCC, les militaires congolais ont réussi à repousser l’attaque après plusieurs heures d’affrontements.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-013.s: Kivu Morning Post quoted a Wazalendo spokesperson in the area as saying that on the morning of Tuesday 4 November 2025 intense fighting broke out around Mikenge between Wazalendo of the FDCC of General Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin and 'the enemies of the AFC Twitwaneho M23, Red Tabara FNL ZABAMPEMA', and that the Wazalendo had already occupied a large part of Mikenge, including its stadium, and all of Bilalombili had fallen.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-013.l: Mikenge and Bilalombili, Hauts Plateaux (Itombwe), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-013.a: Wazalendo of the FDCC (Gen. Kakobanya Nakalambi Justin) vs 'AFC Twitwaneho M23, Red Tabara FNL ZABAMPEMA' (spelling as printed)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-013.n: Partisan claim: the Wazalendo's own account of the battle, relayed by an outlet; no Twirwaneho or AFC/M23 account of the same day in this source. The same article says the fighting followed an alert by Twirwaneho and former senator Moïse Nyarugabo about the encirclement and humanitarian blockade of Minembwe by Burundian and Congolese armies (separate claim). Social-media posts (not fetched, leads only) show Moïse Nyarugabo alleging drone strikes on Mikenge around 15 Nov.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-013.vn: Partisan (Wazalendo spokesperson) account, attributed. Date and opposing-force wording are in the same quotation on the page but outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap).
src: les wazalendo du FDCC du Général KAKOBANYA NAKALAMBI Justin ont déjà occupé une grande partie de MIKENGE, tout BILALOMBILI est déjà tombé, une partie de MIKENGE également tombé y compris le stade du dit lieu” , a déclaré à Kivu Morning Post un porte-parole des Wazalendo dans la zone.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the fighting around Mikenge followed an alert by Twirwaneho and by former senator Moïse Nyarugabo about the encirclement and humanitarian blockade of Minembwe and several Banyamulenge villages by the Burundian and Congolese armies.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-014.l: Minembwe and Banyamulenge villages, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-014.a: Burundian and Congolese armies (alleged by Twirwaneho and Moïse Nyarugabo)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-014.n: Allegation by a party (Twirwaneho, an AFC/M23-affiliated group) and a Banyamulenge politician, relayed by a Goma outlet. The Burundian army's reply of 12 Nov (BBC Gahuza) and the OCHA access findings are in other claims in the project. No Congolese government reply found in this page.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-014.vn: Removed '4 November' from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the date field carries it and the page prints 'mardi 4 novembre 2025'). The blockade is Twirwaneho's and Nyarugabo's allegation, relayed. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only).
src: Ces affrontements surviennent après l’alerte de Twirwaneho et de l’ex-sénateur Moïse Nyarugabo concernant l’encerclement et le blocus humanitaire de Minembwe ainsi que de plusieurs villages banyamulenge par les armées burundaise et congolaise.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-015.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that in the Ruzizi plain at Uvira, a precarious calm was reported at Katogota, an area under the control of AFC/M23 troops.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-015.l: Katogota, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-015.n: Radio Maendeleo is a Bukavu community radio; page dated 2025-12-08 and refers to Sunday 7 December. Single source for this place; corroborated in general terms by the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani barometer of 15 Dec listing Katogota among clashes. Handle with the Luvungi claim below.
src: Plus loin, dans la plaine de la Ruzizi à Uvira, l’on rapporte un calme précaire à Katogota, une zone sous contrôle des troupes de l’AFC/M23.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-016.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that AFC/M23 troops 'would have advanced' to Luberizi and 'would have taken' control of a good part of Luvungi and Lubarika, according to residents who spoke of a notable absence of FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian army elements since the evening of Saturday 6 December.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-016.l: Luberizi, Luvungi, Lubarika, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-016.n: Conditional tense in the source ('auraient'); resident accounts only. SOS Médias Burundi (7 Dec, other claim) lists Katogota, Luvungi, Bwegera, Luberizi and Mutarule as recently taken by the M23. The date is the Saturday-evening start of the absence described; reported 2025-12-08.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-016.vn: Verbatim; conditional ('auraient') kept; residents' account. '23' flag is the M23 name. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only).
src: Ces dernières auraient avancé jusqu’à Luberizi et auraient pris le contrôle d’une bonne partie de Luvungi et de Lubarika, à en croire des habitants sur place qui parlent d’une absence remarquable des FARDC, Wazalendo et des éléments de l’armée burundaise depuis samedi 06 décembre dans la soirée.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more than thirty people were killed on Sunday evening in the town of Sange after a bomb exploded in the middle of an inhabited area; according to several testimonies, the blast followed internal clashes between FARDC soldiers, a group of Congolese soldiers returning from the front and trying to flee towards Uvira having reportedly been stopped at the Sange bridge by another FARDC detachment; the provisional toll was at least 7 Burundian soldiers and 7 civilians, plus an undetermined number of Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.l: Sange, Uvira territory (Ruzizi plain), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.a: FARDC detachments (per witnesses cited by the source); cause not established
r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.x: SOS Médias Burundi: more than 30 killed; provisional toll of at least 7 Burundian soldiers and 7 civilians plus an undetermined number of Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo
r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.n: Burundi-based outlet, single account; cause contested: unfetched social-media posts (leads only) say a long-range bomb was fired from Bugarama (Rwanda) on Sange, and a TV5Monde snippet (15 Dec; page not retrievable) quotes a witness that bombs fell 'whose origin was unknown, M23 or the army'. Toll differs across leads (12 dead in an unfetched post; 'nine' in the TV5 snippet). Dateline 7 Dec 2025 (Sunday) so the day is stated; page published 8 Dec. No FARDC, Burundian or AFC/M23 statement on this event found.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-017.vn: Removed the dateline (not in any excerpt; page prints 'Bukavu, 7 décembre 2025' with 'dimanche soir', which fixes the day). Witnesses' account kept attributed and conditional; the page adds 'L’échange de tirs aurait dégénéré jusqu’au lancer d’un explosif'. Single outlet; cause contested by other unfetched leads (see raw notes). Cause contested: SOS Médias Burundi's witnesses describe an intra-FARDC exchange of fire; other leads (not fetched) blame long-range fire from Rwanda or bombs of unknown origin. Tolls differ across leads.
src: Plus de trente personnes ont été tuées dimanche soir dans la cité de Sange, au Sud-Kivu, après l’explosion d’une bombe survenue en pleine zone habitée, alors que les forces congolaises — appuyées par l’armée burundaise et des miliciens Wazalendo — subissent une pression croissante dans la plaine de la Rusizi.

Selon plusieurs témoignages, la déflagration est survenue après des affrontements internes entre soldats des FARDC. Un groupe de militaires congolais revenant du front et tentant, selon des témoins, de fuir vers Uvira, aurait été stoppé au pont de Sange par un autre détachement FARDC.
Le bilan provisoire fait état d’au moins 7 militaires burundais, 7 civils, ainsi qu’un nombre encore indéterminé de soldats congolais et de miliciens Wazalendo tués.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.s: Congovirtuel reported that the Burundian lieutenant-colonel killed in the Rusizi plain was identified as Lt-Col Athanase Minani, a former FAB officer who commanded the 8th battalion of the Burundian contingent in the DRC; it said the incident, around 4 December 2025, also killed three of his guards and at least 20 Burundian soldiers during fighting intensified that week. SOS Médias Burundi likewise named Lt-Col Athanase Minani as the first senior officer the Burundian army had lost since its official intervention in eastern Congo in March 2023.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.l: Rusizi (Ruzizi) plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.a: Burundian army: Lt-Col Athanase Minani, commander of the 8th battalion of the Burundian contingent in the DRC, per Congovirtuel
r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.x: Congovirtuel: Minani, three guards and at least 20 Burundian soldiers killed; SOS Médias Burundi: not given beyond 'several other young officers' (see notes)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.n: Two independent-looking outlets name the same officer; both are local/analysis outlets and Burundi's own confirmation was not fetched (a Burundian presidential decree of 1 July 2025 promoting an 'MINANI Athanase' to Lt-Col appeared in a search snippet; not fetched, lead only). A further 'Rwandan outlet' IGIHE report (6 Dec) and africa-insight (9 Dec) not retrievable/fetched. The Congovirtuel page says 'around 4 December'; SOS Médias dates the clashes from 1 Dec. SOS also says 'several other young officers' were killed. Congovirtuel is a Kinshasa-leaning analysis site.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-018.vn: Statement unchanged; actor corrected to drop 'FDNB', which neither page prints. Independence: SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec, Bukavu dateline, byline Adam Ntwari) and Congovirtuel (9 Dec, byline Aimé Binda) cite no common source; Congovirtuel's details (8th battalion, ~4 Dec, three guards, 20 soldiers, 'M23 drone strike' in its headline) are not in SOS, so it is not a relay of SOS; but Congovirtuel names no source at all, so a shared upstream (e.g. IGIHE or Burundian social media) cannot be ruled out. The death and name are carried by two outlets; the circumstances only by Congovirtuel. Death and identity reported by two outlets; battalion, date and companions' deaths rest on Congovirtuel alone, which gives no source. Congovirtuel's headline attributes the death to an M23 drone strike; SOS Médias does not give a cause.
src: Ancien officier des Forces armées burundaises (ex-FAB), le lieutenant-colonel Minani commandait le 8e bataillon du contingent burundais en République démocratique du Congo (RDC) au moment de sa mort. Cet incident, survenu aux alentours du 4 décembre 2025, a également entraîné la mort de trois de ses gardes et d’au moins 20 soldats burundais lors de combats intensifiés cette semaine-là.

Lors de ces affrontements qui se sont intensifiés depuis le lundi 1er décembre, l’armée burundaise a perdu le premier haut gradé depuis son intervention officielle à l’est du Congo en mars 2023. Il s’agit du lieutenant-colonel Athanase Minani.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that the fear of population in the Tanganyika sector of Fizi was precipitated and aggravated by the movements of FARDC, Burundian and Wazalendo soldiers fleeing the Uvira front to take refuge in Fizi; it quoted Sammy Amimo, vice-president of civil society in Fizi territory, as saying Mboko town was overwhelmed by displaced people, with more than 18 000 families having arrived although the rebels had not yet reached the Tanganyika sector.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.l: Mboko, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.a: soldiers of the FARDC, Burundian army and Wazalendo (movements), per Actualite.cd sources
r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.x: Sammy Amimo (civil society): more than 18 000 families in Mboko
r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.n: Civil-society figure, not verified by humanitarian agencies. Marks Mboko as not yet reached by rebels on 12 Dec; Actualite.cd of 22 Dec has the AFC-M23 holding Mboko.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-019.vn: Verbatim; 18 000 families is a civil-society figure. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only).
src: Mais selon des sources d’ACTUALITE.CD dans la région, cette peur a été surtout précipitée et aggravée par les mouvements des militaires FARDC, burundais et wazalendo fuyant le front à Uvira pour se réfugier dans le Fizi.
La cité de Mboko est débordée par les déplacés, plus de 18 000 familles sont venues ici bien que les rebelles ne soient pas encore arrivés dans le secteur de Tanganyika.
a dit à ACTUALITE.CD Sammy Amimo, le vice-président de la société civile dans le territoire de Fizi.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-020.s: FiziMedia reported, according to several concordant local sources, an attempted assassination on Tuesday 23 December 2025 at about 7 a.m. at Mwandiga against Mwami Ngena Milingita, chief of the Balala-Sud grouping (Mutambala sector, Fizi territory); the alleged author was said to be an individual claiming to belong to the Wazalendo CNPSC movement led by William Amuri Yakutumba, named Efaro and acting under a commander known as Asumani; no victim was recorded.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-020.l: Mwandiga, Balala-Sud grouping, Mutambala sector, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-020.a: an individual claiming to belong to Wazalendo CNPSC (William Amuri Yakutumba), per the source
r1-SKS-2025Q4-020.n: Single local outlet (FiziMedia, Fizi). The residents' statement was published on WhatsApp per the source; no official reaction yet at publication. Named as the source prints. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-020.vn: All on the page; Mwandiga and 'no victim' outside the stored excerpts (excerpt gap). Conditional ('serait', 's’agirait') kept as 'said to be'. Names as printed. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: FiziMedia (23 Dec 2025) supports every clause with the hedges kept ('présumé auteur serait', 'Il s'agirait'); the place (Mwandiga), the 'concordant local sources' attribution and 'no victim recorded' are not in the stored excerpts, so those passages are added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: FiziMedia (23 Dec 2025) supports every clause with the hedges kept ('présumé auteur serait', 'Il s'agirait'); the place (Mwandiga), the 'concordant local sources' attribution and 'no victim recorded' are not in the stored excerpts, so those passages are added.
src: Une tentative d’assassinat a visé, ce mardi 23 décembre 2025 vers 7 heures du matin, Sa Majesté Mwami Ngena Milingita, chef du groupement Balala-Sud, dans le secteur de Mutambala, territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.

D’après les informations recueillies sur place, le présumé auteur serait un individu se réclamant du mouvement Wazalendo CNPSC, dirigé par William Amuri Yakutumba. Il s’agirait d’un certain Efaro, originaire du même groupement, agissant sous les ordres d’un commandant connu sous le nom d’Asumani.
L’incident s’est produit à Mwandiga, selon plusieurs sources locales concordantes.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.s: SOSOYAMBOKA.NET, relaying an OCHA communiqué, reported that OCHA recalled that since January 2025 the Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux area had seen a resurgence of armed clashes with serious incidents, including attacks on civilians and the pillaging of health structures, that since May 2025 the Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe axis had been completely closed, controlled or blocked by armed groups, and that in August 2025 armed actors at Point Zéro reaffirmed their refusal of any humanitarian access; it added that, according to South Kivu's Commission Mouvement de Population (October 2025), close to 172 000 displaced and returnees were enclaved without access to essential goods or aid.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.l: Minembwe, Itombwe and Hauts Plateaux health zones; Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe axis, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.a: armed groups controlling or blocking the axis (not named by the source)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.x: OCHA / CMP South Kivu (October 2025): close to 172 000 displaced and returnees enclaved
r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.n: Relay: the page (published 2025-11-25) is an aggregator that presents the OCHA mission communiqué; the OCHA original was not located (Actualite.cd of 2025-11-25 carries a related OCHA alert already cited elsewhere). The page's text also gives June 2025 medicine blockage at Mulima and July-September 2025 child mortality at Minembwe HGR (not claimed here: before the unit period). Armed actors are not named in the page; Twirwaneho and Burundian-army roles are claimed by other parties (see Kivu Morning Post claim).
r1-SKS-2025Q4-021.vn: Aggregator relay (SOSOYAMBOKA.NET, 25 Nov 2025) of an OCHA mission communiqué; origin set to OCHA and graded B as one credible UN origin, not A, because the OCHA original was not located and the relay contains an error (it places these South Kivu health zones in 'Nord-Kivu'). Relayed from OCHA by an aggregator; OCHA's original communiqué was not located. The 172 000 figure is a Commission Mouvement de Population estimate cited by OCHA.
ent: Commission Mouvement de Population du Sud-Kivu
src: OCHA rapelle que depuis janvier 2025, la région est le théâtre d’une recrudescence d’affrontements armés, accompagnée d’incidents graves : attaques contre les civils, pillage de structures de santé et destructions de biens essentiels.

Il souligne que depuis mai 2025, l’axe stratégique Fizi–Lusuku–Point Zéro–Mikenge–Minembwe est totalement fermé, contrôlé ou bloqué par des groupes armés, plongeant la région dans un isolement quasi complet.
En août 2025, lors d’une mission d’accès à Point Zéro, OCHA rapporte que des acteurs armés ont réaffirmé leur refus de tout accès humanitaire.

D’après les estimations de la Commission Mouvement de Population du Sud-Kivu (octobre 2025), près de 172 000 personnes déplacées et retournées se trouvent aujourd’hui enclavées, sans accès aux biens essentiels ni à l’aide humanitaire.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-022.s: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani stated in its civic barometer that Burundi, whose troops fight alongside the FARDC, had deployed more than 10 000 soldiers in the high and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga. The figure carries a footnote (6) to a Koaci.com article whose URL is dated 7 February 2025 and refers to 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers deployed. The same barometer says that after the clashes in the Ruzizi plain and the capture of Uvira by the AFC-M23 many Burundian soldiers fled the fighting to return to their country, and 'quelques milliers' (a few thousand) remained in the high and middle plateaux of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-022.l: High and middle plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-022.x: Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani: more than 10 000 Burundian soldiers (figure footnoted to an outside press article)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-022.n: Local civil-society coalition (South Kivu); the figure is footnoted to another source in the PDF and is not an independent count. The superscript '6' is part of the extracted text. Burundi's official acknowledgement of troop numbers not found here.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-022.vn: Removed the issue number and coverage dates from the statement (no excerpt prints them; they are in the source title). The figure is not the coalition's own count: its footnote 6 cites a Koaci article URL dated 2025/02/07 headed '10000 soldats burundais supplementaires deployes', i.e. a February 2025 report of additional troops, which the barometer presents as a deployment total. The same page adds that after Uvira's fall many Burundian soldiers fled home but 'quelques milliers' remained in the Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira plateaux. The 10 000 figure is footnoted to a February 2025 press report of additional Burundian troops, not a December 2025 count; the barometer also says only a few thousand Burundian soldiers remained after Uvira fell. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: footnote 6 to a Koaci.com article dated 2025/02/07 on 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: after the fall of Uvira many Burundian soldiers went home; a few thousand remained 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-020: The statement presents the 10 000 figure as a current deployment. The barometer footnotes it to a Koaci article of 7 February 2025 about 10 000 additional troops, and the same page says only a few thousand remained after Uvira fell. The statement needs both caveats so that a February 2025 press figure does not read as a December 2025 count.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): footnote 6 to a Koaci.com article dated 2025/02/07 on 10 000 additional Burundian soldiers; after the fall of Uvira many Burundian soldiers went home; a few thousand remained | cut 'The figure is not the coalition's own count' (an inference; the page prints only the footnote)
src: Le Burundi, dont les troupes combattent aux côtés des FARDC, a déployé plus de 10 000 soldats6 dans les hauts et moyens plateaux d’Uvira, Fizi et Mwenga.

À la suite des affrontements dans la plaine de la Ruzizi et de la prise d’Uvira par l’AFC-M23, de nombreux soldats burundais ont fui les combats pour retourner dans leur pays. Plusieurs centaines de militaires, policiers et responsables congolais ont également traversé la frontière pour se réfugier au Burundi. Toutefois, quelques milliers de militaires burundais restent toujours présents en République démocratique du Congo, notamment dans les hauts et moyens plateaux de Mwenga, Fizi et Uvira.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-023.s: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that the AFC-M23 rebels had issued a communiqué asking Burundi to withdraw its forces and proposing the opening of a humanitarian corridor to facilitate their return.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-023.l: Eastern DRC (Burundian forces in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga plateaux)
r1-SKS-2025Q4-023.n: Second-hand report of the communiqué; the communiqué itself, its date and text were not located. Treat as 'AFC/M23 says' via a civil-society monitor.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-023.vn: Verbatim (barometer p.4). Second-hand: footnote 7 says the message was given by the deputy chief of staff of the ARC (AFC-M23's army), General Byamungu, in a speech at Uvira, which differs from the body's 'communiqué'; date not given. The barometer's footnote attributes this message to a speech at Uvira by the deputy chief of staff of the AFC/M23's armed wing, not a written communiqué.
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 ont diffusé un communiqué dans lequel ils demandent au Burundi de retirer ses forces, proposant l’ouverture d’un corridor humanitaire pour faciliter leur retour

r1-SKS-2025Q4-024.s: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani reported that Burundi had affirmed its will to keep its troops on Congolese soil and to continue operations alongside the FARDC, in line with the bilateral partnership, according to its foreign minister, Édouard BIZIMANA.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-024.n: Second-hand; the original statement/interview and its date were not located here (other claims in the project record Bizimana's RFI interview, per Iwacu). Superscript '8' is a footnote marker in the extracted text.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-024.vn: Verbatim (barometer p.4). Second-hand; footnote 8 cites a Jeune Afrique article ('le Burundi a le droit de se défendre s'il est attaqué selon Édouard Bizimana'), so the statement originates in that interview; date not given. excerpt_en flags checked: the English renders the excerpt alone (capitalisation/expanded acronyms only). Second-hand: the barometer cites a Jeune Afrique interview with the minister for this position.
src: De son côté, le Burundi a affirmé sa volonté de maintenir ses troupes sur le sol congolais et de poursuivre les opérations aux côtés des FARDC, conformément au partenariat bilatéral entre les deux pays afin d’assurer aussi la sécurité de son pays, à en croire son Ministre des affaires étrangères, Édouard BIZIMANA8.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-025.s: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said in its barometer no. 9 (November-15 December 2025) that in zones officially under government administration the massive presence of Wazalendo militias was causing growing concern among the population, and that women were not spared the violence of these militias: some were publicly whipped and stripped, others were victims of rape and of mass sexual violence in front of their relatives.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-025.l: Zones officially under government administration (places not specified by the source), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-025.n: General statement by a civil-society coalition: no places, dates, counts or survivors given. Included as a lead for the period; location is not specified in the source so it may include areas outside this unit. The barometer is hosted on ipb.org.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-025.vn: On the page (barometer p.7-8). General allegation without places, dates or counts; '9' is the issue number printed in the title ('Numéro 09'). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-019: Attribution drift: the excerpts do not contain the clause 'Wazalendo militias commit brutality against civilians'. Excerpt 0 speaks only of 'growing concern' at their massive presence, and the violence against women is the one act the excerpts attribute to 'ces milices'. The amended statement stays with the excerpts and keeps the Coalition's attribution. The allegation is general, with no places, dates or counts. No search spent; no Wazalendo or FARDC response was found in the input.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: Dans les zones officiellement placées sous administration gouvernementale, la présence massive des milices Wazalendo continue de susciter une inquiétude croissante parmi les populations.

Des femmes ne sont pas épargnées par ces violences de la part de ces milices. Elles sont aussi publiquement fouettées et déshabillées. D’autres sont victimes de viols et d’autres de violences sexuelles en masse et devant leurs familiers.

r1-SKS-2025Q4-026.s: The Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani listed among the situation's consequences that populations of the middle and high plateaux of Fizi and Mwenga were besieged and deprived of any humanitarian assistance, notably in the villages of Minembwe, Mikenge, Ndondo and Kahololo and surroundings.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-026.l: Minembwe, Mikenge, Ndondo, Kahololo and surroundings (Fizi and Mwenga plateaux), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2025Q4-026.n: Bullet item in the barometer's table of effects; corroborated in substance by the OCHA access findings in the SOSOYAMBOKA claim and by the BBC Gahuza/Twirwaneho blockade accounts already in the project.
r1-SKS-2025Q4-026.vn: Verbatim (barometer table of effects). No actor named.
src: Des populations des moyens et hauts plateaux de Fizi et Mwenga assiégés et privés de toute assistance humanitaire, notamment dans les villages de Minembwe,Mikenge, Ndondo et Kahololo et ses environs.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that the village of Point zéro, on the boundary between Fizi and Mwenga territories on the Mitumba range, in the high plateaux, passed under the control of Twirwaneho fighters, allies of the AFC/M23 rebels, from the morning of Friday 16 January 2026; according to its sources in the area, the fighters attacked the FARDC position that morning, forcing the army to withdraw.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-001.a: Twirwaneho (described as allies of AFC/M23); FARDC
r1-SKS-2026Q1-001.n: Same event as existing r1-UV-2026Q1-007 / UC-BI-FDLR-025 lines (Ebuteli, GoE) but a separate local source; SOS Médias Burundi also dates the fall to 16 January.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-001.vn: Removed 'two days of fighting' and 'FARDC supported by Wazalendo': this page prints neither (those details are in the SOS Médias Burundi article, claim 1). Page says fighting had been intense at Tuwetuwe since Thursday 15 January. Same event as existing Point Zéro lines; separate local outlet.
src: Le village “Point zéro” situé à la limite entre les territoires de Fizi et de Mwenga sur la chaîne de Mitumba, dans le hauts plateaux est passé sous contrôle des combattants Twirwaneho, alliés des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 depui le matin de ce vendredi 16 janvier 2026

r1-SKS-2026Q1-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that after Twirwaneho took Point Zéro on Friday 16 January, elements of FARDC, of the Burundian national defence force (printed 'FNDB') and Wazalendo groups withdrew to the localities of Mulima and Mutambala.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-002.l: Point Zéro to Mulima and Mutambala (Fizi)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-002.a: Twirwaneho; FARDC, FDNB ('FNDB' in source), Wazalendo
r1-SKS-2026Q1-002.n: Single Burundi-based outlet citing local sources. Source date 17 Jan; fall dated 16 Jan by the source.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-002.vn: Figure 16 is printed on the page ('ce vendredi 16 janvier'), not in the stored excerpt; page also says the fall followed two days of fighting against FARDC backed by Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo.
ent: Force nationale de défense du Burundi (FNDB)
src: Après la prise de la zone par les rebelles, des éléments des FARDC, de la Force nationale de défense du Burundi (FNDB) et des groupes Wazalendo se sont repliés vers les localités de Mulima et Mutambala

r1-SKS-2026Q1-003.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that FARDC, supported by the Burundian defence force (FDNB) and Wazalendo militiamen, retook the locality of Point Zéro in Fizi territory on 'Friday', from Twirwaneho fighters.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-003.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date: the article has a Bukavu dateline of 31 January and also says fighting continued 'ce samedi 31 janvier', so the Friday is 30 January. Single outlet citing local sources in Minembwe; mentions combat drones used.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-003.vn: Excerpt exact and supports the retake; excerpt_en flag is only translated proper nouns (Armed Forces of the DRC). Local sources in Minembwe say combat drones were used. Date 30 January computed from 'ce vendredi' in an article datelined Bukavu, 31 January 2026, which also reports fighting 'ce samedi 31 janvier'.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) et des miliciens Wazalendo, ont repris ce vendredi le contrôle de la localité stratégique de Point Zéro, dans le territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-004.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a Congolese army drone had reportedly bombed the commercial centre of Madegu, wounding three civilians.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-004.x: SOS Médias Burundi: three civilians wounded
r1-SKS-2026Q1-004.n: Residents' account relayed by one outlet; the day is not stated for the strike itself. No FARDC account found in this source.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-004.vn: Removed '31 January' from the statement (no excerpt prints it) and kept the conditional. Date stays approximate: page says 'Après la reprise de Point Zéro, les affrontements se sont poursuivis ce samedi 31 janvier'. Residents' account; the source uses the conditional ('aurait bombardé'). The strike's day is not given; the article reports it right after fighting 'ce samedi 31 janvier'.
src: Des habitants rapportent qu’un drone de l’armée congolaise aurait bombardé le centre commercial de Madegu, faisant trois civils blessés.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, an honorary Congolese senator, said that on Thursday 12 February 2026 the FARDC coalition, supported by drones and mortars aimed at the villages of Minembwe, killed a 101-year-old woman named Mukuzakabano Elisabeth; the outlet's next sentence says two other women were wounded in this attack, during which the hospital of Bidegu was bombed.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.l: Bidegu and Minembwe villages (Hauts Plateaux, Fizi)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.a: FARDC coalition (drones, mortars), per Moïse Nyarugabo
r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.x: Kivu Morning Post (citing Nyarugabo): one killed (aged 101), two women wounded
r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.n: Single account from a Banyamulenge-community political figure (an interested party), relayed by a Goma outlet; not independently verified. FARDC account of the same period: see the Radio Okapi 2 Feb claim (denies fighting in populated areas). Article also says shelling of Kalingi, Bidegu, Rubemba, Karongi, Mukoko and Ilundu on 10-12 Feb per Nyarugabo.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-005.vn: Narrowed attribution: the hospital/wounded sentence is the outlet's narration, not a quoted Nyarugabo statement. Name printed as given. Single account from an interested party (Banyamulenge political figure), relayed by one outlet; the wounded women and the hospital bombing are in the outlet's narration following his account, not in a direct quote. No independent confirmation found; the FARDC says it does not fight in populated areas (Radio Okapi, 2 Feb).
src: a déclaré Moïse Nyarugabo, sénateur honoraire congolais. Il explique que, le jeudi 12 février 2026, la coalition FARDC, appuyée par des drones et des mortiers dont les canons sont dirigés vers les villages de Minembwe, a tué une vieille dame de 101 ans, du nom de Mukuzakabano Elisabeth.
Deux autres femmes ont été blessées lors de cette attaque au cours de laquelle l’hôpital de Bidegu a été bombardé.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-006.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Angolan Presidency announced in a communiqué on Thursday a ceasefire between Kinshasa and AFC/M23 from 18 February 2026, an announcement it said came as the FARDC had launched an offensive on several villages of Minembwe.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-006.n: Date computed from weekday ('Jeudi') and article date 13 Feb. Context for the highlands fighting; the Angolan communiqué itself was not fetched.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-006.vn: Removed '(12 February 2026)' from the statement: the excerpt prints only 'Jeudi'. Second clause is on the page. Announcement date (12 February) computed from 'Jeudi' in an article dated 13 February; the Angolan communiqué itself was not fetched.
src: Jeudi, dans un communiqué, la Présidence angolaise a annoncé un cessez-le-feu entre Kinshasa et l’AFC/M23 à partir du 18 février 2026.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 accused the FARDC of multiple ceasefire violations despite the negotiation process under way in Doha, and said it was open to any peace and de-escalation initiative.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-007.n: Party account relayed by media; the AFC/M23 communiqué itself not found. Date is article date.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-007.vn: Party statement relayed by media; second clause on the page, not in the excerpt. Date is article date.
src: L’AFC/M23 a accusé les FARDC de violations multiples du cessez-le-feu malgré le processus de négociation en cours à Doha.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola Sud operations in South Kivu, Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, said on Monday 2 February that the army had been fighting for five days to retake Minembwe, regarded as the stronghold of Twirwaneho and its allies.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-008.a: FARDC (Sukola Sud operations) vs Twirwaneho, AFC/M23, RED Tabara, Gumino
r1-SKS-2026Q1-008.n: Radio Okapi (local radio). Casualty claim ('more than 35 combatants neutralised') is the FARDC's own and unverified.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-008.vn: Statement as reported is accurately captured; the date 2 February is on the page. Grade B is for the fact that he said it; the content is a party account. He also claimed 'more than 35 combatants neutralised' the day before and described the enemy as M23-AFC backed by the Rwandan army allied to Twirwaneho, Gumino and RED Tabara: party claims, unverified.
src: Selon le porte-parole des opérations Sukola Sud au Sud-Kivu, le sous-lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, l’armée combat depuis cinq jours pour reprendre le contrôle de Minembwe, considéré comme le fief des Twirwaneho et de leurs alliés.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, FARDC spokesperson, said the enemy was dropping bombs blindly in populated areas where civilians were, while the regular army 'does not fight in agglomerations' and protects the population.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-009.n: FARDC account only; set against Twirwaneho-side and community accounts of FARDC drone/mortar strikes on Minembwe villages (Kivu Morning Post 13 Feb; SOS Médias Burundi 1 Feb). Quote is in the source inside quotation marks, attributed to Mbuyi Reagan in the preceding sentence.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-009.vn: Quote verbatim, attributed on the page. Partisan denial; contrasts with residents' and Banyamulenge-community accounts of FARDC drone and mortar strikes (SOS Médias Burundi 1 Feb; Kivu Morning Post 13 Feb).
src: Face à ces pertes, ils larguent des bombes à l’aveuglette dans les agglomérations où se trouve la population civile. Mais nous, l’armée régulière, nous ne combattons pas dans les agglomérations, nous protégeons la population

r1-SKS-2026Q1-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that the administrator of Fizi territory, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, said the number of internally displaced people was approaching one million across Fizi territory, and that fighting on Thursday 5 February at 'Point Zéro' caused a new mass displacement.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-010.a: FARDC vs armed groups Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android and Vijana Power (per Radio Okapi)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-010.x: Samy Badibanga Kalonji (administrator): 'plus d'un million' (approaching one million) internally displaced in Fizi territory
r1-SKS-2026Q1-010.n: Single official's estimate, unverified and not broken down; he says it includes people displaced last year and recently, from Fizi, Uvira city, Mwenga, Kabambare (Maniema) and parts of Tanganyika. Compare Mercy Corps/OCHA household counts.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-010.vn: Statement accurate. Actor corrected: the page names the armed groups as Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android and Vijana Power ('Les combats ont opposé les FARDC aux groupes armés Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, FNL Zabampema, Android et Vijana Power'); it does not name Gumino or Wazalendo for this fighting. Single official's estimate; his direct quote says 'plus d'un million'. He says it includes people from Fizi, Uvira city, Mwenga, Kabambare (Maniema) and parts of Tanganyika.
src: L’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, reformule son appel à une aide humanitaire d’urgence en faveur des personnes rendues vulnérables par ces guerres à répétition. Selon lui, le nombre de déplacés internes avoisine désormais un million sur l’ensemble du territoire de Fizi.
Les combats de jeudi 5 février, dans la petite contrée communément appelée « Point Zéro », ont provoqué un nouveau déplacement massif de populations.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Kalonji Badibanga, said displaced people in Fizi territory were sheltering in schools and churches, and that the Tanganyika lakeshore, a focus of cholera and measles, exposed children to major epidemic risks.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-011.l: Lake Tanganyika shore, Makobola-Mboko, Fizi-centre, Point Zéro Kwa Mulima (Fizi)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-011.a: not applicable (epidemic context); displacement from fighting between AFC-M23 and FARDC
r1-SKS-2026Q1-011.n: Official statement of an administrator; no case counts given. Not an attack on health care; recorded as epidemic context.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-011.vn: Supported by page; epidemic context, not an attack on health care. Name order differs from the 7 Feb article ('Samy Badibanga Kalonji'). Schools/churches detail is Radio Okapi's narration. Date is the publication date.
src: « Le littoral du Tanganyika, foyer de choléra et rougeole, expose particulièrement les enfants à des risques épidémiques majeurs. », déplore M. Badibanga.

Ces populations, venues notamment d'Uvira et de différentes zones de Fizi, se concentrent sur quatre axes principaux : le littoral du lac Tanganyika, Makobola-Mboko, Fizi-centre et Point Zéro Kwa Mulima.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-012.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo have recovered Mikenge since Sunday 1 March, according to Pacifique Kararuka, president of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise at Kipupu.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-012.n: Also reported by SOS Médias Burundi (existing r1-ATR-SK-2026-008); this is a second outlet with named local civil-society source. Actualite.cd also states AFC/M23 elements have occupied Mikenge since March 2025 (outlet's own wording).
r1-SKS-2026Q1-012.vn: Supported; second outlet to SOS Médias Burundi with a named local civil-society source. '1 March' comes from the outlet's lede ('depuis ce dimanche 1 er mars'), not from Kararuka's quote.
src: « C'est depuis dimanche que les FARDC appuyées par les wazalendo ont récupéré Mikenge et d'autres entités. Et ce sont les FARDC avec les wazalendo de Kakobanya qui mènent les opérations dans cette zone », dit Pacifique Kararuka, président de la Nouvelle société civile congolaise à Kipupu.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC spokesperson in the region, Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said villages including Mikenge, Kakenge, Bilalombili and Bidegu 1 had been retaken, and that five elements were captured, 17 surrendered and 11 bodies left on the ground, among them a brigade commander of AFC/M23 and a logistics officer of Twirwaneho.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-013.n: FARDC figures, unverified; the source says the quote concerns the FARDC riposte in Fizi. The spokesperson's name is printed 'Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji' here and 'Mbuyi Reagan' by Radio Okapi. The excerpt's 'en même le sol' is the page's own wording. AFC/M23 reply not found.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-013.vn: Quote supported in full on the page; brigade-commander clause is on the page beyond the stored excerpt. FARDC figures, unverified party claims. Rank printed 'lieutenant' here and 'sous-lieutenant' by Radio Okapi on 2 Feb; name order also differs.
src: de nouvelles cités et villages stratégiques ont été reconquis notamment Mikenge, Kakenge, Bilalombili et Bidegu 1. Outre ces villages récupérés par l’armée républicaine, plusieurs rebelles ont été neutralisés, cinq éléments capturés, 17 rendus et 11 corps abandonnés en même le sol
dit le lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, porte-parole de l’armée dans la région.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-014.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, citing local sources, that FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo now control strategic areas in the centre of Mikenge, including the main hospital, while Twirwaneho actors were reportedly still in the surrounding area.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-014.n: Swahili edition of an existing French-language SOS Médias Burundi report (r1-ATR-SK-2026-008); counts as the same origin, not independent. Hospital named only as 'main hospital'.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-014.vn: Supported. Date approximate (article datelined 2 March, published 4 March). Swahili edition of SOS Médias Burundi's own reporting; same origin as its French report, not independent.
src: Kulingana na vyanzo vya ndani, FARDC (Vikosi vya Wanajeshi vya Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo), FDNB (Kikosi cha Kitaifa cha Kidemokrasia cha Burundi), na wanamgambo wa Wazalendo sasa wanadhibiti maeneo ya kimkakati katikati mwa Mikenge, pamoja na hospitali kuu.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-015.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that on Sunday fighting was also reported in several villages of Minembwe including Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi and Kakenge.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-015.l: Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi, Kakenge (Minembwe, Fizi)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-015.a: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo vs Twirwaneho and M23
r1-SKS-2026Q1-015.n: Date computed from 'Jumapili hii' (this Sunday) with dateline 2 March; Sunday = 1 March. Machine-style Swahili; the same article elsewhere says the attacks were repelled by Twirwaneho and M23.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-015.vn: Supported. The article adds that FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo attacks were reportedly repelled by Twirwaneho and M23 ('waliripotiwa kufanya mashambulizi lakini wakazuiwa na wapiganaji wa Twirwaneho na M23'). Sunday = 1 March from dateline 'Machi 2, 2026'.
src: Wakati Mikenge akiwa amenaswa tena, mapigano pia yameripotiwa Jumapili hii katika vijiji kadhaa vya Minembwe, vikiwemo Bidegu, Ilundu, Rugezi, Kalingi, Kalongi, na Kakenge.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing a Mercy Corps humanitarian report for February, that 15 200 households from the highlands were recorded in Maniema province, in Kabambare and Pangi territories, and said clashes between FARDC with Wazalendo and Ngumino-Twirwaneho allied to AFC/M23 in the Fizi highlands caused the movements, while the report also attributes part of the Kabambare displacement to heavy rains.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.l: Kabambare and Pangi territories, Maniema (displaced from Fizi highlands)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.a: displacement linked to FARDC/Wazalendo vs Ngumino-Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 fighting
r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.x: Mercy Corps (via Actualite.cd): 15 200 households; Kabambare about 11 040, Pangi 4 160
r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.n: Figure in statement as given; the article adds that part of the Kabambare movement is due to heavy rains in Ndandalukala (OCHA cited). Breakdown: Kabambare about 11 040 households (Lusangi 7 940; Kabambare 3 100); Pangi 4 160 (Kampene).
r1-SKS-2026Q1-016.vn: Figures checked on the page. Flagged numbers are in the figures field and printed on the page. Breakdown per the quoted report: Kabambare about 11 040 households (Lusangi 7 940; Kabambare health zone 3 100); Pangi 4 160 (Kampene). The rain sentence is the outlet's narration between quotes from the report; the next sentence cites OCHA via the report.
src: Selon un rapport humanitaire de Mercy Corps du mois de février, 15 200 ménages en provenance des hauts plateaux sont recensés dans la province du Maniema.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that intense fighting opposed the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition and AFC/M23 rebels from the morning of Tuesday 17 March in the villages of Kabunango and Runingu in the Uvira grouping, South Kivu, and that traffic was cut on the RN5 linking Bukavu and Uvira; Martin Mafikiri of the Nouvelle société civile congolaise said both sides had reinforced in the Ruzizi plain.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-017.l: Kabunango, Runingu, Kabunambo, Sange, Biriba, Kasambura (Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory)
r1-SKS-2026Q1-017.n: Corroborates existing Radio Okapi claim r1-UV-2026Q1-049 (Luvungi/Kabunambo) with a different set of villages; the page also names Biriba, Kasambura. Source is Martin Mafikiri's civil-society account.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-017.vn: The opening account is the outlet's own narration, not Mafikiri's; Mafikiri is credited only with the remark that both camps reinforced in the Ruzizi plain. Attribution fixed. Another civil-society actor reported heavy fighting toward Kabunambo and Sange; the outlet also lists Biriba and Kasambura.
src: D’intenses affrontements opposent depuis la matinée de ce mardi 17 mars, la coalition FARDC/wazalendo aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans les villages de Kabunango, Runingu dans le groupement d’Uvira au Sud-Kivu.
Le trafic est ainsi coupé sur la RN5 reliant les villes de Bukavu et Uvira.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-018.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the rebellion (AFC/M23), the 17 March fighting in the Ruzizi plain was a 'guerre généralisée' (generalised war) waged by the government army and its allies.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-018.n: AFC/M23 position reported secondhand; no FARDC/Kinshasa account of who started the 17 March fighting found in this source.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-018.vn: Supported; 17 and M23 printed on the page and in the title. Party position reported secondhand; the outlet says 'la rébellion' in an article about AFC/M23 fighting on 17 March; no direct AFC/M23 communiqué cited.
src: D’après la rébellion, il s’agit d’une « guerre généralisée » menée par l’armée gouvernementale et ses alliés.

r1-SKS-2026Q1-019.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Wazalendo militiamen operating at Runingu announced on Sunday the prohibition of entry into Uvira city for anyone coming from areas controlled by M23, citing suspected spying on FARDC positions; Ruzizi plain residents of Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi and Sange said they were turned away from the Kashatu market at Runingu.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-019.l: Runingu, Kashatu market; Uvira city entrance
r1-SKS-2026Q1-019.n: Date computed from 'ce dimanche' and publication date 16 March (Monday), so Sunday 15 March. Single Burundi-based outlet. The same article says the Ruzizi plain localities (Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi, Sange) are under M23 control, and that civil society fears effects on access to fields.
r1-SKS-2026Q1-019.vn: Supported by the page; single Burundi-based outlet. Sunday = 15 March, computed from publication date 16 March. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, Uvira 16 Mar 2026: Wazalendo at Runingu announced on Sunday (15 Mar) a ban on entry to Uvira for anyone from M23-held areas; Ruzizi plain residents say they were turned away from Kashatu market. All clauses are on the page; the spying justification was in no stored excerpt, now added.
src: Les miliciens Wazalendo opérant dans la localité de Runingu, dans le territoire d’Uvira au Sud-Kivu, ont annoncé ce dimanche l’interdiction d’entrée dans la ville d’Uvira pour toute personne en provenance des zones contrôlées par le mouvement rebelle Mouvement du 23 mars (M23).
Des habitants de la plaine de la Ruzizi, notamment de Kamanyola, Luvungi, Luberizi et Sange, affirment avoir été empêchés d’accéder au marché de Kashatu, situé dans la localité de Runingu.

Les miliciens affirment suspecter certains voyageurs d’activités d’espionnage visant à identifier les positions militaires des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), ainsi que celles de leurs alliés présents dans la ville.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-001.s: MSF said that on 1 May 2026 its team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu for a needs assessment was stopped at a checkpoint controlled by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men then fired among themselves while the team was caught in the middle. MSF said all staff later returned safely to Bukavu.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-001.a: Wazalendo elements (checkpoint), as described by MSF
r1-SKS-2026Q2-001.n: Primary MSF statement; existing claim r1-SV-2026-020 relays this via Kivu Morning Post. MSF says incidents are 'neither isolated nor limited to one armed group'.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-001.vn: All three excerpts exact on the retained MSF page; the safe-return clause is on the page (lead paragraph). MSF statement, attributed as MSF's. MSF's own account of its own incident (press release 8 May 2026). MSF does not say who fired; the team was afterwards urged to continue towards Mwenga.
src: On 1 May, an MSF team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga, and Kitutu, in South Kivu, as part of an assessment of humanitarian and medical needs, were involved in a security incident.
“After safely passing several checkpoints controlled by Wazalendo elements along the way, our team was stopped at one of them,” says Julia Garcia Zamora, MSF head of mission in South Kivu.
“The situation then escalated with armed men firing among themselves while our team were caught in the middle.”

r1-SKS-2026Q2-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that on 17 June 2026 FARDC (supported by the Burundian army and Wazalendo) and Twirwaneho allied to AFC-M23 fought on three axes around Minembwe centre: axis 1 (Mikenge to Gitavi) led by the army and Wazalendo; axis 2 (Bidegu-Kalingi) led by the special forces Hiboux and Serpent noir using combat drones; axis 3 (Kakenge) led exclusively by the Burundian army and FDLR units, according to local and security sources.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-002.l: Minembwe centre, Gitavi, Bidegu, Kalingi, Ilundu, Kakenge (Hauts Plateaux), Fizi/Mwenga
r1-SKS-2026Q2-002.a: FARDC, Wazalendo, FDNB, forces spéciales Hiboux, Serpent noir, FDLR (per local sources) vs Twirwaneho/AFC-M23
r1-SKS-2026Q2-002.n: Single outlet, anonymous local sources; FDLR role on axis 3 is an allegation by local sources. FARDC/Kinshasa account of the same days is in the Actualite.cd claim.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-002.vn: Excerpts exact; figure flags are axis numbers and the 'M23' name, both printed on the page (clause quotes). excerpt_en flags are capitalisation/translation artefacts only. Single outlet, anonymous sources: C. Order of battle (Hiboux, Serpent noir, FDNB, FDLR units) is Kivu Morning Post's, from unnamed local and security sources; not confirmed by FARDC or Burundi.
src: Les affrontements, ce mercredi 17 juin 2026, se concentrent sur trois axes importants.
L’offensive de l’armée sur l’axe 2, Bidegu-Kalingi, est dirigée par les forces spéciales Hiboux et Serpent noir, qui s’appuient sur des drones de combat.
Axe 3 : il est exclusivement dirigé par l’armée burundaise et des unités FDLR, selon des sources locales et sécuritaires.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, in an account of the 17 June 2026 fighting around Minembwe whose opening it attributes to local sources, that on axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi) several houses of Banyamulenge civilians were burned by the army and Wazalendo militiamen in the first village of Gitavi. The article gives no specific source for this incident and carries no FARDC response.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-003.a: the army and Wazalendo militiamen, per Kivu Morning Post's local sources
r1-SKS-2026Q2-003.n: Single outlet; no FARDC response found.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-003.vn: Excerpt exact; the page does not date the burning itself, so the day was removed from the statement and date_precision set to approximate. No FARDC response on the page. The article (17 June 2026) does not give the day of the burning; it is reported in its account of that day's fighting, so the date is approximate (on or shortly before 17 June). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: account attributed to local sources 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 17 June 2026; axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-024: Read the retained page: the burning sentence carries no attribution of its own; 'selon des sources locales' attaches to the article's opening account of the fighting. The article's framing is sympathetic to the Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 side (e.g. it says they 'ont réussi à stopper l’offensive'), so the allegation is single-outlet and unconfirmed; grade C is right. Amend to show how the sourcing actually runs.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): account attributed to local sources; 17 June 2026; axis 1 (Mikenge towards Gitavi)
src: plusieurs maisons de civils Banyamulenge ont été incendiées par l’armée et les miliciens Wazalendo. L’incident a eu lieu dans le premier village de Gitavi.

La situation est très tendue à Minembwe, dans les Hauts-Plateaux du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la RDC, suite aux combats intenses entre les Twirwaneho alliés à l’AFC-M23 et les FARDC, appuyées par l’armée burundaise et les milices Wazalendo depuis 48 h, selon des sources locales.
Les affrontements, ce mercredi 17 juin 2026, se concentrent sur trois axes importants. Sur l’axe 1, axe Mikenge vers Gitavi,

r1-SKS-2026Q2-004.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the humanitarian blockage at Minembwe was intensifying, with no exit and no resupply of food and medicines, and that humanitarian access was blocked. It said the Mahoro Peace association, which groups Congolese nationals living in the United States, had indicated that 32 civilians were wounded between 8 and 11 June.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-004.n: Figure from a diaspora association (Banyamulenge-linked per SOS Médias Burundi), not independently verified. Cause of access block not stated.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-004.vn: Excerpts exact. 'blocage' rendered as 'blockage' (not 'blockade', which implies a deliberate act the source does not state); the 17 June date stays in the date field only. Figure attributed to Mahoro Peace. The figure of 32 wounded is Mahoro Peace's (a US-based association; SOS Médias Burundi describes it as grouping members of the Banyamulenge community), not verified. The outlet does not say who imposes the blockage.
src: Pour l’heure, le blocage humanitaire s’accentue : pas de sortie ni de ravitaillement en vivres et en médicaments. L’accès des humanitaires est bloqué.
L’association Mahoro Peace, qui regroupe des ressortissants congolais résidant aux États-Unis, a indiqué que 32 civils ont été blessés entre le 8 et le 11 juin.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud-Kivu, Lieutenant Reagan Kalonji, said FARDC had since the evening of Tuesday 16 June retaken total control of Kitavi village, the Irundu agglomeration and positions at the Ugeafi school at Madegu near Minembwe centre, and that on 17 June the army was trying to retake the Minembwe-centre airfield. The Fizi territory administrator Sammy Badibanga said the clashes created a catastrophic humanitarian situation.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-005.l: Kitavi, Irundu, Madegu (Ugeafi school), Minembwe centre airfield, Fizi
r1-SKS-2026Q2-005.a: FARDC supported by Wazalendo, vs Twirwaneho/Red Tabara allied to AFC/M23 (as the source states)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-005.n: FARDC announcement relayed by an established outlet; contested by residents (see DW Swahili claim). Note the page prints 'Sammy Badibanga' here and 'Samy Badibanga' in Mediacongo/Radio Okapi.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-005.vn: Excerpts exact; every clause found on the page. Grade B is for the fact that FARDC made this announcement (credible outlet), not for the control change itself. FARDC announcement only; contested by residents and a human rights defender quoted by DW Swahili (18 June) and by the Twirwaneho/M23 account carried by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline 19 June). The page also spells the spokesperson 'Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji'.
src: c'est depuis mardi 16 juin dans la soirée que les FARDC ont repris le contrôle total du village Kitavi, de l'agglomération d'Irundu, des positions de l'école Ugeafi situées à Madegu aux abords de Minembwe centre.
l'administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Sammy Badibanga, a indiqué que ces affrontements ont créé une situation humanitaire catastrophique pour les habitants du milieu.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-006.s: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army claimed to have controlled Minembwe since Wednesday evening and that Twirwaneho had fled, but that residents denied it. Human rights defender Maniragaba Byashonyi said no FARDC soldiers were in the centre of Minembwe and that the centre was controlled by MRDP/Twirwaneho.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-006.a: FARDC (claim); MRDP/Twirwaneho (as described by local residents)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-006.n: Directly contradicts the FARDC announcement (Actualite.cd 18 June). Date of 'Wednesday evening' computed from weekday and publication date (17 June 2026). The Byashonyi quote is cited as printed; the page's excerpt begins mid-quotation.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-006.vn: Excerpts exact; Byashonyi's name and role are on the page. Credible outlet reporting two opposing accounts, both attributed. DW Swahili published 18 June 2026 (Thursday), so 'Wednesday evening' is 17 June. Residents' and the defender's account contradicts the FARDC announcement (Actualite.cd, 18 June); each account is kept separately.
src: jeshi la Kongo ladai limedhibiti Minembwe tangu Jumatano jioni na Twirwaneho wamekimbia, lakini wakaazi wanakanusha taarifa hiyo huku.
Katikati mwa mji huu unadhibitiwa na kundi la kujilinda la MRDP/Twirwaneho. Wanajeshi wa FARDC wamefukuzwa, waliokuwa Ilundu wamerejea Bidegu, na waliotoka Kalingi wamefukuzwa na wamerudi Kalingi.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, after fighting around Minembwe, the FARDC, the FDNB and their allies had reportedly withdrawn to the localities of Lwiko, Mutunda and Miko, leaving several peripheral positions of Minembwe under the control of Twirwaneho/M23 fighters. It said the FARDC had not published a detailed communiqué at the time of writing, while local military sources confirmed a strategic repositioning after particularly violent clashes in the Ilundu and Bidegu areas.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-007.l: Minembwe periphery, Lwiko, Mutunda, Miko, Ilundu, Bidegu, Fizi/Mwenga
r1-SKS-2026Q2-007.n: Burundian outlet with Banyamulenge-leaning sourcing; conditional tense ('se seraient retirés'). Conflicts with the FARDC claim of 16-18 June gains. Date range approximate: 'près d'une semaine' to 19 June.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-007.vn: Excerpts exact. Raw statement turned the outlet's conditional narration into 'local sources said ... withdrew'; corrected to keep the conditional and the outlet as narrator. Dateline day moved to the date field. The withdrawal is reported in the conditional ('se seraient retirés'); dateline Minembwe, 19 June 2026, after 'près d'une semaine' of fighting. Contradicts the FARDC announcement of 16-18 June gains; each account kept separately.
src: Les FARDC, la FDNB et leurs alliés se seraient ensuite retirés vers les localités de Lwiko, Mutunda et Miko, laissant plusieurs positions périphériques de Minembwe sous le contrôle des combattants Twirwaneho/M23.

Les FARDC n’ont pas publié de communiqué détaillé au moment de la rédaction, mais des sources militaires locales confirment un repositionnement stratégique après des affrontements particulièrement violents dans les zones d’Ilundu et de Bidegu.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi quoted former national deputy Moïse Nyarugabo as saying 'La menace sur Minembwe est écartée', that despite Sukhoi bombardments, drones and heavy artillery the forces engaged had been pushed back beyond the Lwiko river; it reported he accused the coalition of bombardments causing civilian losses and mass displacement.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-008.n: Speaker is a former deputy, not an office-holder; his affiliation to Twirwaneho is not stated in the excerpt.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-008.vn: Excerpt exact; name and accusation on the page. Party-aligned claim reported by one outlet: C. Speaker is a former national deputy; the page does not state a party affiliation. Date is approximate (article dateline 19 June, published 21 June).
src: « La menace sur Minembwe est écartée. Malgré les bombardements de Soukhoï, des drones et l’artillerie lourde, les forces engagées ont été repoussées au-delà de la rivière Lwiko », a-t-il déclaré.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimonies, that clashes had intensified since Friday 3 April 2026 in the Bijombo area of Uvira territory between FARDC supported by FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fighters on one side and Twirwaneho fighters affiliated with the M23 on the other, displacing thousands of civilians; Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango and Kajembwe were among the most affected localities.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-009.l: Bijombo (Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango, Kajembwe), Uvira territory
r1-SKS-2026Q2-009.a: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo, Gumino vs Twirwaneho (per testimonies gathered by the outlet)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-009.n: Single outlet; dateline Bukavu 6 April 2026. Residents' accounts only; no FARDC/Burundi response found in the page.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-009.vn: Excerpts exact; all clauses on the page. Party line-up is from residents' testimonies gathered by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline Bukavu, 6 April 2026); no FARDC or Burundi response on the page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr: per residents' testimonies, FARDC with FDNB elements, Wazalendo and Gumino fight M23-affiliated Twirwaneho in Bijombo, intensified since Friday 3 April 2026. All clauses are on the page; displacement and affected localities were in no stored excerpt, now added.
src: According to testimonies gathered from residents, the fighting involves the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by elements of the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), the Wazalendo militias backed by Kinshasa, and fighters from the Gumino group, against Twirwaneho fighters affiliated with the M23.
The clashes have intensified since Friday, April 3, 2026.

For several days, clashes have pitted various armed groups against loyalist forces, causing the displacement of thousands of civilians. The localities of Muramvya, Masata, Nyakirango, Irango, and Kajembwe are among the areas most affected by this violence.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-010.s: SOS Médias Burundi quoted a resident of Muramvya village (Bijombo area), 'Yohana', as saying residents were fleeing because 'the Wazalendo are threatening civilians and stealing our livestock', and that some residents were hiding in the bush, others had fled to the forests and many had taken refuge in churches in Masoro and Gahuna.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-010.n: Single anonymous-style resident testimony (first name only, as printed); date is the dateline (6 April).
r1-SKS-2026Q2-010.vn: Excerpt exact; Masoro/Gahuna clause is on the page. One resident's testimony, first name only as printed. Date is the article dateline (6 April 2026). 2026-10-28: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr. The hiding/churches clause is part of Yohana's own quote, not the outlet's report, so it is attributed to him; the stored excerpt omitted it and is replaced by the full contiguous quote. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (English), dateline Bukavu 6 Apr 2026, posted 8 Apr. The hiding/churches clause is part of Yohana's own quote, not the outlet's report, so it is attributed to him; the stored excerpt omitted it and is replaced by the full contiguous quote.
src: “Some residents are hiding in the bush, others have fled to the forests, while many have taken refuge in churches in Masoro and Gahuna. We are fleeing because the Wazalendo are threatening civilians and stealing our livestock,” testifies Yohana, a resident of the village of Muramvya.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-011.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is', saying 'It’s understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are trapped.'
r1-SKS-2026Q2-011.l: not stated by the source (article on Bijombo, Uvira territory, and Minembwe)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-011.n: Date of the BBC interview not given by the page; reported 2026-04-08 and may predate April. Original BBC item not located.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-011.vn: Excerpt exact. Date was '2026-04' with month precision, which implies the interview took place in April; the page gives no date, so it is set to the report date with approximate precision. Location is not given for the remark. The BBC interview is undated on the page; 8 April 2026 is only the date SOS Médias Burundi reported it, and the interview may be earlier. 'Acknowledged' is the outlet's verb.
src: The spokesperson for the Burundian army, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that Banyamulenge are trapped in areas “where the enemy is” : “It’s understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are trapped.”

r1-SKS-2026Q2-012.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué MRDP-Twirwaneho denounced ongoing attacks on civilians in Minembwe and Mikenge, rejected FARDC accusations that Minembwe served as a sanctuary for Burundian RED-Tabara rebels, demanded the immediate withdrawal of Burundian forces from Congolese territory and called for an independent international investigation into human rights violations in the region. The outlet quoted Colonel Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, in the communiqué, as calling those accusations false.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-012.l: Minembwe, Mikenge (Hauts Plateaux de Fizi, Itombwe, Uvira)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-012.n: Party communiqué, cited for what the party said only. The communiqué also alleges massacres, forced displacement, sexual violence and hostage-taking by the coalition, with no incident detail. Outlet publisher is KMP; communiqué is Twirwaneho's.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-012.vn: Excerpts exact. Raw said the communiqué 'cited' the colonel; the page says he made the statement in the communiqué, so that clause was narrowed to what he is quoted as saying. Date stays in the date field. Party communiqué, cited only as what MRDP-Twirwaneho said. Dated by the article ('ce jeudi', 11 June 2026). The communiqué also alleges massacres, forced displacement, sexual violence and hostage-taking by the coalition, with no incident detail.
src: Le MRDP-Twirwaneho rejette catégoriquement les accusations des FARDC selon lesquelles Minembwe servirait de sanctuaire aux rebelles burundais du RED-Tabara.

Le Twirwaneho exige le retrait immédiat des forces burundaises du territoire congolais et appelle à une enquête internationale indépendante sur les violations des droits humains commises dans la région.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-013.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 08:00 on Friday 15 May 2026 Kinshasa had ordered the deployment of heavily armed combat helicopters from Kalemie to join strikes on Minembwe and surroundings, in addition to combat drones, heavy artillery and Sukhoi-25 jets. Fighting was reported at Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu and Kalingi (Fizi) and at Mikenge (Mwenga).
r1-SKS-2026Q2-013.l: Minembwe, Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu, Kalingi, Mikenge, Fizi/Mwenga
r1-SKS-2026Q2-013.n: Party claim, not verified; the headline says 'avions de combat' while the quote says helicopters. No FARDC reply to this claim found.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-013.vn: Excerpts exact; speaker name and Sukhoi-25 clause are on the page. AFC/M23 claim, not verified. The headline says 'avions de combat' while the quoted statement speaks of combat helicopters.
src: “Depuis 8h00 ce vendredi 15 mai 2026, le régime de Kinshasa a ordonné le déploiement massif d’hélicoptères de combat lourdement armés en provenance de Kalemie afin de participer aux frappes en cours contre Minembwe et ses environs.
Des combats ont été signalés dans les localités de Kakenge, Kalonge, Bidegu et Kalingi, en territoire de Fizi, ainsi qu’à Mikenge, dans le territoire de Mwenga.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-014.s: Actualite.cd reported (9 June) that Mikenge village (Mwenga) was hit by bombardments on the night of Sunday to Monday '7 juin', leaving at least two dead and 6 wounded including two children; it said the army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho rebel coalition and, according to an army communiqué, the air attacks hit FARDC positions at Mikenge and its surroundings, causing heavy material damage.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-014.x: Actualite.cd: at least 2 dead, 6 wounded including 2 children
r1-SKS-2026Q2-014.n: Date as printed is internally inconsistent (7 June 2026 is a Sunday; 'lundi 7 juin'). May overlap with existing draft SKC-2026H1#14 (Ilundu, 7 June). AFC/M23 had accused FARDC of the opposite attribution on other occasions; no Twirwaneho/M23 reply to this specific claim found.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-014.vn: Excerpts exact; attribution clause on the page. Date range 2026-06-07/2026-06-08 with 'range' precision is the honest rendering of the inconsistent date. Date as printed is internally inconsistent: 7 June 2026 is a Sunday, but the page says 'la nuit du dimanche au lundi 7 juin'; the night of 7-8 June is kept as a range. The casualty figure is the outlet's, not attributed; the perpetrator attribution is FARDC's. The page spells the group 'Twirweneho'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho coalition 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-024: Read the retained page: the FARDC attribution sentence is printed (not in the stored excerpt, which only carries the 'positions des FARDC' clause). The FARDC communiqué as relayed describes hits on its own positions, not on civilians. The edition should not show two separate civilian-casualty incidents without this flag.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): army attributed the bombardments to the AFC/M23-Twirweneho coalition | cut the sentence comparing the toll with an Actualite.cd report of the previous day on Ilundu: that report is not cited by this claim; the possible duplicate belongs in notes or a discrepancy record
src: Le village de Mikenge dans le territoire de Mwenga au Sud-Kivu a été le théâtre des bombardements la nuit du dimanche au lundi 7 juin faisant au moins deux morts et 6 blessés dont deux enfants.

Ces attaques aériennes ont touché des positions des FARDC à Mikenge et ses environs, dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi-Uvira au Sud-Kivu causant également d’énormes dégâts matériels, selon un communiqué de l’armée.
L’armée attribue ces bombardements dont les FARDC attribués à la coalition rebelle AFC/M23-Twirweneho.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-015.s: Mediacongo, carrying a piece credited 'Patrick Kitoko, Opinion Info / MCP', reported that, according to a FARDC communiqué of 20 May 2026, the Mikenge general hospital was reportedly 'intentionally targeted' and 'completely destroyed' during drone strikes that hit localities including Kalingi and Mikenge in the early morning, with a provisional toll of several civilian victims that reportedly included hospital staff members. FARDC also accused Rwanda and its 'proxies' of being behind the offensive. The communiqué was signed by FARDC acting spokesperson Lieutenant-Colonel Mongba Hazukay Mak. Africa-Infos.cd (21 May) reported the same communiqué, no. 13.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-015.l: Mikenge general hospital, Mikenge (Mwenga territory); the page places the attacks in the Minembwe highlands, Fizi territory
r1-SKS-2026Q2-015.a: RDF/AFC/M23 coalition, as alleged by FARDC communiqué
r1-SKS-2026Q2-015.n: FARDC account only; for the same date BCNUDH attributes the bombardment differently (existing claim r1-SV-2026-015) and the page notes it is a FARDC claim. No AFC/M23 response to this specific allegation found.

src: Selon les FARDC, l’hôpital général de Mikenge aurait été « intentionnellement ciblé » et « complètement détruit » lors de ces attaques.

Les FARDC accusent également le Rwanda et ses « supplétifs » d’être à l’origine de cette nouvelle offensive, malgré les engagements pris dans le cadre des accords de Washington et du processus de paix de Doha.
Selon l’armée Congolaise, ces attaques ont notamment touché l’Hôpital Général de Mikenge qui aurait été « intentionnellement ciblé » puis complètement détruit au cours des bombardements.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that at 14:00 on Wednesday 24 June 2026 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont bombardé, à l’aide de drones de combat, l’hôpital général de Minembwe, y compris le pavillon pédiatrique'. The outlet also quoted AFC/M23 deputy coordinator Bertrand Bisimwa: « Le bombardement d’un hôpital en temps de guerre est un crime de guerre ». This is an AFC/M23 allegation; the article gives no casualty figure for the hospital and carries no FARDC response.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-016.n: Party claim carried by a Goma-based outlet; no independent confirmation, casualty figure or FARDC response found. Original post on X not opened. Counter-reporting: Habari Express (2026-06-26): Date: 25 June vs 24 June in the claim
