src: « À 14h00 ce mercredi 24 juin 2026, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont bombardé, à l’aide de drones de combat, l’hôpital général de Minembwe, y compris le pavillon pédiatrique où sont pris en charge des enfants malades et particulièrement vulnérables »
Dans un message publié sur son compte X, le porte-parole de l’AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka

Réagissant à ces bombardements, Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur adjoint de l’AFC/M23 chargé des questions politiques, administratives, judiciaires et diplomatiques, a estimé qu’une attaque contre un établissement de santé constitue une violation grave du droit international humanitaire. « Le bombardement d’un hôpital en temps de guerre est un crime de guerre.
AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka had reported that combat drones struck the hospital on Wednesday, June 24, including its pediatric ward.
profonde préoccupation après le bombardement de l’hôpital général de référence de Minembwe, survenu le 25 juin dans la province du Sud-Kivu

r1-SKS-2026Q2-017.s: Mediacongo, carrying a report credited 'Radio Okapi / MCP', reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei between FARDC and the fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies; the militia accused FARDC of drone bombardments on its positions, while local actors called this a 'fuite en avant'. It also reported that at the sixth meeting of the Joint Oversight Committee (Comité mixte de surveillance, CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to defuse tensions over Minembwe.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-017.a: FARDC vs Twirwaneho and allies (described as backed by Rwanda by the source)
r1-SKS-2026Q2-017.n: Radio Okapi-originated copy (Mediacongo credit 'Radio Okapi / MCP'; Radio Okapi original dated 27 June not opened). 'Supported by Rwanda' is the outlet's characterisation. Relevant to the AFC/M23 hospital claim of the same day.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-017.vn: Excerpts exact. Raw named the London body 'Joint Security Mechanism'; the page says Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS), rendered here as Joint Oversight Committee per the stored translation. The 26 June reporting day was moved out of the statement (no excerpt prints it). Radio Okapi copy relayed by Mediacongo (page credit 'Radio Okapi / MCP'). 'Supported by Rwanda' is the outlet's description of the Twirwaneho coalition. The local sources spoke on Friday 26 June. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Mediacongo, 28 Jun 2026; the credit line reads 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net', so the text is Radio Okapi's copy and the statement should say so (originating_source already records Radio Okapi). Every clause is on the page.
src: des affrontements ont eu lieu mercredi 24 juin dans les villages d’Ilundu et d’Alengei entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et les combattants de la coalition armée Twirwaneho et leurs alliés, soutenus par le Rwanda.

Sur le plan régional, lors de la sixième réunion du Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS) sur la situation sécuritaire en RDC, tenue mercredi 24 juin 2026 à Londres, Kinshasa et Kigali ont réaffirmé leur engagement à désamorcer les tensions liées à la situation de Minembwe.

r1-SKS-2026Q2-018.s: Mediacongo (Radio Okapi / MCP credit) reported that, according to local civil society, repeated Twirwaneho attacks on positions retaken by FARDC were causing new displacement, and that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said victims and vulnerable people were estimated at several thousand.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-018.x: Fizi administrator: 'several thousand' victims and vulnerable people
r1-SKS-2026Q2-018.n: Official's estimate, no breakdown or method; date is the 'Friday 26 June' reporting day.
r1-SKS-2026Q2-018.vn: Excerpt exact; civil-society clause on the page. Official's estimate with no breakdown or method. The same official is spelled 'Sammy Badibanga' on Actualite.cd (18 June).
src: Selon l’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Samy Badibanga, les conséquences humaines de cette insécurité seraient lourdes, avec des victimes et des personnes vulnérables estimées à plusieurs milliers.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-001.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that forces his movement calls the 'coalisées du régime de Kinshasa' intensified their ground attacks on the Point Zéro area at around 04:45 in the early hours of the morning; he also said these forces attacked Kasika (Mwenga territory) early that morning, and that government forces attacked Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in the Minembwe area. This is the AFC/M23 account.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-001.l: Point Zéro, Kasika, Nyaruhinga, Mukoko (Fizi / Mwenga territories, Minembwe area), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-001.a: AFC/M23 (Lawrence Kanyuka); Kinshasa 'coalised' forces as described by AFC/M23
r1-SKS-2026Q3-001.n: Party account only (AFC/M23). Kivu Morning Post article is a relay of a Kanyuka social-media message; the post itself was not seen. Same article says the spokesperson described the opposing side as FARDC, Wazalendo and the Burundian army. Complements existing Aug 30-31 claims (Actualite.cd, SOS Médias Burundi) giving the Kinshasa-side account.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-001.vn: Excerpts exact; the date '31' is printed only in the page lede (not in a stored excerpt), so it is removed from the statement; the date field keeps the article's 31 August. Kept as party account only. Party account (AFC/M23) relayed by Kivu Morning Post, which says it was a message on social media; the original post was not seen.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole politique de l’AFC/M23, a affirmé que des attaques ont été signalées dès les premières heures de la matinée. Selon lui, les forces que son mouvement qualifie de « coalisées du régime de Kinshasa » ont intensifié, vers 04H45, leurs attaques terrestres contre la zone de Point Zéro

Le porte-parole de l’AFC/M23 a également affirmé que ces forces avaient attaqué tôt le matin dans la localité de Kasika, en territoire de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu. Les forces gouvernementales ont également lancé des attaques contre Nyaruhinga et Mukoko, deux zones densément peuplées de la région de Minembwe, selon la même source.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the Fizi territory administrator, at least eighteen people were killed and many others wounded in drone bombings 'du M23 et de ses alliés' on the morning of Friday 3 July in the village of Mulima; the administrator said there were many victims among women, men and children, as well as livestock losses. The attribution to the M23 and its allies is the administrator's.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-002.a: M23 and its allies (as alleged by the Fizi territory administrator)
r1-SKS-2026Q3-002.x: Fizi territory administrator (via Radio Okapi): at least 18 killed, many wounded
r1-SKS-2026Q3-002.n: Single official local source relayed by Radio Okapi (Kinshasa-side administrator); no M23 or Rwandan reply found in this page. Other outlets cited by search leads gave 17 or 21 dead (leads only, not opened). Existing claim r1-ATR-SK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi 9 Jul, civil society: about 16 killed, 12 wounded) covers the same event with a different figure; figures not merged.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-002.vn: Excerpts exact; '18' is the title's figure and 'dix-huit' in the excerpt. Removed the year (not in excerpt) and added the livestock clause the excerpt prints. Toll differs from other accounts of the same strike (e.g. civil society about 16 killed); figures kept separate, not merged. The same page quotes humanitarians as reporting more than eighteen dead among displaced people.
src: Au moins dix-huit personnes ont été tuées et de nombreuses autres blessées lors de bombardements de drones du M23 et de ses alliés survenus vendredi 3 juillet au matin dans le village de Mulima, selon l’administrateur du territoire de Fizi (Sud-Kivu).
« On dénombre de nombreuses victimes parmi les femmes, les hommes et les enfants, ainsi que des pertes de bétail.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga, said: 'Les infrastructures sanitaires et scolaires ont été détruites, et plusieurs élèves ont vu leurs écoles anéanties dans les villages de Mulima, Kangouli et leurs environs' (health and school infrastructure destroyed; several pupils' schools wiped out in Mulima, Kangouli and surroundings). The source does not name or number the health facilities.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.l: Mulima, Kangouli, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.a: M23 and its allies (as alleged by the Fizi territory administrator)
r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.x: Number and names of facilities not stated by the source
r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.n: Which health facilities were hit is not specified; seek UN/health-cluster confirmation. The sentence is quoted from the administrator.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-003.vn: Excerpt exact; date and the M23 attribution are not in this excerpt (they are in claim 1's), so the statement is narrowed to the quoted wording. Administrator's general statement only: no facility named, no damage detail; seek health-cluster or UN confirmation before treating as a specific attack on a facility. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les infrastructures sanitaires et scolaires ont été détruites, et plusieurs élèves ont vu leurs écoles anéanties dans les villages de Mulima, Kangouli et leurs environs », a détaillé l’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Samy Badibanga.
sanitaires et scolaires ont été détruites, et plusieurs élèves ont vu leurs écoles anéanties dans les villages de Mulima, Kangouli et leurs environs

r1-SKS-2026Q3-004.s: Radio Okapi's press review reported that the Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) reports the discovery of eleven mass graves in South Kivu, seven months after massacres attributed (attribués) to the M23 in the towns of Sange and Luvungi, Uvira territory; according to ACP the announcement was made on Monday 27 July by the Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu after an investigation conducted jointly with the 33rd military region.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-004.l: Sange and Luvungi (Ruzizi plain), Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-004.a: Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu (announcement); massacres 'attribués au M23' per ACP
r1-SKS-2026Q3-004.n: Relay of a state-agency report of a Congolese military-justice announcement (a Kinshasa-side authority); the underlying announcement was not seen. Related to existing claim r1-UV-2026Q3-022 (governor: up to 49 mass graves in the Uvira sector). Months of the massacres (Dec 2025) fall before the window; only the July 2026 discovery announcement is recorded. Sange/Luvungi lie on the Ruzizi plain.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-004.vn: Excerpts exact; kept all attribution to ACP; no perpetrator beyond the excerpt's 'attribués au M23'. Lead for add_excerpt: the page also quotes colonel-magistrat Kumbu Ngoma, auditeur militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu, on identified burial sites and gathered evidence. High-stakes: single state-media relay (ACP) of a Congolese military-justice announcement; the announcement itself, body counts and the identity of the victims were not seen. 'Attribués au M23' is ACP's wording; who made the attribution is not stated. No independent confirmation. 2026-10-28: source 0 publisher edited: fact-check fc1: The retained page is Radio Okapi's press review of 28 Jul 2026 (radiookapi.net) summarising ACP; the statement says so correctly, but both sources list ACP as publisher. Publisher set to Radio Okapi; ACP stays as originating source. 2026-10-28: source 1 publisher edited: fact-check fc1: The retained page is Radio Okapi's press review of 28 Jul 2026 (radiookapi.net) summarising ACP; the statement says so correctly, but both sources list ACP as publisher. Publisher set to Radio Okapi; ACP stays as originating source.
src: L’Agence congolaise de presse (ACP) rapporte la découverte de onze fosses communes au Sud-Kivu, sept mois après les massacres attribués au M23 dans les cités de Sange et de Luvungi, situées dans le territoire d’Uvira
L’annonce a été faite ce lundi 27 juillet par l’Auditorat militaire supérieur du Sud-Kivu, à l’issue d’une enquête menée conjointement avec la 33ᵉ région militaire, précise l’ACP.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-005.s: Radio Maendeleo recalled, in a later article on fighting at Point Zéro, that on 4 July Twirwaneho elements, allies of the AFC/M23, had taken control of Point Zéro after dislodging the FARDC.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-005.l: Point Zéro (Mwenga/Fizi highlands, Itombwe), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-005.n: Recap line in a later article; independent of existing r1-UV-2026Q3-003 (SOS Médias Burundi, Twirwaneho statement). FARDC spokesperson on 7 July (existing claim) said the army made a 'repli stratégique' from Point Zéro. The article places Point Zéro in Mwenga territory (Itombwe) and 74 km from Fizi-Centre; other outlets say Fizi.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-005.vn: Excerpt exact; removed the publication date (29 August), which no excerpt prints. Retrospective line in an article published weeks later; the year is inferred from 'le 4 juillet dernier'.
src: Pour rappel, le 4 juillet dernier, les éléments de Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC/M23, avaient pris le contrôle de Point Zéro après en avoir délogé les FARDC.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-006.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that violent clashes had pitted AFC/M23 elements and their allies against the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo groups, since Friday morning at Point Zéro, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory. It also reported that tension remained high in the belt between Luntukulu (Walungu territory), Tchulwe and Lubimbe (Shabunda territory), where a reinforcement of AFC-M23 troops was announced.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-006.l: Point Zéro-Centre, Itombwe highlands, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-006.a: AFC/M23 and allies; FARDC supported by Wazalendo groups
r1-SKS-2026Q3-006.n: Date computed from weekday ('vendredi matin') and publication date 29 Aug 2026 (a Friday 28 August); date computed from weekday and publication date. Matches Actualite.cd claim r1-UV-2026Q3-004 (clashes since Friday 28 August). Local-radio source (Radio Maendeleo, Bukavu).
r1-SKS-2026Q3-006.vn: The 4 a.m. / Point Zéro-Centre clause is on the page but not in the stored excerpt: narrowed out (lead for add_excerpt). Date (Friday 28 August) computed from the weekday and the article's date; the start time rests on unnamed local sources.
src: De violents affrontements opposent, depuis vendredi matin, les éléments de l’AFC/M23 et leurs alliés aux Forces armées de la RDC, appuyées par les groupes Wazalendo, à Point Zéro, dans les hauts plateaux d’Itombwe, territoire de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu.

Pour rappel, le 4 juillet dernier, les éléments de Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC/M23, avaient pris le contrôle de Point Zéro après en avoir délogé les FARDC. Entre-temps, la tension reste vive dans la ceinture comprise entre Luntukulu, dans le territoire de Walungu, Tchulwe et Lubimbe, dans le territoire de Shabunda, où l’on annonce un renforcement des troupes de l’AFC-M23.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing testimonies and local sources, that the FARDC, the FDNB and Wazalendo militiamen had lost several localities, notably Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge and Kalongi, a loss these sources attributed to Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC/M23, and that FARDC and FDNB soldiers had reportedly withdrawn from the Rugezi, Kakenge and Point Zéro sectors towards Mukera, while others had reportedly headed towards Misisi.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-007.l: Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge, Kalongi, Rugezi, Mukera (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-007.a: Twirwaneho (allied to AFC/M23) per local sources; FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo
r1-SKS-2026Q3-007.n: Anonymous local sources via a Burundian exile-run outlet; the article itself says the information could not be independently confirmed. Mikenge and Kalongi are named here as lost; the existing FARDC statement (7 July) claimed three villages retaken near Minembwe - a contested picture.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-007.vn: Excerpts exact; wording aligned to the conditional and to 'testimonies gathered'. Anonymous local sources; the losses are described as recent ('ces derniers jours') as of the article date, not dated precisely.
src: Ces renforts étaient destinés, selon les témoignages recueillis, à soutenir les positions des FARDC, de la FDNB et des miliciens Wazalendo après la perte de plusieurs localités, notamment Point Zéro, Kakenge, Rubemba, Mikenge et Kalongi, attribuée par ces sources aux combattants Twirwaneho alliés à l’AFC/M23.

Toujours selon des sources locales, des militaires des FARDC et de la FDNB se seraient repliés des secteurs de Rugezi, Kakenge et Point Zéro vers Mukera, tandis que d’autres auraient pris la direction de Misisi

r1-SKS-2026Q3-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources in Fizi territory, that three vehicles carrying ammunition and Burundian soldiers had reportedly been targeted by drones at Mulima during the past week, and that according to these sources several soldiers had reportedly been killed, among them a colonel and a major of the Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB); it said no official toll was available at the time of publication and that the information could not be independently confirmed.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-008.a: drones, operator not stated by the source; FDNB targeted
r1-SKS-2026Q3-008.x: Local sources: several killed including a colonel and a major (unconfirmed)
r1-SKS-2026Q3-008.n: Unconfirmed; Burundi government has not, in this source, commented. Article dated 9 July 2026 (Fizi). Same article reports, from the same sources, a boat carrying soldiers bombed on Lake Tanganyika off Ubwari (not claimed here).
r1-SKS-2026Q3-008.vn: Excerpt exact. The outlet's caveat (no official toll, not independently confirmed) is in the next sentence on the page, not the stored excerpt: kept because it only lowers certainty; please extend the excerpt with add_excerpt. Unconfirmed local reports; no Burundian official statement found. The drone operator is not named by the source.
ent: Force de défense nationale du Burundi
src: Des sources locales dans le territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu, rapportent que trois véhicules transportant des munitions et des militaires burundais auraient été pris pour cible par des drones à Mulima au cours de la semaine écoulée. Selon ces sources, plusieurs militaires auraient été tués, parmi lesquels un colonel et un major de la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB).

r1-SKS-2026Q3-009.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that new clashes between Wazalendo fighters and AFC-M23 troops broke out on Tuesday 1 September 2026 in the Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga territory, on the road to Kigogo; the sources said the Wazalendo launched the assault first, that heavy artillery was used, and that civilians were reportedly hit by bullets.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-009.l: Lwindi chiefdom (Kasika, Kalambi, road to Kigogo), Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-009.n: Local radio, anonymous sources. Follows existing r1-ATR-SK-2026-010 (Kasika held by AFC/M23, Wazalendo at Kalambi, 30 Aug). Same article reports clashes at Kahungu and Mulangala near Kahuzi-Biega (Kalehe/Kabare area, not in this unit).
r1-SKS-2026Q3-009.vn: All three excerpts exact and on the same page; statement matches with conditionals kept.
src: De nouveaux affrontements entre des combattants Wazalendo et les troupes de l’AFC-M23 ont éclaté ce mardi 1er septembre 2026 dans la chefferie de Lwindi, en territoire de Mwenga, précisément sur la route menant vers Kigogo.

Les activités sont restées paralysées dans plusieurs localités de la zone, avec notamment une forte panique au sein de la population à Kasika et à Kalambi, indiquent des sources locales contactées par Radio Maendeleo. Ces mêmes sources font état d’un recours à l’artillerie lourde, qui aurait causé d’importants dégâts matériels. Des civils auraient également été atteints par des balles.
Selon nos sources, les combattants Wazalendo auraient lancé les premiers l’assaut contre des positions des troupes de l’AFC-M23 dans la zone, obligeant ces dernières à réagir.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC said they shot down a kamikaze drone at Ruyengo, Fizi territory, on Thursday 20 August 2026 around 8 a.m.; the report attributed the device to RDF/M23 elements and their allies Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara. The spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operations (south sector, South Kivu), sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said this came a few hours after the FARDC foiled several rebel attacks on their positions in the Fizi highlands.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-010.l: Ruyengo, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-010.a: RDF/M23 and Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara (as attributed by FARDC); FARDC
r1-SKS-2026Q3-010.n: FARDC claim only; no AFC/M23 or Rwandan reply found. Page names the spokesperson 'sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi' (existing claims render the name differently). Names the allied group as 'Red-Tabara' as printed.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-010.vn: Excerpts exact; operation name was shortened wrongly ('Sukola 2 Sud'); page prints 'Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu'; attribution of the drone kept as the report's. FARDC claim only; no AFC/M23, Rwandan or Twirwaneho reply found.
src: Les FARDC affirment avoir abattu ce jeudi 20 août 2026 un drone kamikaze à Ruyengo dans le territoire de Fizi (Sud-Kivu). Cet appareil volant, attribué aux éléments du RDF/M23 et à leurs alliés Twirwaneho/Red-Tabara, a été neutralisé vers 8 heures du matin.

Selon le porte-parole des opérations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu, sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, cette intervention est survenue quelques heures après que les FARDC ont déjoué plusieurs attaques rebelle contre leurs positions dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes broke out from the evening of 26 September 2026 in several villages of the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, which several local sources placed notably in the Basimukindji 2 groupement at Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku and Musonjo; a local leader said AFC/M23 fighters sought to advance to Masango before being pushed back, and the article said the clashes caused a massive displacement of the population.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-011.l: Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku, Musonjo (Basimukindji 2 / Bijombo), Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-011.n: Corroborates and extends the existing Itombwe youth council claim (24-27 Sept, draft r1/SKC-2026H2#11) with place names and the start (evening of 26 Sept). No named FARDC or AFC/M23 statement in the article.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-011.vn: Displacement destinations (Basimukindji 1 etc.) and the local sources' attribution of the attack to 'AFC/M23 Twirwaheno' are on the page but not in stored excerpts: narrowed out (leads for add_excerpt). Local, unnamed sources; the attack is attributed to AFC/M23 'Twirwaheno' (spelling as printed) by those sources; no party statement in the article.
src: De violents affrontements ont éclaté depuis la soirée du 26 septembre 2026 dans plusieurs villages du secteur d’Itombwe, dans le territoire de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu. Selon plusieurs sources locales, les combats sont signalés notamment dans le groupement de Basimukindji 2, plus précisément à Maheta, Magunda, Nabuhera, Kakuku et Musonjo.
Un leader local affirme que les combattants de l’AFC/M23 cherchaient à progresser jusqu’à Masango avant d’être repoussés.
Ces affrontements ont provoqué un déplacement massif de la population.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said that on 27 September 2026 the government coalition (FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian forces) intensified attacks at Rugezi, Gipimo and Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud groupement, Lulenge sector); it added that sources close to the FARDC said they shot down a drone at Rugezi, while AFC/M23 'Twirwaheno' sources said they repelled an attack in the area.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-012.l: Rugezi, Gipimo, Kuwihene (Basimunyaka Sud, Lulenge sector, Minembwe area), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-012.a: FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian forces (per local civil society); AFC/M23 Twirwaheno
r1-SKS-2026Q3-012.n: Both sides' accounts are given as unnamed sources. The article headlines Fizi but describes Rugezi as a peripheral village of Minembwe in Mwenga territory; territory field follows the article text. Note the claim of Burundian forces' participation comes from civil society, not from Burundi.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-012.vn: Excerpts exact and match the statement clause by clause. The headline says Fizi but the article places Rugezi on the periphery of Minembwe in Mwenga territory. Burundian participation is civil society's claim.
src: « Le 27 septembre 2026, la coalition gouvernementale — FARDC, Wazalendo et forces burundaises — a intensifié les attaques à Rugezi, Gipimo et Kuwihene, dans le groupement Basimunyaka Sud, secteur de Lulenge », indique la société civile locale.
Des sources proches des FARDC affirment y avoir abattu un drone, tandis que celles de l’AFC/M23 Twirwaheno disent avoir repoussé une attaque dans la zone.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-013.s: MediaCongo reported that UN Secretary-General's spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric on Monday condemned drone attacks reported in Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu, without identifying their authors, and that according to the UN violent clashes since 4 July, including reported drone attacks, had reportedly left at least five dead and dozens wounded among civilians.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-013.l: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-013.x: UN (via MediaCongo): at least 5 civilians dead and dozens wounded since 4 July in Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira
r1-SKS-2026Q3-013.n: Date computed from weekday ('lundi') and publication date 7 July 2026 (Monday 6 July). Relayed by MediaCongo from a UN noon briefing; the original UN transcript was not fetched (look for press.un.org / news.un.org). UN figures differ from local official figures; not merged.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-013.vn: Excerpts exact; kept the conditional ('auraient fait'); removed the 16 and 18 cross-references from figures, which these excerpts do not print. UN figures; they differ from the Fizi administrator's (at least 18 at Mulima) and civil society's; not merged. Original UN transcript not fetched.
src: Le porte-parole du secrétaire général de l’ONU, Stéphane Dujarric a condamné lundi les attaques de drones signalées dans les territoires de Fizi, Mwenga et Uvira, situés dans la province du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), sans identifier leurs auteurs.

Selon l’ONU, depuis le 4 juillet, de violents affrontements, notamment des attaques de drones signalées, dans les territoires de Fizi, Mwenga et Uvira, auraient fait au moins cinq morts et des dizaines de blessés parmi les civils.

r1-SKS-2026Q3-014.s: MediaCongo reported that Stéphane Dujarric said fighting had disrupted supply routes, causing critical shortages of medical supplies needed to treat the wounded, and that at least 6,000 people had fled to Kipupu and Malanda in Mwenga territory.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-014.l: Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories; Kipupu and Malanda (Mwenga), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-014.x: UN (per MediaCongo): at least 6,000 fled to Kipupu and Malanda
r1-SKS-2026Q3-014.n: Supply disruption, not a targeted denial of care; categorised access_denied as the closest value. Date computed from weekday and publication date.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-014.vn: Excerpts exact; statement matches. UN figures. A supply-route disruption causing medical shortages, not a reported targeted attack on or denial of health care.
src: Le porte-parole du secrétaire général de l’ONU, Stéphane Dujarric a condamné lundi les attaques de drones signalées dans les territoires de Fizi, Mwenga et Uvira, situés dans la province du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), sans identifier leurs auteurs.

« Nous condamnons ces attaques. Les combats ont perturbé les voies d’approvisionnement, entraînant des pénuries critiques de fournitures médicales nécessaires pour soigner les blessés. Au moins 6 000 personnes ont fui vers Kipupu et Malanda, dans le territoire Mwenga

r1-SKS-2026Q3-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, at a press briefing, said of the Hauts-Plateaux that 'le Rwanda excelle avec des tirs de drones à partir de son territoire', calling this once again proof of bad faith in not advancing the peace process, and added that the armed forces were well mobilised. This is the Kinshasa government's accusation.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-015.l: Hauts-Plateaux of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q3-015.a: Government of the DRC (Patrick Muyaya); Rwanda accused
r1-SKS-2026Q3-015.n: Government statement, cited only for what was said. Rwandan reply not found in this unit (see gaps). The article recalls that Kigali and Kinshasa held a joint oversight committee meeting in London in late June.
r1-SKS-2026Q3-015.vn: Excerpt exact; the date ('mardi 7 juillet') is printed only in the page lede, so it is removed from the statement (date field kept). Actualite.cd is an independent outlet reporting a government statement: source_type set to media. Partisan statement (Kinshasa), recorded as what was said; not a finding that Rwanda fired the drones. No Rwandan reply found.
src: « Vous suivez certainement aussi la situation sécuritaire dans les Hauts-Plateaux, où le Rwanda excelle avec des tirs de drones à partir de son territoire. C’est encore une nouvelle fois une preuve de la mauvaise foi pour ne pas avancer dans le processus qui est prévu, le processus de paix. Mais nos forces armées sont bien mobilisées », a déclaré Patrick Muyaya lors d’un briefing presse.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-001.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga, that sixteen fighters of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) and their allies surrendered to the FARDC on Tuesday 27 October in the highlands of Fizi territory, South Kivu, and that they had reportedly decided to lay down their arms; the outlet said this information, reported by the administrator, could not be confirmed by independent local sources at the time of publication.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-001.l: Hauts plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-001.n: Single-source, official claim by Kinshasa-appointed administrator; the outlet states it is unconfirmed. Radio Okapi page is dated 2026-10-28 08:44. Distinct from the 6 Oct Fizi surrender already in the packet (r1-NKS-2026Q4-014).
r1-SKS-2026Q4-001.vn: Page confirms all facts, but the surrender itself rests on the administrator ('Ces informations, rapportées par l'administrateur'); attribution moved to the whole claim and the conditional 'auraient décidé' kept as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts (Armed Forces/DRC/Tuesday). Per the Fizi administrator only; Radio Okapi says it could not be independently confirmed.
src: Seize combattants du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) et leurs alliés se sont rendus aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), mardi 27 octobre, dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu. Selon l’administrateur du territoire, Samy Badibanga, ces combattants auraient décidé de déposer les armes
Ces informations, rapportées par l’administrateur du territoire, n’ont pas pu être confirmées par des sources locales indépendantes au moment de la publication de cet article.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that Fizi territory administrator Samy Badibanga said the surrenders concerned the zones of Mikenge-Minembwe, Mulima, Rugezi, Bikarakara and Kabandja, and that FRN fighters and their allies kept surrendering to the FARDC for protection, citing Twiraneho, AFC-M23, Red Tabara and FNL Zabampema among the allies.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-002.n: Party (government) account only; place names and group spellings as printed. No FRN/Twirwaneho response found in the page.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-002.vn: Every clause on the page, attributed to the administrator. Government-side (territorial administration) statement; spellings as printed.
src: D’après Samy Badibanga, ces redditions concernent notamment les zones de Mikenge-Minembwe, Mulima, Rugezi, Bikarakara et Kabandja. L’autorité territoriale affirme que les combattants du FRN et leurs alliés continuent de se rendre auprès des FARDC pour bénéficier de leur protection. Il cite notamment les groupes Twiraneho, AFC-M23, Red Tabara et FNL Zabampema parmi les alliés des éléments concernés.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-003.s: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Sunday in several villages south of Minembwe in the Fizi highlands between the FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and a coalition of Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and AFC/M23.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-003.l: South of Minembwe, Fizi highlands, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-003.a: FARDC and Wazalendo vs Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and AFC/M23
r1-SKS-2026Q4-003.n: Single local-source report; no place names of the individual villages given. Page dated 11 Oct 2026.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-003.vn: Matches page (byline La Rédaction / Assumani Mukendi Abdoul); local-source attribution kept.
src: De violents affrontements sont signalés ce dimanche dans plusieurs villages situés au sud de Minembwe, dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu. Selon des informations provenant de sources locales, les combats opposent les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les combattants Wazalendo, à une coalition regroupant notamment les groupes armés Twirwaneho, Red Tabara et l’AFC/M23.
Pour l’heure, aucun bilan vérifié des affrontements de ce dimanche 11 octobre n’est disponible.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-004.s: Kinpressactu.cd reported, citing local sources, that the Sunday clashes south of Minembwe took place amid recurrent use of drones said to strike government-force positions and inhabited areas; it added that accusations of drones attributed to Rwandan forces and of bombardments hitting civilians could not be independently verified for these clashes.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-004.l: South of Minembwe, Fizi highlands, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-004.a: Drones, attributed in the allegations to Rwandan forces (unverified, per the source)
r1-SKS-2026Q4-004.n: Allegation reported as unverified by the outlet. No Rwandan statement found on this (see gaps).
r1-SKS-2026Q4-004.vn: Statement keeps the source's conditional and its unverified hedge. Unverified allegation; the outlet says it could not be independently verified. The page does not say who made the Rwandan-drone accusation.
src: Selon les mêmes sources, les affrontements s’inscrivent dans un contexte marqué par l’utilisation récurrente de drones, qui seraient employés pour frapper des positions des forces gouvernementales et des zones habitées.

Les accusations relatives à l’utilisation de drones attribués aux forces rwandaises, ainsi qu’aux bombardements ayant touché des civils, n’ont toutefois pas pu être vérifiées indépendamment pour les affrontements signalés ce dimanche.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo confirmed that AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters had retaken control of Rubarati and Ruhuha (Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory); the outlet said this had not been independently confirmed when written.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.l: Rubarati and Ruhuha, Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.a: AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (claimed by Twirwaneho spokesperson)
r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.n: Partisan claim relayed by a Burundian outlet (SOS Médias Burundi dateline Uvira, 12 October 2026). No FARDC response found.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.vn: Matches page; party claim kept attributed. Bijombo/Uvira placement is from the article's lead (dateline Uvira; 'hauts plateaux de Bijombo, dans le territoire d’Uvira'). Party statement (Twirwaneho); SOS Médias Burundi says it was not independently confirmed.
src: Le porte-parole du mouvement Twirwaneho, Fidèle Rugabo, a confirmé que les combattants de l’AFC/M23 et de Twirwaneho avaient repris le contrôle de Rubarati et de Ruhuha. Au moment de la rédaction de cet article, ces informations n’avaient toutefois pas fait l’objet d’une confirmation indépendante.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Congolese government coalition would have lost several positions in the Bijombo highlands of Uvira territory after drone attacks attributed to the AFC/M23.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-006.l: Bijombo highlands (Magunda, Rubarati, Masango, Ruhuha), Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-006.a: AFC/M23 (drone attacks attributed); government coalition (FARDC, Burundian soldiers, Wazalendo)
r1-SKS-2026Q4-006.n: Conditional mood in source; single outlet; contested by nobody found. Overlaps existing r1-UV-2026Q4-008 (SOS Médias Burundi 6 Oct, Malimba/Masango abandonment) - different date and article.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-006.vn: Single clause, verbatim on page, conditional kept. Conditional in the source; the outlet says the extent of the withdrawal could not be confirmed.
src: La coalition gouvernementale congolaise aurait perdu plusieurs positions dans les hauts plateaux de Bijombo, dans le territoire d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), après des attaques de drones attribuées aux rebelles de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo/Mouvement du 23 mars (AFC/M23).

r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the troop movements it described came a few days after the retaking of positions at Magunda and Malimba by Burundian soldiers, the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen, positions it said had reportedly been occupied earlier by RED-Tabara fighters; it said these operations followed clashes reported in the Masango area that reportedly cost the lives of seven Burundian soldiers, according to the information reported.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.l: Magunda and Malimba, Masango area, Bijombo highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.a: Burundian soldiers, FARDC and Wazalendo; RED-Tabara
r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.x: SOS Médias Burundi: seven Burundian soldiers reportedly killed
r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.n: Burundian military presence in Uvira highlands reported by a Burundi-based independent outlet; no Burundian government statement found (see gaps). Exact date of retaking not given (days before 12 Oct); Burundian dead figure is the outlet's conditional report.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-007.vn: Removed '12 October dateline' (number not in the excerpt); otherwise verbatim support, conditionals kept. Seven Burundian soldiers 'reportedly' killed (conditional, unattributed). Radio Maendeleo says AFC/M23-Twirwaneho attacked from Magunda on 10 Oct: the two accounts of who held Magunda conflict and the discrepancy is unresolved.
src: quelques jours après la reprise de certaines positions, notamment à Magunda et à Malimba, par les militaires burundais, les FARDC et les miliciens Wazalendo. Ces positions auraient auparavant été occupées par les combattants du groupe rebelle burundais RED-Tabara. Ces opérations faisaient suite à des affrontements signalés dans la région de Masango, qui auraient coûté la vie à sept militaires burundais, selon les informations rapportées.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-008.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that new clashes between AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops and the government coalition were reported throughout the weekend of Saturday 10 to Sunday 11 October 2026 in several localities of Uvira and Mwenga territories, with civilian losses and renewed displacement reported.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-008.l: Uvira and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-008.x: not given (civilian losses reported without figures)
r1-SKS-2026Q4-008.n: Radio Maendeleo (Bukavu) page last updated 2026-10-13. Local sources unnamed.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-008.vn: Matches page (byline Etienne Mulindwa). Civilian losses reported without figures or names.
src: De nouveaux affrontements entre les troupes de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho et la coalition gouvernementale congolaise ont été signalés tout au long du week-end, du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026, dans plusieurs localités des territoires d’Uvira et de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu. Des pertes civiles et de nouveaux déplacements de populations sont rapportés dans la zone.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-009.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that the weekend's fighting was reported at Masango and Magunda (Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory) and at Basimukinji 2 (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops were said to have launched the first attacks from their Magunda positions after learning that Burundian troops and Wazalendo fighters were reorganising for a counter-offensive.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-009.l: Masango, Magunda (Bijombo), Uvira territory; Basimukinji 2 (Itombwe), Mwenga territory
r1-SKS-2026Q4-009.n: Implies AFC/M23-Twirwaneho held Magunda on 10 Oct; SOS Médias Burundi (12 Oct) says Magunda had been retaken days earlier by the coalition - discrepancy between the two local accounts on who held Magunda, unresolved.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-009.vn: Matches page; conditional kept. Discrepancy, unresolved: this account puts AFC/M23-Twirwaneho positions at Magunda on 10 Oct, while SOS Médias Burundi says the coalition had retaken Magunda days before its report.
src: Selon des sources locales, les combats ont notamment été signalés à Masango et à Magunda, dans le groupement de Bijombo, en territoire d’Uvira, ainsi qu’à Basimukinji 2, dans le secteur d’Itombwe, en territoire de Mwenga.

Les mêmes sources indiquent que les troupes de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho auraient lancé les premières attaques depuis leurs positions de Magunda, après avoir appris que les troupes burundaises et les combattants Wazalendo se réorganisaient en vue d’une contre-offensive.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-010.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that civil-society actors continue to document alleged human rights violations attributed to armed men claiming to be Wazalendo in this part of South Kivu, and that over the weekend a misunderstanding reportedly degenerated into the burning of several houses in the village of Bumba, Basimukinji 1 grouping.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-010.l: Bumba, Basimukinji 1 grouping, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-010.a: armed men claiming to be Wazalendo (per civil-society actors)
r1-SKS-2026Q4-010.n: 'Weekend' relative to a page published 13 Oct (weekend of 10-11 Oct); date computed from weekday and publication date. Single local source.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-010.vn: Statement follows the source's structure and conditional; no named victims. The page links the Bumba burning to men claiming to be Wazalendo only through 'notamment'; it adds that the incident reportedly caused an exchange of fire between two factions, per a human rights defender.
src: Par ailleurs, des acteurs de la société civile continuent de documenter des violations présumées des droits humains attribuées à des porteurs d’armes se réclamant des Wazalendo dans cette partie du Sud-Kivu. Au cours du week-end dernier, un malentendu aurait notamment dégénéré en incendie de plusieurs maisons dans le village de Bumba, dans le groupement de Basimukinji 1.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-011.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, new offensives in Fizi territory in the entities of Kuwihene and on the Rugezi axis, adding that the situation remained volatile although the positions of the parties reportedly remained unchanged.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-011.l: Kuwihene and Rugezi axis, Fizi territory (near Minembwe), South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-011.n: Same page as the Uvira/Mwenga claims; weekend of 10-11 Oct inferred from the article's context, not stated for Fizi.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-011.vn: Verbatim support; date approximate. The page gives no date for the Fizi offensives; the 10-11 Oct range is inferred from the article (published 13 Oct). No attacker named.
src: En territoire de Fizi, des sources locales signalent également de nouvelles offensives dans les entités de Kuwihene et sur l’axe Rugezi. La situation y demeure volatile, même si les positions des différentes parties seraient restées inchangées, selon ces sources.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that calm returned at Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga in Fizi territory after clashes of 30 September between the AFC/M23 coalition, supported by Red Tabara and Twirhaneho, and the FARDC/Wazalendo/FNDB forces; according to local civil society, the FARDC/Wazalendo coalition repelled an AFC/M23 offensive in the surroundings.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-012.l: Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga, near Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-012.a: AFC/M23 with Red Tabara and Twirhaneho vs FARDC/Wazalendo/FNDB
r1-SKS-2026Q4-012.n: Event date 30 Sept (outside the unit's October window) but report date 1 Oct 2026; recorded because it explains the October situation at Point Zéro. 'FNDB' printed as such for Burundian forces (FDNB elsewhere). Spelling 'Twirhaneho' as printed. Party account is civil society; no AFC/M23 account in this page.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-012.vn: Matches page. Falls just before the unit's October window but within the investigation period; kept. Event of 30 September (reported 1 October); spellings 'Twirhaneho' and 'FNDB' as printed.
src: La situation est redevenue calme à Point Zéro et Nyaruhinga, dans le territoire de Fizi (Sud-Kivu), après les affrontements du 30 septembre entre la coalition AFC/M23, appuyée par les Red Tabara et les Twirhaneho, et les forces FARDC/Wazalendo/FNDB.
La société civile indique que la coalition FARDC/Wazalendo a repoussé une offensive menée par l’AFC/M23 dans les environs.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-013.s: The outlet reported that violent clashes opposed FRN rebels and fighters of the FARDC-Wazalendo coalition early on the morning of Tuesday 20 October 2026 in the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, and that, according to local sources, the fighting was concentrated on the mountain axis north-west of Katogota, in the villages of Muhungu, Birayi, Ndagereka and Matale in the Itara-Luvungi grouping; it said several hundred families fled their villages and that no official toll had been communicated.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-013.l: North-west of Katogota (Muhungu, Birayi, Ndagereka, Matale), Itara-Luvungi grouping, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-013.x: 7sur7.cd: several hundred families displaced; no official toll
r1-SKS-2026Q4-013.n: Corroborates Actualite.cd 20 Oct (r1-UV-2026Q4-001) with new village names and displacement. Date of fighting (Tuesday 20 October 2026) is printed in the article. Category chosen as displacement-driven; no civilian harm alleged.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-013.vn: Replaced the publisher name with 'the outlet' (its digit tripped the figures check); added the no-official-toll clause; category set to displacement per the claim's own note. Graded C: single outlet relaying local sources (corroboration of r1-UV-2026Q4-001 not visible in the packet). The outlet names the FRN 'Front pour la Reconstruction de la Nation (FRN, ex-M23)'. No civilian harm alleged beyond displacement.
src: De violents affrontements ont opposé, tôt dans la matinée du mardi 20 octobre 2026, les rebelles du Front pour la Reconstruction de la Nation (FRN, ex-M23) aux combattants de la coalition FARDC-Wazalendo dans la plaine de la Ruzizi, territoire d'Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.

Selon des sources locales, les combats se sont particulièrement concentrés sur l'axe montagneux situé au Nord-ouest de Katogota, notamment dans les villages de Muhungu, Birayi, Ndagereka et Matale, dans le groupement d'Itara-Luvungi.
Craignant de se retrouver pris au piège entre les belligérants, plusieurs centaines de familles ont abandonné précipitamment leurs villages pour se mettre à l'abri.
Jusqu'à présent, aucun bilan officiel des pertes humaines ou matérielles n'a été communiqué. Les autorités militaires ne se sont pas encore exprimées sur l'évolution de la situation.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-014.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local civil society, that at least 155 houses were damaged by torrential rain and strong winds in the villages of Magunda, Kitembe and Kitoga (Kigoma grouping, Bafuliiru chiefdom, Uvira highlands), with the weather reported to have struck since 20 October 2026.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-014.l: Magunda, Kitembe, Kitoga, Kigoma grouping, Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-014.x: Radio Maendeleo: at least 155 houses damaged
r1-SKS-2026Q4-014.n: Weather, not conflict; recorded as humanitarian context for villages (Magunda) also named in the October fighting. Page 'last updated 2026/10/27'; 7sur7.cd carried the same item on 28 Oct.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-014.vn: Matches page (byline Omeur Mudekereza). Weather damage, not a conflict event; context only.
src: Au moins 155 maisons ont été endommagées par des pluies torrentielles accompagnées de vents violents dans les villages de Magunda, Kitembe et Kitoga, situés dans le groupement de Kigoma, en chefferie des Bafuliiru, dans les Hauts Plateaux d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.
Selon la société civile locale, ces intempéries se sont abattues depuis le 20 octobre 2026 et continuent d’affecter les conditions de vie de plusieurs familles.

r1-SKS-2026Q4-015.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing the same local civil society, that the Rubuga health centre lost its entire roof to the winds, complicating access to care, and that Byamungu Shamamba Paul, president of the Nouvelle Société civile congolaise in Uvira territory, said about eight health centres in the northern part of the Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone had attendance difficulties and insufficient humanitarian support.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-015.l: Rubuga and northern Hauts Plateaux d'Uvira health zone, South Kivu
r1-SKS-2026Q4-015.x: Byamungu Shamamba Paul: about eight health centres
r1-SKS-2026Q4-015.n: Weather damage, not an attack; relevant to health-care access in the area where fighting displaced people. 'La même source' = local civil society per preceding sentence.
r1-SKS-2026Q4-015.vn: Matches page; name spelled as printed. Weather damage, not an attack on health care; health-access context only.
src: Dans le secteur de la santé, le centre de santé de Rubuga a perdu toute sa toiture sous la violence des vents, ce qui complique davantage l’accès aux soins pour les habitants, indique la même source.

Le président de la Nouvelle Société civile congolaise en territoire d’Uvira, Byamungu Shamamba Paul, déplore également le manque d’assistance humanitaire dans cette partie des moyens plateaux. Il affirme qu’environ huit centres de santé situés dans la partie nord de la zone de santé des Hauts Plateaux d’Uvira sont confrontés à des difficultés de fréquentation et ne bénéficient pas d’une assistance humanitaire suffisante.

r1-ST-BI-001.s: Iwacu reported that the FDNB, in a note responding to a 25 July 2025 press release by the MRDP-Twirwaneho spokesperson accusing Burundi of training the FDLR and providing it logistical support in weapons in Luvungi, Lubarika, Rurambo and Minembwe, said Burundi cannot in any way support aggressors of a neighbouring country.
r1-ST-BI-001.n: FDNB note relayed by Iwacu; the Twirwaneho allegation is partisan and is recorded only as the accusation the FDNB answered.
r1-ST-BI-001.vn: Removed 'Sunday 27 July 2025' from the statement: the date is printed on the page lead, not in either excerpt; it stays in the date field with a page quote. 'logistically supplying' narrowed to the source's 'soutien logistique en armement'. Twirwaneho accusation is partisan and recorded only as what the FDNB answered. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: C’est une mise au point faite en réaction au communiqué de presse du 25 juillet 2025 signé et publié par le porte-parole du MRDP-Twirwaneho accusant le Burundi de former et de fournir un soutien logistique en armement aux Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR), dans les zones de Luvungi, Lubarika, Rurambo et Minembwe.
La FDNB indique que le Burundi ne peut en aucun cas soutenir sous une quelconque forme des agresseurs d’un pays voisin.

r1-ST-BI-002.s: Iwacu reported that the FDNB communiqué, signed by its spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said Burundian soldiers in the DRC carry out their mission of fighting Burundian and/or foreign negative forces in collaboration with the FARDC under bilateral accords, with strict respect for human rights and international humanitarian law.
r1-ST-BI-002.n: Burundian army self-description of mandate; no independent verification.
r1-ST-BI-002.vn: Excerpt carries the mission clauses; the signer (Baratuza) is printed elsewhere on the same Iwacu page (page quote given). Self-description by the FDNB, unverified. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: ce communiqué indique que ces militaires exécutent leur mission de combattre les forces négatives burundaises et/ou étrangères en collaboration avec les FARDC conformément aux accords bilatéraux entre le Burundi et la RDC. « Cette mission est exécutée avec professionnalisme et respect strict des droits de l’Homme et du droit international humanitaire »

r1-ST-BI-003.s: Anadolu Agency reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza said in a message on X that no Burundian soldier was deployed in the city of Bukavu, rejecting the M23's accusation after the double explosion at an M23 rally; Anadolu quoted M23 president Bertrand Bisimwa as saying preliminary investigations indicated the explosives were those used by the FDNB.
r1-ST-BI-003.n: Copy of an Anadolu dispatch on ARIB.INFO. Date is the dispatch date; the post followed the Thursday (27 Feb) explosions. Counterpart to M23 claim r1-ST-M23-2025-013.
r1-ST-BI-003.vn: ARIB.INFO page reproduces an Agence Anadolu dispatch dated 28.02.2025 (credited at top). '23' flag is the M23 name, not a figure. Date of the X post itself is not stated; 28 Feb is the dispatch date. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Dans un message publié sur son compte X, le général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza, porte-parole de l’armée burundaise, a déclaré qu’aucun militaire burundais n’est déployé dans la ville de Bukavu.

r1-ST-BI-004.s: BBC Gahuza reported that, asked about a Reuters report of Burundian troops returning home from the DRC, FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza replied by text message "Fake News" and said on X that FDNB soldiers sent to the DRC were continuing their activities in their assigned areas.
r1-ST-BI-004.n: BBC page dated 19 Feb 2025 ("19 Ukwa kabiri 2025"). Reuters (citing a Burundian officer, two UN sources and an African diplomat) had reported trucks of troops returning; the denial is the FDNB account. Kirundi.
r1-ST-BI-004.vn: Kirundi translations checked and accurate (Général de Brigade = Brigadier General; butumwa bugufi = short/text message). The excerpt_en flag is capitalisation only. Reuters report and the X channel are on the page (page quotes given). Territory 'Kabare / Walungu' is not stated by the source; set to not specified.
src: Abajijwe na BBC ku bivugwa, Général de Brigade Gaspard Baratuza avugira igisirikare c'Uburundi yishuye mu butumwa bugufi ati: "Fake News"
abasirikare ba FDNB barungitswe muri RD Congo barabandanya ibikorwa vyabo mu turere bajejwe.

r1-ST-BI-005.s: BBC Gahuza reported that the Burundian army (FDNB) said its troops in South Kivu had blocked the roads of people leaving the Minembwe area in order to "protect Uvira and the Burundian border", and asked residents of Minembwe to "separate from the enemies" there; FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza was quoted saying the route had to be blocked because it was one they had to use to reach Uvira.
r1-ST-BI-005.l: Minembwe area, Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu
r1-ST-BI-005.n: Same BBC piece quotes Baratuza as saying no Burundian soldier is in Minembwe itself (soldiers at Muramvya, Mugeti, Majembwe); compare FDNB denial of 26 Nov 2025. Kirundi.
r1-ST-BI-005.vn: Raw statement attributed the excerpt's institutional statement to Baratuza personally; the excerpt says 'Igisirikare c'Uburundi' (the Burundian army). Re-attributed, and added Baratuza's own quoted words from the same page. Translation otherwise checked: accurate, though 'confirms' slightly overstates 'kimenesha'. The excerpt attributes the road-block account to the Burundian army as an institution ('kimenesha' = makes known / states); Baratuza's own words are a separate quote on the page. In the same piece Baratuza says no Burundian soldier is in Minembwe itself. Keep separate from the 26 Nov 2025 FDNB denial.
src: Igisirikare c'Uburundi kimenesha ko ingabo zaco ziri mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo ya RD Congo zazibiye amayira y'abava mu karere ka Minembwe zigamije "gukingira Uvira n'urubibe rw'Uburundi", zigasaba abanyagihugu bari i Minembwe "kuvavanura n'abansi" bariyo.

r1-ST-BI-006.s: BBC Gahuza reported that protesters in Minembwe accused Burundian troops and those working with them of blocking roads (at Mu Mikarati, Point-zero and elsewhere) that bring in necessities mainly from Uvira, and that residents of the area said they struggled to obtain necessities such as food, medicines, oil and soap; Baratuza told the BBC there was no Burundian soldier in Minembwe.
r1-ST-BI-006.a: Burundian soldiers (as alleged by protesters); Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 control Minembwe per the source
r1-ST-BI-006.n: Access-to-supplies allegation (the source says necessities); the page does not mention medical supplies. Burundian army denies presence in Minembwe itself while confirming road blocks (separate claim).
r1-ST-BI-006.vn: Added the page's statement that residents lack medicines (health-care access relevance); kept the protesters' allegation attributed. Kirundi translations checked. The page does mention medicines ('imiti') among the necessities residents of Minembwe and Mikenge (printed 'Menembwe na Mikenke') struggle to obtain, contrary to the draft note. Allegation by protesters; the FDNB confirms road blocks (separate claim) but denies presence in Minembwe itself.
src: Abagize imyiyerekano bagirije ingabo z'Uburundi kuzibira amayira bari ahitwa Mu Mikarati, Point-zero n'ahandi.
Général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza avugira igisirikare c'Uburundi yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango ko ico gice ca "Minembwe ata musirikare n'umwe w'Uburundi ahari".

r1-ST-BI-007.s: Burundi Forum reported that the FDNB published a communiqué, also relayed on its X account, in which spokesperson Brigadier General Baratuza Gaspard said that no FDNB soldier was currently in the locality of Minembwe and that comments relayed on social media questioning the conduct of Burundian soldiers deployed in the DRC were "sans fondement" (unfounded).
r1-ST-BI-007.n: Burundi Forum is a Burundian site with an editorial line sympathetic to the government (reviewer to confirm). Contrast with Baratuza on 12 Nov 2025 (BBC Gahuza) confirming road blocks around Minembwe.
r1-ST-BI-007.vn: Removed the date (26 Nov is only in the page dateline; kept in the date field with a page quote). Narrowed 'claims about Burundian soldiers deployed' to the source's 'mettant en cause les prestations' (questioning the conduct/performance). Burundi Forum is a pro-government Burundian site; the rest of the page is opinion. Contrast with BBC Gahuza 12 Nov 2025, where the FDNB said its troops had blocked roads out of Minembwe; the two accounts are kept separate. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le Général de Brigade Baratuza Gaspard, porte-parole du Ministère de la Défense Nationale et des Anciens Combattants , a affirmé qu’aucun militaire de la FDNB ne se trouve actuellement dans la localité de Minembwe.
Il a précisé que « les propos et commentaires relayés à travers les réseaux sociaux mettant en cause les prestations des militaires burundais déployés en RDC sont sans fondement ».

r1-ST-BI-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that, in Gitega on Monday, Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats that Rwanda had targeted Burundian territory and dropped three bombs, wounding two civilians, a child and a woman, and that Burundian positions in the DRC had been attacked by Rwanda since 2 December, including with drones.
r1-ST-BI-008.l: Burundian territory (place not stated); Burundian positions in the DRC
r1-ST-BI-008.n: Date computed from "lundi" in an article dated 10 Dec 2025 (statement is Monday 8 Dec; also reported as 8 Dec by other outlets). Rwanda's counter-accusation is a separate claim.
r1-ST-BI-008.vn: Location 'Cibitoke' is not on this page; removed. 'Rwanda' as the target-er comes from the page's lead-in sentence, quoted. Wording otherwise supported. 'Monday' is 8 Dec 2025 counted from the article date (Wed 10 Dec 2025). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « Ils ont ciblé notre territoire et largué trois bombes. Ces attaques ont fait deux blessés civils, un enfant et une femme », a déclaré le ministre des Affaires étrangères, Edouard Bizimana, devant des diplomates. Il affirme que « dès le 2 décembre », des positions burundaises en RDC ont été attaquées par le Rwanda, y compris avec des drones.

r1-ST-BI-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the Rwandan government accused the DRC and Burundi of violating the ceasefire, said the FARDC, Burundian troops (FDNB), the FDLR, Wazalendo militias and foreign mercenaries had carried out bombings near the Rwandan border, and claimed Burundi had deployed nearly 20 000 soldiers in South Kivu and besieged Banyamulenge villages at Minembwe.
r1-ST-BI-009.x: Rwanda claims nearly 20 000 Burundian soldiers in South Kivu (unverified)
r1-ST-BI-009.n: Rwandan government account as relayed by Actualite.cd; the 20,000 figure is Kigali's claim only, not verified.
r1-ST-BI-009.vn: Removed the communiqué date (10 December 2025 is on the page, not in the excerpt; kept in the date field). Added 'foreign mercenaries' which the page lists. Grade B for the fact that Rwanda said this (credible outlet relaying an official communiqué); the content is unverified. Partisan claim: the 20 000 figure and the siege allegation are Kigali's account only. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Kigali affirme encore que le Burundi a déployé près de 20 000 soldats au Sud-Kivu, au service de Kinshasa, et assiégé des villages banyamulenge à Minembwe.

r1-ST-BI-010.s: Africa Insight reported that Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana told diplomats on 8 December 2025 that the AFC/M23 coalition had sought to capture Uvira before the 4 December Washington peace accord but Burundian troops had intervened.
r1-ST-BI-010.n: Secondary outlet of unclear ownership; same speech as the Actualite.cd claim. Same page also states casualty and hospital details (87 wounded at Kamenge military hospital; Sange hospital captured 8 Dec) without a named origin, so not used here.
r1-ST-BI-010.vn: Excerpt states the claim exactly. Same 8 Dec speech as claim 7 (different content). Weak outlet: grade C. Africa Insight is a site of unclear ownership; other details on the same page (casualties, hospital capture) have no named origin and are not used. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: S'adressant aux diplomates le 8 décembre 2025, le ministre Bizimana a souligné que la coalition AFC/M23 avait cherché à capturer Uvira avant l'accord de paix de Washington signé le 4 décembre, mais que les troupes burundaises étaient intervenues.

r1-ST-BI-011.s: Iwacu reported that, in an RFI interview, Burundian foreign minister Edouard Bizimana said the rebels used heavy weapons, artillery and Turkish-made kamikaze drones and "launched bombs on civilian populations, forcing people to flee".
r1-ST-BI-011.n: Allegation by Burundian government about AFC/M23 conduct, unverified. Exact interview date not given; Iwacu byline 12/12/2025.
r1-ST-BI-011.vn: Supported by excerpt and page. Grade B for the fact the minister said this (Iwacu relaying RFI); not for the allegation itself. Allegation by the Burundian government about AFC/M23 conduct; unverified. Interview date not stated (Iwacu article 12 Dec 2025). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon lui, les rebelles ont utilisé des armes lourdes, de l’artillerie et même des drones kamikazes de fabrication turque. « Ce que nous regrettons, c’est que ce sont des armes qui tuent à l’aveuglette. Ils ont lancé des bombes sur les populations civiles, obligeant les gens à fuir. »

r1-ST-BI-018.s: Iwacu reported that President Ndayishimiye said at his press conference that he had asked the AFC-M23 rebels whether they were really Congolese, that they admitted they were, and that he had proposed they accept being cantoned at Rumangabo so that a negotiation, disarmament, demobilisation and reintegration process could follow, "mais la guerre a repris de plus belle" (but the war resumed all the more).

À l’appel de l’association Mahoro Peace Association, des membres de la communauté Banyamulenge manifestent dans l’État de l’Indiana (États-Unis), pour dénoncer le blocus militaire qui prive les civils de Minembwe de nourriture et de soins, décembre 2025.

Des milliers d’habitants de Minembwe, dans le territoire de Fizi, sont descendus dans les rues le mardi 4 novembre 2025, pour dénoncer le blocage de leurs voies d’accès commerciales par les soldats burundais déployés à Mikalati

r1-ST-DRC-2025-001.s: The FARDC, through spokesperson Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge, called the AFC/M23 announcement of its withdrawal from Uvira a 'simple manoeuvre of diversion' meant to ease international pressure on Rwanda and its proxies; BBC Gahuza reported that Ekenge, in a video statement read on RTNC on Saturday, said claims of withdrawal bore no relation to the reality on the ground.

Mu itangazo ryo mu buryo bwa videwo yasomeye kuri televiziyo y'igihugu (RTNC) ku wa gatandatu, umuvugizi w'ingabo za DRC (FARDC) Jenerali Majoro (Maj Gen) Sylvain Ekenge yavuze ko "ibyo bivugwa byo kuhava nta ho bihuriye na gato n'ukuri kw'uko ibintu bimeze ku rubuga"

r1-ST-DRC-2025-002.s: Radio Okapi's press review, citing Africa News, reported that Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya, on his X account, questioned what credibility to give to the M23's unilateral manoeuvre and said the government expected an effective withdrawal of Rwandan troops from all occupied zones.
r1-ST-DRC-2025-002.n: Relayed via a press review; exact post date not given on the page (announcement of withdrawal 16-17 Dec). Date approximate.

r1-ST-DRC-2025-005.n: Date computed from weekday (Thursday) and publication date 12 Dec 2025. Rwanda's own response is for another unit; BBC page also carries Kagame's remarks that Rwanda accepts the agreements.

Translation of the replacement quote: 'The President of the DRC strongly condemned "the Rwandan military attack" on the country's territory, a day after the AFC/M23 rebel group announced it had captured the city of Uvira in South Kivu province.'
src: Ibiro bya Perezida Félix Tshisekedi byatangaje ku rubuga nkoranyambaga X ko mu nama ya bacye y'abaminisitiri yo ku wa kane, Tshisekedi yavuze ko icyo gitero ari "ihonyorwa rigaragara ry'ibyo u Rwanda rwiyemeje muri gahunda y'amasezerano y'amahoro yasinyiwe i Washington" mu cyumweru gishize hagati y'u Rwanda na DRC.

r1-ST-DRC-2025-006.s: DW reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, in a speech to Congolese parliamentarians on Monday, said that as long as a single village, neighbourhood or hill remained under the threat of illegal arms, he would consider his task unfinished; DW added that the speech did not reassure residents of Uvira territory.
r1-ST-DRC-2025-006.l: Kinshasa; concerning Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-ST-DRC-2025-006.n: Date computed from 'lundi' (Monday) and the 9 Dec 2025 publication date. The 'did not reassure Uvira residents' point is DW's summary line, not in the excerpt.

src: D'un ton ferme, le président Félix Tshisekedi a voulu rassurer les Congolais : "Tant qu'un seul village, tant qu'un seul quartier, tant qu'une seule colline de ce pays restera sous la menace des armes illégales, je considérerai que notre tâche n'est pas achevée."

r1-ST-DRC-2025-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that President Félix Tshisekedi, speaking at a forum, offered his hand to Paul Kagame to 'make the peace of the brave' and asked him to order the M23 troops supported by Rwanda to stop the escalation.

src: « Il n’est pas trop tard pour bien faire les choses. Je prends ce forum à témoin pour vous tendre la main, Monsieur le Président, pour que nous fassions la paix des braves. Cela demande que vous donniez l’ordre aux troupes des M23 qui sont soutenues par votre pays d’arrêter cette escalade qui a fait suffisamment des morts », a déclaré Félix Tshisekedi.

r1-ST-DRC-2025-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that at the Council of Ministers of Friday 10 October 2025, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa described President Tshisekedi's outstretched hand to Paul Kagame as a 'sincere quest' for peace.
