src: Le communiqué affirme que, le 10 août 2026, plus de 100 familles d’origine rwandaise ont franchi la frontière par la piste de Kabuhanga, dans le territoire de Nyiragongo.
Elles auraient ensuite été installées à Rwibiranga, dans le groupement de Buhumba, notamment dans des entrepôts construits par le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM).
Kinshasa dénonce également l’imposition de taxes dans les zones contrôlées par l’AFC/M23.
Les structures sanitaires, notamment les hôpitaux publics et privés, ainsi que les orphelinats, seraient également soumis à des taxes et impôts que Kinshasa qualifie d’illégaux.

r1-ST-DRC-2026-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that local civil society and notables of Kaniola, Walungu territory, denounced rapes, which they presented as a means of terrorising communities, after the AFC/M23 incursion, per testimonies collected on the spot.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-013.a: AFC/M23 (as alleged by local civil society and the provincial government)
r1-ST-DRC-2026-013.n: Radio Okapi relays local actors without individual victim details; no figures given. Slug truncated in search display but page fetched live. Date: statement of Tuesday 8 September per page.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-013.vn: Supported; Walungu and the AFC/M23 incursion are in the article lead. Allegation by local actors; no figures or individual victims given. '23' flag is from 'M23' only.
src: Des témoignages recueillis sur place font également état de violences sexuelles commises contre des femmes, notamment à domicile ou dans les champs. La société civile et des notables de Kaniola dénoncent notamment des viols qu’ils présentent comme un moyen de terroriser les communautés.

r1-ST-DRC-2026-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that the South Kivu provincial government spokesperson, Me Luganywa-Bashizi Didier, condemned the abuses reported at Kaniola and called for those responsible to be brought to justice.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-014.n: Radio Okapi names the provincial spokesperson as Luganywa-Bashizi Didier; Actualite.cd/Radio Okapi elsewhere give 'Didier Kabi': possible name discrepancy, flagged.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-014.vn: Supported. The call for justice is made by 'l’exécutif provincial' on the page. Name spelled as Radio Okapi prints it; the drafter reports a different rendering elsewhere ('Didier Kabi'), not checked here.
src: Au nom du gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu, le porte-parole, Me Luganywa-Bashizi Didier, a condamné ces exactions.

r1-ST-DRC-2026-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Birambizo general referral hospital was again the target of looting on Wednesday 19 August; in the same report it said, citing local sources, that unidentified armed men took medicines, medical equipment and office supplies in the night of Monday to Tuesday. The two dates on the page do not agree.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-015.l: Birambizo general referral hospital, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-ST-DRC-2026-015.a: unidentified armed men (looting); AFC/M23 military cadres (arrests of health workers), per a hospital agent
r1-ST-DRC-2026-015.n: Page says looting on Wednesday 19 Aug and also 'night of Monday to Tuesday' (possible internal date inconsistency, flagged). Date computed from weekday and publication date.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-015.vn: Draft settled on 19 August; the page is internally inconsistent, so both dates are stated and the date set to a range. Both sources are one page. The page gives two dates for the looting: Wednesday 19 August and the night of Monday to Tuesday (17-18 August, given publication on Thursday 20 August). Both are stated; neither is preferred. Perpetrators unidentified.
src: Des hommes armés non identifiés ont emporté des médicaments, du matériel médical et des fournitures de bureau dans la nuit de lundi à mardi, selon des sources locales.
a de nouveau été la cible d’un pillage mercredi 19 août.

r1-ST-DRC-2026-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that since 13 August several health workers at Birambizo general referral hospital (Rutshuru) had been arrested by persons presented as AFC/M23 military cadres, in circumstances still to be clarified, among them the director of nursing care; according to a hospital agent, fearing further arrests several officials of the hospital had left the area, which contributed to disrupting the hospital's functioning and access to care for several days.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-016.a: AFC/M23 (persons presented as military cadres of the AFC/M23)
r1-ST-DRC-2026-016.n: Circumstances unclarified per source; AFC/M23 response not found. Individuals not named.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-016.vn: Kept the source's 'circumstances still to be clarified' hedge and attributed the disruption to the hospital agent, as the page does. Arrested staff are not named. Radio Okapi also reports two health-zone agents and a teacher arrested earlier. AFC/M23 response not found. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Aug 2026. All clauses are on the page, but the stored excerpt carries only the arrests sentence; the director and the fear/disruption clauses (attributed to the hospital agent) were added as excerpts. The page says the situation 'contributed to' disrupting care, now reflected. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Aug 2026. All clauses are on the page, but the stored excerpt carries only the arrests sentence; the director and the fear/disruption clauses (attributed to the hospital agent) were added as excerpts. The page says the situation 'contributed to' disrupting care, now reflected. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Aug 2026. All clauses are on the page, but the stored excerpt carries only the arrests sentence; the director and the fear/disruption clauses (attributed to the hospital agent) were added as excerpts. The page says the situation 'contributed to' disrupting care, now reflected.
src: Depuis le 13 août, plusieurs agents de santé avaient été arrêtés par des personnes présentées comme des cadres militaires de l’AFC/M23, dans des circonstances qui restent à clarifier.
Parmi les personnes interpellées figure notamment le directeur des soins infirmiers.

Craignant de nouvelles arrestations, plusieurs responsables de l’établissement avaient quitté la zone. Cette situation avait contribué à perturber le fonctionnement de l’hôpital et l’accès aux soins pendant plusieurs jours, rapporte l'agent de l’hôpital.

r1-ST-DRC-2026-017.s: MediaCongo reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame reminded the African Union facilitators on Wednesday that Rwanda would maintain its posture as long as the root causes of the conflict are not resolved; the outlet wrote that by root causes he mainly alluded to the 'continuing presence' of the FDLR in eastern DRC, and that according to Kagame the FDLR represent a direct and existential security threat.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-017.n: Date computed from weekday ('mercredi') and publication 9 Oct 2026. Rwandan presidency readout quoted by MediaCongo; Kagame's own words on the FDLR are paraphrased by the outlet. Outlet's framing of Kagame as 'designated by the Congolese government as a destabilising actor' is the outlet's characterisation. Meeting: AU facilitators Sahle-Work Zewde, Uhuru Kenyatta, Mokgweetsi Masisi, Yackoley Kokou Johnson.
r1-ST-DRC-2026-017.vn: Draft presented the outlet's interpretation ('fait principalement allusion') as Kagame's words; re-attributed. 'génocide' appears only inside the outlet's description of the FDLR and is not used in the statement. The posture and FDLR lines are MediaCongo's paraphrase of Kagame; the Rwandan presidency readout it quotes speaks only of root causes and next steps in the AU-led process. Meeting date (Wednesday 7 October) computed from the weekday and publication on 9 October.
src: Selon Kagame, les FDLR, groupe armé fondé par des extrémistes hutus ayant fui le Rwanda après avoir participé au génocide des Tutsis en 1994, représentent une menace sécuritaire directe et existentielle.

r1-ST-M23-2025-001.s: Imvaho Nshya, a Rwandan outlet, reported that AFC/M23 announced it had closed the airspace of Goma in order to stop DRC forces from continuing to use Goma airport to drop bombs on the population.
r1-ST-M23-2025-001.n: Rwandan state-linked outlet relaying an M23 communiqué dated Sunday 26 January 2025 (page dated 26 Jan). Evidence of what M23 said, not of the DRC conduct alleged. Kinshasa response not found.
r1-ST-M23-2025-001.vn: Excerpt (Kinyarwanda) states AFC/M23 announced closing Goma airspace for the stated reason; page dated 26 Jan 2025 and says the M23 statement came out on Sunday. Rwandan state-linked outlet relaying a party statement. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (country name rendered in English), not added content. Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-linked outlet; the DRC conduct alleged is M23's claim, not established.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 watangaje ko wafunze ikirere cy’i Goma mu rwego rwo gukumira ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC) zikomeza kwifashisha ikibuga cy’indege cya Goma mu kumisha ibisasu mu baturage.

r1-ST-M23-2025-002.s: Al Jazeera reported that M23 announced the capture of Goma on Monday, which the DRC government described as a "declaration of war" by Rwanda.
r1-ST-M23-2025-002.n: Records both the M23 claim and the government characterisation, as reported by Al Jazeera; the government characterisation is not a first-hand quote on this page.
r1-ST-M23-2025-002.vn: Excerpt carries both the M23 announcement and the DRC government characterisation as reported by Al Jazeera. The same page separately quotes FM Therese Kayikwamba Wagner at the UNSC on Sunday calling it 'a declaration of war'; the 'described' wording is Al Jazeera's paraphrase.
src: Earlier on Monday, M23 announced the capture of Goma, which the DRC government described was a “declaration of war” by Rwanda.

r1-ST-M23-2025-003.s: BBC News reported that Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government and vowed to continue the offensive to Kinshasa.
r1-ST-M23-2025-003.n: Page published Thursday 30 January 2025; the statement was made on or shortly before that date.
r1-ST-M23-2025-003.vn: BBC page (Plett-Usher and Rukanga, 30 Jan 2025) prints both clauses in the excerpt.
src: The rebel leader whose fighters have captured Goma, the biggest city in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, has vowed to continue their offensive all the way to the capital, Kinshasa. Corneille Nangaa, who heads an alliance of rebel groups that includes the M23, said their ultimate aim was to topple President Félix Tshisekedi's government.

r1-ST-M23-2025-004.s: BBC News reported that on Thursday Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.
r1-ST-M23-2025-004.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (page dated Thursday 30 January 2025).
r1-ST-M23-2025-004.vn: Excerpt matches statement exactly; Thursday = 30 Jan 2025 (page dated Thursday 30 January).
src: On Thursday, Nangaa presented the rebels as the new administrators of Goma, telling journalists they were there to stay and would get services up and running again.

r1-ST-M23-2025-005.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the M23 installed a new North Kivu provincial administration with Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, until then adviser to the M23 military coordinator, as governor, assisted by vice-governors Minani Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shadrack, and that the Alliance Fleuve Congo also announced other appointments including Julien Katembo as mayor of Goma.
r1-ST-M23-2025-005.n: The page text names the installation as 'jeudi' and the swearing-in as 'vendredi' (page dated Saturday 8 Feb); a photo caption on the page dates the Goma stadium event 6 February 2025. A different source (Les Souverain Libre / social media) spells the governor 'Bahati Musanga Joseph'; the page also prints 'Bahati Musanga Erasto' elsewhere in other outlets. Another outlet (Radio Elle FM Goma, Nov 2025) prints 'Bahati Musanga Erasto'. Kinshasa's own appointment of a military governor is out of this unit.
r1-ST-M23-2025-005.vn: Page says the M23 installed the new administration (Thursday) and that Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto 'est le nouveau gouverneur'; only the 'other appointments' (including the Goma mayor) are explicitly said to have been announced by the AFC. Narrowed so the governor/vice-governor appointment is not presented as an AFC announcement the page does not state. Spelling of the governor's name differs across outlets: 'Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto' (SOS Médias Burundi), 'Erasto Bahati Musanga' (Al Jazeera), 'Bahati Musanga Erasto' (Radio Elle FM), 'Jean Bahati Musanga' (Actualite.cd, EU sanctions list report, 17 Mar 2025). Date: page (8 Feb) says installed 'jeudi' and sworn in 'vendredi'; photo captions date the Goma stadium presentation 6 February 2025.
src: Bahati Musanga Joseph alias Erasto, jusqu’ici conseiller du coordinateur militaire du M23 est le nouveau gouverneur de province.

Le nouveau gouverneur de l’une des régions très riche en minerais au Congo, sera assisté par Minani Ngarambe Willy, vice-gouverneur en charge des questions politiques, administratives et juridiques et Amani Bahati Shadrack , en charge des questions économiques et financières notamment.
L’Alliance Fleuve Congo a également annoncé d’autres nominations. Elles concernent les administrateurs des territoires occupés ou encore le maire de la ville de Goma en la personne de Julien Katembo.

r1-ST-M23-2025-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the new governor, speaking in Kinyarwanda, said he had identified three main threats to security: former prisoners released by the Congolese authorities as M23 fighters were about to enter Goma, the local militias known as the Wazalendo, and the Hutu FDLR.
r1-ST-M23-2025-006.n: Party account only; the characterisations (including 'génocidaires') are the speaker's, relayed by the outlet. Date: event 6 Feb 2025 per photo caption on the page; see previous claim.
r1-ST-M23-2025-006.vn: Both excerpts are on the page as one continuous quote; 'S'exprimant en Kinyarwanda' is in the preceding sentence on the page. Characterisations are the speaker's. excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts. Party statement; the labels used for the Wazalendo and FDLR are the speaker's as relayed by the outlet.
src: le nouveau gouverneur a déclaré avoir recensé trois menaces principales contre la sécurité de ses sujets : « les anciens prisonniers qui ont été libérés par les autorités congolaises alors que les combattants du M23 s’apprêtaient à entrer dans la ville de Goma,
les milices locales entretenues par les autorités congolaises connues communément comme ‘les Wazalendo’ et enfin les génocidaires Hutus-FDLR ( Forces de libération du Rwanda)

r1-ST-M23-2025-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Corneille Nangaa, head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, promised "une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes" (a responsible administration that must be accountable).
r1-ST-M23-2025-007.n: Party statement as relayed by a Burundian exile outlet; see appointments claim for date reasoning.
r1-ST-M23-2025-007.vn: Excerpt exact and matches statement; party promise relayed by one outlet.
src: Corneille Nangaa, responsable de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) à laquelle est affilié le groupe armé, a promis « une administration responsable qui doit rendre des comptes ».

r1-ST-M23-2025-008.s: Al Jazeera reported that the AFC/M23 said in a statement posted on X that, in response to the humanitarian crisis it attributed to the regime in Kinshasa, it declared a ceasefire starting 4 February 2025 for humanitarian reasons; Al Jazeera added that there was no immediate comment from the DRC government.
r1-ST-M23-2025-008.n: Announced late Monday 3 Feb for effect from Tuesday 4 Feb. The 'no immediate comment' observation is from an excerpt other than the one quoted; Studio Hirondelle (existing claim NKS-2025Q1#25) and the later Muyaya 'decoy' quote (NKS-2025Q1#26) cover Kinshasa's reaction.
r1-ST-M23-2025-008.vn: Statement text is in the excerpt; the 'no immediate comment' clause is printed on the same page (not in the stored excerpt). Al Jazeera adds the announcement was made late on Monday for a ceasefire from Tuesday.
src: “The Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) informs the public that in response to the humanitarian crisis caused by the regime in Kinshasa it declares a ceasefire starting 4 February 4 2025 for humanitarian reasons,” the rebels said in a statement posted on X.

r1-ST-M23-2025-009.s: Al Jazeera reported that a rebel alliance that includes M23 said, in a statement read on local radio on Monday, that it would assist the population of Bukavu who were "abandoned" by the army and allied combatants, and that its forces had been working to restore security.
r1-ST-M23-2025-009.n: Party statement; the claim of satisfaction among the population is the party's own.
r1-ST-M23-2025-009.vn: Excerpt carries both clauses; party statement read on local radio Monday 17 Feb 2025.
src: In a statement read on local radio on Monday, a rebel alliance that includes M23 said it would assist the population of Bukavu who were “abandoned” by the army and allied combatants. “Our forces have been working to restore the security for the people and their property, much to the satisfaction of the entire population,” it said.

r1-ST-M23-2025-010.s: Al Jazeera reported that Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.
r1-ST-M23-2025-010.l: Bukavu and Goma, North and South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2025-010.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (page dated Monday 17 Feb 2025; reopening on Tuesday = 18 Feb). Announcement made on or before 17 Feb.
r1-ST-M23-2025-010.vn: Statement supported. Date corrected: the claim is an announcement; the page (dated 17 Feb 2025) gives no announcement day, only that ports would reopen 'on Tuesday' (18 Feb). Date set to the page date as the latest possible announcement date. Announcement made on or before 17 Feb 2025 (page date); the reopening was announced for Tuesday 18 Feb.
src: Erasto Bahati Musanga, the rebel-appointed governor of North Kivu, announced that ports in Bukavu and Goma would reopen on Tuesday.

r1-ST-M23-2025-011.s: DW reported that, after two explosions at an M23 rally in Bukavu, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack and said in a statement that it condemned "the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations".
r1-ST-M23-2025-011.x: DW (citing Reuters, AP, AFP): at least 11 killed, around 65 injured
r1-ST-M23-2025-011.n: Party accusation, not an established finding. DW credits Reuters, AP and AFP in its byline.
r1-ST-M23-2025-011.vn: Excerpt carries the M23 accusation and quote; 'two explosions' and the figures are printed in the DW page body (headline prints 'at least 11'). DW byline: 'Emmy Sasipornkarn with Reuters, AP, AFP'. Party accusation, not an established finding. Casualty figures are DW's (with wire agencies).
src: Meanwhile, M23 accused the Congolese authorities of being behind the attack. "We are accusing and condemning vigorously the criminal regime of Kinshasa, which just implemented its plan of exterminating civilian populations," the group said in a statement.

r1-ST-M23-2025-012.s: DW reported that Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the Bukavu rally attack "a heinous terrorist act".
r1-ST-M23-2025-012.n: Government account of the same event; Reuters (28 Feb) headline says the government and M23 traded blame, but the Reuters page could not be fetched with the helper so it is not cited.
r1-ST-M23-2025-012.vn: Excerpt exact; DW with Reuters, AP, AFP.
src: Congo's president, Felix Tshisekedi, called the attack "a heinous terrorist act."

r1-ST-M23-2025-013.s: The New Times (Rwanda) reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at Burundi after the Bukavu rally explosions and said preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives belonged to the Burundian army.
r1-ST-M23-2025-013.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; a party allegation. No Burundian response found (see gaps).
r1-ST-M23-2025-013.vn: Excerpt carries both clauses; Rwandan state-aligned outlet (byline Alice Kagina); party allegation. Party allegation; no Burundian response was found by this unit.
src: Moments after the attack, Bertrand Bisimwa, the president of M23, pointed an accusing finger at neighbouring Burundi, which is allied with the Kinshasa regime in the fight against the rebel group that controls much of eastern DR Congo. Preliminary investigations indicated that the explosives used in the terrorist attack belong to the Burundian army, he said.

r1-ST-M23-2025-014.s: The New Times reported that, according to the group's leader, the explosives at the AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu on 27 February killed at least 11 people and injured 65, six of them in critical condition.
r1-ST-M23-2025-014.x: The New Times (citing the group's leader): at least 11 dead, 65 injured, of whom six in critical condition
r1-ST-M23-2025-014.n: Figures attributed by the outlet to the group's leader (the page names Nangaa as having given a press conference); the two blast casualty figures match DW's.
r1-ST-M23-2025-014.vn: Statement supported by the excerpt. Figures field corrected: it cited DW, which is not a source of this claim; figures now only as The New Times attributes them to the group's leader (the page goes on to say Nangaa gave them at a press conference).
src: The explosives that hit a huge crowd of people who had turned up in their thousands for an AFC/M23 rally in Bukavu, on February 27, caused the death of at least 11 people and injured 65, of whom six are in critical condition, according to group’s leader.

r1-ST-M23-2025-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday, AFC/M23 announced it would not take part in the Luanda talks planned for Tuesday 18 March under Angolan mediation, denouncing individual European Union sanctions on several of its leaders.
r1-ST-M23-2025-015.l: Luanda (Angola); statement concerns North and South Kivu conflict
r1-ST-M23-2025-015.n: Geography: statement about a process concerning the Kivus; location outside phase-1 area kept as statement-only.
r1-ST-M23-2025-015.vn: Excerpt exact and supports statement; excerpt_en flag is translation artefact (weekday/EU names).
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) ne participera pas aux discussions de Luanda prévues ce mardi 18 mars sous la médiation angolaise. Dans un communiqué publié ce lundi, le mouvement rebelle dénonce les sanctions individuelles prises par l’Union européenne contre plusieurs de ses dirigeants

r1-ST-M23-2025-016.s: Anadolu reported that the Alliance Fleuve Congo, a rebel alliance that includes M23, announced on Saturday that it was withdrawing from the town of Walikale and its surroundings, a few days after taking control of the area; Anadolu said residents saw rebel elements still in the town that afternoon.
r1-ST-M23-2025-016.n: Date computed from weekday (page dated 22 March 2025, Saturday). A Kivu Morning Post page refers to a 'communiqué du dimanche 23 mars 2025'; the two outlets differ on the communiqué's day.
r1-ST-M23-2025-016.vn: Both excerpts on the Anadolu page (byline James Tasamba, Kigali, 22 Mar 2025); Anadolu says the announcement was a communiqué by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka on X. Day of the communiqué differs: Anadolu and Kivu Morning Post say Saturday (22 Mar); Kanyuka's later post refers to 'the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025'.
src: L'Alliance Fleuve Congo, une alliance rebelle qui inclut les rebelles du M23, a annoncé samedi son retrait de la ville de Walikale et de ses environs dans l'est de la République Démocratique du Congo, quelques jours après avoir pris le contrôle de cette zone riche en minerais.
Cependant, des éléments rebelles étaient encore visibles dans la ville samedi après-midi, malgré l'annonce du retrait, selon des habitants.

r1-ST-M23-2025-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Lawrence Kanyuka, spokesperson of AFC-M23, said on X that, contrary to the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025, the FARDC and their coalition forces had not withdrawn their attack drones from Walikale, delaying the repositioning of AFC/M23 forces.
r1-ST-M23-2025-017.n: Party statement. The same outlet reports M23 residents' accounts that M23 had not left; see next claim for the FARDC response.
r1-ST-M23-2025-017.vn: Excerpt carries the quote; 'delaying the repositioning' is the next sentence of the same quote on the page, and the page says Kanyuka said it on X on Monday 24 March 2025. Goma-based outlet ('La Rédaction').
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23, a confirmé cette présence, précisant qu’elle résultait du refus de l’armée de lever ses mesures. « Contrairement à ce qui a été indiqué dans le communiqué du dimanche 23 mars 2025, les FARDC et leurs forces coalisées n’ont pas retiré leurs drones d’attaque de Walikale.

r1-ST-M23-2025-018.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the FARDC took note of the announced M23 withdrawal from Walikale and committed to avoiding any offensive action, calling on the Wazalendo to do the same.
r1-ST-M23-2025-018.n: Counterpart account; the page does not give the date or channel of the FARDC statement and does not name a spokesperson.
r1-ST-M23-2025-018.vn: Excerpt exact. The '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). The outlet narrates the FARDC position without a named spokesperson, channel or date; date field is the page date. The FARDC position is the outlet's narration; no FARDC spokesperson, channel or date is given on the page.
src: Les FARDC ont également pris acte de ce retrait et se sont engagées à éviter toute action offensive, appelant les Wazalendo à faire de même pour favoriser la désescalade

r1-ST-M23-2025-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced the break of its agreement with the SADC after violent clashes in Goma, accusing SAMIDRC regional forces, in coordination with the FARDC, of military operations including attacks on the night of 11 April 2025.
r1-ST-M23-2025-019.n: DISCREPANCY: the page says 'vendredi 12 avril 2025' but 12 April 2025 was a Saturday; date kept as 12 April as printed. Party account of an incident; no SADC/SAMIDRC or FARDC response found in this search.
r1-ST-M23-2025-019.vn: Both excerpts exact and support the statement. Date discrepancy kept visible: the page prints 'vendredi 12 avril 2025', but 12 April 2025 was a Saturday. Source date inconsistency: 'vendredi 12 avril 2025' (12 April 2025 was a Saturday). Party accusation.
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) a annoncé vendredi 12 avril 2025 la rupture de son accord avec la SADC (Communauté de développement de l’Afrique australe) après des affrontements violents dans la ville de Goma
Le mouvement rebelle accuse les forces régionales de la SAMIDRC, en coordination avec les FARDC, de mener des opérations militaires, y compris des attaques survenues dans la nuit du 11 avril 2025.

r1-ST-M23-2025-020.s: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC government delegates and the AFC/M23 rebellion, after talks in Doha under Qatari auspices, agreed to work towards a truce in view of an effective ceasefire, in a joint declaration made public on Wednesday 23 April 2025 and read on RTNC.
r1-ST-M23-2025-020.l: Doha (Qatar); concerns North and South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2025-020.n: Page printed 'Porte-parole civile' as written. Statement is bilateral; each side's own account of it is not separately recorded here.
r1-ST-M23-2025-020.vn: Excerpt 0 carries the agreement; the 'joint declaration made public on Wednesday 23 April 2025 and read on RTNC' clause is printed on the same page.
src: À l’issue de pourparlers tenus à Doha sous l’égide de l’État du Qatar, les délégués du gouvernement congolais et la rébellion de l'AFC/M23 ont convenu de travailler à la conclusion d’une trêve, en vue de l’instauration d’un cessez-le-feu effectif.

Dans le texte conjoint signé par Lawrence Kanyuka Porte-parole civile de l'AFC/M23 et Papy Mbuyi Kanguvu chef de la délégation congolaise et Directeur général adjoint de la Direction Générale des Migrations (DGM)

r1-ST-M23-2025-021.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23, led by Corneille Nangaa, said on Monday it took note of the agreement signed in Washington on 27 June between the DRC and Rwanda while expressing strong reservations and reaffirming demands for a more inclusive peace process.
r1-ST-M23-2025-021.l: Place of statement not stated (concerns North and South Kivu)
r1-ST-M23-2025-021.n: Party position; place where Nangaa made the statement is not stated on the page.
r1-ST-M23-2025-021.vn: Statement supported by excerpt. Location corrected: the page does not say where Nangaa made the statement (it calls it a message published on DRC independence day).
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23), mouvement politico-militaire dirigé par Corneille Nangaa, a déclaré lundi prendre acte de l’accord signé à Washington le 27 juin entre la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) et le Rwanda, tout en exprimant de vives réserves et en réaffirmant ses exigences pour un processus de paix plus inclusif.

r1-ST-M23-2025-022.s: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Corneille Nangaa, political coordinator of AFC-M23, announced that the movement regretted the widespread violation of the ceasefire on all front lines by what he called the regime in Kinshasa, which he said trampled point II of the Declaration of Principles signed in Doha on 19 July 2025.
r1-ST-M23-2025-022.n: Rwanda-based outlet; page dated 2 Sep 2025 and refers to a conference 'held in Goma on Monday' (Monday = 1 Sep 2025, computed from weekday). Party accusation, not an established fact. The page says Nangaa and Bisimwa jointly presided.
r1-ST-M23-2025-022.vn: Excerpt carries the quote (byline Vincent Gasana); page says the conference was held in Goma on Monday with Nangaa and Bisimwa presiding. '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). Party accusation relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet.
src: “We regret, we are obliged to inform the Congolese people and the entire International Community of the widespread violation of the ceasefire on all front lines by the tyrannical regime in Kinshasa, thereby definitively trampling point II, of the Declaration of Principles, signed in Doha on July 19 th 2025” announced the rebel movement’s Political Coordinator , Corneille Nangaa

r1-ST-M23-2025-023.s: KT Press reported that, in a formal statement before the Q&A at a Goma media briefing, Nangaa accused Tshisekedi of tearing up the Doha peace agreement signed in July 2025 and of choosing war over dialogue, and said Kinshasa's coalition forces had launched fresh offensives across eastern Congo in violation of the ceasefire.
r1-ST-M23-2025-023.n: Same briefing as the previous claim, separate article. Date computed: page dated 2 Sep 2025, photo caption says 'speaking on Monday'. The page also quotes Nangaa alleging that over 30,000 men and combat aircraft and drones were used by Kinshasa's coalition; that is a party figure and is not repeated as fact.
r1-ST-M23-2025-023.vn: Excerpt carries both clauses; page places the briefing in Goma; caption says 'speaking on Monday'. Party accusation relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet.
src: Earlier, in a formal statement delivered before the Q&A, Nangaa accused Tshisekedi of tearing up the Doha peace agreement signed in July 2025 and of choosing war over dialogue. He said Kinshasa’s coalition forces had launched fresh offensives across eastern Congo in violation of the ceasefire.

r1-ST-M23-2025-024.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese government and the AFC-M23 rebels signed on Tuesday 14 October 2025 in Doha, under Qatari mediation, a mechanism to monitor and verify the ceasefire in the provinces of North and South Kivu.
r1-ST-M23-2025-024.l: Doha (Qatar); applies to North Kivu and South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2025-024.n: Radio Okapi (UN-founded, Congolese). The page says the actors and modalities of implementation had not yet been revealed.
r1-ST-M23-2025-024.vn: Excerpt exact; Radio Okapi, 14 Oct 2025. Page adds that actors and modalities of implementation were not yet revealed.
src: Le gouvernement congolais et les rebelles de l'AFC-M23 ont signé le mardi 14 octobre 2025 à Doha, sous la médiation du Qatar, un mécanisme de surveillance et de vérification du cessez-le-feu dans les provinces du Nord et du Sud-Kivu.

r1-ST-M23-2025-025.s: KT Press reported that AFC/M23 rejected French President Emmanuel Macron's announcement of the planned reopening of Goma International Airport, calling it "premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation", in a statement issued by Corneille Nangaa.
r1-ST-M23-2025-025.n: Rwanda-based outlet; date is the report date (31 Oct 2025); Macron's announcement is stated to have been on Thursday 30 October. Statement date itself is not printed. The page also says AFC/M23 accused government forces of drone strikes and of the destruction of humanitarian planes; those are party allegations not repeated here.
r1-ST-M23-2025-025.vn: Narrowed attribution: the excerpt has the group (AFC/M23) calling the decision 'premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation'; the page says this came in a statement issued by Corneille Nangaa (next sentence), not that Nangaa used that exact phrase. Statement date not printed; page dated 31 Oct 2025 and says Macron's announcement was on Thursday 30 October.
src: The Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) rebel movement which controls North and South Kivu provinces of eastern DR Congo, has rejected the recent announcement by French President Emmanuel Macron regarding the planned reopening of Goma International Airport, calling the decision “premature, disconnected from reality, and made without consultation.”

r1-ST-M23-2025-026.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 announced in a communiqué that it would unilaterally withdraw its forces from the city of Uvira, presenting the decision as a confidence-building measure to support the Doha peace process; it said the withdrawal was conditional on security guarantees including demilitarisation, protection of civilians and deployment of a neutral force. BBC Gahuza reported Nangaa said M23 would withdraw at the request of United States mediation.
r1-ST-M23-2025-026.n: DATE DISCREPANCY: Actualite.cd (posted 00:14 on 16 Dec) says 'ce mardi'; BBC Gahuza says the statement was of Monday and announced Tuesday morning; TRT Afrika (citing Reuters) says Nangaa posted on X on Monday (15 Dec). The date field uses 15 Dec; reconcile at verification. Party statement of intent, not evidence that the withdrawal occurred.
r1-ST-M23-2025-026.vn: Actualite.cd (Clément Muamba) and BBC Gahuza (Didier Bikorimana) independently report the announcement; Actualite.cd also prints the communiqué's 'comme demandé par la médiation des États-Unis'. Date discrepancy kept: Actualite.cd says 'ce mardi'; BBC Gahuza says a Monday statement announced Tuesday morning; date field 15 Dec (statement day per BBC Gahuza). Statement of intent, not evidence the withdrawal occurred. Day discrepancy: Monday 15 Dec (BBC Gahuza: statement of Monday, released Tuesday morning) vs 'ce mardi' (Actualite.cd).
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) a annoncé ce mardi qu’elle retirerait unilatéralement ses forces de la ville d’Uvira, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo, présentant cette décision comme une mesure de confiance destinée à soutenir le processus de paix de Doha, a-t-elle indiqué dans un communiqué.

L’AFC/M23 précise toutefois que ce retrait est conditionné à des garanties de sécurité, appelant les garants du processus de paix à assurer la gestion de la ville, notamment sa démilitarisation, la protection des civils et des infrastructures, ainsi que le contrôle du cessez-le-feu par le déploiement d’une force neutre.
Yagize ati: "AFC/M23 izakura ku bwayo [nta we igishije inama] ingabo zayo mu mujyi wa Uvira bijyanye n'ubusabe bw'ubuhuza bwa Leta Zunze Ubumwe [z'Amerika]."

r1-ST-M23-2025-027.s: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed", adding that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and that the city should be occupied by a neutral force; residents told Reuters the rebels had not withdrawn.
r1-ST-M23-2025-027.n: TRT Afrika republishes Reuters reporting; the original Reuters piece was not fetched. Date computed: page published Wednesday 17 Dec 2025.
r1-ST-M23-2025-027.vn: Excerpt carries the Ngoma quote; the residents clause is in the page's lede. TRT Afrika page ends 'SOURCE : Reuters'.
src: M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma told Reuters on Wednesday that "we are ready to leave (Uvira), but our conditions have to be reviewed." The spokesperson added that the citizens of Uvira needed protecting and it should be occupied by a neutral force.

r1-ST-M23-2025-028.s: BBC News reported that M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was "under way", with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace", and that Bisimwa in a post on X urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".
r1-ST-M23-2025-028.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date 18 Dec 2025. Same page reports Uvira residents telling the BBC on Thursday that it was not clear M23 were leaving; that is not part of this statement claim.
r1-ST-M23-2025-028.vn: Excerpt carries all clauses; BBC (Rukanga and Makumeno), 18 Dec 2025; Wednesday = 17 Dec. The same page reports Uvira residents telling the BBC on Thursday it was not clear the M23 were leaving.
src: M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal was "under way," with spokesman Willy Ngoma adding that this was "for the sake of peace". In a post on X, Bisimwa urged mediators and international partners to ensure the city was protected from "reprisals, violence and remilitarisation".

r1-ST-M23-2025-029.s: TRT Afrika, relaying Reuters, reported that DRC Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announced M23 withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion", alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda; the page also says Rwanda's government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
r1-ST-M23-2025-029.n: Government account; Rwanda's silence is only 'did not immediately respond', which is not a finding that Rwanda said nothing.
r1-ST-M23-2025-029.vn: Both excerpts on the TRT Afrika page ('SOURCE : Reuters'). '23' flag is from 'M23' (false positive). Rwanda's 'did not immediately respond' is not a finding that Rwanda said nothing.
src: However, DR Congo's Communications Minister Patrick Muyaya dismissed the announcement of a withdrawal from Uvira as a "diversion," alleging it was an attempt to relieve pressure on Rwanda, which Kinshasa and the United Nations accuse of backing the rebels.
Rwanda's government spokesperson did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

r1-ST-M23-2025-030.s: BBC News reported that Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground, having earlier called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".
r1-ST-M23-2025-030.n: Date is the page's date; the statement's exact day is not printed. Compare the same speaker's 'diversion' remark to Reuters on 17 Dec.
r1-ST-M23-2025-030.vn: Excerpt carries both clauses; statement day not printed (date is the page date). The same BBC page also reports DR Congo's government calling the reported withdrawal a 'diversion'.
src: Muyaya described the M23's decision to leave Uvira as a "positive sign" but said the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground. Earlier he had called for "vigilance" in response to the "alleged withdrawal".

r1-ST-M23-2025-031.s: Radio Elle FM Goma reported that the de facto governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, launched a large reforestation operation in Goma on a Salongo day, saying "Nous avons trouvé une ville et un parc dévastés"; in the same report the outlet wrote that disorderly felling of trees by armed groups such as the FDLR and Mai-Mai militias had profoundly affected biodiversity.
r1-ST-M23-2025-031.n: Local outlet operating under M23-controlled Goma; the page is dated 8 Nov 2025 and the event is described as taking place 'ce samedi' (8 Nov 2025 was a Saturday). Attribution of tree felling to armed groups is the governor's/outlet's wording on the page, not independently verified.
r1-ST-M23-2025-031.vn: The tree-felling attribution is not clearly the governor's: on the page it follows 'Selon lui...' as the outlet's own sentence. Narrowed to keep that as the outlet's wording. Governor title and Salongo launch are printed on the page; title prints 'Le Gouverneur Bahati Musanga Erasto'. '23' flag is from 'M23'. Local outlet operating in M23-controlled Goma. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Elle FM (8 Nov 2025, byline Grace Wasingya Nestor) supports every clause; the stored excerpts carry only the quote and the FDLR/Mai-Mai sentence, so the launch passage is added. The FDLR sentence directly follows 'Selon lui' (according to him) and may be the governor's view paraphrased; the statement's 'the outlet wrote' is literal to the page.
src: « Nous avons trouvé une ville et un parc dévastés. Nous voulons désormais que les animaux du parc puissent se reproduire à nouveau pour attirer les touristes étrangers », a-t-il ajouté.
L’abattage désordonné d’arbres par les groupes armés tels que les FDLR ou encore les milices Maï-Maï, a profondément affecté la biodiversité.

Le Gouverneur sous l’AFC M23 du Nord-Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, a donné le coup d’envoi d’une vaste opération de reboisement dans la ville de Goma, marquant une étape importante dans les efforts de restauration écologique et de lutte contre la déforestation. L’initiative a été lancée lors d’une journée de Salongo ce samedi

r1-ST-M23-2026-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa said in a recent statement that 'À ce jour, pas un seul prisonnier n’a été libéré, en violation flagrante des accords signés', accusing the Kinshasa government of blocking implementation of the Doha commitments.
r1-ST-M23-2026-001.n: Party statement; cited only for what the party said. The article says 'déclaration récente'; date taken from publication date (jeu 01/01/2026). Kinshasa's position on prisoner releases not located in this unit.
r1-ST-M23-2026-001.vn: Page confirms quote and accusation; '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'. Party statement, cited only for what was said. The page says 'déclaration récente'; the date is the publication date.
src: À ce jour, pas un seul prisonnier n’a été libéré, en violation flagrante des accords signés », a déclaré Corneille Nangaa.

r1-ST-M23-2026-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Corneille Nangaa said that in the zones controlled by the AFC/M23 'la population vit désormais dans la paix, la dignité et la sécurité retrouvées', and accused the central government of promoting hate speech, saying 'Le discours de haine est désormais devenu une doctrine d’État'.
r1-ST-M23-2026-002.l: AFC/M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-002.n: Party claim about conditions in its zones, not evidence of those conditions; contrast UN/HRW claims recorded by other units. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.
r1-ST-M23-2026-002.vn: Both passages on page; same article. Party claim about conditions in its own zones; not evidence of those conditions. Made in Nangaa's end-of-2025 address to the nation. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Corneille Nangaa a affirmé que, dans les zones contrôlées par l’AFC/M23, « la population vit désormais dans la paix, la dignité et la sécurité retrouvées », ajoutant que « la jeune administration s’installe » et que « la justice est en pleine relance ».
Corneille Nangaa a accusé le pouvoir central de promouvoir des discours de haine et de division. « Le discours de haine est désormais devenu une doctrine d’État » , a-t-il affirmé

r1-ST-M23-2026-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a statement posted on X on 3 February, Corneille Nangaa presented as a response to what he called an indiscriminate military campaign by the central government the AFC/M23's claimed operation against what it described as the Congolese army's drone command centre in Kisangani (Tshopo).
r1-ST-M23-2026-003.l: Kisangani, Tshopo (claimed target); statement on Minembwe and Hauts-Plateaux, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-003.n: Claim of responsibility is the party's own. Kinshasa/Tshopo side recorded in the next claim. Elsewhere than the Kivus, kept as a statement about this conflict.
r1-ST-M23-2026-003.vn: Supported verbatim. Claim of responsibility is the party's own. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le mouvement politico-militaire AFC/M23 affirme avoir mené une opération ciblée contre ce qu’il décrit comme le centre de commandement des drones de l’armée congolaise à Kisangani, dans la province de la Tshopo.

Dans une déclaration publiée sur le réseau social X le 3 février, le coordonnateur politique de l’AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, a présenté cette action comme une réponse directe à ce qu’il qualifie de campagne militaire indiscriminée menée par le pouvoir central depuis la fin janvier.

r1-ST-M23-2026-004.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Tshopo provincial authorities and the FARDC announced they had neutralised eight explosive-laden kamikaze drones in the night of 31 January to 1 February 2026, and that the Tshopo authorities accused the AFC/M23 of trying to target Bangoka airport.
r1-ST-M23-2026-004.n: Kinshasa-side account paired with the AFC/M23 claim of the Kisangani operation (previous claim).
r1-ST-M23-2026-004.vn: Supported; grade lowered B->C: one local outlet relaying a party (government) statement. Kinshasa-side account as relayed by a single Goma-based outlet; the Tshopo/FARDC original statement was not opened. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: les autorités provinciales de la Tshopo et les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) ont annoncé avoir neutralisé huit drones kamikazes chargés d’explosifs, dans la nuit du 31 janvier au 1ᵉʳ février 2026. Les autorités de la province de la Tshopo ont accusé l’AFC/M23 d’avoir tenté de viser l’aéroport de Bangoka

r1-ST-M23-2026-005.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué reacting to an African Union Commission statement, the AFC/M23 said that since 22 January 2026 localities including Minembwe, Twangiza, Rwitsankuku, Katogota, Sange, Kalundu port, Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Lubero, Mwenga and Kalehe had been targeted by 'huit à douze drones d’attaque pilotés par des mercenaires étrangers', that these strikes allegedly hit civilian targets including hospitals, schools and churches, and that its own drone-neutralisation operation caused no civilian loss.
r1-ST-M23-2026-005.l: Minembwe, Hauts-Plateaux, South Kivu and other localities named
r1-ST-M23-2026-005.a: AFC/M23 (statement); strikes attributed by AFC/M23 to the central government and its allies
r1-ST-M23-2026-005.n: Allegation of strikes on hospitals is unverified and the party's own. Exact statement date not on the page; the AFC/M23 reaction to the AU Commission statement is dated 6 Feb on X (lead only); page published 2026-02-07. Candidate health_care_access lead: ask which hospitals.
r1-ST-M23-2026-005.vn: Page dates the communiqué to Friday 6 February 2026 (draft had month only); date field corrected, page passage given as clause support. Allegation of strikes on hospitals is the party's own and unverified; no hospital is named. The communiqué was signed by permanent secretary Benjamin Mbonimpa per the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le mouvement affirme que, depuis le 22 janvier 2026, plusieurs localités des Hauts-Plateaux et du Sud-Kivu auraient été ciblées par « huit à douze drones d’attaque pilotés par des mercenaires étrangers », citant notamment Minembwe, Twangiza, Rwitsankuku, Katogota, Sange, le port de Kalundu, Masisi, Walikale, Rutshuru, Lubero, Mwenga et Kalehe.
Ces frappes auraient touché « des cibles civiles, dont des hôpitaux, des écoles et des églises, causant la mort de nombreux civils, femmes et enfants compris ».
Concernant son action militaire, l’AFC/M23 assure que « l’opération de neutralisation des drones, qui visait exclusivement des moyens militaires, n’a causé aucune perte civile

r1-ST-M23-2026-006.s: Anadolu reported that on Sunday the Congolese army said in a statement that AFC/M23 and its coalition had launched drone attacks on Saturday evening on its positions at Mikenge and Kakenge in South Kivu and on civilian areas at Point Zero, with a provisional toll of four civilians killed and eight injured, mostly women and children, while Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Rwanda.
r1-ST-M23-2026-006.l: Mikenge, Kakenge, Point Zero, Minembwe highlands, Fizi, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-006.a: FARDC (statement); attack attributed to AFC/M23 and its coalition
r1-ST-M23-2026-006.x: FARDC statement: 4 civilians killed, 8 injured, mostly women and children (provisional)
r1-ST-M23-2026-006.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (20 April 2026, Monday). Anadolu article by James Tasamba, Kigali dateline; the same page carries Kanyuka's counter-claim of a Masisi shelling. Single-sided army account.
r1-ST-M23-2026-006.vn: Supported; figures spelled out in excerpt match. Single-sided army account. The date is computed from the weekday and the 20 April publication date. Anadolu's lead says the army also accused the Rwandan army.
src: But on Sunday, the army said AFC/M23 rebels and its coalition launched deadly drone attacks Saturday evening on its positions in South Kivu’s Mikenge and Kakenge localities as well as on areas inhabited by civilians at Point Zero. “The provisional toll indicates that four civilians were killed and eight others injured, mostly women and children,” the army said in a statement.

r1-ST-M23-2026-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced in a communiqué on Sunday 26 April that they had shot down on Saturday 25 April 2026 a UAV belonging to the Rwandan army, intercepted at Point Zéro in the Minembwe highlands, Fizi territory.
r1-ST-M23-2026-007.l: Point Zéro, Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe, Fizi, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-007.a: FARDC (statement); drone attributed to Rwandan army
r1-ST-M23-2026-007.n: Single-source army claim; no Rwandan reaction located (see gaps).
r1-ST-M23-2026-007.vn: Supported verbatim. Army claim only; no Rwandan reaction located. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Dans un communiqué dimanche 26 avril, les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont annoncé avoir abattu, en plein vol, samedi 25 avril 2026, un drone de type UAV appartenant à l’armée rwandaise. L’appareil a été intercepté au Point Zéro, dans les Hauts Plateaux de Minembwe, en territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-ST-M23-2026-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from Saturday 25 April to Sunday the Kinshasa regime's coalition forces carried out simultaneous, sustained bombardments at Gakenke, Mikenke and their surroundings in the Minembwe region, using kamikaze combat drones and KT-6 type drones, which the movement called a flagrant violation of the ceasefire.
r1-ST-M23-2026-008.a: AFC/M23 (Kanyuka); strikes attributed to 'forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa'
r1-ST-M23-2026-008.n: Paired with the FARDC claim of the same days. Place names as printed ('Gakenke'); the Anadolu piece prints 'Kakenge'/'Mikenge' for what appear to be nearby localities (not asserted as the same).
r1-ST-M23-2026-008.vn: Drone-type and ceasefire clause were on the page but not in the excerpt; excerpt extended with the next sentence. Party account, paired with but kept separate from the FARDC claim of the same days. Place names as printed. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole du mouvement rebelle, a déclaré que du samedi 25 avril au dimanche, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont mené des bombardements simultanés, soutenus et ininterrompus à Gakenke, Mikenke ainsi que leurs environs, dans la région de Minembwe.

r1-ST-M23-2026-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that, in a communiqué, the rebel movement's spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka gave a provisional toll of at least 21 civilians killed and more than 67 wounded, among them women and children, in drone strikes the rebellion blamed on government forces against the public market of Mushaki, and that the movement called the attack a serious violation of international humanitarian law.
r1-ST-M23-2026-009.l: Mushaki market, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-009.a: AFC/M23 (Kanyuka); strikes attributed by AFC/M23 to government forces
r1-ST-M23-2026-009.x: Kanyuka communiqué (via Actualite.cd): at least 21 civilians killed, more than 67 wounded
r1-ST-M23-2026-009.n: Headline of the page says 'plus d'une dizaine de morts' (independent count not verified here). Check Actualite.cd's own sourcing and MONUSCO/US condemnation referenced by Kivu Morning Post 2026-05-11. Casualty figures differ between Kanyuka and Nangaa.
r1-ST-M23-2026-009.vn: Figures field carried Nangaa's toll from another source; narrowed to this page. IHL clause added to the excerpt (next sentence on page). Casualty figures differ between Kanyuka's communiqué and Nangaa's account (separate claim); kept separate. Actualite.cd's own lead, citing one resident, gives a different toll and dates the attack to Friday 8 May; not merged here. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: La rébellion accuse les forces gouvernementales d’avoir mené, une nouvelle fois, des frappes de drones meurtrières contre le marché public de Mushaki.

Dans un communiqué, le porte-parole du mouvement rebelle, Lawrence Kanyuka, a fait état d’un bilan provisoire faisant état d’au moins 21 civils tués et de plus de 67 blessés, parmi lesquels des femmes, des enfants et d’autres personnes vulnérables.

r1-ST-M23-2026-010.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to AFCM23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, the Congolese army's drone attack on Mushaki, forty kilometres from Goma, killed 20 people and wounded about sixty civilians.
r1-ST-M23-2026-010.a: AFC/M23 (Nangaa); attack attributed to the Congolese army (FARDC)
r1-ST-M23-2026-010.x: Nangaa (via Kivu Morning Post): 20 dead, about sixty wounded
r1-ST-M23-2026-010.n: The page dates the Rwandan statement to 'le week-end dernier' and the attack to 8 May 2026; Nangaa's press statement is dated to 'vendredi' in a sister KMP article (not fetched), so the date is approximate. Actualite.cd dates a further strike on 9 May.
r1-ST-M23-2026-010.vn: Removed 'in a statement to the press in Goma on Friday': not on this page (draft took it from an unfetched sister article). Toll is Nangaa's; when and where he gave it is not stated on this page. The attribution of the attack to the army is the outlet's narration of party accounts. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: l’attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise à Mushaki, à quarante kilomètres de Goma, qui a fait 20 morts et une soixantaine de blessés parmi la population civile, selon Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur de l’AFCM23.

r1-ST-M23-2026-011.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Rwandan Minister of Foreign Affairs, Oliver Nduhungirehe, deplored in a statement the weekend before the silence of the international community and the UN mission in the DRC in the face of the 'crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo', speaking the day after the Congolese army drone attack on Mushaki.
r1-ST-M23-2026-011.n: Rwandan government position only. The page also prints the spelling 'Olivier Nduhungirehe'. Date approximate (weekend before 11 May).
