src: Le ministre des Affaires étrangères de la République du Rwanda a déploré, le week-end dernier, dans une déclaration, le silence de la communauté internationale et de la Mission onusienne en RDC face aux « crimes du gouvernement de la République du Congo » . Oliver Nduhungirehe l’a dit le lendemain de l’attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise à Mushaki

r1-ST-M23-2026-012.s: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka told Reuters he knew of no mass graves during the group's time in Uvira, and accused the DRC government of spreading propaganda aimed at damaging its image.
r1-ST-M23-2026-012.n: M23's denial of the mass-grave allegations; pairs with the governor's claim in the next claim. BBC says it could not independently verify how the people died.
r1-ST-M23-2026-012.vn: Supported; Reuters relay credited. AFC/M23 denial; kept separate from the governor's account. BBC says it could not independently verify how the people died.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 Lawrence Kanyuka yabwiye ibiro ntaramakuru Reuters ko nta makuru y'imva rusange yigeze amenya mu gihe uwo mutwe wamaze muri Uvira, anashinja leta ya DRC gukwirakwiza icengezamatwara rigamije kwangiza isura yawo.

r1-ST-M23-2026-013.s: BBC Gahuza reported, citing Reuters, that two mass graves had been found in Uvira, and that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told reporters in Uvira that the graves were in the Kilomoni and Kavimvira areas, one holding 31 bodies and the other 141; BBC said it could not independently verify how the people died.
r1-ST-M23-2026-013.l: Kilomoni and Kavimvira, Uvira, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-013.a: Authorities in Kinshasa's appointed South Kivu government (Purusi); cause of death and perpetrators not attributed by the source
r1-ST-M23-2026-013.x: Purusi (via BBC Gahuza/Reuters): one grave with 31 bodies, another with 141; BBC lead: at least 172 bodies in two graves
r1-ST-M23-2026-013.n: Figure (172) differs from the 151 civilians in the provincial communiqué already recorded; do not merge. M23's denial is the previous claim.
r1-ST-M23-2026-013.vn: Draft said 'one in Kilomoni and one at Kavimvira'; the page says only that the graves were found in those two areas. Figures field narrowed to what this page prints. Figures as printed (31 + 141; lead 'nibura 172'). They differ from the provincial communiqué figure recorded elsewhere in the project; do not merge. The page says Purusi's remarks were recorded on Tuesday and broadcast on Thursday.
src: Jean-Jacques Purusi, Guverineri w'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo washyizweho n'ubutegetsi bw'i Kinshasa, yabwiye abanyamakuru mu mujyi wa Uvira ko izo mva zabonetse mu gace ka Kilomoni no mu gace ka Kavimvira. Yongeyeho ko imva imwe yari irimo imirambo 31 naho indi irimo imirambo 141

r1-ST-M23-2026-014.s: Umuryango reported that the AFC/M23 announced that fighting in the Minembwe commune, South Kivu, had ended after it said it had taken areas held by the FARDC and their allies, and said it had captured Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu and Rwitsankuku; the message was given by AFC/M23 deputy leader Bisimwa during a visit to the area.
r1-ST-M23-2026-014.l: Minembwe commune: Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu, Rwitsankuku; Fizi/Mwenga highlands, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-014.a: AFC/M23 with MRDP Twirwaneho (per the movement)
r1-ST-M23-2026-014.n: Rwandan privately-owned, state-aligned outlet; party claim of capture, not independently confirmed. Page date is Saturday 11 Jul 2026; the date of the visit is not given. Names Bisimwa 'Bertand' as printed. Compare Radio Okapi/Actualite.cd Point Zéro reports of July-August in other units; Kinshasa's account of these places not located here.
r1-ST-M23-2026-014.vn: Bisimwa name was in no excerpt and was spelled differently from the page; excerpt extended to the next sentence and name spelled as printed. excerpt_en flags are translation of DRC/Province terms, faithful. Party claim of capture, not independently confirmed. The page prints his name as 'Bertand Bisimwa' (sic). Date of the visit not given; page dated Saturday 11 July 2026. Per the page, Bisimwa said AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho fighters had joined forces.
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 ryatangaje ko ibikorwa by’imirwano muri Komini ya Minembwe, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, byasojwe nyuma y’uko rivuga ko ryigaruriye ibice byari bifitwe n’ingabo za Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) n’abo bafatanyaga.
AFC/M23 ivuga ko yamaze kwigarurira uduce turimo Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu na Rwitsankuku, twari dusanzwe turwanirwamo hagati y’impande zihanganye.

r1-ST-M23-2026-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa called on Burundian President and African Union chair Évariste Ndayishimiye to guarantee humanitarian access to the Minembwe highlands, denouncing what he called a 'blocus humanitaire' affecting the mostly Banyamulenge Tutsi zone.
r1-ST-M23-2026-015.a: AFC/M23 (Nangaa); blockade attributed by Nangaa to the Kinshasa authorities
r1-ST-M23-2026-015.n: The page says 'jeudi 18 septembre 2026' but 18 September 2026 falls on a Friday; the date is as printed and the weekday may be wrong. Allegation of denial of food, medicines and humanitarian access (health care access lead). Burundi's and Kinshasa's replies not located (see gaps).
r1-ST-M23-2026-015.vn: Supported verbatim. The page prints 'jeudi 18 septembre 2026', but 18 September 2026 is a Friday; date kept as printed, weekday may be wrong. Party allegation of a blockade depriving civilians of food and medicines. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le coordonnateur de l’Alliance du Fleuve Congo/Mouvement du 23 Mars (AFC-M23) a appelé, jeudi 18 septembre 2026, le président de la République du Burundi et président en exercice de l’Union africaine, Évariste Ndayishimiye, à garantir l’accès humanitaire dans les hauts plateaux de Minembwe, en province du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la RDC.
Corneille Nangaa a dénoncé ce qu’il qualifie de « blocus humanitaire » qui, selon lui, affecte la zone de Minembwe, habitée majoritairement par la communauté tutsi Banyamulenge.

r1-ST-M23-2026-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at a press conference in Goma on Wednesday 7 October 2026 the AFC/M23 accused the Congolese authorities of imposing a blockade on the people of Minembwe; Corneille Nangaa said they faced shortages of food, medicines and basic necessities and attributed the blockade to the Kinshasa regime and a coalition of FARDC, Burundian forces, FDLR, Wazalendo and mercenaries.
r1-ST-M23-2026-016.l: Minembwe, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu (subject); statement in Goma
r1-ST-M23-2026-016.a: AFC/M23 (Nangaa); blockade attributed by Nangaa to FARDC, Burundian forces, FDLR, Wazalendo and mercenaries
r1-ST-M23-2026-016.n: Page title also mentions US welcome of a first ceasefire-monitoring mission to Minembwe. Party allegation of shortages of medicines; not independently confirmed here.
r1-ST-M23-2026-016.vn: Date and press-conference clause are in the article's first paragraph (clause support from page). Party allegation of medicine shortages; not independently confirmed here. Nangaa also used the word 'génocide' at this press conference (party's own wording). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon le responsable de l’AFC/M23, les populations de Minembwe sont confrontées à des pénuries de nourriture, de médicaments et de produits de première nécessité, notamment d’eau, de sel, de savon, d’huile et de sucre.

Il a attribué cette situation à un blocus qu’il impute au « régime de Kinshasa » et à une coalition comprenant, selon lui, les FARDC, des forces burundaises, les FDLR, les Wazalendo et des mercenaires.

r1-ST-M23-2026-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at the same press conference Corneille Nangaa said that in the night of 23 to 24 September a humanitarian convoy of UN and NGO organisations had been blocked at Mulima on its way to Minembwe, and that the convoy, headed by OCHA, ACTED and Médecins du Monde, was according to the AFC/M23 deliberately attacked by the Kinshasa coalition forces.
r1-ST-M23-2026-017.l: Mulima, on the route to Minembwe, Fizi, South Kivu
r1-ST-M23-2026-017.a: Alleged by AFC/M23: 'forces coalisées de Kinshasa'
r1-ST-M23-2026-017.n: Party claim only; OCHA/ACTED/MdM and Kinshasa accounts of this convoy incident not yet located; priority for the next gap round.
r1-ST-M23-2026-017.vn: Supported verbatim; location territory not on page. Party claim only; OCHA/ACTED/MdM and Kinshasa accounts not located. The page does not name Mulima's territory (draft location says Fizi). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: un incident survenu dans la nuit du 23 au 24 septembre, affirmant qu’un convoi humanitaire comprenant notamment des organisations de l’ONU et des ONG avait été bloqué à Mulima alors qu’il se dirigeait vers Minembwe. Le convoi, chapeauté par OCHA, ACTED et Médecins du Monde, a été, selon l’AFC/M23, délibérément attaqué par les forces coalisées de Kinshasa.

r1-ST-M23-2026-018.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the vice-presidents of the Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa, presented the FRN's organisation in Goma on Wednesday 21 October, and that Nangaa set out an institutional architecture of four organs including a Collège des fondateurs of 20 members and a Conseil de la révolution of five members.
r1-ST-M23-2026-018.a: FRN (successor to AFC/M23) led by Joseph Kabila
r1-ST-M23-2026-018.n: Adds structure detail to FRN claims already in the project (12 October founding). Whether the FRN armed wing is the ARC is as the page says: it mentions ARC soldiers killed on the front lines.
r1-ST-M23-2026-018.vn: Supported; grade lowered B->C (single local outlet relaying the movement's own presentation). Structure as the movement presents it. Per the page, the FRN is the renamed AFC-M23 (12 October declaration), led by Joseph Kabila. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les vice-présidents du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), Corneille Nangaa et Bertrand Bisimwa, ont présenté mercredi 21 octobre à Goma, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), l’organisation et les orientations du FRN, nouveau mouvement politico-militaire dirigé par l’ancien président Joseph Kabila.

Corneille Nangaa a par ailleurs présenté une nouvelle architecture institutionnelle du mouvement, qui comprend, selon lui, quatre organes : le Collège des fondateurs, composé de 20 membres ; le Conseil de la révolution, constitué de cinq membres selon la formule « 4+1 » ;

r1-ST-M23-2026-019.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa condemned on Wednesday 19 August 2026 remarks by opposition politician Martin Fayulu about the Banyamulenge community, calling them 'irresponsables' and 'incendiaires', in a statement on X.
r1-ST-M23-2026-019.n: Fayulu's original remarks are not quoted on this page; they are not recorded here.
r1-ST-M23-2026-019.vn: Supported. Per the page, Fayulu spoke at a press conference in Brussels; his remarks are summarised there, not recorded as a separate claim. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le coordonnateur de l’AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, a condamné mercredi 19 août 2026 les propos tenus par l’opposant Martin Fayulu au sujet de la communauté banyamulenge, les qualifiant d’« irresponsables », d’« incendiaires » et de nature à fragiliser davantage la cohésion nationale en République démocratique du Congo.

r1-ST-MED-2025-001.s: UN News reported that the UN Security Council unanimously adopted a resolution in which it demanded that the M23 immediately cease hostilities, withdraw from all areas it controls and fully reverse the establishment of illegitimate parallel administrations in DRC territory, and in which its 15 members called on the Rwanda Defence Forces to stop supporting the armed group and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory without preconditions.
r1-ST-MED-2025-001.l: eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu)
r1-ST-MED-2025-001.n: Resolution 2773 per other items in the packet; the page does not print the number in this passage. Rwanda's and DRC's reactions are separate claims elsewhere.
r1-ST-MED-2025-001.vn: All clauses on the page; 'unanimously' was not in the excerpt, so placed via clause_support; 'fully' and 'immediately' restored from the source wording. Graded B: one UN News report, not an investigation. The page links the text as Security Council resolution 2773 (2025); the article itself does not number the resolution in the passage.
src: The Council demanded that the M23 immediately cease hostilities, withdraw from all areas that it controls, “and fully reverse the establishment of illegitimate parallel administrations in the DRC territory.” The 15 members called on the Rwanda Defence Forces to stop supporting the armed group and immediately withdraw from Congolese territory “without preconditions.”

r1-ST-MED-2025-002.s: UN News reported that in the same resolution the Security Council strongly condemned all attacks directed against civilians and infrastructure, including UN, humanitarian and medical personnel, and condemned summary executions and maiming, sexual and gender-based violence, human trafficking and the recruitment and use of children.
r1-ST-MED-2025-002.n: Relevant to the priority on sexual violence and attacks on health care: a Council-level statement, not an incident finding.
r1-ST-MED-2025-002.vn: Excerpt exact and covers both clauses; same article and resolution as claim 0. B: single UN News report of a Council text.
src: The resolution strongly condemned all attacks directed against civilians and infrastructure, including UN, humanitarian and medical personnel. It also condemned summary executions and maiming, sexual and gender-based violence, human trafficking and the recruitment and use of children.

r1-ST-MED-2025-003.s: The Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs published a joint statement between Qatar, the DRC and Rwanda in which the Heads of State reaffirmed the commitment of all parties to an immediate and unconditional ceasefire as agreed at the EAC-SADC summit.
r1-ST-MED-2025-003.a: State of Qatar (mediator), DRC and Rwanda heads of state
r1-ST-MED-2025-003.n: The excerpt says 'said summit' (the EAC-SADC summit of 8 February 2025 named earlier on the page). Date from the Reuters/Al Jazeera headlines in search results (18 March 2025); the page date was not shown in the fetched text. Reuters (originating) also reported the meeting.
r1-ST-MED-2025-003.vn: Excerpt exact. The retained page prints the date (dateline 'Doha - 18 March 2025', 'Tuesday, March 18, 2025') and names the summit as the joint EAC-SADC summit in Dar es Salaam; the clause_support quotes carry these, so the date no longer rests on search listings. Credited as a joint statement of all three states, hosted by the Qatari MFA.
src: The Heads of State reaffirmed the commitment of all parties to an immediate and unconditional ceasefire as agreed at the said summit.

r1-ST-MED-2025-004.s: The African Union Peace and Security Council adopted a communiqué that unequivocally condemned the activities of M23 and its supporters, ADF, FDLR and other armed groups.
r1-ST-MED-2025-004.a: African Union Peace and Security Council
r1-ST-MED-2025-004.n: Communiqué text; the date of the meeting is in the document title/search listing and the document's reference to the 1261st meeting on 14 February 2025.
r1-ST-MED-2025-004.vn: Excerpt exact (PDF text). Removed a stray comma. The PDF prints the 1261st meeting and 14 February 2025 (clause_support).
src: Unequivocally condemns the activities of M23 and its supporters, Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR) and other armed groups

r1-ST-MED-2025-005.s: The African Union Peace and Security Council communiqué commended Angola's President João Manuel Lourenço, Chair of the ICGLR and AU Champion for Peace and Reconciliation, for mediating between the DRC and Rwanda and called on the two parties to return urgently to the Luanda Process.
r1-ST-MED-2025-005.a: African Union Peace and Security Council; Angola (mediator)
r1-ST-MED-2025-005.n: See previous claim on the date.
r1-ST-MED-2025-005.vn: Excerpt exact; name spelled as printed. Same communiqué as claim 3 (14 February 2025, printed in the PDF).
src: Commends the efforts of H.E. João Manuel Lourenço, President of the Republic of Angola, the Chair of ICGLR and AU Champion for Peace and Reconciliation, for mediating between the DRC and Rwanda; and calls on the two parties to urgently return to the Luanda Process

r1-ST-MED-2025-006.s: The SADC communiqué of its Extraordinary Summit stated that the Summit terminated the mandate of SAMIDRC and directed the commencement of a phased withdrawal of SAMIDRC troops from the DRC.
r1-ST-MED-2025-006.l: SADC (decision on the deployment in eastern DRC)
r1-ST-MED-2025-006.n: Date 13 March 2025 from the SADC search listing and the later SADC press release ('13 March 2025 Summit decision'); fetched text does not print the date in the excerpt.
r1-ST-MED-2025-006.vn: Excerpt exact. The retained PDF prints the date (header '13 March 2025', 'Done on 13th March 2025'), carried in clause_support; the SADC press release (claim 6) also gives the 13 March 2025 Summit.
src: Summit terminated the Mandate of SAMIDRC and directed the commencement of a phased withdrawal of SAMIDRC troops from the DRC.

r1-ST-MED-2025-007.s: SADC said in a press release that it had officially commenced the withdrawal of SAMIDRC from eastern DRC as of 29 April 2025, by road through Rwanda to the troop-contributing countries.
r1-ST-MED-2025-007.vn: Excerpt exact; press release dated 01 May 2025 and the claim date is the start of the withdrawal, both printed.
src: The Southern African Development Community (SADC) has officially commenced with the withdrawal from the Eastern DRC as of 29 April 2025. The withdrawal is being conducted by road, transiting through the Republic of Rwanda to the respective Troop Contributing Countries (TCCs).

r1-ST-MED-2025-008.s: US Senior Advisor Massad Boulos said at a State Department digital press briefing that the US position was that Rwanda should cease all military support of M23 and withdraw all Rwandan troops from DRC territory.
r1-ST-MED-2025-008.n: Speaker identified from the transcript's speaker label (MR BOULOS) preceding the passage; the date 17 April 2025 comes from the search listing of the briefing.
r1-ST-MED-2025-008.vn: Excerpt exact. The transcript prints the date (April 17, 2025), carried in clause_support. No other speaker label falls between 'MR BOULOS:' and the passage.
src: I will also reiterate our position that Rwanda should cease all military support of M23 and withdraw all Rwandan troops from DRC territory.

r1-ST-MED-2025-009.s: UN News reported that Secretary-General António Guterres welcomed the peace agreement between the DRC and Rwanda signed on Friday in Washington, DC, and said in a statement that evening that the accord was a significant step towards de-escalation, peace and stability in the eastern DRC and the Great Lakes region.
r1-ST-MED-2025-009.n: Peace agreement signed Friday 27 June 2025 (see existing POL claims); statement that evening.
r1-ST-MED-2025-009.vn: Excerpt exact. Date moved from the article date (28 June, Saturday) to the Friday of the signing evening (27 June), which the page gives by weekday; the precise day is computed, flagged in the note. The statement was issued on the evening of the Friday signing; the UN News article is dated 28 June 2025 (a Saturday), so the statement date of 27 June is computed from the weekday.
src: UN Secretary-General António Guterres has welcomed the peace agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and Rwanda signed on Friday in the United States capital, Washington, DC. The accord is “a significant step towards de-escalation, peace and stability in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Great Lakes region,” he said in a statement that evening.

r1-ST-MED-2025-010.s: UN News reported that MONUSCO head Bintou Keita told the Security Council that armed groups were not only seizing territory but attempting to install a parallel administration, recently appointing a governor and two vice-governors in Bukavu and financial and mining officials in North Kivu.
r1-ST-MED-2025-010.n: Date computed from weekday ('Thursday') and publication date 27 March 2025. Page spacing inside the quoted phrase is reproduced as printed.
r1-ST-MED-2025-010.vn: Excerpt exact; 27 March 2025 was a Thursday, so the date matches. Graded B, not A: one UN News report of a briefing, which is a statement, not an investigation finding. UN News describes the groups as 'affiliated with Rwanda-backed M23 rebels'; Keita's words refer to 'these armed groups'.
src: Bintou Keita, who briefed the Security Council in New York on Thursday over escalating violence and displacement in the country since M23 overran the key cities of Goma and Bukavu last month. These armed groups are not only seizing territory, she explained, but also attempting to install “ a parallel administration ”, recently appointing a governor and two-vice governors in Bukavu as well as financial and mining officials in North Kivu.

r1-ST-MED-2025-011.s: UN News reported that, at the Security Council meeting that renewed the MONUSCO mandate, the United States said negotiations were "yet again disrupted" by M23 advances "supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces", and Ambassador Jennifer Locetta said M23 must immediately withdraw at least 75km from Uvira and return to compliance with its obligations under the Framework Agreement.
r1-ST-MED-2025-011.n: Partisan? No: a state party speaking. Date of the meeting taken from article date 19 Dec 2025.
r1-ST-MED-2025-011.vn: Restored 'yet again' and kept the RDF support as the US's words in quotation marks; the 75km demand is attributed to Locetta as printed. 19 December 2025 was a Friday, matching 'on Friday'.
src: The United States said negotiations were “yet again disrupted” by M23 advances “supported by the Rwanda Defence Forces,” and urged the group to comply with its commitments under the Doha framework. “M23 must immediately withdraw at least 75km from Uvira and return to compliance with all of its obligations undertaken in the Framework Agreement,” said Jennifer Locetta

r1-ST-MED-2025-012.s: UN News (French) reported that in its resolution renewing the MONUSCO mandate the Security Council strongly condemned the M23 offensive in South Kivu, carried out with the support of the Rwandan Defence Force, and demanded their immediate withdrawal from Congolese territory.
r1-ST-MED-2025-012.n: Resolution adopted with the MONUSCO mandate renewal (article dated 19 Dec 2025). excerpt_en flag is only about capitalised English proper nouns that the French prints with different spelling (Security Council = Conseil de sécurité; Rwandan Defence Force = Force de défense rwandaise).
r1-ST-MED-2025-012.vn: Excerpt exact. The excerpt_en flag is a false positive: it is a faithful translation, and the capitalised English words are translations of French proper nouns. Graded B: one UN News report. 'Demands their immediate withdrawal' is UN News's paraphrase outside the quoted resolution text.
src: Dans sa résolution, le Conseil de sécurité « condamne fermement l’offensive menée par le M23 au Sud-Kivu, avec le soutien de la Force de défense rwandaise » et exige leur retrait immédiat du territoire congolais.

r1-ST-MED-2026-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing the final communiqué it received, that the African Union Peace and Security Council asked the group of facilitators to propose urgent measures to defuse the situation in eastern DRC and to report to the AU Mediator.
r1-ST-MED-2026-001.a: African Union Peace and Security Council
r1-ST-MED-2026-001.n: Communiqué of the PSC 1323rd meeting (29 Dec 2025, ministerial) published on peaceau.org 6 Jan 2026; Actualite.cd date used. Page date taken from URL; communiqué received 7 Jan per the article.
r1-ST-MED-2026-001.vn: Date moved from the communiqué's receipt date to the meeting date the page prints; numbers outside the stored excerpt removed from the statement (orchestrator may add_excerpt the meeting sentence). Per the article (outside the stored excerpt), the decision was taken at the PSC's 1323rd ministerial meeting on 29 December 2025; Actualite.cd received the communiqué on 7 January 2026.
ent: Conseil de Paix et de Sécurité de l'Union Africaine
src: Le Conseil de Paix et de Sécurité de l'Union Africaine prie le Groupe de facilitateurs de proposer des mesures urgentes visant à désamorcer la situation dans l’est de la RDC et de faire rapport au Médiateur de l’UA

r1-ST-MED-2026-002.s: The Qatari foreign ministry said on 2 February 2026 that the DRC government and AFC/M23 had signed in Doha the terms of reference stemming from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region, and that the two parties renewed their commitment to the ceasefire and the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace signed between them on November 15, 2025.
r1-ST-MED-2026-002.vn: Mediator's own release; page prints date and both clauses.
src: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Alliance Fleuve Congo / March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) have signed the terms of reference stemming from the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region.
The two parties also renewed their commitment to the ceasefire and the Doha Framework Agreement for Peace signed between them on November 15, 2025

r1-ST-MED-2026-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that the DRC responded favourably to the Angolan proposal and officially accepted the principle of a ceasefire in the east, and that, according to the Presidency of the Republic, this acceptance of the ceasefire from 18 February was made "in a spirit of responsibility, appeasement and search for a peaceful solution to the conflict".
r1-ST-MED-2026-003.n: Presidency statement relayed by Actualite.cd; the Angolan proposal followed a Luanda meeting per the same article. Date from article date (14 Feb 2026).
r1-ST-MED-2026-003.vn: Separated the outlet's narration (acceptance) from what the Presidency is quoted as saying. Statement date not given; article dated 14 February 2026.
src: Selon la Présidence de la République, cette acceptation du cessez-le-feu à partir du 18 février prochain s’inscrit « dans un esprit de responsabilité, d’apaisement et de recherche d’une solution pacifique au conflit ».

r1-ST-MED-2026-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23, while not joining the Angolan scheme, which it says it does not recognise, also reaffirmed its commitment to implement, without delay and in good faith, the ceasefire mechanism agreed under the Doha process.
r1-ST-MED-2026-004.n: Actualite.cd's wording 'soutenue par le Rwanda' is the outlet's; AFC/M23 contests it. Party position relayed by media, not primary communiqué.
r1-ST-MED-2026-004.vn: Fixed the ambiguous 'which it said': the page says the non-recognition is the AFC/M23's own stated position. Party position relayed by media; no primary AFC/M23 communiqué cited. The outlet's 'soutenue par le Rwanda' is its own description.
src: Sans pour autant s’inscrire dans le schéma angolais, qu’elle dit ne pas reconnaître, la rébellion de l’AFC/M23, soutenue par le Rwanda, a de son côté également réaffirmé son engagement à mettre en œuvre, sans délai et de bonne foi, le mécanisme de cessez-le-feu convenu dans le cadre du processus de Doha.

r1-ST-MED-2026-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the senior US adviser for Africa, whom it called "Monsieur Afrique de l'administration Trump", wrote on X that, encouraged by the DRC's acceptance of Angola's ceasefire proposal, all parties must immediately cease hostilities, including drone attacks that continue to cost innocent civilians their lives, and that the priority is now to make the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism agreed in Doha operational.
r1-ST-MED-2026-005.n: Matches the lead X post by @US_SrAdvisorAF of 2026-02-13 (x.com/US_SrAdvisorAF/status/2022417672508469382); cited here via Actualite.cd. Outlet does not print the adviser's name in the excerpt.
r1-ST-MED-2026-005.vn: Speaker attributed as printed in the stored excerpt ('Monsieur Afrique de l'administration Trump'). The page elsewhere names him as Massad Fares Boulos, conseiller principal pour l'Afrique au Département d'État; that name can be added only if the orchestrator extends the excerpt (source_edits.py add_excerpt). The X post is cited through Actualite.cd, not the post itself; post date not printed on the page (article dated 14 February 2026).
src: Encouragés par l'acceptation par la RDC de la proposition de cessez-le-feu angolaise, nous insistons sur la nécessité d'agir concrètement sur le terrain. Toutes les parties doivent immédiatement cesser les hostilités, y compris les attaques de drones qui continuent de coûter la vie à des civils innocents.

La priorité est désormais de rendre opérationnel le Mécanisme de surveillance et de vérification du cessez-le-feu convenu à Doha. L'approbation rapide du protocole d'accord y afférent permettra de renforcer la confiance, de garantir la responsabilité et de protéger les civils", a écrit sur X Monsieur Afrique de l'administration Trump.

r1-ST-MED-2026-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that the East African Community summit of heads of state held on Saturday 7 March 2026 in Arusha urged the African Union, in its final communiqué, to provide the financial and logistical resources needed for the AU-led mediation process on eastern DRC.
r1-ST-MED-2026-006.n: Excerpt ends at the attribution to the final communiqué. The article also gives the AU mediation architecture (Lomé meeting 16-17 Jan 2026, Togolese president Gnassingbé as AU mediator) in other paragraphs.
r1-ST-MED-2026-006.vn: Page prints the date, place and communiqué text.
src: "Le Sommet a exhorté l'Union Africaine à fournir les ressources financières et logistiques nécessaires au processus de médiation dirigé par l'Union Africaine sur l'Est de la République Démocratique du Congo afin d'assurer un engagement rapide et durable jusqu'à son point", lit-on dans le communiqué final

r1-ST-MED-2026-007.s: UN News reported that on Thursday Vivian van de Perre, MONUSCO Deputy Special Representative for protection and operations, told the Security Council that recent hostilities between the government and AFC/M23 were marked by growing use of offensive drones and continued GPS jamming and spoofing, and that a recent 'joint exploratory mission' to Uvira found that security guarantees and freedom of movement are indispensable before peacekeepers can be deployed.
r1-ST-MED-2026-007.n: UN official's briefing as reported by UN News; same briefing the lead X posts mention (US chaired the session on 26 Mar).
r1-ST-MED-2026-007.vn: Added the Uvira clause carried by source 1, which the draft statement left out.
src: « Les récentes hostilités entre le gouvernement et l'AFC/M23 ont également été marquées par le recours croissant à des drones offensifs, ainsi que par la poursuite du brouillage et de la falsification des signaux GPS », a précisé Mme van de Perre.

Mme van de Perre a ajouté qu’une récente « mission exploratoire conjointe » à Uvira a permis de constater que des garanties de sécurité et la liberté de circulation sont indispensables avant de pouvoir procéder à un déploiement de Casques bleus.

r1-ST-MED-2026-008.s: A joint statement by the Government of the DRC and the AFC, together with the United States, Qatar, Togo as African Union mediator, the AU Commission and Switzerland, on talks in Montreux, Switzerland, said the Parties agreed to facilitate rapid, unimpeded, safe and sustained humanitarian access and freedom of movement for humanitarian personnel, goods and services, and agreed to refrain from any attack, destruction or removal of objects indispensable to the survival of the civilian population, including hospital and school facilities.
r1-ST-MED-2026-008.a: Joint: DRC Government, AFC/M23, State of Qatar, United States, Togo (AU mediator), AU Commission, Switzerland
r1-ST-MED-2026-008.n: Joint party statement (partisan on both sides: cited for what the parties said they agreed). Montreux venue and participants are in the page text outside this excerpt; lead X post US_SrAdvisorAF 2026-04-19 refers to the Switzerland meeting.
r1-ST-MED-2026-008.vn: Credited the statement to all the authors the page lists (it was released jointly, not by the two parties alone); added the hospital-protection commitment (health-care focus). Meeting dates (13-17 April) are on the page outside the stored excerpt. Commitments are the signatories' own words, not evidence of implementation.
src: The Parties agreed to facilitate rapid, unimpeded, safe, and sustained humanitarian access and freedom of movement for humanitarian personnel, goods, and services

r1-ST-MED-2026-009.s: UN News reported that MONUSCO head James Swan told the Security Council that the security situation in the east remained highly unstable, with heavy fighting between AFC/M23, supported by Rwandan forces (as UN News wrote), and the FARDC allied with Wazalendo, and that clashes were mainly in Rubaya and around Rutshuru in North Kivu and in the high plains of South Kivu.
r1-ST-MED-2026-009.n: The 'supported by Rwandan forces' phrasing is UN News's paraphrase of the briefing. Briefing date from article date 26 Jun 2026 (Swan briefed the Council that week).
r1-ST-MED-2026-009.vn: Page supports each clause; the 'supported by Rwandan forces' wording is flagged as UN News's. Briefing date not printed; article dated 26 June 2026.
src: Heavy fighting has continued between the Alliance Fleuve Congo/23rd of March Movement (AFC/M23), supported by Rwandan forces, and the Congolese Army (FARDC) allied with the Wazalendo armed group.
Clashes are mainly occurring in two locations in North Kivu, namely Rubaya, an important mining centre, and in the area around Rutshuru, but also in the high plains of South Kivu.

r1-ST-MED-2026-010.s: UN News reported that Swan said the use of offensive drones, artillery and heavy weapons had sharply increased risks to civilians and infrastructure, that AFC/M23 had partially withdrawn from some areas but continued to consolidate parallel administrative structures, and called for swift deployment of the ceasefire monitoring mechanism under the Doha process.
r1-ST-MED-2026-010.n: Single UN-sourced article (UN News is the UN's own outlet).
r1-ST-MED-2026-010.vn: All three clauses on the page; two only on the page, supplied as quotes.
src: Although the AFC/M23 has partially withdrawn from some areas, the group continues to consolidate parallel administrative structures in territory under its control.

r1-ST-MED-2026-011.s: A joint statement by the governments taking part in the Sixth Joint Oversight Committee for the Peace Agreement between the DRC and Rwanda, published by the US State Department, said that the DRC updated on its work to neutralize the FDLR and Rwanda updated on the process of its disengagement of forces/lifting of defensive measures.
r1-ST-MED-2026-011.a: Joint: Governments of the US, DRC, Rwanda, Qatar, Togo (AU mediator), AU Commission
r1-ST-MED-2026-011.n: Joint statement; claims of progress are the parties' own, not verified. Page also records the JOC concern over escalating fighting and drone strikes and the Ebola outbreak.
r1-ST-MED-2026-011.vn: Credited to all the governments that released it (page: 'released by the Governments of the United States of America, the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the Republic of Rwanda, the State of Qatar, the Republic of Togo ... and the African Union Commission'); the meeting was held on 24 June 2026 in London per the page. Progress claims are the signatories' own, not verified.
src: The DRC updated on its work to neutralize the FDLR, and Rwanda updated on the process of its disengagement of forces/lifting of defensive measures.

r1-ST-MED-2026-012.s: A joint statement by the representatives of the DRC Government and of the AFC, published by the US State Department after meetings in Switzerland, said the Parties developed a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement and agreed on the importance of a standardized method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations.
r1-ST-MED-2026-012.a: Joint: DRC Government and AFC/M23 representatives, released with Qatar, US, Togo (AU mediator), Switzerland, AU Commission
r1-ST-MED-2026-012.n: URL as returned by search (path ends 'doha-proce', truncated by the search display; fetch succeeded). Page also mentions a reconnaissance mission on 20 August ahead of the first EJVM+ verification mission scheduled for 24 August in Minembwe.
r1-ST-MED-2026-012.vn: Removed the publication date (shown with the source); credited the statement's authors; added the clause carried by source 1. Page gives meetings August 17-21.
src: Following this evaluation, the Parties developed a roadmap setting out sequenced steps and timelines for negotiations under the Doha Framework Agreement
The Parties agreed on the importance of a standardized method for reporting allegations of ceasefire violations.

r1-ST-MED-2026-013.s: A joint statement by the governments taking part in the sixth Joint Security Coordination Mechanism meeting in Geneva (DRC, Rwanda, US, Qatar, Togo as AU mediator, AU Commission), published by the US State Department, said the DRC and Rwanda agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification of Washington Accords implementation on the ground.
r1-ST-MED-2026-013.a: Joint: Governments of the US, DRC, Rwanda, Qatar, Togo (AU mediator), AU Commission
r1-ST-MED-2026-013.n: Meeting date: page published 13 Aug 2026; lead US post says representatives met 12-13 August. Date precision approximate.
r1-ST-MED-2026-013.vn: Credited all authors; the page itself gives the meeting dates (12-13 August), so the date is a range, not approximate.
src: The DRC and Rwanda agreed to advance two initiatives to strengthen monitoring and verification of Washington Accords implementation on the ground.

r1-ST-MED-2026-014.s: UN News reported, in its own account around a Security Council meeting, that fighting continued in the highlands of Mwenga, Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu, causing new displacement and hindering aid delivery, and that the first two missions of the ceasefire verification mechanism had gone to Minembwe (South Kivu) and then Masisi (North Kivu).
r1-ST-MED-2026-014.a: UN News (its own reporting of the Security Council meeting)
r1-ST-MED-2026-014.n: Descriptive lines are UN News's own reporting around Swan's briefing, not direct quotes of Swan.
r1-ST-MED-2026-014.vn: Actor was MONUSCO, but these lines are UN News narration, not attributed to Swan.
src: Au Sud-Kivu, les affrontements se poursuivent dans les hauts plateaux de Mwenga, Fizi et Uvira, provoquant de nouveaux déplacements et entravant l’acheminement de l’aide.
Deux premières missions du mécanisme chargé de vérifier le cessez-le-feu se sont rendues dans l’est du pays : à Minembwe, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, puis à Masisi, au Nord-Kivu.

r1-ST-MED-2026-015.s: UN News reported that Néné Bintu Iragi, president of South Kivu civil society, told the Security Council that in territories controlled by AFC/M23 there were killings, arson, arbitrary detentions and 'collective punishments' and a parallel administration imposing taxes on the population.
r1-ST-MED-2026-015.a: AFC/M23 (as alleged by Néné Bintu Iragi)
r1-ST-MED-2026-015.n: Allegation by a civil-society leader, relayed by UN News; no AFC/M23 reply found in this page. Not a party statement; a mediator/UN-forum statement. No specific incidents named.
r1-ST-MED-2026-015.vn: Page supports name, role and allegation. Allegation by a civil-society leader; no specific incidents named; no AFC/M23 reply on the page.
src: Dans les territoires contrôlés par l’AFC/M23, elle a dénoncé assassinats, incendies, détentions arbitraires et « punitions collectives », ainsi qu’une administration parallèle imposant ses taxes à la population.

r1-ST-MED-2026-016.s: UN News reported, in its account of an address by Deputy High Commissioner for Human Rights Awa Dabo to the UN Human Rights Council, that OHCHR documented at least 1.080 victims of conflict-related sexual violence across the country (a national figure) between June 2025 and May 2026, mainly women and children, that the real figures are probably much higher, and that armed groups were reportedly responsible for 74% of the victims recorded.
r1-ST-MED-2026-016.n: UN News heading places the dialogue at the Human Rights Council; the 2 Oct date is the article's. Figures nationwide, not Kivu-only; OHCHR said real figures are probably much higher. Sexual-violence figure is national; separate from the 9 Mar 2026 UNJHRO report claim already held.
r1-ST-MED-2026-016.vn: The excerpt alone does not say 'conflict-related sexual violence'; the page's preceding sentence does, supplied as quote; national scope made explicit; 'probably much higher' caveat added. National figure for the whole DRC, not specific to North or South Kivu. Dialogue date not printed; article dated 2 October 2026.
src: Entre juin 2025 et mai 2026, le HCDH a documenté au moins 1.080 victimes à travers le pays, principalement des femmes et des enfants.
Les groupes armés seraient responsables de 74 % des victimes recensées.

r1-ST-MED-2026-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, according to the outlet, said that a momentum had been interrupted because of Rwanda's expansionist aims expressed through the AFC/M23 rebellion in South Kivu, and the outlet added that he alluded to the rebels' occupation of Uvira and their announced withdrawal under US pressure, a withdrawal the outlet said Kinshasa disputed.
r1-ST-MED-2026-017.n: Burundi government position; Rwanda's response not found here. Statement date approximate (article 17 Jan 2026; the speech date is not given in the excerpt). Ndayishimiye assumed the AU chair in Feb 2026 per other pages. The 'withdrawal disputed by Kinshasa' is the outlet's wording.
r1-ST-MED-2026-017.vn: Date corrected from the article date to the speech date the page prints (outside the stored excerpt); weekday mismatch flagged. Per the article, the speech was given at the New Year exchange of wishes with the diplomatic corps in Burundi on 'jeudi 14 janvier 2026'; 14 January 2026 fell on a Wednesday, so the date is approximate. The Uvira passage is the outlet's paraphrase, not a quote.
src: Selon le Chef de l'État burundais, cet élan a été interrompu en raison des visées expansionnistes du Rwanda, exprimées à travers la rébellion de l’AFC/M23 dans la province du Sud-Kivu.

Il a fait allusion aux récentes offensives de la rébellion, qui ont conduit à l’occupation de la ville stratégique d'Uvira, avant qu’elle n’annonce son retrait sous la pression des États-Unis, un retrait contesté par le gouvernement de Kinshasa.

r1-ST-MED-2026-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that, despite the ceasefire announced for 18 February at noon, clashes continued in eastern DRC between the FARDC and AFC/M23; it said the truce had been proposed on 11 February by Angola after a meeting in Luanda, and that the DRC officially adhered to it while AFC/M23 had committed to an immediate halt to hostilities under the Doha process.
r1-ST-MED-2026-018.l: Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
r1-ST-MED-2026-018.a: FARDC; AFC/M23; Wazalendo (PARECO) as named by the outlet
r1-ST-MED-2026-018.n: Local reporting (Radio Okapi, Kinshasa/Goma) on the 18 Feb ceasefire after the Angolan proposal; complements the Actualite.cd claims. Fighting localities named in the page: Mitimingi, Kaunda, Mbiso (Masisi).
r1-ST-MED-2026-018.vn: All clauses on the page; the DRC adherence clause is outside the stored excerpts and supplied. The page also reports fighting in Fizi (South Kivu) around 'Point Zéro' and in Masisi and Rutshuru. 2026-10-28: source 2 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 20 Feb 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt for the adherence clause omits its first half ('Si la RDC a officiellement adhéré ...'), so the full sentence is added.
src: En dépit du cessez-le-feu annoncé pour le 18 février à midi, les affrontements se poursuivent dans l’est de la RDC entre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et la rébellion de l’AFC/M23.
La trêve avait été proposée le 11 février par l’Angola, à l’issue d’une rencontre diplomatique tenue à Luanda.
l’AFC/M23 s’était, de son côté, engagée à un arrêt immédiat des hostilités dans le cadre du processus de Doha
Si la RDC a officiellement adhéré au cessez-le-feu proposé par l’Angola, l’AFC/M23 s’était, de son côté, engagée à un arrêt immédiat des hostilités dans le cadre du processus de Doha

r1-ST-RW-001.s: Reuters reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and M23 rebels to withdraw from Goma.
r1-ST-RW-001.n: Reuters copy on VOA. Kagame posted on X per the same page; the post URL is a lead only.
r1-ST-RW-001.vn: Reuters copy on VOA (byline By Reuters); excerpt carries the statement verbatim.
src: Rwanda's President Paul Kagame said he agreed with the U.S. government on the need for a ceasefire in eastern Congo but gave no indication of bowing to calls for Rwandan troops and the M23 rebels they support to withdraw from Goma.

r1-ST-RW-002.s: CNN reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, asked in an interview whether there were Rwandan troops inside the DRC, answered 'I don't know' and said Rwanda would do anything to protect itself.
r1-ST-RW-002.n: Interview on Monday; CNN article published 2025-02-03, so the date is the publication date and Monday is 3 February.
r1-ST-RW-002.vn: CNN exclusive interview; both clauses on page; second clause is on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Kagame's full answer: "is there a problem in Congo that concerns Rwanda? And that Rwanda would do anything to protect itself? I'd say 100%".
src: In an exclusive interview with CNN on Monday, Kagame was asked if there were any Rwandan troops inside the DRC. “I don’t know,” Kagame said, despite the fact that he is commander-in-chief of the Rwandan Defence Force.

r1-ST-RW-003.s: Al Jazeera reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame, at a news conference in Kigali, said that the FDLR's presence in the DRC is Rwanda's main concern and that 'if this problem is not resolved, it is natural for Rwanda to remain involved' in the conflict; Al Jazeera added that Rwanda denies Kinshasa's allegations against it.
r1-ST-RW-003.n: Date is Al Jazeera's publication date; the conference date was not given in the excerpt.
r1-ST-RW-003.vn: Draft said Rwanda denies 'allegations of sending troops'; Al Jazeera's denial sentence covers both the M23-support and troop allegations, and is Al Jazeera's narration, not a quoted Rwandan statement. Kagame is named on page. Al Jazeera's denial sentence follows its statement that Kinshasa accuses Kigali of supporting the M23 and of sending Rwandan troops into Congolese territory; it is Al Jazeera's narration, not a quoted Rwandan statement.
src: Speaking at a news conference in Kigali, Kagame reiterated that the FDLR’s presence in the DRC is Rwanda’s main concern, adding that “if this problem is not resolved, it is natural for Rwanda to remain involved” in the conflict.

r1-ST-RW-004.s: Al Jazeera reported that Kagame said Rwanda has information that Congolese authorities 'are arming the FDLR and integrating its members into their own forces'.
r1-ST-RW-004.n: Counter-claim against Kinshasa; Kinshasa's account of the same issue to be found in the DRC statements units.
r1-ST-RW-004.vn: Excerpt verbatim; attribution kept. Rwandan allegation against Kinshasa, attributed; Kagame said the evidence includes testimony from former FDLR members.
src: Kagame said Rwanda has information that Congolese authorities “are arming the FDLR and integrating its members into their own forces”.

r1-ST-RW-005.s: The Government of Rwanda said in a statement that responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu cannot be placed on Rwanda, and condemned the FARDC and the Burundian army (FDNB), together with the FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries, which it said have been systematically bombing civilian villages close to the Rwandan border using fighter jets and attack drones.
r1-ST-RW-005.l: South Kivu, near the Rwandan border
r1-ST-RW-005.n: Party statement. Contested event: Kinshasa and Burundi accounts of the December 2025 Uvira fighting are for other units.
r1-ST-RW-005.vn: Bombing clause was on the page, not in the excerpt (clause_support maps it); dateline moved to the note since the excerpt does not print it. Party statement, dated 'Kigali, 10 December 2025' on the page. The ministry's own wording is 'DRC-backed FDLR genocidal militias'. It adds that AFC/M23 'has said it has been forced to counter' the bombing.
src: The responsibility for ceasefire violations, ongoing attacks and fighting in South Kivu, DRC cannot be placed on Rwanda. Rwanda condemns the Congolese Army (FARDC) and the Burundian Army (FDNB), together with its coalition of the DRC-backed FDLR genocidal militias, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries,

r1-ST-RW-006.s: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that, as a result of the past week's bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens had fled across the border to Bugarama in western Rwanda, where they were accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.
r1-ST-RW-006.l: Kamanyola, Walungu/Uvira area; Bugarama and Nyarushishi, Rwanda
r1-ST-RW-006.n: Rwandan figure and attribution only; no independent confirmation found in this unit.
r1-ST-RW-006.vn: Removed the '10 December 2025' date from the statement (not in the excerpt; the claim date and source date carry it). Content is Rwanda's allegation only; no independent confirmation in this unit. Rwandan government allegation; not independently confirmed.
src: As a result of this past week’s bombing of Kamanyola from Burundi, over 1000 Congolese citizens have fled across the border to Bugarama, in Western Rwanda, where they are accommodated at the Nyarushishi Transit Camp.

r1-ST-RW-007.s: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the Burundian Army had amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC and had laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.
r1-ST-RW-007.x: Rwanda government: close to 20,000 Burundian troops
r1-ST-RW-007.n: Rwandan allegation about Burundian deployment; territory tag Fizi is for Minembwe (Itombwe area) and should be checked.
r1-ST-RW-007.vn: Removed the '10 December 2025' date from the statement (not in the excerpt; the claim date and source date carry it). Content is Rwanda's allegation only; no independent confirmation in this unit. Rwandan government allegation; not independently confirmed.
src: The Burundian Army has amassed close to 20,000 troops in South Kivu in the service of the Government of DRC, and notably laid siege to Banyamulenge villages in Minembwe in a deliberate attempt to starve the residents.

r1-ST-RW-008.s: The Government of Rwanda said in its statement on ceasefire violations that the DRC had openly stated it would not observe any ceasefire and was fighting to recapture territories lost to AFC/M23 even as the peace process unfolded, and that the DRC's failure to neutralize the FDLR as stipulated in the June 2025 Peace Agreement continued to delay the resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC.
r1-ST-RW-008.n: Excerpt covers the first clause (DRC would not observe ceasefire); the FDLR sentence is in the same page but not in this excerpt.
r1-ST-RW-008.vn: FDLR clause is on the page, not in the excerpt (clause_support maps it). Date removed from statement text. Rwanda's characterisation of Kinshasa's position; no Congolese statement to that effect is cited here.
src: The DRC has openly stated that it would not observe any ceasefire, and was fighting to recapture territories lost to AFC/M23, even as the peace process unfolded.

r1-ST-RW-009.s: The Government of Rwanda welcomed, in a statement carried on its foreign ministry's news listing, 'today's signing' of the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the DRC Government and the AFC/M23.
r1-ST-RW-009.n: Cited from the ministry's news listing page (teaser); the full statement page was not located. Listing page content changes over time.
r1-ST-RW-009.vn: Narrowed to what the teaser prints: removed the Kigali dateline (not on the listing) and the date (not in the excerpt; claim date carries it). Cited from the ministry listing teaser only, which dates it Saturday, 15 November 2025; the full statement page was not read and the listing prints no Kigali dateline. French and Kinyarwanda versions are listed the same day.
src: The Government of Rwanda welcomes today’s signing of the Doha Framework for a Comprehensive Peace Agreement between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23.

r1-ST-RW-010.s: Jeune Afrique published an interview with Rwandan President Paul Kagame under the headline quote 'N’attendez pas de moi que je lève nos mesures de défense alors que vous laissez Félix Tshisekedi faire ce qu’il veut' (Do not expect me to lift our defence measures while you let Félix Tshisekedi do what he wants).
r1-ST-RW-010.n: Article behind a paywall; only the headline quote and standfirst were read. Date from search listing (3 Apr 2026); the interview date is not stated. Standfirst sentence on four months after the accord is not in the excerpt.
r1-ST-RW-010.vn: Per the brief the claim may say no more than the headline quote: removed the standfirst clause (war continuing four months after the Washington accord) and 'exclusive', which are not in the excerpt. Paywalled; only the headline quote was read. The headline does not say whom Kagame was addressing. The page caption dates the interview to 26 March 2026 in Kigali.
src: Paul Kagame : « N’attendez pas de moi que je lève nos mesures de défense alors que vous laissez Félix Tshisekedi faire ce qu’il veut »

r1-ST-RW-011.s: DW reported that Rwandan army spokesperson Ronald Rwivanga said that five civilians were killed and 25 were wounded on the outskirts of the border town of Gisenyi.
r1-ST-RW-011.x: Rwanda army spokesperson: 5 civilians killed, 25 wounded
r1-ST-RW-011.n: Casualties on the Rwandan side of the border; DW attributes the Reuters report of artillery exchange to UN sources. Check the page for wire credits.
r1-ST-RW-011.vn: Figure 'five' is printed as a word in the excerpt; flag resolved. Wire credit at page end noted in originating_source. Casualties on the Rwandan side of the border (Gisenyi), as stated by the Rwandan army spokesperson; DW story credited "(AFP, AP, Reuters)".
src: Rwandan army spokesperson Ronald Rwivanga said that five civilians were killed and 25 were wounded on the outskirts of the border town of Gisenyi.

r1-ST-RW-013.s: Taarifa (Rwandan outlet), in an article on remarks by Nduhungirehe, wrote that following the capture of Uvira by the M23 on 10 December 2025 (Taarifa's date), Rwandan and Burundian security officials held meetings at the shared border on 14 and 28 December to discuss confidence-building measures and de-escalation mechanisms; Taarifa narrates this sentence itself and attributes the surrounding remarks to Nduhungirehe.
r1-ST-RW-013.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the 10 December capture date is Taarifa's wording and other sources give other dates for the capture (to be reconciled by the Uvira unit). The excerpt does not itself carry the 'Nduhungirehe said' attribution: the page attributes the paragraph to him in the following sentence and the sentence before.

Taarifa relays an interview Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe gave to Jeune Afrique, and quotes him next: 'These contacts were aimed at calming tensions and avoiding further deterioration'.
src: Following the capture of the Congolese town of Uvira by the M23 movement on 10 December 2025, Rwandan and Burundian security officials held meetings at the shared border on 14 and 28 December to discuss confidence-building measures and de-escalation mechanisms.

r1-ST-RW-015.l: M23-held areas of North and South Kivu
r1-ST-RW-015.n: General rejection, not a specific reply to the HRW January 2026 sexual-violence report; no direct Rwandan reply to that report found.

src: Between 165 and 167 women were assaulted by male inmates during the jailbreak, an internal UN document seen by the BBC says. The report states that most of the women were killed after the inmates set fire to the prison. The BBC has not been able to verify the reports.

La mission a confirmé que, lors de l'évasion massive de la prison de Munzenze, le 27 janvier, la plupart des 160 femmes détenues – ainsi que de nombreux nourrissons – sont mortes, et qu'un nombre indéterminé d'entre elles ont été violées collectivement, dans certains cas devant leurs enfants, par des détenus hommes qui s'étaient introduits de force dans le quartier des femmes.

src: Selon des autorités judiciaires, lors de l’évasion massive de la prison de Muzenze à Goma le 27 janvier, au moins 165 prisonnières ont été violées. « La plupart d’entre elles auraient été tuées par la suite, dans un incendie dont les circonstances restent floues », a précisé le chef des droits de l'homme.

La mission a confirmé que, lors de l'évasion massive de la prison de Munzenze, le 27 janvier, la plupart des 160 femmes détenues – ainsi que de nombreux nourrissons – sont mortes, et qu'un nombre indéterminé d'entre elles ont été violées collectivement, dans certains cas devant leurs enfants, par des détenus hommes qui s'étaient introduits de force dans le quartier des femmes.

r1-SV-2025-004.s: The OHCHR summary report of the fact-finding mission on North and South Kivu included satellite imagery of Munzenze Central Prison, Goma, captioned as showing its condition after a prison break and fire which killed the majority of the prison's 160 female inmates on 27 January 2025.
r1-SV-2025-004.l: Munzenze Central Prison, Goma (gereza ya Munzenze), North Kivu
r1-SV-2025-004.x: OHCHR FFM: 160 female inmates, majority killed

r1-SV-2025-007.s: OHCHR's Fact-Finding Mission reported a pattern of widespread rape and other sexual violence, primarily against women and girls but also men, boys and LGBT individuals, by M23 during cordon-and-search operations, house-to-house searches and in detention, and by FARDC and Wazalendo during their retreat from the frontlines in January and February.
r1-SV-2025-007.a: M23; FARDC; Wazalendo (as attributed by the FFM)
r1-SV-2025-007.n: UN fact-finding mission summary; period given as 'January and February' for FARDC/Wazalendo retreat, M23 operations undated in the passage. Province field set to North Kivu for the record; covers both provinces.
r1-SV-2025-007.vn: Excerpt exact in summary report; statement matches, including the attribution split by party.
src: The FFM identified a pattern of widespread use of rape and other forms of sexual violence primarily against women, girls but also men, boys, including LGBT individuals by M23 during cordon-andsearch operations, house-to-house searches and in detention, as well as by FARDC and Wazalendo, during their retreat from the frontlines in January and February.

r1-SV-2025-008.s: The report of the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission on North and South Kivu (A/HRC/60/80, submitted to the UN Human Rights Council) stated that a victim recounted M23 conducting house-to-house searches for FARDC soldiers in Katindo neighbourhood, Goma, and that she was gang-raped by three M23 members, together with her mother.

The clashes facilitated the escape of a reported 770 inmates from Uvira prison on 19 February, including some sentenced for war crimes and crimes against humanity.

r1-SV-2025-014.s: FIDH and other signatory organisations stated that reports indicate mass prison escapes at Muzenze prison in Goma, and also in Bukavu, Uvira and Kalehe in South Kivu and in Kalemie in Tanganyika province.
r1-SV-2025-014.n: Tanganyika is outside phase 1; kept only as part of one sentence. NGO statement (FIDH with partners).
r1-SV-2025-014.vn: Clause on late-January M23 arrival now carried by a page passage; joint statement credited to signatories; excerpt_en restricted to the excerpt. Joint NGO statement relaying unspecified 'reports'; does not date the individual escapes. Same statement places the escapes after the arrival of M23 in North and South Kivu from late January 2025 and the disintegration of local authorities (replacement quote).
src: Les rapports font état d’ évasions massives à la prison de Muzenze à Goma au Nord-Kivu, mais aussi à Bukavu, Uvira et Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, et à Kalemie dans la province du Tanganyika.

r1-SV-2025-015.s: Amnesty International reported that, of 14 survivors of sexual violence from North and South Kivu it interviewed, eight said they were gang raped by M23 fighters, five said they were gang raped by Wazalendo fighters and one said she was gang raped by FARDC soldiers.
r1-SV-2025-015.a: M23; Wazalendo; FARDC (as stated by survivors to Amnesty)
r1-SV-2025-015.x: Amnesty: 14 survivors interviewed (eight M23, five Wazalendo, one FARDC)
r1-SV-2025-015.n: Survivors are pseudonymised by Amnesty; no names recorded.
r1-SV-2025-015.vn: Figures written as the source prints them; date widened because the page dates some cases to January 2024. Counts are survivors' accounts ('said'). Some Wazalendo cases in the sample predate the window (two in January 2024, per the same page).
src: Of the 14 survivors of sexual violence from North and South Kivu, interviewed by Amnesty International, eight said they were gang raped by M23 fighters, five said they were gang raped by Wazalendo fighters, and one said she was gang raped by FARDC soldiers.

r1-SV-2025-016.s: Amnesty International reported that all survivors of gang rape by M23 fighters said the perpetrators wore uniforms resembling M23's and spoke Kinyarwanda, and that these gang rapes took place between March and May 2025 when the fighters controlled Goma and Bukavu.
r1-SV-2025-016.vn: Excerpt exact; statement matches. Identification of perpetrators rests on survivors' description of uniforms and language.
src: All the survivors of gang rape by M23 fighters said the perpetrators wore uniforms that resembled those of the M23 and spoke Kinyarwanda, which is spoken by some M23 fighters. The gang rapes by M23 fighters took place between March and May 2025 when the fighters controlled Goma and Bukavu in eastern DRC.

r1-SV-2025-017.s: Amnesty International reported that in Rutshuru and Masisi territories in North Kivu, and in Kalehe territory in South Kivu, Wazalendo groups raped women and girls, including one woman gang raped in late March 2025.
r1-SV-2025-017.n: Same page also mentions earlier incidents (January 2024), outside the window and not recorded.
r1-SV-2025-017.vn: Excerpt exact; statement matches. Date '2025-03' applies to the one dated case only.
src: In Rutshuru and Masisi territories in North Kivu province, as well as Kalehe territory in South Kivu province, Wazalendo groups raped women and girls. One woman was gang raped in late March 2025.

r1-SV-2025-018.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing various sources in Katoyi sector, that a group of Wazalendo militiamen raped at least 11 women and a 13-year-old girl on Sunday 31 August in the locality of Remeka, Masisi territory, and that some victims were also publicly humiliated, stripped and forced to walk naked in the market.
r1-SV-2025-018.l: Remeka, Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-SV-2025-018.x: Radio Okapi: at least 11 women and one 13-year-old girl

src: D’après diverses sources contactées par Radio Okapi dans le secteur de Katoyi, un groupe de miliciens Wazalendo a violé au moins 11 femmes ainsi qu’une fillette de 13 ans le dimanche 31 août dernier, dans la localité de Remeka.

« Aucun décès ni blessé n’a été recensé au sein de la communauté depuis le retrait des troupes rwandaises » , a précisé Muyaya

Dans cette mise au point, ce mouvement rebelle soutenu par le Rwanda rappelle que son retrait d’Uvira s’est effectué en pleine journée, dans le calme et sous les regards des caméras du monde entier.

Elle les présente comme démontrant l’ampleur des exactions commises à Uvira non pas par ses éléments, mais, selon Lawrence Kanyuka, par la coalition gouvernementale composée des FARDC, des FNDB, des FDLR, des Wazalendo et de mercenaires étrangers.

The FARDC account (communiqué n°13) differs in the claimed casualties (civilians and hospital staff); AFC/M23 reply not found.
