BCNUDH does not name the territory; Africa-Infos.cd places the area in the highlands of Fizi territory. The FARDC account (communiqué n°13) describes civilian and hospital-staff victims instead.
src: De même, le 20 mai 2026, au cours des affrontements armés opposant les éléments de l’AFC/M23 aux forces loyalistes, l’hôpital de Mikenge a été visé par un bombardement attribué à des éléments de l’AFC/M23. Selon les sources, plusieurs militaires des FARDC blessés et malades qui s’y trouvaient auraient été tués.

r1-SV-2026-016.s: Africa-Infos.cd reported that in its press communiqué n°13 of 20 May 2026 the FARDC denounced attacks attributed to a coalition of the RDF and the AFC/M23 in several localities of Minembwe, said that several drone strikes targeted Kalingi and Mikenge in the Minembwe highlands from the first hours of the morning, and said that the Mikenge General Hospital was reportedly "intentionally targeted" and then completely destroyed.
r1-SV-2026-016.l: Kalingi and Mikenge, Minembwe hauts plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-2026-016.n: Party account. FARDC statement of 20 May; the article is dated 21 May. Compare the BCNUDH claim on the same hospital (different casualty description).
r1-SV-2026-016.vn: 'hit' narrowed to 'targeted' (ont visé); the army's conditional (aurait été) kept; added the attribution to the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition that the source prints. Party account. Compare the BCNUDH account of the same hospital strike (different casualty description).
src: Dans ce communiqué de presse n°13, les FARDC affirment que plusieurs frappes de drones ont visé dès les premières heures de la matinée les localités de Kalingi et Mikenge, dans les hauts plateaux de Minembwe.
Selon l’armée Congolaise, ces attaques ont notamment touché l’Hôpital Général de Mikenge qui aurait été « intentionnellement ciblé » puis complètement détruit au cours des bombardements.

Le mercredi 20 mai 2026, les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo ont publié un nouveau communiqué dénonçant des attaques attribuées à la coalition RDF/AFC-M23 dans plusieurs localités de Minembwe.

r1-SV-2026-017.s: BCNUDH reported that on 2 January 2026 three women, two men, a girl and a boy were killed and 42 others wounded in Masisi-centre, North Kivu, by shells presumed to have been dropped by drone by the FARDC, exploding in a residential quarter; Actualite.cd reported that, according to available information, a Congolese army drone targeted AFC/M23 positions in the Mont Ngaliema quarter of Masisi-centre, and that a provisional toll gave four civilians dead and seven wounded.
r1-SV-2026-017.l: Masisi-centre (Mont Ngaliema quarter), Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-SV-2026-017.a: drone of the Congolese army (FARDC), as reported
r1-SV-2026-017.x: BCNUDH: three women, two men, a girl and a boy killed; 42 wounded. Actualite.cd (provisional toll, local sources): four dead and seven wounded among civilians.
r1-SV-2026-017.n: Figures differ by source: BCNUDH 7 killed/42 wounded; local sources 4 killed/7 wounded (provisional); MSF: two died after admission. BCNUDH adds the strike reportedly missed its likely target, an AFC/M23 cadre residence (not cited here). Possible earlier UV/NKS claims on Masisi not checked beyond the period packet.
r1-SV-2026-017.vn: The drone-targeting sentence is the outlet's 'selon les informations disponibles', not MSF's; removed 'relaying MSF'. 'reportedly dropped' put back to 'presumed' (présumément). Figures field rewritten to the printed words. Tolls differ: BCNUDH seven killed and 42 wounded; Actualite.cd's local sources four dead and seven wounded (provisional); MSF, per Actualite.cd, said at least 42 wounded were admitted and two died after admission. BCNUDH prints 'Masis-centre'. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-008: 'from local sources' is not in either Actualite.cd excerpt (the toll is just 'un bilan provisoire'); removed. Kept 'presumed' (presumement). BCNUDH's breakdown here (three women, two men, a girl, a boy) differs from its January note (two women, a girl, a boy among seven). Fresh search: TV5Monde (9 Jan 2026, headline seen via search/extract only, not retained) reports 'le M23 accuse les FARDC d'avoir bombarde Masisi-Centre, Kinshasa dement et accuse a son tour le groupe rebelle' and 'six personnes' killed in an 'explosion'; the Kinshasa denial is not in this claim and should be researched and recorded as a separate statement claim (retain the page first).; excerpt-support: nothing to add
src: Le 2 janvier 2026, à Masis-centre, province du Nord-Kivu, trois femmes, deux hommes, une fille et un garçon ont été tués et 42 autres blessés par des obus présumément largués par drone par des FARDC explosant dans un quartier résidentiel de Masisi-Centre.

Ce bilan a été communiqué vendredi 2 janvier 2026 par l’organisation humanitaire Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), à la suite d’une frappe aérienne survenue dans une zone résidentielle de Masisi-centre. Selon les informations disponibles, un drone de l’armée congolaise a ciblé des positions des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans le quartier Mont Ngaliema, à Masisi-centre.

Un bilan provisoire fait état de quatre morts et sept blessés parmi les civils, ainsi que de plusieurs bâtiments endommagés par la frappe. Les blessés ont été évacués vers l’hôpital général de référence de Masisi.

r1-SV-2026-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Bitale agglomeration came under the control of AFC/M23 rebels on the morning of Monday 15 June 2026, after two days of intense fighting against the FARDC and Wazalendo militiamen.
r1-SV-2026-019.n: Trimmed excerpt: the exact end phrase was matched in the page text; check_raw to confirm. Single outlet.
r1-SV-2026-019.vn: Matches the page (Actualite.cd's own reminder paragraph). Single outlet. Not in the existing Bitale claim, which covers only the MSF patients.
src: l’agglomération de Bitale est passée sous le contrôle des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans la matinée du lundi 15 juin 2026, après deux jours d’intenses affrontements contre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et les miliciens Wazalendo.

r1-SV-2026-020.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Wazalendo militiamen targeted a convoy of agents on a mission on the Mwenga – Kamituga axis in South Kivu; it quoted MSF as saying that on 1 May an MSF team travelling to Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu to assess humanitarian needs faced a security incident, and that all its staff were safe and continuing their planned activities in Mwenga.
r1-SV-2026-020.l: Mwenga–Kamituga axis, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-2026-020.n: The attribution to Wazalendo is the outlet's own, not MSF's; MSF's communiqué does not name a perpetrator. No casualties. The outlet links the incident to the Kinshasa–AFC/M23 humanitarian access memorandum signed in Switzerland (Doha process) on the same day-range.
r1-SV-2026-020.vn: Removed the 'positive and constructive exchanges' clause, which no stored excerpt carries. The attribution to Wazalendo is the outlet's; the MSF communiqué it quotes names no perpetrator and speaks of a 'security incident'. No casualties reported.
src: Des miliciens Wazalendo, ces groupes armés alliés à l’armée congolaise, ont pris pour cible un convoi d’agents en mission dans la province du Sud-Kivu, sur l’axe Mwenga – Kamituga.
« Le 1er mai, alors qu’une équipe de MSF se rendait à Mwenga, Kamituga et Kitutu, au sud-ouest de Bukavu, afin d’évaluer les besoins humanitaires, elle a été confrontée à un incident de sécurité.
Tous les membres de notre personnel sont sains et saufs et poursuivent actuellement leurs activités humanitaires prévues à Mwenga

r1-SV-2026-021.s: BCNUDH reported that in January 2026 it documented at least 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence affecting 61 victims (39 women, 21 girls and one man), 59 per cent fewer than the 147 victims documented in December 2025, which it explained mainly by intensified fighting and insecurity that limited humanitarian access to victims and led to under-documentation.
r1-SV-2026-021.a: M23, Nyatura, Raïa Mutomboki, ADF, FARDC, PNC (per BCNUDH)
r1-SV-2026-021.x: BCNUDH January 2026: 46 cases, 61 victims (39 women, 21 girls, 1 man); December 2025: 147 victims (102 women, 45 girls)
r1-SV-2026-021.n: UN body monthly report (published later, April 2026 on the MONUSCO site; date is the report period end). The apostrophes in the second excerpt are straight quotes in the source text.
r1-SV-2026-021.vn: Matches the January 2026 BCNUDH report. Sources 2-3 (perpetrator breakdown) support the actor field.
src: Au cours du mois de janvier, le BCNUDH a documenté au moins 46 cas de violences sexuelles liées aux conflits (VSLC), touchant 61 victimes (39 femmes, 21 filles et un homme). Ce chiffre représente une diminution de 59 pour cent par rapport au mois précédent[4] , où 147 victimes (102 femmes et 45 filles) avaient été documentées en décembre 2025.

Cette diminution de 59 % des cas documentés en janvier 2026 s'explique principalement par l'intensification des combats et de l'insécurité, qui a rendu les populations déplacées plus difficiles à atteindre et a considérablement limité l'accès des humanitaires aux victimes, entraînant une sous-documentation des violences plutôt qu'une réelle diminution de celles-ci.

Le M23 arrive en tête, avec 21 victimes (13 femmes et huit filles), suivi des Nyatura (quatre victimes : deux femmes et deux filles), les Raïa Mutomboki (trois victimes : deux femmes et une fille), les ADF (deux femmes).
25 victimes (15 femmes, neuf filles et un homme) sont attribuées aux FARDC, deux femmes à la PNC, et une fille à un fonctionnaire de l’État affecté aux services des mines et énergie.

r1-SV-2026-022.s: ReliefWeb, republishing a MONUSCO item, reported that BCNUDH said in a press release that 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented last year, affecting 1 534 victims (854 women and 672 girls), that North and South Kivu concentrate nearly 80 per cent of documented victims, that armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of victims, with M23 first with 439 victims, and that FARDC, PNC and ANR members were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.
r1-SV-2026-022.l: Eastern DRC (North Kivu and South Kivu concentrate about 80% of documented victims)
r1-SV-2026-022.a: armed groups (M23 first), FARDC, PNC and ANR, per BCNUDH
r1-SV-2026-022.x: BCNUDH (last year): 887 cases; 1 534 victims (854 women, 672 girls); N+S Kivu nearly 80%; armed groups 75% of victims; M23 439 victims; State actors in 19% of cases
r1-SV-2026-022.n: Covers calendar year 2025 and the whole country (about 80% in the Kivus); statement date is the release date. Source is ReliefWeb relaying MONUSCO/BCNUDH.
r1-SV-2026-022.vn: Matches the ReliefWeb copy of the MONUSCO item; arithmetic gap surfaced. Figures cover calendar year 2025, nationwide. As printed, 854 women and 672 girls add up to 1,526, not 1,534 (the remainder is not broken down).
src: Selon les données collectées par le BCNUDH, 887 cas de violences sexuelles liées au conflit ont été documentés l’année passée, affectant 1 534 victimes, dont une majorité écrasante de femmes (854) et de filles (672).

Les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu concentrent à elles seules près de 80 % des victimes documentées, confirmant la persistance d’un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement fragile dans l’Est du pays. D’après le BCNUDH, les groupes armés sont responsables de 75 % des victimes.

Le Mouvement du 23 mars (M23) arrive en tête avec 439 victimes, suivi des groupes Wazalendo, de la Coopérative pour le développement du Congo (CODECO), de divers groupes Maï-Maï, ainsi que des Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR) et des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF).

Le BCNUDH note également avec préoccupation l’implication d’acteurs étatiques, notamment des membres des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), de la Police nationale congolaise (PNC) et de l’Agence nationale de renseignement (ANR), dans 19 % des cas documentés.

r1-SV-2026-023.s: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations, and that humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in such cases since 2024, disproportionately affecting women and girls.
r1-SV-2026-023.l: Eastern DRC (North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri)
r1-SV-2026-023.a: AFC/M23, per UN Group of Experts
r1-SV-2026-023.n: Report S/2026/466 dated 5 June 2026 (circulated 11 June). Reporting period is 2025; recorded here as the 2026 publication. Claim is general, not Kivu-only.
src: 11. AFC/M23 was the leading perpetrator of conflict-related sexual violence according to cases documented and verified by the United Nations (see S/2025/858, para. 80 and annex 37). Humanitarian actors recorded a dramatic increase in cases of such violence since 2024, with cases disproportionately affecting women and girls (see annexes 4 and 5).

r1-SV-2026-024.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that it reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026, entitled "Note Explicative", that AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in health care; that following its distribution the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (IPS) initiated a series of inspections of humanitarian actors' premises; that IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents, access to confidential patient files containing names of victims, and consumption records for supplies such as PEP kits and dignity kits; and that some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease distributing dignity kits.
r1-SV-2026-024.l: North Kivu (AFC/M23-run provincial health department, Goma)
r1-SV-2026-024.n: Group of Experts annex relying on confidential sources and a document it reviewed. Related: late-March and April 2026 meetings agreed that only aggregate data would be shared (see next claim). The Group's own assessment in para. 8 (not cited) says the actions may deter victims.
r1-SV-2026-024.vn: The deterrence clause and the 'Note Explicative' title were not in the stored excerpts: the title is on the page in the sentence after the excerpt (clause_support) and the deterrence point is in the note only. Verbs aligned with the source ('initiated a series of inspections'). The Group based this on confidential sources and a document it reviewed. It separately notes (para. 8) that AFC/M23's actions may deter victims of sexual violence from accessing humanitarian assistance.
src: The Group reviewed a document dated 11 February 2026 that the AFC/M23 distributed to multiple humanitarian actors involved in the provision of health care, including governmental and non-governmental organisations and international organisations.

5. Following the distribution of this note, the AFC/M23-run Provincial Health Inspection Department (Inspection Provinciale de la Santé or IPS) initiated a series of inspections of the premises of humanitarian actors.

IPS inspectors requested aggregate data on sexual violence incidents and access to confidential patient files containing names of victims and other personal information. They also requested access to consumption records for supplies such as PEP kits and dignity kits.
Some humanitarian actors were ordered to cease the distribution of dignity kits to curb the number of what they alleged to be “fake” victims seeking humanitarian assistance.

r1-SV-2026-025.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that at a joint meeting in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23, attended by AFC/M23 officials including Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete, Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs, AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data, affirmed that it did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files; further meetings in late March and April 2026 resulted in an agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared.
r1-SV-2026-025.l: North Kivu (meeting between AFC/M23 and humanitarian actors, late March 2026)
r1-SV-2026-025.n: Excerpt may exceed 60 words; trim if check_raw complains. Report of what AFC/M23 officials said by the UN Group of Experts (confidential sources), not a public statement by AFC/M23.
r1-SV-2026-025.vn: Added the two officials the source names as present (source 1 prints them), for investigators; otherwise unchanged. The Group's account (confidential sources) of what AFC/M23 said at a closed meeting, not a public AFC/M23 statement. Being named is not a finding of individual responsibility.
src: 6. A joint meeting was held in late March 2026 between humanitarian actors and AFC/M23 at which the issue of sexual violence data was discussed.

AFC/M23 officials present at the meeting included Colonel John Imani Nzenze, AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and the AFC/M23 liaison with humanitarian actors, and Ms. Chantal Kayitaba Murekatete (S/2025/858, annex 39), Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs.

At the meeting, the AFC/M23 reprimanded humanitarian actors and accused them of inventing data. It affirmed that AFC/M23 did not tolerate sexual violence and criticised the lack of perpetrator data in patient files as this made it more difficult for it to punish perpetrators.

Further meetings between the AFC/M23 and humanitarian actors were held in late March and April 2026, resulting in an agreement that only aggregate data on sexual violence would be shared in the future.

r1-SV-2026-026.s: Amnesty International said that the two sexual violence survivors it interviewed about abuses by CMC-FDP fighters in Rutshuru territory were held in conditions that amount to sexual slavery.
r1-SV-2026-026.l: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu (Mudugudu base)
r1-SV-2026-026.x: Amnesty: 16 victims, survivors and family members interviewed remotely (March-April 2026); two sexual violence survivors
r1-SV-2026-026.n: Amnesty NGO research (remote interviews). Events 2025, report 2026; included because it concerns Wazalendo SV in North Kivu. Survivors unnamed. The area Bukombo is described as controlled by M23. CMC-FDP denial recorded separately.
r1-SV-2026-026.vn: The rest of the draft (CMC-FDP abuses, 16 interviews, June-December 2025) is already r1-POL-2026-011 from the same page; narrowed to the one finding not stated there.
src: An armed group backed by the Congolese army (FARDC) has killed and tortured civilians, looted property, and abducted women as sexual slaves in Rutshuru territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Amnesty International said today.

Between March and April 2026, Amnesty International conducted remote interviews by secure phone applications with 16 victims, survivors, and family members of civilians killed, raped, tortured, abducted, or ill-treated by CMC-FDP fighters between June and December 2025.
The two sexual violence survivors that Amnesty International interviewed were held in conditions that amount to sexual slavery.

r1-SV-2026-027.s: Amnesty International reported that CMC-FDP said it "categorically rejects" the allegations that its fighters raped, sexually enslaved or forced women to "marry" its commanders, and that no complaints, official reports or referrals had been brought to the attention of its internal disciplinary or judicial bodies regarding the incidents.
r1-SV-2026-027.l: Bukombo area, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-SV-2026-027.n: Denial as reported by Amnesty; the party's own channel was not located.
r1-SV-2026-027.vn: The general denial by spokesperson Gashegu on 16 June 2026 is already r1-POL-2026-012; narrowed to the specific denial of the sexual-violence allegations, which that claim does not state. Party denial as reported by Amnesty.
src: CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026. CMC-FDP denied responsibility for the abuses documented here and asserted that “CMC-FDP remains committed to respecting human rights and the discipline of its combatants.”

CMC-FDP said that it “categorically rejects” the allegations that its fighters raped, sexually enslaved or forced women to “marry” its commanders. “No complaints, official reports, or referrals have been brought to the attention of our internal disciplinary or judicial bodies regarding the mentioned incidents.”

r1-SV-2026-028.s: Amnesty International reported that, in research into M23 abuses at the Rubaya and Lomera mines, it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital; Amnesty said it wrote to the M23 spokesperson and an M23 mining representative on 11 August 2026 and had received no response at the time of publication.
r1-SV-2026-028.l: Rubaya coltan mine area (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera gold mine (Kabare, South Kivu)
r1-SV-2026-028.x: Amnesty: 18 artisanal miners summarily killed; at least nine of them beaten and died at health centres or before reaching hospital.
r1-SV-2026-028.n: Amnesty report AFR 62/1454/2026 (21 September 2026); incident dates not stated in the cited passages. Interviews were conducted January-April 2026. Province: Rubaya is in North Kivu (Masisi); Lomera is in Kabare, South Kivu.
r1-SV-2026-028.vn: The two mine names rest on the report's scope passage (page, not the stored excerpt): extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt. Date range 2026-01/2026-09 was not supported. The cited passages give no dates for the killings; the date shown is the report's publication date. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: letter of 11 August 2026; no response; Rubaya and Lomera mines 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-012: Read the report: attribution ('M23 or their collaborators') holds, and dated cases in the section fall inside the window (one death in February 2025; seven deaths January-March 2026). Added the right-of-reply passage so M23's silence is recorded rather than omitted.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): letter of 11 August 2026; no response; Rubaya and Lomera mines
src: Amnesty International documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners by M23 or their collaborators, at least nine of whom were beaten brutally and died at health centres or before they reached the hospital.
Of the 26 people interviewed by Amnesty International, 16 were miners or civilians who lived near mining areas who said that M23 or its mine security guards had tortured or illtreated them.

Amnesty International wrote to the M23 spokesperson and an M23 mining representative on 11 August 2026. The organization shared its findings and requested information about the conduct of M23 fighters and its representatives who administer the Rubaya and Lomera mines in relation to specific allegations documented in this briefing. At the time of publication, the organization had not received any response from M23 representatives.

r1-SV-2026-029.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23, in a clarification dated 22 September signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, "formally and in their entirety" rejected the accusations in Amnesty International's report on abuses at mining sites in areas under its control, calling them "not established and insufficiently substantiated".
r1-SV-2026-029.n: Partisan statement relayed by a Goma outlet; answers the 21 September 2026 Amnesty report.
r1-SV-2026-029.vn: Page read in full from the retained capture. Party statement; recorded only as what AFC-M23 said.
src: Dans une « mise au point » datée du 22 septembre, l’AFC-M23 « rejette formellement et dans leur ensemble » les accusations formulées dans le rapport d’Amnesty International, qu’elle juge « non établies et insuffisamment étayées ».
écrit le mouvement dans une mise au point signée par Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur Adjoint de l’AFC-M23.

r1-SV-2026-030.s: Radio Okapi reported that UN independent experts, in a communiqué published on 21 July in Geneva, denounced serious and systematic violations against civilians; according to Radio Okapi, the experts said AFC/M23 had reportedly set up a system of control based on fear in the areas it administers, and the communiqué reported arbitrary arrests and detentions, acts of torture including sexual violence, and cases of forced labour and forced recruitment of civilians.
r1-SV-2026-030.l: AFC/M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
r1-SV-2026-030.n: Relayed by Radio Okapi; the OHCHR press release (ohchr.org, 21 July 2026) could not be retrieved by the page tool, so it is not cited. Conditional "aurait" in the outlet's wording.
r1-SV-2026-030.vn: Attributed to Radio Okapi reporting the experts' statement; 'had set up' put back to the conditional. The OHCHR release itself could not be retrieved; this rests on Radio Okapi's account of it. The outlet's conditional (aurait) is kept.
src: Selon les experts onusiens, l’AFC/M23 aurait mis en place un véritable système de contrôle fondé sur la peur dans les zones qu’il administre. Le communiqué fait état d’arrestations et de détentions arbitraires, d’actes de torture, y compris de violences sexuelles, ainsi que de cas de travail forcé et de recrutement forcé de civils.

Dans un communiqué publié le 21 juillet à Genève, en Suisse, ces experts dénoncent des violations graves et systématiques commises contre les populations civiles. Ils appellent à une relance urgente du cessez-le-feu et exhortent toutes les parties impliquées dans le conflit à respecter leurs obligations en matière de protection des civils.

r1-SV-2026-031.s: Human Rights Watch reported, based on interviews with 102 former detainees and dozens of other sources, that the M23 detained thousands of captured fighters and civilians, some as young as 12, and that the M23's apparent aim of taking security measures to locate soldiers, militiamen and officials opposed to it gradually turned into a vast, systematic campaign of mass arrests and incommunicado detention targeting civilians with real or perceived links to the army, in particular young men and adolescents.
r1-SV-2026-031.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; Goma; Bukavu
r1-SV-2026-031.a: M23 and Rwandan forces, per HRW
r1-SV-2026-031.x: HRW: 102 former detainees interviewed; thousands of fighters and civilians detained, some as young as 12.
r1-SV-2026-031.n: NGO report of 10 June 2026 (87 pages) on events from January 2025; sexual violence is not a focus in the cited passages. Report not previously cited in the period packet. Second excerpt may exceed word limit; trim if flagged.
r1-SV-2026-031.vn: 'began with soldiers and police in Goma and Bukavu' is not what the excerpt says; rewritten to the excerpts. Category changed from forced_recruitment to detention_abduction, which the cited passages describe. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: HRW French report (10 Jun 2026) supports both clauses. In the stored excerpt 'Celui-ci' refers back to the M23's 'objectif manifeste' of taking security measures, a sentence the excerpt leaves out; it is added and the wording is aligned to it. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: HRW French report (10 Jun 2026) supports both clauses. In the stored excerpt 'Celui-ci' refers back to the M23's 'objectif manifeste' of taking security measures, a sentence the excerpt leaves out; it is added and the wording is aligned to it.
src: Celui-ci s’est progressivement transformé en une vaste campagne systématique d’arrestations massives et de détentions au secret ciblant les civils ayant des liens réels ou supposés avec l’armée, en particulier les jeunes hommes et les adolescents.

Ce rapport, basé sur des entretiens avec 102 anciens détenus et des dizaines d’autres sources, documente la détention par le M23 de milliers de combattants capturés et de civils, dont certains âgés d’à peine 12 ans

L’objectif manifeste du M23 était de prendre des mesures de sécurité pour localiser les soldats, les miliciens et les fonctionnaires opposés au M23 et à l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC), la coalition politico-militaire dont fait partie le M23.

r1-SV-2026-032.s: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to several witnesses, M23 captain Gaston executed a certain colonel Amurabi at Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a defence lawyer in the military justice system in Goma according to a former detainee and Congolese judicial and military intelligence sources.
r1-SV-2026-032.a: M23 commander "capitaine Gaston" (nicknamed Longangi), per HRW
r1-SV-2026-032.n: Event dated 2025 (before the unit period); included because the report was published in 2026 and names a victim and a commander. The excerpt spans HRW footnote markers. Names as HRW prints them.

src: D’après plusieurs témoins, le capitaine Gaston a exécuté un certain colonel Amurabi à Rumangabo aux alentours de juin 2025. [98] Le colonel Amurabi était un défenseur judiciaire dans le système de justice militaire à Goma, selon un ancien détenu ainsi que des sources judiciaires et du renseignement militaire congolais.

r1-SV-2026-033.s: BCNUDH reported that of the 2 607 violations and abuses documented in the first half of 2026, 78 per cent (2,068) were committed by armed groups, 20 per cent (536) by State agents and 25 by foreign armed forces, and that AFC/M23 remained the main perpetrator among armed groups, followed by the Wazalendo groups.

r1-SV-2026-033.x: BCNUDH H1 2026: 2 607 violations; armed groups 2,068 (78%); State agents 536 (20%); foreign armed forces 25 (1%); AFC/M23 995; Wazalendo 476
r1-SV-2026-033.n: The report gives a province split (North Kivu 1,655 = 63%, South Kivu 544 = 21%, Ituri 376, Maniema 32) and ADF 230, FARDC 392, not cited in an excerpt. Context claim.
r1-SV-2026-033.vn: Matches the report. Context claim; not Kivu-only.
src: Sur les 2 607 violations et abus documentés au cours du semestre, 78 pour cent (2 068) des violations et abus ont été commis par les groupes armés, tandis que 20 pour cent, soit 536 des violations documentées ont été commises par les agents de l’Etat et 25 violations soit 1 pour cent commises par les forces armées étrangères.
Parmi les groupes armés, l’AFC/M23 demeure le principal auteur des avec 995 violations, suivie des groupes Wazalendo (476 atteintes)

r1-SV-NK-2025-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the NGO "Rien sans les femmes" raised the alarm over rising rape cases against women and girls in Lubero-centre, Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that more than 250 rape cases had been documented in local hospitals since the start of 2025, according to Bernadette Kurabe, the organisation's focal point. Radio Okapi's report gave 253 cases between January and April 2025; the source does not attribute the cases to a perpetrator.
r1-SV-NK-2025-001.x: Rien sans les femmes (per Radio Okapi): more than 250 rape cases documented in local hospitals since start of 2025; 253 cases recorded between January and April 2025; the source says the figure covers only victims who went to hospitals and is probably below reality
r1-SV-NK-2025-001.n: Single local NGO figure relayed by Radio Okapi; hospital-based count, not a UN-verified figure. Date range: start of 2025 to publication date, since the page states no other period.
r1-SV-NK-2025-001.vn: All excerpts on retained page; single local NGO via Radio Okapi; no perpetrator named. excerpt_en flag is only capitalisation of translated names (Radio Okapi/North Kivu); translation matches the excerpt.
src: L’ONG « Rien sans les femmes » tire la sonnette d’alarme face à la montée des cas de viols sur des femmes et des jeunes filles à Lubero-centre, dans le territoire de Lubero, province du Nord-Kivu.
Depuis le début de l’année 2025, plus de 250 cas de viol ont été documentés dans des hôpitaux locaux, selon Bernadette Kurabe, point focal de cette organisation.
Selon Bernadette Kurabe, 253 cas de viol ont été recensés entre janvier et avril 2025.

r1-SV-NK-2025-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that a local human rights NGO based in Walikale-centre said at least about thirty cases of sexual violence were recorded among displaced people in the villages of Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana between 17 and 23 March, and that in Makana two young girls who allegedly resisted attempted rape were shot dead at point-blank range by their armed attackers. Radio Okapi said the displaced had fled Walikale-centre since its occupation by rebel forces on 17 March. According to the head of the NGO, rape victims were referred to the health centres of Ndjingala and Bisie, which are struggling to meet needs for lack of medicines and because of the massive influx of displaced people.
r1-SV-NK-2025-002.l: Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu and Makana villages (Walikale-Kisangani axis), Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-002.a: armed men (not further identified by the source); source refers to "forces rebelles" occupying Walikale-centre on 17 March
r1-SV-NK-2025-002.x: Local NGO (per Radio Okapi): at least about thirty cases of sexual violence, 17-23 March; two girls killed
r1-SV-NK-2025-002.n: Single local NGO (unnamed in the article), relayed by Radio Okapi. Village spelled "Njingala" in one sentence and "Ndjingala" in another by the source. Perpetrators not identified; the article ties the displacement to rebel occupation of Walikale-centre on 17 March but does not attribute the rapes to a named group. Includes health-centre strain (shortage of medicines) as context.
r1-SV-NK-2025-002.vn: Page attributes the health-centre strain to the NGO head ('selon le responsable de l’ONG'), not to Radio Okapi; attribution corrected. Excerpt_en flags are capitalisation only. The NGO is not named; the source spells the village both Njingala and Ndjingala. The source does not attribute the rapes to a named group.
src: Une ONG locale de défense des droits de l’Homme, basée à Walikale-centre, rapporte des cas de viols et autres incidents sécuritaires ayant entraîné des pertes humaines.

Selon cette organisation, au moins une trentaine de cas de violences sexuelles ont été enregistrés parmi les déplacés dans les villages de Njingala, Mafombi, Mubi, Logu et Makana entre le 17 et le 23 mars.
Dans le village de Makana, deux jeunes filles qui auraient résisté à des tentatives de viol ont été tuées à bout portant par leurs agresseurs armés.
Ces habitants ont quitté Walikale-centre depuis l’occupation de ce chef-lieu par des forces rebelles le 17 mars dernier.
Les victimes de viol ont été orientées vers les centres de santé de Ndjingala et Bisie, qui peinent à répondre aux besoins en raison du manque de médicaments et de l’afflux massif de déplacés

r1-SV-NK-2025-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting between AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC took place in the Bwito (Rutshuru territory) and Bahunde (Masisi territory) chiefdoms of North Kivu between 28 September and 8 October 2025, and that, according to civil society, the fighting caused at least 4 deaths, 13 disappearances and the rape of 8 women.
r1-SV-NK-2025-003.l: Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru) and Bahunde chiefdom (Masisi), North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-003.a: AFC-M23 and FARDC (fighting parties); the source does not attribute the rapes to a party
r1-SV-NK-2025-003.x: Civil society (per Radio Okapi): at least 4 killed, 13 missing, 8 women raped
r1-SV-NK-2025-003.n: Civil-society tally relayed by Radio Okapi; perpetrator of the rapes not stated. The same article mentions the looting of Muliki health centre (see separate health claim) and says civil society criticised reprisals attributed to M23.
r1-SV-NK-2025-003.vn: Both passages on retained page; rapes not attributed to a party. Excerpt_en flag is capitalisation only.
src: Des combats violents ont opposé les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) dans les chefferies de Bwito et Bahunde, situées respectivement dans les territoires de Rutshuru et Masisi au Nord-Kivu entre le 28 septembre et le 8 octobre 2025.
Selon la société civile, ce conflit a provoqué la mort d’au moins 4 personnes et la disparition de 13 autres, ainsi que le viol de 8 femmes.

r1-SV-NK-2025-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that the fighting between AFC-M23 and the FARDC in the Bwito and Bahunde chiefdoms between 28 September and 8 October 2025 also caused heavy material damage: several dozen houses were burned, including the Nyabiteja primary school in the Kihondo grouping, and the health centre of Muliki was also looted, along with the theft of about twenty cattle. The source does not say who looted the health centre.
r1-SV-NK-2025-004.l: Muliki health centre, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-004.n: Same civil-society source as the sexual violence claim for the period; no perpetrator named for the looting. Whether Muliki is in Bwito or Bahunde is not stated; the source names Muliki without a chiefdom, so location is given at the level of the fighting zone only (reviewer: check). Supplies looted is the closest fit of the health tag (centre looted).
r1-SV-NK-2025-004.vn: The draft said 'citing civil society' for the looting; the page narrates the damage itself ('Ces affrontements ont aussi causé...'), so attribution narrowed. Territory set to both since Muliki's chiefdom is not stated. Source 0 retained as context. Muliki's chiefdom is not stated by the source; the damage is narrated by Radio Okapi in a civil-society report, but the looting is not explicitly attributed to civil society or to any party.
src: Selon la société civile, ce conflit a provoqué la mort d’au moins 4 personnes et la disparition de 13 autres, ainsi que le viol de 8 femmes.

Des combats violents ont opposé les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) dans les chefferies de Bwito et Bahunde, situées respectivement dans les territoires de Rutshuru et Masisi au Nord-Kivu entre le 28 septembre et le 8 octobre 2025.
plusieurs dizaines de maisons ont été incendiées, dont l’école primaire de Nyabiteja dans le groupement Kihondo.
Le centre de santé de Muliki a également été pillé, avec en prime le vol d’une vingtaine de bovins.

r1-SV-NK-2025-006.s: CSDF, a Congolese women's health and rights organisation, said that June 2025 marked a notable deterioration in the security and human rights situation in Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories; that, according to protection monitoring data covering 22 health zones, 842 violations were documented; that serious incidents rose by more than 35 per cent compared with May, with Masisi alone accounting for 50 per cent of the cases, followed by Nyiragongo (21 per cent) and Rutshuru (12 per cent); and that June 2025 was the annual peak of gender-based violence, with 247 documented cases (17 per cent of all violations of the month), of which 93 per cent were rapes.
r1-SV-NK-2025-006.l: Masisi, Nyiragongo and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-006.a: not attributed by the source (the source cites fighting between M23 and Wazalendo groups as context)
r1-SV-NK-2025-006.x: CSDF-RDC: 842 violations documented in June 2025 (22 health zones); 247 GBV cases (17 per cent of violations), 93 per cent rapes; Masisi 50 per cent of the cases, Nyiragongo 21 per cent, Rutshuru 12 per cent
r1-SV-NK-2025-006.n: Local NGO monitoring (protection-cluster style data); no perpetrator breakdown given. The 22 health zones are not named by the source. The 50/21/12 per cent split is of the month's violations/cases generally (the source says "des cas"), not of GBV cases only.
r1-SV-NK-2025-006.vn: The page does not print the expansion 'Centre de Santé et Développement de la Femme' (removed) and does not say the monitoring is CSDF's own ('Selon les données du monitoring de protection'), so narrowed. Removed 'mainly women and adolescent girls in displacement and return areas' wording compression; kept figures. Single local organisation: grade C, not B. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: serious incidents up more than 35% on May 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-005: Figure-scope problem found on the retained page: the '50 % des cas' for Masisi follows a sentence on a more than 35% rise in serious incidents compared with May, not the 842 violations; the statement attaches the shares to the 842 violations. Also the page says the 842 violations affected more than 1,100 returnees (64% of identified victims). No perpetrator named, which the statement respects.; excerpt-support: added the sentence on the more than 35% rise in serious incidents compared with May as an excerpt
src: Le mois de juin 2025 a marqué une détérioration notable de la situation sécuritaire et de la protection des droits humains dans les territoires de Masisi, Nyiragongo et Rutshuru
Selon les données du monitoring de protection couvrant 22 zones de santé, 842 violations ont été documentées
avec Masisi représentant à lui seul 50 % des cas, suivi de Nyiragongo (21 %) et Rutshuru (12 %)

Le mois de juin 2025 a été le pic annuel des violences basées sur le genre (VBG), avec 247 cas documentés, soit 17 % de l’ensemble des violations du mois. Fait particulièrement alarmant, 93 % de ces cas sont des viols
Par rapport au mois de mai, où les violations restaient concentrées dans certains foyers de tensions, le mois de juin a enregistré une augmentation de plus de 35 % des incidents graves

r1-SV-NK-2025-007.s: UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that nearly 500 cases of sexual violence were reported within a single week in the Goma area, including more than 150 involving children, and that this number likely represents only a fraction of the actual survivors, namely those who managed to reach care.
r1-SV-NK-2025-007.x: UNFPA: nearly 500 reported cases in a single week in the Goma area, more than 150 involving children
r1-SV-NK-2025-007.n: Mediacongo (2025-02-23, relaying the UNFPA statement) dates the UNFPA declaration 17 February; the week itself is not dated in the UNFPA text. Existing drafts hold UNHCR's 895 cases figure for the first half of February; this is a separate UN figure.
r1-SV-NK-2025-007.vn: Verbatim on retained UNFPA page dated 21 February 2025; the week is not dated. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Nearly 500 reported cases of sexual violence were reported within a single week in the Goma area, including more than 150 involving children. This number likely represents only a fraction of the actual survivors, those who managed to reach care
Près de 500 cas de violence sexuelle ont été signalés en une semaine dans la région de Goma, dont plus de 150 impliquant des enfants.

r1-SV-NK-2025-008.s: UNFPA said in a statement in February 2025 that its eight UNFPA-supported mobile clinics, safe spaces and listening centers were only partially functional, that the other facilities providing treatment and counselling to survivors in displacement camps had been looted, that medical supplies and equipment worth millions of dollars had been looted from storage facilities in Goma, and that Goma, with more than 2 million inhabitants, had only three functioning hospitals able to provide clinical care to survivors of sexual assault.
r1-SV-NK-2025-008.l: Goma and displacement camps around Goma, North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-008.x: UNFPA: eight supported facilities partially functional; three functioning hospitals able to treat survivors in Goma (population over 2 million); looted supplies worth "millions of dollars"
r1-SV-NK-2025-008.n: UNFPA does not name who looted the facilities or supplies. The same statement says movement restrictions imposed by "the de facto authorities in control of Goma" hampered aid delivery (not recorded here as a separate claim).
r1-SV-NK-2025-008.vn: All three passages verbatim on retained page; no looter named.
src: The eight UNFPA-supported mobile clinics, safe spaces, and listening centers are only partially functional, while the rest of the facilities that provide medical treatment and counseling to survivors in displacement camps have been looted.
Medical supplies and equipment worth millions of dollars have also been looted from storage facilities in Goma

In Goma, with more than 2 million inhabitants, there are only three functioning hospitals able to provide clinical care to survivors of sexual assault and a handful of community-level health clinics that can provide basic emergency care.

r1-SV-NK-2025-009.s: MSF said that between January and April 2025 more than 7,400 victims and survivors of sexual violence received treatment at Ministry of Health facilities supported by MSF in Goma, and that an additional 2,400 were treated in Saké during the same period.
r1-SV-NK-2025-009.l: Goma and Saké (Masisi territory), North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-009.x: MSF: more than 7,400 treated in Goma, 2,400 in Saké, January-April 2025
r1-SV-NK-2025-009.n: Health-facility data. Existing drafts hold MSF's UN Security Council briefing (about 28,000 in the first six months of 2025); this is the Goma/Saké breakdown. The MSF text places Saké "west of the city" of Goma; the territory (Masisi) is the reviewer's geographic knowledge, not stated in the excerpt.
r1-SV-NK-2025-009.vn: Verbatim on retained page; the page's context is 2025 (M23/AFC takeover of Goma). MSF places Saké 'west of the city'; Masisi territory is not stated by the source.
src: Between January and April, more than 7,400 victims and survivors of sexual violence received treatment at Ministry of Health facilities supported by MSF in Goma. West of the city, in Saké, an additional 2,400 victims and survivors were treated during the same period.

r1-SV-NK-2025-010.s: MSF said that in February 2025 the M23/AFC armed group ordered the dismantling of displacement camps, effectively forcing their residents to leave, and quoted a patient it called Nasha (MSF says patients' names have been changed), who said that after the Rusayo displaced persons camp was destroyed she moved to the courtyard of a school, where armed men broke in one evening at 10:30 pm, attacked her and shot her husband dead when he tried to protect her.
r1-SV-NK-2025-010.l: Goma area (Rusayo displaced persons camp and a school courtyard), North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-010.a: M23/AFC (camp dismantling, as MSF states); "armed men" (attack on Nasha, not further identified)
r1-SV-NK-2025-010.n: The date of the attack on "Nasha" is not stated (she visited MSF in May); the asterisk indicates a changed name, so she is not listed in victims_named. The article places this in a section on sexual violence but the quoted words say "They attacked me" without specifying rape, so the claim is filed under displacement/attack context. Which camps were dismantled is not stated beyond Rusayo in the quote; the MSF text describes "a displaced persons camp alongside some 650,000 others on the edge of Goma" (not used here).
r1-SV-NK-2025-010.vn: Pseudonym made explicit with the page's own footnote; Nasha listed in victims_named as a pseudonym per policy v1. Date of the attack on Nasha is not stated (she visited MSF in May). The armed men are not identified.
src: But in February 2025, the M23/AFC armed group ordered the dismantling of camps, effectively forcing their residents to leave.

“I lived in the Rusayo displaced persons camp,” says Nasha. “After it was destroyed, we moved to the courtyard of a school where we built a shelter.” “Armed men broke in one evening at 10:30 pm,” she continues. “They attacked me. When my husband tried to protect me, they shot him dead.”

r1-SV-NK-2025-011.s: The BBC reported that a 22-year-old woman, Pascaline, said she was raped by two men at Munzenze prison in Goma in the early hours of 27 January, and that her attackers came over the wall from the men's block right next door called "Safina"; a second woman, Nadine, 22, said she was also raped by two men. The BBC said it could not verify how many women were raped that night, out of a total of 167 who, sources say, were being held, and reported that 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.
r1-SV-NK-2025-011.a: attackers from the adjoining men's block, per the survivors quoted
r1-SV-NK-2025-011.x: BBC: 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death according to two sources; BBC cannot verify how many of the 167 women held were raped
r1-SV-NK-2025-011.n: First-person testimony to the BBC in Goma; Pascaline is quoted as willing to be identified. Existing drafts (SV-2025#0-3) hold the BBC/UN figures of 165-167 women assaulted; this claim adds survivor testimony and names. "Nadine" is printed without a surname. Nadine's age (22) is in the preceding sentence of the article ("Nadine, 22, has also come back to the prison").
r1-SV-NK-2025-011.vn: Supported on retained page; Nadine's age placed with a replacement quote; 'two sources' attribution kept with the figure; detainee status added to victims_named. The BBC says Pascaline is willing to be identified; it does not say whether Nadine is a real name. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 5 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: "He told me that if I tried to escape, he would kill me." Pascaline, 22, recalls the words of her rapist at a prison in Goma, the largest city in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, in the early hours of 27 January.

He was the second man to rape her at Munzenze prison. The first attack was so violent that she passed out. Her attackers came over the wall from the men's block right next door called "Safina", she says.
Nadine says she was also raped by two men. "They came with alcohol," she tells the BBC. "They wanted to drug people. They took me by force. They took all the women here."
A total of 132 female prisoners and at least 25 children burned to death, according to two sources.
The BBC cannot verify how many women were raped that night, out of a total of 167 who, sources say, were being held.

Les acteurs judiciaires ont confirmé qu’au moins 164 femmes ont été violées par des détenus de sexe masculin lors de l'évasion. Au moins 150 femmes ont également péri dans un incendie au cours de cette évasion.
“DRC officials report that at least 165 women were raped by male inmates during the mass prison break,” the United Nations said in a report four days later.

r1-SV-NK-2025-012.s: The BBC reported that a survivor who does not want to be identified, whom the BBC calls Florence (a name the BBC gave her), said that in this case the attackers at Munzenze prison were fellow inmates, who were not armed or in uniform; the BBC noted that the fire and the rapes are "shrouded in confusion, with all sides eager to blame someone else".
r1-SV-NK-2025-012.n: "Florence" is a name the BBC assigns ("We are calling her Florence") to a survivor who asked not to be identified. The sentence before the excerpt in the article records that human rights groups say rape is widely used as a weapon of war by M23 and government forces; the BBC treats the prison case as unclear.
r1-SV-NK-2025-012.vn: Pseudonym made explicit with the BBC's own words (replacement quote); age left out because no stored excerpt prints it. Florence also told the BBC that soldiers and police surrounding the prison fired bullets and tear gas into the women's section instead of putting out the fire (not part of this claim).
src: The fire and the rapes are shrouded in confusion, with all sides eager to blame someone else.

However, in this case, Florence says it was fellow inmates. "You could see they were prisoners. Some came without shoes. When they climbed onto the roof of the women's prison, they were calling the names of those they knew. And none of the attackers were armed or in uniform.

r1-SV-NK-2025-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its report on the main trends of human rights violations in the DRC for the month of January, recorded in North Kivu eight victims of conflict-related sexual violence, of whom three were attributed to M23 members, three to the FDLR and two to the FARDC.

r1-SV-NK-2025-013.x: BCNUDH (per Actualite.cd): North Kivu, eight victims of conflict-related sexual violence in January (three attributed to M23 members, three to the FDLR, two to the FARDC)

The page headline attributes most cases nationally to CODECO (Ituri). The excerpt does not give the year of the report; the page is dated 2025-03-22 and the article says January "dernier".

province du Nord-Kivu avec huit victimes (trois attribuées aux membres du M23, trois aux FDLR et deux aux FARDC)

r1-SV-NK-2025-014.s: Human Rights Watch reported, from a survivor account, that in February, after the M23 took control of Goma, four M23 fighters forced their way into the house of a 22-year-old woman called Patience (a pseudonym, per HRW), tied her to her bed and two of them raped her; HRW said the fighters then forced her out of the house and took her to a nearby camp, where for three days multiple fighters raped her and three other women who had been taken there.
r1-SV-NK-2025-014.l: Goma and a nearby camp, North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-014.x: HRW: two fighters raped the woman at home; multiple fighters raped her and three other women over three days in the camp
r1-SV-NK-2025-014.n: Page dated 2026-01-12 (the dateline text reads "January 12, 2025", apparently a typo). Survivor testimony gathered by HRW with SOFEPADI. Pseudonym, not a real name.
r1-SV-NK-2025-014.vn: All passages verbatim on retained HRW page; pseudonym marked.
src: In February, after the M23 took control of Goma, North Kivu’s provincial capital, four M23 fighters forced their way into 22-year-old Patience’s house, where she lived with her infant son. The fighters demanded to know if her husband was there, struck her son with a gun, tied her to her bed, and then two fighters raped her.
They then forced her out of the house, leaving her son behind, and took her to a nearby camp.
She spent three days in the camp, during which time multiple fighters raped her and three other women who had been taken there.
For their privacy and security, the names of sexual violence survivors are pseudonyms.

r1-SV-NK-2025-015.s: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 fighters abducted a woman it called Justine (a pseudonym, per HRW) from her home in Goma in March 2025 during an apparent forced recruitment operation, beat her and her 20-year-old son and forced her to walk to their camp near the city, where two men took her to a secluded area, beat her and raped her; HRW said she arrived at the hospital within 72 hours but the hospital had no PEP kits.
r1-SV-NK-2025-015.l: Goma and an M23 camp near the city, North Kivu
r1-SV-NK-2025-015.n: Survivor testimony via HRW; pseudonym. HRW adds that she later fled to Uganda and tested HIV positive (not used in the statement).
r1-SV-NK-2025-015.vn: All passages verbatim on retained HRW page; pseudonym marked. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: M23 fighters abducted Justine from her home in Goma in March 2025. Six armed men broke into her house during an apparent forced recruitment operation and demanded to see her husband. After Justine told them that her husband was not home, they beat her and her 20-year-old son and then forced her to walk to their camp near the city.
There, two men took her to a secluded area, beat her and raped her.
Justine arrived at the hospital within 72 hours, but the hospital had no PEP kits.
For their privacy and security, the names of sexual violence survivors are pseudonyms.

The gang rapes by M23 fighters took place between March and May 2025 when the fighters controlled Goma and Bukavu in eastern DRC. Five survivors said M23 fighters raped them at M23 military positions.

r1-SV-NK-2025-016.s: Human Rights Watch reported that, according to UNFPA, in May 2025 only 7 of 34 health zones in North Kivu had a minimal supply of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits, and that by September only 895 complete kits were available for the entire province, where hundreds of cases occur each week; HRW also said IMA World Health had ordered 116,000 kits in early 2025 but the funding was withdrawn so the kits never made it to health centres in eastern Congo.
r1-SV-NK-2025-016.a: not applicable (funding withdrawal and supply shortage; not an attack by a party)
r1-SV-NK-2025-016.x: HRW citing UNFPA: 7 of 34 North Kivu health zones with minimal PEP supply in May 2025; 895 complete kits for the whole province in September 2025; HRW: 116,000 kits ordered by IMA World Health in early 2025, never delivered
r1-SV-NK-2025-016.n: A supply shortage context, not an attack on a facility; the "supplies_looted" tag is the nearest fit in the allowed list and should be reviewed (closer to epidemic/supply context). HRW is relaying UNFPA.
r1-SV-NK-2025-016.vn: Verbatim on retained page. The health tag 'supplies_looted' does not fit (nothing was looted); editor should retag (no 'supply shortage' value in the list; closest is facility/access context). A supply shortage after funding withdrawal, not an attack on facilities.
src: According to UNFPA, in May 2025 only 7 of 34 health zones in North Kivu had a minimal supply. By September, only 895 complete kits were available for the entire province, where hundreds of cases occur each week.
IMA World Health had ordered 116,000 kits in early 2025, but then the funding was withdrawn so these kits never made it to health centers in eastern Congo.

r1-SV-SK-2025-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing humanitarian sources, that five young girls of the same family were raped by armed men in the locality of Kalungu, 15 km south of Minova in Buzi grouping, and were treated at a local hospital centre.
r1-SV-SK-2025-001.l: Kalungu, Buzi grouping, Kalehe territory (South of Minova), South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-001.a: armed men (not further identified by the source)
r1-SV-SK-2025-001.x: Actualite.cd: five young girls of one family (Kalungu)
r1-SV-SK-2025-001.n: Single outlet, anonymous humanitarian sources. The article's headline places the event in the context of M23/RDF-FARDC clashes in Kalehe but the text does not name the perpetrators' group. Exact date of the Kalungu rapes is not stated (reported 22 Jan 2025).
r1-SV-SK-2025-001.vn: Statement said 'Kalehe territory' as a fact about Kalungu and 'health centre'; the article only places Kalungu relative to Minova/Buzi in an article on Kalehe clashes, and says 'centre hospitalier'. Narrowed. Exact date of the Kalungu rapes not stated (article of 22 January 2025). Perpetrators' group not named. The article is about clashes in Kalehe territory. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Selon des sources humanitaires, cinq jeunes filles d’une même famille ont été violées par des hommes armés dans la localité de Kalungu, située à 15 km au sud de Minova, dans le groupement de Buzi. Elles ont été prises en charge par un centre hospitalier local.

Des sources humanitaires rapportent cinq filles d’une même famille violées par des hommes en armes dans la localité de Kalungu. Elles ont été prises en charge dans le Centre hospitalier de la localité.

r1-SV-SK-2025-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that at Bihovu, in Lowa-Numbi village (Shanje), two women were also victims of rape on 14 January.
r1-SV-SK-2025-002.l: Bihovu, Shanje, Lowa-Numbi village, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-002.n: Single outlet. The excerpt gives no perpetrator.
r1-SV-SK-2025-002.vn: Excerpt matches; excerpt_en is a faithful translation (flag is the capitalised 'At'). Kalehe territory supported by the page: fighting extended to Kalehe 'notamment dans les localités de ... Shanje'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: À Bihovu, une agglomération de Shanje dans le village de Lowa-Numbi, deux femmes ont également été victimes de viols le 14 janvier.
Les mêmes sources rapportent deux femmes violées le 14 janvier dans l’aire de santé de Bihovu, dans le territoire de Kalehe.

r1-SV-SK-2025-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that a court in Bukavu, which it calls the 'tribunal de grande instance' (a civil-party lawyer quoted in the article thanks the Bukavu 'tribunal militaire de garnison'), sentenced to death on Friday 14 February 2025 212 soldiers accused of murder, attempted murder, rape and fleeing the enemy, for acts committed during the M23 advance in localities and villages of Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories.
r1-SV-SK-2025-003.l: Bukavu (verdict); offences in Kalehe, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-003.a: FARDC soldiers (as tried by the Bukavu military court)
r1-SV-SK-2025-003.n: The page says 'tribunal de grande instance' in the first sentence and 'tribunal militaire de garnison' later; the source treats these as the same trial. The article describes it as an accelerated trial held as the M23 took Kavumu airport that day. See also the next claim for the dates and villages of the acts. Conviction is a first-instance military-court verdict as reported by the outlet.
r1-SV-SK-2025-003.vn: Raw statement called it the 'garrison military court' as a fact; the article's own narration says tribunal de grande instance. Both names now attributed. First-instance verdict as reported. The article names the court inconsistently; the headline (latest capture) says 72 acquitted while the text says 'Septante' (70). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le tribunal de grande instance de Bukavu a condamné à mort ce vendredi 14 février 2025, 212 militaires accusés de meurtres, tentatives de meurtres, viols et fuite devant l'ennemi. Ces faits ont été commis lors de l’avancée des rebelles du M23 dans plusieurs localités et villages des territoires de Kalehe, Kabare et de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu.

Le 14 février dernier, 212 autres militaires des FARDC avaient également été condamnés à la peine capitale pour des crimes graves, dont des meurtres, viols et tentatives de meurtre, commis à Bukavu, dans le Sud-Kivu.

Le tribunal de grande instance de Bukavu vient de rendre un verdict d’ampleur sans précédent : 212 militaires ont été condamnés à la peine capitale pour une série de crimes effroyables, notamment des meurtres, des viols et des tentatives de meurtre.

r1-SV-SK-2025-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that from 6 to 8 February 2025, acts of vandalism and killings were committed by soldiers deployed in the villages of Katana, Kabamba, Miti and Kasheke as far as Kamanyola.
r1-SV-SK-2025-004.l: Katana, Kabamba, Miti, Kasheke to Kamanyola, Kabare and Walungu territories, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-004.a: soldiers deployed in those villages (FARDC soldiers per the context of the trial)
r1-SV-SK-2025-004.x: not given for the 6-8 February acts
r1-SV-SK-2025-004.n: The excerpt says 'militaires' without naming the force; the paragraph is part of an article about FARDC soldiers tried at Bukavu. Casualty numbers not given.
r1-SV-SK-2025-004.vn: Excerpt matches; force not named in the sentence, actor field already hedged. Territory widened: Kamanyola is not Kabare; source gives villages only.
src: Du 6 au 8 février 2025, des actes de vandalisme et meurtres ont été commis par des militaires déployés dans les villages de Katana, Kabamba, Miti, Kasheke jusqu'à Kamanyola.

r1-SV-SK-2025-005.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that civil-society organisations reported more than 1 000 victims of sexual violence in South Kivu between January and June, mainly women and adolescent girls, while official sources reported 127 cases of sexual violence in South Kivu in the first two weeks of February alone.
r1-SV-SK-2025-005.x: Civil-society organisations (cited by the UN mission): more than 1,000 victims, January-June 2025; official sources (cited by the UN mission): 127 cases, first two weeks of February 2025
r1-SV-SK-2025-005.n: French text of the UN fact-finding mission report A/HRC/60/80; the English advance version is already cited by existing claims (SV-2025#6-12) but not for these figures. The footnote numbers 47 and 48 are part of the page text. The report does not give the underlying organisations; footnotes 47-48 are not reproduced here.
r1-SV-SK-2025-005.vn: Text matches; figure '1000' flag is the formatting '1 000'. Graded B, not A: the mission relays unverified third-party figures. The mission relays these figures from civil-society and official sources; it does not present them as its own findings.
src: Des organisations de la société civile ont fait état de plus de 1 000 victimes de violences sexuelles entre janvier et juin dans le Sud-Kivu, principalement des femmes et des adolescentes 47, tandis que des sources officielles ont fait état de 127 cas de violences sexuelles au Sud-Kivu au cours des deux premières semaines de février seulement48.

r1-SV-SK-2025-006.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that in South Kivu a man was stripped completely naked, beaten until he lost consciousness, and raped by several members of the FARDC and Wazalendo who were going from house to house looting.
r1-SV-SK-2025-006.n: Sexual violence against a man; no locality or exact date in the text. The surrounding paragraph concerns the retreat of FARDC and Wazalendo from the front lines in January and February 2025 (the preceding sentence of the report).
r1-SV-SK-2025-006.vn: Para 56 of A/HRC/60/80; date range from para 55 context (retreat in January-February 2025), kept as range.
src: Au Sud-Kivu, un homme a été entièrement déshabillé, roué de coups jusqu’à ce qu’il perde connaissance, et violé par plusieurs membres des FARDC et des Wazalendo qui passaient de maison en maison pour piller.

r1-SV-SK-2025-007.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that, according to the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), 199 people convicted of sexual and gender-based crimes escaped from the prisons of Goma, Bukavu and Kabare.
r1-SV-SK-2025-007.l: Goma, Bukavu and Kabare prisons (North and South Kivu)
r1-SV-SK-2025-007.x: BCNUDH via the UN mission: 199 people convicted of sexual and gender-based crimes escaped from the prisons of Goma, Bukavu and Kabare
r1-SV-SK-2025-007.n: Figure covers three prisons, including Goma (North Kivu), so it is not South Kivu only.
r1-SV-SK-2025-007.vn: Para 70 matches. Territory field said Bukavu only; the figure covers three prisons incl. Goma. The report does not date these escapes in this sentence; the range follows the Goma (January) and Bukavu/Kabare (14 February) escapes described elsewhere in the report.
src: Selon le Bureau conjoint des Nations Unies pour les droits de l’homme en République démocratique du Congo (BCNUDH), 199 personnes reconnues coupables de crimes sexuels et fondés sur le genre se sont évadées des prisons de Goma, Bukavu et Kabare

r1-SV-SK-2025-008.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 14 February two further prison escapes, in Bukavu and in Kabare, allowed detainees to flee, some of them convicted of crimes under international law; a footnote cites BCNUDH figures of 2 285 detainees escaping from Bukavu central prison and 221 from Kabare prison.
r1-SV-SK-2025-008.l: Bukavu central prison and Kabare prison, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-008.x: BCNUDH via the UN mission (footnote): 2 285 detainees escaped from Bukavu central prison; 221 from Kabare prison
r1-SV-SK-2025-008.n: The numbers come from a footnote (18) of the report; the main text gives the date and the categories of escapees.
src: Le 14 février, deux autres évasions de prisons, à Bukavu et à Kabare, ont permis la fuite de détenus, dont certains condamnés pour des crimes relevant du droit international

Selon le Bureau conjoint des Nations Unies pour les droits de l’homme en République démocratique du Congo (BCNUDH), 2 285 et 221 détenus, respectivement, se sont évadés de la prison centrale de Bukavu et de la prison de Kabare.

r1-SV-SK-2025-009.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that from 15 to 17 February 2025 soldiers of the FARDC units Guépard and Satan II summarily executed at least 20 civilians in Kamanyola after hundreds of their soldiers died in clashes with the Wazalendo; it said most victims were men and adolescents suspected of being Wazalendo members or supporters, and that according to credible sources the number of victims would be much higher, although further investigation would be needed to confirm it.
r1-SV-SK-2025-009.a: FARDC units Guépard and Satan II
r1-SV-SK-2025-009.x: UN mission: at least 20 civilians summarily executed; credible sources: number 'much higher', not confirmed
r1-SV-SK-2025-009.n: Territory of Kamanyola entered as Walungu following standard administrative usage; the source says only Kamanyola, South Kivu. The existing claim SV-2025#12 covers the Kamanyola/Uvira clashes of mid-February but not these executions. No FARDC response found (see gaps).
r1-SV-SK-2025-009.vn: Raw statement turned the report's conditional ('serait ... seraient nécessaires') into 'credible sources put the number much higher'; restored the hedge. Territory/location 'Walungu/Uvira border, Ruzizi plain' is the researcher's, not the source's. The higher toll is conditional in the report and unconfirmed.
src: Du 15 au 17 février 2025, des soldats des unités Guépard et Satan II des FARDC ont sommairement exécuté au moins 20 civils à Kamanyola, après que des centaines de leurs soldats sont morts dans des affrontements avec les Wazalendo.

r1-SV-SK-2025-010.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said girls were victims of sexual violence and were used for sexual purposes by commanders and other members of armed groups, and as cooks or messengers; the sentence sits in its section on the recruitment and use of children (which opens on Wazalendo groups), in a paragraph (para. 61) that otherwise describes boys apparently under 18 at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira and carrying weapons in Fizi territory. The sentence itself names no group.
r1-SV-SK-2025-010.l: South Kivu (locality not given in the sentence)
r1-SV-SK-2025-010.a: commanders and other members of armed groups
r1-SV-SK-2025-010.n: The sentence does not name the armed group or place. The surrounding paragraph (para 61) concerns boys seen armed at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira and carrying AK-47s in Fizi territory; that context is not asserted here. Period is the mission's reporting window (January to July 2025).
r1-SV-SK-2025-010.vn: Para 61 matches; context sentence on page. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: section on the recruitment and use of children 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: para. 61: boys at Wazalendo checkpoints, patrolling Uvira, carrying weapons in Fizi 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: Read para. 60-61 on the retained PDF: the context is recruitment of children by Wazalendo groups (Fizi, Uvira), which the claim's vague 'passage on the use of children by armed groups' hides; amended to give the context while keeping the sentence's own 'armed groups' (no attribution to Wazalendo added). No fresh search.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): section on the recruitment and use of children; para. 61: boys at Wazalendo checkpoints, patrolling Uvira, carrying weapons in Fizi
src: Des filles ont été victimes de violences sexuelles et utilisées à des fins sexuelles par des commandants et d’autres membres de groupes armés, et en tant que cuisinières ou messagères.
C. Enrôlement et utilisation d’enfants 60. La mission a reçu des preuves crédibles concernant l’enrôlement et l’utilisation de personnes de moins de 18 ans par les groupes Wazalendo.

61. Selon des témoignages corroborés, des garçons manifestement âgés de moins de 18 ans ont été vus portant des armes à des postes de contrôle des Wazalendo dans le Sud-Kivu, patrouillant à Uvira et portant des fusils AK-47 dans le territoire de Fizi.

r1-SV-SK-2025-011.s: The UN fact-finding mission report said that on 9 March a shell reportedly hit the paediatric ward of Walungu hospital, killing five people, including two children.
r1-SV-SK-2025-011.l: Walungu hospital, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-011.x: UN mission: five killed, including two children
r1-SV-SK-2025-011.n: Attribution differs by source: Radio Okapi (next claim) cites several sources in Walungu saying M23 fired the shell. Walungu centre was held by M23 at the time per Radio Okapi.
r1-SV-SK-2025-011.vn: Para 28 matches; 'reportedly' preserves the conditional. The mission hedges ('aurait touché') and does not attribute the shell.
src: Le 9 mars, un obus aurait touché le service pédiatrique de l’hôpital de Walungu, tuant cinq personnes, dont deux enfants.

r1-SV-SK-2025-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that at least five people hospitalised at the Fonds social du Kivu (FSKI) hospital in Walungu died on Sunday, a day the article prints as '9 janvier' (9 January) although it was published in March, after a shell hit the roof of the paediatric ward; it said several sources in Walungu said the shell was fired by the M23 rebels, who it said were occupying the administrative centre of Walungu territory.
r1-SV-SK-2025-012.l: FSKI hospital, Walungu centre, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-012.a: M23 (according to several sources in Walungu quoted by Radio Okapi)
r1-SV-SK-2025-012.x: Radio Okapi: at least five dead, several others seriously wounded, including patients and carers
r1-SV-SK-2025-012.n: The page prints 'dimanche 9 janvier' but is dated 10 March 2025 and refers to testimony 'ce lundi 10 mars'; the UN mission gives 9 March, so 'janvier' is read as a typographical error (flagged, not corrected in the excerpt). Attribution rests on unnamed local sources; the UN mission does not attribute. No M23 or FARDC statement found.
r1-SV-SK-2025-012.vn: Raw dated the claim 2025-03-09 and silently read 'janvier' as March; a claim may not state a date its excerpt does not print. Discrepancy now in the statement; date set to the month. Date discrepancy: the article prints 'dimanche 9 janvier' but is dated 10 March 2025, cites testimony 'ce lundi 10 mars' and refers to the fright of 'la veille'; the UN mission (A/HRC/60/80, para 28) gives 9 March. 9 March is likely but is not printed by this source. M23 attribution rests on unnamed local sources. Radio Okapi is UN-run (MONUSCO); the UN mission may share its origin.
src: Au moins cinq personnes internées à l’hôpital Fonds social du Kivu (FSKI) à Walungu, dans le Sud-Kivu, ont perdu la vie dimanche 9 janvier, suite à l'explosion d'un obus qui a touché le toit du pavillon de la pédiatrie.
Plusieurs sources à Walungu affirment que l'obus a été tiré par les rebelles du M23, qui occupent actuellement le chef-lieu du territoire de Walungu.

r1-SV-SK-2025-013.s: The Congolese National Human Rights Commission (CNDH-RDC) reported that on 19 April 2025 Pascaline NGWASI, coordinator of the Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés, was arrested, beaten and raped by M23/AFC members in the Mabenga neighbourhood of Bukavu.
r1-SV-SK-2025-013.n: Single source: a Congolese state commission whose report is addressed to national authorities and the UN; treat M23/AFC attribution as the commission's account. M23/AFC position not found. The report prints the survivor's name and a photograph; name listed under policy v1 and censored in the edition.
r1-SV-SK-2025-013.vn: Excerpt matches; name printed. Attribution kept as the CNDH's. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
ent: Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés
src: En date du 19 avril 2025, Mme Pascaline NGWASI, Coordinatrice de « l'Association des Mères Célibataires pour le Bien-être des Enfants Abandonnés », a été arrêtée, frappée et violée par des membres du M23/AFC dans le Quartier MABENGA dans la Ville de Bukavu, Province du Sud-Kivu.

r1-SV-SK-2025-014.s: The CNDH-RDC reported, in a section on violations of the right to health, that on Friday 2 May 2025 five decomposing bodies of Wazalendo members were found who had been abducted on 24 April 2025 by M23/AFC-RDF rebels from the hospital of Mushenyi, where they were being treated for gunshot wounds after the fighting at Nyanfunze, towards Kaziba; it named the five.
r1-SV-SK-2025-014.l: Mushenyi hospital, South Kivu (the CNDH files the case under the heading 'KALEHE'; territory otherwise not stated)
r1-SV-SK-2025-014.x: five bodies found 2 May; abducted 24 April
r1-SV-SK-2025-014.n: Single source (CNDH). The report files the case under 'Cas d'atteinte au droit à la santé à KALEHE' although Mushenyi and Kaziba are in Walungu territory; location is reported as the source prints it. Wounded combatants removed from a hospital: recorded here under health care access, with the victims' status as combatants per the source's own description (Wazalendo).
r1-SV-SK-2025-014.vn: Raw territory 'Walungu' and location '(Walungu territory)' were the researcher's inference against the source's own heading. Territory now says what the source prints, with the discrepancy noted. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. Territory discrepancy: the report files Mushenyi under 'KALEHE'; Mushenyi/Kaziba are generally placed in Walungu territory. Unresolved; check before relying on the location. Victims were combatants receiving medical care, per the source.
src: Vendredi, 02 mai 2025, il avait été découvert 5 corps sans vie en décomposition de membres WAZALENDO, enlevés le 24 avril 2025 à l’hôpital de MUSHENYI par les rebelles du M23/AFC-RDF là où ils suivaient les soins de leurs blessures par balle à l’issu des combats de NYANFUNZE, vers KAZIBA.
Ces WAZALENDO sont identifiés comme suit : - Mwalungwe Manu ; - Kapeshi Claude ; - Innocent Alias Nyoka ; - Namuto Buhende ; - Adrien Hyrondele.

r1-SV-SK-2025-015.s: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 April 2025 AFC/M23 elements perpetrated what it calls a 'massacre' in the village of Kakaba-Bushwege (Mushenyi sector), summarily executing five civilians and wounding several others after, it said, mistaking villagers wearing traditional boots called 'GODIO' for Wazalendo; it named three victims and two young boys of the Chibwana family.
r1-SV-SK-2025-015.l: Kakaba-Bushwege village, Mushenyi sector, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-015.x: CNDH: five civilians summarily executed, several wounded
