r1-SV-SK-2025-015.n: Single source (CNDH). 'Massacre' is the source's word. The two boys of the Chibwana family are not individually named. Territory (Walungu) inferred from Mushenyi sector as in the same report's other entries; the excerpt gives sector only.
r1-SV-SK-2025-015.vn: 'Massacre' put in quotes as the CNDH's word; territory 'Walungu' was inferred, not printed. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. The source gives the sector only; its Mushenyi hospital entry is filed under 'KALEHE'.
src: Le 23 avril 2025, des éléments du groupe armé AFC/M23 ont perpétré un massacre dans le Village de KAKABA-BUSHWEGE, dans le Secteur de MUSHENYI. Les assaillants, confondant certains villageois portant des bottines traditionnelles, communément appelé « GODIO » avec des membres du groupe armé WAZALENDO, ont exécuté sommairement cinq civils et blessé plusieurs autres.
Les victimes identifiées sont : - Bashanga Lugabinja ; - Mitima Kabugi ; - Juvénal Bashomberwa Kabugi ; - Deux jeunes garçons de la famille Chibwana.

r1-SV-SK-2025-016.s: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Monday 30 June 2025 M23 soldiers entered the locality of Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, and killed 6 civilians in reprisal for the alleged presence of Wazalendo in the area under their control; a caption names one victim, Francis, from Kalebero.
r1-SV-SK-2025-016.l: Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-016.n: Single source (CNDH). The UN mission separately reported M23 summary executions of dozens of people in Walungu and Kabare in June and July (collective punishment); this CNDH entry may be one of them but the sources do not link them.
r1-SV-SK-2025-016.vn: Both excerpts match. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
src: Lundi, 30 juin 2025, les militaires M23 ont fait incursion dans la localité de MUKU, Groupement KAMISIMBI dans le territoire de WALUNGU au Sud-Kivu et ont tué 6 civils en représailles à la présence présumée de Wazalendo dans la zone sous leur contrôle.
Photo de la victime Francis, originaire de Kalebero et tué à Muku

r1-SV-SK-2025-017.s: The CNDH-RDC reported that on Sunday 29 June 2025 M23 soldiers killed 4 civilians in the locality of Kaniola (Walungu territory) and set fire to several civilians' houses.
r1-SV-SK-2025-017.x: CNDH: 4 civilians killed; several houses burned
r1-SV-SK-2025-017.vn: Excerpt matches; Walungu from the section heading on the page. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
src: Le dimanche 29 juin 2025, les militaires du M23 ont tué 4 civils dans la localité de Kaniola et incendié plusieurs maisons de paisibles citoyens.

r1-SV-SK-2025-018.s: The CNDH-RDC reported that on 23 May 2025 the lifeless body of Pascal KILOZO was found in the Kavimvira neighbourhood of Uvira, on the shore of Lake Tanganyika; it said the circumstances of death were unknown but raised concern about a possible extrajudicial execution or murder.
r1-SV-SK-2025-018.l: Kavimvira neighbourhood, avenue Nyagaa, Uvira, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-018.n: Uvira was then under FARDC/Wazalendo control (per the same report's introduction). Cause of death not established.
r1-SV-SK-2025-018.vn: Excerpt matches. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account.
src: Vendredi, 23 mai 2025, le corps sans vie de monsieur Pascal KILOZO a été découvert dans le Quartier Kavimvira, avenue Nyagaa, Ville d’UVIRA, au bord du Lac Tanganyika. Les circonstances de sa mort restent inconnues, mais l’état dans lequel le corps a été retrouvé soulève de sérieuses inquiétudes quant à une possible exécution extrajudiciaire ou meurtre.

r1-SV-SK-2025-019.s: The CNDH-RDC reported that during the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 a child musician was killed in Bukavu by elements identified as belonging to M23-AFC; it said several consistent testimonies suggested the child had recently performed a song about freedom.
r1-SV-SK-2025-019.n: Single source (CNDH); the child is not named in the text and the motive reported by the CNDH is its reading of witness accounts.
r1-SV-SK-2025-019.vn: Excerpt matches; motive clause on the page. CNDH-RDC is a Congolese state human rights commission (an organ of a party to the conflict); this is its uncorroborated account. The motive is conditional in the source ('aurait').
src: Dans la nuit du 4 au 5 avril 2025, un enfant artiste musicien a été froidement assassiné à Bukavu, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, par des éléments identifiés comme appartenant au mouvement armé M23-AFC.

r1-SV-SK-2025-020.s: The CNDH-RDC report said that the Council of Ministers of 28 February 2025, in its record, established for South Kivu that up to 27 February 2025 the city of Bukavu had recorded more than 1.130 wounded, more than 29 deaths in care establishments and 16 people who died at the rally.
r1-SV-SK-2025-020.x: DRC government (Council of Ministers record of 28 February 2025) via CNDH: more than 1.130 wounded; more than 29 deaths in care establishments; 16 dead at the rally, up to 27 February 2025
r1-SV-SK-2025-020.n: Government figure, relayed by the CNDH (the report says it is based on government figures from the city's health structures); the Council of Ministers record itself was not opened. The 'meeting' is not described in the excerpt.
r1-SV-SK-2025-020.vn: Date moved from the end of the counting period (27 Feb) to the date of the statement (28 Feb); figures written as printed ('1.130'). Government figures relayed by a state commission; the Council of Ministers record itself was not opened.
src: le Conseil des Ministres du 28 février 2025, dans son compte rendu, établit le bilan ci-après pour le Sud-Kivu, « jusqu’au 27 février 2025, la ville de Bukavu a enregistré plus de 1.130 blessés, plus de 29 décès dans les établissements de soins et 16 personnes décédées lors du meeting ».

r1-SV-SK-2025-021.s: UM News reported that during an attack by armed men on the night of March 18 on the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu, a nurse was sexually assaulted and another beaten, according to the centre's medical director Dr Jimmy Kasongo; medicine and money were also stolen.
r1-SV-SK-2025-021.l: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-021.a: armed gunmen (not identified by the source)
r1-SV-SK-2025-021.x: UM News: one nurse sexually assaulted, one nurse beaten
r1-SV-SK-2025-021.n: Single outlet (church news service) relaying the medical director. Which nurse was sexually assaulted is not stated; the nurse named in the article was beaten. The same article says Irambo was ransacked a month earlier by 'armed rebels' (February) and that Majengo Health Center in Goma was attacked on 19 March.
r1-SV-SK-2025-021.vn: Both excerpts match; Ntumba's transfer to Bukavu General Hospital is printed on the page. Church news service reporting on its own facility; byline is a communicator for the church's Kivu Conference. Attackers not identified.
src: At Irambo, a nurse was sexually assaulted and another was beaten during the attack, according to Dr. Jimmy Kasongo, medical director of the health center. Medicine and money also were stolen.
Nurse on duty Bienfait Kabeya Ntumba (right) recounts how he was beaten during an attack on the United Methodist Irambo Health Center on the night of March 18 in Bukavu, Congo.

r1-SV-SK-2025-022.s: UM News reported that gunmen looted the medicine supplies of the United Methodist Irambo Health Center in Bukavu during an attack on the night of March 18, with more than $4,500 dollars and 789,200 Congolese francs also stolen, and that pharmacist Sandra Bontamba said the attack came 24 hours after the hospital had received essential medicines.
r1-SV-SK-2025-022.l: Irambo Health Center, Bukavu, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-022.x: UM News: More than $4,500 dollars and 789,200 Congolese francs stolen; medicine stock taken
r1-SV-SK-2025-022.n: Same single outlet as the previous claim. The same page also says it was the second time in a month the centre was ransacked (February, by 'armed rebels'); not asserted here.
r1-SV-SK-2025-022.vn: Text matches; removed a stray ';.' and used the source's 'gunmen'. Church news service reporting on its own facility. Attackers not identified. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Sandra Bontamba, pharmacist at the Irambo Health Center, said the attack came 24 hours after the hospital received essential medicines. “I regret in the sense that even the stock of medicines that the hospital stocked up on yesterday was taken away,” Bontamba said.
The gunmen also looted the hospital’s medicine supplies and stole patients’ personal belongings, including telephones, clothes and watches.
Material damage included three damaged doors. More than $4,500 dollars and 789,200 Congolese francs were stolen, compromising essential funds for hospital services.
Nurse on duty Bienfait Kabeya Ntumba (right) recounts how he was beaten during an attack on the United Methodist Irambo Health Center on the night of March 18 in Bukavu, Congo.

r1-SV-SK-2025-023.s: The Guardian reported that patients at hospitals in Bukavu described sustaining serious injuries during the chaotic withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies in the days before M23 rebels marched in: Priscilla Nabintu, 22, said a bullet hit her [in the shin] as she lay on her bed at home near Katana; Ghislaine Ntakwinja, 41, said unidentified gunmen shot her in her right hand in her house; and Mugisho Shalukoma, 20, was recovering from a leg amputation, the result of gunshot wounds. Esperance Mwamini Birindwa, an ICRC nurse, said 162 people had been admitted with injuries related to the M23 takeover between 14 and 24 February.
r1-SV-SK-2025-023.l: Bukavu (general hospital) and near Katana, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-023.a: unidentified gunmen; the article ties the shooting to the withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies
r1-SV-SK-2025-023.x: Guardian citing an ICRC nurse: 162 people admitted with injuries related to the M23 takeover, 14-24 February
r1-SV-SK-2025-023.n: Reporting by Prosper Heri Ngorora in Bukavu and Carlos Mureithi in Nairobi. The article gives 14 February for M23's arrival in Bukavu; the UN mission says M23 entered on 16 February (existing claims differ). Three of those with gunshot and shrapnel injuries died per the same ICRC nurse (not asserted here).
r1-SV-SK-2025-023.vn: Raw said all three were at the general hospital and blended the article's framing with the patients' own accounts; rewritten so each clause carries its own source. Individual patients do not name who shot them (Shalukoma: 'I didn't see the person who shot me'); the link to the withdrawal is the Guardian's framing. The article dates M23's arrival in Bukavu to 14 February; the UN mission says 16 February.
ent: International Committee of the Red Cross
src: Patients at hospitals in the second-largest city in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo have described how they sustained serious injuries during the chaotic withdrawal of the Congolese army and its allies in the days before Rwanda-backed M23 rebels marched in.
“I was lying on my bed at home, near Katana,” said 22-year-old Priscilla Nabintu from her bed in Bukavu’s general hospital. “All of a sudden, a bullet hit me [in the shin] and I started bleeding.”
Mugisho Shalukoma, 20, was recovering from a leg amputation, the result of gunshot wounds.
Ghislaine Ntakwinja, 41, said she was in her house when unidentified gunmen shot her in her right hand.

Esperance Mwamini Birindwa, a nurse with the International Committee of the Red Cross, which operates at the general hospital, said 162 people had been admitted with injuries related to the M23 takeover between 14 and 24 February.

r1-SV-SK-2025-024.s: The Guardian quoted ICRC project manager Emmanuel Konin as saying that, despite all efforts, evacuations sometimes take longer than expected because of access difficulties and that some patients whose lives could have been saved had died of their injuries.
r1-SV-SK-2025-024.l: Eastern DRC (ICRC operations; place not stated)
r1-SV-SK-2025-024.n: Quote is about ICRC operations in the conflict zone generally; the article does not state that it applies to South Kivu only. Goma warehouse looting is on the same page and is North Kivu.
r1-SV-SK-2025-024.vn: Dropped the Goma warehouse clause: it is not in the excerpt and is North Kivu. The quote is not tied to Bukavu by the source, so territory 'Bukavu (city)' removed.
src: “Despite all our efforts, evacuations sometimes take longer than expected because of access difficulties,” said ICRC project manager Emmanuel Konin. “Some patients whose lives we could have tried to save are already dead from their injuries.”

r1-SV-SK-2025-025.s: DW reported that a woman it called Riziki (not her real name) said that three soldiers broke into her house to loot and that one of them came into her bedroom to rape her but she resisted; DW said the crime took place in February in Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu.
r1-SV-SK-2025-025.l: Kavumu village, about 30 km north of Bukavu, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-025.a: three soldiers (force not named in the passage)
r1-SV-SK-2025-025.x: one attempted rape reported by one survivor
r1-SV-SK-2025-025.n: Single survivor account relayed by DW; the survivor is identified only by a pseudonym and is not listed as a named victim. The text calls it an attack she 'survived'; the incident is an attempted rape as she describes it. DW's text 'Congolese military and allied Wazalendo militias from the North Kivu province' is from its introduction and is not tied to this case.
r1-SV-SK-2025-025.vn: Raw statement 'the others told him to leave' omitted 'but he refused'; narrowed to the excerpts. 'Kabare territory' was inferred. Pseudonymous survivor; force of the soldiers not named. On the page she says the others shouted at him to leave 'but he refused', and that they left after her son came to her rescue.
src: Riziki (not her real name) told DW that she survived an attack. "Three soldiers broke into my house to loot," Riziki said. "One of them came into my bedroom to rape me, but I resisted."
The crime took place in February in Kavumu village, about 30 kilometers (18 miles) north of Bukavu.

r1-SV-SK-2025-026.s: DW reported that in South Kivu MSF had assisted almost 700 people in the Kalehe and Uvira regions since the start of 2025, and that according to MSF's report the vast majority of attacks reported by victims in 2025 were committed at gunpoint, with perpetrators remaining unaccountable.
r1-SV-SK-2025-026.l: Kalehe and Uvira regions, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-026.x: MSF via DW: almost 700 people assisted in Kalehe and Uvira regions since the start of 2025 (DW: for North Kivu, almost 7,400 victims and survivors between January and April 2025)
r1-SV-SK-2025-026.n: Context in the article is MSF's report on sexual violence (the article's subject); the South Kivu excerpt itself says 'people' and 'attacks', so the sexual-violence framing comes from the article's headline and the neighbouring excerpt on North Kivu. The end date of the South Kivu count is not stated; the report date is 30 June 2025. MSF report itself not opened.
r1-SV-SK-2025-026.vn: Raw attributed the 700 figure to 'MSF's report' (DW states it in its own voice); end date 2025-04 was borrowed from the North Kivu figure. Territory now includes Uvira. The South Kivu sentence says 'people', not explicitly victims of sexual violence; the article is about sexual violence. End of the count period not stated (article of 30 June 2025).
src: In South Kivu, MSF has assisted almost 700 people in the Kalehe and Uvira regions since the start of 2025. According to MSF's report, the vast majority of attacks reported by victims in 2025 were committed at gunpoint, with perpetrators remaining unaccountable.
MSF reports treating almost 40,000 victims there in 2024; between January and April 2025, there were almost 7,400 victims and survivors.

r1-SV-SK-2025-027.s: Christianity Today reported that on a recent visit to Panzi Hospital in Bukavu, 185 of its 450 patients were receiving treatment for sexual violence, and that after the rebels captured Bukavu in February the hospital remained operational in the following weeks, treating injuries and gunshot wounds and delivering 110 babies.
r1-SV-SK-2025-027.x: Christianity Today: 185 of 450 patients treated for sexual violence at the time of the visit
r1-SV-SK-2025-027.n: Magazine feature; visit date not given ('recent'); publication date from URL path (2025/05) and search listing (7 May 2025). The page dates it May 2025; the search listing for the page shows 15 June, probably an update.
r1-SV-SK-2025-027.vn: Removed 'M23' (a number the excerpts do not print; the excerpt says 'the rebels'). Visit date unknown, so precision is approximate. The visit date is not given ('recent'); the article is in the May/June 2025 issue. The page's preceding sentence names the M23 as the rebels.
src: On a recent visit to Panzi Hospital, 185 of its 450 patients were receiving treatment for sexual violence.
The rebels captured Bukavu in February. In the following weeks, the hospital remained operational, treating injuries and gunshot wounds and delivering 110 babies—a sign of life continuing.

r1-SV-SK-2025-028.s: The Global Protection Cluster's March 2025 protection update said that further mass prison escapes from Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira followed during the offensive towards the South Kivu capital, and that some escapees had been convicted or were suspected of serious human rights violations, including sexual and gender-based crimes.
r1-SV-SK-2025-028.l: Bukavu, Kabare and Uvira prisons, South Kivu
r1-SV-SK-2025-028.n: Corroborates the escapes at Bukavu and Kabare (UN mission) and gives Uvira (also in FIDH; existing claim SV-2025#13). Interagency protection cluster document, not an independent investigation. The same document repeats the BBC/UN figure of at least 165 women raped at Munzenze (Goma).
r1-SV-SK-2025-028.vn: Wording 'followed during' restored; territory widened from Bukavu to the three prisons named. Interagency analysis, not an investigation; gives no dates or numbers for these escapes.
src: D’autres évasions massives des prisons de Bukavu, Kabare et Uvira ont suivi lors de l’offensive vers la capitale du Sud Kivu. Il sied de noter que certains évadés avaient été reconnus coupables ou étaient soupçonnés de graves violations des droits humains, dont de crimes sexuels et sexistes.

r1-SV-SK-2025-029.s: The UNFPA situation report covering April 2025 said that in Minova, South Kivu, activities were still paused due to limited access, though implementing partners were prepared to resume operations as soon as the situation improved.
r1-SV-SK-2025-029.n: The excerpt does not specify which activities (the section concerns sexual and reproductive health and GBV response). The cause 'limited access' is the sitrep's wording; the sitrep does not attribute it to a party.
r1-SV-SK-2025-029.vn: Excerpt matches the sitrep (covering 1-30 April 2025, issued 30 June 2025).
src: In the South Kivu province, UNFPA is strengthening the response in one health facility through deployed midwives. In Minova, South Kivu, activities are still paused due to limited access, though implementing partners are prepared to resume operations as soon as the situation improves.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing (its letter of 5 June 2026) the FDLR was fragmented into three principal factions, FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP), and that all three had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-001.n: UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466), copy hosted on ecoi.net. Alias detail from FDLR, Wazalendo and intelligence sources per the report's footnote.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-001.vn: Excerpt states factions and designations; finding is the Group's.
src: At the time of writing, FDLR (Cde.005) was fragmented into three principal factions: FDLR-FOCA, FDLR-RUD and FDLR-Force de protection du peuple (FPP) (see S/2025/466, para. 92). All three factions had recently adopted alternative designations to obscure their FDLR affiliation: FDLR-FOCA was referred to as “Bataillon jungle”; FDLR-RUD as “FDP-R”; and FDLR-FPP as “FPP”.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-002.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) and "General" Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) remained FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader respectively; it named "Brigadier-General" Emmanuel Nsengiyumva as overall FDLR-RUD leader and "Colonel" Dan Hategekimana as FDLR-FPP leader.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-002.n: Spelling 'Ntawuguka' as printed here; S/2025/446 prints 'Ntawunguka'. Sanctions designations (CDi.024, CDi.003) appear in the report.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-002.vn: All names, ranks (in the Group's quotation marks) and aliases are printed in the excerpt. Spelling discrepancy: S/2026/466 prints 'Ntawuguka' (alias Omega Israel); S/2025/446 prints 'Ntawunguka' (alias Omega). Both kept as printed. Aliases Faida/Fayida Hakimu and Dan Simplice are printed in the excerpt.
src: “Major-General” Pacifique Ntawuguka (alias Omega Israel) (CDi.024) and “General” Gaston Iyamuremye (alias Victor Byiringiro) (CDi.003) remained, respectively, FDLR-FOCA military commander and political leader. The overall FDLR -RUD leader was “Brigadier-General” Emmanuel Nsengiyumva (alias Faida/Fayida Hakimu), and the FDLR-FPP leader was “Colonel” Dan Hategekimana (alias Dan Simplice)

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the traditional FDLR-RUD area of operations was in the Bwisha and Bwito chefferies, Rutshuru territory, and that at the time of drafting FDLR-RUD units were particularly active in Jomba, Binza, Busanza and Bukoma, overlapping with the FDLR-FPP area in Rutshuru territory.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-003.l: Bwisha and Bwito chefferies; Jomba, Binza, Busanza, Bukoma, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
src: The traditional FDLR-RUD area of operations was in the Bwisha and Bwito chefferies, Rutshuru territory. At the time of drafting, FDLR-RUD units were particularly active in Jomba, Binza, Busanza and Bukoma, overlapping with the FDLR-FPP area of operations in Rutshuru territory.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR-FOCA, the largest FDLR faction, remained active on several major front lines in North Kivu, notably in Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories, and that its special unit, the Commando de recherche et d'action en profondeur (CRAP), was reported to have active units on the outskirts of Goma and infiltrated in Goma town.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-004.l: Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale (North Kivu); outskirts of Goma
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-004.n: Source of CRAP claim cited in report to FDLR-CRAP and Wazalendo sources.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-004.vn: Matches excerpt; 'reported to have' hedge kept. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Small precision fix: the source says 'several major front lines ... notably in' those four territories; the statement dropped 'several' and 'notably' and so read as an exhaustive list.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'several' and 'notably' are in source 0
ent: Commando de recherche et d’action en profondeur (CRAP)
src: FDLR-FOCA, the largest FDLR faction, remained active on several major front lines in North Kivu, notably in Nyiragongo, Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories. 154 The FDLR-FOCA special unit, known as the Commando de recherche et d’action en profondeur (CRAP), reported to have active units on the outskirts of Goma and infiltrated in Goma town

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR sources claimed the group's overall strength exceeded 10,000 combatants, while United Nations and intelligence sources estimated total FDLR strength at between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-005.x: FDLR sources: more than 10,000; UN and intelligence sources: 3,500 to 4,500
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-005.n: The report also cites the Washington Agreement estimate of 3,000 to 3,500 (not in this excerpt).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-005.vn: Each figure kept attributed to its stated origin. Strength figures diverge sharply: FDLR's own claim (>10,000, half active) vs UN/intelligence estimate (3,500-4,500). Both reported by the Group of Experts.
src: FDLR sources representing different factions claimed that the group’s overall strength exceeded 10,000 combatants, with half active at the time of drafting and others ready for mobilization.
United Nations and intelligence sources estimated that the total FDLR strength was between 3,500 and 4,500 combatants

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since April 2025 RDF units had led joint operations with AFC/M23 aimed at neutralizing the FDLR, and that RDF and AFC/M23 systematically destroyed and burned civilian settlements inhabited by members of FDLR, their families or alleged supporters.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-006.n: Two excerpts, same document. Report says photographic evidence, satellite imagery and NASA fire data corroborated several incidents.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-006.vn: Both clauses verbatim in the Group's report (paras 36, 41); the page places operations in Nyiragongo and Rutshuru (Bwito, Bwisha).
src: Since April 2025, RDF units have led joint operations with AFC/M23 aimed at neutralizing FDLR (S/2025/446, paras. 39 and 71 and annex 23).
Throughout these operations, RDF and AFC/M23 systematically destroyed and burned civilian settlements inhabited by members of FDLR, their families or alleged supporters.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported, citing United Nations sources, that on 30 May 2025 AFC/M23 ordered the evacuation of over 240 households from five villages (Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri and Kiganda), leading to mass displacement of civilians.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-007.l: Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri, Kiganda (Rutshuru territory per the report context)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-007.x: UN sources via Group of Experts: over 240 households, five villages
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-007.n: Footnote 40 of the report, attached to the anti-FDLR operations section. Territory inferred from the report's section on Rutshuru operations; the footnote itself does not name it.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-007.vn: Verbatim; location context confirmed on the page (Burambo listed in Binza). Appears in a footnote (fn 40) of S/2025/858 attached to the Binza (Rutshuru) section; the footnote cites UN sources.
src: according to United Nations sources, on 30 May 2025, AFC/M23 ordered the evacuation of over 240 households from five villages (Burambo, Kiyeye, Mayi ya Chumvi, Ngeri and Kiganda ), leading to mass displacement of civilians.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since June 2025 VDP/Wazalendo units, often operating jointly with FDLR, had conducted incursions and ambushes against AFC/M23 and RDF, either to recapture strategic positions or to disrupt their advances and supply lines.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-008.l: Masisi, Rutshuru, Nyiragongo, Walikale territories and outskirts of Goma (North Kivu)
src: Since June 2025, VDP/Wazalendo units, often operating jointly with FDLR, have conducted incursions and ambushes against AFC/M23 and RDF, either to recapture strategic positions or to disrupt AFC/M23 and RDF advances and supply lines.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that between mid- to late September and October 2025 FARDC increased air strikes, notably in Bibwe, Mpeti and Minjenje between 19 and 21 September, relying on VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements to conduct asymmetric ground operations.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-009.l: Bibwe, Mpeti, Minjenje (northern Masisi / Walikale, North Kivu)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-009.a: FARDC with VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-009.n: Territory not named in the excerpt; verify (the report places Bibwe on the Bibwe-Pinga axis).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-009.vn: Statement verbatim; location corrected: the page places Bibwe in northern Masisi on the Rutshuru-Masisi-Walikale corridor, not a Lubero axis.
src: To halt the advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF, between mid- to late September and October, FARDC increased air strikes, notably in Bibwe, Mpeti and Minjenje between 19 and 21 September, relying on VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR elements to conduct asymmetric ground operations.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC expressed its commitment to neutralizing the FDLR, publicly stated that it did not support the FDLR and called on FDLR combatants to disarm and surrender.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-010.vn: Verbatim. The Group reports the Government's public position; it does not itself assess whether the Government supported FDLR in this sentence (see claim 12).
ent: Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
src: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expressed its commitment to this objective, publicly stated that it did not support FDLR and called on FDLR combatants to disarm and surrender (see annex 6).

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the bulk of FDLR forces operated in areas controlled by AFC/M23 and RDF, beyond the operational reach of the FARDC, affecting the latter's ability to neutralize FDLR elements that refused to surrender.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-011.l: AFC/M23- and RDF-controlled areas of North Kivu
src: However, the bulk of FDLR forces operated in areas controlled by AFC/M23 and RDF, beyond the operational reach of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), affecting the latter’s ability to neutralize FDLR elements that refused to surrender.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-012.s: Congolese media reported that on Friday 10 October 2025 the FARDC issued a communiqué, signed by army spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, calling on all FDLR factions to lay down their arms and warning that in case of refusal the FARDC would proceed to disarmament by constraint or by force; the UN Group of Experts likewise reported that FARDC issued a communiqué on 10 October 2025 calling on FDLR to disarm and surrender, warning of forced disarmament.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-012.n: The 7sur7 excerpt gives the date in the lead sentence of the same page (10 October 2025), not in the excerpt; the UN report gives the date. The communiqué is also described as implementing the operational order of 1 October 2025 (7sur7).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-012.vn: Date and weekday come from the 7sur7 page lead (not the stored excerpt), supplied as replacement quote; GoE independently confirms the date. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (faithful translation).
src: « Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo appellent toutes les factions des FDLR à déposer les armes », déclare le communiqué signé par le général-major Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, porte-parole de l’armée.
L’armée prévient qu'en cas de refus, « les FARDC procéderont au désarmement par contrainte ou par usage de la force »

FARDC issued a communiqué on 10 October 2025 in which it called upon FDLR to disarm (S/2024/969, paras. 67–73) and surrender, warning that failure to comply would result in forced disarmament (see annex 35).

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-013.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the FARDC announcement triggered tensions between FARDC and FDLR and between FARDC and certain Wazalendo factions, and that subsequently some FARDC officers and government actors sought to reassure FDLR of their continued cooperation, given the essential role of FDLR in ongoing operations on the ground.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-013.a: FARDC officers and government actors; FDLR
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-013.n: Group of Experts assessment from its own sources; the DRC government is not recorded here as having said this publicly.
src: The announcement triggered tensions between FARDC and FDLR, and betwee n FARDC and certain Wazalendo factions (S/2024/969, paras. 67–77). Subsequently, some FARDC officers and government actors sought to reassure FDLR of their continued cooperation, given the essential role of FDLR in ongoing operations on the ground.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Regional Integration Floribert Anzuluni confirmed at a press briefing in Kinshasa on Tuesday 28 July that the FDLR had signed a protocol of demilitarisation, demobilisation and cantonment.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-014.n: Whether the FDLR confirmed signing was not found in this page.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-014.vn: Verbatim; excerpt_en flag false positive. This is the DRC government's announcement; no FDLR statement confirming the signature was opened in this round.
src: le ministre de l'Intégration régionale, Floribert Anzuluni, a confirmé la signature, par les FDLR (Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda), d'un protocole de démilitarisation, de démobilisation et de cantonnement. Selon le ministre qui s'exprimait ce mardi 28 juillet lors du briefing de presse à Kinshasa

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-015.s: Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe considered the DRC's announcement of an FDLR surrender protocol a 'grossière manipulation' that is in no way consistent with the Washington accords.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-015.n: Exact date of Nduhungirehe's remark not given; page dated 2026-08-05, after Kinshasa's 28 July announcement.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-015.vn: Verbatim attributed quote. Party statement ('Rwanda says'); the page does not give the date or venue of the minister's remark.
src: Le ministre rwandais des Affaires étrangères, Olivier Nduhungirehe, estime que l’annonce du protocole de reddition des FDLR constitue une « grossière manipulation » qui n’est « en rien conforme aux accords de Washington, qui ne le prévoit nulle part ».

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-016.s: Afrikarabia reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, on X, rejected a 'protocole négocié avec une milice génocidaire que le gouvernement de la RDC continue d'armer et de soutenir' and said the FDLR remain integrated in the Congolese army and active on the front lines.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-016.n: The X post itself was not opened; attribution rests on Afrikarabia. The page text has a spacing artefact ('r estent').
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-016.vn: Attributed party statement; quote kept as printed. Party statement. 'Milice génocidaire' is Kigali's wording, quoted. Afrikarabia's rendering of the Makolo quote is garbled ('restent intégrés ... actifs sur les lignes de fronts ne changent rien'); the original X post was not opened.
src: Mais à Kigali, on ne veut pas entendre parler d’un « protocole négocié avec une milice génocidaire que le gouvernement de la RDC continue d’armer et de soutenir », comme l’a souligné sur le réseau X la porte-parole du gouvernement rwandais. Yolande Makolo estime que les FDLR « r estent intégrés à l’armée congolaise et actifs sur les lignes de fronts

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-017.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that key FDLR commanders and combatants were compelled to relocate to localities in Rutshuru, Masisi and Nyiragongo territories, and that FDLR military commander and sanctioned individual "Major-General" Pacifique Ntawunguka (alias Omega) and other key leaders, fearing RDF attacks, withdrew to the vicinity of the Nyiragongo volcano and inside Virunga National Park.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-017.l: Nyiragongo volcano area and Virunga National Park (North Kivu)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-017.n: Report dated April 2025; exact dates not given.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-017.vn: Raw causal clause ('as AFC/M23 and RDF advances disrupted') is only on the page, not in the excerpt; narrowed to the excerpt. Date narrowed to the report period. Spelling as printed in S/2025/446 ('Ntawunguka', alias Omega); S/2026/466 prints 'Ntawuguka' (alias Omega Israel). On the page (para 71) the relocation follows the Group's statement that AFC/M23 and RDF territorial advances disrupted FDLR presence. The report does not date the withdrawal more precisely.
src: Key commanders and combatants were compelled to relocate to localities in Rutshuru, 53 Masisi 54 and Nyiragongo territories. FDLR military commander and sanctioned individual “Major-General” Pacifique Ntawunguka, alias Omega (CDi.024) 55 and other key leaders, fearing RDF attacks, withdrew in the vicinity of the Nyiragongo volcano and inside the Virunga National Park.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-018.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 March 2025 AFC/M23 transferred several FDLR captives to the Government of Rwanda, including 'Brigadier-General' Ezechiel Gakwerere; according to AFC/M23 they had been arrested during their raid on Goma, while the Group itself reported that most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals, and it records 'controversies around his arrest and transfer' in an annex.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-018.n: The report adds that most of these arrests occurred during operations targeting hospitals (see the health-care claims of other units, Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho, 1 and 3 March).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-018.vn: Verbatim; name printed. Arrest circumstances are AFC/M23's account as reported by the Group. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Group's own finding on the arrests 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: annex on controversies around his arrest and transfer 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Better explanation in the same source: the next sentence of para. 73 gives the Group's own finding on the arrest circumstances (hospital raids), which the claim omits and which links this to the hospital-raid claims (r1-GOE-055).; excerpt-support: added two excerpts: para. 73 ('Most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals') and the annex 39 title
src: On 1 March 2025, AFC/M23 transferred several FDLR captives to the Government of Rwanda, including high-profile commander “Brigadier-General” Ezechiel Gakwerere, (see annex 38). According to AFC/M23, these individuals were arrested during their raid on Goma.
Most, including Gakwerere, were arrested during armed operations targeting hospitals
Additional information on Gakwerere and controversies around his arrest and transfer to the Rwandan authorities

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-019.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 4 January 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre and retained it despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-019.a: AFC/M23 and RDF; counter-attacks by Wazalendo, FDLR, FDNB and FARDC
src: On 4 January 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF took control of Masisi centre in North Kivu and managed to retain control despite repeated attempts by Wazalendo, FDLR, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and FARDC to retake it.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-020.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that about two weeks later AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu, and that the 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before their arrival, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-020.a: AFC/M23 and RDF; FARDC and FDNB retreating
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-020.x: Group of Experts: 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-020.vn: Supported; 'about' is a slight softening of the Group's 'Two weeks later', acceptable. The Group says 'Two weeks later', counting from the 4 January 2025 capture of Masisi centre in the preceding sentence (claim 18).
src: Two weeks later, AFC/M23 and RDF captured Minova town in Kalehe Territory, South Kivu – a key strategic location facilitating further military operations targeting Goma. The 2,500 FARDC and FDNB troops based in Minova retreated before the arrival of AFC/M23 and RDF troops, leaving behind significant quantities of military equipment.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 the majority of 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably in the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area and in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that heavy clashes between FDNB (supported by FARDC and Wazalendo) and AFC/M23 (supported by RDF) resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-021.l: Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-021.x: Group of Experts: 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops; several hundreds of FDNB casualties (sources: FDNB, security, Government of Burundi, FARDC and intelligence sources per footnote)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-021.vn: Verbatim; footnote sources confirmed on page. Troop-strength figures differ across sources: GoE 7,000-9,000 (April 2025); SOS Médias Burundi 'more than 10,000'; Actualite.cd relaying CRG/CIC 12,000-15,000 (claim 42). Casualty footnote 211 cites FDNB, security, Government of Burundi, FARDC and intelligence sources.
src: In early April, the majority of the 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops were positioned in South Kivu, notably the Ruzizi Plain along the tri-border area, and in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe (see annex 72). Heavy clashes between FDNB supported by FARDC and Wazalendo, and AFC/M23 supported by RDF, resulted in several hundreds of FDNB casualties.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in February 2025 the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced Burundi's readiness to fight back; it also reported that in mid-March the two countries agreed on verbal and military de-escalation, reportedly concluding a non-aggression agreement.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-022.n: Report also cites a Rwandan Minister of Foreign Affairs message on X for the mid-March de-escalation (reportedly).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-022.vn: Verbatim. Burundi's accusation is a party statement reported by the Group; 'reportedly' hedge kept.
src: In February 2025, the President of Burundi, Évariste Ndayishimiye, accused Rwanda of intending to invade Burundi, including through its backing of the Burundian armed opposition group Red Tabara, and announced the readiness of Burundi to fight back
In mid-March, both countries agreed on verbal and military de -escalation, reportedly concluding a non-aggression agreement.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that during more than a month of controlling Uvira, AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases and dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border, and that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-023.a: AFC/M23 (forced FDNB withdrawal); AFC/M23 and RDF (withdrawal from Uvira)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-023.n: Report states AFC/M23 had captured Uvira on 10 December 2025 (para. 74, not excerpted here).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-023.vn: The Group attributes the forced FDNB withdrawal to AFC/M23 alone, not RDF; 'diplomatic pressure' clause is on the page (para 77), supplied as replacement quote.
src: After controlling Uvira for over a month – during which AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases, 84 dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border and established a parallel administration – AFC/ M23 and RDF troops eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-024.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors, launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who had reinforced MRDP/Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-024.l: From Uvira towards Minembwe, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-024.a: FARDC with Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors
src: In late January 2026, FARDC, with support from Wazalendo, FDNB and private military contractors (see paras. 143–144), launched an offensive from Uvira towards Minembwe against MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23, who reinforced MRDP/ Twirwaneho in August 2025 and February 2026.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-025.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, temporarily seized Point Zero, Kanguli and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga-Fizi road, and that FARDC-FDNB forces regained these positions on 29 January.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-025.l: Point Zero, Kanguli, Tuwe-Tuwe, Mwenga-Fizi road, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-025.a: AFC/M23 coalition incl. Twirwaneho; FARDC-FDNB forces
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-025.n: The 29 January date refers to the regaining; the seizure is 'late January 2026'.
src: In late January 2026, the AFC/M23 coalition, including Twirwaneho combatants, launched an offensive and temporarily seized the strategic positions of Point Zero, Kanguli, and Tuwe-Tuwe along the Mwenga–Fizi road. Although FARDC-FDNB forces subsequently regained these positions on 29 January

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-026.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that several Wazalendo factions carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain; for example FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-026.l: Uvira axis, Ruzizi Plain, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
src: Several Wazalendo factions also carried out joint operations with FDNB, which relied on them for intelligence and knowledge of the terrain. For example, FDNB operated with Yakutumba along the Uvira axis and the Ruzizi Plain prior to the AFC/M23 takeover and relied on Ngomazito elements as scouts in the Hauts Plateaux.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-027.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments; the Group stated it did not substantiate intentional targeting of the civilian population.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-027.a: MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 (allegation); FARDC and FDNB (accused)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-027.n: Party allegation attributed to the parties. The Group states it did not substantiate intentional targeting.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-027.vn: Allegation and the Group's finding kept separate. 'Campaign of extermination' is the wording of MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders as reported by the Group; the Group did not substantiate intentional targeting.
src: MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 leaders alleged that FARDC and FDNB committed a premeditated, systematic and targeted campaign of extermination against the Banyamulenge population, including through aerial bombardments of densely populated areas. 99 While the civilian population in the Hauts Plateaux has been exposed to significant risks from ongoing hostilities, the Group of Experts did not substantiate their intentional targeting.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-028.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that additional AFC/M23 public justifications for the offensive on Uvira cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB, and said it did not identify evidence that such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the DRC.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-028.a: AFC/M23 spokespersons (as described by the Group of Experts); FARDC, FDNB
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-028.n: The sentence before names AFC/M23 spokespersons and affiliated social media networks as the source of the public justifications.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-028.vn: Verbatim; attribution to AFC/M23 justifications supported by the preceding page sentence (replacement quote). '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'. The 'additional claims' follow, on the page, public justifications 'including statements by AFC/M23 spokespersons and affiliated social media networks'.
src: Additional claims cited the presence of FDLR-FOCA elements operating alongside FARDC and FDNB. The Group of Experts did not identify evidence th at such elements posed a direct threat to Rwanda justifying military intervention in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (see S/2025/446, annex 24).

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-029.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that security concerns led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as 'military zones' on 9 December 2025, and that on 25 February 2026 Burundi reopened a number of crossings.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-029.n: 25 February 2026 reopening is in the following sentence of the same paragraph; not within the excerpt.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-029.vn: Reopening clause is on the page (annex text right after the excerpt), so supported; excerpt gap flagged for add_excerpt. '25' flag resolved by that passage. The Group adds that the reopening reflected a transition to controlled, securitized border management, not diminished security concerns. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: S/2026/466 supports both clauses, but the stored excerpt carries only the 9 December 2025 closure; the next sentence, on the 25 February 2026 reopening, is added.
src: Security concerns regarding the cross-border movement of armed actors led Burundi to close border posts with the DRC and designate several frontier areas as “military zones” on 9 December 2025.
On 25 February 2026, Burundi reopened a number of crossings, citing economic, humanitarian, and operational/military considerations.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-030.s: The UN Group of Experts assessed that control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens the influence of AFC/M23 over the northern 'gate' of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-030.l: Ruzizi Plain, Katogota, RN5, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-030.n: Analytical assessment by the Group of Experts, not an incident report; date is approximate.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-030.vn: Source uses present tense ('offers'), not 'would offer'; 'defensive lines' clause narrowed out (page-only). Assessment by the Group: graded A as a documented UN finding, but it is analysis, not an event. Month '2025-09' not printed; narrowed.
src: Notably, control of Katogota and surrounding heights strengthens AFC/M23’s influence over the northern ‘gate’ of the Ruzizi Plain and offers options of advancing toward Uvira by bypassing strong FDNB and FARDC/Wazalendo blocking positions along RN5.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, an attack on Saturday by Burundian soldiers in the town of Mikalati, Fizi territory, against residents returning from the weekly market in Bijombo (Uvira territory); its headline section gives four civilians killed, mass abductions and over 100 missing.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.l: Mikalati (Mu Mikarati), Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.a: Burundian soldiers (FDNB), as attributed by local sources
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.x: SOS Médias Burundi section heading: four civilians killed, mass abductions, over 100 missing
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.n: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday') and publication date 2025-12-07. No victims named. Unverified local-source account; no official statement from Burundi or DRC as of Sunday morning per same page.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031.vn: Supported as attributed; grade C (anonymous local sources, single outlet). Rests on unnamed local sources; the casualty figures appear only in a section heading, not in sourced body text. The date (6 December 2025) is inferred from 'Saturday' in a report datelined 7 December 2025. No official statement from Burundi or the DRC as of 7 December.
src: Mikalati : four civilians killed, mass abductions, and over 100 missing Several local sources report an attack carried out on Saturday by Burundian soldiers in the town of Mikalati, in the Fizi territory, against residents returning from the weekly market in Bijombo, located in the neighboring Uvira territory

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-032.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a survivor, now a refugee in Mikenge, described meeting Burundian soldiers at Mikalati who attacked, looted and abducted many people, especially women.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-032.a: Burundian soldiers, as described by one survivor
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-032.n: Single anonymous witness. Date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-12-07. 'Women abducted' is not described as sexual violence by the source.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-032.vn: Verbatim; attributed to survivor. Single unnamed survivor account relayed by one outlet.
src: A survivor, now a refugee in Mikenge, describes the attack : “We were returning after buying salt, soap, oil, and sugar. When we arrived in Mikalati, we encountered Burundian soldiers who attacked us, looted what we had, and abducted many people, especially women.”

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the survivor said the military commander ordered the soldiers 'to kill the men and collect their belongings', that the Wazalendo community claims 45 people, mostly women, are being held at the Mikalati military site, and that no official statement had been issued by the Burundian or Congolese governments as of Sunday morning.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.l: Mikalati military site, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.a: Burundian soldiers (alleged); Wazalendo community (claim on detainees)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.x: Wazalendo community claim: 45 people, mostly women, held
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.n: Partisan-side figure (Wazalendo community). Burundi and DRC governments: no statement as of the page, see gaps.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-033.vn: Each clause attributed as on the page. The '45 held' figure is a claim by the Wazalendo community (a party aligned against the FDNB's adversaries but also a belligerent); the order quote is from one unnamed survivor.
src: According to him, the military commander ordered them “to kill the men and collect their belongings.” The Wazalendo community claims that 45 people, mostly women, are being held at the Mikalati military site. No official statement had been issued by the Burundian or Congolese governments as of Sunday morning.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that OCHA had already warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe, due, according to local sources, to a blockade imposed for a month by the Burundian army.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034.l: Minembwe, Fizi/Mwenga Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034.a: Burundian army (FDNB), as alleged by local sources
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034.n: OCHA's own warning not opened; relayed by SOS Médias Burundi. FDNB spokesperson's account is a separate claim.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034.vn: Verbatim; attribution kept with SOS Médias and local sources. The OCHA warning itself was not opened; the blockade attribution to the Burundian army is 'according to local sources'. FDNB's own account of the road closures is in claims 34-35; the demonstrators' account in claim 36. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) had already warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe, due to a blockade imposed for a month by the Burundian army, according to local sources.

Le 5 novembre 2025, la communauté Banyamulenge et d’autres habitants avaient déjà manifesté pour dénoncer le siège imposé, selon eux, par l’armée burundaise et les FARDC, en coalition avec les miliciens wazalendo.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-035.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that some Banyamulenge are trapped in areas 'where the enemy is' and said it is understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are blocked.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-035.n: Relay of a BBC interview; see the BBC Gahuza claim for the primary report (dated 2025-11-12).
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-035.vn: Date of the BBC remark is not 7 Dec; narrowed to a range. Origin is the BBC, so not independent of claim 35. Relay of a BBC interview; the BBC Gahuza article of 12 November 2025 (claim 35) carries a similar Baratuza quote ('Point-zero ... is the route they must use to fetch food they give to the enemies, that is why it is closed'). The SOS Médias English wording is a translation of that interview, not the original.
src: The spokesperson for the FDNB, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged on the BBC that some Banyamulenge are trapped in areas “where the enemy is” : “It’s understandable that those who go to buy food for the enemy are blocked.”

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-036.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army stated that its troops in South Kivu had blocked the roads of people leaving the Minembwe area in order to 'protect Uvira and the Burundi border', and that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told BBC Gahuzamiryango that in Minembwe there was not one Burundian soldier.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-036.n: Publication date read from the page header '12 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025' (Kirundi, month 11 = November). The page dateline is read as 12 November 2025.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-036.vn: 'Confirmed' upgraded the verb; corrected to 'stated'. excerpt_en flags are false positives (proper-noun renderings). Party statement (FDNB). Kirundi 'kimenesha' = makes known/states; rendered 'stated' rather than 'confirmed'. On the same page Baratuza says Burundian troops are at Muramvya, Mugeti and Majembwe. Translations are the researcher's, from Kirundi.
src: Igisirikare c'Uburundi kimenesha ko ingabo zaco ziri mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo ya RD Congo zazibiye amayira y'abava mu karere ka Minembwe zigamije "gukingira Uvira n'urubibe rw'Uburundi", zigasaba abanyagihugu bari i Minembwe "kuvavanura n'abansi" bariyo.
Général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza avugira igisirikare c'Uburundi yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango ko ico gice ca "Minembwe ata musirikare n'umwe w'Uburundi ahari".

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-037.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that demonstrators in Minembwe (an area controlled by the Twirwaneho group together with AFC/M23) accused Burundian troops and those working with them of blocking the roads that bring supplies, mainly from Uvira, at Mu Mikarati, Point-zero and elsewhere, and asked that the Burundian troops return home.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-037.l: Minembwe; Mu Mikarati; Point-zero, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-037.a: Burundian troops (FDNB), as alleged by demonstrators
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-037.n: Demonstrators were in a Twirwaneho/AFC/M23-controlled area (partisan context). Demonstrators' words quoted in the same page also describe the blockade as hunger-inducing; no legal label recorded.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-037.vn: Attributed account; translation faithful. Demonstrators' account (in an area held by Twirwaneho with AFC/M23); FDNB's account is claim 35.
src: Mu ndwi iheze i Minembwe, ahagenzurwa n'umuhari wa Twirwaneho ufatanije na AFC/M23, habereye imyiyerekano ikomeye yiyamiriza ko ingabo z'Uburundi n'abakorana na zo bugaye amayira ashikanayo ivya nkenerwa ahanini bakura mu muji wa Uvira.
Abagize imyiyerekano bagirije ingabo z'Uburundi kuzibira amayira bari ahitwa Mu Mikarati, Point-zero n'ahandi. Basaba ko ingabo z'Uburundi zisubira mu gihugu cazo

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-038.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of continuing to attack the positions of its soldiers sent to eastern DRC; that Burundi's Minister of Foreign Affairs Edouard Bizimana, speaking on Monday before representatives of countries in Burundi, said without giving proof that the aim of the attacks was for Rwanda and M23 to capture Uvira before 25 December 2025; and that the Rwandan government had not yet responded.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-038.n: Weekday 'ejo ku wa mbere' (yesterday, Monday) -> 2025-12-08; date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-12-09.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-038.vn: Full name and 'Monday' came from the page, not the excerpt; supplied as replacement quote. Removed awkward 'according to BBC'. Party statement. The page (published 9 December 2025) says 'yesterday Monday', i.e. 8 December 2025. BBC notes the claim was made without proof.
src: Uburundi buragiriza Urwanda ko ari rwo rubandanya rutera ibirindiro vy'abasirikare babwo barungitswe mu buseruko bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo, kandi ko igihugu kidashobora kurera amaboko mu gihe kizobandanya giterwa.

Umushikiranganji Bizimana, ata cemezo atanze, yavuze ko intumbero y'ibi bitero bikomeye bivugwa mu turere tw'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo ari uko Urwanda na M23 bipfuza kuba bafashe igisagara ca Uvira imbere y'uwa 25 Kigarama (12) uno mwaka wa 2025.
Nta co reta y'Urwanda irashikiriza kuri ibi birego, mbere n'umushikiranganji ajejwe imigenderanire ntarishura

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-039.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least 272 Burundian soldiers are serving sentences of up to life imprisonment in Murembwe Central Prison in southwestern Burundi after refusing to be sent to fight in the DRC.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-039.l: Burundi (Murembwe Central Prison); related to deployment in DRC
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-039.n: Dateline 'Fizi, July 9, 2026'; the sentencing figure is a current-status claim by the outlet without an attributed source in the excerpt.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-039.vn: Statement verbatim; date 2026-07-09 not printed, narrowed to the report month. SOS Médias does not give its source for the 272 figure. The same article cites an internal DRC Interior Ministry report of more than 29,000 Burundian soldiers deployed between August 2022 and December 2025 (not part of this claim).
src: Meanwhile, at least 272 Burundian soldiers are currently serving sentences of up to life imprisonment. They were sent to Murembwe Central Prison in southwestern Burundi after refusing to be sent to fight in the DRC.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-040.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that an incursion followed by systematic looting by armed men assimilated to former FDLR fighters was reported on the night of Sunday 14 September 2025 in the lakeside village of Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, according to an anonymous local source; the page says no human incident was reported.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-040.l: Nyakakoma, Binza grouping, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-040.a: Armed men presumed to be FDLR
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-040.n: Single anonymous local source; the village lies in an AFC/M23-controlled zone per the page. The page names Heps-EPER condemning armed violence at Bishusha (not excerpted). Victim count: none reported.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-040.vn: Supported as attributed; grade C (anonymous local source, single outlet). Perpetrators only 'presumed' FDLR per an anonymous resident; the resident said the attackers were seeking a local 'notable du M23'. Village in an AFC/M23-controlled area. Single outlet (byline 'La Rédaction').
src: Une incursion suivie de pillage systématique par des hommes armés assimilés aux anciens combattants rwandais FDLR a été signalée la nuit du dimanche 14 septembre 2025 dans le village lacustre de Nyakakoma, en groupement Binza, territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-041.s: Radio Okapi reported that long lines of Burundian soldiers were seen on Wednesday 10 December at the Gatumba border returning to their country, according to local sources in Uvira and Bujumbura; it added that Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-041.l: Gatumba border (Burundi side) / Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-041.n: Page republished/modified 2026-02-21; original publication 2025-12-11. The Burundian ambassador's denial is a separate claim.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-041.vn: Verbatim; regraded C because the observation rests on anonymous local sources and is contested. Rests on unnamed local sources; denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC (claim 41). Article first published 11 December 2025 (modified 21 February 2026, hence the URL date). The same page says the Congolese side of the Gatumba post was controlled by AFC-M23 after its entry into Uvira. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 11 Dec 2025 (modified 21 Feb 2026, hence the URL path), carries the sighting per local sources, but the same report ends by saying Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers; the statement leaves that denial out. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, published 11 Dec 2025 (modified 21 Feb 2026, hence the URL path), carries the sighting per local sources, but the same report ends by saying Burundi's ambassador to the DRC denied this departure of part of the Burundian soldiers; the statement leaves that denial out.
src: De longues files de militaires burundais ont été aperçus mercredi 10 décembre à la frontière de Gatumba en train de rentrer dans leur pays, selon des sources locales à Uvira et Bujumbura.
Mais ce départ d'une partie des militaires burundais est démenti par l'ambassadeur du Burundi en RDC.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-042.s: Radio Okapi reported that the departure of part of the Burundian soldiers from Uvira was denied by Burundi's ambassador to the DRC.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-042.a: Government of Burundi (ambassador to the DRC)
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-042.n: The ambassador is not named on the page.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-042.vn: Verbatim. The ambassador is not named on the page; the denial is reported without a quotation.
src: Mais ce départ d'une partie des militaires burundais est démenti par l'ambassadeur du Burundi en RDC.

r1-UC-BI-FDLR-043.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group (CRG) and the Center on International Cooperation (CIC), that the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 by the M23 and the Rwandan Defence Forces put the Burundian contingent deployed alongside the Congolese army out of action; the article also states that between 12 000 and 15 000 FDNB soldiers were deployed on the eastern Congolese front against the M23/Rwanda alliance.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-043.x: Actualite.cd relaying CRG/CIC: 12 000 to 15 000 FDNB soldiers
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-043.n: The CRG/CIC report itself was not opened (a lead: cic.nyu.edu, April 2026). UN GoE (S/2025/446) gave 7,000 to 9,000 Burundian troops for early April 2025, a different date.
r1-UC-BI-FDLR-043.vn: 'Capture of Uvira' wording is in the page lead (replacement quote); the troop figure sentence is not explicitly attributed to CRG/CIC, so stated as the article's. The CRG/CIC report itself was not opened. Troop figures diverge: 12,000-15,000 here; GoE 7,000-9,000 (April 2025, claim 20); SOS Médias 'more than 10,000' (Dec 2025).
src: le 10 décembre 2025 par le M23 et les Forces de défense rwandaises a mis hors jeu le contingent burundais déployé aux côtés de l'armée congolaise, constituant un tournant militaire majeur dans le conflit, selon un rapport publié en avril 2026 par le Congo Research Group (CRG) et le Center on International Cooperation (CIC)
Entre 12 000 et 15 000 soldats des Forces de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) étaient déployés sur le front oriental congolais contre l'alliance M23/Rwanda.

r1-UC-FARDC-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC Ministry of Defence announced on 29 January 2025 that, by presidential order of Tuesday 28 January, general-major Evariste Somo Kakule was appointed military governor of North Kivu province under the state of siege.
r1-UC-FARDC-001.a: FARDC / Ministry of Defence of the DRC
r1-UC-FARDC-001.n: Page also says he previously commanded the 31st rapid reaction brigade at Kindu; the page text names his predecessor only in a truncated line. Appointment came days after the fall of Goma.
r1-UC-FARDC-001.vn: Statement supported by the page; the 28 January order date sits on the page next to the stored excerpt (clause_support given; excerpt gap). Radio Okapi relays the Ministry of Defence's X account. Radio Okapi says he succeeds général-major Peter Cirimwami Nkuba, who died of wounds after being shot at the front (the page prints this name in full; the research note's 'truncated' remark is wrong). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Jan 2025, carries every clause; the stored excerpt gives the 29 January announcement but not the 28 January presidential order, which is in the next sentence (quoting the ministry's X account). Excerpt added; statement unchanged. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le ministère de la Défense et nationale et des Anciens combattants annonce ce mercredi 29 janvier, la nomination du général-major Evariste Somo Kakule gouverneur militaire de la province du Nord-Kivu, sous état de siège.
« Par ordonnance présidentielle du mardi 28 janvier, le général-major Evariste Somo Kakule, est nommé gouverneur militaire du Nord-Kivu » , annonce le compte X du ministère de la Défense.

r1-UC-FARDC-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that the new military governor of North Kivu had been commander of the 31st rapid reaction brigade of the FARDC based at Kindu in Maniema province.
r1-UC-FARDC-002.vn: Excerpt states it verbatim. Page adds he was until then also commander of the southern axis of the Grand Nord operational sector, south of Lubero. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le nouveau gouverneur du Nord-Kivu, était commandant de la 31ème Brigade de réaction rapide des FARDC, basée à Kindu dans la province du Maniema.

r1-UC-FARDC-003.s: Cocorico.cd reported that brigade general Muhondosi Muyusa Constantin was named commander of the 34th military region in North Kivu, whose headquarters had been relocated from Goma to Walikale because of the occupation of Goma by AFC/M23 forces.
r1-UC-FARDC-003.n: Search snippet of another outlet (actu30.cd) says he took up the post on Tuesday 18 March 2025; that page was not fetched.
r1-UC-FARDC-003.vn: Excerpt supports appointment, rank, and HQ relocation from Goma to Walikale due to AFC/M23 occupation. Page also says he took up post after joining the HQ at Walikale and previously handled operations and intelligence in the 21st and 31st military regions. The actu30.cd 18 March date was not fetched and is not used. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: C’est dans un contexte de tensions accrues avec les rebelles du M23 que le général de brigade Muhondosi Muyusa Constantin a été nommé commandant de la 34ᵉ région militaire au Nord-Kivu. Cette nomination intervient alors que l’état-major de la région a été délocalisé de Goma à Walikale, en raison de l’occupation de Goma par les forces de l’AFC/M23.

r1-UC-FARDC-004.s: Cocorico.cd reported that the situation at Walikale remained under FARDC control despite the departure of part of the population, and that the army had slowed the rebels' advance, pushing them back to Mpofi as they advanced toward Walikale-centre.
r1-UC-FARDC-004.n: Single local outlet; the page does not name the rebels in this passage. Treat as lead for frontline map.
r1-UC-FARDC-004.vn: Narrowed to the excerpt: removed the region number (not in the excerpt) and added the population-departure clause the excerpt prints. Single outlet; rebels unnamed in this passage. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: À l'heure actuelle, la situation à Walikale reste sous contrôle des FARDC, malgré le départ d’une partie de la population. L’armée a réussi à freiner la progression des rebelles, les repoussant jusqu’à Mpofi alors qu’ils avançaient vers Walikale-centre.

r1-UC-FARDC-005.s: 7sur7.cd reported on 22 October 2025 that newly appointed FARDC commanders had arrived in Uvira, among them brigade general Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques as new commander of the 33rd military region and general AMULI CIVIRI as commander of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.
r1-UC-FARDC-005.n: Kivu Times (kivutimes.com) dates the arrival to 'mercredi 23 octobre 2025' in its text; 22 October 2025 was a Wednesday, so the Kivu Times date looks like an error.
r1-UC-FARDC-005.vn: Excerpt supports arrival date, names and posts verbatim. SOS Médias Burundi (same day) independently prints 'Général de Brigade Amuli Civiri' and 'Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques' and says the two took office that Wednesday arriving from Kinshasa. 22 Oct 2025 was a Wednesday. The '7' flag is the outlet name 7sur7.cd. 33rd military region commander sequence in the sources is not reconciled: La Presse Africaine names brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien as commander on 26 June 2025; 7sur7.cd and SOS Médias Burundi say Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques (Oct 2025) replaced the late general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel; Congorassure.cd (Jan 2026) says Dunia Kashindi Fabien was designated provisional commander. No source found says when Mwaku took over or what became of Ilunga Kabamba. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les commandants de l'armée congolaise nouvellement nommés au Sud-Kivu sont arrivés dans la ville d'Uvira, ce mercredi 22 octobre 2025. Il s'agit notamment du général de brigade Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques, nouveau commandant de la 33ᵉ région militaire, et du général AMULI CIVIRI, commandant secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.

r1-UC-FARDC-006.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the army spokesperson of operational sector Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, sub-lieutenant Mbuyi Kalonji Reagan, said the new 33rd military region commander replaces the late brigade general Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, who died after feeling unwell while on duty, and that general Civiri replaces general Mwehu Lumbu Evariste.
r1-UC-FARDC-006.n: Predecessor chain for the 33rd military region and Sukola 2 Sud.
r1-UC-FARDC-006.vn: Excerpt supports every clause (spokesperson's statement). SOS Médias Burundi gives a different cause of death for Mwaku Mbuluku ('décédé récemment des suites d'une maladie') and the border post as Kavimvira-Gatumba (7sur7.cd: 'Kamvivira-Bujumbura'); both kept as each source prints. Cause of death differs: 7sur7.cd quotes the spokesperson as 'décédé de suites d'un malaise pendant son service'; SOS Médias Burundi writes 'décédé récemment des suites d’une maladie'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: le sous-lieutenant Mbuyi Kalonji Reagan, indique que ces généraux sont arrivés via la frontière Kamvivira-Bujumbura. Il rappelle que le nouveau commandant de la 33ᵉ région militaire remplace le feu général de brigade Mwaku Mbuluku Jean-Daniel, décédé de suites d'un malaise pendant son service, et le général Civiri remplace le général Mwehu Lumbu Evariste.

r1-UC-FARDC-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that general Olivier Gasita, in charge of intelligence and operations in the 33rd military region, was not affected by the October 2025 reshuffle and remained in post despite demonstrations in Uvira in September; the same report said that, according to several local sources, he had left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was staying in Kinshasa.
r1-UC-FARDC-007.n: Kivu Times (23 Oct 2025) separately says Gasita remained 'Commandant Région Adjoint' in charge of operations and intelligence, with no official communication on a replacement. The page goes on to say organisers' accusations referred to his Banyamulenge origin; not recorded here because the excerpt is cut in the source text I retained. A Facebook snippet earlier names Amuli Civiri as replacing Gasita in an operations post: unresolved, treat as conflict.
r1-UC-FARDC-007.vn: Excerpt supports the statement verbatim, but the same page qualifies 'remains in post' (see note). Single exile-based Burundian outlet. Same SOS Médias Burundi page: 'Selon plusieurs sources locales, le Général Gasita a quitté Uvira le 8 octobre 2025 et séjourne actuellement à Kinshasa.' It also says the September demonstrators denounced 'mauvaise gestion des opérations militaires' and cited his Banyamulenge origin, accusations some observers call a pretext. Actualite.cd (20 Sep 2025, cited in this unit for the Mwenga memorandum) separately says Wazalendo and some civil society actors in Uvira refused the posting of general Olivier Gasita as 'commandant second en charge des opérations et renseignements de la 33e région militaire'. A Facebook snippet naming Amuli Civiri as Gasita's replacement was not verified. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: left Uvira on 8 October 2025, staying in Kinshasa 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-019: 'Remained in post' leaves out a qualification printed on the same page: according to several local sources, Gasita left Uvira on 8 October 2025 and was in Kinshasa. A search found DW ('Retour au calme après "le départ" du général Gasita d'Uvira') and Kivu Morning Post ('Le Général Gasita quitte Uvira…'), which both report his departure from Uvira. 'In post' must not be read as 'present in Uvira'.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): left Uvira on 8 October 2025, staying in Kinshasa 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Certaines figures militaires controversées n’ont pas été concernées par ce remaniement. C’est le cas du Général Olivier Gasita, chargé du renseignement et des opérations au sein de la 33e Région Militaire, qui reste en poste malgré les manifestations organisées en septembre dernier à Uvira.
Selon plusieurs sources locales, le Général Gasita a quitté Uvira le 8 octobre 2025 et séjourne actuellement à Kinshasa.

r1-UC-FARDC-008.s: Congorassure.cd reported on 26 January 2026 that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien had been designated provisional commander of the 33rd military region, covering South Kivu and Maniema, according to an official note from the FARDC chief of general staff that the outlet said it had seen.
r1-UC-FARDC-008.n: Single outlet. Dunia Kashindi Fabien is already named 33rd military region commander in earlier coverage (12 April 2025 meeting at Runingu per Facebook snippets; 26 June 2025 per La Presse Africaine) and Ilunga Kabamba was named in October 2025: commander sequence in the 33rd region needs reconciliation. Page text also says the colonel Kavungiro Balimenyere Marc is assigned administration and logistics.
r1-UC-FARDC-008.vn: Excerpts support the statement; the official-note attribution is the outlet's ('consultée par CONGORASSURE.CD'). The '26' flag is the source date. The same note, per the outlet, names colonel Babadi Bakenge Jean-Philippe deputy commander for operations and intelligence, and colonel Kavungiro Balimenyere Marc for administration and logistics. See the 33rd military region sequence note on the 22 October 2025 arrival claim: Dunia Kashindi Fabien is also named commander in June 2025 (La Presse Africaine), before Mwaku Mbuluku and Ilunga Kabamba. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
