src: Le général de brigade Dunia Kashindi Fabien a été désigné commandant provisoire de la 33e région militaire, une zone stratégique couvrant les provinces du Sud-Kivu et du Maniema, dans un contexte sécuritaire particulièrement tendu dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

Selon une note officielle émanant du chef d’état-major général des Forces armées congolaises (FARDC), consultée par CONGORASSURE.CD , cette réorganisation du commandement prévoit également la nomination du colonel Babadi Bakenge Jean-Philippe comme commandant adjoint chargé des opérations et des renseignements.

r1-UC-FARDC-009.s: Congorassure.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi returned to Uvira on Friday 23 January after several weeks of absence, to the applause of the population, having left the city shortly before 10 December 2025.
r1-UC-FARDC-009.n: Single outlet; 'assaillants' is the outlet's wording for AFC/M23.
r1-UC-FARDC-009.vn: Excerpt states it verbatim; 23 January 2026 was a Friday. Single outlet; the 10 December 2025 capture date is the outlet's. Consistent with BBC Gahuza (18 Jan 2026), which says the governor was then in Bujumbura. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Vendredi 23 janvier, le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a effectué son retour à Uvira après plusieurs semaines d’absence, sous les applaudissements de la population. Il avait quitté la ville peu avant le 10 décembre 2025, date coïncidant avec sa prise par les assaillants.

r1-UC-FARDC-010.s: BBC Gahuza reported that Uvira residents confirmed that Wazalendo fighters entered the city on the morning of Sunday and FARDC soldiers entered in the evening, after AFC/M23 announced on Saturday that it had left the city 'fully'.
r1-UC-FARDC-010.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article published 18 January 2026, a Sunday). Kinshasa and Washington said M23 had not left Uvira earlier, per the same article; other units cover the M23 withdrawal statements.
r1-UC-FARDC-010.vn: Excerpt and next sentence support all clauses; 18 Jan 2026 (publication) was a Sunday. The '23' flag is 'AFC/M23'. Residents' account as reported by BBC Gahuza; Kinshasa and Washington had said M23 had not left after its earlier withdrawal announcement (same article). 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Abaturage mu mujyi wa Uvira bemeje ko abarwanyi ba Wazalendo binjiye muri uyu mujyi mu gitondo cyo kuri iki cyumweru, nyuma nimugoroba abasirikare ba FARDC na bo binjira muri Uvira.

r1-UC-FARDC-011.s: BBC Gahuza reported that the South Kivu governor on the government-controlled side, then in Bujumbura where he had taken refuge, said the government had information that some M23 fighters remained in Uvira, urged great caution and asked the population to avoid ethnic violence.
r1-UC-FARDC-011.n: Governor is not named in the passage (Congorassure names Jean-Jacques Purusi as governor who had left Uvira). Date computed from publication date.
r1-UC-FARDC-011.vn: Excerpt supports each clause. The excerpt_en flag is the word 'South' rendering 'Kivu y'Epfo'; the translation is faithful to the excerpt alone. Further down, BBC Gahuza names the governor 'Jean Jacques Pulusi Sadiki' (Congorassure.cd: 'Jean-Jacques Purusi') and reports, from his voice message to the BBC, that he said the remaining M23 fighters wore civilian clothes and were armed, and that M23 fighters had gone to positions at Sange and Luvungi.
src: Guverineri w'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo ahagenzurwa na leta, uri i Bujumbura mu Burundi aho yahungiye, yatangaje ko bafite amakuru ko hari abarwanyi ba M23 basigaye muri Uvira, ati: "Ni ukwitonda cyane", yasabye kandi abatura kwirinda urugomo rushingiye ku moko.

r1-UC-FARDC-012.s: BBC Gahuza reported that other videos circulating on social media showed looting that took place after the M23 fighters left Uvira; the passage does not attribute the looting.
r1-UC-FARDC-012.n: Videos not verified by the outlet in this passage.
r1-UC-FARDC-012.vn: Excerpt supports it; unverified social-media videos, looting unattributed.
src: Andi mashusho yagaragaje ibikorwa by'ubusahuzi byabaye nyuma yo 'kugenda' kw'abarwanyi ba M23.

r1-UC-FARDC-013.s: Mediacongo reported that the High Military Court opened debate in Kinshasa on Friday 25 September (2026) in the case of two general-majors prosecuted for their alleged role in the loss of Bukavu during the AFC/M23 offensive in South Kivu in 2025: Robert Anvul Yav, who then commanded the South Kivu military region, and André Ehonza Uketi, former head of operations Sukola 2 Nord.
r1-UC-FARDC-013.n: Name spellings differ across outlets: Mediacongo 'Robert Anvul Yav'; Jeune Afrique (2 Oct 2026, paywalled) 'Robert Yav Avul Ngola' and says the two generals are tried since 25 September; RFI snippet 'Robert Avul Yav'. Verify before profiling. Year of the opening taken from page date 25.09.2026.
r1-UC-FARDC-013.vn: Both excerpts verbatim; 25 Sep 2026 was a Friday. Stage is 'prévenus' / 'poursuivis' (accused, prosecuted), not convicted; the page stresses the facts remain accusations. Spelling kept as Mediacongo prints it. Name spelling differs across outlets and is not reconciled: Mediacongo prints 'Robert Anvul Yav'; per the research notes (pages not retained, not verified here) Jeune Afrique prints 'Robert Yav Avul Ngola' and an RFI snippet 'Robert Avul Yav'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: La Haute Cour militaire ouvre ce vendredi 25 septembre à Kinshasa les débats dans le dossier de deux généraux-majors poursuivis pour leur rôle présumé dans la perte de Bukavu lors de l’offensive de l’AFC/M23 au Sud-Kivu, en 2025.
Les prévenus sont Robert Anvul Yav, qui commandait alors la région militaire du Sud-Kivu, et André Ehonza Uketi, ancien responsable des opérations Sukola 2 Nord.

r1-UC-FARDC-015.a: FARDC officers (as alleged by the prosecution)

Selon les éléments de l’accusation rapportés dans le dossier, certains équipements remis étaient défectueux et certaines munitions périmées.

r1-UC-FARDC-016.s: Mediacongo reported that, in earlier hearings, the two accused generals contested the prosecution's reading of events, explaining that AFC/M23 forces had a significant advantage in men and equipment.
r1-UC-FARDC-016.a: Robert Anvul Yav; André Ehonza Uketi (the accused)

r1-UC-FARDC-017.s: Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court handed prison sentences of under five years to four general officers of the army and police accused of fleeing before the enemy in the east, and that its first president, lieutenant general magistrate Joseph Mutombo, announced that divisional commissioner Jean Romuald Ekuka, former vice-governor of North Kivu, was sentenced to 36 months in prison (the page prints the offence as 'libertété').
r1-UC-FARDC-017.n: Radio Okapi relays ACP; page prints 'libertété' (sic, evidently lâcheté). The page does not state which battle; other outlets link the case to the fall of Goma (not fetched).
r1-UC-FARDC-017.vn: The page does not say 'cowardice' for Ekuka: it prints 'libertété', likely a typo, so the offence is kept as printed; added the court president and the under-five-years framing. The verdict date (Friday 5 December, a Friday in 2025) is on the page next to the excerpt and kept in the date field. Wire copy credited to ACP. The page does not say which battle. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

r1-UC-FARDC-018.s: Radio Okapi, citing ACP, reported that the High Military Court president said deputy divisional commissioner Eddy Léonard Mukuna was sentenced to 24 months for cowardice, brigade general Papy Lupembe to 12 months for cowardice before the enemy, and Danny Yangba Tene to 12 months in prison for the same charge.

r1-UC-FARDC-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that about ten Wazalendo groups active in Mwenga and Shabunda territories wrote to the President and the FARDC chief of general staff demanding the replacement of commander Tshihutu Vela of the 3306 regiment based in Mwenga, accusing him in a joint memorandum, among other grievances, of appropriating arms and ammunition at the expense of the other groups.
r1-UC-FARDC-019.a: Wazalendo groups of Mwenga and Shabunda; FARDC 3306 regiment
r1-UC-FARDC-019.n: Date is the page date; memorandum date not stated. Memorandum allegations against the commander and a provincial politician (also named on the page) are the Wazalendo groups' claims, not findings.
r1-UC-FARDC-019.vn: Both excerpts verbatim; memorandum allegations are the groups'. Page also says the memorandum followed two days of tension between two Wazalendo groups, one allegedly backed by the regiment commander, with 8 dead per local civil society (lead, not recorded here). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Une dizaine de groupes de Wazalendo, actifs dans les territoires de Mwenga et Shabunda dans la province du Sud-Kivu, ont écrit au président de la République et au chef d'Etat-Major des FARDC pour réclamer le remplacement du commandant Tshihutu Vela du régiment 3306 basé à Mwenga.
Dans un mémorandum conjointement signé par ces derniers, ils accusent leur collaborateur de plusieurs autres griefs notamment " s'accaparer d'armes et munitions au détriment des autres groupes

r1-UC-FARDC-020.s: Actualite.cd reported that commander Tshihutu is also accused, in collaboration with former provincial interior minister Albert Foka Maik, of appropriating the retrocession of 48.000 USD (as the page prints it) given by the province each month to the Wazalendo of Mwenga-Shabunda.
r1-UC-FARDC-020.a: Wazalendo groups of Mwenga and Shabunda (allegation)
r1-UC-FARDC-020.n: Allegation by armed groups against a commander and a politician; no response found.

Allegation by armed groups, no response found. The same page later names 'l'Honorable Albert Kahasha Murhula alias Foka-Mike'; whether this is the same person as 'Albert Foka Maik' is not stated by the page. The page also relays 'other sources' saying 50.000 USD is received from Chinese operators at the Karhembo Kala gold site (not recorded). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

r1-UC-FARDC-021.s: La Presse Africaine reported that brigade general Dunia Kashindi Fabien, 33rd military region commander, said at the funeral of self-proclaimed Wazalendo general Rukumeta Biriho Pierre in Uvira on Thursday 26 June 2025 that the Wazalendo were giving everything for the defence of South Kivu and had sworn never to betray Congo or Uvira.
r1-UC-FARDC-021.n: Local outlet with a patriotic framing ('barbare', 'balkanisation'); cited only for what the general said. The page's own account of how the deceased died is garbled and not recorded.
r1-UC-FARDC-021.vn: Excerpts plus page support each clause; 26 June 2025 is printed as 'ce jeudi 26 juin 2025'. Local outlet with patriotic framing; cited only for what the general said. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: C’est par le général de brigade Dunia Kashindi Fabien, commandant de la 33e région militaire, à l’occasion des funérailles du général autoproclamé des Wazalendo Rukumeta Biriho Pierre décédé le 14 juin dernier après s’être tiré dessus à Kageregere dans le champ de bataille le 26 mai 2025.

« Les Wazalendo sont en train de tout donner pour la défense de cette province du Sud-Kivu. Ce sont eux, jour et nuit, quelles que soient les intempéries, quelles que soient les conditions difficiles, qui ont prêté serment de ne jamais trahir le Congo, de ne jamais trahir Uvira

r1-UC-FARDC-022.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within a 10-kilometre radius of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and quoted a community leader saying they killed seven people and destroyed houses, health centers and schools.
r1-UC-FARDC-022.x: HRW (community leader quoted): seven people killed
r1-UC-FARDC-022.n: HRW also reports it used satellite imagery and geolocated photographs to confirm that houses were burned in Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko on that day, and interviewed relatives of a 60-year-old man and a 25-year-old man killed (not named). A military source said there was no known presence of opposing armed groups near Bibokoboko at the time. Some of this probably already exists in other units: check at promote.
r1-UC-FARDC-022.vn: Both excerpts verbatim; HRW documented investigation. The death toll is the quoted community leader's figure. HRW adds (same page) that it interviewed relatives of a 60-year-old man and a 25-year-old man killed in the attack, and used satellite imagery and verified, geolocated photographs to confirm houses were burned in Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko that day; a military source and residents said no opposing armed groups were known to be near Bibokoboko at the time.
src: On March 3, Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within a 10-kilometer radius around Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, South Kivu.

“They [the Wazalendo] said we are not Congolese, that we are Rwandan. They said they came to Bibokoboko to ‘clean out’ the Banyamulenge,” a community leader said. “They killed seven people and destroyed houses, health centers, and schools.”

r1-UC-FARDC-023.s: Human Rights Watch quoted a Banyamulenge community leader as saying that Wazalendo fighters who attacked villages around Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, in the 3 March 2025 attack destroyed health centers, among other buildings.
r1-UC-FARDC-023.a: Wazalendo (as alleged by a community leader quoted by HRW)
r1-UC-FARDC-023.x: Number of health centers not stated
r1-UC-FARDC-023.n: Single quoted community-leader claim; HRW's satellite imagery confirmation refers to burned houses, not to health centers. Facility names not given.
r1-UC-FARDC-023.vn: Supported; the '3' flag resolved by a replacement passage that carries the 3 March date with the quote. HRW's imagery confirmation covers burned houses, not health centers, so the health-center destruction rests on one quoted community leader. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: “They [the Wazalendo] said we are not Congolese, that we are Rwandan. They said they came to Bibokoboko to ‘clean out’ the Banyamulenge,” a community leader said. “They killed seven people and destroyed houses, health centers, and schools.”
Les structures sanitaires locales ont été pillées, laissant la population sans accès aux soins de santé.

r1-UC-FARDC-024.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander detained and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.
r1-UC-FARDC-024.a: a Wazalendo commander (not named in the passage)
r1-UC-FARDC-024.x: HRW: one 48-year-old man, died according to a relative and a neighbour
r1-UC-FARDC-024.n: HRW adds that the commander, later implicated in the killing of a Congolese soldier, was removed from his post but has not faced prosecution (next sentences of the release). Victim not named.
r1-UC-FARDC-024.vn: Excerpt verbatim; HRW documented. Commander and victim not named. HRW adds that the commander, later implicated in the killing of a Congolese soldier, was removed from his post but has not faced prosecution for the killings.
src: On March 3, in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander detained and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television. A relative and a neighbor said the man died of his injuries.

r1-UC-FARDC-025.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira, after accusing him of being Rwandan, shooting him twice in the hip; he died from his injuries according to two sources.
r1-UC-FARDC-025.vn: Excerpt verbatim; HRW documented, two sources. Victim not named.
src: On February 14, Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira, after accusing him of being Rwandan. They shot him twice in the hip, and he died from his injuries, according to two sources.

r1-UC-FARDC-026.s: Human Rights Watch reported that, following the M23's capture of Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered over 20 Banyamulenge households in Uvira, stealing goods and threatening residents, and in one case shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.
r1-UC-FARDC-026.x: HRW: over 20 households; at least three people beaten; one woman shot
r1-UC-FARDC-026.n: Date is 'following the capture of Bukavu' (mid-February 2025); exact days not given.
r1-UC-FARDC-026.vn: Excerpt verbatim; date only 'following the M23's capture of Bukavu'.
src: Following the M23’s capture of Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered over 20 Banyamulenge households in Uvira, stealing goods and threatening residents. In one case, they shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.

r1-UC-FARDC-027.s: Human Rights Watch reported that the interim governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told the media on April 23 that the province was unable to collect taxes because of the Wazalendo fighters, who should 'not take the place of the state'.
r1-UC-FARDC-027.n: Relayed by HRW; original media report not retrieved.
r1-UC-FARDC-027.vn: Excerpt verbatim; HRW relays a media statement (original media report not retrieved).
src: The interim governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told the media on April 23 that the province was unable to collect taxes because of the Wazalendo fighters, who should “not take the place of the state.”

r1-UC-FARDC-028.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on April 4 an armed group commander wrote to President Félix Tshisekedi complaining that Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi, a National Assembly member who coordinates support for the Wazalendo coalition in South Kivu, was not fully distributing government funding to all Wazalendo armed groups.
r1-UC-FARDC-028.a: Wazalendo armed group commander (unnamed); Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi
r1-UC-FARDC-028.n: Allegation by an unnamed commander as relayed by HRW. HRW also cites the UN Group of Experts on Bitakwira's alleged hate speech (not recorded here).
r1-UC-FARDC-028.vn: Excerpt verbatim; the complaint is the unnamed commander's, relayed by HRW.
src: On April 4, an armed group commander wrote to President Félix Tshisekedi complaining that Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi, a member of the National Assembly who coordinates support for the Wazalendo coalition in South Kivu, was not fully distributing government funding to all the Wazalendo armed groups.

r1-UC-FARDC-029.s: Human Rights Watch reported that military and other sources estimate about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters, although the exact figure is unknown, and that in September 2023 some members of the coalition formed the Patriotic Defense Volunteers (VDP), an 'official' auxiliary force.
r1-UC-FARDC-029.x: HRW: about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters (military and other sources' estimate)
r1-UC-FARDC-029.n: Estimate, with HRW's own caveat. Date is the report date; the VDP formation (Sept 2023) is background.
r1-UC-FARDC-029.vn: Excerpt verbatim; estimate with HRW's own caveat.
ent: Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie
src: Military and other sources estimate there are currently about 20,000 Wazalendo fighters, although the exact figure is unknown. In September 2023, some members of the Wazalendo coalition formed the Patriotic Defense Volunteers (Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie, VDP), an “official” auxiliary force.

r1-UC-FARDC-030.s: Human Rights Watch reported that military, humanitarian and other sources expressed concern about the Congolese army's lack of command and control over the Wazalendo, who in some instances have reportedly disarmed or attacked Congolese soldiers.
r1-UC-FARDC-030.n: Context for FARDC-Wazalendo relations; see also the Umunota 8 May 2025 claim.
src: Military, humanitarian, and other sources expressed concern about the Congolese army’s lack of command and control over the Wazalendo, who in some instances have reportedly disarmed or attacked Congolese soldiers.

r1-UC-FARDC-031.s: Umunota, a Rwandan outlet, reported, citing information from Uvira, that heavy gunfire heard overnight in Uvira city was fired at FARDC soldiers who had gone to steal in Murugenge, Kavimvira, and that local Wazalendo then intervened and exchanged fire with them for about an hour and a half.
r1-UC-FARDC-031.a: FARDC soldiers (accused of looting) and Wazalendo, as the outlet says
r1-UC-FARDC-031.n: Single Rwandan outlet, unnamed sources; no corroboration found. Rwanda is a party to the conflict, so the outlet's framing of FARDC may be partisan. Lead only.
r1-UC-FARDC-031.vn: Removed the date from the statement (the page dates it to the night into Thursday 08/05/2025, kept in the date field) and added who fired (local Wazalendo) from the following sentence. Single Rwandan outlet (Rwanda is a party), unnamed sources; lead only. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Umunota (Kinyarwanda, 8 May 2025) supports every clause, citing information from Uvira; the stored excerpt carries only the gunfire-at-FARDC clause, so the passage on local Wazalendo intervening and the hour-and-a-half exchange is added.
src: Amakuru aturuka uvira ahamya ko ariya masasu yarimo araswa abasirikare ba FARDC bari bagiye kwiba i Kavimvira mu gace kayo kitwa Murugenge.
Nyuma yaho aba basirikare bimenyekanye ko baje kwiba, ni bwo wazalendo bo muri ako gace batabaye maze zikozanyaho nabo umuriro uraka mu rugamba rwamaze igihe kingana n’isaha n’igice.

r1-UC-M23-001.s: Actualite.cd, summarising a UN Group of Experts report transmitted to the Security Council, reported that the experts wrote that the offensive on Uvira was carried out under the direct command of Makenga and Byamungu, and that James Kabarebe, a retired RDF general, was established to have played a key role in coordinating it.
r1-UC-M23-001.l: Uvira and the Bukavu-Uvira corridor, South Kivu
r1-UC-M23-001.a: AFC/M23 (Makenga, Byamungu); retired RDF general James Kabarebe as coordinator, per the report
r1-UC-M23-001.n: Relay of the UN GoE report (S/2026/466, 5 June 2026 per UN list), read by the outlet on 1 July 2026; the quoted sentences are the report's. Should be corroborated against the report text itself. The article gives 'MM. Makenga et Byamungu' without first names.
r1-UC-M23-001.vn: Excerpt on retained page; quote is the outlet's French rendering of the GoE report. Checked against the retained S/2026/466 text (para. 75: 'conducted under the direct command of Mr. Makenga and Mr. Byamungu. Retired RDF General James Kabarebe'), which matches. Attribution to the Group kept. The underlying report (S/2026/466, letter dated 5 June 2026) is retained and says the same; the outlet gives surnames only.
src: « L’offensive sur Uvira a été menée sous le commandement direct de MM. Makenga et Byamungu. Il a été établi que James Kabarebe, général à la retraite de la RDF, avait joué un rôle clé dans la coordination de l’offensive.

r1-UC-M23-002.s: Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that the experts recalled that Uvira was taken on 10 December 2025 and that AFC/M23 and RDF forces advanced rapidly south as far as Makobola, about twenty kilometres from Uvira.
r1-UC-M23-002.a: AFC/M23 and RDF forces, per the report
r1-UC-M23-002.n: Relay of the UN GoE report. Date of capture as stated by the report via Actualite.cd; other outlets give 10-12 December (Kigali Today says 12 December), a discrepancy to settle in the Uvira units.
r1-UC-M23-002.vn: Exact excerpt; matches S/2026/466 para. 74 ('The capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 and the rapid advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF forces southwards to Makobola, 20 km south of Uvira'). excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact (AFC/M23 casing); translation is faithful. Other outlets give 10-12 December for the capture of Uvira; this date is the Group's.
src: le Groupe d’experts rappelle que la prise d’Uvira, le 10 décembre 2025, et l’avancée rapide des forces de l’AFC/M23 et de la RDF vers le sud, jusqu’à Makobola, située à une vingtaine de kilomètres d’Uvira

r1-UC-M23-003.s: Actualite.cd, relaying a UN Group of Experts report, reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 after sustained international diplomatic pressure.
r1-UC-M23-003.a: AFC/M23 and RDF troops, per the report
r1-UC-M23-003.n: Relay of UN GoE report. The same article quotes the report as calling the withdrawal 'a strategic manoeuvre' followed by redeployment to adjacent areas; AFC/M23 presented it as a goodwill gesture. Party accounts of the withdrawal belong to the Uvira units.
r1-UC-M23-003.vn: Exact excerpt; matches S/2026/466 para. 77 ('eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, following sustained international diplomatic pressure'). The Group adds that the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas (per Actualite.cd's quotation of the report).
src: les troupes de l’AFC/M23 et de la RDF se sont finalement retirées de la ville le 18 janvier 2026, à la suite de pressions diplomatiques internationales soutenues.

r1-UC-M23-004.s: The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that John Imani Nzenze is an M23 commander and M23's chief of intelligence, regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, whom it described as the U.S.- and UN-sanctioned overall military commander of M23.
r1-UC-M23-004.l: North and South Kivu (M23 area of operations)
r1-UC-M23-004.n: Official designation text of a sanctioning government (attribute to OFAC). The same release says the designation was 'in close coordination with the United Nations'. Province left as 'other' because the release names no territory for Nzenze.
r1-UC-M23-004.vn: Exact excerpt; page dated June 2, 2026 confirms the designation. Publication date taken out of the statement (shown with the source). A sanctions designation states the designating government's finding, not a judicial one.
src: John Imani Nzenze ( Nzenze )is an M23 commander and M23’s chief of intelligence. He is regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, the U.S.- and UN-sanctioned overall military commander of M23.

r1-UC-M23-005.s: The U.S. Department of the Treasury stated that, following the 15 November 2025 signing in Qatar of a peace framework agreement between the DRC government and M23, M23 seized Uvira and later withdrew, while still controlling Goma and Bukavu.
r1-UC-M23-005.n: Excerpt spans three adjacent sentences of the release. Release text says 'Following the signing, M23 seized the strategic port city of Uvira' and that M23 'eventually withdrew'.
r1-UC-M23-005.vn: Exact excerpt; publication date removed from the statement.
src: On November 15, 2025, the DRC government and M23 signed a peace framework agreement in Qatar. Following the signing, M23 seized the strategic port city of Uvira located in South Kivu province along the DRC-Burundi border. Although M23 eventually withdrew from Uvira, the rebel group still controls Goma and Bukavu,

r1-UC-M23-006.s: The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston is M23's civilian spokesperson and a public relations officer for the Congo River Alliance, which it described as a U.S.-sanctioned coalition of rebel groups that seeks to overthrow the DRC government.
r1-UC-M23-006.a: M23 / Congo River Alliance (Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston)
r1-UC-M23-006.n: Official sanctions text; the characterisation of the AFC is the U.S. government's. Same release designates two companies owned by Kanyuka (Kingston Fresh, Kingston Holding).
r1-UC-M23-006.vn: Exact excerpt; page dated February 20, 2025. Date removed from the statement.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka Kingston ( Kanyuka ) is M23’s civilian spokesperson and a public relations officer for the Congo River Alliance, a U.S.-sanctioned coalition of rebel groups that seeks to overthrow the DRC government.

r1-UC-M23-007.s: The U.S. Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions on him, said that James Kabarebe, a former RDF general and Rwanda's Minister of State for Regional Integration, is a Rwandan government liaison to M23 and orchestrates RDF support for the armed group.
r1-UC-M23-007.a: James Kabarebe (Rwanda) / M23 / RDF, per OFAC
r1-UC-M23-007.n: U.S. government allegation in a sanctions release; Rwanda's government rejected the designation as 'unjustified and unfounded' (snippet seen in search results, not fetched; a Rwandan party-statement unit should fetch the primary).
r1-UC-M23-007.vn: Exact excerpt carries the liaison clause; name and post are printed on the same page (clause_support). Date removed from the statement.
src: Kabarebe is a Rwandan government liaison to M23 and orchestrates RDF support for the armed group.

r1-UC-M23-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the European Union announced sanctions on M23 figures including Bertrand Bisimwa (head of the political wing, already under UN sanctions), 'Jean Bahati Musanga' [as printed by Radio Okapi] (North Kivu governor appointed by the rebels), Désiré Rukomera (in charge of M23 recruitment and propaganda) and Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa (deputy head of finance).
r1-UC-M23-008.l: North Kivu (M23-appointed governorate) and M23 structures
r1-UC-M23-008.n: Radio Okapi says Bisimwa was 'already under UN sanctions'; the CRG/CIC report (April 2026) lists his earlier sanction as a US one (25 July 2024) and EU (17 March 2025), not UN. Not resolved here. The EU Council press release (consilium.europa.eu) could not be fetched by the page helper; verifier should use it as primary.
r1-UC-M23-008.vn: Exact excerpt; page published 17/03/2025 says 'L’Union européenne a annoncé, lundi 17 mars'. Date removed from statement; 'already under UN sanctions' added from the excerpt. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact. Name discrepancy: Radio Okapi prints 'Jean Bahati Musanga'; the UN Group of Experts prints 'Bahati Musanga Joseph' / 'Joseph Bahati Musanga' (alias Bahati Erasto) and Actualite.cd 'Joseph Musanga Bahati' for the M23-appointed North Kivu governor. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Namesake check: a search for the EU listing shows other outlets (opinion-info.cd, heshimardc.net) and the UN Group of Experts naming the governor 'Joseph Bahati Musanga' / 'Bahati Musanga Joseph', while Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd and Mediacongo print 'Jean'. The first name is unreliable; mark it as printed and link the person to the Group's 'Bahati Musanga Joseph' profile only with that caveat. The EU regulation (2025/509) was not fetched.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'Jean Bahati Musanga' is printed in source 0
src: Bertrand Bisimwa, chef de l’aile politique du groupe armé, qui était déjà sous sanctions des Nations unies. Jean Bahati Musanga, gouverneur du Nord-Kivu nommé par les rebelles, ainsi que Désiré Rukomera, responsable du recrutement et de la propagande du M23, et Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa, chef adjoint des finances du groupe, sont également concernés.

r1-UC-M23-009.s: Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that M23 chief of staff General Sultani Makenga has been under UN, US and EU sanctions since November and December 2012, and that General Baudouin Ngaruye, commander of the first operational sector, and Innocent Kaina are under the same three regimes since the same period.
r1-UC-M23-009.n: Relay of CRG/CIC; the underlying report is cited separately. CRG/CIC's own sanctions table is garbled in text extraction for Ngaruye (shows 'United Nati...' truncated), so the 'three regimes' claim for Ngaruye rests on this article.
r1-UC-M23-009.vn: Exact excerpt; page says 'selon un rapport publié en avril 2026 par le Congo Research Group (CRG) et le Center on International Cooperation (CIC)'. Sanction dates are the outlet's summary of the CRG report, not checked against the sanctions lists. excerpt_en flag is a translation artefact.
src: Le chef d'état-major du M23, le général Sultani Makenga, est sous sanctions onusiennes, américaines et européennes depuis novembre et décembre 2012, pour violations graves du droit international humanitaire. Le général Baudouin Ngaruye, commandant du premier secteur opérationnel, et Innocent Kaina, figure influente du mouvement, font l'objet des mêmes trois régimes de sanctions depuis la même période.

r1-UC-M23-010.s: Afrikarabia reported that Willy Ngoma, military spokesperson of the AFC/M23, was killed by a drone strike and that, according to first indications, the drone attack was launched by the Congolese army at Rubaya, Masisi territory; Actualite.cd, in an article on a CRG/CIC report, described him as former spokesperson and military commander of M23 and wrote that he was killed on 24 February 2026 in a drone strike near the Rubaya mining site, North Kivu.
r1-UC-M23-010.a: Drone strike attributed to the Congolese army per Afrikarabia's 'first indications'; target AFC/M23 military spokesperson Willy Ngoma
r1-UC-M23-010.n: Afrikarabia (Christophe Rigaud) calls Ngoma 'porte-parole militaire'; Actualite.cd/CRG calls him 'ancien porte-parole et commandant militaire'. EU sanction date differs: Afrikarabia says December 2022; Actualite.cd/CRG says April 2024 (UN Feb 2024). Kinshasa and AFC/M23 reactions not found in this unit; see gaps. The page says 'ce mardi' and is dated 24 Feb 2026 (a Tuesday); RFI (via Facebook, not fetched) reports 'night of 23 to 24 February'.
r1-UC-M23-010.vn: All three excerpts exact. Attribution to the Congolese army kept as Afrikarabia's 'first indications', not a finding. Publication date of Afrikarabia removed; the 24 February 2026 date is Actualite.cd's. Afrikarabia also notes Kinshasa had issued no communiqué. Afrikarabia wrote that Kinshasa had published no communiqué on the strike ('Aucun communiqué n’a été publié pour l’instant'). EU sanction date differs between the outlets (Afrikarabia: December 2022; Actualite.cd: April 2024).
src: Willy Ngoma, porte-parole militaire de l’AFC/M23, a été tué par une frappe de drone ce mardi.
Selon les premiers éléments, ce haut cadre a été frappé par une attaque de drone lancée par l’armée congolaise à Rubaya, dans le territoire de Masisi.

Willy Ngoma, ancien porte-parole et commandant militaire du M23, avait été sanctionné par l'ONU en février 2024 et par l'Union européenne en avril 2024. Il a été tué le 24 février 2026 dans une frappe de drone près du site minier de Rubaya, au Nord-Kivu.

r1-UC-M23-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the overall military command of AFC/M23 remained under 'General' Sultani Makenga, with political leadership held by Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa.
r1-UC-M23-011.n: Date is the report date (3 July 2025); describes the situation across the reporting period, not one day. The same paragraph states that Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa were in frequent contact with Makenga and Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that Nangaa was gradually sidelined by Rwanda.
r1-UC-M23-011.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 para. 8; the Group's finding.
src: The overall military command of Alliance Fleuve Congo/Mouvement du 23 mars (AFC/M23) remained under “General” Sultani Makenga (CDi.008), and political leadership with Bertrand Bisimwa and Corneille Nangaa.

r1-UC-M23-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa remained in frequent contact with Makenga, Bisimwa and 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze, and that the military and political leadership of AFC/M23 continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services.
r1-UC-M23-012.a: AFC/M23 leadership; Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services, per the Group of Experts
r1-UC-M23-012.n: Report date used; GoE footnote says Ngenzi frequently travelled between Kigali and Goma. Rwanda has contested the Group's findings in other settings (no statement fetched here).
r1-UC-M23-012.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 para. 8; both clauses in the single excerpt; stated as the Group's finding.
src: The military and political leadership of AFC/M23 continued to receive instructions and support from the Government of Rwanda and its intelligence services (see paras. 34–56 below). The Rwandan-Congolese national Fred Ngenzi Kagorora 1 and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa remained in frequent contact with Messrs. Makenga and Bisimwa and “Colonel” Imani Nzenze.

r1-UC-M23-013.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 5 February 2025 AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments, designating Bahati Musanga Joseph (also known as Bahati Erasto) as governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shaddrak as deputy governors.
r1-UC-M23-013.n: Same report notes (para. 98, video footage) that on 6 February 2025 Bahati Erasto spoke in Kinyarwanda justifying house-to-house operations. Kinshasa's spokesperson Patrick Muyaya was quoted in a Facebook post (not fetched) calling the appointment information false; to be sourced from a news outlet.
r1-UC-M23-013.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 annex; names as printed. The same report also prints 'Joseph Bahati Musanga (alias Bahati Erasto)'; Radio Okapi prints 'Jean Bahati Musanga'.
src: On 5 February 2025, AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments with the aim of formalizing its control and authority. It designated Bahati Musanga Joseph, also known as Bahati Erasto (S/2024/432, paras. 35, 36 and 102) as governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy and Amani Bahati Shaddrak as deputy governors.

r1-UC-M23-014.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 28 February AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments in South Kivu, naming Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba as governor with Dunia Musumbuko Bwenge and Gishinge Gasinzira Juvénal as deputy governors.
r1-UC-M23-014.n: Year inferred from the report's context (2025 report, appointments after Bukavu capture). Crisis Group (snippet, not fetched) says M23 quickly replaced Birato; CRG/CIC annex lists Patrick Busu Bwa Ngwi / Manu Birato moved to Goma (garbled table), so later governor changes need a separate claim once fetched.
r1-UC-M23-014.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 annex. The same report spells the governor 'Emmanuel Birato Rwihimbwa' in para. 26 and 'Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba' in the annex.
src: On 28 February, the AFC/M23 announced new administrative appointments in South Kivu. It appointed Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba as the governor of South Kivu, with Dunia Musumbuko Bwenge and Gishinge Gasinzira Juvénal as deputy governors.

r1-UC-M23-015.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained two principal intelligence entities: the Directorate of Security and Intelligence, headed by Basile Gasigwa (a.k.a. 'Gas'), and a military intelligence unit led by 'Colonel' Imani Nzenze.
r1-UC-M23-015.n: Report date used. The next sentences in the report say these bodies are responsible for surveillance, arrests, identity checks and internal punitive actions and that Gasigwa reports to Makenga.
r1-UC-M23-015.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/446 para. 96; the Group's finding. The report adds that Gasigwa reports to Makenga.
ent: Direction de sûreté et de renseignement
src: AFC/M23 maintains two principal intelligence entities: the Directorate of Security and Intelligence (Direction de sûreté et de renseignement), comprising intelligence and immigration services, headed by Basile Gasigwa, a.k.a. “Gas”; 102 and a military intelligence unit, led by “Colonel” Imani Nzenze.

r1-UC-M23-016.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources confirmed 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa was in command of all training centres, with the support of AFC/M23 and Rwandan trainers.
r1-UC-M23-016.l: AFC/M23 training centres (locations not given in excerpt)
r1-UC-M23-016.a: AFC/M23 (Léon Kanyamibwa) with Rwandan trainers, per the Group of Experts
r1-UC-M23-016.n: Report date used. Related: forced recruitment context appears in the same section; not recorded here.
r1-UC-M23-016.vn: Exact excerpt; the Group reports what AFC/M23 sources confirmed, and the statement keeps that attribution. The same paragraph names AFC/M23 camps at Tshanzu, Rutshuru, Bwito, Bwiza and Nyongera.
src: AFC/M23 sources confirmed that “Colonel” Léon Kanyamibwa was in command of all training centres, with the support of AFC/M23 and Rwandan trainers

r1-UC-M23-017.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 August 2025 'General' Sultani Makenga unveiled the AFC/M23 'elite police force' under the movement's internal security structure, named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC), placed under the command of 'Colonel' Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.
r1-UC-M23-017.l: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
r1-UC-M23-017.n: The report adds that the new police units were deployed primarily in Goma and Bukavu and that insiders reported RDF elements embedded in the M23/PRC (not in the excerpt, so not asserted).
r1-UC-M23-017.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2025/858 para. 28; names and ranks (in quotation marks as printed) match.
src: On 24 August 2025, “General” Sultani Makenga (CDi.008) unveiled the AFC/M23 “elite police force” operating under the movement’s internal security structure. 26 Named Police révolutionnaire congolaise (M23/PRC) (see annex 11), it was placed under the command of “Colonel” Guillaume Eboko, a former FARDC officer.

r1-UC-M23-018.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 14 September AFC/M23 publicized the 'pass-out' of 7,437 'commandos' who had finished their training in Rumangabo; that the graduation ceremony was presided over by 'General' Sultani Makenga and AFC Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa, who said the cohort would form four brigades of 'commando' units; and that the Group could not independently confirm the number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23.
r1-UC-M23-018.x: AFC/M23: 7,437 'commandos' (announced; not independently confirmed by the Group)
r1-UC-M23-018.n: Rumangabo is in Rutshuru territory (place not stated in the excerpts; identify via gazetteer). Report also quotes Kanyuka calling the cohort an 'elite unit' of ex-FARDC, Mai-Mai Wazalendo and new recruits.
r1-UC-M23-018.vn: All excerpts exact (S/2025/858). Narrowed: the excerpt says AFC/M23 'publicized' the pass-out on 14 September, not that the ceremony took place that day. The Group adds that security and intelligence sources considered the numbers likely inflated, while AFC/M23 imagery shows several thousand combatants.
src: On 14 September, AFC/M23 publicized the “pass-out” of 7,437 “commandos” who had finished their training in Rumangabo.
The Group could not independently confirm the precise number of 7,437 announced by AFC/M23.

The graduation ceremony was presided over by AFC/M23-ARC121 commander “General” Sultani Makenga (CDi.008) and AFC’s Political Coordinator, Corneille Nangaa. In his address, Nangaa stated that the cohort would form four brigades of “commando” units and claimed that an additional 12,000 recruits would undergo the next phase of ARC military and ideological training.

r1-UC-M23-019.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 October AFC/M23 announced the graduation of an additional 9,350 'commandos' at the Tchanzu training centre, a number the Group could not independently confirm, and that 'General' Sultani Makenga presided over the ceremony, attended also by 'Colonel' Léon Kanyamibwa, AFC/M23 commander in charge of trainings.
r1-UC-M23-019.l: Tchanzu training centre, Rutshuru, North Kivu
r1-UC-M23-019.x: AFC/M23: 9,350 'commandos' (announced; not independently confirmed by the Group)
r1-UC-M23-019.n: Territory not in the excerpt; the Tchanzu centre location is for the gazetteer to confirm.
r1-UC-M23-019.vn: Both excerpts exact (S/2025/858). Rephrased to follow the excerpt ('announced the graduation'); the Group also could not confirm the 9,350 figure. The Group wrote that it could not independently confirm the numbers of 7,437 and 9,350 publicized by AFC/M23. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: S/2025/858 para. 23 and annex 9 carry every clause; the statement omitted the Group's own caveat in annex 9 that it could not independently confirm the 9,350 figure, which is added (the claim's figures field already notes it). 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: S/2025/858 para. 23 and annex 9 carry every clause; the statement omitted the Group's own caveat in annex 9 that it could not independently confirm the 9,350 figure, which is added (the claim's figures field already notes it).
src: On 1 October, it announced the graduation of an additional 9,350 “commandos” at the Tchanzu training centre.
“General” Sultani Makenga presided over the ceremony, which was attended also by “Colonel” Léon Kanyamibwa, AFC/M23 commander in charge of trainings (S/2025/446, para. 24).
The Group could not independently confirm the numbers of 7,437 and 9,350 publicized by AFC/M23 (see below).

r1-UC-M23-020.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma, targeting Heal Africa on 1 March and CBCA Ndosho on 3 March (2025) in operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered, and that a total of 164 patients were abducted, 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho; it reported that AFC/M23 leaders Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga publicly denied responsibility.
r1-UC-M23-020.l: Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals, Goma, North Kivu
r1-UC-M23-020.x: UN Group of Experts: 164 patients abducted (48 from Heal Africa, 116 from CBCA Ndosho)
r1-UC-M23-020.n: Year 2025 from the report (para. 105 and following paragraph on April 2025). Report adds that male caregivers were briefly detained and released and that on 5 March AFC/M23 searched Virunga Hospital, arresting an unconfirmed number of suspected FARDC elements.
r1-UC-M23-020.vn: Both excerpts exact (S/2025/446 para. 105); 'armed night raids' is on the same page ('AFC/M23 conducted armed night raids on hospitals in Goma'). The Group adds that male caregivers were briefly detained and released, and that on 5 March an AFC/M23 search operation targeted Virunga Hospital in Goma. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: AFC/M23 leaders' public denials (para. 107) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-003: Same paragraph set as r1-GOE-055: the Group records AFC/M23's public denials (para. 107), which this claim omits (check 8). Also overlaps r1-GOE-055 almost entirely; editor may merge.; excerpt-support: added para. 107 (public denials by Bisimwa, Kanyuka and Makenga) as an excerpt
src: Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals were targeted, on 1 and 3 March, respectively, as part of operations tracking FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR combatants who had not surrendered (see para. 21 above).
A total of 164 patients were abducted – 48 from Heal Africa and 116 from CBCA Ndosho
Following the incidents in March, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and “General” Makenga issued public denials of responsibility

r1-UC-M23-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the night of 4 to 5 April 2025 armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF-supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements and opened fire within the grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.
r1-UC-M23-021.x: UN Group of Experts: 1 killed, 3 injured, 2 staff assaulted
r1-UC-M23-021.n: The report says the soldiers did not enter the hospital ward but bullets struck treatment areas. Victims unnamed in the report.
r1-UC-M23-021.vn: Exact excerpt (S/2025/446 para. 106); figures are spelled out in the excerpt (one, three, two). The Group adds that soldiers did not enter the ward but bullets struck the treatment areas.
src: On the night of 4 to 5 April 2025, armed AFC/M23 elements entered the MSF supported Kyeshero Hospital compound in Goma in search of FARDC elements who had completed medical treatment but remained at the hospital for fear of being recruited. The AFC/M23 elements opened fire within the facility grounds, killing one person, injuring three and assaulting two staff members.

r1-UC-M23-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, following the March 2025 hospital incidents, Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and 'General' Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming compliance with international humanitarian law and an aim of securing hospitals from 'infiltrated rogue combatants'; the Group wrote that witnesses confirmed no weapons were found in the hospitals.
r1-UC-M23-022.n: Excerpt gives the denial; the Group's counter-finding ('witnesses confirmed that no weapons were found in the hospitals') is the next sentence of the report. Original AFC/M23 communiqués (annex 52) not fetched; to be sourced from the party channel or press.
r1-UC-M23-022.vn: Exact excerpt (S/2025/446 para. 107) carries the denials; the rebuttal sentence is on the same page and paragraph (clause_support).
src: Bertrand Bisimwa, Lawrence Kanyuka and “General” Makenga issued public denials of responsibility, claiming they had acted in full compliance with international humanitarian law and with the aim of securing the hospitals from “infiltrated rogue combatants” who had been “endangering” patients and medical staff (see annex 52).

r1-UC-M23-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported a further alarming surge in cases of sexual violence across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict, both in the immediate aftermath of the fighting and during the subsequent consolidation of AFC/M23 control.
r1-UC-M23-023.a: all armed actors party to the conflict, per the Group of Experts
r1-UC-M23-023.n: Report date used; the passage is context, not an incident record. The same report separately documents FARDC rapes of three girls aged 13 to 17 between 31 January and 2 February 2025 (other units).
r1-UC-M23-023.vn: Exact excerpt (S/2025/446 para. 76); the 'aftermath ... consolidation of AFC/M23 control' clause continues the same sentence on the page. A general trend finding, not a single incident.
src: incidents of sexual violence on a massive scale (see S/2024/432, paras. 91 and 121, and annex 60), 65 a further alarming surge in cases has been reported across North and South Kivu, attributed to all armed actors party to the conflict

r1-UC-M23-024.s: According to Radio Okapi, a communiqué published on Friday 7 March 2025 by the DRC Ministry of Justice announced a reward of 5.000.000 USD for anyone enabling the arrest of the 'convicts' (condamnés) Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa and Sultani Makenga.
r1-UC-M23-024.n: The same article reports a further USD 4,000,000 reward for 'accomplices en fuite' Perrot Luwara and Irenge Baelenge (not in the excerpt) and that a Kinshasa military court issued an international arrest warrant for Nangaa on 5 February (year implied 2025). Date 7 March is the communiqué day printed on the page.
r1-UC-M23-024.vn: Exact excerpt; figure written as the excerpt prints it. 'Convicts' is the communiqué's word, quoted. The same communiqué, per Radio Okapi, offers a further 4.000.000$ for information leading to the arrest of 'complices en fuite' Perrot Luwara and Irenge Baelenge.
src: selon un communiqué publié vendredi 7 mars par le ministère de la Justice. « Le ministre d'État, ministre de la Justice et garde des sceaux annonce qu'une récompense de 5.000.000 USD est offerte à toute personne permettant l'arrestation des condamnés Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa et Sultani Makenga »

r1-UC-M23-025.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, General Sultani Makenga as M23 chief of staff and General Byamungu Bernard (“Taiga/Tiger One”) as deputy chief of staff.
r1-UC-M23-025.l: M23 military high command (North and South Kivu)
r1-UC-M23-025.n: Table extracted from a PDF annex; row/column alignment of the annex is partly scrambled in text extraction, so only the first two rows (adjacent in the text) are asserted. The UN GoE (via Actualite.cd) names Makenga and Byamungu as direct commanders of the Uvira offensive.
r1-UC-M23-025.vn: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex (as of December 2025). CRG also gives Makenga's call sign as 'Bravo Five'.
src: A. Military High Command Position Name / Rank Chief of Staff General Sultani Makenga (“Bravo Five”) Deputy Chief of Staff General Byamungu Bernard (“Taiga/Tiger One”)
Annex: M23 Military and Political Structure (as of December 2025) — A. Military High Command

r1-UC-M23-026.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Brigadier General Baudouin Ngaruye as commander of the 1st Operational Sector (Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters in Rutshuru town).
r1-UC-M23-026.l: Nyiragongo to Lubero, headquarters Rutshuru town, North Kivu
r1-UC-M23-026.n: Actualite.cd (relaying the same report) calls Ngaruye 'commandant du premier secteur opérationnel'. The report text also says Ngaruye was reassigned from commander of operations in Goma to lead the northern sector based in Rutshuru.
r1-UC-M23-026.vn: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex.
src: 1st Operational Sector (Nyiragongo → Lubero, headquarters in Rutshuru town) Position Sector Commander Name / Rank Brigadier General Baudouin Ngaruye
Annex: M23 Military and Political Structure (as of December 2025) — A. Military High Command

r1-UC-M23-027.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Brigadier General Gacheri Eraston as commander of the 2nd Operational Sector (Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters in Mushaki).
r1-UC-M23-027.l: Masisi-Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters Mushaki, North Kivu
r1-UC-M23-027.n: The EU/CRG sanctions table lists 'Justin Gacheri Musanga' as zone commander and the Critical Threats brief (lead only) lists Justin Gacheri Musanga as deputy commander; the relationship between 'Gacheri Eraston' and 'Justin Gacheri Musanga' is not established by any fetched source - do not merge.
r1-UC-M23-027.vn: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex. Actualite.cd's summary of the same report names a 'Justin Gacheri Musanga, commandant de zone'; whether this is the same person is not established.
src: 2nd Operational Sector (Masisi–Walikale and South Kivu, headquarters in Mushaki) Position Name / Rank Notes Sector Commander Brigadier General Gacheri Eraston
Annex: M23 Military and Political Structure (as of December 2025) — A. Military High Command

r1-UC-M23-028.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, the M23 Headquarters Regiment as now deployed to South Kivu, with its 1st battalion deployed in the Uvira operation and its 2nd battalion deployed to Minembwe.
r1-UC-M23-028.n: Annex table text; the rows are adjacent in extraction. Corroborates, as a different source, the M23 role in the Uvira offensive; the RDF role is covered by the UN GoE via Actualite.cd.
r1-UC-M23-028.vn: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex.
src: Headquarters Regiment (now deployed to South Kivu) HQ regiment 1st battalion (deployed in Uvira operation) HQ regiment 2nd battalion (deployed to Minembwe)
Annex: M23 Military and Political Structure (as of December 2025) — A. Military High Command

r1-UC-M23-029.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) listed, as of December 2025, Corneille Nangaa as AFC coordinator, Bernard Bisimwa (president of M23) as deputy coordinator, Freddy Kanyiki as deputy coordinator and Benjamin Mbonimpa as secretary general.
r1-UC-M23-029.n: Table extraction; role-to-name pairing taken from the adjacent row text.
r1-UC-M23-029.vn: Exact excerpts from the CRG/CIC annex ('Political leadership: AFC'), as of December 2025. The CRG annex prints 'Bernard Bisimwa'; the UN Group of Experts, OFAC-era press and Radio Okapi print 'Bertrand Bisimwa'.
src: Coordinator Corneille Nangaa Deputy Coordinator Bernard Bisimwa, President of M23 Deputy Coordinator Freddy Kanyiki Secretary General Benjamin Mbonimpa
Annex: M23 Military and Political Structure (as of December 2025) — A. Military High Command

r1-UC-M23-030.s: The Congo Research Group / NYU Center on International Cooperation (April 2026) reported that a commander who later reconciled with Makenga and joined the reconstituted M23 in 2022 was reassigned from commander of operations in Goma to lead the northern sector based in Rutshuru, and that the two had more recently clashed again over revenue collection; the report identifies him as Baudouin (Baudouin Ngaruye).
r1-UC-M23-030.n: Publication date used; the reassignment date is not stated. Analytical claim by the research group; sources of the rivalry not given in the excerpt.
r1-UC-M23-030.vn: Exact excerpt; the subject ('He') is named on the page as 'Baudouin' and elsewhere as 'Baudouin Ngaruye' (clause_support). '2022' is when he joined, not 'since'.
src: Although he later reconciled with Makenga and joined the reconstituted M23 in 2022, frictions have remained. He was reassigned from his position as commander of operations in Goma to leading the northern sector based in Rutshuru. More recently, the two have clashed again over revenue collection.

r1-UC-M23-031.s: BBC News reported that former president Joseph Kabila was named leader of a new rebel coalition, announced at a press conference at his residence in Goma by the coalition's adviser Claude Ibalanky, with M23 leader Sultani Makenga as one of Kabila's four deputies and the other three also from the AFC-M23 alliance; BBC said the Congolese government had not commented.
r1-UC-M23-031.a: Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN); Joseph Kabila; Sultani Makenga
r1-UC-M23-031.n: BBC says the unveiling was 'on Monday' (article dated 13 October 2026, a Tuesday): date computed from weekday and publication date. This is a leadership change relevant to the AFC/M23 command structure; the UN GoE (S/2026/466, para. 58) separately reported a forthcoming reshuffle. Radio Okapi (snippet, not fetched) reports the C64 coalition rejecting Kabila-linked FRN positions; see party-statement gap.
r1-UC-M23-031.vn: All excerpts exact. Publication date removed; the coalition's name (Front for the Refoundation of the Nation, FRN) is on the page but in no excerpt, so it is given in clause_support and the note only. BBC names the coalition the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN); its unveiling was 'on Monday' (12 October 2026). Kabila had previously denied links to M23.
src: Claude Ibalanky, the coalition's adviser, announced the group's leadership at a press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma
M23 leader Sultani Makenga will serve as one of Kabila's four deputies in the new movement. The other three also come from the AFC-M23 alliance
He had previously denied having links to the M23 rebel group. The Congolese government has not commented.

r1-UC-M23-032.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of writing, multiple AFC/M23 and intelligence sources said a comprehensive reshuffle of AFC/M23 leadership and structure was forthcoming, including a change of the movement's name, and that Joseph Kabila was expected to assume a prominent position.
r1-UC-M23-032.l: AFC/M23-held areas, North and South Kivu
r1-UC-M23-032.n: Report date 5 June 2026 per the UN's list of reports (search result); the date inside the PDF was not checked. Preceded the 12 October 2026 FRN announcement reported by the BBC.
r1-UC-M23-032.vn: Exact excerpt from S/2026/466 para. 58; the statement keeps it as what AFC/M23 and intelligence sources told the Group, a forecast at the time of writing.
src: At the time of writing, multiple AFC/M23 and intelligence sources reported that a comprehensive reshuffle of AFC/M23 leadership and structure was forthcoming – including a change of the movement’s name – and that Mr. Kabila was expected to assume a prominent position.

r1-UC-M23-033.s: Citing a UN communiqué, the news site reported that the Security Council's 1533 sanctions committee approved on 14 July the listing of six individuals and two entities, among them Corneille Nangaa, presented as head of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23), and Colonel John Imani Nzenze, M23 intelligence chief, sanctioned for alleged involvement in planning and supporting the rebel movement's activities.
r1-UC-M23-033.l: UN Security Council, New York (listing); targets are AFC/M23 leaders
r1-UC-M23-033.n: Radio Okapi (17 July 2026) says the committee added the names 'jeudi 16 juillet 2026' (the announcement day); 7sur7 gives approval 14 July and the UN communiqué 16 July. The UN press release (press.un.org/en/2026/sc16416.doc.htm) could not be fetched by the page helper. Radio Okapi's list of the six also names Sébastien Uwimbabazi and Gustave Kubwayo (FDLR), Muhammed Lumisa (ADF), Charles Sematama (Twirwaneho).
r1-UC-M23-033.vn: Both excerpts exact. Communiqué date removed from statement. 'Présumée' kept as 'alleged'. Outlet name dropped from the statement text only because the number check reads '7sur7' as a figure; the source is shown with the claim. Date discrepancy: 7sur7.cd gives 14 July for the committee's approval (communiqué of 16 July); Radio Okapi says the committee added the names on Thursday 16 July 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: le Comité des sanctions du Conseil de sécurité, créé en vertu de la résolution 1533 (2004), a approuvé, le 14 juillet, l'inscription de six individus et de deux entités sur sa liste

Parmi les personnes visées figure Corneille Nangaa, présenté comme le chef de l'Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23). John Imani Nzenze, colonel et chef du renseignement du M23, est également sanctionné pour son implication présumée dans la planification et le soutien aux activités du mouvement rebelle.

r1-UC-M23-034.s: Radio Okapi reported that the two entities added to the UN sanctions list were the Alliance Fleuve Congo and the armed group Twirwaneho.
r1-UC-M23-034.n: Date is the day Radio Okapi gives for the committee's addition (Thursday 16 July 2026); 7sur7 gives approval on 14 July.

src: Deux entités sont également visées : l’Alliance Fleuve Congo et le groupe armé Twirwaneho

r1-UC-M23-035.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the UN sanctions listing included Colonel Charles Sematama, military chief of the Twirwaneho group, active in the Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu and accused of abuses against civilians.

src: le colonel Charles Sematama, chef militaire du groupe Twirwaneho, actif dans les Hauts Plateaux du Sud-Kivu et accusé d'exactions contre les populations civiles.

r1-UC-RDF-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in January and February 2025 a conservative estimate of 6,000 RDF troops, including RDF special forces, were active in North Kivu and northern territories of South Kivu.
r1-UC-RDF-001.l: North Kivu and northern South Kivu
r1-UC-RDF-001.x: Group of Experts: conservative estimate of 6,000 troops
r1-UC-RDF-001.n: Footnote 25 of the report adds that former RDF and Rwandan intelligence reported at least 10,000 RDF troops; not used as an excerpt. Perpetrator-neutral deployment claim.
r1-UC-RDF-001.vn: Excerpt is para. 36 of S/2025/446; figure, months and places match. The '25' after 6,000 is a footnote marker.

r1-UC-RDF-002.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that at the time of writing an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.
r1-UC-RDF-002.l: AFC/M23 controlled territories, North and South Kivu
r1-UC-RDF-002.n: Report text says the footprint was reduced after the takeover of Goma.

src: At the time of writing, an estimated 1,000 to 1,500 RDF troops remained active in AFC/M23 controlled territories, including in urban centres.

r1-UC-RDF-003.s: The UN Group of Experts, citing its previous reports, reported in July 2025 that Major-General Ruki Karusisi (described as RDF Special Force Commander), Major-General Eugène Nkubito (RDF 3rd Division Commander) and Lieutenant-General Mubarakh Mugunga (RDF Army Chief of Staff) played key roles in planning and commanding military operations in North Kivu and South Kivu.

played key roles in planning and commanding military operations in North Kivu and South Kivu (S/2023/431, para. 59 and annex 35; S/2023/990, para. 30; and S/2024/432, para. 43 and annex 30)

r1-UC-RDF-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF operations were conceived and coordinated, among others, by General James Kabarebe, Army Chief of Staff Major-General Vincent Nyakarundi and Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa, and that RDF established forward headquarters in Gisenyi, Rwanda, bordering Goma town.
r1-UC-RDF-004.n: Attribution to named sources is in the report paragraph before the excerpt; the excerpt starts at the finding.
r1-UC-RDF-004.vn: Paras 40-41 of S/2025/446; all three excerpts exact and on point. The Group attributes the coordination finding to RDF sources, sources close to RDF, AFC/M23 and Rwandan officials, and intelligence and diplomatic sources.
src: RDF operations were conceived and coordinated, among others, by General James Kabarebe, a retired RDF military officer currently serving as Minister of State for Regional Integration

as well as the Army Chief of Staff, Major-General Vincent Nyakarundi, 29 and the President of the Rwandan Military High Court in charge of justice and discipline within the RDF, Brigadier General Patrick Karuretwa.
RDF established forward headquarters in Gisenyi, Rwanda, bordering Goma town

r1-UC-RDF-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF soldiers were briefed by 'Colonel' Espoir Rukinisha about their tasks, and that according to RDF sources interviewed by the Group, Rukinisha was the commander of the third bataillion in Bigogwe, Rwanda, before joining M23 in 2023.
r1-UC-RDF-005.n: Date not stated in the excerpt; the page places the briefing around the takeover of Goma (late January 2025). Reviewer to confirm.
r1-UC-RDF-005.vn: Excerpt exact (annex to S/2025/446). The draft's 2025-01/2025-02 date was inferred, not printed; removed. 'who arrived in Goma' is page-only, so dropped from the statement and kept as context. 'bataillion' spelled as printed. The report (annex) does not date the briefing; it places Rukinisha's role 'during the takeover of Goma'. The date field is left undated rather than inferred.
src: RDF soldiers were briefed by “Colonel” Espoir Rukinisha about their tasks. According to RDF sources interviewed by the Group, Rukinisha was the commander of the third bataillion in Bigogwe, Rwanda, before joining M23 in 2023.

r1-UC-RDF-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 25, 26 and 27 January 2025 RDF troop reinforcements, including RDF Special Forces, arrived from Kitchanga, Kibumba and Kanyamahoro in the DRC, as well as from Gisenyi, Rwanda.
r1-UC-RDF-006.l: Goma area (Kitchanga, Kibumba, Kanyamahoro), North Kivu
r1-UC-RDF-006.n: Part of the report's account of the capture of Goma.

r1-UC-RDF-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that it documented the presence of soldiers of the following RDF brigades and battalions in North Kivu in February and March 2025: 107 Brigade (55th, 79th, 87th, 85th, 57th, 15th, 03rd, 06th and 04th Battalions), 135 Brigade (27th and 29th Battalions) and 109 Brigade (69th, 85th, '72rd' [as printed] and 75th Battalions).

The report prints '72rd Battalion' (likely 72nd) and lists an 85th Battalion under both 107 and 109 Brigades; both as printed. Footnote 246 gives the source as 'RDF and intelligence sources.'

135 Brigade 27th Battalion 29th Battalion 109 Brigade 69th Battalion 85th Battalion 72rd Battalion 75th Battalion

r1-UC-RDF-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that elements of the RDF 3rd Division, under Major General Eugene Nkubito, operated predominantly in North Kivu, and the 4th Division was mainly deployed in South Kivu under Brigadier General Vincent Gatama until his redeployment to Mozambique in late 2025, both supported by special forces under Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi.
r1-UC-RDF-008.n: Report cites intelligence, AFC/M23 sources, captured RDF soldiers; footnote says Gatama was referenced in late 2025 as RSF JTF commander in Mozambique.
r1-UC-RDF-008.vn: Para. 99 of S/2026/466; both excerpts exact. Spelling 'Eugene' as printed here (S/2025/446 prints 'Eugène').

Both divisions were supported by special forces units, under the command of Brigadier-General Stanislas Gashugi.

r1-UC-RDF-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 1 December 2025 President Kagame appointed retired General James Kaberebe as his Senior Defence and Security Advisor, and on 29 January 2026 appointed Brigadier-General Jean-Paul Nyirabutama as his deputy.
r1-UC-RDF-009.l: Rwanda (decisions concerning operations in eastern DRC)
r1-UC-RDF-009.n: Spelling 'Kaberebe' / 'Kabarebe' as printed in the report. Appointment dates are Rwandan-side decisions; the report links both to AFC/M23 liaison.

r1-UC-RDF-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain, including jamming systems, BM21-type multi-barrel rocket launchers, GPS-guided 120 mm mortars, kamikaze and first-person-view drones, aiming for a rapid victory.
r1-UC-RDF-010.x: Group of Experts: over 8,000 RDF troops (Uvira offensive)
r1-UC-RDF-010.n: Perpetrator-neutral deployment. The paragraph sits in the report's account of the December 2025 AFC/M23 offensive on Uvira (the report says M23 and RDF took Uvira on 10 December 2025); the excerpt itself does not name Uvira. Cross-border shelling from Kamanyola on 4-5 December is mentioned in the next sentence (not cited).
r1-UC-RDF-010.vn: Para. 76 of S/2026/466 verbatim. Date supported on the page, not in the excerpt (flagged in note). The excerpt does not itself print a date; the 2025-12 dating rests on the report's cross-reference placing paras 72-76 (this is para. 76) in the account of the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025.
src: Rwanda deployed over 8,000 RDF troops, including special forces, and transferred heavy, advanced military equipment to the frontlines on the Ruzizi Plain, including jamming systems, BM21-type multi-barrel rocket launchers, GPS-guided 120 mm mortars, kamikaze and first-person-view drones, aiming for a rapid victory.

r1-UC-RDF-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026 following sustained international diplomatic pressure, after controlling the city for over a month.
r1-UC-RDF-011.n: The report also says the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas.

The Group adds that the withdrawal was followed by redeployment to adjacent areas, 'in breach of withdrawal commitments'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc2: S/2026/466 para. 77 supports the statement in full, but the stored excerpt omits 'for over a month' and 'following sustained international diplomatic pressure'; the full contiguous sentence is added.
src: AFC/ M23 and RDF troops eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026

After controlling Uvira for over a month – during which AFC/M23 forced the withdrawal of FDNB, captured large FARDC bases, 84 dominated the entire Ruzizi plain along the Burundian border and established a parallel administration – AFC/ M23 and RDF troops eventually withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, following sustained international diplomatic pressure

r1-UC-RDF-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 February 2026 approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.
r1-UC-RDF-012.n: Report cites intelligence, civil society, researchers and diplomatic sources.
r1-UC-RDF-012.vn: Annex text of S/2026/466 verbatim (the page wraps '25' to the next line).

r1-UC-RDF-013.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis and an undetermined number elsewhere, including towards Fizi.
r1-UC-RDF-013.l: South Kivu (Ruzizi Plain, Moyens and Hauts Plateaux, Ngweshe-Mwenga, Fizi)
r1-UC-RDF-013.vn: Annex text of S/2026/466 verbatim; figures match.
src: As of mid-February 2026, RDF deployments in South Kivu were as follows: approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain–Moyens Plateaux axis; 800 troops in the Hauts Plateaux; 1,800 troops along the Ngweshe–Mwenga axis; and an undetermined number elsewhere, including in direction of Fizi.

r1-UC-RDF-014.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that new RDF troop and materiel reinforcements were documented in April passing through Nyangezi-Kamanyola towards the Ruzizi Plain, Lemera in the Moyens Plateaux and the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga, and that RDF positioned anti-aerial defence systems (MANPADS) and conducted attacks with kamikaze and armed drones, notably between 10 and 19 April.
r1-UC-RDF-014.l: Ruzizi Plain, Lemera, Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga
r1-UC-RDF-014.n: Year inferred from the section (post-January 2026 withdrawal from Uvira; report dated 5 June 2026). Reviewer to confirm.
r1-UC-RDF-014.vn: Excerpt exact (annex, S/2026/466). Removed the inferred '(2026)' from the statement and date. The passage does not print the year of 'April'; the context (final report of 5 June 2026, after the January 2026 withdrawal from Uvira) points to April 2026, but this is an inference.
src: new RDF troop and materiel reinforcements with new troops and materiel reinforcements were documented in April passing through Nyangezi-Kamanyola towards Ruzizi Plaine, Lemera in the Moyens Plateaux, and others towards the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Mwenga. RDF positioned sophisticated weaponry, including anti-aerial defense systems (MANPADS) and conducted attacks with kamikaze and armed drones, notably between 10 and 19 April

r1-UC-RDF-015.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the US designated Vincent Nyakarundi (Chief of Staff of the RDF), Major-General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander), General Mubarakh Muganga (Chief of Defence Staff) and Stanislas Gashugi (Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025) for their leadership roles within the RDF.
r1-UC-RDF-015.n: Corroborates the Treasury designation already cited in POL-2026; adds the UN report's wording of the four officers' posts.
r1-UC-RDF-015.vn: Annex of S/2026/466 verbatim; US and March 2026 printed elsewhere on the page.
src: Accordingly, Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF; Major-General Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander; General Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff; and Stanislas Gashugi, Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025

r1-UC-RDF-016.s: Human Rights Watch reported that the US sanctioned the Rwandan army and four commanders (Maj. Gen. Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen. Ruki Karusisi, Gen. Mubarakh Muganga and Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi), and that military and UN sources told HRW several thousand Rwandan soldiers, including special forces, crossed into the DRC in the weeks before the December Uvira offensive.
r1-UC-RDF-016.n: The date of the US announcement (2 March 2026) is from the HRW text ('Le 2 mars 2026, le gouvernement des États-Unis a annoncé'), which is not in the excerpts; Al Jazeera says Monday.
r1-UC-RDF-016.vn: Both excerpts exact; excerpt_en translations are faithful (flag triggered by sentence-initial capitals and 'UN' for 'onusiennes'). 'Maj. Gen./Brig. Gen.); S/2026/466 calls him 'General'.
src: Des sources militaires et onusiennes ont déclaré à Human Rights Watch que plusieurs milliers de soldats rwandais, y compris des forces spéciales, avaient traversé la frontière congolaise dans les semaines précédant l'offensive sur Uvira en décembre.

Parmi les personnes sanctionnées figurent le général de division Vincent Nyakarundi, chef d'état-major de l'armée rwandaise, le général de division Ruki Karusisi, commandant de la 5e division d'infanterie et ancien commandant des forces spéciales, le général Mubarakh Muganga, chef d'état-major de la défense, et le général de brigade Stanislas Gashugi, commandant des forces d'opérations spéciales.

r1-UC-RDF-017.s: AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said in a statement that the US sanctions 'unjustly' target Rwanda and 'misrepresent the reality and distort the facts of the conflict' in eastern DRC, and accused the DRC of violating the peace agreement.
r1-UC-RDF-017.n: Day of the statement not given on the page; reported 3 March 2026. Page byline: 'By AP and Reuters'.
r1-UC-RDF-017.vn: Exact; byline AP and Reuters on Al Jazeera. Day of Makolo's statement not on the page, so date set to undated with the report date.
src: Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said in a statement that the sanctions “unjustly” target Rwanda and “misrepresent the reality and distort the facts of the conflict” in eastern DRC. She accused DRC of violating the peace agreement

r1-UC-RDF-018.s: AP and Reuters (as published by Al Jazeera) reported that the Congolese government said it welcomed the US sanctions on the Rwandan military, describing them as 'a strong signal in support of respect' for its territorial integrity and sovereignty.
r1-UC-RDF-018.n: Day of the statement not given; reported 3 March 2026.
r1-UC-RDF-018.vn: Exact; byline AP and Reuters. Day of the Congolese statement not printed; date set to undated with the report date.
src: The Congolese government, however, said it welcomed the sanctions, describing them as “a strong signal in support of respect” for its territorial integrity and ⁠sovereignty.
