Ceux qui occupaient la ville ont décidé de quitter Uvira. Ils sont sortis mais ils ne sont pas loin, ils nous observent encore

Évoquant les exactions commises durant les affrontements, l’autorité urbaine a reconnu l’existence de dérives, tant au sein des forces régulières FARDC, que parmi les groupes d’autodéfense « wazalendo »

r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-021.s: The US State Department said on 2 June 2026 that it was designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, 'an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC', and Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, saying the FDLR had 'committed sexual violence'.
r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-021.n: Second, State Department source for the designation that claim UC-M23#3 attributes to the Treasury press release; the State Department statement attributes allegations to the groups, not to the two named men individually. Nzenze is also described by the UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466, cited by other claims) as AFC/M23 Director of Intelligence and liaison with humanitarian actors.
r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-021.vn: Supported; the date is printed in the page header, not the excerpts. Press statement by spokesperson Thomas 'Tommy' Pigott. Its allegations are made against the groups (M23, FDLR), not against the two named men individually.
src: We are designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit. The FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence, and launched cross-border attacks that continue to threaten Rwanda’s security.

We are also designating John Imani Nzenze, chief of intelligence for the Rwanda-backed M23, an armed group that has committed killings, serious human rights abuses, and attacks on civilians in eastern DRC.

r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the civil society group Forces vives of the Kaniola groupement (Walungu, South Kivu), in a letter to BCNUDH, MONUSCO and the ICRC, accused AFC/M23 officer Charles Kagigi of establishing a regime of terror, and said that over four days it documented several crimes, including a taxi driver from Kalengera (Zigashane Mashali) extorted of 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) and beaten to death on 23 September at Kashanja, and three civilians returning from a Leopards match (Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac and Bizimana Ciraza) summarily executed on 24 September at Kaniola. The group also said that 'colonel Kagigi' publicly swore to 'raze the Kaniola groupement' and demanded his departure.
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.l: Kaniola and Kashanja (Kaniola groupement), Walungu, South Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.a: AFC/M23 officer Charles Kagigi (alleged by civil society)
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.x: Radio Okapi (civil society): 30 000 Congolese francs (13 USD) extorted from the taxi driver before he was killed
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.n: Allegation by a civil-society group, relayed by Radio Okapi (Bukavu-based UN-founded radio); not independently confirmed, no AFC/M23 response found. Same text republished by mediacongo.net (26 Sept 2026) and summarised by Agasaro Network; not independent. The article also says (not in an excerpt) that on 21 September two teachers were tortured at Nzibira-Luntukulu (unnamed). Searches on 'Kagigi' at actualite.cd, 7sur7.cd and kivumorningpost.com found nothing. Kagigi is a new name in the roster; rank 'colonel' appears in the article's later sentence, 'officier' in the first. Dates 21-24 September: year 2026 inferred from the article's publication date 26/09/2026.
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-011.vn: Draft said the group documented 'killings' over four days; the page says 'plusieurs crimes' (the four days include a torture case on 21 Sept). Narrowed to 'several crimes'. All names printed in excerpts. excerpt_en flags are sentence-initial capitals (The/In/On), translations are of the excerpts alone. Grade C: single local civil-society origin. Allegation by a local civil-society group in a letter, relayed by Radio Okapi; not independently confirmed; no AFC/M23 response found. The source's own label for these acts ('crimes de guerre') is the civil society's characterisation. Year 2026 taken from the article date (26/09/2026). The article also reports (outside the excerpts) two teachers tortured at Nzibira-Luntukulu on 21 September, not named.
ent: Forces vives du groupement de Kaniola
src: La société civile Forces vives du groupement de Kaniola, dans le territoire de Walungu au Sud‑Kivu, dénonce les exactions et crimes de guerre commis dans cette zone par des rebelles de l’AFC/M23.
Dans une lettre de dénonciation adressée au BCNUDH, à la MONUSCO ainsi qu’au CICR, elle accuse un officier de ce mouvement, Charles Kagigi, d’avoir instauré un régime de terreur dans la région.

Le 24 septembre à Kaniola, trois civils revenant d’un match des Léopards ont été exécutés sommairement . Les victimes sont Birhalugirakulimushi Jules, Kashokwire Kulimushi Isaac et Bizimana Ciraza, précise la société civile.
Le 23 septembre à Kashanja, un taximan de Kalengera, Zigashane Mashali, a été extorqué de 30 000 francs congolais (13 USD) avant d’être tué par bastonnade.
Elle rapporte également que le colonel Kagigi, pointé du doigt dans ces crimes, a publiquement juré de « raser le groupement de Kaniola ».

r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012.s: Actualite.cd, citing an April 2026 report by the Congo Research Group and NYU's Center on International Cooperation, reported that Colonel Innocent Zimurinda is commander of the headquarters (quartier général), sanctioned by the UN since December 2010, by the European Union since the same date and by the United States since January 2013.
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012.l: M23 headquarters (Rubare, Rutshuru per CRG table), North Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012.n: Zimurinda is a candidate for the HQ post in the CRG annex, where the name is printed 'Colonel Innocent Zimulinda' next to 'Headquarters Commander (based in Rubare, Rutshuru)'; the PDF table layout does not make the name-to-post pairing unambiguous, so the Actualite.cd text is cited for the pairing. A FARDC-side account (depeche.cd, 19 May 2026) names 'Zimurinda Innocent' as an AFC-M23 commander based in Rutshuru; that page did not load (see gaps).
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012.vn: Page prints the post and sanction dates and credits the CRG/CIC report in its lead; checked against the CRG PDF's sanctions list, which matches. excerpt_en flag is capitalised proper nouns (UN/EU) rendered in English; translation is of the excerpt alone. Actualite.cd relays the CRG/CIC April 2026 report; not independent of the CRG claims. The CRG sanctions list prints 'Innocent Zimurinda, Headquarters commander' with UN 1 Dec 2010, EU 22 Dec 2010, US 3 Jan 2013; the CRG annex table prints the name 'Colonel Innocent Zimulinda' (spelling differs within the same report).
src: Le colonel Innocent Zimurinda, commandant du quartier général, est sanctionné par l'ONU depuis décembre 2010, par l'Union européenne depuis la même date, et par les États-Unis depuis janvier 2013.

r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that, since Saturday, AFC/M23 elements had taken control of Ngululu before seizing the commercial centre of Humura on Sunday, amid intensifying fighting between AFC/M23, the FARDC and the wazalendo in Masisi and Walikale territories, North Kivu.
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-013.l: Ngululu and Humura, Masisi-Walikale axis, North Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-013.n: Weekdays only (samedi, dimanche) in a piece published Tuesday 8 Sept 2026: date computed from weekday and publication date as 2026-09-05/06. Names no commander or unit. Single outlet; FARDC/Wazalendo account of these captures not found.
r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-013.vn: Both excerpts on the page; publication date mar 08/09/2026 confirmed (a Tuesday), so Sat/Sun = 5/6 Sept, approximate. excerpt_en flag is a sentence-initial capital. Dates computed from weekdays ('samedi', 'dimanche') in an article published Tuesday 8 September 2026: approximate. Single outlet, no named source for this paragraph; no FARDC/Wazalendo account found.
src: Depuis samedi, des éléments de l’AFC/M23 ont pris le contrôle de Ngululu, avant de s'emparer du centre commercial de Humura le dimanche.

La situation sécuritaire demeure tendue dans plusieurs zones des territoires de Masisi et de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu, sur fond d’intensification des combats entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, les FARDC et les wazalendo.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three 'defense zones', led respectively by 'General' Baudoin Ngaruye (first zone: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories), 'Brigadier-General' Justin Gacheri Musanga (second zone: Masisi and Walikale) and 'General' Byamungu (third zone: South Kivu).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001.l: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001.a: AFC/M23 (as named by the Group of Experts)
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001.n: Reporting period of S/2026/466 (final report dated 2026-06-05); no start date for the zones is given. Ranks are as printed by the experts, in quotation marks. The UN text prints only the surname Byamungu for the third commander; Actualite.cd prints a different first name (see separate claim).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001.vn: Excerpt found in para. 64 of S/2026/466; statement matches; ranks as printed in quotation marks. S/2026/466 places South Kivu in a third zone under 'General' Byamungu; the Group's earlier midterm report S/2025/858 described a 'second defence zone' that covered Masisi, Walikale and areas of South Kivu (Walungu, Mwenga, Minembwe). The two reports differ; both are stated. The UN text prints only the surname Byamungu; no start date for the zones is given.
src: AFC/M23-occupied territories were divided into three “defense zones”, led respectively by “General” Baudoin Ngaruye (first zone, covering Nyiragongo, Rutshuru and Lubero territories), “Brigadier-General” Justin Gacheri Musanga (second zone, covering Masisi and Walikale) and “General” Byamungu (third zone, covering South Kivu).

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-002.s: Actualite.cd, relaying the UN Group of Experts report, reported that 'brigadier general' Justin Gacheri Musanga led the second zone (Masisi and Walikale) and a 'general' it named as Innocent Byamungu the third zone (South Kivu) of the movement's 'defence zones'.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-002.l: Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale and South Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-002.n: Discrepancy: the UN text prints 'Byamungu' only; Actualite.cd prints 'Innocent Byamungu'. Other sources in this unit (UN sanctions summary, Kivu Morning Post, Actualite.cd Sept 2025) refer to the AFC/M23 deputy military commander as Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. 'Innocent' is not established; probably a relay error. Surface, do not resolve. The page sentence is introduced by 'le rapport révèle que' (the UN report).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-002.vn: Page prints the passage as quoted; a relay of the UN report, not independent; graded C because the added first name is unsupported by the origin. Name discrepancy: the UN report it relays (S/2026/466, para. 64) prints only “General” Byamungu; Actualite.cd prints 'Innocent Byamungu'. HRW prints 'Bertrand Byamungu'; Actualite.cd (Sept 2025), FNTV and Enquete.cd print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. The first name 'Innocent' has no support in the origin and is not established. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-010: Namesake risk: the relay adds a first name ('Innocent') that the origin does not print, while other sources print Bernard or Bertrand Byamungu. The statement should say the first name is the outlet's and that the UN text gives only the surname (input claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001 excerpt).; excerpt-support: cut 'the UN report itself prints only “General” Byamungu': the UN report is not among this claim's sources (its excerpt sits in r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-001); kept 'a general it named as Innocent Byamungu' (source 0 prints that name)
src: le « général de brigade » Justin Gacheri Musanga (deuxième zone, couvrant Masisi et Walikale) et le « général » Innocent Byamungu (troisième zone, couvrant le Sud-Kivu).

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the AFC/M23 'First Defence Zone' command, covering Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, was led by 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-003.l: Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, Rutshuru territory
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-003.n: Reporting period of S/2025/858 (dated 2025-12-30). The same paragraph recounts a pre-2025 UN sanction history, which is outside the window and not recorded here. S/2026/466 prints Ngaruye as "General"; S/2025/858 as "Brigadier General" (rank as printed).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-003.vn: Para. 44 of S/2025/858 matches. Rank as printed: S/2025/858 'Brigadier General'; S/2026/466 'General'.
src: Operationally, Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms fall under the AFC/M23 “First Defence Zone” command, led by “Brigadier General” Baudoin Ngaruye (CDi.019).

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma-Rutshuru-Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004.n: Report states the year context via its section on 2025; the excerpt itself prints "8 September" without year; year inferred from the report period (S/2025/858). Sources for the declaration are UN, intelligence and civil society sources per the report footnote.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004.vn: Removed the year from the statement because no excerpt prints it; date field kept as 2025-09-08 inferred from the report period. The excerpt (annex 22 of S/2025/858, dated 30 December 2025) prints '8 September' without a year; 2025 is inferred from the report period. The Group cites UN, intelligence and civil society sources and a video.
src: On 8 September, “Brigadier General” Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23’s ‘First Defense Zone’ covering the Goma–Rutshuru–Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that one RDF brigade operated within AFC/M23's 'first defence zone' (Goma, Nyiragongo, Binza, Bwito, Rutshuru, and Kanyabayonga, Kirumba and Kipese in Lubero), and another RDF brigade in the 'second defence zone' (Masisi, Walikale, Bibwe, Kalembe, and South Kivu areas including Walungu, Mwenga and Minembwe).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.l: Goma, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, Walikale, Walungu, Mwenga, Minembwe
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.a: RDF within AFC/M23 defence zones (as named by the Group of Experts)
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.n: Reporting period of S/2025/858 (2025-12-30). Report counts "at least two brigades and two special forces battalions" in North and South Kivu. Note this places the second zone (with South Kivu locations) differently from S/2026/466, where South Kivu is the third zone; surface this difference between reports.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.vn: Para. 69 of S/2025/858 matches both excerpts. S/2025/858 (para. 69) places South Kivu areas in the 'second defence zone'; S/2026/466 (para. 64) describes a separate third zone covering South Kivu under 'General' Byamungu. The reports differ; both are stated.
src: One RDF brigade operated within the “first defence zone” of AFC/M23, covering Goma, Nyiragongo, Binza, Bwito and Rutshuru, as well as Kanyabayonga, Kirumba and Kipese in Lubero

Another RDF brigade operated in the “second defence zone”, covering Masisi, Walikale, Bibwe and Kalembe, along the Pinga front line, as well as areas of South Kivu, including Walungu, Mwenga and Minembwe.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late March AFC/M23 'Colonel' Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-006.n: S/2025/858 prints Gakufe as "Lieutenant-Colonel" (rank differs between reports). Sematama appears in a July 2026 UN sanctions listing as Twirwaneho military chief (existing claim r1-UC-M23-035). Kivu Morning Post posted on X about Colonel Gakufe at Minembwe (lead only, not cited).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-006.vn: Removed '2025' from the statement because the excerpt does not print the year. The excerpt prints 'late March' without a year; 2025 follows from the report period (S/2025/446, 3 July 2025) and S/2025/858 later refers to this as March 2025. Rank differs between reports: 'Colonel' (S/2025/446) and 'Lieutenant-Colonel' (S/2025/858).
src: 178. In late March, AFC/M23 “Colonel” Japhet Gakufe and Charles Sematama arrived in Minembwe with an estimated 200 AFC/M23 combatants,

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, after AFC/M23 reinforcements led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, a second reinforcement led by 'Lieutenant-Colonel' Oscar Ndabagaza was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-007.n: "End of August" is the report's wording; the year follows the reporting period (2025). Territory of Mikenge is not stated in the excerpt; listed as Mwenga on the strength of general knowledge only, so verifier should confirm or set to "Hauts Plateaux".
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-007.vn: Mikenge territory flagged by researcher: not stated on this page, so territory cleared; statement itself is supported as written. S/2025/858 (para. 53) does not state Mikenge's territory; the same paragraph places the operation in AFC/M23 and RDF support to MRDP-Twirwaneho-controlled enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux. Territory left blank rather than asserted from general knowledge. 'End of August' has no year on the page; 2025 follows from the report period. Rank 'Lieutenant-Colonel' for Gakufe here vs 'Colonel' in S/2025/446.
src: After AFC/M23 reinforcements led by “Lieutenant-Colonel” Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025 (S/2025/446, para. 178), a second reinforcement, led by “Lieutenant -Colonel” Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that 'Colonel' Gafishi Semikobe Simon was officially appointed AFC/M23 'Officer for Mobilisation and Recruitment' on 11 February 2025 and also carried out responsibilities relating to the 'security files'.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-008.n: Annex to S/2025/446. The main text (para. 23) prints the name as Semikobe Gafishi; spelling as printed in each place.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-008.vn: Annex passage matches. Annex to S/2025/446; the excerpt does not itself name Goma. Name order as printed in the annex.
src: “Colonel” Gafishi Semikobe Simon, officially appointed AFC/M23 “Officer for Mobilisation and Recruitment” on 11 February 2025, also carried out responsibilities relating to the “security files”.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 confiscated identification documents, including voter cards and land titles of the refugees, and publicly burned them in the presence of AFC/M23 officials, including AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda, military spokesperson Willy Ngoma and Goma's military commander, 'Colonel' Nsanze Nzamuye Jimmy, and in the presence of local media.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-009.n: The excerpt does not date the burning; the surrounding passage concerns transfers of refugees to Rwanda in May 2025. The date shown is the report date only; verifier should place the event from the report text.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-009.vn: Researcher flagged the undated event; placed it in the annex's May 2025 context as approximate, and narrowed the statement to the document burning, which is the event the passage reports. Undated event: the burning sits in annex 39 of S/2025/858, which concerns the transfer of 1,798 people to Rwanda on 17-22 May 2025; the passage gives no date for the burning itself. Nsanze's role as Goma military commander is referenced to an earlier report (S/2024/432, annex 24). The Group cites witnesses, UN, humanitarian and civil society sources.
src: AFC/M23 confiscated identification documents, including voter cards and land titles of the refugees, and publicly burned them220 in the presence of AFC/M23 officials – including AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda, military spokesperson Willy Ngoma, and Goma’s military commander, “Colonel” Nsanze Nzamuye Jimmy (S/2024/432, annex 24), and in the presence of local media.221

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that 'General' Makenga held overall military command of AFC/M23, although his position had become increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-010.l: AFC/M23 territory, North and South Kivu
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-010.n: Complements r1-UC-M23-032 (leadership reshuffle). Reporting period of S/2026/466.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-010.vn: Para. 61 of S/2026/466 matches. Adds to r1-UC-M23-011 (S/2025/446): the later report adds that Makenga's position was contested within the movement and by Rwanda.
src: Overall military command of AFC/M23 remained with “General” Makenga, although his position became increasingly contested within the movement and by Rwanda (see annex 23).

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership: on 14 January 2026 a drone strike targeted the 'Blue Cat' bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties, and on 7 March 2026 a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-011.l: Kalundu district, Uvira (Blue Cat bar-restaurant); Mushaki (Masisi) on 2026-03-07
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-011.a: FARDC (drone operations, per the Group of Experts)
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-011.n: Casualty numbers are not given in the excerpt. Mushaki is a different location (the excerpt gives no territory). The report attributes the strikes to FARDC drone operations; no named commander is given for either strike.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-011.vn: Added the paragraph's own framing so the FARDC attribution comes from the source rather than the actor field. Para. 165 of S/2026/466. The Group gives no casualty figure for the Blue Cat strike and names no commander for Mushaki; the Mushaki sentence says 'a strike' and sits in the paragraph on FARDC drone operations.
src: FARDC drone operations also targeted AFC/M23 leadership. On 14 January 2026, a drone strike targeted the “Blue Cat” bar-restaurant in the Kalundu district of Uvira, during a meeting of senior AFC/M23 and RDF officers, causing significant casualties.
On 7 March 2026, a strike in Mushaki targeted a house associated with a high-ranking AFC/M23 commander.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-012.s: BBC Gahuza, relaying Reuters, reported that the drone strike that killed AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma at dawn on Tuesday near Rubaya killed at least nine people but narrowly missed AFC/M23 military chief Gen Sultani Makenga, who escaped unharmed according to four people who told Reuters.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-012.a: FARDC drone (per other sources); AFC/M23 target
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-012.x: BBC/Reuters sources: at least nine killed
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-012.n: Date computed from weekday ("Tuesday") and the UN Group of Experts date of 24 February 2026 for the Rubaya strike (existing claim r1-UC-M23-010); BBC page date shown is approximate (page header not clearly dated, verifier to confirm). Reuters story not fetched. Language: Kinyarwanda/Kirundi (BBC Gahuza). Wazalendo spokesperson claim that Makenga sheltered in a church is in the page but not recorded here.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-012.vn: Page and date confirmed; Rubaya location added by a replacement quote; credited to Reuters. BBC Gahuza page published 26 February 2026 ('Yatangajwe 26 Ukwa kabiri 2026'); the information is Reuters', from four unnamed people. 'uwari umuvugizi' means 'who was the spokesperson' (Ngoma, killed in the strike), not a former spokesperson. The page says BBC could not reach M23 or FARDC for comment. Tuesday 24 February 2026 agrees with the UN Group's date for the Rubaya strike.
src: Igitero cy'indege nto y'intambara itajyamo umupilote (drone) cyishe uwari umuvugizi wa gisirikare w'umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa AFC/M23, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, mu rukerera rwo ku wa kabiri, cyiciwemo abantu nibura icyenda ariko gihushaho gato umukuru wa gisirikare w'uwo mutwe, Jenerali (Gen) Sultani Makenga, wahunze nta nkomyi, nkuko abantu bane babibwiye ibiro ntaramakuru Reuters.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014.s: Human Rights Watch reported that its research and the United Nations indicate that the M23's Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera directed military training with support from other M23 officers, and that Rwandan military trainers operated in both Rumangabo and Tshanzu.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014.n: Date shown is year-level (HRW says conduct was in 2025). HRW also names Kanyamibwa and Masozera in its recommendation to sanction M23 camp commanders and instructors (not recorded as separate claim). Kanyamibwa is also in r1-UC-M23-016 (UN GoE).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014.vn: Narrowed to the passage's own structure: the sentence ties Rumangabo and Tshanzu to the Rwandan trainers clause. The passage is in HRW's section on 'M23 and Rwandan Commanders and Forces at the Centers'. HRW also writes that Rumangabo and Tshanzu are the M23's two main training centers.
src: Human Rights Watch research and the United Nations indicate that the M23’s Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Masozera directed military training with support from other M23 officers, and that Rwandan military trainers operated in both Rumangabo and Tshanzu.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-015.s: Human Rights Watch reported, in its section 'Summary Executions and Beatings' on former detainees from Rumangabo, that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', was named by a dozen former detainees as having been particularly brutal in his treatment of recruits, and that detainees often referred to him by the nickname Longangi.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-015.n: Allegation by former detainees as reported by HRW; the excerpt itself does not name Rumangabo, the surrounding section concerns Rumangabo (HRW elsewhere in the report quotes a detainee held at Rumangabo in May 2025). Verifier to confirm camp attribution against the page and shorten the statement if unsupported.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-015.vn: Camp attribution checked against the page: Rumangabo is supported by the following sentence, not by the excerpt; statement left as written. Allegation by former detainees as reported by HRW, in its section on executions and beatings at Rumangabo. The excerpt does not name the camp; the next sentences on the page do: 'Several witnesses said that Gaston executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025.' HRW adds that Amurabi was a legal defender in the military justice system in Goma, and that former detainees said Gaston was reprimanded after the execution but returned to the camp the following month. LEAD: extend the excerpt (source_edits.py add_excerpt) to record the Amurabi execution allegation as its own claim with Amurabi in victims_named. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: HRW section on summary executions and beatings at Rumangabo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Place slippage: the excerpt does not tie the brutality allegation to Rumangabo; the camp comes from the section heading and the next sentence (the Amurabi execution 'in Rumangabo'). Amended so the camp is HRW's section context, not part of the detainees' allegation. Allegation stays with 'a dozen former detainees'.; excerpt-support: added the section heading and opening sentence as an excerpt; wording follows the heading ('Summary Executions and Beatings') and its first sentence ('Many former detainees from Rumangabo')
src: One M23 commander, “Captain Gaston,” was named by a dozen former detainees as having been particularly brutal in his treatment of recruits. [96] Detainees often referred to Gaston by the nickname Longangi,

Summary Executions and Beatings Many former detainees from Rumangabo said that even minor infractions—such as responding late to a whistle, searching for food, asking for water, moving without permission, asking to go to the latrines, speaking Lingala, or taking too long to walk—resulted in brutal punishment.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-016.s: Human Rights Watch reported that senior AFC/M23 leaders including Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, Maj. Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bertrand Bisimwa, and commanders such as Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, Bertrand Byamungu, John Imani Nzenze and Willy Ngoma, were all reported to have been seen at the Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers in 2025.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-016.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu training centers, Rutshuru territory
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-016.n: HRW writes "Bertrand Byamungu" here; the UN and other sources print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu. Presence at a site is not a finding of responsibility for abuses there.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-016.vn: Passage matches; the identity of 'both training centers' is supplied by another passage on the same page. HRW's wording is hedged ('reported to have been seen'). HRW prints 'Bertrand Byamungu'; other sources print Bernard (Maheshe) Byamungu, the UN only 'Byamungu'. Being seen at a site is not a finding of responsibility.
src: Senior AFC/M23 leaders, including AFC leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, M23 military commander Maj. Gen. Sultani Makenga, M23 President Bertrand Bisimwa, and other M23 leaders or commanders such as Gen. Baudoin Ngaruye, Bertrand Byamungu, John Imani Nzenze, and Willy Ngoma, were all reported to have been seen at both training centers in 2025

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that in early December 2025 more than 100 Mai-Mai fighters surrendered to AFC/M23 in Uvira in the presence of General Byamungu Maheshe, described as deputy commander of the AFC/M23.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-017.x: Kivu Morning Post: more than 100 Mai-Mai fighters
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-017.n: Single local outlet; source for the surrender figures is not stated in the excerpt. The page prints "AF-CM23" (typo for AFC/M23).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-017.vn: Passage matches; kept at C as a lead. Single local outlet, unsigned ('La Rédaction'), in an aside to a report on a Masisi surrender; it gives no source for the Uvira surrender. 'Early December 2025' sits awkwardly with other reports placing AFC/M23's entry into Uvira on 10 December 2025; not resolved. Name printed as 'Byamungu Maheshe'.
src: Au début du mois de décembre 2025, plus de 100 combattants maïmaï s’étaient rendu à l’AFC-M23 à Uvira, en présence du Général Byamungu Maheshe commandant adjoint de l’AF-CM23.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-018.s: Actualite.cd reported that the day after attacks on Wazalendo positions on 25 September in the groupements of Kaniola and Kamisimibi, General Bernard Byamungu, described as the movement's number two, held a public meeting at Nzibira in Walungu territory.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-018.n: "Le lendemain" (the next day) is relative to 25 September; the date 26 September is computed from that. Sentence on Wazalendo positions is attributed by the page to the M23 offensive context ("le M23 a progressé depuis Nzibira").
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-018.vn: Passage matches; Walungu territory supported by the preceding sentence. The page does not say who targeted the Wazalendo positions; the surrounding sentence concerns M23's advance from Nzibira. 26 September is computed from 'le lendemain'.
src: Le 25 septembre, des positions Wazalendo ont été visées dans les groupements de Kaniola et Kamisimibi. Le lendemain, le général Bernard Byamungu, numéro deux du mouvement, a tenu un meeting public à Nzibira.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-019.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Monday 29 December, at an exchange of wishes of senior AFC/M23 cadres in Goma, the military coordinator of the AFC/M23 and ARC chief of staff, General-Major Sultani Makenga, told participants: 'Soyez en état de guerre, cette guerre nous allons la gagner'.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-019.n: Titles as printed by the outlet. Three excerpts from one page (one contiguous passage each).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-019.vn: All three passages match one page. Byline Blaise Basabose, Kivu Morning Post, 30 December 2025. Titles as printed by the outlet.
src: Le coordonnateur militaire de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo/Mouvement du 23 mars (AFC/M23) et chef d’état-major de l’Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC), le général-major Sultani Makenga, a appelé lundi 29 décembre
Il s’exprimait à l’occasion d’un échange de vœux réunissant les hauts cadres de l’AFC/M23 à Goma
« Soyez en état de guerre, cette guerre nous allons la gagner » , a déclaré Sultani Makenga

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-020.s: Enquete.cd reported from Goma on 24 May 2026, according to sources close to the rebellion, that Bernard Maheshe Byamungu, alias 'Tiger One', described as one of the main military chiefs of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition, had died after being wounded in a drone strike.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-020.l: Goma (dateline); strike location not stated in the excerpt
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-020.n: CONTRADICTED the same week: FNTV (23 May) reported that the dead man was a Wazalendo colonel with the same surname and that Gen. Bernard Byamungu was alive (separate claim). The UN Group of Experts final report (5 June 2026) names Byamungu among zone leaders without mentioning a death. Treat the death as unconfirmed.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-020.vn: Passage matches; recorded only as a single partisan-sourced report, kept separate from the denial. UNCONFIRMED AND CONTESTED. Enquete.cd (byline Junior Kanyiki) relies on unnamed sources close to the rebellion and one unnamed M23 officer. FNTV, a day earlier (23 May 2026), retracted its own report and said the man killed was a Wazalendo colonel with the same surname and that Gen. Bernard Byamungu was alive. The UN Group's final report (5 June 2026) lists a 'General' Byamungu as a zone commander and mentions no death. No AFC/M23 statement found. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-010: Single report from unnamed sources close to the rebellion; FNTV had retracted a similar report a day earlier (Wazalendo colonel namesake, general alive), the UN Group's report of 5 June 2026 still lists a 'General' Byamungu as zone commander, and a fresh search found no confirmation and no AFC/M23 statement (earlier death rumours about 'General Byamungu' also circulated). The 'AFC/M23-RDF coalition' framing is the outlet's. Keep it only as an unconfirmed, contested report next to the retraction; if D is not in the rubric, keep C with a mandatory 'unconfirmed; contested' flag.
src: Goma, 24 mai 2026- Bernard Maheshe Byamungu, alias « Tiger One », l’un des principaux chefs militaires de la coalition AFC/M23-RDF, est décédé après avoir été blessé lors d’une frappe de drone, selon des sources proches de la rébellion.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-021.s: FNTV reported on 23 May 2026 that, after checking with several local sources and Wazalendo movements, it could give a clear denial that General Bernard Byamungu of the AFC/M23 had died: the man killed in the drone attack was a Wazalendo commander with the same name, colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, active in the Uvira high plateaux.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-021.a: Wazalendo (colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, per FNTV); AFC/M23 (General Bernard Byamungu)
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-021.n: Outlet states it had first relayed the rumour without full cross-checking. The URL slug and title in search results ("Tiger One tombe") differ from the corrected page title. Single local outlet; its sources are unnamed. Conflicts with Enquete.cd claim of the same week.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-021.vn: Passage matches; Ruvungi placed by the page's opening paragraph. UNCONFIRMED. FNTV (byline Freddy Tshiyoyo) says it had first relayed the rumour without full cross-checking; its sources are unnamed. It says witnesses attributed the drone strikes at Ruvungi locally to the rebels. Conflicts with the Enquete.cd report of 24 May 2026; neither is established.
src: Après vérification auprès de plusieurs sources locales et de mouvements Wazalendo, nous sommes en mesure d’apporter un démenti clair : le général Bernard Byamungu est vivant. L’homme décédé dans cette attaque n’est pas le cadre militaire de l’AFC/M23, mais un commandant Wazalendo portant le même nom : le colonel Byamungu Ruduga Abdallah, actif dans les hauts plateaux d’Uvira.

r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-022.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that FARDC brigadier general François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) led by Joseph Kabila; FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said he joined the ranks of the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC).
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-022.a: FRN / ARC (partisan account by FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka)
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-022.n: Party claim (FRN/AFC-M23 side, spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka); no FARDC/government statement found yet. Page is dated 28 October 2026 ("6 hours ago" at search time); the 12th military region is a FARDC region (Kongo-Central), not an AFC/M23 unit, which resolves the roster lead "12e région militaire". Relevant to ARC (M23 army) recruitment of FARDC officers.
r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-022.vn: Both passages match; kept at C as a party account. Party claim (FRN spokesperson). The page says 'official sources' (unnamed) had him travel via Lufu and Luvu (Angola) before reaching Goma, and quotes the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu vice-governor. No FARDC or government statement found. Event outside the Kivus apart from the Goma arrival.
ent: Front pour la Refondation de la Nation
src: Le général de brigade François KAMANZI, commandant des opérations de la 12ᵉ Région militaire, au Kongo-Central, a rejoint le mouvement politico-militaire Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), dirigé par Joseph KABILA.
a rejoint les rangs des Lions de Sarambwe, au sein de l’Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC) », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole du FRN.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that the staff of the 34th military region announced it had detained at Walikale two Wazalendo commanders accused of indiscipline and of violence that seriously affected civilians: self-proclaimed generals Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, of the COPACO movement (Coalition des Patriotes au Congo), and Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-001.a: 34th military region staff (FARDC); Wazalendo/VDP commanders of COPACO
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-001.n: Army communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd; the arrest is the army's account. The two commanders' response not found. Not in the existing UC-FARDC or UCD-FARDC-WZ claims (which hold the South Kivu Wazalendo).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-001.vn: Excerpt matches the page and supports every clause; attribution to the army kept. The arrests and the accusations are the army's account (34th military region communiqué relayed by Actualite.cd); no response from the two commanders was found.
src: L’état-major de la 34ᵉ région militaire a annoncé avoir interpellé à Walikale, deux commandants des wazalendo accusés d’être impliqués dans des actes d’indiscipline et des violences ayant gravement affecté les populations civiles. Il s’agit des généraux autoproclamés Kirikicho Mirimba, alias Mwana Mayi, du mouvement COPACO (Coalition des Patriotes au Congo), et Musubao Kalimba, alias Kasilasi.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the military authorities, the two Wazalendo commanders had been engaged in fratricidal clashes for nearly 17 months, the most recent being the fighting of 15 to 18 February 2026 in the groupements of Tushunguti and Zirhalo, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory (South Kivu); according to the army, these clashes caused 14 civilian deaths, 7 seriously wounded and 7 women victims of rape.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.l: Tushunguti and Zirhalo groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe (South Kivu)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.a: the two Wazalendo commanders detained by the army, as characterised by the military authorities
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.x: army (via Actualite.cd): 14 civilians killed, 7 seriously wounded, 7 women victims of rape
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.n: Figures are the army's, via one outlet; no UN/NGO figure found for this clash. Location is in South Kivu (Kalehe) but the units are those arrested in North Kivu (Walikale).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-002.vn: Statement reordered so the link to the two commanders is explicitly the army's; figures field had a unit ordinal; actor no longer names people the excerpts do not print. Toll and the link between the Kalehe fighting and the two commanders are the army's account; the page does not say which side committed the rapes. Survivors not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les violents combats survenus du 15 au 18 février 2026 dans les groupements de Tushunguti et Zirhalo, situés dans la chefferie de Buhavu, en territoire de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu sont les plus récents. Selon l’armée, ces affrontements ont fait 14 morts parmi les civils, 7 blessés graves et 7 femmes victimes de viol
D’après les autorités militaires, les deux commandants se livrent depuis près de 17 mois à des affrontements fratricides.

Le cas le plus flagrant est celui des derniers affrontements du 15 au 18 Fev 26, dans les groupements de Tushunguti et Zirhalo, chefferie de Buhavu, territoire de Kalehe dont le bilan est de 14 paisibles citoyens tués, 7 autres grièvement blessés, 07 femmes violées

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that fifty-four soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC had been appearing since Monday 26 October before the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, North Kivu, prosecuted notably for murder, abandoning post, dissipation of war munitions and refusal to obey.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-003.n: First North Kivu source for the 3411th/3415th regiment numbering in this unit. Verdict not yet reported at the date of the page.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-003.vn: Figure spelled as the excerpt prints it; actor no longer asserts the regiment's parent region, which the page does not state. Prosecution stage only: the page says the verdict was expected in early November. Being prosecuted is not a finding of guilt.
ent: tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma
src: Cinquante-quatre militaires du 3415e régiment des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) comparaissent depuis le lundi 26 octobre devant le tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma, siégeant en audience foraine à Walikale, au Nord-Kivu. Ils sont notamment poursuivis pour assassinat, abandon de poste, dissipation de munitions de guerre et refus d’obéissance.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, the defendants were arrested on 20 October following incidents at Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, on the border with Masisi territory, which left two dead, a soldier and a civilian; the page says the facts allegedly occurred during an altercation between the soldiers and Military Police elements trying to stop them from leaving the combat zone without authorisation.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.l: Ntoto, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale (territory), North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.a: FARDC soldiers (the defendants) and Military Police elements, per the 34th military region spokesperson
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.x: Radio Okapi, citing the 34th military region spokesperson: two dead (a soldier and a civilian)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.n: Date of the incident is not stated; the arrest date (20 October) is given. The page's 'a soldier and a civilian' dead and wounded are not named.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-004.vn: Supported; figures field rewritten without bare numerals; actor narrowed to what the page says. 20 October is the arrest date; the incident date is not printed. The page also reports two wounded (a soldier and a civilian). The cause is conditional on the page ('se seraient produits').
src: Selon le major Dieudonné Kasereka, chargé de communication de la 34e Région militaire, les prévenus ont été interpellés le 20 octobre à la suite d’incidents survenus à Ntoto, dans le groupement de Waloa Loanda, à la frontière avec le territoire de Masisi. Ces incidents ont fait deux morts, un militaire et un civil
Les faits se seraient produits lors d’une altercation entre les militaires et des éléments de la Police militaire qui tentaient de les empêcher de quitter sans autorisation la zone de combat.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that another group of ten soldiers of the same regiment had been convicted on 1 September to sentences ranging from ten months of prison to principal penal servitude for opening fire on their company commander.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-005.a: FARDC soldiers of the same regiment as the Walikale defendants
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-005.n: The year is not printed in the sentence; the page is dated 2026-10-27 and says 'le 1er septembre dernier'. Place of the 1 September trial not stated in the excerpt.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-005.vn: Removed the regiment number that this excerpt does not print; territory not stated by the page. 'The same regiment' is the 3415th regiment named earlier in the same Radio Okapi report (see the claim on the 54 defendants). Year inferred from 'le 1er septembre dernier' on a page dated 27 October 2026. Court findings concern the convicted soldiers only; the court and place are not stated.
src: Un autre groupe de dix militaires du même régiment avait été condamné le 1er septembre dernier à des peines allant de dix mois de prison à des peines de servitude pénale principale, pour avoir ouvert le feu sur leur commandant de compagnie.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that three FARDC soldiers, all from the 21st principal defence brigade, were sentenced to twenty years in prison each for collective rape in Lubero: the court found them guilty of sexually assaulting a 28-year-old woman in the village of Kimbulu during the night from Sunday to the previous Monday, and ordered them to pay jointly 10,000 US dollars to the victim in reparation.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.l: Kimbulu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.a: three soldiers of the 21st principal defence brigade, FARDC (convicted)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.x: Radio Okapi: three convicted, twenty years each; 10,000 USD damages jointly
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.n: Victim not named. Date of the assault computed from 'dimanche à lundi dernier' relative to a 9 July 2026 publication (verdict given 'il y a deux jours'); the exact date is not printed. First FARDC-unit-named sexual violence case for Lubero in this unit's scope. Single outlet.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-006.vn: Supported by excerpts and title; statement no longer depends on page-only details (tribunal name, fines moved to note); figures rewritten. Court findings concern the three convicted soldiers only. The tribunal is the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal per the page; each was also fined 250,000 Congolese francs. The survivor is not named by the source. Offence date not printed; relative to a page dated 9 July 2026. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: 21ᵉ brigade de défense principale des FARDC
src: Les trois condamnés sont tous issus de la 21ᵉ brigade de défense principale des FARDC. Le tribunal les a reconnus coupables d'avoir agressé sexuellement une femme de 28 ans dans le village de Kimbulu. Les faits se sont déroulés au cours de la nuit de dimanche à lundi dernier.
Les trois militaires sont condamnés au paiement solidaire de 10 000 dollars américains en faveur de la victime, en réparation des préjudices subis.
Les trois condamnés, tous issus de la 21ᵉ brigade de défense principale des FARDC, ont été reconnus coupables d’avoir agressé sexuellement une femme de 28 ans.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was sentenced to seven years of penal servitude for the rape of a 15-year-old girl; according to the court, the facts took place in the village of Kaviseghe, and the soldier allegedly had sexual relations with the adolescent several times in his room.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.l: Kaviseghe village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.a: a FARDC soldier (unit not stated, convicted)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.x: Radio Okapi: one soldier convicted, seven years
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.n: Minor victim; not named by the source. Hearing 'lundi dernier' (Monday before 21 August 2026, computed 17 August); date of the offence not stated.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-007.vn: Tribunal name and Kipese hearing are page-only (not in the excerpt): moved to the note; 'citing local sources' applied only to the hearing details on the page, so removed from the statement. The victim is a minor and is not named by the source. Per the page, the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal ruled 'lundi dernier' at a circuit hearing at Kipese, Lubero territory, 'selon des sources locales'. Court findings concern the convicted soldier only. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: un autre militaire a été condamné à sept ans de servitude pénale pour le viol d’une adolescente âgée de 15 ans. Selon le tribunal, les faits se sont déroulés au village de Kaviseghe. Le militaire aurait eu à plusieurs reprises des rapports sexuels avec l’adolescente dans sa chambre.
Selon le tribunal, les faits se sont déroulés au village de Kaviseghe.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was found guilty of the murder of three people (his partner, their child and another soldier) in facts dating back to 12 August at the village of Katundu; according to the elements retained by the court, he had opened fire point-blank on his partner in a context of jealousy.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.l: Katundu village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.a: a FARDC soldier (unit not stated, convicted)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.x: Radio Okapi: three killed (his partner, their child, a soldier)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.n: Family/intimate-partner killing by a soldier; recorded because the brief asks for all alleged violations by FARDC personnel. Victims not named.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-008.vn: Sentence, damages and hearing place are not in the excerpt: moved to the note; statement limited to the excerpt. Per the page, the Butembo-Lubero garrison military tribunal, at a circuit hearing at Kipese (Lubero territory), sentenced him to death and to 20,000 US dollars in damages; the child was a girl ('leur fillette') who, with the other soldier, died of wounds. Victims not named. Court findings concern the convicted soldier only.
src: Dans la première affaire, un militaire des FARDC a été reconnu coupable du meurtre de trois personnes : sa concubine, leur enfant et un autre militaire. Les faits remontent au 12 août, au village de Katundu. Selon les éléments retenus par le tribunal, le militaire avait ouvert le feu à bout portant sur sa concubine dans un contexte de jalousie.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal (North Kivu) sentenced three FARDC officers (two lieutenants and a captain) to death for desertion and breach of orders, after they had been recruited, according to the court, by a man presenting himself as coordinator of the Comité national des patriotes (CONAP); two men presenting themselves as Wazalendo commanders got twenty years in prison for, notably, illegally recruiting soldiers and spreading false information, having set up, according to military justice, a clandestine recruitment network in the Malepe quarter of Beni using without mandate the name of the Réserve armée de la défense (RAD); the verdict came on the evening of Friday 10 July.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009.a: Beni garrison military tribunal; three FARDC officers; self-styled CONAP coordinator and a collaborator (convicted)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009.x: Radio Okapi: three FARDC officers sentenced to death; two self-styled Wazalendo commanders, twenty years each
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009.n: The two Wazalendo 'commanders' are not named; the page says the group presented itself as the national patriots committee (CONAP). Illustrates the RAD (Réserve armée de la défense) as a name in use; the court said the recruiters used it without a mandate.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009.vn: Clarified that the CONAP man recruited the three officers (per the court) and that the RAD network is military justice's finding; figures rewritten. Per the page, the self-styled coordinator was convicted with one collaborator ('Quant au prétendu coordonnateur des Wazalendu, il est condamné avec un de ses collaborateurs à vingt ans de prison'); neither is named. The convicted have five days to appeal. Court findings concern the convicted only.
ent: tribunal militaire de garnison de Beni
src: Le tribunal militaire de garnison de Beni (Nord-Kivu) a condamné à la peine capitale trois officiers des FARDC pour désertion et violation de consignes.
Deux hommes se présentant comme des commandants Wazalendo ont, eux, écopé de vingt ans de prison pour avoir notamment recruté illégalement des militaires et diffusé de fausses informations.
Le verdict est tombé vendredi 10 juillet soir, à l'issue d'un procès en flagrance.
Les militaires condamnés à la peine de mort sont deux lieutenants et un capitaine.

Selon le tribunal, ils avaient été recrutés par un homme, qui se présentait comme coordonnateur du Comité national des patriotes, le CONAP, une structure qui prétendait de regrouper l'ensemble des groupes Wazalendo du pays.

Selon la justice militaire, ils avaient mis en place, dans le quartier Malepe à Beni, un réseau clandestin de recrutement des civils et des militaires, en utilisant abusivement, et sans mandat officiel, le nom de la Réserve armée de la défense, la RAD.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that a member of the Wazalendo movement called « Far West » was sentenced to death on Wednesday 6 May, the Butembo garrison military tribunal having found him guilty of the murder of a motorcyclist and of the rape followed by murder of his female customer, facts which occurred the previous week at Kimbulu, Lubero territory; Lubero civil society also demanded the outright abolition of the « Far West » movement, which it accuses of being involved in serious human rights violations.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010.a: a member of the Wazalendo movement 'Far West'
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010.x: Radio Okapi: two killed (a motorcyclist and his female customer); one death sentence
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010.n: Offence date computed from 'la semaine dernière' relative to the 6 May hearing and a 9 May publication; the later 5 May communiqué quoted on the page says 'jeudi dernier' for the double killing (30 April 2026 if the Thursday before 5 May). Victims not named. Same village (Kimbulu) as the July 2026 collective rape by 21st-brigade soldiers. Contradicting reporting: Actualite.cd (2026-05-07): verdict date: Thursday 7 May instead of Wednesday 6 May
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-010.vn: 'Motard' / 'cliente' translated as printed; figures rewritten without bare numerals. The convicted man and the victims are not named. A civil society communiqué of 5 May quoted on the page dates the double killing to 'jeudi dernier' and describes the victims as a motorcycle-taxi driver and his customer. Court findings concern the convicted man only; the civil society accusation against the movement is its own. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 3 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 4 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 5 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: tribunal militaire de garnison de Butembo
src: Cet appel intervient après la condamnation à la peine de mort, mercredi 6 mai, d’un membre du mouvement Wazalendo dénommé « Far West ».

Ce dernier a été reconnu coupable par le tribunal militaire de garnison de Butembo du meurtre d’un motard, ainsi que du viol suivi du meurtre de sa cliente, des faits survenus la semaine dernière à Kimbulu, dans le territoire de Lubero.
Elle demande également la suppression pure et simple du mouvement « Far West », qu’elle accuse d’être impliqué dans de graves violations des droits humains.
Le jugement est tombé à l'issue d'une audience foraine tenue à Kimbulu, dans le territoire de Lubero.
Le tribunal a précisé que cette dernière avait subi un viol avant d'être froidement exécutée.

Selon le tribunal, la jeune femme avait d’abord été violée avant d’être exécutée. En plus de la peine capitale, le tribunal a décidé d’interdire le fonctionnement du groupe de miliciens Far West sur toute l’étendue du territoire de Lubero.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the rebels of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) and the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo, continued for the third consecutive day on Sunday 18 October 2026 at Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu, the FARDC and Wazalendo having launched an offensive against FRN positions there to dislodge the rebels; the outlet says Kibati has for about two years been one of the main foci of confrontation between the FRN and government forces supported by the Wazalendo in that part of Walikale.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-011.l: Kibati, Luberike groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-011.a: FARDC and Wazalendo (offensive); FRN rebels (as the source names them)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-011.n: The source does not say that the FRN is the same as the AFC/M23 (other 2026 pages in this unit use FRN and ARC for the rebel side in Rutshuru). Actualite.cd says Kibati has been a main focus of confrontation for about two years. No casualty figures yet. Excerpt is >60 words? see check.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-011.vn: Removed 'since Friday', which the page attaches to the fighting, not to the offensive; added the third excerpt's context. The page does not say whether the FRN is the same organisation as the AFC/M23; do not equate them on this source. The page says the human and material toll was not yet known and that FRN reinforcements reached Kibati on Saturday morning (per sources at Kashebere).
ent: Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)
src: Les affrontements entre les rebelles du Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) et les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les Wazalendo, se poursuivent pour la troisième journée consécutive, ce dimanche 18 octobre 2026, à Kibati, dans le groupement Luberike, en territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu.
Les FARDC et les Wazalendo ont lancé une offensive contre les positions du FRN dans cette zone, dans le but de déloger les rebelles.

Depuis environ deux ans, Kibati constitue l’un des principaux foyers de confrontation entre le FRN et les forces gouvernementales appuyées par les Wazalendo dans cette partie du territoire de Walikale.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that two AFC/M23 commanders deployed at Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, were kidnapped by Wazalendo in the night of Sunday to Monday 30 June, the sources not giving their identities; on the Monday the AFC/M23 searched the forest of Kirumburumbu and Muuli in vain and forced farmers to leave their fields to continue the search.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.l: between Kirumburumbu and Muuli villages, near Misinga, Ikobo groupement, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.a: Wazalendo (as local sources say); AFC/M23 commanders as victims
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.x: local sources via Actualite.cd: two commanders kidnapped
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.n: Single outlet, anonymous local sources; the fate of the two commanders was unknown at the time of publication. Captors' headquarters said to be at Buhimba.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-012.vn: Supported; figures rewritten; search detail made precise. Per the page the captors took the two to Buhimba, where they set up their headquarters, and the commanders' fate was unknown by evening. Single outlet, local sources.
src: Deux commandants des rebelles de l'AFC/M23 qui étaient déployés à Misinga, dans le groupement Ikobo (territoire de Walikale), au Nord-Kivu ont été enlevés par les wazalendo la nuit de dimanche à lundi 30 juin, a appris ACTUALITE.CD des sources locales. Ces dernières ne donnent pas l’identité de ces deux rebelles kidnappés.

Ce lundi, les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 ont lancé des recherches dans la forêt de Kirumburumbu et Muuli afin de retrouver les auteurs du kidnapping de leurs commandants mais en vain. Ils se sont rabattus sur les cultivateurs qui étaient dans leurs champs. Ils les ont contraints de quitter les champs pour qu'ils poursuivent les recherches.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing several local sources, that two Wazalendo factions, the ACNDH group led by self-proclaimed general Jean-Marie and another group led by Ignace Sauli, clashed at Shengesha, Masisi territory, fighting with heavy and light weapons throughout the day and driving residents to flee; the outlet also reported clashes the same day involving CMC-FDP Wazalendo in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, concentrated in Mudugugudu village.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-014.l: Shengesha, Bashali chiefdom, Masisi; Mudugugudu, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-014.a: Wazalendo ACNDH (self-proclaimed general Jean-Marie); Wazalendo group of Ignace Sauli; CMC-FDP
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-014.n: Same 'Ignace Sauli' appears as 'Ignace Dunia Sauli' in the KMP piece on Biramba (30 June 2025); the source here does not state they are the same person. Date: day not printed for the Shengesha clash; 'samedi' refers to the Mudugugudu fighting (Saturday 1 Nov 2025, computed).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-014.vn: Date taken from the page into the date field; statement limited to the excerpts. The page dates the Shengesha clash to 'samedi 1er novembre 2025' (date field). 'Ignace Sauli' here and 'Ignace Dunia Sauli' in a June 2025 KMP report may be the same person; the source does not say so. Per the page, AFC-M23 regained control of the Mudugugudu area by Saturday evening. Per the page, Shengesha is in the Bashali chiefdom. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-007: The excerpt says clashes 'entre les Wazalendo du CMC-FDP' with no second party; the retained page goes on that the Wazalendo had reinstalled in Mudugugudu after AFC-M23's temporary withdrawal and that AFC-M23 retook the area by Saturday evening, so 'clashes between CMC-FDP Wazalendo' wrongly implies an intra-CMC-FDP fight. Amended to 'involving'. Also: independent_origins 2 is one outlet (KMP, local sources).; excerpt-support: nothing to add
src: Selon plusieurs sources locales, il s’agit des combattants Wazalendo du groupe ACNDH, dirigés par le général autoproclamé, Jean-Marie, et d’un autre groupe mené par Ignace Sauli.

Les deux factions se sont affrontées à l’arme lourde et légère tout au long de la journée. Ces affrontements ont provoqué une vive panique au sein de la population locale, contrainte de fuir vers des zones jugées plus sûres.

Par ailleurs, d’autres affrontements ont été signalés le même jour entre les Wazalendo du CMC-FDP dans le groupement de Bukombo, chefferie de Bwito territoire de Rutshuru. Les combats se sont concentrés dans le village de Mudugugudu,

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to first reports, Wazalendo led by self-proclaimed general Ignace Dunia Sauli attacked M23 positions at Biramba, Masisi territory, causing exchanges of heavy-weapon fire, after fighting at Luhonga on Sunday 29 June.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-015.l: Biramba and Luhonga, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-015.a: Wazalendo led by self-proclaimed general Ignace Dunia Sauli; AFC-M23
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-015.n: Only early reports; no casualty figures in the cited passage. Identifies a Wazalendo commander (Ignace Dunia Sauli) active in Bashali Mokoto, Masisi.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-015.vn: Statement limited to the excerpt and title (Biramba, Masisi); the 30 June date and groupement, printed on the page but not in the stored excerpt, are in the note and the date field. Per the page, the Biramba clashes broke out on Monday 30 June 2025 at Biramba (Lwama locality near Luhonga, Bashali Mokoto groupement); much of the population had left on the Sunday evening towards Mpati or neighbouring villages. Early reports only; no casualty figures.
src: Selon les premières informations, les Wazalendo, conduits par le général autoproclamé Ignace Dunia Sauli, ont lancé une attaque contre les positions des éléments M23, entraînant un échange de tirs d’armes lourdes. Des combats avaient déjà été enregistrés dimanche 29 juin à Luhonga.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least nine civilians were killed and several others seriously wounded, among them three children including a five-year-old girl, in an armed incursion by presumed CMC-FDP Wazalendo militiamen into Bishusha groupement, Rutshuru territory, in the night of Monday to Tuesday 28 October 2025; according to anonymous health sources at Bishusha Centre, the armed men came in around 19 h, largely targeting local traders, and goods and shops were looted.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-016.l: Bishusha groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-016.x: Kivu Morning Post: at least nine civilians killed; several wounded including three children
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-016.n: Area under AFC-M23 control per the page; the attribution to CMC-FDP is 'presumed' and rests on anonymous health sources and a victim quote. Excerpt must be checked for length.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-016.vn: Supported; the toll is the outlet's lead (also given by a health source), so 'citing health sources' narrowed to the clauses it carries; figures rewritten. Attribution to CMC-FDP is 'presumed'; a health source quoted on the page calls the attackers 'bandits assimilés aux CMC-FDP'. Per the page, AFC-M23 elements intervened and exchanged fire with the assailants, and the wounded were being treated at a local health facility. Victims, including the injured children, are not named.
src: Au moins neuf civils ont été tués et plusieurs autres grièvement blessés dans une incursion armée des présumés miliciens Wazalendo CMC-FDP dans le groupement de Bishusha en territoire de Rutshuru dans la province du Nord-Kivu, la nuit du lundi au mardi 28 octobre 2025.

Selon nos sources sanitaires à Bishusha Centre, sous couvert d’anonymat, c’est autour de 19 h que ces hommes, armés, ont menées une incursion dans cette agglomération, ciblant en grande partie des opérateurs économiques de la région, qui figurent en nombre parmi les victimes. Lors de l’attaque, plusieurs biens et boutiques des habitants ont été pillés.
Parmi les blessés, on compte trois enfants, dont une fillette de 5 ans, ainsi qu’un homme dont l’état est critique.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the administrator of Rutshuru territory under the FRN, Euphrem Kabasha, accused the Wazalendo of the CMC of being behind an attack that killed civilians at Kabizo, saying that in the night of 25 to 26 October, at about 1:30, Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, was attacked by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi, and that five people were killed.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.l: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.a: FDLR with Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi, as alleged by the FRN-side Rutshuru territory administrator
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.x: administrator of Rutshuru territory under the FRN (via Kivu Morning Post): five killed
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.n: The accusation comes from the administrator of the rebel-held administration (the page says 'sous le FRN'); treat as that party's claim. The source does not say whether FRN is the AFC/M23's new name; Actualite.cd's account of the same night is a separate claim (ambush on an FRN convoy).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017.vn: Statement limited to the administrator's words in the excerpts; the outlet's own 'at least five' lead (page only) moved to the note; figures rewritten. Partisan account: the accuser is the administrator of the rebel-held (FRN) administration. Kivu Morning Post's own lead says at least five people were killed in the night of 25 to 26 October 2026. The page also says the ARC intervened; it does not say whether the FRN or ARC is the AFC/M23. Actualite.cd reports the same night differently (Wazalendo ambush on an FRN convoy near Kabizo and Katovu, three rebel fighters killed); neither outlet mentions the other's account. Victims not named.
src: L’administrateur du territoire de Rutshuru sous le FRN accuse les Wazalendo du CMC d’être à l’origine de cette attaque qui a coûté la vie à ces paisibles civils.

« Dans la nuit du 25 au 26 octobre, vers 1 h 30, l’agglomération de Kabizo, dans le groupement de Tongo, chefferie de Bwito, a encore une fois été victime d’une attaque meurtrière menée par les FDLR, en compagnie des Nyatura CMC FDP de Gashegu Héritier et Mbitezi.
Cette attaque a visé les populations civiles et cinq personnes ont été tuées », a déclaré Euphrem Kabasha, administrateur du territoire de Rutshuru.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-018.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local sources, the Wazalendo ambushed a convoy of FRN rebels heading to Kabizo to install a new commander, near Kabizo and Katovu, Rutshuru, with a provisional toll of three rebel fighters killed, per sources in the area.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-018.l: Kabizo-Katovu road, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-018.x: local sources via Actualite.cd: three rebel fighters killed (provisional)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-018.n: A different account of the same night as the Kabizo killings reported by KMP (five civilians killed, per the rebel-side administrator). The two sources do not mention each other's toll.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-018.vn: Statement limited to the excerpt and title; date and road detail (page only) moved to the note. Per the page, the fighting between FRN rebels and Wazalendo took place in the night of Sunday to Monday 26 October on the road linking Kabizo and Katovu (Bwito chiefdom), and farmers stayed away from their fields that Monday. A different account of the same night from the Kivu Morning Post report, in which the FRN-side administrator says five people were killed at Kabizo by the FDLR and Nyatura CMC FDP; keep both.
src: D’après des sources locales, les wazalendo ont tendu une embuscade à un convoi des rebelles qui se dirigeait vers Kabizo pour y installer un nouveau commandant. Le bilan provisoire de cette attaque fait état de trois combattants rebelles tués, selon des sources dans la zone.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that self-proclaimed general Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », was shot dead during fighting between his Wazalendo group and that of his rival Fiston Njoli at Butembo, according to Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, president of the communal civil society; the fighting began on a Sunday morning on Munzambaye hill, Vulamba commune, and lasted until Monday 5 January, and the body was reportedly displayed publicly at Furu.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019.l: Munzambaye hill, Congo Ya Sika quarter, Vulamba commune, Butembo, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019.a: Wazalendo group of Kakule Kaputu alias « Tango Fort »; Wazalendo group of Fiston Njoli
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019.n: Single local outlet; the date of the Sunday (4 January 2026, computed from the publication date and 'lundi 5 janvier'). Civil society also condemned the displaying of the body.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-019.vn: Every clause is in the excerpts; the Sunday is 4 January 2026 by calendar, which the page does not print. The Wazalendo synergy Front Nord gave a different place (Vuvatsi, towards Kitovo) and called it an armed operation, not a targeted killing (separate claim). The display of the body is reported ('aurait été').
src: Le général autoproclamé Kakule Kaputu, alias « Tango Fort », a été abattu lors des affrontements opposant son groupe Wazalendo à celui de son rival Fiston Njoli, à Butembo, dans le Nord-Kivu.
Les combats ont éclaté dimanche matin sur la colline Munzambaye, dans le quartier Congo Ya Sika, commune de Vulamba, à l’ouest de la ville. Ils se sont poursuivis jusqu’au lundi 5 janvier,
Selon Paluku Jean-Baptiste Muyisa, président de la société civile communale, Kakule Kaputu a été mortellement atteint par balle et est décédé sur le champ.
son corps a été transporté à Furu, où il aurait été exposé publiquement,

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the spokesperson of the Wazalendo synergy Front Nord, John Mangaiko, had declared on 6 January 2026 at Butembo that Kakule Kaputu (« Tango Fort ») was killed in an armed operation and not in a targeted assassination, describing Tango Fort as an armed fighter involved in attacks on other Wazalendo and in acts of insecurity against the population; the outlet added that in a video published on 4 March 2026 at Burondo, Lubero territory, the political-military movement Bana Bateseka, a member of the Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord, announced the dissolution of the armed group Tango Fort, and that according to the video its deputy commander, colonel Thembo, announced his rallying to Bana Bateseka with all his fighters.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020.l: Butembo and Burondo, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020.a: Wazalendo synergy Front Nord (spokesperson John Mangaiko); Bana Bateseka (Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020.n: Mangaiko's account (a different place name, Vuvatsi towards Kitovo, from civil society's Munzambaye hill) is the Wazalendo synergy's account of the same death. Colonel Thembo's rally is per the Bana Bateseka video as reported.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020.vn: 'Joined it' narrowed to 'announced his rallying', per the video as reported; Burondo added from the excerpt. Mangaiko's account (per the page: killed in clashes with another Wazalendo faction at Vuvatsi, towards Kitovo) differs in place from civil society's (Munzambaye hill). The rally is per the Bana Bateseka video as reported, not independently confirmed. Two dates: 6 January 2026 (statement) and 4 March 2026 (video).
src: Le porte-parole de la synergie des Wazalendo Front Nord, John Mangaiko, avait déclaré le 6 janvier 2026 à Butembo que ce dernier avait été tué lors d’une opération armée et non dans un assassinat ciblé.
Selon lui, Tango Fort était un combattant porteur d’arme impliqué dans des attaques contre d’autres Wazalendo et dans des actes d’insécurité contre la population.

Le mouvement politico-militaire Bana Bateseka, membre des Wazalendo Front Grand-Nord, a annoncé dans une vidéo publiée le 4 mars 2026 dans l’agglomération de Burondo, en territoire de Lubero, la dissolution du groupe armé Tango Fort.
Selon cette vidéo, le colonel Thembo, commandant adjoint du groupe Tango Fort, a annoncé son ralliement à l’idéologie de Bana Bateseka avec l’ensemble de ses combattants.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-021.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing an administrative and security source in Masisi, that the self-proclaimed general Mutayomba, a Wazalendo commander on the Katoyi axis, was wounded in fighting against the AFC-M23 at Luke, Masisi territory, on 'Friday 21 May 2026'; the administrative source said he was lightly wounded and evacuated by helicopter to Beni, while a FARDC military source confirmed the injury but described it as serious.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-021.l: Luke, Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-021.a: Wazalendo commander self-proclaimed general Mutayomba, FARDC allies
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-021.n: DISCREPANCY: the page says 'vendredi 21 mai 2026', but 21 May 2026 was a Thursday; the day is kept as printed. Article dated 2026-06-01 but says 'Depuis plus d'une semaine' and 'au cours du week-end' rumours of death. Links to the existing claim naming 'Jams Mutayomba' under Wazalendo command (Radio Okapi 2026-10-05).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-021.vn: All clauses in the excerpts; weekday mismatch stated in the note. DISCREPANCY: the page prints 'vendredi 21 mai 2026', but 21 May 2026 fell on a Thursday; the date is kept as printed. The two sources disagree on the severity of the injury. The page is dated 1 June 2026.
src: Le général autoproclamé Mutayomba, l’un des commandants des Wazalendo, ces milices alliées aux FARDC, a été blessé le vendredi 21 mai 2026 à Luke, dans le territoire de Masisi.

Selon une source administrative et sécuritaire congolaise à Kivu Morning Post , le général autoproclamé Mutayomba, qui figure parmi les commandants des Wazalendo sur l’axe Katoyi, a été blessé lors des combats contre les combattants de l’AFC-M23.

« Il a été légèrement blessé lors des combats de vendredi à Luke. Il a été évacué d’urgence par hélicoptère vers Beni » , a déclaré une source administrative du territoire de Masisi. Une information confirmée par une source militaire des FARDC, qui évoque toutefois une blessure grave.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-022.s: Brigadier general Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commander of the 34th military region, reiterated his appeal for the surrender of the M23 members still active, the outlet reported.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-022.a: 34th military region, FARDC (commander Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin)
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-022.n: Shows Muhondosi still in post as 34th military region commander in October 2025 (the earlier UC-FARDC claim holds his March 2025 appointment). The page's own spelling is 'Muyuwa'; the March 2025 Cocorico.cd claim spells 'Muyusa'. Page headline: near 40 M23 fighters surrender to the FARDC (headline not cited).
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-022.vn: Removed the publication date (shown with the source) and the outlet name, whose digits the checker reads as a figure; single clause, supported verbatim; territory 'Goma' not stated by the page. Name spelled 'Muyuwa' as this page prints it (another source spells 'Muyusa'). The page, dated 20 October 2025, reports 38 AFC/M23 fighters surrendering that day to the 34th military region.
