src: Le général de brigade Muhondosi Muyuwa Constantin, commandant de la 34e région militaire, a réitéré son appel à la reddition des membres du M23 encore actifs.

r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-023.s: Actualite.cd reported that major-general Nyembo Abdallah, interim commander of the 3rd defence zone, had been staying in Walikale since Friday 21 November, a visit which major Dieudonné Kasereka, communication officer of the 34th military region, said was part of an inspection of the troops and of command; the delegation was received by the commander of the 34th region.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-023.a: 3rd defence zone (FARDC) interim commander Nyembo Abdallah; 34th military region
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-023.n: Adds a post for Nyembo Abdallah after the July 2025 telegram that sent him to the 31st military region (existing claims): by November 2025 Actualite.cd calls him interim commander of the 3rd defence zone. The 34th region commander is not named on this page.
r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-023.vn: Year removed (not printed in the excerpt); Kigoma airfield (page only) moved to the note. The page (dated 24 November 2025) does not name the 34th region commander. 'Interim' is the page's wording for Nyembo Abdallah's post at the 3rd defence zone. Per the page, the reception took place at the Kigoma airfield.
src: Le commandant ad intérim de la 3e zone de défense, le général-major Nyembo Abdallah séjourne à Walikale depuis vendredi 21 novembre; Selon le major Dieudonné Kasereka, chargé de communication de la 34ème région militaire, cette visite s'inscrit dans le cadre d'inspection des troupes et de commandement.
cette délégation a été accueillie par le commandant de la 34ème région

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 reinforcements led by "Lieutenant-Colonel" Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025, and that a second reinforcement, led by "Lieutenant -Colonel" Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked while crossing hostile areas before reaching Mikenge at the end of August 2025; it described these as support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-001.l: Minembwe and Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-001.n: S/2025/858 is already cited by other units; this claim adds the Ndabagaza reinforcement and the dating. Ranks in quotation marks as printed by the Group.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-001.vn: Para. 53 of S/2025/858 prints both reinforcements and frames them as AFC/M23 and RDF military support to besieged MRDP-Twirwaneho-controlled enclaves. Ranks in quotes as printed. 'End of August' is 2025 by context (March 2025 sentence, report of 30 Dec 2025).
src: After AFC/M23 reinforcements led by “Lieutenant-Colonel” Japhet Gakufe reached Minembwe in March 2025 (S/2025/446, para. 178), a second reinforcement, led by “Lieutenant -Colonel” Oscar Ndabagaza, was blocked as it attempted to cross hostile areas before finally reaching Mikenge at the end of August.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories there was a sharp escalation in human rights violations, including conflict-related sexual violence, extortion and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23; it also said that Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba had expanded their operations and perpetrated abuses, and that at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu between January and June 2025.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.l: Uvira and Fizi territories, South Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.a: Mai-Mai Yakutumba, Raia Mutomboki and other Wazalendo factions aligned with Yakutumba
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.x: Group of Experts: at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims in South Kivu, January-June 2025 (province-wide, not attributed to a single group)
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.n: The 325-case figure is South Kivu province-wide and is not attributed to a named group by this passage. Raia Mutomboki is named only generally (no faction leader or place).
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002.vn: All three passages exact on the retained PDF (annex 38, 'Alarming surge in conflict-related sexual violence'). Statement keeps the figure separate from the group attribution. From annex 38 of S/2025/858. The 325-case figure is province-wide, drawn from verified reports gathered by UN-supported national NGOs, and the annex says it reflects underreporting in government-controlled areas; it is not attributed to Yakutumba or any single group.
src: In areas under the control of Mai-Mai Yakutumba and affiliated Wazalendo armed groups in Uvira and Fizi territories, the recent months were marked by a sharp escalation in human rights violations, including conflict-related sexual violence (CRSV), extortion, and summary executions of civilians accused of collaborating with AFC/M23.

The security vacuum created by the absence of FARDC, and the prevailing climate of impunity has enabled various armed groups – predominantly Raia Mutomboki and other factions aligned with Yakutumba – to expand their operations and perpetrate abuses with little restraint.

Between January and June 2025, at least 325 cases of sexual violence affecting over 400 victims were documented in South Kivu province alone, exceeding the total figures recorded in all other provinces combined for the same period.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in its final report that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-003.n: Sematama already appears in earlier claims; this adds the strength estimate in the final report (S/2026/466, para. 84).
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-003.vn: Para. 84 of S/2026/466 prints the estimate and leader.
src: 84. The strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama (see S/2025/446, para. 176).

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks, and that, as previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-004.n: The 'as previously reported' recruitment statement refers to earlier Group reports (S/2023/431); the time of the 2025-26 events is approximate (the report says Minembwe encircled since mid-2025). Excerpt includes the footnote marker '97' as printed in the extracted PDF text.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-004.vn: Para. 87 of S/2026/466; 'as previously reported' kept, so the recruitment statement is the Group's restatement of earlier findings, not a new 2026 documentation. The Group says the compulsory recruitment of boys aged 10-12 and able-bodied men was 'previously reported'; the date of that practice is not fixed by this passage.
src: 87. Concomitantly, MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving Minembwe, including through coercion and threats of violence, fearing defections and information leaks. 97 As previously reported, all boys between 10 and 12 years of age and all able-bodied men were compelled to join Twirwaneho and participate in combat

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that, although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23, RED Tabara combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF across several axes; that FNL elements were present in the Nyaburunda forest (Uvira territory), in mountainous areas near Sange and in Magunda, where they co-locate with RED Tabara units; and that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-005.l: Masango, Magunda, Kipupu, Nyaburunda forest, Sange, Kamombo sector; Uvira, Mwenga and Fizi territories, South Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-005.n: No named RED-Tabara or FNL commander in this passage; leaders not found in the Group's text searched.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-005.vn: Draft said both groups 'fought alongside MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23' and dropped RDF; the excerpt says RED Tabara fought alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF, and for FNL only presence and joining the coalition by mid-February 2026. Narrowed to the printed wording. From annex 26 of S/2026/466. RED Tabara's denial is recorded as reported by the Group; no RED Tabara or FNL statement was opened.
src: RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory), and Kipupu (Mwenga territory). Although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23, Red Tabara combatants have taken part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho, and RDF across several axes

FNL elements were present in the Nyaburunda forest (Uvira territory), in mountainous areas near Sange, and in Magunda, where they co-locate with Red Tabara units. By mid-February 2026, RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi accuses Rwanda of supporting RED-Tabara, that Burundian authorities identify Alexis Sinduhije, a former journalist and president of the opposition party MSD, currently in exile in Belgium, as the group's leader, and that Kigali rejects these accusations.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-006.a: Government of Burundi; Government of Rwanda; RED-Tabara
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-006.n: The attribution of leadership is Burundian authorities' claim; the page does not give RED-Tabara's own position. Speaker for official_statement not named by the page.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-006.vn: Exact on the retained page (12 Oct 2026, section 'Gitega and Kigali accuse each other'); background summary by the outlet, attributions kept separate. Two separate attributed positions: Burundi's naming of Sinduhije as RED-Tabara leader is the Burundian authorities' claim; Kigali's rejection is Rwanda's position as summarised by the outlet. No RED-Tabara or Sinduhije response is on the page, and no named speaker or date is given for either position.
src: Burundi accuses Rwanda of supporting RED-Tabara. Burundian authorities identify Alexis Sinduhije, a former journalist and president of the opposition party Movement for Solidarity and Democracy (MSD), currently in exile in Belgium, as the group’s leader. Kigali rejects these accusations.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that two ADF units, led by "Mzee" Meya Sebagala in Ituri Province and by sanctioned commander Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, alias Abwakasi (CDi.040), in Lubero territory, were responsible for most ADF mass casualty attacks, and that supply rendezvous sites were overseen by senior ADF figures including Mzee Meya, Abwakasi and Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007.n: Abwakasi already appears in one earlier claim; Meya Sebagala and Kasibante are new. Meya's area is Ituri (outside phase 1) and is recorded as the Group's attribution.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007.vn: Paras. 16-17 of S/2026/466; 'They' in source 1 refers to the supply rendezvous sites of para. 17. Meya's unit is in Ituri (outside phase 1), attributed to the Group.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-008.x: Group of Experts: Abwakasi unit over 600 civilians killed, an estimated 25,000 displaced, at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites destroyed; Meya's group over 230 civilians killed (2025; the passage does not give the territory split)
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-008.n: The preceding paragraph places Abwakasi's earlier area in Lubero; the passage itself does not state where the 600 killings occurred, so the location is the Group's attribution of Abwakasi's area of operations, and some attacks may be outside North Kivu.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-008.vn: Para. 23 of S/2026/466; figures exact. r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that ADF commander Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender, reportedly died from injuries sustained during clashes with Shujaa forces on 14 March 2026 along the Lindi River (in Asangwa, Bapere sector), which divides Lubero territory from Tshopo Province; the Group said it could not independently confirm his death.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-009.n: Death unconfirmed by the Group; footnote marker '31' printed inside the extracted excerpt.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-009.vn: Para. 30 of S/2026/466; 'reportedly' and the Group's non-confirmation preserved. Death reported, not confirmed: the Group says it could not independently confirm it.

src: FARDC therefore relied increasingly on Wazalendo armed groups, including the Union des patriotes pour la libération du Congo (UPLC) led by “General” Germain Kambale Mayani, as well as on elements from the Nduma défense du Congo –Rénové (NDC-R) of sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwissa (CDi.033) (see S/2024/969, para. 30) and on a local detachment of the Alliance des patriotes pour un Congo libre et souverain (APCLS) led by “General” Fimbo.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-012.n: Names as printed by the Group; the page does not give their units or places in this sentence.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-013.s: Actualite.cd, reporting on a UN Group of Experts report, said the experts wrote that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa, head of the NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati in Walikale territory, that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and troops were based at Lukweti in Masisi territory, and that the CMC-FDP led by Dominique Ndaruhutse was in Virunga National Park taking part in fighting in areas of Rutshuru territory.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-013.l: Walikale, Masisi and Rutshuru territories, North Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-013.n: Local outlet relaying the UN Group of Experts midterm report; the Group's own report text was not checked for these two sentences. Statement avoids dates beyond 'since June 2025' phrasing of the article, so the date range is approximate.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-013.vn: Exact on the retained Actualite.cd page, which credits the passages to the UN experts. Checked against the retained S/2025/858 PDF: the Kibati/Lukweti passage is printed there, so the relay is faithful but not independent of the Group's report already cited by other units. excerpt_en flags reviewed: the English is a faithful translation of each excerpt alone (flag triggered by capitalisation/punctuation differences). Relay of S/2025/858 (para. 83 area); the same wording appears in the Group's report text retained for this project. Dates approximate (the article places VDP/Wazalendo activity 'Depuis juin 2025').
src: "Guidon Shimiray Mwissa , chef du NDC-R et commandant du VDP, a déplacé son quartier général de Pinga à Kibati, territoire de Walikale pour contenir l'avancée du RDF et de l'AFC/M23 le long de la frontière, axe Walikale-Kibua-Kashebere-Masisi.

Le leader de l'APCLS Janvier Karairi Boingo et les troupes étaient basées à Lukweti, territoire de Masisi, tandis que le CMC-FDP dirigé par Dominique Ndaruhutse se trouvaient dans le parc national des Virunga et participaient à des combats dans des zones telles que Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo, Kalengera, en territoire de Rutshuru

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Colonel Mustapha of Twirwaneho, an ally of AFC-M23, was reportedly killed in a CH-4 drone strike by the Congolese army at Rugezi in Fizi territory on Thursday 28 August 2025, according to a Wazalendo spokesperson in South Kivu, who said eleven Twirwaneho fighters died with him; it also reported that AFC-M23 and Twirwaneho fighters accused the Congolese army and its allies of launching several drone attacks in Fizi territory in violation of the ceasefire.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-014.a: FARDC (drone strike, per Wazalendo spokesperson); Twirwaneho
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-014.x: Wazalendo spokesperson (via Kivu Morning Post): Colonel Mustapha and eleven Twirwaneho fighters killed; no independent confirmation in the article
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-014.n: Single local outlet; death claimed by a Wazalendo spokesperson (party to the conflict) and not independently confirmed. A Facebook repost quoted the same spokesperson text (lead only, not cited). Local outlet: Kivu Morning Post (Bukavu/Goma).
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-014.vn: Exact on the retained page; conditional 'aurait été tué' kept as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flags reviewed: translations match the excerpts (the English of source 1 drops 'de Doha'; nothing is added). The death and the toll of eleven are a Wazalendo spokesperson's claim (a party to the fighting), relayed by one local outlet and not independently confirmed. AFC-M23/Twirwaneho did not confirm or deny his death on this page.
src: Le colonel Mustapha de Twirwaneho, allié à l’AFC-M23, aurait été tué dans une frappe d’un drone CH-4 de l’armée congolaise à Rugezi, dans le territoire de Fizi. L’attaque a eu lieu ce jeudi 28 août 2025, selon un porte-parole des Wazalendo au Sud-Kivu, qui affirme que onze combattants Twirwaneho sont morts aux côtés du colonel Mustapha.

Ce jeudi, les combattants de l’AFC-M23 et Twirwaneho ont accusé l’armée congolaise et ses alliés d’avoir lancé plusieurs attaques dans le territoire de Fizi au moyen de drones CH-4, en violation du cessez-le-feu décrété dans l’accord de principe de Doha.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that Twirwaneho was structured and militarised by Michel Rukunda, alias Makanika, a FARDC deserter who had been deputy commander at Walikale, and that he was killed in a Congolese army drone strike in Fizi in February 2025; it also reported that the group was active in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-015.n: Background sentence written by the outlet itself (not attributed to HRW). Makanika appears in earlier claims (roster); this adds the outlet's wording on his post and death.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-015.vn: Exact on the retained page (15 Apr 2026). The 'active in' clause is on the page in the preceding sentence, outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap). Background written by the outlet itself, not attributed to HRW. Only the February 2025 death falls in the window; the outlet's account of the group's 2019-2020 founding is not used.
src: Twiwraneho a été structuré et militarisé par Michel Rukunda, alias Makanika, déserteur des FARDC dont il était commandant adjoint à Walikale. Il a été tué dans une frappe de drone de l'armée congolaise à Fizi, au mois de février 2025.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-016.s: Actualite.cd, quoting a Human Rights Watch report, reported that residents of Minembwe and UN and diplomatic sources said Twirwaneho had forced families to provide one fighter or pay financial compensation to the armed group, and that it carried out reprisals in case of refusal.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-016.l: Minembwe, Hauts Plateaux, Fizi, South Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-016.n: HRW's own page (hrw.org/fr/news/2026/04/14/...) is already cited by an existing claim; this is a local relay with one quote. Statement narrowed: the 'prevented civilians from leaving' clause is in a later sentence not in this excerpt, so removed.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-016.vn: Exact on the retained page as a quoted HRW passage; not independent of HRW's own report, cited by an existing claim. Local relay quoting HRW; HRW attributes the information to residents of Minembwe and UN and diplomatic sources.
src: « Le Twirwaneho a menacé et enrôlé de force des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux. Des habitants de Minembwe ainsi que des sources onusiennes et diplomatiques ont déclaré que le Twirwaneho avait contraint des familles à fournir un combattant ou à verser une compensation financière au groupe armé, et qu’ils exerçaient des représailles en cas de refus.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-017.s: 7sur7.cd reported that MONUSCO, in a press release of 21 November 2025, condemned ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in Lubero territory, saying at least 17 civilians, including women admitted to the maternity ward, were killed in a Catholic Church health centre at Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, and four pavilions housing patients were set on fire; MONUSCO also cited abductions and looting of medicines in other localities.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-017.l: Byambwe, Bapere sector / Baswagha chiefdom, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-017.x: MONUSCO (via 7sur7.cd): 89 civilians killed in Bapere sector and Baswagha chiefdom, including at least 20 women and an undetermined number of children; at least 17 killed at the Byambwe health centre
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-017.n: Local outlet relaying a MONUSCO press release; the MONUSCO text itself was not opened. The communique says violence against civilians in medical structures may constitute crimes; not repeated here (vocabulary rule).
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-017.vn: All three passages exact on the retained page. The figures flag '7' comes from the publisher name '7sur7.cd' in the statement, not from a figure. excerpt_en flags reviewed: the English translates each excerpt (MONUSCO acronym expansion shortened only). src: Dans un communiqué de presse rendu public ce vendredi 21 novembre 2025, la Mission de l'Organisation des Nations unies pour la stabilisation en République démocratique du Congo (MONUSCO) a condamné fermement les attaques meurtrières menées par le groupe armé des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) entre le 13 et le 19 novembre 2025 dans plusieurs localités du territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. D’après ce même communiqué, le bilan des attaques dans le secteur de Bapere et la chefferie de Baswagha est de 89 civils tués, dont au moins 20 femmes et un nombre encore indéterminé d'enfants.

Dans la localité de Byambwe(à 60 km à l'ouest de Lubero), au moins 17 civils, dont des femmes internées dans la maternité, ont été tués dans un centre de santé de l'Église catholique. Au cours de l'attaque, quatre pavillons abritant des malades ont été incendiés.

La même source indique que les localités de Mabiango, Tunarudi, Sambalysa, Thucha et Butsili ont également été la cible d'exactions comprenant des enlèvements, des pillages de médicaments, des incendies de maisons

La zone de santé de Biena confirme l’attaque. Un membre du personnel soignant évoque l’incendie du pavillon de maternité et du bloc opératoire, ainsi que le pillage des médicaments. Il affirme que 17 personnes, dont quatre femmes allaitantes, ont été exécutées sur leur lit d’hôpital.

Tout se passe dans la nuit du 14 au 15 novembre 2025, lorsque les présumés combattants ADF-NALU font incursion et tuent au moins 28 personnes, incendient un centre de santé de la paroisse et ravagent plusieurs habitations.

r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-018.s: The US State Department spokesperson said that the United States was designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, and said the FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence and launched cross-border attacks.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-018.n: Official US statement (a party to diplomacy, not neutral on the FDLR). Treasury's sb0518 release (already cited by another unit) gives the unit name CRAP and alias; this State release is a separate page. The sexual-violence and child-soldier wording is the US government's allegation about the FDLR as a group, not about Kubwayo individually.
r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-018.vn: Exact on the retained State Department press statement of 2 June 2026, issued by spokesperson Thomas "Tommy" Pigott. US government statement and allegation about the FDLR, as 'the US says'.
src: We are designating Gustave Kubwayo, commander of an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit. The FDLR has carried out ethnic violence against civilians, used child soldiers, committed sexual violence, and launched cross-border attacks that continue to threaten Rwanda’s security.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001.s: CongoRassure reported that a new battalion, the '22ᵉ Task Force (TAFOK)', was being mobilised in the border town of Gatumba before deployment to Bukavu, bringing the total of Burundian battalions in the DRC to sixteen, five of them positioned in the Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira to hunt Burundian rebels; that the Burundian regiment was under the command of 'général Pontien Hakizimana, alias Mingi' and structured in four brigades of three battalions each; and that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10 000 soldiers, a strength currently fluctuating between 8 000 and 12 000.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001.l: Bukavu, Kalehe, Kamanyola, Kavumu; Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001.x: CongoRassure: sixteen battalions in the DRC, five in the Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira; FDNB strength nearly 10 000 (between 8 000 and 12 000)
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001.n: Single, lesser-known Congolese outlet; the page names no original source (its content closely tracks RFI's 7 Feb 2025 report, which could not be fetched). The commander attribution appears nowhere else in the existing claims; treat as a lead. Author byline: Diddy Kambale Mastaki. Compare UN GoE S/2025/446 (14 battalions in early April 2025).
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-001.vn: All facts on retained page; added Kalehe/Kamanyola/Kavumu (location field) with quote; figures written as the page prints them (10 000 etc.). excerpt_en flags are translation artefacts (DRC/RDC, South Kivu/Sud-Kivu), translations cover the excerpts only. Single outlet (CongoRassure, byline Diddy Kambale Mastaki); the page cites no source for the commander, structure or figures. The commander attribution is a lead only. Troop figures conflict with other sources and dates; kept as printed. The page also places Burundian forward positions at Kalehe, Kamanyola and Kavumu (see the replacement quote; location field).
ent: Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB)
src: Un nouveau bataillon, la 22ᵉ Task Force (TAFOK), est en cours de mobilisation dans la ville frontalière de Gatumba avant d’être déployé à Bukavu, capitale du Sud-Kivu. Avec ce renfort, le nombre total de bataillons Burundais en RDC s’élève désormais à seize, dont cinq sont positionnés dans les Hauts et Moyens-Plateaux de Fizi et Uvira pour traquer les rebelles burundais.
Le régiment Burundais est placé sous le commandement du général Pontien Hakizimana, alias Mingi, et est structuré en quatre brigades, chacune composée de trois bataillons.

la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) a renforcé son engagement en déployant près de 10 000 soldats sur le territoire Congolais. Ces troupes, dont l’effectif oscille actuellement entre 8 000 et 12 000 hommes,

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several concordant security sources, a new redeployment of Burundian soldiers to the DRC observed between 29 December 2025 and 4 January 2026, toward Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Tanganyika province, in particular Kalemie, carried out from the Burundian navy position near the Rumonge fishing port, with about ten military vehicles mobilised according to police and military sources; a soldier contacted said the main objective would be to reinforce two Burundian battalions left isolated in mountainous areas of eastern DRC.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-002.l: Rumonge (Burundi) to Fizi territory (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) and Kalemie
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-002.x: SOS Médias Burundi: two Burundian battalions described as isolated; about ten military vehicles (une dizaine) mobilised
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-002.n: Local Burundian monitor citing anonymous security sources. Article first appeared 9 January 2026 (same text under a different title) and was republished 12 January. Complements UN GoE S/2026/466 (FDNB role in Jan 2026 FARDC offensive from Uvira).
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-002.vn: Supported; added vehicles figure with quote; kept conditional; graded C because every element rests on anonymous sources of one outlet. src: Un nouveau redéploiement de militaires burundais vers la République démocratique du Congo (RDC) a été observé entre le 29 décembre 2025 et le 4 janvier 2026, selon plusieurs sources sécuritaires concordantes.

Selon un militaire contacté, l’objectif principal serait de renforcer deux bataillons burundais restés isolés dans des zones montagneuses de l’est de la RDC, alors que la pression militaire du M23 continue de s’intensifier.
notamment dans le territoire de Fizi (Bibokoboko, Point Zéro, Milimba) ainsi que dans la province du Tanganyika, en particulier la ville de Kalemie, chef-lieu provincial.

Le redéploiement s’est effectué à partir de la position de la marine burundaise située près du port de pêche de Rumonge, une ville portuaire stratégique située dans le sud-ouest du Burundi, sur les rives du lac Tanganyika.

D’après des sources policières et militaires, une dizaine de véhicules militaires et moyens de transport logistiques chargés de soldats burundais ont été mobilisés à partir du mercredi 31 décembre 2025.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-003.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several security sources, that a large part of the Burundian soldiers withdrew in December 2025 following M23 advances in South Kivu and losses suffered by the FDNB; it reported that the secretary general of the CNDD-FDD had spoken of a 'strategic withdrawal' ('retrait stratégique'), saying Burundi remained master of its military decisions, and quoted Révérien Ndikuriyo as having declared: 'it is like at home, we go there when we want'.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-003.n: Burundian party statement relayed by a local monitor; the 'retrait stratégique' wording is attributed by the outlet to the CNDD-FDD secretary general, the second excerpt gives the quoted remark. Contrast with the FDNB spokesperson's denial of any withdrawal (19 Feb 2025, separate claim) and the UN GoE statement that FDNB were forced out of Uvira (existing claim UC-BI-FDLR#22).
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-003.vn: Original statement fused two sentences into a direct naming the page does not make; narrowed to what each sentence says. The page does not itself name the CNDD-FDD secretary general in the 'retrait stratégique' sentence; it attributes the next quote to Révérien Ndikuriyo. No date or venue given for either remark. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, 12 Jan 2026. All clauses are on the page; the stored excerpt began mid-sentence and omitted the December 2025 withdrawal clause, now added. The page does not itself state that Ndikuriyo is the CNDD-FDD secretary general; the statement rightly keeps the two attributions separate.
src: à la suite des avancées spectaculaires du M23 dans le Sud-Kivu et des pertes subies par la FDNB (Force de défense nationale du Burundi). Récemment, le secrétaire général du CNDD-FDD, l’ancienne rébellion hutu au pouvoir au Burundi depuis 2005, a évoqué un « retrait stratégique », affirmant que le Burundi restait maître de ses décisions militaires.
« C’est comme chez nous, nous y allons quand nous voulons », avait déclaré Révérien Ndikuriyo

Plusieurs sources sécuritaires soulignent que ces nouveaux mouvements de troupes interviennent après un retrait d’une grande partie des militaires burundais opéré en décembre 2025, à la suite des avancées spectaculaires du M23 dans le Sud-Kivu et des pertes subies par la FDNB (Force de défense nationale du Burundi).

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-004.s: Anadolu Agency reported that the Burundian army spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, said on X that, contrary to what Reuters and social networks reported, FDNB soldiers deployed in the DRC continued to carry out their missions in their sectors of responsibility.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-004.l: eastern DRC (parts not specified by the source)
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-004.n: Responds to Reuters' report of 18 Feb 2025 (four sources said Burundi was withdrawing forces; Reuters page could not be fetched, so that account is not recorded). Anadolu is the original publisher of this article (AA/Bujumbura, Jean Bosco Nzosaba); the quote is from the spokesperson's X post.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-004.vn: Byline and quote verified on retained page. Party statement (FDNB) as reported by Anadolu (AA/Bujumbura, Jean Bosco Nzosaba). AA adds that he did not specify which parts of the DRC remain under Burundian responsibility.
src: « Contrairement aux propos véhiculés par Reuters et repris par d'autres réseaux sociaux, les militaires de la FDNB (forces de défenses nationales du Burundi) déployés en RDC continuent à exécuter leurs missions dans leurs secteurs de responsabilité », a déclaré le général de brigade Gaspard Baratuza sur X.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-005.s: Iwacu reported that at a press conference on Thursday 16 January the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, rejected allegations that Burundian soldiers had been captured or killed by M23 in eastern DRC, saying those captured were not Burundians, while neither confirming nor denying casualties, which he called a military secret.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-005.x: no figure given by the spokesperson ("secret militaire")
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-005.n: Same press conference is summarised by SOS Médias Burundi (25 Jan 2025) and Igihe (17 Jan 2025, Rwandan outlet, page not retrievable). Iwacu is a Bujumbura outlet.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-005.vn: All clauses on retained page; '16' carried by replacement quote. FDNB party statement as reported by Iwacu (byline Stine Akimana, 16/01/2025).
src: « Ceux qui sont capturés par le M23 ne sont pas des Burundais.
le porte-parole de l’armée burundaise, n’a ni confirmé ni infirmé les faits, il s’est contenté de souligner que « le nombre de prisonniers ou de morts est un secret militaire ».

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Thursday, January 23, 2025, according to its sources, the Kamenge military hospital in Bujumbura counted 81 injured and 19 dead Burundian soldiers from fighting with M23 in Congolese territory, and that the army buried Lieutenant Patience Gapara, killed in the fighting with M23 in North Kivu; by its own estimate, 7,500 to 9,000 Burundian soldiers were on Congolese soil.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.l: Kamenge military hospital, Bujumbura; North Kivu fighting
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.x: SOS Médias Burundi (own estimate, sources): 81 injured, 19 dead at Kamenge on 23 Jan 2025; 7,500 to 9,000 Burundian soldiers in the DRC. FDNB spokesperson: no figure (military secret)
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.n: Local monitor with anonymous sources; the FDNB declined to give casualty figures (see Iwacu claim). Troop estimate is the outlet's own.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.vn: Verified on retained page. Casualty figures rest on anonymous medical sources; the troop range is the outlet's own estimate. The FDNB gave no figure (military secret). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-001: Attribution drift: the casualty count rests on the outlet's anonymous sources ('according to our sources'), which the statement dropped. Restored; troop range marked as the outlet's own estimate. Exile outlet, single origin, C.; excerpt-support: nothing to add; 'according to our sources' and 'According to our estimates' are in sources 0 and 2
src: On Thursday, January 23, 2025, the Kamenge military hospital in the north of the commercial city of Bujumbura counted 81 Burundian soldiers who were injured during the fighting with the M23 on the Congolese territory and 19 dead – a situation that evolves every day, according to our sources.
On Thursday, the Burundian army buried Lieutenant Patience Gapara, who was recently killed in the fighting with the M23 in the province of North Kivu in eastern Congo.
According to our estimates, the small East African nation has between 7,500 and 9,000 soldiers on the Congolese soil.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed in Ruzizi near the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops deployed to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), a deployment the article said was estimated (without saying by whom) at approximately two battalions, in addition to operations in April 2026 at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with the FARDC and Wazalendo.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-007.l: Kalundu port (Uvira), Bijombo (Uvira territory), Itombwe (Mwenga territory)
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-007.x: SOS Médias Burundi: approximately two battalions
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-007.n: Single local source, no named commander. The page also says Burundian forces with FARDC and Wazalendo have launched several offensives since December 2025 to retake Minembwe 'without managing to dislodge the M23 and Twirwaneho fighters'.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-007.vn: Verified on retained page; April-operations clause added to quotes. Single local monitor; no named source for the landing or the estimate. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: April 2026 operations at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with FARDC and Wazalendo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-023: 'A deployment it estimated' puts the estimate in SOS Médias Burundi's mouth; the page uses an agentless passive ('est estimé'), as the verifier noted on the duplicate r1-UV-2026Q2-009. Searched for a Burundian denial of the 15 May landing: none found (only a February 2026 ambassador denial about a withdrawal). Lead: Uvira had been taken by M23 on 10 December 2025 (actualite.cd 5 April 2026), so control of Uvira in May 2026 should be confirmed in the frontline data. Duplicate of r1-UV-2026Q2-009 (English vs French page).; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): April 2026 operations at Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu with FARDC and Wazalendo
src: On May 15, 2026, several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed in Ruzizi, near the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before deploying troops to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory).
The deployment is estimated at approximately two battalions, aiming to rebalance the power dynamics in the Minembwe area and control movement between Rurambo, Bijombo, and Minembwe.

These operations are in addition to those already conducted in April 2026 in several strategic locations, including Point Zero, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi, and Bidegu, as part of joint operations with the FARDC and the Wazalendo militias supported by Kinshasa.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported in May 2026 that the FDNB is accused by several local and international organisations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including road blockades, destruction of property and looting targeting civilians, and that the FDNB spokesperson, Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza, acknowledged that movement restrictions could be imposed on individuals considered 'collaborators with the enemy'.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-008.n: The accusing organisations are not named on the page. Compare existing claims UC-BI-FDLR#30-36 (Dec 2025 Mikalati and Minembwe) from SOS Médias Burundi and BBC Gahuza.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-008.vn: Verified on retained page. The accusing organisations are not named; the page gives no date or venue for the spokesperson's remark.
src: The Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) is accused by several local and international organizations of human rights violations in the Minembwe area, including cases of road blockades, destruction of property, and looting targeting civilians.

FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza acknowledged that movement restrictions could be imposed on individuals considered “collaborators with the enemy,” particularly in areas where trade with local markets is observed.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-009.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported, citing SOS Medias, that vehicles carrying Burundian soldiers were seen at Kitoga, Muhuzi and in the Itombwe forest and that Burundian soldiers were reinforced in other areas including Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu and Point Zero in Fizi; it said, without giving a source, that there were now about 20 thousand Burundian troops in South Kivu, mostly in Uvira and Fizi.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-009.l: Kitoga, Muhuzi, Itombwe, Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu, Point Zero; Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-009.x: Umuryango.rw: about 20 thousand Burundian troops in South Kivu (figure unsourced; other sources in this unit give lower figures)
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-009.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet (partisan on contested facts); the 20,000 figure is the outlet's own, unsourced, and far above UN GoE figures. Deployment locations relay SOS Médias Burundi. Treat the figure as a party-aligned estimate only.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-009.vn: Locations relay SOS Médias Burundi (origin kept); the 20,000 figure is not attributed to SOS Medias on the page, so source 1's origin corrected to Umuryango.rw. Wording aligned with the page. Rwandan partisan outlet (byline Brenda Mizero, 17 Oct 2025): usable only as 'Umuryango.rw says'. The 20 thousand figure is the outlet's own and unsourced; it conflicts with the other figures in this unit. The article also says Burundi had been sending troops to key areas of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories to stop AFC/M23 (replacement quote).
src: Urubuga SOS Medias rwatangaje ko imodoka zitwaye abasirikare b’u Burundi zagaragaye muri santere ya Kitoga, Muhuzi no mu ishyamba rya Itombwe, kandi ko bongerewe mu bindi bice birimo Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu na Point Zero muri Fizi.
Ubu muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo hari izigera ku bihumbi 20, ziganje mu bice byo muri Uvira na Fizi.

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010.s: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that EU foreign ministers adopted sanctions including three Rwandan generals, Eugène Nkubito, Pascal Muhizi and Ruki Karusisi, describing Karusisi as commander of the special forces deployed in the DRC, and listing Nkubito as commander of the RDF 3rd Division and Muhizi as commander of the RDF 2nd Division. TRT Afrika reported that those sanctioned by the EU included special forces commander Ruki Karusisi and two army division commanders, Eugene Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010.l: eastern DRC (RDF deployment); sanctions announced in Brussels
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010.n: The 2nd Division commander (Pascal Muhizi, Brigadier General) is not in earlier UC-RDF claims, which name the 3rd and 4th/5th Divisions; the EU Official Journal text (Implementing Regulation 2025/509) and Council press release could not be fetched (bot protection, not bypassed) and would be the primary sources. ACP is the Congolese state news agency (partisan on Rwanda). The TRT page carries no wire credit but shows a Reuters photo credit; its date is taken from the search result (17 Mar 2025). Rwanda's foreign ministry statement that day was aimed at Belgium; no Rwandan reaction to the commander listings was found in these sources.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010.vn: ACP narrates, it does not cite an 'EU source' for the generals; discrepancy within ACP surfaced; TRT clause separated. EU listing as reported by ACP (Congolese state agency) and TRT Afrika; the EU Official Journal text was not fetched. ACP is internally inconsistent on Karusisi's role and spelling (current vs former special forces commander; 'Ruki'/'Ruzi'). Only ACP gives the division numbers.
src: Du côté rwandais, trois généraux sont sanctionnés. Il s’agit d’Eugène Nkubito, Pascal Muhizi et Ruki Karusisi, commandant des forces spéciales déployées en RDC,
Eugène Nkubito, commandant 3 ème division RDF, Pascal Muhizi, Commandant 2 ème division RDF,
The three people sanctioned by the EU on Monday included special forces commander Ruki Karusisi and two army division commanders, Eugene Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi,

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-011.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Goma, 3 March 2026) reported that the United States announced sanctions on Monday against the RDF and four of its senior officers, whom Washington accuses of actively supporting the M23 rebellion, and that OFAC designated General Mubarakh Muganga, Major General Vincent Nyakarundi, Major General Ruki Karusisi (commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former special forces commander) and Brigadier General Stanislas Gashugi (current commander of Rwandan special forces); Kigali immediately denounced the sanctions as 'unjust' and 'unilateral'.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-011.n: Corroborates UC-RDF#14/#15 (UN GoE and HRW). Swahili edition of a Burundian monitor; the dateline says 3 March 2026 while the announcement is dated 2 March elsewhere. The page also states Kigali's reaction (statement of 2 March calling the sanctions 'unilateral').
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-011.vn: Muganga and Nyakarundi were in no excerpt: added replacement quote. Exact date not printed for the designation; set to month. The page gives the announcement day only as 'Monday' (dateline Goma, 3 March 2026; posted 9 March); Kigali's reaction is dated 2 March. Date kept at month precision. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: dateline Goma 3 March 2026; US sanctions; Kigali's denunciation 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: OFAC designations of Muganga and Nyakarundi 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-028: Read the retained page: the names and the four-officer count are supported, but the stored excerpt omits Muganga and Nyakarundi and the claim leaves out the stated basis (alleged support to M23, a US accusation) and Kigali's immediate rejection printed in the same paragraph. Added both; Muganga/Nyakarundi need an add_excerpt with the quote below. Single relay of OFAC; the OFAC release itself was not in the input.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): dateline Goma 3 March 2026; US sanctions; Kigali's denunciation; OFAC designations of Muganga and Nyakarundi
src: Meja Jenerali Ruki Karusisi, kamanda wa Kitengo cha 5 cha watoto wachanga wa RDF na kamanda wa zamani wa kikosi maalum; Brigedia Jenerali Stanislas Gashugi, kamanda wa sasa wa kikosi maalum cha Rwanda.

Goma, Machi 3, 2026 – Mgogoro wa kidiplomasia unaozingira mzozo wa mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo (DRC) unaongezeka. Marekani ilitangaza vikwazo Jumatatu dhidi ya Jeshi la Ulinzi la Rwanda (RDF) na maafisa wake wakuu wanne wa kijeshi, wanaotuhumiwa kuunga mkono kikamilifu uasi wa M23. Mara moja Kigali ilishutumu vikwazo hivyo na kusema “si vya haki” na “vya upande mmoja.”

Idara ya Hazina ya Marekani, kupitia Ofisi yake ya Udhibiti wa Mali za Kigeni (OFAC), iliteua: Jenerali Mubarakh Muganga, Mkuu wa Majeshi wa Rwanda, afisa wa ngazi ya juu zaidi katika RDF; Meja Jenerali Vincent Nyakarundi, Mkuu wa Majeshi ya Rwanda;

r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-012.s: RFI's Invité Afrique Midi episode on the state visit of the Burundian president to Kinshasa, with Jean-Jacques Wondo, a strategy and security analyst at Afridesk, as guest, was headlined: '«On peut estimer à 10 000 le nombre de soldats burundais toujours présents au Congo»'.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-012.x: RFI headline of an interview with Jean-Jacques Wondo (Afridesk): 10 000 Burundian soldiers
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-012.n: Analyst estimate from a podcast page (headline); the audio was not transcribed so the basis of the estimate is unknown. The page says nothing on the geographic split between provinces.
r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-012.vn: Headline attribution narrowed to what the page shows; the president is named on the page as 'Evariste Ndayishimiye' (replacement quote). The quoted headline is presented as the guest's estimate but the page text does not attribute it in words; the audio was not transcribed, so the basis of the estimate is unknown. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: «On peut estimer à 10 000 le nombre de soldats burundais toujours présents au Congo»
Jean-Jacques Wondo, analyste spécialiste des questions de stratégie et de sécurité à Afridesk est l'invité d'Afrique Midi.

r1-UNHR-001.s: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Jeremy Laurence said OHCHR has documented summary executions of at least 12 people by the M23 between 26 and 28 January.
r1-UNHR-001.l: Goma and surrounding areas, North Kivu (place not specified in the excerpt)
r1-UNHR-001.n: Place of the executions is not given in this excerpt; the article's context is Goma. Perpetrator as alleged by OHCHR.
r1-UNHR-001.vn: Excerpt on page verbatim; UN News relays OHCHR briefing. Place of the executions is not stated in the article; perpetrator as alleged by OHCHR.
src: Spokesperson Jeremy Laurence said OHCHR has documented summary executions of at least 12 people by the M23 between 26 and 28 January.

r1-UNHR-002.s: UN News reported, in the section of its article on the OHCHR briefing, that in other areas under M23 control in South Kivu, such as Minova, fighters have occupied schools and hospitals, forced IDPs out of camps and subjected the civilian population to forced conscription and forced labour.
r1-UNHR-002.n: The sentence itself carries no attribution; the preceding paragraph of the article reports the OHCHR briefing. Also covers occupation of hospitals (health care).
r1-UNHR-002.vn: Narrowed attribution: the page does not attribute this sentence to OHCHR explicitly. The sentence carries no explicit attribution on the page; it sits within UN News' account of the OHCHR briefing.
src: Meanwhile, in other areas under M23 control in South Kivu, such as Minova, fighters have occupied schools and hospitals, forced IDPs out of camps and subjected the civilian population to forced conscription and forced labour.

r1-UNHR-003.s: UN News reported that OHCHR has documented cases of conflict-related sexual violence by the army and allied Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory, South Kivu, and is verifying reports that 52 women were raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu, including alleged reports of gangrape.
r1-UNHR-003.a: the army and allied Wazalendo fighters (documented cases, Kalehe); Congolese troops (52 rapes, reports being verified), per OHCHR
r1-UNHR-003.x: OHCHR: 52 women reported raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu (being verified)
r1-UNHR-003.n: The 52-woman figure is unverified (OHCHR 'verifying reports'). The ONU Info French version names the FARDC as 'Forces armées congolaises (FARDC)'.
r1-UNHR-003.vn: Statement supported; actor narrowed to the source's words (army / Congolese troops) and the two clauses separated (documented vs. being verified). The 52-women figure is unverified: OHCHR said it was verifying reports. The page does not place the 52 cases in Kalehe.
src: The Office has also documented cases of conflict-related sexual violence by the army and allied Wazalendo fighters in Kalehe territory, located in South Kivu. It is also verifying reports that 52 women were raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu, including alleged reports of gangrape.

r1-UNHR-004.s: UN News reported that DRC officials report at least 165 women were raped by male inmates during the mass prison break from Goma's Muzenze prison on 27 January, as M23 began its assault on the town.
r1-UNHR-004.n: Figure from DRC officials relayed by the UN, not verified by OHCHR in this text. Corroborates BBC claims already drafted (SV-NK-2025#10/#11).
r1-UNHR-004.vn: Verbatim on page; origin is DRC officials, not OHCHR. Figure is from DRC officials, relayed by UN News; not stated as verified by OHCHR. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Additionally, DRC officials report that at least 165 women were raped by male inmates during the mass prison break from Goma’s Muzenze prison on 27 January , as M23 began its assault on the town.
Selon les autorités judiciaires, lors de l'évasion massive de la prison de Munzenze à Goma le 27 janvier au moins 165 prisonnières ont été violées
At least 165 women were raped by male inmates after a mass breakout from a prison in the Democratic Republic of Congo , the United Nations said, citing officials in the central African nation.

r1-UNHR-005.s: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani said OHCHR had confirmed cases of summary execution of children by M23 after they entered the city of Bukavu, and that OHCHR was also aware that children were in possession of weapons.
r1-UNHR-005.n: The 'three children' figure is stated in the article's lead; the quoted excerpt says 'cases'. 'Last week' relative to 18 Feb 2025; exact days not given. Date computed from publication date.
r1-UNHR-005.vn: Verbatim; three-children figure placed in replacement quote. The 'three children' figure is UN News' summary in its lead of the OHCHR alert; exact dates not given ('last week'). 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-013: The statement turned 'We are also aware that children were in possession of weapons' into a bare fact, which can read as a finding about the executed children; restored as what OHCHR said it was aware of. Searched (FR) for an M23 denial: none in results; RFI snippet mentions three children killed in the 'quartier latin' on 16 February (lead, unverified).; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: “Our office has confirmed cases of summary execution of children by M23 after they entered the city of Bukavu last week. We are also aware that children were in possession of weapons,” said OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani.

r1-UNHR-006.s: UN News reported that the OHCHR spokesperson condemned attacks on hospitals and humanitarian warehouses as well as threats against the judiciary, directly linked to the rapid advance of the M23 fighters across North Kivu and South Kivu.
r1-UNHR-006.n: No specific facility named in this excerpt.
r1-UNHR-006.vn: Verbatim on page; general, no facility named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: The OHCHR spokesperson also condemned attacks on hospitals and humanitarian warehouses as well as threats against the judiciary, directly linked to the rapid advance of the M23 fighters across North Kivu and South Kivu.
Over 70 (or 6%) of the health facilities in North Kivu have been affected, with some completely destroyed and others struggling to restart operations.
Medical supplies and equipment worth millions of dollars have also been looted from storage facilities in Goma, leaving thousands of women and girls without access to quality medical care.

r1-UNHR-007.s: UN News reported that OHCHR spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani noted break-outs from Kabare and Bukavu central prisons on 14 February.
r1-UNHR-007.l: Kabare and Bukavu central prisons, South Kivu
r1-UNHR-007.n: The article adds that OHCHR received protection requests from witnesses and victims who feared retaliation from escapees.
r1-UNHR-007.vn: Verbatim on page; no perpetrator stated.
src: Other worrying developments stemming from the crisis include break-outs from Kabare and Bukavu central prisons on 14 February, OHCHR’s Ms. Shamdasani noted.

r1-UNHR-008.s: UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in South Kivu more than half of the aid groups providing critical support to survivors of sexual violence report being unable to reach those in need due to insecurity and continuous displacement.
r1-UNHR-008.x: UNHCR: more than half of aid groups supporting sexual violence survivors
r1-UNHR-008.n: UNHCR (not OHCHR) briefing. Access to services for sexual violence survivors.
r1-UNHR-008.vn: Verbatim; single UNHCR statement, graded B (not a documented investigation). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Ms. Byun said that in South Kivu, more than half of the aid groups providing critical support to survivors of sexual violence “report being unable to reach those in need due to insecurity and continuous displacement”.
Since the beginning of the year, over 400,000 people–predominantly women and children–have been displaced in North and South Kivu, exacerbating their vulnerability to exploitation and violence.

r1-UNHR-009.s: UN News reported that UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun said that in North Kivu the destruction of health facilities, including mortuaries, and overcrowded hospitals increase the risk of spreading infectious diseases, including cholera, malaria, and measles.
r1-UNHR-009.n: 'she' = UNHCR spokesperson Eujin Byun named earlier in the article.
r1-UNHR-009.vn: 'she' is the UNHCR spokesperson named earlier on the page. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 3 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Meanwhile, in North Kivu, “the destruction of health facilities, including mortuaries, and overcrowded hospitals increase the risk of spreading infectious diseases, including cholera, malaria, and measles,” she said.
Over 70 (or 6%) of the health facilities in North Kivu have been affected, with some completely destroyed and others struggling to restart operations.
The threat of infectious diseases has multiplied. Cholera, malaria, measles, meningitis, mpox and tuberculosis are among the infectious threats in the area.

r1-UNHR-010.s: UN News reported, in a passage on humanitarian assessments in Goma, that WHO and partners, after an assessment with the Government over the past five days, reported that 700 people had been killed and 2,800 injured were receiving treatment in health facilities, with numbers expected to rise.
r1-UNHR-010.x: WHO and partners: 700 killed; 2,800 injured (as of the report)
r1-UNHR-010.n: Place 'Goma' inferred from the article's heading context (humanitarian situation in Goma); the excerpt itself does not name it. Other sources give different casualty figures; these are per-source.
r1-UNHR-010.vn: Origin is WHO and partners, not OHCHR; Goma scope narrowed to the page's framing. The page does not explicitly say the 700/2,800 figures are for Goma only; they follow a sentence on Goma. Casualty figures differ across sources.
src: The World Health Organization ( WHO ) and partners conducted an assessment with the Government over the past five days. They report that 700 people have been killed and 2,800 injured are receiving treatment in health facilities

r1-UNHR-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) said in a communiqué that it documented 2.767 human rights violations and abuses and IHL violations across the whole territory of the DRC in the first half of 2025.
r1-UNHR-011.l: DRC-wide (conflict provinces include North and South Kivu)
r1-UNHR-011.x: BCNUDH: 2.767 violations and abuses, DRC-wide, first half of 2025 (not a Kivu figure)
r1-UNHR-011.n: DRC-wide figure; the article also gives 2,378 in conflict provinces (86 per cent) in the same passage of the report. Provincial split for Kivus is not in this excerpt.
r1-UNHR-011.vn: Figures field had 'H1' (stray '1'); rewritten. DRC-wide scope made explicit. DRC-wide figure, not specific to North or South Kivu. Radio Okapi relays the BCNUDH communiqué.
src: Dans un communiqué publié lundi 24 novembre, le Bureau conjoint des Nations unies aux droits de l’homme (BCNUDH) dit avoir documenté 2.767 violations et atteintes aux droits de l’homme et violations du droit international humanitaire sur l’ensemble du territoire de la RDC au cours du premier semestre de l’année 2025.

r1-UNHR-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on the first half of 2025 accuses State agents of responsibility for sexual violence against 70 victims, including the FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim).
r1-UNHR-012.a: FARDC (69 victims) and PNC agents (one victim), per BCNUDH
r1-UNHR-012.x: BCNUDH: 70 victims attributed to State agents (FARDC 69, PNC one), DRC-wide, first half of 2025 (not a Kivu figure)
r1-UNHR-012.n: DRC-wide; the excerpt does not give the provinces. Relayed by Radio Okapi from the BCNUDH report.
r1-UNHR-012.vn: 'namely' softened to 'including' (notamment); period anchored to the report's half-year scope. DRC-wide; the article gives no provincial breakdown of these victims.
src: Le rapport du BCNUDH accuse aussi les agents de l’Etat d’avoir été responsables des violences sexuelles à l’encontre de 70 victimes, notamment les FARDC (69 victimes) et des agents de la PNC (une victime).

r1-UNHR-013.s: ONU Info reported that, according to BCNUDH data, 887 cases of conflict-related sexual violence were documented the previous year, affecting 1,534 victims, including 854 women and 672 girls, and that North and South Kivu account for close to 80 per cent of documented victims.
r1-UNHR-013.l: DRC; North Kivu and South Kivu account for close to 80% of victims
r1-UNHR-013.a: armed groups responsible for 75% of victims; State actors in 19% of documented cases, per the report
r1-UNHR-013.x: BCNUDH: 887 cases; 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls); about 80% in North and South Kivu
r1-UNHR-013.n: Annual figures for 2025, date_precision set to year-level (flagged 'month' only because the schema has no year value). Another figure of 1,534 victims was posted by Actualite.cd on Facebook; this page is the UN News copy.
r1-UNHR-013.vn: Verbatim; UNFPA is only the photo credit, origin is BCNUDH. DRC-wide annual totals (2025, 'l'année passée' in an article of March 2026); only the ~80% share is specific to the Kivus.
src: Selon les données collectées par le Bureau conjoint des Nations Unies pour les droits de l’homme en République démocratique du Congo (BCNUDH), 887 cas de violences sexuelles liées au conflit ont été documentés l’année passée, affectant 1534 victimes, dont une majorité écrasante de femmes (854) et de filles (672).
Les provinces orientales du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu concentrent à elles seules près de 80 % des victimes documentées

r1-UNHR-014.s: ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, armed groups are responsible for 75 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims the previous year, with the M23 first at 439 victims, followed by Wazalendo groups, and that State actors including FARDC, the Police nationale congolaise and the Agence nationale de renseignement were involved in 19 per cent of documented cases.
r1-UNHR-014.a: M23 (439 victims); Wazalendo; State actors FARDC, PNC and ANR (19% of cases)
r1-UNHR-014.x: BCNUDH: armed groups 75% of victims; M23 439 victims; State actors 19% of cases
r1-UNHR-014.n: DRC-wide, annual 2025 figures; provincial split of perpetrators not given in the excerpts.
r1-UNHR-014.vn: Verbatim. DRC-wide 2025 figures, not Kivu-specific. 75% refers to victims, 19% to cases.
src: D’après le rapport, les groupes armés sont responsables de 75 % des victimes. Le Mouvement du 23 mars (M23) arrive en tête avec 439 victimes, suivi des groupes Wazalendo,

L’ONU note également avec préoccupation l’implication d’acteurs étatiques, notamment des membres des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC), de la Police nationale congolaise et de l’Agence nationale de renseignement, dans 19 % des cas documentés.

r1-UNHR-015.s: ONU Info reported that, per the BCNUDH report, 70 per cent of conflict-related sexual violence victims have access to emergency medical care but fewer than 2 per cent receive holistic care including legal, psychological and social support.
r1-UNHR-015.x: BCNUDH: 70% emergency care; under 2% holistic care
src: Si 70 % des victimes ont accès à des soins médicaux d’urgence, moins de 2 % bénéficient d’une prise en charge holistique, comprenant un accompagnement juridique, psychologique et social.

r1-UNHR-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH recorded 61 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in January 2026, a 59 per cent drop from December 2025.
r1-UNHR-016.x: BCNUDH: 61 victims in January 2026 (59% below December 2025)
r1-UNHR-016.n: The article says the same report names the AFC/M23, ADF, Wazalendo groups and FDLR among armed-group perpetrators. DRC-wide report; Kivu share not in this excerpt.
r1-UNHR-016.vn: Verbatim; the page says the report is for January 2026. DRC-wide monthly figure, not Kivu-specific.
src: Autre sujet d’inquiétude retenu dans ce rapport, il y a des violences sexuelles liées aux conflits. Le BCNUDH a recensé 61 victimes en janvier, soit une baisse de 59 % par rapport à décembre 2025,

r1-UNHR-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report notes that 42 political actors were still detained in January 2026, amid arrests judged arbitrary.
r1-UNHR-017.n: Not Kivu-specific; included as BCNUDH context. Excerpt does not say who detained them.
r1-UNHR-017.vn: Actor 'State authorities' was inferred; set to not stated. DRC-wide; the article does not say who detained them or where.
src: Le Bureau note également un resserrement de l’espace civique : 42 acteurs politiques étaient encore détenus en janvier, dans un contexte marqué par des arrestations jugées arbitraires.

r1-UNHR-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH documented 46 cases of conflict-related sexual violence in June 2026, against 40 in May, affecting 73 victims (56 women, 15 girls and 2 men), of whom North Kivu accounts for 52 and South Kivu 12, and that the AFC/M23 is cited for 34 victims.
r1-UNHR-018.l: North Kivu (52 victims), South Kivu (12), Ituri (8)
r1-UNHR-018.a: Non-State armed groups (77% of victims); AFC/M23 cited for 34 victims
r1-UNHR-018.x: BCNUDH: 46 cases; 73 victims; North Kivu 52 (73%); South Kivu 12; Ituri 8; AFC/M23 34
r1-UNHR-018.n: Report published 20 Aug 2026 per Radio Okapi. Latest BCNUDH monthly figure found. Total June 2026 violations: 657 DRC-wide.
r1-UNHR-018.vn: Verbatim; year from the article's lead. The 34 AFC/M23 victims are a DRC-wide count; the article does not split them by province.
src: Le BCNUDH a également documenté 46 cas de violences sexuelles liées aux conflits en juin, contre 40 en mai. Ces faits ont concerné 73 victimes : 56 femmes, 15 filles et 2 hommes. Le Nord-Kivu concentre 73 % des victimes, soit 52 personnes, devant le Sud-Kivu avec 12 victimes et l’Ituri avec 8.
Les groupes armés non étatiques sont identifiés comme les principaux auteurs présumés, avec 77 % des victimes. L’AFC/M23 est cité dans le rapport pour 34 victimes.

r1-UNHR-019.s: The ICRC reported that violence and fighting in North and South Kivu hinder the movement of sick people, limit the transport of the wounded and make medical supplies hard to deliver, and have led to health-care workers leaving and medical facilities being looted or destroyed.
r1-UNHR-019.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (109 health centres studied)
r1-UNHR-019.a: not attributed to a named party
r1-UNHR-019.x: ICRC: 2,351 wounded treated in ICRC-supported hospitals in the first quarter of 2025 (172% increase over 2024); study of 109 health centres, April and May 2025
r1-UNHR-019.n: ICRC is not a UN body but is a primary humanitarian source. Release date 17 June 2025 from search listing. The release also mentions funding cuts as a factor.
r1-UNHR-019.vn: Figures field had 'Q1' (stray '1'); rewritten. ICRC attributes the decline also to drastic funding cuts; no party named as responsible.
src: The violence and fighting have led to a security situation that hinders the movement of sick people, limits the transport of the wounded and makes medical supplies hard to deliver. It has also led to health-care workers leaving and medical facilities being looted or destroyed.
In the first quarter of 2025, 2,351 wounded people were treated in ICRC-supported hospitals, which is nearly as many as were treated in all of 2024. That’s a 172% increase over 2024.

r1-UV-2025Q1-001.s: Radio Okapi reported on 17 February 2025 that calm had returned to the city of Uvira after clashes that caused the death of 12 people, civilians and soldiers, and that the violence broke out the day before after an altercation between FARDC soldiers and a group of Wazalendo fighters. It cited Serge Kigwati, president of the Société civile des nationalistes congolais, as saying the altercation began when the Wazalendo tried to disarm soldiers returning from the northern front and heading south, and the FARDC refused to hand over their weapons.
r1-UV-2025Q1-001.a: FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo fighters (per Radio Okapi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-001.x: Radio Okapi: 12 people killed, civilians and soldiers
r1-UV-2025Q1-001.n: Perpetrator of individual deaths not stated. Later Actualite.cd reports 17 dead on 18-19 Feb (separate claim); Fides (relaying Radio Okapi) gives 12 on 17 Feb.
r1-UV-2025Q1-001.vn: Page read in full; every clause on the page. The refusal clause is in Radio Okapi's narration and in Kigwati's quote.
src: Le calme est revenu ce lundi 17 février dans la ville d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu) après des affrontements qui ont causé la mort de 12 personnes, civils et militaires. Ces violences ont éclaté la veille, à la suite d’une altercation entre des soldats FARDC et un groupe de combattants Wazalendo.

Selon le président de la Société civile des nationalistes congolais, Serge Kigwati, l’altercation a commencé lorsque les Wazalendo ont tenté de désarmer des militaires revenant du front Nord et se dirigeant vers le Sud de la province.

r1-UV-2025Q1-002.s: MediaCongo reported that live-fire exchanges shook the city of Uvira on Sunday 16 February 2025 at the Kalundu port, where it said the FARDC and the Wazalendo clashed, the Wazalendo trying to prevent the FARDC from boarding a boat bound for Kalemie.
r1-UV-2025Q1-002.l: Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-002.n: Credited on page to 'Le hautpanel / MCP'; single outlet, no casualty figures. Article date taken from URL context (17 Feb); event date is 16 Feb as stated.
r1-UV-2025Q1-002.vn: Page supports; credited at foot to 'Le hautpanel / MCP, via mediacongo.net'. excerpt_en flag is only the expansion of FARDC.
src: Des échanges de tirs à balles réelles secouent la ville d’Uvira, ce dimanche 16 février 2025, plus précisément au port de Kalundu, où des affrontements violents opposent les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) à leurs alliés de circonstance, les Wazalendo.
Ces derniers tentent activement d’empêcher les FARDC d’embarquer sur un bateau en direction de Kalemie, afin de fuir l’intensification des combats dans la région.

r1-UV-2025Q1-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least 17 people were killed on Tuesday and Wednesday in the city of Uvira in spontaneous clashes between Congolese soldiers and Wazalendo militiamen (its headline says about ten dead; the local source it quotes gives a toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo combined), and quoted an unnamed local source who said the Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition, and that soldiers seized phones, money and other goods, broke down doors and shot civilians who resisted.
r1-UV-2025Q1-003.a: Congolese soldiers and wazalendo militiamen (per Actualite.cd and an unnamed local source)
r1-UV-2025Q1-003.x: Actualite.cd: at least 17 killed (civilians, soldiers, wazalendo per the local source); headline: about ten
r1-UV-2025Q1-003.n: Headline says 'une dizaine' (about ten) while the lede says at least 17; figure from an anonymous local source. Sits beside Radio Okapi's 12 dead on 16-17 Feb. Weekday dates (Tuesday 18, Wednesday 19) computed from the 19 Feb publication date.
r1-UV-2025Q1-003.vn: Page read; anonymous local source carries the looting and the refusal clause. Headline says 'une dizaine de morts'; lede says at least 17. Sits beside Radio Okapi's 12 dead (17 Feb). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: headline says about ten dead 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: local source's toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo; unnamed local source 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Read the retained page: the refusal and looting account is one unnamed local source; the toll mixes civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo and conflicts with the headline's 'une dizaine'. Statement now carries both figures and the toll's scope so it is not read as civilian deaths.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): headline says about ten dead; Wazalendo refused to let soldiers leave for Kalemie with weapons and ammunition; local source's toll of more than 17 civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo; unnamed local source
src: Au moins 17 personnes ont été tuées ces mardi et mercredi dans la ville d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu) où des affrontements spontanés ont éclaté entre des militaires congolais et des miliciens wazalendo.
Les militaires ravissent les téléphones, l’argent et d’autres biens de la population, ils cassent les portes des maisons et tout civil qui résiste reçoit une balle.
Affrontements FARDC-Wazalendo à Uvira : une dizaine de morts signalés
Les wazalendo refusent à ce que les militaires puissent partir à Kalemie avec des armes et munitions, ils veulent qu’ils leur laissent ces effets à Uvira avant de partir.
Aujourd’hui nous avons déjà un bilan de plus de 17 personnes, civils, militaires et wazalendo tués dans ces circonstances », a indiqué à ACTUALITE.CD une source locale qui ne veut pas être citée.

r1-UV-2025Q1-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that all detainees of the Uvira prison (named 'prison Mulunge d’Uvira' in the article) escaped that morning, and that the mass escape from the central prison of Uvira was confirmed notably by sources of the local Catholic church. A local activist told Actualite.cd that the prison doors were broken by fleeing soldiers who wanted to free their detained comrades and that other civilians also left.
r1-UV-2025Q1-004.l: Uvira central prison, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-004.a: fleeing soldiers broke the prison doors (per a local activist quoted by Actualite.cd)
r1-UV-2025Q1-004.n: Category is a closest fit (prison escape). Fides gives a different account (authorities decided to release prisoners; separate claim). FIDH (SV-2025-014) mentions escapes at Uvira generally. Prison name as printed ('Mulunge').
r1-UV-2025Q1-004.vn: Removed '19 February 2025' (publication date, not in excerpt; date field keeps it). Added the activist's account of who broke the doors, printed on the page. Fides (same day) says the state authorities decided to release the prisoners; the activist also says some had been released two days earlier under a presidential pardon. Unresolved discrepancy.
src: tous les détenus de la prison Mulunge d’Uvira se sont évadés ce matin. L’évasion massive à la prison centrale d’Uvira est confirmée notamment par des sources de l’église catholique locale.

r1-UV-2025Q1-005.s: Agenzia Fides reported that the state authorities had even decided to release the prisoners before the rebels' arrival in Uvira, and that the withdrawal of Burundian soldiers a few days after the fall of Bukavu would have favoured the rebels' advance towards Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q1-005.n: Unattributed in the Fides text; conflicts in framing with the 'escape' account (Actualite.cd) - an unresolved discrepancy. Burundian withdrawal hedged ('aurait').
r1-UV-2025Q1-005.vn: Removed publication date from statement. Fides gives no source for the release claim; conflicts with the Actualite.cd escape account.
src: Le retrait des soldats burundais quelques jours après la chute de la ville de Bukavu aurait favorisé l'avancée des rebelles vers Uvira, où la tension monte ; les autorités étatiques ont même décidé de libérer les prisonniers avant l'arrivée des rebelles.

r1-UV-2025Q1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that after taking Bukavu and Kamanyola, the rebels conquered the cité of Sange, about 30 kilometres from Uvira, on Wednesday 19 February, and described the M23 as supported by the Rwandan army.
r1-UV-2025Q1-006.a: M23, supported by the Rwandan army (per Radio Okapi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-006.n: Frontline claim. Actualite.cd (19 Feb) separately says AFC/M23 rebels arrived at Sange 'at least 35 km' from Uvira (headline seen only in search results, not fetched). Weekday date explicit on page.
src: Pendant ce temps, le M23, soutenu par l'armée rwandaise, poursuit sa conquête dans la région. Après avoir pris Bukavu et Kamanyola, les rebelles ont conquis la cité de Sange, située à environ 30 kilomètres d'Uvira, mercredi 19 février.

r1-UV-2025Q1-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that acts of pillage and violence were reported in Uvira, that armed persons were looting and ransacking shops and homes, and that the office of the Uvira bishopric was vandalised and priests and the bishop were assaulted and robbed of their belongings. It said local sources attributed these acts to FARDC soldiers and to undisciplined Wazalendo fighters.
r1-UV-2025Q1-007.a: FARDC soldiers and undisciplined Wazalendo fighters (per local sources cited by Radio Okapi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-007.n: Vatican News (separate claim) gives the bishopric incident in more detail; Vatican News's local source says it is unclear who is responsible and that both FARDC and Wazalendo profit from the panic.
r1-UV-2025Q1-007.vn: Removed publication date from statement (not in excerpt).
src: Des personnes armées pillent et saccagent des commerces et des habitations. Le bureau de l'Évêché d'Uvira a été vandalisé. Des prêtres ainsi que l'évêque ont été agressés et dépouillés de leurs biens.
Les sources locales attribuent ces actes inciviques à des militaires des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et à des combattants Wazalendo indisciplinés qui sèment la terreur parmi la population civile.

r1-UV-2025Q1-008.s: Vatican News reported that on Thursday 20 February three FARDC soldiers entered the episcopal seat of Uvira, forcing Mgr Muyengo Mulombe and two priests to hand over their phones and cash, and that the priests named in the article are Ricardo Mukuninwa and Bernard Kalolero.
r1-UV-2025Q1-008.l: Episcopal seat, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-008.n: Single outlet citing a local source. Page also says the amount handed over was about 50,000 FC (150 dollars), and that another community of priests of the parish Saints Anges Gardiens was visited by armed men.
r1-UV-2025Q1-008.vn: Page read in full; FARDC identification printed in the body. Names spelled as printed. Article by Marie Duhamel; details from a local source. Actualite.cd (23 Feb) says only 'trois militaires'.
src: Ce jeudi 20 février, trois militaires ont pénétré au siège épiscopal de la ville, forçant Mgr Muyengo Mulombe et deux prêtres à leur remettre leurs téléphones et liquidités.
Muyengo Mulombe, ainsi que deux prêtres qui se trouvaient à ses côtés, les pères Ricardo Mukuninwa et père Bernard Kalolero, tous jetés à terre.

r1-UV-2025Q1-009.s: Kivutimes reported that night attacks by 'uncontrolled soldiers' were wreaking havoc in Uvira, notably in the Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo and Mulongwe quarters, despite measures taken by the military authorities of the Sokola 2 Sud operational sector. It added, citing sources close to the institutions, that on Thursday 20 February these soldiers looted the CENI warehouse in Uvira and a Bralima depot at the Kalundu port.
r1-UV-2025Q1-009.l: Uvira city quarters (Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo, Mulongwe) and Kalundu port, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-009.a: 'uncontrolled soldiers', often identified as soldiers who fled M23-held areas of Goma and Bukavu (per Kivutimes)
r1-UV-2025Q1-009.n: Local outlet, single source. The article's date (21 Feb) coincides with the 'Friday 21 February' night it describes, so the report may have been posted or updated later; treat the night-attack date as approximate.
r1-UV-2025Q1-009.vn: Narrowed to what the stored excerpts print; time and origin of the attackers moved to the note with a verbatim quote.
