The page dates the night attacks to the night of Friday 21 February 2025 from about 21h00 and says the attackers were often identified as soldiers who fled M23-held Goma and Bukavu (see replacement quote); these details are not in the stored excerpt.
src: Malgré les mesures prises par les autorités militaires du secteur opérationnel sokola 2 sud du Sud-Kivu pour traquer ces éléments devenus des voleurs, les attaques continuent de faire des ravages, notamment dans des quartiers comme Kimanga, Nyamianda, Kabindula, Kilibula, Songo et Mulongwe.

Ces militaires incontrôlés, jeudi 20 février 2025 ont pillés l’entrepôt de la CENI/ Uvira et un dépôt de la bralima se trouvant au port de Kalundu, font savoir des sources proches de ces institutions.

r1-UV-2025Q1-010.s: Actualite.cd, in an article built on a message by the Bishop of Uvira, reported that banks, pharmacies, markets and health centres had closed in Uvira, and quoted Mgr Sébastien-Joseph Muyengo Mulombe describing systematic looting with violence and killings, including in family homes and convents.
r1-UV-2025Q1-010.a: not attributed by the source (armed groups including routed soldiers and unidentified fighters, per the article)
r1-UV-2025Q1-010.n: The closure statement is the article's own sentence following the bishop's quote; it does not say which health centres or for how long. The same article says political-administrative authorities and much of the police and army fled to Burundi, Kalemie or Tanzania (not separately excerpted).
r1-UV-2025Q1-010.vn: Page supports; the closure sentence is the outlet's narration. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « Nous vivons une situation traumatisante, avec des crépitements de balles jour et nuit, des pillages systématiques avec violence, voire des tueries, y compris dans des maisons familiales, des couvents de prêtres et de religieuses », a déclaré Mgr Sébastien-Joseph Muyengo Mulombe, évêque d’Uvira, dans un message adressé aux habitants. Banques, pharmacies, marchés et centres de santé ont fermé leurs portes.
Les marchés, banques, pharmacies et centres de santé ont fermé, laissant la population dans une grande précarité.

r1-UV-2025Q1-011.s: MSF said that the Hôpital Général de Référence in Uvira had repeatedly been caught in crossfire, endangering patients and staff, that medical activities had to be interrupted again the previous week with patients sheltering, and that armed men entered the hospital premises, moving and firing inside.
r1-UV-2025Q1-011.l: Hôpital Général de Référence, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-011.a: armed men; not further identified by MSF (MSF describes clashes between FARDC and Wazalendo in the city)
r1-UV-2025Q1-011.x: MSF: hospitals receiving about ten wounded per day from 17 Feb, including civilians
r1-UV-2025Q1-011.n: MSF primary statement; Radio Okapi (25 Feb) relays it. Date range approximate: 'last week' relative to 23 Feb, and MSF says the situation peaked on 15 Feb. MSF names staff only anonymised.
r1-UV-2025Q1-011.vn: Removed publication date from statement; figures field (from 17 Feb, about ten wounded per day per structure) supported by replacement quote (page spells 'févier'). MSF does not identify the armed men. MSF testimony page dated 23 Feb 2025; staff names anonymised.
src: A plusieurs reprises, l’Hôpital général de Référence à Uvira s’est retrouvé pris sous des tirs croisés, mettant gravement en danger les patients et le personnel. La semaine dernière, les activités médicales ont à nouveau dû être interrompues et les patients ont dû se mettre à l’abri pour éviter d’être touchés. Des hommes armés ont également pénétré dans les locaux de l’hôpital, se déplaçant et tirant à l'intérieur.

r1-UV-2025Q1-012.s: MSF said that it had been forced to reduce its teams in Uvira, where they had supported the Ministry of Health in diagnosing and treating mpox patients for several months, and that it redirected part of its activity to supporting the care of war wounded by delivering medical supplies to several health structures in the Uvira health zone.
r1-UV-2025Q1-012.n: Actualite.cd (3 Mar) says humanitarian organisations such as MSF were forced to withdraw staff from Uvira; MSF's own words are 'reduce' - recorded as a discrepancy of wording.
r1-UV-2025Q1-012.vn: Redirection clause is on the page, not in the stored excerpt; supplied. MSF says it was 'forced to reduce' its teams; Actualite.cd (3 Mar) says MSF withdrew its staff. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: redirected activity to war wounded via medical supplies in Uvira health zone 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Wording only: the source says 'contrainte de réduire' (forced to reduce), which is the health-access point; Actualite.cd's 'withdrew' (in note) is a stronger version not supported by MSF.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): redirected activity to war wounded via medical supplies in Uvira health zone
src: MSF a été contrainte de réduire ses équipes à Uvira, où elles donnaient un appui au ministère de la Santé dans le diagnostic et la prise en charge des patients atteints de la Mpox depuis plusieurs mois.

MSF réoriente une partie de ses activités dans le soutien de la prise en charge des blessés de guerre en acheminant du matériel médical vital dans plusieurs structures médicales de la zone de santé d'Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q1-013.s: MSF stated that Burundian authorities now estimated at 35'000 the number of people who would have been displaced since the start of February.
r1-UV-2025Q1-013.x: MSF, citing Burundian authorities: 35'000 people said to have been displaced since early February
r1-UV-2025Q1-013.n: Figure is the Burundian authorities' estimate as relayed by MSF; Vatican News cites UNHCR for 42,000 people reaching Burundi in two weeks (not separately claimed). Scope of the 35,000 (all of the Kivus vs Uvira) is not stated.
r1-UV-2025Q1-013.vn: Kept the source's conditional ('se seraient déplacées') and its number format; origin is the Burundian authorities.
src: Les autorités Burundaises estiment maintenant à 35'000 le nombre de personnes qui se seraient déplacées depuis début février.

r1-UV-2025Q1-014.s: OCHA said it was alarmed by the escalation of violence and insecurity in Uvira, and that clashes and rising crime were putting local communities and humanitarian workers in extreme danger, with humanitarian partners reporting multiple incidents of looting and sexual violence.
r1-UV-2025Q1-014.n: UN daily briefing note; no number of incidents, dates, victims or perpetrators given. Date is the publication date (reported). Only UN-level indication found for sexual violence in Uvira city in Q1; a Facebook post (not cited) says the FARDC accused the Rwandan army and AFC/M23 of looting and sexual violence in Uvira - not verified.
r1-UV-2025Q1-014.vn: Page supports verbatim. No number, date, victims or perpetrators given for the sexual violence incidents. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: OCHA is alarmed by the recent escalation of violence and insecurity in Uvira, a city about 100 kilometers south of Bukavu, in the Democratic Republic of the Congo . Clashes and rising crime in Uvira are putting local communities and humanitarian workers in extreme danger, with humanitarian partners reporting multiple incidents of looting and sexual violence.
à Uvira, où des viols et des pillages ont également été signalés, selon les partenaires humanitaires de l’ONU

r1-UV-2025Q1-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu operation, Jérémie Meya (lieutenant Jérémie Meya Gbe), said the FARDC had begun an operation to track down fleeing soldiers and alleged perpetrators of various harassments in Uvira, with the stated aim of 'cleaning' Uvira and the localities of the Ruzizi plain so the population could go about its business safely.
r1-UV-2025Q1-015.l: Uvira city and the Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-015.n: FARDC acknowledgement of indiscipline by its own soldiers; the page also quotes Meya's objective sentence on restoring order and discipline after 'acts of barbarity and indiscipline' by soldiers fleeing the front lines.
r1-UV-2025Q1-015.vn: Page supports; full name, rank and the Ruzizi-plain clause supplied from the page.
src: Les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) ont entamé une opération de traque des militaires fuyards et présumés auteurs de différentes tracasseries à Uvira. A en croire le porte-parole de l'opération Sukola 2 sud Sud-Kivu, Jérémie Meya, cette opération vise le nettoyage de la ville d'Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q1-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that over the previous few days at least 20 dead and more than 60 people wounded by bullets had been taken in charge in the Uvira health zone, and that humanitarian organisations had recorded a toll of about a hundred wounded; it did not say whether the dead and wounded were civilians or combatants, or who caused the casualties.
r1-UV-2025Q1-016.x: Actualite.cd: at least 20 dead and more than 60 bullet-wounded taken in charge in the Uvira health zone; 'une centaine' (about a hundred) wounded per humanitarian organisations
r1-UV-2025Q1-016.n: Article does not name who is counting or the period precisely; figures may include soldiers. Compare Radio Okapi 12 dead (17 Feb) and Actualite.cd 17 dead (19 Feb).
r1-UV-2025Q1-016.vn: Figures field rewritten in the source's own wording ('une centaine'), not the numeral. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Figure scope: the source does not say the casualties were civilians, and the same days' clashes involved soldiers and Wazalendo (Actualite.cd 19 Feb counts civilians, soldiers and Wazalendo together). Added so the claim is not read as a civilian toll under attack_on_civilians.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: Depuis quelques jours, au moins 20 morts et plus de 60 blessés par balles ont été pris en charge dans la zone de santé d'Uvira. Un bilan d'une centaine de blessés a été enregistré par les organisations humanitaires.

r1-UV-2025Q1-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that political-administrative authorities, FARDC soldiers and police settled in the city of Uvira on Monday 24 February, and that governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi, his deputy and about 600 uniformed men, including police and soldiers, who had left Bukavu some days earlier for Burundi, arrived in Uvira through the Kavimvira border.
r1-UV-2025Q1-017.l: Uvira city (Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-017.a: South Kivu provincial government (Governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-017.x: Radio Okapi: about 600 uniformed men (police and soldiers) with the governor and deputy governor
r1-UV-2025Q1-017.n: The deputy governor is not named in this article (later SOS Médias Burundi names Jean Jacques Elekano as vice-governor). The provincial government's own account is in the next claim.
src: Des autorités politico-administratives, des militaires des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et des policiers se sont installés ce lundi 24 février, dans la ville d’Uvira au Sud-Kivu.

Le gouverneur Jean-Jacques Pulusi, son vice-gouverneur et environ 600 hommes en uniformes, dont des policiers et militaires, avaient quitté la ville de Bukavu il y a quelques jours pour se rendre au Burundi. Toutes ces personnes sont arrivées à Uvira par la frontière de Kavimvira située entre le Burundi et la RDC.

r1-UV-2025Q1-018.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing the communication cell of the South Kivu governor, that the provincial executive head and his deputy were now staying in Uvira and would continue to administer South Kivu from there because Bukavu, the capital, was under rebel occupation.
r1-UV-2025Q1-018.n: Statement relayed second-hand through Radio Okapi; the date given is the 24 Feb arrival. The page adds that the DRC ambassador to Burundi, Willy Mulamba Mabika, facilitated the return.
r1-UV-2025Q1-018.vn: Page supports; statement is the communication cell's as relayed.
src: Selon la cellule de Communication du gouverneur de province, le chef de l'exécutif provincial et son adjoint séjournent désormais à Uvira. C'est à partir de cette ville qu'ils vont continuer à administrer la province du Sud-Kivu, étant donné que Bukavu, la capitale, est sous occupation des rebelles.

r1-UV-2025Q1-019.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources on Saturday 29 March, that cohabitation between the FARDC and the Wazalendo was becoming difficult, notably in Uvira, and that the two parties had set up two parallel commands, which made operational coordination difficult.
r1-UV-2025Q1-019.n: Anonymous local sources; the page adds that Wazalendo suspect FARDC soldiers of corruption and of collaborating with the rebels, and that a reconciliation meeting was planned for that weekend.
r1-UV-2025Q1-019.vn: Page supports. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Mar 2025, carries every clause, attributed to local sources. The stored excerpt is cut before 'rendant difficile la coordination militaire'; the full sentence is added. Statement unchanged.
src: La cohabitation entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et ses partenaires, les combattants Wazalendo devient difficile, notamment dans la ville d’Uvira, rapportent des sources locales ce samedi 29 mars. Selon ces sources, ces deux parties bien que poursuivant le même objectif, protéger la ville contre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, ont mis en place deux commandements parallèles

Selon ces sources, ces deux parties bien que poursuivant le même objectif, protéger la ville contre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, ont mis en place deux commandements parallèles, rendant difficile la coordination militaire sur le plan opérationnel.

r1-UV-2025Q1-020.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several witnesses, that Wazalendo-affiliated fighters under the command of 'generals Mayele and Makanaki' had multiplied acts of pillage in the Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters of Uvira, targeting the Banyamulenge community, and that some Wazalendo justified the attacks by accusing the Banyamulenge of complicity with the M23; a community leader it quoted rejected that accusation as false.
r1-UV-2025Q1-020.l: Songo, Kabindula and Nyamianda quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-020.a: Wazalendo fighters under 'generals Mayele and Makanaki' (per witnesses cited by SOS Médias Burundi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-020.n: Burundi-based outlet; witnesses unnamed except 'David M.', a trader from Kabindula (partial name), who describes theft of his phone, computer and clothes. Spellings 'Mayele' and 'Makanaki' as printed; not to be confused with Twirwaneho's Colonel Makanika (spelled differently). Date is the report date (25 Mar), activity described as ongoing in March.
r1-UV-2025Q1-020.vn: Page supports; Banyamulenge targeting and the M23 justification are on the page, supplied. Article by Adam Ntwari (SOS Médias Burundi). A community leader quoted rejects the accusations. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: targeting the Banyamulenge community 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Wazalendo justification: Banyamulenge complicity with M23 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: community leader rejected the accusation as false 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Attribution is hedged ('selon plusieurs témoins') and kept. Read the retained page: the 'community leader rejects the accusations' line in the note refutes the M23-complicity charge, not the looting; added as the counter-account. No Wazalendo response on the page.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): targeting the Banyamulenge community; Wazalendo justification: Banyamulenge complicity with M23; community leader rejected the accusation as false
src: Selon plusieurs témoins, des combattants affiliés aux Wazalendo, sous le commandement des généraux Mayele et Makanaki, ont multiplié les actes de pillage dans les quartiers de Songo, Kabindula et Nyamianda.

La communauté Banyamulenge, vivant dans la ville d’Uvira, à l’est de la République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), continue d’être la cible d’exactions commises par certains combattants des groupes armés Wazalendo
Certains combattants Wazalendo justifient ces attaques en accusant la communauté Banyamulenge de complicité avec le groupe armé M23, actif dans l’est du pays.
Un leader communautaire réfute ces accusations : « Ce sont de fausses allégations.

r1-UV-2025Q1-021.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Friday 21 March 2025 Wazalendo fighters attacked the premises of the organisation Ebenezer International Ministry in Uvira, taking several electronic devices, including computers and Motorola phones.
r1-UV-2025Q1-021.n: Single local source; an organisation official is quoted anonymously.
src: Le vendredi 21 mars 2025, des combattants Wazalendo ont attaqué les locaux de l’organisation Ebenezer International Ministry à Uvira, emportant plusieurs équipements électroniques, dont des ordinateurs et des téléphones Motorola.

r1-UV-2025Q1-022.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean Jacques Elekano, condemned the violence against the Banyamulenge in Uvira and called for respect for all communities, saying in a communiqué that surveillance had been reinforced and calling on law enforcement to act firmly against these abuses.
r1-UV-2025Q1-022.n: Communiqué not found on an official site; quoted via SOS Médias Burundi only. The page also says the Banyamulenge say no concrete measure has been taken.
r1-UV-2025Q1-022.vn: Page supports. Communiqué date not given; 25 Mar is the report date.
src: Le vice-gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean Jacques Elekano, a condamné ces violences et appelé au respect de toutes les communautés. « Il est impératif que chacun puisse vivre en paix, sans discrimination. Nous avons renforcé la surveillance et appelons les forces de l’ordre à agir fermement contre ces exactions, » a-t-il déclaré dans un communiqué.

r1-UV-2025Q1-023.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 14 February Wazalendo fighters killed a 25-year-old Munyamulenge man in Mulongwe, Uvira territory, after accusing him of being Rwandan; he was shot twice in the hip and died of his wounds, according to two sources.
r1-UV-2025Q1-023.n: Report published 2025-05-23, event dated 14 Feb by HRW; victim not named. 'Mulongwe' is also a quarter of Uvira city (Kivutimes) and a Burundian refugee camp; HRW says 'in Uvira territory'.
src: Le 14 février, des combattants Wazalendo ont tué un homme munyamulenge de 25 ans à Mulongwe, dans le territoire d’Uvira, après l'avoir accusé d'être rwandais. Ils lui ont tiré deux balles dans la hanche et il est mort de ses blessures, selon deux sources.

r1-UV-2025Q1-024.s: Human Rights Watch reported that after the M23 took Bukavu, Wazalendo fighters entered more than 20 Banyamulenge homes in Uvira, stealing property and threatening residents, and that in one case they shot a woman in the head and beat at least three people.
r1-UV-2025Q1-024.x: HRW: more than 20 Banyamulenge homes entered; in one case a woman shot in the head and at least three people beaten
r1-UV-2025Q1-024.n: Period not precisely dated by HRW ('after the taking of Bukavu', which other claims date 16 Feb); end of range is the report date. HRW does not say whether the woman survived. Corroborates the SOS Médias Burundi 25 Mar account of Wazalendo looting of Banyamulenge homes.
r1-UV-2025Q1-024.vn: The draft split 'in one case' from the beatings; HRW puts both in the one case. Figures rewritten in the source's words. HRW does not say whether the woman survived or give dates for individual incidents.
src: Après la prise de Bukavu par le M23, des combattants Wazalendo sont entrés dans plus de 20 foyers banyamulenge à Uvira, volant des biens et menaçant les habitants. Dans un cas, ils ont tiré une balle dans la tête d'une femme et ont battu au moins trois personnes.

r1-UV-2025Q1-025.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March in Sange, Uvira territory, a Wazalendo commander arrested and whipped a 48-year-old man accused of stealing a television, and that a relative and a neighbour said the man died of his injuries.
r1-UV-2025Q1-025.a: a Wazalendo commander (not named by HRW)
r1-UV-2025Q1-025.n: Victim and commander not named in this passage. HRW adds the commander was later involved in the killing of a Congolese soldier and was dismissed but not prosecuted for those killings (not excerpted).
r1-UV-2025Q1-025.vn: Page supports. HRW adds that the commander was later dismissed but not prosecuted.
src: Le 3 mars, à Sange, dans le territoire d'Uvira, un commandant Wazalendo a arrêté et fouetté un homme, âgé de 48 ans, accusé d'avoir volé une télévision. Un proche et un voisin ont déclaré que l'homme était décédé des suites de ses blessures.

r1-UV-2025Q1-026.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 3 March Wazalendo fighters attacked several Banyamulenge villages within 10 km of Bibokoboko, Fizi territory, and that a military source and residents said there was no known presence of opposing armed groups near Bibokoboko at the time.
r1-UV-2025Q1-026.l: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-026.x: HRW (quoting a community leader): seven people killed
r1-UV-2025Q1-026.n: Outside Uvira territory (Fizi) but in the same Wazalendo/Banyamulenge dynamic and recorded here for the Uvira investigation; a community leader quoted by HRW says seven people were killed and homes, medical centres and schools destroyed (see next claim).
r1-UV-2025Q1-026.vn: Statement unchanged; figures field removed because the seven-killed figure is a community leader's quote carried by claim 26, not by this excerpt.
src: Le 3 mars, des combattants Wazalendo ont attaqué plusieurs villages banyamulenge situés dans un rayon de 10 kilomètres autour de Bibokoboko, dans le territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu. Une source militaire et des habitants ont déclaré qu'il n'y avait pas de présence connue de groupes armés opposés près de Bibokoboko au moment de l'attaque.

r1-UV-2025Q1-027.s: Human Rights Watch quoted a community leader as saying, of the 3 March Wazalendo attack around Bibokoboko in Fizi territory, that the fighters said they had come to 'clean' the Banyamulenge, killed seven people and destroyed homes, medical centres and schools.
r1-UV-2025Q1-027.l: Bibokoboko area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-027.a: Wazalendo fighters (per a community leader quoted by Human Rights Watch)
r1-UV-2025Q1-027.n: Quote of an unnamed community leader. HRW separately confirmed with satellite imagery and geolocated photographs that houses were burned that day in several villages including Madjdja, Lulimba I and Bibokoboko (not excerpted here). Which medical centres is not stated. Contradicting reporting: Kivu Times (2025-03-06): Figure: at least 8 civilians killed (including a woman), versus 7 in the claim
r1-UV-2025Q1-027.vn: Date and Fizi location supplied from the adjoining HRW paragraph; quote attributed to an unnamed community leader as HRW does. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « Ils [les Wazalendo] ont dit que nous n'étions pas congolais, que nous étions rwandais. Ils ont dit qu'ils étaient venus à Bibokoboko pour ‘nettoyer’ les Banyamulenge », a déclaré un chef de communauté. « Ils ont tué sept personnes et détruit des maisons, des centres médicaux et des écoles . »

Les habitants de Bibokoboko, une localité située dans le territoire de Fizi, ont été frappés par une série d’attaques sanglantes menées par les groupes armés Mai Mai et leurs alliés en date du 3 Mars 2025.

r1-UV-2025Q1-028.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing hospital sources, that the Uvira health zone faced an outbreak of cholera among soldiers, with at least 40 cases hospitalised in the cholera treatment unit of the Uvira general hospital, and a medical official quoted as saying the unit was completely overwhelmed with patients lying on the floor.
r1-UV-2025Q1-028.l: Uvira general hospital, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-028.x: Actualite.cd: at least 40 cholera cases hospitalised
r1-UV-2025Q1-028.n: The page also says the situation had deteriorated in preceding weeks because of Wazalendo-FARDC clashes, hospitals saw an influx of wounded, and humanitarian organisations such as MSF withdrew staff (MSF's own word is 'reduce teams'). OCHA (7 Mar via search result, not fetched) reports 200+ new cases and two deaths in Uvira over two days.
r1-UV-2025Q1-028.vn: Page supports; quote supplied. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: La zone de santé d'Uvira, dans le Sud-Kivu, fait face à une flambée de cas de choléra parmi les militaires. Au moins 40 cas sont en hospitalisation à l'Unité de traitement du choléra (UTC) à l'hôpital général d'Uvira, renseigne à ACTUALITE.CD, des sources hospitalières.
Au moins 40 cas sont en hospitalisation à l’hôpital général, renseigne le portail d’information Actualite, des sources hospitalières.

r1-UV-2025Q1-029.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least 90 soldiers from the North and South Kivu fronts had been appearing since Wednesday 12 February before the military garrison tribunal of Uvira on various counts, notably fleeing before the M23 and extortion.
r1-UV-2025Q1-029.l: Military garrison tribunal, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-029.x: Actualite.cd: at least 90 soldiers appearing before the Uvira military garrison tribunal
r1-UV-2025Q1-029.n: Category is a closest fit (trial of soldiers). The page says the trial runs alongside one in Bukavu with 282 soldiers; the military magistrate is named as Lt Col Lwamba Songe (not in this excerpt); the accused were allegedly caught with 59 AK-47s and some were already on a boat bound for Tanganyika.
r1-UV-2025Q1-029.vn: 'Tried' in figures implied a completed trial; narrowed to 'appearing'. 'griefs' rendered as counts. Trial stage only (comparaissent); no verdict reported. Prosecutor named on the page as lieutenant colonel magistrat Lwamba Songe.
src: Au moins 90 militaires venus des fronts au Nord et Sud-Kivu Kivu comparaissent depuis ce mercredi 12 février devant le tribunal militaire garnison d'Uvira pour différents griefs notamment la fuite devant le M23, l’extorsion.

r1-UV-2025Q1-030.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 rebels took control of the villages Rurambo and Kigarama, in the Bafuliro chiefdom in the Uvira highlands, following the allegiance of the Rushaba wazalendo group to the AFC/M23.
r1-UV-2025Q1-030.l: Rurambo and Kigarama, Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory (highlands), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-030.a: AFC/M23 with the allied Rushaba wazalendo group (per Actualite.cd)
r1-UV-2025Q1-030.n: Page quotes a local notable describing fighting on 'yesterday' (12 March) from 04:00 to 17:00 against the wazalendo group of Ruma Hondwa; date computed from 'hier' and the 13 March publication date. Earlier in March the M23 advanced from Kaziba (Walungu).
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont pris le contrôle des villages Rurambo et Kigarama, dans la chefferie de Bafuliro, dans les hauts plateaux d'Uvira (Sud-Kivu). C’est à la suite de l’allégeance du groupe wazalendo Rushaba à la rébellion de l’AFC/M23.

r1-UV-2025Q1-031.s: Actualite.cd reported that local civil society said Rushaba had been with Nyamusaraba in the 'Task force' together with the Burundian forces before deserting it, starting clashes at Kashama and allying with the M23. The article describes the Task force as composed of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo, and quotes another source on site as saying there was a coalition of Banyamulenge based in Kahololo/Marungu, Rushaba wazalendo and M23 elements from Kaziba.
r1-UV-2025Q1-031.l: Kashama, Kigarama and Uvira highlands, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-031.a: Task force of Congolese soldiers, Burundian soldiers and wazalendo; Rushaba wazalendo group (per Actualite.cd)
r1-UV-2025Q1-031.n: Local civil society source; evidence of Burundian forces still working with a Task force in the Uvira highlands in mid-March. The same page says the villages Murambi, Kitoga, Babingwa, Kitembe and Kahusi remained under the government coalition's control.
r1-UV-2025Q1-031.vn: The coalition clause is attributed on the page to 'une autre source sur place', not to the article itself; attribution restored.
src: « Rushaba était avec Nyamusaraba dans la Task force ensemble avec les forces burundaises, il a déserté dans la Task force et a débuté les affrontements à Kashama et s'est allié au M23 », a souligné la société civile locale.

r1-UV-2025Q1-032.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Minembwe group of villages in Fizi territory fell on Friday into the hands of fighters of the armed group Twirwaneho, two days after the death of Colonel Makanika, the group's military chief, killed in a drone attack. Citing witnesses, it said Twirwaneho fighters occupied all FARDC positions in several named localities, and a Twirwaneho fighter told the outlet that the soldiers had abandoned several weapons and ammunition.
r1-UV-2025Q1-032.n: Friday date computed from weekday and the 23 Feb (Sunday) publication date, i.e. 21 Feb; Makanika's death (about 19 Feb) said to be 'two days' earlier. Single local source. Twirwaneho's allegiance to AFC/M23 after Makanika's death is reported by Actualite.cd on 13 Mar (see Rurambo claim).
r1-UV-2025Q1-032.vn: Draft attributed the fall itself to witnesses (the page states it as the outlet's own) and put 'FARDC' into the fighter's quote, which says 'les militaires'. Corrected. The fall of Minembwe is the outlet's narration; witnesses are cited for the positions. The fighter's quote is a party's claim.
src: Le groupement de villages de Minembwe, situé dans le territoire de Fizi, province du Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), est tombé ce vendredi aux mains des combattants du groupe armé Twirwaneho.
Cette prise intervient deux jours après la mort du colonel Makanika, chef militaire de ce groupe composé de membres de la communauté Banyamulenge, tué lors d’une attaque de drone.

r1-UV-2025Q1-033.s: SOS Médias Burundi quoted residents of Minembwe, who came out to celebrate Twirwaneho's capture of the area (which the article, dated 23 February 2025, places 'ce vendredi'), as saying that FARDC soldiers and Maï-Maï militiamen had looted their cows, killed people, stolen from fields and houses and raped their women and girls; the residents gave no dates, places or numbers for these acts, and the article sets them in a context of insecurity it dates to 2017. It said it tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson.
r1-UV-2025Q1-033.a: FARDC soldiers and Maï-Maï militiamen (alleged by residents quoted by SOS Médias Burundi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-033.n: Unverified general allegation by unnamed residents in a context of celebration of one party's capture; no dates, numbers or victims. The article says it tried to reach a FARDC spokesperson (outcome not excerpted).
r1-UV-2025Q1-033.vn: Page supports; FARDC no-comment line supplied. General allegation by unnamed residents celebrating one party's capture; no dates, numbers or victims. SOS Médias Burundi says it tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: capture 'ce vendredi' 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: residents celebrating the capture 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: context of insecurity dated to 2017 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-014: Time slippage: the residents' imperfect-tense accusations are undated and the page frames them within insecurity 'depuis 2017', so they cannot be placed in the 2025 window. Statement now says so and carries the FARDC no-comment; speakers are partisan-adjacent (celebrating one party's capture).; excerpt-support: added 4 excerpt(s): capture 'ce vendredi'; residents celebrating the capture; tried without success to reach a FARDC spokesperson; context of insecurity dated to 2017 | replaced the inferred date 'about 21 February 2025' with the article's own wording ('ce vendredi', article dated 23 February 2025)
src: « Nous sommes heureux, car les militaires des FARDC et les miliciens Maï-Maï pillaient nos vaches, tuaient les gens, volaient dans les champs et les maisons et violaient nos femmes et nos filles », ont témoigné des habitants.

Le groupement de villages de Minembwe, situé dans le territoire de Fizi, province du Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), est tombé ce vendredi aux mains des combattants du groupe armé Twirwaneho.
À Minembwe, plusieurs habitants sont sortis de chez eux pour exprimer leur joie après la prise de la localité.
Nous avons tenté de joindre un porte-parole des FARDC dans la région pour un commentaire, sans succès.
Cette communauté, principalement composée de pasteurs, vit dans une insécurité persistante depuis 2017

r1-UV-2025Q1-034.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the rebels' advance, after their capture of Bukavu and Kamanyola, came as Burundian troops began to withdraw from Congolese soil, after having fought alongside the FARDC and the Wazalendo under bilateral cooperation between the Burundian and Congolese governments.
r1-UV-2025Q1-034.l: Kamanyola / Ruzizi plain towards Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q1-034.n: Burundi has not (in sources found) publicly announced this in the Q1 window beyond a Burundian interior-ministry statement that 100+ Congolese police fled to Burundi from Uvira. Reuters (found only as search results, not fetched) says Burundi withdrew most of its 12,000 troops in February; Burundi/DRC officials confirmed a troop reduction on 25 Feb per Critical Threats (digest, not cited). The Fides piece is a hedged second source in a separate claim.
r1-UV-2025Q1-034.vn: Removed the Fides sentence: Fides is not a source of this claim. 'FDNB' is not printed on the page; removed from actor. Agenzia Fides separately says the Burundian withdrawal 'would have' favoured the advance (claim 4).
src: This advance by the rebels comes as Burundian troops begin to withdraw from the Congolese soil, after having fought alongside the FARDC – the Congolese army and the Wazalendo as part of bilateral cooperation between the Burundian and Congolese governments.

r1-UV-2025Q1-035.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that at least a hundred Congolese police officers had fled to Burundi from Uvira, as announced on Wednesday in Bujumbura by the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs.
r1-UV-2025Q1-035.a: Burundian Ministry of Interior (statement relayed by SOS Médias Burundi)
r1-UV-2025Q1-035.n: Date computed from weekday ('Wednesday') and the 20 Feb publication date, i.e. 19 Feb. Minister is not named on the page. Burundi government statement as relayed, not seen on an official site.
r1-UV-2025Q1-035.vn: Page supports verbatim; minister not named.
ent: Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs
src: At least a hundred Congolese police officers have fled to Burundi from Uvira, the Burundian minister in charge of internal affairs announced Wednesday in the commercial capital Bujumbura.

r1-UV-2025Q1-036.s: BBC News Afrique reported that Wazalendo fighters reportedly wanted to seize the Congolese army's weapons and ammunition, accusing the soldiers of having deserted the front lines and fallen back south to Kalemie. An unnamed source told the BBC that the Wazalendo rose up to oppose the abuses of the regular army and asked the regular troops to give them their weapons, and that about 15 000 Congolese had crossed into Burundi. The BBC said it could not independently verify this information.
r1-UV-2025Q1-036.a: Wazalendo (motive as described by an unnamed source to the BBC)
r1-UV-2025Q1-036.x: unnamed BBC source: about 15 000 Congolese crossed into Burundi
r1-UV-2025Q1-036.n: BBC states it could not verify independently; page is dated by search result (22 Feb) and refers to events on Wednesday (19 Feb). Gives the Wazalendo's side of why they disarmed FARDC soldiers; no Wazalendo spokesperson found speaking directly.
r1-UV-2025Q1-036.vn: The draft put the BBC's own hedged narration ('auraient voulu') in the unnamed source's mouth; split the two and added the BBC's no-verification line, printed on the page. Byline Alfred Lasteck and Ashley Lime, published 22 Feb 2025. Event date approximate.
src: Les combattants Wazalendo auraient voulu s'emparer des armes et des munitions de l'armée congolaise, accusant les soldats d'avoir déserté les lignes de front et de s'être repliés plus au sud, à Kalemie. « Le Wazalendo s'est levé pour s'opposer aux abus de l'armée régulière et a demandé aux troupes régulières de lui donner leurs armes », a déclaré la source, ajoutant qu'environ 15 000 Congolais sont passés au Burundi.

r1-UV-2025Q1-037.s: Human Rights Watch reported that military, humanitarian and other sources expressed concern about the lack of command and control by the Congolese army over the Wazalendo, who in some cases were said to have even disarmed or attacked soldiers.
r1-UV-2025Q1-037.n: Context for the FARDC-Wazalendo clashes in Uvira; not itself an incident claim. HRW also names Justin Bitakwira Bihona Hayi as the National Assembly member coordinating support to Wazalendo in South Kivu and says an armed-group commander complained on 4 April that he was not distributing government funds fully (outside Q1 window; not excerpted).
r1-UV-2025Q1-037.vn: Page supports; HRW's hedge ('auraient') kept as 'were said to have'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Des sources militaires, humanitaires et autres ont exprimé leur inquiétude quant au manque de commandement et de contrôle exercés par l'armée congolaise sur les Wazalendo, qui, dans certains cas, auraient même désarmé ou attaqué des soldats

r1-UV-2025Q2-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing several of its sources, that two groups of Wazalendo militiamen led by self-proclaimed generals René Makanaki and Itongwa (head of the Landa Bango group) fought each other on Saturday 5 April in the Mulongwe commercial centre and its surroundings in Uvira; a local civil society actor said some wounded were taken to the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), and the sources said Néné Rubota, spokesperson of a synergy of Wazalendo armed groups led by General Gashumba, was shot and wounded.
r1-UV-2025Q2-001.l: Mulongwe (commercial centre), Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-001.a: Wazalendo groups of self-proclaimed generals René Makanaki and Itongwa (Landa Bango), as Actualite.cd names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-001.n: Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Report states calm returned the next day. Reasons for the fight per sources quoted: clearance fees and leadership (not in excerpt).
r1-UV-2025Q2-001.vn: All clauses on the retained page; single outlet relaying anonymous sources. The same page also spells the first commander 'Makanika' in a quoted passage; spelling unconfirmed.
src: Deux groupes de miliciens Wazalendo conduits notamment par les généraux autoproclamés René Makanaki et Itongwa, chef du groupe Landa Bango, se sont affrontés la journée du samedi 5 avril à Mulongwe dans le centre commercial et ses environs, selon plusieurs sources d’Actualite.cd.
" Les activités étaient paralysées, perturbées. Il y a quand même quelques blessés amenés à l'HGR d'Uvira ", dit un acteur de la société civile locale.
Ces mêmes sources rajoutent que Néné Rubota porte parole d'une synergie des groupes armés wazalendo dirigé par le général Gashumba a été blessé par balle et a été acheminé à l'HGR d'Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that, for several days, Wazalendo of different groups controlled the city of Uvira, which it described as the provisional capital of South Kivu.
r1-UV-2025Q2-002.a: Wazalendo of different groups, as Actualite.cd says
r1-UV-2025Q2-002.n: Contrast with UN Group of Experts (see GoE claims): Wazalendo de facto control from February; FARDC HQ and governorate re-established in Uvira early March. Excerpt also records two civil society actors denouncing attacks and threats by Wazalendo.
src: Depuis plusieurs jours, ce sont les Wazalendo de différents groupes qui contrôlent la ville d'Uvira. Au moins deux acteurs de la société civile ont dénoncé les attaques et menaces dont ils sont victimes de la part des Wazalendo dans cette capitale provisoire de la province du Sud-Kivu.

r1-UV-2025Q2-003.s: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that from February, as DRC authorities and security actors largely withdrew from Uvira, Wazalendo armed groups took de facto control of Uvira city and its surroundings, used disproportionate force and committed widespread abuses, targeting Banyamulenge communities in particular.
r1-UV-2025Q2-003.l: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-003.a: Wazalendo armed groups, as the Group of Experts names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-003.n: Final report of the Group of Experts; sources cited in its footnote: civil society, FARDC, UN, researchers. Report period extends to its drafting (before 3 July 2025).
r1-UV-2025Q2-003.vn: Statement supported (para. 173); end date corrected to the report's transmission date (page: 'Le présent rapport a été communiqué le 6 mai 2025 au Comité'). The Group's final report (S/2025/446) was transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 and published 3 July 2025; its 'present' is about early May 2025, not June.
src: À partir de février, alors que les autorités de la République démocratique du Congo et les acteurs de la sécurité se sont largement retirés d’Uvira, les groupes armés Wazalendo ont pris le contrôle de facto de la ville d’Uvira et de ses environs
où ils ont eu recours à un usage disproportionné de la force et commis des atteintes généralisées, ciblant en particulier les communautés banyamulenge

r1-UV-2025Q2-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, to restore security, the FARDC headquarters and the South Kivu governorate were relocated to Uvira in early March, and that in early April DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo and former RAD national coordinator General Padiri travelled from Bujumbura to Uvira to appease the Wazalendo groups.
r1-UV-2025Q2-004.a: FARDC; Guy Kabombo; General Padiri; Wazalendo factions
r1-UV-2025Q2-004.n: Adds that the minister travelled from Bujumbura (SOS Médias Burundi also says he came after a stay in Burundi). The Group's text calls Padiri 'ancien coordonnateur national de la RAD', whereas Radio Okapi and SOS Médias Burundi (7-8 April) call him the current national coordinator (Radio Okapi: 'général Padiri Bulenda'; SOS Médias: 'lieutenant général Padiri Bulenda') - discrepancy to surface.
r1-UV-2025Q2-004.vn: Supported (para. 174); date widened because the statement includes the early-March relocation.
src: Dans le but de rétablir la sécurité, le quartier général des FARDC et le gouvernorat du Sud-Kivu ont été réinstallés à Uvira au début du mois de mars.

Début avril, le Ministre de la défense de la République démocratique du Congo, Guy Kabombo, et l’ancien coordonnateur national de la RAD, le général Padiri, se sont rendus de Bujumbura à Uvira pour apaiser les groupes Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q2-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at a meeting, Wazalendo factions complained of lack of support, military logistics and funding, and that to calm them the Defence Minister announced that all Wazalendo leaders would be placed under the authority of the RAD.
r1-UV-2025Q2-005.a: Guy Kabombo (DRC Minister of Defence), as the Group of Experts reports
r1-UV-2025Q2-005.vn: 'in Uvira' removed: the report says only 'Lors d'une réunion' (in the passage on the Uvira visit), not where the meeting was held.
src: Lors d ’une réunion, les factions Wazalendo se sont plaintes du manque de soutien, de logistique militaire et de financement. Pour les calmer, le Ministre a annoncé que tous les dirigeants des Wazalendo seraient placés sous l’autorité de la RAD (voir par. 62).

r1-UV-2025Q2-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that DRC Defence Minister Guy Kabombo announced in Uvira on Monday 7 April that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city depend exclusively from now on on the national coordinator of the Armed Defence Reserve (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.
r1-UV-2025Q2-006.a: Guy Kabombo, DRC Minister of Defence
r1-UV-2025Q2-006.n: The announcement is reported through local civil society, as the page states. Corroborated by UN Group of Experts (para. 174).
r1-UV-2025Q2-006.vn: Radio Okapi attributes the account to local civil society (headline '(société civile)'); attribution kept.
src: Le ministre de la Défense nationale a annoncé, lundi 7 avril à Uvira (Sud-Kivu), que les combattants locaux Wazalendo qui appuient l'armée dans la défense de cette cité, dépendent désormais exclusivement du coordonnateur national de la Réserve armée de la défense (RAD), le général Padiri Bulenda.
Au cours de la rencontre avec les acteurs de la société civile d'Uvira, Guy Kabombo, ministre de la Défense nationale
Le ministre a fait cette annonce au cours d'une rencontre avec diverses couches de la population, notamment des notables de la région et des combattants Wazalendo, rapporte la société civile locale.

r1-UV-2025Q2-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during his visit to Uvira on a Monday (dateline 7 April 2025), Defence Minister Guy Kabombo, accompanied by Lieutenant General Padiri Bulenda (national coordinator of the Wazalendo) and a Burundian army delegation, praised the commitment of the Burundian army, the Burundian National Defence Force (FDNB); SOS Médias Burundi stated in its own narration that the FDNB had deployed nearly 10.000 soldiers in the DRC.
r1-UV-2025Q2-007.l: Uvira (arrival at Kavimvira border), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-007.x: SOS Médias Burundi (own narration, not attributed to the minister): nearly 10.000 FDNB soldiers in the DRC
r1-UV-2025Q2-007.n: SOS Médias Burundi is a Burundian outlet run by journalists in the country and in exile. The figure of about 10,000 is not independently confirmed; the UN Group of Experts (annex) estimates at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu in early April and about 14 battalions (see separate claim).
r1-UV-2025Q2-007.vn: Original attributed the 10.000 figure to Kabombo ('which he said'); the page has it as a relative clause in SOS Médias's narration. The troop figure is the outlet's narration, not a quote from the minister. The UN Group of Experts gives its own, lower estimates for the FDNB deployment (see the FDNB deployment claim from the same unit).
ent: Force de défense nationale du Burundi
src: SOS Médias Burundi Uvira, 7 avril 2025 – Le ministre congolais de la Défense, Guy Kabombo, s’est rendu ce lundi dans la ville d’Uvira,
le ministre était accompagné du lieutenant général Padiri Bulenda, coordinateur national des Wazalendo, et d’une délégation de l’armée burundaise.
Lors de son intervention, le ministre Kabombo a salué l’engagement de l’armée burundaise, la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB), qui a déployé près de 10.000 soldats en RDC.

r1-UV-2025Q2-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), fighters complained that the Burundian army had reportedly forbidden them from attacking M23 positions at Kamanyola, and that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo replied that the restrictions aimed to avoid uncoordinated actions that could compromise joint operations, while reaffirming the Congolese government's confidence in the FDNB.
r1-UV-2025Q2-008.n: Single outlet. Later SOS Médias Burundi (15 May) repeats that Wazalendo accuse some Burundian units of slowing their offensives. No Burundian government statement found (see gaps).
src: SOS Médias Burundi Uvira, 7 avril 2025 – Le ministre congolais de la Défense, Guy Kabombo, s’est rendu ce lundi dans la ville d’Uvira,

Le ton est monté lorsque des combattants ont dénoncé le fait que l’armée burundaise leur aurait interdit d’attaquer les positions du M23 à Kamanyola. Le ministre a répondu que ces restrictions visaient à éviter des actions non coordonnées pouvant compromettre les opérations conjointes, tout en réaffirmant la confiance du gouvernement congolais envers la FDNB.

r1-UV-2025Q2-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that during the Defence Minister's visit to Uvira (dateline 7 April 2025), abuses were reported, notably illegal tax levies at the Kavimvira post, Kalundu port and along the road axes.
r1-UV-2025Q2-009.l: Kavimvira post, Kalundu port, Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-009.n: The source places this within 'tensions internes entre les Wazalendo, les FARDC et la population civile' without naming who levied the taxes. Compare HRW 23 May (Wazalendo roadblock collections in March-April).
r1-UV-2025Q2-009.vn: Unattributed abuses; page does not name who levied the taxes.
src: SOS Médias Burundi Uvira, 7 avril 2025 – Le ministre congolais de la Défense, Guy Kabombo, s’est rendu ce lundi dans la ville d’Uvira,
Des abus ont été signalés, notamment des prélèvements illégaux de taxes aux postes de Kavimvira, du port de Kalundu et le long des axes routiers.

r1-UV-2025Q2-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that the new commander of the 33rd military region, General Dunia, began on Tuesday 8 April the identification of Wazalendo fighters in Uvira, to distinguish genuine from false Wazalendo and give the government a list of those deserving benefits.
r1-UV-2025Q2-010.a: General Dunia, commander of the 33rd military region (as Radio Okapi names him)
r1-UV-2025Q2-010.n: The same page says the command relationship between Wazalendo and FARDC at Uvira had been a serious problem before the minister's visit. SOS Médias Burundi (13 June) names a 'général Alexis Dunia' as a self-proclaimed Wazalendo general; the two may or may not be the same person - not established.
r1-UV-2025Q2-010.vn: Excerpt matches. Not to be confused with the self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'general' Alexis Dunia named in a June 2025 SOS Médias Burundi report.
src: Le nouveau commandant de la 33ᵉ région militaire, le général Dunia, a entamé, mardi 8 avril, l’identification des combattants Wazalendo à Uvira (Sud-Kivu). À travers cette opération, cet officier militaire entend distinguer les vrais des faux Wazalendo afin de fournir au gouvernement la liste de ceux qui méritent les avantages liés à la hiérarchie nationale.

r1-UV-2025Q2-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and Wazalendo exchanged fire from Thursday 24 April at Rugenge and in the heights of Uvira, over occupation of certain positions; sources quoted said the cause was a camp-management dispute.
r1-UV-2025Q2-011.l: Rugenge and the hills above Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-011.a: FARDC and Wazalendo, as Actualite.cd names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-011.n: Two parties' accounts recorded in separate claims (Sukola 2 communiqué; Wazalendo discontent per Radio Okapi/MediaCongo). No casualty figure given in this source.
r1-UV-2025Q2-011.vn: 'occupation of positions' clause is on the page next to the excerpt.
src: Les Forces armées de la RDC et les wazalendo s’échangent des tirs depuis ce jeudi 24 avril à Rugenge et dans les hauteurs d'Uvira (territoire d'Uvira), au Sud-Kivu.
« C'est le problème de la gestion d'un camp. Les FARDC veulent être au-dessus des wazalendo et ces derniers ne supportent pas, c'est ça la cause », disent plusieurs sources.

r1-UV-2025Q2-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that the army described the gunfire as a redeployment of its forces: a communiqué signed by Lieutenant Elongo Kyondwa Marc, spokesperson of the Sukola 2 operational sector, said the shots heard in the hills overlooking Uvira were due to loyalist soldiers redeploying on different ridges to ensure maximum protection of the city.
r1-UV-2025Q2-012.n: Party account (FARDC); contrasts with the account of local sources that FARDC and Wazalendo clashed over positions.
src: « Les coups des balles entendues dans les collines surplombant la ville d'Uvira sont dus à un redéploiement des militaires des forces loyalistes dans différentes crêtes des collines en vue d'assurer une protection maximale de la ville d'uvira », dit un communiqué signé par le lieutenant Elongo Kyondwa Marc, porte-parole du secteur opérationnel sukola 2.

r1-UV-2025Q2-013.s: MediaCongo, relaying Radio Okapi and MCP, reported that on Friday 25 April heavy gunfire between FARDC and Wazalendo shook Uvira again; Sukola 2 Sud-Sud spokesperson Lieutenant Marc Elongo said the fighting was linked to the redeployment of FARDC from Katongo to the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, and that the Wazalendo, displeased, expressed opposition by firing, suspecting this regular army unit of collaborating with rebels in the Fizi Hauts Plateaux.
r1-UV-2025Q2-013.l: Uvira hills; Katongo to Hauts Plateaux of Fizi, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-013.n: Page credits 'MediaCongo Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net'; the original Radio Okapi page was not opened. The page names the spokesperson as lieutenant Marc Elongo; Actualite.cd prints Elongo Kyondwa Marc.
r1-UV-2025Q2-013.vn: Page credits 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net'; independent of the Actualite.cd report of the same days.
src: La ville d’Uvira est de nouveau secouée, ce vendredi 25 avril 2025, par des tirs nourris entre les FARDC et les Wazalendo.

tandis que le porte-parole du secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Sud-Sud, le lieutenant Marc Elongo, appelle la population au calme. Il précise que ces combats sont liés au redéploiement des FARDC de Katongo vers les Hauts plateaux de Fizi.

Les Wazalendo, mécontents de ce mouvement, ont exprimé leur opposition par des coups de feu, soupçonnant cette unité de l’armée régulière de collaborer avec les rebelles dans les Hauts plateaux de Fizi.

r1-UV-2025Q2-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that FARDC and their wazalendo allies clashed again on the morning of Thursday 1 May in two neighbourhoods of Uvira: according to local sources fighting began about 5:00 a.m. at Kasenga and spread to the hills overlooking the city; shooting stopped in the city centre around 10:00 but continued in the surrounding hills. The reasons given by different sources were control and management of certain positions in and around the city.
r1-UV-2025Q2-014.l: Kasenga and Kakombe, hills overlooking Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-014.a: FARDC and wazalendo, as Actualite.cd names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-014.n: Corroborated by Radio Okapi (2 May) and SOS Médias Burundi (2 May).
src: Les Forces armées de la RDC et leurs alliés wazalendo se sont de nouveau affrontés dans la matinée de ce jeudi 1er mai dans deux quartiers de la ville d'Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.
Selon les sources locales, les affrontements ont débuté aux environs de 5h00 du matin à Kasenga avant de s'étendre dans les collines surplombant la ville.
Vers 10h00 locales, les échanges des tirs ont cessé au centre-ville mais se poursuivaient dans les collines entourant la ville d'Uvira.
Les raisons de ces affrontements sont notamment le contrôle et la gestion de certaines positions dans la ville et ses environs, d’après différentes sources.

r1-UV-2025Q2-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that calm returned on Friday 2 May in the communes of Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe in Uvira, 24 hours after fighting between the FARDC and Wazalendo; according to local sources the clash wounded civilians, but the number of victims was not specified.
r1-UV-2025Q2-015.l: Kasenga, Kavimvira and Mulongwe communes, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-015.a: FARDC and Wazalendo, as Radio Okapi names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-015.x: Radio Okapi: civilian wounded, number not specified
r1-UV-2025Q2-015.n: Another outlet (Facebook relays of Actualite.cd/Radio Okapi, not opened) reported 11 dead in two days; no opened page I could fetch carried a death toll - not recorded as a figure.
src: Le calme est revenu ce vendredi 2 mai dans les communes de Kasenga, Kavimvira et Mulongwe, situées dans la ville d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu), 24 heures après les combats entre les Forces armées de la RDC et les combattants Wazalendo.
Selon des sources locales, l’accrochage entre ces deux camps a occasionné des blessés parmi la population civile, mais le nombre de victimes n’a pas été précisé.

r1-UV-2025Q2-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Sud-Sud operations confirmed that the points of divergence had been smoothed out and that the FARDC were securing the city, upstream and downstream, describing a misunderstanding maintained by a small group of Wazalendo.
r1-UV-2025Q2-016.n: Party account (FARDC); names not printed by the page.
src: Le porte-parole des opérations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud confirme que les points de divergence ont été aplanis et que les FARDC assurent la sécurité de la ville, en amont comme en aval. Il évoque un malentendu qui était entretenu par un petit groupe de Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q2-017.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the South Kivu provincial administration continued to publicly deny any clash between FARDC and Wazalendo in the Uvira region, that it had received no official statement from the local FARDC command despite repeated attempts to contact it, and, citing several local testimonies, that the hostilities were triggered by an FARDC attempt to install new military positions at Kituntu, about ten kilometres from Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q2-017.l: Kasenga and Kakombe hills, Kituntu, Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-017.a: South Kivu provincial administration; FARDC; Wazalendo
r1-UV-2025Q2-017.n: Provincial denial reported by an outlet; Actualite.cd and Radio Okapi independently report the clashes. Page lead says 'Malgré les dénégations des autorités provinciales'. SOS Médias dateline is Bukavu although the report concerns Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q2-017.vn: Conditional 'auraient été déclenchées' kept via 'citing testimonies'.
src: Pourtant, l’administration provinciale du Sud-Kivu continue de nier publiquement l’existence de tout affrontement entre les FARDC et les Wazalendo dans la région d’Uvira.
À l’heure où nous publions cet article, aucune déclaration officielle n’a été émise par le commandement local des FARDC, malgré nos multiples tentatives de contact.

D’après plusieurs témoignages recueillis sur place, les hostilités auraient été déclenchées par une tentative des FARDC d’installer de nouvelles positions militaires à Kituntu, une localité située à une dizaine de kilomètres d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q2-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that fighting broke out between Wazalendo and AFC/M23 rebels in the territories of Uvira and Walungu, with the agglomerations of Katogota and Kamanyola in a spiral of violence since Monday 5 May; according to local sources the Wazalendo launched a surprise attack first on forward M23 positions, the clashes lasted eight hours on the hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, civilians were wounded, and both sides suffered losses according to a human rights activist.
r1-UV-2025Q2-018.l: Katogota, Kamanyola, hills of Rutebe, Kayange and Luzinzi, Ruzizi plain (Uvira/Walungu border), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-018.a: Wazalendo; AFC/M23, as Radio Okapi names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-018.n: No AFC/M23 account of this clash found (see gaps).
src: Des combats ont éclaté entre les combattants Wazalendo et les rebelles du M23 dans les territoires d’Uvira et de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu. Depuis lundi 5 mai, les agglomérations de Katogota et Kamanyola, situées entre ces deux territoires, sont plongées dans une spirale de violences.
Selon des sources locales, les Wazalendo ont lancé en premier une attaque surprise contre plusieurs positions avancées des rebelles de l’AFC-M23.
Les affrontements se sont intensifiés sur les collines de Rutebe, Kayange et Luzinzi, où les hostilités ont duré huit heures.
Des blessés ont été enregistrés parmi les civils, tandis que les deux camps ont également subi des pertes humaines, selon un activiste des droits de l’homme présent dans la plaine de la Ruzizi.

r1-UV-2025Q2-019.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on the Wednesday before its publication the FARDC chief of staff, Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe, and his Burundian counterpart, General Prime Niyongabo, head of the FDNB, crossed the border at Kavimvira escorted by a large Burundian military contingent and headed to the 'Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu' operational sector, where they held a closed meeting; they left around 16:50 for Bujumbura without a statement to the press.
r1-UV-2025Q2-019.l: Uvira (Kavimvira crossing, Sokola 2 Sud operational sector), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-019.n: Date computed from weekday ('ce mercredi') and publication date 15 May; a lapresseafricaine.net snippet (not opened) gives 14 May. Section 'Selon des sources sécuritaires locales' speculation about drones is not recorded. No official statement on the meeting found.
r1-UV-2025Q2-019.vn: Sources 0 and 1 carry the same excerpt; both fine.
src: les chefs d’état-major congolais et burundais se sont rencontrés ce mercredi à Uvira.

Elle a réuni le chef d’état-major des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC), le lieutenant-général Jules Banza Mwilambwe, et son homologue burundais, le général Prime Niyongabo, à la tête de la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB).
Les deux officiers supérieurs, escortés par un important dispositif militaire burundais, ont franchi la frontière à Kavimvira avant de se diriger vers le secteur opérationnel Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu.

Vers 16h50, les deux généraux ont quitté Uvira en direction de Bujumbura sans faire de déclaration à la presse, laissant planer un voile d’incertitude sur les décisions prises au cours de cette rencontre discrète mais cruciale.

r1-UV-2025Q2-020.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that tensions between FARDC, Wazalendo militias and Burundian troops were worsening notably in the Katogota and Kamanyola areas, and that Wazalendo militiamen accuse certain Burundian units of slowing their offensives against the M23.
r1-UV-2025Q2-020.l: Katogota and Kamanyola areas, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-020.n: Allegation by Wazalendo as reported; no Burundian response found.
src: Cette rencontre intervient alors que les tensions entre les FARDC, les milices Wazalendo et les troupes burundaises ne cessent de s’exacerber, notamment dans les zones de Katogota et Kamanyola. Les miliciens Wazalendo accusent certaines unités burundaises de freiner leurs offensives contre le M23

r1-UV-2025Q2-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early April 2025 approximately 14 FDNB battalions under the 'Task Force Congo' (TAFOC) umbrella were still on DRC territory, of which 10 were reportedly in the Ruzizi Plain, two in and around Uvira and two in the Hauts Plateaux near Minembwe, and that FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated at least 7,000 troops in South Kivu.
r1-UV-2025Q2-021.l: Ruzizi Plain, Uvira and Hauts Plateaux (near Minembwe), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-021.x: UN Group of Experts: approximately 14 FDNB battalions; at least 7,000 troops estimated in South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-021.n: From the English-language annex text embedded in the French PDF. The Group says deployed battalions were probably not fully constituted (650 soldiers per organic battalion).
r1-UV-2025Q2-021.vn: Annex 72 text matches. The same report elsewhere gives 7 000 to 9 000 Burundian soldiers, most in South Kivu, in early April; SOS Médias Burundi gives nearly 10.000.
src: Early April 2025, approximately 14 FDNB battalions operating under the “Task Force Congo” (or “TAFOC”) umbrella were still present on DRC territory (S/2024/432, annex 53). While 10 TAFOC battalions were reportedly deployed in the Ruzizi Plain, two were deployed in and around Uvira, and two others in the Hauts Plateaux, close to Minembwe.
However, FARDC, FDNB and intelligence sources estimated that early April 2025, at least 7,000 troops were deployed in South Kivu.

r1-UV-2025Q2-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its final report, the AFC/M23 controlled mining areas in Kalehe, Walungu and Mwenga territories as far as Kamanyola in the south, while the FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo kept control of the Ruzizi plain and held positions along the Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira road, blocking the AFC/M23 advance towards Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q2-022.l: Kamanyola - Sange - Uvira road, Ruzizi plain, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-022.a: AFC/M23 (with RDF per the Group); FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo
r1-UV-2025Q2-022.n: Exact date of the situation is 'at the time of the report'; the report was dated 3 July 2025, so mid-2025 is approximate. Sources cited by the Group: FARDC, AFC/M23, civil society, UN, intelligence services, researchers.
r1-UV-2025Q2-022.vn: Date corrected from June to the report's reference time (transmitted 6 May 2025). 'At the time of the report': the report was transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 (published 3 July 2025).
src: À l’heure de l’établissement du présent rapport, la rébellion contrôlait des zones minières riches en minerais dans les territoires de Kalehe, Walungu et Mwenga, jusqu’à Kamanyola dans le sud

En revanche, les FARDC, la FDNB et les Wazalendo ont gardé le contrôle de la plaine de la Ruzizi et tenu des positions le long de la route Kamanyola-Sange-Uvira, bloquant la marche des AFC/M23 vers Uvira

r1-UV-2025Q2-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, at the time of its report, relations between FARDC and Wazalendo had improved and some Wazalendo groups had left the centre of Uvira at the request of FARDC command.
r1-UV-2025Q2-023.n: The sentence is split across a page break in the PDF text ('relations entre les FARDC et les ... [footnotes] ... Wazalendo s’étaient améliorées'); the excerpt begins after the footnote block. 'At the date of drawing up this report' per the Group.
r1-UV-2025Q2-023.vn: Date corrected from June to the report's reference time. 'At the time of the report': transmitted to the Sanctions Committee on 6 May 2025 (published 3 July 2025).
src: Wazalendo s’étaient améliorées et certains groupes Wazalendo avaient quitté le centre d’Uvira à la demande du commandement des FARDC 201.

r1-UV-2025Q2-024.s: Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Pulusi returned to Uvira, the provisional capital of the province, on Tuesday 20 May after four months' absence, and, in an address to residents, said he carried a message from the head of state announcing the 'beginning of the end' of the M23 war; a local civil society actor said that for them the end of the war means the withdrawal of the rebels from occupied territories, among other things.
r1-UV-2025Q2-024.n: Name spelling varies on the page and in the URL ('Pulusi' vs 'Purusi'); other outlets print 'Purusi'. The same page says some inhabitants were sceptical.
r1-UV-2025Q2-024.vn: Matches. Radio Okapi spells the name 'Pulusi' in the text and 'Purusi' in the headline and tags.
src: Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Pulusi, est revenu à Uvira, chef-lieu provisoire de la province, mardi 20 mai, après une absence de quatre mois.
Dès l'entame de son allocution devant les habitants d'Uvira, le gouverneur a déclaré qu’il portait un message du chef de l’État, annonçant le « début de la fin » de la guerre du M23.

Un acteur de la société civile locale a déclaré : « Pour nous, la fin de la guerre signifie la cessation des bruits des bottes, le retrait des rebelles des territoires occupés et la reprise des activités socio-économiques ».

r1-UV-2025Q2-025.s: Human Rights Watch said that in April it received credible information of Wazalendo fighters beating and whipping men and women they accused of having acted inappropriately, and quoted an Uvira resident as saying that some Wazalendo act as if they were the police.
r1-UV-2025Q2-025.l: South Kivu (resident quoted is from Uvira)
r1-UV-2025Q2-025.a: Wazalendo fighters, as Human Rights Watch names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-025.n: HRW does not state in these sentences that the April beatings took place in Uvira; the Uvira quotation is a resident's general remark. Treat the location as South Kivu. Other incidents in the same HRW release (Mulongwe 14 February; Sange 3 March; Bibokoboko 3 March) fall before the 1 April start of this unit and were not recorded here.
r1-UV-2025Q2-025.vn: Location of the April beatings not given by HRW beyond South Kivu context.
src: En avril, Human Rights Watch a reçu des informations crédibles faisant état de combattants Wazalendo battant et fouettant des hommes et des femmes qu'ils accusaient d'avoir agi de façon inappropriée.
« Certains Wazalendo agissent comme s'ils étaient la police et pensent qu'ils peuvent résoudre les conflits entre civils », a déclaré un habitant d'Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.

r1-UV-2025Q2-026.s: Human Rights Watch reported that South Kivu's interim governor, Jean-Jacques Elakano, told media on 23 April that the province could not collect taxes because of Wazalendo fighters, who should not 'substitute for the State'; HRW also reported that in March and April Wazalendo set up roadblocks on main roads linking several South Kivu towns, where they harassed residents and collected 500 to 1 000 Congolese francs per person.
r1-UV-2025Q2-026.x: Human Rights Watch: 500 to 1 000 Congolese francs per person at Wazalendo roadblocks
r1-UV-2025Q2-026.n: Discrepancy to surface: HRW calls Elakano 'gouverneur intérimaire'; the elected-appointed governor Jean-Jacques Purusi/Pulusi was reported by Radio Okapi (21 May) to have been absent from Uvira for four months, returning 20 May. HRW's roadblock sentence does not name Uvira.
src: Le gouverneur intérimaire du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, a déclaré aux médias le 23 avril que la province n'était pas en mesure de collecter des impôts à cause des combattants Wazalendo, qui ne devraient « pas se substituer à l'État ».

En mars et avril, des combattants Wazalendo ont mis en place des barrages routiers sur les routes principales reliant plusieurs villes du Sud-Kivu, où ils ont harcelé les habitants et collecté entre 500 et 1 000 francs congolais (entre 0,17 et 0,34 dollars US) par personne.

r1-UV-2025Q2-027.s: Imurenge.com, a Banyamulenge community website, reported that, since February 2025, reports indicate that over 40 Banyamulenge individuals in Uvira had been assaulted and robbed, one young man killed and a woman seriously injured, and that Wazalendo militias were preventing many Banyamulenge from returning to work at Kalundu port and the Kavimvira border post.
r1-UV-2025Q2-027.l: Uvira city (Kalundu port, Kavimvira border post), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-027.a: Wazalendo militias, as Imurenge.com names them
r1-UV-2025Q2-027.x: Imurenge.com: over 40 Banyamulenge assaulted; one young man killed; one woman seriously injured
r1-UV-2025Q2-027.n: Community website; 'reports indicate' is not attributed to a named monitor. Corroborated in general terms by UN Group of Experts (para. 173) and HRW (23 May). The killing and injury may overlap with incidents HRW dates to February; not independently established. Page says the 'Uvira Security Committee' issued directives, but its members were not named.
r1-UV-2025Q2-027.vn: Attributed as the site's account. The same page describes two individual incidents of 17 April in Uvira with two named persons (an abduction near Maendeleo port and a seizure/robbery in Gasenga); not captured as claims; lead for a gap round. Imurenge.com is a Banyamulenge community website (an interested party); figures are its own and unsourced ('reports indicate').
src: Since February 2025, reports indicate that over 40 Banyamulenge individuals in Uvira have been assaulted. Victims have been robbed of their phones, money, clothing, and other personal items. One young man was killed, and a woman was seriously injured during these attacks.

Even as peace returns for others, many Banyamulenge residents remain blocked from returning to their jobs, particularly at the Kalundu port and the Kavimvira border post. These areas once provided stable income for hundreds, but Wazalendo militias are preventing their return.

The Uvira Security Committee has held meetings and issued directives urging an end to the harassment of Banyamulenge citizens. However, many community members say these statements have yet to be followed by real protection or enforcement.

r1-UV-2025Q2-028.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several local sources, that Banyamulenge police officers, teachers and women travelling towards Bijombo in Uvira territory were arrested, tortured and stripped of their belongings by Wazalendo elements on Wednesday 11 June 2025 (date per the photo caption), the victims including seven police officers, four teachers and two women; the victims said they were intercepted by men of the self-proclaimed generals Landabango and Alexis Dunia while on the road to Bijombo under escort of Burundian soldiers, and the Wazalendo reportedly then arrested them, accusing them of belonging to the M23. The outlet reported that police officers and teachers were freed through the intervention of the deputy mayor of the city of Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q2-028.l: Road to Bijombo, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-028.a: Wazalendo of self-proclaimed generals Landabango and Alexis Dunia, as the victims say
r1-UV-2025Q2-028.x: SOS Médias Burundi: seven police officers, four teachers, two women
r1-UV-2025Q2-028.n: Single outlet relaying local sources and victims' statements; no named victims. Open letter to the governor by local organisations including CEPCC is reported on the same page. The article's headline and dateline say Bukavu, while the events concern Uvira territory. The 'ce mercredi' in the text and the photo caption date (11 June 2025) agree. No Wazalendo or FARDC response found. The 'général Alexis Dunia' named here may be distinct from the FARDC 33rd military region commander General Dunia (Radio Okapi, 9 April) - not established.
r1-UV-2025Q2-028.vn: Conditional 'auraient arrêtés' restored; release narrowed to police officers and teachers as the page says; date anchored to the caption; territory is Uvira territory, not the city. An open letter from local organisations including CEPCC, quoted by the outlet, places the incident between the Bavira chiefdom and a Wazalendo camp led by 'general Dunia'. The self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'general' Alexis Dunia is not the FARDC 33rd military region commander General Dunia.
ent: maire adjoint de la ville d'Uvira
src: Des policiers, des enseignants et des femmes Banyamulenge, en déplacement vers Bijombo, ont été arrêtés, torturés et dépouillés par des éléments des Wazalendo, selon plusieurs sources locales. Parmi les victimes figurent sept policiers, quatre enseignants et deux femmes.
Ils affirment avoir été interceptés par les hommes des généraux autoproclamés Landabango et Alexis Dunia, alors qu’ils étaient en route vers Bijombo sous escorte de soldats burundais.
Les Wazalendo les auraient ensuite arrêtés, accusés d’appartenir au M23.
un policier issu de la communauté Banyamulenge blessé à la tête par des miliciens Wazalendo, dans le territoire d’Uvira (RD Congo), le mercredi 11 juin 2025

Des policiers et enseignants Banyamulenge, visiblement traumatisés, ont pu être libérés grâce à l’intervention du maire adjoint de la ville d’Uvira. Ils ont pu regagner leurs familles ce mercredi soir.

r1-UV-2025Q2-029.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that more and more young Burundians were joining Wazalendo militias in Uvira territory, with testimonies in the neighbourhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi and Kiliba, and that some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps or the Sange transit centre had also been seen in Wazalendo ranks; it also cited regional security sources saying nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers, supported by Imbonerakure, were officially in the DRC.
r1-UV-2025Q2-029.l: Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi, Kiliba (Uvira territory); Mulongwe and Lusenda camps; Sange transit centre, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-029.x: SOS Médias Burundi: nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers (regional security sources)
r1-UV-2025Q2-029.n: Recruitment is described by the source as driven by promises of pay, not as coerced; recorded as unit/actor context, not as forced recruitment. A National Refugee Commission agent in Baraka is quoted as saying refugees have had no assistance for over five months. Unverified; no Burundian government response found.
r1-UV-2025Q2-029.vn: English edition of SOS Médias Burundi, dateline 24 May 2025; locations are in Uvira territory, not only the city.
src: More and more young Burundians are joining these militias in the Uvira territory, abandoning their daily activities—agriculture, commerce, motorcycle taxis, or hairdressing—seduced by promises of remuneration and a better future.

In the neighborhoods of Kasenga, Kavimvira, Kilibula, Kawizi, and Kiliba, testimonies are multiplying. Some refugees from the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps, or the Sange transit center, have also been seen in the ranks of the Wazalendo.
According to regional security sources, nearly 10,000 Burundian soldiers—supported by members of the ruling party’s youth league, the Imbonerakure—are officially present in the DRC.

r1-UV-2025Q2-030.s: MSF said that since February, in collaboration with the health ministry, it had treated nearly 400 war-wounded and 800 cholera cases in three dedicated treatment centres in South Kivu, and that Uvira was hosting more than 250 000 displaced people since the start of the fighting.
r1-UV-2025Q2-030.l: Uvira and Ruzizi health zones, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-030.x: MSF: nearly 400 war-wounded and 800 cholera cases treated since February; Uvira hosting more than 250 000 displaced people
r1-UV-2025Q2-030.n: Treatment figures cover three centres, not only Uvira (Actualite.cd's relay of the MSF release places them in the Uvira and Ruzizi health zones). The '2' in 'personnes2' in the displaced-persons excerpt is a footnote marker in the page text. MSF has been present in Uvira since September 2024 for a mpox response (same page).
r1-UV-2025Q2-030.vn: Matches. The same MSF page reports gunfire inside a hospital and medical facilities hit in Uvira in February 2025 (outside this unit's window). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Depuis février, MSF a traité, en collaboration avec le ministère de la santé, près de 400 blessés de guerre et 800 cas de choléra dans trois centres de traitement spécifiques.
Depuis le début des affrontements dans la région, Uvira abrite plus de 250 000 personnes2 déplacées
Dans la ville d'Uvira, les acteurs humanitaires estiment que plus de 554 000 personnes ont été affectées par la crise, dont 270 000 déplacés internes.
