r1-UV-2025Q2-031.s: MSF said that persistent insecurity had made the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira almost impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the front line, and MSF reported adapting by crossing different countries to bring aid and provide care on each side.
r1-UV-2025Q2-031.l: Bukavu - Kamanyola - Uvira road, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q2-031.n: Date is the publication date; the access constraint is described as ongoing. MSF does not attribute the insecurity to a party.
src: L’insécurité persistante a rendu la route entre Bukavu, Kamanyola et Uvira quasiment infranchissable, rendant impossible la circulation des organisations humanitaires entre les deux côtés de la ligne de front. Pour surmonter cette situation, MSF s'est adapté en traversant différents pays pour acheminer l’aide et fournir des soins de chaque côté.

r1-UV-2025Q2-032.s: MSF's medical lead in Uvira, Dr Aurora Revuelta, said MSF had intensified its response to strengthen capacity to care for war wounds, cholera cases and victims and survivors of sexual violence.
r1-UV-2025Q2-032.x: not stated by the source (no count of sexual violence cases given)
r1-UV-2025Q2-032.n: Records MSF's statement on care provision only; the page gives no incident, date or perpetrator for any sexual violence.
r1-UV-2025Q2-032.vn: Matches. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: “C’est dans ce contexte que nous avons intensifié notre réponse pour renforcer les capacités de prises en charge des blessures de guerre, de cas de choléra, et des victimes et survivantes de violences sexuelles“ explique Dr Aurora Revuelta, responsable médicale MSF à Uvira.

«Nous avons intensifié notre réponse pour prendre en charge les blessures de guerre, les cas de choléra et les violences sexuelles», précise la Dr Aurora Revuelta, responsable médicale de MSF à Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q2-033.s: MSF said that Kamanyola, close to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and had also seen its health system weakened by violence, and that while some stability had been restored in the town, most fighting continued in the surrounding hills, making access to fields impossible.
r1-UV-2025Q2-033.n: Consistent with the UN Group of Experts (Kamanyola as the southern limit of AFC/M23 control).
r1-UV-2025Q2-033.vn: Original implied M23/AFC control weakened the health system; MSF says the health system was weakened 'by violence'.
src: Cette localité, sous contrôle du M23/AFC, a également vu son système de santé fragilisé par la violence.

Alors qu’une certaine stabilité a été rétablie en ville, permettant à une partie de la communauté de revenir, la plupart des combats continuent de se dérouler dans les collines aux alentours, rendant l’accès aux champs impossible

r1-UV-2025Q2-034.s: Actualite.cd reported that the UN Deputy Special Representative and Humanitarian Coordinator Bruno Lemarquis, in Uvira since 28 June, said the UN was there to assess security for the physical return of UN agencies to South Kivu, to study humanitarian access and the mechanisms for opening a humanitarian corridor, and to consider support to the provincial institutions provisionally installed in Uvira.
src: Le Représentant Spécial adjoint du Secrétaire Général des Nations Unies, Coordonnateur résident des Nations Unies et Coordonnateur des opérations humanitaires en République Démocratique du Congo, Bruno Lemarquis séjourne depuis la journée du 28 Juin à Uvira dans la province du Sud-Kivu
Nous sommes ici pour 3 questions importantes à savoir : la question sécuritaire dans la province du Sud-Kivu pour envisager le retour physique des agences du système des Nations Unies
Nous venons aussi pour étudier l'accès humanitaire car, il faut des mécanismes pour l'ouverture d'un couloir humanitaire.
Enfin, avec l'installation provisoire des institutions dans la ville d'Uvira, nous envisageons un appui aux institutions provinciales.

r1-UV-2025Q2-035.s: Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, based in Uvira since the fall of Bukavu to the M23, said Lemarquis's visit proved that peace, stability and security were returning, and that the authorities would do everything to eradicate the multiple barriers erected in places to facilitate the opening of a humanitarian corridor so that the population, including in areas occupied by the 'aggressors', could receive medicines, food and other assistance.
r1-UV-2025Q2-035.a: Governor Jean Jacques Purusi (DRC provincial government)
r1-UV-2025Q2-035.n: Party statement (DRC provincial government). Second quotation: the page attributes it to the governor ("a indiqué le gouverneur Jean Jacques Purusi").
src: Le Représentant Spécial adjoint du Secrétaire Général des Nations Unies, Coordonnateur résident des Nations Unies et Coordonnateur des opérations humanitaires en République Démocratique du Congo, Bruno Lemarquis séjourne depuis la journée du 28 Juin à Uvira dans la province du Sud-Kivu

Reçu par le gouverneur Jean Jacques Purusi basé actuellement à Uvira après la prise de la ville de Bukavu par les M23, Purusi a indiqué que cette visite est une preuve que la paix, la stabilité et la sécurité reviennent dans cette partie.

Nous allons tout faire pour éradiquer les multiples barrières érigées par-ci par-là pour faciliter l'ouverture d'un couloir humanitaire afin que la population, même se trouvant dans les zones occupées par les agresseurs, bénéficie de l'aide en médicaments, vivre et autres assistances

r1-UV-2025Q3-001.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a 17-minute audio message broadcast on 19 July, General Makanaki (Makanaki Kasimbira John, described by the outlet as an influential Wazalendo figure) said that any truck coming from Bukavu must be burned by the Wazalendo and would not pass the Luvingi bridge, saying 'These are the trucks that bring the M23'; the outlet described the convoy as 55 trucks of food and medicine for displaced people in Uvira, and South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi had said an agreement had been reached between all parties concerned.
r1-UV-2025Q3-001.l: Luvungi bridge on the Bukavu-Uvira route (Luvingi), Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-001.a: General Makanaki Kasimbira John (described by the source as an influential Wazalendo figure)
r1-UV-2025Q3-001.n: Threat to burn convoy, not a reported attack; the source says 55 trucks of food and medicine. Whether the convoy was ultimately blocked is not stated in the excerpts. SOS Médias Burundi (24 Jul) separately says a humanitarian corridor Bukavu-Uvira was blocked (not cited here). The 55-truck figure is on the page but outside the excerpts.
r1-UV-2025Q3-001.vn: Page (SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu dateline 21 July 2025) states every clause; the Purusi and 'food and medicine' clauses come from the page body, supplied as replacement quotes. Makanaki's statement is known from an audio message as reported by SOS Médias Burundi; the audio itself was not retrieved. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 55 trucks; Makanaki Kasimbira John, influential Wazalendo figure 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: agreement between all parties concerned 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-017: Read the retained page: every clause is supported, and 'he stated' in source 1 is Governor Purusi. But the statement leaves out the reason Makanaki gave in the same quote ('These are the trucks that bring the M23') and the size of the convoy (55 trucks), both on the page; the strongest true version gives his stated reason, attributed to him. The threat is known only from SOS Médias Burundi's account of an audio not retrieved.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): 55 trucks; Makanaki Kasimbira John, influential Wazalendo figure; agreement between all parties concerned
src: In a 17-minute audio message broadcast on July 19, General Makanaki expressed firm opposition to humanitarian convoys from Bukavu. “We do not want any trucks coming from Bukavu to Uvira. I, Makanaki, warlord, say that any truck coming from Bukavu must be burned by the Wazalendo. It will not pass the Luvingi bridge. These are the trucks that bring the M23,” he declared.
“These trucks are carrying medicine and food to help our population, and everything will be unloaded in the presence of the population, the security services, and the Wazalendo,” he stated.

While 55 trucks loaded with food and medicine are being delivered to the displaced people living in Uvira, a bitter disagreement is raging between the Governor of South Kivu, Jean Jacques Purusi, and General Makanaki Kasimbira John, an influential Wazalendo figure in the region.
Governor Purusi declared last weekend that an agreement had been reached between all parties concerned

r1-UV-2025Q3-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that Médecins sans frontières announced in a communiqué of Friday 25 July the end of its mission in Uvira from the end of July 2025, ending care for new war-wounded patients and cholera patients at the Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira; MSF cited the attainment of the medical objectives set when the project began in November 2024.
r1-UV-2025Q3-002.l: Hôpital général de référence d'Uvira, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-002.n: MSF's stated reason is that objectives were met (fewer gunshot cases); the source does not link it to insecurity. Recorded because it changes civilian access to trauma and cholera care in Uvira. Ben Taleb Zied (MSF project coordinator) named on the page but not in excerpts.
r1-UV-2025Q3-002.vn: Supported by the Radio Okapi page; the excerpt_en flag is the expansion 'Uvira General Reference Hospital', a faithful translation.
src: Dans un communiqué rendu public vendredi 25 juillet, MSF précise que cette décision entraîne l’arrêt de la prise en charge des nouveaux cas de blessés de guerre ainsi que des patients atteints de choléra à l’Hôpital général de référence d’Uvira.
L’organisation humanitaire justifie ce retrait par l’atteinte des objectifs médicaux fixés lors du lancement du projet, en novembre 2024.

r1-UV-2025Q3-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on the previous Sunday, the M23-AFC coalition denounced the reinforcement of government troops on several axes, notably Shabunda, Uvira and Kalemie, and accused the Congolese authorities of violating the ceasefire.
r1-UV-2025Q3-003.l: Uvira, Shabunda, Kalemie (as named in the communiqué)
r1-UV-2025Q3-003.n: Date computed from 'dimanche dernier' and publication date 2025-08-12 (Tuesday), i.e. Sunday 2025-08-10. The communiqué itself was not opened; Radio Okapi relays it. A party statement, evidence of what AFC/M23 said only.
r1-UV-2025Q3-003.vn: Excerpt carries the statement exactly; partisan origin, so C. Party statement (AFC/M23) as relayed by Radio Okapi; the communiqué itself was not retrieved. 'Previous Sunday' relative to an article of Tuesday 12 August 2025.
src: Dans un communiqué publié dimanche dernier, la coalition M23–AFC a dénoncé le renforcement des troupes gouvernementales sur plusieurs axes, notamment à Shabunda, Uvira et Kalemie. Elle accuse les autorités congolaises de violer les termes du cessez-le-feu en vigueur.

r1-UV-2025Q3-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that on the southern axis the FARDC and Wazalendo control a large portion of the Ruzizi plain beyond the city of Uvira, while the rebels keep their hold on the Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis and on certain localities of the Ruzizi plain chiefdom; according to concordant sources cited by Radio Okapi, the rebel coalition's troops were redeploying with heavy equipment towards the Walungu and Uvira axes to consolidate their positions.
r1-UV-2025Q3-004.l: Ruzizi plain beyond Uvira; Nyangezi–Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-004.n: Single outlet, 'sources locales'; the page gives no precise localities for the Ruzizi plain split. The M23 move is described as 'since the weekend' (9-10 Aug).
r1-UV-2025Q3-004.vn: Attribution fixed: on the page 'concordant sources' carries only the redeployment; the Ruzizi control picture is Radio Okapi's own narration. Single outlet for a frontline picture: C.
src: Les FARDC et les Wazalendo contrôlent une large portion de la plaine de la Ruzizi, au-delà de la ville d’Uvira. Les rebelles conservent leur emprise sur l’axe Nyangezi–Kamanyola et sur certaines localités relevant de la chefferie de la plaine de la Ruzizi.
Elles se redéploient avec des équipements lourds vers les axes Walungu et Uvira, dans le but de consolider leurs dispositifs militaires.

r1-UV-2025Q3-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that a FARDC soldier was shot dead and several civilians were wounded after an altercation on Monday 25 August between the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters at Mulongwe, Uvira territory; according to local sources it was triggered by a dispute over the control of vehicles carrying people from Burundi who had come for the burial of a colonel, and the Sokola 2 South Kivu spokesperson said the soldier was hit by a stray bullet while protecting the convoy.
r1-UV-2025Q3-005.n: Perpetrator disputed: local sources point to a Wazalendo-FARDC altercation, the military spokesperson says stray bullet. Number of civilians wounded not given. Overlaps with SOS Médias Burundi's account of the 26 Aug clashes (separate claim). The colonel's burial: Radio Okapi (3 Sep) names 'colonel Patrick'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-005.vn: All clauses on the page; the 'stray bullet' is the spokesperson's conditional account ('aurait été atteint') and is attributed. Radio Okapi (3 September) later gave a toll of at least five Wazalendo killed and fourteen arrested for the 25 August clashes (see claim 7); the tolls differ. 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-017: Attribution is fine (stray bullet kept as the spokesperson's conditional account), but the grade overstates independence: the three 'origins' are one Radio Okapi article (its own reporting, unnamed local sources, and the FARDC Sokola 2 spokesperson, a party). Radio Okapi's own 3 September report of the same 25 August clashes gives a different toll (at least five Wazalendo killed, fourteen arrested, per military authorities: r1-UV-2025Q3-008), which this statement does not mention. One article with a party confirmation and a conflicting later toll fits C, like the companion claim.
src: Un soldat des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) a été abattu et plusieurs civils blessés à la suite d’une altercation survenue ce lundi 25 août entre les forces armées de la RDC et les combattants Wazalendo, à Mulongwe, dans le territoire d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu).
Selon des sources locales, l’incident aurait été déclenché par une dispute liée au contrôle de véhicules transportant des individus en provenance du Burundi.
Le porte-parole de l’opération Sokola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu a confirmé l’incident, précisant que le militaire décédé aurait été atteint par une balle perdue alors qu’il assurait la protection du convoi.

r1-UV-2025Q3-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Tuesday the border town of Uvira saw violent clashes between the FARDC and the local Wazalendo militias, concentrated in the Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters; bodies of both sides were lying along the road linking Kasenga to Kavimvira.
r1-UV-2025Q3-006.l: Kavimvira and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-006.n: Date computed from 'mardi' and the page's photo caption (Tuesday 26 August 2025). Single (Burundian) outlet reporting from Bukavu; no casualty figure. Source says violence 'auraient éclaté' after Wazalendo tried to deploy at the Kavimvira border and a tax directorate warehouse.
r1-UV-2025Q3-006.vn: Supported; single outlet. The page's photo caption dates the clashes to Tuesday 26 August 2025; no body count is given.
src: la ville frontalière d’Uvira a été le théâtre, mardi, de violents affrontements entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et les milices locales Wazalendo. Les combats, concentrés dans les quartiers de Kavimvira et Kasenga, ont paralysé toute activité
Mardi, plusieurs corps des deux camps gisaient le long de la route reliant Kasenga à Kavimvira.

r1-UV-2025Q3-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the spokesperson of the South Kivu provincial government, Luganywa Bashizi Didier Kabi, relayed the position of governor Jean Jacques Purusi, who condemned the oral and physical violence of the previous two days in certain quarters of Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q3-007.n: Statement date is the publication date; no exact day given by the source.
r1-UV-2025Q3-007.vn: Excerpt carries the full statement; names printed on the page. Official statement verbatim: B.
src: Le porte-parole du gouvernement provincial, Luganywa Bashizi Didier Kabi, a relayé la position du gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean Jacques Purusi : « Le gouverneur condamne avec la plus grande fermeté les violences orales et physiques survenues ces deux derniers jours dans certains quartiers d’Uvira, entre des frères et sœurs d’une même famille, pour des raisons inavouées. »

r1-UV-2025Q3-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo and the army had clashed on 25 August over the arrival of a delegation from Burundi for the funeral of colonel Patrick, who had recently died, and that, according to the military authorities, these clashes caused the death of at least five Wazalendo fighters and the arrest of fourteen others.
r1-UV-2025Q3-008.x: Radio Okapi citing military authorities: at least 5 Wazalendo killed, 14 arrested
r1-UV-2025Q3-008.n: Single-source military figure; the page does not say the deaths and arrests all occurred on 25 August ('ces accrochages' covers the days since). SOS Médias Burundi (27 Aug) links to an article titled 'l’inhumation du Colonel Patrick Gisore interrompue par les Wazalendo' (not opened). Names detainees: none.
r1-UV-2025Q3-008.vn: 'Ces groupes' on the page are the Wazalendo and FARDC, who clashed with each other; the draft read it as the Wazalendo alone opposing the arrival. Narrowed to the page's reading. Toll is the military authorities' figure. Radio Okapi's 26 August report (claim 4) gave one FARDC soldier killed; the two accounts differ.
src: Ces groupes s'étaient opposés le 25 août dernier, à l’arrivée d’une délégation venue du Burundi pour les obsèques du colonel Patrick, décédé récemment. Ces accrochages ont causé la mort d'au moins cinq combattants Wazalendo et l’arrestation de quatorze autres, selon les autorités militaires.

r1-UV-2025Q3-009.s: Afrikarabia reported that President Félix Tshisekedi's appointment of General Olivier Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region, and his taking up duty in Uvira on 1 September, were at the heart of the unrest, with civil society organisations and above all the Wazalendo militias leading the protest; SOS Médias Burundi reported that General Gasita was entrenched in an Uvira hotel under the joint protection of the FARDC and of 'militaires burundais'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-009.n: Titles differ across outlets: 'commandant adjoint de la 33e région militaire' (Afrikarabia, SOS), 'chargé des opérations et du renseignement' (Radio Okapi). Name printed as Olivier Gasita (Radio Okapi: Olivier Gasita Mukunda per other pages). Burundian soldiers' protection stated by SOS Médias Burundi, not independently confirmed.
r1-UV-2025Q3-009.vn: Source 1 was cited but its fact was not in the statement; added and attributed. Leadership of the protest reworded to the page ('mais surtout les milices Wazalendo'). Actualite.cd (9 Sept) describes Gasita as deputy commander in charge of operations and intelligence 'depuis janvier', which differs from the 1 September date of taking up duty given by Afrikarabia and SOS Médias Burundi. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Au coeur de ces troubles, il y a la nomination, par le président Félix Tshisekedi, du général Olivier Gasita comme commandant adjoint de la 33e région militaire et sa prise de fonction dans la ville d’Uvira le 1er septembre.
Le Général Gasita est actuellement retranché dans un hôtel d’Uvira, sous protection conjointe des FARDC et de militaires burundais.

r1-UV-2025Q3-010.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing local sources, that General Gasita arrived in Uvira escorted by Burundian soldiers of the FDNB as well as FARDC elements.
r1-UV-2025Q3-010.n: Single outlet citing local sources. Burundi's government made no statement found on this escort (see gaps).
r1-UV-2025Q3-010.vn: Excerpt states it, attributed to local sources. Single outlet: C.
src: Selon des sources locales, le général est arrivé à Uvira escorté par des soldats burundais de la FDNB ainsi que par des éléments des FARDC, signe que Kinshasa prend très au sérieux les menaces qui pèsent sur sa sécurité.

r1-UV-2025Q3-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that since 2 September the local 'forces vives' and Wazalendo combatants had erected barricades on strategic axes, notably towards the Burundian border, paralysing cross-border trade and lake operations at Kalundu port, and that, according to several sources, the port was under the exclusive surveillance of the Wazalendo.
r1-UV-2025Q3-011.l: Axes towards the Burundi border and Kalundu port, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-011.n: Radio Okapi's 3 Sep article says activities paralysed 'depuis la matinée du mercredi 3 septembre' naming Mulongwe, Kasenga and 'Kanvinvira' (sic, Kavimvira); other outlets and HRW say 2 September. Radio Okapi 5 Sep says the barricades were on the 'Kilomoni' axis linking Uvira to the border. Prices: tomato from 500 to 1,000 francs (Radio Okapi 6 Sep).
r1-UV-2025Q3-011.vn: Source 1's fact (Wazalendo control of Kalundu port) was not in the statement; added with its attribution.
src: Depuis le 2 septembre, les forces vives locales et les combattants Wazalendo ont érigé des barricades sur les axes stratégiques, notamment vers la frontière burundaise, paralysant les activités commerciales transfrontalières et les opérations lacustres au port de Kalundu.
Actuellement, selon plusieurs sources, ce port est sous la surveillance exclusive des Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q3-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Nouvelle société civile congolaise announced a partial suspension of the strike from Friday 5 September, after three days of a movement launched by Wazalendo combatants and citizen movements against the appointment of General Olivier Gasita as commander of operations and intelligence.
r1-UV-2025Q3-012.n: Radio Okapi adds that despite the announced suspension activities remained suspended and traders hesitated to reopen for fear of looting. Coordinator Mafikiri Mashimango named on the page.
src: La Nouvelle société civile congolaise annonce la suspension partielle de la grève dès ce vendredi 5 septembre. Ce mouvement, lancé depuis trois jours par des combattants Wazalendo et des mouvements citoyens, protestait contre la nomination du général Olivier Gasita comme commandant des opérations et du renseignement au Sud-Kivu.

r1-UV-2025Q3-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Wazalendo accuse General Gasita of being a double agent serving the M23 rebellion and of having played a decisive role in the take of Bukavu by that armed group in February 2025.
r1-UV-2025Q3-013.n: An accusation by a party (Wazalendo), unproven; SOS Médias Burundi (7 Sep) calls similar accusations 'non prouvées' for Gasita. Date is the article's reporting of the ongoing dispute (published 5 Sep).
r1-UV-2025Q3-013.vn: Excerpt states the accusation verbatim, attributed to the Wazalendo. An accusation by the Wazalendo, reported by Radio Okapi; not a finding.
src: Les Wazalendo accusent le général Gasita d’être un agent double au service de la rébellion du M23 et d’avoir joué un rôle déterminant dans la prise de Bukavu par ce groupe armé en février 2025.

r1-UV-2025Q3-014.s: Afrikarabia reported that the deputy Justin Bitakwira, who is also coordinator of the Wazalendo in South Kivu, accuses General Gasita of collusion with the M23 and of having delivered a speech calling on the Wazalendo to let the rebels pass, which would have facilitated the fall of Bukavu.
r1-UV-2025Q3-014.a: Justin Bitakwira (deputy and Wazalendo coordinator in South Kivu, per source)
r1-UV-2025Q3-014.n: Date approximate (September 2025). Accusation, unproven. The speaker is a member of parliament; the page says he was sanctioned by the EU (not cited here).
r1-UV-2025Q3-014.vn: Excerpt carries the statement. Category is an accusation by a political/militia figure, not an official statement in the strict sense. An accusation by Justin Bitakwira as reported by Afrikarabia; the conditional 'aurait facilité' is kept.
src: Olivier Gasita a été la cible du député Justin Bitakwira qui est aussi coordonnateur des Wazalendo au Sud-Kivu. Il accuse le général Gasita de collusion avec le M23 et d’avoir prononcé un discours appelant les Wazalendo à laisser passer les rebelles, ce qui aurait facilité la chute de Bukavu.

r1-UV-2025Q3-015.s: Radio Okapi reported, according to concordant sources, that on 2 September at Kalungwe two civilians, including a moto-taxi driver and his client, were wounded by a bullet fired by a Wazalendo fighter after refusing to take part in the demonstration that day.
r1-UV-2025Q3-015.n: 'selon des sources concordantes'. Victims not named. Place spelled 'Kalungwe' by Radio Okapi.
r1-UV-2025Q3-015.vn: The page attributes the incident to 'sources concordantes'; attribution added.
src: La tension est accentuée par un incident survenu la veille (2 septembre) à Kalungwe, où deux civils dont un conducteur de moto-taxi et son client ont été blessés par balle tirée par un combattant Wazalendo après avoir refusé de participer à la manifestation de ce jour

r1-UV-2025Q3-016.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local medical sources, that three civilians, including two moto-tricycle drivers, wounded during the Wazalendo demonstrations against General Gasita's appointment died on Thursday 4 September.
r1-UV-2025Q3-016.x: Radio Okapi: 3 civilians died on 4 September
r1-UV-2025Q3-016.n: The page does not say who shot them. Radio Okapi 5 Sep (second article) says they died after being taken to hospital. Overlaps possibly with the 'two new civilian deaths' reported 6 Sep (separate claim). Victims not named.
r1-UV-2025Q3-016.vn: Excerpt states it; 'Trois' printed in words; the source spells 'Wazalelendo' (typo). The deaths are reported without stating who caused the injuries. A second Radio Okapi article of 5 September also reports the three deaths, after being taken to hospital.
src: Trois civils, dont deux conducteurs de moto-tricycles, blessés lors des manifestations des combattants Wazalelendo, contre la nomination du général Gasita au Renseignement à Uvira (Sud-Kivu), sont décédés jeudi 4 septembre, ont rapporté des sources médicales locales

r1-UV-2025Q3-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Thursday, the deputy mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda, deplored the disturbances to public order, called for the end of the demonstrations while saying the demonstrators' demands had been heard, and invited the organisers to an emergency meeting on Friday 5 September.
r1-UV-2025Q3-017.n: Thursday = 2025-09-04 (date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-09-05).
r1-UV-2025Q3-017.vn: Meeting clause is on the page, supplied as a replacement quote.
src: Dans un communiqué publié jeudi, le maire adjoint d’Uvira, Kifara Kapenda, a déploré les troubles à l’ordre public et appelé à la fin des manifestations, tout en affirmant que les revendications des manifestants avaient été entendues.

r1-UV-2025Q3-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent clashes between the FARDC and the Wazalendo had been reported, causing two new civilian deaths according to local civil society, and that a meeting between urban authorities, military leaders and demonstrators had produced no significant progress.
r1-UV-2025Q3-018.x: Radio Okapi (local civil society): 2 new civilian deaths
r1-UV-2025Q3-018.n: Date is the publication date; the page gives no exact date of the clashes. 'Nouveaux' suggests additional to earlier deaths; may overlap with 4-5 Sep deaths. The same page states 'Les autorités militaires, de leur côté, réaffirment leur soutien à l’officier contesté.'
r1-UV-2025Q3-018.vn: Supported; meeting clause supplied from the page. Toll from local civil society. The meeting was held on Friday (5 September); the article is dated 6 September. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 6 Sept 2025, carries both clauses; the stored excerpt carries only the clashes/deaths clause, so the meeting clause (held Friday) needs its own excerpt.
src: Des accrochages violents entre les FARDC et les Wazalendo ont été signalés, faisant deux nouveaux morts parmi les civils, selon la société civile locale.
Une réunion tenue vendredi entre les autorités urbaines, les responsables militaires et les manifestants n’a débouché sur aucune avancée significative.

r1-UV-2025Q3-019.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a 5-year-old child died in an explosion during the night of 6 to 7 September in Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q3-019.n: Single outlet. Cause of the explosion not stated. The SOS article of 7 Sep says the child died 'dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi' (5-6 Sep), a one-night discrepancy between the two SOS pages. HRW (existing claim) reports on 5 September an 8-year-old boy killed when a shell struck his house; it is unclear whether these are the same or different incidents.
r1-UV-2025Q3-019.vn: Excerpt supports the statement; the date conflict within the same outlet is noted. Discrepancy: an earlier SOS Médias Burundi article (Bukavu dateline 7 September) places the death in the night 'de vendredi à samedi' (5 to 6 September); this article says the night of 6 to 7 September. The cause of the explosion is not stated.
src: Un enfant de 5 ans est mort dans une explosion dans la nuit du 6 au 7 septembre.

r1-UV-2025Q3-020.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced in a communiqué acts of discrimination, physical violence and intimidation, including women and girls beaten in Kabindula and denial of access to drinking water, some demonstrators saying 'Allez puiser au Rwanda'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-020.l: Kabindula quarter, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-020.a: as alleged by the Mutualité des Banyamulenge: demonstrators/Wazalendo-led protesters (not specified in the excerpt)
r1-UV-2025Q3-020.n: Allegation by a community organisation, relayed by one outlet. HRW (15 Sep, existing source) separately reports Banyamulenge denied access to water points. No sexual violence is alleged in this excerpt.
r1-UV-2025Q3-020.vn: Excerpt states the communiqué's allegations verbatim. Allegations in a community association's communiqué; perpetrators are not identified beyond 'certains manifestants'.
src: Dans un communiqué, la Mutualité des Banyamulenge dénonce des actes de discrimination, de violence physique et d’intimidation : Femmes et jeunes filles battues dans Kabindula ; Refus d’accès à l’eau potable, certains manifestants déclarant : « Allez puiser au Rwanda » ;

r1-UV-2025Q3-021.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Mutualité des Banyamulenge denounced the abduction of a FARDC soldier and a policeman, both Banyamulenge.
r1-UV-2025Q3-021.n: Allegation by a community organisation (excerpt starts at the list item; the attribution to the Mutualité is in the preceding sentence of the page). Single outlet. Persons not named. Perpetrator not specified.
r1-UV-2025Q3-021.vn: Excerpt supports; it is the list item of the communiqué introduced by 'la Mutualité des Banyamulenge dénonce'. Allegation by the Mutualité des Banyamulenge; no perpetrator, date or names given. SOS Médias Burundi's 9 September article repeats it (1 FARDC soldier and 1 policeman).
src: Enlèvement d’un soldat FARDC et d’un policier, tous deux Banyamulenge.

r1-UV-2025Q3-022.s: Afrikarabia reported that a Wazalendo official issued a call giving '10 jours aux Tutsi d’Uvira pour quitter la ville', and that Kinshasa said it did not know the author of the message, which could be 'une manipulation'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-022.a: a Wazalendo official (as reported by the source)
r1-UV-2025Q3-022.n: A threat reported by one outlet; the message itself was not seen; authorship unverified (Kinshasa suggests manipulation). Date: after Gasita's departure on 9 Sep, before the 14 Sep publication.
r1-UV-2025Q3-022.vn: Excerpt supports both clauses. The author of the message is unidentified; Kinshasa suggested it could be a manipulation. The message's date is not given.
src: Un responsable Wazalendo a même lancé un appel en donnant « 10 jours aux Tutsi d’Uvira pour quitter la ville. Au-delà, vous ne pourrez pas dire qu’on ne vous a pas prévenu », dit le message. Kinshasa indique ne pas connaître l’auteur de ce message, qui pourrait être « une manipulation ».

r1-UV-2025Q3-023.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to local sources, at least 5 people were killed and about twenty wounded, several seriously, after FARDC fire to disperse demonstrators in Uvira on 8 September, while the FARDC's official version, per the same page, was one 12-year-old child killed by a stray bullet and 9 wounded (4 soldiers and 5 civilians).
r1-UV-2025Q3-023.l: Uvira city (town hall, Sokola 2 headquarters), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-023.x: SOS Médias Burundi, civil sources: at least 5 killed, about 20 wounded (also 'plus de 9'); FARDC version: 1 child aged 12 killed, 9 wounded (4 soldiers, 5 civilians)
r1-UV-2025Q3-023.n: Figures differ by source and are not merged: SOS Médias Burundi cites civil sources 5 killed, 'une vingtaine' / 'plus de 9' wounded (the page gives both); Afrikarabia (14 Sep) cites civil society of Uvira for 6 dead overall; Radio Okapi (10 Sep) 'au moins huit' dead across the protests. HRW (existing claim) says an 8-year-old boy was killed; Radio Okapi/FARDC say a 12-year-old. Victims not named. Complements existing r1-SV-2025-028 (HRW).
r1-UV-2025Q3-023.vn: All figures on the page; the date comes from the dateline ('ce lundi', 8 September 2025). The same page gives two civil-source wounded figures: 'une vingtaine' in the text and 'plus de 9' in the summary box. Contested toll: compare Radio Okapi (claim 23) and the later at-least-eight cumulative toll (claim 25).
src: Selon des sources locales, au moins 5 personnes ont été tuées et une vingtaine d’autres blessées, dont plusieurs grièvement, après des tirs des FARDC (Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo) pour disperser les manifestants.
Sources civiles : 5 morts, plus de 9 blessés Version officielle des FARDC : 1 enfant de 12 ans tué par une balle perdue, 9 blessés (dont 4 militaires et 5 civils)

r1-UV-2025Q3-024.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the spokesperson of operations Sokola 2, sub-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, the disturbances in Uvira left 1 dead (a 12-year-old child hit by a bullet) and 9 wounded (4 FARDC soldiers and 5 civilians); Radio Okapi reported that the incidents broke out when demonstrators deemed uncontrolled tried to force the entrance of a military base, and that one of them was reportedly caught with a grenade, according to the military authorities; civil society denounced a violent repression and called on the President of the Republic to intervene.
r1-UV-2025Q3-024.x: FARDC spokesperson: 1 dead (child, 12), 9 wounded (4 soldiers, 5 civilians)
r1-UV-2025Q3-024.n: FARDC account of the 8 Sep shooting; the spokesman's name appears elsewhere as 'Reagan Kalonji' (SOS Médias Burundi). Contradicts HRW's description (shots at unarmed protesters, boy aged 8) and civil-society counts. Actualite.cd (9 Sep) also reports one killed and at least nine wounded by bullets after the army's repression.
r1-UV-2025Q3-024.vn: The draft put the base-entry and grenade narration in the spokesperson's mouth; on the page it is Radio Okapi's narration with the grenade attributed to 'les autorités militaires'. Source 2 (civil society) was cited but unused; added. FARDC account of a contested event; SOS Médias Burundi gives at least 5 killed per local sources (claim 22).
src: Selon le porte-parole des opérations Sokola 2, le sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, les troubles ont fait : 1 mort : un enfant de 12 ans atteint par balle, 9 blessés : dont 4 militaires des FARDC et 5 civils.

Les incidents ont éclaté lorsque des manifestants jugés incontrôlés ont tenté de forcer l’entrée d’une base militaire. L’un d’eux aurait été surpris en possession d’une grenade, selon les autorités militaires.
La société civile, de son côté, dénonce une répression violente et appelle le Président de la République à intervenir pour éviter une escalade entre les FARDC et les miliciens Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q3-025.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that automatic-weapon fire was heard for at least twenty minutes, at around 10 o'clock local time, near the Uvira town hall in the Kimanga quarter on Monday 8 September 2025, that law enforcement elements were firing in the air to disperse demonstrators, and that several sources spoke of dead and wounded among civilians and the security forces.
r1-UV-2025Q3-025.l: Kimanga quarter near the town hall, Uvira city, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-025.a: law enforcement elements (as described by the source)
r1-UV-2025Q3-025.n: Wording 'tiraient en l’air' contrasts with accounts of live fire at demonstrators (SOS Médias Burundi, HRW). Titled 'Des morts et des blessés' but the cited paragraph gives no casualty figure. Procession started at the Kavimvira roundabout per the same page.
r1-UV-2025Q3-025.vn: '10:00' replaced with the source's '10 heures'; casualty sentence from the page added. Kivu Morning Post is based in Goma (under AFC/M23 control at the time).
src: Des tirs d’armes automatiques ont retenti pendant au moins vingt minutes, vers 10 heures locales, près de la mairie d’Uvira, dans le quartier Kimanga, en ce lundi 8 septembre 2025. Des éléments de l’ordre tiraient en l’air pour disperser les manifestants

r1-UV-2025Q3-026.s: Radio Okapi reported that the demonstrations, organised by civil society and supported by Wazalendo fighters, had been violently repressed by the FARDC; that at least eight people died during the successive demonstrations in Uvira and about ten were wounded, including soldiers; and that the bishop of Uvira, Mgr Sébastien Moyengo, had condemned the disproportionate use of force against civilians.
r1-UV-2025Q3-026.a: FARDC (force used, per the bishop's condemnation)
r1-UV-2025Q3-026.x: Radio Okapi: at least 8 dead, about 10 wounded (all protests)
r1-UV-2025Q3-026.n: Cumulative toll across protests (2-8 Sep), not a single event; Radio Okapi's own sub-counts earlier are 3 (4 Sep) + 1 or more (8 Sep) + 2 (6 Sep). Deaths not itemised by date or cause.
r1-UV-2025Q3-026.vn: Added the page's own statement that the FARDC repressed the protests, which grounds the actor field. Cumulative toll for the protests of early September; Afrikarabia (14 Sept) cites a civil-society toll of 6 dead. Tolls vary by source.
src: Ces manifestations, organisées par la société civile et soutenues par les combattants Wazalendo, avaient été violemment réprimées par les FARDC. Au moins huit personnes sont mortes lors de ces différentes manifestations, une dizaine ont été blessées dont des militaires. L’évêque d’Uvira, Mgr Sébastien Moyengo, avait condamné l’usage disproportionné de la force contre les civils

r1-UV-2025Q3-027.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing military sources, that General Olivier Gasita left Uvira at dawn on Tuesday 9 September at around 3 a.m., without other details on his real destination; Afrikarabia reported that he was exfiltrated from Uvira to Bujumbura and then Kinshasa.
r1-UV-2025Q3-027.n: Radio Okapi gives no destination; Afrikarabia names Bujumbura then Kinshasa. Kinshasa's official reason is not given in these excerpts.
r1-UV-2025Q3-027.vn: Departure date corroborated by two outlets; destination from Afrikarabia only, attributed.
src: Il a quitté cette ville du Sud-Kivu à l’aube de mardi 9 septembre. L’information a été confirmée à Radio Okapi par des sources militaires, précisant qu’il est parti aux alentours de 3 heures du matin, sans autres détails sur sa destination réelle.
le 9 septembre en pleine nuit, le général Gasita a été exfiltré d’Uvira vers Bujumbura, au Burundi voisin, puis vers Kinshasa.

r1-UV-2025Q3-028.s: Radio Okapi reported that social and economic activities resumed on Wednesday 10 September in Uvira, 24 hours after General Gasita's departure, with shops reopening and public transport resuming, while schools remained closed because parents feared new demonstrations.
r1-UV-2025Q3-028.n: Education access: schools closed since the strike began (2 Sep).
src: Les activités sociales et économiques ont repris ce mercredi 10 septembre à Uvira, au Sud-Kivu, 24 heures après le départ du général Olivier Gasita.
Cependant, les écoles restent fermées, les parents préférant la prudence par crainte de nouvelles manifestations.

r1-UV-2025Q3-029.s: Actualite.cd reported that after an inter-institutional meeting chaired on Monday 8 September in Kinshasa by President Félix Tshisekedi, National Assembly president Vital Kamerhe said the Head of State is preoccupied by the Uvira tensions and seeks solutions through a government mission sent to Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q3-029.n: Meeting also attended per the page by Sama Lukonde, Judith Suminwa and Dieudonné Kamuleta.
r1-UV-2025Q3-029.vn: Meeting clause supplied from the page (the page has several captures; the passage is in the latest).
src: Faisant la restitution de cette séance de travail, en ce qui concerne les tensions à Uvira, Vital Kamerhe a indiqué que « le Chef de l’État est préoccupé par cette situation et y cherche des solutions à travers une mission gouvernementale qui est diligentée à Uvira, en vue de trouver la solution à cette question. »

r1-UV-2025Q3-030.s: Radio Okapi reported that a government delegation led by Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani was in Uvira with the mission of reconciling local communities, easing tensions and restoring state authority; the delegation also included Aimé Boji (Industry), Floribert Anzuluni (Regional Cooperation), Eliezer Ntambwe (minister delegate for Defence in charge of veterans), FARDC chief of staff General Jules Banza and national police commissioner general Benjamin Alongaboni. SOS Médias Burundi reported that Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo arrived escorted by Burundian and Congolese soldiers.
r1-UV-2025Q3-030.a: DRC government delegation; FDNB (escort, per SOS Médias Burundi)
r1-UV-2025Q3-030.n: Date: SOS Médias Burundi (dated 12 Sep) says the delegation arrived 'Alhamisi hii' (Thursday = 2025-09-11); Radio Okapi (12 Sep) says it is staying in Uvira. SOS gives his title as Deputy Prime Minister for security; Radio Okapi as vice-Premier ministre et ministre de l'Intérieur. SOS says the Deputy PM met only Wazalendo representatives at first. Burundian escort is stated only by SOS Médias Burundi (one outlet).
r1-UV-2025Q3-030.vn: Source 1 (delegation list) was cited but unused; members added from the excerpt. The excerpt_en flags reflect translated titles only. SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) says the delegation arrived in Uvira on Thursday (11 September 2025).
src: Une délégation gouvernementale conduite par le vice-Premier ministre et ministre de l’Intérieur, Jacquemain Shabani, séjourne à Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, avec pour mission de réconcilier les communautés locales, apaiser les tensions et rétablir l’autorité de l’État.

Aux côtés du ministre de l’Intérieur, la délégation comprend également : Aimé Boji, ministre de l’Industrie, Floribert Anzuluni, ministre de la Coopération régionale, Eliezer Ntambwe, ministre délégué à la Défense chargé des anciens combattants, Le Général Jules Banza, chef d’état-major des FARDC, Le commissaire divisionnaire Benjamin Alongaboni, Commissaire Général de la Police nationale congolaise.
Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo aliwasili akisindikizwa na wanajeshi wa Burundi na Kongo.

r1-UV-2025Q3-031.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the FARDC spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, firmly rejected the demonstrators' demands, saying the Wazalendo have no instruction to give within the Armed Forces of the DRC and calling on the 'real' Wazalendo not to fall into the enemy's trap.
r1-UV-2025Q3-031.n: Exact day not given on this page (published 7 Sep); the statement is placed around 6 Sep by HRW's report of a press conference (not re-cited here as the HRW page is already used in an existing claim).
r1-UV-2025Q3-031.vn: Excerpt carries the quote verbatim. The statement's own date and venue are not given (reported 7 September 2025).
src: Le Général-Major Sylvain Ekenge, porte-parole de l’armée congolaise, a fermement rejeté les revendications des manifestants : « Les Wazalendo n’ont aucune instruction à donner au sein des Forces Armées de la RDC. Il y a des vrais Wazalendo et des faux ; j’en appelle aux vrais à ne pas tomber dans le piège de l’ennemi »

r1-UV-2025Q3-032.s: Afrikarabia reported that the spokesperson of the Congolese army supported General Olivier Gasita, saying that a soldier does not belong to communities and that 'un militaire communautaire n’existe pas'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-032.n: Afrikarabia does not name the spokesperson in this passage; SOS Médias Burundi names Sylvain Ekenge for a separate statement. Date approximate.
r1-UV-2025Q3-032.vn: Supported by the excerpt. Afrikarabia does not name the spokesperson; SOS Médias Burundi names the army spokesperson as Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge (claim 30).
src: Le porte-parole de l’armée congolaise a tout de même apporté son soutien à Olivier Gasita : « Un militaire n’appartient pas à des communautés, il est au service de la nation toute entière. Que des gens des mauvaises foi ne nous rabaissent pas dans des considérations communautaires, un militaire communautaire n’existe pas ».

r1-UV-2025Q3-033.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the Wazalendo militias criticise the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), present in Uvira as part of bilateral military cooperation, for not conducting offensives against the M23.
r1-UV-2025Q3-033.n: Date is the publication date; presence is a general condition, not an event. No numbers of Burundian troops are given in this excerpt.
r1-UV-2025Q3-033.vn: Excerpt states it (SOS Médias Burundi narration of the Wazalendo's criticism).
src: Militias also criticize the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), although present in Uvira as part of bilateral military cooperation, for not conducting offensives against the M23.

r1-UV-2025Q3-034.s: The SOS Torture Burundi Justice Newsletter stated that Burundi reportedly deployed an additional contingent of 700 soldiers to Uvira on August 21, 2025, to reinforce more than 24 battalions of Burundian soldiers already deployed in eastern DRC to counter the advance of the M23.
r1-UV-2025Q3-034.x: SOS Torture Burundi newsletter: 700 additional soldiers to Uvira; more than 24 battalions already deployed in eastern DRC
r1-UV-2025Q3-034.n: Hedged ('reportedly') in the newsletter, which footnotes a source not opened here. Burundi government made no statement on this found. SOS Médias Burundi (7 Sep) says Burundi has about 10,000 soldiers on Congolese soil (different figure scope).
r1-UV-2025Q3-034.vn: Removed the issue number from the statement text; the originating source is the Burundi Daily article the newsletter footnotes, so this is a relay, single origin: C. Hedged ('reportedly'); the newsletter's footnote 26 cites a Burundi Daily article of 31 August 2025 ('Uvira surrounded, Ndayishimiye dispatches military reinforcements'), which was not opened. No Burundian government confirmation found.
src: Burundi reportedly deployed an additional contingent of 700 soldiers to Uvira on August 21, 2025, to reinforce more than 24 battalions of Burundian soldiers already deployed in eastern DRC to counter the advance of the M23.

r1-UV-2025Q3-035.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in recent weeks 332 Burundian refugees in 74 households, who had lived in the Mulongwe and Lusenda camps and the Kavimvira transit centre in South Kivu, were repatriated to Burundi via the Gatumba border post; refugees trying to farm at Kahwizi and Kiliba reported being attacked, and a refugee, Niyonkuru, said that Wazalendo militiamen attack them on the way to the fields.
r1-UV-2025Q3-035.l: Mulongwe camp, Kavimvira transit centre (Uvira), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-035.a: Wazalendo militiamen (as alleged by a refugee quoted by the source)
r1-UV-2025Q3-035.n: Allegation about Wazalendo comes from one named refugee (first name/surname 'Niyonkuru') quoted by the outlet; no date. Page also says the Bukavu-Uvira humanitarian corridor (200 tonnes of food and medicine) was blocked, per local sources (not cited). Name 'Niyonkuru' printed as a quoted refugee; not harmed per the excerpt.
r1-UV-2025Q3-035.vn: Gatumba/camp details came from the page, not the excerpt; supplied. Named the speaker Niyonkuru as printed (policy v1) and added the Kahwizi/Kiliba location the excerpt gives. The attack allegation is one refugee's account; no dates or casualties given. The same page reports that the Bukavu-Uvira humanitarian corridor was blocked by Wazalendo under Makanaki Kasimbira John, according to local sources (see claim 0). The page says the operation was run by Burundi's refugee commission (CNR) with UNHCR. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi, dateline Uvira 24 July 2025, posted 25 July: 332 refugees (74 households) repatriated in recent weeks; refugees farming at Kahwizi and Kiliba report attacks, Niyonkuru blaming Wazalendo. All clauses are on the page; the camps and Gatumba clauses were in no stored excerpt, now added.
src: Ces dernières semaines, 332 réfugiés burundais, regroupés en 74 ménages, ont été rapatriés depuis la République démocratique du Congo vers le Burundi.
Des réfugiés qui tentaient de cultiver des terres à Kahwizi et Kiliba rapportent avoir été attaqués. « Les miliciens Wazalendo nous attaquent sur le chemin des champs », déplore Niyonkuru.

L’opération a été menée par la Commission nationale chargée des réfugiés (CNR), en collaboration avec le Haut Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), via le poste frontalier de Gatumba, à l’ouest du pays. Ces réfugiés vivaient depuis plusieurs années dans les camps de Mulongwe, Lusenda et dans le centre de transit de Kavimvira, tous situés dans la province congolaise du Sud-Kivu,

r1-UV-2025Q3-036.s: A UN Peacebuilding Support Office briefing on the DRC (September 2025) stated that Uvira had been at the center of tensions, both in relation to a possible AFC/M23 advance and to growing strain between the FARDC and wazalendo factions.
r1-UV-2025Q3-036.n: Context-level UN statement; the briefing is dated 30 Sep 2025 per search metadata.
r1-UV-2025Q3-036.vn: Excerpt found verbatim in the PDF ('Briefing on the situation in the DRC – September 2025'). Analytical context, not an incident.
src: Uvira itself, located near Burundi’s economic capital Bujumbura, has been at the center of tensions, both in relation to a possible AFC/M23 advance and to growing strain between the FARDC and wazalendo factions.

r1-UV-2025Q3-037.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published from Goma, AFC/M23 communication head Lawrence Kanyuka warned that AFC/M23 'will no longer tolerate the barbaric surge of hate speech in Uvira, in Ituri and in the rest of the DRC'.
r1-UV-2025Q3-037.n: Partisan party statement (AFC/M23), cited only for what it said; the exact communiqué date is not stated in the excerpt (Kivu Morning Post article dated 4 Sep; the Twirwaneho communiqué cited on the same page is dated 3 Sep). The title says it 'threatens to intervene'; the excerpted sentence is a warning only.
r1-UV-2025Q3-037.vn: Excerpt carries the quote verbatim; byline Blaise Basabose. Party statement (AFC/M23). The article (4 September) does not give the communiqué's date explicitly; 3 September is approximate.
src: Dans un communiqué publié depuis Goma, Lawrence Kanyuka, chef du département de communication, a averti que l’AFC/M23 « ne tolérera plus la flambée barbare des discours de haine à Uvira, en Ituri et dans le reste de la République Démocratique du Congo tout comme les crimes abjects qui en découlent » .

r1-UV-2025Q3-038.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the movement (identified in the quoted passage as MRDP-Twirwaneho) affirms that Burundian troops and FDLR elements crossed the border at Runingu to reinforce the FARDC and Wazalendo in the area, and that it wrote that the presence of foreign troops worsens the security and humanitarian crisis.
r1-UV-2025Q3-038.l: Runingu border crossing, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q3-038.a: MRDP-Twirwaneho (claimant); Burundian troops and FDLR (as alleged)
r1-UV-2025Q3-038.n: Partisan claim by an armed group allied to AFC/M23 (what it said, not established fact). The page's paragraph structure leaves it slightly ambiguous whether 'le mouvement' is MRDP-Twirwaneho; the quote is attributed to it. Not independently confirmed; Burundi's government response not found. Runingu is on the Ruzizi plain near the Rwanda/DRC border of Uvira territory.
r1-UV-2025Q3-038.vn: Excerpt supports; allegation kept attributed. Partisan allegation (MRDP-Twirwaneho, allied with AFC/M23); not corroborated. The quoted passage also uses the term 'génocidaire', which is the movement's wording.
src: Le mouvement affirme que des troupes burundaises et des éléments FDLR ont franchi la frontière à Runingu pour renforcer les FARDC et les Wazalendo dans la zone. « La présence de troupes étrangères engagées dans une mission à caractère génocidaire sur le sol congolais, malgré les accords en cours entre gouvernements, aggrave une crise sécuritaire et humanitaire déjà alarmante » , écrit le MRDP-Twirwaneho.

r1-UV-2025Q4-001.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 10 December 2025 M23 and Rwandan forces entered Uvira after several days of fighting in South Kivu, and that witnesses said hostilities in the city had largely ended when these forces took control.
r1-UV-2025Q4-001.a: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW names them)
r1-UV-2025Q4-001.n: HRW report published 2026-05-14; field research after the M23 departure. Other outlets date the entry 9 Dec (evening) or 10 Dec; Kigali Today dates the capture 12 Dec. Dates differ by source.
r1-UV-2025Q4-001.vn: Excerpt verbatim in HRW report summary; documented NGO field investigation. Entry date differs by source: Afrikarabia 'mardi soir' (9 Dec), BBC/HRW 10 Dec, Kigali Today 12 Dec.
src: Le 10 décembre 2025, le M23 et les forces rwandaises sont entrés dans Uvira après plusieurs jours de combats dans le Sud-Kivu qui ont provoqué le déplacement de dizaines de milliers de personnes. Des témoins ont déclaré que les hostilités dans la ville avaient en grande partie cessé quand ces forces ont pris le contrôle

r1-UV-2025Q4-002.s: Afrikarabia reported that AFC/M23 rebels had entered Uvira on Tuesday evening, and that testimonies on site spoke of the flight of civil and military authorities during that day while the rebellion was at Kiliba, some fifteen kilometres north of Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q4-002.n: Date computed from weekday ('mardi soir') and publication date 2025-12-10. Contested the next day by the provincial governor (see BBC 10 Dec claim).
r1-UV-2025Q4-002.vn: Removed publication date from statement (number not in excerpt; source date shown with source). Byline Christophe Rigaud on page. 'Tuesday evening' read as 9 Dec 2025 from the article date (10 Dec). The page's own photo caption says '10 décembre 2025 au soir de l'entrée'; BBC and HRW give 10 Dec. Discrepancy unresolved.
src: les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 sont bien entrés dans Uvira mardi soir. Les témoignages sur place faisaient déjà état de la fuite des autorités civiles et militaires dans la journée, alors que la rébellion se tenait à Kiliba, à une quinzaine de kilomètres au Nord d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2025Q4-003.s: BBC reported that the M23 said it had 'liberated' the city of Uvira, while South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city.
r1-UV-2025Q4-003.n: Two accounts of control in one passage. BBC also cites AFP and Radio Okapi. The governor's denial was overtaken by events (the M23 announced withdrawal on 16 Dec).
r1-UV-2025Q4-003.vn: Removed publication date from statement. Two party accounts kept attributed.
src: The M23 rebel group said it had "liberated" the city, while UN-backed Radio Okapi quoted residents as saying that rebel fighters were on major streets. However, South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told local media that the army and allied militia remained in control of the city, which is just 27km (17 miles) from Burundi's capital, Bujumbura, across Lake Tanganyika.

r1-UV-2025Q4-004.s: Al Jazeera reported, citing its correspondent in Uvira, that government forces and allied militias known as Wazalendo, which had been using the city as a headquarters, began fleeing even before M23 fighters entered.
r1-UV-2025Q4-004.n: Month precision: the exact day of the flight is not stated. Corroborated in substance by HRW ('semblent avoir principalement fui Uvira').
r1-UV-2025Q4-004.vn: Removed publication date; the correspondent's name is printed on the page (byline 'Al Jazeera Staff and News Agencies'). HRW (14 May 2026) separately says the Congolese army and allied militias appear to have mainly fled Uvira before M23 and Rwandan forces arrived.
src: Uaykani said government and allied militias, known as “Wazalendo”, which had been using the city as a headquarters, began fleeing even before M23 fighters entered.

r1-UV-2025Q4-005.s: Al Jazeera reported that regional authorities said at least 400 civilians, including children, had been killed in violence between the cities of Bukavu and Uvira, both then under M23 control.
r1-UV-2025Q4-005.l: Between Bukavu and Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q4-005.x: Regional authorities (via Al Jazeera): at least 400 civilians killed between Bukavu and Uvira
r1-UV-2025Q4-005.n: Unverified authorities' figure. UN News (10 Dec) reported at least 70 civilians killed across South Kivu; HRW later documented 62 cases in Uvira. Figures are not merged.
r1-UV-2025Q4-005.vn: Removed publication date; figures field narrowed to what this source prints (UN/HRW figures belong to other claims). Perpetrator not attributed by source. Unverified authorities' figure; the authorities are not named. UN (10 Dec) gave at least 70 civilians killed across South Kivu; figures are not comparable.
src: Regional authorities say at least 400 civilians, including children, have been killed in the violence that took place between the cities of Bukavu and Uvira, both now under M23 control.

r1-UV-2025Q4-006.s: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented 62 cases of summary executions and unlawful killings in Uvira during the M23 and Rwandan-forces occupation, the victims being 54 men, 2 women, 5 boys and one girl.
r1-UV-2025Q4-006.a: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW attributes)
r1-UV-2025Q4-006.x: HRW: 62 documented cases (54 men, 2 women, 5 boys, 1 girl)
r1-UV-2025Q4-006.n: HRW says it received no reply to its 14 April 2026 letter to M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa. HRW states these cases are a fraction of the total. Counts are documented cases only.
r1-UV-2025Q4-006.vn: Figures verbatim; occupation period on the same page. HRW says these cases are only a fraction of civilians summarily executed during the occupation. HRW wrote to M23 leader Bertrand Bisimwa on 14 April 2026.
src: Human Rights Watch a documenté 62 cas d’exécutions sommaires et de meurtres illégaux, dont les victimes étaient 54 hommes, 2 femmes, 5 garçons et une fille.

r1-UV-2025Q4-007.s: Human Rights Watch reported that residents said that during the occupation of Uvira, M23 and Rwandan forces carried out systematic searches in several areas, in particular the Kasenga and Rugenge neighbourhoods.
r1-UV-2025Q4-007.l: Kasenga and Rugenge, Uvira (city), South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q4-007.a: M23 and Rwandan forces (as HRW attributes)
r1-UV-2025Q4-007.n: Context for the killings and abductions HRW documents; see the 62-cases claim.
src: Des habitants ont raconté que, pendant leur occupation d’Uvira, le M23 et les forces rwandaises ont mené des fouilles systématiques dans plusieurs zones, en particulier dans les quartiers de Kasenga et de Rugenge.

r1-UV-2025Q4-008.s: Human Rights Watch reported that it documented rapes and other sexual violence by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women and girls, and that survivors described being raped under threat of being killed, with a firearm pointed at them, at home or in the fields.
r1-UV-2025Q4-008.a: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers (as HRW attributes)
r1-UV-2025Q4-008.n: Survivors are not named in this record. HRW does not state a total number of rape cases in the cited passage. A related UFMP count is reported by DW.
src: Human Rights Watch a également documenté des viols et d’autres violences sexuelles commis par des combattants du M23 et des soldats rwandais sur des femmes et des filles. Les survivantes ont décrit avoir été violées sous la menace d’être tuées, avec une arme à feu braquée sur elles, à leur domicile ou dans les champs

r1-UV-2025Q4-009.s: Human Rights Watch reported that the lack of operational health services in Uvira during the occupation left survivors of sexual violence without access to essential care, including HIV post-exposure prophylaxis.
r1-UV-2025Q4-009.n: The cited passage does not say why services were not operational.
r1-UV-2025Q4-009.vn: Single clause, verbatim; cause of the lack of services not stated, as the draft notes.
src: Le manque de services de santé opérationnels à Uvira pendant l’occupation a laissé les survivantes sans accès à des soins essentiels, notamment à la prophylaxie post-exposition (PEP) pour prévenir l’infection par le VIH.

r1-UV-2025Q4-010.s: Human Rights Watch reported that M23 abducted a number of men and boys, often near military bases in Uvira, with no mention of a link to the Wazalendo, and that HRW considers they were probably forcibly recruited into M23.
r1-UV-2025Q4-010.n: 'Enforced disappearance' is HRW's own term, quoted via translation, not a finding of this record.
src: Enfin, le M23 a enlevé un certain nombre d’hommes et de garçons, souvent à proximité de bases militaires à Uvira, sans qu’il ait été fait mention d’un lien entre les individus et les Wazalendo. Human Rights Watch considère qu’ils ont probablement été recrutés de force dans le M23 et qu’ils ont fait l’objet d’une disparition forcée.

r1-UV-2025Q4-011.s: The Union des femmes des médias pour la paix (UFMP), in a report cited by Deutsche Welle, recorded 183 cases of rape in December in the city of Uvira, followed by 220 in January and 626 in February.
r1-UV-2025Q4-011.x: UFMP (via DW): 183 rape cases in December; 220 in January; 626 in February; 1,029 in total
r1-UV-2025Q4-011.n: Year of 'December' not printed in the excerpt; DW's article is dated 2026-04-17 so December 2025 is inferred. Methodology of the UFMP count is not given on the page. The count spans the occupation and its aftermath. Contradicting reporting: UFMP Sud-Sud-Kivu (LinkedIn post) (2026-04-01): January figure: UFMP's own post gives 320 for January and a total of 1,129; DW gives 220 for January and a total of 1,029. DW's 220 appears to be an error or a different version.
r1-UV-2025Q4-011.vn: Verbatim; single civil-society origin relayed by DW (byline Mitima Delachance). Year of 'December' inferred from DW's 17 April 2026 date. UFMP methodology not given. DW also reports, per UFMP, that barely 30% of victims received prevention kits (STI and pregnancy). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: Union des femmes des médias pour la paix (UFMP)
src: Les chiffres publiés par l’Union des femmes des médias pour la paix (UFMP) suscitent une vive indignation et illustrent l’ampleur des violences sexuelles . Le rapport fait état de 183 cas de viol recensés en décembre, 220 en janvier et 626 en février, soit un total de 1 029 cas documentés en trois mois seulement dans la ville d’Uvira .

1 129 cas de violences sexuelles ont été enregistrés entre décembre 2025 et février 2026. Selon les professionnels de santé, ces chiffres traduisent une situation alarmante. Dans les détails, 183 cas ont été documentés en décembre, 320 en janvier, et un pic préoccupant de 626 cas en février.

r1-UV-2025Q4-012.s: The ICRC reported that an ICRC and DRC Red Cross team evacuated 21 people wounded by weapons, seven of them children, over 40 km to Uvira, where they were being treated by medical teams of the ICRC-supported Uvira general referral hospital; the ICRC said the fighting of the past week in Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga and Fizi territories made rescue and transfer of the wounded extremely difficult.
r1-UV-2025Q4-012.l: Sange to Uvira, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q4-012.x: ICRC: 21 wounded evacuated, including 7 children, over 40 km
r1-UV-2025Q4-012.n: Date is the ICRC release date; the evacuation happened in the week before. Photo caption on the page places an evacuation at Sange (Uvira). ICRC head of the Uvira office quoted: Djibril Mamadou Diallo.
r1-UV-2025Q4-012.vn: Removed release date from statement; added the territories the source names. Grade B: single (credible, first-hand operational) origin, not an investigation. ICRC release of 7 Dec 2025; the evacuation date is not given. A photo caption places a Red Cross evacuation at Sange (Uvira).
src: Une équipe du Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) et de la Croix-Rouge de la RDC a évacué 21 blessés par armes, parmi eux sept enfants, sur une distance de 40 km jusqu’à la ville d’Uvira. Ces blessés sont pris en charge par des équipes médicales de l’Hôpital général de référence d’Uvira, soutenu par le CICR.

Malgré les besoins urgents, les combats dévastateurs de cette dernière semaine dans les territoires d’Uvira, Walungu, Mwenga et de Fizi au Sud-Kivu rendent extrêmement difficile le secours aux blessés et notamment leur transfert vers des structures médicales appropriées.

r1-UV-2025Q4-013.s: The ICRC reported that, between 2 and 16 December, more than 193 people wounded by weapons were treated in hospitals it supports, 110 of them at the Uvira general referral hospital (HGR), 63 at the Bukavu provincial general referral hospital and 20 at the Fizi general referral hospital.
r1-UV-2025Q4-013.l: Uvira, Bukavu and Fizi hospitals, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q4-013.x: ICRC (18 Dec): more than 193 wounded 2-16 Dec; 110 at Uvira HGR; 63 Bukavu; 20 Fizi
r1-UV-2025Q4-013.n: Another ICRC release (12 Dec) put admissions at the Uvira HGR at nearly 100 for 2-11 Dec.
r1-UV-2025Q4-013.vn: Removed release date (18 Dec) from statement. Grade B: single ICRC origin. Same ICRC page quotes its medical coordinator saying Fizi HGR received 'près de 20' wounded and Uvira HGR 'plus de 100' since 2 Dec; the ICRC also supported dignified burials in Uvira and the Ruzizi plain from 11 Dec. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: Hôpital Provincial Général de Référence de Bukavu (HPGRB)
Hôpital Général de Référence de Fizi (HGR)
src: En RDC : Plus de 193 blessés par armes pris en charge du 2 au 16 décembre, dans les hôpitaux le CICR soutien, dont 110 à l’Hôpital General de Référence d’Uvira (HGR), 63 à l’Hôpital Provincial Général de Référence de Bukavu (HPGRB) et 20 à l’Hôpital Général de Référence de Fizi (HGR).
La majorité de ces blessés est actuellement prise en charge par le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) à l'Hôpital Général de Référence d'Uvira (HGR).

r1-UV-2025Q4-014.s: UN News reported that the UN deputy spokesperson said humanitarian partners reported more than 200,000 people displaced across South Kivu and at least 70 civilians killed in the current escalation.
r1-UV-2025Q4-014.x: UN (10 Dec): >200,000 displaced across South Kivu; at least 70 civilians killed
r1-UV-2025Q4-014.n: Figure covers South Kivu, not Uvira alone. UN spokesperson on the page: Farhan Haq (Deputy Spokesperson).
r1-UV-2025Q4-014.vn: Removed date; speaker name sits on the page, not in the excerpt. Grade B: one UN origin (spokesperson relaying partners), not an investigation. Province-wide figure, not Uvira alone. BBC (10 Dec) cites the UN at least 74 killed, mostly civilians.
src: a prévenu mercredi l'ONU. « Nos partenaires humanitaires signalent que plus de 200 000 personnes ont été déplacées à travers le Sud-Kivu et qu'au moins 70 civils ont été tués lors de l'escalade actuelle.

r1-UV-2025Q4-015.s: UN News reported that between 5 and 8 December nearly 25,000 people crossed the border into Burundi, including Congolese nationals, returning Burundians and third-country migrants, and that in Uvira at least 32 WFP-supported schools suspended classes to house displaced families, depriving more than 12,000 children of school meals, the UN Deputy Spokesperson said.
r1-UV-2025Q4-015.x: UN: ~25,000 crossed to Burundi 5-8 Dec; 32 WFP-supported schools in Uvira suspended classes; >12,000 children without school meals
r1-UV-2025Q4-015.n: Border-crossing figure is for 5-8 Dec (before the 10 Dec entry), as the UN states it.
r1-UV-2025Q4-015.vn: Statement had attributed the border figure to the Deputy Spokesperson; the excerpt does not; reworded so the attribution covers the schools passage, which names him. Border-crossing figure covers 5-8 Dec, before the M23 entry into Uvira.
src: Entre le 5 et le 8 décembre, près de 25 000 personnes ont franchi la frontière vers le Burundi, dont des ressortissants congolais, des Burundais de retour au pays et des migrants en provenance de pays tiers.

À Uvira, au moins 32 écoles soutenues par le PAM ont suspendu les cours afin d'héberger les familles déplacées. Cette situation a perturbé le programme de repas scolaires et prive plus de 12 000 enfants de ce qui est souvent leur seul repas chaud et nutritif de la journée, a précisé M. Haq.

r1-UV-2025Q4-016.s: BBC Afrique reported that, according to the UN, the Uvira offensive caused dozens of deaths, at least 100 wounded and more than 200,000 displaced, and that at least 30,000 civilians fled to Burundi.
r1-UV-2025Q4-016.l: Uvira (city), South Kivu and Burundi border
r1-UV-2025Q4-016.x: UN (via BBC Afrique, 19 Dec): dozens killed; >=100 wounded; >200,000 displaced; >=30,000 to Burundi
r1-UV-2025Q4-016.n: The UN figure of 200,000 displaced is the same South Kivu figure reported on 10 Dec by UN News; BBC applies it to the offensive.
r1-UV-2025Q4-016.vn: Removed publication date. Relays the UN, so not an independent origin for the UN figures. The 200,000 displaced figure is the UN's South Kivu-wide figure (UN News, 10 Dec), which BBC applies to the Uvira offensive. Not independent of the UN claim.
src: Selon l'ONU, l'offensive d'Uvira a fait des dizaines de morts, au moins 100 blessés et plus de 200 000 déplacés. Au moins 30 000 civils ont fui vers le Burundi.

r1-UV-2025Q4-017.s: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a 'widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces' along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a 'blatant violation' of the ceasefire and of commitments under recent peace agreements; Kigali denied the accusations.
r1-UV-2025Q4-017.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (2025-12-12). Anadolu is a Turkish state agency; its text is taken as reporting, with the statement attributed to the Congolese government.
r1-UV-2025Q4-017.vn: Verbatim; party statement attributed. 'Wednesday' read as 10 Dec 2025 from the article date (Fri 12 Dec). Anadolu (byline James Tasamba, Kigali dateline) is a Turkish state agency; the government's original text was not opened.
src: On Wednesday, the Congolese government attributed the violence in Uvira to a “widespread offensive launched in recent days by the Rwandan Defense Forces” along the Kamanyola-Uvira axis, calling it a “blatant violation” of the ceasefire and the commitments made under recent peace agreements. Kigali denied the accusations.

r1-UV-2025Q4-018.s: Anadolu reported that on Wednesday Rwanda accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under the Washington peace deal.
r1-UV-2025Q4-018.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (2025-12-12). Nouvel Obs (10 Dec) also describes a Rwandan communiqué condemning Congolese and Burundian armies (snippet only; not fetched).
r1-UV-2025Q4-018.vn: Single clause, verbatim. Date from 'Wednesday' and article date. BBC (10 Dec) separately reports a Rwandan foreign ministry statement on X saying the ceasefire violation 'cannot be placed on Rwanda' and that Congolese and Burundian armies had 'systematically' bombed villages near Rwanda's border.
src: Instead, Rwanda on Wednesday accused the Congolese and Burundian armies of violating a ceasefire provided under a Washington peace deal championed by US President Donald Trump.

r1-UV-2025Q4-019.s: Anadolu reported that Rwandan President Paul Kagame said on Thursday that Burundian soldiers deployed in eastern DRC spend days shelling civilians, and Anadolu noted there was no immediate reaction from Burundi.
r1-UV-2025Q4-019.n: Date computed from weekday ('Thursday') and publication date 2025-12-12. Same article quotes Kagame saying more than 20,000 Burundian soldiers are in Congo and that they shell people in Minembwe with artillery and drones; these are Kagame's assertions, not verified.
r1-UV-2025Q4-019.vn: Verbatim; party claim attributed. Kagame's assertions (including more than 20,000 Burundian soldiers in Congo, shelling in Minembwe with artillery and drones) are a party's claims, unverified. Said at a swearing-in ceremony in Kigali.
src: Burundian soldiers deployed to the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo spend days shelling civilians, Rwandan President Paul Kagame said Thursday, highlighting Burundi’s military involvement in the conflict in South Kivu province. There was no immediate reaction from Burundi.

r1-UV-2025Q4-020.s: Anadolu reported that Burundi's Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned on Monday that 'any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated'.
r1-UV-2025Q4-020.n: Date computed from weekday; the article is dated 2025-12-12 so 'Monday' is read as 8 Dec. The page does not give the Monday's date. Excerpt may contain curly quotes as on the page.
r1-UV-2025Q4-020.vn: Single clause, verbatim; date approximate. 'Monday' read as 8 Dec 2025; the article does not give the date. BBC (10 Dec) separately quotes Bizimana to AFP calling M23 advances 'a slap in the face'.
src: But on Monday, Burundi’s Foreign Minister Edouard Bizimana warned that “any attack targeting Burundian citizens or soldiers deployed in the DRC will never be tolerated.

r1-UV-2025Q4-021.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that captured Burundian soldiers would be handed over to their country's authorities, and that Uvira was totally under M23 control.
r1-UV-2025Q4-021.n: Partisan statement relayed by SOS Médias Burundi (originating: AFC/M23 communiqué). Date computed: 'mercredi soir' with article dated 2025-12-11 gives 2025-12-10. The M23 claim of captured Burundian soldiers is the party's; no independent figure given.
r1-UV-2025Q4-021.vn: Verbatim; 'mercredi soir' with article dated Thu 11 Dec gives 10 Dec. Party statement. Kanyuka also called on FARDC and Wazalendo still in Uvira to surrender (same page).
src: « Les soldats burundais capturés seront remis aux autorités de leur pays dans le strict respect des droits humains », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC/M23, dans un communiqué qu’il a partagé avec SOS Médias Burundi mercredi soir. Il a ajouté que la ville d’Uvira est totalement sous contrôle du M23

r1-UV-2025Q4-022.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Burundian delegation was forced to go to Luvungi, in South Kivu, to demand the return of its captured soldiers and negotiate a secure corridor for its troops encircled in the Hauts-Plateaux.
r1-UV-2025Q4-022.a: Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and AFC/M23
r1-UV-2025Q4-022.n: Single local-exile outlet (SOS Médias Burundi) relying on 'sources sécuritaires' per its text; no confirmation from Burundi (Anadolu: no immediate reaction). Burundi's presence figures are contested; Kagame says >20,000, which is a partisan assertion.
r1-UV-2025Q4-022.vn: Single clause, verbatim (outlet narration). Kept at C. Single exile-run outlet; its following paragraph attributes the delegation details (four senior Burundian security officials, release of soldiers including a colonel, corridor for troops in Lemera groupement) to security sources in Cibitoke. No Burundian confirmation found.
src: une délégation burundaise, qui a emprunté Cibitoke, la région frontalière avec le vaste pays de l’Afrique centrale, a été contrainte de se rendre à Luvungi, dans le Sud-Kivu à l’est du Congo, pour réclamer la restitution de ses militaires capturés et négocier un corridor sécurisé permettant à ses troupes encerclées dans les Hauts-Plateaux de regagner le Burundi.

r1-UV-2025Q4-023.s: Al Jazeera reported that AFC leader Corneille Nangaa posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday confirming that fighters would withdraw from Uvira 'as per United States mediation request', and that the coalition called the move a 'unilateral trust-building measure' and called for a neutral force to monitor the ceasefire.
r1-UV-2025Q4-023.n: Date: the page is dated 2025-12-16 and says the statement was posted 'on Tuesday' (16 Dec). Partisan statement; the post itself was not opened. Al Jazeera's correspondent in Uvira reported 'nothing had changed' as of Tuesday morning with M23 fighters still seen.
r1-UV-2025Q4-023.vn: Removed publication date from statement; party statement attributed. 'Tuesday' read as 16 Dec 2025 (article date). Al Jazeera's correspondent said 'nothing had changed' as of Tuesday morning. The X post itself was not opened.
src: Corneille Nangaa, leader of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) rebel coalition, which includes the M23 group, posted a signed statement on X on Tuesday that confirmed fighters would withdraw from the town located in South Kivu province, near the border with Burundi, “as per United States mediation request”.

The coalition called the move a “unilateral trust-building measure” aimed at giving the “Doha peace process the maximum chance to succeed”, calling on “guarantors of the peace process” to oversee demilitarisation and protection of the town’s population and infrastructure, and to monitor the ceasefire with “the deployment of a neutral force”.

r1-UV-2025Q4-024.s: BBC Afrique reported that M23 chief Bertrand Bisimwa said on Wednesday that the withdrawal from Uvira was 'underway', with spokesperson Willy Ngoma adding it was 'in the interest of peace'.
