r1-UV-2025Q4-024.n: Date computed from weekday ('mercredi') and article date 2025-12-19. Bisimwa also urged mediators to ensure the city is protected from 'reprisals, violence and remilitarisation' (same page).
r1-UV-2025Q4-024.vn: Removed publication date. 'Wednesday' read as 17 Dec 2025 from the article date (19 Dec). Bisimwa also urged mediators on X to protect the city from 'reprisals, violence and remilitarisation'.
src: Le chef du M23, Bertrand Bisimwa, a déclaré mercredi que le retrait était « en cours », le porte-parole Willy Ngoma ajoutant que c'était « dans l'intérêt de la paix ».

r1-UV-2025Q4-025.s: Kigali Today reported that the rebel coalition announced it was ready to leave Uvira, asking that soldiers and all other armed people be removed from the city and that neutral forces be deployed to protect civilians and infrastructure and help enforce the ceasefire.
r1-UV-2025Q4-025.n: Kigali-based outlet; party statement relayed. The page states that AFC/M23 seized Uvira on 12 December 2025, which differs from other outlets (9/10 Dec).
r1-UV-2025Q4-025.vn: Removed publication date; added the demilitarisation request the excerpt carries. Kigali-based outlet (byline Jean Claude Munyantore). It states AFC/M23 seized Uvira on 12 December 2025, which differs from other sources (9/10 Dec). The statement's subject is AFC/M23 as named in the page title.
src: Mu byo uyu mutwe usaba kugira ngo wubahirize ibyo wiyemeje, harimo kandi ko umujyi wa Uvira wakurwamo abasirikare n’abandi bose bitwaje intwaro bahasanzwe, hakabaho kurinda abaturage n’ibikorwa remezo, ari yo mpamvu usaba ko hashyirwaho ingabo zitabogama zanafasha kubahiriza ihagarikwa ry’imirwano (ceasefire).

r1-UV-2025Q4-026.s: Al Jazeera reported that US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday that Rwanda's actions in eastern DRC were a 'clear violation' of the peace deal, and said in a post on X that the United States would take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept.
r1-UV-2025Q4-026.n: Context statement by a mediator. The post (x.com/SecRubio/status/1999829630618919050) was not opened; the page says 'Saturday' and is dated 2025-12-13.
r1-UV-2025Q4-026.vn: Removed publication date. 'Saturday' = 13 Dec 2025 (article date). Al Jazeera (16 Dec) quotes the same post as a 'clear violation of the Washington Accords'. The X post was not opened.
src: Rwanda’s actions in eastern DRC are a “clear violation” of the peace deal US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said on Saturday. “The United States will take action to ensure promises made to the president are kept,” he said in a post on X.

r1-UV-2025Q4-027.s: The International Contact Group for the Great Lakes (United States, Belgium, Denmark, the EU, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Sweden, Switzerland and the UK) urged M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and called on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC.
r1-UV-2025Q4-027.a: International Contact Group for the Great Lakes
r1-UV-2025Q4-027.n: Official joint statement published by the US State Department. Also expresses concern at increased use of attack and suicide drones (same page).
r1-UV-2025Q4-027.vn: Removed date (number not in excerpt; it is the source date); fixed 'withdraw' to 'withdraw from eastern DRC'. Credited to all ICG members, not to the hosting State Department. Grade B: one primary origin. Joint statement dated 9 Dec 2025 (Media Note, Office of the Spokesman). It also expresses concern at increased use of attack and suicide drones.
src: The ICG urges the M23 and the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) to immediately halt offensive operations in eastern DRC, in particular in South Kivu, and calls on the RDF to withdraw from eastern DRC

r1-UV-2025Q4-028.s: BBC Afrique reported that the DRC government spokesperson Me Didier Kabi called the rebels' announced withdrawal from Uvira a 'mise en scène' orchestrated by the rebels to reduce pressure from partners, and that the DRC authorities said they held credible information of a 'dissimulation teintée de retrait'; BBC Afrique noted that government forces had not returned to the city.
r1-UV-2025Q4-028.n: Government account; BBC could not independently confirm. Date: the page is dated 2025-12-19 and says the briefing came 'the day after' the M23 announcement (17 Dec), so about 18 Dec. Kabi also said M23 troops remained 9 km from Uvira and at Kiliba (same page).
r1-UV-2025Q4-028.vn: The 'forces had not returned' clause is BBC's narration, not the government's statement: re-attributed. Grade raised to B: a credible outlet reporting an on-record official statement. BBC says the briefing came 'au lendemain' of the AFC/M23 leaders' withdrawal announcement. Kabi also said M23 forces remained 9 km from Uvira and had not passed Kiliba (12 km). BBC describes both Kabi and Patrick Muyaya as government spokesperson.
src: Pour le porte-parole du gouvernement, Me Didier Kabi, cette annonce est une "mise en scène" orchestrée par les rebelles pour réduire la pression des partenaires qui pèse sur eux. Les autorités de la RDC indiquent détenir des informations crédibles qui "font état d'une dissimulation teintée de retrait".
Le gouvernement congolais maintient donc son scepticisme quant à ce retrait, les forces gouvernementales n'étant pas retournées dans la ville.

r1-UV-2025Q4-029.s: BBC Afrique reported that DRC government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya told the BBC Newsday programme that the M23 announcement aimed to 'divert the attention of the American mediation team', which he said was preparing to take measures against Rwanda, and that he called the decision to leave Uvira a 'positive sign' while saying the government needed to confirm the situation on the ground.
r1-UV-2025Q4-029.n: Date approximate: the page (2025-12-19) does not give the day of the interview. Muyaya also posted on X questions about mass graves and soldiers disguised as civilians (same page).
r1-UV-2025Q4-029.vn: Kept the full quoted purpose rather than a paraphrase that dropped 'preparing to take measures against Rwanda'; date set as a range. Day of the interview not given; range runs from the 16 Dec announcement to the 19 Dec article. Muyaya also asked on X about mass graves and soldiers disguised as civilians.
src: Le porte-parole du gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo, Patrick Muyaya, a déclaré à l'émission BBC Newsday que l'annonce du M23 visait à « détourner l'attention de l'équipe de médiation américaine, qui se prépare à prendre des mesures contre le Rwanda ».
M. Muyaya a qualifié la décision du M23 de quitter Uvira de « signe positif », mais a ajouté que le gouvernement devait confirmer la situation sur le terrain.

r1-UV-2025Q4-030.s: BBC Afrique reported that a local civil-society member, speaking anonymously, said some M23 troops had begun to withdraw from Uvira but that police belonging to the same group continued to arrive, while another inhabitant expressed doubts about the withdrawal.
r1-UV-2025Q4-030.n: Anonymous source; BBC does not give the day (a resident refers to 'jeudi matin', i.e. 18 Dec).
r1-UV-2025Q4-030.vn: Removed publication date; anonymous sources kept at C. The inhabitant spoke to the BBC 'jeudi matin' (18 Dec); the civil-society member's day is not given.
src: Un membre de la société civile locale, qui a souhaité rester anonyme pour des raisons de sécurité, a déclaré à la BBC que certaines troupes du M23 avaient commencé à se retirer. Cependant, il a ajouté que des policiers appartenant au même groupe continuaient d'affluer.

r1-UV-2025Q4-031.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dated Uvira, 24 November 2025) that clashes between groups claiming allegiance to the Wazalendo and the FARDC had left about six people dead and more than fifteen wounded between Sunday and Monday, 24 November 2025.
r1-UV-2025Q4-031.a: groups claiming allegiance to Wazalendo and FARDC
r1-UV-2025Q4-031.x: SOS Médias Burundi: about 6 killed, more than 15 wounded (Sun-Mon); FARDC statement: 4 killed, 14 wounded (Sunday)
r1-UV-2025Q4-031.n: Single exile-run outlet; toll differs from the FARDC statement (4 killed, 14 wounded) recorded separately. Neighbourhoods Kalundu and Kalimabenge named elsewhere on the page as hit by gunfire since Monday afternoon.
r1-UV-2025Q4-031.vn: Verbatim. Category changed: the source describes armed clashes between Wazalendo-affiliated groups and the FARDC, and does not say the dead were civilians. Single exile-run outlet; the FARDC's own toll (4 killed, 14 wounded, for Sunday) is recorded separately. The page says Kalundu and Kalimabenge neighbourhoods were hit by gunfire from Monday afternoon. Victims' status (civilian or combatant) not given for this toll.
src: Mapigano kati ya makundi yanayodai utiifu kwa Wazalendo na Jeshi la DRC (FARDC) yamesababisha takriban watu sita kuuawa na wengine zaidi ya kumi na tano kujeruhiwa kati ya Jumapili na Jumatatu, Novemba 24, 2025.

r1-UV-2025Q4-032.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement published on 23 November the FARDC denounced violence by what it called 'fake Wazalendo'; per the army, Sunday's clashes killed four people (one FARDC soldier, two Wazalendo fighters, a civilian motorcycle rider) and wounded 14.
r1-UV-2025Q4-032.x: FARDC: 4 killed (1 soldier, 2 Wazalendo, 1 civilian motorcyclist); 14 wounded (9 civilians, 2 soldiers, 3 Wazalendo)
r1-UV-2025Q4-032.n: Official FARDC statement as relayed by SOS Médias Burundi; the FARDC statement itself was not opened.
r1-UV-2025Q4-032.vn: Verbatim (Swahili). The army also said it recovered three AK-47 rifles. The FARDC statement itself was not opened. SOS Médias' own toll (about 6 killed, 15+ wounded, Sun-Mon) differs.
src: Katika taarifa iliyochapishwa mnamo Novemba 23, FARDC ilishutumu ghasia zinazofanywa na kile wanachoita “Wazalendo feki,”

Kwa mujibu wa jeshi hilo, mapigano ya Jumapili yalisababisha vifo vya watu wanne: askari mmoja wa FARDC, wapiganaji wawili wa Wazalendo, na mwendesha pikipiki raia. Wengine 14 walijeruhiwa, wakiwemo raia tisa, wanajeshi wawili na wapiganaji watatu wa Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q4-033.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 23 November, at Luvungi in the Ruzizi plain, a man known as Huruma, described as a 'fake Wazalendo' and as having been a guardian (mlezi) of the Holy Family Parish, fired live rounds during diocesan youth celebrations at the Holy Family Catholic Church, killing two people and wounding five; the Diocese of Uvira strongly condemned the act.
r1-UV-2025Q4-033.l: Luvungi, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2025Q4-033.a: 'fake Wazalendo' (as FARDC and SOS Médias name them)
r1-UV-2025Q4-033.n: Single outlet. The shooter is named only as 'Huruma' by the source. Victims are not named.
r1-UV-2025Q4-033.vn: Narrowed the translation of 'aliyekuwa mlezi' and 'sherehe za vijana kijimbo'. Single outlet. 'Huruma' is the alleged shooter as named by the source; being named is not a finding of responsibility. 'Mlezi' (guardian/patron) is ambiguous; draft's 'former caretaker' over-translated it. Wounded were taken to Luvungi hospital and Uvira's main hospital. Victims not named.
src: Jumapili, Novemba 23, katika Uwanda wa Ruzizi huko Luvungi, mtu mmoja aliyejulikana kwa jina la Huruma, aliyetolewa kwa jina la Wazalendo feki na aliyekuwa mlezi wa Parokia ya Familia Takatifu, alifyatua risasi za moto wakati wa sherehe za vijana kijimbo katika Kanisa Katoliki la Familia Takatifu. Shambulio hilo lilisababisha vifo vya watu wawili na watano kujeruhiwa.
Dayosisi ya Uvira ililaani vikali kitendo hicho, huku majeruhi wamelazwa katika hospitali ya Luvungi na hospitali kuu ya Uvira kwa matibabu ya dharura.

r1-UV-2025Q4-034.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in Sange on Saturday 22 November two Wazalendo were killed in clashes between two rival groups, those of Kamama and Ngomanzito, according to local sources.
r1-UV-2025Q4-034.n: Single outlet citing local sources; 'Kamama' and 'Ngomanzito' are names of groups/leaders as printed.
r1-UV-2025Q4-034.vn: Single clause, verbatim; local sources attributed.
src: Katika mji wa Sange, Jumamosi, Novemba 22, Wazalendo wawili waliuawa katika mapigano kati ya makundi mawili hasimu, yale ya Kamama na Ngomanzito, kulingana na vyanzo vya ndani.

r1-UV-2025Q4-035.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that several Uvira members of parliament, including national deputy Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, condemned abuses and killings attributed to some Wazalendo elements.
r1-UV-2025Q4-035.n: Date follows the article's Uvira dateline (24 Nov); the day of the condemnation is not stated. The response of the deputies is a political statement, not an administrative measure; category chosen for lack of a closer fit.
r1-UV-2025Q4-035.vn: Single clause, verbatim. Category changed: a political statement by deputies, not de facto governance. Day of the condemnation not stated; article dateline Uvira, 24 Nov 2025.
src: Wakikabiliwa na ongezeko hili, wabunge kadhaa kutoka Uvira, akiwemo Justin Bitakwira Bihona-Hayi, naibu wa kitaifa kutoka Uvira, walilaani dhuluma na mauaji yanayohusishwa na baadhi ya vipengele vya Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2025Q4-036.s: Actualite.cd reported that during the disorder that night, FARDC soldiers and their wazalendo allies stripped and ransacked the Iàmba health centre in the Bangwe sub-village (Nundu health zone) at Makobola, and a member of the Iàmba health-area development committee said they broke the doors from the pharmacy, looted all the medicines and took all the equipment from the head nurse's office.
r1-UV-2025Q4-036.a: FARDC soldiers and wazalendo (as Actualite.cd's sources attribute)
r1-UV-2025Q4-036.n: Single outlet, citing local sources; the FARDC were not quoted. 'Fizi' territory, but linked by the source to troops returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira.
r1-UV-2025Q4-036.vn: Statement's date figure is not in the excerpts (date is in the date field and on the page); reworded to the excerpts. Grade C: single outlet on unnamed local sources, uncorroborated. Single outlet citing local sources; FARDC not quoted. Actualite.cd calls it the main health facility serving the area. Civil society demanded an inquiry. Makobola is in Fizi territory.
src: Lors des désordres cette nuit-là, ces militaires et wazalendo ont dépouillé et saccagé le centre de santé Iàmba, situé dans le sous-village de Bangwe, dans la zone de santé Nundu.

"Ils ont cassé les portes à partir de la pharmacie et pillé tous les médicaments avant de s'introduire dans le bureau de l'infirmière titulaire où ils ont emporté tous les matériels en saccageant le bureau", a dit à ACTUALITE.CD , un cadre du comité de développement de l’aire de santé d’Iàmba.

r1-UV-2025Q4-037.s: Actualite.cd reported that multiple cases of sexual assault of women were reported in the FARDC and wazalendo expedition into Makobola; a local civil-society actor said the women were forced to help carry looted goods and returned to their homes after being raped.
r1-UV-2025Q4-037.a: FARDC soldiers and wazalendo (as Actualite.cd's sources attribute)
r1-UV-2025Q4-037.n: Number of survivors not given. Survivors are not named. A civil-society demand for an inquiry is reported on the page.
r1-UV-2025Q4-037.vn: Removed day numbers absent from the excerpts. Grade C: single outlet, unnamed sources. Number of survivors not given; survivors not named. Same night of 29-30 Dec as the health-centre looting.
src: Des multiples cas d’agression sexuelle dont des femmes ont été victimes sont aussi rapportés dans cette expédition des FARDC et wazalendo dans la cité de Makobola.

"Ils ont forcé les portes des maisons des habitants et emportaient tout ce qu’ils ont trouvé, même la nourriture. Et ils ont obligé les femmes de les aider à transporter et ces dernières devraient regagner leurs maisons après avoir été violées", a dit un acteur de la société civile locale.

r1-UV-2025Q4-038.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to its sources in the region, the Makobola disorder broke out after a disagreement, for reasons not yet clarified, between soldiers of the Guépard unit returning from the Kigongo front at Uvira and soldiers of the Hiboux unit; some sources spoke of dissension between the commands of the two units.
r1-UV-2025Q4-038.l: Makobola, Fizi territory, South Kivu (Kigongo front, Uvira)
r1-UV-2025Q4-038.a: soldiers of the 'Guépard' and 'Hiboux' units (as Actualite.cd's sources describe them)
r1-UV-2025Q4-038.n: Units are named by the source without further identification (the page does not say whether 'Guépard' and 'Hiboux' are FARDC units; it describes 'militaires'). Commanders not named. Place 'Kigongo' is a front position near Uvira per the source.
r1-UV-2025Q4-038.vn: Actor narrowed to the source's wording; grade C (single outlet on unnamed sources). The page heads the story as FARDC and wazalendo looting but does not state the units' formation or commanders.
src: Selon des sources d’ ACTUALITE.CD dans la région, des troubles ont éclaté dans la cité suite à une mésentente entre des militaires de l’unité Guépard qui revenaient du front de Kigongo à Uvira et ceux de l'unité Hiboux pour des raisons non encore élucidées. Certaines sources contactées parlent de dissension entre les commandements de deux unités.

r1-UV-2025Q4-039.s: BBC reported that Burundi had shut its border with DR Congo, a Burundian military source was quoted as saying by AFP.
r1-UV-2025Q4-039.n: Original source AFP (per the BBC page); the BBC text does not name the Burundian source. Border posts named in other reports (Gatumba, Vugizo) were not opened.
r1-UV-2025Q4-039.vn: Removed publication date; wire origin credited to AFP. SOS Médias Burundi (11 Dec) separately reports Burundian authorities closed the Gatumba-Kavimvira and Vugizo posts.
src: Burundi has shut its border with DR Congo, a Burundian military source was quoted as saying by AFP news agency.

r1-UV-2026Q1-001.s: Ebuteli (Kivu Security Barometer) reported that on 16 January the AFC/M23 rebels withdrew from the city of Uvira and repositioned at Sange, about 30 km from Uvira, a crossroads to the middle and high plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, notably towards Mulenge and Lubarika.
r1-UV-2026Q1-001.l: Uvira city to Sange, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q1-001.n: Conflicts with SOS Médias Burundi (separate claim), which says the last M23 elements began leaving on Saturday evening (17 Jan) and finished Sunday morning (18 Jan). Ebuteli is a local monitor; Congo Indépendant and others show M23/RDF/AFC elements still near the city (Kabunambo) on 19 Jan.
r1-UV-2026Q1-001.vn: Excerpt on the page, in Ebuteli's January 2026 section on Uvira; statement matches. Withdrawal date differs across sources: 16 Jan (Ebuteli), Saturday evening to Sunday morning 17-18 Jan (SOS Médias Burundi), 18 Jan (FARDC communiqué), 'fin janvier' (Radio Okapi, 17 Mar).
src: Le 16 janvier, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 se sont retirés de la ville d’Uvira. Ils se sont repositionnés à Sange, située à environ 30 km d’Uvira, carrefour d’accès aux moyens et hauts plateaux d’Uvira et de Fizi, notamment vers Mulenge et Lubarika.

r1-UV-2026Q1-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the last elements of the rebel movement began leaving the city of Uvira on Saturday evening and completed the operation on Sunday morning.
r1-UV-2026Q1-002.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article dated 2026-01-20; Saturday = 2026-01-17, Sunday = 2026-01-18). Differs from Ebuteli's 16 January. Single local outlet.
r1-UV-2026Q1-002.vn: Removed the publication date (on 20 January) from the statement per the project rule. The movement is the M23 (actor field), named in the preceding sentence on the page; the name is kept out of the corrected statement because no excerpt prints it. Weekdays only in the source; with the article dated 20 January 2026 they fall on 17-18 January. Differs from Ebuteli (16 Jan).
src: Les derniers éléments du mouvement ont commencé à quitter la ville samedi soir pour achever l’opération dimanche matin.

r1-UV-2026Q1-003.s: Ebuteli reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo retook the city of Uvira on 18 January, and that several abuses, often linked to attempted extortion, followed; an army communiqué reported by Actualite.cd also dated the retaking to Sunday 18 January 2026.
r1-UV-2026Q1-003.n: FARDC communiqué (via Actualite.cd) and Ebuteli agree on 18 January. Congo Indépendant (2026-01-21) writes 'samedi 18 janvier', but 18 January 2026 was a Sunday. Radio Okapi (2026-03-17) elsewhere dates the M23 withdrawal to 'fin janvier 2026'.
r1-UV-2026Q1-003.vn: The raw statement credited only Ebuteli though it rests on two sources; added the FARDC communiqué clause. Grade lowered A->B: one credible monitor plus a party's communiqué. The second source is the army's own communiqué (a party). Congo Indépendant writes 'samedi 18 janvier', but 18 January 2026 was a Sunday.
src: Alors que les FARDC et les Wazalendo reprenaient la ville le 18 janvier, plusieurs exactions s’en sont suivies, souvent liées à des tentatives d’extorsion.
Selon un communiqué de l’armée parvenu à la rédaction d’ACTUALITE.CD ce lundi 19 janvier 2026, cette reprise de contrôle est intervenue la veille, soit le dimanche 18 janvier 2026.

r1-UV-2026Q1-004.s: Congo Indépendant reported, citing local sources, that M23/RDF/AFC elements remained on 19 January in the Ruzizi plain and close to the city, notably at Kabunambo, less than one kilometre from the centre.
r1-UV-2026Q1-004.l: Kabunambo and Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory
r1-UV-2026Q1-004.n: Single media outlet citing unnamed local sources; relayed in Radio Okapi/Actualite.cd framing as 'faux retrait'.
r1-UV-2026Q1-004.vn: Excerpt on the page; attributed to unnamed local sources as the page says.
src: Sur le terrain, le calme observé lundi 19 janvier reste apparent. Des sources locales signalent la présence persistante d’éléments M23/RDF/AFC dans la plaine de la Ruzizi et à proximité immédiate de la ville, notamment à Kabunambo, à moins d’un kilomètre du centre.

r1-UV-2026Q1-005.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Wazalendo militias, taking advantage of the vacuum left by the M23, advanced towards Uvira and took control of the village of Kirungu, 15 km from the city, and fired on several mountains overlooking Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q1-005.a: Wazalendo militias (described as supported by Kinshasa)
r1-UV-2026Q1-005.n: Exact date not stated; follows the M23 departure of 17-18 Jan. Radio Okapi (2026-03-17) later reports Kirungu fell to a rebel coalition on 16 March, so the village changed hands.
r1-UV-2026Q1-005.vn: Supported; 'M23' is printed in the preceding sentence on the page. Radio Okapi puts Kirungu four hours' walk upstream of Uvira and reports it fell to the rebel coalition on 16 March 2026.
src: Cependant, les milices Wazalendo, soutenues par Kinshasa, ont profité de ce vide pour progresser vers Uvira, prenant le contrôle du village de Kirungu, à 15 km de la ville, et tirant sur plusieurs montagnes surplombant Uvira, provoquant panique et déplacements de populations.

r1-UV-2026Q1-006.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the locality of Kirungu, four hours' walk upstream of Uvira, fell on the evening of Monday 16 March under the control of the rebel coalition, a site linking Uvira to the middle and high plateaux of Minembwe.
r1-UV-2026Q1-006.a: rebel coalition (Radio Okapi's description: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Ngumino, FNL-Zabampema and AFC-M23)
r1-UV-2026Q1-006.n: Single outlet, local sources. FARDC/government account of Kirungu not found in this unit.
r1-UV-2026Q1-006.vn: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches.
src: La localité de Kirungu, située à quatre heures de marche à pied en amont d'Uvira, est tombée lundi 16 mars dans la soirée sous le contrôle de la coalition rebelle, selon des sources locales.
Ce site stratégique relie Uvira aux moyens et hauts plateaux de Minembwe, bastion de la coalition Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Ngumino, FNL-Zabampema et AFC-M23.

r1-UV-2026Q1-007.s: Ebuteli reported that the Twirwaneho occupied the zones around the 'point zéro', a strategic position controlling the high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, and that the FARDC had thinned out the middle and high plateaux to position themselves in the city of Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q1-007.l: Point zéro, high plateaux of Fizi and Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q1-007.vn: Excerpt on the page in the January 2026 report.
src: Les Twirwaneho ont occupé les zones autour du « point zéro », position stratégique pour le contrôle des hauts plateaux de Fizi et d'Uvira. La zone des moyens et des hauts plateaux avait été dégarnie par les FARDC pour se positionner dans la ville d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q1-008.s: Human Rights Watch said that the M23 withdrew from Uvira in January 2026 and maintains positions to its north, in the Ruzizi Plain, and in the Hauts Plateaux, the highlands southwest of the city, and that fighting continues between the M23 and Congolese forces and their Wazalendo allies.
r1-UV-2026Q1-008.l: North of Uvira, Ruzizi Plain and Hauts Plateaux
r1-UV-2026Q1-008.n: HRW researchers visited Uvira in March 2026.
r1-UV-2026Q1-008.vn: Both passages on the HRW page. Grade B rather than A: positions are background in an interview by HRW researchers, not a documented finding of the investigation.
src: The M23 withdrew from Uvira in January 2026 and maintains positions to its north, in the Ruzizi Plain, and in the Hauts Plateaux, the highlands southwest of the city.
Despite the withdrawal, the M23 maintains strongholds just north of the city and fighting continues between the M23 and Congolese forces and their Wazalendo allies.

r1-UV-2026Q1-009.s: Actualite.cd reported that an army communiqué signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba, acting FARDC spokesperson, deplored the systematic pillage of the city by soldiers of the AFC/M23-RDF coalition before their evacuation, and said some twenty civilians involved in looting were arrested and would be brought before the courts.
r1-UV-2026Q1-009.n: Party statement (Kinshasa/FARDC); the pillage accusation against M23/RDF is not independently confirmed here. M23's rebuttal is a separate claim.
r1-UV-2026Q1-009.vn: Party statement, relayed accurately by Actualite.cd (byline Clément Muamba).
src: Dans le même document, signé par le lieutenant-colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba, commandant adjoint du service de communication et d’information des FARDC, chargé des opérations et du renseignement et porte-parole ad intérim des FARDC, l’armée déplore le pillage systématique de la ville par les militaires de la coalition AFC/M23-RDF avant leur évacuation.
Elle précise qu’une vingtaine de civils impliqués dans ces actes de pillage ont été interpellés et seront déférés devant la justice.

r1-UV-2026Q1-010.s: Congo Indépendant reported that the army deplored systematic pillage attributed to M23/RDF/AFC elements before their evacuation, and that the rebels rejected these accusations and blamed the abuses on the army and its Wazalendo allies.
r1-UV-2026Q1-010.n: Rebel rebuttal is relayed without a named speaker or primary link. Date window = FARDC communiqué (19 Jan) to publication (21 Jan).
r1-UV-2026Q1-010.vn: Excerpt on the page; statement matches. The rebel rebuttal is relayed without a named speaker or link.
src: l’armée déplore des pillages systématiques imputés aux éléments de la coalition M23/RDF/AFC avant leur évacuation. Du berger à la bergère, les rebelles rejettent ces accusations et imputent les exactions à l’armée et ses alliés Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2026Q1-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that Defence Minister Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita told the Council of Ministers that security forces had returned to Uvira to ensure public order and that the scenario of chaos foreseen by the rebellion after its withdrawal had been foiled.
r1-UV-2026Q1-011.n: Government account as reported by Actualite.cd from the Council of Ministers minutes; party statement.
r1-UV-2026Q1-011.vn: Excerpt on the page; the Council date is on the page (page-only clause).
src: Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, a fait état du retour des forces de sécurité à Uvira afin d’y assurer l’ordre public et la sécurité des populations. À cette occasion, il a indiqué que le scénario de chaos présagé par la rébellion après son retrait de la ville avait été déjoué

r1-UV-2026Q1-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the DRC government announced a plan for the progressive restoration of State authority in the city of Uvira and its surroundings, including coordinated security, judicial and humanitarian measures.
r1-UV-2026Q1-012.n: Radio Okapi published 2026-01-20; a government communiqué dated 19 January is referred to in the same article.
src: Le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo annonce la mise en œuvre d’un plan de restauration progressive de l’autorité de l’État dans la ville d’Uvira et ses environs. Ce plan inclut des mesures sécuritaires, judiciaires et humanitaires coordonnées, destinées à rétablir durablement la sécurité, protéger les populations civiles et favoriser la stabilisation de cette partie du territoire national.

r1-UV-2026Q1-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that the government communiqué of Monday 19 January denounced the deportation of civilian populations, in particular members of the Banyamulenge community, alleging that some were forced to leave Uvira by the AFC/M23 to be used as justification for the movement's presence on Congolese soil.
r1-UV-2026Q1-013.n: Government allegation, unverified; AFC/M23 reply not found in this unit.
r1-UV-2026Q1-013.vn: Excerpt on the page; conditional 'auraient' kept as an allegation.
src: Dans son communiqué publié le lundi 19 janvier, le gouvernement congolais dénonce la déportation de populations civiles, en particulier des membres de la communauté Banyamulenge. Certains auraient été forcés de quitter Uvira par l’AFC/M23 afin d’être utilisés comme justification de la présence du mouvement armé sur le sol congolais.

r1-UV-2026Q1-014.s: Congo Indépendant reported that, after an emergency meeting chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya gave a stocktake of 1,500 dead, 3,000 displaced and 12,000 children out of school and separated from their parents.
r1-UV-2026Q1-014.x: Government spokesperson (per Congo Indépendant): 1,500 dead; 3,000 displaced; 12,000 children
r1-UV-2026Q1-014.n: The article writes 'lundi 20 janvier 2026' but 20 January 2026 was a Tuesday (the same article says 'lundi 19 janvier' elsewhere), so the day is uncertain. The '3.000 déplacés' figure is as printed and is far below the ~267,000 refugees/displaced the same article cites later. The article names the spokesperson as Patrick Muyaya elsewhere (not in this excerpt). The 1,500 figure is the one the government later repeated (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) and Ebuteli counts 151 civilians killed in Uvira territory for December; HRW says 'at least several dozen'.
r1-UV-2026Q1-014.vn: Supported; the spokesperson's name is printed elsewhere on the page (page-only clause). The article dates the meeting 'lundi 20 janvier 2026', but 20 January 2026 was a Tuesday. '3,000 displaced' is as printed and far below the 267,000 the same article gives.
src: A l’issue d’une « réunion d’urgence » présidée, lundi 20 janvier 2026, par la Première ministre Judith Suminwa, le porte parole du gouvernement a fait un compte-rendu aux allures d’ « état des lieux »: 1.500 morts, 3.000 déplacés, 12.000 enfants non scolarisés et séparés de leurs parents.

r1-UV-2026Q1-015.s: Congo Indépendant reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said the withdrawal of the Rwandan forces could not be interpreted as a gesture of appeasement nor as the end of the aggression.
r1-UV-2026Q1-015.n: Exact day not stated beyond the January emergency meeting.
src: Pour le porte-parole du gouvernement, Patrick Muyaya, le retrait des forces rwandaises ne saurait être interprété comme un geste d’apaisement ni comme la fin de l’agression.

r1-UV-2026Q1-016.s: Congo Indépendant reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, sceptical, spoke of a 'faux retrait' (false withdrawal) and called for vigilance, judging that the enemy remains active and cunning.
r1-UV-2026Q1-016.n: Date approximate: placed in the article's account of 19 January.
r1-UV-2026Q1-016.vn: Excerpt on the page; the article gives no date for the remark, so the date is approximate.
src: Tel un « chat échaudé qui craint l’eau froide », le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, reste sceptique. Aussi, parle-t-il d’un « faux retrait » et appelle à la vigilance, estimant que l’ennemi demeure actif et rusé.

r1-UV-2026Q1-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa, in a letter of Thursday 15 January 2026 to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, announced that he had placed the city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community.
r1-UV-2026Q1-017.n: Party statement relayed by a Congolese outlet that also frames it as controversial; the letter itself was not seen. Kinshasa's reading (diversion from US pressure on Kigali) is in the same article.
r1-UV-2026Q1-017.vn: Excerpt on the page; letter itself not seen.
src: Ce retrait fait suite à une correspondance adressée le jeudi 15 janvier 2026 au Secrétaire général des Nations unies, António Guterres, par le coordonnateur politique de la rébellion de l’AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa. Dans cette lettre, il annonçait avoir placé la ville stratégique d’Uvira sous la responsabilité de la communauté internationale.

r1-UV-2026Q1-018.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a message on X on Wednesday 14 January, accused Congolese authorities of repeated ceasefire violations and said drones of the Kinshasa coalition forces bombed the port of Kalundu around 2:20 p.m., causing significant material damage and loss of life.
r1-UV-2026Q1-018.n: Party statement; SOS Médias Burundi says Kanyuka gave no figures. Post itself not opened.
r1-UV-2026Q1-018.vn: Excerpt on the page (English edition). SOS Médias Burundi says he gave no figures.
src: In a message posted on Wednesday, January 14, on the social media X (formerly Twitter), AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accused Congolese authorities of repeated violations of the ceasefire in effect in eastern DRC. He claims that drones belonging to the Kinshasa coalition forces bombed the port of Kalundu around 2:20 p.m., causing significant material damage and loss of life.

r1-UV-2026Q1-019.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing a MONUSCO communiqué, that MONUSCO and the ICGLR (CIRGL) were on a mission in Uvira from 23 to 27 February to prepare deployment of the joint ceasefire monitoring mechanism, and quoted acting Special Representative Vivian Van de Perre as saying MONUSCO's mandate in South Kivu is focused on ceasefire monitoring and does not include protection of civilians.
r1-UV-2026Q1-019.n: Mediator/UN context. Note the PoC limitation for investigators.
src: En mission du 23 au 27 février à Uvira (Sud-Kivu), la Mission de l’Organisation des Nations unies pour la stabilisation en RDC (MONUSCO) et la Conférence internationale sur la région des Grands Lacs (CIRGL) préparent le déploiement du Mécanisme conjoint de suivi du cessez-le-feu.

Contrairement au Nord-Kivu et à l’Ituri, le mandat de la MONUSCO au Sud-Kivu est axé sur le suivi du cessez-le-feu et n’inclut pas la Protection des civils (PoC), conformément à la Résolution 2808 (2025) », a déclaré la Représentante spéciale intérimaire du Secrétaire général de l’ONU en RDC, Vivian Van de Perre.

r1-UV-2026Q1-020.s: Iwacu reported that on 2 January 2026 the secretary general of Burundi's ruling CNDD-FDD party, Révérien Ndikuriyo, said at a Bujumbura press conference: 'Nous avons un accord qui nous permet d’intervenir au Congo', a reply Iwacu described as radically different from the Burundian ambassador's earlier claim of withdrawal.
r1-UV-2026Q1-020.l: Bujumbura (statement on Burundian forces in eastern DRC)
r1-UV-2026Q1-020.n: Speaker is a party official, not a state office; the article also quotes him on Burundian soldiers still being there (not used as an excerpt because the page prints an ellipsis). Burundian government/army did not comment on Uvira in the pages fetched.
r1-UV-2026Q1-020.vn: Both excerpts on the page (byline Stine Akimana). On the same page Ndikuriyo is also quoted: 'les militaires burundais sont toujours là'.
src: Le 2 janvier 2026, lors d’une conférence de presse tenue à Bujumbura dans une salle pleine à craquer, largement dominée par les couleurs rouge, vert et blanc du parti au pouvoir, le secrétaire général du CNDD-FDD, Révérien Ndikuriyo, a livré une réponse radicalement différente.
« Nous avons un accord qui nous permet d’intervenir au Congo.

r1-UV-2026Q1-021.s: Iwacu reported that on 17 December 2025 Burundi's ambassador to the EU, Thérence Ntahiraja, told the European Parliament that the Burundian army had withdrawn its troops from eastern DRC after the peace accord, and that this is why the Rwandan army and the M23 advanced easily to Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q1-021.l: Brussels (statement on Burundian forces and Uvira)
r1-UV-2026Q1-021.n: Outside the unit's quarter but included because it frames the Burundian presence question; contradicted by Ndikuriyo (2 Jan) and by Ebuteli, which reports FDNB-supported FARDC attacks on 7 and 10 Jan.
r1-UV-2026Q1-021.vn: Supported; the 'reason' clause is printed on the page next to the excerpt (page-only clause). Statement dated 17 December 2025, before this unit's quarter.
src: Le 17 décembre 2025, devant le Parlement européen à Bruxelles, l’ambassadeur du Burundi auprès de l’Union européenne, Thérence Ntahiraja, s’est en effet exprimé sur la situation sécuritaire à l’Est de la RDC, aux côtés de son homologue congolais Christian Ndongala Nkuku.

le diplomate burundais a déclaré sans ambiguïté que « au lendemain de la signature de l’accord de paix de la RDC, l’armée burundaise a retiré ses troupes qui se trouvaient à l’Est de la RDC dans le but de respecter cet accord »

r1-UV-2026Q1-022.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents' testimony, that from Sunday to Tuesday several civilians were killed in Uvira, some for refusing to hand over their phones, others for an appearance likened to Tutsi, or accused of collaborating with the M23; some testimonies named Wazalendo elements as perpetrators, others unidentified armed bandits.
r1-UV-2026Q1-022.a: Wazalendo elements (some testimonies) and unidentified armed bandits, per SOS Médias Burundi
r1-UV-2026Q1-022.n: Date range computed from weekdays ('dimanche' 18 Jan to 'mardi' 20 Jan); date computed from weekday and publication date. Single local outlet; no count of victims given. Ethnic profiling element (appearance read as Tutsi).
r1-UV-2026Q1-022.vn: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches.
src: Depuis dimanche et jusqu’à ce mardi, des cas de tueries, de pillages et de violences sexuelles sont signalés dans plusieurs quartiers de la ville, selon des témoignages d’habitants.

Plusieurs civils ont été tués, certains pour avoir refusé de remettre leurs téléphones, d’autres en raison de leur apparence assimilée aux Tutsi, ou encore accusés de collaborer avec le M23. Certains témoignages désignent des éléments Wazalendo comme auteurs de violences, tandis que d’autres actes seraient commis par des bandits armés non identifiés.

r1-UV-2026Q1-023.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that shops, houses and stores were regularly pillaged by armed men in Uvira from Sunday to Tuesday.
r1-UV-2026Q1-023.a: armed men (not identified in this sentence)
r1-UV-2026Q1-023.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date. Radio Okapi (2026-01-18/19) also reported pillage and gunfire in Uvira on the day of the FARDC return (headlines seen in search results, pages not fetched).
src: Depuis dimanche et jusqu’à ce mardi, des cas de tueries, de pillages et de violences sexuelles sont signalés dans plusieurs quartiers de la ville, selon des témoignages d’habitants.
Des boutiques, maisons et magasins sont régulièrement pillés par des hommes armés.

r1-UV-2026Q1-024.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing residents, cases of sexual violence in several quarters of Uvira between Sunday and Tuesday; it wrote that a woman was reportedly killed after giving food to Wazalendo fighters, who reportedly then assaulted her ('violentée'), and that young girls were targeted for their looks or for refusing to give up their phones.
r1-UV-2026Q1-024.a: Wazalendo fighters (for the woman's case, per testimony)
r1-UV-2026Q1-024.n: The French 'violentée' means assaulted/abused and does not itself specify rape; the article's general sentence refers to 'violences sexuelles'. Unverified local testimony via a Burundian outlet; no victim names given; no health-care information. Date computed from weekdays.
r1-UV-2026Q1-024.vn: Both excerpts on the page; conditionals kept. 'violentée' does not itself specify rape; the source does not say the girls' targeting was sexual.
src: Depuis dimanche et jusqu’à ce mardi, des cas de tueries, de pillages et de violences sexuelles sont signalés dans plusieurs quartiers de la ville, selon des témoignages d’habitants.

Une femme aurait été tuée après avoir donné de la nourriture à des combattants Wazalendo, qui l’auraient ensuite violentée. Dans plusieurs familles, des jeunes filles ont été prises pour cible pour leur faciès ou pour avoir refusé de céder leurs téléphones.

r1-UV-2026Q1-025.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that security sources within the FARDC said more than twenty Banyamulenge families remained under the protection of the regular forces, as some community leaders called on their own members and on the FARDC to stop the pillage and killings.
r1-UV-2026Q1-025.n: Unnamed FARDC sources. Contrast with reports of destroyed Banyamulenge property (HRW) and Banyamulenge displacement allegations. Published 2026-01-20.
r1-UV-2026Q1-025.vn: The page says community leaders called on 'leurs éléments' (their own members) and the FARDC; it does not name the Wazalendo, so that was narrowed out. The leaders' call is page-only (excerpt gap).
src: Des sources sécuritaires au sein des FARDC indiquent que plus de vingt familles de la communauté Banyamulenge restent actuellement sous protection des forces régulières.

r1-UV-2026Q1-026.s: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January the Mai-Mai Kuruninga killed a boy in Kalundu quarter and a man in Kabindula quarter, and the Mai-Mai Landa Bango killed a woman in Sondo quarter, in Uvira city.
r1-UV-2026Q1-026.l: Kalundu, Kabindula and Sondo quarters, Uvira city
r1-UV-2026Q1-026.x: Ebuteli: a boy, a man and a woman killed (three people)
r1-UV-2026Q1-026.n: Ebuteli adds that the abuses were often linked to extortion attempts. No victim names printed.
r1-UV-2026Q1-026.vn: Statement unchanged; figures written in words as the source prints them (the '1' figures were in no excerpt).
src: Les Mai-Mai Kuruninga ont tué un garçon dans le quartier Kalundu et un homme dans le quartier Kabindula, le 19 janvier. Les Mai-Mai Landa Bango ont tué une femme dans le quartier Sondo le 19 janvier.

r1-UV-2026Q1-027.s: Ebuteli reported that on 19 January a group of ten unidentified armed men killed a man in Kilibuli quarter, accusing him of collaborating with the M23, and that on 24 January, during a robbery in Kasenga quarter, unidentified armed men killed a 22-year-old civilian.
r1-UV-2026Q1-027.l: Kilibuli and Kasenga quarters, Uvira city
r1-UV-2026Q1-027.x: Ebuteli: a man killed (Kilibuli, 19 January); a civilian aged 22 killed (Kasenga, 24 January)
r1-UV-2026Q1-027.n: Two separate incidents grouped by source; 'le même jour' refers to 19 January in the source's sequence.
r1-UV-2026Q1-027.vn: Statement unchanged; '19 January' rests on the preceding sentence on the page ('le même jour'), page-only clause. Figures reworded.
src: Le même jour, un groupe de dix hommes armés non identifiés a tué un homme dans le quartier de Kilibuli. Les assaillants l’ont accusé de collaborer avec le M23.
Au quartier Kasenga, lors d'un braquage, le 24 janvier, des hommes armés non identifiés ont tué un civil âgé de 22 ans.

r1-UV-2026Q1-028.s: Ebuteli counted at least 21 civilians killed in Uvira territory in January 2026, against at least 151 in December 2025, the month the M23 took Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q1-028.x: Ebuteli: >=21 civilians killed in Uvira territory in January 2026; >=151 in December 2025
r1-UV-2026Q1-028.n: Monitor tally for the whole territory, not just the city. Compare with the Government's 1,500 dead figure for 10 Dec-18 Jan (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) and HRW's 'at least several dozen' for the takeover.
r1-UV-2026Q1-028.vn: Excerpt on the page; figures match. Monitor tally for the whole territory, all perpetrators.
src: Des tueries de civils ont été documentées pendant et après le retour des groupes Wazalendo à Uvira. Bien que très préoccupantes, les exactions du mois de janvier sont en baisse par rapport à décembre 2025, marqué par la prise d’Uvira par le M23 (au moins 151 civils tués sur le territoire d’Uvira en décembre, contre 21 en janvier).

r1-UV-2026Q1-029.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several eyewitness accounts, that a drone attributed to the FARDC bombed a bar called Blue Cut near the Kalundu public port around 2:30 p.m. on Wednesday, reportedly causing deaths and numerous injuries among civilians as well as significant material damage.
r1-UV-2026Q1-029.l: Blue Cut bar, Kalundu public port, Uvira city
r1-UV-2026Q1-029.x: SOS Médias Burundi: 'several' civilians dead and numerous injured; no figures
r1-UV-2026Q1-029.n: Date from 'Wednesday, January 14' in the same article (dateline 15 January). No count given ('several civilians injured and some dead' per a resident). Local report; AFC/M23 sources suggest the drones came from Burundi, which could not be independently verified; FARDC/Burundi response: none found (article says neither had responded).
r1-UV-2026Q1-029.vn: Excerpt on the page. No casualty count. The article says neither Congolese nor Burundian authorities had responded.
src: According to several eyewitness accounts gathered on site, a drone attributed to the FARDC bombed a bar called Blue Cut, located near the Kalundu public port, around 2:30 p.m. The attack reportedly caused deaths and numerous injuries among civilians, as well as significant material damage.

r1-UV-2026Q1-030.s: Ebuteli reported that on 14 January a FARDC kamikaze drone air strike in Kalundu quarter, Uvira city, targeted and destroyed a hotel in which an M23 meeting was being held, and that the toll could be several dozen victims among civilians, fighters and M23 cadres.
r1-UV-2026Q1-030.x: Ebuteli: could be several dozen victims among civilians, fighters and M23 cadres
r1-UV-2026Q1-030.n: Same date and place as the SOS Médias Burundi report of a drone strike on the Blue Cut bar, but Ebuteli says a hotel hosting an M23 meeting; the two accounts may describe one strike or two and are kept separate. The toll is conditional ('pourrait être'). Ebuteli puts this under an intensification of FARDC air offensives.
r1-UV-2026Q1-030.vn: Excerpt on the page. Toll is conditional. May be the same strike as SOS Médias Burundi's 'Blue Cut bar' report.
src: Au quartier Kalundu, en ville d'Uvira le 14 janvier, une autre frappe aérienne par drone kamikaze des FARDC a ciblé et détruit un hôtel dans lequel se tenait une réunion du M23. Le bilan pourrait être de plusieurs dizaines de victimes parmi les civils, les combattants et les cadres du M23.

r1-UV-2026Q1-031.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that sources close to the AFC/M23 denied that M23 members were present at the Blue Cut bar in Kalundu when it was hit by a drone, asserting that no leaders or fighters from the movement were there.
r1-UV-2026Q1-031.n: Anonymous partisan-adjacent sources. The 'claims' denied are local reports that the strike was based on intelligence about M23 members gathered at the bar.
r1-UV-2026Q1-031.vn: Excerpt on the page; the 'claims' denied are the local reports of M23 members at the bar (preceding sentence).
src: Sources close to the AFC/M23 deny these claims, asserting that no leaders or fighters from the movement were present at the time of the attack.

r1-UV-2026Q1-032.s: Human Rights Watch said that the South Kivu governor and the Congolese army commander took steps to control Wazalendo groups in Uvira, that some Wazalendo had been arrested for threatening and shooting at civilians, and that HRW visited them in military detention cells.
r1-UV-2026Q1-032.n: HRW's visit was in March 2026; arrest dates not given. Arrested persons not named.
r1-UV-2026Q1-032.vn: HRW's own observation during its March 2026 visit.
src: The South Kivu governor and Congolese army commander have taken some steps to control Wazalendo groups in the city. Some Wazalendo have been arrested for threatening and shooting at civilians, and we were able to visit them in the military detention cells.

r1-UV-2026Q1-033.s: Human Rights Watch said there had been a lot of damage to houses, government buildings and property of Banyamulenge, as well as destruction and looting of goods during the military withdrawal, although it was difficult to identify those responsible.
r1-UV-2026Q1-033.n: Radio Okapi / Congo Indépendant list damage to State services (DGDA, DGI, DGM, DGRAD, OCC) in a separate claim.
src: There has been a lot of damage to houses, government buildings, and property of Banyamulenge, as well as the destruction and looting of goods during the military withdrawal, although it is difficult to identify those responsible.

r1-UV-2026Q1-034.s: Congo Indépendant reported that destruction and pillage targeted essential public services in Uvira, including the customs (DGDA), tax (DGI), immigration (DGM) and administrative revenue (DGRAD) directorates and the OCC quality-control agency.
r1-UV-2026Q1-034.a: not attributed in this passage (the army attributes pre-evacuation pillage to the M23/RDF/AFC coalition)
r1-UV-2026Q1-034.n: Government-leaning framing; perpetrators not stated in the passage.
r1-UV-2026Q1-034.vn: Excerpt on the page; perpetrators not stated.
src: Des destructions et pillages ont visé des services publics essentiels. C’est le cas notamment de: DGDA (Douane), DGI (Impôts), DGM (Immigration), DGRAD (recettes administratives), OCC (surveillance et contrôle de qualité).

r1-UV-2026Q1-035.s: Congo Indépendant reported that more than 267,000 people were now refugees or displaced, nearly 250,000 of them in Burundi, and that Minister of State Ève Bazaiba, who stayed in Burundi, called it a 'human tragedy'.
r1-UV-2026Q1-035.x: Congo Indépendant: more than 267,000 refugees or displaced, nearly 250,000 of them in Burundi
r1-UV-2026Q1-035.n: Figure source not named in the passage. Radio Okapi (2026-04-07, Government report) gives more than 300,000 displaced.
r1-UV-2026Q1-035.vn: Statement unchanged; removed the Radio Okapi 300,000 figure from `figures`, which this source does not print. The source of the figures is not named ('selon les chiffres disponibles').
src: Selon les chiffres disponibles, plus de 267.000 personnes sont désormais réfugiées ou déplacées, dont près de 250 000 au Burundi. Ministre d’État en charge des Affaires sociales et humanitaires, Ève Bazaiba a séjourné au Burundi. Elle parle de « tragédie humaine ».

r1-UV-2026Q1-036.s: Human Rights Watch said that M23 fighters committed sexual violence against women and girls, especially those who ventured out to find food on their farmlands where they were isolated and vulnerable, and that most of these women and girls had not received any medical care.
r1-UV-2026Q1-036.n: HRW does not give a date for these assaults beyond the occupation (about 10 Dec 2025-18 Jan 2026); the range is that occupation, so part falls before the unit's quarter. HRW interviews were in March 2026. The lack of medical care is stated for most survivors; no facility attack is described. No names given.
r1-UV-2026Q1-036.vn: Both passages on the page; HRW on-site research. HRW gives no dates or count; the date range is the occupation period (entry on 10 December 2025 per residents interviewed by HRW).
src: M23 fighters also committed sexual violence against women and girls, especially as those who ventured out to find food on their farmlands where they were isolated and vulnerable to assault. Most of these women and girls had not received any medical care.
Uvira was occupied for just over a month by the M23.

r1-UV-2026Q1-037.s: Radio Okapi reported that a Government report, presented in Kinshasa on a Tuesday by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba, said about 14,400 women were raped in five weeks of occupation of Uvira by the Rwandan army and its proxies.
r1-UV-2026Q1-037.a: Rwandan army and its 'supplétifs' (proxies), per the DRC Government report
r1-UV-2026Q1-037.x: DRC Government report: about 14,400 women raped in five weeks of occupation of Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q1-037.n: Government (party) figure, a roughly ten-page report not seen; method and sources not stated; much higher than any NGO/UN figure seen in this unit. HRW documents sexual violence by M23 fighters without a count. The DW/UFMP figure of 'more than a thousand' sexual violence cases over three months (search snippet, 2026-04-17) was not fetched.
r1-UV-2026Q1-037.vn: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to what the source says (the date range 10 Dec-18 Jan is printed for the children figure, not the rape figure). Party figure; the report's method and sources are not stated. src: Plus de 1 500 personnes ont perdu la vie et environ 14 400 femmes ont été violées en cinq semaines d’occupation de la ville d’Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, par l’armée rwandaise et ses supplétifs. Ces chiffres sont contenus dans un rapport du Gouvernement, présenté mardi à Kinshasa devant la presse par le ministre des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba.

Entre le 10 décembre 2025 et le 18 janvier 2026, plus de 12 000 enfants ont été affectés et exposés à la déscolarisation, à des traumatismes psychologiques ainsi qu’à des séparations familiales, indique le rapport gouvernemental.
Human Rights Watch a également documenté des viols et d’autres violences sexuelles commis par des combattants du M23 et des soldats rwandais sur des femmes et des filles.

Le ministre congolais des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba, a présenté le 7 avril un rapport officiel documentant plusieurs violations commises contre les populations civiles dans cette partie de l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo. Selon ce document, plus de 14 400 femmes ont été victimes de viols durant la période d’occupation.

r1-UV-2026Q1-038.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented by Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba on a Tuesday said more than 1,500 people died and more than 300,000 were forced to flee during the occupation of Uvira, with bombings, summary executions, abductions, sexual violence and pillage creating a climate of generalised terror.
r1-UV-2026Q1-038.a: Rwandan army and its proxies, per the DRC Government report
r1-UV-2026Q1-038.x: DRC Government report: more than 1,500 dead; more than 300,000 forced to flee
r1-UV-2026Q1-038.n: Party figures; contradicted in scale by HRW ('at least several dozen' killed at the takeover) and Ebuteli (151 killed in Uvira territory in December, 21 in January). Not a finding.
r1-UV-2026Q1-038.vn: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to this source (HRW and Ebuteli figures moved to the note). The 'climate of terror' clause is Mbemba's, printed on the page (page-only). Party figures. HRW says the M23 and Rwandan forces killed 'at least several dozen' when they took Uvira; Ebuteli counts at least 151 civilians killed in Uvira territory in December 2025 and 21 in January 2026.
src: Plus de 1 500 personnes ont perdu la vie et environ 14 400 femmes ont été violées en cinq semaines d’occupation de la ville d’Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, par l’armée rwandaise et ses supplétifs. Ces chiffres sont contenus dans un rapport du Gouvernement, présenté mardi à Kinshasa devant la presse par le ministre des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba.
Selon ce document, plus de 300 000 personnes ont été contraintes de fuir leurs foyers dans la précipitation dans ce chef-lieu provisoire du Sud-Kivu.

r1-UV-2026Q1-039.s: Human Rights Watch said its research indicated that the M23 and Rwandan forces killed at least several dozen people when they took Uvira, adding that it is difficult to know who is buried in all reported mass graves.
r1-UV-2026Q1-039.n: Takeover phase (10 Dec 2025) precedes the unit's quarter but is the only independent count of the killings in the Government's 1,500 claim. HRW visited three burial sites.
src: According to our research, the M23 and Rwandan forces killed at least several dozen people when they took Uvira.
However, at this stage, it is difficult to know exactly who is buried in all the mass graves that have been reported on, including when they were buried, and how they died.

r1-UV-2026Q1-040.s: The DRC Council of Ministers of 27 February heard, from Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani after his mission, that mass graves had been found in Uvira, one near the World Food Programme office on the road to Kavimvira reportedly containing about 35 bodies per local sources, and a second at Kilomoni; no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.
r1-UV-2026Q1-040.l: Kavimvira road and Kilomoni, Uvira city
r1-UV-2026Q1-040.a: not attributed ('identity of the perpetrators ... unknown', per the Government)
r1-UV-2026Q1-040.x: Council of Ministers: ~35 bodies at the first site (local sources)
r1-UV-2026Q1-040.n: Government account. Spelled 'Kavinvira' in the article. Provincial government figure (151) is a separate claim. Later Government report (Radio Okapi 2026-04-07) lists three graves at Mayi ya Moto with 115 bodies and Kilomoni with 31, so site names differ across sources.
r1-UV-2026Q1-040.vn: All five excerpts on the page. Grade lowered B->C: a single outlet relaying a party's (the government's) account. Government account. The article spells the quarter both 'Kavinvira' and 'Kavimvira'.
src: Cette information ressort d’une note d’information du Vice-Premier ministre, ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité, de la Décentralisation et des Affaires coutumières, Jacquemain Shabani, à la suite de sa mission dans cette partie du pays
Selon l’exposé du patron de la territoriale lors de la 80ᵉ réunion du Conseil des ministres, tenue vendredi 27 février 2026
ces fosses communes ont été mises au jour dans le quartier Kavinvira ainsi que sur un autre site situé à Kilomoni, tous deux dans la ville d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.
La première fosse a été découverte à proximité du bureau du Programme alimentaire mondial, sur l’axe routier menant vers Kavimvira. Selon les sources locales, ce site contiendrait environ 35 corps.
aucune exhumation officielle n’a encore été menée et l’identité des auteurs ainsi que celle des victimes demeure inconnue

r1-UV-2026Q1-041.s: Actualite.cd reported that the South Kivu provincial government, in a communiqué of 28 February 2026, said preliminary findings were that 151 civilians were buried in the mass graves, 121 at the Kavinvira cemetery and 30 in an enclosure in Kilomoni quarter, and that 'these executions took place on the eve of the forced withdrawal, on 18 January 2026, of the AFC/M23 elements, supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)'. The national government's account of the Council of Ministers meeting of Friday 27 February 2026 said no official exhumation had yet taken place and the identity of perpetrators and victims remained unknown.
r1-UV-2026Q1-041.l: Kavinvira cemetery and Kilomoni quarter, Uvira city
r1-UV-2026Q1-041.a: AFC/M23 supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), per the provincial government
r1-UV-2026Q1-041.x: South Kivu provincial government: 151 civilians buried (121 at Kavinvira cemetery, 30 at Kilomoni)
r1-UV-2026Q1-041.n: Party (provincial government) attribution and count; the national Council of Ministers the day before said perpetrators and victims were unknown and gave ~35 bodies at one site. HRW could not say who is buried in all graves. The communiqué's legal characterisation is not reproduced here. 121+30=151 as printed.
r1-UV-2026Q1-041.vn: Statement unchanged; `figures` narrowed to this source (the Council of Ministers' ~35 is a separate claim). Party account. The national Council of Ministers the day before said perpetrators and victims were unknown. The communiqué's legal characterisations are not reproduced. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Council of Ministers of 27 February 2026 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: no official exhumation; perpetrators and victims unknown 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-022: Attribution drift in the actor field: as relayed, the communiqué dates the executions to the eve of the AFC/M23/RDF withdrawal and frames them as massacres, but the quoted sentence does not itself name who carried them out; 'forced' is the provincial government's word. Quote the sentence and add the national government's contrary 'perpetrators unknown' (claim r1-UV-2026Q1-040). Actor field should read 'implied: AFC/M23 with RDF support, per the provincial government'. One search found no AFC/M23 response on a citable page.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): Council of Ministers of 27 February 2026; no official exhumation; perpetrators and victims unknown
src: Pour sa part, le gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu va plus loin dans un communiqué rendu public le samedi 28 février 2026.

Selon ce document, les constats préliminaires établis par l’autorité provinciale indiquent que cent cinquante-et-une (151) personnes civiles ont été inhumées dans ces fosses communes, dont cent vingt-et-une (121) au cimetière de Kavinvira et trente (30) dans un enclos situé au quartier Kilomoni.
Toujours selon le gouvernement provincial, ces exécutions sont intervenues à la veille du retrait forcé, le 18 janvier 2026, des éléments de l’AFC/M23, appuyés par les Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)
réunion du Conseil des ministres, tenue vendredi 27 février 2026
Toutefois, aucune exhumation officielle n’a encore été menée et l’identité des auteurs ainsi que celle des victimes demeure inconnue", précise le gouvernement dans le compte rendu de la réunion.

r1-UV-2026Q1-042.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday listed three mass graves at Mayi ya Moto containing 115 bodies, one at Kilomoni with 31 bodies, one at Kala, two at Rutembo and two tombs at Kaponda.
r1-UV-2026Q1-042.l: Mayi ya Moto, Kilomoni, Kala, Rutembo, Kaponda, Uvira area
r1-UV-2026Q1-042.a: Rwandan army and its proxies, per the Government report
r1-UV-2026Q1-042.x: Government report: Mayi ya Moto 115; Kilomoni 31; others unspecified
r1-UV-2026Q1-042.n: Report date, not the date of burial; locations are partly different from the 27-28 Feb official accounts (Kavinvira). Not independently verified; HRW says it visited three burial sites and that many more exist.
src: Le document, d’une dizaine de pages, révèle également la découverte de fosses communes, témoignant de l’ampleur des pertes humaines.

Selon le ministre des Droits humains : trois fosses communes ont été découvertes à Mayi ya Moto contenant 115 corps ; une fosse à Kilomoni avec 31 corps ; une fosse à Kala ; deux fosses à Rutembo ; et deux tombes à Kaponda.

r1-UV-2026Q1-043.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Government report presented that Tuesday said the Government had identified more than 162 trucks from Rwanda involved in organised looting operations.
r1-UV-2026Q1-043.a: trucks from Rwanda, per the Government report
r1-UV-2026Q1-043.n: Party claim; no dates or evidence in the article.
src: Le même rapport indique que le Gouvernement a identifié plus de 162 camions en provenance du Rwanda impliqués dans des opérations de spoliation organisée.

r1-UV-2026Q1-044.s: Ebuteli reported that FARDC supported by the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and the Wazalendo attacked M23 fighters at Kabimba village on 7 January and at Kifuta village on 10 January, in Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom, in the middle plateaux of Uvira territory.
r1-UV-2026Q1-044.l: Kabimba and Kifuta, Kalungwe groupement, Bavira chiefdom
r1-UV-2026Q1-044.n: Evidence of FDNB participation in operations in Uvira territory in January; contrast with the ambassador's 17 Dec 2025 claim of withdrawal. Burundi did not comment in the pages seen.
src: les FARDC, appuyés par la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) et les Wazalendo, ont attaqué le 7 janvier les combattants du M23 au village de Kabimba et, le 10 janvier, au village de Kifuta, dans le groupement Kalungwe, en chefferie de Bavira, dans les moyens plateaux du territoire d'Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q1-045.s: Ebuteli reported that on 11 January Twirwaneho fighters allied with the M23 attacked FARDC and Wazalendo positions at Abala village in the high plateaux of Fizi, and that in reprisal the FARDC targeted Mukoko village with drones on 11 and 12 January and recovered arms and ammunition lost at Abala.
r1-UV-2026Q1-045.l: Abala and Mukoko, Basilocha groupement, high plateaux of Fizi
r1-UV-2026Q1-045.a: Twirwaneho allied with M23 vs FARDC and Wazalendo
r1-UV-2026Q1-045.n: Fizi territory, included as the Uvira front's southern flank.
src: Le 11 janvier, dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Fizi, dans le groupement Basilocha, les Twirwaneho alliés au M23 ont attaqué les positions tenues par les FARDC et les Wazalendo au village d'Abala.
En représailles, les FARDC ont ciblé le village de Mukoko avec des drones les 11 et 12 janvier et ont récupéré des armes et des munitions perdues à Abala.

r1-UV-2026Q1-046.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that residents said a FARDC drone was shot down in Fizi territory by Twirwaneho fighters after clashes in which the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo and elements of the FDNB, fought Twirwaneho fighters, described as a military ally of the AFC/M23 in South Kivu.
r1-UV-2026Q1-046.a: FARDC, Wazalendo, FDNB elements vs Twirwaneho
r1-UV-2026Q1-046.n: Date computed from weekday and the article's dateline: 'On Thursday' = 15 January 2026. Residents' report; no independent confirmation per the article; neither Congolese nor Burundian authorities had officially responded.
r1-UV-2026Q1-046.vn: Both excerpts on the page; 'Thursday' with a 15 January dateline is 15 January. The article says no independent confirmation was obtained.
src: On Thursday, residents also reported that a FARDC drone was shot down at ground zero in the Fizi territory by fighters from the Twirwaneho armed group, following violent clashes.

According to the same sources, these clashes pitted the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo militia and elements of the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB), against Twirwaneho fighters, a military ally of the AFC/M23 in South Kivu.

r1-UV-2026Q1-047.s: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January the Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara coalition and the FNL attacked the Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo in the villages of Kilumbi and Abala in Fizi territory, killing three Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo.
r1-UV-2026Q1-047.a: Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara and FNL vs Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo
r1-UV-2026Q1-047.n: Combatant casualties; shows Red Tabara and FNL (Burundian armed groups) in the Fizi/Uvira highlands.
src: Le 29 janvier, la coalition rebelle Twirwaneho/M23/Red Tabara et les Forces nationales de libération (FNL) a attaqué les Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo dans les villages de Kilumbi et d’Abala en territoire de Fizi. Cette attaque a fait un bilan de trois morts dans les rangs des Mai-Mai Mutetezi Bolingo.

r1-UV-2026Q1-048.s: Ebuteli reported that on 29 January a grenade thrown by M23 fighters killed five civilians and wounded eleven in Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, in the Ruzizi plain.
r1-UV-2026Q1-048.l: Rutanga quarter, Sange commune, Ruzizi plain
r1-UV-2026Q1-048.n: Sange is where Ebuteli says the M23 repositioned after leaving Uvira. No names printed.
r1-UV-2026Q1-048.vn: Excerpt on the page; the figures are printed in words (cinq, onze). 2026-10-28: confidence edited: red-team rt-022: Single source (Ebuteli) attributes the grenade to M23 fighters, but the attribution is contested: SOS Médias Burundi (30 Jan 2026) reported four dead and eleven wounded and, citing local sources, that 'un individu non identifié aurait lancé l'engin explosif'; The New Times (Kigali, 30 Jan 2026) reported that 'The AFCM23 rebel movement blamed the government coalition for the attack' (party X says). The toll also differs (five vs four dead). Keep the statement as Ebuteli's account, grade C, and record the SOS Médias and AFC/M23 accounts as separate claims (search leads; extract text is not verbatim, so re-fetch before citing).
src: Dans la plaine de la Ruzizi, à Sange, le 29 janvier, une grenade lancée par des combattants du M23 a tué cinq civils et en a blessé onze autres au quartier Rutanga dans la commune de Sange.

r1-UV-2026Q1-049.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant local sources, violent clashes on Tuesday 17 March between the FARDC and AFC-M23 rebels at Luvungi, near Kabunambo, with bombardments, driving civilians from Runingu towards Uvira, and described the clashes as ending the relative truce around Uvira observed since the AFC-M23 withdrawal.
r1-UV-2026Q1-049.n: Radio Okapi says the withdrawal was 'fin janvier' while other sources date it 16-18 January. Ebuteli and others report earlier fighting in the highlands in January, so 'truce' applies to the city's immediate surroundings. Critical Threats (lead only) and an unfetched Facebook post also place Ruzizi plain fighting on 5 March.
r1-UV-2026Q1-049.vn: Both excerpts on the page; bombardments and flight towards Uvira are page-only clauses. Radio Okapi dates the M23 withdrawal to 'fin janvier 2026'; other sources give 16-18 January.
src: D'intenses mouvements de populations civiles secouent ce mardi 17 mars la localité de Runingu, au Sud-Kivu, suite à de violents combats opposant les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) aux rebelles de l'Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC-M23) à Luvungi, près de Kabunambo rapportent des sources concordantes locales.
Ces affrontements brisent la trêve relative observée autour d'Uvira depuis le retrait de l'AFC-M23 fin janvier 2026.

r1-UV-2026Q1-050.s: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 33rd military region had announced the closure of road traffic from Runingu on the Bukavu-Uvira axis, leaving public transport vehicles and humanitarian convoys blocked there.
r1-UV-2026Q1-050.n: 'Hier' relative to the 17 March article, so 16 March (computed from publication date). Speaker not named.
r1-UV-2026Q1-050.vn: Excerpt on the page. 'Hier' in an article of 17 March: date computed as 16 March. Speaker not named.
src: Le porte-parole de la 33e région militaire avait déjà annoncé hier la fermeture du trafic routier à partir de Runingu, sur l'axe Bukavu-Uvira. Plusieurs véhicules de transport en commun et convois humanitaires sont bloqués sur place

r1-UV-2026Q1-051.s: Radio Okapi reported that the authorities of the DRC and Burundi agreed to reopen on Monday 23 February 2026 the common border between Bujumbura and Uvira, through the Kavimvira and Gatumba border posts, with traffic resuming immediately, after the population of Uvira had been cut off from Bujumbura since the AFC-M23's temporary occupation of the city on 10 December 2025.
r1-UV-2026Q1-051.l: Kavimvira border post, Uvira / Gatumba, Burundi
r1-UV-2026Q1-051.a: Governments of the DRC and Burundi
r1-UV-2026Q1-051.n: Closure dates differ by source: Ebuteli says the border stayed closed through January despite the M23 withdrawal. Search results (RFI, France 24; not fetched) also report the 23 February reopening and that the border was reopened militarily on 19 January. FEC-Uvira operator quoted anonymously raised concerns about harassment and taxes.
src: Les autorités de la République démocratique du Congo et du Burundi ont convenu de rouvrir, lundi 23 février 2026, la frontière commune entre les villes de Bujumbura et Uvira. Le trafic a immédiatement repris, à la grande satisfaction des populations des deux pays voisins.

L’ouverture des postes frontaliers de Kavimvira et Gatumba constitue un soulagement majeur pour la population d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu, restée coupée de Bujumbura, la capitale burundaise, depuis l’occupation temporaire de la ville par l’AFC-M23 le 10 décembre 2025.

r1-UV-2026Q2-001.s: 7sur7.cd reported that Bukavu-Uvira road traffic resumed on Wednesday 1 April 2026, fifteen days after FARDC and Wazalendo elements had suspended it in the Ruzizi plain, and that since 15 March the traffic had been cut at Kasambura by FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo elements.
r1-UV-2026Q2-001.l: Kasambura, Ruzizi plain (Bukavu-Uvira road, RN5), Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-001.a: FARDC and Wazalendo elements (as named by the source)
r1-UV-2026Q2-001.n: Single Congolese outlet; the 15 March start date is the source's. Transporters quoted in the article denounced several paying barriers. The road was suspended again in May (see DW Swahili claim).
r1-UV-2026Q2-001.vn: Both excerpts are on the page (byline Alphonse Muderwa) and carry every clause. The '7' flag is the outlet's name, not a figure. The excerpt_en flags are only about the English capitalisation of 'Wednesday'/'Fifteen'; the translations are faithful. Single Congolese outlet. Transporters quoted on the page also complained of several paying barriers on the road.
src: Le trafic Bukavu-Uvira a repris le mercredi 1ᵉʳ avril 2026. Quinze jours après sa suspension par des éléments FARDC et Wazalendo dans la plaine de la Ruzizi, les usagers ont finalement rejoint les deux grandes villes du Sud-Kivu.
Il sied de rappeler que depuis le 15 mars dernier, le trafic Bukavu-Uvira était coupé au niveau de Kasambura dans la plaine de Ruzizi par des militaires FARDC et des éléments Wazalendo.

r1-UV-2026Q2-002.s: DW (Swahili) reported that Jean-Jacques Elakano, speaking to journalists in Uvira, said the government feared AFC/M23 rebels were using trade and family travel between Bukavu and Uvira to infiltrate areas controlled by the government army; a DW photo caption said the governor of South Kivu, based in Uvira, had said travel would stay suspended until the rebels left Bukavu.
r1-UV-2026Q2-002.n: Single outlet. The statement date is not given on the page; the date is the DW publication date (11 May 2026 per the search listing). Other outlets in the search results call the official 'gouverneur intérimaire' or 'vice-gouverneur'; DW's caption says 'governor'. Civil society voices in the article objected to the closure.
r1-UV-2026Q2-002.vn: The 'suspended until the rebels leave Bukavu' line is a photo caption crediting 'the governor of South Kivu in Uvira'; the body text does not give Elakano a title or put that line in his mouth. Split the two attributions. The body also quotes Elakano: 'Sasa njia itafungwa... Lengo letu ni kuhakikisha tunairejesha Bukavu' (the road will now be closed; our aim is to retake Bukavu). The statement date is not given; the date is DW's publication date (11 May 2026, byline Mitima DeLachance). Elakano's title is not printed in the article body.
src: Akizungumza mbele ya wanahabari mjini Uvira, Jean-Jacques Elakano amesema serikali inahofia kuwa waasi wa AFC/M23 wanatumia shughuli za biashara na safari za kifamilia kati ya Bukavu na Uvira kujipenyeza katika maeneo yanayodhibitiwa na jeshi la serikali.
Gavana wa Kivu Kusini aliye mjini Uvira amesema usafiri utaendelea kusimamishwa hadi waasi hao watakapoondoka Bukavu

r1-UV-2026Q2-003.s: DW (Swahili) reported that since Saturday AFC/M23 fighters had been withdrawing from the Sange area and some hill villages towards the north of Uvira district, and that videos circulating online showed government soldiers and Wazalendo groups entering the village of Sange.
r1-UV-2026Q2-003.l: Sange, Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-003.a: AFC/M23 (withdrawing); government soldiers and Wazalendo groups (entering)
r1-UV-2026Q2-003.n: Date computed from weekday ('since Saturday') and the 11 May publication date, so Saturday = 9 May; approximate. SOS Médias Burundi dates the departure to Monday 11 May; Igihe (search snippet only) dates it 10 May. Not confirmed by AFC/M23 at the time per DW.
r1-UV-2026Q2-003.vn: Excerpt exact and covers the statement. DW attributes the withdrawal to 'reports from the Uvira area' (taarifa kutoka eneo la Uvira) and the entry to online videos; the statement keeps both attributions. 'Since Saturday' with an 11 May article = 9 May (computed). Withdrawal date differs by source: DW says 'since Saturday' (9 May, computed from the 11 May publication date); SOS Médias Burundi says Monday (11 May, computed from its 12 May dateline); Igihe 10 May (snippet only, not verified). Each claim states only its own source's date. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Wakati huohuo, taarifa kutoka eneo la Uvira zinaeleza kuwa tangu Jumamosi kumekuwa na harakati za kujiondoa kwa wapiganaji wa AFC/M23 kutoka eneo la Sange pamoja na baadhi ya vijiji vya milimani kuelekea kaskazini mwa wilaya hiyo. Video zilizosambaa mitandaoni zinaonesha wanajeshi wa serikali ya Kongo pamoja na makundi ya Wazalendo wakiingia katika kijiji cha Sange.

r1-UV-2026Q2-004.s: DW (Swahili) reported that the Congolese army said the AFC/M23 rebels had left the villages of Nyakabere, Mutarule and Luberizi, a claim that DW said AFC/M23 had not confirmed so far.
r1-UV-2026Q2-004.l: Nyakabere, Mutarule, Luberizi, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-004.n: Army claim, not a verified fact. Date is the DW publication date. AFC/M23's own account was not found in an opened page (see gaps).
r1-UV-2026Q2-004.vn: Excerpt exact; the army claim and DW's note that AFC/M23 had not confirmed it are both in the one sentence. Party claim kept attributed. Army claim, not independently confirmed; date is DW's publication date.
src: Jeshi la Kongo pia limesema waasi hao wameondoka katika vijiji vya Nyakabere, Mutarule na Luberizi, madai ambayo hadi sasa hayajathibitishwa na AFC/M23.

r1-UV-2026Q2-005.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that AFC/M23 rebels left several localities of the Ruzizi plain in Uvira territory on Monday; according to local sources they withdrew from Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera and Luvungi towards Katogota, and residents of Sange, Luberizi and Lemera took to the streets to celebrate their departure.
r1-UV-2026Q2-005.l: Ruzizi plain (Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera, Luvungi), Uvira territory; Katogota, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-005.n: Dateline 12 May 2026; 'ce lundi' = Monday 11 May (date computed from weekday and dateline). The same article says some local sources link the withdrawal to US diplomatic pressure and that other groups reportedly headed towards Kamanyola (not captured as an excerpt). DW Swahili dates the movement from Saturday 9 May; Igihe (snippet only) 10 May. Discrepancy surfaced, not resolved. The UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466) wrote that RDF and AFC/M23 withdrawals amounted to tactical repositioning.
r1-UV-2026Q2-005.vn: All three excerpts are on the page (dateline 'Bukavu, 12 mai 2026', byline Leila Keza). 'Ce lundi' with a 12 May dateline = 11 May (computed). The page also says some local sources link the withdrawal to US diplomatic pressure ('serait lié', conditional) and that other groups 'auraient pris la direction de Kamanyola'; not added to the statement.
