Withdrawal date differs by source: SOS Médias Burundi says Monday (11 May, computed); DW Swahili 'since Saturday' (9 May, computed); Igihe 10 May (snippet only). The UN Group of Experts (S/2026/466, para. 49) wrote that no RDF or AFC/M23 withdrawals were documented in South Kivu at the time of drafting.
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 ont quitté ce lundi plusieurs localités de la Plaine de la Rusizi, dans le territoire d’Uvira au Sud-Kivu.

Selon des sources locales, les rebelles se sont retirés de Kabunambo, Sange, Mutarule, Luberizi, Bwegera, Lemera et Luvungi pour se diriger vers Katogota, une zone qu’ils occupaient déjà en décembre 2025 avant l’accord de Washington.
Dans plusieurs localités, notamment à Sange, Luberizi et Lemera, des habitants sont descendus dans les rues pour célébrer le départ des rebelles du M23.

r1-UV-2026Q2-006.s: MediaCongo reported that since dawn on Wednesday 6 May 2026 violent clashes opposed AFC/M23 rebels, supported according to several sources by the Rwandan defence forces, to FARDC and Wazalendo self-defence groups, concentrated in the Ruzizi plain at Kigoro, Kigurwe and Kabunambo about 26 kilometres north of Uvira; it said no official toll had been given and that the city remained under government-force control.
r1-UV-2026Q2-006.l: Kigoro, Kigurwe, Kabunambo, Ruzizi plain (RN5), c. 26 km north of Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-006.a: AFC/M23 (backed per several sources by RDF) vs FARDC and Wazalendo
r1-UV-2026Q2-006.n: Single outlet (credited L.M., congo-press.com / MCP). The RDF involvement is the source's 'selon plusieurs sources' attribution, not established. Kabunambo was named four days later among localities AFC/M23 left (SOS Médias Burundi, 11 May). The article says 'no official toll' had been communicated. AFC/M23's and Rwanda's accounts of 6 May were not found.
r1-UV-2026Q2-006.vn: Excerpts exact; the 'no official toll' clause is on the page but not in the stored excerpts, so supplied as a replacement quote. RDF support stays attributed to 'several sources'. Credit at end of page: 'L.M. congo-press.com (MCP) / mediacongo.net'. RDF involvement is per unnamed 'several sources' in the article, not established.
ent: Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo
src: Depuis l’aube de ce mercredi 6 mai 2026, de violents affrontements opposent les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, appuyés selon plusieurs sources par les Forces de défense rwandaises, aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo et aux groupes d’autodéfense Wazalendo.
Les combats se concentrent dans la plaine de la Ruzizi, notamment dans les localités de Kigoro, Kigurwe et Kabunambo, situées à environ 26 kilomètres au nord d’Uvira, sur l’axe stratégique de la RN5.

Bien que la ville reste, pour l’heure, sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales, la progression des combats à quelques dizaines de kilomètres seulement laisse craindre une dégradation rapide de la situation.

r1-UV-2026Q2-007.s: La Presse Africaine reported that, in a security assessment presented on Thursday 7 May 2026, the chiefs of six quarters of Uvira (Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda) painted a dark picture of the security situation; according to this assessment, armed robbery, killings, abductions, death threats, torture and other abuses were reported almost daily, especially at night, and the outlet wrote that this violence was reportedly attributed ('seraient attribuées') largely to uncontrolled elements of the VDP Wazalendo and of the FARDC, and in part to unidentified armed men.
r1-UV-2026Q2-007.l: Uvira (city): Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu and Nyamianda quarters, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-007.a: as alleged in the assessment: uncontrolled elements of VDP Wazalendo and FARDC; unidentified armed men
r1-UV-2026Q2-007.x: no figures given in the excerpt
r1-UV-2026Q2-007.n: Single local outlet reporting a local-leaders' assessment at a quarterly security meeting; allegations are general, with no individual incidents, dates or victims. Wording 'seraient attribuées' is the source's. FARDC and Wazalendo accounts not found.
r1-UV-2026Q2-007.vn: The draft put the attribution in the chiefs' mouths ('which they said were attributed'); the page has the outlet writing a conditional ('seraient attribuées') after 'Selon ce diagnostic'. Kept the conditional and the outlet as narrator. Byline Pascal Bahunde (LPA Sud-Kivu); the meeting was a quarterly security meeting run by Search for Common Ground (project 'Tukutane Tena'). General allegations at a security meeting; no individual incidents, dates or victims given.
src: Dans un rapport d'évaluation sécuritaire présenté ce jeudi 7 mai 2026, les chefs de six quartiers, dont : Kimanga, Kabindula, Songo, Kilibula, Kalundu et Nyamianda, ont dressé un tableau sombre de la situation sécuritaire qui prévaut dans leurs entités respectives.
Selon ce diagnostic, des actes de vol à main armée, assassinats, enlèvements, menaces de mort, tortures et autres exactions sont signalés quasi quotidiennement, en particulier durant la nuit.

Ces violences seraient attribuées, dans une large mesure, à des éléments non contrôlés des VDP Wazalendo et des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et d'autres aux porteurs d'armes non identifiés.

r1-UV-2026Q2-008.s: Kivutimes reported that Uvira had for more than three months faced a multiplication of arbitrary arrests without trial and that, according to several local sources, some arrests were reportedly carried out by certain Wazalendo, often to obtain ransoms from detainees' families; Mapenzi Manyebwa, coordinator of the Uvira civil society synergy, denounced arrests made without respect for legal procedures, with citizens paying fines outside any judicial logic.
r1-UV-2026Q2-008.a: certain Wazalendo (per several local sources, as named by the source)
r1-UV-2026Q2-008.x: no figures given; "more than three months" per source
r1-UV-2026Q2-008.n: Single local outlet; article produced under the Habari za Mahali project (funded by La Benevolencija, run in Uvira by UNPC, COMEL-RDC and UFMP) per its footer. No individual detainee named. The article also notes that only certain services (prosecutor, judicial police, and within limits ANR and military intelligence) may lawfully detain.
r1-UV-2026Q2-008.vn: Excerpts exact and carry each clause; the Wazalendo attribution stays with 'several local sources' and the conditional. Name spelled as printed. The Wazalendo allegation is conditional ('seraient menées') and from unnamed local sources. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Kivutimes (18 May 2026, Habari za Mahali project funded by La Benevolencija) uses the conditional 'seraient menées' for the Wazalendo arrests; the statement dropped it. The page also cites a psychologist on family harms including exposure of children to GBV and early marriage.
src: Depuis plus de trois mois, la ville d’Uvira fait face à une multiplication d’arrestations arbitraires et sans procès, plongeant de nombreuses familles dans la détresse. Selon plusieurs sources locales, certaines arrestations seraient menées par certains Wazalendo souvent dans le but d’obtenir des rançons auprès des familles des détenus.

Mapenzi Manyebwa, coordinateur de la synergie des sociétés civiles et mouvements citoyens d’Uvira, dénonce des arrestations effectuées sans respect des procédures juridiques, où des citoyens paient des amendes sans qu’aucune logique judiciaire ne soit suivie.

r1-UV-2026Q2-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 15 May 2026 several boats carrying Burundian soldiers landed at Ruzizi, not far from the port of Kalundu in Uvira, before troops were deployed towards Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory); the article said the deployment was estimated (without saying by whom) at about two battalions, aimed at rebalancing the balance of forces in the Minembwe area and controlling movements between Rurambo, Bijombo and Minembwe.
r1-UV-2026Q2-009.l: Ruzizi near Kalundu port, Uvira (city); onward to Bijombo (Uvira territory) and Itombwe (Mwenga territory), South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-009.n: Single Burundi-based independent outlet; no unit designation, commander or official Burundian/Congolese confirmation found. The article describes the deployment as reinforcing operations against M23 and Twirwaneho in the highlands. The same article says Burundian forces had run joint operations with FARDC and Wazalendo at Point Zéro, Mulima, Mikenge, Kakenge, Kalingi and Bidegu in April 2026 (not captured as an excerpt).
r1-UV-2026Q2-009.vn: Draft shortened the stated aim to 'aimed at the Minembwe area'; restored the source's wording. Who made the estimate is not stated on the page ('est estimé'). Single Burundi-based outlet; no unit designation, commander or official confirmation. The same article says these forces reinforce operations 'contre le M23 et Twirwaneho dans les hauts plateaux'. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: SOS Médias Burundi (French), dateline Uvira 19 May 2026, posted 20 May. The page says 'Le déploiement est estimé à environ deux bataillons' in the passive, naming no estimator; the statement's 'it estimated' attributes the estimate to the outlet, so it is corrected. All other clauses match.
src: Le 15 mai 2026, plusieurs embarcations transportant des militaires burundais ont accosté à Ruzizi, non loin du port de Kalundu à Uvira, avant de déployer des troupes vers Bijombo (territoire d’Uvira) et Itombwe (territoire de Mwenga).
Le déploiement est estimé à environ deux bataillons, visant à rééquilibrer les rapports de force dans la zone de Minembwe et à contrôler les mouvements entre Rurambo, Bijombo et Minembwe.

r1-UV-2026Q2-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that at a press conference in Kinshasa on Saturday 6 June the army's interim spokesperson, Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay, firmly denounced the continuation of attacks despite ongoing diplomatic initiatives, and that, according to the military authorities, several localities of North Kivu and the highlands of Fizi and Uvira in South Kivu continued to be the scene of attacks.
r1-UV-2026Q2-010.l: Kinshasa (press conference); North Kivu localities and the Hauts Plateaux of Fizi and Uvira, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-010.n: Party statement: the FARDC accusation is a claim by one party. Radio Okapi is a UN-founded, Congo-based radio; the page quotes the spokesperson. AFC/M23 and Rwanda responses not found.
r1-UV-2026Q2-010.vn: Removed the year, which neither excerpt prints (the page is dated 07/06/2026). The FARDC accuse 'la coalition RDF/AFC-M23' in a direct quote on the page; the statement keeps the claim as the army's. Party statement (FARDC). AFC/M23 and Rwanda replies not found.
src: Lors d’une conference de presse tenu samedi 6 juin à Kinshasa, le porte-parole intérimaire de l’armée, le lieutenant-colonel Mak Hazukay, a fermement dénoncé la poursuite des attaques malgré les initiatives diplomatiques en cours.
Selon les autorités militaires, plusieurs localités du Nord-Kivu ainsi que les hauts plateaux de Fizi et d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu, continuent d’être le théâtre d’attaques.

r1-UV-2026Q2-011.s: The ICRC reported that between 15 May and 15 June 2026 the five hospitals it supports in North and South Kivu recorded a total of 303 casualties, 30% more than for 15 April-14 May, and that, in a sign of intensifying hostilities in the Hauts Plateaux, the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi in South Kivu had admitted 170 casualties (56% of the 303 patients).
r1-UV-2026Q2-011.l: Uvira General Referral Hospital (with Bukavu and Fizi hospitals), South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-011.x: ICRC: 303 casualties across five ICRC-supported hospitals in the Kivus, 15 May-15 June 2026 (+30% vs 15 April-14 May); 170 casualties (56%) admitted at the Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi hospitals together (no separate Uvira figure)
r1-UV-2026Q2-011.n: ICRC press feature. Figures are for the three South Kivu hospitals combined; Uvira alone is not broken out. The 303 figure is of casualties/patients as the page words it (the page also says 'patients admitted'). Moussa Badji (ICRC medical coordinator) appears elsewhere on the page, not in these excerpts.
r1-UV-2026Q2-011.vn: Figures match the page exactly. Removed the Ebola clause, which sits on the page but in no stored excerpt. The page does not name the Uvira General Referral Hospital; it says 'the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi'. No separate figure for Uvira; 170 is for the three South Kivu hospitals combined. The location field's 'Uvira General Referral Hospital' is not printed on the page.
src: Between 15 May and 15 June 2026, the five hospitals that the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is supporting in North and South Kivu provinces (Democratic Republic of the Congo, DRC) recorded a total of 303 casualties – 30% more than for the period 15 April–14 May.

In a sign of intensifying hostilities in the Hauts Plateaux , the hospitals in Bukavu, Uvira and Fizi, in South Kivu, have admitted 170 casualties – 56% of the 303 patients admitted to ICRC-supported facilities.

r1-UV-2026Q2-012.s: DW reported that the repatriation of Congolese refugees who had fled to Burundi during the AFC-M23 occupation of Uvira in December began on Thursday, and that in Uvira the returnees were received at a transit centre where they were expected to receive resettlement kits.
r1-UV-2026Q2-012.l: Busuma camp (Burundi) to Uvira (city), South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-012.x: "hundreds" of refugees per DW headline; convoy count per body text not captured in the excerpts
r1-UV-2026Q2-012.n: Thursday = article date 23 April 2026 (page header states 23/04/2026). DW credits a Reuters image only. Another outlet in search results (Reuters via Facebook, snippet only) also reports Burundi starting to return Congolese refugees; not cited.
r1-UV-2026Q2-012.vn: Removed '23 April 2026', which no excerpt prints (the page is dated 23/04/2026 and says 'ce jeudi'; the date field carries it). The body figure (about 500 people, about ten convoys from Busuma camp) is in the replacement quote but in no stored excerpt, so it is left out of the statement and given in the note; extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt to add it. Byline Mitima Delachance. DW body text: 'Environ 500 Congolais ont traversé la frontière de Kavimrira' (DW's spelling, presumably Kavimvira), in about ten convoys from Busuma camp in Burundi to Uvira. Returnees Victorina Asele Ngondé and Mushombé Mbirizé are quoted on the page.
src: Le rapatriement des réfugiés congolais qui ont fui au Burundi l'occupation de la ville d'Uvira par les rebelles de l'AFC-M23, en décembre dernier, a débuté, ce jeudi, dans la province du Sud-Kivu
A Uvira , ces retournés ont été accueillis dans un centre de transit, où ils devraient bénéficier de kits de réinstallation.

r1-UV-2026Q2-013.s: OCHA's South Kivu situation report stated that armed clashes had intensified in the territories of Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe and Shabunda, and that rapid multisectoral assessments in March counted more than 542 200 returnees at provincial level, most of them concentrated in Uvira territory.
r1-UV-2026Q2-013.l: South Kivu (Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe, Shabunda territories); returnees concentrated in Uvira territory
r1-UV-2026Q2-013.x: more than 542 200 returnees at provincial level (March 2026 rapid multisectoral assessments), majority in Uvira territory
r1-UV-2026Q2-013.n: Covers March 2026 (before the unit's period); included because it is the UN baseline published in the period and quantifies returns to Uvira territory. Title wording is partly reconstructed from the URL and listing; the page title as fetched was not captured separately.
r1-UV-2026Q2-013.vn: Figure written as the source prints it (542 200) to clear the figure flag. The page says the report covers 1-31 March 2026 (in replacement_quotes; note only). Grade lowered from A to B: a single OCHA situation report compiling partner assessments is one credible non-partisan origin, not an investigation. Situation report #4 (21 April 2026), covering 1-31 March 2026, before this unit's period.
src: Les affrontements armés se sont intensifiés dans les territoires de Fizi, Mwenga, Uvira, Kalehe et Shabunda, aggravant les besoins humanitaires et les risques de nouveaux déplacements.
Les évaluations rapides multisectorielles réalisées en mars font état de plus de 542 200 personnes retournées à l’échelle provinciale, dont la majorité est concentrée dans le territoire d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q2-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Kavimvira bridge on the RN5 in Uvira collapsed on Tuesday 16 June; according to local health sources one person died and two were injured, a medical source quoted saying three people were injured, of whom a young boy died in hospital after a blow to the head and the other two had light injuries, while the NSCC Sud-Sud civil society group said in a statement that its field investigations showed three deaths, including two minors aged 14 and 17 and an adult, plus an injured woman. Local authorities had not yet commented officially on the circumstances of the collapse or the final toll.
r1-UV-2026Q2-014.l: Kavimvira bridge, RN5, Uvira (city), South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-014.x: Local health sources / medical source: 1 dead (a young boy), 2 lightly injured. NSCC Sud-Sud: 3 dead (two minors aged 14 and 17, one adult) and 1 injured woman. Discrepancy unresolved.
r1-UV-2026Q2-014.n: Not a conflict event; recorded as an Uvira event at the Kavimvira border crossing area that affects movement on the RN5. Death-toll discrepancy between sources is surfaced, not resolved. A modern bridge was reportedly under construction by EIS-EKA per NSCC coordinator. Victims are not named in the excerpts. Local authorities had not yet commented on the cause per the article.
r1-UV-2026Q2-014.vn: Removed the year (not in excerpt). Replaced 'the article does not attribute the collapse to the conflict' (an inference from absence) with the page's own statement that local authorities had not commented on the circumstances. Kept the two tolls separate, each attributed. No victim is named on the page. Toll differs: one dead (local health / medical source) vs three dead (NSCC Sud-Sud). Not presented as a conflict event.
src: Une personne a perdu la vie et deux autres ont été blessées lors de l’effondrement du pont de Kavimvira, survenu mardi 16 juin sur la Route nationale n°5 (RN5), à Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, selon des sources sanitaires locales.

Il y a eu trois blessés et parmi ces trois blessés, un a succombé à l’hôpital. Il s’agit d’un jeune garçon qui a reçu un coup à la tête et qui est décédé. Les deux autres présentent des blessures légères

De son côté, la Nouvelle Société Civile Congolaise (NSCC) Sud-Sud affirme que ses enquêtes de terrain font état d’un bilan plus lourd. Dans un communiqué publié mardi dans la soirée, l’organisation évoque trois décès, dont deux mineurs âgés de 14 et 17 ans ainsi qu’un adulte, en plus d’une femme blessée.

r1-UV-2026Q2-015.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the Human Rights Watch report 'Nous sommes des civils !', HRW documented eight cases of rape committed by M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers against women in and around Uvira between December 2025 and January 2026, with survivors describing being raped in their fields or homes, often under threat of death or at gunpoint.
r1-UV-2026Q2-015.l: Uvira (city) and surroundings (incl. Katala, Uvira territory), South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-015.a: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers (as alleged in the HRW report relayed by the source)
r1-UV-2026Q2-015.x: HRW (via Actualite.cd): eight rape cases documented
r1-UV-2026Q2-015.n: Relay of the HRW report, which another claim already cites; submitted here as a separate Congolese-media account in the unit's period. The events are dated December 2025-January 2026 (by the source), i.e. before this unit's window; the date field is the stated span at month precision. Survivors are not named in the page. HRW says survivors identified the perpetrators partly by Kinyarwanda and uniforms (not in these excerpts). Rwanda/AFC-M23 denials of the HRW findings were not found in an opened page (see gaps).
r1-UV-2026Q2-015.vn: Excerpt exact; the 'fields or homes / under threat of death or at gunpoint' clause is printed in the page body and the headline, supplied as a replacement quote. Every finding stays attributed to HRW. A relay of HRW, so not independent of the HRW origin; graded B as relayed (the HRW report itself would carry its own grade). Relay of HRW's report; events December 2025-January 2026 (before this unit's quarter). Survivors are unnamed on the page.
src: Selon le rapport, Human Rights Watch a documenté huit cas de viol commis par des combattants du M23 et des soldats rwandais sur des femmes dans et autour d’Uvira entre décembre 2025 et janvier 2026.
Les hommes, dont elle a identifié les uniformes comme étant ceux de militaires rwandais, l’ont violée.

r1-UV-2026Q2-016.s: Actualite.cd, relaying the Human Rights Watch report, reported that a woman assaulted while working in her field at Katala, Uvira territory, on 15 December, went to the Kavimvira medical centre in Uvira for care but could not be treated and left without essential medicines, receiving only a small number of tablets; HRW said survivors stressed the near-total lack of accessible health services during the M23 and Rwandan occupation, notably the absence of timely PEP treatment.
r1-UV-2026Q2-016.l: Kavimvira medical centre, Uvira (city); Katala, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r1-UV-2026Q2-016.a: not attributed by the source (service unavailable during M23/Rwandan occupation per HRW)
r1-UV-2026Q2-016.n: Pre-window event (Dec 2025) reported in the window; precedes the unit's period. Date '15 December' is the date of the assault in the source; the clinic visit followed ('ensuite') without a stated date. The survivor is unnamed in the page. The page states the 'Rwandan soldiers' attribution via HRW.
r1-UV-2026Q2-016.vn: Excerpts exact; the passage is HRW's ('a fait remarquer HRW dans son rapport') and the woman's account is relayed from the report. The page also says she identified the assailants' uniforms as Rwandan soldiers'; not needed for this health-access claim. The clinic visit followed the 15 December assault without a stated date. Assault dated 15 December (2025, per the report's Dec 2025-Jan 2026 span); clinic visit date not given. Survivor unnamed. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Elle s’est ensuite rendue au centre médical de Kavimvira à Uvira pour obtenir des soins, mais n’a pas pu être traitée. Elle est repartie sans médicaments essentiels, ne recevant qu’un petit nombre de comprimés.
Une autre femme citée dans le rapport, a raconté qu’elle a été agressée le 15 décembre alors qu’elle travaillait dans son champ à Katala, dans le territoire d’Uvira.

Dans tous ces témoignages, les survivantes ont souligné le manque quasi total de services de santé accessibles pendant l’occupation par le M23 et le Rwanda, en particulier l’absence de traitement PEP en temps voulu et de soins adéquats pour les blessures et les infections provoquées par les violences sexuelles.
She sought medical assistance afterwards at Kavimvira medical center in Uvira but was not able to be treated. She left without essential medication, receiving only a limited number of pills.

r1-UV-2026Q2-017.s: In the standfirst of an article, Jeune Afrique said that Uvira, the provisional capital, occupied for a month by AFC/M23 rebels, had remained a major fallback point for the wazalendo, militiamen who, seeking recognition and influence, had become as unavoidable as they were cumbersome; the summary of the series the article belongs to said the rebels had for now pulled back but that Uvira lived under permanent tension.
r1-UV-2026Q2-017.a: Wazalendo (militias allied to the Congolese army, per the source)
r1-UV-2026Q2-017.n: Paywalled series; only the standfirst/summary text and opening lines were retrievable, so the body (including a named Wazalendo-linked figure in Mulongwe quarter) is not captured. 'Published 9 June at 19:03, modified 10 June' per the page.
r1-UV-2026Q2-017.vn: Paywalled: the article body is not available. Source 0 is the article's standfirst; source 1 is the series summary ('Issu de la série Dans l'est de la RDC, Uvira face à la guerre'), not the article's text, so the statement now says which is which. 'Rear base' changed to the source's 'fallback point' (point de repli). Nothing from behind the paywall is used; the person named in the opening lines is not added. Paywalled article (by Romain Gras, in Uvira; published 9 June, modified 10 June); only the standfirst and the series summary were read.
src: Occupée pendant un mois par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, la capitale provisoire du Sud-Kivu, en RDC, est restée un point de repli majeur pour les wazalendo. En quête de reconnaissance et d’influence, ces miliciens sont devenus aussi incontournables qu’encombrants.
Les rebelles ont pour l’instant reculé, mais entre les wazalendos, alliés de circonstance de Kinshasa, et les équilibres régionaux qui se jouent à ses portes, Uvira vit sous tension permanente.

r1-UV-2026Q2-018.s: The UN Group of Experts on the DRC reported in its final report that in South Kivu no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued, and that additional RDF reinforcements arrived from Rwanda in April, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.
r1-UV-2026Q2-018.l: South Kivu (province-level statement; includes the Ruzizi plain north of Uvira)
r1-UV-2026Q2-018.a: RDF and AFC/M23 (as named by the Group of Experts)
r1-UV-2026Q2-018.n: UN panel report, document printed 19 June 2026 (ecoi.net listing date 11 June 2026). The paragraph is written before the May withdrawals from the Ruzizi plain were reported by media; it conflicts in time, not in fact, with the 10-11 May withdrawal reports. In the report, para 77 gives 18 January 2026 as the date AFC/M23 and RDF withdrew from Uvira city; this is outside the unit's period and not captured here. Footnote markers appear in the page text after 'systems'.
r1-UV-2026Q2-018.vn: Excerpt is para. 49 of S/2026/466 (letter dated 5 June 2026, distributed 11 June 2026), read in the retained PDF. The section opens 'At the time of drafting', so the 'no withdrawals documented' finding is as of the drafting date. Finding as of drafting (before 5 June 2026). It is in tension with the media reports of an AFC/M23 withdrawal from the Ruzizi plain on 9-11 May (DW, SOS Médias Burundi); the discrepancy is surfaced, not resolved. Para. 47 says the North Kivu withdrawals 'amounted to tactical repositioning'.
src: In South Kivu, no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued. Additional RDF reinforcements from Rwanda arrived in April, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.

r1-UV-2026Q2-019.s: Human Rights Watch said in a press release that Congolese armed forces and armed groups in the Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu were obstructing the delivery of humanitarian aid and preventing civilians from fleeing the fighting, and that the UN had described humanitarian access restrictions to the Hauts Plateaux, an area covering parts of the Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories, as 'severe'.
r1-UV-2026Q2-019.l: Hauts Plateaux of South Kivu (parts of Fizi, Mwenga and Uvira territories)
r1-UV-2026Q2-019.a: Congolese armed forces and armed groups in the Hauts Plateaux (as named by HRW)
r1-UV-2026Q2-019.n: Press release based on HRW interviews (Minembwe: Twirwaneho/M23-controlled; Baraka: Congolese army and Wazalendo). Mostly Fizi-area; included because the Hauts Plateaux include parts of Uvira territory. Not specific to the city of Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q2-019.vn: Both excerpts exact on the HRW page; statement follows them and keeps HRW and UN attributions separate. Mostly concerns the Fizi-area Hauts Plateaux; not specific to the city of Uvira.
src: Les forces armées congolaises et les groupes armés présents dans les Hauts Plateaux du Sud-Kivu entravent l’acheminement de l’aide humanitaire et empêchent les civils de fuir les combats dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo , a déclaré aujourd’hui Human Rights Watch.
L’ONU a qualifié de « sévères » les restrictions humanitaires pesant sur l’accès aux Hauts Plateaux du Sud-Kivu, une zone couvrant certaines parties des territoires de Fizi, Mwenga et Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q2-020.s: Radio Okapi reported, a year after the Washington peace accord, that the territories of Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale in North Kivu and those of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga in South Kivu remained the most affected by violence, with civilians displaced and material destruction.
r1-UV-2026Q2-020.l: North Kivu (Masisi, Rutshuru, Walikale) and South Kivu (Uvira, Fizi, Mwenga)
r1-UV-2026Q2-020.n: General context line; title reconstructed from the URL slug and may be abbreviated. No incident-level detail.
r1-UV-2026Q2-020.vn: Excerpt exact (page dated 27/06/2026; full title 'Kivu: un an après l’accord de Washington, les combats persistent sur le terrain'). General context line only. Context only; no incident-level detail.
src: Les territoires de Masisi, Rutshuru et Walikale au Nord-Kivu, ainsi que ceux d’Uvira, Fizi et Mwenga au Sud-Kivu, demeurent les plus touchés par les violences. Les combats ont entraîné le déplacement de milliers de civils, contraints de fuir leurs villages. Les destructions matérielles sont également importantes

r1-UV-2026Q3-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that Lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, said the positions of Kimete, Wihene and Kashamata had been retaken by the army, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho - RDF - Red Tabara elements had been forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.
r1-UV-2026Q3-001.l: Kimete, Wihene, Kashamata, highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga
r1-UV-2026Q3-001.n: FARDC claim relayed by a Congolese outlet, unverified; the article says the area is enclaved with poor phone coverage. The article is dated Tuesday 7 July and says the army 'ce lundi' announced its offensive; date 6 July computed from weekday and publication date.
r1-UV-2026Q3-001.vn: Excerpt carries every clause; party account kept attributed. Territory widened: the article places the fighting in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga around Minembwe. FARDC claim; the outlet says the area is enclaved and independent information arrives late. Date computed from 'ce lundi' in an article of Tuesday 7 July.
src: Selon le lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, porte-parole de l'opération Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, « les positions stratégiques de Kimete, Wihene et Kashamata ont été reprises par l'armée loyaliste ». « Les éléments de la coalition rebelle AFC/M23-Twirwaneho - RDF - Red Tabara ont été contraints de se replier en direction de Rugezi et Bigaragara, au sud de Minembwe », selon le porte-parole militaire.

r1-UV-2026Q3-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC denounced drone bombings attributed to the AFC/M23 the previous weekend in the village of Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, and other densely populated villages, killing about ten people according to the army communiqué.
r1-UV-2026Q3-002.l: Bidjaga, east of Point Zéro, highlands of Mwenga/Fizi
r1-UV-2026Q3-002.x: FARDC communiqué via Actualite.cd: about ten dead
r1-UV-2026Q3-002.n: Army communiqué relayed by media, no independent verification. Weekend date computed from publication date (7 July).
r1-UV-2026Q3-002.vn: Excerpt states the FARDC communiqué's allegation and toll ('une dizaine de morts, d'après le communiqué de l'armée'); kept attributed to the army. Single clause chain from one excerpt.
src: Les FARDC ont par ailleurs dénoncé des bombardements des drones attribués à l'AFC/M23 le week-end dernier dans le village de Bidjaga, à l’est de Point Zéro et d’autres villages densément peuplés faisant une dizaine de morts, d’après le communiqué de l’armée.

r1-UV-2026Q3-003.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in a statement signed by Fidèle Rugabo, the military spokesperson for the armed group Twirwaneho, the fighters claimed to have launched an offensive on Saturday, July 4, against the Point Zero position, before taking control after several hours of fighting; the outlet said no official reaction had been recorded at the time of publication.
r1-UV-2026Q3-003.l: Point Zero (Point Zéro), Itombwe sector, Mwenga
r1-UV-2026Q3-003.n: Partisan claim as reported by a Burundian outlet; the same outlet reports FARDC/FDNB withdrawal only from unverified local sources. Contradicted by FARDC claims and by Actualite.cd of 31 Aug saying Point Zéro was still occupied by AFC/M23 and under attack, so control changed hands or was contested.
r1-UV-2026Q3-003.vn: Original credited the claim to Twirwaneho and M23 'in a statement signed by Rugabo'; the signed statement is Twirwaneho's. Narrowed to the excerpt; the joint M23 claim and the location are on the page (lead) and in the note/location field. Party claim. The article's lead says the Twirwaneho armed group and the M23/AFC-M23 jointly claim the capture of Point Zero, in the Itombwe sector of Mwenga territory. Actualite.cd of 31 August says Point Zéro was then occupied by the AFC/M23 and under attack, so control was contested over the quarter.
src: In a statement signed by Fidèle Rugabo, the military spokesperson for the armed group Twirwaneho, the fighters claim to have launched an offensive on Saturday, July 4, against the Point Zero position, before taking control after several hours of fighting.

r1-UV-2026Q3-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that clashes at Point Zéro, on the limit of Fizi and Mwenga territories, had multiplied since Friday 28 August, with heavy weapons and drones used by both belligerents, according to local sources.
r1-UV-2026Q3-004.l: Point Zéro, border of Fizi and Mwenga
r1-UV-2026Q3-004.a: FARDC, wazalendo and Burundians vs AFC/M23
r1-UV-2026Q3-004.n: Same article says Point zéro is occupied by the AFC/M23 and that the army wants to retake it; not cited in this excerpt.
r1-UV-2026Q3-004.vn: Supported by the excerpt; local sources attribution kept. SOS Médias Burundi (31 Aug) independently reports fighting in the same highlands from Sunday 30 August.
src: Les affrontements se sont multipliés depuis le vendredi 28 août dernier, au village stratégique Point zéro, à la limite entre les territoires de Fizi et de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu. Selon des sources locales, les affrontements à l’arme lourde se sont intensifiés à cet endroit, les deux belligérants mettant également en contribution des drones.

r1-UV-2026Q3-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that a civil-society actor in the Fizi area said that from 4 a.m. on 31 August the government force FARDC, wazalendo and the Burundians launched a drone attack at Point zéro, causing massive displacement.
r1-UV-2026Q3-005.a: FARDC, wazalendo and Burundians (as described by a civil-society actor)
r1-UV-2026Q3-005.n: Single unnamed civil-society source; Burundian participation also reported by SOS Médias Burundi (31 Aug). No Burundi government statement found.
r1-UV-2026Q3-005.vn: Excerpt is the civil-society actor's quote verbatim; attribution kept, single unnamed source.
src: « Depuis 4h du matin aujourd'hui le 31 août, la force gouvernementale FARDC, wazalendo et les burundais ont lancé une attaque à l'aide des drones à point zéro. Cette situation occasionne de déplacement massif et une crise humanitaire

r1-UV-2026Q3-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira that fighting had been reported since Sunday in several areas of the territories of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga, between the FARDC supported by the FDNB and Wazalendo militias, and AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters.
r1-UV-2026Q3-006.l: Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha, Uvira territory (also Fizi, Mwenga)
r1-UV-2026Q3-006.a: FARDC, FDNB, Wazalendo vs AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho
r1-UV-2026Q3-006.n: Single outlet (Burundian independent media) relaying local sources; 'dimanche' = 30 August (computed from weekday and publication date). The detail on Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha and drones is in the following sentences of the same article. The Burundian government has not been found commenting.
r1-UV-2026Q3-006.vn: Excerpt supports it; Actualite.cd's same-day report of fighting at Point Zéro, Malimba and Rubarati corroborates the fighting.
src: Uvira, 31 août 2026 — Des combats sont signalés depuis dimanche dans plusieurs zones des territoires de Fizi, Uvira et Mwenga, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC). Les affrontements opposent les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC), appuyées par la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) et les milices Wazalendo entretenues par Kinshasa, aux combattants de l’AFC/M23 et de Twirwaneho.

r1-UV-2026Q3-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that a Wazalendo fighter present in the Malimba area said that the FARDC, the FDNB and the Wazalendo had retaken positions previously held by AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara fighters at Malimba, Ruhuha and Rubarati; SOS Médias Burundi noted this could not be independently verified.
r1-UV-2026Q3-007.a: Wazalendo fighter (anonymous) on behalf of FARDC/FDNB/Wazalendo
r1-UV-2026Q3-007.n: Anonymous combatant; unverified per the outlet.
r1-UV-2026Q3-007.vn: Both clauses on the page; party claim, unverified per the outlet. Anonymous combatant. Actualite.cd (31 Aug) separately cites local sources saying Malimba and Rubarati were retaken by the FARDC and Wazalendo, also unconfirmed.
src: Un combattant des milices Wazalendo entretenues par Kinshasa, présent dans la zone de Malimba, affirme que les FARDC, la FDNB et les milices Wazalendo entretenues par Kinshasa ont repris plusieurs positions précédemment occupées par des combattants de l’AFC/M23, de Twirwaneho et de Red Tabara à Malimba, Ruhuha et Rubarati.

r1-UV-2026Q3-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo said his fighters had repelled several attacks by the FARDC, the FDNB, the Wazalendo militias and the FDLR, citing in a post on X Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma and Point Zéro in Fizi and Mwenga territories; SOS Médias Burundi said these claims could not be independently verified.
r1-UV-2026Q3-008.l: Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma, Point Zéro, Fizi and Mwenga
r1-UV-2026Q3-008.n: Party claim; source_type marked partisan_afc_m23 as Twirwaneho is allied with the AFC/M23. The X post itself was not opened.
r1-UV-2026Q3-008.vn: Supported; party claim kept attributed. Territory is Fizi and Mwenga as the article states.
src: De son côté, le porte-parole de Twirwaneho, Fidèle Rugabo, affirme que ses combattants ont repoussé plusieurs attaques menées par les FARDC, la FDNB, les milices Wazalendo entretenues par Kinshasa et les FDLR. Dans un message publié sur le réseau social X, il cite notamment Kabanju, Kipupu, Nyamabuguma et Point Zéro, dans les territoires de Fizi et Mwenga.

r1-UV-2026Q3-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that two FDNB officers, Captain Félicien Kanjori and Major Jérémie Nitunga, were arrested after the drone strike attributed to the M23 on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi; they were reportedly arrested by mercenaries in the area and suspected of passing intelligence. The outlet said the Congolese and Burundian armies had not yet communicated on the arrests.
r1-UV-2026Q3-009.a: not attributed beyond 'mercenaries present in the area'
r1-UV-2026Q3-009.n: Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Outside Uvira city but records Burundian (FDNB) presence in the Fizi/Uvira theatre. Arrest date not given (reported 1 September).
r1-UV-2026Q3-009.vn: Every clause on the page; names printed in the excerpt. Single outlet, unnamed sources. The outlet adds that no public, independent evidence shows the officers passed intelligence, and that their reported transfer to Kinshasa (DEMIAP) is unconfirmed.
src: Deux officiers de la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB), le capitaine Félicien Kanjori et le major Jérémie Nitunga, ont été arrêtés après la frappe de drones attribuée au M23 contre l’hôtel Mwalu, à Fizi, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

r1-UV-2026Q3-010.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on 19 August 2026 the Mwalu hotel in Fizi was struck by drones, seriously injuring two people including the manager, Mwando Lukaba, with significant material damage; an FARDC spokesperson in the region attributed the attack to the M23 and said two bombs were dropped, which the outlet said could not be independently verified.
r1-UV-2026Q3-010.a: M23 (as attributed by an FARDC spokesperson)
r1-UV-2026Q3-010.x: SOS Médias Burundi: two seriously injured
r1-UV-2026Q3-010.n: The outlet says the hotel hosted several Congolese and Burundian military officials; the target character is the outlet's account of local sources.
r1-UV-2026Q3-010.vn: Supported; attribution stays with the FARDC spokesperson.
src: Le 19 août 2026, l’hôtel Mwalu, à Fizi, a été frappé par des drones. Deux personnes, dont le gérant de l’établissement, Mwando Lukaba, ont été grièvement blessées et d’importants dégâts matériels ont été enregistrés. Un porte-parole des FARDC dans la région avait attribué l’attaque au M23 et indiqué que deux bombes avaient été larguées par des drones.

r1-UV-2026Q3-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the citizen platform MCLA-RDC said in a communiqué published Tuesday 4 August 2026 that at least four armed incidents were recorded between 1 and 4 August, causing the deaths of four people, several injuries and concern among residents.
r1-UV-2026Q3-011.x: MCLA-RDC via Radio Okapi: 4 killed 1-4 August
r1-UV-2026Q3-011.n: Civil-society movement claim relayed by Radio Okapi; the article places the incidents in Uvira. City authorities had not yet communicated officially, per Radio Okapi. Radio Okapi of 13 Aug (separate claim) reports at least six killed since the start of August per local sources; figures not additive.
r1-UV-2026Q3-011.vn: Excerpt supports the statement exactly; graded C as a single civil-society origin. Citizen-movement figures relayed by Radio Okapi; the city authorities had not communicated. Overlaps with the 'at least six killed since the start of August' figure (not additive).
src: Dans un communiqué publié mardi 4 août 2026, la plateforme citoyenne fait état d’au moins quatre incidents armés enregistrés entre le 1er et le 4 août, ayant causé la mort de quatre personnes, plusieurs blessés et semé l’inquiétude parmi les habitants.

r1-UV-2026Q3-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to MCLA-RDC, on 1 August in the Kavimvira quarter of Uvira a woman identified as Aimée Vumilia, aged 31 and mother of five children, was reportedly hit by a bullet, and on 2 August the lifeless body of a man was found in the Murambia zone of the Mulongwe-Kasenga quarter.
r1-UV-2026Q3-012.n: Names-only detail on the MCLA-RDC claim. Whether Aimée Vumilia died is not stated in the excerpt.
r1-UV-2026Q3-012.vn: Excerpt prints the name, age and the conditional 'aurait été touchée'; statement keeps 'reportedly'.
src: Le 1er août, dans le quartier Kavimvira, une femme identifiée comme Aimée Vumilia, âgée de 31 ans et mère de cinq enfants, aurait été touchée par balle. Le 2 août, dans le quartier Mulongwe-Kasenga, le corps sans vie d’un homme a été retrouvé dans la zone de Murambia.

r1-UV-2026Q3-013.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at least six people had been killed since the start of August in several quarters of Uvira, amid a recrudescence of night attacks attributed to armed men.
r1-UV-2026Q3-013.x: Radio Okapi (local sources): at least 6 killed since start of August
r1-UV-2026Q3-013.n: Figure is from unnamed local sources; overlaps with MCLA-RDC figure of 4 deaths for 1-4 August (not additive).
r1-UV-2026Q3-013.vn: Narrowed: the vehicle-handover clause (six 4x4s on 11 August) is not in the excerpt and is not part of this incident claim. Single anonymous-local-source figure, so C.
src: Cette réception intervient dans un contexte marqué par une recrudescence des attaques nocturnes attribuées à des hommes armés. Selon des sources locales, au moins six personnes ont été tuées depuis le début du mois d’août dans plusieurs quartiers d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q3-014.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing official local sources, that police vehicles received in Uvira had been kept hidden for nearly a year in Burundi after the capture of Uvira by the AFC/M23 rebels.
r1-UV-2026Q3-014.l: Uvira, South Kivu (vehicles handed over; earlier held in Burundi)
r1-UV-2026Q3-014.n: Single outlet quoting official local sources. Date is the handover date (Tuesday 11 August per the article). Context on Burundi's role as refuge for Congolese state equipment during the AFC/M23 occupation.
r1-UV-2026Q3-014.vn: 'six PNC vehicles' was not in the excerpt; narrowed. Category changed from looting_or_destruction: the source describes state vehicles kept safe in Burundi, not looting. Discrepancy: Uvira was taken on 10 December 2025 (HRW, UV-2025Q4), about eight months before the August 2026 handover, not 'nearly a year'; recorded as the source says.
src: Selon des sources officielles locales, ces véhicules étaient restés cachés pendant près d’un an au Burundi, après la prise d’Uvira par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r1-UV-2026Q3-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that users of the Uvira-Luvungi, Mwenga-Uvira and Uvira-Fizi-Baraka roads denounced barriers erected by certain Wazalendo fighters, and that according to several testimonies it collected on Tuesday 4 August, taxes of 10 000 to 50 000 Congolese francs would be demanded of travellers.
r1-UV-2026Q3-015.x: Radio Okapi (testimonies): 10 000 to 50 000 Congolese francs per traveller
r1-UV-2026Q3-015.n: Testimonies gathered by Radio Okapi; the youth council of Mwenga alleges ill-treatment of those who refuse or delay payment (see separate official_statement claim).
r1-UV-2026Q3-015.vn: The source's conditional ('seraient exigées') was rendered as fact ('are made to pay'); restored. Figures written as the excerpt prints them. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 4 Aug 2026, carries every clause, the taxes in the conditional ('seraient exigées'); the stored excerpt lacks the roads and the barriers clause, added here.
src: Selon plusieurs témoignages recueillis ce mardi 4 aout par Radio Okapi, des taxes allant de 10 000 à 50 000 francs congolais seraient exigées aux voyageurs, suscitant de vives inquiétudes au sein de la population.

Les usagers des routes Uvira-Luvungi, Mwenga-Uvira et Uvira-Fizi-Baraka ( Sud-Kivu) dénoncent la multiplication des barrières érigées par certains combattants Wazalendo, engagés aux côtés des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) dans la lutte contre l’AFC/M23.

r1-UV-2026Q3-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Vice-Governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, urged all Wazalendo components to act responsibly and respect the provisions set by the Provincial Security Council, and called for the dismantling of all unauthorised barriers.
r1-UV-2026Q3-016.n: Provincial authority statement as reported by Radio Okapi. Other pages call him interim governor (Radio Okapi 3 Aug).
r1-UV-2026Q3-016.vn: Official statement as reported; excerpt supports both clauses.
src: Réagissant à ces dénonciations, le vice-gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, a exhorté toutes les composantes des Wazalendo à faire preuve de responsabilité et à respecter les dispositions arrêtées par le Conseil provincial de sécurité. Il a notamment appelé au démantèlement de toutes les barrières non autorisées, afin de mettre fin aux perceptions illégales signalées par les usagers.

r1-UV-2026Q3-017.s: Actualite.cd reported that six civil-society actors of Baraka, including their president Etunda Maisha Albert, were released on the afternoon of 27 August from Uvira central prison; they had been arrested on 13 August at Baraka-Centre in Fizi territory and transferred to Uvira days later.
r1-UV-2026Q3-017.a: not attributed in the cited passage
r1-UV-2026Q3-017.n: Same article (later passages) says local civil society reports they were arrested for denouncing illegal barriers erected by soldiers in the village of Katanga, Baraka, and names others arrested (Mukindula Ally le Bon, Shabani Denis, Augustin Balongelwa, Elias Wasirene); not cited here. Actor responsible for arrest not named in excerpt.
r1-UV-2026Q3-017.vn: Supported; release confirmed on the page by the Fizi civil-society president. Later on the page: local civil society says they were arrested for denouncing an illegal barrier set up by soldiers at Katanga (Baraka), which the local FARDC commander had authorised; the page also names Mukindula Ally le Bon, Shabani Denis, Augustin Balongelwa and Elias Wasirene among those arrested. These are not in the stored excerpt, so they are leads only.
src: Six acteurs clés de la société civile de Baraka, dont son président Etunda Maisha Albert, le vice-président de la FEC/Baraka, ainsi que plusieurs autres membres, ont été libérés dans l’après-midi du 27 août de la prison centrale d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu. Ces acteurs avaient été arrêtés le 13 août à Baraka-Centre, dans le territoire de Fizi, avant d’être transférés à Uvira quelques jours plus tard.

r1-UV-2026Q3-018.s: Actualite.cd reported that shots were heard in Uvira from early morning on Wednesday 16 September, at Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda and elsewhere, and that a local civil-society source said a fourth-year primary pupil of EP Umoja de Kamongola was shot dead at Kalundu.
r1-UV-2026Q3-018.l: Uvira city (Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda)
r1-UV-2026Q3-018.a: shooters not identified in the excerpt (see next claim)
r1-UV-2026Q3-018.x: Actualite.cd: at least one pupil killed
r1-UV-2026Q3-018.n: Local civil-society source via Actualite.cd; the pupil is not named. Schools sent pupils home, trade was disrupted and transport between Bukavu and Uvira was suspended, per the same article.
r1-UV-2026Q3-018.vn: All clauses on the page; the date sits in the lead paragraph (excerpt gap only).
src: Ces sources parlent des tirs entendus à Kavimvira, Kasenga, Kalundu, Mulongwe, Kimanga, Nyamianda et ailleurs. Au moins un écolier est mort dans la matinée. « Un élève de quatrième année primaire de l 'EP Umoja de Kamongola a été tué par balles à Kalundu », confie à ACTUAITE.CD une source de la société civile locale.

r1-UV-2026Q3-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that many sources described the 16 September shooting in Uvira as an expression of 'anger' by wazalendo after one of their members was arrested by the army on 5 September, the reasons for which were not known; residents said leaflets demanding his release had circulated the previous day.
r1-UV-2026Q3-019.n: Unnamed sources; no FARDC, provincial government or Wazalendo statement on the incident found in the searches run.
r1-UV-2026Q3-019.vn: Supported; attribution to unnamed sources kept, no party statement found.
src: De nombreuses sources rapportent qu’il s’agit d’une expression de « colère » des wazalendo après l'arrestation d'un des leurs par l’armée depuis le 5 septembre dernier. Les motifs de cette arrestation ne sont pas connues.

r1-UV-2026Q3-020.s: Actualite.cd reported that on 15 September the Congolese National Police dispersed a C64 coalition demonstration in Uvira against changing the constitution, and that rapporteur François Igilima said four people were arrested and taken away by the police.
r1-UV-2026Q3-020.x: François Igilima: four arrested; Actualite.cd headline: at least 4
r1-UV-2026Q3-020.n: Other witnesses in the same article name Ensemble pour la République's Uvira federal president Guylain Kikwire among those arrested, and the article says the mayor banned the event citing Ebola; these are in other passages and are not cited here. Not directly about armed conflict: records a state administration measure in Uvira.
r1-UV-2026Q3-020.vn: Supported clause by clause. Other witnesses on the page name Guylain Kikwire (Ensemble pour la République federal president in Uvira) among those arrested; the mayor had banned the event citing Ebola.
src: Le rapporteur du cadre de concertation de la société civile congolaise, François Igilima, indique que quatre personnes ont été arrêtées et amenées par la police.

r1-UV-2026Q3-021.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced 18 soldiers of the Simba battalion to death for cowardice at the front in a verdict delivered on 4 September, without extenuating circumstances; the trial had opened on 23 August.
r1-UV-2026Q3-021.n: Verdict date (4 Sept), trial opening (23 Aug) and tribunal president Lt-Col Mupenda Munangi Joël are in later sentences of the same article. SOS Médias Burundi later (6 Oct 2026, out of window) reports a similar sentence for 27 Republican Guard soldiers at Uvira. Names of the convicted not printed.
r1-UV-2026Q3-021.vn: Supported; procedural stage (sentence at first instance) kept. First-instance sentence by a garrison military tribunal as reported; no appeal outcome is reported.
src: Le tribunal militaire garnison d’Uvira a condamné à la peine de mort 18 militaires du bataillon Simba, poursuivis pour lâcheté au front. Dans son réquisitoire, le ministère public avait requis la peine de mort contre l’ensemble des prévenus, accusés d’avoir fait preuve de lâcheté au front.

r1-UV-2026Q3-022.s: MediaCongo reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi said that preliminary estimates counted up to 49 mass graves identified in the Uvira sector and that more than 241 bodies had already been counted in three of them alone. This entry is dated by the article reporting the statement: the graves relate to killings during the earlier rebel occupation of the city (see actor), not to events of this quarter.
r1-UV-2026Q3-022.a: DRC provincial government of South Kivu (speaker); AFC/M23 and allies alleged
r1-UV-2026Q3-022.x: Governor Purusi (via MediaCongo / Top Congo FM): up to 49 mass graves in the Uvira sector; more than 241 bodies in three of them
r1-UV-2026Q3-022.n: Statement by a party (DRC provincial government), not independent forensic findings; the article says forensic doctors were awaited for exhumations and DNA sampling. In the following sentence the article reports the governor's estimate of more than 340 bodies in total, attributed to massacres during the 30 days of occupation (not cited here); media on 11 Sept (Actu7/Top Congo) carried a version with 110 mass graves (not opened here: Actu7 page could not be fetched); the two grave counts (49 vs 110) differ and are not reconciled. Killings relate to the Dec 2025-Jan 2026 occupation, outside this quarter; date is the date of the statement (article date). No AFC/M23 or Rwandan response found.
r1-UV-2026Q3-022.vn: Statement made explicit that the entry is dated by the report while the graves concern the December 2025-January 2026 occupation. Figures field had unsourced social-media numbers (110, 340, 11 Sept); removed to the note. Party statement (provincial government), not a forensic finding: the article says forensic doctors were still awaited for exhumations and DNA sampling. Only the cited figure stands. Social-media headlines of mid-September carried a count of 110 graves that no retained page supports; the two grave counts are not reconciled. The article's next sentence gives a possible total of more than 340 bodies (not in the stored excerpt). Date of the broadcast itself not given; the article is of 30 September 2026.
src: Selon le gouverneur Jean-Jacques Purusi, les estimations préliminaires recensent jusqu'à 49 fosses communes identifiées dans le secteur d'Uvira. « Rien que dans trois de ces fosses communes, nous comptabilisons déjà plus de 241 corps », a précisé le chef de l'exécutif provincial.

r1-UV-2026Q3-023.s: Radio Okapi reported that at the GENOCOST day ceremony in Uvira on Sunday 2 August, survivors of the recent occupation of the city by the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition recounted violence they said they witnessed or suffered, notably executions of civilians, disappearances and other serious human rights violations.
r1-UV-2026Q3-023.l: Place du Monument, Mulongwe commune, Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q3-023.n: Survivor testimony at an official commemoration, no individual accounts printed; the ceremony was chaired by interim governor Jean-Jacques Elakano M'Yewa on behalf of Governor Purusi, who announced continued identification of victims linked to the mass graves and a provincial GENOCOST memorial project in Uvira (same article). Attribution to RDF/AFC-M23 is the article's wording about the occupation.
r1-UV-2026Q3-023.vn: Supported; testimony stays attributed to survivors. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 3 Aug 2026, carries every clause; the stored excerpt does not name the survivors as survivors of the occupation of Uvira by the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition, so that sentence is added.
src: Devant une assistance silencieuse et émue, ils ont relaté les violences dont ils disent avoir été témoins ou victimes, notamment des exécutions de civils, des disparitions et d’autres atteintes graves aux droits humains.
L’un des moments marquant de cette commémoration a été la prise de parole de plusieurs survivants de la récente occupation de la ville d’Uvira par la coalition RDF/AFC-M23.

r1-UV-2026Q3-024.s: Global Voices, republishing an article by IciCongo, reported that health actors recorded more than 1 100 cases of rape in only three months in the Uvira health zone. This entry is dated by the article's publication; the article does not attribute perpetrators or name the data holder, and it dates the three months inconsistently (see note).
r1-UV-2026Q3-024.l: Uvira health zone (zone de santé d'Uvira)
r1-UV-2026Q3-024.a: perpetrators not attributed in the excerpt
r1-UV-2026Q3-024.x: Global Voices/IciCongo: more than 1 100 rape cases in three months (health actors)
r1-UV-2026Q3-024.n: Page subtitle gives the period as December 2025 to February 2026 ('Entre décembre 2025 et février 2026, plus de 1100 cas de viol enregistrés dans la zone de santé d'Uvira'); published in this quarter. The source does not name the data owner or attribute perpetrators. Civil-society coordinator Mapenzi Manyebwa calls the figure an alarm signal in a later passage. Not for use as a count of conflict-related cases without a data owner.
r1-UV-2026Q3-024.vn: Dated by report date with the period made explicit; grade lowered to C (single outlet, unnamed data owner, period stated two ways on the page). The rape count concerns an earlier period, not this quarter: the article's subtitle gives December 2025 to February 2026, while its body refers to figures of the first quarter of 2026. The data owner is unnamed ('acteurs de santé') and the cases are not described as conflict-related. Do not use as a count of conflict-related sexual violence. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Les acteurs de santé ont enregistré plus de 1 100 cas de viol en seulement trois mois dans la zone de santé d’Uvira.
1 129 cas de violences sexuelles ont été enregistrés entre décembre 2025 et février 2026. Selon les professionnels de santé, ces chiffres traduisent une situation alarmante.

r1-UV-2026Q3-025.s: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH) recorded 2 607 violations in conflict-affected provinces between January and June 2026, concerning 5 032 victims, and noted that despite the AFC/M23's withdrawal from Uvira and the Ruzizi plain, reprisals, displacement and an intensification of fighting continued to be reported in the highlands.
r1-UV-2026Q3-025.l: Conflict-affected provinces; Uvira, Ruzizi plain and highlands mentioned
r1-UV-2026Q3-025.a: AFC/M23 (expansion noted by BCNUDH); perpetrators of reprisals not specified
r1-UV-2026Q3-025.x: BCNUDH via Radio Okapi: 2 607 violations, 5 032 victims in conflict-affected provinces (Jan-Jun 2026)
r1-UV-2026Q3-025.n: BCNUDH findings relayed by Radio Okapi; the primary BCNUDH report was not located. The article headline gives about 3 000 violations nationwide.
r1-UV-2026Q3-025.vn: Supported; relay of a UN body, origin named. Radio Okapi relays a BCNUDH communiqué of 22 September 2026; the nationwide total in the same article is 2 996 violations.
src: Entre janvier et juin 2026, le BCNUDH a recensé 2 607 violations dans les provinces affectées par les conflits, concernant 5 032 victimes. Le Bureau relève la poursuite des hostilités et de l’expansion territoriale de l’AFC/M23. Malgré son retrait d’Uvira et de la plaine de la Ruzizi, des représailles, des déplacements de populations et une intensification des combats ont continué à être signalés dans les hauts plateaux.

r1-UV-2026Q3-026.s: Radio Okapi reported that Uvira's national deputy Claude Misare, in a letter of Monday 17 August to the Minister of National Defence, asked for clarification on the destination of resources for the support of Wazalendo deployed in combat zones.
r1-UV-2026Q3-026.a: Claude Misare, national deputy for Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q3-026.n: Statement by an elected official, not the executive. The same article reports the deputy as affirming that more than 4 million US dollars would be disbursed monthly by the Treasury for these fighters ('seraient décaissés'); that is a claim in a different passage, not cited here and not verified.
r1-UV-2026Q3-026.vn: Supported; elected official's statement. The deputy's claim that more than 4 million US dollars a month would be disbursed (conditional) is in another passage and unverified.
src: Dans une lettre adressée lundi 17 août au ministre de la Défense nationale, Claude Misare demande des éclaircissements sur la destination de ces ressources, notamment sur les mécanismes de prise en charge des Wazalendo déployés dans les zones de combat.

r1-UV-2026Q3-027.s: Radio Okapi reported that Uvira was largely paralysed on Wednesday 5 August by a ville morte day called by local forces vives to press the central government over the deteriorating security situation in the highlands of Uvira and in Fizi, with civil society asking for modern military equipment for the FARDC and Wazalendo.
r1-UV-2026Q3-027.l: Uvira city, also Sange and Kawizi
r1-UV-2026Q3-027.n: The demand for equipment and the spread to Sange and Kawizi are in later passages of the same article; no major incident was reported during the day.
src: Les activités socio-économiques sont restées largement paralysées ce mercredi 5 aout dans la ville d'Uvira, à la suite d'un appel à une journée ville morte lancé par les forces vives locales.

Ces affrontements signalés à près de 50 kilomètres de la Route Nationale numéro 5 ont perturbé le trafic entre Bukavu et Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q4-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced 27 soldiers to death for cowardice before the enemy on Friday, in a trial of 112 soldiers prosecuted after fleeing clashes; the verdict was given on 2 October, with five years for 54 soldiers.

Le verdict, rendu le 2 octobre, comprend également des peines de cinq ans de servitude pénale pour 54 militaires.

r1-UV-2026Q4-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that six women soldiers were among those convicted of violating orders and cowardice, with the sentences passed against them not specified.

Le verdict a été rendu samedi 3 octobre, après environ 2 semaines d’audiences à la prison centrale d’Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q4-010.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that the situation remained tense on Friday 2 October at Kabindula, seat of the Bavira chiefdom in Uvira territory, after the installation of a new groupement head, Kabale Ghislain, who replaces Romain Lenge, who had been acting.

La cérémonie d’intronisation de Kabale Ghislain s’est déroulée sous haute protection. Il remplace Romain Lenge, qui assurait jusque-là l’intérim à la tête de la chefferie.

src: Des combats ont opposé lundi 26 octobre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) aux combattants du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) dans plusieurs localités des territoires de Fizi et de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu.

D’après des sources de la société civile, les combats se sont concentrés dans les zones de Kawihene, Rugezi, Point Zéro et leurs environs, dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi. Les deux camps auraient fait usage de drones et d’artillerie lourde au cours des affrontements.

Ces dernières assurent que cette agglomération demeure sous leur contrôle.

r1-UV-2026Q4-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that Captain Sylvain Bijanu, spokesperson of the 33rd military region, rejected the information about an FRN advance towards Uvira, and that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi denounced a 'media war' by FRN fighters and called Uvira a 'fortress' protected by the FARDC and their allies.

src: Le porte-parole de la 33ᵉ région militaire, le capitaine Sylvain Bijanu, a également rejeté les informations faisant état d’une progression du FRN vers Uvira.

De son côté, le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a dénoncé ce qu’il qualifie de « guerre médiatique » menée par les combattants du FRN pour semer la psychose au sein de la population. Il a assuré que la ville d’Uvira reste sous la protection des FARDC et de leurs alliés, la qualifiant de « forteresse »

r1-UV-2026Q4-019.s: Taarifa Rwanda reported, citing frontline sources, that FRN fighters captured the Kahwizi (Kawizi) locality less than 10 kilometres from Uvira city.
r1-UV-2026Q4-019.l: Kahwizi (Kawizi), less than 10 km from Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q4-019.x: Taarifa: less than 10 km from Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q4-019.n: Taarifa is a Rwandan outlet reported as pro-Kigali and uses anonymous sources; denied by FARDC and local forces per Radio Okapi. Classified partisan out of caution; not a state agency.
r1-UV-2026Q4-019.vn: Excerpt verbatim. source_type changed from partisan_rwanda_government to partisan_rwanda_aligned_media: Taarifa is not a Rwandan state organ (unlike Imvaho Nshya or MINAFFET), but is treated as partisan; it stays 'Taarifa says'. src: Fighters of the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) captured Kahwizi(Kawizi) locality located less than 10 kilometers from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu.

r1-UV-2026Q4-020.s: The Rio Times reported that Taarifa wrote on 27 October that FRN fighters had captured the villages of Gitabo, Nyabigega and Mangwa, and had taken Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango and Rugomero, heading toward Runingu.
r1-UV-2026Q4-020.l: Gitabo, Nyabigega, Mangwa, Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango, Rugomero; Runingu
r1-UV-2026Q4-020.x: Rio Times relaying Taarifa: Runingu less than 7 km from Uvira
r1-UV-2026Q4-020.n: Secondhand relay of a Rwandan outlet's claim; denied by the army per Radio Okapi. Rio Times is a digest outlet; treat as lead.
r1-UV-2026Q4-020.vn: Excerpt verbatim on the Rio Times page; originating source is Taarifa; not independent confirmation of anything. Second-hand relay of a partisan-aligned Rwandan outlet; the Taarifa article naming these villages was not retained (the retained Taarifa page does not name them). Rio Times adds that no Congolese outlet or official source had confirmed rebels hold these villages.
src: Taarifa, a Rwandan news site, wrote on Tuesday 27 October that FRN fighters had captured the villages of Gitabo, Nyabigega and Mangwa. It added that the rebels had taken Kuwamabuye, Nyarurango and Rugomero and were heading toward Runingu, which it put less than 7 km from Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q4-021.s: The Rio Times reported that Congolese officials said the rebels had not advanced, and that Radio Okapi reported the army and the South Kivu governor call Uvira calm and secure.
r1-UV-2026Q4-021.n: Relay of Radio Okapi; the primary Radio Okapi page is cited in separate claims.

src: Congolese officials say the rebels have not advanced, after a report by the Rwandan news site Taarifa on Tuesday 27 October 2026. Radio Okapi, a Congolese radio network, reported the same day that the army and the South Kivu governor call Uvira calm and secure.

des rumeurs largement relayées sur les réseaux sociaux ont fait état d’une avancée des troupes du Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) vers le village de Kawizi, situé à environ 10 kilomètres de la ville d’Uvira.

src: Le Parlement citoyen pour la démocratie et la bonne gouvernance alerte sur cette situation dans une note rendue publique et consultée par Radio Maendeleo ce mardi 27 octobre 2026.

Cette prise de position fait suite à des alertes concernant des arrestations, des agressions et des enlèvements présumés d’habitants dans plusieurs zones du Sud-Kivu, particulièrement sur l’axe Nyangezi-Kamanyola, en territoire de Walungu.
Dans cette zone, le Parlement citoyen évoque notamment l’interpellation d’une dizaine de jeunes originaires des villages de Bujenjere et Nacirhongwe
alors qu’ils se trouvaient le long de la route nationale numéro 5, sur l’axe Bukavu-Uvira.

r1-UV-2026Q4-030.s: Agenzia Fides reported that fighting resumed on 26 October in South Kivu on the Fizi highlands, and that the city of Uvira, a bastion of government forces supported by elements of the Burundian army and by pro-government Wazalendo militiamen engaged in fighting against rebel forces led by former president Joseph Kabila, "remains the main target".
r1-UV-2026Q4-030.n: Fides is a Catholic missionary news agency.

src: Le 26 octobre, les combats ont repris dans le Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), sur les hauts plateaux de Fizi.

La ville d’Uvira, bastion des forces gouvernementales soutenues par des éléments de l’armée burundaise et par les miliciens pro-gouvernementaux Wazalendo, engagés dans les combats contre les forces rebelles menées par l’ancien président congolais Joseph Kabila, reste la cible principale.

src: L’ACMEJ rapporte par ailleurs que, lors d’un discours prononcé à Kamanyola le 17 octobre, une délégation du FRN et du Rwanda aurait fait part à la population civile de son intention de lancer une nouvelle offensive contre les villages de la plaine de Ruzizi, les zones des hauts plateaux et une partie du territoire de Mwenga.
La reprise des combats près d’Uvira avait été annoncée par une note envoyée le 23 octobre à l’Agence Fides par l’ACMEJ
Selon l’organisation, l’objectif serait de reprendre Uvira et d’avancer vers Fizi

Le plan prévoit d’atteindre Lubarika, de descendre vers Luvungi et de procéder à la conquête de la ville d’Uvira

r1-UV-2026Q4-034.s: BBC Gahuza reported a statement by FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka that Brigadier General François Kamanzi was head of operations in the 12th military region in Kongo-Central province and that two other senior soldiers also chose to join the FRN.

src: Le ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité publique et du Développement communautaire, Léonidas Ndaruzaniye, a annoncé jeudi que les personnes originaires de ces territoires, mais aussi celles qui y ont simplement transité, ne seront pas autorisées à entrer au Burundi.
Le ministre a ensuite poursuivi son intervention à huis clos. « Nous sommes les alliés de Kinshasa »

r1-UV-2026Q4-036.s: Actualite.cd reported that the public hearings of the Uvira trial opened on 15 September in flagrante procedure and concerned soldiers who fled clashes between the FARDC and fighters of the AFC/M23 coalition, RED Tabara and Twirhaneho.

Two women human rights defenders protesting forced expulsions of civilians in Uvira, South Kivu, were reportedly abducted and tortured by M23 elements. Their fate and whereabouts remain unknown.

src: “We are horrified by the gravity and brutality of the abuse committed against human rights defenders and their families,” the experts said. “There are allegations of attempted killings, repeated kidnappings, torture, sexual violence and death threats at the hands of M23, targeting those peacefully documenting abuses, supporting their communities and speaking out against violations.”

Des allégations font état de tentatives d’assassinat, d’enlèvements répétés, de torture, de violences sexuelles et de menaces de mort perpétrées par le M23, visant ceux qui documentent pacifiquement les exactions, soutiennent leurs communautés et dénoncent les violations

r2-G-BLOCKED-003.s: UN experts said that a woman human rights defender working on LGBT rights was abducted multiple times and severely tortured and continues to be aggressively pursued, and that in another case armed men allegedly raided a defender's home and abducted and violently assaulted his spouse to force her to reveal his whereabouts.

src: One woman human rights defender working on LGBT rights was abducted multiple times, severely tortured and continues to be aggressively pursued.

src: Selon son président, les récits recueillis évoquent des violences sexuelles liées au conflit – « y compris l’esclavage sexuel » –, des recrutements forcés, des homicides illégaux, des arrestations arbitraires, ainsi que des attaques contre des écoles et des établissements de santé.

Les combats ont profondément affecté les systèmes de santé, l’éducation, le commerce et la gouvernance locale. À cette dégradation s’ajoute désormais l’épidémie d’ Ebola qui sévit actuellement dans l’est congolais et complique encore davantage l’accès aux populations et le travail des organisations humanitaires.
Les attaques contre des infrastructures essentielles, telles que des écoles et des établissements de santé, figurent aussi parmi les violations documentées.

Une société prise au piège ONU Info Les viols, les viols collectifs, les agressions d'une violence extrême et les assassinats de civils constituent une caractéristique récurrente du mode opératoire du M23, affirment des experts.
RDC : une commission de l’ONU alerte sur une crise des droits humains « d'une gravité exceptionnelle » 29 juin 2026
Ses membres ne prétendent ni établir les responsabilités ni mesurer, à ce stade, l’ampleur exacte des crimes dénoncés.

r2-G-BLOCKED-007.s: UN News reported that the Security Council renewed on Monday, until 1 July 2027, the sanctions regime on armed groups active in the DRC and the mandate of its Group of Experts, and in its resolution reaffirmed its demand for an 'immediate and unconditional' withdrawal of Rwandan forces from Congolese territory, an end to Kigali's support for M23 and an end to Congolese army support for the FDLR.

Date 29 June 2026 inferred from 'lundi' and the page date (29 June 2026 is a Monday).
src: Dans sa résolution, le Conseil réaffirme son exigence d'un retrait « immédiat et inconditionnel » des forces rwandaises du territoire congolais, la fin du soutien de Kigali au M23 et la cessation de l’appui apporté par l'armée congolaise aux FDLR.
le Conseil de sécurité de l’ONU a renouvelé lundi jusqu'au 1er juillet 2027 le régime de sanctions visant les groupes armés actifs en RDC, ainsi que le mandat du groupe d'experts

r2-G-BLOCKED-008.s: MSF reported that the current frontline at Katogota in South Kivu bisects the road connecting Bukavu and Uvira, and that M23/AFC's position on Katogota was putting pressure on Uvira, which was under government control.
r2-G-BLOCKED-008.a: M23/AFC; Congolese government forces (as MSF describes)

src: The current frontline at Katogota in South Kivu bisects the vital road connecting the cities of Bukavu and Uvira, significantly limiting access for the communities and isolating them on either side.
The position of M23/AFC on Katogota, at the frontline, has been putting significant pressure on Uvira, which is under government control.

r2-G-BLOCKED-009.s: MSF reported that the area of Kamanyola, next to Katogota, was under M23/AFC control and that its healthcare system had been weakened by violence.

src: the situation in the city of Kamanyola, next to Katogota, is equally complex. This area, under M23/AFC control, has also seen its healthcare system weakened by violence.

r2-G-BLOCKED-010.a: Congolese army and Wazalendo (clashes, per residents quoted by MSF); shooter not identified for the facility gunfire
r2-G-BLOCKED-010.n: MSF does not name the shooter or the facilities in this passage; an MSF-quoted patient's mother described gunfire inside Uvira General hospital (same page).

Same page quotes a mother at the mpox centre of Uvira General hospital: 'We all panicked when we heard gunfire inside the hospital'. src: In February, residents reported increased violence and clashes in Uvira between the Congolese army and its alleged allies, the Wazalendo fighters - a coalition of armed groups opposed to M23/AFC. Medical facilities were not spared from gunfire, hampering patients' access to care.

Les habitants décrivent des scènes de pillages, de violence accrue, et des affrontements au sein de la ville entre les soldats de l’armée congolaise (FARDC) et les combattants Wazalendo. Les structures médicales n’ont pas été épargnées par les tirs, compromettant la prise en charge des patients.

r2-G-BLOCKED-011.s: MSF reported that persistent insecurity had rendered the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola and Uvira nearly impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the frontline, so MSF crossed various countries to deliver aid on each side.
r2-G-BLOCKED-011.l: Bukavu - Kamanyola - Uvira road, South Kivu
src: Persistent insecurity has rendered the road between Bukavu, Kamanyola, and Uvira nearly impassable, making it impossible for humanitarian organisations to move between the two sides of the frontline. To overcome this situation, MSF has adapted by crossing various countries to deliver aid and provide care on each side.

r2-G-BLOCKED-012.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 authorities announced on Tuesday (23 June 2026 per the page) that drivers coming from Butembo, Beni and Ituri province would no longer be allowed to enter entities under AFC/M23 control, with the stated aim of limiting the spread of Ebola.

r2-G-BLOCKED-012.n: Health: epidemic_context (Bundibugyo strain). Page date not shown in fetched text beyond 'mardi 23 juin'; year 2026 from the 22 May 2026 reminder in the same article. Stated aim is the authorities' own. Related to Africanews 20 Aug 2026 restrictions (blocked, different measure).
