src: Pour rappel, depuis le 23 mai 2026, le transport des passagers entre les villes de Goma et Butembo demeure suspendu jusqu’à nouvel ordre par le gouvernorat du Nord-Kivu, sous l’administration de l’AFC/M23.

r2-G-CMD-001.s: The FARDC, in a communiqué reported by the news site, confirmed the defection of Kasereka Kabido, head of the FPP/AP/FCR movement and a member of the Wazalendo, and that according to FARDC spokesperson major-general Sylvain Ekenge, Kabido and his group had chosen to rally to Rwanda and its M23/AFC allies.
r2-G-CMD-001.a: FARDC (spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge); Kasereka Kabido, FPP/AP/FCR
r2-G-CMD-001.n: Page text says communiqué dated '11 mars 2024', evidently a typo for 2025 (page dated 11 March 2025). Mediacongo (10 Mar 2025) says Kabido 'Kisiano Kabido' - name variant. Statement of FARDC, party account.
r2-G-CMD-001.vn: Excerpt exact; defection clause added from the same page via replacement quote; meta sentence moved to note. FARDC (party) account. The article (11 March 2025) says the communiqué is dated '11 mars 2024', apparently a typo. Mediacongo (10 March 2025) prints the name as 'Kabido' and once 'Kisiano Kabido'. The '7' flag comes from the outlet name 7sur7.cd and is not a figure.
src: Selon le général-major Sylvain Ekenge, porte-parole des FARDC, Kasereka Kabido et son groupe ont choisi de se rallier au Rwanda et à ses alliés du M23/AFC.

r2-G-CMD-002.s: Mediacongo reported that the self-proclaimed general Kabido and his armed group FPP/AP had officially joined the AFC-M23, which it described as a politico-military movement backed by Rwanda according to several national and international reports, and that the self-proclaimed general Shimiray Guidon, described as the commander of the Wazalendo across North Kivu, condemned this act of treason in a communiqué.
r2-G-CMD-002.n: Excerpt includes sentence 'un mouvement politico-militaire soutenu par le Rwanda, selon plusieurs rapports nationaux et internationaux' - Mediacongo's wording, not independently verified. Date: article dated 10 Mar 2025 per search listing; verify.
r2-G-CMD-002.vn: Narrowed the attribution of 'several reports' to what the sentence supports; Wazalendo condemnation is a party statement. 'selon plusieurs rapports' most naturally qualifies the Rwanda-backed description, not the joining, which Mediacongo states itself. The same article reports the Mai-Mai Kifuafua commander also distanced his group from Kabido's FPP/AP. The excerpt_en flags are translation wording (Nord-Kivu/North Kivu), not added content.
src: le général autoproclamé Kabido et son groupe armé FPP/AP ont officiellement adhéré à l’AFC-M23, un mouvement politico-militaire soutenu par le Rwanda, selon plusieurs rapports nationaux et internationaux.
Le commandant des Wazalendo à travers le Nord-Kivu, le général autoproclamé Shimiray Guidon, a, dans un communiqué, condamné cet acte de trahison.

r2-G-CMD-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 September (2025) 'Brigadier General' Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23's 'First Defense Zone' covering the Goma–Rutshuru–Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at capturing Butembo and Kisangani.
r2-G-CMD-003.n: Report year inferred from S/2025/858 (reporting period 2025). Report cites 'UN, intelligence, and civil society sources'. Statements of intent attributed to Ngaruye by GoE; AFC/M23's own account not retrieved. S/2025/858 is already cited elsewhere in the investigation, but this commander/zone item may be new.
r2-G-CMD-003.vn: Exact excerpt, matches PDF text; GoE documented investigation. Group of Experts finding (annex 22, footnote 178: UN, intelligence and civil society sources). The annex prints no year; 2025 follows from the report S/2025/858. Body para. 44 names Ngaruye as leading the 'First Defence Zone' covering Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms.
src:
On 8 September, “Brigadier General” Baudoin Ngaruye, commander of AFC/M23’s ‘First Defense Zone’ covering the
Goma–Rutshuru–Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, declared in Kirumba that AFC/M23 intended to resume hostilities aimed at
capturing Butembo and Kisangani.

r2-G-CMD-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9–11 June (2025), claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.
r2-G-CMD-004.l: Kanyabayonga and Kirumba, Lubero, North Kivu
r2-G-CMD-004.n: Year inferred from report scope. Civilian de facto official, included as a statement of the de facto authority.
r2-G-CMD-004.vn: Exact excerpt, matches PDF text. Group of Experts finding (annex 22, footnote 177). The annex prints no year; 2025 follows from the report S/2025/858. Statement of a de facto official as reported by the Group; no AFC/M23 account retrieved.
src:

June, claimed that Lubero, Butembo, and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.

r2-G-CMD-005.s: Human Rights Watch reported that several witnesses said that one M23 commander, 'Captain Gaston', executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025, and that Amurabi was a legal defender (défenseur judiciaire) in the military justice system in Goma, according to a former detainee and judicial and Congolese military intelligence sources.
r2-G-CMD-005.x: HRW: a dozen former detainees named Gaston
r2-G-CMD-005.n: Excerpt contains footnote markers [96]-[99] as printed. HRW says Gaston was reprimanded after the killing but continued abusing recruits. M23/AFC response to the report not searched in this unit.
r2-G-CMD-005.vn: Narrowed to the new detail (the Amurabi execution); kept 'several witnesses said' and HRW attribution; the 'dozen detainees' clause already stands in 015. Allegation resting on witnesses quoted by HRW. The 'dozen former detainees' and the nickname Longangi are already in r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-015. HRW also writes that former detainees said Gaston was reprimanded after the execution and later returned to the camp. No M23 response found.
src: One M23 commander, “Captain Gaston,” was named by a dozen former detainees as having been particularly brutal in his treatment of recruits. [96]

Several witnesses said that Gaston executed a Colonel Amurabi in Rumangabo around June 2025. [98] Amurabi was a legal defender (défenseur judiciaire) in the military justice system in Goma, according to a former detainee and judicial and Congolese military intelligence sources.

r2-G-CMD-006.s: Human Rights Watch recommended that concerned governments sanction RDF and M23 commanders responsible for serious abuses in 'training centers' and military and unofficial detention sites, including RDF Special Force commander Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi, and M23 camp commanders and instructors Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Mas0zera, identified in this report.
r2-G-CMD-006.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Tchanzu), Rutshuru, North Kivu
r2-G-CMD-006.a: RDF Special Force (Stanislas Gashugi); M23 (Léon Kanyamibwa, Bertin Mas0zera)
r2-G-CMD-006.n: 'Mas0zera' is printed with a zero in this recommendation; elsewhere the report prints 'Masozera' (already in claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014). Gashugi appears to be new to the roster. Report date from search listing.
r2-G-CMD-006.vn: Kept HRW's own wording; removed the 'allegation' framing and the paraphrase 'which it said it identified'. A recommendation addressed 'To Concerned Governments', not a finding or a sanction. Gashugi is named only once in the report text retained, in this recommendation. 'Mas0zera' is printed with a zero here; the report body prints 'Masozera' (r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-014).
src: Sanction RDF and M23 commanders responsible for serious abuses perpetrated in “training centers” and military and unofficial detention sites, including RDF Special Force commander Brig. Gen. Stanislas Gashugi, and M23 camp commanders and instructors Léon Kanyamibwa and Bertin Mas0zera, identified in this report.

r2-G-CMD-008.s: The US Treasury (OFAC), announcing sanctions, said that John Imani Nzenze is an M23 commander and M23's chief of intelligence, regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, the overall military commander of M23, and that Gustave Kubwayo, commonly known as 'Colonel Sirkoof', is an FDLR commander and the leader of the Commando de Recherche et d’Action en Profondeur, an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit, who led an FDLR operational command structure in Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu, that formed in 2022.
r2-G-CMD-008.n: Government (US) designation statement; OFAC's allegations about the individuals. Press release date 2 June 2026 from Reuters/search listing, not on page text; verify. Fits Nyiragongo-territory FDLR commander structure (Kubwayo).
r2-G-CMD-008.vn: Removed the garbled 'was designated as leader ... who led' phrasing; wording now follows the release. US government designation statement (press release dated June 2, 2026 on the page). The Nzenze description is already in r1-UC-M23-004; the Kubwayo designation is new. Dropped the 2012–2013 clause to keep the claim focused; it stands in r1-UC-M23-004.
ent: Commando de Recherche et d’Action en Profondeur
src: John Imani Nzenze ( Nzenze )is an M23 commander and M23’s chief of intelligence. He is regarded as one of the closest collaborators and confidants of Sultani Makenga, the U.S.- and UN-sanctioned overall military commander of M23. Nzenze has been an M23 leader since the armed group’s first rebellion from 2012–2013

Gustave Kubwayo ( Kubwayo ), commonly known as “Colonel Sirkoof,” is an FDLR commander and the leader of the Commando de Recherche et d’Action en Profondeur , an FDLR intelligence and special operations unit. In addition to this unit, Kubwayo led an FDLR operational command structure in North Kivu’s Nyiragongo territory that formed in 2022

r2-G-CMD-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Monday 8 September 2025 civil society in Uvira marched to demand the departure of general Olivier Gasita, recently named FARDC commander in charge of operations and intelligence of the 33rd military region; the population accused him of having facilitated the capture of Bukavu by AFC/M23, and Wazalendo militiamen were at the front of the opposition, while the FARDC spokesperson had three days earlier reaffirmed that Gasita enjoyed the army's confidence.
r2-G-CMD-009.n: Radio Okapi also reports the march was repressed with at least four dead per local sources (separate incident claim likely already in UV unit).
r2-G-CMD-009.vn: Both excerpts exact and match the page. The accusation against Gasita is the protesters' allegation, not a finding. The same article says the march was violently repressed, with at least four dead per local sources (provisional).
src: La ville d’Uvira a été le théâtre lundi 8 septembre 2025 d’une manifestation pacifique organisée par la société civile pour exiger le départ du général Olivier Gasita, récemment nommé commandant en charge des opérations et du renseignement de la 33ᵉ région militaire des FARDC.

Depuis une semaine, la population d’Uvira s’oppose à l’affectation du général Olivier Gasita, l’accusant d’avoir facilité la prise de Bukavu par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23. En première ligne de cette contestation figurent les miliciens Wazalendo. Pourtant, il y a trois jours, le porte-parole des FARDC a réaffirmé que le général Gasita jouissait de la confiance de l’armée

r2-G-DOC-446-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that one man, reportedly accused of being an M23 member due to his ethnicity, was lynched on 25 January in the Lushagala internally displaced persons camp in Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-001.l: Lushagala IDP camp, Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-001.a: not attributed by the source (mob violence)
r2-G-DOC-446-001.n: S/2025/446 para. 78 (footnote: open-source video footage, UN, humanitarian and civil society sources). Year 2025 follows from context (after the capture of Goma). Paragraph says over a dozen such mob-violence incidents were documented, primarily in Kinshasa.
r2-G-DOC-446-001.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Year 2025 follows from para. 78 context ('Following the capture of Goma').
src: One man, reportedly accused of being an M23 member due to his ethnicity, was lynched on 25 January in the Lushagala internally displaced persons camp in Goma.

r2-G-DOC-446-002.s: The UN Group of Experts (annex 43) quoted a WHO report of 7 February 2025 that since 26 January 3082 injured and 843 dead had been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-446-002.x: WHO (as quoted by the Group): 3082 injured, 843 dead, 31 health facilities, 26 Jan-7 Feb 2025
r2-G-DOC-446-002.n: S/2025/446 annex 43 (para. 79), quoting WHO. Para. 79 itself notes publicly reported figures varied between 900 and 2,900 dead and over 3,000 wounded and that the exact toll remained undetermined.
r2-G-DOC-446-002.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). WHO figures quoted by the Group in annex 43; para. 79 notes the toll remained undetermined. Figures are WHO's, as quoted by the Group; the Group says the exact toll remained undetermined and publicly reported figures varied.
src: On 7 February 2025 WHO reported that “since 26 January, 3082 injured and 843 dead have been reported from 31 health facilities in and around Goma, North Kivu”.

r2-G-DOC-446-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that over 1,000 wounded were registered in Goma between 23 and 28 January, including civilians, many of them women and children.
r2-G-DOC-446-003.n: S/2025/446 para. 82 (footnote cites a reliefweb ICRC/humanitarian appeal). Year inferred from the paragraph context (2025).
r2-G-DOC-446-003.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). 'in Goma' carried by the preceding sentence of para. 82.
src: Over 1,000 wounded were registered between 23 and 28 January – including civilians, many of them women and children.

r2-G-DOC-446-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 27 January 2025 heavy cross-border exchanges of artillery fire between the DRC and Rwandan forces caused civilian casualties on both sides of the border; in Goma the Birere neighbourhood near the airport was severely impacted, with at least 53 civilian fatalities documented, mainly women and children, after at least five shells struck homes in Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods between 27 and 28 January 2025. The Group does not say which side fired those shells; it adds that residents reported FARDC heavy artillery positioned near residential areas.
r2-G-DOC-446-005.l: Birere, Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods, Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-005.a: Cross-border artillery exchange between the DRC (FARDC) and Rwandan forces; the source adds residents reported FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas
r2-G-DOC-446-005.x: At least 53 civilian fatalities; at least five shells
r2-G-DOC-446-005.n: S/2025/446 para. 85 (civilian, humanitarian and UN sources). The same paragraph attributes the exchange to heavy cross-border artillery fire between the DRC and Rwandan forces; shooter of the specific shells is not stated in this sentence.
r2-G-DOC-446-005.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Cross-border artillery context from the opening of para. 85. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: 27 January 2025 cross-border artillery exchange (first part of the sentence, before a page break) 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: civilian casualties on both sides of the border (second part of the sentence, after the page break) 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-029: Para. 85 in context: the Group places the 53 deaths in the context of a cross-border artillery exchange between DRC and Rwandan forces but does not say which side fired the shells that hit Mapendo and Kahembe, and adds that residents reported FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas, and that DRC-origin fire killed 5 civilians in Gisenyi. The statement should keep the shells unattributed and carry that context.; excerpt-support: added 3 excerpt(s): 27 January 2025 cross-border artillery exchange (first part of the sentence, before a page break); civilian casualties on both sides of the border (second part of the sentence, after the page break); FARDC heavy artillery near residential areas
src: In Goma, the Birere neighbourhood near Goma airport was severely impacted, with at least 53 civilian fatalities documented, mainly women and children, after at least five shells struck several homes in Mapendo and Kahembe neighbourhoods between 27 and 28 January 2025.

85. On 27 January 2025, as intense fighting centred around Goma airport and Mont Goma, where remaining FARDC and Wazalendo elements resisted, heavy cross border exchange of artillery fire between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and
Rwandan forces resulted in civilian casualties and severe damage to civilian homes and infrastructure, on both sides of the border.
Residents reported that FARDC heavy artillery was positioned near residential areas.

r2-G-DOC-446-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 46 that, according to local sources verified by UN sources, the FARDC bombing of Nyabibwe (Kalehe territory) on 6 February 2025 caused three civilian injuries (a man and his two children) and impacted at least 35 civilian homes, with no fatalities.
r2-G-DOC-446-006.x: Group/UN-verified local sources: 3 civilians injured, at least 35 homes impacted, no fatalities; AFC/M23: 4 killed including an infant
r2-G-DOC-446-006.n: S/2025/446 annex 46 (para. 86). Para. 86 says FARDC bombarded Nyabibwe targeting AFC/M23 positions. The AFC/M23 contrary claim is recorded as a separate claim.
r2-G-DOC-446-006.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Date, place and FARDC as the bomber are in the annex 46 heading and para. 86 on the same page. The Group's count (three injured, no fatalities) contradicts the AFC/M23 claim of four killed; both accounts are recorded separately.
src: Local sources, verified by UN sources, reported three civilian injuries (a man and his two children), and at least 35 civilian homes impacted, but no fatalities:

r2-G-DOC-446-007.s: The UN Group of Experts recorded that an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claimed deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant.
r2-G-DOC-446-007.x: AFC/M23: four fatalities including an infant (contradicted by the Group's local/UN-verified sources: no fatalities)
r2-G-DOC-446-007.n: S/2025/446 annex 46; para. 86 states the bombing 'resulted in injuries to three civilians' contrary to AFC/M23 claims that four civilians were killed. Cited here only for what AFC/M23 said.
r2-G-DOC-446-007.vn: Recorded only as what AFC/M23 claimed, as reproduced by the Group; the Group's own sources contradict it (para. 86). AFC/M23 claim; the Group reports three civilians injured and no fatalities.
src: Below, an AFC/M23 communiqué issued on 6 February 2025 claiming the deliberate targeting of Nyabibwe by FARDC bombing, resulting in the massacre of civilians, notably four fatalities including an infant:

r2-G-DOC-446-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that from 26 to 27 January, in Goma, retreating FARDC and Wazalendo systematically looted civilian homes and shops, engaging in theft, extortion and the shooting of civilians resisting extortion.
r2-G-DOC-446-008.n: S/2025/446 para. 88 and annex 47 (video of 26 Jan 2025 showing three armed uniformed individuals robbing and shooting a civilian). Sources: civil society, UN, audiovisual documentation.
r2-G-DOC-446-008.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: From 26 to 27 January, in Goma, retreating FARDC and Wazalendo systematically looted civilian homes and shops, engaging in theft, extortion and the shooting of civilians resisting extortion

r2-G-DOC-446-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported, without stating where, that MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February, and that FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.
r2-G-DOC-446-009.n: S/2025/446 para. 88. The paragraph discusses retreating FARDC between Kalehe and Kavumu on 6-8 February; the exact place of these three rapes is not given. Year 2025 inferred from context. Victims not named.
r2-G-DOC-446-009.vn: Same sentence is already in r1-GOE-063, which records it 'without stating where'; this claim adds the FARDC confirmation and arrests. The draft location/province/territory (South Kivu, Kalehe) were inferred from the surrounding paragraph about 6-8 February: the source gives no place for these rapes, so they are removed. The report gives no place for these rapes. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-032: Para. 88 places the 6 to 8 February events 'between Kalehe and Kavumu', but the rapes of 31 January to 2 February are given no place, and the paragraph opens with Goma on 26 to 27 January. The verifier said the place fields were removed, but province is still 'South Kivu' and territory is still 'Kalehe'. That is time and place slippage. The amended text says the place is not stated, and province and territory should be cleared.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: MONUSCO documented the rape of three girls aged 13 to 17 by FARDC soldiers between 31 January and 2 February. FARDC authorities confirmed the violations and reported the arrest of alleged perpetrators.

r2-G-DOC-446-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 10 February at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu, accused of desertion, the murder of at least 12 civilians, rape, looting and other crimes committed in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories.
r2-G-DOC-446-010.l: Bukavu (military court); offences in villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories, South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-010.x: At least 84 soldiers; at least 12 civilians allegedly murdered
r2-G-DOC-446-010.n: S/2025/446 para. 88 (UN and FARDC sources; footnote cites an AP story). Allegations as stated by the Group; not a finding of individual responsibility.
r2-G-DOC-446-010.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Accused, not convicted: procedural stage kept as 'appeared before a military court, accused of'.
src: On 10 February, at least 84 FARDC soldiers appeared before a military court in Bukavu, accused of desertion, the murder of at least 12 civilians, rape, looting and other crimes committed in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories.

r2-G-DOC-446-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in Bukavu at least six children who had dressed up in military uniforms and played with weapons discarded by fleeing FARDC soldiers were killed by AFC/M23 soldiers conducting security sweeps on 16 February.
r2-G-DOC-446-011.n: S/2025/446 para. 99 (humanitarian sources, researchers, video/photographic evidence). The Group says this raises 'questions of excessive use of force'. Children not named.
r2-G-DOC-446-011.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Year 2025 from context (Bukavu taken 16 February 2025).
src: In Bukavu, at least six children who had dressed up in military uniforms and played with weapons discarded by fleeing FARDC soldiers were killed by AFC/M23 soldiers conducting security sweeps on 16 February

r2-G-DOC-446-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 February the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified AFC/M23 search operations as necessary to apprehend 'Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses'.
r2-G-DOC-446-012.n: S/2025/446 para. 98 (video footage of Bahati Erasto speaking in Kinyarwanda, 6 February 2025). Cited for what he said; the Group links the sweeps to extrajudicial killings, arrests and torture.
r2-G-DOC-446-012.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Speaker as the Group names him; cited for what he said.
src: On 6 February, the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Erasto, justified the operations as necessary to apprehend “Wazalendo and FDLR, mercenaries and FARDC who are still hiding in the houses”.

r2-G-DOC-446-013.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 imposed sentences, typically beatings or summary executions, arbitrarily, and that perceived disloyalty, theft or sexual violence were generally punished by death.
r2-G-DOC-446-013.l: AFC/M23-held areas of North and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-013.n: S/2025/446 para. 95 (AFC/M23 insiders, intelligence, UN, former combatants). Date is general (2025 occupation); the paragraph also says AFC/M23 relied on civilian informants and lacked detention facilities.
r2-G-DOC-446-013.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Subject AFC/M23 carried by para. 95.
src: Sentences – typically beatings or summary executions – were imposed arbitrarily. Perceived disloyalty, theft or sexual violence were generally punished by death.

r2-G-DOC-446-014.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 operated clandestine detention sites where detainees were held incommunicado, subjected to torture and in many cases either disappeared or later found dead, their bodies discarded in public or remote areas.
r2-G-DOC-446-014.l: Goma and other AFC/M23-held areas, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-014.n: S/2025/446 para. 104; the paragraph goes on to name sites in Goma (Mont Goma, Katindo camp, 'Chien méchant' cell, Stade de l'unité, Mugunga police academy).
r2-G-DOC-446-014.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: AFC/M23 operated clandestine detention sites where detainees were held incommunicado, subjected to torture and in many cases either disappeared or later found dead, their bodies discarded in public or remote areas.

r2-G-DOC-446-015.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that multiple corroborated testimonies identified the Stade de l’Unité in Goma as a holding and detention site operated by AFC/M23 and RDF forces, notably used for detaining and forcibly recruiting individuals.
r2-G-DOC-446-015.l: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-015.n: S/2025/446 annex 51 (para. 103), in the context of a video of 18 March 2025; the AFC/M23 call for surrender at the Stade de l'Unité began on 27 January (annex 12).
r2-G-DOC-446-015.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: Multiple corroborated testimonies identified the Stade de l’Unité as a holding and detention site operated by AFC/M23 and RDF forces, notably used for detaining and forcibly recruiting individuals

r2-G-DOC-446-016.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that a video filmed on 17 February 2025, two days after AFC/M23 took control of Bukavu, shows the public beating of an individual by men in military uniforms.
r2-G-DOC-446-016.a: men in military uniforms; the annex attributes the assault to AFC/M23 and RDF forces
r2-G-DOC-446-016.x: about 27 blows with a stick in a 1-minute video
r2-G-DOC-446-016.n: S/2025/446 annex 51 (item 1), video received by the Group on 17 February 2025 from a confidential source in Bukavu; the annex states the assault 'was carried out by AFC/M23 and RDF forces who had just taken control of the city'. Victim not identified.
r2-G-DOC-446-016.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Attribution of the assault to AFC/M23 and RDF forces and the 27 blows are in the annex 51 text.
src: A video filmed on 17 February 2025, two days after AFC/M23 took control of Bukavu, shows the public beating of an individual by men in military uniforms.

r2-G-DOC-446-017.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 51 that video footage provided to it on 18 March 2025 documents severe corporal punishment inflicted by several armed individuals in uniform at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-017.l: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-017.a: armed individuals in uniform (equipment consistent with RDF issue, one with a 'PU' military police armband, per annex 51)
r2-G-DOC-446-017.n: S/2025/446 annex 51 (item 4). Date is that the footage was provided to the Group; the date of the beating itself is not given. Victim not identified.
r2-G-DOC-446-017.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Equipment consistent with RDF issue and the 'PU' armband are in the annex text.
src: Video footage filmed and provided to the Group on 18 March 2025 documents an incident of severe corporal punishment inflicted by several armed individuals in uniform at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma.

r2-G-DOC-446-018.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 22 February 2025 at least 17 civilian men were executed near Katindo camp, in Karisimbi commune, Goma, and verified the deaths of at least 17 male victims through photographic and video evidence corroborated by witness testimony; according to witnesses cited by the Group, the killings took place during ongoing AFC/M23 sweeping operations in the Katindo neighbourhood.
r2-G-DOC-446-018.l: Katindo neighbourhood (near Katindo camp, Afia Bora), Karisimbi commune, Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-018.a: AFC/M23 (identified by witnesses and local population; a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed responsibility)
r2-G-DOC-446-018.x: Group-verified: at least 17 men; reported (witnesses): at least 50 killed or forcibly disappeared on 22-23 February; video: 11 bodies at one site, 6 at another
r2-G-DOC-446-018.n: S/2025/446 annex 49 (para. 101). Annex adds: 11 bodies in one compound and six at Afia Bora; on 22-23 Feb at least 50 civilians reported killed or forcibly disappeared (unverified); roundup of men at 'Terrain des scouts' on 23 Feb. Victims not named. AFC/M23 denial recorded separately.
r2-G-DOC-446-018.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The link to AFC/M23 sweeping operations rests on witnesses in annex 49, and a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed responsibility (claim 19). Figures 11 and 6 (two sites) and 50 (reported, unverified; claim 18) are on the page. The Group verified at least 17 deaths; that the killings took place during AFC/M23 sweeping operations is reported by witnesses. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: witnesses: AFC/M23 sweeping operations in Katindo 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-030: Checked the retained PDF (annex 49): the Group's own finding is the 17 executions near Katindo camp; the link to AFC/M23 sweeping operations is stated as what 'witnesses reported', though the Group also writes that AFC/M23 combatants were seen arriving in trucks and rounding up men. The statement presents the AFC/M23 context as the Group's flat finding; amended to restore the witness basis. Note the FFM (r2-G-DOC-HRC-005) places what is probably the same 22-23 February operation in Kasika neighbourhood with at least 21 victims: a discrepancy to surface, not merge silently.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): witnesses: AFC/M23 sweeping operations in Katindo
src: On 22 February 2025, at least 17 civilian men were executed near Katindo camp, in Karisimbi commune, Goma.
The Group was able to verify the deaths of at least 17 male victims through a combination of photographic and video evidence, corroborated by multiple witness testimonies.
Witnesses reported that the killings took place within a larger context of ongoing sweeping military operations by AFC/M23 in the Katindo neighborhood.

r2-G-DOC-446-019.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that during door-to-door searches by AFC/M23 on 22 and 23 February in the Katindo area of Goma, at least 50 civilians were reported to have been killed or forcibly disappeared, with executions taking place on the streets and in civilian homes.
r2-G-DOC-446-019.x: Reported: at least 50 killed or forcibly disappeared (unverified); Group-verified: 17
r2-G-DOC-446-019.n: S/2025/446 annex 49. Reported figure, not verified by the Group (the Group verified 17).
r2-G-DOC-446-019.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The 50 figure is reported and not verified by the Group (it verified 17); the door-to-door searches on 22-23 February rest on multiple witnesses. Reported figure; the Group verified 17 deaths.
src: During these raids, at least 50 civilians were reported to have been killed or forcibly disappeared, with executions taking place on the streets and in civilian homes.

r2-G-DOC-446-020.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that a source close to AFC/M23 confirmed the group's responsibility for the Katindo incident, stating that AFC/M23 acknowledged internally that it was a 'bad incident' involving the summary execution of men accused of taking 'drugs'.
r2-G-DOC-446-020.a: AFC/M23 (per a source close to AFC/M23)
r2-G-DOC-446-020.n: S/2025/446 annex 49. Anonymous source close to the group, reported by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-446-020.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Anonymous source close to AFC/M23, as reported by the Group.
src: A source close to AFC/M23 confirmed the group's responsibility for the incident, stating that AFC/M23 acknowledged internally that it was a “bad incident” involving the summary execution of men accused of taking “drugs,” with M23 security forces having killed many of those apprehended.

r2-G-DOC-446-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that after a France24 report on the Katindo killings, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as 'fake news' and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa's propaganda, and denied having spoken to France24.
r2-G-DOC-446-021.n: S/2025/446 annex 49 (links an X post by Kanyuka; exact day not stated in the text). The France24 report alleged an M23 spokesperson confirmed the killings occurred during a 'sweeping and clearing' and that victims were ex-FARDC, Wazalendo or drug users.
r2-G-DOC-446-021.vn: Quote verified. The report gives no date for Kanyuka's reply; the draft's '2025-02' is not printed. Narrowed to a range from the incident (22 February) to the report date.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as "fake news" and blatant misinformation aligned with Kinshasa’s propaganda. He further denied having spoken to France24 regarding the matter.

r2-G-DOC-446-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bertrand Bisimwa admitted the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping Goma but claimed they were carried out lawfully, in a statement published on X on 9 March 2025.
r2-G-DOC-446-022.n: S/2025/446 annex 49 (footnote: statement published on X, 9 March 2025). The Group contrasts it with consistent reports of summary executions. Annex 52 gives 10 March for a statement with the same X link; date as footnoted in annex 49.
r2-G-DOC-446-022.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Date 9 March 2025 from footnote 310 of annex 49 (annex 52 gives 10 March for the same X link; noted). Annex 52 dates the same X post 10 March 2025.
src: Bertrand Bisimwa admitted to the existence of regular daily and nocturnal patrols sweeping the city, but claimed that these were carried out lawfully, succeeding to ensure security for all

r2-G-DOC-446-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published by its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions.
r2-G-DOC-446-023.l: Kinshasa (communiqués on Goma and eastern DRC)
r2-G-DOC-446-023.n: S/2025/446 annex 49; captions reproduce communiqués of 23 February, 15 March and 12 April 2025 (images; text not extracted). Cited for what the Government said.
r2-G-DOC-446-023.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Communiqué dates (23 February, 15 March, 12 April 2025) are in the annex 49 captions.
src: The Government of the DRC, through official communiqués regularly published through its Minister of Interior, Shabani Lukoo Bihango, denounced the scale and systematic nature of abuses perpetrated by AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army, including summary executions:

r2-G-DOC-446-024.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that following the takeover of Minova on 21 January 2025, local sources and intelligence reports indicated AFC/M23 rounded up all the local youth and men and transported them in trucks to an undisclosed location.
r2-G-DOC-446-024.n: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21). Date = takeover date given by the annex (para. 14 gives about two weeks after 4 January); the round-up date follows the takeover.
r2-G-DOC-446-024.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: following the takeover of Minova on 21 January 2025, local sources and intelligence reports indicated that AFC/M23 rounded up all the local youth and men, and transported them in trucks to an undisclosed location.

r2-G-DOC-446-025.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that multiple sources said AFC/M23 systematically abducted men, adolescents and children in conquered territories, including in and around urban settings such as Minova, Goma and Bukavu.
r2-G-DOC-446-025.l: Minova, Goma and Bukavu, North and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-025.n: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21): 'forced recruitments reached unprecedented levels' since the Group's last report. Children not named.
r2-G-DOC-446-025.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: Multiple sources, including civil society leaders, human rights defenders, UN sources, humanitarian organizations, eyewitnesses and former AFC/M23 combatants reported that AFC/M23 systematically abducted men, adolescents and children in conquered territories, in rural areas but also in and around urban settings including in Minova, Goma and Bukavu.

r2-G-DOC-446-026.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the morning of 29 January 2025 social media footage showed hundreds of FARDC gathered at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma, and that images show hundreds loaded onto trucks and taken to Rumangabo for accelerated military training.
r2-G-DOC-446-026.l: Stade de l’Unité, Goma, to Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-026.x: 'hundreds' on 29 January; 'over two thousand' in days (local and intelligence sources)
r2-G-DOC-446-026.n: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21). The annex says most were under duress and that over two thousand former FARDC and Wazalendo were taken to Rumangabo in a matter of days; also that on 22 February approx. 2,000 FARDC and PNC were brought from Bukavu to Rumangabo via Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-026.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: On the morning of 29 January 2025, social media footage showed hundreds of FARDC gathered at the Stade de l’Unité in Goma. Images received by the Group show that hundreds were loaded onto trucks and taken to Rumangabo for accelerated military training

r2-G-DOC-446-027.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in response to increasing AFC/M23 attacks starting January 2025, VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR intensified the recruitment of new combatants, including children, in their areas of influence and in internally displaced persons camps.
r2-G-DOC-446-027.l: VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR areas of influence and IDP camps, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-027.n: S/2025/446 para. 64 (see annex 36). Specific territories are not given in the sentence.
r2-G-DOC-446-027.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: In response to increasing AFC/M23 attacks starting January 2025, VDP/Wazalendo and FDLR intensified the recruitment of new combatants, including children, in their respective areas of influence and in internally displaced persons camps.

r2-G-DOC-446-028.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 January 2025 AFC/M23 dismantled the N’shanga IDP camp in Kalehe territory to repurpose the site for the reinforcement of its elements advancing towards Sake.
r2-G-DOC-446-028.l: N’shanga IDP camp, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-028.n: S/2025/446 annex 48 (para. 93). Place is as printed (the camp is more commonly placed in Masisi territory; the source says Kalehe).
r2-G-DOC-446-028.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Kalehe territory as printed by the source. The report places the N’shanga camp in Kalehe territory.
src: On 24 January 2025, AFC/M23 dismantled the N’shanga IDP camp in Kalehe territory to repurpose the site for the reinforcement of their elements advancing towards Sake.

r2-G-DOC-446-029.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 28 January 2025, in Minova, local sources reported that AFC/M23 elements destroyed IDP camps and forced IDPs to return home.
r2-G-DOC-446-029.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: On 28 January 2025, in Minova (20km south of Sake), local sources reported that AFC/M23 elements destroyed IDP camps and forced IDPs to return home and resume a normal life.

r2-G-DOC-446-030.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that between 27 and 29 January widespread looting, mainly by the population, of humanitarian warehouses, including those of UNFPA, MSF and the ICRC, resulted in acute shortages of food, medicines and emergency relief supplies.
r2-G-DOC-446-030.n: S/2025/446 annex 41 (para. 78). Excerpt keeps the footnote number 268 as printed in the extracted text. The annex adds that replenishment was hindered by the closure of Goma airport and trucks held at Gisenyi.
r2-G-DOC-446-030.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Two excerpts are consecutive parts of one sentence in annex 41.
src: Between 27 and 29 January, the widespread looting, mainly by the population, of humanitarian warehouses

including those of the World Food Programme (WFP), International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), 268 United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), UNHCR, IOM, Save the Children, and UNICEF—resulted in acute shortages of food, medicines, and emergency relief supplies.

r2-G-DOC-446-031.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 39 that the DRC Government stated that the arrest of FDLR 'Brigadier General' Ezechiel Gakwerere was staged by the Government of Rwanda to sustain the narrative of FARDC-FDLR cooperation, in order to justify Rwanda's act of aggression.
r2-G-DOC-446-031.l: Goma, North Kivu (arrest); statement by Kinshasa
r2-G-DOC-446-031.n: S/2025/446 annex 39 (para. 73); date of the statement not given (arrest/transfer 1 March 2025 per para. 73). Cited for what the Government said.
r2-G-DOC-446-031.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Cited for what the Government said; adds to r1-UC-BI-FDLR-018 (Gakwerere transfer).
src: The DRC Government stated that the arrest was staged by the Government of Rwanda to sustain the narrative of FARDC-FDLR cooperation, in order to justify Rwanda’s act of aggression.

r2-G-DOC-446-032.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 39 that FDLR spokesperson Cure Ngoma denied Ezechiel Gakwerere's cooperation with the FARDC, acknowledging his FDLR membership but insisting he was no longer active as he was sick and under medical treatment in Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-032.n: S/2025/446 annex 39 (para. 73). Excerpt keeps the report's typo 'he has was'. Date of the statement not given.
r2-G-DOC-446-032.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Cited for what the FDLR spokesperson said; 'he has was' is the report's typo.
src: FDLR spokesperson, Cure Ngoma, denied the allegations of Gakwerere’s cooperation with the FARDC, and raised concerns over RDF incursions in the DRC. While acknowledging Gakwerere’s FDLR membership, Cure Ngoma insisted that he has was no longer active within the movement, as he was sick and under medical treatment in Goma.

r2-G-DOC-446-033.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 7 March 2025 'General' Kasereka Kasyano Kabidon announced the allegiance of the Front commun de la résistance (FCR), a Wazalendo coalition, to AFC/M23, but several FCR members disavowed the announcement and reiterated their loyalty to the Government.
r2-G-DOC-446-033.l: North Kivu (location of announcement not stated)
r2-G-DOC-446-033.n: S/2025/446 para. 69 (annex 37, including an X post by Lawrence Kanyuka dated 9 March announcing that FCR had joined the AFC/M23 alliance).
r2-G-DOC-446-033.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: On 7 March 2025, “General” Kasereka Kasyano Kabidon announced the allegiance of the Front commun de la résistance (FCR), a Wazalendo coalition, to AFC/M23
However, several FCR members disavowed Mr. Kabidon’s announcement and reiterated their loyalty to the Government

r2-G-DOC-446-034.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Justin Ndayishimiye, a member of the national Parliament, convened a meeting on 19 March 2025 with VDP/Wazalendo commanders from Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories in Katoyi, Masisi territory, to restore VDP/Wazalendo-FARDC coordination and cohesion.
r2-G-DOC-446-034.a: VDP/Wazalendo commanders from Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale; FARDC
r2-G-DOC-446-034.n: S/2025/446 para. 69 (sources: VDP, civil society, intelligence, FARDC, researchers).
r2-G-DOC-446-034.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Purpose of the meeting carried by the preceding clause of para. 69.
src: Justin Ndayishimiye, a member of the national Parliament, convened a meeting on 19 March with VDP/Wazalendo commanders from Masisi, Rutshuru and Walikale territories in Katoyi, Masisi territory.

r2-G-DOC-446-035.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 20 that on 24 January 2025 RDF troops positioned in Kanyamahoro and Kibumba attacked FARDC Special Forces and PMC positions in Kibati, north-east of Goma, with ZU-23 MM anti-aircraft guns and Type 63 multiple rocket launchers.
r2-G-DOC-446-035.l: Kibati, north-east of Goma, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-035.n: S/2025/446 annex 20 (para. 35): photographs, video, intelligence, MONUSCO sources, eyewitnesses and sources close to RDF/Rwandan Government. Kibati lies in Nyiragongo territory (territory is our gloss).
r2-G-DOC-446-035.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The draft's Nyiragongo territory tag is the researcher's gloss; the source says only 'Kibati, north-east of Goma', so the tag is dropped.
src: On 24 January 2025, RDF troops positioned in Kanyamahoro and Kibumba attacked FARDC Special Forces and PMC positions in Kibati, north-east of Goma, with ZU-23 MM anti-aircraft guns and Type 63 multiple rocket launchers.

r2-G-DOC-446-036.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 25 January 2025 a MONUSCO armoured personnel carrier at a blocking position in Sake was struck by hostile fire, killing one peacekeeper and injuring four others; military analysts indicated the damage was most likely caused by a missile strike, and analysis of the missile’s trajectory, eyewitness testimony and military analysis indicates that it was fired from the RDF position on the Bulenga peninsula.
r2-G-DOC-446-036.x: Para. 53: 1 killed, 4 injured; para. 80: 3 killed, 37 injured over the Goma hostilities
r2-G-DOC-446-036.n: S/2025/446 para. 53 (annex 29). Para. 80 gives overall MONUSCO figures for the Goma hostilities: three peacekeepers killed and 37 injured.
r2-G-DOC-446-036.vn: Draft said 'the missile' as a given; the Group says the damage was 'most likely' caused by a missile strike. Hedge restored. Para. 80 overall figures (3 killed, 37 injured) are in the figures field only.
src: On 25 January 2025, an armoured personnel carrier belonging to MONUSCO, posted at one of the Mission’s blocking positions in Sake, was struck by hostile fire (see para. 29 above). One peacekeeper was killed and four others were injured.
Analysis of the missile’s trajectory, coupled with eyewitness testimony and military analysis, indicates that it was fired from the RDF position on the Bulenga peninsula

r2-G-DOC-446-037.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that during the night of 11-12 April 2025 a group of reportedly 200 Wazalendo and FDLR combatants attacked AFC/M23 positions in Goma, including the neighbourhoods of Ndosho, Mugunga, Kyeshero and Lac Vert.
r2-G-DOC-446-037.l: Ndosho, Mugunga, Kyeshero and Lac Vert, Goma; clashes also in Rusayo, Rumoka and Lushaga, Nyiragongo territory
r2-G-DOC-446-037.a: Wazalendo and FDLR combatants (attackers); AFC/M23 and RDF (responders)
r2-G-DOC-446-037.n: S/2025/446 annex 23 (para. 39). Video, audio, eyewitnesses, civil society, intelligence and UN sources.
r2-G-DOC-446-037.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: During the night of 11-12 April 2025, a group of reportedly 200 Wazalendo and FDLR combatants, organized in several units, attacked AFC/M23 positions in Goma, including the neighborhoods of Ndosho, Mugunga, Kyeshero, and Lac Vert.

r2-G-DOC-446-038.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that sources said up to 52 individuals were killed in the 11-12 April attack on Goma, including at least 12 AFC/M23 combatants and/or RDF soldiers, a figure the Group could not independently verify; eyewitness, security, intelligence and MONUSCO sources reported RDF reinforcements crossed the border into Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-038.x: Sources: up to 52 killed, including at least 12 AFC/M23 and/or RDF; not independently verified by the Group
r2-G-DOC-446-038.n: S/2025/446 annex 23. Casualty figure explicitly unverified by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-446-038.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Casualty figure explicitly not verified by the Group. The Group could not independently verify the casualty figure.
src: Sources reported that up to 52 individuals were killed in the attack, including at least 12 AFC/M23 combatants and/or RDF soldiers. The Group could not independently verify this information.
Eyewitnesses, security, intelligence and MONUSCO sources reported that RDF reinforcements crossed the border into Goma to reinforce AFC/M23 and repel the Wazalendo/FDLR attack.

r2-G-DOC-446-039.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 23 that the SADC stated in an official communiqué that 'SAMIDRC has not participated in any joint operations' and refuted AFC/M23's allegations, which it qualified as 'inaccurate and misleading'.
r2-G-DOC-446-039.n: S/2025/446 annex 23 (date of the SADC communiqué not given in the text; the context is the 11-12 April attack). The Group also notes none of the Wazalendo involved belonged to the group sheltering at MONUSCO bases or to SAMIDRC, contrary to AFC/M23's report.
r2-G-DOC-446-039.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Cited for what SADC said; the communiqué's date is not given (context: 11-12 April attack).
src: In an official communiqué, the Southern African development Community (SADC) stated that “SAMIDRC has not participated in any joint operations” and refuted AFC/M23’s allegations which it qualified as “inaccurate and misleading”

r2-G-DOC-446-040.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 3 January 2025 the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo armed groups of the VDP coalition and the FDNB, clashed with the M23/AFC on the Kitchanga-Kayabayonga axis.
r2-G-DOC-446-040.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-040.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 3 January 2025, the FARDC supported by Wazalendo armed groups of the VDP coalition and the FDNB, clashed with the M23/AFC on axis Kitchanga-Kayabayonga.

r2-G-DOC-446-041.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 19 January 2025 the FARDC, supported by FDLR combatants and the Coalition of Patriotic Movements for the Defense of the Nation (CMPDN), attacked AFC/M23 in Masisi centre.
r2-G-DOC-446-041.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-041.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 19 January 2025, the FARDC supported by combatants of the FDLR and the Coalition of Patriotic Movements for the Defense of the Nation (CMPDN) - composed of PARECO-FF, PARECO/Mahoro, FDDH, and GAV – attacked AFC/M23 in Masisi centre;

r2-G-DOC-446-042.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 20 February the FARDC, with APCLS, CMC-FDP and NDC-R combatants, clashed with AFC/M23 and RDF in Mabanga, Rutubogo and Karisimbi.
r2-G-DOC-446-042.l: Mabanga, Rutubogo and Karisimbi (as printed), North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-042.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-042.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 20 February, the FARDC together with combatants of APCLS, CMC-FDP and NDC-R clashed with AFC/M23 and RDF in Mabanga, Rutubogo, Karisimbi

r2-G-DOC-446-043.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 23-24-25 February 2025 the FARDC, with ANCDH and APCLS combatants, clashed in Kalembe, at the border between Masisi and Lubero territories.
r2-G-DOC-446-043.l: Kalembe, border of Masisi and Lubero territories, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-043.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-043.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 23-24-25 February 2025, the FARDC together with combatants of ANCDH and APCLS clashed in Kalembe, at the border between Masisi and Lubero territories;

r2-G-DOC-446-044.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 6 March 2025 AFC/M23 clashed with the FARDC and VDP in Kamandi Lac, along the shores of Lake Edward.
r2-G-DOC-446-044.l: Kamandi Lac, Lake Edward shore, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-044.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-044.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 6 March 2025, AFC/M23 clashed with the FARDC and VDP in Kamandi Lac, located along the shores of Lake Edward.

r2-G-DOC-446-045.s: The UN Group of Experts listed in annex 36 that on 10 April 2025 AFC/M23 attacked the FPP-AP stronghold in Bunyatenge, Lubero territory.
r2-G-DOC-446-045.n: S/2025/446 annex 36 (para. 64), a non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations; the annex does not give casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-446-045.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Item in annex 36's non-exhaustive list of armed confrontations.
src: On 10 April 2025, AFC/M23 attacked the FPP-AP stronghold in Bunyatenge, Lubero territory;

r2-G-DOC-446-046.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 72 that several hundred FDNB troops were deployed north of Bukavu, in Katana and Nyamukubi, to contain AFC/M23 and RDF, and that on 31 January an additional 2,000 Burundian troops were sent to Kamanyola in the Ruzizi Plain.
r2-G-DOC-446-046.l: Katana and Nyamukubi (north of Bukavu); Kamanyola, Ruzizi Plain, South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-046.x: Several hundred; additional 2,000 sent to Kamanyola on 31 January
r2-G-DOC-446-046.n: S/2025/446 annex 72 (para. 179). Territory for Katana/Nyamukubi (Kabare) is our gloss; the annex says only 'north of Bukavu'.
r2-G-DOC-446-046.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The draft's Kabare territory tag is the researcher's gloss; the annex says only 'north of Bukavu', so the tag is dropped. Annex 72 also has 'March and April 2015' (a typo for 2025) elsewhere; not used.
src: Several hundred FDNB troops were deployed north of Bukavu, in Katana and Nyamukubi, to contain AFC/M23 and RDF from taking Bukavu and Kavumu. On 31 January, an additional 2,000 Burundian troops were sent to Kamanyola in the Ruzizi Plain, near the tri-border area between Burundi, Rwanda and the DRC.

r2-G-DOC-446-047.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early February 2025 AFC/M23 expanded its influence into South Kivu, establishing exclusive control over key mineral trading centres in Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory.
r2-G-DOC-446-047.l: Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-047.n: S/2025/446 para. 109. Para. 17 gives 6 February for the Nyabibwe break-through.
r2-G-DOC-446-047.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Distinct from r1-GOE-074 (military break-through); this is the mineral-trading-centre control.
src: In early February 2025, AFC/M23 expanded its influence into South Kivu, establishing exclusive control over key mineral trading centres in Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory.

r2-G-DOC-446-048.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that further military advances towards Uvira resulted in the paralysis of mining activities in Kamanyola, and that the Alphamin Bisie tin mine in Walikale territory suspended operations from 13 March to mid-April 2025.
r2-G-DOC-446-048.l: Kamanyola (South Kivu); Bisie, Walikale territory (North Kivu)
r2-G-DOC-446-048.n: S/2025/446 para. 109. The Group states resumption coincided with the AFC/M23 withdrawal from Walikale (para. 18). Impact statement, not an attributed abuse.
r2-G-DOC-446-048.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: Further military advances towards Uvira resulted in the paralysis of mining activities in Kamanyola.
Similarly, in Walikale territory, the Alphamin Bisie mine, a major industrial tin producer, suspended operations from 13 March to mid-April 2025.

r2-G-DOC-446-049.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 looted 186 tons of untagged 3T minerals in Nyabibwe, South Kivu, smuggling them to Rwanda through Mukwija port in Kalehe territory.
r2-G-DOC-446-049.l: Nyabibwe and Mukwija port, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-049.n: S/2025/446 para. 115 (source: ITSCI). Date not stated beyond 'since January 2025' for the wider looting of more than 500 tons in Goma and Bukavu.
r2-G-DOC-446-049.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
src: AFC/M23 also looted 186 tons of untagged 3T minerals in Nyabibwe, South Kivu, smuggling them to Rwanda through Mukwija port in Kalehe territory.

r2-G-DOC-446-051.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF took Bukavu on 16 February, Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.
r2-G-DOC-446-051.l: Bukavu to Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura (Burundi)
r2-G-DOC-446-051.n: S/2025/446 para. 169. Withdrawal date is around 14-16 February (Kavumu 14 Feb, Bukavu 16 Feb).
r2-G-DOC-446-051.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Adds the withdrawal directions to r1-GOE-074; Bukavu 16 February carried by para. 169. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: Government authorities, FDNB and FARDC withdrew towards Kamanyola, Uvira and Bujumbura in Burundi.

r2-G-DOC-446-052.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 9 and 25 March an airplane operating for the benefit of RDF conducted three landings in Minembwe to evacuate at least 16 wounded Twirwaneho and provide pharmaceutical and military supplies.
r2-G-DOC-446-052.a: RDF (aircraft operating for its benefit); Twirwaneho
r2-G-DOC-446-052.x: Three landings; at least 16 wounded evacuated
r2-G-DOC-446-052.n: S/2025/446 para. 175 (diplomatic and UN sources, researchers). Dates listed as 9 and 25 March; the Group counts three landings in total. Minembwe territory (Fizi) is our gloss.
r2-G-DOC-446-052.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). The draft's Fizi territory tag is the researcher's gloss; the source names only Minembwe, so the tag is dropped.
src: On 9 and 25 March, an airplane operating for the benefit of RDF conducted three landings in Minembwe to evacuate at least 16 wounded Twirwaneho and provide pharmaceutical and military supplies.

r2-G-DOC-446-053.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, as previously reported, a significant portion of the Banyamulenge community rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda, that these dissidents were systematically persecuted and intimidated by members of their own community, including abroad, and that some, including in the diaspora, were targeted for assassination, their names circulating on hit-lists called 'akagara'.
r2-G-DOC-446-053.l: Hauts Plateaux, South Kivu, and diaspora
r2-G-DOC-446-053.a: members of the Banyamulenge community (as alleged by the source)
r2-G-DOC-446-053.n: S/2025/446 para. 176 (refugees, civil society, eyewitnesses, dissidents, imagery, social media). Context: a significant portion of Banyamulenge rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda.
r2-G-DOC-446-053.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). 'Dissidents' defined by the preceding sentence of para. 176. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: significant portion of Banyamulenge rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-032: Read para. 176 in full. The 'dissidents' are 'a significant portion of the Banyamulenge community [that] rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda' (an 'As previously reported' clause citing S/2023/431). The draft phrase 'dissidents of AFC/M23 and Rwanda support' is ambiguous, so the amended text uses the source's own words. The paragraph gives no date or place for the persecution or hit-lists. The 'Fizi' territory and 'Hauts Plateaux' location come from neighbouring paragraphs (175 and 177), so the place fields should read 'not stated (community-wide, including diaspora)'. The 2025 timing is the report period, not a date of the acts.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): significant portion of Banyamulenge rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda
src: These dissidents were systematically persecuted and intimidated by members of their own community, including abroad. Some dissidents, including in the diaspora, were targeted for assassination, their names circulating on hit-lists called “akagara”.
As previously reported, a significant portion of the Banyamulenge community rejected support for AFC/M23 and Rwanda (S/2023/431, para. 143).

r2-G-DOC-446-054.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in March 2025 a prominent civil society member from the Bweza groupement, displaced in Goma, was kidnapped by Ephrem Kabasha, the AFC/M23 appointed territorial administrator of Nyiragongo, from the office of Bukuma chefferie and taken to an underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya and tortured, then released the same evening.
r2-G-DOC-446-054.l: Bukuma chefferie office, Goma; underground cell north of Kanyaruchinya, North Kivu
r2-G-DOC-446-054.n: S/2025/446 annex 17 (para. 27); torture and same-day release are stated in the next sentences of the annex (not in the excerpt, which covers the abduction only). Victim not named. Note: the annex elsewhere calls Kabasha territorial administrator of Masisi; para. 27 says Nyiragongo.
r2-G-DOC-446-054.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Torture and same-day release are in the next sentences of annex 17 (page, not the excerpt). Territory tag removed: 'Nyiragongo' is Kabasha's title, not a stated location of the event. Discrepancy in the report: this passage and para. 27 call Ephrem Kabasha the AFC/M23 territorial administrator of Nyiragongo (annex 16 also lists him as AT for Nyiragongo), while another annex 17 passage calls him territorial administrator of Masisi.
src: In March 2025, a prominent member of the civil society in the Bweza groupement, at the time living as a displaced person in Goma, was kidnapped by Ephrem Kabasha, the AFC/M23 appointed territorial administrator (“AT”) of Nyiragongo, while the individual was at the office of Bukuma chefferie.

r2-G-DOC-446-055.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that in mid-February 2025 Ephrem Kabasha, recently appointed by AFC/M23 as territorial administrator of Masisi, prohibited all associations, including civil society, during a speech in Kaseni.
r2-G-DOC-446-055.n: S/2025/446 annex 17 (para. 27). Discrepancy inside the report: para. 27 and other annex 17 passages call Kabasha territorial administrator of Nyiragongo. Location of Kaseni not stated.
r2-G-DOC-446-055.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Territory tag removed: 'Masisi' is Kabasha's title in this passage, and the source does not say where Kaseni is. Discrepancy in the report: this annex 17 passage calls Ephrem Kabasha territorial administrator of Masisi; para. 27, other annex 17 passages and annex 16 call him territorial administrator of Nyiragongo.
src: in mid-February 2025, Ephrem Kabasha, recently appointed by AFC/M23 as territorial administrator of Masisi, prohibited all associations, including civil society, during a speech in Kaseni.

r2-G-DOC-446-056.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 17 that on 7 January 2025 Ndayambaje Birahira, AFC/M23-appointed deputy provincial coordinator in charge of public finances and taxes in North Kivu, threatened the family of a prominent civil society actor from Rutshuru and obliged the family to leave their house, which AFC/M23 expropriated with all its contents.
r2-G-DOC-446-056.n: S/2025/446 annex 17 (para. 27). The annex says the house was then occupied by Ndayambaje, Bahati Erasto and Willy Manzi (corroborated by the Group in January 2025). Victim not named.
r2-G-DOC-446-056.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Name spelled as this passage prints it (annex 16 spells 'Ndayambaje Birihari'). The report spells the name 'Ndayambaje Birahira' here and 'Ndayambaje Birihari' in annex 16.
src: On 7 January 2025, Ndayambaje Birahira, AFC/M23-appointed deputy provincial coordinator in charge of public finances and taxes in North Kivu, threatened the family of a prominent civil society actor from Rutshuru, and obliged his family to leave their house in the Rutshuru. AFC/M23 expropriated the house and all its contents.

r2-G-DOC-446-057.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 71 that Nicolas Kyalangalilwa Mulondani, Federal President of the party Leadership et Gouvernance pour le Développement (LGD) in South Kivu, officially announced his allegiance to AFC/M23 on 22 February, and that Samy Jean Takimbula, Vice-President of the Bureau de Coordination de la Société Civile of South Kivu, pledged support on 23 February and was disavowed by the BCSC/SK President.
r2-G-DOC-446-057.n: S/2025/446 annex 71 (para. 171). Annex also lists a 20 February declaration by 35 individuals thanking AFC/M23 for 'liberating the province of South Kivu'.
r2-G-DOC-446-057.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent).
ent: Leadership et Gouvernance pour le Développement
Bureau de Coordination de la Société Civile of South Kivu
src: Nicolas Kyalangalilwa Mulondani, the Federal President of the political party “Leadership et Gouvernance pour le Développement” (LGD) in South Kivu, officially announced his allegiance to the AFC/M23 on 22 February.

Samy Jean Takimbula, the Vice-President of the “Bureau de Coordination de la Société Civile of South Kivu (BCSC/SK)”, pledged support for AFC/M23 on 23 February. Thereupon, Samy Jean Takimbula was disavowed by the President of the BCSC/SK.

r2-G-DOC-446-058.s: The UN Group of Experts reported in annex 12 that on 22 February approximately 2,000 FARDC and PNC were brought from Bukavu to Rumangabo camp, via Goma.
r2-G-DOC-446-058.l: Bukavu to Rumangabo camp, Rutshuru territory, via Goma
r2-G-DOC-446-058.n: S/2025/446 annex 12 (para. 21); para. 169 gives 'approximately 2,000 FARDC and PNC were captured and brought to the Rumangabo training camp'. Annex 12 says the group was taken as part of coercive recruitment.
r2-G-DOC-446-058.vn: Excerpt is on the retained PDF and supports the statement; attributed to the Group. Same origin as the existing S/2025/446 claims (not independent). Adds to the existing Rumangabo forced-recruitment material; para. 169 says they were 'captured'.
src: On 22 February, approximately 2,000 FARDC and PNC were brought from Bukavu to Rumangabo camp, via Goma.

r2-G-DOC-466-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 15 August 2025 at about 05:00 ADF elements carried out an incursion into Mangoli village, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, killing at least 32 civilians with bladed weapons; an undetermined number of persons were abducted and at least 28 houses were looted and burned.
r2-G-DOC-466-001.l: Mangoli village, about 15 km north of Bandulu, Bapere sector, Lubero territory
r2-G-DOC-466-001.a: ADF (Abwakasi group per annex 9 section heading)
r2-G-DOC-466-001.x: Group of Experts: at least 32 killed; at least 28 houses looted and burned; abductees undetermined
r2-G-DOC-466-001.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 9, para. 5. Annex 9 places the paragraph under "Attacks in Abwakasi's operational area, in Lubero territory".
r2-G-DOC-466-001.vn: Excerpt exact and matches statement; Group of Experts documented investigation (annex 9 para 5).
src: On 15 August 2025 at approximately 05:00 hours, ADF elements carried out an incursion into the village of Mangoli, located approximately 15 kilometers north of Bandulu, Bapere sector, Lubero territory, killing at least 32 civilians using bladed weapons. An undetermined number of persons were abducted. The assailants also looted and set fire to at least 28 houses.

r2-G-DOC-466-002.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on the night of 15 to 16 August 2025 ADF elements carried out an incursion into the Mbimbi neighborhood of the town of Oicha, killing nine civilians and injuring two others; the assailants set fire to 19 houses and burned five motorcycles.
r2-G-DOC-466-002.x: Group of Experts: nine civilians killed, two injured; 19 houses and five motorcycles burned
r2-G-DOC-466-002.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 9, para. 6 (text runs across a page break; two excerpts from the same page text). Oicha is the capital of Beni territory (not stated in the excerpt; the territory field is the drafter's knowledge and should be checked).
r2-G-DOC-466-002.vn: Territory tag 'Beni' was the researcher's inference; the page does not state it (the paragraph sits under a Lubero-territory heading). Territory set to not specified; figures written as printed (words). The Group lists this incident in annex 9 under the heading for Abwakasi's operational area in Lubero territory; the report does not name the territory of Oicha.
src: On the night of 15 to 16 August 2025, between approximately 20:00 and 22:00 hours, ADF elements carried out an incursion into the town of Oicha, in the Mbimbi neighborhood.
killing of nine civilians and the injury of two others. The assailants set fire to 19 houses and burned five motorcycles.

r2-G-DOC-466-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout 2025 attacks perpetrated under Abwakasi's command led to the killing of over 600 persons, making it the deadliest of all ADF units, and resulted in the displacement of an estimated 25,000 people and the destruction of at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites.
r2-G-DOC-466-003.x: Group of Experts: over 600 killed; about 25,000 displaced; at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites destroyed
r2-G-DOC-466-003.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 9, para. 9 (also main text para. 23). Date precision: calendar year 2025.
r2-G-DOC-466-003.vn: Excerpt does not restrict the figures to Lubero territory; statement narrowed to the excerpt wording. Date is the calendar year, so precision set to range.
src: Throughout 2025, the attacks perpetrated under Abwakasi’s command led to the killing of over 600 persons, making it the deadliest of all ADF units. The attacks resulted in the displacement of an estimated 25,000 people and the destruction of at least 26 villages and 9 mining sites.

r2-G-DOC-466-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that one humanitarian actor stated that between January and June 2025 nearly 28,000 victims of sexual violence sought care at facilities it supported in eastern DRC, and that 75 percent of these attacks were committed by armed individuals.
r2-G-DOC-466-004.l: eastern DRC (provinces not broken down in this passage)
r2-G-DOC-466-004.x: Humanitarian actor (unnamed), as cited by the Group: nearly 28,000 victims sought care; 75 percent of attacks by armed individuals
r2-G-DOC-466-004.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 4, para. 6 (Documentation by humanitarian actors). Figure is care-seeking, not UN-verified; the actor is not named in the passage (footnote 287 cites a statement to the UN Security Council of 12 December 2025).
r2-G-DOC-466-004.vn: Exact; correctly attributed as a relay. Care-seeking figure from an unnamed humanitarian actor relayed by the Group; not verified by the Group.
src: One humanitarian actor reported that between January and June 2025, nearly 28,000 victims of sexual violence sought care at facilities they supported in eastern DRC, noting that 75 percent of these attacks were committed by armed individuals.

r2-G-DOC-466-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported (S/2026/466) that it received information about, but was not able to investigate, new cases of conflict-related sexual violence in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements leading to the birth of children; the sentence cites the Group's earlier report S/2023/990 (para. 21, annex 12) and gives no dates for the cases.
r2-G-DOC-466-005.l: Ituri and North Kivu (places not specified)
r2-G-DOC-466-005.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 4, "Investigations by the Group of Experts", para. 1. The Group did not verify these cases. Date is the reporting period only.
r2-G-DOC-466-005.vn: Exact; Group's own hedge preserved; C appropriate for uninvestigated information. The Group says it was not able to investigate these cases. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: The sentence is verbatim in S/2026/466, but it is footnoted to S/2023/990, para. 21, annex 12, so the cases are not shown to fall in 2025-2026 (claim date '2025/2026'). The Amnesty page (5 May 2026) separately documents forced marriage and forced pregnancy by the ADF but does not carry the Group's statement.
