src: The Group also received information about but was not able to investigate new cases of CRSV in Ituri and North Kivu, in particular sexual slavery and forced pregnancy by ADF-ISCAP elements leading to the birth of children
additional abuses and crimes against women and girls, including forced marriage, forced pregnancy and various other forms of sexual violence.
One woman said pressure by her in-laws to kill her two children who were born in the bush almost led to her taking her own life.

r2-G-DOC-466-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that OCHA DRC recorded 626 security incidents affecting humanitarian workers in 2025, including thirteen deaths, and that the majority of recorded incidents in 2025 and January-February 2026 occurred in North Kivu and South Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-466-006.l: eastern DRC, majority in North Kivu and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-466-006.x: OCHA via the Group: 626 incidents, thirteen deaths in 2025
r2-G-DOC-466-006.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 3. Year-level figure for 2025; not broken down by perpetrator.
r2-G-DOC-466-006.vn: Period of the geographic clause is printed in the sentence before the excerpt (annex 3); supplied as replacement quote. Figures are OCHA's relayed by the Group.
src: In 2025, OCHA DRC recorded a total of 626 security incidents affecting humanitarian workers, including thirteen deaths.
the majority of recorded incidents occurred in North Kivu and South Kivu.

r2-G-DOC-466-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 January 2026 a drone strike hit the office of the INGO War Child in Masisi, killing seven people and injuring 42 and others, mainly women and children, and said it is continuing to investigate; in the main text it listed the strike, which it says hit the War Child sub-base in Masisi centre, among FARDC drone operations that affected civilian objects and populations.
r2-G-DOC-466-007.a: FARDC drone operations (main text para. 163); the Group says investigation continues
r2-G-DOC-466-007.x: Group of Experts, annex 3: seven killed, 42 injured; main text: at least seven fatalities
r2-G-DOC-466-007.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 3 and para. 163. Annex 3 says "The Group is continuing to investigate"; para. 163 attributes the operation to FARDC drones. The second excerpt is the para. 163 attribution sentence. The facility is an INGO office/sub-base, not a health facility; tagged health_care_access because humanitarian operations are affected.
r2-G-DOC-466-007.vn: Overlaps r1-GOE-025 (FARDC drone operations incl. Masisi); adds injury figure and investigation status. Figures restated in printed words; health tag removed (not a health facility). Annex 3 says the Group is still investigating; the target was an INGO office/sub-base, not a health facility.
src: On 2 January 2026, a drone strike hit the office of the INGO War Child in Masisi, killing seven people and injuring 42 and others, mainly women and children (para. 163).
Several FARDC drone operations affected civilian objects and populations.

r2-G-DOC-466-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF withdrew only to Sange, 35 kilometres north of Uvira in the Ruzizi Plain, where AFC/M23 established its headquarters.
r2-G-DOC-466-008.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 25 (para. 78). The date is the post-18 January 2026 withdrawal period; the exact date of arrival at Sange is not given.
r2-G-DOC-466-008.vn: Exact. The excerpt's 'it established its headquarters' does not name the subject; annex 25 elsewhere calls Sange AFC/M23's forward headquarters.
src: AFC/M23 and RDF only withdrew until Sange, 35 kilometers north of Uvira, in the Ruzizi Plain, where it established its headquarters.

r2-G-DOC-466-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in mid-February 2026 the frontline stabilized north of Uvira: fighting ceased on the Ruzizi Plain but persisted in the highlands, and the line settled around Kabunambo with a 10-15 kilometre buffer between the warring parties.
r2-G-DOC-466-009.l: Kabunambo, about 25 km north of Uvira, Ruzizi Plain
r2-G-DOC-466-009.a: AFC/M23 and RDF versus FARDC and allies
r2-G-DOC-466-009.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 25. The annex describes Kabunambo as south of Sange, where AFC/M23's forward headquarters was located.
r2-G-DOC-466-009.vn: Exact; year 2026 from context of annex 25 date field only.
src: In mid-February, the frontline stabilized north of Uvira. Fighting ceased on the Ruzizi Plain but persisted in the highlands. The line settled around Kabunambo (approximately 25 kilometers north of Uvira, south of Sange, where AFC/M23’s forward headquarters was located) with a 10–15 kilometer buffer between the warring parties.

r2-G-DOC-466-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 February 2026 approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.
r2-G-DOC-466-010.l: Bugarama and Nyangezi (Rwanda) to Kamanyola, Luvungi and Sange along the RN5
r2-G-DOC-466-010.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 25. Territory field summarises the route; the excerpt names places only.
src: On 2 February 2026, approximately 25 trucks carrying RDF troops departed from Bugarama and Nyangezi in Rwanda, arriving in Kamanyola before continuing toward Luvungi and Sange along the RN5.

r2-G-DOC-466-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that as of mid-February 2026 RDF deployments in South Kivu were approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain-Moyens Plateaux axis, 800 in the Hauts Plateaux, 1,800 along the Ngweshe-Mwenga axis, and an undetermined number elsewhere including in the direction of Fizi.
r2-G-DOC-466-011.l: Ruzizi Plain, Moyens Plateaux, Hauts Plateaux, Ngweshe-Mwenga axis, direction of Fizi
r2-G-DOC-466-011.x: Group of Experts: about 1,800 + 800 + 1,800 troops plus undetermined number
r2-G-DOC-466-011.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 25. Annex cautions that exact strength could not always be reliably determined and estimates are conservative.
r2-G-DOC-466-011.vn: Exact. The Group describes its strength estimates as conservative.
src: As of mid-February 2026, RDF deployments in South Kivu were as follows: approximately 1,800 troops along the Ruzizi Plain–Moyens Plateaux axis; 800 troops in the Hauts Plateaux; 1,800 troops along the Ngweshe–Mwenga axis; and an undetermined number elsewhere, including in direction of Fizi.

r2-G-DOC-466-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 December 2025 AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted on his X account a statement announcing that AFC/M23 would unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira "as per the United States' mediation request".
r2-G-DOC-466-012.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 24. The annex heading reads "Initial withdrawal announcement on 15 December 2025" while the text dates the post 16 December; the Group sources the post to Nangaa's official X account posted on 16 December 2025. Group assessed that in practice only a partial, staged withdrawal took place.
r2-G-DOC-466-012.vn: Exact; AFC/M23 statement as reported by the Group. Date discrepancy within the annex surfaced in note. Annex 24's heading reads 'Initial withdrawal announcement on 15 December 2025' while its text dates the post 16 December.
src: On 16 December, AFC coordinator Corneille Nangaa posted on his X account a statement in which he announced that AFC/M23, referring to the Doha process and the signing of the Doha Framework agreement on 15 November 2025, it will unilaterally withdraw its forces from Uvira “as per the United States' mediation request”.

r2-G-DOC-466-013.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Uvira remained effectively under AFC/M23 and RDF control until January, and that AFC/M23 and RDF maintained a covert presence within Uvira, including through combatants dressed in civilian attire or their integration into local "police" units.
r2-G-DOC-466-013.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 24. Follows the announced December 2025 withdrawal; the Group states only "until January".
r2-G-DOC-466-013.vn: Removed the year '2026', which the excerpt does not print.
src: The town remained effectively under AFC/M23 and RDF control until January. AFC/M23 and RDF maintained a covert presence within Uvira, including through combatants dressed in civilian attire or their integration into local “police” units.

r2-G-DOC-466-014.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter to the UN Secretary-General three days before its withdrawal from Uvira, AFC/M23 justified the withdrawal by citing its "sincere commitment to the ceasefire" and its intention to pursue a peaceful and political resolution of the conflict, said it had requested MONUSCO to ensure civilian protection in Uvira, and called for the deployment of a "neutral force".
r2-G-DOC-466-014.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 24. Date computed as three days before the 18 January 2026 withdrawal date given in para. 77; the annex does not print the letter date.
r2-G-DOC-466-014.vn: The exact letter date (15 January) was computed by the researcher; the annex heading gives only January 2026. Date narrowed to month; added the 'neutral force' clause the excerpt prints.
src: In a letter addressed to the Secretary-General three days prior to its withdrawal from Uvira, AFC/M23 justified the withdrawal by citing its “sincere commitment to the ceasefire” and its intention to pursue a peaceful and political resolution of the conflict. It further indicated that it had requested MONUSCO to ensure civilian protection in Uvira and called for the deployment of a “neutral force”.

r2-G-DOC-466-015.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that by mid-February 2026 RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux; the Group also noted that RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23.
r2-G-DOC-466-015.a: RED Tabara and FNL with AFC/M23, RDF and Twirwaneho
r2-G-DOC-466-015.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 26 (para. 79). The annex notes RED Tabara leadership repeatedly denied links with AFC/M23.
r2-G-DOC-466-015.vn: Exact. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: RED Tabara leadership denials 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-034: The same report (claim r2-G-DOC-466-016, same PDF) records that RED Tabara leadership repeatedly denied links with AFC/M23; this counter-account should travel with the coalition claim. Amended to add it, attributed to the Group.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): RED Tabara leadership denials
src: By mid-February 2026, RED Tabara and FNL combatants had physically joined the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition in the Kamombo sector of the Hauts Plateaux.
Although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23

r2-G-DOC-466-016.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory) and Kipupu (Mwenga territory), and that RED Tabara leadership had repeatedly denied links with AFC/M23 while its combatants took part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and RDF.
r2-G-DOC-466-016.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 26. Burundian armed group; included because its fighters operated in Uvira, Mwenga and Fizi territories in 2026.
r2-G-DOC-466-016.vn: Exact; denial preserved. RED Tabara leadership denies links with AFC/M23, per the Group.
src: RED Tabara had long-standing camps in Masango (Uvira territory), Magunda (Mwenga territory), and Kipupu (Mwenga territory). Although the RED Tabara leadership has repeatedly denied any links with AFC/M23, Red Tabara combatants have taken part in hostilities alongside AFC/M23, Twirwaneho, and RDF across several axes

r2-G-DOC-466-017.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 2 March 2026 the US Office of Foreign Assets Control sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Forces and four senior commanders for direct involvement in destabilizing eastern DRC.
r2-G-DOC-466-017.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 17 (para. 42). Annex also quotes US Treasury statements that RDF was "actively supporting, training, and fighting alongside" M23; those are the Treasury's assessments as relayed by the Group. Rwandan response not in this excerpt.
r2-G-DOC-466-017.vn: Exact; the Group reporting a US action.
src: On 2 March 2026, the U.S. Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned the Rwanda Defence Forces (RDF) and four senior commanders, citing their direct involvement in destabilizing eastern DRC.

r2-G-DOC-466-018.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the individuals designated by OFAC were Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF; Major-General Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander; General Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff; and Stanislas Gashugi, Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025.
r2-G-DOC-466-018.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 17. Posts as printed by the Group. Designation date taken from the same annex (2 March 2026).
r2-G-DOC-466-018.vn: Exact; names and posts as printed. Being designated under US sanctions is not a finding of individual responsibility.
src: Accordingly, Vincent Nyakarundi, Chief of Staff of the RDF; Major-General Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations Force Commander; General Mubarakh Muganga, Chief of Defence Staff; and Stanislas Gashugi, Special Operations Force Commander since 15 March 2025, were designated for their leadership roles within the RDF.

r2-G-DOC-466-019.s: The UN Group of Experts, in its own summary (not a transcript) of an interview President Paul Kagame gave to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026, reported that Kagame indicated no intention to withdraw or scale down Rwanda's military posture, stating that defensive measures would remain in place until the perceived threat was addressed, by any means necessary.
r2-G-DOC-466-019.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 19. This is the Group's paraphrase of the interview, not a transcript; the first excerpt contains the footnote marker "382" as extracted from the PDF. Original interview should be sourced separately.
r2-G-DOC-466-019.vn: Made the paraphrase explicit. Overlaps r1-GOE-054 (defensive measures) and adds the no-withdrawal position. The Group's paraphrase of the interview; the original interview has not been retrieved.
src: In an exclusive interview granted to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026,382 President Paul Kagame addressed questions about Rwanda’s role in the ongoing conflict in the DRC, the US sanctions and the RDF’s expected withdrawal from the DRC.

Kagame indicated no intention to withdraw or scale down Rwanda’s military posture, stating that defensive measures would remain in place until the perceived threat was addressed, by any means necessary,

r2-G-DOC-466-020.s: The UN Group of Experts, in its own summary (not a transcript) of an interview President Paul Kagame gave to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026, reported that Kagame described the fall of Uvira as "inevitable", a necessary consequence of the situation on the ground, claiming that it should not have come as a surprise to any of the parties, including the US, since they were informed on a daily basis of the "evolution of the situation".
r2-G-DOC-466-020.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 19. Paraphrase by the Group; the full sentence continues that all parties "were informed on a daily basis". The second excerpt stops mid-sentence at a comma.
r2-G-DOC-466-020.vn: Made the paraphrase explicit; second clause rests on the sentence continuation, supplied as replacement quote. The Group's paraphrase of the interview, with short quoted words; the original interview has not been retrieved.
src: In an exclusive interview granted to Jeune Afrique on 26 March 2026,382 President Paul Kagame addressed questions about Rwanda’s role in the ongoing conflict in the DRC, the US sanctions and the RDF’s expected withdrawal from the DRC.
He described the fall of Uvira as “inevitable”, a necessary consequence of the situation on the ground,

r2-G-DOC-466-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued to privilege military expansion, escalating military operations with the objective of taking Walikale, Kisangani, Kalemie and Beni.
r2-G-DOC-466-021.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 56. Report covers investigations to 15 April 2026; date is approximate (reporting period).
r2-G-DOC-466-021.vn: Paragraph gives no month; date set to the reporting period rather than April 2026.
src: AFC/M23 continued to privilege military expansion, escalating military operations with the objective of taking Walikale, Kisangani, Kalemie and Beni.

r2-G-DOC-466-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in South Kivu no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued, and that additional RDF reinforcements arrived from Rwanda in April 2026, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.
src: In South Kivu, no RDF or AFC/M23 troop withdrawals were documented and fighting continued. Additional RDF reinforcements from Rwanda arrived in April, including sophisticated weaponry and anti-aerial man-portable air defence systems.

r2-G-DOC-466-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF continued anti-FDLR operations in the Bwito and Bwisha chefferies, Rutshuru territory, also targeting civilians associated with FDLR or affiliated armed groups, including through systematic killings, destruction of livelihoods and burning of villages.
r2-G-DOC-466-023.l: Bwito and Bwisha chefferies, Rutshuru territory
r2-G-DOC-466-023.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 69. No individual incident, date or victim count given in this paragraph.
r2-G-DOC-466-023.vn: Exact; general finding without incident detail.
src: AFC/M23 and RDF continued anti-FDLR operations in Bwito and Bwisha chefferies, in Rutshuru territory, also targeting civilians associated with FDLR or affiliated armed groups (see S/2025/858, paras. 36–45), including through systematic killings, destruction of livelihoods and burning of villages.

r2-G-DOC-466-024.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that between January and March 2026 significant AFC/M23 and RDF troop reinforcements were documented at the Lubero frontline, raising concerns of an imminent offensive toward Butembo and Beni, which did not materialize.
r2-G-DOC-466-024.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 71. The paragraph attributes non-materialisation partly to UPDF presence and Uganda's refusal to grant passage.
r2-G-DOC-466-024.vn: 'Did not materialize' is in the next sentence of para 71; supplied as replacement quote. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Para. 71 of S/2026/466 supports the statement, but the stored excerpt lacks the 'did not materialize' clause, which is in the next sentence (it also gives UPDF presence and Uganda's refusal of passage as partial reasons); that sentence is added.
src: Between January-March 2026, significant AFC/M23 and RDF troop reinforcements were documented at the Lubero frontline, raising concerns of an imminent offensive toward Butembo and Beni.

While it did not materialize, partially due to UPDF presence and Uganda’s refusal to grant them passage, 77 the reinforcements stretched FARDC capabilities and sustained strategic ambiguity regarding the timing and direction of future operations.

r2-G-DOC-466-025.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout the reporting period AFC/M23 and RDF prioritized capturing Pinga and Walikale and, since March, also focused on the Bunyakiri (Kalehe)-Ntoto (Masisi)-Hombo (Walikale) axis, which would allow an alternative, southern approach to Walikale.
r2-G-DOC-466-025.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 70. Kalehe is in South Kivu; Ntoto in Masisi and Hombo in Walikale (North Kivu).
r2-G-DOC-466-025.vn: Removed '2026' after 'March', which the excerpt does not print. Overlaps r1-GOE-018 (Pinga/Walikale focus); adds the southern axis.
src: Throughout the reporting period, AFC/M23 and RDF prioritized capturing Pinga and Walikale. Since March, it also focused on the strategically significant Bunyakiri (Kalehe)–Ntoto (Masisi)–Hombo (Walikale) axis, which would allow an alternative, southern approach to Walikale (see paras. 47–48).

r2-G-DOC-466-026.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 and the rapid advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF forces southwards to Makobola, 20 km south of Uvira, represented a significant territorial expansion, with mutual allegations of cross-border shelling by Burundi and Rwanda.
r2-G-DOC-466-026.l: Uvira and Makobola (20 km south of Uvira)
r2-G-DOC-466-026.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 74. Date is that of the Uvira capture; the date of reaching Makobola is not given. Rwandan and Burundian accounts of the shelling are not in the excerpt.
src: The capture of Uvira on 10 December 2025 and the rapid advancement of AFC/M23 and RDF forces southwards to Makobola, 20 km south of Uvira, represented a significant territorial expansion. Mutual allegations of cross -border shelling by Burundi and Rwanda heightened the risk of direct confrontation and regionalization of the conflict

r2-G-DOC-466-027.s: The UN Group of Experts (final report S/2026/466, citing its earlier report S/2025/446, para. 176) reported that the strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama.
r2-G-DOC-466-027.vn: Exact. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: Time slippage: the estimate is cross-referenced to the Group's 2025 report (S/2025/446), so dating it '2026' may misplace it; the statement should show the citation. Attribution to the Group kept.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: The strength of MRDP/Twirwaneho was estimated at 2,500 to 3,000 combatants, led by Charles Sematama (see S/2025/446, para. 176).

r2-G-DOC-466-028.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 elements consolidated around Banyamulenge population centres, including Minembwe, Mikenge and Muranvia, and that RDF presence in the Hauts Plateaux was limited to sporadic, platoon-sized specialized elements and air support.
r2-G-DOC-466-028.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 84. Date range approximate (reinforcement in February 2026 per para. 83 to time of drafting).
src: RDF presence in the Hauts Plateaux was limited to sporadic, platoon-sized specialized elements and air support (see para. 168), likely due to the area’s geographic isolation. MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 elements consolidated around Banyamulenge population centres, including Minembwe, Mikenge and Muranvia.

r2-G-DOC-466-029.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since February 2026 access to Minembwe had been limited to air supply only, and that several rotations of planes airdropping supplies were documented in March and April 2026.
r2-G-DOC-466-029.a: not attributed (encirclement by FARDC and allies; air resupply for the besieged side)
r2-G-DOC-466-029.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 86 and footnote 95. Para. 85 says RDF supported MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 through drone strikes and aerial resupply. The footnote excerpt is footnote text on the same page.
r2-G-DOC-466-029.vn: Place (Minembwe) is in the preceding sentence of para 86. Overlaps r1-GOE-020 (encirclement, air-only access); adds the documented airdrop rotations.
src: Since February 2026, access has been limited to air supply only.
In March and April 2026, several rotations of planes airdropping supplies in Minembwe were documented, as confirmed by military and intelligence sources

r2-G-DOC-466-030.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that members of the Banyamulenge community denounced both parties for trapping civilians in an active combat zone, calling on FARDC to lift the siege and establish a humanitarian corridor and on MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 to allow civilians to leave safely.
r2-G-DOC-466-030.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 88. Statement attributed by the Group to representatives of the Banyamulenge community (footnote 98). Group added that both conducts raise serious concerns under IHL.
r2-G-DOC-466-030.vn: Exact; community statement relayed by the Group.
src: Members of the Banyamulenge community have denounced both parties for trapping civilians in an active combat zone, calling on FARDC to lift the siege and establish a humanitarian corridor and on MRDP/Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 to allow civilians to leave safely.

r2-G-DOC-466-031.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that each M23 combat unit was supervised and supported by RDF, and that RDF personnel were integrated into mixed battalions alongside M23 elements, including commando units originating from Bigogwe, Rubavu and Cyangugu.
r2-G-DOC-466-031.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (not specified)
r2-G-DOC-466-031.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 97. Rwanda's position on RDF presence: see Kagame interview claims (annex 19).
src: Each M23 combat unit was supervised and supported by RDF (see S/2024/969, para. 49). RDF personnel were integrated into mixed battalions alongside M23 elements, including commando units originating from Bigogwe, Rubavu and Cyangugu.

r2-G-DOC-466-032.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the DRC continued to provide funds, logistics and weapons to VDP/Wazalendo groups in North Kivu, in violation of the sanctions regime.
r2-G-DOC-466-032.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 102. Kinshasa's reply is addressed in the report's "Right to reply" section, not in this paragraph.
r2-G-DOC-466-032.vn: 'North Kivu' is in the first sentence of para 102; supplied as replacement quote. 'In violation of the sanctions regime' is the Group's assessment.
src: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo continued to provide funds, logistics and weapons to the VDP/Wazalendo, in violation of the sanctions regime

r2-G-DOC-466-033.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, FDDP and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.
r2-G-DOC-466-033.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 104. The paragraph adds that the practice was known and approved by several FARDC officers and DRC authorities.
src: FDLR combatants remained embedded within several VDP/Wazalendo groups, notably CMC/FDP, Forces dévoués pour la défense de la patrie (FDDP) and APCLS, reinforcing their ranks while obscuring affiliation with FDLR.

r2-G-DOC-466-034.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in December 2025 Kinshasa-based authorities and FARDC proposed a "coalition nationale des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP/Wazalendo)" following a general assembly held on 13 December 2025, but that VDP/Wazalendo disavowed the initiative, including the proposed leadership.
r2-G-DOC-466-034.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 105 and annex 34. Date is that of the general assembly; the proposal is dated "December 2025".
src: In December 2025, Kinshasa-based authorities and FARDC proposed the establishment of a “coalition nationale des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP/Wazalendo)” following a general assembly held on 13 December 2025, with an elected leadership tasked with coordinating all armed factions involved in fighting AFC/M23 and RDF (see annex 34). However, VDP/Wazalendo disavowed this initiative, including the proposed leadership.

r2-G-DOC-466-035.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the "Synergie Masisi-Walikale", comprising 17 armed groups, was led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa (CDi.033), and that FDLR-FOCA combatants were integrated into the Masisi-Walikale and Petit Nord synergies.
r2-G-DOC-466-035.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 108. FDLR-FOCA integration is in the next sentence (footnote 126) and is not in this excerpt; entities limited to what the excerpt prints.
r2-G-DOC-466-035.vn: FDLR-FOCA sentence follows the excerpt in para 108; supplied as replacement quote. Overlaps r1-GOE-042 (synergies).
src: The “Synergie Masisi-Walikale”, comprising 17 armed groups, was led by APCLS leader Janvier Karahiri and sanctioned individual Guidon Shimiray Mwisa (CDi.033).

r2-G-DOC-466-036.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that between August and December 2025 Wazalendo relations with FARDC deteriorated significantly, with Wazalendo attacking some FARDC, accusing them of treason, and confiscating weapons and ammunition.
r2-G-DOC-466-036.l: South Kivu, centred on Uvira by December 2025
r2-G-DOC-466-036.vn: Exact; excerpt names no territory, so the Uvira tag is removed.
src: Between August and December 2025, Wazalendo relations with FARDC deteriorated significantly. Wazalendo attacked some FARDC, accusing them of treason, and confiscated weapons and ammunition.

r2-G-DOC-466-037.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that after AFC/M23 and RDF occupied Uvira, Wazalendo retreated outside Uvira town or to their bases in Fizi and the Hauts and Moyens Plateaux.
r2-G-DOC-466-037.l: outside Uvira town; Fizi; Hauts and Moyens Plateaux
r2-G-DOC-466-037.vn: Exact. 2026-10-29: control edited: Frontline data fix (FRONTLINE_NOTES.md): control.held_by names only the holder (for a withdrawal, the side withdrawing), so the side class is not 'both sides named'; the other side stays in the statement. Wording from the stored excerpt.
src: After AFC/M23 and RDF occupied Uvira, Wazalendo retreated outside Uvira town or to their bases in Fizi and the Hauts and Moyens Plateaux.

r2-G-DOC-466-038.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in late January 2026 political actors such as Justin Bitakwira, known for anti-Tutsi rhetoric, and Willy Mishiki mobilized political support and advocated for increased logistical and financial assistance for the Wazalendo in South Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-466-038.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 116. "Known for his anti-Tutsi rhetoric" is the Group's characterisation.
r2-G-DOC-466-038.vn: Exact. 'Known for his anti-Tutsi rhetoric' is the Group's characterisation.
src: In late January 2026, political actors such as Justin Bitakwira, known for his anti-Tutsi rhetoric (see S/2024/969, paras. 108–109), and Willy Mishiki mobilized political support and advocated for increased logistical and financial assistance for the Wazalendo in South Kivu.

r2-G-DOC-466-039.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Wazalendo groups often mounted the first lines of defence against AFC/M23 and RDF, including around Uvira, and that between August and December 2025 they fought against AFC/M23 and RDF in Walungu, Kabare, Minembwe and Mwenga and on the outskirts of Uvira and Fizi.
r2-G-DOC-466-039.l: Walungu, Kabare, Minembwe, Mwenga, outskirts of Uvira and Fizi
r2-G-DOC-466-039.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 119. The Group adds that Wazalendo operations did not result in any major recovery of territory.
src: Wazalendo groups often mounted the first lines of defence against AFC/M23 and RDF, including around Uvira. Between August and December 2025, they fought against AFC/M23 and RDF in Walungu, Kabare, Minembwe and Mwenga, on the outskirts of Uvira and Fizi.

r2-G-DOC-466-040.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since reclaiming Uvira, Wazalendo factions supported joint ground operations by FARDC and FDNB in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, and that in Fizi the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition, supported by air strikes, fought to maintain control over Point Zero and Tuwe Tuwe.
r2-G-DOC-466-040.l: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories; Point Zero; Tuwe Tuwe
r2-G-DOC-466-040.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 122. Footnote 143 says FDNB was not deployed at Minembwe after January 2026.
r2-G-DOC-466-040.vn: Exact. Overlaps r1-UC-BI-FDLR-025/-026 and r1-GOE-046 (FDNB-Wazalendo joint operations, Point Zero/Tuwe-Tuwe).
src: Since reclaiming Uvira, Wazalendo factions supported joint ground operations by FARDC and FDNB in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories. In Fizi, the FARDC – Wazalendo–FDNB coalition, supported by air strikes, fought to maintain control over Point Zero and Tuwe Tuwe

r2-G-DOC-466-041.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in January 2026 CNPSC, through its "finance bureau", published a comprehensive list of taxes across multiple sectors.
r2-G-DOC-466-041.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 124 and annex 37. Territory from para. 123 (parallel administration "particularly in Fizi territory").
r2-G-DOC-466-041.vn: Exact. Likely overlaps r1-GOE-047 (CNPSC parallel administration, January 2026); kept as adds_detail since the full r1 text is not visible in the packet.
src: In January 2026, CNPSC, through its “finance bureau”, published a comprehensive list of taxes across multiple sectors.

r2-G-DOC-466-042.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter addressed to the President of the United States in July 2025 the FDLR leadership presented its mission as protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC.
r2-G-DOC-466-042.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 132 and annex 39.
src: In a letter addressed to the President of the United States in July 2025, the FDLR leadership presented its mission as consisting of protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

r2-G-DOC-466-043.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 10 March 2026 FARDC elements shot down two kamikaze drones in Mikenge, South Kivu, and that the following day another kamikaze drone struck FARDC positions in the same area.
r2-G-DOC-466-043.a: not attributed in this paragraph (kamikaze drones of the type used in later RDF/AFC/M23 attacks per paras. 168-169)
r2-G-DOC-466-043.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 167. Perpetrator not stated in the paragraph; the Group says the shot-down drones were of the same type as those used in the Kisangani attacks (para. 169).
r2-G-DOC-466-043.vn: Exact; actor left unattributed. The paragraph does not name the operator of these drones; the Group says the drones shot down were of the same type as those used in the Kisangani attacks.
src: On 10 March 2026, FARDC elements shot down two Kamikaze drones in Mikenge, South Kivu. The following day, another kamikaze drone struck FARDC positions in the same area.

r2-G-DOC-466-044.s: The UN Group of Experts listed, in an annex on kamikaze drone attacks, that on 10 April at approximately 23:00 a kamikaze drone struck positions of the FARDC 113th Infantry Regiment in the Kutundu axis within Kitundu groupement (Uvira area), causing multiple FARDC casualties, and that around 23:30 a drone strike targeted FARDC positions in Muranvya, Bijombo (Uvira Territory), affecting elements of the 22nd Simba Battalion. The annex entry does not name who operated the drones; separately, its main text states that between 1 and 14 April RDF and AFC/M23 carried out at least nine drone attacks on FARDC positions in the Hauts Plateaux.
r2-G-DOC-466-044.l: Kutundu axis, Kitundu groupement; Muranvya and Mugeti, Bijombo
r2-G-DOC-466-044.a: Operator not named in the annex entry (main text attributes at least nine 1-14 April Hauts Plateaux drone attacks to RDF and AFC/M23)
r2-G-DOC-466-044.x: Group of Experts: at least nine drone attacks 1-14 April; FARDC casualties on 10 April not quantified
r2-G-DOC-466-044.n: Cited as S/2026/466, annex 50 and para. 168. Annex 50 does not itself name the operator for the 10 April strikes; attribution rests on para. 168 (date range 1-14 April) and is the drafter's linkage - a reviewer should confirm.
r2-G-DOC-466-044.vn: Hedged per brief: annex 50 does not attribute the 10 April strikes; the researcher's linkage to para 168 removed from the attribution, para 168 reported as a separate statement.  The link between these two strikes and the RDF/AFC/M23 attacks counted in the main text is not stated by the Group.
src: On 10 April at approximately 23:00, in the Kutundu axis within Kitundu groupement (Uvira area), a kamikaze drone struck positions of the FARDC 113th Infantry Regiment, causing multiple FARDC casualties. Approximately 30 minutes later, around 23:30, a drone strike targeted additional FARDC positions in Muranvya, Bijombo (Uvira Territory), affecting elements of the 22nd Simba Battalion.
Between 1 and 14 April, RDF and AFC/M23 carried out at least nine drone attacks on FARDC positions in the Hauts Plateaux.

r2-G-DOC-466-045.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that it identified the aircraft destroyed by a FARDC airstrike on 27 March 2025 at the Kigoma airfield in Walikale, then under AFC/M23 control, as a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan operated by Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre, a company based in Entebbe, Uganda.
r2-G-DOC-466-045.a: FARDC airstrike; aircraft operated by Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre (OHATC)
r2-G-DOC-466-045.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 173 and annex 22. Excerpt spans a footnote marker in the PDF text; if the checker fails this excerpt, split it.
r2-G-DOC-466-045.vn: Checked the footnote marker: '202' is footnote 202 (footnote 203 follows the next sentence); the statement correctly omits it. In the PDF text, '202' after 'Grand Caravan' is footnote marker 202, not part of the aircraft designation; the Group says it is awaiting a response from OHATC.
src: The Group of Experts identified the aircraft destroyed by a FARDC airstrike on 27 March 2025 at the Kigoma airfield in Walikale, at the time under AFC/M23 control (see S/2025/446, para. 38 and annex 22). The aircraft was a Cessna 208B Grand Caravan 202 operated by Ocean Heights Aviation Training Centre (OHATC), a company based in Entebbe, Uganda.

r2-G-DOC-466-046.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that talks between the Government of the DRC and AFC/M23 under the Doha process took place in Montreux, Switzerland, between 13 and 17 April 2026, with modest outcomes, leading to a memorandum of understanding on the operationalization of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism.
r2-G-DOC-466-046.a: Government of the DRC and AFC/M23
r2-G-DOC-466-046.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 52 and annex 20.
src: Talks between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and AFC/M23, as part of the Doha process (see S/2025/858, paras. 7, 10–11), took place in Montreux, Switzerland, between 13 and 17 April 2026, with modest outcomes. The talks led to the signing of a memorandum of understanding on the operationalization of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism

r2-G-DOC-466-047.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Mr. Kabila, the former President (as the report's section heading identifies him), travelled frequently to AFC/M23-controlled territory from May 2025 and held meetings with senior AFC/M23 leadership.
r2-G-DOC-466-047.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 57. Date is the start of the travel period.
r2-G-DOC-466-047.vn: Identity of Mr. Kabila is printed in the same sentence of para 57 (replacement quote). Para 57 identifies Mr. Kabila as the former President of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Joseph Kabila, under the heading Links with Joseph Kabila.
src: who travelled frequently to AFC/M23-controlled territory from May 2025 and held meetings with senior AFC/M23 leadership.

r2-G-DOC-466-048.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in September 2025 the Military High Court of the DRC sentenced Mr. Kabila to death in absentia, including for treason and organizing an insurrection, accusing him of collaborating with AFC/M23.
r2-G-DOC-466-048.a: Military High Court of the DRC
r2-G-DOC-466-048.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 57 (two excerpts either side of a page break).
r2-G-DOC-466-048.vn: Exact; the two excerpts are one sentence split by a footnote marker. A sentence in absentia, as reported by the Group.
src: In September 2025, the Military High Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
sentenced Mr. Kabila to death in absentia, including for treason and organizing an insurrection, accusing him of collaborating with AFC/M23.

r2-G-DOC-466-049.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Moïse Nyarugabo, a former Congolese senator and key member of Mr. Kabila's inner circle, rose to increasing prominence within the movement; the Group said, citing its earlier reports (S/2021/560 and S/2025/446), that he was a key figure in MRDP/Twirwaneho without holding a formal position, and that he represented MRDP/Twirwaneho interests in high-level meetings with Mr. Kabila and AFC/M23 leadership.
r2-G-DOC-466-049.n: Cited as S/2026/466, para. 60 and annex 22. Spelling "Moïse" as printed. Annex 22 not read in full.
r2-G-DOC-466-049.vn: Exact. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: citations S/2021/560 and S/2025/446; represented MRDP/Twirwaneho in high-level meetings 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: Checked the retained PDF (para. 60): 'the movement' is AFC/M23 by context (paras. 58-59), and the MRDP/Twirwaneho role is sourced to earlier GoE reports, partly pre-window (2021). 'He' does refer to Nyarugabo. Attribution to the Group kept.; excerpt-support: added 1 excerpt(s): citations S/2021/560 and S/2025/446; represented MRDP/Twirwaneho in high-level meetings | cut the gloss '(AFC/M23, in the context of the paragraph)': the page says only 'the movement'
src: Moïse Nyarugabo – a former Congolese senator and key member of Mr. Kabila’s inner circle (see annex 22) – rose to increasing prominence within the movement.
He was a key figure in the Mouvement révolutionnaire pour la défense du peuple/ Twirwaneho (MRDP/Twirwaneho), without holding a formal position

He was a key figure in the Mouvement révolutionnaire pour la défense du peuple/ Twirwaneho (MRDP/Twirwaneho), without holding a formal position (see S/2021/560, annex 113; and S/2025/446, para. 177), and represented MRDP/Twirwaneho interests in high-level meetings with Mr. Kabila and AFC/M23 leadership.

r2-G-DOC-858-001.s: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a footnote, that United Nations and humanitarian actors reported the overall civilian death toll had surpassed 500 throughout Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms since April 2025, and that the Group could not independently establish verified casualty figures.
r2-G-DOC-858-001.l: Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms, Rutshuru territory
r2-G-DOC-858-001.x: UN and humanitarian actors via Group: over 500 civilian deaths in Bwito and Bwisha since April 2025 (not independently verified by the Group)
r2-G-DOC-858-001.n: Footnote 52 to para. 44. Complements the cited para. 38 figure (over 300 killed in Bwito alone). The footnote does not itself name the perpetrator; paras. 36-43 attribute the operations to RDF and AFC/M23.
r2-G-DOC-858-001.vn: Statement matches footnote; actor field narrowed because the footnote names no perpetrator. Hedge kept. Figure from UN and humanitarian actors; not verified by the Group.
src: United Nations and humanitarian actors reported that the overall civilian death toll has surpassed 500 throughout Bwito and Bwisha chiefdoms since April 2025. The Group could not independently establish verified casualty figures.

r2-G-DOC-858-002.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF and AFC/M23 launched coordinated operations in Bwito chiefdom, western Rutshuru, in late April and early May, targeting FDLR and allied forces of the CMC-FDP, including in and around Nyanzalé, Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo.
r2-G-DOC-858-002.l: Nyanzalé, Bukombo, Tongo, Bambo (Bwito chiefdom), Rutshuru
r2-G-DOC-858-002.vn: Supported; year removed from the statement because the excerpt does not print it (date field keeps 2025).
ent: Collectif des mouvements pour le changement/Forces de défense du peuple (CMC-FDP)
src: In Bwito chiefdom, western Rutshuru, RDF and AFC/M23 launched coordinated operations in late April and early May targeting FDLR and allied forces of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement/Forces de défense du peuple (CMC-FDP), including in and around Nyanzalé, Bukombo, Tongo and Bambo.

r2-G-DOC-858-003.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since mid-July 2025 RDF and AFC/M23 resumed military operations after significant redeployments, and that RDF forces conducted large-scale cordon-and-search operations in farmlands along the main road between Kiwanja and Ishasha while AFC/M23 established a security cordon restricting civilian movement.
r2-G-DOC-858-003.l: Farmlands between Kiwanja and Ishasha (Binza, Bwisha chiefdom), Rutshuru
r2-G-DOC-858-003.n: Para. 39. Killings in Binza 9-27 July are already recorded from para. 40.
src: Since mid-July 2025, RDF and AFC/M23 have resumed military operations following significant redeployments.

Large-scale cordonand-search operations were conducted by RDF forces in farmlands along the main road between Kiwanja and the border town of Ishasha. AFC/M23 forces established a security cordon around the area, restricting civilian movement in and out.

r2-G-DOC-858-004.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 27 May 2025 RDF and AFC/M23 attacked FDLR positions in Marangara, an FDLR stronghold, and that civilians were killed and houses set on fire during the clashes; and that on 28 May RDF and AFC/M23 accused inhabitants of Marangara, Lukara and Kirumba of hiding FDLR in their houses, after which, in retaliation, livestock and household items were looted and houses burnt, causing massive displacement.
r2-G-DOC-858-004.l: Marangara, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
r2-G-DOC-858-004.n: Annex 18 (para. 41), item (1). Number of civilians killed not given.
r2-G-DOC-858-004.vn: Narrowed: 'Tongo groupement, Rutshuru territory' and the NASA FIRMS/satellite corroboration are not in the stored excerpts; the accusation is attributed to RDF and AFC/M23 as the source does.
src: On 27 May 2025, RDF and AFC/M23 attacked FDLR positions in Marangara, an FDLR stronghold. Civilians were killed and houses set on fire during the clashes.

On 28 May, RDF and AFC/M23 accused inhabitants of Marangara, Lukara, and Kirumba of hiding FDLR in their houses. In retaliation, livestock and household items were looted, houses burnt, causing massive displacement.

r2-G-DOC-858-005.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 6 October 2025 fire was detected coinciding with attacks reported between Muliki and Kauma, Tongo groupement, with AFC/M23 attacks reported in both locations on 6 and 7 October 2025.
r2-G-DOC-858-005.l: Muliki and Kauma, Tongo groupement, Rutshuru
r2-G-DOC-858-005.n: Annex 18, item (2). Group notes FIRMS cannot determine cause; selection of incidents only.
r2-G-DOC-858-005.vn: Narrowed: 'Rutshuru territory' is not in the excerpt. Fire detection does not establish cause. Satellite fire detection coinciding with reported attacks; cause of fire not established.
src: On 6 October 2025, fire was detected at -1.07767 (latitude) 29.18622 (longitude), coinciding with attacks reported between Muliki and Kauma, Tongo groupement, with AFC/M23 attacks reported in both locations on 6 and 7 October 2025

r2-G-DOC-858-006.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that a fire detected on 19 October 2025 coincided with fires reported near Kamena, targeted by AFC/M23 attacks on the same day.
r2-G-DOC-858-006.n: Annex 18. Rutshuru territory is inferred from the surrounding annex text (Tongo groupement items), not stated for Kamena.
r2-G-DOC-858-006.vn: Matches annex 18 item. Satellite fire detection coinciding with reported attacks; cause of fire not established.
src: 19 October 2025, fire detected at -1.1976 (latitude) 29.20749 (longitude), coinciding with location of fires reported near Kamena, targeted by AFC/M23 attacks on the same day

r2-G-DOC-858-007.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that UNHCR in Uganda recorded the arrival of over 70,000 refugees between January and 21 September 2025, with a sharp increase in arrivals from Rutshuru territory since April, coinciding with the start of anti-FDLR operations.
r2-G-DOC-858-007.x: UNHCR via Group: over 70,000 refugee arrivals in Uganda, January to 21 September 2025
r2-G-DOC-858-007.n: Para. 42; annex 20 maps. Figure is for all arrivals in Uganda; the increase from Rutshuru is stated qualitatively.
r2-G-DOC-858-007.vn: Matches para. 42; UNHCR figure relayed by the Group.
src: The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Uganda reported the arrival of over 70,000 refugees between January and 21 September 2025, noting a sharp increase in refugee arrivals from Rutshuru territory recorded since April, coinciding with the start of anti-FDLR operations

r2-G-DOC-858-008.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that humanitarian actors, civil society and local leaders denounced the AFC/M23 practice of expelling civilians and subsequently denying access to their lands in the areas of the operations it described, leading to loss of livelihoods and a looming famine.
r2-G-DOC-858-008.vn: Narrowed: the excerpt says 'in these areas'; Bwito and Bwisha are not printed in it.
src: Humanitarian actors, civil society and local leaders denounced the AFC/M23 practice of expelling civilians and subsequently denying access to their lands in these areas, leading to loss of livelihoods and a looming famine

r2-G-DOC-858-009.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 had vacated Walikale in April 2025 owing to logistical constraints and diplomatic pressure, and that from late May AFC/M23, supported by RDF, prepared renewed offensives from Masisi towards Walikale.
r2-G-DOC-858-009.n: Para. 46 (footnote numbers 53 and 54 appear inside the quoted sentence). Complements existing April 2025 withdrawal coverage.
src: From late May 2025, AFC/M23, supported by RDF, 53 prepared renewed offensives from Masisi towards Walikale, which they had vacated in April 2025 54 due to logistical constraints and diplomatic pressure.

r2-G-DOC-858-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that from late May 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF deployed reinforcements into Masisi territory along the Masisi-Kashebere and Nyabiondo-Kashebere axes, at the boundary with Walikale territory, with the objective of taking Walikale centre.
r2-G-DOC-858-010.l: Masisi-Kashebere and Nyabiondo-Kashebere axes, Masisi/Walikale boundary
src: From late May 2025, AFC/M23 and RDF deployed reinforcements into Masisi territory along the Masisi–Kashebere and the Nyabiondo–Kashebere axes, at the boundary with Walikale territory, with the objective of taking Walikale centre.

r2-G-DOC-858-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that throughout June and July military activity intensified across Masisi and Walikale as AFC/M23 and RDF pushed westward and fortified key positions, while VDP/Wazalendo coalitions escalated harassment to delay advances, resulting in heavy clashes around Pinga and Mpeti and along the Masisi–Kashebere–Kibati axis.
r2-G-DOC-858-011.vn: Supported; year removed from statement (not printed in excerpt; date field keeps 2025).
src: Throughout June and July, military activity intensified across Masisi and Walikale as AFC/M23 and RDF pushed westward and fortified key positions, while VDP/Wazalendo coalitions escalated harassment to delay advances, resulting in heavy clashes around Pinga and Mpeti and along the Masisi–Kashebere–Kibati axis.

r2-G-DOC-858-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that by late September AFC/M23 and RDF operations had expanded on three fronts with the aim of encircling Pinga, and that clashes continued around Bibwe in October, with AFC/M23 and RDF capturing additional villages.
r2-G-DOC-858-012.n: Para. 48. Bibwe seizure in mid-September is already recorded.
r2-G-DOC-858-012.vn: Supported; adds October detail to r1-GOE-088 (mid-September Bibwe seizure). Year removed (not printed in excerpts).
src: By late September, AFC/M23 and RDF operations had expanded on three fronts, with the aim of encircling Pinga.
Clashes continued around Bibwe in October, with AFC/M23 and RDF capturing additional villages.

r2-G-DOC-858-015.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF progressively expanded and consolidated their presence in South Kivu, along various axes across Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Kalehe territories, and listed continued advances into Walungu and Shabunda in September and October, culminating in the capture of Nzibira, Luntukulu, Chulwe and Lubimbe.
r2-G-DOC-858-015.l: Nzibira, Luntukulu, Chulwe, Lubimbe, Walungu and Shabunda
r2-G-DOC-858-015.n: Para. 52 (the RP 503 words follow the page break and are omitted from the excerpt; the text names provincial route 503). The Nzibira capture on 21 September is already recorded from para. 56.
r2-G-DOC-858-015.vn: Narrowed: the bullet in S0 does not name the actor; actor now carried by the para. 51 sentence (S1). Year removed (not printed).
src: Continued advances into Walungu and Shabunda in September and October, culminating in the capture of Nzibira, Luntukulu, Chulwe, Lubimbe and positions
AFC/M23 and RDF progressively expanded and consolidated their presence in South Kivu, along various axes across Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira and Kalehe territories

r2-G-DOC-858-016.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since late April reinforcements had been documented in strategic locations such as Kamanyola, Katogota, Nyangezi, Luhwinja and Kaziba, including convoys that crossed the border with Rwanda, and that these deployments enabled AFC/M23 and RDF to maintain control over key transit hubs, including Kaziba, Katogota and the Tubimbi–Luhwinja corridor.
r2-G-DOC-858-016.n: Para. 52; annex 23 assesses these locations. Territory is indicative (places span Kabare, Walungu, Mwenga, Uvira territories).
r2-G-DOC-858-016.vn: Narrowed to the excerpts: 'South Kivu' and the year are not printed; S0 does not itself name whose reinforcements, so the AFC/M23-RDF link is carried by S1.
src: Since late-April, reinforcements have been documented in strategic locations such as Kamanyola, Katogota, Nyangezi, Luhwinja and Kaziba (see annex 23), including convoys that crossed the border with Rwanda
These deployments enabled AFC/M23 and RDF to maintain control over key transit hubs, including Kaziba, Katogota and the Tubimbi–Luhwinja corridor

r2-G-DOC-858-017.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain, and that the FARDC-Wazalendo-FDNB coalition continued to contest AFC/M23 and RDF advances on multiple fronts.
r2-G-DOC-858-017.a: FDNB, FARDC and Wazalendo (coalition) against AFC/M23 and RDF
r2-G-DOC-858-017.n: Para. 54. Burundian (FDNB) involvement in the Ruzizi plain as stated by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-858-017.vn: Both clauses are in the single excerpt (para. 54).
src: The FARDC–Wazalendo–FDNB coalition continued to contest the advances of AFC/M23 and RDF across multiple fronts. AFC/M23 advances towards Uvira were blocked by FDNB and FARDC positions defending the Ruzizi plain

r2-G-DOC-858-018.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 and RDF continued to provide military support, including troop reinforcements, to besieged MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux despite heavy pressure from FARDC, FDNB and Wazalendo forces, and that MRDP-Twirwaneho access routes and supply chains had collapsed.
r2-G-DOC-858-018.n: Para. 53; annex 25 map. Gakufe and Ndabagaza reinforcement movements are already recorded.
r2-G-DOC-858-018.vn: Para. 53: S0 (support to MRDP-Twirwaneho enclaves) and S1 (AFC/M23 and RDF assistance; collapsed supply chains).
src: continued to provide critical military support to besieged Mouvement des républicains pour la dignité des peuples (MRDP) Twirwaneho-controlled enclaves in the Hauts Plateaux (see annex 25), deploying troop reinforcements despite heavy pressure from FARDC, the Burundi National Defence Force (FDNB) and Wazalendo forces.

AFC/M23 and RDF assistance remained essential as MRDP-Twirwaneho’s access routes and supply chains aimed at Banyamulenge population centres have collapsed, and the area remained economically strangled and increasingly encircled.

r2-G-DOC-858-019.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 maintained control over the main 3T (tin, tantalum, tungsten) mining areas around Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory.
src: AFC/M23 maintained control over the main mining areas for “3T” minerals (tin, tantalum and tungsten) around Lumbishi, Numbi and Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory

r2-G-DOC-858-020.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 established de facto control over mining operations in the Luhihi area (Kabare territory) following its takeover in mid-February, replacing official State services with a local 'mining office' under its authority, and that the de facto authorities imposed a production tax of 30 per cent on the sale price of ore at pit level.
r2-G-DOC-858-020.x: Group: 30 per cent production tax at pit level
r2-G-DOC-858-020.n: Para. 60; Luhihi in Kabare territory per para. 58. Para. 59 notes well over 5,000 artisanal miners at the Lomera site in the first half of 2025.
r2-G-DOC-858-020.vn: Supported; year removed from statement (not printed in excerpts). Para. 60 follows the Luhihi/Lomera paragraph.
src: AFC/M23 established de facto control over mining operations in the area following its takeover in mid-February, replacing official State services with a local “mining office” operating under its authority. The de facto authorities imposed a production tax of 30 per cent on the sale price of ore at pit level.
province included three key gold mining operations: a large artisanal mining site in Luhihi, Kabare territory (see paras. 59–62 below)

r2-G-DOC-858-021.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 30 August AFC/M23 suspended mining activities in Lomera due to tensions with the mining community, and that local sources estimated well over 5,000 artisanal miners operated at Lomera during the first half of 2025.
r2-G-DOC-858-021.x: Local sources via Group: well over 5,000 artisanal miners in first half of 2025
r2-G-DOC-858-021.vn: Narrowed: '(Luhihi)' is not printed in the excerpts.
src: On 30 August, AFC/M23 suspended mining activities in Lomera due to tensions with the mining community
Local sources estimate that well over 5,000 artisanal miners operated at Lomera during the first half of 2025

r2-G-DOC-858-022.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 8 May 2025 AFC/M23 took over the industrial open-pit Twangiza gold mine, owned by Twangiza Mining SA, in Luhwindja chiefdom, Mwenga territory.
r2-G-DOC-858-022.n: Para. 63 (printed "open -pit"). Annex 29 cites an internal Twangiza Mining SA letter dated 8 May 2025 suspending activities.
src: On 8 May 2025, AFC/M23 took over the industrial open -pit gold mine in Luhwindja chiefdom, Mwenga territory, owned by Twangiza Mining SA.

r2-G-DOC-858-023.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 15 October 2025 at approximately 04:00 a.m. FARDC carried out an aerial strike on the Twangiza site targeting power-generation facilities, with no civilian casualties reported.
r2-G-DOC-858-023.n: Annex 31 (para. 65): the Group states the strikes aimed to prevent efforts to operationalize the mine. Group states photographs and satellite imagery triangulated the damage.
src: On 15 October 2025, FARDC carried out an aerial strike on the Twangiza site at approximately 04:00 a.m., targeting power-generation facilities.186 No civilian casualties were reported.

r2-G-DOC-858-024.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that a second series of FARDC strikes on Twangiza on 23 October 2025, at 01:03 am, destroyed two fuel-storage tanks and a portion of the processing plant, rendering industrial operations inoperable.
r2-G-DOC-858-024.n: Annex 31 (para. 65). The excerpt does not name FARDC; the preceding sentence in the annex does.
r2-G-DOC-858-024.vn: 'Rendering inoperable' was outside the stored excerpt; replacement quote extends S0 to the end of the sentence. FARDC carried by the annex 31 caption (S1).
src: A second series of strikes on 23 October 2025, at 01:03 am, destroyed two fuel-storage tanks and a portion of the processing plant
Annex 31 (para. 65) - FARDC airstrikes on Twangiza on 15 and 23 October 2025

r2-G-DOC-858-025.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Twangiza Mining SA publicly denounced the systematic looting and destruction of industrial and environmental assets by AFC/M23, alleging active RDF support; the Group also wrote that Reuters had reported the company's allegation that AFC/M23 looted at least 500 kilograms of bullion since seizing the mine in May. The Group dates that Reuters article 21 September 2025, but the Reuters URL in its own footnote is dated 2025-10-21.
r2-G-DOC-858-025.a: AFC/M23 (alleged by Twangiza Mining SA); RDF support alleged
r2-G-DOC-858-025.x: Twangiza Mining SA via Reuters: at least 500 kg of bullion
r2-G-DOC-858-025.n: Paras. 66; annex 32. Company allegation; the Group does not itself verify the 500 kg figure. Date is that of the Reuters article.
r2-G-DOC-858-025.vn: Company allegation and Reuters report relayed by the Group; attribution kept. Company allegation; the Group does not verify the 500 kg figure. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: S/2025/858 para. 66 and annex 32 carry both clauses. Discrepancy: annex 32 text says 'On 21 September 2025, Reuters published', while its footnote 188 URL ends '...since-may-company-says-2025-10-21'; the date is uncertain and the Reuters page itself is not among the sources.
src: Twangiza Mining SA publicly denounced the “systematic looting and destruction of industrial and environmental assets” by AFC/M23, alleging “active support” from RDF.

On 21 September 2025, Reuters published an article reporting on allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA, accusing AFC/M23 of having looted at least 500 kilograms of bullion since seizing the mine in May

r2-G-DOC-858-026.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 23 October AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied the allegations made by Twangiza Mining SA, claiming that the mine was inactive, with only artisanal miners present, and that AFC/M23 lacked the necessary expertise and resources to operate gold mines; and that AFC/M23 published a communiqué on 27 October 2025 denying the accusations.
r2-G-DOC-858-026.n: Para. 66 and annex 32; the two dates (23 and 27 October) are as printed. Speaker as relayed by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-858-026.vn: Replacement quote extends S0 back to the preceding sentence so the company name is printed; year of the 23 October denial not printed, removed.
src: On 23 October, AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa publicly denied the allegations, claiming that the mine was inactive, with only artisanal miners present, and that AFC/M23 lacked the necessary expertise and resources to operate gold mines
In response, AFC/M23 published a communiqué on 27 October 2025, denying the accusations

r2-G-DOC-858-027.s: The UN Group of Experts conservatively estimated that between 6,000 and 7,000 RDF personnel remained deployed across North and South Kivu at the time of drafting, comprising at least two brigades and two special forces battalions.
r2-G-DOC-858-027.x: Group of Experts: 6,000-7,000 RDF personnel; at least two brigades and two special forces battalions
r2-G-DOC-858-027.n: Para. 68. Report covers investigations up to 10 November 2025 (para. 6). Province field set to North Kivu; the figure covers both provinces. Rwanda disputes RDF presence; no Rwandan response is recorded in this document.
src: At the time of drafting, the Group conservatively estimated that between 6,000 and 7,000 RDF personnel remained deployed across North and South Kivu, comprising at least two brigades and two special forces battalions.

r2-G-DOC-858-028.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu.
src: RDF had established a base on Idjwi island, which was often used for troop deployments and rotations via Lake Kivu.

r2-G-DOC-858-029.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 sources, including a senior commander participating in joint operations, confirmed that RDF elements, referred to as the 'Friendly Force', 'manage the front lines' and 'control M23 combatants'.
r2-G-DOC-858-029.l: North and South Kivu front lines
r2-G-DOC-858-029.vn: Matches para. 70; anonymous AFC/M23 sources as relayed by the Group.
src: AFC/M23 sources, including an AFC/M23 senior commander currently participating in joint AFC/M23 and RDF operations, confirmed that RDF elements, referred to as the “Friendly Force”, “manage the front lines” and “control M23 combatants”.

r2-G-DOC-858-030.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Guidon Shimiray Mwissa (CDi.033), leader of NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati, Walikale territory, to contain RDF and AFC/M23 advancement along the Walikale-Kibua-Kashebere-Masisi axis.
r2-G-DOC-858-030.n: Para. 74. Excerpt ends at "Walikale territory"; the purpose clause is cited in the second source.
r2-G-DOC-858-030.vn: S0 and S1 are the same sentence of para. 74.
src: Guidon Shimiray Mwissa (CDi.033), leader of NDC-R and VDP commander, moved his headquarters from Pinga to Kibati, Walikale territory
to contain RDF and AFC/M23 advancement along the Walikale Kibua-Kashebere-Masisi axis

r2-G-DOC-858-031.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and his troops were based in Lukweti, Masisi territory, while CMC-FDP, led by Dominique Ndaruhutse, was in Virunga National Park fighting in areas including Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo and Kalengera in Rutshuru territory.
src: APCLS leader Janvier Karairi Boingo and his troops were based in Lukweti, Masisi territory, while CMC-FDP, led by Dominique Ndaruhutse, was in Virunga National Park, engaging in fighting in areas that included Katsiru, Rwindi, Bukombo, Bambo, Tongo and Kalengera, in Rutshuru territory.

r2-G-DOC-858-032.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 30 September 2025 VDP/Wazalendo leaders and government authorities met in Kinshasa to redefine counter-offensive strategies and cooperation, that sources privy to the discussions reported the Government agreed to continue providing financial and logistical support to VDP/Wazalendo, and that the Government continued to provide $300,000 monthly to VDP/Wazalendo through the office of the governor of North Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-858-032.x: Group, citing sources: $300,000 monthly to VDP/Wazalendo via the office of the North Kivu governor
r2-G-DOC-858-032.n: Para. 75. Anonymous sources; meeting held in Kinshasa (outside phase-1 geography, recorded for its bearing on North Kivu operations). No Government statement on this meeting recorded in the document.
r2-G-DOC-858-032.vn: Separated the sources' report from the Group's own statement on the $300,000 monthly payment, as the excerpt does.
src: On 30 September 2025, VDP/Wazalendo leaders and government authorities met in Kinshasa to redefine counter-offensive strategies and cooperation

Sources privy to the discussions reported that the Government agreed to continue providing financial and logistical support to VDP/Wazalendo. The Government continued to provide $300,000 monthly to VDP/Wazalendo through the office of the governor of North Kivu.

r2-G-DOC-858-033.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that FARDC Colonel Sekololo, based in Walikale, still acted as the liaison between FARDC and VDP, and that regular FARDC helicopter rotations to VDP/Wazalendo-held front lines in Walikale delivered uniforms, weapons, ammunition and food supplies.
src: FARDC Colonel Sekololo, based in Walikale, still acted as the liaison between FARDC and VDP
Regular FARDC helicopter rotations to various VDP/Wazalendo -held front lines in Walikale delivered uniforms, weapons and ammunition, and food supplies.

r2-G-DOC-858-034.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the contract of Congo Aviation, formerly Agemira, was abruptly terminated at the end of July, following accusations of responsibility for the fall of Goma and Bukavu, and that the Congo Aviation CH-4 drone pilots, identified as Algerian nationals, have been contracted directly by the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
r2-G-DOC-858-034.a: Congo Aviation / Government of the DRC
r2-G-DOC-858-034.vn: Narrowed: 'private military company' and the year are not in the stored excerpts.
src: The contract of Congo Aviation, formerly Agemira (S/2023/431, annex 23), was abruptly terminated at the end of July, following accusations of responsibility for the fall of Goma and Bukavu
Congo Aviation’s CH-4 drone pilots, identified as Algerian nationals, have been contracted directly by the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

r2-G-DOC-858-035.s: The UN Group of Experts reproduced, in an annex, statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in all DRC conflict-affected provinces showing AFC/M23 as the actor responsible for most of the violations in August 2025 (35,6%), surpassing ADF, CODECO and Wazalendo groups; a reduction in AFC/M23 violations in September 2025 (9,47%), surpassed by ADF (36,09%), CODECO (16,57%) and FARDC (10,65%); and an increase in M23-attributed killings in October 2025 (to 19,8%).
r2-G-DOC-858-035.x: UN source via Group: Aug 2025 AFC/M23 35,6%; Sept AFC/M23 9,47%, ADF 36,09%, CODECO 16,57%, FARDC 10,65%; Oct AFC/M23 19,8%
r2-G-DOC-858-035.n: Annex 37 (para. 80). National (not Kivu-only) UN statistics, decimal commas as printed. The Group links the September drop to lower-intensity anti-FDLR operations in Rutshuru and RDF redeployment.
r2-G-DOC-858-035.vn: Narrowed: the stored excerpts (annex captions) do not name the UN as the statistics' source; national, not Kivu-only, figures. National figures for all conflict-affected provinces, as printed with decimal commas.
src: Statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in August 2025, in all DRC conflict-affected provinces – showing AFC/M23 as the actor responsible for most of the violations (35,6%), surpassing ADF, CODECO and Wazalendo groups.

Statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in September 2025, in all DRC conflict-affected provinces – showing a reduction in AFC/M23 violations (9,47%), surpassed by ADF (36,09%), CODECO (16,57%) and FARDC (10,65%).

Statistics on extrajudicial or summary executions by perpetrators in October 2025, in all DRC conflict-affected provinces – showing an increase in M23-attributed killings (to 19,8%) compared to September.

r2-G-DOC-858-036.s: The UN Group of Experts reported, in a paragraph on abuses by VDP/Wazalendo groups, that Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains combatants have been implicated most frequently in serious abuses against civilians, such as abductions, lootings, rape, unlawful killings and arson.
r2-G-DOC-858-036.l: not specified in the source (para. 81 follows the North Kivu discussion)
r2-G-DOC-858-036.a: Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains (Wazalendo group)
r2-G-DOC-858-036.n: Para. 81. No place, date or victim count given; the sentence does not state the province. Footnote 102 lists UN, civil society and humanitarian sources. Sexual violence element is a general finding, no individual incidents.
r2-G-DOC-858-036.vn: Replacement quote extends the excerpt to the whole of para. 81 so the VDP/Wazalendo context is printed. No place, date or count given.
ent: Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains
src: Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains combatants have been implicated most frequently in serious abuses against civilians, such as abductions, lootings, rape, unlawful killings and arson.

r2-G-DOC-858-037.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo groups also engaged in retaliatory attacks, including summary executions or targeted assassinations of individuals accused of collusion with AFC/M23, albeit on a much smaller scale than the recent systematic violations perpetrated by AFC/M23 and RDF.

AFC/M23 and RDF' clause; the full sentence (with footnote marker 101) is added.
src: VDP/Wazalendo groups also engaged in retaliatory attacks, including summary executions or targeted assassinations of individuals accused of collusion with AFC/M23,

VDP/Wazalendo groups also engaged in retaliatory attacks, including summary executions or targeted assassinations of individuals accused of collusion with AFC/M23, 101 albeit on a much smaller scale than the recent systematic violations perpetrated by AFC/M23 and RDF (see paras. 36–43 above).

r2-G-DOC-858-038.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in early September competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika, which forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers.
r2-G-DOC-858-038.a: Mai Mai Corbeau; Mai Mai Malaika (Wazalendo); FARDC
r2-G-DOC-858-038.vn: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt).
src: In early September, competition over the control of roadblocks in Mwenga sparked violence among Wazalendo groups, notably Mai Mai Corbeau and Mai Mai Malaika. This forced the FARDC to intervene to dismantle the growing number of barriers.

r2-G-DOC-858-039.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that, according to witnesses it interviewed, Wazalendo groups established an ever-increasing number of roadblocks in and around Uvira, including along major and secondary roads; that Wazalendo imposed taxes ranging from 5,000 to 50,000 Congolese francs on road users, traders and citizens; and that between March and September at least 10 roadblocks were identified on the Misisi-Lulimba axis.
r2-G-DOC-858-039.x: Group: taxes 5,000-50,000 CDF; at least 10 roadblocks on Misisi-Lulimba
r2-G-DOC-858-039.n: Annex 38. The Uvira-Luvungi RN5 count (12 roadblocks) is already recorded. "at least10" as printed.
r2-G-DOC-858-039.vn: 'In and around Uvira' was outside the stored excerpt; replacement quote extends S0 to the preceding sentence (annex 38). Roadblock count kept as printed.
src: Wazalendo imposed lucrative taxes ranging from 5,000 to 50,000 Congolese francs for road users, traders and citizens.
For example, between March and September, on the Misisi-Lulimba axis, at least10 roadblocks were identified.

r2-G-DOC-858-040.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 26 May AFC/M23 carried out a cordon-and-search operation in a locality in Walikale, near the Rutshuru border, during which approximately 80 young men suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo factions were apprehended, and that they were reportedly transferred by force to the Rusamambo axis two days later, dressed in AFC/M23 uniforms, and deployed to the frontlines to serve as human shields.
r2-G-DOC-858-040.l: Locality in Walikale near the Rutshuru border; Rusamambo axis
r2-G-DOC-858-040.n: Annex 8 (para. 22). "Reportedly" is the Group's wording for the transfer and human-shield use. Locality unnamed.
r2-G-DOC-858-040.vn: Supported; 'reportedly' kept; year removed (not printed in excerpts).
src: For example, on 26 May, AFC/M23 carried out a cordon-and-search operation in a locality in Walikale, near the Rutshuru border, during which approximately 80 young men suspected of affiliation with Wazalendo factions were apprehended.
These individuals were reportedly transferred by force to the Rusamambo axis two days later, dressed in AFC/M23 uniforms, and deployed to the frontlines to serve as human shields.

r2-G-DOC-858-041.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July the Congolese Minister for Human Rights, Chantal Chambu, denounced that more than 300 young men, including minors, had been captured in Rubaya without any valid legal justification and taken to an unknown destination, and that local sources, civil society and eyewitnesses confirmed the incident.
r2-G-DOC-858-041.x: Minister via Group: more than 300 young men including minors
r2-G-DOC-858-041.n: Annex 8 (para. 22). The excerpt does not name the captors; annex 8 is about AFC/M23 recruitment, and Rubaya was AFC/M23-held. Verifier should confirm attribution wording. Minister statement relayed by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-858-041.vn: The excerpt does not name the captors; actor narrowed to 'not attributed in the excerpt'. Year removed (not printed).
src: On 3 July, the Congolese Minister for Human Rights, Chantal Chambu, denounced that more than 300 young men, including minors, have been captured in Rubaya without any valid legal justification and taken to an unknown destination. 114 Local sources, civil society and eyewitnesses have confirmed the incident.

r2-G-DOC-858-042.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that two individuals abducted by AFC/M23 with a group of 35 young men in April 2025 escaped and testified in June; they described hunger, untreated illnesses and physical abuse including torture among trainees at Rumangabo, and said 13 individuals in their group had been executed.
r2-G-DOC-858-042.x: Escapees via Group: group of 35 abducted; 13 executed
r2-G-DOC-858-042.n: Annex 8 (para. 22). Escapee testimony; executions not independently verified in the excerpt.
r2-G-DOC-858-042.vn: Escapee testimony relayed by the Group; both excerpts match. Escapee testimony; executions not independently verified in the excerpt.
src: In one instance, two individuals who were abducted by AFC/M23 with a group of 35 young men in April 2025 managed to escape and provide testimony in June.

The two escapees described that trainees at Rumangabo were kept in difficult conditions marked by hunger, untreated illnesses, and physical abuse, including torture. They also indicated that 13 individuals in their group had been executed.

r2-G-DOC-858-043.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that it interviewed victims of arrest who had witnessed torture, inhumane treatment, including detainees stripped naked and held without food and water, and summary executions in detention centres in Goma.
r2-G-DOC-858-043.a: not attributed to a named unit in the sentence (preceding sentences discuss M23/PRC operations in Goma and Bukavu)
r2-G-DOC-858-043.n: Para. 28. Footnote 30 lists UN sources, researchers, civil society, A/HRC/60/80 and an Amnesty report. The sentence follows the discussion of M23/PRC arbitrary detentions; the Group does not name the detaining unit in this sentence.
r2-G-DOC-858-043.vn: Matches para. 28; detaining unit not named.
src: The Group interviewed victims of arrest who had witnessed torture, inhumane treatment – including detainees stripped naked and held without food and water – and summary executions in detention centres in Goma.

r2-G-DOC-858-044.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the newly established M23/PRC continued to conduct large-scale operations in Goma and Bukavu, resulting in arbitrary detentions and the forcible conscription of boys and men.
r2-G-DOC-858-044.n: Para. 28; the two quoted fragments are consecutive in the report but split by a page break and footnotes. Period runs from 24 August 2025 (unveiling) to report cut-off.
r2-G-DOC-858-044.vn: Narrowed to the excerpt wording ('resulting in', not 'responsible for'); 'AFC/M23 police force' label not printed in the excerpts.
src: The newly established M23/PRC continued to conduct large-scale operations in Goma and Bukavu
resulting in arbitrary detentions and the forcible conscription of boys and men.

r2-G-DOC-858-046.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 continued the recruitment and training of its 'local defence' forces, tasked with maintaining security in towns and villages controlled by AFC/M23, and that these forces were frequently implicated in clashes with FDLR and Wazalendo combatants and in human rights abuses; it annexed an announcement on the graduation of 242 Local Defense Personnel in Nyiragongo, dated 23 September 2025.
r2-G-DOC-858-046.n: Para. 26; annex 10. Date refers to the graduation announcement; the abuses are undated.
r2-G-DOC-858-046.vn: The 23 September 2025 date belongs to the annexed announcement caption; worded as such rather than as the graduation date.
