src: AFC/M23 also continued the recruitment and training of its “local defence” forces, tasked with maintaining security in towns and villages controlled by AFC/M23
However, these forces were frequently implicated in clashes with FDLR and Wazalendo combatants and in human rights abuses.
Announcement on the graduation of 242 Local Defense Personnel in Nyiragongo, 23 September 2025

r2-G-DOC-858-048.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 September FARDC's 3rd Defense Zone command reported that it received 30 alleged AFC/M23-ARC combatants, including two minors, who surrendered voluntarily to the FARDC, while 15 others were captured during clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-858-048.x: FARDC via Group: 30 surrendered (including two minors); 15 captured
r2-G-DOC-858-048.n: Annex 9. FARDC claim relayed by the Group; not verified by it.
r2-G-DOC-858-048.vn: FARDC claim relayed by the Group; year removed (not printed).
src: On 24 September, FARDC’s 3rd Defense Zone command reported that it received 30 alleged AFC/M23-ARC combatants, including two minors, who surrendered voluntarily to the FARDC, while 15 others were captured during clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu.

r2-G-DOC-858-049.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 24 February AFC/M23 forces issued an ultimatum to residents of Karenga, who had returned to Karenga after the dismantling of IDP camps around Goma in early February, to leave by the next day or be shot.
r2-G-DOC-858-049.n: Annex 39 (para. 86). Karenga is placed in Masisi territory in annex 40. Residents then sought refuge in collective shelters in Sake.
r2-G-DOC-858-049.vn: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt).
src: On 24 February, AFC/M23 forces had issued an ultimatum to residents of Karenga – who had returned to Karenga after the dismantling of IDP camps around Goma, in early February – to leave by the next day, or be shot.

r2-G-DOC-858-050.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in Sake, prior to transferring the refugees to Goma, AFC/M23 screened them, separating women and children from men, amid reports of physical violence, and that at least 180 men accused of FDLR affiliation were separated and brought to Stade de l’Unité in Goma, from where they were taken to an unknown location and their whereabouts remain unknown.
r2-G-DOC-858-050.l: Sake and Stade de l’Unité, Goma
r2-G-DOC-858-050.n: Annex 39. Date approximate: the roundup was 12 May; the separation date is not stated. Disappeared-persons lead for investigators.
r2-G-DOC-858-050.vn: Wording aligned with the excerpt ('refugees', as the Group writes). Adds the 180-men detail to r1-GOE-092 (12 May roundup).
src: In Sake, prior to transferring the refugees to Goma, AFC/M23 screened the refugees, separating women and children from men, among reports of physical violence. At least 180 men accused of FDLR affiliation were separated and brought to Stade de l’Unité in Goma. From there, they were taken to an unknown location and their whereabouts remain unknown.

r2-G-DOC-858-051.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that at least 72 Congolese nationals transferred to Rwanda were returned to the DRC after successfully demonstrating their Congolese citizenship, while other Congolese citizens were unlawfully deported to Rwanda without having been given the opportunity to prove their citizenship.
r2-G-DOC-858-051.n: Annex 39. The excerpt does not name the actor; the surrounding annex attributes the transfers to AFC/M23 in coordination with Rwandan authorities. Verifier may narrow actor.
r2-G-DOC-858-051.vn: Statement supported; actor field narrowed because the excerpt names no actor.
src: At least 72 Congolese nationals transferred to Rwanda were returned to the DRC after successfully demonstrating their Congolese citizenship. However, other Congolese citizens were unlawfully deported to Rwanda, without having been given the opportunity to prove their citizenship.

r2-G-DOC-858-052.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 17 May Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”
r2-G-DOC-858-052.n: Annex 39. Statement as relayed by the Group (footnote 223); original post not checked.
r2-G-DOC-858-052.vn: Narrowed: year and 'from Goma' are not printed in the excerpt. Quoted language is the minister's, as relayed by the Group.
src: On 17 May, Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”

r2-G-DOC-858-053.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka echoed, shortly thereafter, the statement by Rwanda's foreign minister that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”
r2-G-DOC-858-053.n: Annex 39. "This statement" refers to the Nduhungirehe statement in the preceding sentence. Wording of Kanyuka's statement is not reproduced.
r2-G-DOC-858-053.vn: Replacement quote extends S0 back to the start of the minister's sentence so 'Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs' is printed. Kanyuka's own wording not reproduced by the Group.
src: stated that the transferred individuals were “previously held hostages by the FDLR genocidal force.”223 AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka echoed this statement shortly thereafter.

r2-G-DOC-858-054.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that since January 2025 at least 5,798 individuals were repatriated to Rwanda, primarily from Masisi territory but also from Rutshuru territory, and that a confidential source with direct knowledge of repatriation operations referred to recent repatriations, including the repatriation of 227 Rwandan refugees on 23 October, primarily Hutu women and children from Masisi and Rutshuru territories.
r2-G-DOC-858-054.x: Group: 5,798 repatriated since January 2025; 227 on 23 October
r2-G-DOC-858-054.n: Annex 39. The same sentence (a confidential source) reports continued AFC/M23 pressure on those returning; not asserted here.
r2-G-DOC-858-054.vn: The 227 figure comes from a confidential source cited by the Group; attribution added via replacement quote. Year of 23 October not printed, removed.
src: Since January 2025, at least 5,798 individuals were repatriated to Rwanda, primarily from Masisi territory, but also from Rutshuru territory.
including the repatriation of 227 Rwandan refugees on 23 October, primarily Hutu women and children from Masisi and Rutshuru territories

r2-G-DOC-858-055.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in May and June 2025 the Congolese government accused AFC/M23 and Rwanda of ethnic cleansing by resettling “Rwandan families” with Rwandan identity cards in eastern DRC, and annexed an official communiqué by the DRC Minister of Interior of 14 May 2025 accusing Rwanda of orchestrating an ethnic cleansing and repopulation operation.
r2-G-DOC-858-055.n: Annex 40 (para. 88). DRC accusation reported by the Group; the Group notes the returnee origins cannot be determined without UNHCR oversight. No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply to these communiqués is recorded in the document.
r2-G-DOC-858-055.vn: Garbled clause rewritten to the caption's wording. Government accusation as relayed by the Group; 'ethnic cleansing' is the government's term, attributed. 'Ethnic cleansing' is the DRC government's accusation, not a finding.
src: In May and June 2025, the Congolese government accused AFC/M23 and Rwanda of ethnic cleansing by resettling “Rwandan families” with Rwandan identity cards in eastern DRC
Official communique by DRC Minister of Interior of 14 May 2025, accusing Rwanda of orchestrating an ethnic cleansing and repopulation operation

r2-G-DOC-858-056.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 16 June AFC/M23 appointed Jean-Damascène Mwigimba as provincial director for its own iteration of the Commission Nationale pour les Réfugiés (CNR), overseeing cross-border refugee movements.
r2-G-DOC-858-056.n: Annex 13 (para. 31); also annexes 39 and 40. The UNHCR-office threat is cited elsewhere (existing claim on Chantal Murekatete Kayitaba).
r2-G-DOC-858-056.vn: Narrowed: the UNHCR-office threat and the year are not in the stored excerpt.
src: On 16 June, AFC/M23 appointed Jean-Damascène Mwigimba as provincial director for its own iteration of the Commission Nationale pour les Réfugiés (CNR), overseeing cross-border refugee movements

r2-G-DOC-858-057.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that local sources confirmed AFC/M23 began in July 2025 to build a centre in Karenga, Masisi territory, including a transit site, a school and a health centre.
r2-G-DOC-858-057.n: Annex 40. Karenga is the area from which residents were expelled in February (see annex 39 claim). The annex adds that the facilities were meant for returning Congolese refugees and that UNHCR was not involved; not asserted here.
r2-G-DOC-858-057.vn: Matches annex 40; local sources as relayed by the Group.
src: Local sources confirmed that in July 2025, AFC/M23 begun the construction of such a centre in Karenga, Masisi territory – the area affected by the forced expulsions documented in February (see para.) – including a transit site, a school, and a health centre.

r2-G-DOC-858-058.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 9 October AFC/M23 installed Bashali Luanda Jaques on the throne of the Bashali chefferie during a ceremony in Kitchanga, in contravention of traditional succession procedures and despite objections from the Bashali royal family representing the legitimate Mwami, Bashali N'siyi Minihire Roger.
r2-G-DOC-858-058.n: Annex 12 (para. 30). The Group describes the appointment as unlawful.
r2-G-DOC-858-058.vn: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpt). Names as printed.
src: On 9 October, AFC/M23 installed Bashali Luanda Jaques on the throne of the Bashali chefferie during a ceremony in Kitchanga, in contravention of traditional succession procedures and despite objections from the Bashali royal family representing the legitimate Mwami, Bashali N’siyi Minihire Roger.

r2-G-DOC-858-059.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23 converted villages into towns or communes, including in Sake, Ngungu, Rubaya and Bweremana in Masisi territory, abolishing all customary rights, and that in August AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto announced plans to subdivide Goma into four communes instead of the existing two.
r2-G-DOC-858-059.n: Annex 13 (para. 31). Conversion date not stated; August date is for the Goma announcement.
r2-G-DOC-858-059.vn: Supported; year removed (not printed in excerpts).
src: AFC/M23 initiated the transformation of several entities previously governed under customary law into administrative entities through the conversion of villages into towns or communes, including in Sake, Ngungu, Rubaya and Bweremana, in Masisi territory,130 abolishing all customary rights.
In August, AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto announced plans to subdivide Goma into four communes instead of the existing two.

r2-G-DOC-858-060.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 19 June AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto authorized the resumption of operations within the land registry and property title divisions in North Kivu, and that on 25 July Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, AFC/M23-appointed governor of South Kivu, issued land management laws, including new procedures for obtaining building permits and cadastral documents.
r2-G-DOC-858-060.n: Annex 13. Two decisions (19 June and 25 July) in one claim; the Group says they interfere with land administration. Annex 14 says the former South Kivu governor Birato Rwihimba was reassigned in June to an investment department, which is in tension with the 25 July "governor" label; as printed in the document.
r2-G-DOC-858-060.vn: Supported; years removed (not printed in excerpts). Elsewhere the report says Birato Rwihimba was reassigned in June; the 'governor' label for 25 July is as printed.
src: On 19 June, AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor Bahati Erasto authorized the resumption of operations within the land registry and property title divisions in North Kivu.
On 25 July, Emmanuel Birato Rwihimba, AFC/M23-appointed governor of South Kivu issued land management laws, including new procedures for obtaining building permits and cadastral documents.

r2-G-DOC-858-061.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 29 May 2025 AFC/M23 announced an arbitration court for local conflicts in Goma, that on 12 August it created a 25-member Commission pour la Restauration de la Justice presided by Delion Kimbulungu Mutangala, and that on 3 November the commission announced 378 successful magistrate candidates.
r2-G-DOC-858-061.n: Annex 15 (para. 33). Third excerpt is short by necessity; the 3 November date is in the preceding sentence of the annex.
r2-G-DOC-858-061.vn: Four excerpts carry the four clauses.
ent: Commission pour la Restauration de la Justice (CRJ)
src: On 29 May, AFC/M23 announced the creation of an arbitration court for local conflicts in Goma.
On 12 August, AFC/M23 created a 25-member Commission pour la Restauration de la Justice (CRJ), presided by Delion Kimbulungu Mutangala
On 3 November 2025, the CRJ announced the results of the recruitment process for magistrates held in Goma on 14 September 2025.
The results of the recruitment process, listing 378 successful candidates, are on file with the Secretariat.

r2-G-DOC-858-062.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government declared it would invalidate all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 in violation of the country’s constitutional order, and annexed a statement of the DRC Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature, dated 12 September 2025, declaring all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 a violation of the constitutional order of the DRC.
r2-G-DOC-858-062.a: Government of the DRC; Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature
r2-G-DOC-858-062.n: Para. 33; annex 16 (document provided by a DRC Government source).
r2-G-DOC-858-062.vn: Garbled sentence repaired to the excerpt wording.
src: The Government declared that it would invalidate all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 in violation of the country’s constitutional order
Annex 16 (para. 33) - DRC Conseil Supérieur de la Magistrature statement declaring all judicial acts undertaken by AFC/M23 as violation of the DRC’s constitutional order, 12 September 2025

r2-G-DOC-858-063.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Rwanda was signed in Washington, D.C. on 27 June 2025, brokered by the United States of America in consultation with Qatar and Togo (as African Union mediator).
r2-G-DOC-858-063.a: Governments of the DRC and Rwanda; United States, Qatar, Togo (mediators)
r2-G-DOC-858-063.n: Para. 7. Recorded as political context for the Kivu conflict.
src: culminated on 27 June 2025 in the signing of the Peace Agreement between the Democratic Republic of the Congo and the Republic of Rwanda in Washington, D.C., brokered by the United States of America in consultation with Qatar and Togo (as African Union mediator).

r2-G-DOC-858-064.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that on 3 July Benjamin Mbonimpa, head of the AFC/M23 delegation in Doha, and Freddy Rukema Kanyiki, AFC/M23's deputy coordinator, reiterated the need for the DRC Government to agree to several trust-building measures, and that the Doha Declaration of Principles, brokered by Qatar, was signed by the DRC Government and AFC/M23 on 19 July 2025 and welcomed by the Government of Rwanda.
r2-G-DOC-858-064.a: Government of the DRC; AFC/M23; Qatar (mediator)
r2-G-DOC-858-064.vn: Narrowed to excerpt wording (measures the DRC Government was asked to agree to).
src: on 3 July, Benjamin Mbonimpa, the head of AFC/M23 delegation in Doha, and Freddy Rukema Kanyiki, AFC/M23’s deputy coordinator, reiterated the need for the DRC Government to agree to several trust-building measures
the Doha Declaration of Principles, brokered by Qatar, was signed by the DRC Government and AFC/M23 on 19 July 2025, and welcomed by the Government of Rwanda.

r2-G-DOC-858-065.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the parties maintained active engagement in Doha and on 18 September signed a formal prisoner exchange agreement as part of confidence-building measures, and that on 14 October both sides concluded an agreement establishing a ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism.
r2-G-DOC-858-065.n: Para. 11; annex 5. The parties are named in the preceding sentence of para. 11 (talks stalled; "the parties maintained active engagement in Doha"). Location Doha inferred from that sentence.
r2-G-DOC-858-065.vn: Supported; year removed (not printed). The parties are the DRC Government and AFC/M23 per the preceding text, not printed in the excerpt.
src: the parties maintained active engagement in Doha and, on 18 September, they signed a formal prisoner exchange agreement as part of confidence-building measures.
On 14 October, both sides concluded an agreement establishing a ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism

r2-G-DOC-858-066.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in July 2025 Benjamin Mbonimpa, AFC/M23 permanent secretary and chief negotiator at Doha, stated that AFC/M23 was proposing federalism as a form of governance.
r2-G-DOC-858-066.n: Para. 20 (footnote cites a post on X). As relayed by the Group.
r2-G-DOC-858-066.vn: Matches para. 20; statement as relayed by the Group.
src: In July 2025, Benjamin Mbonimpa, the permanent secretary and chief negotiator of AFC/M23 at Doha, stated that AFC/M23 was proposing federalism as a form of governance.

r2-G-DOC-858-067.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expected AFC/M23 to withdraw and accept cantonment, while AFC/M23 leaders insisted on maintaining control of current positions and seeking integration into State structures.
r2-G-DOC-858-067.n: Para. 16. Group characterisation of the parties' positions; dates approximate.
r2-G-DOC-858-067.vn: Narrowed: 'under the Doha Declaration' is not in the excerpt. Group's characterisation of the parties' positions.
src: The Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo expected AFC/M23 to withdraw and accept cantonment, while AFC/M23 leaders insisted on maintaining control of current positions and seeking integration into State structures.

r2-G-DOC-858-068.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that in a letter addressed to the US President, as facilitator of the Washington peace process, the FDLR leadership alleged that the FDLR's assigned mission consisted of protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC, and expressed concern that the neutralisation plan was being implemented in an indiscriminate manner, potentially targeting civilians.
r2-G-DOC-858-068.n: Annex 7 (para. 15). The 2 July date is from the annex caption "FDLR letter of 2 July 2025 addressed to the President of the United States"; not in the excerpt - verifier may narrow date to 2025-07.
r2-G-DOC-858-068.vn: The 2 July date is only in the annex caption, not the stored excerpt: date narrowed to 2025 (approximate). 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: QA 0.4 (A4): the date is a year only (2025), so approximate in the edition vocabulary (day, approximate, month, range); precision was day
src: In a letter addressed to the US President, acting as facilitator of the Washington peace process, the FDLR leadership alleged that the FDLR’s assigned mission consisted of protecting the Rwandese refugee community in the DRC. They expressed concern that the neutralisation plan was being implemented in an indiscriminate manner, potentially targeting civilians.

r2-G-DOC-858-069.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that VDP/Wazalendo spokesperson Jules Mulumba called for the recognition of the VDP/Wazalendo as legitimate stakeholders and requested their inclusion in peace negotiations, and stated that they rejected any agreements from Doha that did not consider their demands.
r2-G-DOC-858-069.n: Annex 7. Dates from the annex caption "Letters of 9 and 14 November 2025, signed by Jules Mulumba"; not in the excerpt.
r2-G-DOC-858-069.vn: The 9 and 14 November dates are only in the annex caption, not the stored excerpt: date narrowed to 2025 (approximate).
src: VDP/Wazalendo spokesperson Jules Mulumba called for the recognition of the VDP/Wazalendo as legitimate stakeholders and requested their inclusion in peace negotiations. He stated that the VDP-Wazalendo rejected any agreements from Doha that did not consider their demands

r2-G-DOC-HRC-001.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 members committed retaliatory killings immediately after seizing localities, and that several civilians were summarily executed in Minova, South Kivu, in January immediately after M23 took control.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-001.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 30. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Territory (Kalehe) is the compiler's administrative placement; the report names only Minova, South Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-001.vn: Para. 30 says exactly this; Kalehe is the compiler's placement of Minova (correct administratively).
src: M23 members committed retaliatory killings immediately after seizing localities, targeting civilians– primarily men – suspected of collaborating with Government forces. For example, several civilians were summarily executed in Minova, South Kivu, in January immediately after M23 took control.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-002.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in June and July M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories (South Kivu), as apparent collective punishment.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-002.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 30. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
src: In June and July, M23 summarily executed dozens of individuals following confrontations with Government forces in Walungu and Kabare territories (South Kivu), as apparent collective punishment.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-003.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that from 8 to 29 July M23 members, accompanied by civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers, attacked several farms in Bishwa chefferie in Rutshuru and allegedly executed hundreds of civilians, mainly Hutu; the FFM said it could not fully investigate these incidents given time constraints.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-003.l: Bishwa chefferie [as printed in para. 31; para. 19 prints Bwisha], Rutshuru territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-003.a: M23 members, with civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers
r2-G-DOC-HRC-003.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 31. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 19 describes the same offensive in Bwisha chefferie, a predominantly Hutu area and traditional FDLR stronghold.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-003.vn: Para. 31 checked; hedges ('alleged RDF soldiers', 'allegedly executed') kept. The time-constraints caveat sits in the next sentence of para. 31 (page, not excerpt). The report spells the chiefdom 'Bishwa' in para. 31 and 'Bwisha' in para. 19. Footnote 35 gives a separate OHCHR figure (at least 319 killed in Rutshuru, 9-21 July), a different date range from para. 31's 8-29 July.
src: From 8 to 29 July, M23 members, accompanied by civilians armed with machetes and alleged RDF soldiers attacked several farms in Bishwa chefferie in Rutshuru and allegedly executed hundreds of civilians – mainly Hutu’s.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-004.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission stated in a footnote that OHCHR reported M23 killed at least 319 civilians in Rutshuru from 9 to 21 July.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-004.x: OHCHR (cited in FFM report): at least 319 civilians
r2-G-DOC-HRC-004.n: A/HRC/60/80 footnote 35 to para. 31. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Different figure and date range from the 'hundreds' and 8-29 July of para. 31; both are the report's own.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-004.vn: Footnote 35 verbatim; statement attributes the figure to OHCHR as cited by the FFM, not to the FFM's own finding. This is OHCHR's figure quoted in a footnote; the FFM's own text (para. 31) says 'allegedly executed hundreds' for 8-29 July.
src: OHCHR reported M23 killed at least 319 civilians in Rutshuru from 9 - 21 July.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-005.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that at least 21 civilians, including adolescent boys below 18, were executed in M23 cordon-and-search operations in the Kasika neighborhood of Goma on 22 and 23 February; armed M23 members went door to door rounding up local youth, allegedly on accusations of criminality, and killed most victims at point blank range.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-005.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 32. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Footnote 37 cites S/2025/446 annex 49 for the higher figure. Footnote 37: the number of victims is likely higher, some reporting up to 50 killed (e.g. S/2025/446 annex 49).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-005.vn: Para. 32 verbatim. Footnote 37: the number of victims is likely higher, some reporting up to 50 killed (citing S/2025/446 annex 49).
src:
at least 21 civilians,
including adolescent boys below 18, were executed during such operations in the Kasika
neighborhood of Goma on 22 and 23 February. Armed M23 members went from door to door
rounding up local youth, allegedly on accusations of criminality, and killed most victims at
point blank range.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-006.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 16 February in Bukavu M23 members killed a man, allegedly for failing to present identification documents; on 22 February a man was executed for stealing a telephone, and the same day two men accused of filming an M23 convoy were publicly executed, the perpetrators reportedly stating to bystanders that 'no indiscipline will be tolerated'.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-006.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 33. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). The report does not say in which town the 22 February executions took place (the paragraph opens with Bukavu for 16 February).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-006.vn: Para. 33 verbatim; the report does not place the 22 February executions. The report names Bukavu only for the 16 February killing; it does not say where the 22 February executions took place.
src:
on 16 February in Bukavu, M23 members killed a man, allegedly for failing to
present identification documents. On 22 February, a man was executed for stealing a
telephone. The same day two men accused of filming an M23 convoy were publicly executed,
with the perpetrators reportedly stating to bystanders that “no indiscipline will be tolerated”.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-007.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission recorded at least 11 children deliberately shot at and killed by M23 for no discernable reason; examples given were a 17-year-old boy shot in the head at a bar in Goma in February, and a woman and her two young children shot in April.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-007.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 34. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). The report does not give the location of the April killing.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-007.vn: Para. 34 verbatim. Date widened: the 'at least 11' total has no period of its own; the examples are February and April, within the report's January-July 2025 scope (para. 5). The report does not give the place of the April killing.
src:
The FFM recorded at least 11 children deliberately shot at and killed by M23 for no
discernable reason. For example, in February in Goma, M23 elements shot a 17-year-old boy
in the head at a bar. M23 also encircled a woman fleeing and holding her two young children
in April. They shot at her and the two children while she pleaded for mercy, killing all three.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-008.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 13 February in Goma M23 members killed Delcat Idengo, a singer and activist known for songs critical of both M23 and the Congolese authorities.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-008.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 36. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-008.vn: Para. 36 verbatim; name printed in the excerpt. Corroborates r1-GOE-067 (Group of Experts, a separate UN body).
src:
On 13 February in Goma,
M23 members killed Delcat Idengo, a singer and activist known for songs critical of both
M23 and the Congolese authorities.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-009.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in at least four incidents in Goma M23 entered hospitals to locate suspected FARDC, Wazalendo and FDLR members being treated or hiding there, detaining hundreds of people, including patients, medical personnel and accompanying family members.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-009.x: FFM: at least four incidents; hundreds detained
r2-G-DOC-HRC-009.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 38. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Hospitals are not named and dates are not given; period is the report's Jan-Jul 2025 scope (para. 5).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-009.vn: Para. 38 verbatim; hospitals and dates not given, range is the report period.
src:
In at least four incidents in Goma, M23 also entered hospitals to locate suspected
FARDC, Wazalendo, and FDLR members being treated or hiding there, detaining hundreds
of people – including patients, medical personnel and accompanying family members.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-010.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that M23 detained thousands of civilians, primarily during cordon-and-search operations conducted almost daily since January.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-010.l: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-HRC-010.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 38. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Ransom detail is from para. 39, not in the excerpt, so it is omitted from the claim; see next claim.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-010.vn: Para. 38 verbatim. Territory set to not specified: the paragraph is not limited to Goma.
src:
M23 detained thousands of civilians, primarily during cordon-and-search operations
conducted almost daily since January.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-011.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that many of those detained, mostly able-bodied men and boys around 15 and older, were loaded into trucks and taken away.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-011.l: M23-controlled areas, North and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-HRC-011.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 39. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the excerpt in the final text; see fix below. Para. 38-39 sit in the section on patterns of violations in M23-controlled areas; the excerpt itself names no actor.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-011.vn: Para. 39 verbatim; actor M23 from the context of paras. 38-39 (detentions by M23).
src:
Many of those detained – mostly able-bodied men and boys around 15 and older –
were loaded into trucks and taken away.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-012.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 17 February AFC/M23 issued instructions giving a one-week ultimatum for parents to retrieve their children.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-012.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 41. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the ultimatum; footnote 39 says the instructions were written and verbal ones issued by de facto authorities and collected by the FFM.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-012.vn: Para. 41 verbatim; Goma is the paragraph's setting (children on the streets of Goma).
src:
On 17 February, AFC/M23 issued instructions39 giving a one-week
ultimatum for parents to retrieve their children.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-013.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported accounts indicating that some guards at improvised M23-run detention sites in North and South Kivu were Rwandans, and said it received credible information that senior M23 commanders, including M23's military leader, were present at some of these sites; their names were retained on file.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-013.l: Improvised detention sites, North and South Kivu
r2-G-DOC-HRC-013.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 44. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Commanders are not named in the public text. Statement date is the report's 2025 scope; no month given. Annex IV (map of sites) is image-only in the text retrieved.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-013.vn: Para. 44 verbatim; names withheld by the FFM.
src:
Accounts
indicated that some guards were Rwandans. The FFM also received credible information that
senior M23 commanders, including M23’s military leader, were present at some of these
detention sites. Their names have been retained on file.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-014.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that individuals forcefully recruited or otherwise detained were transported to former FARDC camps in Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Rutshuru territory) for 're-education' and military 'training' for three to four months, before being reportedly deployed to the front line.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-014.l: Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps, Rutshuru territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-014.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 46. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 45 states 'Thousands of civilians – including adolescent girls and boys – were forcibly recruited after being detained during search operations'. Para. 48: recruits stated most instructors and guards were Rwandan nationals, including some RDF members in uniforms.
src:
Individuals forcefully recruited or otherwise detained were transported to former
FARDC camps in Rumangabo and Tshanzu (Rutshuru territory)41 to undergo “re-education”
and military “training” for three to four months, before being reportedly deployed to the front
line.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-015.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that guards from Tshanzu removed women from their enclosures at night, and that many women detainees, unable to endure the hunger, were subjected to sexual exploitation and forced to exchange sex for food.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-015.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 47. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Same paragraph: detainees who tried to escape were executed in front of other detainees and bodies displayed; one survivor said 'Tshanzu was hell'.
src:
Guards from Tshanzu removed women from their enclosures at night, and many women
detainees, unable to endure the hunger, were subjected to sexual exploitation, forced to
exchange sex for food.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-019.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that other incidents in M23 detention included so-called 'corrective rapes', forced nudity, non-consensual touching and sexual slurs, perpetrated either by M23 guards or by co-detainees with the instigation or acquiescence of de facto authorities.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-019.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 50. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-019.vn: Para. 50 verbatim; adds the 'corrective rapes' sentence to r1-SV-2025-010.
src:
Other incidents included so called “corrective rapes”, forced nudity, non-consensual touching, sexual slurs, and other sexualized acts intended to
humiliate, perpetrated either by M23 guards or by co-detainees with the instigation, or
acquiescence of de facto authorities.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-020.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after capturing Goma, M23 members ordered tens of thousands of IDPs living in camps around the city to dismantle their shelters and return to their villages.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-020.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 51. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Annex V lists camps shown emptied by satellite imagery: Don Bosco Ngangi, Bushagara, Mudja, Buhimba, Rusayo, Bulengo, Lushagala, Lwashi, Kashaka, Rego. Month assumed from footnote 42 ('End of February over 500,000 IDPs...'); the paragraph itself gives no date.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-020.vn: Para. 51 verbatim. Date narrowed to January-February: Goma was taken by 29 January (para. 13) and para. 52 dates a return 'following the forced dismantlement' to 25 February; March was not supported.
src:
After capturing Goma, M23 members ordered tens of thousands of IDPs living in
camps around the city to dismantle their shelters and return to their villages.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-021.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 25 February Hutu families who had returned to Karenga (Masisi territory, North Kivu) after the forced dismantlement of their camp were ordered to leave the town within a day and were threatened that if they did not comply, 'the Red Cross would come to collect [their] bodies'.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-021.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 52. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-021.vn: Para. 52 verbatim; actor M23 from the paragraph's lead sentence ('once again expelled by M23').
src:
on 25 February,
Hutu families who had returned to Karenga (Masisi territory, North Kivu) following the
forced dismantlement of their camp were ordered to leave the town within a day and were
threatened that if they did not comply, “the Red Cross would come to collect [their] bodies”.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-022.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that between 10 and 13 May M23 forces detained hundreds of people, mostly men and adolescent boys, during cordon-and-search operations in Goma, Nyiragongo and Sake and took them to Goma stadium, where they were grouped by presumed affiliation.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-022.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 53. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 54: UNHCR stated on 22 May that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'.
src:
Between 10 and 13 May, M23 forces detained
hundreds of people, mostly men and adolescent boys, during cordon-and-search operations
in Goma, Nyiragongo, and Sake and took them to Goma stadium, where they were grouped
by presumed affiliation

r2-G-DOC-HRC-023.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 22 May UNHCR stated that more than 1,700 'Rwandan nationals' brought to a transit center after cordon-and-search operations had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted 'under pressure'.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-023.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 54. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-023.vn: Para. 54 verbatim; the figure is UNHCR's as relayed by the FFM (footnote 44: RFI and UNHCR).
src: On 22 May, UNHCR stated that more than 1,700 “Rwandan nationals” brought to a transit center after cordon-andsearch operations had been returned to Rwanda after screening interviews conducted “under pressure”.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-024.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in North Kivu women and adolescent girls were subjected to gang rapes by retreating FARDC and Wazalendo, and that one woman was held hostage, tied to a tree and raped daily for two weeks by multiple perpetrators until her family paid a ransom.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-024.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 56. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Section VII.A places the pattern in the retreat from the frontlines in January and February (para. 55). The report gives no locality.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-024.vn: Para. 56 verbatim. Relation set to adds_detail: the first clause is r1-SV-2025-011; the hostage case is new detail. The report does not say the hostage case was in North Kivu or who the perpetrators were beyond 'multiple perpetrators'.
src:
In North Kivu, women and adolescent girls were subjected to gang rapes by retreating FARDC and
Wazalendo. One woman was held hostage, tied to a tree and raped daily for two weeks by
multiple perpetrators until her family paid a ransom.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-026.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during their retreat soldiers from the 'Satan II' and 'Guépard' units repeatedly entered homes, looted property and raped civilians, following a consistent pattern across multiple locations and over a wide geographic area.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-026.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 78. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-026.vn: Para. 78 verbatim; January-February from the same paragraph ('in January and February').
src:
During their retreat, soldiers from the ‘Satan II’ and
‘Guépard’ units repeatedly entered homes, looted property, and raped civilians, following a
consistent pattern across multiple locations and over a wide geographic area.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-027.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported community mobilization campaigns with door-to-door visits and mass gatherings, particularly between February and April in Fizi territory, South Kivu, during which boys and girls were encouraged to enroll.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-027.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 60. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-027.vn: Para. 60 verbatim; Wazalendo from the paragraph's lead sentence.
src:
Community mobilization campaigns with door-to-door visits and mass
gatherings were conducted, particularly between February and April in Fizi territory, South
Kivu, during which boys and girls were encouraged to enroll to “save their homeland from

r2-G-DOC-HRC-028.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported verified witness accounts of boys visibly under 18 carrying weapons at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira, and bearing AK-47 rifles in Fizi territory.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-028.l: South Kivu: checkpoints, Uvira, Fizi territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-028.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 61. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt; girls/sexual-purposes sentence is already cited by an r1 claim.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-028.vn: Para. 61 verbatim; the paragraph gives no date, range is the post-February period of Wazalendo control within the report scope.
src:
According to verified witness accounts, boys visibly under 18 years of age were seen
carrying weapons at Wazalendo checkpoints in South Kivu, patrolling in Uvira, and bearing
AK-47 rifles in Fizi territory.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-029.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission examined allegations of at least six children killed when M23 entered Bukavu, who had taken uniforms and weapons left behind by fleeing Wazalendo and FARDC members; it could not determine the precise circumstances of their deaths.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-029.a: not determined by the FFM (children killed when M23 entered Bukavu)
r2-G-DOC-HRC-029.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 62. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Month from para. 14 (Bukavu entered 16 Feb); para. 62 itself gives no date.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-029.vn: Para. 62 verbatim. Actor corrected: the report says the children were killed 'when M23 entered Bukavu' but could not determine the circumstances, so it does not attribute the killings to M23. Month from para. 14 (Bukavu entered two days after 14 February).
src:
The FFM examined allegations of
at least six such children killed when M23 entered Bukavu but could not determine the
precise circumstances of their deaths.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-030.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after February Wazalendo groups capitalized on the security vacuum left by retreating Congolese forces to assert control over Uvira and parts of Fizi territory, establishing parallel administrative and judicial structures, conducting informal trials and carrying out illegal arrests.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-030.l: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-030.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 63. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
src:
After February, Wazalendo groups capitalized on the security vacuum left by the
retreat of Congolese security forces to assert control over Uvira and parts of Fizi territory,
South Kivu. They established parallel administrative and judicial structures, conducted
informal trials and carried out illegal arrests.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-031.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission identified at least 13 detention sites under the direct authority of self-proclaimed Wazalendo 'generals', where detainees were routinely subjected to torture and other forms of ill-treatment.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-031.l: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-031.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 63. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Generals not named in the public text.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-031.vn: Para. 63 verbatim; sites not located in the public text beyond the paragraph's Uvira/Fizi setting.
src:
The FFM identified at least 13 detention sites
under the direct authority of self-proclaimed Wazalendo “generals”, where detainees were
routinely subjected to torture and other forms of ill-treatment.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-032.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that Wazalendo groups substantially restricted freedom of movement with numerous checkpoints in Uvira and along the Uvira-Kamanyola or Uvira-Fizi roads, where civilians were required to pay 'fees'.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-032.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 64. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the checkpoint-fees sentence; Bashi discrimination is the next sentence of para. 64.
src:
Wazalendo groups substantially restricted freedom of movement with numerous
checkpoints in Uvira and along the Uvira–Kamanyola or Uvira-Fizi roads, where civilians
were required to pay “fees”.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-033.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission said it received multiple reports of members of the Tutsi community being killed, and of others being denied access to local markets on ethnic grounds.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-033.l: not specified (para. 65, in the report's section on FARDC, Wazalendo and affiliated groups)
r2-G-DOC-HRC-033.a: not attributed by the source (section VII.D concerns FARDC, Wazalendo and affiliated groups)
r2-G-DOC-HRC-033.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 65. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Place and date not given in the paragraph; placed under the section on FARDC, Wazalendo and affiliated groups. Proposed grade B because of limited detail.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-033.vn: Para. 65: narrowed to the excerpt (the hate-speech labels are in an earlier sentence not in the stored excerpt). Place and perpetrators are not given; territory 'Uvira' was not supported. The same paragraph says Tutsi and Banyamulenge populations were repeatedly labelled 'foreigners' or 'proxies of Rwanda'. No place, date or perpetrator is given.
src:
The FFM received multiple reports of members of the Tutsi community being
killed, and others being denied access to local markets on ethnic grounds.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-034.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the escalation of violence in January led to a sharp rise in sexual violence reported by the United Nations and humanitarians, with cases involving children tripling in one month.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-034.x: child cases tripled in one month
r2-G-DOC-HRC-034.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 66. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Excerpt contains footnote numerals 50 and 51 as printed; statement trimmed to the excerpt (UNICEF attribution is footnote 51). Footnote 51 gives UNICEF as the source of the tripling.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-034.vn: Para. 66 verbatim; footnote 51 credits UNICEF for the tripling.
src: The escalation of violence in January led to a sharp rise in sexual violence reported by the United Nations and humanitarians,50 with cases involving children tripling in one month.51

r2-G-DOC-HRC-035.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that sexual violence took place mainly in the form of gang rapes by up to seven perpetrators, during or after military operations, in the context of disruption of law and order or during the displacement of populations fleeing armed conflict.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-035.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 66. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt.
src:
Sexual violence took place mainly in the form of gang rapes by up to seven
perpetrators, during or after military operations, in the context of disruption of law and order
or during the displacement of populations fleeing armed conflict.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-036.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in some instances victims were abducted and subjected to sexual slavery; for example, a 19-year-old woman was abducted, taken to an unknown location to become the 'wife' of an FDLR element who raped her for two days.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-036.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 67. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Survivor unnamed; date and place not given.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-036.vn: Para. 67 verbatim; the 'in some instances ... sexual slavery' clause is the sentence before the excerpt (page). 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: A/HRC/60/80, para. 67, supports the whole statement, but the stored excerpt omits the opening sentence on abduction and sexual slavery that the statement carries; the full contiguous passage is added.
src:
For example, a 19-year-old woman was abducted, taken to an unknown location to become the
“wife” of an FDLR element who raped her for two days.

In some instances, victims were abducted and subjected to sexual slavery. For example, a 19-year-old woman was abducted, taken to an unknown location to become the “wife” of an FDLR element who raped her for two days.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-037.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported cases of sexual violence against men and boys and LGBT individuals, including a verified case of a 13-year-old boy raped along with his mother, a 14-year-old boy beaten and forced to have sexual intercourse with a female relative in front of his siblings, and a documented case of forced nudity, beatings and public humiliation of an LGBT individual by Wazalendo members.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-037.a: Wazalendo members (LGBT case); not attributed for the two boys' cases
r2-G-DOC-HRC-037.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 68. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Minors unnamed in the source.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-037.vn: Para. 68 verbatim; perpetrators of the two boys' cases not given.
src:
the FFM verified the case
of a 13-year-old boy who was raped along with his mother, and a 14-year-old boy who was
beaten and forced to have sexual intercourse with a female relative in front of his siblings. A
case of forced nudity, beatings, homo-transphobic insults against and public humiliation of
an LGBT individual by Wazalendo members was also documented.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-038.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that it confirmed that, during the mass escape from Munzenze prison on 27 January, most of the 160 women inmates, along with numerous infants, died, and that an undetermined number were gang-raped, in some cases in front of their children, by male inmates who had forced their way into the women's ward.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-038.x: FFM: most of 160 women inmates died
r2-G-DOC-HRC-038.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 69. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Sources differ on cause: some reported prisoners set fire to cells, others described detonations from shelling. Annex VI (satellite images) is image-only. Likely overlaps in part existing r1 claims on the Munzenze escape. Footnote 53: official sources (Government of the DRC) reported that 144 women and 30 infants died.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-038.vn: Para. 69 verbatim. Adds the FFM's confirmed finding to r1-SV-2025-004 (annex caption of the same report) and relates to r1-GOE-062 / r1-SV-2025-001/003 (165-167 women per other sources). Figures differ by source: the FFM says most of 160 women inmates died; footnote 53 cites official (DRC Government) sources for 144 women and 30 infants dead; other r1 sources give 165-167 women raped. The FFM records two accounts of the cause: prisoners setting fire to cells, and detonations from shelling.
src:
during the mass escape from Munzenze prison on 27
January, most of the 160 women inmates – along with numerous infants – died, and that an
undetermined number were gang-raped, in some cases in front of their children, by male
inmates who had forced their way into the women’s ward.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-039.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission confirmed repeated rapes, other ill-treatment and death threats by an escapee previously convicted by national judicial authorities, against victims and human rights defenders who had testified against him in court.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-039.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 70. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Date, place and prison not given.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-039.vn: Para. 70 verbatim. Date set to the report's January-July 2025 period (the raw '2025' had no precision flag basis); place, prison and date not given.
src:
For example, the FFM confirmed repeated rapes, other ill-treatment and
death threats by an escapee previously convicted by national judicial authorities against
victims and human rights defenders who had testified against him in court.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-040.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that victims' access to appropriate healthcare remained severely constrained due to ongoing hostilities, limited financial resources, threats against healthcare personnel, non-payment of salaries to medical staff, insufficient post-exposure prophylaxis kits and a reduction in international funding to health and support providers.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-040.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 71. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
src:
Victims’ access to appropriate healthcare remained
severely constrained due to ongoing hostilities, their limited financial resources, threats
against healthcare personnel, non-payment of salaries to medical staff, insufficient postexposure prophylaxis kits, and a reduction in international funding to health and support
providers.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-041.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that shells reportedly struck the maternity ward of Charité Maternelle Hospital in Goma on 28 January, killing and injuring several civilians, including newborns and pregnant women.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-041.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 28. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Para. 28 opens with 'Medical facilities were also impacted'. The Walungu Hospital strike of 9 March in the same paragraph is already cited in r1.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-041.vn: Para. 28 verbatim; 'reportedly' hedge kept, no perpetrator named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src:
Reportedly, shells struck the maternity ward of Charité Maternelle Hospital in
Goma on 28 January, killing and injuring several civilians, including newborns and pregnant
women.
Several shells struck the Charité Maternelle Hospital in central Goma, "killing and injuring civilians, including newborns and pregnant women", Lemarquis said on Monday

r2-G-DOC-HRC-042.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 24 January multiple projectiles, including a 122mm rocket, struck the Rusayo IDP camp, killing at least 14, mostly women and children, and injuring many others.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-042.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 25. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt; the FARDC-weapons observation (para. 25) is quoted in the next claim.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-042.vn: Para. 25 verbatim ('The FFM documented several attacks on displacement sites'); no perpetrator named. Discrepancy: the UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-065) reports bombs from RDF-controlled positions striking Rusayo 1 and 2 camps on 26 January, killing at least 12; the FFM gives 24 January and at least 14, and names no perpetrator. Same or separate strikes not established.
src:
on 24 January, multiple projectiles, including a 122mm rocket, struck the Rusayo
IDP camp, killing at least 14, mostly women and children, and injuring many others.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-043.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 27 February at least 13 individuals were killed when explosions occurred during an M23-organized gathering at Place de l'Indépendance in Bukavu; it could not identify the perpetrator of the explosions.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-043.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 27. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-043.vn: Para. 27 verbatim; perpetrator not identified by the FFM.
src:
On 27 February, at least 13 individuals were killed
when explosions occurred during an M23-organized gathering at Place de l'Indépendance in
Bukavu. The FFM could not identify the perpetrator of these explosions.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-044.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in June clashes between M23 and Wazalendo, including shelling by all parties in Kabare territory, resulted in dozens of civilians killed.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-044.a: M23, Wazalendo and other parties (shelling by all parties)
r2-G-DOC-HRC-044.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 27. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
src:
In June, clashes
between M23 and Wazalendo, including shelling by all parties in Kabare territory, resulted
in dozens of civilians killed.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-045.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 23 January M23 and RDF launched a coordinated offensive on Sake, 25 km west of Goma, eventually overwhelming FARDC troops supported by MONUSCO and SAMIDRC as well as private military companies contracted by the Congolese Government.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-045.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 12. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement trimmed to the excerpt; the 27 January entry into Goma is in the next sentence and the next claim.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-045.vn: Para. 12 verbatim. 2026-10-29: territory edited: Frontline data fix: the claim's location is 'Sake and Goma'; Sake (its control place, '25 km west of Goma' per the excerpt) is in Masisi territory.
src:
On 23 January, M23 and RDF launched a coordinated offensive on Sake – 25
km west of Goma – eventually overwhelming FARDC troops supported by the United
Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
(MONUSCO) and the Southern African Development Community Mission in the
Democratic Republic of the Congo (SAMIDRC), as well as private military companies
contracted by the Congolese Government.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-046.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the spontaneous withdrawal of some FARDC troops from their positions, the killing of the Military Governor of North Kivu and the desertion of senior FARDC officers further accelerated the breakdown of Congolese defenses, and that by 29 January M23 and RDF had taken full control of Goma.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-046.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 13. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
src:
The spontaneous withdrawal of some FARDC troops from their positions, the killing
of the Military Governor of North Kivu and the desertion of senior FARDC officers further
accelerated the breakdown of Congolese defenses. By 29 January, M23 and RDF had taken
full control of the city.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-047.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 14 February M23 seized Kavumu airport and two days later entered the provincial capital Bukavu without resistance, as Government forces had withdrawn toward the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-047.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 14. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Paragraph opens: 'In early February, with RDF support, M23 continued advancing into South Kivu.' Statement relies on that sentence only for the actor.
src: In early February, with RDF support, M23 continued advancing into South Kivu. On 14 February, it seized Kavumu airport, and two days later entered the provincial capital Bukavu without resistance, as Government forces had withdrawn toward the Ruzizi Plain and Uvira.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-049.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that after the Uvira and Kamanyola clashes most FARDC troops withdrew further, effectively ceding control of Uvira and parts of Fizi territory to Wazalendo.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-049.l: Uvira and parts of Fizi territory
r2-G-DOC-HRC-049.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 17. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-049.vn: Para. 17 verbatim; follows the mid-February clashes.
src:
Thereafter, most FARDC troops withdrew further, effectively
ceding control of Uvira and parts of Fizi territory to Wazalendo.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-050.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that upon capturing Goma and Bukavu, AFC/M23 appointed 'administrators' to formalize its control as de facto authority and introduced its own 'tax collection system', and that civil servants and customary chiefs opposing M23 were replaced with individuals supportive of M23.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-050.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 15. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Footnote 21 gives BBC as source for the mining-activities tax; footnote 19: M23 appointed new governors and other local authorities in North and South Kivu.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-050.vn: Para. 15 verbatim. Date widened to January-February: Goma was taken in January (para. 13), Bukavu in February (para. 14).
src:
Upon capturing Goma and Bukavu, AFC/M23 appointed “administrators” to
formalize its control as de facto authority.19 AFC/M23 introduced its own “tax collection
system”, generating revenue through the imposition of new “taxes” or the diversion of
existing ones,20 including on mining activities.21 Civil servants and customary chiefs
opposing M23 were replaced with individuals supportive of M23.22

r2-G-DOC-HRC-051.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission described a '10 houses system' implemented in M23-held areas as an administrative structure for local chiefs appointed by M23 to monitor residents' movements and report daily on suspicious activities.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-051.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 37. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Statement limited to the excerpt (description of the system).
src:
The implementation of a “10 houses system” – an administrative
structure for local chiefs appointed by M23 to monitor residents’ movements and report daily
on suspicious activities

r2-G-DOC-HRC-052.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that the Government of Rwanda has consistently denied allegations of its direct involvement with M23, including in response to the report.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-052.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 8. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Excerpt copied as printed (the PDF text drops the space in 'hasconsistently'). Rwanda's own response text is not published in the report.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-052.vn: Para. 8 verbatim (the '23' flag is the M23 name). A party account (Rwanda's denial) as relayed by the FFM; Rwanda's own response text is not published.
src:
The Government of Rwanda
hasconsistently denied allegations of its direct involvement with M23,5
including in response
to this report.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-053.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported in a footnote that Rwanda denied, in its response to the report, the finding of active and decisive involvement of the RDF alongside M23 during the capture of Goma.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-053.n: A/HRC/60/80 footnotes 23 and 30. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-053.vn: Footnote 23 verbatim; Rwanda's denial is a party account relayed by the FFM. Footnote 30 adds that Rwanda, in its response, 'refuted being part of the conflict'.
src: FFM’s findings reaffirmed Group of Experts’ findings (S/2025/446, paras. 35-36) on active and decisive involvement of RDF alongside M23 during the capture of Goma. Rwanda denied this claim in its response to this report.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-054.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported in a footnote that, in its response to the report, the Congolese Government noted that formal orders were issued by the President and the FARDC Chief of Staff to prohibit any collaboration with the FDLR.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-054.n: A/HRC/60/80 footnote 8 to para. 9. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-054.vn: Footnote 8 verbatim; DRC Government party account relayed by the FFM.
src:
In its response to this report,
the Congolese Government noted that formal orders were issued by the President and FARDC Chief of
Staff to prohibit any collaboration with FDLR.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-055.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission cited a May 2025 AFC Secretariat document titled 'AFC/M23's reaction to allegations human rights violations in the Goma and Bukavu' as the source for M23's 'stated objective' of restoring order, security and stability.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-055.n: A/HRC/60/80 footnote 34 to para. 29. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). The report cites the document only as the source of the 'stated objective'. The document's own text was not retrieved; the claim records what the FFM cited, not the AFC's words.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-055.vn: Footnote 34 verbatim; records only what the FFM cited. The 'stated objective' clause is para. 29 (page). Party document (AFC/M23); its own text was not retrieved.
src: AFC Secretariat, AFC/M23’s reaction to allegations human rights violations in the Goma and Bukavu, May 2025.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-056.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 27 June senior ministers of the DRC and Rwanda signed a Peace Agreement in Washington.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-056.a: Governments of the DRC and Rwanda
r2-G-DOC-HRC-056.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 18. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-056.vn: Para. 18 verbatim. Actor and location corrected: the claim is the Washington signing only (M23 and Doha belong to claim 56).
src:
On 27 June, senior ministers of the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Rwanda
signed a Peace Agreement in Washington

r2-G-DOC-HRC-057.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that on 19 July there followed a Declaration of Principles between the Government of the DRC and M23 in Doha, committing to reaching a comprehensive peace agreement by 18 August.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-057.a: Government of the DRC and M23
r2-G-DOC-HRC-057.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 18. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-057.vn: Para. 18: the excerpt does not use the word 'signed' (para. 88 does); narrowed to the excerpt's wording.
src:
This was followed, on 19 July, by a
Declaration of Principles between the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo
and M23 in Doha, committing to reaching a comprehensive peace agreement by 18 August.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-058.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that in July both M23 and FARDC reinforced their positions in South Kivu near the Burundian border, and that M23 maintained military pressure in North Kivu, targeting residual FARDC, FDLR and Wazalendo forces in Lubero, Rutshuru and Walikale territories.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-058.l: South Kivu near the Burundian border; Lubero, Rutshuru and Walikale territories
r2-G-DOC-HRC-058.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 19. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). 'terrotories' is as printed in the source.
src:
In July, both M23 and
FARDC reinforced their positions in South Kivu, near the Burundian border, making the
security situation highly volatile and raising concerns about renewed violence and further
regionalization of the conflict. M23 also maintained military pressure in North Kivu,
targeting residual FARDC, FDLR, and Wazalendo forces in Lubero, Rutshuru and Walikale
terrotories.

r2-G-DOC-HRC-059.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that cross-border shelling between the FARDC and RDF allegedly resulted in civilian casualties, with Rwandan authorities reporting at least 16 deaths and 177 injured in Gisenyi, including women and children; the FFM said it was unable to corroborate civilian casualties.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-059.x: Rwandan authorities (cited in footnote 33): at least 16 deaths and 177 injured
r2-G-DOC-HRC-059.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 24. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Event is in Rwanda; kept as context for the Goma fighting. The report does not give the date; month inferred from the Goma context in paras. 23-24 and not stated.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-059.vn: Para. 24 verbatim. The casualty figures are the Government of Rwanda's (footnote 33), a party; the FFM could not corroborate them. Date set to the report period: the paragraph gives none (raw date format was not a valid date). Figures are Rwanda's (party) as cited by the FFM; uncorroborated.
src: Cross-border shelling between the FARDC and RDF also allegedly resulted in civilian casualties, with Rwandan authorities reporting at least 16 deaths and 177 injured in Gisenyi, including women and children.33 The FFM was unable to corroborate civilian casualties

r2-G-DOC-HRC-060.s: The OHCHR fact-finding mission reported that during the fighting for Goma three UN peacekeepers were killed, allegedly in a targeted attack by M23 and RDF (source: Spokesman for the Secretary-General).
r2-G-DOC-HRC-060.n: A/HRC/60/80 para. 23. The text is the English advance unedited version of 5 September 2025; the FFM's standard is 'reasonable grounds to believe' (para. 4). Footnote 32: Spokesman for the Secretary-General. Date inferred from the 'fighting for Goma' context.
r2-G-DOC-HRC-060.vn: Para. 23; 'allegedly' kept; footnote 32 credits the Spokesman for the Secretary-General. Date narrowed to January: the fighting for Goma ran from 23 January to 29 January (paras. 12-13).
src:
Three UN peacekeepers were also
killed, allegedly in a targeted attack by M23 and RDF.32

r2-G-LOCAL-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing medical sources it contacted, that the Mweso general referral hospital (Masisi) was overwhelmed by the high number of war-wounded arriving from combat zones, in the context of continuing clashes between AFC/M23 and the FARDC supported by local militias.
r2-G-LOCAL-001.n: Capacity strain from war-wounded, not an attack on the facility; included as context for civilian access to care. Local outlet citing unnamed medical sources. Kivu and Masisi hospitals not previously in packet for Nov 2025.
r2-G-LOCAL-001.vn: Page dated 06/11/2025 says it; context clause sits in the sentence before the excerpt, so the excerpt is extended. '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'. The page says the wounded are both civilians and AFC/M23 combatants.
src: D’après des sources médicales contactées par ACTUALITE.CD, l’hôpital général de référence de Mweso est actuellement débordé par le nombre élevé des blessés de guerre en provenance des zones de combats.

r2-G-LOCAL-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that MSF announced the early end of its medical activities in Baraka, Fizi health zone, South Kivu, because of the deteriorating security situation, saying it had evacuated its teams after the M23 advance and the capture of Uvira, and that activities at Baraka general hospital and three health centres had ended.
r2-G-LOCAL-002.a: MSF (announcing); security situation attributed to fighting between M23 and the FARDC with Wazalendo
r2-G-LOCAL-002.x: Actualite.cd, citing MSF: more than 25,000 people treated for malaria in Baraka between August and December
r2-G-LOCAL-002.n: Exact day of the closure not given; the page is dated 2025-12-12. Packet holds only an MSF Baraka item for Jan-Apr 2026 (r1-ATR-SK-2026-014). Original MSF release not opened; Actualite.cd relays MSF.
r2-G-LOCAL-002.vn: All clauses on the page (12/12/2025). Excerpt 0 extended to carry the announcement and Fizi health zone. Actualite.cd relays MSF; exact closure day not given. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: L’organisation précise avoir évacué ses équipes après l’avancée du M23 et la prise de la ville d’Uvira, située à environ une centaine de kilomètres de Baraka. Les activités médicales à l’hôpital général de Baraka, ainsi que dans trois centres de santé, sont désormais terminées, selon MSF.
Entre août et décembre, les équipes de l’ONG à Baraka ont pris en charge plus de 25 000 personnes atteintes de paludisme.
MSF a évacué ses équipes de la ville. Les activités médicales à l’hôpital général de Baraka ainsi que dans trois centres de santé sont terminées.

r2-G-LOCAL-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that four civilians of Bukumbirwa were missing since Monday 27 October 2025 after Wazalendo elements of the CMC group, led by a self-proclaimed general named Bigabo, passed through fields at Mahasha near Bukumbirwa (Muronga, Walikale), and that the group accuses them of complicity with the AFC-M23; an anonymous resident was quoted.
r2-G-LOCAL-003.a: Wazalendo of the CMC group led by self-proclaimed general Bigabo, as the source says
r2-G-LOCAL-003.n: Single local outlet citing an anonymous resident; victims unnamed. Date given as the Monday 27 October 2025 in the text. No packet item for Mahasha/Bukumbirwa on this date.
r2-G-LOCAL-003.vn: Page (28 Oct 2025, 'La Rédaction') says all of it; excerpt extended to carry the anonymous resident. '4' flag is 'Quatre'. Victims unnamed.
src: Quatre civils de Bukumbirwa ont été portés disparus depuis lundi 27 octobre 2025, lors du passage des éléments Wazalendo du groupe CMC dirigé par le général autoproclamé Bigabo, dans les champs de Mahasha, près de Bukumbirwa, en localité Muronga, territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu. Ces habitants sont accusés par ce groupe d’être en complicité avec l’AFC-M23.

r2-G-LOCAL-004.s: 7sur7.cd reported that Congolese human rights minister Chantal Mwavita said that between 28 and 29 June more than 300 young people were arrested by the M23 at Rubaya and about twenty others at Rugendo (Kabare), were presented publicly at a meeting as volunteers, and that she denounced this as forced recruitment.
r2-G-LOCAL-004.a: M23 / M23-RDF, per the Congolese human rights minister
r2-G-LOCAL-004.x: Minister Mwavita: more than 300 arrested at Rubaya; about twenty at Rugendo
r2-G-LOCAL-004.n: Party (Kinshasa) allegation; the article also says 'according to independent sources in occupied areas' young people have been abducted and accused of working with Wazalendo. Page spells the minister's title 'ministe'. The packet categories searched did not include forced_recruitment, so overlap with other rounds is possible.
r2-G-LOCAL-004.vn: Page (4 Jul 2025) quotes the minister with the 28-29 June dates and Rugendo figure; source 1 excerpt extended to the contiguous quotation. Kept attributed to the minister; grade C (partisan). Party (Kinshasa) allegation. The page also says, citing independent sources in occupied areas, that young people have been abducted and accused of working with Wazalendo.
src: Plus de 300 jeunes ont été arrêtés lors du bouclage mené par les éléments du M23/AFC dans le territoire de Masisi en province du Nord-Kivu. En majorité des adolescents, ces jeunes ont été arrêtés dans la cité minière de Rubaya, puis amenés dans une destination inconnue fin juin dernier, annonce la ministre des droits humains

Ils ont été ensuite présentés publiquement lors d'un meeting comme des volontaires ayant rejoint la rébellion à Birava », a indiqué Maître Chantal Mwavita, ministe Congolaise en charge des droits humains.
Dans la foulée, elle a dénoncé un recrutement forcé des jeunes par les éléments du M23-RDF.

r2-G-LOCAL-005.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the Congolese Interior Ministry, in an official communiqué, denounced actions in AFC-M23-held areas of North Kivu including more than 272 assassinations and summary executions, more than 300 rapes and more than 300 acts of torture, which it said occurred mainly between 20 September and 2 October 2025 in Rutshuru, Walikale and Masisi territories.
r2-G-LOCAL-005.a: AFC-M23, per the Congolese Interior Ministry
r2-G-LOCAL-005.x: Interior Ministry per 7sur7.cd: more than 272 assassinations and summary executions; more than 300 rapes; more than 300 acts of torture (including on pupils)
r2-G-LOCAL-005.n: Partisan (Kinshasa) allegation, cited only for what the ministry said; not verified. 7sur7.cd names the Interior Ministry; the minister is not named in the excerpt. Related Kinshasa figures at the UN Security Council on 13 October are quoted in the Mediacongo/Radio Okapi item (next claim). Not found in the period packet (which holds the April 297-killings communiqué).
