r2-G-LOCAL-005.vn: Page (11 Oct 2025) supports every clause; AFC-M23 named in the sentence before excerpt 0, so it is extended. Statement keeps the conditional as 'it said'. Party (Kinshasa) allegation; the page uses the conditional ('auraient été commises').
src: Dans un communiqué officiel du ministère de l’Intérieur, les autorités congolaises dénoncent une série d’actes criminels perpétrés dans les zones sous contrôle de ce mouvement armé
Parmi les faits rapportés figurent plus de « 272 assassinats et exécutions sommaires, plus de 300 cas de viols, ainsi que plus de 300 actes de torture, y compris sur des élèves ».
Ces exactions auraient été commises principalement entre le 20 septembre et le 2 octobre 2025, dans les territoires de Rutshuru, Walikale et Masisi, avec un pic de violence dans le quartier Ndendere.

r2-G-LOCAL-006.s: Radio Okapi/MCP, via Mediacongo, reported that the Congolese Interior Minister said he had recorded at least 123 assassinations and 223 rapes in North and South Kivu in October (2025), according to a communiqué received by Radio Okapi on Saturday 1 November; the page headline says 'more than 120' assassinations.
r2-G-LOCAL-006.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (areas under rebel occupation)
r2-G-LOCAL-006.a: rebels / AFC-M23, per the Congolese Interior Minister
r2-G-LOCAL-006.x: Interior Minister per Radio Okapi/MCP: at least 123 assassinations; 223 rapes; hundreds of abductions and forced recruitments
r2-G-LOCAL-006.n: Party (Kinshasa) figure; the article credits 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net', so the originating source is Radio Okapi. Headline says 'plus de 120', body says 'au moins 123'. The page is only fetched by page_text.py via the browser-UA route it uses for the excerpt checker; no block was bypassed by me. The same page reports rebels contest such reports as false on their X accounts.
r2-G-LOCAL-006.vn: Page credits 'Radio Okapi / MCP, via mediacongo.net'; excerpt extended to the next sentence for the 1 November communiqué. Headline clause is from the title. Party (Kinshasa) figures. The same page says rebel leaders contest such reports as false on X.
src: Le ministre de l’Intérieur, de la Sécurité, de la Décentralisation et des Affaires coutumières affirme avoir recensé, au cours du mois d’octobre dernier, au moins 123 cas d’assassinats et 223 cas de viols dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu.

r2-G-LOCAL-007.s: Radio Okapi/MCP, via Mediacongo, reported that the Congolese Interior Minister said more than 100 young people from Bukavu were kidnapped and forcibly enrolled between 14 and 28 October (2025) at camp Sayo, then taken to an unknown destination.
r2-G-LOCAL-007.a: not attributed by name; Bukavu was under rebel occupation per the same page
r2-G-LOCAL-007.x: Interior Minister per Radio Okapi/MCP: more than 100 young people
r2-G-LOCAL-007.n: Government allegation only; perpetrator is not named in the excerpt. Camp Sayo is as printed by the source.
r2-G-LOCAL-007.vn: Excerpt exact and fully supports; year from page context (October 2025 headline). Government allegation; the page does not name the perpetrator in this sentence.
src: Le ministre a également indiqué que plus de 100 jeunes de la ville de Bukavu (Sud-Kivu) ont été kidnappés et enrôlés de force entre les 14 et 28 octobre derniers au camp Sayo, puis acheminés vers une destination inconnue.

r2-G-LOCAL-008.s: 7sur7.cd reported that, according to a communiqué of the South Kivu provincial government signed by its spokesperson Luganywa Bashizi Didier, six civilian men, including patients and health-care staff, were killed by AFC/M23 rebels in Irambi Katana grouping (Kabare) in an attack on the night of 23 to 24 November 2025 on the Cahoboka dispensary; the communiqué said the victims were forcibly taken from the facility and subjected to cruel treatment before being summarily executed.
r2-G-LOCAL-008.l: Cahoboka dispensary, Irambi Katana grouping (Katana), Kabare
r2-G-LOCAL-008.a: AFC/M23, per the South Kivu provincial government
r2-G-LOCAL-008.x: South Kivu provincial government per 7sur7.cd: 6 civilian men killed, among them patients and care staff
r2-G-LOCAL-008.n: Allegation by a party (provincial government in Kinshasa's camp); the page adds 'other local sources' say the civilians were killed on the pretext of collaborating with Wazalendo. No AFC/M23 response found in this unit. Spokesperson spelled 'Luganywa Bashizi Didier' here (cf. variant noted in gap_round_notes). Not in the period packet (checked 'Cahoboka', 'dispens', 23-24 Nov). Related packet items r1-UV-2025Q4-031/-033 (23-24 Nov, Ruzizi plain) are different events.
r2-G-LOCAL-008.vn: All three excerpts exact and support. 'Kabare' is on the page ('groupement d'Irambi Katana dans le territoire de Kabare'). '7' flag is '7sur7.cd'. Allegation by the South Kivu provincial government. The page adds that other local sources say the civilians were killed on the pretext of collaborating with Wazalendo.
src: Selon un communiqué du gouvernement provincial du Sud-Kivu et signé par son porte-parole, Luganywa Bashizi Didier, ces civils ont été tués dans une attaque perpétrée dans la nuit du 23 au 24 novembre 2025 contre le dispensaire de Cahoboka à Katana.

Au total, six hommes civils, parmi lesquels des malades et des membres du personnel soignant, ont été tués par des rebelles de l'AFC/M23 dans le groupement d'Irambi Katana, dans la province du Sud-Kivu.

Ce communiqué souligne que les victimes ont été d'abord arrachées de force de l'enceinte de cette structure médicale, et ont ensuite été soumises à des traitements cruels avant d'être exécutées sommairement.

r2-G-LOCAL-009.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report it said was made public on Tuesday 18 November, that the looting of health structures on 16 October at Rwindi and Birambizo (Rutshuru territory) deprived nearly 92,500 people of access to care.
r2-G-LOCAL-009.x: OCHA per Actualite.cd: nearly 92,500 people deprived of access to care
r2-G-LOCAL-009.n: Relayed from OCHA's October situation report (not opened here). The excerpt begins inside a quoted passage; the page frames it as 'précise le rapport' (the OCHA report). Year 2025 from the page URL date. Packet has Birambizo hospital items for Aug 2026 only.
r2-G-LOCAL-009.vn: Removed the year '2025' from the publication date (no excerpt prints it); otherwise supported. Perpetrator not named. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le pillage des structures de santé, le 16 octobre, à Rwindi et Birambizo, a privé près de 92 500 personnes de l’accès aux soins", précise le rapport rendu public ce mardi 18 novembre.
Le pillage des structures de santé, le 16 octobre, à Rwindi et Birambizo, a privé près de 92 500 personnes de l’accès aux soins.

r2-G-LOCAL-010.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report, that protection actors documented 2,504 incidents in South Kivu, including 263 cases of gender-based violence, 137 cases of sexual violence and 366 cases of violations of children's rights; the headline says the sexual violence and child rights cases were recorded in July.
r2-G-LOCAL-010.l: South Kivu (Walungu, Kabare, Kalehe, Fizi, Uvira, Mwenga)
r2-G-LOCAL-010.x: OCHA per Actualite.cd: 2,504 incidents; 263 gender-based violence cases; 137 sexual violence cases; 366 child rights violations
r2-G-LOCAL-010.n: The reporting month (July) comes from the headline, not the excerpt; the article text does not state the period of the 2,504 incidents. Original OCHA report not opened. Not in packet (searched '137', '2 504').
r2-G-LOCAL-010.vn: Dropped '22 August' and the 332 figure (not in excerpt; the page says the report was published 22 August and adds 332 children associated with armed groups). Rest exact. The article text does not state the period covered by the 2,504 incidents; July comes from the headline. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: D’après le rapport de cet organe du secrétariat des Nations Unies, des acteurs de protection ont documenté 2 504 incidents, dont 263 cas de violences basées sur le genre, 137 cas de violences sexuelles et 366 cas de violations des droits de l’enfant.
Des acteurs de protection ont également documenté 2 504 incidents, dont 263 cas de violences basées sur le genre, 137 cas de violences sexuelles et 366 cas de violations graves des droits de l’enfant

r2-G-LOCAL-011.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing an OCHA report, that two health facilities were attacked in Kalehe and Uvira territories of South Kivu.
r2-G-LOCAL-011.n: No names or dates of the facilities; month taken from the page's headline context (July). Lead for investigators: ask OCHA/Health Cluster for the underlying incident list. Excerpt includes an unrelated food-assistance clause that cannot be split. Contradicting reporting: OCHA (2025-08-22): Highlights name Kabare and Uvira territories, not Kalehe and Uvira as in Actualite.cd's body text; Actualite.cd's own text says Kalehe and Uvira.
r2-G-LOCAL-011.vn: Removed '22 August (2025)' (not in the excerpt). Supported otherwise. No facility names, dates or perpetrators given; the period is approximate (headline says July). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: contradicted; added 0 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 1 verified contradicting source(s) recorded in notes; not regraded pending review.
src: Deux établissements de santé ont été attaqués dans les territoires de Kalehe et d’Uvira, avec une assistance alimentaire à plus de 270 000 personnes partagée avec le territoire de Walungu.

r2-G-LOCAL-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that more than 74 civilians were killed and 83 wounded in South Kivu since 2 December 2025 in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 (the source adds 'appuyés par les combattants Wazalendo', supported by Wazalendo fighters); the report cites a communiqué of Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) on the escalation of violence. The page does not say who produced the figures.
r2-G-LOCAL-012.a: FARDC and M23, each with allied fighters (not attributed by victim)
r2-G-LOCAL-012.x: Radio Okapi: more than 74 civilians killed, 83 wounded in 7 days (headline)
r2-G-LOCAL-012.n: The page does not say who produced the 74/83 figures; Lemarquis's communiqué is cited in the next paragraph. Headline says 'au moins 74', text says 'plus de 74'. Not in packet (searched '74 civil', 'Lemarquis' only Sept ADF item). Local outlet; UN original communiqué not opened.
r2-G-LOCAL-012.vn: Both excerpts exact and support. '7' flag is the headline's '7 jours' (figures field only). The page does not say who produced the 74/83 figures; the headline says 'at least 74', the text 'more than 74'. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: The English 'the M23, supported by Wazalendo fighters' reads as Wazalendo supporting M23; in the French 'appuyés' is plural and cannot agree with 'le M23' alone. Also both excerpts are from one Radio Okapi page, so independent_origins should be 1, not 2.; excerpt-support: cut the grammatical reading that 'appuyés' agrees with the FARDC, not the M23 (an interpretation the page does not print; the phrase is quoted instead)
src: Plus de 74 civils ont été tués et 83 blessés dans les affrontements opposant les FARDC et le M23, appuyés par les combattants Wazalendo, depuis le 2 décembre 2025 au Sud-Kivu.

Dans un communiqué consulté ce mercredi 10 décembre par Radio Okapi, le coordonnateur des opérations humanitaires en RDC et chef de la MONUSCO par intérim, Bruno Lemarquis, s’est dit préoccupé par l’escalade des violences,

r2-G-LOCAL-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué seen on 10 December 2025, Bruno Lemarquis (humanitarian coordinator and acting head of MONUSCO) said the escalating violence in South Kivu notably hinders medical evacuations and affects schools and other civilian infrastructure.
r2-G-LOCAL-013.n: Generic statement, no specific incident or perpetrator.
r2-G-LOCAL-013.vn: Exact; page (10 Dec 2025) on South Kivu fighting. Generic, no incident or perpetrator. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Dans un communiqué consulté ce mercredi 10 décembre par Radio Okapi, le coordonnateur des opérations humanitaires en RDC et chef de la MONUSCO par intérim, Bruno Lemarquis, s’est dit préoccupé par l’escalade des violences, qui entravent notamment les évacuations médicales et affectent les écoles ainsi que d’autres infrastructures civiles.

Les évacuations médicales sont entravées par la poursuite des combats et la présence de barrages routiers. Des attaques contre des infrastructures civiles, y compris des écoles, ont également été signalées ces derniers jours.
Les évacuations médicales restent difficiles en raison de barrages routiers et de la poursuite des hostilités.

r2-G-LOCAL-014.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that four people were killed and eleven wounded on Thursday 29 January 2026 around 18:30 in Sange, Uvira territory, by a grenade explosion; according to local sources an unidentified individual threw the device in the middle of the town, and MP Justin Bitakwira publicly accused the M23 of being behind it. The M23 held a meeting with residents of Sange on 30 January and called on anyone illegally holding arms or munitions to hand them in.
r2-G-LOCAL-014.a: unidentified individual per local sources; M23 accused by Justin Bitakwira
r2-G-LOCAL-014.x: SOS Médias Burundi: 4 killed, 11 wounded (Ebuteli item r1-UV-2026Q1-048 in the packet gives 5 killed, 11 wounded)
r2-G-LOCAL-014.n: Discrepancy with Ebuteli item r1-UV-2026Q1-048 (5 killed, 11 wounded, M23 attributed): SOS gives 4 killed and an unidentified thrower per local sources. Surface both. Third source entry may fail if the excerpt boundary is wrong; see check_raw.
r2-G-LOCAL-014.vn: Byline Adam Ntwari, SOS Médias Burundi, Bukavu 30 Jan 2026. Excerpt 1 extended to carry the M23 meeting clause. Figures field trimmed to this source's numbers (r1 discrepancy moved to note). Casualty figure differs from another source in the timeline (5 killed); surface both. Attribution of the thrower rests on unnamed local sources.
src: quatre personnes ont été tuées et onze autres blessées jeudi 29 janvier 2026 vers 18h30 dans la cité de Sange, territoire d’Uvira, à la suite de l’explosion d’une grenade.
Selon des sources locales, un individu non identifié aurait lancé l’engin explosif en pleine agglomération, provoquant un drame au sein de la population civile.
De son côté, Justin Bitakwira, député national de la circonscription d’Uvira dans le Sud-Kivu, a publiquement accusé le M23 d’être à l’origine de l’explosion qui a coûté la vie à quatre personnes.

r2-G-LOCAL-015.s: Actualite.cd reported, in an article on the Forum des ONGI en RDC condemning drone strikes in Goma, that in January 2026 the office of the international organisation War Child in Masisi, North Kivu, had already suffered significant damage following an air attack in the area.
r2-G-LOCAL-015.n: Single-sentence mention; exact day, attacker and casualties not given. Lead: look for War Child / OCHA access reports. Related packet items: r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/-004 (UNICEF worker killed in Goma, 11 March 2026).
r2-G-LOCAL-015.vn: Removed the acronym FONGI (not in excerpt or title); used the title's name. Sentence follows the FONGI communiqué passage, so attributed to it. Exact day, attacker and casualties not given.
src: En janvier 2026, le bureau de l’ONG internationale War Child à Masisi, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, avait déjà subi d’importants dégâts à la suite d’une attaque aérienne dans la zone.

r2-G-LOCAL-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Forum des ONGI en RDC, in a communiqué condemning drone strikes in Goma, recalled that in 2025, 13 humanitarians were killed in the region against 9 in 2024, and that 626 security incidents targeting them were recorded in 2025 against 428 the previous year, citing OCHA.
r2-G-LOCAL-016.l: eastern DRC (communiqué on Goma, North Kivu)
r2-G-LOCAL-016.x: FONGI citing OCHA: 13 humanitarians killed in 2025 (9 in 2024); 626 security incidents in 2025 (428 in 2024)
r2-G-LOCAL-016.n: 'Cette région' is not defined in the excerpt (the communiqué concerns eastern DRC); geography is therefore approximate. Adds detail to packet items r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/-004.
r2-G-LOCAL-016.vn: Removed the 11 and 12 March dates and the FONGI acronym (not in excerpt); page says 'communiqué ce jeudi 12 mars' on strikes 'le 11 mars'. 'This region' is not defined in the sentence; the communiqué concerns eastern DRC.
src: L’organisation rappelle qu’en 2025, 13 humanitaires ont été tués dans cette région, contre 9 en 2024. Au total, 626 incidents sécuritaires les visant ont été recensés en 2025, contre 428 l’année précédente (OCHA 2025 ; OCHA 2024).

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-001.s: Radio Moto Butembo-Beni reported that about a hundred road users had been blocked at Kanyabayonga, in the south of Lubero, since 3 October 2026 (the page prints 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026') after the closure of the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja, Kanyabayonga-Kibirizi, Kanyabayonga-Rwindi and Kanyabayonga-Vitshumbi axes, a measure it said followed the confirmation of six new Ebola cases in the Kayna and Alimbongo health zones and was confirmed in a communiqué of the AFC/M23 administration that controls the area. It said the AFC/M23 administration at Rutshuru announced the suspension of traffic on the Kanyabayonga–Kikuku, Kanyabayonga–Vitshumbi, Kanyabayonga–Kiwanja and Nyakakoma–Ishasha axes, with only goods vehicles and humanitarian vehicles with the governor's prior authorisation allowed. Users at Kiwanja asked for Ebola prevention measures to be reinforced while allowing traffic to resume.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-001.a: AFC/M23 administration at Rutshuru, as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-001.n: Single local outlet (Radio Moto Oicha/RMBB, Butembo-Beni). Page date taken from URL (8 Oct 2026). The page says 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026' but 3 Oct 2026 is a Saturday: weekday/date inconsistency in the source, kept as printed. The headline links the closure to Ebola at Kayna and Alimbongo; the excerpts do not state the reason for the closure. Shows AFC/M23 holding Kanyabayonga in Oct 2026. Does not duplicate r1-NKS-2026Q3-010 (Enquete.cd 3 Sep Kayna case).
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-001.vn: Original said four axes 'from Kanyabayonga' but the communiqué list includes Nyakakoma-Ishasha; narrowed to the lists as printed and added the stated Ebola reason and the Kiwanja attribution from passages contiguous with the excerpts. excerpt_en flags are translation of French weekday/month words only. Single local outlet: C. The source prints 'vendredi 3 octobre 2026', but 3 October 2026 was a Saturday; the weekday/date mismatch is the source's and is left as printed. The two axis lists in the article (blocked axes vs. communiqué axes) differ; both are given as printed.
src: Une centaine d’usagers sont bloqués depuis vendredi 3 octobre 2026 à Kanyabayonga, au sud de Lubero. Ceci est la conséquence de la fermeture des axes Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja, Kanyabayonga-Kibirizi, Kanyabayonga-Rwindi et Kanyabayonga-Vitshumbi.

Dans son communiqué de ce lundi, l’administration AFC/M23 à Rutshuru annonce la suspension du trafic sur les axes Kanyabayonga-Kikuku, Kanyabayonga-Vitshumbi, Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja et Nyakakoma-Ishasha. Seuls les véhicules de marchandises avec chauffeur et aide-chauffeur, et les véhicules humanitaires avec autorisation préalable du gouverneur, sont autorisés, précise la même source.
Ils demandent le renforcement des mesures de prévention contre Ebola tout en permettant la reprise du trafic.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that after five days of occupation the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army withdrew from Kasugho, an agglomeration of 21 thousand ('21 milles') inhabitants at the foot of the Tayna gorilla reserve, 45 km west of Lubero-centre, and that a resident who requested anonymity said the rebels withdrew without fighting in the night to 7 March and headed for Bunyatenge.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-002.a: M23 rebels, as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-002.n: CONFLICTS with BETO of the same day (separate claim): BETO says the withdrawal followed intense FARDC/VDP-M23 clashes. Night 'jeudi à vendredi' = 6-7 March 2025, computed from the page's own 'vendredi 7 mars'. Capture date (about 2 March) is from search-result snippets only and not retained, so not stated here. Kasugho was not before in the period packet.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-002.vn: Figure written as the page prints it ('21 milles'); weekday wording dropped. 'AP' flags come from 'FPP/AP' in the title (an armed group), a false positive: no agency credit; article signed Claude Sengenya. Conflicting account: BETO the same day says the withdrawal followed intense FARDC/VDP-M23 clashes. The 'without fighting' account rests on one anonymous resident.
src: Après cinq jours d'occupation, les rebelles du M23 soutenus par l'armée rwandaise se sont retirés de Kasugho, importante agglomération de 21 milles habitants située au pied de la réserve des gorilles de Tayna, à 45 kilomètres à l'ouest de Lubero-centre (Nord-Kivu).
Un habitant qui a requis l'anonymat rapporte à ACTUALITE.CD que les rebelles se sont retirés, sans combat, dans la nuit du jeudi à ce vendredi 7 mars, et ont pris la direction de Bunyatenge,

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-003.s: BETO reported that M23 elements withdrew from Friday 7 March from three villages of Lubero territory, Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, about 45 km west of Lubero centre, after intense clashes between the FARDC supported by VDP and the M23; it also said the Ugandan army (UPDF) had for some weeks occupied the neighbouring village since the M23 threatened Lubero-centre.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-003.a: M23; FARDC supported by VDP; UPDF (as named by the source)
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-003.n: Contradicts Actualite.cd 7 Mar ('sans combat'): the two outlets disagree on whether there was fighting before the withdrawal; neither names a commander. The page byline reads 'AFP La Rédaction' (BETO editorial desk, Kinshasa); treat as possible agency relay, unconfirmed. 'Neighbouring village' (UPDF) is not named in the excerpt; Actualite.cd places UPDF at Kagheri 15 km from Kasugho.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-003.vn: All three passages verified on the retained page. Byline decision: the page ends 'Merveilles Kiro' and the style (local witness quotes, VDP term) is local reporting; 'AFP' sits in a header template line beside 'La Rédaction', so originating_source is BETO. Contradicts Actualite.cd of the same day, which reports a withdrawal 'sans combat' per an anonymous resident. BETO's header reads 'AFP La Rédaction', but the article is signed by Merveilles Kiro and carries no AFP dateline or end credit; it is treated as BETO's own reporting, not AFP copy.
src: Les éléments du Mouvement du 23 mars se sont retirés, depuis le matin de vendredi le 7 Mars, de trois villages du territoire de Lubero notamment Kasugho, Katoyo et Kagheri qui sont situés à plus au-moins 45 kilometres à l’Ouest de Lubero centre.

Cela, après d’intenses affrontements qui ont opposés les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) appuyés par les Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie ( VDP) dans ce coin et les rebelles du M23.
Depuis quelques semaines, l’armée Ougandaise (UPDF) occupe le village voisin depuis que le M23 menaçait Lubero-centre.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-004.s: BETO, in a 7 March 2025 article whose byline reads 'AFP La Rédaction Kinshasa' and which is signed Merveilles Kiro, reported that during their withdrawal from Kasugho the M23 rebels were accused of looting, including equipment of the RTCT Kasugho radio and villagers' shops, and quoted a witness as saying they took the new mixer, the computer and the microphones from their base at the radio; Actualite.cd quoted an anonymous resident as saying that before leaving the rebels looted, notably at radio Tayna and in shops.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-004.a: M23 rebels (accused), as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-004.n: Two local outlets agree (Actualite.cd quotes an anonymous resident; BETO a witness). Not independent proof of who looted: both say rebels 'accused'/per resident. perpetrator_alleged: M23.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-004.vn: Witness quote was on the page next to the excerpt; replacement quote extends the excerpt contiguously. Two separately reported local accounts; 'AP' flag is from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Allegation from a witness (BETO) and an anonymous resident (Actualite.cd); BETO's 'RTCT Kasugho' and Actualite.cd's 'radio Tayna' appear to refer to the same Radio Télévision Communautaire Tayna sub-station, per BETO's wording. 2026-10-28: source 0 originating_source edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved. 2026-10-28: source 0 originating_basis edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved. 2026-10-28: statement edited: fact-check fc1: Both pages (7 March 2025) carry every clause. The BETO page's byline credits 'AFP' alongside 'La Rédaction Kinshasa' while the text is signed by Merveilles Kiro; the page does not make clear whether it is AFP copy, so the credit is surfaced rather than resolved.
src: Pendant leur retrait, les rebelles sont accusés avoir commis des actes de pillages. C’est le cas des matériels de la RTCT Kasugho qui ont été emportés. Les rebelles ont aussi pillé des boutiques des villageois.

Le matin, les habitants ont constaté que les rebelles n'étaient plus dans la localité. Mais avant de partir, il y ont commis un pillage, notamment à la radio Tayna et dans des boutiques. Vraiment, Kasugho a été pillé ", regrette cet habitant.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that by the evening it still could not establish who controlled Kasugho: civil society sources spoke of Ugandan UPDF soldiers, a unit of which was deployed on the axis from Lubero centre to Kasugho, while the local authority said Kasugho was controlled by Wazalendo militiamen; Paluku Kuliumbwa said the UPDF soldiers were not yet at Kasugho but at Kagheri, 15 km away, and that the Wazalendo controlled Kasugho. The outlet also reported, per its sources on the spot and confirmed by Paluku Kuliumbwa, the state's delegated official at Kasugho, that Wazalendo who returned after the rebels' withdrawal came across an armed man in a drunken state, taken to be an M23 rebel, and shot him dead.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-005.a: Wazalendo; UPDF; fonctionnaire délégué de l'État Paluku Kuliumbwa (as named by the source)
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-005.n: Two competing accounts of who held Kasugho (civil society: UPDF presence; local state official: Wazalendo) are recorded together; the outlet itself says it could not determine control. The shot man is unnamed; killing of a man described as armed, attributed to Wazalendo by local sources, confirmed by the official. Anonymous/local sourcing.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-005.vn: The excerpt for the killing began 'ils ont croisé' without the subject; the replacement quote adds the contiguous preceding sentence that names the Wazalendo. Weekday dropped. 'AP' flags are from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Control of Kasugho after the withdrawal is disputed (UPDF per civil society; Wazalendo per the local state official); both accounts are kept. The man killed is unnamed and is described only as armed, drunk and 'assimilé' to the M23.
src: Jusque vendredi soir, ACTUALITE.CD peine à noter qui contrôle Kasugho. Si les sources de la société civile parlent des militaires ougandais de UPDF dont une unité est déployée sur l'axe Lubero-centre-Kasugho, l'autorité locale lui précise à ACTUALITE.CD que Kasugho est contrôlé par les miliciens Wazalendo.
"Les militaires de UPDF ne sont pas encore à Kasugho. Ils sont à Kagheri (à 15 Km de Kasugho). Ce sont les Wazalendo qui contrôlent Kasugho", a réagi Paluku Kuliumbwa.

Et sur place, ils ont croisé un homme armé en état d'ivresse, assimilé aux rebelles du M23 et l'ont abattu, selon nos sources sur place. Informations confirmées à ACTUALITE.CD par le fonctionnaire délégué de l'État à Kasugho, Paluku Kuliumbwa.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that Uganda's chief of defence staff, General Muhoozi Kainerugaba, argued in an X post the previous week that the M23 rebels backed by the Rwandan army should fall back 20 km south of their positions in Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho); the outlet noted that some said the M23 was ceding place to the Ugandan army at Kasugho.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-006.l: Lubero territory (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho), North Kivu
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-006.n: Relayed in a news article; the X post itself was not opened (lead for a statement-specific search; posts may be deleted). Date range computed from 'la semaine dernière' relative to Friday 7 March 2025 (week of 24 Feb-2 Mar); exact post date unknown. Possibly already held in the Uganda statements set; check at promote.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-006.vn: Verified on page. Cited to the outlet. 'AP' flag from 'FPP/AP' (false positive). Second-hand: the X post was not seen; Actualite.cd paraphrases it and adds that it aimed 'en vue de libérer les espaces sous influence de l'Ouganda'. Post date is only 'la semaine dernière' relative to 7 March 2025.
src: Bien que des langues affirment qu'ils cèdent place à l'armée ougandaise dont le chef d'État major, le général Muhoozi Kainerugaba, fils de Yoweri Museveni, a argué, dans un post sur X la semaine dernière que les rebelles du M23 soutenus par l'armée rwandaise devraient reculer de 20 Km au Sud de leurs positions actuelles de Lubero (Kitsombiro, Kipese, Kasugho)

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that the rebels kept control of the stretch from Kanyabayonga to Kitsombiro, a distance of nearly 100 km towards Butembo, and were still positioned at Kitsombiro, about 30 km from Lubero-centre, described as their current target.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-007.a: Rebels (M23), as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-007.n: Frontline snapshot, 20 Mar 2025, Actualite.cd. Kanyabayonga/Kirumba/Kayna/Alimbongo were captured BEFORE the window (Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba late June 2024 per Reuters/DW/RFI snippets; Alimbongo 17 Dec 2024 per Radio Okapi headline; Mbingi 18 Dec 2024 per Actualite.cd snippet); in-window control is recorded as 'holds'.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-007.vn: Excerpt verified on page; statement matches; single clause from one source. In-window 'holds' snapshot (20 March 2025). The capture of Kanyabayonga dates from 2024, before the window, and is not stated here.
src: Mais encore que pour Lubero, Kinshasa ne contrôle qu'une partie. Car les rebelles gardent toujours le contrôle de Kanyabayonga à Kitsombiro, une distance de près de 100 Km en direction de Butembo, et sont toujours positionnés à Kitsombiro, près de 30 Km de Lubero-centre, chef-lieu du territoire, leur actuelle cible.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-008.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that the M23 also controlled gold-bearing zones such as Musigha, in the Bunyatenge area of Lubero, forcing the self-proclaimed general Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido, leader of the FPP-AP group, to rally them to 'keep his mining interests'.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-008.a: M23; Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido (FPP-AP), as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-008.n: Local sources, unnamed. Relevant to Bunyatenge front: Actualite.cd on 7 Mar 2025 describes Bunyatenge as FPP/AP stronghold, while this says the M23 held Musigha and Kabido rallied; r1 holds a BETO item on Kabido's arrest in Butembo 12 Jun 2025. Whether 'rallied' means an alliance with M23 is the outlet's local-source claim only.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-008.vn: Excerpt verified on page; attribution to local sources kept. Rests on unnamed local sources; 'de les rallier' is ambiguous and is not evidence of a formal alliance.
src: les rebelles du M23 contrôlent également des zones aurifères comme celle de Musigha, dans la région de Bunyatenge (Lubero), contraignant le général autoproclamé Kasereka Kasiyano Kabido, le leader du controversé groupe FPP-AP de les rallier pour "conserver ses intérêts miniers", indiquent des sources locales à ACTUALITE.CD.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local and security sources, that clashes between the FARDC, backed by Wazalendo fighters, and the M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, resumed at about 4 am on 14 January in the villages of Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, about 60 km from Lubero-Centre, with heavy and light weapons heard as far as Kayna and Kirumba; that other fighting was reported a little further east in the village of Luofu and around the rural area of Kirumba; and that, per security sources, the FARDC, keeping their initial positions, were replying to M23 attacks by shelling rebel positions with artillery and combat helicopters.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009.l: Kamandi Gite, Kibanda, Luofu, Kirumba, Kayna (Lubero), North Kivu
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009.a: FARDC and Wazalendo; M23 supported by Rwanda (as named by the source)
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009.n: Frontline just before the Goma offensive: M23 holds Kayna/Kirumba axis from Dec 2024, FARDC 'keep their initial positions'. No casualty figures in the article. No M23 or Rwanda account found for this date.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009.vn: 'Heard as far as Kayna and Kirumba' was on the page next to the excerpt (replacement quote extends it contiguously); 'west of Kayna' sat in a separate paragraph and was removed; shelling clause attributed to security sources; weekday dropped. No casualty figures given. The shelling account is from security sources (the FARDC side).
src: Des sources locales et sécuritaires rapportent que les affrontements entre les FARDC, appuyés par les combattants Wazalendo, et les rebelles du M23, soutenus par le Rwanda, ont repris vers 4 heures du matin, ce mardi 14 janvier. Ces combats localisés dans les villages de Kamandi Gite et Kibanda, à plus ou moins 60 kilomètres de Lubero-Centre.

Pendant ce temps, d’autres combats étaient signalés un peu plus à l’est dans le village de Luofu et aux environs de la zone rurale de Kirumba. Des sources sécuritaires confirment ces affrontements sans plus de détails.

Elles précisent par ailleurs que les FARDC, qui gardent leurs positions initiales, répliquent vigoureusement aux attaques des rebelles du M23 soutenus par le Rwanda, en pilonnant les positions rebelles à l’artillerie et aux hélicoptères de combats.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-010.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that AFC/M23, reinforced by the RDF, consolidated its positions in Lubero territory in anticipation of future operations and that in mid-October 2025 AFC/M23 and RDF redeployed additional troops from Tchanzu to the Lubero front line along the Kanyabayonga-Kirumba axis, reportedly including recruits who had graduated on 1 October.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-010.a: AFC/M23 and RDF, as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-010.n: Paragraph 49 of S/2025/858; footnote markers 60 and 61 appear inside the excerpt as printed. Source is the UN report cited elsewhere for other paragraphs; this passage is new. Pairs with the 'first defence zone' claim r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-005.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-010.vn: Para. 49 verified verbatim in the retained PDF; statement matches including 'reportedly'.
src: Simultaneously, AFC/M23, reinforced by RDF, consolidated its positions in Lubero territory, in anticipation of future operations. 60 In mid-October, AFC/M23 and RDF redeployed additional troops from Tchanzu to the Lubero front line, along the Kanyabayonga–Kirumba axis, which reportedly included recruits that had graduated on 1 October (see para. 23 above). 61

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-011.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that sources reported on 16 September 2025 the deployment of at least 15 fully loaded trucks with AFC/M23 combatants coming from the AFC/M23-ARC training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga, in Lubero territory, two days after a pass-out ceremony.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-011.a: AFC/M23-ARC, as named by the source
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-011.n: Wording is the report's: it places the Rumangabo camp 'in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga', although Rumangabo is otherwise known as a Rutshuru location; the geography may be a drafting slip, so the destination of the trucks is not stated and the place is entered as printed. 'Sources' are not named. Footnote marker 122 omitted at the end of the excerpt.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-011.vn: Verified verbatim in the retained PDF (followed by footnote 122). Not a duplicate of r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-002 (Uvira/Fizi item from the same report). The report's wording 'training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga' is printed as is and not corrected; Rumangabo is elsewhere known as a Rutshuru location, so the phrase may be a drafting slip and the trucks' origin/destination are ambiguous.
src: Two days after the pass-out ceremony, on 16 September, sources reported the deployment of at least 15 fully loaded trucks with AFC/M23 combatants coming from the AFC/M23-ARC training camp in Rumangabo in Kirumba, near Kanyabayonga, in Lubero territory.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-012.s: The UN Group of Experts reported that Bahati Erasto, North Kivu's AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9 and 11 June, claimed that Lubero, Butembo and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-012.n: Annex 22 of S/2025/858 (sources: UN, intelligence sources, civil society, per footnote). Year 2025 is from the report's reporting period; the excerpt prints '9-11 June' without a year. The Ngaruye 8 September statement from the same annex is already held (r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-004). No AFC/M23 or Kinshasa reaction found to this specific remark.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-012.vn: Annex 22 passage verified verbatim in the retained PDF. A statement by an AFC/M23 official as reported by the Group.
src: Bahati Erasto, North Kivu’s AFC/M23-appointed governor, during visits to Kanyabayonga and Kirumba between 9–11 June, claimed that Lubero, Butembo, and Beni would soon fall under AFC/M23 control. 177

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-013.s: Actualite.cd, relaying MONUSCO, reported that ninety-two defendants were appearing before the Butembo garrison military tribunal sitting at Lubero-Centre, accused of several charges including sexual violence, in hearings launched on 26 June with MONUSCO support and expected to last about ten days; MONUSCO's public information section in Beni said the defendants, including 45 FARDC soldiers and 47 civilians, were prosecuted for rapes, sexual violence, abduction of children and extortion of funds, crimes committed between 2021 and 2024.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-013.a: 45 FARDC soldiers and 47 civilians (accused), per MONUSCO as relayed
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-013.n: The offences date from 2021-2024, before the window; the hearings (26 June 2025) are in the window and are an accountability event for sexual violence in Lubero territory, not a front incident. Perpetrator groups (soldiers and civilians) are as stated by MONUSCO; not attributed to a party. Ligue des femmes du Nord-Kivu coordinator Hélène Makule asked for exemplary sanctions.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-013.vn: Framed as an in-window trial event, not as 2025 offences. Tribunal and Lubero-Centre were in the lead paragraph, now supplied as a contiguous replacement quote; '92' is printed in the title and in words in the excerpts. Procedural stage kept ('poursuivis', 'comparaissent' = prosecuted, appearing). A 2025 trial event: the offences are stated as committed between 2021 and 2024, before the window. Defendants are accused/prosecuted; no verdict is reported.
src: "Quatre-vingt-douze prévenus dont 45 militaires de Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et 47 civils sont poursuivis pour viols, violences sexuelles, enlèvements d’enfants et extorsion de fonds, des crimes commis entre 2021 et 2024", indique de la section de l'information publique de la Monusco à Beni.

Ils sont accusés de plusieurs griefs dont des violences sexuelles. Durant une dizaine de jours, des prévenus auront à se défendre devant les juges lors de ces audiences lancées le 26 juin grâce à l'appui de la mission onusienne (MONUSCO) qui rapporte l'information.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that three displaced adults had died of hunger at Lubero-Centre in the previous month and that the displacement site in the territory office compound faced hunger, lack of access to medical care and a total lack of humanitarian assistance. Kathungu Thamweya Charline, president of the displaced in Lubero commune, told the outlet that five children had also died, that several other displaced people were bedridden in local health facilities without adequate care, and that no humanitarian aid had arrived for more than three months. The outlet said humanitarian organisations could no longer reach the area because of persistent insecurity, and that the displaced were fleeing violent clashes between the FARDC and AFC/M23 in several entities of south Lubero, some coming from areas regularly attacked by other armed groups.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-014.a: Not attributed (conditions); clashes FARDC vs AFC/M23 cited as cause of displacement
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-014.n: Single local source (a displaced-community leader), not independently confirmed. The article also says humanitarian organisations can no longer reach the zone 'because of persistent insecurity, mainly linked to ADF activism'; the 'three months without aid' and the causes are per the source. Dead are unnamed. Links the front displacement to health-care access (no access to medical care).
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-014.vn: 'Died of hunger in the previous month' and 'more than three months' were outside the stored excerpts; replacement quotes extend the excerpts contiguously. 'At the displacement site' for the children's deaths was not stated and was removed. Added the ADF access cause and mixed displacement origins the page states, for balance. The dead are unnamed. The page attributes the lack of humanitarian access mainly to ADF activity ('principalement liée à l’activisme des combattants ADF'), not to the M23 front, and says some displaced come from areas regularly attacked by the ADF and local armed groups; the ADF is named only in passages outside the stored excerpts, so it is given here as a caveat.
src: Ces informations ont été révélées à ACTUALITE.CD cd jeudi 9 octobre par Kathungu Thamweya Charline, présidente des déplacés dans la commune de Lubero. Selon elle, la situation des déplacés est de plus en plus précaire. En plus des trois adultes décédés, cinq enfants ont également perdu la vie.

Le site de déplacés installé dans la concession du bureau du territoire, fait face à une crise aiguë marquée par la faim, l’absence d’accès aux soins médicaux et le manque total d’assistance humanitaire.

Les déplacés actuellement à Lubero Centre fuient les violents affrontements entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et les combattants de l'AFC/M23 dans plusieurs entités du sud du territoire de Lubero.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-015.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the Kayna health zone was affected by the Ebola epidemic with a confirmed case, a 21-year-old man from Butembo intercepted on 2 September at a checkpoint in the Itsu health area; it said this came two months after AFC-M23 had announced the end of the epidemic in the zones under its administration, and that, per the Lubero administrator Kiwewa Mitela, surveillance was reinforced in the Kayna and Kirumba health zones.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-015.l: Kayna health zone, Lubero, North Kivu
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-015.a: Not applicable (epidemic); AFC-M23 administration named as announcing end of epidemic
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-015.n: Adds the AFC-M23 'end of epidemic' announcement and the cross-front surveillance (Kinshasa-appointed administrator for zones that the M23 holds) to r1-NKS-2026Q3-010 (Enquete.cd, 3 Sep, health crisis cell of the rebel administration). Epidemic context only; 'Kayna' here is the health zone. The page title cites 'dix-septième épidémie' in its first line; strain Bundibugyo per same article.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-015.vn: All passages verified on the retained page. The figure flag '7' comes from the outlet name '7sur7.cd' (false positive). The page does not say which authority appointed Kiwewa Mitela; nothing on that is added.
src: Le premier cas confirmé à Kayna concerne un jeune homme de 21 ans, en provenance de Butembo.

Le jeune homme a été intercepté le 2 septembre à un point de contrôle dans l’aire de santé d’Itsu, avant d’être placé en quarantaine. Les résultats de ses échantillons, rendus publics le 3 septembre, se sont révélés positifs au virus Ebola.

À la suite de cette confirmation d'après l'administrateur de Lubero, Kiwewa Mitela, les activités de surveillance communautaire et de sensibilisation ont été renforcées dans les zones de santé de Kayna et Kirumba. Cette nouvelle détection intervient alors que deux mois plus tôt, l’AFC-M23 avait annoncé la fin de l’épidémie dans les zones placées sous son administration.

r2-G-NKN-FRONT-016.s: Actualite.cd reported that in the south of Lubero territory the Kayna health zone faced serious operating difficulties, and that at Kanyabayonga the Vuvogho health centre struggled to give adequate care for lack of funds; the head nurse Paluku Mupanda said its operation rested almost entirely on patients' contributions, a consequence of the absence of partners in the health sector, and the centre regularly ran out of medicines, notably for malaria.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-016.l: Vuvogho health centre, Kanyabayonga (Lubero), North Kivu
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-016.n: Health-access context in an M23-held town (Kanyabayonga) about three weeks after the late-March 2026 pull-back from nearby villages; the article does not mention M23, the front, looting or an attack, so no cause beyond 'absence of partners' is stated. Not categorised health_care_access/attack because no violence is reported.
r2-G-NKN-FRONT-016.vn: 'South Lubero' and the funding shortfall were in the lead paragraph; replacement quote extends the excerpt contiguously. Category set to health_care_access (civilian access to care), with no attack implied. Access-to-care context only: the article does not mention the M23, the front, looting or any attack.
src: Selon l’infirmier titulaire, Paluku Mupanda, le fonctionnement du centre repose presque entièrement sur les contributions des malades, des ressources insuffisantes pour couvrir les besoins essentiels. Ceci est consécutif à l'absence de partenaires intervenant dans le secteur de la santé.
Le centre enregistre régulièrement des ruptures de stocks en médicaments, notamment pour le traitement du paludisme, l’une des pathologies les plus fréquentes dans la région.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi territory passed on Sunday 9 March under the occupation of the M23/AFC rebels, which it described as backed by Rwanda, after intense fighting between those rebels and the FARDC, supported by fighters of the APCLS of Janvier Kalahiri.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001.a: AFC/M23 against FARDC supported by APCLS
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001.n: Radio Okapi 10 Mar 2025 spells the APCLS leader Janvier Kalahiri here and Janvier Karairi in a second article of the same day. Nyabiondo is the chief town of Osso-Banyungu sector (same page). Not in period packet before this claim (packet holds Nyabiondo only for 2026 and 25 Apr 2025).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001.vn: Excerpt matches the page and this event (published 9 Mar 2025). Name Janvier Kalahiri as printed; a second Radio Okapi page of 10 Mar prints 'Janvier Karairi'. Radio Okapi spells the APCLS leader 'Janvier Kalahiri' here and 'Janvier Karairi' in its 10 March article.
src: La cité de Nyabiondo dans le territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu) est passée, ce dimanche 9 mars, sous occupation des rebelles M23/AFC, appuyés par le Rwanda. La chute de Nyabiondo intervient après d’intenses combats entre ces rebelles et les FARDC, appuyées par des combattants de l’APCLS de Janvier Kalahiri.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that the occupation of Nyabiondo on Sunday 9 March caused a massive displacement of inhabitants of at least six villages, who according to local notables took refuge at the Kashebere health centre, while others went towards Kibua and the surrounding bush.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-002.l: Nyabiondo, Kashebere, Kibua; Masisi and Walikale
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-002.n: Two excerpts from the same page. The source lists eight place names after saying "at least six villages". Health-centre use as shelter noted; no attack on it reported.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-002.vn: Supported; the date '9 March' is printed in the page's lead sentence just before the stored excerpt (page-only clause). The page lists eight place names after 'at least six villages'; the statement keeps the source's wording.
src: a entraîné un déplacement massif des habitants d'au moins six villages. Il s’agit notamment des localités de Loashi, Bukombo, Bonde, Nyabiondo, Burore, Kaanja, Bushani et Ngeshe, dans la province du Nord-Kivu.

Ces habitants, dont plusieurs étaient déjà des déplacés, ont trouvé refuge au centre de santé de Kashebere, tandis que d'autres se sont dirigés vers Kibua et dans la brousse environnante, selon des notables locaux.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that several local sources said the M23 rebels were aiming at Walikale-centre in order to reach the Bisiye deposits.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-003.a: M23 rebels (per local sources cited by Radio Okapi)
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-003.n: Alleged aim reported by anonymous local sources; spelling "Bisiye" as printed by Radio Okapi (Bisie mine, Alphamin). Same page says the rebels advanced without fighting to Kaanja, 6 km from Nyabiondo, on Monday 10 March.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-003.vn: Anonymous local sources' allegation of intent; 'M23' is carried by the page title. Spelling 'Bisiye' as printed.
src: Plusieurs sources locales affirment que les rebelles visent Walikale-centre pour accéder aux gisements de Bisiye.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that local actors lamented the absence of humanitarian aid in the area affected by the fighting around Nyabiondo, with the exception of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which continued to support the Nyabiondo hospital.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-004.n: Health-access context: MSF support to Nyabiondo hospital as of 10 Mar 2025, the day after the M23 capture.
src: Cependant, les acteurs locaux déplorent l'absence d'aide humanitaire dans la région affectée par les combats, à l'exception de Médecins sans frontières (MSF), qui continue d'apporter son soutien à l'hôpital de Nyabiondo.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the company Alphamin Bisie Mining (ABM) announced the immediate suspension of its mining operations from Friday 14 March because of growing risks to the safety of its staff.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-005.a: Alphamin Bisie Mining (company communiqué as reported)
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-005.n: Company statement relayed by Actualite.cd (byline Josué Mutanava, Goma). The same page says a reduced staff would remain for minimal services including the hospital.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-005.vn: Company announcement relayed by Actualite.cd (byline Josué Mutanava, Goma); same page quotes the communiqué.
src: la société Alphamin Bisie Mining (ABM) a annoncé la suspension immédiate de ses activités d’exploitation minière à partir de ce vendredi 14 mars, en raison des risques croissants pour la sécurité de son personnel.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that clashes particularly shook the locality of Kibati, where the AFC/M23 and the FARDC-wazalendo coalition fought violently over control of the village, and that, according to its sources, at the end of Thursday 13 March the belligerents shared control of Kibati, the outcome remaining uncertain.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-006.n: Single local-source account in an article about the mining company; earlier than the Kibati items in the period packet (25 Apr 2025 onwards).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-006.vn: Matches the excerpt exactly; unnamed sources, so C.
src: Les affrontements ont particulièrement secoué la localité de Kibati, où l’AFC/M23 et les forces coalisées FARDC-wazalendo se sont livrés à de violents combats, se disputant le contrôle de ce village stratégique. Selon les sources, à la fin de la journée du jeudi 13 mars, les belligérants se sont partagé le contrôle de Kibati, mais l’issue de la confrontation demeure incertaine.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-007.s: Actualite.cd reported, in a headline, that the Kibua general hospital in Walikale territory received medicines six months after its looting by AFC/M23 rebels, and quoted its medical director, Dr Isaac Bihango, as saying the aid would help relaunch medical activity and that medical prescriptions, which had become the system of care, would now be a thing of the past.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-007.a: AFC/M23 rebels (as stated in the headline)
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-007.n: Looting date is not given in the body: "six months" before 26 Sep 2025 points to about March 2025, whereas existing claim r1-HC-NK-2025-009 (Radio Okapi 2 Oct 2025) says massive looting of four Walikale referral hospitals occurred in January: flag as a date discrepancy. Attribution to AFC/M23 appears in the headline and in the sentence calling the MP's base a "victim of pillage de rebelles de l'AFC/M23".
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-007.vn: Supported. Looting date not given in the body; the headline's 'six months' before 26 Sep 2025 points to about March 2025, which conflicts with 'January' in r1-HC-NK-2025-009 (Radio Okapi). Source's wording kept; looting date approximate. Looting date conflict: Actualite.cd's headline says 'six months' before 26 September 2025 (about March 2025); Radio Okapi (r1-HC-NK-2025-009) places the looting of Walikale referral hospitals in January 2025. The perpetrator attribution rests on the headline and on the outlet's narration. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: partially_corroborated; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Walikale : l'hôpital général de Kibua appuyé en médicaments six mois après son pillage par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23

Dr Isaac Bihango, a fait savoir que cette aide vient à point nommé car elle va appuyer le bon fonctionnement de cette structure sanitaire et relancer ainsi les activités médicales. Pour lui, les ordonnances médicales qui étaient devenues le système de prise en charge médicale vont désormais appartenir au passé.

La société civile de Walikale au Nord-Kivu, dénonce le pillage systématique de plusieurs hôpitaux et centres de santé par des éléments présumés de la rébellion M23 entre le 3 et le 4 avril 2025. Ces actes ont particulièrement touché la zone de santé de Kibua, où l’hôpital général de référence et le centre de santé de Mungazi ont été dépouillés

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Kibua general hospital released 13 people who had been blocked at the hospital for failure to pay their bills after treatment, thanks to the medicines aid received on 26 September.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-008.n: Cost barrier / detention of patients for unpaid bills, not conflict violence; recorded as a civilian access-to-care lead. Not attributed to any armed actor.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-008.vn: Supported; the 26 September date is on the page (page-only clause).
src: hôpital général de Kibua a libéré 13 personnes qui étaient bloquées à l'hôpital faute de paiement de leurs factures après le traitement grâce à cet appui.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local civil society, that displaced people and their host families in Walikale territory received no humanitarian assistance and that for nearly four months several health structures in the region had been deprived of supplies of medicines and other essential inputs, a crisis it attributed to instability caused by the M23's occupation of several North Kivu localities.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-009.n: The causal sentence is the outlet's own wording, not attributed to civil society. Related to existing r1-HC-NK-2025-009.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-009.vn: Supported; causal sentence is the outlet's narration and the statement says so.
src: Selon la société civile locale, les populations déplacées par le conflit ainsi que leurs familles d’accueil ne bénéficient d’aucune assistance humanitaire. Depuis près de quatre mois, plusieurs structures sanitaires de la région sont privées d’approvisionnements en médicaments et autres intrants essentiels.
Cette crise résulte de l’instabilité sécuritaire provoquée par l’occupation de plusieurs localités du Nord-Kivu par la rébellion du M23.
Fiston Misona, président de la société civile de Walikale, tire une nouvelle fois la sonnette d’alarme auprès des autorités et des organisations humanitaires

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-010.s: The ICRC reported, in a press release on access to health care in the Kivus, that a man identified as Shukuru said he was wounded at Pinga in July in Walikale territory and was evacuated to Beni for care, at the Beni general referral hospital about 300 km from where he was wounded.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-010.n: Year of the July injury is inferred from the 2025 release ("Depuis le début de l’année"); the excerpt does not print the year. The name "Shukuru" is given as a first name only and the release does not say whether it is a pseudonym. Weapon type and perpetrator not stated.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-010.vn: Removed the inferred year '(2025)': the quote does not print it (release dated 7 Oct 2025). The release's pseudonym footnote ('[1] Prénom d’emprunt') marks 'docteur Pierre', not Shukuru. The year of the July injury is inferred from the release date (7 October 2025); the quote says only 'July'.
src: J’étais blessé à Pinga au mois de juillet, dans le territoire de Walikale, et j’ai été évacué à Beni pour y recevoir des soins », raconte Shukuru, soigné à l’hôpital général de référence (HGR) de Beni au Nord-Kivu, soit à environ 300 km du lieu où il a été blessé.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the M23 rebellion was intensifying its campaign to recruit young people in North Kivu for what it calls the Congolese revolutionary army (ARC), through a recruitment and mobilisation committee, and that the campaign also took place in the town of Kitshanga, Bukoma groupement, which the article places in Rutshuru territory.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-011.n: The source describes voluntary-style recruitment through ideological sessions; it does not say it is forced. Radio Okapi places Kitshanga in Rutshuru territory; Kitshanga is commonly placed in Masisi territory (flag for gazetteer). Territory field set to Masisi on that basis, to be verified.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-011.vn: Supported; the committee detail is on the page outside the stored excerpts. Radio Okapi places Kitshanga in Rutshuru; territory field kept as Masisi with the source's wording noted. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: Radio Okapi, 29 Apr 2025, carries every clause in its own voice, including Kitshanga 'en territoire de Rutshuru' as the statement flags. The recruitment and mobilisation committee clause was on no stored excerpt; that passage is added.
src: La rébellion du M23 intensifie sa campagne de recrutement des jeunes au Nord-Kivu, pour le compte de ce qu’elle appelle armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC).

La campagne de recrutement a lieu également dans les territoires. Notamment dans le territoire de Nyiragongo, chefferie Bukumu, et dans la cité de Kitshanga, groupement Bukoma, en territoire de Rutshuru.
Une structure dénommée comité de recrutement et de mobilisation est à pied d’œuvre à travers les quartiers de la ville de Goma et les localités des territoires de la province.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on Monday 28 April by an anonymous local human rights organisation, PARECO-FF Wazalendo fighters led by the militia chief Kigingi Jean de Dieu were accused of abuses against civilians in Katoyi sector, Masisi territory, including setting up a parallel fiscal and judicial administration and levying illegal taxes, with the organisation's remarks said to be corroborated by local administrative sources.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-012.a: PARECO-FF (Coalition des patriotes résistants congolais - Force de frappe), led by Kigingi Jean de Dieu
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-012.n: Anonymous NGO communiqué corroborated, per the outlet, by local administrative sources. Three excerpts of one page. Party account of PARECO-FF: no statement found.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-012.vn: Allegations attributed to the anonymous NGO as relayed by Radio Okapi; name as printed.
src: Dans un communiqué publié ce lundi 28 avril, une organisation locale de défense des droits humains, qui a souhaité garder l’anonymat pour des raisons de sécurité,

Selon cette organisation, dont les propos sont corroborés par des sources administratives locales du secteur de Katoyi, au moins dix formes de violations des droits humains auraient été perpétrées par le groupe armé PARECO-FF, dirigé par le chef milicien Kigingi Jean de Dieu.

Parmi ces abus figurent l’instauration d’une administration fiscale et judiciaire parallèle imposée par cette milice dans le secteur de Katoyi. Le groupe, qui se revendique membre de la coalition VDP/Wazalendo, impose des taxes illégales dans tous les villages

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to the same anonymous local human rights organisation and administrative sources, the Katoyi sector office was reportedly vandalised and looted at the beginning of April by Kigingi's militiamen.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-013.n: Conditional ("aurait") and anonymous source; date is "early April" (month precision).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-013.vn: Restored the source's conditional ('aurait même été vandalisé et pillé').
src: Le bureau du secteur de Katoyi aurait même été vandalisé et pillé au début du mois d’avril par les miliciens de Kigingi, selon ces mêmes sources.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a memorandum addressed on Friday 17 October to the military and civil authorities of North Kivu, notables of the Bahunde chiefdom and Osso-Banyungu sector in Masisi territory accused three Wazalendo factions, the UPDC of Noah Maachano and PARECO-FF factions commanded by Kigingi Jean de Dieu and Mutayomba Jam's, of abuses against civilians, listing disrespect for customary authority, illegal taxes on goods and illegal exploitation of some mining sites.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-014.l: Ufamandu 1er (Bahunde chiefdom) and Nyamaboko 1er groupement, Osso-Banyungu sector, Masisi
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-014.a: UPDC (Noah Maachano); PARECO-FF factions of Kigingi Jean de Dieu and Mutayomba Jam’s
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-014.n: Notables' memorandum relayed by Radio Okapi; no response of the named groups found. Three excerpts of one page. Financial extortion at roadblocks (1,000 to over 2,000 Congolese francs) also described on the page.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-014.vn: Dropped 'systematic' (the page's 'exactions systématiques' is in a conditional sentence, not the accusation itself); the page prints the name with a typographic apostrophe, 'Mutayomba Jam’s'.
src: Dans un mémorandum adresse vendredi 17 octobre aux autorités militaires et civiles de la province du Nord-Kivu, certains notables de la chefferie des Bahunde et du secteur Osso-Banyungu, territoire de Masisi accusent trois factions des miliciens Wazalendo d'exactions contre des civils.

Le groupe armé Union des patriotes et démocrates pour la défense du Congo (UPDC), de Noah Maachano, ainsi que les factions de la Coalition des patriotes résistants congolais (PARECO-FF), commandées respectivement par Kigingi Jean de Dieu et Mutayomba Jam’s, sont particulièrement pointés du doigt.
ils énumèrent le non-respect du pouvoir coutumier local, la perception de taxes illégales sur les marchandises, l’exploitation illégale de certains sites miniers.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga (AFC/M23) attacked from the morning the positions of the Wazalendo of the ANCDH at Kalungu, after reinforcing their troops in men and equipment during the past week; the article places the fighting on the Tuesday and is dated Wednesday 9 July.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015.l: Kalungu and Kinyana, Bashali Mokoto groupement, Masisi
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015.a: AFC/M23 (men of Corneille Nangaa and Sultani Makenga per the source) against Nyatura Wazalendo of the ANCDH led by Jean-Marie Bonané
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015.n: Date computed from weekday ("mardi") and the 9 July publication date. ANCDH is "Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains" (same page, led by Jean-Marie Bonané). Existing claim r1-NKW-2025H2-013 mentions the ANCDH for November only.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-015.vn: Supported; AFC/M23 and the 9 July date are on the page outside the stored excerpt. Date 8 Jul computed from 'mardi': approximate.
src: Selon des sources locales, les hommes de Corneille Nangaa et Sultani Makenga ont attaqué dès le matin les positions des Wazalendo de l’ANCDH à Kalungu, après avoir renforcé leurs troupes en hommes et en matériel au cours de la semaine dernière.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-016.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 rebels temporarily dislodged Nyatura fighters from Bupfuhi, a locality that was said to have been burned.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-016.n: Conditional ("aurait été incendiée"); the source does not say who burned it. Date computed from "mardi".
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-016.vn: Conditional kept; no arsonist named. Date computed from 'mardi': approximate.
src: Les rebelles ont temporairement délogé les combattants Nyatura de Bupfuhi, une localité qui aurait été incendiée, toujours selon les mêmes sources.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-017.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local notables, that between 5 a.m. and 8 a.m. AFC-M23 fought the Wazalendo of the ANCDH of Jean-Marie Bonane on the hills overlooking the villages concerned, and that residents of Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri and Bibwe were seen with their luggage moving towards Bulende, Kasopo and Lukweti.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-017.l: Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri, Bibwe; Bashali Mokoto, Masisi
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-017.n: The page spells the leader "Jean-Marie Bonane" here and "Bonané" in the 9 July article. Date 21 Oct 2025 is the publication date ("ce mardi").
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-017.vn: Supported; spelling 'Bonane' as printed on this page.
src: Selon certaines notabilités locales, entre 5 heures du matin et 8 heures locales, des combats ont opposé l’AFC-M23 aux Wazalendo de l'Alliance des nationalistes congolais pour la défense des droits humains (ANCDH) de Jean-Marie Bonane dans les collines surplombant ces villages.

Certains habitants des villages Kinyana, Nyabikeri, Rwankeri, Bibwe et leurs environs ont été vus avec leurs bagages en train de se déplacer, ce mardi dans la matinée, vers Bulende, Kasopo et Lukweti.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-018.s: Radio Okapi reported that the day before, attacks by Wazalendo on the town of Nyabiondo in Masisi caused the death of a child and injured four other people.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-018.x: Radio Okapi: 1 child killed, 4 other people wounded
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-018.n: Child victim unnamed in the source. "La veille" is relative to the 21 Oct 2025 article. Wazalendo faction not specified. Child unnamed in the source (not listed in victims_named).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-018.vn: Removed the computed date from the statement; 'la veille' relative to the 21 Oct 2025 article, so the 20 Oct date field is approximate. Child unnamed.
src: La veille, des attaques des Wazalendo sur la cité de Nyabiondo, toujours à Masisi , ont causé le décès d’un enfant alors que quatre autres personnes ont été blessées.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-019.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that hundreds of displaced families who had fled recent fighting between AFC-M23 and Wazalendo groups were living in alarming conditions at Mweso, in schools and churches, without humanitarian assistance.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-019.n: The page says they fled villages around the Ngeri tea garden (Kashanje, Bweru, Kivuye) in Masisi and Rutshuru; the displaced are concentrated in the compound of the Institut technique médical de Mweso. Number undetermined ("thousands" estimated).
src: Des centaines de familles déplacées, contraintes de fuir les récents affrontements entre les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 et les groupes armés Wazalendo, vivent dans des conditions alarmantes à Mweso dans le groupement Bashali Mokoto, territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Selon des sources locales, ces personnes hébergées dans des écoles et des églises, sont vulnérables et totalement dépourvues d’assistance humanitaire.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-020.s: Radio Okapi reported that in a communiqué made public on Monday the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army of using heavy artillery and drones against its positions from 3 a.m. until late in the evening.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-020.n: Cited only for what AFC-M23 said. Date computed from the weekday ("lundi") in an article of Wed 29 Oct that places the fighting on "la veille" (28 Oct); Actualite.cd Facebook snippet also says Tuesday 28 October. Day discrepancy to be resolved. The communiqué itself was not found.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-020.vn: Party statement as relayed by Radio Okapi; communiqué not seen. The Monday (27 Oct) communiqué sits awkwardly with fighting 'la veille' (28 Oct) of the 29 Oct article: date approximate, discrepancy noted. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué to 'lundi' but places the main fighting 'la veille' of its Wednesday 29 October article; the day is unresolved.
src: Dans un communiqué rendu public lundi, l’AFC-M23 accuse l’armée congolaise d’avoir mis à contribution une artillerie lourde et des drones contre leurs positions depuis 3 heures du matin jusque tard dans la soirée.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-021.s: Radio Okapi reported that other sources indicated that, after the fighting at Kibati, the Wazalendo reportedly withdrew to Mikumbi and Miba, 3 km further west, leaving the area in the hands of the AFC/M23 rebels.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-021.l: Kibati, Mikumbi, Miba; Luberike groupement, Walikale
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-021.n: Competing account ("d'autres sources") with no casualty figures ("Aucun bilan"). Later Kibati items in the packet: 10 and 18 Sep 2026.
src: D’autres sources indiquent qu’après ces affrontements, les Wazalendo se seraient repliés vers Mikumbi et Miba, à 3 kilomètres plus à l’ouest de Kibati, laissant la zone entre les mains des rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-022.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the shooting at Kibati had stopped after a day of fighting reported on Thursday in the area, and that the FARDC and wazalendo maintained their presence in the centre of Kibati while the AFC/M23 rebels controlled the hills overlooking the town.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-022.n: Between existing claims r1-NKW-2026H2-012 (10 Sep) and -013 (18 Sep, centre of Kibati back under AFC/M23 control). Same page: traffic suspended on the Kashebere-Mungazi road.
src: Selon des sources d’ACTUALITE.CD, les tirs ont cessé après une journée de combats signalés jeudi dans cette zone. À ce stade, les FARDC et les wazalendo maintiennent leur présence dans le centre de Kibati, tandis que les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 contrôlent les collines surplombant l’agglomération.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-023.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing civilian and military sources, that on the morning of Monday 28 September two positions held by wazalendo fighters at Kaleta and Bitoyi, in the Ufamandu groupements of Masisi territory, were targeted at about 7 a.m. by air strikes attributed to the AFC/M23 rebels.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-023.l: Kaleta and Bitoyi, Ufamandu groupements, Masisi
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-023.n: Drone use (conditional) and the absence of any toll are stated elsewhere on the page. Journal de Kinshasa carries the same report. AFC/M23 account: none found.
src: Deux positions occupées par des combattants wazalendo ont été visées le matin de lundi 28 septembre par des frappes aériennes attribuées aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans le territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu, d'après des sources civiles et militaires. Les attaques ont ciblé les villages de Kaleta et Bitoyi, dans les groupements d’Ufamandu, vers 7 heures locales, précisent ces sources.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-024.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that at Burungu, in the Bashali chiefdom, at least eight civilians were reportedly killed and six others wounded on Saturday evening, a toll that could not be independently confirmed at the time of publication.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-024.x: Radio Okapi (local sources): at least 8 civilians killed, 6 wounded; unconfirmed
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-024.n: Date computed from "samedi soir" and the Monday 28 Sep 2026 publication date. Context: fighting around Miko near Remeka on 26 and 27 Sep. No perpetrator given. Burungu not in period packet.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-024.vn: Figures printed as words; unconfirmed; no perpetrator given. Date computed from 'samedi soir': approximate.
src: À Burungu, dans la chefferie des Bashali, au moins huit civils auraient été tués et six autres blessés samedi soir, selon des sources locales. Ce bilan n’a pas pu être confirmé indépendamment au moment de la publication de cet article.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-025.s: Journal de Kinshasa reported, citing local and military sources, that for the first time since the start of fighting in the area the town of Pinga in Walikale territory was targeted on Monday 28 September 2026 by an attack attributed to the AFC/M23, drones targeting FARDC positions and causing panic and a temporary suspension of activities in the town.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-025.n: Single outlet; photo credit "Média Congo" on the page (not stated as the text source). The page says no official toll was available. A YouTube snippet (not opened) claims at least 5 Republican Guard soldiers were killed in a drone strike on 28 Sept at Pinga: unverified, listed in gaps. Radio Okapi item of 28 Sep covers Masisi strikes only.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-025.vn: Supported; single outlet (byline Cyntiche PANDI; photo credit Média Congo).
src: Pour la première fois depuis le début des combats dans cette zone, la cité stratégique de Pinga, dans le territoire de Walikale (Nord-Kivu), a été visée lundi 28 septembre 2026 par une attaque attribuée aux rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

Selon des sources locales et militaires, des drones ont ciblé des positions des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), provoquant un mouvement de panique et la suspension temporaire des activités dans la cité.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-026.s: Journal de Kinshasa reported that the attack on Pinga came only 24 hours after the FARDC, supported by wazalendo, retook several positions around Mindjendje, notably Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa and Luola.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-026.l: Mindjendje area: Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa, Luola; Walikale
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-026.n: Date derived from "24 hours before" the 28 Sep attack (approximate). Retaken from whom is not stated in the excerpt; later Actualite.cd/Congo Quotidien items (27 Oct 2026) report renewed FARDC-FRN fighting at Luola and the Tchad hill.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-026.vn: Supported; date derived from '24 heures': approximate; from whom retaken not stated.
src: L’attaque contre Pinga intervient seulement 24 heures après la reprise par les FARDC, appuyées par les wazalendo, de plusieurs positions autour de Mindjendje , notamment Tchad, Kahongoboka, Kukibingu, Bubolwa et Luola

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-027.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting began on Saturday 24 October when the army and wazalendo attacked the positions of the FRN rebels on the Rushihe hill overlooking Katobo (Banamulindwa, Kisimba groupement, Walikale), and that the government coalition dislodged the rebels and took control of the position.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-027.l: Rushihe hill, Katobo, Banamulindwa locality, Kisimba groupement, Walikale
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-027.a: FARDC supported by wazalendo against FRN rebels
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-027.n: "FRN" is not expanded on the page; this is not AFC/M23. Existing claim r1-ATR-NK-2026-007 records M23 retaking Katobo on 26 May 2026. Check unit roster for FRN.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-027.vn: Supported; FRN is not expanded on the page.
src: Selon des sources d’ACTUALITE.CD, les combats ont éclaté le samedi 24 octobre, lorsque l'armée et les wazalendo ont lancé une attaque contre les positions des rebelles du FRN établies sur cette hauteur. À l’issue des affrontements, la coalition gouvernementale a réussi à déloger les rebelles et à prendre le contrôle de cette position stratégique.

Un calme précaire s’observe ce lundi 26 octobre à Katobo, dans la localité de Banamulindwa (groupement Kisimba), dans le territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu, après des affrontements ayant opposé les rebelles du FRN aux FARDC appuyées par les wazalendo sur la colline stratégique de Rushihe, qui surplombe le village de Katobo.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-028.s: Actualite.cd reported that after the fighting at Rushihe a precarious calm was observed on Monday 26 October at Katobo, and that gunfire from heavy and light weapons caused displacement, with several Katobo inhabitants fleeing to Ihula and others taking refuge in the forest.
src: Un calme précaire s’observe ce lundi 26 octobre à Katobo, dans la localité de Banamulindwa (groupement Kisimba), dans le territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu, après des affrontements ayant opposé les rebelles du FRN aux FARDC appuyées par les wazalendo sur la colline stratégique de Rushihe, qui surplombe le village de Katobo.
Les échanges de tirs d’armes lourdes et légères ont provoqué un déplacement de la population. Plusieurs habitants de Katobo ont fui vers Ihula, tandis que d’autres se sont réfugiés dans la forêt

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029.s: Actualite.cd reported that a new landslide on Tuesday 3 March 2026 at the Kasasa mining site in the Rubaya mining zone (Masisi) reportedly cost the lives of more than a hundred people, mostly artisanal diggers, and said it came about a month after a collapse on 28 January 2026 at the same site that had killed more than 400 people, not counting the missing.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029.a: not applicable (mine collapse; Rubaya under AFC/M23 control)
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029.x: Actualite.cd 4 Mar 2026: more than 100 dead on 3 March (provisional); more than 400 dead on 28 January
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029.n: Figures conflict with existing claims on the January collapse (Actualite.cd 31 Jan 2026: at least 226 dead on Thursday 29 January; r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-018): this page gives 28 January and "more than 400". TV5Monde snippets (not opened) refer to a 3 March slide with "200 dead, including 70 children" per the DRC government; not cited. For the discrepancy register.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029.vn: Tolls kept per source and provisional ('aurait'). Conflicts with an existing Actualite.cd claim of at least 226 dead on 29 January (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-018).
