Toll and date of the January collapse differ between Actualite.cd reports: more than 400 dead on 28 January (this page) vs at least 226 dead on 29 January (31 January report).
src: Un nouvel éboulement s’est produit ce mardi 3 mars 2026 sur le site minier de Kasasa, dans la zone minière de Rubaya (territoire de Masisi) au Nord-Kivu. L’incident aurait coûté la vie à plus d’une centaine de personnes, en majorité des creuseurs artisanaux qui exploitent le coltan dans cette mine, selon les différentes sources.

Ce nouveau drame intervient à peine un mois après une autre catastrophe survenue le 28 janvier 2026, sur le même site de Kasasa, où un éboulement avait coûté la vie à plus de 400 personnes, sans compter les disparus.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-030.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Rubaya mining zone, rich in coltan, cassiterite, gold and tourmaline, remained under the control of the M23 rebels.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-030.n: Holds-status for the frontline layer; the page adds that the M23 is "soutenu par le Rwanda selon plusieurs rapports des autorités congolaises et des experts onusiens" (outside the stored excerpt). The Amnesty 21 Sep 2026 briefing also describes Rubaya as M23-controlled.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-030.vn: Removed the publication date '4 March 2026' from the statement (shown with the source).
src: La zone minière de Rubaya, riche en coltan, cassitérite, or et tourmaline, demeure sous le contrôle des rebelles du M23

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-031.s: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that Katoyi (Gatoyi) has changed hands repeatedly since late 2025: AFC-M23 captured it in November 2025, FARDC and PARECO-Wazalendo forces retook it in December, and further fighting returned control to AFC-M23 around February and March 2026.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-031.n: Rwanda-aligned outlet: usable as "KT Press says". Existing claim r1-NKS-2026Q4-010 has Radio Okapi on the FARDC-Wazalendo retaking Katoyi centre on 6 Oct 2026. The page presents the Aug 2026 advance as targeting the FDLR (pro-AFC-M23 sources); other local reporting calls it clashes with FARDC-Wazalendo.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-031.vn: Rwandan state-aligned outlet: partisan, usable only as 'KT Press says'. KT Press is a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; its account is recorded as the outlet's claim only.
src: Katoyi, sometimes rendered as Gatoyi, is a separate but strategically connected area. It has changed hands repeatedly since late 2025. AFC-M23 captured it in November 2025 before FARDC and PARECO-Wazalendo forces retook it in December. Further fighting returned control to AFC-M23 around February and March 2026.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-032.s: KT Press (Rwanda) reported that by 24-25 August 2026 the AFC-M23-appointed administrator of Masisi had visited Remeka, taken part in community work and launched maintenance of the Ngungu-Remeka road, and had urged remaining Wazalendo fighters to join AFC-M23.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-032.n: Partisan, Rwanda-aligned outlet; the administrator is not named on the page. Complements existing r1-NKW-2026H2-006 (Remeka retaken 20 Aug).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-032.vn: Partisan outlet; administrator unnamed on the page.
src: By August 24–25, the AFC-M23-appointed administrator of Masisi had visited Remeka, participated in community work and launched maintenance of the Ngungu-Remeka road. He called for peaceful coexistence and urged remaining Wazalendo fighters to join AFC-M23.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-033.s: Kivu Morning Post, relaying MSF, reported that MSF had documented many cases of sexual violence against women, girls and children in eastern DRC since early January 2025, and had collected testimonies in Goma, Sake, Rutshuru and Masisi, in which victims said they were forced at gunpoint.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-033.a: not attributed by the source (armed men)
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-033.n: MSF itself (not fetched) is the originating source; KMP is a relay. Excerpts are two sentences of the same page. South Kivu figure (more than 700 victims treated by MSF since the start of 2025) is on the page but outside the excerpts. Page does not date the underlying MSF release (30 Jul 2025 is the KMP URL date). Relates to existing r1-SV-NK-2025-009 (MSF, 7,400 victims Jan-Apr).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-033.vn: KMP relays MSF (originating source). The page prints 'Ruthsuru' (typo for Rutshuru). Relay of MSF; not independent of other MSF-sourced claims (e.g. r1-SV-NK-2025-009). The page spells the place 'Ruthsuru'. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: De nombreux cas de violences sexuelles contre des femmes, filles et enfants de l’est de la RDC ont été documentés par MSF depuis début janvier 2025. Cette région est en proie à l’insécurité en raison des combats entre les FARDC et les rebelles du M23. MSF a recueilli des témoignages à Goma, Sake, Ruthsuru et Masisi.
Les victimes ont raconté avoir été contraintes sous la menace d’armes à feu.
Au Nord-Kivu à Goma, dans les territoires de Rutshuru, Masisi et Walikale

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-034.s: Amnesty International reported that one interviewee said he could hear the screams of detainees being tortured inside the shipping containers that M23 uses as detention cells near the Rubaya mine.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-034.n: Documented investigation by a major NGO, but the interview was anonymous (names changed); date of the detentions is not given, so date is the briefing date (reported 2026-09-21). Amnesty states that neither M23 nor Rwandan government officials responded to its request for comment. Complements existing r1-ATR-NK-2026-019/-020 (killings; ndake pit).
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-034.vn: Narrowed to the new element: the container cells themselves are already in verified r2-G-UNDOCS-012 (same Amnesty page). Amnesty's finding from an interviewee's account; date is the briefing date. Same Amnesty briefing as r2-G-UNDOCS-012 (container cells, ndake); neither M23 nor Rwanda responded to Amnesty.
src: Near the Rubaya mine, M23 uses three shipping containers as detention cells. One interviewee said he could hear the screams of detainees as they are being tortured inside the containers.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-035.s: Amnesty International reported that seven miners recounted how M23 detained miners and threatened to send them to M23 military training centres if they failed to pay ransoms for their release.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-035.l: Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu) mining sites
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-035.n: The English release says "seven miners"; the French full report ties it to Lomera and Rubaya. Date precision: briefing date (reported 2026-09-21). Not a confirmed case of forced enlistment: the threat is of being sent to training centres.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-035.vn: Supported verbatim; a threat, not a confirmed enlistment. Same Amnesty briefing as r2-G-UNDOCS-011..014 (not independent of it).
src: Seven miners recounted how M23 detained miners and threatened to send them to M23 military training centres if they failed to pay ransoms for their release.

r2-G-NKW-MASISI-036.s: Amnesty International reported that, in Rubaya, miners said Rwandans play a dual role as civilian miners or mineshaft managers but also take part in hostilities when needed alongside M23 fighters.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-036.a: Rwandans present at Rubaya (per miners), alongside M23
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-036.n: Testimony of unnamed miners summarised by Amnesty; Rwandan government response: Amnesty says none received. Rwanda account: no statement found.
r2-G-NKW-MASISI-036.vn: Miners' accounts reported by Amnesty; graded as r2-G-UNDOCS-014 (same briefing). Rwanda: Amnesty says no response.
src: In Rubaya, miners said Rwandans play a dual role as civilian miners or mineshaft managers but also take part in hostilities when needed alongside M23 fighters.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting broke out on Sunday after an attack on AFC/M23 rebels in the village of Bangwi, where intense clashes lasted all day, causing mass displacement of the population towards Swima and Mboko.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-001.l: Makobola, Bangwi, Swima (Fizi/Uvira territories), South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-001.a: AFC/M23 (attacked, per Actualite.cd's sources; attacker not named in the passage)
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-001.n: Date: article published Mon 22 Dec 2025; 'dimanche' = 21 Dec 2025 (date computed from weekday and publication date). Kivutimes (separate claim) says the fighting began 'samedi 21 décembre 2025' (21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday): weekday/date mismatch in that outlet. Marine-unit detail is in a separate claim.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-001.vn: Narrowed to the excerpt: the Monday marine-unit clause is claim 1; names not printed in the excerpt (FARDC, wazalendo, M'massa Etùba) removed from entities_named; date narrowed to the Sunday. 'Dimanche' in an article dated Monday 22 Dec 2025 is read as 21 Dec 2025. Kivutimes (separate claim) dates the start to 'samedi 21 décembre 2025' (21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday) and says the FARDC launched the offensive on Bangwi.
src: Selon nos sources, les combats ont éclaté dimanche après une attaque contre les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 dans le village de Bangwi où d’intenses affrontements ont duré toute la journée provoquant le déplacement massif de la population vers Swima et Mboko.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that the AFC/M23 had deployed a marine unit on Lake Tanganyika that took part in the fighting at Makobola and its surroundings.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002.l: Makobola, Lake Tanganyika, Fizi/Uvira territories, South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002.a: AFC/M23 'marins' (marine unit), as Actualite.cd's sources describe it
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002.n: Single-source claim about a lake-borne unit; Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025) says only that the rebels used a speedboat ('hors-bord') to shell the area.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-002.vn: Excerpt says 'les rebelles'; the AFC/M23 attribution and Makobola are in the title and the next sentence of the page. AFC/M23 is printed in the title. Single outlet citing unnamed sources. Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025) says only that the rebels used a speedboat ('hors-bord') to shell the area.
src: Selon les sources d’ ACTUALITE.CD , les rebelles ont déployé une unité marine sur le lac Tanganyika et cette dernière participe également aux combats.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that, despite FARDC reinforcements sent to the wazalendo from Kalemie, the town of Mboko, located 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the control of AFC-M23 fighters.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-003.n: CONFLICT: Kivutimes, 23 Dec 2025 (separate claim), says Mboko 'reste sous la menace directe' of AFC-M23 fighters, i.e. threatened not held. Radio Okapi 15 Dec 2025 reports AFC/M23 occupied 'Makobola 2'. Control of Mboko is unresolved; treat as contested/unverified.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-003.vn: Excerpt exact and says what the statement says; the conflict with Kivutimes is surfaced, not resolved. CONTESTED, unresolved: Kivutimes (23 Dec 2025, separate claim) says Mboko 'reste sous la menace directe' of AFC-M23 fighters, i.e. threatened, not held. The two accounts are kept side by side.
src: Malgré les renforts des FARDC aux wazalendo en provence de Kalemie, la cité de Mboko située à 55 km au nord de la ville de Baraka reste toujours sous contrôle des combattants de l’AFC-M23.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-004.s: Kivutimes reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC-M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo, around Makobola since 'samedi 21 décembre 2025', and that, per the outlet, military authorities had not yet communicated an official casualty toll while families fled explosive devices.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-004.n: Kivutimes (Uvira-based local outlet) calls 21 Dec 2025 a Saturday; it was a Sunday. Actualite.cd says fighting began 'dimanche'. Date range kept. Kivutimes attributes Rwandan-force support to 'international actors' only.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-004.vn: Both excerpts exact; quoted date kept as printed. Kivutimes prints 'samedi 21 décembre 2025'; 21 Dec 2025 was a Sunday (Actualite.cd says the fighting began 'dimanche'). The weekday/date mismatch is the outlet's and is left as printed. Kivutimes attributes Rwandan support to AFC-M23 to 'les acteurs internationaux' only.
src: Depuis le samedi 21 décembre 2025, de violents combats opposent les rebelles de l’AFC-M23, soutenu par les forces de défense rwandaises selon les acteurs internationaux, aux Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC), soutenues par les résistants patriotes « Wazalendo ».

Pour l’heure, les autorités militaires n’ont pas encore communiqué de bilan humain officiel, mais la crise humanitaire s’aggrave avec des familles entières désormais sans abri, fuyant la trajectoire des engins explosifs.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-005.s: Kivutimes reported that the town of Mboko, about 55 km north of Baraka, remained under the direct threat of AFC-M23 fighters, who were maintaining pressure on that axis.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-005.n: Contradicts the Actualite.cd 22 Dec 2025 line that Mboko 'reste sous contrôle' of AFC-M23.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-005.vn: Excerpt exact and matches the statement. CONTESTED, unresolved: Actualite.cd (22 Dec 2025, separate claim) says Mboko 'reste toujours sous contrôle' of AFC-M23 fighters. The two accounts are kept side by side.
src: La cité de Mboko, carrefour stratégique situé à environ 55 km au nord de la ville de Baraka, reste sous la menace directe des combattants de l’AFC-M23, qui maintiennent leur pression sur cet axe vital du Sud-Kivu.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent fighting broke out on Friday around Minembwe between Twirwaneho fighters allied to AFC-M23 and Wazalendo militiamen integrated into the Congolese army, and that the Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke (FABB) of General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito said they were continuing to defend their positions.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.l: Minembwe; Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (high plateaux), Fizi territory, South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.a: Twirwaneho/AFC-M23; Wazalendo (FABB, General Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito)
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.x: no casualties reported by the source
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.n: Wazalendo account only; no Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 account found on this date (see gaps). Roster lead: FABB, Gen. Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito (Biloze Bishambuke).
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-006.vn: The spokesperson's allegation is split out to claim 6 so it is not merged into the outlet's narration; the date number is left to the date field (not in any excerpt); 'AFC-M23' is not printed in that form in an excerpt, removed from entities_named. The date (21 Nov 2025) is in the article's lede. The Wazalendo spokesperson's allegation that 'AFC Twirwaneho M23' attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni is a party statement (claim 6). No Twirwaneho or AFC-M23 account found.
src: « Le matin de ce vendredi, l’AFC Twirwaneho M23, en violation de l’accord-cadre de Doha, a attaqué Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma et Kwasabuni, sur les hauts plateaux au sud de Minembwe, devenus cibles ce matin », a déclaré un porte-parole des Wazalendo.
De leur côté, les Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke (FABB) du général Delphin Kalembe Ngomanzito affirment continuer à défendre leurs positions.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-007.s: A Wazalendo spokesperson told Kivu Morning Post that the AFC Twirwaneho M23 attacked Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma and Kwasabuni, on the high plateaux south of Minembwe, on the morning of Friday 21 November 2025, in violation of the Doha framework agreement.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-007.l: Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma, Kwasabuni (south of Minembwe), Fizi territory, South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-007.a: Wazalendo (unnamed spokesperson) accusing AFC Twirwaneho M23
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-007.n: Partisan statement; cite only as 'Wazalendo says'.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-007.vn: Excerpt exact; the date is in the article's lede, the weekday in the quote. Party statement: cite only as 'a Wazalendo spokesperson said'. The 'violation of the Doha framework agreement' is the spokesperson's characterisation. No Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 response found (see gaps).
src: « Le matin de ce vendredi, l’AFC Twirwaneho M23, en violation de l’accord-cadre de Doha, a attaqué Kinyokwe, Timbyangoma et Kwasabuni, sur les hauts plateaux au sud de Minembwe, devenus cibles ce matin », a déclaré un porte-parole des Wazalendo.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that, over the weekend, AFC/M23 rebels occupied the localities of Kipupu (Mwenga territory) and Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), a few days after the taking of Uvira.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008.l: Kipupu (Mwenga territory); Makobola 2 (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008.n: Published Mon 15 Dec 2025: 'ce weekend' = 13-14 Dec (date computed from weekday and publication date). Complements Actualite.cd 22 Dec fighting at Makobola.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008.vn: The '15 December 2025' anchor is not printed in the excerpt; moved to the date field and the note. 'Ce weekend' in an article dated Monday 15 Dec 2025 is read as 13-14 Dec 2025 (computed, not printed). SOS Médias Burundi (Oct 2025, claim 19) lists Kipupu among places in Fizi territory; Radio Okapi places it in Mwenga territory.
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 poursuivent leur progression au Sud-Kivu. Ce weekend, ils ont occupé les localités de Kipupu dans le territoire de Mwenga et Makobola 2 dans le territoire de Fizi, quelques jours après la prise d’Uvira.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Fizi territory administrator, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, called on the international community, in particular the United States, to compel Rwanda to withdraw the troops that, he said, support the AFC-M23 rebels, and said 'all batteries are being put in motion' to reconquer the territories already in rebel hands.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-009.n: Name variant in packet: 'Samy Kalonji Badibanga' / 'Sammy Kalonji Badibanga'; here printed 'Samy Badibanga Kalonji'.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-009.vn: Both excerpts exact; the statement's attribution ('he said') matches Radio Okapi's reported speech. Official (territorial administration) statement, reported by Radio Okapi. Name printed 'Samy Badibanga Kalonji' here; other outlets may print other orders/spellings.
src: L’administrateur de Fizi, Samy Badibanga Kalonji, déplore cette avancée et demande à la communauté internationale, particulièrement les États-Unis, de contraindre le Rwanda à retirer ses troupes qui soutiennent les rebelles de l’AFC-M23.
« Toutes les batteries sont mises en marche pour reconquérir les territoires déjà aux mains des rebelles et les repousser afin de ramener la paix dans le territoire de Fizi », a déclaré M. Badibanga.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-010.s: BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that a Congolese government war plane carried out strikes on Monday in the Minembwe area, controlled by Twirwaneho fighters in South Kivu.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-010.x: not given; BBC says no information had been published on whether civilians were killed
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-010.n: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere' = Monday) and publication 11 March 2025 -> 10 March 2025. Q1 item (another agent deepens SKS-2025Q1); added because the Kinyarwanda BBC page was not in the packet. Same page also gives Twirwaneho and pro-government accounts (separate claims).
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-010.vn: Statement supported; the resident's name is not printed in the excerpt, so it is removed from entities_named and figures. Kinyarwanda original; translation checked ('ingabo za leta' = government forces; 'nk'uko abahatuye babivuga' = according to residents). 'Ku wa mbere' (Monday) in an article dated 11 Mar 2025 is read as 10 Mar 2025. A resident quoted on the page told BBC he knew of no one killed but had heard of injuries elsewhere.
src: Indege y'intambara y'ingabo za leta ya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DR Congo) ku wa mbere yakoze ibitero mu gace ka Minembwe kagenzurwa n'abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo, nk'uko abahatuye babivuga.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-011.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group said these air strikes also targeted Kiziba hill, on which the main hospital in Minembwe stands, as well as the University Eben-Ezer Minembwe (UEMI), two secondary schools and the Methodist church.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-011.l: Kiziba hill, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-011.a: Congolese government aircraft, as alleged by Twirwaneho
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-011.n: Party claim (Twirwaneho) relayed by BBC; BBC does not confirm damage to the hospital. Counter-account in next claim.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-011.vn: 'hit' narrowed to 'targeted' to match 'byibasiye' and the hill-hospital relation kept as the source states it. Party statement (Twirwaneho). Translation checked: 'byibasiye' = targeted/attacked; 'umusozi wa Kiziba uriho ibitaro bikuru' = Kiziba hill, on which the main hospital stands. Twirwaneho does not say in this passage that the hospital building was hit, and BBC does not confirm damage. Counter-account from government supporters is claim 11; BBC could not reach the army. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Umutwe wa Twirwaneho uvuga ko ibi bitero by'indege byibasiye kandi n'umusozi wa Kiziba uriho ibitaro bikuru mu Minembwe, University Eben-Ezer Minembwe izwi nka UEMI, amashuri abiri yisumbuye, n'urusengero rwa Méthodiste.

Umutwe wa Twirwaneho uvuga ko ibi bitero by’indege byibasiye kandi n’umusozi wa Kiziba uriho ibitaro bikuru mu Minembwe, University Eben-Ezer Minembwe izwi nka UEMI, amashuri abiri yisumbuye, n’urusengero rwa Méthodiste.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-012.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that some government supporters, heard in DR Congo media, said the strikes aimed only at destroying the Minembwe airstrip and a Twirwaneho weapons store, and that the BBC could not reach the government army side to respond to accusations of targeting civilians.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-012.a: government supporters (unnamed); FARDC side not reached
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-012.n: No official FARDC statement on the 10 March strikes found in this unit's searches.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-012.vn: Both excerpts exact; Kinyarwanda translation checked. Pro-government counter-account, kept separate from the Twirwaneho allegation (claim 10). Unnamed speakers; not an official FARDC statement. No FARDC statement found.
src: Bamwe mu bashyigikiye uruhande rwa leta bumvikanye mu binyamakuru byo muri DR Congo bavuga ko ibi bitero byari bigamije gusa gusenya ikibuga cy'indege cya Minembwe, n'ububiko bw'intwaro bwa Twirwaneho.
BBC yagerageje kuvugisha uruhande rw'ingabo za leta kuri ibi barushinja byo kwibasira abasivile ntibyashoboka kugeza ubu.

r2-G-SKS-FIZI-013.s: MSF said that, in the Hauts-Plateaux on the heights above Baraka, 57 000 people remained isolated, surrounded by armed groups, and that humanitarian access was impossible for the moment; MSF's medical project lead in Fizi said people were afraid to pass armed groups' checkpoints to reach its medical care.
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-013.l: Hauts-Plateaux above Baraka, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-013.a: armed groups (not individually named in the passage)
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-013.x: MSF: 57 000 people isolated in the Hauts-Plateaux above Baraka
r2-G-SKS-FIZI-013.n: MSF names Maria Santo as medical project lead in Fizi in the same release (quote about checkpoints). The release also gives malaria (19,000 treated Aug-Nov) and cholera (652 patients, Sep-Oct) figures at Baraka and Lweba.

Selon des sources locales, cette nouvelle mobilisation intervient à la suite d’affrontements sanglants ayant eu lieu la semaine dernière à Kahololo (territoire d’Uvira) et plus récemment à Rugezi (territoire de Fizi).

src: Significant reinforcements have also been observed in Minembwe, Mikalati, Kipupu, and at Point Zero, in the Fizi territory.

Bukavu, October 16, 2025 – Despite the signing of a ceasefire agreement on October 14 in Doha between the Congolese government and the M23 rebel movement, tensions remain high in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Units of the Burundi National Defense Force (FDNB) continue their massive deployment in several strategic areas of South Kivu, particularly in the territories of Fizi, Mwenga, and Uvira. For several days, military convoys from Burundi have been reported in the towns of Kitoga, Muhuzi, and the dense Itombwe forest.

r2-G-UNDOCS-008.s: The UN Secretary-General reported that, with MONUSCO support, the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus conducted its first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August 2026 and a second mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September.
r2-G-UNDOCS-008.a: Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus; MONUSCO
r2-G-UNDOCS-008.vn: Matches para 23 and the summary. ecoi.net copy is the UN's own PDF of S/2026/748 (job no. 26-13360, dated 21 September 2026), so verbatim; origin is the UN Secretary-General.
src: enabling the first ceasefire monitoring and verification mission in Minembwe, South Kivu, on 24 and 25 August. The Mission similarly supported the second Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus mission to Masisi, North Kivu, from 10 to 12 September

r2-G-UNDOCS-009.s: The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO verified 366 grave violations affecting 276 children (80 girls and 196 boys), including 142 cases of recruitment and use, 111 of abduction and 69 of killing and maiming, with 269 cases in North Kivu and 97 in Ituri, and that MONUSCO with UNICEF secured the release of 47 children detained by FARDC, including 11 girls, associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups.
r2-G-UNDOCS-009.a: not attributed in this passage; FARDC held the 47 children, who were associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups
r2-G-UNDOCS-009.x: SG report: 366 grave violations, 276 children; 142 recruitment and use, 111 abduction, 69 killing and maiming; 269 in North Kivu, 97 in Ituri; 47 children released by FARDC
r2-G-UNDOCS-009.n: The two Wazalendo-affiliated groups are not named in the passage.
r2-G-UNDOCS-009.vn: Figures match; extra territory/province corrected from 'North Kivu' to the source's North Kivu and Ituri scope. ecoi.net copy is the UN's own PDF of S/2026/748 (job no. 26-13360, dated 21 September 2026), so verbatim; origin is the UN Secretary-General. Scope is North Kivu and Ituri combined (269 and 97), not Kivu-only; perpetrators of the 366 violations are not given in this passage.
src: MONUSCO verified 366 grave violations affecting 276 children (80 girls and 196 boys), including 142 cases of recruitment and use, 111 cases of abduction and 69 cases of killing and maiming, with 269 cases in North Kivu and 97 in Ituri.

MONUSCO, in close collaboration with the United Nations Children’s Fund, secured the release of 47 children detained by FARDC, including 11 girls, associated with two Wazalendo-affiliated armed groups.

r2-G-UNDOCS-010.s: The UN Secretary-General reported that MONUSCO documented 518 protection incidents across North Kivu and Ituri resulting in 470 civilian deaths, including 61 women and 56 children, with ADF and M23 the two largest perpetrators, with 214 and 170 fatalities respectively.
r2-G-UNDOCS-010.x: SG report: 518 incidents; 470 civilian deaths (61 women, 56 children); ADF 214, M23 170
r2-G-UNDOCS-010.n: Combined North Kivu and Ituri figure; the report says counts are likely underreported due to access restrictions in North Kivu.
r2-G-UNDOCS-010.vn: Matches page; scope fields corrected to North Kivu and Ituri. ecoi.net copy is the UN's own PDF of S/2026/748 (job no. 26-13360, dated 21 September 2026), so verbatim; origin is the UN Secretary-General. Combined North Kivu and Ituri figure, not Kivu-only; the report says counts are likely underreported due to access restrictions in North Kivu.
src: MONUSCO documented 518 protection incidents across North Kivu and Ituri, resulting in 470 civilian deaths, including 61 women and 56 children, with the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and M23 being the two largest perpetrators, with 214 and 170 fatalities, respectively.

r2-G-UNDOCS-011.s: Amnesty International reported (21 September 2026) that it documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners at the Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu) mines, with witnesses and family members reporting that 10 were beaten to death, two were shot dead and six abducted miners were later found dead; it attributed the abuses to Rwanda-backed M23 fighters. The press release does not say when the killings took place. Neither M23 nor Rwandan government officials responded to Amnesty International's request for comment.
r2-G-UNDOCS-011.l: Mines near Rubaya (North Kivu) and Lomera mine (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
r2-G-UNDOCS-011.x: Amnesty: 18 miners killed (10 beaten to death, two shot dead, six abducted and later found dead)
r2-G-UNDOCS-011.n: Dates of individual killings not given in the press release; the date field is the report date. Victims are pseudonymised by Amnesty ('Evariste*', 'Innocent*' with asterisk = changed names) so none recorded. Amnesty's press release also contains a legal characterisation ('may amount to war crimes') which is Amnesty's and not repeated here. M23 and Rwanda did not respond to Amnesty (second excerpt); see also KMP 23 Sep 2026 already cited, in which AFC/M23 rejected the accusations.
r2-G-UNDOCS-011.vn: Killings and breakdown verbatim. Date moved to report month per brief; '26 interviewed' dropped from figures (not in an excerpt); Masisi not printed, so removed from location; non-response added from source 1. Amnesty's press release of 21 September 2026 gives no dates for the killings; the date is the report date (month precision). Victims are pseudonymised by Amnesty. Amnesty interviewed 26 people (page, not in stored excerpt). Amnesty's own legal characterisations are not repeated. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: publication date 21 September 2026 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Rubaya (North Kivu), Lomera (South Kivu) 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-035: Attribution matches Amnesty's (it 'documents M23 violations including summary killings'). Time slippage risk: the retained press release gives no dates for the 18 killings, so some may predate 1 Jan 2025; the statement should say so (the full briefing, amnesty.org/en/documents/afr62/1454/2026/en/, is a lead for dates). One search (FR) found only relays (RFI, Africanews, Radio Okapi, actualite.cd), no AFC/M23 or Rwandan denial. Also, 'Kabare territory' in the location field is not printed on the Amnesty page.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): publication date 21 September 2026; Rubaya (North Kivu), Lomera (South Kivu)
src: The organization documented the summary killing of 18 artisanal miners at the Rubaya and Lomera mines. Witnesses and family members reported that 10 were beaten to death, two were shot dead and six abducted miners were later found dead.
Neither M23 nor Rwandan government officials responded to Amnesty International’s request for comment.
coltan mines near Rubaya in North Kivu province, and Lomera, a gold mining site in South Kivu province.

r2-G-UNDOCS-012.s: Amnesty International reported that M23 uses three shipping containers as detention cells near the Rubaya mine, and that more than 20 miners who worked at the Rubaya mine were kept in an underground cell known as a ndake and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.
r2-G-UNDOCS-012.l: Near the Rubaya mine, North Kivu
r2-G-UNDOCS-012.x: Amnesty: three shipping containers; more than 20 miners in a ndake
r2-G-UNDOCS-012.n: Time of detentions not stated in the release; date is the report date. The release says the containers are used to torture detainees per one interviewee (not recorded as fact here).
r2-G-UNDOCS-012.vn: Verbatim; date set to report month with month precision; Masisi not printed so location narrowed. No dates of detention given; date is the report month (21 September 2026 release). One interviewee said he heard detainees being tortured in the containers (single account, not stated as fact).
src: Near the Rubaya mine, M23 uses three shipping containers as detention cells.
More than 20 miners who worked at the Rubaya mine were kept in a ndake and beaten three times a day by M23 fighters.

r2-G-UNDOCS-013.s: Amnesty International reported, in a briefing published on 21 September 2026 that gives no date for the detention, that in Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu) M23 detained four men, accused them of communicating with authorities in Kinshasa and suspected them of having links to the Wazalendo armed group.
r2-G-UNDOCS-013.n: Second part of the claim (quote) is in the same paragraph; excerpt covers the detention only. The quote is not repeated as fact.
r2-G-UNDOCS-013.vn: Verbatim; date set to report month (month precision). No date of detention given; date is the report month. Amnesty quotes one victim saying the detention-site supervisor threatened to kill him and 'say you were Wazalendo'. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: publication date 21 September 2026 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: Lomera in Kabare territory, South Kivu 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-034: Re-read the retained Amnesty page and ran one search for an M23 response (none found in results). The briefing gives no date for the Lomera detention; the claim's 2026-09 date is the publication month. Amended to say so, so the event is not read as September 2026.; excerpt-support: added 2 excerpt(s): publication date 21 September 2026; Lomera in Kabare territory, South Kivu
src: In Lomera, M23 detained four men and accused them of communicating with authorities in Kinshasa and suspected them of having links to the Wazalendo armed group.
the port of Lomera, a gold mining site in Kabare territory, South Kivu province

r2-G-UNDOCS-014.s: Amnesty International reported that testimonies indicate Rwandans are present at Rubaya and Lomera and that, in both places, security guards, some of whom identified as Rwandan and spoke Kinyarwanda, collaborate with M23 and have beaten and ill-treated miners.
r2-G-UNDOCS-014.a: security guards identified as Rwandan, collaborating with M23
r2-G-UNDOCS-014.n: Amnesty reports that neither M23 nor Rwandan officials responded to its request for comment; Rwanda has previously denied involvement in the DRC (not searched here).
r2-G-UNDOCS-014.vn: Verbatim; first clause is on the page next to the excerpt; date set to report month. Based on interviewee testimony; Amnesty says neither M23 nor Rwandan officials responded to its request for comment. Date is the report month.
src: In Lomera and Rubaya, security guards, some of whom have identified as Rwandan and spoke Kinyarwanda, the language of Rwanda, collaborate with M23 and have beaten and ill-treated miners.

r2-G-UNDOCS-015.s: IPIS reported, citing an interviewee, that women in Wazalendo-controlled zones such as Walungu and Shabunda territories frequently report being extorted at arbitrary checkpoints, accompanied by invasive and intimate body searches typically justified by suspicion of mineral smuggling.
r2-G-UNDOCS-015.l: Walungu and Shabunda territories, South Kivu
r2-G-UNDOCS-015.n: IPIS says the accounts are not exhaustive or statistically representative; single interviewee; no date of incidents.
r2-G-UNDOCS-015.vn: Verbatim; single partner source, grade C; date set to briefing month. Single interviewee relayed by IPIS (briefing of 30 October 2025); IPIS says its partners' accounts are not exhaustive or statistically representative. No incident dates; the date is the briefing month. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: both armed groups distanced themselves
src: One interviewee indicated that in Wazalendo-controlled zones, such as Walungu and Shabunda territories, women frequently report being extorted at arbitrary checkpoints, where they are forced to pay in cash or kind. These encounters are often accompanied by invasive and intimate body searches, typically justified by suspicions of mineral smuggling.
Moreover, both armed groups have distanced themselves from these violations.

r2-G-UNDOCS-016.s: IPIS reported that a source mentioned that ten women were allegedly executed in Shabunda territory for resisting Wazalendo demands for forced payments at mining-site entrances, 'jeton corporel' (body tokens) and invasive searches.
r2-G-UNDOCS-016.n: Single anonymous source relayed by IPIS; date and place within Shabunda not given. The same IPIS passage says both armed groups have distanced themselves from these violations (separate sentence).
r2-G-UNDOCS-016.vn: Verbatim; 'such demands' refers to the preceding sentence on Wazalendo practices (page). Grade C; date set to briefing month. Single unnamed source relayed by IPIS, doubly hedged ('reportedly', 'allegedly'); no date or locality. IPIS adds that both armed groups have distanced themselves from these violations. Date is the briefing month. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: coercive practices by Wazalendo: forced payments, jeton corporel, invasive searches 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: supports red-team amend: both armed groups distanced themselves
src: Non-compliance has reportedly led to extreme punishments; for example, a source mentioned that ten women were allegedly executed in Shabunda territory for resisting such demands.

Women are particularly exposed to abuse due to illegal taxation and coercive practices by Wazalendo, including forced payments at mining site entrances, the imposition of “jeton corporel” (body tokens), and invasive searches.
Moreover, both armed groups have distanced themselves from these violations.

r2-G-UNDOCS-017.s: IPIS reported that, according to reports, no post-rape kits are available in the mining areas under Wazalendo control and women attempting to engage local organisations risk being targeted; that its partners indicated local women's organisations have been prevented from operating in certain Wazalendo-controlled zones; and that, in the affected areas, where according to its sources the justice system is effectively absent, some health facilities exist but are severely under-resourced and many international and national NGOs have suspended their operations due to insecurity.
r2-G-UNDOCS-017.l: Wazalendo-controlled mining areas in the Kivus (not specified further)
r2-G-UNDOCS-017.n: Location unspecified beyond 'mining areas under Wazalendo control'; IPIS says its sources are partner organisations and not representative.
r2-G-UNDOCS-017.vn: Raw statement tied the NGO suspensions to Wazalendo zones and omitted attribution; narrowed to the page's wording. Second and third clauses are on the page, not in the stored excerpt. IPIS relays partner organisations and unnamed reports; not statistically representative. The NGO-suspension point is about 'many of the affected areas', not only Wazalendo zones. Date is the briefing month. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: IPIS (30 Oct 2025) supports each clause, but the stored excerpt carries only the post-rape-kits sentence. On the page, 'according to our sources' and 'in many of the affected areas' belong to the justice-system sentence, not the NGO-suspension sentence; the wording is realigned and the passages are added.
src: According to reports, no post-rape kits are available in the mining areas under Wazalendo control, and women attempting to engage local organizations risk being targeted.
In certain Wazalendo-controlled zones, our partners indicated that local women’s organizations have been prevented from operating.

According to our sources, the justice system is effectively absent in many of the affected areas, where no judicial services are operational. Some health facilities do exist, but they are severely under-resourced, and many international and national NGOs have suspended their operations due to insecurity.

r2-G-UNDOCS-018.s: IPIS reported that by late February 2026 the pro-government Wazalendo coalition launched a large-scale offensive on AFC/M23 positions in the Osso and Bahunde chiefdoms south of Masisi town, and, supported by FARDC air strikes, temporarily recaptured several villages including Chugi, Kibabi and Kaniro, which AFC/M23 quickly regained while retaining control of the coltan mines around Rubaya.
r2-G-UNDOCS-018.l: Bahunde and Osso chiefdoms, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r2-G-UNDOCS-018.a: Wazalendo coalition (with FARDC air strikes) against AFC/M23
r2-G-UNDOCS-018.n: IPIS text carries spaces before punctuation as fetched. Adds village names for the Masisi late-Feb 2026 offensive.
r2-G-UNDOCS-018.vn: All clauses on the page (consecutive paragraph); '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23', not a figure. IPIS publication dated 25 June 2026; exact dates of the recapture and loss of the villages not given. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: IPIS (25 Jun 2026) supports every clause; the stored excerpt carries only the recapture sentence, so the offensive and AFC/M23-regain sentences around it are added. 2026-10-28: source 0 sources.append edited: fact-check fc1: IPIS (25 Jun 2026) supports every clause; the stored excerpt carries only the recapture sentence, so the offensive and AFC/M23-regain sentences around it are added.
src: Supported by FARDC air strikes , Wazalendo fighters temporarily recaptured several villages , notably Chugi , Kibabi and Kaniro ( Bahunde chiefdom ).

By late February 2026, intense clashes erupted in Masisi territory (North Kivu), where the pro-government Wazalendo coalition launched a large-scale offensive on AFC/M23 positions in the Osso and Bahunde chiefdoms south of Masisi town
AFC/M23, however, quickly regained control of these localities and, crucially, retains control of the coltan mines around Rubaya.

r2-G-UNDOCS-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that the UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its 2025 report, documented 887 cases of sexual violence affecting 1,534 victims, including 854 women and 672 girls, in 2025, and that North Kivu and South Kivu account for nearly 80 per cent of victims recorded.
r2-G-UNDOCS-019.l: Democratic Republic of the Congo (countrywide; North Kivu and South Kivu nearly 80 per cent of victims)
r2-G-UNDOCS-019.a: M23 (439 victims); Wazalendo; CODECO; Mai-Mai groups; FDLR; ADF; FARDC, PNC, ANR
r2-G-UNDOCS-019.x: Radio Okapi citing BCNUDH 2025 report: 887 cases; 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls); North and South Kivu nearly 80% of victims
r2-G-UNDOCS-019.n: DISCREPANCY: a second Radio Okapi item of 13 Mar 2026 (https://www.radiookapi.net/2026/03/13/actualite/securite/plus-de-6-000-violations-des-droits-de-lhomme-documentees-en-2025-en) reports BCNUDH annual report 'violences sexuelles liées au conflit ont augmenté de 59 %, avec 1 479 victimes'; the figures 1,534 and 1,479 differ (possibly different scope or date of data). Do not merge. Nationwide totals.
r2-G-UNDOCS-019.vn: Raw statement carried 439, 19 per cent and '8 March 2026', which no stored excerpt prints (the year is not printed with the date), and dropped the conditional 'seraient'. Narrowed to the excerpt; discrepancies recorded in the note. DISCREPANCY, not merged: a Radio Okapi item of 13 March 2026 on the same BCNUDH annual report gives 1,479 victims of conflict-related sexual violence (up 59 per cent); this article gives 1,534. The article's own breakdown (854 women + 672 girls = 1,526) also does not sum to 1,534. The page (not the stored excerpt) adds that M23 accounted for 439 victims and that state agents (FARDC, PNC, ANR) 'seraient responsables' (would be responsible) for 19 per cent of cases; that is a lead for re-extraction. 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 2 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page. 2026-10-28: source 1 publisher edited: fact-check fc2: Radio Okapi (9 March 2026) carries the statement verbatim, citing the BCNUDH 2025 report published 8 March; Actualite.cd and the ReliefWeb copy agree on 887 cases, 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls) and ~80% in the Kivus. The ReliefWeb page lists its source as MONUSCO, originally published 9 Mar 2026 (posted 11 Mar), not a BCNUDH press release itself. 2026-10-28: source 1 originating_source edited: fact-check fc2: Radio Okapi (9 March 2026) carries the statement verbatim, citing the BCNUDH 2025 report published 8 March; Actualite.cd and the ReliefWeb copy agree on 887 cases, 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls) and ~80% in the Kivus. The ReliefWeb page lists its source as MONUSCO, originally published 9 Mar 2026 (posted 11 Mar), not a BCNUDH press release itself. 2026-10-28: source 1 originating_basis edited: fact-check fc2: Radio Okapi (9 March 2026) carries the statement verbatim, citing the BCNUDH 2025 report published 8 March; Actualite.cd and the ReliefWeb copy agree on 887 cases, 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls) and ~80% in the Kivus. The ReliefWeb page lists its source as MONUSCO, originally published 9 Mar 2026 (posted 11 Mar), not a BCNUDH press release itself. 2026-10-28: source 1 date edited: fact-check fc2: Radio Okapi (9 March 2026) carries the statement verbatim, citing the BCNUDH 2025 report published 8 March; Actualite.cd and the ReliefWeb copy agree on 887 cases, 1,534 victims (854 women, 672 girls) and ~80% in the Kivus. The ReliefWeb page lists its source as MONUSCO, originally published 9 Mar 2026 (posted 11 Mar), not a BCNUDH press release itself. 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: En 2025, le BCNUDH a documenté 887 cas de violences sexuelles ayant touché 1 534 victimes, dont 854 femmes et 672 filles. L’Est du pays reste l’épicentre de la crise : le Nord‑Kivu et le Sud‑Kivu concentrent près de 80 % des victimes recensées.
887 cas de violences sexuelles liées au conflit ont été documentés l’année passée, affectant 1 534 victimes, dont une majorité écrasante de femmes (854) et de filles (672)

les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu concentrant près de 80 % des victimes recensées. Dans son dernier rapport, le BCNUDH indique que les groupes armés sont responsables de 75 % des victimes documentées. Le Mouvement du 23 mars (M23) arrive en tête avec 439 victimes

r2-G-UNDOCS-020.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH report on November 2025 recorded 91 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in one month, mostly women and girls, an increase of 28 per cent in thirty days, with North Kivu and South Kivu remaining the epicentres.
r2-G-UNDOCS-020.l: Democratic Republic of the Congo; North Kivu and South Kivu named as epicentres
r2-G-UNDOCS-020.a: armed groups (M23, Wazalendo, ADF) and state agents per the monthly report overall
r2-G-UNDOCS-020.x: Radio Okapi citing BCNUDH: 91 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in November 2025, +28%
r2-G-UNDOCS-020.n: Headline figure for the same report: 542 violations in November 2025 (title says 'plus de 500').
r2-G-UNDOCS-020.vn: Removed '20 January 2026' (no stored excerpt prints it; the year is not printed with the date); rest verbatim. Countrywide count; the article does not give a Kivu-only figure. It uses '28 per cent' both for overall violations versus October and for sexual violence, so the sexual-violence rise may be misreported. The page says the report was published on Tuesday 20 January.
src: En un mois, 91 victimes (majoritairement des femmes et des filles) ont été recensées, soit une hausse de 28 % en seulement trente jours. Les provinces du Nord et du Sud-Kivu demeurent les épicentres de cette barbarie.

r2-G-UNDOCS-021.s: Radio Okapi reported that the BCNUDH monthly report for May 2026 counted 59 victims of conflict-related sexual violence, mostly women and girls, and that state actors, mainly FARDC soldiers, were designated as first responsible for nearly half of these abuses, ahead of armed groups.
r2-G-UNDOCS-021.l: Democratic Republic of the Congo (80 per cent of violations in Ituri and the two Kivus)
r2-G-UNDOCS-021.a: state actors, mainly FARDC soldiers; armed groups
r2-G-UNDOCS-021.x: Radio Okapi citing BCNUDH: 59 victims of conflict-related sexual violence in May 2026
r2-G-UNDOCS-021.n: Same article gives 'plus de 1200' violations in its first sentence but '481 violations ... près de 1 200 personnes' later: internal inconsistency in the Radio Okapi text (violations vs victims); not used. Countrywide; the Kivus are not separated for sexual violence.
r2-G-UNDOCS-021.vn: Removed 'released on 24 July 2026' ('24' not in a stored excerpt); rest verbatim; inconsistency stated in note. The article is internally inconsistent: its headline and first sentence give 'plus de 1200' violations including '59 cas de violence sexuelle', while later it gives 481 violations affecting nearly 1,200 people, and 59 victims (not cases) of sexual violence. Both versions are kept as printed, not merged. Countrywide; the Kivus are not separated for sexual violence. Report released 24 July 2026 per the page.
src: Sur le plan des violences sexuelles liées au conflit, le rapport comptabilise 59 victimes, majoritairement des femmes et des jeunes filles. Si le chiffre global baisse par rapport à avril, les acteurs étatiques, principalement des militaires FARDC, sont désignés comme premiers responsables de près de la moitié de ces exactions, devant les groupes armés.

r2-G-UNDOCS-022.s: UN News (Kiswahili), relaying Radio Okapi, reported that the DRC government announced a phased plan to restore State authority in Uvira after the departure of AFC/M23 fighters, and that a government spokesperson called the M23 departure a "short-lived event" and said the only acceptable outcome was full, effective and unconditional withdrawal of AFC/M23 and the Rwandan army from the whole DRC.
r2-G-UNDOCS-022.n: Spokesperson not named in the page. The page also says the government (statement of Monday 19 January) denied claims of forced transfer of civilians, notably Banyamulenge, and said the departing group forced some people to leave Uvira; and that the government said the withdrawal was accompanied by repeated looting. Plan details (statement date 19-20 January) taken from the first paragraph; check against existing ST-DRC claims for duplicates.
r2-G-UNDOCS-022.vn: Removed 'on 20 January 2026' from the statement ('20' not in the stored excerpt; date field carries it). Plan and Radio Okapi clauses are on the page, not in the stored excerpt. Grade B: one credible relay of a party's statement. Partisan statement: this records what the DRC government said, not a finding. The spokesperson is not named on the page. The page also reports the government saying the withdrawal was accompanied by repeated looting and denying forced transfers of civilians (statement of Monday 19 January). English is a translation of the Swahili.
src: Msemaji wa serikali amesema kuondoka kwa M23 ni “tukio la muda mfupi” na akasisitiza kuwa matokeo pekee yanayokubalika ni “kuondoka kikamilifu, kwa ufanisi na bila masharti kwa AFC/M23 na jeshi la Rwanda kutoka katika eneo zima la DRC.”

r2-G-UV-CTRL-001.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported from Uvira, citing several consistent accounts, that elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia, supported by some civilians, ransacked homes, businesses and places of worship belonging to the Banyamulenge community in various neighbourhoods of the city; it named among the victims a resident, Sifa, whose two-story house was reportedly completely looted before being destroyed.
r2-G-UV-CTRL-001.a: elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia (SOS Médias Burundi)
r2-G-UV-CTRL-001.n: Adds Banyamulenge-specific detail to existing r1-UV-2026Q1-023 (SOS pillage 18-20 Jan). Article datelined Uvira 19 January 2026. HRW 20 Jan 2026 independently documents looting of a Banyamulenge Methodist church (separate claim).
r2-G-UV-CTRL-001.vn: Removed '20 January 2026' (no excerpt prints it; dateline reads 19 January). Downgraded to C: one local outlet, attribution hedged. Attribution to Wazalendo is SOS Médias Burundi's ('elements believed to be affiliated'); single local outlet.
src: According to several consistent accounts, elements believed to be affiliated with the Wazalendo militia, supported by some civilians, ransacked homes, businesses, and places of worship belonging to this community in various neighborhoods of the city.
Among the victims is a resident identified as Sifa, whose two-story house was reportedly completely looted before being destroyed.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bukavu) that the burial in Uvira of Colonel Patrick Gisore, of the Banyamulenge community, and his wife Yvonne Nyamahoro, who died in a military plane crash in Kisangani, turned violent on a Monday; according to several witnesses armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo interrupted the ceremony and intercepted the funeral procession in Kilomoni, while other members of the Banyamulenge community were arrested in Mulongwe or forcibly locked inside a church; local sources said some assailants fired live ammunition at people outside the church and looting took place. Human Rights Watch separately said that since August 25 Wazalendo fighters had prevented the funeral of an army colonel from the Banyamulenge community and his wife for several days and robbed people there.
r2-G-UV-CTRL-002.l: Kilomoni and Mulongwe, Uvira city, South Kivu
r2-G-UV-CTRL-002.a: armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo (SOS Médias Burundi); Wazalendo fighters (HRW)
r2-G-UV-CTRL-002.n: Date from dateline 25 August 2025 and 'Monday' (25 Aug 2025 is a Monday); HRW gives 25 August. SOS says the Bukavu dateline; SOS says Kisangani crash 16 August. Two independent sources (local monitor and HRW). SOS also names a witness-reported car looting of Alexis Rukatura (not in a cited excerpt, so not listed).
r2-G-UV-CTRL-002.vn: Dateline gives no date ('Bukavu' only); 25 August comes from HRW, so the date is attributed to HRW. Passive 'were arrested' kept passive. Two independent origins (SOS, HRW).
src: According to several witnesses, the ceremony was abruptly interrupted by armed elements claiming to be Wazalendo. They intercepted the funeral procession in Kilomoni, while other members of the Banyamulenge community were arrested in Mulongwe or forcibly locked inside the church of the 37th Community of the Assemblies of God of Congo (CADC).

Local sources report that some assailants opened fire with live ammunition on those gathered outside the church. In the confusion, looting took place : vehicles, cell phones, mattresses, money, and church equipment were taken.

The burial of Colonel Patrick Gisore, from the Banyamulenge community, and his wife Yvonne Nyamahoro, who died in a military plane crash in Kisangani on August 16, turned violent on Monday in Uvira, eastern DRC.
Tensions had escalated since August 25, when Wazalendo fighters prevented the funeral of an army colonel from the Banyamulenge community and his wife for several days and robbed people there.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-003.s: Human Rights Watch reported that on 2 September 2025 Wazalendo militias set up roadblocks in Uvira, particularly along a major route to the Burundi border, and that for several days Wazalendo fighters intermittently prevented people from fleeing across the border, witnesses said; a border officer told HRW that the Wazalendo 'did not want to see people fleeing to Burundi'.

For several days, Wazalendo fighters intermittently prevented people from fleeing across the border, witnesses said. A border officer told Human Rights Watch: “[the Wazalendo] did not want to see people fleeing to Burundi.”

src: In Burundi on September 8, police and ruling party youths detained hundreds of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers, according to several witnesses and media reports . They were given the “choice” of going to an official camp or returning to Congo, which about 80 people did.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-007.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported (dateline Bujumbura, 23 January 2026) that a delegation of South Kivu provincial authorities led by the mayor of Uvira returned to Uvira from Bujumbura via the Gatumba–Kavimvira border crossing on a day the outlet gives as 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026'; that the Burundi-Congo border at Gatumba had remained closed since 10 December 2025, after the fall of Uvira to the M23; and that since the capture of Bukavu almost a year earlier a large part of the province's Congolese officials had resided in Bujumbura.
r2-G-UV-CTRL-007.l: Gatumba-Kavimvira border; Uvira city, South Kivu
r2-G-UV-CTRL-007.a: South Kivu provincial authorities; Burundian authorities (border closure)
r2-G-UV-CTRL-007.n: Date conflict: the article says 'jeudi 23 janvier 2026' but 23 January 2026 is a Friday; Actualite.cd (existing r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-020) says the mayor returned on Thursday (22 Jan), and Congorassure says the governor returned Friday 23 January. Date given as a range. Single local source.

src: Une délégation d’autorités de la province du Sud-Kivu, à l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC), conduite par le maire de la ville d’Uvira, est rentrée ce jeudi 23 janvier 2026 à Uvira en provenance de Bujumbura, la capitale économique du Burundi
La frontière burundo-congolaise de Gatumba reste fermée depuis le 10 décembre 2025, après la chute d’Uvira face aux rebelles du M23, perturbant le passage des personnes et des marchandises.
Depuis la prise de Bukavu, chef-lieu de la province du Sud-Kivu, il y a près d’une année, une grande partie des officiels congolais de la province résident à Bujumbura.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-008.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a session of Burundi's Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation in Bujumbura, Foreign Minister Édouard Bizimana announced that the Burundi-Congo border would remain closed until further notice, insisted that the M23 was lying when it claimed to be withdrawing from the city of Uvira, and said this apparent withdrawal hid a strategy of regrouping its fighters.
r2-G-UV-CTRL-008.n: Swahili edition of an SOS Médias Burundi article (page dated 6 Feb 2026, dateline 2 Feb 2026). The border reopened 23 February 2026 (existing Radio Okapi claim r1-UV-2026Q1-051). Complements existing Bizimana statements r1-ST-BI-012/013.

The regrouping clause was not in the stored excerpt: added from page. Dateline '2' supplied by replacement quote. C: single outlet relaying a party statement. Partisan statement (Government of Burundi), reported by one outlet; recorded as what the minister said. Translation from Swahili checked.
src: Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje na Ushirikiano wa Kimataifa wa Burundi, Édouard Bizimana, alitangaza kwamba mpaka wa Burundi na Kongo utaendelea kufungwa hadi ilani nyingine. Akizungumzia hali ya usalama mashariki mwa DRC, Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Burundi alisisitiza kuwa M23 inadanganya inapodai kujiondoa katika mji wa Uvira.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi (in Swahili) reported that the South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, had assured Uvira residents after crossing the border that the Burundi-Congo border would reopen within two to three days, by 30 January 2026 at the latest.

Ijumaa iliyopita, baada ya kuvuka mpaka, alikuwa amewahakikishia wakazi wa Uvira—mji mkuu wa muda wa jimbo hilo—kwamba mpaka wa Burundi na Kongo ungefunguliwa tena ndani ya siku mbili hadi tatu, ifikapo Januari 30, 2026, hivi karibuni zaidi.

r2-G-UV-CTRL-010.s: Iwacu reported that, according to UNHCR, more than 84,000 people from South Kivu had crossed into Burundi since the beginning of December 2025, bringing the total of Congolese refugees and asylum seekers in Burundi to more than 200,000, and that UNHCR declared a level 2 emergency for Burundi needing USD 33 million.

src: Face à l’aggravation de la crise, le Haut-Commissariat des Nations-unies pour les réfugiés a déclaré une situation d’urgence de niveau 2 pour le Burundi, avec un besoin de mobilisation de 33 millions de dollars américains. Selon le HCR, depuis le début du mois de décembre, plus de 84 000 personnes en provenance du Sud-Kivu ont franchi la frontière. Ce nouvel afflux porte à plus de 200 000 le nombre total de réfugiés et demandeurs d’asile congolais présents sur le territoire burundais

r2-G-UV-CTRL-011.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition, dateline Bujumbura) reported that at a meeting in Bujumbura the UNHCR representative in Burundi, Brigitte Mkanga-Eno, expressed concern at the humanitarian funding shortfall: of the USD 33 million needed for emergency needs only USD 6 million had been raised so far, an amount she said was insufficient, especially for health services, sanitation and access to clean water.

Selon ce document, plus de 14 400 femmes ont été victimes de viols durant la période d’occupation.
