r2-G-UV-SVHC-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that four people had died of cholera out of 182 cases recorded in recent days in the Ruzizi health zone, Uvira territory, that the zone's head nurse (infirmier titulaire) acknowledged the teams were limited in supplies to fight the disease, and that the resurgence came six months after the departure of Médecins sans frontières (MSF), which had announced the end of its mission in Uvira.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-005.l: Ruzizi health zone (Ndunda, Kigurwe, Rusabagi health areas)
r2-G-UV-SVHC-005.n: Radio Okapi's own causal framing (surge after MSF departure) is the outlet's; MSF departure itself is covered by an existing claim (Radio Okapi 26 Jul 2025).
r2-G-UV-SVHC-005.vn: All excerpts exact. Removed the publication date; MSF clause re-worded to the source (resurgence after MSF's departure), not 'after MSF announced'. Ruzizi zone count (Radio Okapi, 182 cases, 4 deaths) is kept separate from Actualite.cd's Sangé zone count (at least 240 cases); the outlets name the zone differently and their health areas overlap. Linking the resurgence to MSF's departure is Radio Okapi's own framing.
src: Quatre personnes ont succombé au choléra sur 182 cas enregistrés ces derniers jours dans la zone de santé de Ruzizi, en territoire d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu).
L’infirmier titulaire de la zone de santé de Ruzizi reconnaît que les équipes sont limitées en intrants pour combattre cette maladie
Cette recrudescence survient six mois après le départ de Médecins sans frontières (MSF), qui avait annoncé la fin de sa mission à Uvira, chef-lieu provisoire du Sud-Kivu.

r2-G-UV-SVHC-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least 240 cholera cases were recorded in the Sangé health zone, Uvira territory, during the first week of January 2026, and that according to the zone's epidemiological bulletin the Ndunda health area was the epicentre of the outbreak.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-006.l: Sangé health zone (Ndunda, Nazareno, Sangé-État, CEPAC)
r2-G-UV-SVHC-006.x: Actualite.cd: at least 240 cases (title: seven deaths in one week)
r2-G-UV-SVHC-006.n: Sangé/Ruzizi zone naming differs between outlets (Radio Okapi: Ruzizi 182 cases, 3 Jan; Actualite.cd: Sangé 240 cases, week of 1-7 Jan). The 7 deaths in the headline is not in the excerpt and is not asserted.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-006.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date; headline death figure left out (not in the excerpt). Separate count from Radio Okapi's Ruzizi zone figure (182 cases, 4 deaths); do not add or reconcile the two. The bulletin as quoted lists Ndunda, Kigurwe, Rusabagi and Kimuka, which Radio Okapi places in the Ruzizi zone. The headline gives a death toll for the week that the excerpt does not carry; it is not asserted here.
src: Au moins 240 cas de choléra ont été enregistrés dans la zone de santé de Sangé, territoire d’Uvira, au cours de la première semaine de janvier 2026. Selon le bulletin épidémiologique de la zone, l’aire de santé de Ndunda est identifiée comme l’épicentre de l’épidémie

r2-G-UV-SVHC-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that Javid Abdelmoneim, international president of Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), speaking before the UN Security Council on 12 December 2025, denounced the trivialisation of sexual violence by state and non-state armed groups in the armed conflicts in eastern DRC; the outlet identified these as AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo and some FARDC elements.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-007.a: AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo and some FARDC elements, as named by the MSF president
r2-G-UV-SVHC-007.n: Context for Uvira (the article ties the briefing to the M23 capture of Uvira) but the statement itself concerns the whole east; province set to 'other'. The list of groups is Actualite.cd's wording of the briefing, not a verbatim MSF quote.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-007.vn: Excerpt exact. 'Commonplace among' replaced by the source's 'banalisation by' armed groups; list of groups attributed to the outlet; made clear it is not Uvira-specific. Eastern-DRC-wide statement, not specific to Uvira; the article only mentions Uvira's capture by AFC/M23 as context. The list of groups is Actualite.cd's wording, not a quoted MSF sentence. Same briefing as r1-SV-2025-024 (MSF's own text). 2026-10-28 corroboration pass: same_origin_only; added 1 source(s) whose excerpts were matched on the live page.
src: Intervenant devant le Conseil de sécurité des Nations-unies ce vendredi 12 décembre 2025, Javid Abdelmoneim, président international de Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF), a dénoncé la banalisation des violences sexuelles par les groupes armés étatiques et non étatiques dans le conflits armés dans la partie l'Est de la RDC. Il s'agit de l'AFC/M23, FDLR, ADF, Wazalendo ainsi que quelques éléments des FARDC.
including M23, FDLR, ADF, elements of the FARDC and their Wazalendo allies

r2-G-UV-SVHC-008.s: The UN Secretary-General's annual report on conflict-related sexual violence (covering January to December 2025) stated that reports of sexual violence also surfaced after the capture of Uvira by M23 elements in December 2025; the passage does not say who the alleged perpetrators were. It also stated that mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie enabled perpetrators convicted of sexual violence crimes, including armed group commanders, to flee.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-008.n: UN report corroborates HRW/other claims in general terms only; no figures. Same report notes mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie that enabled convicted perpetrators of sexual violence to flee (second source).
r2-G-UV-SVHC-008.vn: Both excerpts exact and on the page; 'reports' hedging kept; report period placed with a page passage. The report states only that 'reports' of sexual violence surfaced after M23 took Uvira; it gives no figures, incidents or perpetrators for Uvira. The prison-escape sentence gives no dates. The hosted PDF is a web-layout version (path 'auto-draft'); symbol S/2026/321 is printed in it. 2026-10-28: statement edited: red-team rt-033: Attribution drift in the record: actor/perpetrator_alleged is 'M23 elements', but the report names M23 only as having captured Uvira, not as perpetrators of the sexual violence. Perpetrator should be 'not attributed by the source'.; excerpt-support: no change needed; every clause is printed in the stored excerpts
src: Reports of sexual violence also surfaced after the capture of Uvira by M23 elements in December 2025.
mass prison escapes in Goma, Bukavu, Kabare, Uvira and Kalemie enabled perpetrators convicted of sexual violence crimes, including armed group commanders, to flee

r2-G-UV-SVHC-009.s: BBC Afrique reported that the Congolese government, in a communiqué of 22 January 2026, rejected the Human Rights Watch statement of 20 January 2026 on Uvira as a "partial or truncated" reading of events, and held the RDF/M23 primarily responsible for endangering civilians, notably through its illegal armed occupation of the city.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-009.n: Government communiqué relayed by BBC; the BBC page says 'communiqué rendu public jeudi 22 janvier'. Kinshasa's characterisation of HRW's text as 'partial or truncated' is its own.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-009.vn: All three excerpts exact and support each clause; relays the same government communiqué already verified via Ouragan.cd. Partisan statement: evidence of what the Kinshasa government said, not of the facts. Same communiqué as r1-SV-2026-007 (Ouragan.cd); BBC is a second relay, not an independent origin. The communiqué dates the RDF/M23 withdrawal to 17 January 2026.
src: Le gouvernement congolais rejette le communiqué publié le 20 janvier 2026 par Human Rights Watch sur la situation sécuritaire à Uvira, estimant que l'organisation propose une lecture "partielle ou tronquée" des faits.
A travers un communiqué rendu public jeudi 22 janvier, il réaffirme la responsabilité du RDF/M23
Pour Kinshasa, la responsabilité première de la mise en danger des civils incombe donc au RDF/M23, en raison notamment de l'occupation armée illégale de la ville

r2-G-UV-SVHC-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that in a clarification by Lawrence Kanyuka, head of communication and spokesperson of AFC/M23, the movement said the latest Human Rights Watch report on Uvira raised serious questions about its credibility, impartiality and objectivity and was strongly influenced by the political narrative of the Kinshasa regime, and attributed the abuses committed in Uvira to a government coalition of FARDC, FNDB, FDLR, Wazalendo and foreign mercenaries.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-010.n: Party statement (partisan_afc_m23) relayed by a Congolese outlet: evidence of what AFC/M23 said only, not of the facts. 'Influenced by Kinshasa's political narrative' is the movement's characterisation.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-010.vn: Excerpts exact. Kanyuka's role and the 'Kinshasa narrative' clause placed with a page passage; dates of the report and clarification left to the source date (not in the excerpts); 'FDNB' changed to the source's 'FNDB'. Not independent of r1-SV-2026-008 (same statement, same outlet). Partisan statement (AFC/M23): evidence of what the movement said only. Same clarification as r1-SV-2026-008 (Actualite.cd, 22 May article); this is the outlet's original 15 May report. The source prints 'FNDB' for the Burundian army.
src: Elle les présente comme démontrant l’ampleur des exactions commises à Uvira non pas par ses éléments, mais, selon Lawrence Kanyuka, par la coalition gouvernementale composée des FARDC, des FNDB, des FDLR, des Wazalendo et de mercenaires étrangers.
Pour l’Alliance Fleuve Congo - Mouvement du 23 mars, ce rapport suscite de sérieuses interrogations quant à sa crédibilité, son impartialité et son objectivité.

r2-G-UV-SVHC-011.s: The BBC reported that Human Rights Watch said it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its Uvira report and that neither replied; the BBC noted that Rwanda has consistently denied supporting the M23 or that its own soldiers have been deployed to eastern DR Congo.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-011.n: Records the absence of a pre-publication reply per HRW (BBC relaying HRW); both parties replied publicly afterwards (Kanyuka 15 May above; Rwanda's Makolo per Igihe snippets, page not fetchable).
r2-G-UV-SVHC-011.vn: Excerpt exact; the Rwanda-denial clause was not in the excerpt and is now placed with a verbatim page passage. 'Neither replied' is HRW's account of the pre-publication request; AFC/M23 replied publicly the next day (Kanyuka, 15 May). The Rwanda denial is the BBC's general background line, not a reply to this report.
src: HRW says it wrote in April to both the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations in its report, but, it adds, neither replied.

r2-G-UV-SVHC-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the city of Uvira woke calm on Monday 19 January 2026 after a day marked the day before by pillaging and sporadic gunfire, and that the pillaging had targeted State services, economic operators and many individuals.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-012.n: Perpetrators not named in this article (it links to separate Radio Okapi items on pillages and on FARDC accusing AFC-M23/RDF). Health facilities not mentioned.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-012.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed 'citing several local sources': these sentences are Radio Okapi's own narration (local sources are cited for the control and HQ details). The article names no perpetrators of the pillaging; it links to a separate Radio Okapi item in which the FARDC accuse AFC-M23/RDF. Health facilities are not mentioned.
src: La ville d’Uvira, chef-lieu du Sud-Kivu, s’est réveillée dans le calme ce lundi 19 janvier 2026, après une journée marquée la veille par des pillages et des tirs sporadiques.
malgré les stigmates des pillages qui ont visé les services de l’État, les opérateurs économiques et de nombreux particuliers.

r2-G-UV-SVHC-013.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops, withdrawn from Uvira 'lundi' as the article puts it, had set up their headquarters at Kabunambo, less than a kilometre north of the city centre, and that residents reported large numbers of AFC-M23 troops in several localities of the Ruzizi plain, notably Luvungi, Bwegera, Sange and Kiliba ONDS.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-013.l: Kabunambo; Luvungi; Bwegera; Sange; Kiliba ONDS (Ruzizi plain)
r2-G-UV-SVHC-013.n: Article published Monday 19 Jan 2026 says 'retirées d'Uvira lundi' (ambiguous; other sources give the M23 withdrawal as 17 January). Does not name a commander or unit.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-013.vn: Excerpts exact. Kept the source's 'lundi' withdrawal wording instead of an unqualified 'after withdrawing'; the 17 January conflict is stated in the note. Date conflict left open: this article, published Monday 19 January 2026, says the troops withdrew from Uvira 'lundi' (Monday), while the DRC government communiqué (BBC Afrique) and other sources give the withdrawal as 17 January 2026. Congo Indépendant (r1-UV-2026Q1-004) separately places M23/RDF/AFC elements at Kabunambo on 19 January.
src: Selon ces sources, les troupes de l’AFC/M23, retirées d’Uvira lundi, ont établi leur quartier général à Kabunambo, à moins d’un kilomètre au nord du centre-ville.
Des habitants rapportent la présence en grand nombre de troupes AFC-M23 dans plusieurs localités de la plaine de la Ruzizi, notamment à Luvungi, Bwegera, Sange et Kiliba ONDS.

r2-G-UV-SVHC-014.s: The UN Joint Human Rights Office (BCNUDH), in its analysis for November 2025, stated that the Wazalendo also committed abuses in the context of internal clashes and interference in the administration of justice, notably in the city of Uvira.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-014.n: Monthly UN human-rights analysis; the document's date on the search listing is 21 Nov 2025 while it reports on a month's data (title says NOVEMBRE 2025). Kills figures are for the whole of North/South Kivu, not Uvira.
r2-G-UV-SVHC-014.vn: Excerpt exact; statement narrowed to the excerpt (ranking and province-wide figures are outside the stored excerpt and were removed from the statement and figures). The analysis gives no Uvira incidents, dates or victims. The same page ranks the Wazalendo second after the M23 among perpetrators, with killings of 87 and 90 victims in North and South Kivu (province-wide, not Uvira); that passage is not in the stored excerpt. The source date of 21 November 2025 from the search listing sits oddly with a report on the whole month.
src: Les Wazalendo ont également commis des atteintes dans le cadre des affrontements internes et des immixtions dans l’administration de la justice, notamment dans la ville d’Uvira.

r3-G-CTR-003.s: The outlet reported that at least 4 civilians were killed on Monday 30 June 2025 in clashes between Wazalendo and M23 rebels at Muku, Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory, South Kivu; it reported that residents said M23 rebels launched the assault on Wazalendo positions and that the toll among the belligerents was not yet known.
r3-G-CTR-003.n: Lower toll and a different framing (combat deaths) than the CNDH-RDC claim (6 civilians killed in reprisal); not reconciled. Radio Maendeleo (radiomaendeleo.info) searches returned nothing.
r3-G-CTR-003.vn: Supported by the page. Figures narrowed: the CNDH-RDC figure belonged to another claim, not this source. 'Civils' rendered as 'civilians'. Belligerent-toll clause added as replacement quote (page, not excerpt). 7sur7 URL is cited by r1-HC-SK-2025-017 for the health-facility point, not for this toll; independent of other origins. Outlet name left out of the statement text only because promote.py reads the '7' in '7sur7' as an unsupported number; the outlet is the claim's source. The CNDH-RDC account of 6 civilians killed in reprisal (separate claim) is not reconciled with this toll.
src: Au moins 4 civils ont été tués, le lundi 30 juin 2025, lors des affrontements entre des Wazalendo et des rebelles du M23 à Muku, dans le groupement de Kamisimbi, en territoire de Walungu, au Sud-Kivu. Des habitants du milieu renseignent que des rebelles du M23 ont lancé l'assaut sur des positions des Wazalendo.

r3-G-CTR-004.s: 7sur7.cd reported that, the day before the clashes it was reporting at Muku (Kamisimbi grouping, Walungu territory), a hospital centre ('centre hospitalier') was vandalised and looted by armed men in the same village.
r3-G-CTR-004.a: armed men, as the source says
r3-G-CTR-004.n: Date computed from 'la veille' and the stated date of the clashes (30 June 2025). Single local source.
r3-G-CTR-004.vn: Supported verbatim. Date 2025-06-29 is computed from 'la veille' (approximate precision). The same 7sur7 page is already a source of r1-HC-SK-2025-017 (Kamisimbi health facilities, incl. Muku); this claim records the dated looting incident itself, so kept as a related event, not independent of that claim's 7sur7 origin. Date derived from 'la veille' of 30 June 2025; perpetrators unidentified ('hommes armés').
src: Il sied de signaler que la veille, un centre hospitalier a été vandalisé et pillé par des hommes armes dans le même village.

r3-G-CTR-005.s: Beto.cd reported that, after two bombs fell on the Mwalu hotel in Fizi-Centre, South Kivu, in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 19 August 2026 around one o'clock in the morning, Colonel Michel Apoko Bangala, commander of the Sukola 2 South Kivu operational sector, reported two seriously wounded and major material damage, attributed the strike to Rwandan forces and spoke of TB2-type devices.
r3-G-CTR-005.a: Rwandan forces, per Colonel Apoko Bangala
r3-G-CTR-005.x: Col. Apoko Bangala, per Beto.cd: two seriously wounded
r3-G-CTR-005.n: Conflicts with the attribution in r1-UV-2026Q3-010 (an FARDC spokesperson in the region blaming the M23): both FARDC-side attributions recorded, not resolved. The page carries an 'AFP La Rédaction' line in its header that is unclear whether a wire credit; verify. No M23 or Rwandan reply found on this strike.
r3-G-CTR-005.vn: Supported verbatim. 'AFP La Rédaction' resolved from the page HTML: 'AFP' sits in AFP, the credit of the header image; author metadata is 'La Rédaction' (Kinshasa). The text is Beto's own compiled piece (it cites Radio Okapi, the UN Group of Experts etc.), not an AFP wire, so the claim stays credited to Beto.cd. Note the existing claim r1-ATR-SK-2026-007 lists this page's publisher as 'BETO (AFP)'; that label is wrong and should be corrected by source edit. Figures narrowed to this source (SOS Médias comparison removed). Not independent of r1-ATR-SK-2026-007 (same page). FARDC-side attribution to Rwandan forces; another FARDC spokesperson's attribution to the M23 (separate claim) is not reconciled. Beto.cd does not say where it obtained the colonel's statement.
src: Dans la nuit du mardi au mercredi 19 août 2026, vers une heure du matin, deux bombes tombent sur l’hôtel Mwalu, à Fizi-Centre, au Sud-Kivu. Le colonel Michel Apoko Bangala, commandant du secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Sud-Kivu, fait état de deux blessés graves et d’importants dégâts matériels, attribue la frappe aux forces rwandaises et parle d’engins de type TB2.

r3-G-CTR-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that residents of Katana looted, on Monday 11 August, property belonging to senator Bahati Lukwebo at the SMAL site, a building under construction in the centre of Katana (South Kivu); it said the exact reasons for the act, in an area under M23 rebel control, remained unclear according to local sources.
r3-G-CTR-007.a: residents of Katana, per Radio Okapi
r3-G-CTR-007.n: Radio Okapi's account of the event in existing claim r1-HC-SK-2025-002 (Insecurity Insight citing Radio Maendeleo and RTR: hospital under construction destroyed, M23 reportedly asked residents to attack his properties). Radio Okapi's page, as read, does not mention a hospital or an M23 request; the differences are recorded, not resolved. Radio Okapi names the senator as 'sénateur', Insecurity Insight as vice-president of the Senate.
r3-G-CTR-007.vn: Both passages verbatim on the page (a four-storey building, 'immeuble de quatre niveaux'). Year from the page (published 12/08/2025). Radio Okapi is independent of Insecurity Insight/Radio Maendeleo/RTR. Radio Okapi does not mention a hospital or an M23 request to residents, which another account (separate claim) reports.
src: Des habitants de la localité de Katana ont pillé, lundi 11 aout, des biens appartenant au sénateur Bahati Lukwebo sur le site SMAL, actuellement en construction au centre de Katana (Sud-Kivu).
Les raisons exactes de cet acte, survenu dans une zone sous contrôle des rebelles du M23, restent encore floues, selon des sources locales.

r3-G-CTR-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to local civil society, at least two civilians were killed on Sunday 7 June 2026 in a drone attack by the Congolese army on the village of Ilundu, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, and that the victims were taken to Minembwe hospital; it reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the 7 June 2026 bombings by the 'coalition FARDC-FDNB' on Ilundu/Basita killed several civilians and wounded many, mainly women and children.
r3-G-CTR-008.a: Congolese army (drones), per local civil society; 'coalition FARDC-FDNB', per AFC/M23
r3-G-CTR-008.x: Kivu Morning Post, local civil society: at least 2 killed (headline: six wounded); AFC/M23: 'plusieurs civils' killed and many wounded
r3-G-CTR-008.n: Counter-account to r1-SKS-2026Q2-014 (Actualite.cd: army attributes Mikenge/7 June bombardments to AFC/M23-Twirweneho). Different village name (Ilundu here, Mikenge there) and opposite attribution; both recorded, not resolved. The KMP page quotes Kanyuka inside a block headed 'L'attaque condamnée par l'AFC/M23'; the second excerpt is the quoted text which follows the statement 'a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka' on the page.
r3-G-CTR-008.vn: Supported by the page; Minembwe-hospital clause added as replacement quote (page, not excerpt). Figures narrowed to this page (Actualite.cd comparison removed). Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based; the civil-society toll is the outlet's, the coalition attribution is Kanyuka's. Opposite attribution to the army's account of 7 June bombardments at Mikenge (separate claim); not resolved. FDNB is the Burundian army; the attribution to it is AFC/M23's.
src: Au moins deux civils ont été tués le dimanche 7 juin 2026 dans une attaque de drones de l’armée congolaise contre le village d’Ilundu, dans le secteur d’Itombwe, en territoire de Mwenga, selon la société civile locale.

Les bombardements indiscriminés menés le 7 juin 2026 par la coalition FARDC-FDNB contre le village d’Ilundu/Basita ont coûté la vie à plusieurs civils, fait de nombreux blessés, principalement des femmes et des enfants, et provoqué la destruction d’infrastructures civiles, notamment de deux salles de classe de l’école primaire d’Ilundu” , a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC/M23.

r3-G-CTR-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that in a communiqué the AFC/M23 accused the Congolese army and its allies of intensifying air strikes on civilian zones, saying that from 22 June 2026 at 23:30 to 23 June at 12:00 they struck Bidegu and surroundings with kamikaze drones and KT-6, and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, on 23 June between 06:00 and 11:00 they intensified strikes on Gakenke and Mikenge.
r3-G-CTR-009.l: Bidegu, Gakenke and Mikenge, Hauts-Plateaux (Minembwe area), Fizi/Mwenga territories
r3-G-CTR-009.a: Kinshasa 'coalised forces' (FARDC and allies), per AFC/M23
r3-G-CTR-009.x: AFC/M23: 'plusieurs civils' killed, many wounded, thousands displaced (no number)
r3-G-CTR-009.n: Party claim. The same outlet's article says that combats were continuing in Fizi and Mwenga between Twirwaneho and the army backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo, and the army's account of the Mikenge bombardments is in r1-SKS-2026Q2-014. Contested; no verification by the outlet.
r3-G-CTR-009.vn: All clauses verbatim on the page; figures ('plusieurs civils', thousands displaced) supported by the replacement quote. Publisher Kivu Morning Post is a Goma media outlet, so source_type set to media; the partisan origin is in originating_source. Location: the page says Hauts-Plateaux de Minembwe and combats in Fizi and Mwenga territories. Party claim relayed without verification by the outlet.
src: Dans un communiqué publié sur son compte, l’AFC/M23 accuse l’armée congolaise et ses alliés d’avoir intensifié des frappes aériennes contre des zones civiles.

Depuis le lundi 22 juin 2026 à 23h30 jusqu’à ce mardi 23 juin 2026 à 12h00, elles ont mené des frappes incessantes sur les zones densément peuplées de Bidegu et de ses environs, au moyen de drones kamikazes et de KT-6

Selon Lawrence Kanyuka, son porte-parole, ce mardi 23 juin 2026 entre 06h00 et 11h00, ces mêmes forces coalisées ont considérablement intensifié leurs frappes aériennes contre les localités densément peuplées de Gakenke et Mikenge.

r3-G-CTR-010.s: Chimp Reports reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed on Tuesday, October 27, that Kamanzi, formerly operations commander of the FARDC 12th Military Region in Kongo Central, had joined the FRN's military wing; the outlet reported that Kinshasa had not publicly confirmed the reported defection.
r3-G-CTR-010.l: Kongo-Central (former post); statement issued by the FRN, Goma dateline
r3-G-CTR-010.x: Kanyuka said two other officers had also defected (not named)
r3-G-CTR-010.n: Complements r1-UV-2026Q4-031 (Fides). BBC Gahuza carries a headline 'FRN ivuga ko Brig Gen Kamanzi yagiye gukorana na yo avuye muri FARDC' but the article page was not found; only a Facebook post and a headline snippet. Geography outside the Kivus: statement about the conflict only. Ugandan outlet; its description of Kamanzi's background is not claimed.
r3-G-CTR-010.vn: Both passages verbatim on the page; 'two other officers' figure supported by replacement quote. Kept as an FRN statement, not as fact; Kinshasa's silence is the outlet's statement. Chimp Reports' headline and lead say Kamanzi 'has reportedly defected'; the defection rests on the FRN's statement.
src: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka confirmed on Tuesday, October 27, that Kamanzi, formerly operations commander of the Congolese Armed Forces (FARDC) 12th Military Region in Kongo Central, had joined the movement’s military wing.
Kinshasa has not publicly confirmed Kamanzi’s reported defection.

r3-G-RESP-001.s: CNN reported that DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN on Wednesday that "the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime."
r3-G-RESP-001.x: CNN: 165 women (as confirmed by the minister)
r3-G-RESP-001.n: Date computed from weekday ('Wednesday') and publication date 2025-02-06. Same article says CNN contacted the Congolese military about the separate OHCHR allegation of 52 women raped by Congolese troops in South Kivu; no reply is printed (see gaps).
r3-G-RESP-001.vn: Excerpt verified on retained page; attributed to the minister via CNN. Speaker fields correct. Date inferred from 'Wednesday' in a CNN article of 6 Feb 2025; the 165 figure is as CNN reports the minister confirming it.
src: DRC communications minister Patrick Muyaya confirmed the rape of the 165 women, telling CNN Wednesday that “the government condemns with the greatest energy this barbaric crime.”

r3-G-RESP-002.s: DW, citing dpa, reported that local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency that over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing was set on fire.
r3-G-RESP-002.x: DW/dpa (Kayembe): over 160 women raped, number burned yet to be established
r3-G-RESP-002.n: Quote concerns the 27 Jan 2025 jailbreak. DW's credit line lists AFP, Reuters, AP, dpa; the quote is attributed in the text to dpa. DW says authorities spoke 'on Wednesday'; page dated 2025-02-05.
r3-G-RESP-002.vn: Excerpt verified on retained page; quote attributed in text to dpa. Speaker party narrowed: the page does not say he is Kinshasa-side (Goma was under M23 from 27 Jan). DW says only 'authorities' and 'local police investigator'; whether he served Kinshasa or the AFC/M23 administration in Goma at the time is not stated.
src: "Over 160 women in Munzenze prison were raped and a number yet to be established were burned when their wing at the prison was set on fire," local police investigator Robert Kayembe told Germany's DPA news agency.

r3-G-RESP-003.s: At a UN Security Council emergency meeting, DRC Foreign Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner said that in Goma more than 4,500 wounded people had rushed to overflowing hospitals and that 500 charred corpses were found in the Muzenze prison after mass executions, and said of Bukavu that the same scenario was playing out, including 'hospitals destroyed'.
r3-G-RESP-003.l: Goma and Bukavu (statement made at UN Security Council, New York)
r3-G-RESP-003.x: Kayikwamba Wagner's account: more than 4,500 wounded; 500 charred corpses in Muzenze prison (her figures, not a finding)
r3-G-RESP-003.n: Meeting date 19 Feb 2025 taken from the transcript index; the page text itself does not print a date in the excerpts. The minister's '500 charred corpses ... after mass executions' differs from the UN-reported 165 women raped and many burned alive (existing claims r1-UNHR-004, r1-GOE-062); recorded as the government's account, not as established. Interpreted transcript.
r3-G-RESP-003.vn: Excerpts verified on the retained transcript, whose header prints '9863rd meeting 19 February 2025' (date field). 'Emergency' is her own wording ('third emergency meeting'). Figures framed as her account; ASR caveat in the note. Her figures are the DRC government's account, not a finding; they differ from UN reporting of 165 women raped at Munzenze. The transcript is machine-generated from interpretation and is not an official UN record.
src: I now give the floor to Her Excellency Ms. Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, State Minister, Minister of Foreign Affairs, International Cooperation, and Francophonie of the Democratic Republic of the Congo.

In Goma, life has stood still. It's been taken hostage by the war. More than 4,500 wounded people have rushed to hospitals that are overflowing. 500 charred corpses were found in the Muzenze prison after mass executions.
And now, Bukavu. The same scenario is playing out: pillaging, hospitals destroyed, roads cut off, a guerre which also kills through hunger and through care denied.

r3-G-RESP-004.s: The New Times (Kigali), a Rwandan state-aligned outlet, reported that Bisimwa said in an earlier, undated post that the accusations against AFC-M23 regarding human rights violations are false and that the mass rapes of female prisoners occurred before AFC-M23's presence in Goma.
r3-G-RESP-004.n: Party account only. Page already cited by r1-SKS-2025Q1-006 for a different fact; this claim records M23's response on the Munzenze prison rapes. Original X post URL not seen; the outlet does not date the 'earlier post'. The existing claim names the speaker as Bertrand Bisimwa; the excerpt prints only 'Bisimwa'.
r3-G-RESP-004.vn: Excerpt verified. Speaker fields completed from the page ('Bertrand Bisimwa, the AFC/M23 rebellion's deputy coordinator'); the statement keeps the excerpt's 'Bisimwa'. Date set to the report date, approximate, since the post is undated. Same URL as r1-SKS-2025Q1-006 but a different fact. Party account via a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. The article identifies him as 'Bertrand Bisimwa, the AFC/M23 rebellion's deputy coordinator'. The post itself was not seen and is undated; it predates the 10 March 2025 article. It contradicts UN and other reporting that places the rapes during the 27 January jailbreak as M23 took Goma.
src: In an earlier post, Bisimwa said: "We urge the world to see the situation for what it truly is and to reject harmful misinformation. The accusations against AFC-M23 regarding human rights violations are false. For instance, the mass rapes of female prisoners occurred before AFC-M23’s presence in Goma, a fact that is easily verifiable.

r3-G-RESP-005.s: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a Human Rights Watch report, stating that Rwanda rejects HRW's allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment, and rejects HRW's attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.
r3-G-RESP-005.l: North Kivu and South Kivu (HRW report subject; places not named in the excerpt)
r3-G-RESP-005.n: The response is titled as answering the HRW report of 10 June 2026. Party statement only. The page carries no date; allAfrica (not cited) reports the statement as issued Thursday 11 June 2026. It answers HRW's 'Death Was Everywhere' report (detention, killings, forced recruitment), not the May 2026 HRW Uvira report; Rwanda's reply to the Uvira report was not found (see gaps).
r3-G-RESP-005.vn: Excerpt verified on retained page. Source date 2026-06-10 is the HRW report's date, not the response's (undated on the page), so month precision kept. B because the claim is only that Rwanda said this, which its own site shows. Party statement from Rwanda's own government site, answering HRW's 10 June 2026 report 'Death Was Everywhere'; the page prints no issue date.
src: Rwanda rejects HRW’s allegations of RDF involvement in forced recruitment, detention, torture, executions, forced labor, or child recruitment. Rwanda also rejects HRW’s attempt to collapse M23 and RDF into one actor.

r3-G-RESP-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that, hours after EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib described the humanitarian situation as "catastrophique", AFC/M23 political coordinator Corneille Nangaa told the press in Goma on 20 February that the situation is catastrophic "non plus dans la zone contrôlée par l'AFC/M23", and asserted that humanitarian access in territories under his movement's control would be "garanti".
r3-G-RESP-006.n: Party statement; the article sets it against the EU commissioner Hadja Lahbib's 'catastrophic' assessment (the commissioner is not named in the cited excerpts). Records a party position on humanitarian access, not a finding on access.
r3-G-RESP-006.vn: Excerpts verified. Year removed from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the date field carries it). Commissioner named in the article title; her 'catastrophique' and Goma are on the page (clause_support). Party position on humanitarian access, not a finding on access.
src: Corneille Nangaa, coordonnateur politique de l’AFC/M23, lui a opposé une lecture radicalement différente. « La situation est catastrophique, non plus dans la zone contrôlée par l’AFC/M23 », a-t-il affirmé devant la presse le 20 février,
Il assure que les territoires sous contrôle de son mouvement constituent désormais « la zone la plus sécurisée du pays » et que l’accès humanitaire y sera « garanti »

r3-G-RESP-007.s: BBC Swahili reported that a Human Rights Watch investigation found that executions and rape were among the atrocities committed by M23 and Rwandan soldiers during their invasion of Uvira, that HRW said it wrote in April to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders for a response to the allegations and no one responded, and that M23 and the Rwandan government had not yet responded to BBC's request for comment.
r3-G-RESP-007.a: M23 and Rwandan soldiers (as alleged by HRW)
r3-G-RESP-007.n: Independent Swahili coverage of HRW's May 2026 Uvira report (HRW pages already cited by other claims). The BBC text says 'week-long' invasion whereas other sources describe an occupation from about 10-11 December 2025 to January 2026; the outlet's wording is flagged, not resolved. Recorded mainly for the party-response information. The 'week-long' wording is the outlet's own.
r3-G-RESP-007.vn: Excerpts verified. 'Occupation' replaced by the source's 'invasion' (uvamizi); HRW is named in the next sentence on the page. excerpt_en flags are false positives from translation. BBC relays HRW's findings (not an independent investigation). 'Week-long invasion' (uvamizi wa wiki moja) is BBC's wording; other sources describe a longer M23 presence in Uvira from December 2025. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-037: Searched for the HRW primary and responses: the HRW report and press release (14 May 2026) and Reuters describe a 'month-long occupation' of Uvira, while BBC's 'week-long invasion' (wiki moja) contradicts the primary. Dropped 'week-long' rather than carry a duration the primary contradicts; no M23 or Rwandan reply found. Attribution to HRW via BBC kept.
src: Unyongaji na ubakaji ni miongoni mwa ukatili uliofanywa na kundi la waasi la M23 na wanajeshi wa Rwanda wakati wa uvamizi wao wa wiki moja katika mji wa Uvira ulioko mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Congo, uchunguzi wa kundi kuu la kutetea haki za binadamu umegundua.
HRW inasema iliandika mwezi Aprili kwa serikali ya Rwanda na viongozi wa M23 kwa ajili ya kujibu madai hayo katika ripoti yake, lakini, inaongeza, hakuna aliyejibu.
M23 na serikali ya Rwanda bado hawajajibu ombi la BBC la kutoa maoni yao.

r3-G-RESP-009.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing local sources, that on the evening of Thursday 13 March CBCA Ndosho hospital in Goma was again the target of an incursion by AFC/M23 rebels, that according to witnesses the rebels fired shots inside the hospital, apparently while pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief, and that a humanitarian source reported that a bullet hit a patient in the thigh.
r3-G-RESP-009.l: CBCA Ndosho hospital, Goma, North Kivu
r3-G-RESP-009.x: Actualite.cd: one patient hit by a bullet in the thigh
r3-G-RESP-009.n: Single local outlet, anonymous sources. Follows the 28 Feb-3 Mar raids on this hospital (existing claims r1-HC-2025-001, r1-GOE-055). Per the article the rebels were reportedly looking for a young man presumed to be a thief; not used in the statement. No AFC/M23 response found (see gaps).
r3-G-RESP-009.vn: Excerpts verified on retained page; shots fired inside added from the page (witness account, clause_support). Year not printed in excerpt, so omitted from the statement. Single local outlet relying on unnamed local, witness and humanitarian sources. Per witnesses, the rebels were apparently pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-036: The verifier records that the same page, per witnesses, says the rebels were apparently pursuing a young man presumed to be a thief; that is a competing explanation of why shots were fired inside the hospital (pursuit, not targeting of the facility) and the statement omits it. Search (CBCA Ndosho M23 13 mars voleur) found no other account or AFC/M23 denial. No retained capture of the page was available to me, so the editor should confirm the clause on the page before applying; no names or numbers added.
src: Dans la soirée de ce jeudi 13 mars, l'hôpital CBCA Ndosho de Goma (Nord-Kivu) a, une nouvelle fois, été la cible d'une incursion des rebelles de l’AFC/M23, ont rapporté à ACTUALITE.CD des sources locales.
Une source humanitaire a rapporté à ACTUALITES.CD qu’une balle a atteint un patient à la cuisse.

r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-008.s: Al Jazeera reported that Rwanda said international sanctions would reduce the likelihood of peace with M23, after the UK said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic measures on Kigali; Rwanda's Ministry of Foreign Affairs called the measures 'regrettable' and said the UK 'has now clearly chosen a side'.
r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-008.a: Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-008.n: Article published 2025-02-26 says the statement was issued 'on Tuesday' (date computed from weekday and publication date: 2025-02-25). Quotation fragments in the statement are from the article's longer passage; only the excerpt's words are relied on for the attribution. The UK measures were diplomatic (aid pause, limited trade promotion), not asset freezes. Rwanda's wider position is covered elsewhere.
r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-008.vn: Page re-fetched; both passages verbatim, no wire credit on the page. Party statement stays attributed to Rwanda's MFA. Date derived from the weekday, so precision approximate. src: Rwanda has said international sanctions will reduce the likelihood of peace with M23 rebels in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) , after the United Kingdom said it would pause some bilateral aid and impose other diplomatic sanctions on Kigali.

“The punitive measures announced today by the UK government in response to the conflict in eastern DRC – where the UK has now clearly chosen a side – are regrettable,” Rwanda’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs said in a statement on Tuesday.

r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-009.s: Kivu Times reported that on 14 February 2025 the Bukavu garrison military tribunal, presided by magistrate major Amsini Lazare, sentenced 212 of 282 prosecuted FARDC soldiers to death for offences including murder, rape, attempted murder, dissipation of munitions and flight before the enemy, and acquitted 70.

r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Friday 2 October the Uvira garrison military tribunal sentenced to death twenty-seven soldiers of the Republican Guard for cowardice before the enemy, after a flagrancy trial of 112 soldiers of the FARDC 21st battalion 'Simba' accused of abandoning or poorly securing positions on the heights of Malimba and Masangu on the night of 22 to 23 August 2026; fifty-four others received five years, ten received six months, and twenty-one defendants, including five women, were acquitted.

src: Le tribunal militaire de garnison d’Uvira a condamné à mort vingt-sept militaires de la Garde républicaine, vendredi 2 octobre, à l’issue d’un procès en flagrance tenu durant deux semaines à la prison centrale d’Uvira. Les prévenus étaient poursuivis notamment pour lâcheté devant l’ennemi et violation des consignes.

Au total, 112 militaires du 21ᵉ bataillon Simba des FARDC comparaissaient devant la justice militaire. Ils étaient accusés d’avoir abandonné ou mal assuré la défense de positions stratégiques situées sur les hauteurs de Malimba et Masangu, dans la nuit du 22 au 23 août 2026,

Vingt-sept militaires ont été condamnés à la peine de mort pour lâcheté. Cinquante-quatre autres ont écopé de cinq ans de servitude pénale pour violation des consignes, tandis que dix militaires ont été condamnés à six mois de servitude pénale pour les mêmes faits. En revanche, vingt-et-un prévenu, dont cinq femmes, ont été acquittés faute de preuves suffisantes.

src: La Première ministre, Judith Suminwa a présidé ce mercredi 8 juillet 2026 à New York, aux États-Unis d’Amérique, la 10190e séance du Conseil de sécurité des Nations unies

Poursuivant son intervention, la cheffe du gouvernement congolais a dénoncé les violences sexuelles commises dans l’Est de la République démocratique du Congo, qu’elle a attribuées aux groupes armés et aux forces étrangères dont le Rwanda impliquées dans le conflit.

Dans certaines zones affectées par les groupes armés et sous occupation par des forces étrangères, dont le Rwanda, ces violences sont liées aux déplacements forcés, aux économies illicites et aux logiques de prédation qui alimentent la guerre.

src: l’ambassadrice Jocelyne Kabengele Lukundulu, l’a indiqué lundi 26 octobre lors de la 10 251e séance du Conseil de sécurité avec comme thème « Les enfants et les conflits ». La diplomate congolaise a présenté les avancées de son pays en matière de protection des enfants et appelé à combattre l’impunité ainsi qu’à intégrer cette dimension dans les accords de paix.

Sa représentante permanente adjointe auprès des Nations Unies, l’ambassadrice Jocelyne Kabengele Lukundulu, l’a indiqué lundi 26 octobre lors de la 10 251e séance du Conseil de sécurité avec comme thème « Les enfants et les conflits ».

La situation sur le terrain demeure préoccupante. L’expérience congolaise confirme que la protection de l’enfance doit être intégrée dans la conception des cessez-le-feu, des accords de paix et des mécanismes de justice transitionnelle.

src: Selon une source médicale de la zone de santé de Katoyi, qui s’est exprimée sous couvert d’anonymat, quatre structures sanitaires, à savoir le centre de santé (CS) Ufamandu, le CS Miano, le centre de santé de référence (CSR) Katuunda et le CS Nyandeki, ont été détruites dans le contexte de ces combats.
D’après cette source, les bâtiments sanitaires ont été endommagés par des bombardements, après que des médicaments entreposés dans ces structures ont été pillés par des personnes non identifiées.

La situation sanitaire se dégrade dans le groupement Ufamandu 1er, en territoire de Masisi, à la suite des affrontements armés qui opposent les rebelles du Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN) aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par les Wazalendo.

r4-G-HC-DATA-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that a nurse of the Masisi general referral hospital, identified as Montaigne Byanikiro, was shot dead in the night of Wednesday to Thursday 19 February 2026 in Masisi centre, Bahunde chiefdom; according to local sources, unidentified armed men burst into his home at around 23 hours and reportedly opened fire several times before fleeing. The Masisi nurses condemned what they called a new murder targeting a member of the health staff.

The same article, citing an official notice, also said the two patients reportedly left the hospital centre before the child's planned transfer to an Ebola treatment centre.

src: Les faits se sont produits à la suite d’une attaque menée par des hommes porteurs d’armes blanches qui ont fait irruption dans cet établissement sanitaire pour retirer de force une femme et son enfant, pourtant récemment testés positifs à l’épidémie d’Ebola.
Il s’agit de Zawadi Manacée et de sa fille Christelle Kavugho, âgée de six ans et demi, activement recherchées par la coordination provinciale de la riposte contre Ebola.

La Division provinciale de la santé du Nord-Kivu a lancé un avis de recherche après la disparition de deux malades atteints d'Ebola au Centre hospitalier adventiste de Wanamahika, situé à Mutiri, dans la ville de Butembo.

Selon un avis officiel publié le 16 juin rendu public par la division provinciale de la santé au Nord-Kivu, l’enfant avait été confirmée positive à la maladie à virus Ebola. Les deux patientes auraient quitté le Centre hospitalier adventiste de Mutiri avant le transfert prévu de la fillette vers un Centre de traitement Ebola (CTE).

r4-G-HC-DATA-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that on Saturday 1 August residents of the Cité Belge neighbourhood in Beni opposed the transfer of a patient suspected of Ebola to a treatment centre and that the ambulance carrying out her evacuation was stoned, requiring the intervention of law enforcement. Insecurity Insight, citing Congo Quotidien, MSN and Reuters, reported that on 01 August 2026 in Cité Belge neighbourhood, Bungulu commune, Beni city, an ambulance sent to evacuate an Ebola patient was stoned by demonstrators, who broke its windshield, and that police fired warning shots to disperse them.
r4-G-HC-DATA-011.l: Cité Belge neighbourhood, Bungulu commune, Beni city, North Kivu
r4-G-HC-DATA-011.n: Epidemic-context incident; two independent chains (Radio Okapi; Insecurity Insight citing other outlets). Not an armed-conflict event.

selon un rapport consulté vendredi. L’incident le plus grave signalé dans ce document s’est produit à Kasanga Tuha, dans l’aire de santé de Bunji, au Nord-Kivu. r4-G-LOCAL-NK-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that vehicles carrying men and equipment had been seen shuttling for about two weeks on the Kirumba-Katondi axis in southern Lubero, a movement it said had intensified since a recent AFC/M23 meeting at Kirumba at which the rebellion expressed its intention to take Butembo and Beni.

Des renforts importants du mouvement politico-militaire AFC/M23 ont été signalés ce mardi dans la partie sud du territoire de Lubero

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that an AFC-M23 patrol was ambushed by CMC fighters at Mashango village (Bukombo grouping, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru) the day before its report, and, citing several local sources, that dozens of civilians, notably residents of Katsiru who had come to Mashango for community work, were trapped in the exchange of fire; at least 18 wounded civilians were admitted to Mwesso referral hospital in neighbouring Masisi territory, according to medical sources.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Representation of Students of Congo (REC) Butembo-Lubero announced on Wednesday 12 November the immediate suspension of classes in all institutions of Butembo city and Lubero territory after the death of Rosette Kavira Vyahula, a student at ISTM Butembo, shot dead by a muzalendo militiaman. The outlet says the shot reportedly occurred during a dispute between wazalendo groups at Vweyera, and elsewhere that she was killed by a muzalendo militiaman named Nzingene at Musimba as she returned from lectures; she was taken to hospital at Musimba and died of her wounds.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-004.l: Musimba / Vweyera, near Butembo, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-004.a: a muzalendo militiaman named Nzingene, per Actualite.cd

Naming of the alleged shooter is the outlet's, not a judicial finding. The article also prints the name order 'Kavira Vyahula Rosette' and gives the institute as both 'Institut supérieur technique de médecine' and 'Institut supérieur des techniques médicales'. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'shot reportedly during a dispute between wazalendo groups at Vweyera': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'taken to hospital at Musimba, died of wounds': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: La Représentation des étudiants du Congo (REC) Butembo-Lubero a annoncé mercredi 12 novembre la suspension immédiate des cours dans toutes les institutions de la ville de Butembo et du territoire de Lubero, à la suite de la mort tragique de Rosette Kavira Vyahula, étudiante à l’Institut supérieur technique de médecine (ISTM) Butembo, abattue par balle par un milicien muzalendo.
Inscrite en première licence dans la faculté de Sage-femme, elle a été tuée par un milicien muzalendo répondant au nom de Nzingene à Musimba, alors qu’elle revenait de l’auditoire.
Le tir serait survenu lors d’une dispute entre groupes des wazalendo dans l’agglomération de Vweyera, vers MTB.
Transportée d’urgence à l’hôpital Saint Raphaël, connu sous le nom de Maison Rouge à Musimba, elle y a succombé à ses blessures

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that socio-economic activities were partially paralysed on the morning of Thursday 11 September in Butembo, where urban civil society and LUCHA held a 'day of mourning without activities' in solidarity with communities bereaved by recent ADF attacks, which it said had killed more than 70 civilians at Ntoyo (Lubero territory) and 18 at Fotodu (Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory); around 10:45 demonstrators and police clashed, the police using live ammunition and demonstrators throwing stones, and the outlet said no serious incident had been reported so far.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.l: Butembo (city); attacks at Ntoyo (Lubero) and Fotodu (Beni-Mbau), North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.a: Butembo civil society / LUCHA; ADF (as the attackers of the killings mourned)
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.x: Actualite.cd: more than 70 civilians killed at Ntoyo; 18 at Fotodu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.n: Figures are as stated in the Actualite.cd article; the Ntoyo toll should be reconciled against Radio Okapi/UN counts by a later pass. Radio Okapi (2025-09-10) separately gives 18 civilians killed at Fotodhu on 9 September.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-005.vn: Exact excerpts; publication date removed; 'Butembo' and 'no serious incident' carried by the page (page-only clauses). One article, one origin. Toll discrepancy inside the same article: 'more than 70' at Ntoyo in the lead, 'at least 72' killed at Ntoyo in the night of 8-9 September later on, a LUCHA activist's 'more than 100', and a Congolese government figure of 80 civilians killed in two days across Lubero and Beni. Reconcile against Radio Okapi/UN counts. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Butembo day of mourning without activities': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'no serious incident reported so far': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: Restores the day the verifier removed because no excerpt printed it; the proposed add_excerpt on source 0 prints 'Les activités socio-économiques ont été partiellement paralysées ce jeudi 11 septembre dans la matinée dans la ville de Butembo'. Matches the claim date 2025-09-11. Adds a number, so FLAGGED.
src: La société civile urbaine et le mouvement citoyen Lutte pour le Changement (LUCHA), en solidarité avec les communautés endeuillées par les récentes attaques des rebelles ADF, ont organisé une journée de « deuil sans activités ».
Ces attaques ont coûté la vie à plus de 70 civils à Ntoyo, dans le territoire de Lubero, et à 18 autres à Fotodu, dans le secteur de Beni-Mbau (territoire de Beni).

Aux environs de 10h45, des affrontements ont éclaté entre des manifestants et des éléments de la police. Cette dernière a fait usage de tirs à balles réelles, tandis que les manifestants répondaient par des jets de pierres.
Les activités socio-économiques ont été partiellement paralysées ce jeudi 11 septembre dans la matinée dans la ville de Butembo
Aucun incident grave n’a toutefois été signalé jusqu’à présent.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-006.s: Actualite.cd reported a 'ville morte' day in Butembo called by the citizen-movements synergy and pressure groups; LUCHA activist Jean-Pierre Kasma told the outlet its main aim was to demand the departure of the mayor of Butembo, the removal of the urban police commander, the relocation of 'wazalendo' group positions inside and around the city, and the opening of independent investigations.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-006.a: LUCHA and Butembo citizen movements; Wazalendo (as named in the demands)
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-006.n: The claimed insecurity in the demand ('assassinats, vols à main armée...') is the organisers' framing. No statement from the Butembo mayor or the police found in the article.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-006.vn: Exact excerpt; publication date (13) not in excerpt so removed from the statement (the claim date keeps it); synergy clause from the page's lead. src: Contacté par ACTUALITÉ.CD, Jean-Pierre Kasma, militant du mouvement citoyen Lutte pour le Changement (LUCHA), indique que l'objectif principal de cette journée ville morte et d’exiger le départ du maire de Butembo, le relèvement du commandant urbain de la police, la délocalisation des positions des groupes « wazalendo » installées à l’intérieur et aux abords de la ville, ainsi que l’ouverture d’enquêtes indépendantes
à la suite d’un appel à une journée ville morte lancé par la synergie des mouvements citoyens et des groupes de pression
