r4-G-LOCAL-NK-007.x: protesters: at least eight murders in under a month
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-007.n: Figure is the protesters' claim as relayed by Radio Okapi; no official tally found.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-007.vn: Exact excerpt; publication date and digit figure removed (not printed in the excerpt). The figure is the protesters' claim; no official tally found. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'day without activities in Beni': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Selon les manifestants, au moins huit meurtres ont été enregistrés en moins d’un mois dans la ville de Beni, impliquant des hommes armés, parmi lesquels des militaires déjà arrêtés.
À l’initiative des mouvements citoyens et des groupes de pression, une journée sans activités a été organisée

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008.s: Radio Okapi reported that an attack attributed to ADF rebels in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May killed at least 26, many of them farmers; according to local civil society it took place in the Babila-Bakaiko farming zones about 40 km west of the rural commune of Oicha (Beni), in the farming blocks of Katere, Manzumbu, Musangwa, Wasafi and Mangambo.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008.l: Babila-Bakaiko farming zones, west of Oicha, Beni territory, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008.x: Radio Okapi: at least 26 killed (many farmers)
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008.n: Task lead said 24 killed for the 6 May Beni attack; this source says at least 26. Night of Tue 5 to Wed 6 May as written by the outlet. No names of victims given.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008.vn: Exact excerpts support every clause; removed the year (not in excerpt) though it is in the claim date. Attribution to the ADF is the outlet's ('attribuée'); the outlet also says FARDC-UPDF joint forces were deployed in pursuit, per local sources. A task lead gave 24 killed; this source says at least 26.
src: Une nouvelle attaque attribuée aux rebelles des ADF la nuit de mardi à mercredi 6 mai a fait au moins 26 morts, parmi lesquels de nombreux agriculteurs.

Selon la société civile locale, l'attaque est survenue dans les zones agricoles de Babila-Bakaiko, situées à environ 40 kilomètres à l’ouest de la commune rurale d’Oicha, Beni (Nord-Kivu). Cette structure citoyenne précise que les civils ont été tués précisément dans les blocs agricoles de Katere, Manzumbu, Musangwa, Wasafi et Mangambo.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009.s: Radio Okapi reported that Denis Mukwege strongly condemned on Monday 1 June the attacks attributed to ADF rebels that killed at least 16 in the localities of Ngadi and Vemba, Beni territory, in the night of 'samedi 31 mai', and that he was particularly alarmed by violence against members of the indigenous pygmy community.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009.l: Ngadi and Vemba, Beni territory, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009.n: Date discrepancy within Radio Okapi: this article says 'samedi 31 mai' but 31 May 2026 was a Sunday; another Radio Okapi item of 2 June refers to a massacre of pygmies on Saturday 30 May 2026 and about 20 dead (not opened). Treat as 30-31 May. Mukwege is a Nobel laureate and public figure, not a party to the conflict.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009.vn: Exact excerpts; only the year removed from the statement. Toll is the outlet's, attribution to ADF kept as 'attributed'. Date discrepancy: the source says 'samedi 31 mai' 2026, but 31 May 2026 was a Sunday; the night may be 30-31 May. Mukwege's statement is not a party's; it uses labels ('terroristes', 'épuration identitaire') that stay his.
src: Le Prix Nobel de la paix 2018, Denis Mukwege, a vivement condamné, lundi 1er juin, les attaques attribuées aux rebelles des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) qui ont fait au moins 16 morts dans les localités de Ngadi et Vemba, dans le territoire de Beni (Nord-Kivu), dans la nuit du samedi 31 mai.
Denis Mukwege s'est particulièrement alarmé des violences visant les membres de la communauté autochtone pygmée.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International, in a report published on Tuesday 5 May, denounced massive abuses by ADF rebels against civilians in North Kivu and Ituri, citing violations including killings, abductions and torture, forced marriages and pregnancies, and repeated sexual violence.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-010.x: no figures in the Radio Okapi summary
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-010.n: Secondhand summary of an Amnesty report (primary report not opened here; a later pass should fetch it from amnesty.org). The summary uses legal labels in a quoted attribution; omitted here.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-010.vn: Exact excerpts; 'murder' rendered 'killings'; year removed from statement. excerpt_en flag is Nord-Kivu/Allied Democratic Forces rendering only. Second-hand summary of an Amnesty report; fetch the primary report from amnesty.org. Radio Okapi also quotes Amnesty's legal characterisation, attributed to the NGO; not used here.
src: Elle évoque plusieurs violations notamment : des meurtres, des enlèvements et tortures, des mariages et grossesses forcées des violences sexuelles répétées.

Dans un rapport publié ce mardi 5 mai, Amnesty International dénonce des exactions massives commises par les rebelles des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) contre des civils au Nord-Kivu et en Ituri.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International, in its report on the ADF, said the attacks target mainly populations but also fields, health centres and homes, often looted and then burned.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-011.n: General statement, no named facility. Specific example in the existing set: Musenge health centre burned (Radio Okapi 2026-01-26, already cited).
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-011.vn: Exact excerpt; removed the report date (number not in excerpt; it stays in the claim date). General statement; no facility named.
src: Les attaques visent essentiellement les populations, mais aussi les champs, les centres de santé et les habitations, souvent pillés puis incendiés, explique l’organisation.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that Amnesty International said it had documented serious human rights abuses in mining zones controlled by the M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu, based on testimony from 26 people, with research on a coltan mine near Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and the Lomera gold site (Kabare, South Kivu); Amnesty said it had documented the summary execution of 18 artisanal miners at Rubaya and Lomera, of whom, according to testimony, ten were reportedly beaten to death, two shot dead and six abducted before being found dead.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.l: Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare, South Kivu)
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.a: M23 (as Amnesty describes the zones as M23-controlled)
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.x: Amnesty (via Radio Okapi): 18 miners executed (reportedly 10 beaten to death, 2 shot, 6 abducted then found dead); 26 people interviewed
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.n: Secondhand summary of an Amnesty briefing; fetch the primary from amnesty.org in a later pass. Spans both provinces; Lomera is South Kivu. Radio Okapi 2025-11-06 forced-recruitment item at Masisi is already cited.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-012.vn: Exact excerpts; publication date removed; the testimony breakdown kept conditional; scope restated to Amnesty's words. Second-hand summary of an Amnesty briefing; fetch the primary. The breakdown is conditional in the source ('auraient été'). Radio Okapi says the M23 and Rwandan authorities did not respond to Amnesty's request for comment. Lomera is in South Kivu.
src: Amnesty International affirme avoir documenté l’exécution sommaire de 18 mineurs artisanaux à Rubaya et Lomera. Selon les témoignages recueillis par l’organisation, dix personnes auraient été battues à mort, deux tuées par balle et six autres enlevées avant d’être retrouvées mortes.
Amnesty International affirme avoir documenté de graves atteintes aux droits humains dans des zones minières contrôlées par le M23 au Nord-Kivu et au Sud-Kivu.

L’organisation dit avoir recueilli les témoignages de 26 personnes, notamment des mineurs artisanaux, des spécialistes du secteur minier, des propriétaires de puits et des proches de victimes. Ses recherches portent notamment sur une mine de coltan près de Rubaya, dans le territoire de Masisi au Nord-Kivu, et sur le site aurifère de Lomera, dans le territoire de Kabare au Sud-Kivu.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-013.s: Kivu Morning Post wrote, without naming a source, that on 2 January an FARDC drone missed its target at Masisi centre, exploding on homes and causing more than 40 civilian wounded and at least 6 dead.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-013.l: Masisi centre, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-013.x: Kivu Morning Post: more than 40 civilians wounded, at least 6 dead
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-013.n: Single local outlet (Goma-based), stated as fact without a named source; no FARDC statement found. Needs corroboration from OCHA/Protection Cluster.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-013.vn: Exact excerpt; removed the article date (not in excerpt). Stated by the outlet as fact without a named source, in an article about Walikale fighting; no FARDC statement found. Needs corroboration (OCHA/Protection Cluster). 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-036: Two searches: the event itself (an explosion at Masisi-centre on 2 January 2026 with civilian dead and dozens wounded) is widely reported, but the FARDC drone attribution is contested: RFI 8 Jan 2026 headline calls it 'une supposée frappe de drone'; TV5Monde 9 Jan 2026: 'RDC: le M23 accuse les FARDC d'avoir bombardé Masisi' and 'zones d'ombre après l'explosion', snippet 'Certaines sources parlent d'une frappe de drone sans être en ...'; beto.cd: 'une explosion que personne ne revendique'. Tolls also vary by date and outlet (Actualite.cd 2 Jan: 4 dead, 7 wounded provisional; KMP 2 Jan: 4 dead, 15+ wounded; SOS Médias Burundi 4 Jan: 7 dead, 40+ wounded). No FARDC statement found. The amend marks the KMP wording as an unsourced assertion; the editor should add the RFI/TV5 counter-accounts as separate claims and keep the C grade.
src: Le 2 janvier, un drone des FARDC a raté sa cible à Masisi centre, explosant sur des habitations et causant plus de 40 blessés civils et au moins 6 morts.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 rebels had taken control of Buhimba and Mahanga (Walikale and Masisi territories) over the weekend after dislodging the Congolese army and the Wazalendo; Kipande Mungo, head of Osso Banyungu sector, told the outlet the rebels had been at Mahanga in Osso since Saturday at 12:00 and the population was dispersed.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-014.l: Buhimba and Mahanga, Walikale and Masisi territories, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-014.n: Weekend of 22-23 Nov 2025 (Saturday 22 Nov). Later KMP item (5 Jan 2026) says Buhimba was under government control after two days of fighting, with M23 withdrawing to Mahanga and Kasopo; see next claims.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-014.vn: Exact excerpt; speaker name and title carried by the page (page-only clause; excerpt_en added it). Publication date removed. Downgraded to C: one local outlet with one named local official. Weekend before the 24 November report. Single local outlet. A later KMP item (5 January 2026) has Buhimba under government control after M23 withdrew. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'speaker Kipande Mungo, head of Osso Banyungu sector': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Les rebelles de l’AFC-M23 ont pris le contrôle des agglomérations de Buhimba et Mahanga, en territoires de Walikale et Masisi, ce week-end après avoir délogé l’armée congolaise et les Wazalendo. « Depuis samedi à 12h00, les rebelles sont à Mahanga dans Osso. La population est dispersée »
a déclaré à Kivu Morning Post Kipande Mungo, chef du secteur Osso Banyungu.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the Congolese army accused the rebels of carrying out several attacks on its positions in Rutshuru, Masisi and Kalehe and said it would not let this happen.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-015.n: Paired with the AFC-M23 counter-accusation in the next claim; neither is dated or sourced to a named spokesperson in the article.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-015.vn: Exact excerpt; publication date removed. No spokesperson or communique named; the outlet's paraphrase.
src: L’armée accuse les rebelles de mener plusieurs attaques contre ses positions à Rutshuru, Masisi et Kalehe, et affirme qu’elle ne va pas laisser faire. De son côté, l’AFC-M23 accuse les FARDC de violer l’accord signé à Doha en rompant le cessez-le-feu.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, for its part, the AFC-M23 accused the FARDC of violating the agreement signed in Doha by breaking the ceasefire.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-016.n: Reported secondhand by Kivu Morning Post; the AFC-M23 communique itself was not located.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-016.vn: Exact excerpt; publication date removed. Party says, as paraphrased by the outlet; the AFC-M23 communique itself was not located.
src: L’armée accuse les rebelles de mener plusieurs attaques contre ses positions à Rutshuru, Masisi et Kalehe, et affirme qu’elle ne va pas laisser faire. De son côté, l’AFC-M23 accuse les FARDC de violer l’accord signé à Doha en rompant le cessez-le-feu.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that relative calm was reported at Buhimba (Waloa Yungu grouping) after two days of violent fighting between FARDC and M23, that M23 fighters had withdrawn to Mahanga and Kasopo in neighbouring Masisi territory, and, citing a local source, that Buhimba remained under government forces' control.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-017.l: Buhimba, Walikale territory (M23 withdrew to Mahanga and Kasopo, Masisi), North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-017.n: Single local source; the handover date of Buhimba back to FARDC is not given (KMP related-article list mentions 'l’AFC-M23 reprend Buhimba', title only, not opened).
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-017.vn: Exact excerpts; attribution narrowed (only the control clause is the local source's); publication date removed. The date Buhimba returned to government control is not given. The same article says Buhimba civilians had been dispersed in the bush or at Lushali and Nyabiondo for nearly six months.
src: À Buhimba, dans le groupement voisin de Waloa Yungu, un calme relatif est signalé après deux jours de combats violents entre les FARDC et le M23. Les combattants du M23 se sont repliés vers Mahanga et Kasopo, en territoire voisin de Masisi.
La localité de Buhimba reste sous contrôle des forces gouvernementales, selon une source locale.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-018.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing a local civil-society source, that Wazalendo launched their first attack on AFC-M23 positions on Saturday 28 February 2026 and that intense fighting pitted AFC-M23 fighters against the Wazalendo from early Monday in Kibati village (Luberike grouping, Walikale). It also reported that the fighting intensified until Sunday 1 March but that AFC-M23 repelled the assaults and held its positions in central Kibati.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-018.l: Kibati, Luberike grouping, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-018.n: Single local source. Other KMP items found (Muheto attack, Jan-Jun 2026 Kibati/Buhimba) not opened.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-018.vn: Exact excerpts; publication date removed; attribution matched to the excerpts. Per the same source, AFC-M23 repelled the assaults through 1 March and held its positions in central Kibati. 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'local civil-society source': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'context: AFC-M23 repelled the assaults and held central Kibati': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: Moves the outcome the verifier kept only in the note into the statement, now carried by a proposed add_excerpt on source 0 ('Les combats se sont intensifiés jusqu'à dimanche 1er mars, mais l'AFC-M23 a repoussé les assauts et maintenu ses positions au centre de Kibati.'). Discrepancy surfaced, not resolved: the article has fighting 'from early Monday' and intensifying 'until Sunday 1 March'; it does not say which Monday. Adds a number, so FLAGGED.
src: D’après notre source, les Wazalendo ont lancé leur première attaque contre les positions de l’AFC-M23 samedi 28 février 2026.
Des combats intenses opposent depuis tôt ce lundi les combattants de l’AFC-M23 aux Wazalendo dans le village de Kibati, situé dans le groupement de Luberike, territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu.
Selon une source locale de la société civile
Les combats se sont intensifiés jusqu’à dimanche 1er mars, mais l’AFC-M23 a repoussé les assauts et maintenu ses positions au centre de Kibati.

r4-G-LOCAL-NK-019.s: Radio Okapi reported that fighting continued, notably around Ngungu, Rubaya, Nyabiondo and on the axis toward Pinga, despite ceasefire appeals, and that control of Rubaya, one of the country's main coltan and cassiterite sites, had remained in AFC/M23 hands for nearly two years.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-019.l: Masisi territory (Ngungu, Rubaya, Nyabiondo, Pinga axis), North Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-019.n: Analysis-style piece; the 'sources civiles et militaires' are unnamed.
r4-G-LOCAL-NK-019.vn: Exact excerpts; publication date removed; the 'civilian and military sources' attribution kept to the fighting clause it belongs to. Analysis piece; sources unnamed. Rubaya was under M23 control from before 2025 per 'nearly two years'; this is the outlet's estimate. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Masisi fighting between FARDC, Wazalendo and AFC/M23, per civilian and military sources': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Les combats se poursuivent notamment autour de Ngungu, Rubaya, Nyabiondo et sur l’axe menant vers Pinga, malgré les appels au cessez-le-feu.
Rubaya, l’un des principaux sites d’exploitation du coltan et de la cassitérite du pays, le contrôle reste entre les mains de l’AFC/M23 depuis près de deux ans.

le territoire de Masisi, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, reste marqué par des affrontements entre les forces armées congolaises, leurs alliés Wazalendo et les rebelles de la coalition AFC/M23, selon plusieurs sources civiles et militaires.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said summary executions of civilians were multiplying, notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory, and that in the night of 23 to 24 November at least 12 people were arrested and then summarily executed by AFC/M23 rebels, who accused them of collaborating with or belonging to the Wazalendo.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.l: Katana groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.a: AFC/M23 (as alleged by Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.x: Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani: at least 12 executed
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.n: Local NGO allegation relayed by Radio Okapi; also concerns removal of a patient from a health centre (health: patients_removed). Excerpt translation is of the passage as copied.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-001.vn: Excerpt exact. Narrowed: the page links Katana/Kabare to the wave of executions (preceding sentence and title), not explicitly to the 12; Coalition's name is in the preceding sentence on the page (page-only clause). NGO allegation, single origin. The page places the executions in a passage on killings 'notably' in Katana groupement and its title says 'à Kabare'; it does not name the village of the 12. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said summary executions were multiplying, notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Dans la nuit du 23 au 24 novembre, la Coalition rapporte qu'au moins 12 personnes ont été arrêtées puis sommairement exécutées par les rebelles de la coalition AFC/M23﻿, les accusant de collaborer avec le groupe Wazalendo ou d’appartenir à ce groupe d’autodéfense

La Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani﻿ exprime sa vive inquiétude face aux « massacres et exécutions sommaires » de civils qui se multiplient dans la province du Sud-Kivu, notamment dans le groupement de Katana﻿, territoire de Kabare

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-002.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani said that, among at least 12 people arrested then summarily executed in the night of 23 to 24 November (in a report on executions notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory), was a patient removed from a health centre before his execution; the victims were aged 20 to 40.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-002.l: Katana groupement, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-002.n: Same page as previous claim, recorded separately for the health-care register. Health centre not named.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-002.vn: Both excerpts exact. Same location narrowing as claim 0. Added victims' age range (printed in source 1 excerpt). Health centre not named; the page does not say where the patient was taken from. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani; executions notably in Katana groupement, Kabare territory': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Dans la nuit du 23 au 24 novembre, la Coalition rapporte qu'au moins 12 personnes ont été arrêtées puis sommairement exécutées par les rebelles
Les victimes étaient âgées de 20 à 40 ans. Parmi elles, un patient retiré d’un centre de santé avant son exécution.

La Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani﻿ exprime sa vive inquiétude face aux « massacres et exécutions sommaires » de civils qui se multiplient dans la province du Sud-Kivu, notamment dans le groupement de Katana﻿, territoire de Kabare

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani also denounced the summary execution of two young men of the same family at Kaniola, Walungu territory, on 21 November, killed and then buried in a mass grave by AFC/M23 elements.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-003.x: Coalition Pamoja kwa Amani: two young men
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-003.n: Single NGO source relayed by a media outlet.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-003.vn: Excerpt exact and carries every clause; NGO allegation attributed.
src: la coalition Pamoja kwa Amani dénonce aussi d'autres exécutions sommaires, comme celle de deux jeunes hommes d’une même famille à Kaniola﻿, territoire de Walungu, le 21 novembre, tués puis enterrés dans une fosse commune par des éléments de l’AFC/M23.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC 3rd defence zone, based in Kisangani, published a communiqué on Friday 8 August in which its spokesperson, Major Mavudisa Kamba, condemned targeted killings of civilians and forced recruitment of minors by the RDF/M23/AFC coalition in South Kivu, and cited the killing of more than 80 civilians on 4 August 2025 at Nyamarongo village, Boavo chefferie, and of six civilians, two of them minors, at Lumbichi on 24 July.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-004.l: South Kivu (Nyamarongo, Boavo chefferie; Lumbichi, as printed)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-004.x: FARDC: more than 80 civilians at Nyamarongo (4 August 2025); six civilians, two of them minors, at Lumbichi (24 July)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-004.n: Party (FARDC) allegation; territory printed as "Kalé" by the page (probable typo, not corrected). A 3rd defence zone based in Kisangani is cited for South Kivu. Needs independent corroboration of the 80+ figure.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-004.vn: All three excerpts exact. Flag '23' resolved: it is the '23' of 'RDF/M23/AFC', which the page prints in its first sentence and title ('coalition RDF/M23/AFC dans la province du Sud-Kivu') but no stored excerpt carries; page-only clause, so kept rather than corrected (a correction would be refused for the number). Extend excerpt 0 with source_edits.py add_excerpt. Party (FARDC) allegation; the page prints the territory as 'Kalé', which is not a South Kivu territory name (possibly Kalehe; unverified). The 80+ figure is uncorroborated here. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'exactions by the RDF/M23/AFC coalition in South Kivu': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'cited the killing of more than 80 civilians on 4 August 2025 at Nyamarongo, Boavo chefferie, and six civilians, two of them minors, at Lumbichi on 24 July': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: La 3eme zone de défense des FARDC, basée à Kisangani, a publié vendredi 08 août un communiqué

Selon le porte-parole de cette zone militaire, le major Mavudisa Kamba, les forces loyalistes condamnent fermement les assassinats ciblés de civils, ainsi que le recrutement forcé de mineurs par ces groupes armés

Le 4 août 2025, plus de 80 civils ont été abattus au village Nyamarongo, dans la chefferie de Boavo, territoire de Kalé. - Le 24 juillet, six autres civils, dont deux mineurs, ont été exécutés à Lumbichi, accusés à tort de refuser de transporter des armes et des munitions.

La 3eme zone de défense des FARDC, basée à Kisangani, a publié vendredi 08 août un communiqué dans lequel elle exprime sa vive indignation face aux exactions commises par la coalition RDF/M23/AFC dans la province du Sud-Kivu

le major Mavudisa a rappelé deux massacres récents perpétrés par cette coalition : - Le 4 août 2025, plus de 80 civils ont été abattus au village Nyamarongo, dans la chefferie de Boavo, territoire de Kalé. - Le 24 juillet, six autres civils, dont deux mineurs, ont été exécutés à Lumbichi, accusés à tort de refuser de transporter des armes et des munitions.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-005.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that AFC-M23 rebels extended their progression in Shabunda territory, South Kivu, by occupying the villages Kimbili and Nyalubemba after an offensive on 20 November against forward positions of the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters, and that, according to local civil society, the Nyalubemba health centre at Kimbili was overwhelmed by civilian and military wounded.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-005.l: Kimbili and Nyalubemba, Bamuguba Sud groupement, Bakisi chefferie, Shabunda territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-005.n: Health-care element (centre overwhelmed) recorded in the same claim. Page also says Maimingi taken 16 November (first incursion into Shabunda).
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-005.vn: Both excerpts exact. excerpt_en flag resolved: the capitalised words ('The', 'FARDC') translate 'Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC)'; it translates the excerpt alone. Page also gives about 1769 households displaced and Maimingi taken on 16 November (not in this claim).
src: Les rebelles de l'AFC-M23﻿ ont étendu leur progression dans le territoire de Shabunda﻿, au Sud-Kivu en occupant les villages Kimbili﻿ et Nyalubemba﻿ à la suite d'une offensive menée le 20 novembre contre les positions avancées des Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et des combattants Wazalendo﻿, rapportent des sources concordantes.
A l'issue des affrontements entre les belligérants, le centre de santé de Nyalubemba﻿ à Kimbili﻿ est débordé par les blessés civils et militaires, selon la société civile locale.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that the ICRC said an assessment carried out between 2 and 10 September 2025 of 240 health facilities in the two Kivus found 85% out of stock of essential medicines and supplies, that transfer of the wounded was hindered by fighting and patients travelled long distances on foot at risk to their lives, and that more than 70% of the 240 structures had received people wounded by weapons.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-006.x: ICRC: 240 facilities assessed; 85% out of stock; more than 70% received weapon-wounded
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-006.n: Covers both provinces; not South-Kivu-specific. Moreillon quote on both zones is later in the page and not in this excerpt, so omitted from reliance.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-006.vn: Both excerpts exact. excerpt_en flags resolved: 'ICRC' renders 'CICR'; translations are of the excerpts alone. Attribution of source 0 to the ICRC rests on the page's opening sentence (page-only). Covers both Kivus; per the ICRC delegation head (later on the page) the assessment covered both AFC/M23-held and government-held areas. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the ICRC (CICR) is the author of the alert': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Une évaluation menée entre le 2 et le 10 septembre 2025 auprès de 240 structures sanitaires réparties dans les deux Kivu révèle que 85% d’entre elles sont en rupture de stock de médicaments et d’intrants essentiels pour soigner les patients et les blessés.

Selon le CICR, le transfert des blessés vers les structures de santé appropriées pose un problème à cause des combats dans cette contrée, où des patients parcourent de longues distances à pied en risquant leur vie afin de trouver les soins adaptés. Plus de 70% de structures de santé sur les 240 évaluées ont reçu des blessés par armes.

Le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR) tire la sonnette d’alarme sur l’accès aux soins de santé dans les provinces du Nord et du Sud-Kivu, de plus en plus compromis en raison de l’activisme des groupes armés.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC announced they had retaken the cité of Mikenge, Fizi territory, South Kivu, on Sunday '1er mard' (read as 1 March), after violent clashes with rebels in the Hauts Plateaux, and that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud South Kivu, Sub-Lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, said several rebels were neutralised, 5 captured and 17 surrendered, and that among 11 bodies found were an AFC-M23 brigade commander and a logistics officer.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.l: Mikenge, Hauts Plateaux, Fizi territory, South Kivu (page says Fizi; other sources place it in Mwenga)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.a: FARDC; RDF-M23-AFC, Twigwaneho, Red-Tabara (as named by FARDC)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.x: FARDC spokesperson: 5 captured, 17 surrendered, 11 bodies found
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.n: Party claim (FARDC). Closes lead on Mikenge. The excerpt/page gives the date as dimanche 1er mard (typo for mars), computed as 1 March 2026 from the page date 2 March 2026. SOS Médias Burundi 4 March 2026 (already cited) reports the Twirwaneho/M23 repelled offensives: contested.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-007.vn: All excerpts exact. Removed the '(2026)' gloss and kept the page's typo visible; 'city' changed to 'cité'. Named the operation. excerpt_en flags resolved: the capitalised words are the English rendering of 'Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo', 'Sud-Kivu' and 'sous-lieutenant'; each translates its excerpt alone. Page also quotes the spokesperson naming 'RDF–M23–AFC et leurs alliés Twigwaneho, Red-Tabara' and other villages retaken (Kakenge, Kisirita, Bilalombili, Bidegu). Party (FARDC) claim, uncorroborated here. Radio Okapi places Mikenge in Fizi territory; Actualite.cd (1 March 2025) places it in Mwenga territory: the territory is a discrepancy between sources.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) annoncent avoir repris, dimanche 1er mard, la cité de Mikenge, située dans le territoire de Fizi, province du Sud-Kivu, après de violents affrontements contre les rebelles dans les Hauts Plateaux.
Le porte-parole des opérations Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, le sous-lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan, confirme que l’armée a repris le contrôle de plusieurs contrées dont la cité stratégique de Mikenge

Il ajoute que lors des combats, plusieurs rebelles ont été neutralisés, 5 capturés, et 17 autres se sont rendus. Parmi les 11 corps retrouvés, figure un commandant brigade de l’AFC-M23 ainsi qu’un officier chargé de la logistique, précise le sous-lieutenant Mbuyi Reagan.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that on 1 March (2025) fighting resumed in Bilalombili village near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, where, according to several local sources, Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and Android elements allied to M23 attacked Wazalendo positions, and that local civil societies denounced the burning of the houses of Bilalombili, which had hosted people displaced from Mikenge, without giving a toll.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-008.l: Bilalombili, near Mikenge, Mwenga territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-008.a: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Android (allied to M23, per local sources); Wazalendo
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-008.n: Local civil-society sources (Nouvelle Société civile Congolaise d'Itombwe). Date: page dated 1 March 2025, text says "ce 1 mars". Mikenge assigned to Mwenga here and Fizi by Radio Okapi 2026; kept as printed. Excerpt 2 spans a quote boundary, translation covers that passage.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-008.vn: Excerpts exact (latest of 3 captures still prints them). Stored excerpt 2 starts mid-word ('civiles locales'); the 'hosted displaced from Mikenge' clause is carried by the page sentence (page-only). excerpt_en flag on source 0 resolved: 'Fighting'/'South Kivu' render the excerpt. The year 2025 comes from the page date and the claim date. Accounts differ on who fought: the outlet's local sources and Parisien Ngini (société civile Itombwe) say Twirwaneho/M23 attacked the Wazalendo, while Pacifique Kararuka (Nouvelle Société civile Congolaise d'Itombwe) speaks of Twirwaneho against the FARDC. Mikenge is placed in Mwenga here and in Fizi by Radio Okapi (2026). 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Bilalombili had hosted people displaced from Mikenge; local civil societies denounced the burning of houses without giving a toll': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Les affrontements ont repris tôt le matin de ce 1 mars dans le village de Bilalombili près de Mikenge dans le territoire de Mwenga au Sud-Kivu.
Selon plusieurs sources locales, les éléments de la coalition Twirwaneho, Red Tabara, Android alliés au M23 qui ont attaqué les positions des Wazalendo.
civiles locales dénoncent le fait que les maisons ont été incendiées sans donner le nombre.
Le village de Bilalombili avait accueilli les déplacés venus de Mikenge et ailleurs, les sociétés civiles locales dénoncent le fait que les maisons ont été incendiées sans donner le nombre.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that clashes took place on Wednesday 24 June in the villages of Ilundu and Alengei, Minembwe zone, Fizi territory, between the FARDC and fighters of the Twirwaneho armed coalition and their allies, described as backed by Rwanda, and that the militia accused the FARDC of drone bombardments of its positions.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-009.l: Ilundu and Alengei, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-009.n: Date computed from weekday and page date (Friday 26 June 2026). "soutenus par le Rwanda" is the outlet voice, not an attributed claim.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-009.vn: Excerpt exact. 'Rwanda-backed allies' narrowed: the French 'et leurs alliés, soutenus par le Rwanda' sits inside the local-sources sentence and does not say whether only the allies or the whole coalition are meant. Minembwe/Fizi from the page's first sentence (page-only). The drone accusation is the militia's; the page adds that local actors called it a 'fuite en avant'. No FARDC statement on the drone accusation is on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Minembwe zone, Fizi territory': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Selon des sources locales ce vendredi 26 juin, des affrontements ont eu lieu mercredi 24 juin dans les villages d’Ilundu et d’Alengei entre les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) et les combattants de la coalition armée Twirwaneho et leurs alliés, soutenus par le Rwanda. La milice accuse les FARDC d’avoir mené des bombardements contre ses positions à l’aide de drones.
La situation sécuritaire reste tendue dans la zone de Minembwe, en territoire de Fizi, au Sud-Kivu.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-010.s: Radio Okapi reported that, at the sixth meeting of the Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS) on the security situation in the DRC, held on Wednesday 24 June 2026 in London, Kinshasa and Kigali reaffirmed their commitment to de-escalate tensions linked to the situation of Minembwe.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-010.l: London (meeting); Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu (subject)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-010.n: Secondary report of a meeting outcome; no primary communiqué found by this unit.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-010.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the label 'Joint Security Mechanism', which the page does not print and which names a different body; kept the page's 'Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS)'. excerpt_en flag resolved: 'Joint Oversight Committee' is the usual English name of the CMS; the translation covers the excerpt alone. Secondary report; no communiqué of the meeting was opened.
src: Sur le plan régional, lors de la sixième réunion du Comité mixte de surveillance (CMS) sur la situation sécuritaire en RDC, tenue mercredi 24 juin 2026 à Londres, Kinshasa et Kigali ont réaffirmé leur engagement à désamorcer les tensions liées à la situation de Minembwe.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-011.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that fighting between Wazalendo fighters and AFC/M23 troops was reported throughout Thursday 2 April 2026 in Tchambombo village, Ziralo groupement, on the Kalehe highlands, and, citing local sources, that many residents fled into the bush and to villages deemed safer.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-011.l: Tchambombo, Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-011.vn: Excerpts exact. Publisher corrected: the statement credited Radio Okapi, but the page is Radio Maendeleo's. 'Citing local sources' moved to the displacement clause, where the page puts it. excerpt_en flag resolved (capitalised 'New' renders 'De nouveaux').
src: De nouveaux combats entre des combattants Wazalendos et les troupes de l’AFC/M23 ont été signalés tout au long de la journée de jeudi 2 avril 2026 dans le village de Tchambombo, groupement de Ziralo, situé sur les hauts plateaux du territoire de Kalehe.
Selon des sources locales, de nombreux habitants ont quitté le village pour se réfugier dans la brousse et dans des villages jugés plus sécurisés.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-012.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that fighting between AFC/M23 troops and Wazalendo fighters was reported on Wednesday 19 November 2025 in Kaniola groupement and at the Mugogo trading centre, Walungu territory, and that several families fled to nearby villages of Kaniola groupement.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-012.l: Kaniola and Mugogo, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-012.n: Radio Maendeleo, Bukavu. Local sources say Wazalendo launched the assault on an AFC/M23 camp (later on the page).
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-012.vn: Excerpts exact (latest of 3 captures). Byline Omeur Mudekereza. According to local sources cited on the page, Wazalendo elements reportedly launched the assault on an AFC/M23 camp and AFC/M23 then fired back (conditional in the source). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'citing local sources': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Des affrontements entre les troupes de l’AFC/M23 et les combattants Wazalendo ont été signalés ce mercredi 19 novembre 2025 dans le groupement de Kaniola ainsi qu’au centre de négoce de Mugogo, en territoire de Walungu.
Plusieurs familles ont fui vers les villages environnants du groupement de Kaniola, notamment Bushushu, Nabishaka, Mwirama et Cindubi.
Selon des sources locales, les hostilités ont débuté vers une heure du matin à Kaniola-centre.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-013.s: Deutsche Welle (Swahili) reported that Amnesty International said M23 fighters backed by Rwanda and Wazalendo groups allied to the Congolese army committed serious atrocities in eastern DRC, including gang rapes of women, and that women from North Kivu and South Kivu gave testimony, 14 of whom recounted being gang-raped; the outlet reported that Beatrice from Bukavu said she was attacked by five M23 soldiers.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-013.a: M23 and Wazalendo (as alleged by Amnesty International)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-013.x: Amnesty (via DW): 14 women recounted gang rape
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-013.n: Secondary report of the Amnesty report (primary not opened by this unit); Amnesty also says (same page) it interviewed more than 53 people.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-013.vn: Checked in Swahili; all three excerpts exact (latest of 3 captures) and the translations render them alone ('Democratic Republic of Congo' = 'Jamhuri ya Kidemokarsi ya Kongo'; 'North/South Kivu' = 'Kivu Kaskazini/Kusini'; 'Fourteen' = 'Wanawake 14'), so the excerpt_en flags are resolved. Byline Iddi Ssessanga. LEAD not in the claim: the page also says 'Beatrice kutoka Bukavu alisema alivamiwa na wanajeshi watano wa M23' (Beatrice from Bukavu said she was attacked by five M23 soldiers); the name is not in a stored excerpt, so it cannot be added here; add it with source_edits.py add_excerpt (may be a pseudonym; the page does not say). Secondary report of an Amnesty International report; the Amnesty report itself was not opened. 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Task 2 support (not in candidates): verifier LEAD; the survivor account is on the page but in no stored excerpt. The page does not say whether 'Beatrice' is a pseudonym. Naming allowed under project policy v1 (behind the censor). 2026-10-29: statement edited: Restores the verifier's LEAD, now carried by a proposed add_excerpt on source 2 ('Beatrice kutoka Bukavu alisema alivamiwa na wanajeshi watano wa M23.'). Name recorded as the outlet prints it; the page does not say whether 'Beatrice' is a pseudonym. Survivor naming allowed under policy v1 (behind the censor). 'alivamiwa' rendered 'attacked' (it can also mean assaulted/raided); the page does not specify the form of the attack.
src: Amnesty International limesema waasi wa M23 wanaoungwa mkono na Rwanda na vikundi vya Wazalendo vinavyoshirikiana na jeshi la Jamhuri ya Kidemokarsi ya Kongo, wametenda ukatili mkubwa mashariki mwa Kongo.
Ukatili huo ni pamoja na kuwabaka wanawake kwa makundi, kuwaua raia kiholela na kushambulia hospitali katika eneo la mashariki mwa Kongo.
Ushuhuda wa wanawake kutoka Kivu Kaskazini na Kivu Kusini unaonesha kiwango cha ukatili huo. Wanawake 14 waliosimulia walibakwa kwa makundi.
Beatrice kutoka Bukavu alisema alivamiwa na wanajeshi watano wa M23.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-014.s: Deutsche Welle (Swahili) reported that Amnesty International said M23 attacks included hospitals, where patients and staff were abducted or detained, and that this happened between February and May 2025 when the group controlled much of Goma and Bukavu.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-014.l: Goma and Bukavu hospitals (North and South Kivu)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-014.n: Secondary report of Amnesty; hospitals not named in this text.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-014.vn: Checked in Swahili; excerpt exact. The excerpt says 'mwaka huu' (this year); the page is dated 20 August 2025, so '2025' in the statement follows from the page date (the year is also in the claim date). excerpt_en flag resolved ('February'/'May' render 'Februari'/'Mei'). Hospitals not named.
src: Amnesty International ilisema mashambulizi ya M23 yalijumuisha hata hospitali, ambako wagonjwa na wahudumu walitekwa au kushikiliwa. Haya yalitokea kati ya Februari na Mei mwaka huu, wakati kundi hilo lilikuwa likidhibiti sehemu kubwa ya Goma na Bukavu.

r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-015.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing several testimonies collected on site, that armed men who fled fighting in South Kivu in December and crossed the Rusizi river into Bukinanyana commune, Bujumbura province, were accused by residents of looting and, according to several testimonies, of sexual violence, with women and girls said to be victims of rape under threat of reprisals if they reported.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-015.l: Kaburantwa and Rugano hills, Bukinanyana, Bujumbura province, Burundi (fighters from South Kivu)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-015.a: Burundian soldiers, FARDC, Wazalendo, FDLR and Tundu94 fighters who fled to Burundi (as named by the outlet)
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-015.n: Location is in Burundi, recorded because the alleged perpetrators are fighters who fled South Kivu in December 2025 (Swahili translation of SOS Médias Burundi article of 22 January 2026). The Burundian authorities are said to be deciding on the fighters; no official Burundian statement found.
r4-G-LOCAL-SWRN-015.vn: Checked in Swahili; excerpt exact and carries only the sexual-violence clause; flight from South Kivu, Rusizi crossing, Bukinanyana/Bujumbura and looting are carried by other page passages (page-only clauses, all verbatim above). Extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt. Location is in Burundi (Kaburantwa and Rugano hills, Bukinanyana). The Swahili text reads as a translation of the French original (Bujumbura dateline 22 January 2026). The Buhayira zone chief is quoted confirming many complaints from residents. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'armed men who fled fighting in South Kivu in December': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'citing several testimonies collected on site, they crossed the Rusizi river into Bukinanyana commune, Bujumbura province': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Bukinanyana, Bujumbura province': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'in December': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'accused by residents of looting': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Hata mbaya zaidi, shuhuda kadhaa huripoti unyanyasaji wa kijinsia. Wanawake na wasichana wanasemekana kuwa waathiriwa wa ubakaji, chini ya vitisho vya vitisho na kulipizwa kisasi ikiwa wataripoti.
Wale waliohusika walikimbia uhasama katika miji na vijiji kadhaa katika jimbo la Kivu Kusini, ambalo linapakana na Burundi.
Kulingana na shuhuda kadhaa thabiti zilizokusanywa kwenye tovuti, walivuka Mto Rusizi
katika eneo la Buganda la tarafa ya Bukinanyana, katika mkoa wa Bujumbura
Wakazi wanashutumu vikundi hivi vilivyojihami kwa kujihusisha na uporaji wa mara kwa mara.

r4-G-UV-DEEP-001.s: BBC News Swahili reported that the military police department of the DRC army said it was holding rebel FARDC soldiers and pro-government Wazalendo fighters linked to indiscriminate shooting in the city of Uvira. A resident told BBC that rebel soldiers were being arrested by the military police and that those looting or firing indiscriminately were being arrested.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-001.a: FARDC military police (as reported); FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo held
r4-G-UV-DEEP-001.n: Live-page entry dated 21 Feb 2025 (Friday); resident refers to disturbances since Wednesday (19 Feb) continuing into Thursday night. Date approximate; page text, not weekday converted in statement. Adds BBC Swahili account to existing Feb 2025 Uvira FARDC/Wazalendo clashes records.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-001.vn: Excerpt real; resident clause sits only on the page, now quoted. Date set to the live entry's date (21 Feb 2025, 'kwa sasa'), approximate, instead of 20 Feb. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (capitalised 'Democratic Republic' rendering 'Jamuhuri ya demokrasia'); translation matches. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'a resident told BBC that rebel soldiers were being arrested by the military police and that those looting or firing indiscriminately were being arrested': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Idara ya kipolisi ndani ya jeshi la Jamuhuri ya demokrasia ya Congo inaripoti kuwashikilia wanajeshi waasi kutoka Jeshi la taifa la Congo (FARDC) na wanamgambo wa Wazalendo wanaoiunga mkono serikali, waliokuwa wakihusishwa na ufyatuaji risasi holela katika mji wa Uvira, mashariki mwa nchi.
kwa sasa tunashuhudia kukamatwa kwa wanajeshi waasi na polisi wa idara ya kijeshi. Wale wanaopora au kufyatua risasi kiholela wanakamatwa,” alisema mkaazi huyo.

r4-G-UV-DEEP-002.s: BBC News Swahili reported that a resident of Uvira told BBC that the disturbances seen since Wednesday continued into Thursday night with gunfire in several areas, and that during the night FARDC soldiers broke into several houses demanding money, phones and food.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-002.n: Single anonymous resident. Date computed from weekday and publication date (live entry 21 Feb 2025). Resident also said two FARDC soldiers' bodies were seen near a bank, which the army had not confirmed (not recorded as a claim).
r4-G-UV-DEEP-002.vn: Page (live entry 21 Feb 2025) prints it as stated; Thursday = 20 Feb 2025. Single unnamed resident.
src: Raia mmoja aliambia BBC kuwa machafuko yaliyoshuhudiwa tangu Jumatano yaliendelea hadi usiku wa Alhamisi, ambapo risasi zilisikika katika maeneo kadhaa. Alisema, “Tulikuwa na wakati mgumu sana. Kulikuwa na milio ya risasi katika maeneo mengi ya mji. Usiku wa jana wanajeshi wa FARDC walivamia nyumba kadhaa kudai pesa, simu na chakula

r4-G-UV-DEEP-003.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported on 10 December 2025 that the city of Uvira fell to the M23 rebel movement on the night of 9 December, and that the fighters entered without encountering resistance.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-003.n: Date discrepancy lead: this outlet says night of 9 December; other outlets say 10 December (e.g. SOS Médias Burundi itself later says night of December 9-10; Gatumba border closed 10 Dec per SOS 3 Feb 2026). Record both; 'night' straddles the dates.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-003.vn: Matches page. The same outlet's 15 Dec 2025 report says the night of 9-10 December.
src: SOS Médias Burundi Uvira, December 10, 2025 – The city of Uvira, in South Kivu, fell to the M23 rebel movement on the night of December 9. The fighters entered the city without encountering any resistance, causing shock and concern among the local population.

r4-G-UV-DEEP-004.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, according to several witnesses, that M23 columns simultaneously entered several neighbourhoods of Uvira including the Mulongwe commercial centre, the Kasenga neighbourhood, the Kavimvira area and the border post with Burundi.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-004.l: Mulongwe, Kasenga, Kavimvira and the Burundi border post, Uvira city
r4-G-UV-DEEP-004.n: Neighbourhood-level entry points; single local outlet citing witnesses. Date range reflects 'night of 9 December' vs 10 December.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-004.vn: Page prints the list of neighbourhoods as stated, attributed to several witnesses.
src: According to several witnesses, M23 columns simultaneously entered several strategic neighborhoods, including : the Mulongwe commercial center, the Kasenga neighborhood, the Kavimvira area, and the border post with Burundi.

r4-G-UV-DEEP-005.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, shortly before the M23 assault, almost all loyalist forces (FARDC and Wazalendo) had abandoned their positions in Uvira, with retreat routes observed towards Kalemie via the port of Kalundu, towards Fizi and, for some soldiers, towards Burundi.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-005.l: Uvira city (port of Kalundu), South Kivu
r4-G-UV-DEEP-005.n: Local outlet; 'reportedly' for Burundi route. Same page says residents reported more than 80 Wazalendo generals, two senior FARDC officers and two Burundian colonels in the city (not recorded; unattributed hearsay).
r4-G-UV-DEEP-005.vn: Matches page. Flag '23' is the 'M23' name, not a figure.
src: Shortly before the assault, almost all loyalist forces—the FARDC and Wazalendo fighters—had abandoned their positions. Several retreat routes were observed : towards Kalemie via the port of Kalundu, towards Fizi, and for some soldiers, towards Burundi, where they reportedly sought refuge.

r4-G-UV-DEEP-006.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, citing a Kasenga resident, that in some streets of Kasenga and Kavimvira the bodies of Wazalendo fighters were still visible in the morning, and that Red Cross teams were seen collecting them.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-006.l: Kasenga and Kavimvira neighbourhoods, Uvira city
r4-G-UV-DEEP-006.n: Combatant bodies, not civilians; category chosen as nearest (casualties of fighting); no figure given. The same page says, per several residents, that the last gunfire rang out early on 11 December. Single local source.
r4-G-UV-DEEP-006.vn: 'the morning after the fighting' narrowed to the page's 'in the morning'. Category attack_on_civilians is a poor fit (combatant dead); editor may recategorise. src: At this meeting, the Burundian Minister of Foreign Affairs, Édouard Bizimana, declared that the Burundi-Congo border will remain closed until further notice. Speaking about the security situation in eastern DRC, the Burundian Foreign Minister asserted that the M23 is lying when it claims to have withdrawn from the city of Uvira.

The announcement was made during a meeting of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Regional Integration and International Cooperation, held in Bujumbura, in the presence of representatives of partner countries and international organizations accredited to Burundi.
According to him, this apparent withdrawal masks a strategy of regrouping and repositioning its fighters.

src: SOS Médias Burundi Uvira, August 5, 2026 – The city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, largely observed a “ghost town” day on Wednesday, called for by the Provincial Coordination of the New Congolese Civil Society (NSCC).

From Kavimvira to Kalundu, traffic was virtually nonexistent. Motorcycles and vehicles remained at a standstill, while markets, shops, and warehouses remained closed, illustrating a strong mobilization of the population.

r5-G-COURT-001.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale-centre, sentenced ten FARDC soldiers of the 3415th regiment on Tuesday 1 September 2026, two of them to death for the murder of their company commander, Captain Musanga Bebeto, together with criminal participation and dissipation of war munitions. According to the prosecution, as reported by the outlet, the soldiers opened fire on their commander during operations against AFC/M23 at Lukole village, Masisi territory, on 30 October 2025. The outlet also reported that, in addition to the sentences, soldiers Seleko Mbele Jubilet, Kongo Byemba, Bwana Bisele and Guy Bashomba were jointly ordered to pay 50,000 US dollars to the civil party in damages.

src: Le verdict a été rendu mardi 1er septembre 2026. Deux militaires ont été condamnés à mort pour l’assassinat du capitaine Musanga Bebeto, leur commandant de compagnie, ainsi que pour participation criminelle et dissipation de munitions de guerre.

Les dix militaires, tous membres du 3415ᵉ régiment, étaient poursuivis notamment pour lâcheté, assassinat et dissipation de munitions de guerre. Les faits remontent au 30 octobre 2025, au village de Lukole, dans le territoire de Masisi, au Nord-Kivu.

Selon l’accusation, ces militaires avaient ouvert le feu sur leur chef, le capitaine Musanga Bebeto, alors qu’ils étaient engagés dans des opérations contre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23, soutenus par le Rwanda selon les autorités congolaises.
Le tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma, siégeant en audience foraine à Walikale-centre, a condamné dix militaires des FARDC à des peines allant de dix mois de servitude pénale à la peine capitale.

Outre les peines prononcées, les militaires Seleko Mbele Jubilet, Kongo Byemba, Bwana Bisele et Guy Bashomba ont été condamnés solidairement à verser 50 000 dollars américains à la partie civile, au titre des dommages et intérêts.

r5-G-COURT-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit chamber at Walikale, sentenced to death on Monday 9 February (2026) Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre, a judicial police officer attached to the Mubi judicial inspectorate, convicted of murder for facts of Saturday 31 January at Mubi Centre. According to the case file as reported, while a wanted man named in the article, presented as a member of an armed group, tried to evade arrest, one of two officers sent to execute an arrest warrant fired without orders and the man died minutes later.
r5-G-COURT-002.l: Mubi Centre (facts), Walikale territory, North Kivu; tribunal sitting at Walikale
r5-G-COURT-002.a: Goma garrison military tribunal; Maleso Buka Pierre, sergeant, judicial police officer, Mubi
r5-G-COURT-002.x: Actualite.cd: one defendant sentenced to death
r5-G-COURT-002.n: Year 2026 inferred from the page date (10/02/2026) and 'ce lundi 9 février'. Not conflict-linked beyond the victim being described as an armed-group member; recorded as a police/military-justice case. The article also mentions a damages award, omitted.
r5-G-COURT-002.vn: Page re-fetched; all elements verbatim; victim name Kambale Muhindo Jean printed in source 1 and spelled as printed. Year 2026 from the page date (10/02/2026); 9 February 2026 was a Monday. 'Mandat d'amener' is a warrant to bring a person before the authority. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma
src: Le tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma, siégeant en chambre foraine à Walikale, au Nord-Kivu, a condamné à la peine de mort, ce lundi 9 février, le sergent Maleso Buka Pierre, agent de police judiciaire affecté à l’Inspection judiciaire de Mubi, reconnu coupable de meurtre. Les faits remontent au samedi 31 janvier, tôt le matin, à Mubi Centre, dans le territoire de Walikale.

Deux agents de police judiciaire avaient été dépêchés pour exécuter un mandat d’amener contre Kambale Muhindo Jean, présenté comme membre d’un groupe armé non autrement identifié et poursuivi pour détention illégale d’armes de guerre.

Selon l’instruction du dossier, alors que la personne recherchée tentait de se soustraire à l’arrestation, l’un des agents, sans avoir reçu d’ordre, a fait usage de son arme à feu en tirant une balle sur la victime. Cette dernière a succombé à ses blessures quelques minutes plus tard.

r5-G-COURT-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Wednesday 10 December (2025) the Goma garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit hearing at Walikale, sentenced six people (three soldiers, two VDP fighters and one civilian): two of the three soldiers accused of losing weapons and war munitions were sentenced to death and the third to 15 years for desertion, and a VDP fighter prosecuted for rape received 20 years of servitude pénale principale.
r5-G-COURT-003.a: Goma garrison military tribunal; FARDC soldiers; VDP fighters
r5-G-COURT-003.x: Actualite.cd: six convicted; two soldiers sentenced to death; one soldier 15 years; one VDP fighter 20 years for rape; a second VDP fighter 20 years for unlawful possession of arms
r5-G-COURT-003.n: Date computed: 'mercredi 10 décembre' with page date 12/12/2025 gives 2025. The page also reports a civil sentenced to death for killing his elder brother with a machete (non-conflict case, not recorded). No details given on the rape (place, date, victim).
r5-G-COURT-003.vn: Page re-fetched; verbatim. The second VDP fighter's 20 years for illegal possession of arms and the civilian's (non-conflict) death sentence are on the page but not in the statement. No detail on the rape (victim, place, date) is given. 10 December 2025 was a Wednesday; year from the page date (12/12/2025). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: Tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma
Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie
src: Six personnes dont trois militaires, deux volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie et un civil poursuivis pour différentes infractions, ont été condamnés mercredi 10 décembre à des lourdes peines par le Tribunal militaire de garnison de Goma siégeant en foraine à Walikale, au Nord-Kivu.

Deux des trois militaires accusés de perte d’armes et de munitions de guerre ont été condamnés à la peine de mort et le troisième à 15 ans de servitude pénale principale pour desertion. Poursuivi pour viol, un combattant VDP a écopé de 20 ans de servitude pénale principale.

r5-G-COURT-004.s: 7sur7.cd reported that the Beni garrison military tribunal, sitting in a circuit chamber at Manyama-Beu (Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory), delivered its verdict on Tuesday 28 July 2026 in a case of two soldiers prosecuted notably for breach of orders during operations against the ADF and for the murder of three civilians the previous weekend: Ahundu Likamba Ruffin was sentenced to 20 years of servitude pénale principale, and Irakunda Bindibikwira to death for breach of orders, murder of three civilians and attempted murder.
r5-G-COURT-004.l: Manyama-Beu, Beni-Mbau sector, Beni territory, North Kivu
r5-G-COURT-004.a: Beni garrison military tribunal; two FARDC soldiers (units not stated)
r5-G-COURT-004.x: 7sur7.cd: three civilians killed; one soldier sentenced to death, one to 20 years
r5-G-COURT-004.n: The page does not say which of the two soldiers was linked to which count beyond what is quoted. Victims of the killings are not named. Existing claim r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-009 (Radio Okapi, 10 July 2026, Beni garrison tribunal) is a different case.
r5-G-COURT-004.vn: Page re-fetched (byline Bantou Kapanza Son, Beni). Figure flag '7' is the '7' in the outlet name 7sur7.cd, not a figure: resolved. The site footer carries injected gambling/SEO links (site hygiene, not article provenance). The page does not say for which count Ahundu Likamba Ruffin was convicted. The three civilians killed are not named. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: tribunal militaire de garnison de Beni
src: Le tribunal militaire de garnison de Beni, siégeant en chambre foraine à Manyama-Beu, dans le secteur de Beni-Mbau, en territoire de Beni, a rendu son verdict le mardi 28 juillet 2026, dans une affaire impliquant deux (2) militaires poursuivis notamment pour violation de consigne lors des opérations militaires contre les ADF et pour le meurtre de trois (3) civils, survenu le week-end dernier.

Le militaire Ahundu Likamba Ruffin a été condamné à 20 ans de servitude pénale principale, au paiement de 500 000 francs congolais à titre de frais d'instance. Le militaire Irakunda Bindibikwira a, quant à lui, été condamné à la peine de mort pour violation de consigne, meurtre de trois civils et tentative de meurtre, des faits commis récemment à Manyama-Beu.

r5-G-COURT-005.s: 7sur7.cd reported, in its article on the Beni garrison military tribunal's Manyama-Beu verdicts, that hearings concerning a third soldier prosecuted for the alleged rape of a 19-month-old girl had been suspended, the case file being examined at Oicha, where the victim was receiving medical care.
r5-G-COURT-005.l: Manyama-Beu / Oicha, Beni territory, North Kivu
r5-G-COURT-005.a: Beni garrison military tribunal; a FARDC soldier (not named by the source)
r5-G-COURT-005.n: Date of the alleged rape not given by the source; the date field is the date of the verdict reported in the same article. Allegation only: no verdict. Victim is a minor and not named by the source.
r5-G-COURT-005.vn: Page re-fetched; verbatim. Figure flag '7' is the outlet name 7sur7.cd: resolved. Neither the soldier nor the child is named by the source. Allegation only; no verdict. The source says hearings were expected to resume. The date is that of the article's verdict report, not of the alleged rape (not given). 2026-10-29: statement edited: fact-check fc3: 7sur7.cd, 29 Jul 2026, introduces this with 'Par ailleurs' and says the file is examined at Oicha; it does not say these hearings were part of the same session at Manyama-Beu, so that qualifier is dropped. Otherwise the excerpt carries the clause verbatim. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Par ailleurs, les audiences concernant un troisième militaire poursuivi pour viol présumé sur une fillette de 19 mois ont été suspendues. Le dossier est examiné à Oïcha, où la victime reçoit des soins médicaux.

r5-G-COURT-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that on Monday 3 November 2025 the AFC/M23, through a justice-revival commission (CRJ) it had set up some months earlier, announced the integration of 378 new magistrates into its judicial system, described by the outlet as now parallel to the government's, following a test held in Goma on 14 September 2025.
r5-G-COURT-006.a: AFC/M23 commission de relance de la justice (CRJ)
r5-G-COURT-006.n: Report of an AFC/M23 announcement; the movement's own wording is partisan and the outlet's account is relayed from it (author Josué Mutanava, Goma). Complements GoE-based claims r2-G-DOC-858-061/062 on the arbitration court and the commission. Searches found no AFC/M23 trial, sentence or execution record for 2025-2026 in the local sources searched.
r5-G-COURT-006.vn: Page re-fetched; verbatim. Party announcement kept attributed. The figures come from the AFC/M23 announcement relayed by the outlet. The page adds (per the movement) 475 files filed, 465 eligible, 378 selected including 18 women, the list read by AFC/M23 deputy permanent secretary Delion Kimbulungu, and over 200 new lawyers sworn in at Beni on 31 October 2025 (government side). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
ent: commission de relance de la justice (CRJ)
src: L’AFC/M23 qui a mis en place depuis quelques mois une « commission de relance de la justice (CRJ), a annoncé ce lundi 3 novembre, l’intégration de 378 nouveaux magistrats dans son système judiciaire, parallèle désormais à celui du gouvernement. Cette intégration fait suite au test d’évaluation organisé le 14 septembre 2025 à Goma.

r5-G-COURT-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that the president of the Constitutional Court and of the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature, Dieudonné Kamuleta, had recalled in a communiqué published on 12 September 2025 that the country's Constitution and organic laws give the Conseil supérieur de la magistrature exclusive power to recruit and manage magistrates nationwide, and that any parallel attempt is therefore, according to him, 'nulle et de nul effet'; the Justice Minister Guillaume Ngefa had announced the forthcoming signature of an ordinance annulling all judicial decisions taken by AFC/M23 leaders.
r5-G-COURT-007.l: Kinshasa (statement); Goma and Bukavu (AFC/M23-held areas concerned)
r5-G-COURT-007.a: Dieudonné Kamuleta; Guillaume Ngefa; DRC Government
r5-G-COURT-007.n: Statement made before the publication date of the article (3 Nov 2025); the 12 Sep 2025 communiqué is also in r2-G-DOC-858-062 (Group of Experts). This is a separate, local-media account. Kamuleta's quoted words are a paraphrase plus a quoted phrase in the source.
r5-G-COURT-007.vn: Narrowed procedural stage: source says Ngefa announced 'la signature prochaine' (forthcoming signature) of an ordinance; the draft said he announced an ordinance annulling decisions. Kamuleta clause restated closer to the source ('avait rappelé'; exclusivity per the Constitution and organic laws). Ngefa's announcement is undated in the source and concerns an ordinance to be signed, not one already signed. The page says Ngefa accuses AFC/M23 leaders of 'ne jurer que par l'amnistie'. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Le président de la Cour constitutionnelle et du Conseil supérieur de la magistrature, Dieudonné Kamuleta avait rappelé, dans un communiqué publié le 12 septembre 2025, que la Constitution et les lois organiques de la République démocratique du Congo confèrent exclusivement au Conseil supérieur de la magistrature le pouvoir de recruter et de gérer les magistrats sur l’ensemble du territoire national.

Toute tentative parallèle est donc, selon lui, « nulle et de nul effet ». De son côté, le ministre de la Justice et Garde des Sceaux, Guillaume Ngefa, avait annoncé la signature prochaine d’une ordonnance annulant toutes les décisions judiciaires prises par les dirigeants de l’AFC/M23, qu’il accuse de ne jurer que par l’amnistie.

r5-G-DISC2-001.s: BBC News Afrique reported that, according to the government, more than 200 people, including 70 children, were killed when a landslide caused a mining area to collapse in eastern DRC; it quoted the Ministry of Mines communiqué giving a provisional toll of more than 200 dead and many injured, and said it could not independently verify the toll. It also reported that the ministry blamed the M23 rebels, that the M23 had not yet commented, that a source at Rubaya told the BBC the collapse was caused by attacks by government forces and that only six people had died, and that the government had not responded to that claim.
r5-G-DISC2-001.l: Rubaya mine, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r5-G-DISC2-001.x: DRC government via BBC: more than 200 dead including 70 children (provisional)
r5-G-DISC2-001.n: Government toll for the 3 March 2026 collapse (existing claim r2-G-NKW-MASISI-029 cites actualite.cd with 'more than a hundred'). TV5 Monde copy could not be fetched. Ouest-France headline snippet says witnesses reported 6 dead (lead only, not cited). Rubaya is under AFC/M23 control.
r5-G-DISC2-001.vn: Both excerpts exact. Added the page's second side (the Rubaya source's six-dead account and the M23's silence), which is the discrepancy this unit is for; written as 'the rebels'/'a source at the mine' because 'M23' and 'Rubaya' are printed on the page but in no stored excerpt or title (page-only clauses; extend the excerpt with source_edits.py add_excerpt). Byline Emery Makumeno, reporting from Kinshasa. The page also mentions a separate late-January collapse at the site with more than 200 dead: a different event. Tolls conflict: the government says more than 200 dead (provisional); an unnamed source at Rubaya told the BBC only six died and blamed government attacks; an existing claim (actualite.cd) gives 'more than a hundred'. None is independently verified. Rubaya is under M23 control. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Ministry of Mines communiqué: provisional toll of more than 200 dead, 70 children, and many injured': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the ministry blamed the rebels': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the rebels had not yet commented; a source at the mine said government attacks caused the collapse and only six died; the government had not responded': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: Restores 'M23' and 'Rubaya', which the verifier generalised to 'the rebels'/'a source at the mine' only because no excerpt printed them; now carried by proposed add_excerpts on source 0 ('...imputé la responsabilité de cette tragédie aux rebelles du M23'; 'Le M23 n'a pas encore fait de commentaires, mais une source à Rubaya a déclaré à la BBC...'). The '23' of M23 may trip the number guard.
src: Selon le gouvernement, plus de 200 personnes, dont 70 enfants, ont été tuées après qu'un glissement de terrain a provoqué l'effondrement d'une zone minière dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo.

La BBC n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier de manière indépendante le nombre de victimes dans cette région reculée, où les agences humanitaires et les principaux établissements médicaux ont peu ou pas accès
« Le bilan provisoire fait état de plus de 200 compatriotes qui ont perdu la vie, dont 70 enfants, et de nombreux blessés », a déclaré le ministère dans un communiqué.
Dans un communiqué, le ministère des Mines a imputé la responsabilité de cette tragédie aux rebelles du M23

Le M23 n'a pas encore fait de commentaires, mais une source à Rubaya a déclaré à la BBC que l'effondrement avait été causé par des attaques des forces gouvernementales et que seules six personnes avaient trouvé la mort. Le gouvernement n'a pas répondu à cette affirmation.

r5-G-DISC2-002.s: MSF said in a communiqué that on 1 May a team travelling between Mwenga, Kamituga and Kitutu in South Kivu was stopped at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, and that armed men opened fire among themselves while the team was in the middle.
r5-G-DISC2-002.a: armed men at a checkpoint held by Wazalendo elements, as MSF describes them
r5-G-DISC2-002.n: MSF's own account. 'Kalimoto' is not printed on the MSF page. Other outlets (actualite.cd, KMP) headline an attack on the convoy by Wazalendo/FARDC and one gives 3 May; MSF says 1 May and describes gunfire between the armed men: discrepancy to register. msf.org text has odd spacing in accented letters, so excerpts avoid those words.
r5-G-DISC2-002.vn: All three excerpts exact (the latest of 4 captures still prints them; the page's split accented letters fall outside the excerpts). Statement matches the excerpts clause by clause; attribution kept to MSF. excerpt_en flags resolved: the capitalised words ('MSF', 'South') render 'de MSF' and 'Sud-Kivu' in the excerpts themselves. MSF's own account (press release, Bukavu, 8 May 2026). It differs from outlets that headline an attack on the convoy by Wazalendo/FARDC and one that gives 3 May. MSF also says confusion arose among the armed men over the team's identity, that the team was pushed to continue to Mwenga, and that false accusations against MSF circulated online.
src: « Après avoir franchi sans difficulté plusieurs points de contrôle tenus par des éléments Wazalendo le long du trajet, notre équipe a été arrêtée à l’un d’eux », explique Julia Garcia Zamora, cheffe de programme de MSF au Sud-Kivu.
La situation a ensuite dégénéré lorsque des hommes armés ont ouvert le feu entre eux alors que notre équipe se trouvait au milieu.
Le 1er mai, une équipe de MSF circulant entre Mwenga, Kamituga et Kitutu, dans le Sud-Kivu

r5-G-DISC2-003.s: RFI reported that the newly built Mwalu hotel in Fizi-centre was hit by a drone strike at one in the morning in the night of 18 to 19 August, that two civilians were seriously injured, and that the Congolese army accuses the AFC/M23 of being behind the attack, citing two explosive devices dropped by drones.
r5-G-DISC2-003.n: RFI copy on Yahoo France (RFI credit on page). Actualite.cd's Facebook post (lead only, not fetched) dates a strike on the Mwalu hotel to the night of Sunday 16 August 2026: date discrepancy to resolve. No AFC/M23 reply on this page. A YouTube title claims Rwanda bombed the hotel (lead only).
r5-G-DISC2-003.vn: All excerpts exact (latest of 4 captures). RFI copy on Yahoo France with the RFI credit on the page, so originating_source is RFI. The hotel's name is in the page sentence after excerpt 2 (page-only clause). Graded B: RFI reports the strike and injuries in its own voice; the perpetrator stays attributed to the FARDC. excerpt_en flags resolved: 'Congolese', 'FARDC', 'AFC' and 'Fizi-centre' render words of each excerpt. The attribution to the AFC/M23 is the FARDC's; no AFC/M23 reply is on the page. A Facebook post by Actualite.cd (not opened) is said to date a strike on the same hotel to the night of 16 August 2026: date to be checked. 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'the newly built Mwalu hotel': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support).
src: Il a été touché par un tir de drone à Fizi-centre, ville sous contrôle de l'armée congolaise (FARDC), à environ 250 kilomètres au sud de Bukavu, le chef-lieu provincial. C'était à une heure du matin. Deux civils ont été grièvement blessés.
L'armée congolaise accuse l'AFC/ M23 d'être à l'origine de cette attaque, évoquant deux engins explosifs largués par des drones.
Dans la nuit du 18 au 19 août, c'est une bâtisse de Fizi-centre qui a été prise pour cible par une attaque de drone.
L'hôtel Mwalu, nouvellement construit, est presque en ruine.

r5-G-DISC2-004.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that two people were killed and six wounded in bombardments in the night of Saturday 6 to Sunday 7 June in Ilundu/Basita village, Minembwe, Fizi territory, and that the Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux, a citizens' collective based in Minembwe, said in a communiqué that the shots, attributed to the FARDC and the Burundian FDNB, targeted an inhabited area of the village; the reported toll names Prince Runezerwa Mahiyaho, aged 19, who died on arrival at the general hospital, and Résor Kigeri Mazuru, who reportedly died at the scene; the outlet said that at publication no official reaction from the FARDC or the FDNB had been obtained.
r5-G-DISC2-004.l: Ilundu/Basita, Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r5-G-DISC2-004.a: FARDC and FDNB, as attributed by the Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux
r5-G-DISC2-004.x: Network via SOS Médias Burundi: 2 killed, 6 wounded
r5-G-DISC2-004.n: Civil-society (Banyamulenge-based) account naming FARDC and FDNB; existing actualite.cd/KMP claims (7 June, drones attributed to FARDC) give the same toll. Night of 6-7 June per this outlet versus 'Sunday 7 June' elsewhere. Victim list includes minors (policy v1). No AFC/M23 spokesperson account found on a fetched page.
r5-G-DISC2-004.vn: All five excerpts exact. Flag on figure '2' resolved: the statement's 'two' is printed as 'deux morts' / 'Deux personnes ont été tuées' (excerpts 1 and 4; excerpt_en 'two dead', 'Two people'), so no digit '2' is needed. Narrowed attribution: the night and the toll are the outlet's lede (excerpt 4) and 'le bilan communiqué', not only the Réseau's words; added the outlet's no-reaction line. Byline David Yemba, Bukavu dateline 7 June 2026. Victims' names are spelled as printed (two minors, policy v1). excerpt_en flag on source 0 resolved: 'Burundian'/'Sunday' render 'du Burundi'/'dimanche'. Civil-society account; the outlet says independent verification of the circumstances was not yet available.
