Résor Kigeri Mazuru 'aurait perdu la vie' (reportedly died) at the scene: conditional in the source. 2026-10-29: source 4 sources.append edited: Verifier clause_support for 'Minembwe, Fizi territory': printed on the retained page but in no stored excerpt (r4/r5 excerpt support). 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-038: The attribution is correctly the Réseau's ('attribués aux'), and the outlet's no-reaction line is kept. One wording fix: the source says the shots 'ont visé une zone habitée' (targeted an inhabited area), not that they 'hit' it. The amend restores that wording and keeps the 'reportedly' on the second death. A search (Ilundu Basita bombardement FARDC réaction) found no FARDC or FDNB denial. Two issues to surface: (1) Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd place Ilundu in Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, while this outlet says Minembwe, Fizi; (2) AFC/M23 (Kanyuka, r3-G-CTR-008) makes the same coalition attribution, so the Réseau and AFC/M23 accounts may not be independent of each other.
ent: Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux
src: Selon un communiqué publié dimanche par le Réseau local de protection des civils dans les Hauts Plateaux, un collectif de citoyens basé à Minembwe, les tirs attribués aux Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et à la Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) ont visé une zone habitée du village.

Le bilan communiqué fait état de deux morts. Il s’agit de Prince Runezerwa Mahiyaho, âgé de 19 ans, décédé à son arrivée à l’hôpital général, et de Résor Kigeri Mazuru, qui aurait perdu la vie sur le lieu du bombardement.
Six autres personnes ont été blessées, parmi lesquelles Bajeneza Murontsi, 7 ans, élève de deuxième année primaire, et Nzabakiza Osée, 12 ans, grièvement touché à plusieurs parties du corps.
Au moment de la publication de cet article, aucune réaction officielle des FARDC ou de la FDNB n’avait été obtenue concernant ces allégations.
Deux personnes ont été tuées et six autres blessées lors de bombardements survenus dans la nuit du samedi 6 au dimanche 7 juin dans le village d’Ilundu/Basita
situé dans la localité de Minembwe, en territoire de Fizi

r6-F-BENI-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that more than 70 bodies, including those of women, children and elderly people, were found on Saturday 15 February in a church building in Maiba village, Lubero territory; civil society believed they were people reported missing who had been abducted on 12 February by unidentified armed men, and said they were found bound and beheaded, probably killed with bladed weapons. Radio Okapi added that concordant sources in the region suspected local armed groups and ADF rebels of being the perpetrators.
r6-F-BENI-001.l: Maiba village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-001.a: unidentified armed men; civil society and concordant sources suspected local armed groups and ADF rebels
r6-F-BENI-001.n: Not previously held (claim_search 'Maiba' returned 0). Radio Okapi has the discovery on Saturday 15 February and abduction on 12 February; Actualite.cd (separate claim) has bodies found the preceding Friday after hostage-taking in the night of 11-12 February. Reporter.cd (16 Feb 2025; fetched, not cited) says Friday 14 February and names a CBECA church at Kasanga near Maiba, chefferie Baswagha. Not matched to any FIRE cluster in this unit (Maiba/Manzya lies south-west of Lubero town).
r6-F-BENI-001.vn: Both excerpts found on the retained page (published sam 15/02/2025 14:03); statement, date, toll ('plus de 70') and hedged attribution match. excerpt_en flag is only capitalised English weekday/month words; translation is faithful. Discrepancy: Radio Okapi gives discovery on Saturday 15 February and abduction on 12 February; Actualite.cd (separate claim) has abduction in the night of 11-12 February and bodies found 'vendredi dernier' (the previous Friday). Perpetrators are suspected, not established: Radio Okapi names local armed groups and the ADF as suspects.
src: Plus de 70 corps, dont ceux des femmes, des enfants, et des personnes de troisième âge, ont été découverts samedi 15 février dans le bâtiment d’une église du village Maiba, en territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu. La société civile pense qu’il s’agit des corps de personnes portées disparues, enlevées le 12 février dernier par des hommes armés non identifiés.

Ces personnes retrouvées ligotées et décapitées, auraient été tuées à l’arme blanche, estime la société civile. Cependant, des sources concordantes dans la région suspectent les groupes armés locaux et les rebelles des ADF d'être les auteurs de ce crime d’une violence effroyable.

r6-F-BENI-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least 70 civilians died in Lubero territory in an act attributed to ADF rebels near Maiba in the Manzya groupement, and that their bodies were found 'vendredi dernier' (the previous Friday) two days after the abduction, according to the local community protection committee. It quoted the committee's coordinator Vitwamba Vianney as saying the victims were taken hostage in the night of 11 to 12 February and that the victims, of all ages, were finished off in a local church.
r6-F-BENI-002.l: Maiba, Manzya groupement, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-002.n: Date of discovery computed from the weekday 'vendredi dernier' and the publication date (15 Feb 2025): 14 February. Conflicts with Radio Okapi's Saturday 15 February (separate claim). Outlet is a national online outlet citing a local civil-society committee.
r6-F-BENI-002.vn: Excerpts exact on retained page (sam 15/02/2025 18:33, byline Dieubon Mughenze). Attribution to ADF is the outlet's/committee's ('attribué'; quote says 'présumés ADF'); statement keeps it attributed. Date range end (14 Feb) is an inference from the weekday, flagged in note. Same event as the Radio Okapi Maiba claim, with differing dates (Friday vs Saturday 15 February for the discovery; night of 11-12 vs 12 February for the abduction). 14 February is inferred from 'vendredi dernier' and the publication date (sam 15/02/2025); the page also quotes the coordinator saying the bodies were found at Kasanga near Maiba in a CBCA church and that the victims went missing at the hands of 'présumés ADF'. The headline says 'autres' (other) 70 bodies.
src: Au moins 70 autres civils ont péri dans le territoire de Lubero au Nord-Kivu. Un forfait attribué aux rebelles ADF près de Maiba dans le groupement Manzya, à une quarantaine de kilomètres de Vuyinga. Deux jours après l'enlèvement, leur corps ont été retrouvés gisant au sol vendredi dernier, rapporte le comité local de protection communautaire.

Pris en otage la nuit du 11 au 12 février, ces victimes ont été ciblées loin du milieu du drame, indique Vitwamba Vianney, coordonnateur de cette structure. Les victimes, tout âge confondu, ont été achevées dans une église locale.

r6-F-BENI-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that fighting between the FARDC and M23 rebels continued on Wednesday 15 January at Luofu, in Lubero territory, North Kivu, and that clashes were also reported in several villages south of Lubero, notably Kamandi Gite and Kibanda, west of the rural commune of Kayna.
r6-F-BENI-003.l: Luofu, Kamandi Gite and Kibanda (west of Kayna), Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-003.n: Adds a day (15 Jan) to existing claim r2-G-NKN-FRONT-009 (Radio Okapi, 14 Jan clashes at Kamandi Gite and Kibanda). Context for FIRE-003 (17 Jan 2025): reports found cover 14-15 January, not 17 January; whether Luofu lies near that cluster was not checked against a gazetteer.
r6-F-BENI-003.vn: Excerpt exact on retained page dated mer 15/01/2025. Page attributes detail to local and security sources and Lubero civil society.
src: Les combats entre les Forces armées de la République Démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et les rebelles du M23 se poursuivent ce mercredi 15 janvier à Luofu, dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Des affrontements sont également signalés dans plusieurs villages au sud de Lubero, notamment à Kamandi Gite et Kibanda, situés à l'ouest de la commune rurale de Kayna.

r6-F-BENI-004.s: Radio Okapi reported that new fighting broke out on Monday 26 January between Wazalendo fighters and AFC/M23 rebels in Mighende village, about thirty kilometres from Lubero-Centre, Lubero territory; according to local sources, AFC/M23 elements attacked a Wazalendo position and burned its camp.
r6-F-BENI-004.l: Mighende village, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-004.n: Single local-sourced report. Date 26 January is stated by the page (year from page date 28/01/2026). Not within a FIRE cluster window of this unit.
r6-F-BENI-004.vn: Excerpt exact; page dated mer 28/01/2026 so 26 January is 2026 (a Monday). Single report citing local sources.
src: De nouveaux combats ont éclaté lundi 26 janvier entre les combattants Wazalendo et les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 dans le village de Mighende, situé à une trentaine de kilomètres de Lubero-Centre, dans le territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu. Selon des sources locales, les éléments de l’AFC/M23 ont attaqué une position des Wazalendo, incendiant leur campement.

r6-F-BENI-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that violent fighting had opposed AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo self-defence groups since Monday 30 March in several localities of southern Lubero territory; according to local and security sources, the first clashes broke out on Monday around 5 am in the villages of Kalonge and Lubango, about thirty kilometres from the territorial capital, where AFC/M23 forces reportedly attacked Wazalendo elements of the Mouvement des résistants des patriotes congolais (MRPC) recently deployed after a partial rebel withdrawal. The fighting displaced civilians, and several sources said AFC/M23 had reportedly retaken control of the villages concerned.
r6-F-BENI-005.l: Kalonge and Lubango villages, southern Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-005.n: Complements held claim r1-NKN-2026H1-002 (23 March 2026 partial M23 withdrawal from Lubero villages). Radio Okapi also reports (same page) new fighting on Tuesday at Katambi, Kirikiri and Byanze and says AFC/M23 reportedly resumed control of the villages concerned; FARDC response is cut off in the passage retrieved. Control entry is hedged ('aurait'). Not matched to a FIRE cluster (nearest FIRE-118, 16 Mar 2026, is two weeks earlier).
r6-F-BENI-005.vn: Excerpts exact (page mar 31/03/2026). Category territorial_control was not carried by the statement; added the page's hedged control clause (contiguous passage containing the full stored excerpt) rather than change category. Control change is hedged by the source ('aurait repris le contrôle').
ent: Mouvement des résistants des patriotes congolais (MRPC)
src: De violents affrontements opposent depuis lundi 30 mars, les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 aux groupes d’auto-défense Wazalendo dans plusieurs localités du sud du territoire de Lubero, au Nord-Kivu.

Selon des sources locales et sécuritaires, les premiers affrontements ont éclaté lundi vers 5 heures du matin dans les villages de Kalonge et Lubango, situés à une trentaine de kilomètres du chef-lieu du territoire. Les forces de l’AFC/M23 auraient attaqué des éléments Wazalendo du Mouvement des résistants des patriotes congolais (MRPC)

r6-F-BENI-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that Lunyasenge, which it described as about fifty kilometres west of Lake Edward, was taken on 2 May by AFC/M23 rebels supported by the Rwandan army, according to Kinshasa and several international reports, and that violent fighting opposed the rebels and Congolese soldiers; the toll remained unclear, but several local sources spoke of heavy human losses.
r6-F-BENI-006.l: Lunyasenge, North Kivu (territory not stated by the source)
r6-F-BENI-006.a: AFC/M23, supported by the Rwandan army per Kinshasa and international reports; FARDC
r6-F-BENI-006.x: Actualite.cd: heavy human losses according to several local sources, toll unclear
r6-F-BENI-006.n: Territory set to Lubero provisionally from the 'Lubero' context of later claims on Lunyasenge (r1-NKN-2026H1-002); this page does not name the territory, reviewers should check against the gazetteer. Lunyasenge is among the lead settlements near FIRE-108 (Jan 2026), a different date.
r6-F-BENI-006.vn: Excerpt exact (page mar 06/05/2025, byline Josué Mutanava, à Goma). Figures field rested on an unexcerpted sentence: supplied the contiguous passage. Territory field (provisionally Lubero) is not stated by the page: cleared to null. The page does not name Lunyasenge's territory; the 'about 50 km west of Lake Edward' description is the outlet's and was not checked against a gazetteer. Rwandan army support is Kinshasa's and international reports' account; no AFC/M23 account was searched for.
src: Lunyasenge, située à une cinquantaine de kilomètres à l’ouest du lac Édouard, a été conquise le 2 mai par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 soutenus par l’armée rwandaise, selon Kinshasa et plusieurs rapports internationaux. Des combats violents ont opposé les rebelles aux militaires congolais.

r6-F-BENI-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that in a communiqué published on 4 May the Congolese army confirmed the loss of Lunyasenge, denouncing a flagrant violation of the ceasefire in force, and that Colonel Mak Hazukay, FARDC spokesperson in the Grand-Nord, reaffirmed the army's will to 'riposter sur tous les fronts' if the threats persisted.
r6-F-BENI-007.n: Party statement (Kinshasa). AFC/M23 account of Lunyasenge not found in the searches run for this unit.
r6-F-BENI-007.vn: Excerpt exact. Statement keeps the communiqué and the spokesperson's remark as separate reported items. Reported via Actualite.cd; the communiqué itself was not retrieved. The page does not say explicitly that Hazukay's words were in the communiqué.
src: Dans un communiqué publié le 4 mai, l’armée congolaise a confirmé la perte de Lunyasenge, dénonçant une violation flagrante du cessez-le-feu en vigueur. Le colonel Mak Hazukay, porte-parole des FARDC au Grand-Nord, a réaffirmé la volonté de l’armée de « riposter sur tous les fronts » si les menaces persistent.

r6-F-BENI-008.s: Actualite.cd reported that the border town of Kasindi, in Beni territory, received on the evening of Monday 5 May the first wave of displaced people fleeing Lunyasenge, taken recently by AFC/M23 rebels.
r6-F-BENI-008.l: Kasindi, Beni territory (displaced from Lunyasenge), North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-008.x: Actualite.cd: number of displaced still to be determined
r6-F-BENI-008.n: Kasindi is a lead settlement for clusters FIRE-111/134 but the dates differ (May 2025 vs 2026). The page also says further waves were expected from Musenda and Katundu, not cited here.
r6-F-BENI-008.vn: Excerpt exact; page also says the number of displaced 'reste à déterminer' (Basongora civil society, Paul Zaidi).
src: La cité frontalière de Kasindi, dans le territoire de Beni (Nord-Kivu), a accueilli dans la soirée du lundi 5 mai la première vague de déplacés fuyant la localité de Lunyasenge, prise récemment par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23.

r6-F-BENI-009.s: ACLED reported that by the end of the first quarter of 2025 the M23-RDF offensive had reached an ADF camp in Lubero territory under the leadership of Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, commonly called Abwakasi.
r6-F-BENI-009.l: ADF camp in Lubero territory (exact place not stated), North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-009.a: M23-RDF offensive; ADF camp under Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (Abwakasi)
r6-F-BENI-009.n: Analytical statement by ACLED, not an event report: no date or village of the encounter is given. Context for the 17 Mar 2025 lead FIRE-021 but not tied to it. Existing GoE claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-008 place Abwakasi's unit in Lubero.
r6-F-BENI-009.vn: Excerpt exact on retained ACLED report page (footnoted sentence). Worded as ACLED's report; date is approximate (by end of March 2025). ACLED analytical report (18 June 2025); it gives no date or place for the encounter, and 'M23-RDF' is ACLED's own label.
src: By the end of the first quarter in 2025, the M23-RDF offensive had reached an ADF camp in Lubero territory under the leadership of Ahmad Mahmood Hassan, who is commonly called Abwakasi.

r6-F-BENI-010.s: Radio Moto Beni-Butembo (RMBB) reported that suspected ADF rebels attacked Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, in the city of Beni, in the night of Saturday to Sunday 31 May 2026, targeting among other places the Ngadi pygmy camp; the provisional toll was at least 7 killed, mostly pygmies including the comedian Shukurani Nzanzu Mangese, six bodies being found early on Sunday and the seventh victim dying of wounds in a health facility, and sources on site said several other civilians were missing.
r6-F-BENI-010.l: Ngadi neighbourhood, Ruwenzori commune, Beni city, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-010.a: suspected ADF rebels ("présumés rebelles de l’ADF")
r6-F-BENI-010.x: RMBB: at least 7 killed (provisional), several civilians missing
r6-F-BENI-010.n: Local community radio, Beni town (RMBB). Adds the named victim and the missing to held claim r4-G-LOCAL-NK-009 (Radio Okapi, Mukwege condemnation). The page is dated 31 May 2026. Ngadi is in Beni city, roughly 50 km from the FIRE-134 cluster at Kasindi (27-31 May 2026); not the same place.
r6-F-BENI-010.vn: Excerpts exact (byline Rédaction RMBB). 'Beni city' was not in the stored excerpt: supplied the contiguous lead sentence. Grade lowered to C: single local radio report, perpetrators 'présumés'.
src: Des présumés rebelles de l’ADF ont signé leur présence au quartier Ngadi en commune Ruwenzori la nuit du samedi à ce dimanche 31 mai 2026. Parmi les endroits ciblés, le camp de pygmées de Ngadi. Le bilan provisoire fait état d’au moins 7 personnes tuées.

Les victimes sont essentiellement des pygmées parmi lesquels l’artiste comédien Shukurani Nzanzu Mangese. Si les six corps sans vie ont été découverts tôt le matin de ce dimanche, la 7ᵉ victime a succombé à ses blessures dans une structure sanitaire où elle a été dépêchée pour des soins. Des sources sur place renseignent que plusieurs autres civils sont portés disparus.

r6-F-BENI-011.s: OCHA reported in a weekly regional 'latest events at a glance' infographic that fighting in Masisi and Lubero had displaced over 100,000 people, disrupted health services and affected food supplies to Lubero, and that a boat carrying people fleeing the fighting on Lake Edward sank, leaving 22 people missing.
r6-F-BENI-011.l: Masisi and Lubero territories; Lake Edward, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-011.x: OCHA: over 100,000 displaced (Masisi and Lubero combined); 22 missing after boat sank
r6-F-BENI-011.n: Infographic text published by OCHA on ReliefWeb. Combined Masisi and Lubero figure, not split by territory. Health-service disruption is stated without facility names.
r6-F-BENI-011.vn: Excerpt exact on ReliefWeb page (Source OCHA, posted 25 Feb 2025). Grade B, not A: a single UN situation infographic, not a documented investigation. The 100,000 figure combines Masisi and Lubero and need not be limited to the 18-24 February week; the infographic gives no date for the boat sinking.
src: Fighting in Masisi and Lubero has displaced over 100,000 people, disrupted health services, and affected food supplies to Lubero. A boat carrying people fleeing the fighting on Lake Edward sank, leaving 22 people missing.

r6-F-BENI-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that Muhindo Tafuteni, president of the local civil society, said ADF activism was continuing in the Bapere sector and the Manzia and Mwenye groupements, and that 'for the month of January alone, we deplore more than 52 people killed'; he also said schools and health structures were no longer functioning in that part of the country.
r6-F-BENI-012.l: Bapere sector and Manzia and Mwenye groupements, Lubero territory, North Kivu
r6-F-BENI-012.a: ADF, as attributed by the civil society speaker
r6-F-BENI-012.x: Muhindo Tafuteni (civil society): more than 52 killed in January 2026
r6-F-BENI-012.n: Civil-society claim, no facility named; sits alongside held claims r1-ATR-NK-2026-010/012 (Jan 2026 tolls; one health post burned). Manzia groupement is the area of lead cluster FIRE-065 (Aug 2025) but the dates differ.
r6-F-BENI-012.vn: Excerpts exact (page 10/02/2026). Reworded so the toll stays in the speaker's words and is not tied to the western area more tightly than the quote allows. The 52 figure is the speaker's; it is not clear from the quote whether it covers only the Bapere/Manzia/Mwenye area. Radio Okapi's own lead gives about 52 killed in January across Beni and Lubero territories. No health facility is named.
src: constituent une double préoccupation, selon Muhindo Tafuteni, président de la société civile locale: « D’un côté, il y a la menace du M23 dans la partie sud.

À l’ouest, dans le secteur de Bapere et les groupements Manzia et Mwenye, l’activisme des ADF se poursuit. Pour le seul mois de janvier, nous déplorons plus de 52 personnes tuées ». Il a également indiqué que les écoles et les structures sanitaires ne fonctionnent plus dans cette partie du pays.

r6-F-FIZ-001.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that fighting broke out on a Thursday morning in the villages of Kahwela, Kivumu and Luhemba in Fizi territory between Wazalendo forces and Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23; it said the Wazalendo accused the Twirwaneho of launching attacks targeting cultivators in those localities.
r6-F-FIZ-001.l: Kahwela, Kivumu, Luhemba (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-001.a: Wazalendo forces; Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23 (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-001.n: Weekday only ('ce jeudi matin'); date computed from weekday and publication date 2025-09-11 (a Thursday). Single local outlet. Kivumu and Luhemba also appear among the settlements near fire cluster FIRE-238 (Aug 2026) but this claim is Sept 2025.
r6-F-FIZ-001.vn: Page read in full; excerpt and weekday sentence verified. Wazalendo accusation kept as party account. Weekday only ('ce jeudi matin'); the day is inferred from the page date (11 Sep 2025, a Thursday). 'Fizi territory' and 'jeudi' are on the page but not in the stored excerpt. The page also carries a Wazalendo CPLC/FABB spokesperson's claim to have repulsed the attack (not in this claim).
src: Les affrontements opposent les forces Wazalendo aux combattants Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC-M23, dans les villages de Kahwela, Kivumu et Luhemba. Les forces Wazalendo accusent les Twirwaneho d’avoir lancé des attaques ciblant des cultivateurs dans ces localités.

r6-F-FIZ-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Twirwaneho fighters allied to the AFC-M23 accused the Congolese army, in coalition with the Burundian army, of a targeted attack on the village of Mikenge near Minembwe, and that according to their statements the attack took place on 10 September with the support of Wazalendo forces.
r6-F-FIZ-002.a: Congolese army (FARDC) in coalition with the Burundian army and Wazalendo, as alleged by Twirwaneho
r6-F-FIZ-002.n: Party account (Twirwaneho) relayed by the outlet; not independently confirmed in the article. Mikenge is in Mwenga territory in other sources; the outlet places it 'near Minembwe'. Relates to the Sept 2025 clusters near Mikenge (e.g. FIRE-081, settlement Kilulwe (Mikenge I)).
r6-F-FIZ-002.vn: Verified on page; attribution to Twirwaneho preserved. Twirwaneho party account relayed by the outlet; not independently confirmed. The page places Mikenge 'près de Minembwe'; other sources place Mikenge in Mwenga territory.
src: De leur côté, les combattants Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC-M23, ont accusé l’armée congolaise, en coalition avec l’armée burundaise, d’avoir mené une attaque ciblée contre le village de Mikenge, près de Minembwe, dans les Hauts-Plateaux du Sud-Kivu. Selon leurs déclarations, l’attaque a eu lieu le 10 septembre avec le soutien des forces Wazalendo.

r6-F-FIZ-003.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that from 10 to 27 August 2026 at least 23 people were killed, 17 seriously wounded and at least six villages burned in fighting between AFC-M23-Twirwaneho troops and the DRC armed forces and their allies in the Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory; it said the figures were given by the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe after monitoring.
r6-F-FIZ-003.l: Itombwe sector (Mwenga territory), South Kivu; fighting also extended to the hauts plateaux of Fizi and the moyens plateaux of Uvira
r6-F-FIZ-003.a: AFC-M23-Twirwaneho troops and FARDC and allies (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-003.x: Radio Maendeleo, citing the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe: at least 23 killed, 17 seriously wounded, at least six villages burned; the villages are not named in the article
r6-F-FIZ-003.n: Local radio (Bukavu) relaying a youth-council monitoring tally; village names not printed. Itombwe sector is in Mwenga territory, outside the Fizi packet, but the same article covers Point Zéro (Fizi) and the 'hauts plateaux de Fizi'. No burning attributed to a specific party.
r6-F-FIZ-003.vn: Figures match the page exactly (23 / 17 / six). Tally from a local youth council relayed by Radio Maendeleo; villages not named; burning not attributed to a party. Itombwe sector is in Mwenga territory (as printed), not Fizi.
ent: Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d’Itombwe
src: Du 10 au 27 Aout 2026, au moins 23 personnes ont été tuées, 17 grièvement blessés et au moins six villages incendiés dans des combats opposant les troupes de l’AFC-M23-Twirwaneho aux Forces Armées de la RDC et leurs alliés dans le secteur d’Itombwe en territoire de Mwenga au Sud-Kivu.
Ces chiffres sont livrés par le Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d’Itombwe au terme d’un monitoring réalisé sur l’état de la zone depuis la reprise des hostilités.

r6-F-FIZ-004.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe counted at least 1100 households, more than six thousand people, displaced in the bush or in host villages in that part of South Kivu, and that sources reported continued drone and mortar bombardments at Point Zéro in Fizi territory, causing panic and new displacement.
r6-F-FIZ-004.l: Itombwe sector (Mwenga); Point Zéro (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-004.x: at least 1100 households, 'plus de six mille personnes' (more than six thousand people) displaced, per the Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d'Itombwe
r6-F-FIZ-004.n: Same article as the previous claim. 'Sources' for the Point Zéro bombardments are unnamed.
r6-F-FIZ-004.vn: Figures field reworded to the printed form; 'Itombwe area' narrowed to the printed 'cette partie du Sud-Kivu'. Figure printed in words ('plus de six mille'), not as 6,000. Sources for the Point Zéro bombardments are unnamed; no party is named as firing. Radio Maendeleo places Point Zéro in Fizi territory; Actualite.cd (19 Sep 2026) places it in Mwenga territory.
ent: Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d’Itombwe
src: Le Conseil Local de la Jeunesse d’Itombwe fait état d’au moins 1100 ménages soit plus de six mille personnes en situation de déplacement dans la brousse ou encore dans des villages d’accueil dans cette partie du Sud-Kivu.

Du côté Point Zéro dans le territoire de Fizi, des sources annonce la poursuite des bombardements à l’aide des drones et autres mortiers, une situation qui continue de provoquer la panique et de nouveaux déplacements des populations.

r6-F-FIZ-005.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that over the weekend and until Monday morning 31 August 2026 the Kipupu-Mikenge axis was the scene of violent clashes between the two sides as far as the area known as Filon 14 in the Itombwe massif.
r6-F-FIZ-005.l: Kipupu-Mikenge axis, up to 'Filon 14' (Itombwe massif), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-005.a: AFC-M23-Twirwaneho and FARDC with allies (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-005.n: Weekend dates computed from 'week-end dernier' and Monday 31 August; range approximate.
r6-F-FIZ-005.vn: Verified on page. 'Les deux antagonistes' is read from the article's opening paragraph; the sentence itself does not name them. Weekend dates are approximate.
src: Déjà le week-end dernier et jusque dans la matinée de lundi 31 août 2026, l’axe Kipupu-Mikenge a été le théâtre de violents affrontements entre les deux antagonistes jusque vers l’espace dit Filon 14 toujours dans le massif d’Itombwe.

r6-F-FIZ-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that nearly 41.900 people displaced by clashes between AFC/M23 elements and FARDC/Wazalendo were living in precarious conditions in villages including Nakiele, Kilumbi and Kanguli in Fizi territory; it quoted civil society as saying its assessments counted 41.952 displaced persons in 8618 households, living without sufficient access to food, drinking water, health care or shelter.
r6-F-FIZ-006.l: Nakiele, Kilumbi, Kanguli health areas (Fizi territory), South Kivu; 17 villages listed incl. Point zéro, Kitasha, Mikenge 1 and 2, Kakenge, Abala
r6-F-FIZ-006.a: not attributed (displacement from AFC/M23 vs FARDC/Wazalendo clashes)
r6-F-FIZ-006.x: 'Près de 41.900 déplacés' (article); '41.952 personnes déplacées regroupées en 8618 ménages' (civil-society assessment quoted)
r6-F-FIZ-006.n: Quote is from the civil-society advocacy note; the article's own headline says 'près de 42.000'. The article states the note comes from 'la société civile des moyens plateaux de Fizi' in one sentence and 'd'Uvira' in another. Sector spelled 'Tanganyika' in the headline.
r6-F-FIZ-006.vn: Numbers restored to the printed form; the 41.952 figure attributed to civil society rather than the outlet. Discrepancy on the page: the advocacy note is attributed to 'la société civile des moyens plateaux de Fizi' in one sentence and the quote to 'la société civile des moyens plateaux d'Uvira' in the next. Headline says 'près de 42.000'. Relevant to civilian access to health care (lack of access stated, no attack on facilities).
src: Près de 41.900 déplacés des affrontements entre les éléments de l'AFC/M23 et les FARDC/Wazalendo vivent dans des conditions précaires dans différents villages notamment Nakiele, Kilumbi et Kanguli dans dans le territoire de Fizi au Sud-Kivu.

Nos évaluations recensent 41.952 personnes déplacées regroupées en 8618 ménages, vivant dans des conditions extrêmement précaires, sans accès suffisant à la nourriture, à l’eau potable, aux soins de santé, aux abris

r6-F-FIZ-007.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that new fighting at the start of the week led to the AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops taking the centre of the village of Kanguli since Wednesday 22 July.
r6-F-FIZ-007.a: AFC/M23-Twirwaneho troops (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-007.n: Year taken from the page's 'Last updated 2026/07/25'. The same article places Kanguli about 40 km from Lusenda refugee camp and about 65 km from Baraka. Kanguli is among the villages listed in the 12 Sept 2026 displacement note (health area Kanguli). Relates to FIRE-185 (23-27 Jul 2026) only in time.
r6-F-FIZ-007.vn: Verified on page. Holder as printed: 'les troupes de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho' took the centre of the village. Year from the page date (25 Jul 2026). The page places Kanguli about 40 km from Lusenda camp and about 65 km from Baraka.
src: de nouveaux combats ont éclaté en début de semaine, conduisant à la prise du centre du village de Kanguli par les troupes de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho depuis le mercredi 22 juillet dernier.

r6-F-FIZ-008.s: Radio Maendeleo reported, citing local sources, that AFC/M23 troops still controlled the village of Point Zéro and its surroundings, while the FARDC kept their positions at Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera and as far as Fizi-Centre.
r6-F-FIZ-008.l: Point Zéro, Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera, Fizi-Centre (Fizi / Mwenga), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-008.a: AFC/M23; FARDC (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-008.n: Kipupu is described in the same article as chef-lieu of Itombwe sector.
r6-F-FIZ-008.vn: Verified on page. Holders as printed: AFC/M23 at Point Zéro; FARDC at Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera, Fizi-Centre. The page calls Kipupu chef-lieu of Itombwe sector.
src: Des sources locales indiquent que les troupes de l’AFC/M23 contrôlent toujours le village de Point Zéro et ses environs, tandis que les FARDC conservent leurs positions à Kipupu, Mulima, Mukera et jusqu’à Fizi-Centre.

r6-F-FIZ-009.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that telecommunication network services remained suspended in the town of Baraka, across Fizi territory and part of the Itombwe sector, a measure in force for more than a month and taken by the authorities for security reasons, notably after the taking of several villages including Point Zéro by AFC/M23; local civil society said even private Starlink connections were blocked.
r6-F-FIZ-009.l: Baraka, Fizi territory and part of Itombwe sector (Mwenga), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-009.x: in force 'for more than a month' (source)
r6-F-FIZ-009.n: Which authority ordered the suspension is not stated.
r6-F-FIZ-009.vn: All clauses found on the page. The authority that ordered the suspension is not named. The Baraka/Fizi/Itombwe scope and the Starlink sentence are on the page but not in the stored excerpt.
src: les services des réseaux de télécommunication demeurent suspendus. Cette mesure, en vigueur depuis plus d’un mois, a été prise par les autorités pour des raisons sécuritaires, notamment après la prise de plusieurs villages, dont la localité stratégique de Point Zéro, par les troupes de l’AFC/M23.

r6-F-FIZ-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that the AFC/M23 seized Kipupu centre on Friday 10 July before withdrawing, that clashes over control were reported at Kipupu on 12-13 July, and that the chef-lieu of the Itombwe sector then returned to the control of the army and its allies.
r6-F-FIZ-010.l: Kipupu (Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-010.a: AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and allies; FARDC and Wazalendo (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-010.n: Kipupu is in Mwenga territory (Itombwe sector); it appears near FIRE-081 (Sept 2025), not near the July 2026 Fizi clusters. Same article lists displacement from Kipupu to Kiseke, Tumungu, Alenga, Nabindi, Natulonge, Mikembenge and Lubunga (conseil local de la jeunesse d'Itombwe).
r6-F-FIZ-010.vn: 'Citing local sources in the Itombwe sector' removed: this passage is the outlet's own narration; local sources are cited for other sentences. The page places Kipupu in Mwenga territory and says calm was observed on 14 July after the government forces retook it. Year from the page date (16 Jul 2026).
src: L’AFC/M23 s'est emparé de Kipupu centre le vendredi 10 juillet avant de se retirer. Du 12 au 13, des affrontements ont été signalés à Kipupu entre les belligérants qui se disputaient le contrôle, avant que le chef-lieu du secteur d'Itombwe ne repasse sous contrôle de l’armée et ses alliés.

r6-F-FIZ-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that the vice-governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Elakano, at a security council meeting held on Monday in Uvira, denied rumours of the fall of Baraka to the rebels and urged the population to stay calm and carry on with their activities.
r6-F-FIZ-011.n: Date computed from 'ce lundi' and the page's 7 July 2026 publication date. The same page reports that several sources announced the taking of Mikenge and Point Zéro by Twirwaneho fighters backed by the RDF (Radio Okapi's wording), and that the Fizi territory administrator denounced violations of Congolese airspace by drones from Rwanda.
r6-F-FIZ-011.vn: Verified on page. Provincial official's statement, recorded as 'the vice-governor said'. Day inferred from 'ce lundi' and the page date (7 Jul 2026).
src: Cette assurance est partagée par le vice‑gouverneur du Sud‑Kivu, Jean‑Jacques Elakano. Lors d’une réunion du conseil de sécurité tenue ce lundi à Uvira, il a démenti les rumeurs évoquant la chute de Baraka aux mains des rebelles, invitant la population au calme et à poursuivre ses activités.

r6-F-FIZ-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that the army announced its 'repli stratégique' from Point Zéro for tactical reasons, and that the spokesperson of operation Sokola 2 South Kivu, sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said the villages retaken by the FARDC were Kashamata, Wihene and Kimete, with the rebels forced to fall back towards Rugezi and Bigaragara, south of Minembwe.
r6-F-FIZ-012.l: Point Zéro; Kashamata, Wihene, Kimete (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-012.a: FARDC; Twirwaneho (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-012.n: Corroborates an existing Actualite.cd claim (r1-UV-2026Q3-001, 6 July) on Kimete/Wihene/Kashamata; adds the Point Zéro withdrawal statement. Radio Okapi spells the group 'Twiraneho'.
r6-F-FIZ-012.vn: Operation name corrected to the printed 'Sokola 2'; 'Fizi territory' clause moved to the page's lead sentence. FARDC party account. The page spells the operation 'Sokola 2' (the draft had 'Sukola 2') and the group 'Twiraneho'. The same page says several sources reported the taking of Mikenge and Point Zéro by Twirwaneho 'appuyés par les RDF' (Radio Okapi's wording).
src: Parallèlement, l’armée annonce son repli stratégique du point zéro pour des raisons tactiques. Selon le porte‑parole de l’opération Sokola 2 ‏Sud -Kivu, le sous‑lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, les villages reconquis par les FARDC sont Kashamata, Wihene et Kimete. Il précise que, lors de ces affrontements, les rebelles ont été contraints de se replier vers Rugezi et Bigaragara, au sud de Minembwe.

r6-F-FIZ-013.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, violent clashes on Wednesday 1 July 2026 at Mikenge and its surroundings in the Minembwe highlands; it said that for a month Twirwaneho allied to the AFC/M23 had been fighting the Congolese army backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo, and that civil-society sources said the fighting reportedly caused several victims.
r6-F-FIZ-013.l: Mikenge and surroundings (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-013.a: Twirwaneho/AFC-M23; FARDC backed by the Burundian army and Wazalendo (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-013.x: 'plusieurs victimes' per civil-society sources; no figure
r6-F-FIZ-013.n: Several statements are in one passage. Mikenge is in Mwenga territory per other sources; tagged Fizi here as the outlet places it in the Minembwe highlands.
r6-F-FIZ-013.vn: Each clause verified on page. 'Plusieurs victimes' is conditional ('auraient') and unquantified. Mikenge is placed in Mwenga territory by other sources.
src: Des affrontements violents ont été signalés ce mercredi 1er juillet 2026 dans les hauts plateaux de Minembwe, en province du Sud-Kivu, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo. Selon des sources locales, ces combats sont enregistrés au niveau de Mikenge et de ses environs.

Depuis un mois, des combats acharnés opposent les Twirwaneho, alliés à l’AFC/M23, aux Forces armées congolaises, appuyées par l’armée burundaise et les miliciens Wazalendo. Des affrontements qui auraient fait plusieurs victimes, selon des sources de la société civile.

r6-F-FIZ-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that on Tuesday 30 June 2026 hundreds of residents of the Banyamulenge community demonstrated in Minembwe to protest against Congolese army drone attacks, which it said had intensified, and called for the withdrawal of Burundian troops present in the highlands of Fizi, Uvira and Mwenga.
r6-F-FIZ-014.a: Banyamulenge residents (protesters); Congolese army drone attacks and Burundian troops as alleged by protesters
r6-F-FIZ-014.n: Minembwe was under Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 control per other KMP reporting of 15 June 2026; protest therefore took place in a de facto-held town.
r6-F-FIZ-014.vn: Verified on page. The same page reports a drone attack on Minembwe hospital the previous week, which the AFC/M23 blamed on the Congolese army, and says the army had made no communication (not in this claim; a lead for health-care access).
src: Hier, mardi 30 juin 2026, des centaines d’habitants de la communauté banyamulenge ont manifesté à Minembwe pour protester contre les attaques de drones de l’armée congolaise, qui se sont intensifiées dans la région. Les manifestants ont également appelé au retrait des troupes burundaises présentes dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi, d’Uvira et de Mwenga.

r6-F-FIZ-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, the association Mahoro Peace Association (MPA) said 32 civilians were wounded during offensives by the Burundian and Congolese armies in the villages of Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi and Bidegu between 8 and 11 June 2026.
r6-F-FIZ-015.l: Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi, Bidegu (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-015.a: Burundian and Congolese armies, as alleged by Mahoro Peace Association
r6-F-FIZ-015.x: Mahoro Peace Association (via Kivu Morning Post): 32 civilians wounded
r6-F-FIZ-015.n: Advocacy association tied to the Banyamulenge community; treat as a party-aligned account. The same article is the only found text on this tally.
r6-F-FIZ-015.vn: Verified on page; figure 32 exact. Association's account relayed by KMP; the article does not describe the association or give a separate confirmation. Perpetrators as alleged by the MPA.
src: Dans un communiqué, l’association Mahoro Peace Association (MPA) a indiqué que 32 civils ont été blessés lors des offensives de l’armée burundaise et congolaise dans les villages de Mikenge, Gakenke, Kalingi et Bidegu entre le 8 et le 11 juin 2026.

r6-F-FIZ-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes took place on Sunday 14 June 2026 at Ilundu, a few kilometres from the centre of Minembwe, between the Twirwaneho and the FARDC, and that over the weekend aerial bombardments by FARDC Sukhoï-25 aircraft were recorded at Minembwe, causing many victims.
r6-F-FIZ-016.l: Ilundu and Minembwe (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-016.a: Twirwaneho; FARDC (Sukhoï-25 aircraft) (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-016.n: The article also says rumours of Congolese/Burundian army and Wazalendo presence in Minembwe were unconfirmed by independent sources. Ilundu is also in existing claims for 24 June 2026.
r6-F-FIZ-016.vn: 'Citing concordant sources' removed: these two sentences are the outlet's narration; 'Sukhoi' restored to the printed 'Sukhoï-25'. 'De nombreuses victimes' is unquantified and unsourced in the article. The page also says rumours of Congolese/Burundian army and Wazalendo presence in Minembwe were not confirmed by independent sources, and (citing concordant sources) that Minembwe remained under Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 control.
src: Des affrontements violents ont eu lieu dimanche 14 juin 2026 à Ilundu, entre le Twirwaneho et les FARDC. Ilundu est situé à quelques kilomètres du centre de Minembwe.
Au cours du week-end, des bombardements aériens menés par des Sukhoï-25 des FARDC ont été enregistrés à Minembwe, faisant de nombreuses victimes.

r6-F-FIZ-017.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 31 mille (31 thousand) people displaced from the hauts plateaux of Fizi, particularly Itombwe and neighbouring villages, were in the moyens plateaux, notably the Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector, Fizi territory; its source said the latest clashes took place 'last Sunday' in the village of Rugezi, causing new waves of displacement.
r6-F-FIZ-017.l: Rugezi (hauts plateaux); Nundu health zone, Tanganyika sector (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-017.a: not attributed in the stored excerpts (the page names Wazalendo and an AFC/M23-Twirwaneho coalition as the parties to the earlier fighting)
r6-F-FIZ-017.x: 'Plus de 31 mille déplacés' (more than 31 thousand displaced)
r6-F-FIZ-017.n: Page dated 2025-06-12; 'dimanche dernier' computed as 8 June 2025. Source for figures: Kalyata Antoine, head of humanitarian affairs for Tanganyika sector (as the page states). Complements r1-SKS-2025Q2-006 (Radio Okapi, 9 June).
r6-F-FIZ-017.vn: Figure restored to printed form; the named official and the bush/shelter clause removed as not in the stored excerpts; actor narrowed. Excerpt gap: the page names the figures' source (the humanitarian-affairs official of Tanganyika sector, named on the page), says numbers rose 10-25 May 2025 after fighting between Wazalendo and a coalition the page lists as AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and a third group, and says some displaced live in the bush without shelter or food; none of this is in the stored excerpts, so it is left out of the statement and figures. 'Dimanche dernier' read as 8 June 2025 from the page date (12 Jun 2025); approximate.
src: Plus de 31 mille déplacés en provenance des hauts plateaux de Fizi particulièrement de Itombwe et villages voisins se retrouvent actuellement dans les moyens plateaux plus particulièrement dans la zone de santé de Nundu, secteur de Tanganyika dans le territoire de Fizi.
Les derniers affrontements ont eu lieu le dimanche dernier dans le village de Rugezi, explique notre source qui ajoute que cela a provoqué de nouvelles vagues de déplacements.

r6-F-FIZ-018.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that more than 53 000 people fled to localities in the Fizi and Nundu health zones between August and October 2026 after intensified clashes in the hauts plateaux of Fizi; it reported OCHA as adding that fighting in early September and from 20 to 25 September reportedly caused civilian casualties and damaged essential infrastructure.
r6-F-FIZ-018.l: Fizi and Nundu health zones (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-018.a: not named in the stored excerpts (OCHA relayed by Radio Maendeleo)
r6-F-FIZ-018.x: 'Plus de 53 000 personnes' fled (Radio Maendeleo, relaying OCHA)
r6-F-FIZ-018.n: Secondary relay of the OCHA report (period 1-30 September 2026 per the article); original OCHA document not located. The article names the armed side as the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)', as printed.
r6-F-FIZ-018.vn: Publication-date clause, the household figure and the FRN naming removed as not in the stored excerpts; number kept in the printed '53 000' form. Secondary relay; the OCHA report itself was not located. Excerpt gap: the page also says the report was published in October 2026 and covers 1-30 September 2026, names the armed side as the 'Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)' against FARDC, Wazalendo and the Burundian army, and gives a further household figure for the Kimbi-Lulenge and Kabambare health zones; these are not in the stored excerpts and are left out. Casualties are conditional ('auraient') and unquantified. Internal inconsistency: an August-October displacement figure in a report said to cover September.
src: Plus de 53 000 personnes ont fui vers plusieurs localités des zones de santé de Fizi et de Nundu entre août et octobre 2026, à la suite de l’intensification des affrontements dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi.

Les combats survenus début septembre, puis du 20 au 25 septembre, auraient également fait des victimes civiles et endommagé des infrastructures essentielles, aggravant ainsi la vulnérabilité des populations, ajoute OCHA.

r6-F-FIZ-019.s: Actualite.cd reported that violent clashes continued at Point Zéro, which it placed in Mwenga territory, from the morning of 'ce 20 Septembre 2026', while several local sources said the fighting resumed there from the morning of 19 September; sources said a coalition of the FARDC, Wazalendo and 'les burundais' faced an AFC/Red Tabara Twirwaneho coalition; it said fighting had spilled over 'since yesterday' into the villages of Biziba Irumba on the periphery of Minembwe in Fizi territory, and that on 18 September fighting was concentrated in Natulonge and Kabindo in Fizi territory.
r6-F-FIZ-019.l: Point Zéro; Biziba Irumba (Minembwe periphery); Natulonge; Kabindo, Fizi / Mwenga, South Kivu
r6-F-FIZ-019.a: FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundians vs AFC/Red Tabara/Twirwaneho (as the source names them)
r6-F-FIZ-019.n: The article's body says the fighting continued 'depuis la matinée de ce 20 Septembre' while the page is dated 19/09/2026: internal date inconsistency, flagged. Natulonge also appears (per Actualite.cd 16 Jul 2026) as a displacement destination south of Kipupu.
r6-F-FIZ-019.vn: Statement rewritten to show the page's own 20 September wording beside the local sources' 19 September, to keep 'depuis hier' unresolved, and to attribute only the 19 September resumption and the coalition line to sources (the Biziba Irumba and 18 September lines are the outlet's narration). Date widened to a range ending 20 Sep. Date discrepancy on the page: the page is dated 19 Sep 2026 but its first sentence says clashes continued from the morning of 'ce 20 Septembre 2026', while local sources date the resumption to 19 September; 'depuis hier' (Biziba Irumba) is therefore 18 or 19 September. Territory discrepancy: Actualite.cd places Point Zéro in Mwenga territory; Radio Maendeleo (25 Jul and 31 Aug 2026) places it in Fizi territory. The coalition line is from unnamed 'sources du milieu'.
src: Les violents affrontements se sont poursuivis depuis la matinée de ce 20 Septembre 2026 au Point zéro dans le territoire de Mwenga au Sud-Kivu.

Selon plusieurs sources locales, c'est depuis la matinée du 19 Septembre que les combats ont repris à cet endroit. Des sources du milieu ajoutent que la coalition FARDC, Wazalendo , les burundais est face à la coalition AFC/Red Tabara Twirwaneho dans la zone.

Dans la zone, les combats ont débordé depuis hier dans les villages de Biziba Irumba dans les périphéries de Minembwe territoire de Fizi. Le 18 Septembre, c'est dans les villages de Natulonge et Kabindo que les combats étaient concentrés dans le territoire de Fizi.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-001.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 01:00 on Friday 16 October 2026 the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime were intensely bombarding Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region with heavy artillery and kamikaze drones.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-001.a: FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation), via spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accusing the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' (FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo militias, foreign mercenaries and elements of the Burundi National Defence Force, as he listed them)
r6-F-MWE-SHA-001.n: Party allegation relayed by a Congolese outlet; no independent confirmation or Kinshasa response on the page. Rugezi is in the Minembwe highlands; the page does not tie it to the Mikenge/Senge settlements of cluster FIRE-282. The source calls the movement FRN and describes it as a coalition led by Joseph Kabila; AFC/M23 is called FRN in the 17 Oct Radio Okapi page too.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-001.vn: Statement verified verbatim on the full page and correctly worded as the FRN spokesperson's claim. Actor field corrected: the page does not say FRN is AFC/M23 (it describes FRN as a coalition led by former head of state Joseph Kabila), so the parenthetical equating the two was an inference and is removed. Party allegation (FRN says); no independent confirmation and no Kinshasa response on the page.
src: « Depuis 1h00, ce vendredi 16 octobre 2026, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa bombardent intensément Rugezi et ses environs, dans la région de Minembwe, à l’aide d’artillerie lourde et de drones kamikazes », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole du FRN.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the FRN accused government forces on Monday 19 October 2026 of having bombarded Rugezi and its surroundings in the Minembwe region between the evening of Saturday 17 and Sunday 18 October 2026; it also reported that Colonel Fidèle Rugabo, described as spokesperson of FRN fighters in the Minembwe area, said the populations of Rugezi and Gipimo were attacked during the night.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-002.l: Rugezi and Gipimo (Minembwe region), South Kivu
r6-F-MWE-SHA-002.a: FRN, accusing government forces (FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai militias, foreign mercenaries, Burundi National Defence Force, as listed by the source)
r6-F-MWE-SHA-002.n: Party allegation relayed by a media outlet; no response from Kinshasa on the page. Dates from weekday-free text (17-18 October stated).
r6-F-MWE-SHA-002.vn: Both passages are on the page verbatim; attribution kept as FRN's accusation; actor list matches the page. Both sources are the same page and the same party origin, so C. Party allegation (FRN says); the 'attacks' timing is the outlet's wording of the FRN account. No Kinshasa response on the page.
src: Le Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN) a accusé, lundi 19 octobre 2026, les forces gouvernementales d’avoir bombardé Rugezi et ses environs, dans la région de Minembwe. Ces attaques ont eu lieu entre la soirée du samedi 17 octobre et le dimanche 18 octobre 2026.
De son côté, le colonel Fidèle Rugabo, porte-parole des combattants du FRN dans la zone de Minembwe, affirme que les populations de Rugezi et de Gipimo ont été attaquées durant la nuit.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to local civil society, clashes between AFC/M23 and FARDC supported by Wazalendo lasted all day Sunday at Kashaka toward Kigogo and on the national road toward Ngenga, which, in the words of the Mwenga civil society president Samuel Itebo, created insecurity at Kasika; State exam papers started late in several villages of Lwindi chiefdom as a result.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-003.l: Kashaka, Kigogo, Ngenga road and Kasika, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
r6-F-MWE-SHA-003.n: Date computed from weekday ('dimanche') and publication date Tuesday 23 June 2026: Sunday 21 June 2026 (page also says the evening of Sunday). Local civil-society source. Kigogo here may or may not be the Kigogo of the RGC lead points for FIRE-152/FIRE-245; the page does not locate it.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-003.vn: Both passages verified on the full page; publication date 2026-06-23 confirmed in page metadata. Single local civil-society origin. excerpt_en flag on source 1 is a false positive (translation matches the excerpt). Date 21 June 2026 is computed from 'dimanche' and the 23 June 2026 (Tuesday) publication date; approximate. The page elsewhere says the belligerents clashed on Sunday evening.
src: « Des affrontements entre l'AFC/M23 et les FARDC appuyées par les wazalendo ont duré toute la journée du dimanche à Kashaka allant vers Kigogo, et sur la route nationale vers Ngenga. Cette situation a créé l'insécurité à Kasika », a dit à ACTUALITE.CD, Samuel Itebo, président de la société civile de Mwenga.

Les épreuves de l’Examen d’Etat ont débuté en retard dans plusieurs villages dans la chefferie de Lwindi (territoire de Mwenga) au Sud-Kivu suite aux violents affrontements entre AFC/M23 et wazalendo dans la zone.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.s: Enquete.cd reported that, according to residents and civil-society actors, several houses were burned at Kiseke (Mwenga territory) after fighting between FARDC and the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition spread to Kiseke and Nabindi, that civilian victims including women and children 'would have died in the flames', and that house fires were also reported at Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge; the page said no official toll had been communicated and did not say who set the fires.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.l: Kiseke, Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu and Senge, Mwenga-Kipupu axis, Mwenga
r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.a: Not attributed by the source (fighting parties: FARDC and the AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho coalition, as the source names them)
r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.x: no official toll communicated (Enquete.cd); civilian deaths in the flames at Kiseke unquantified
r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.n: Local sources, unconfirmed; the page says no official toll had been communicated and that drone use alleged by local and military sources lacked independent confirmation. Unit/commanders not named. Senge also appears among the RGC lead points of cluster FIRE-282 (14-16 October 2026), a different date.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-004.vn: Kiseke burnings and the list of villages match the page verbatim. Corrected to tie the burnings to the fighting only as the page does (fighting spread to Kiseke/Nabindi), to state that no perpetrator of the fires is named, and to add the page's 'no official toll'. The conditional on deaths is preserved. Deaths in the fires are conditional ('auraient péri') and unquantified; the source does not attribute the burnings to either party; drone use alleged by local and military sources lacked independent confirmation.
src: Des habitants ainsi que des acteurs de la société civile rapportent que plusieurs habitations ont été incendiées à Kiseke. Des victimes civiles, parmi lesquelles des femmes et des enfants, auraient péri dans les flammes. D’autres incendies de maisons ont également été signalés dans les villages de Muhabo, Natulinge, Nabindi, Kisemu, Kalulu et Senge.

Selon ces mêmes sources, les combattants de l’AFC/M23-RDF-Twirwaneho sont entrés à Kipupu le vendredi 24 juillet avant de se heurter à une forte résistance des FARDC dans les villages de Bukunji et de Lwemba.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-005.s: Enquete.cd reported that fighting was reported from the morning of 'this Sunday' in the Cidasa-Kasika zone, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga, reportedly opposing FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters and Burundian forces to AFC-M23 elements, and that the fighting had already displaced several residents; new clashes were also reported around the village of Kaulile.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-005.l: Cidasa-Kasika zone and Kaulile, Lwindi chiefdom, Mwenga
r6-F-MWE-SHA-005.a: FARDC supported by Wazalendo and Burundian forces; AFC-M23
r6-F-MWE-SHA-005.n: Date computed from weekday ('ce dimanche') and the page date of 31 August 2026 (a Monday): Sunday 30 August 2026. Radio Maendeleo on the same fighting is already held (r1-ATR-SK-2026-010); this adds the Burundian-forces attribution and displacement as printed by Enquete.cd.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-005.vn: Both passages verified on the full page; dateline and metadata 2026-08-31 confirmed. Conditional wording preserved as 'reportedly'. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (FARDC spelled out in the translation). Each stored excerpt joins two page paragraphs; the wording of each is verbatim. Burundian forces' involvement is conditional in the source ('opposeraient'). Date 30 August 2026 is computed from 'ce dimanche' under a Monday 31 August dateline; approximate.
src: Des combats sont signalés depuis l’avant-midi de ce dimanche dans la zone de Cidasa-Kasika, située dans la chefferie de Lwindi, territoire de Mwenga, au Sud-Kivu. Selon les informations rapportées sur place, les affrontements opposeraient les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), appuyées par des combattants Wazalendo et des forces burundaises, aux éléments de l’AFC-M23.

Ces combats ont déjà provoqué le déplacement de plusieurs habitants, contraints de quitter leurs villages face à la dégradation de la situation sécuritaire. De nouveaux affrontements sont également signalés aux alentours du petit village de Kaulile, toujours dans la chefferie de Lwindi.

r6-F-MWE-SHA-006.s: MSF said that in Shabunda territory more than 260,000 people faced measles and cholera epidemics, due to limited access to drinking water and sanitation facilities, coupled with the displacement of people who fled violence; it said 1,002 cholera cases with 39 deaths had been recorded since 3 July 2026, according to local authorities, and that 7,620 measles cases had been reported, with 467 deaths notified.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-006.x: MSF press release of 4 September 2026: 1,002 cholera cases, 39 deaths (local authorities, since 3 July 2026); 7,620 measles cases, 467 deaths; more than 260,000 people affected
r6-F-MWE-SHA-006.n: Epidemic context for civilian health access in Shabunda, not an attack on health care. Actualite.cd carried the same release on 4 September 2026 (not cited). The release does not state the measles figures' period beyond the sentence quoted.
r6-F-MWE-SHA-006.vn: All figures match the MSF page (4 September 2026). '260 000' is printed with a space in the excerpt, so the 260000 flag is a formatting false positive; '4' in the flag comes from the figures field's release date, not the statement. Corrected 'linked to' to 'due to' (dûes à) and kept the measles figures as reported/notified, as printed. Epidemic context for health access, not an attack on health care. The cholera figures are credited to local authorities; the page gives no period for the measles figures.
src: Dans le territoire de Shabunda, au Sud-Kivu, plus de 260 000 personnes font face à des épidémies de rougeole et de choléra, dûes à un accès limité à l’eau potable et à des installations sanitaires, couplé au déplacement des populations ayant fui les violences.

Depuis le 3 juillet 2026, 1002 cas de choléra avec 39 décès ont été enregistrés dans le territoire de Shabunda,selon les autorités locales. En parallèle, 7620 cas de rougeole ont également été signalés, et 467décès notifiés

r6-F-RUT-001.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources in the region, that at least ten civilians, mostly farmers, were killed on Wednesday 22 January at Kahumiro, near Virunga National Park in Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), and that they were executed by M23/RDF coalition elements.
r6-F-RUT-001.l: Kahumiro, Bambo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (near Virunga park), Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT-001.a: M23/RDF coalition, as alleged by local sources
r6-F-RUT-001.x: Actualite.cd: at least ten civilians killed, toll expected to rise
r6-F-RUT-001.n: Single local outlet; source quoted is Chirac Mafula, youth parliament president in Bwito (named in page). Places the killing 22 Jan, 3 days after the end of cluster FIRE-001 (to 19 Jan); proximity of Kahumiro to the FIRE-001 centre not verified. M23/AFC account not found.
r6-F-RUT-001.vn: Excerpt exact and matches page; excerpt_en flag is a false positive (capitalised 'National Park' translates 'parc national'). Page prints 22 January (publication 23/01/2025, a Thursday; 22 Jan 2025 was a Wednesday). The same page also reports 9 civilians killed by M23 at Kihondo on Wednesday 15 January (possible lead for another claim). Single outlet; the page itself says the facts are hard to confirm with other sources. The page names the youth-parliament speaker both 'Chirac Mafula' and 'Isaac Mafula'.
src: Au moins dix civils ont été tués ce mercredi 22 janvier à Kahumiro, une localité située aux alentours du parc national des Virunga, dans la chefferie de Bwito (territoire de Rutshuru), au Nord-Kivu. Selon nos sources dans la région, les victimes en majorité des agriculteurs, ont été exécutés par les éléments de la coalition M23/RDF

r6-F-RUT-002.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing its sources, that fighting was reported on Tuesday in the Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory), with M23 initiating the attack, in the agglomeration of Lubwe Sud.
r6-F-RUT-002.l: Lubwe Sud, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT-002.n: Within the 1-19 Jan FIRE-001 window; place relation to the cluster not established.
r6-F-RUT-002.vn: Excerpt exact. Excerpt prints only 'ce mardi'; page is dated mar 14/01/2025, so date 2025-01-14 is consistent. Graded C rather than B: single local outlet relying on unnamed sources and a government official.
src: Des affrontements sont signalés ce mardi dans le groupement de Tongo, chefferie de Bwito, (territoire de Rutshuru). Selon les sources d’ACTUALITE.CD, le M23 est à l’initiative de l’attaque. Les combats ont lieu dans l’agglomération de Lubwe Sud

r6-F-RUT-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least five M23/RDF coalition elements were killed in an ambush by wazalendo fighters near Kiseguro in the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), and, citing its sources, that the M23 rebels had been surprised taking agricultural produce from farmers.
r6-F-RUT-003.l: Kiseguro and Ngwenda, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT-003.n: The page prints 'lundi 14 janvier 2025' although 14 January 2025 was a Tuesday; date given as a range. Single local source; pro-government framing.
r6-F-RUT-003.vn: Narrowed attribution: the ambush/toll sentence is the outlet's own narration, while 'selon nos sources' attaches only to the produce-taking clause. Added the Kiseguro/Ngwenda clause the location field relies on. Date range kept, flagged as a weekday/date conflict in the source. Date conflict on the page: it prints 'lundi 14 janvier 2025', but 14 January 2025 was a Tuesday (the article itself is dated Tuesday 14/01/2025, 15:30). The ambush was on Monday 13 or Tuesday 14 January; recorded as a range. Casualty figure is the outlet's, with no party confirmation. The page also reports heavy and light weapons fire for several hours after the ambush at Kiseguro and Ngwenda (not in the stored excerpt).
src: Au moins cinq éléments de la coalition M23/RDF ont été tués lors d'une embuscade tendue, lundi 14 janvier 2025, par les combattants wazalendo, à proximité de Kiseguro, dans le groupement de Binza, en territoire de Rutshuru.

r6-F-RUT-004.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that violent clashes broke out from the morning of Wednesday 12 November 2025 in the Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), particularly in the villages of Maruho, Machazo, Manyoni and Mudugugudu, and that further AFC-M23 attacks on Wazalendo positions were reported at Kibunanwa and Busukura in Mutanda groupement, with displaced people heading to Bambo, Lusogha, Kashalira and Kishishe.
r6-F-RUT-004.n: Overlaps FIRE-098/099 window (11 Nov-8 Dec); proximity of Bukombo/Mutanda villages to cluster centres not established. Page says the fighting violates the Qatar-facilitated ceasefire (publisher's framing).
r6-F-RUT-004.vn: Both excerpts exact and match the page (published 2025-11-12). Both sources are the same article. Graded C rather than B: single local outlet citing unnamed sources and an anonymous resident. The page's statement that the fighting violates the Qatar-facilitated ceasefire is the outlet's framing.
src: De violents affrontements ont éclaté depuis la matinée de ce mercredi 12 novembre 2025 dans le groupement de Bukombo, particulièrement dans les villages de Maruho, Machazo, Manyoni et Mudugugudu, en territoire de Rutshuru.

D’autres attaques ont été signalées dans les villages de Kibunanwa et Busukura par les éléments de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo–M23 contre les positions des Wazalendo en groupement de Mutanda. Des populations déplacées se dirigent vers Bambo, Lusogha, Kashalira et Kishishe.

r6-F-RUT-005.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local sources, that at least three bodies were found on the morning of Tuesday 11 November at Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru), the day after violent clashes between Wazalendo and AFC-M23, and that the victims were said to be three men killed with a bladed weapon.
r6-F-RUT-005.l: Manyoni, Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT-005.x: Kivu Morning Post: at least three bodies
r6-F-RUT-005.n: Bodies unidentified per the page; perpetrator not named; page says it is hard to know which side controls Manyoni.
r6-F-RUT-005.vn: Excerpts exact; '23' flag is a false positive from 'AFC-M23'. Page names no perpetrator and no victims; actor 'not attributed by the source' is correct. Page dates the preceding fighting to Monday 10 November.
src: Au moins trois corps sans vie ont été découverts dans la matinée de ce mardi 11 novembre à Manyoni, un village du groupement Bukombo, dans la chefferie de Bwito, territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu).
Selon des sources locales, les victimes seraient trois hommes tués à l’arme blanche, comme en témoignent les traces observées sur leurs corps.

r6-F-RUT-006.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that at least five people were killed and nine wounded on the night of Friday to Saturday 6 December 2025 during an incursion of armed bandits it described as assimilated to the Wazalendo in the Katsiru agglomeration, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru). A former presenter and journalist of Radio Communautaire de Mweso, Rachid Kazadi, was among the dead.
r6-F-RUT-006.a: AFC-M23 patrollers; armed bandits 'assimilés aux Wazalendo'
r6-F-RUT-006.x: Kivu Morning Post: at least five killed, nine wounded
r6-F-RUT-006.n: Date: Friday night to Saturday per page; page text prints 6 December. Wounded treated at Mweso general referral hospital per page. Anonymous residents; attribution uncertain (resident says it 'could be' Wazalendo). Within the FIRE-098 window (to 8 Dec); proximity unverified.
r6-F-RUT-006.vn: Excerpts exact; '23' flag comes from 'AFC-M23', which no stored excerpt prints, so the patroller exchange was moved to the note pending an excerpt extension. Narrowed so the statement does not imply who caused the casualties. 6 December 2025 was a Saturday, consistent. Perpetrator attribution is uncertain on the page (a resident says it 'could be' Wazalendo). Health: most wounded, including women and children, treated at Mweso general referral hospital. The page also says, citing anonymous sources, that the incursion was followed by an exchange of fire between the bandits and AFC-M23 patrollers, during which the assailants opened fire, hitting several civilians, and quotes a resident saying the bandits' origin is unknown but 'could be' Wazalendo (not in the stored excerpt; extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt).
src: Au moins cinq personnes ont été tuées et neuf autres blessées la nuit du vendredi à ce samedi 6 décembre 2025. C’était lors d’une incursion de bandits armés assimilés aux Wazalendo dans l’agglomération de Katsiru, en groupement de Bukombo, territoire de Rutshuru.
Parmi les personnes décédées figure un ancien animateur et journaliste de la Radio Communautaire de Mweso (RCM), Rachid Kazadi, qui était de passage.

r6-F-RUT-007.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local testimony, that the evacuation order affecting villages of the Binza groupement (Rutshuru), mainly Nyabanira, Kasave and Makoka, was imposed by the M23. A Binza notable said the flight began on 12 July and intensified on Friday 25 July.
r6-F-RUT-007.l: Nyabanira, Kasave, Makoka, Binza groupement, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT-007.a: M23, as named by local testimony
r6-F-RUT-007.n: Context for FIRE-041 (30-31 Jul, Busanga/Kabingu) and FIRE-009 (Kasave named among settlements, but cluster dates are Feb 2025, not July). The page says M23 launched a hunt for FDLR in the area. M23 account not found.
r6-F-RUT-007.vn: Excerpts exact; page published ven 25/07/2025 16:55 (URL path says 26/07, the modification date). Added the FDLR-hunt clause and the 'ongoing armed operations' wording from the page; attribution kept to testimony/notable. Flight began 12 July per a local notable; 25 July is the date it intensified. The page also says, per the same notable, that the M23 launched a hunt for the FDLR in the area (not in the stored excerpt).
src: Selon des témoignages locaux, l’ordre d’évacuation a été imposé par la rébellion du M23, qui intensifie ses offensives dans la zone. Les villages de Nyabanira, Kasave et Makoka sont les principaux touchés par cette injonction.
Un notable du groupement Binza indique que ce mouvement de fuite, amorcé depuis le 12 juillet, s’est intensifié ce vendredi 25 juillet.

r6-F-RUT2-001.s: Opinion Info reported a provisional toll of five dead, nearly twenty seriously wounded and about ten women raped, according to local sources contacted on 4 November 2025, in fighting since the start of that week between M23-AFC rebels and CMC-FDP Wazalendo fighters in Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru; an anonymous community source also mentioned the rape of fifteen women during the fighting. The outlet does not say who committed the rapes.
r6-F-RUT2-001.l: Bukombo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru (villages not named)
r6-F-RUT2-001.a: M23-AFC and CMC-FDP Wazalendo (fighting parties); perpetrators of the rapes not attributed by the source
r6-F-RUT2-001.x: Opinion Info, citing local sources: five dead, nearly twenty seriously wounded, about ten women raped (provisional toll); anonymous community source: rape of fifteen women
r6-F-RUT2-001.n: Single local outlet (Opinion Info, Kinshasa) citing unnamed local sources; illustrative photo only. Perpetrators of the sexual violence not stated; dates from 'since the start of this week' (week of Monday 3 November) so range is computed. Same fighting as Kivu Morning Post reports of 10-12 November (r6-F-RUT-004/005) but earlier. Does not name a village; nearby-area context for FIRE-100 (Bukombo).
r6-F-RUT2-001.vn: Excerpts exact on retained page. Narrowed '4 November' from a publication date to the date the local sources were contacted, as printed; kept the two rape figures separate with their own attributions; non-attribution of perpetrators stated. Both sources are passages of the same article (one origin). 'Since the start of this week' and 'anonymous' come from the page outside the stored excerpts. excerpt_en flag: capitalised Tuesday/November/North are translations of mardi/novembre/Nord, acceptable. Two different figures for rapes (about ten, per local sources; fifteen, per one anonymous community source); the page attributes the rapes to no party. 'Since the start of this week' in an article of Tuesday 4 November; start date is inferred. Page uses an illustrative photo.
src: les rébelles de la coalition M23-AFC aux combattants Wazalendo du groupe CMC-FDP dans le groupement de Bukombo, chefferie de Bwito, en territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu. Le bilan provisoire fait état de cinq morts, près de vingt blessés graves et une dizaine de femmes violées, selon des sources locales contactées, ce mardi 4 novembre 2025
Celle-ci évoque aussi des cas de violences sexuelles, notamment le viol de quinze femmes au cours des affrontements.

r6-F-RUT2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that the situation remained tense on the morning of Monday 10 November in the village of Kinyankuku, Bukombo groupement (Rutshuru), after fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and CMC-FDP wazalendo; citing its sources, it said hostilities began in the night from Sunday to Monday after an attack by AFC/M23 rebels on wazalendo positions. It said access to the fields on the outskirts of Kitshanga, notably on the Bukombo axis, was impossible and that farming was paralysed in the area, including at Kyahemba, a neighbouring locality also affected by the fighting.
r6-F-RUT2-002.l: Kinyankuku (and neighbouring Kyahemba), Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT2-002.a: AFC/M23 rebels (attack on wazalendo positions, per Actualite.cd's sources); CMC-FDP wazalendo
r6-F-RUT2-002.n: Single outlet citing its own unnamed sources; the page says it was unclear who controlled the village. Date computed from 'nuit de dimanche à ce lundi' and the stated Monday 10 November. Fighting about 15 km from Kitshanga centre per the page. Three days before the first FIRE-100 detection, not at its listed settlements.
r6-F-RUT2-002.vn: Excerpts exact. Corrected the draft's misplacement: the impossible access concerned fields on the outskirts of Kitshanga on the Bukombo axis, while Kyahemba was cited for paralysed farming, not for field access. Attack attribution kept to Actualite.cd's sources. excerpt_en flag: 'Monday'/'November'/'North Kivu' translate lundi/novembre/Nord-Kivu. The page says it was difficult to know who controlled the village afterwards. Single outlet citing unnamed sources.
src: Selon les sources d'ACTUALITE.CD, les hostilités ont commencé dans la nuit de dimanche à ce lundi, après une attaque lancée par les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 sur des positions des wazalendo.

La situation est restée tendue le matin de ce lundi 10 novembre dans le village de Kinyankuku, dans le groupement de Bukombo (territoire de Rutshuru) au Nord-Kivu, à la suite des combats entre les rebelles de l’AFC/M23 aux wazalendo du CMC-FDP.

L’accès aux champs périphériques de Kitshanga, notamment sur l’axe Bukombo, a été impossible. Les activités agricoles restent ainsi paralysées dans la zone, y compris à Kyahemba, localité voisine également touchée par ces affrontements.

r6-F-RUT2-003.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that about ten houses were burned between Sunday and Monday 15 December 2025 during fighting between AFC-M23 and CMC-FDP Wazalendo in Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru, and said the fires occurred during AFC-M23 military operations against CMC-FDP in villages including Muko, Karambi and Mashango.
r6-F-RUT2-003.l: Muko, Karambi, Mashango and other villages of Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru
r6-F-RUT2-003.x: Kivu Morning Post: about ten houses burned
r6-F-RUT2-003.n: Single local outlet (Kivu Morning Post, Goma) with an anonymous resident quoted; the article also says residents were hit by bullets and treated at Mweso hospital. 'Sunday' computed as 14 December from the stated Monday 15 December. Not tied to any FIRE-RUT cluster date; recorded as a related Bukombo incident.
r6-F-RUT2-003.vn: Both excerpts exact on the retained page and carry every clause; figures, date and village names as printed; no perpetrator upgrade. excerpt_en flags are translations (Monday/December/Sunday; 'According'). The outlet does not say which party set the fires; it says they occurred during AFC-M23 operations against CMC-FDP and that homes were hit by gunfire, and an anonymous resident spoke of houses burned 'by bombs' during clashes between the two forces. 'Sunday' (14 December) is inferred from the stated Monday 15 December.
src: Une dizaine de maisons ont été incendiées entre dimanche et lundi 15 décembre 2025 lors des affrontements entre les éléments de l’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC-M23) et les Wazalendo du CMC-FDP, dans le groupement de Bukombo, territoire de Rutshuru.

Selon les informations en notre possession, ces incendies sont survenus au cours des opérations militaires menées par l’AFC-M23 contre le CMC-FDP dans plusieurs villages du groupement de Bukombo, notamment Muko, Karambi, Mashango et d’autres

r6-F-RUT2-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that 30 women, accused by AFC/M23 rebels of being informants of the wazalendo on their movements, were abducted by AFC/M23 rebels on 28 December 2025 at Bukombo (Rutshuru) and taken to the Rubona camp, one of the garrisons held by the rebels; it said the Congolese army had accused the rebels of torturing the women, that 27 women were gradually released according to its sources at Bukombo, and that three remained in captivity.
r6-F-RUT2-004.a: AFC/M23 rebels (as reported by Actualite.cd); torture alleged by the Congolese army
r6-F-RUT2-004.x: Actualite.cd: 30 women abducted; 27 released gradually (per its sources at Bukombo); three still in captivity at publication
r6-F-RUT2-004.n: Single outlet relaying its own sources and an army accusation; no AFC/M23 account of the abductions found in this pass. Women unnamed in the source. Not tied to a FIRE-RUT cluster date.
r6-F-RUT2-004.vn: Excerpts exact. Added the abductor as the outlet itself names it (title and lead: 'enlevées par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23'), the release figure's attribution ('selon nos sources à Bukombo') and 'gradually'; army's accusation kept as the army's. Three-held figure rests on the title/lead (excerpt gap). excerpt_en flag: 'December' translates décembre. The torture allegation is the Congolese army's, relayed by the outlet; no AFC/M23 account found. The same page also gives a second reason for the abductions (accused of being wives of wazalendo passing information to their husbands). 'Three still held' is from the page's title and lead paragraph, not the stored excerpts; it refers to the time of publication. Women are not named.
src: 30 femmes accusées par les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 d'être informatrices des wazalendo sur leurs mouvements ont été enlevées le 28 décembre 2025 à Bukombo. L'armée congolaise avait à son tour accusé les rebelles d'avoir torturé ces femmes

ont été enlevées et conduites dans le camp Rubona, l'une des garnisons tenues par les rebelles dans cette partie du territoire de Rutshuru. Au total, 27 autres femmes ont été libérées progressivement selon nos sources à Bukombo.

r6-F-UV-SK-001.s: An early-alert entry on the ehtools humanitarian platform reported more than 18174 people (about 3029 households) displaced in the Miti-Murhesa health zone, Kabare territory, after armed clashes, which the alert dates between 25 July and 2 August 2026, in villages of the Bugobe grouping and around the Kahuzi-Biega National Park; the alert names the CHB de Katana as the structure raising the alarm.
