It listed the displaced as lacking, among other things, essential medicines.
r6-F-UV-SK-001.l: Miti-Murhesa health zone (Mudaka, Bushumba and Miti groupings receiving displaced), Kabare territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-001.a: not attributed by the source (armed clashes)
r6-F-UV-SK-001.x: ehtools alert: more than 18174 people, about 3029 households
r6-F-UV-SK-001.n: Alert status on the page: preliminary diagnosis, awaiting assessment (since 04/08/2026). Locality names in the alert are those printed by the platform. Lies in the Miti and Mudaka area named by the gazetteer for FIRE-207, but the clashes it describes (25 Jul-2 Aug 2026) precede that cluster's window (8-20 Aug). enquete.cd (3 Aug 2026, Mudaka families fleeing fighting) could not be fetched by the page helper.
r6-F-UV-SK-001.vn: All three excerpts are on the retained page and carry every clause. Figure discrepancy (3029 vs 3 929 households) surfaced in the note rather than resolved. Internal discrepancy on the alert page: the header and table give 3029 households, but the alert's own per-village breakdown sums to, and the page states, a total of 3 929 households. The page spells the grouping both 'Bugobe' and 'Bugorhe'. Alert still at preliminary-diagnosis stage (not assessed). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: Plus de 18174 personnes d’environ 3029 ménages déplacés dans la Zone de Santé de Miti-Murhesa, Territoire de Kabare.

Le CHB de Katana alerte sur la situation humanitaire très préoccupante, à la suite des affrontements armés survenus entre le 25 juillet et le 2 août 2026 dans plusieurs villages du groupement de Bugobe ainsi qu'aux alentours du Parc National de Kahuzi-Biega (PNKB).

La plupart ont abandonné leurs biens et leurs moyens de subsistance lors de leur fuite et se trouvent actuellement confrontées à une grave insuffisance alimentaire, au manque d'abris, à l'absence d'accès à l'eau potable, aux médicaments essentiels, aux vêtements et aux articles ménagers de première nécessité.

r6-F-UV-SK-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that a large fire killed two people and affected more than a hundred households in the night of Friday 14 to Saturday 15 August 2026 at Cimpwiji, in the village of Nyamyera, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory; it said the fire started around 1 a.m. while most inhabitants were asleep. The article gives no cause and attributes it to no armed actor.
r6-F-UV-SK-002.l: Cimpwiji, Nyamyera village, Mudusa grouping, Kabare territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-002.x: Actualite.cd: two dead; more than a hundred households affected (provisional)
r6-F-UV-SK-002.n: Residential fire, not a bush or field fire and not attributed to any armed actor; recorded as context for the FIRE-207 review only. Mudusa is not among the gazetteer places near FIRE-207 (Miti, Mudaka), so the location match is not established.

Le feu s’est déclaré vers 1 heure du matin, alors que la plupart des habitants étaient endormis.

r6-F-UV-SK-003.a: Actualite.cd: Wazalendo and AFC/M23 (clashes); the FARDC spokesperson, as quoted by both outlets, attributes the bombs to the RDF/AFC-M23 coalition
r6-F-UV-SK-003.x: Actualite.cd: at least 3 killed (confirmed by military authorities), several wounded; 7sur7.cd: 3 civilians killed, several others wounded
r6-F-UV-SK-003.n: Victims are not named by either outlet. Both outlets rely on the army for the toll and attribution. The spokesperson is named differently by the two (see the two official_statement claims). Possible overlap with the 'mother and her two children' in Radio Okapi 14 Aug 2026 is NOT established; kept separate.

src: Au moins trois personnes, dont une femme et ses deux enfants, ont été tuées et plusieurs autres blessées vendredi 7 août 2026 lors d’affrontements entre les combattants Wazalendo et les éléments de l’AFC/M23 à Bundje, dans le groupement de Ziralo, chefferie de Buhavu, en territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu.
Selon des sources locales, une bombe a été larguée à partir de la ligne de front sur l’axe Mpanama-Chabikere-Katale, dans le village de Bundje.

« Les terroristes de la coalition RDF/AFC-M23 ont tenté sans succès une incursion à Bunje vendredi 07 août. Ils ont lancé à l'aveuglette plusieurs bombes dans des agglomérations peuplées et 3 civils dont une femme et ses deux enfants sont morts.

r6-F-UV-SK-004.vn: Excerpt verbatim; quote matches statement including the 82 mm detail. Rank 'lieutenant' as printed by Actualite.cd. Party (FARDC) account only. Actualite.cd does not give the officer's post or sector. For the same event 7sur7.cd names 'Sous-lieutenant Jérémie Meya', spokesperson of the Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu sector; MediaCongo/ACP elsewhere names 'sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi' as spokesperson of Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu (Uvira/Fizi). src: Selon le porte-parole de l'armée dans le secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu, Sous-lieutenant Jérémie Meya, les victimes ont été tuées dans des bombardements des rebelles du M23.

« Les terroristes de la coalition RDF/AFC-M23 ont tenté sans succès une incursion à Bunje vendredi 07 août. Plusieurs autres personnes ont été blessées », a-t-il déclaré dans une adresse à la presse.
Le porte-parole de l'armée loyaliste dans cette partie souligne que les FARDC condamnent ces violations du droit international et se réservent le droit de riposter.

src: Les affrontements se sont déroulés mardi 11 et mercredi 12 août 2026, après des attaques visant des positions des loyalistes.

Selon le major Dieudonné Kasereka, chargé de communication de la 34e région militaire et porte-parole de la Task Force, les assauts ont concerné plusieurs secteurs, notamment Katale et Mpanama, dans le territoire de Kalehe , ainsi que Kabulungu , dans le territoire de Kabare.
Les FARDC affirment avoir réagi pour contenir les attaques et empêcher une progression des combattants du M23 .

r6-F-UV-SK-008.s: In an article on the fighting of 11 and 12 August 2026 in Kalehe and Kabare territories, Ouragan.cd reported that the shelling had reportedly already caused several deaths, that a woman and her two children were killed in the bombardments according to information given by the military spokesperson, and that other local sources put the toll at at least six civilians killed since the start of the week, a figure the outlet said remained to be confirmed. The article does not date the deaths.

r6-F-UV-SK-008.vn: Draft tied the deaths to 11-12 August; the page does not (conditional 'auraient déjà causé', and 'since the start of the week'). Narrowed to what the page says; conditional kept. src: Les affrontements se sont déroulés mardi 11 et mercredi 12 août 2026, après des attaques visant des positions des loyalistes.

Les tirs auraient déjà causé plusieurs pertes en vies humaines. Une femme et ses deux enfants ont été tués dans les bombardements, selon les informations communiquées par le porte-parole militaire. D’autres sources locales avancent un bilan d’au moins six civils tués depuis le début de la semaine, mais ce chiffre demeure encore à confirmer.

src: Au moins trois civils ont été tués et 18 autres grièvement blessés dans des bombardements survenus samedi 15 août 2026 dans plusieurs localités de la chefferie de Buhavu, en territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu. Le bilan provisoire est communiqué par le commandement du secteur opérationnel Sukola 2 Nord Sud-Kivu.

Selon les FARDC, les bombardements, menés à l’aide de drones et d’artillerie lourde, sont attribués à la coalition RDF/AFC-M23. L’armée congolaise affirme que les tirs ont touché des zones civiles et indique se réserver le droit de riposter afin de protéger les populations.
Un premier bilan non consolidé évoque plus de dix civils tués, mais ce chiffre n’a pas été confirmé par les autorités militaires ni par une source médicale indépendante.

r6-F-UV-SK-010.s: ReelActu reported that local sources said the rebels had retaken control of Lumbishi after several hours of fighting, while clashes in Ziralo grouping opposed AFC-M23 fighters and Wazalendo.
r6-F-UV-SK-010.l: Lumbishi, Ziralo grouping, Kalehe territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-010.n: Contradicts the FARDC claim reported by Radio Okapi on 14 August 2026 that the army had retaken Lumbishi (see next claims); a sequence is possible. Local sources, not independently confirmed.
r6-F-UV-SK-010.vn: Excerpt verbatim; 'les rebelles' kept as printed, the context names AFC-M23 v. Wazalendo. Selon des sources concordantes, les combats, qui se sont intensifiés depuis trois jours sur l’axe Igali, ont fait au moins quatre morts dont une mère et ses deux enfants. Quatre militaires congolais auraient également été blessés.

r6-F-UV-SK-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that more than 815 households had fled violence in the Ziralo grouping, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory, to take refuge at Ramba in the Mubuku grouping, and were living in very difficult conditions without adequate shelter, food, drinking water or access to health care; it quoted Joseph Safari Enakesha, territorial inspector of MSCO-Kalehe, as saying the displaced had lost everything and that children, women and the elderly were sleeping without shelter, food, water or health care.

src: Plus de 815 ménages ont fui les violences dans le groupement de Ziralo, en chefferie de Buhavu, dans le territoire de Kalehe, pour trouver refuge à Ramba, dans le groupement de Mubuku. Cependant, ces familles vivent dans des conditions très difficiles, sans abris adéquats, nourriture, eau potable ni accès aux soins de santé.

« Ces déplacés ont tout perdu, notamment des maisons, des champs, des biens et consorts. Aujourd'hui, des enfants, des femmes et des vieillards dorment sans abri, sans nourriture et sans eau et soins sanitaires », a témoigné Joseph Safari Enakesha, inspecteur territorial du MSCO-Kalehe.

r6-F-UV-SK-014.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing concordant sources, that fighting reported over the previous seven days in a large part of the Hauts Plateaux of Kalehe territory compromised the resumption of classes after the Easter holidays, with schools closed, pupils displaced and teachers fleeing in several localities of the Ziralo grouping.

src: Des affrontements ont été signalés dimanche dans le groupement de Bijombo, dans le territoire d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu, entre des combattants présentés par des sources locales comme affiliés à Twirwaneho et au M23, et des éléments des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ainsi que des miliciens Wazalendo.

Selon les informations recueillies auprès de sources locales, les combats auraient entraîné la prise de plusieurs positions jusque-là occupées par les FARDC et les miliciens Wazalendo dans les zones de Rubarati, Ruhuha et Malimba. Ces informations, qui n’ont pas pu être vérifiées de manière indépendante, font état d’un déplacement des combattants des différents camps après les affrontements.

Cette implication alléguée n’a pas, à ce stade, été confirmée de manière indépendante.

r6-F-UV-SK-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a member of local civil society said Malimba and Rubarati, in the Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, passed under the control of AFC/M23-Twirwaneho on Sunday 23/08/2026 after clashes against the FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundians, while the same source denied reports that Masango-centre had been taken, saying it remained under Wazalendo and Congolese army control.
r6-F-UV-SK-017.l: Malimba, Rubarati, Masango-centre, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-017.n: Single local civil-society source. 'Burundians' as printed (the page does not say which force). Conflicts with Bwiza.com (26 Aug) and the FARDC statement of 1 Sept on Masango; see those claims.
r6-F-UV-SK-017.vn: Excerpts verbatim (byline 'La Rédaction'); statement faithful and attributed. Single local civil-society source. 'Burundians' as printed. On Masango this source (24 Aug) conflicts with Bwiza.com (capture on 26 Aug) and the FARDC statement of 1 Sept; each account is kept separate. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « Malimba et Rubarati, dans le groupement de Bijombo, territoire d’Uvira et dans les hauts plateaux d’Uvira, sont passés sous contrôle de l’AFC/M23-Twirwaneho dimanche 23/08/2026, après des affrontements contre les FARDC, les Wazalendo et les Burundais », a déclaré un membre de la société civile locale à Kivu Morning Post.
Cependant, la même source réfute l’information faisant état de la prise de Masango-centre, qui reste sous le contrôle des Wazalendo et de l’armée congolaise.

r6-F-UV-SK-018.s: Kglnews, writing in Kinyarwanda, reported that, according to information from local structures, heavy fighting was reported on the morning of Sunday in the Uvira mountains, South Kivu, between Wazalendo rebels, which it described as allied with the FDLR, and fighters of the Twirwaneho group within AFC/M23, and that these rebels, mostly Banyamulenge, were said to have taken the areas of Malimba and Rubarati.
r6-F-UV-SK-018.l: Malimba, Rubarati, Uvira mountains, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-018.a: Twirwaneho (within AFC/M23); Wazalendo (described by the outlet as allied with the FDLR)
r6-F-UV-SK-018.n: Kigali-aligned outlet; the FDLR link of the Wazalendo is the outlet's own characterisation and is contested. Date computed from 'this Sunday' and the page's own date 23 August 2026. Independent of SOS Médias Burundi and Kivu Morning Post only as to outlet; likely the same local rumour mill.
r6-F-UV-SK-018.vn: excerpt_en checked: it is a faithful translation of the excerpt alone; the flagged capitalised words are translations ('Sunday' = Cyumweru, 'South' = Amajyepfo), not additions. Removed the draft's 'a Rwandan outlet', which no excerpt prints. The FDLR link of the Wazalendo is the outlet's own characterisation. 'Cyumweru' is read as Sunday (the article is dated 23 August 2026, a Sunday, and its lead says 'kuri uyu wa 23 Kanama 2026'). Likely the same local information circuit as SOS Médias Burundi and Kivu Morning Post, though a separate outlet.
src: Amakuru aturuka mu nzego z’ibanze avuga ko imirwano ikaze yavuzwe mu gitondo cyo kuri iki Cyumweru mu misozi ya Uvira muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo hagati y’inyeshyamba za Wazalendo zifatanyije na FDLR n’abarwanyi b’umutwe wa Twirwaneho ubarizwa muri AFC/M23. Biravugwa ko izi nyeshyamba ziganjemo Abanyamulenge zafashe ibice bya Malimba na Rubarati.

r6-F-UV-SK-019.s: Bwiza.com, writing in Kinyarwanda, reported that on Wednesday 26 August 2026 the village of Masango, in the Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu, was taken by Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 fighters, as shown by videos posted on social media.
r6-F-UV-SK-019.l: Masango, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-019.n: The claim rests on social-media videos described by the outlet, not on a verifiable on-the-ground report. Contradicted by the FARDC statement of 1 September 2026 that Masango is under army control (next claims) and, for 24 August, by Kivu Morning Post's source saying Masango-centre was still held by Wazalendo and the army.
r6-F-UV-SK-019.vn: excerpt_en checked as a faithful translation; the flagged word 'Wednesday' translates 'Gatatu'. Removed 'Kigali-based', which no excerpt prints. Rests on social-media videos the outlet describes, not a verifiable on-the-ground report. Conflicts with Kivu Morning Post's source (24 Aug: Masango-centre still held by Wazalendo and the army) and with the FARDC statement of 1 Sept that Masango is under army control. 'misozi iringaniye' (rendered 'moderate hills') corresponds to the Moyens Plateaux. 'uyu wa Gatatu' = this Wednesday; 26 August 2026 was a Wednesday.
src: Umudugudu wa Masango uherereye mu misozi iringaniye yo muri Gurupoma ya Bijombo, muri Teritwari ya Uvira mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, kuri uyu wa Gatatu, itariki 26 Kanama 2026, wigaruriwe n’abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho na AFC/M23 nk’uko bigaragara mu mashusho yashyizwe ku mbuga nkoranyambaga.

r6-F-UV-SK-020.s: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu, Sub-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, said that after the FARDC's riposte against the RDF coalition and its M23-Twirwaneho and Red Tabara allies in the Uvira and Fizi highlands, the FARDC had neutralised 23 rebels, 11 had surrendered and several weapons had been recovered.
r6-F-UV-SK-020.l: Hauts-Plateaux d'Uvira and Fizi, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-020.x: FARDC: 23 rebels neutralised, 11 surrendered (Hauts-Plateaux d'Uvira and Fizi)
r6-F-UV-SK-020.n: FARDC claim; casualty figures are not independently verified. The page's later paragraph splits the figure as 15 killed and 6 surrendered in Uvira highlands and 8 killed and 5 surrendered in Fizi highlands. The same spokesperson is named 'Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji' elsewhere (Actualite.cd). Wire credit 'ACP / MCP' is printed at the end of the article.
r6-F-UV-SK-020.vn: Excerpts verbatim; wire credit 'ACP / MCP' confirmed at page foot. Draft notes said '15 killed'; the page says 'neutralisés' (corrected in the note). FARDC claim; figures not independently verified. 'Neutralisés' is the army's word and does not specify killed or captured. A later paragraph splits the figures as 15 neutralised and six surrendered in the Uvira highlands and eight neutralised and five surrendered in the Fizi highlands. The page says the information was obtained on Tuesday 1 September 2026 from a military source. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: « À la suite de sa riposte contre la coalition terroriste RDF et ses alliés rebelles du M23-Twirwaneho et Red Tabara dans les Hauts-Plateaux d’Uvira et Fizi,

les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont neutralisé 23 rebelles, 11 éléments se sont rendus et plusieurs armes ont été récupérées », a fait savoir le sous-lieutenant Reagan Mbuyi, porte-parole des opérations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu.

r6-F-UV-SK-021.s: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that, according to a military spokesperson, the agglomerations of Malimba, Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati were now under the control of the loyalist army, and that the M23, Twirwaneho and allied fighters were forced to retreat towards Kashongo and Magunda.
r6-F-UV-SK-021.l: Malimba, Masango, Ruhua (Ruhuha), Rubarati; Kashongo and Magunda, Uvira highlands, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-021.n: Army claim only. No Twirwaneho or AFC/M23 reply to this claim found in this unit. The Twirwaneho spokesperson's later claim to have retaken Rubarati and Ruhuha (12 October 2026) is held in r1-SKS-2026Q4-005.
r6-F-UV-SK-021.vn: Excerpts verbatim; attribution 'Selon lui' kept. Army claim only, conflicting with the local-source, civil-society and Kinyarwanda-media accounts of Malimba, Rubarati, Ruhuha and Masango (23-26 Aug 2026); each kept separate. No Twirwaneho or AFC/M23 reply found. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

Face à la pression militaire des FARDC, a-t-il dit, les combattants du M23, de Twirwaneho et leurs alliés étaient contraints de battre en retraite vers Kashongo et Magunda

r6-F-UV-SK-022.s: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP, reported that the spokesperson of operations Sukola 2 Sud-Sud-Kivu said the FARDC had discovered a mass grave at Masango where civilians killed during the occupation of that agglomeration by what he called 'the forces of evil', including Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23, which he said were supported by Rwanda, were said to be buried.
r6-F-UV-SK-022.d: 2026-09-01 (statement reported 2026-09-02; dates of the killings and of the discovery not given)
r6-F-UV-SK-022.l: Masango, Bijombo grouping, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-022.a: Twirwaneho, Red Tabara and M23 supported by Rwanda, as alleged by the FARDC spokesperson
r6-F-UV-SK-022.x: no count given by the source
r6-F-UV-SK-022.n: Allegation by a party spokesperson only; no independent verification, exhumation, count or date of the killings or of the discovery. The article itself says Masango was occupied (no date); Bwiza.com reports capture by Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 on 26 August. Lead for investigators: ask MONUSCO/UNJHRO or the Congolese authorities for access to the site.
r6-F-UV-SK-022.vn: Made the spokesperson's characterisations ('forces du mal', 'soutenus par le Rwanda') explicitly his. Draft date '2026-08' was an inference from another outlet; set to the statement date, with the event undated. Allegation by a party spokesperson only; conditional ('seraient enterrés'). No count, no date of the killings or of the discovery, no independent verification or exhumation reported. r6-F-UV-SK-023.s: Actualite.cd reported that local leaders said that since 20 August the inhabitants of Nzibira and surrounding localities, in Walungu territory, had been leaving their homes after violent fighting between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo, with mass displacements also reported at Lutunkulu and Luhago, and that each camp accuses the other of being behind the clashes.
r6-F-UV-SK-023.l: Nzibira, Lutunkulu, Luhago, Walungu territory, South Kivu
r6-F-UV-SK-023.n: Place names as printed; the page also prints 'Lutunkulu' where AfriquActu prints 'Luntukulu'. Nearness of Nzibira to the FIRE-249 and FIRE-209 clusters is not established.
r6-F-UV-SK-023.vn: Excerpts verbatim; statement faithful. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 1 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one 2026-10-29: source 2 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: La situation sécuritaire est volatile et préoccupante depuis la matinée du 27 août 2026 dans le village de Nzibira, territoire de Walungu au Sud-Kivu, en raison des affrontements récurrents entre les éléments de l’AFC/M23 et les Wazalendo.

Des leaders locaux indiquent que, depuis le 20 août, les habitants de Nzibira et des localités environnantes abandonnent leurs ménages à la suite de combats violents entre les deux belligérants. Des déplacements massifs sont également signalés dans les villages de Lutunkulu et Luhago, où les habitants ont fui leurs domiciles pour se mettre à l’abri.
Chaque camp accuse l’autre d’être à l’origine des affrontements, qui perturbent gravement les activités de la population et accentuent la crise humanitaire dans la zone.

r6-F-UV-SK-024.s: AfriquActu reported that in the locality of Luntukulu, about 75 km from Bukavu, the Congolese army supported by Wazalendo repelled on Thursday an assault by the M23 supported by the Rwandan army, and that according to local sources the fighting caused significant material damage.
r6-F-UV-SK-024.a: FARDC and Wazalendo; M23 (the outlet says supported by the Rwandan army)
r6-F-UV-SK-024.n: Date computed from the weekday 'jeudi' and the article's URL date 2026-08-20 (a Thursday). Pro-army framing: 'soutenu par l'armée rwandaise' is the outlet's wording, not attributed to a named source.
r6-F-UV-SK-024.vn: Excerpt verbatim; outlet-voice claim, single source. Pro-army framing: 'soutenu par l'armée rwandaise' is the outlet's own wording. 'jeudi' taken as 20 August 2026 (the article date, a Thursday). The same page reports an AFC-M23 communiqué accusing the FARDC of attacking its positions at Rugezi, Nyaruhinga and Mukoko (not part of this claim). 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one

r7-CMD-M23-001.n: Issuing body's own list. The list's entry dates from the 2012 UN designation and the page does not date the title; the 15 Aug 2025 'last updated' date is that of the whole list, so this shows the listed post as held out in 2025, not an appointment date. The Group of Experts (S/2025/858 para 44; S/2026/466 para 64, already recorded) gives his operative post in 2025-26 as commander of the First Defence Zone and calls him 'Brigadier General' / 'General'. No superior is stated here.
r7-CMD-M23-001.vn: All three excerpts exact and printed with the name in the retained PDF (entry 34). Statement attributes the title/position to the listing. Entry-level dates (16/02/2022, late 2014 Rwanda residence) show the listing text is stale; carried as a reader note, not in the statement. Listing's stated title/position, not a finding of the post held in 2025: the 15 August 2025 date is that of the whole list. The entry itself was last updated 16/02/2022 (listed 28/02/2013) and states he entered Rwanda on 16 March 2013 and was living in Ngoma camp, Rwanda, as of late 2014; the UN Group of Experts places him as AFC/M23 First Defence Zone commander in 2025-26.

r7-CMD-M23-005.s: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Eugène Nkubito as Commander of the 3rd Division of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC and more specifically in North Kivu province, in that position since August 2022.
r7-CMD-M23-005.l: North Kivu (as described in the draft)
r7-CMD-M23-005.n: This is the Council's pre-adoption draft text (the adopted act, Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/509 of 17 March 2025, could not be fetched from EUR-Lex: see gaps), so the final wording may differ. Corroborates the tie already recorded from ACP/TRT Afrika (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010) and the Group of Experts (r1-GOE-014) and adds the stated tenure. The post 'since August 2022' predates the window; the deployment to North Kivu is the in-window fact.
r7-CMD-M23-005.vn: Excerpts exact; the PDF header gives only the 2025/… placeholder, confirming draft status. Statement says draft and attributes to the Council document. Corroborates r1-GOE-014 / r1-UC-RDF-008 (Group of Experts) and r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010 (ACP), independent origins. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding.
src: Major-General Eugène Nkubito holds a leading position as Commander of the 3rd Division of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), deployed in eastern DRC and more specifically in the North Kivu province. He has been in this position since August 2022.

r7-CMD-M23-006.s: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Pascal Muhizi as Brigadier-General of the Rwanda Defence Force since June 2021 and Commander of the 2nd Division of the RDF, deployed in Eastern DRC since August 2023.
r7-CMD-M23-006.l: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
r7-CMD-M23-006.n: Council pre-adoption draft text; adopted wording not fetched. Adds tenure to the tie recorded from ACP (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-010). The draft does not say which Kivu the 2nd Division was in; the Group of Experts (S/2026/466 para 99) places the 3rd and 4th Divisions in North and South Kivu and does not mention a 2nd Division, so the 2nd Division's location in the Kivus is a discrepancy to check.
r7-CMD-M23-006.vn: Excerpt exact; statement keeps the source's own construction for 'since August 2023'. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding. The draft's wording leaves unclear whether 'since August 2023' dates the division's deployment or his command; it does not name a province. The Group of Experts (S/2026/466) places the RDF 3rd and 4th Divisions in the Kivus and does not mention a 2nd Division: discrepancy to check.
src: Pascal Muhizi is Brigadier-General of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) since June 2021 and is the Commander of the 2nd Division of the RDF, deployed in Eastern DRC since August 2023.

r7-CMD-M23-007.s: A Council of the European Union draft implementing regulation (document 6582/25, 11 March 2025, marked LIMITE) proposed a statement of reasons describing Major-General Ruki Karusisi as the commander of the Special forces of the Rwanda Defence Force, deployed in eastern DRC.
r7-CMD-M23-007.l: Eastern DRC (as described in the draft)
r7-CMD-M23-007.a: Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), Special Force Command
r7-CMD-M23-007.n: Council pre-adoption draft text; adopted wording not fetched. The header of the draft entry reads 'Commander of the Special Force Command of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF)'. The Group of Experts (S/2026/466, via r2-G-DOC-466-018) later describes him as commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division and former Special Operations commander: a change of post to reconcile.
r7-CMD-M23-007.vn: Excerpt exact; attributed to the Council draft. Council pre-adoption text (number and date left blank, 'OJ: please insert the date of entry into force of this Regulation'); the adopted act's wording was not fetched and may differ. The 'Reasons' are the Council draft's statement of reasons, not an independent finding. The entry's identifying information reads 'Commander of the Special Force Command'; the Group of Experts (S/2026/466, r2-G-DOC-466-018) later calls him commander of the RDF 5th Infantry Division, a later change of post.
src: Major-General Ruki Karusisi is the commander of the Special forces of the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF), deployed in eastern DRC.

r7-CMD-M23-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported, citing local civil society, that Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of 'Monsieur Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik' and of 'Monsieur Grevisse Nsimparinga' systematically looted civilians' property at Chambombo, a village of Nyalugusha in Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe, on Monday 13 April 2026.
r7-CMD-M23-008.l: Chambombo, Nyalugusha village, Ziralo groupement, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
r7-CMD-M23-008.a: Wazalendo of the MCDPIN group of Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik and Grevisse Nsimparinga
r7-CMD-M23-008.n: Names Haguma Kanyengwenye's group as MCDPIN (Actualite.cd 7 April 2026, already recorded in r1-SKN-2026Q2-002, prints 'le MCDPIN de Grevisse Nsimparingira, ainsi que celui de Haguma Kanyengwenye', i.e. a separate group of his, and spells the second name Nsimparingira; Kivu Morning Post prints Nsimparinga and treats the two as one MCDPIN). No post, rank or superior is printed for him in either piece. The same piece says Chambombo was taken by Wazalendo on 13 April and retaken by AFC/M23 around 17:00. Category kept as unit_commander for the unit tie; the looting allegation is the incident attached to it.
r7-CMD-M23-008.vn: Excerpt exact on the retained page (byline 'La Rédaction'); the same page says Chambombo was taken by Wazalendo that Monday and retaken by AFC/M23 around 17h. No existing claim covers this looting or the MCDPIN tie (checked Chambombo claims). Single local outlet relaying civil society. The article prints no post or rank for either man; 'du groupe MCDPIN de' gives a group tie only. Actualite.cd (r1-SKN-2026Q2-002) spells the second name 'Nsimparingira' and treats Haguma Kanyengwenye's group as separate from MCDPIN.
src: Les Wazalendo du groupe MCDPIN de Monsieur Haguma Kanyengwenye Maik Maik et de Monsieur Grevisse Nsimparinga ont systématiquement pillé les biens des paisibles citoyens à Chambombo, village de Nyalugusha, en groupement de Ziralo, dans la chefferie de Buhavu/Kalehe, hier lundi 13 avril 2026. Cette information est rapportée par la société civile locale

r7-CMD-M23-009.s: Amnesty International described Dominique 'Domi' Kamanzi Ndaruhutse as CMC-FDP's top commander and said he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN Group of Experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru's Bwito area.
r7-CMD-M23-009.n: RULE FLAG: this Amnesty page is already cited by existing claims (r1-POL-2026-011, r1-SV-2026-026 and others); it is re-cited here only because none of them records the command and FDLR tie below, which is the tie the brief asks for. Drop this claim if the already-cited rule is applied strictly. The 2024 EU listing the first excerpt mentions is before the window and is not asserted in the statement. The FDLR collaboration is Amnesty's attribution to the Group of Experts, not Amnesty's own finding. Gashegu is printed only as spokesperson; no command post for him is stated. Amnesty says CMC-FDP denied responsibility (existing claim r1-POL-2026-012).
r7-CMD-M23-009.vn: Page already cited by r1-POL-2026-011, r1-SV-2026-026, r1-POL-2026-012 and r1-SV-2026-027 (claim_search); none records the commander or the FDLR tie, so the claim is kept for that tie only. The Gashegu spokesperson / 16 June 2026 written reply clause is narrowed out: it duplicates r1-POL-2026-012. Source 2 no longer carries any clause. Source 1's 'He' follows directly after the name on the page (verified in the retained copy). The FDLR collaboration is Amnesty's attribution to the UN Group of Experts, not Amnesty's own finding. The Group of Experts separately reports CMC-FDP as led by Dominique Ndaruhutse (r2-G-DOC-858-031).
ent: UN group of experts on DRC
src: In July 2024, the European Union sanctioned CMC-FDP’s top commander, Dominique “Domi” Kamanzi Ndaruhutse for “committing acts that constitute serious human rights violations and abuses.”

He has fought with various Nyatura (Kinyarwanda for “hit hard”) groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN group of experts on DRC, collaborated with the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), particularly in Rutshuru’s Bwito area.
CMC-FDP spokesperson Héritier Donald Gashegu responded in writing on 16 June 2026.

r7-CMD-M23-010.s: Deutsche Welle reported that the special session of the State examinations for self-taught secondary candidates was held on Tuesday 25 March in the zones controlled by the M23 rebels in North and South Kivu, and described Chantal Murekatete as an M23 cadre and principal adviser to the provincial governor.
r7-CMD-M23-010.l: M23-controlled zones of North Kivu and South Kivu (ceremony venue not stated in the excerpts)
r7-CMD-M23-010.n: Gives her post independently of the Group of Experts (S/2025/858: 'AFC/M23 focal point for humanitarian affairs'; S/2026/466: 'Special Adviser on Gender, Family and Children, Education, and Social and Humanitarian Affairs', both already recorded). Byline Zanem Nety Zaidi. The governor is not named in the excerpts (the Group of Experts and EU text name the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor as Bahati Musanga / Bahati Erasto, but this page does not). Local-language search results also describe her as 'conseillère du gouverneur du Nord-Kivu' (Kivu Morning Post, Actualite.cd Facebook posts: snippets only, not fetched). Gazette du Continent and La Tempête pages carrying the same title could not be fetched.
r7-CMD-M23-010.vn: Excerpts exact on the retained page (byline Zanem Nety Zaidi, 25/03/2025). 'Presided over the ceremony' narrowed out as grammatically ambiguous. The excerpt_en flag on source 1 concerns only the translated words State/North/South (Etat/Nord/Sud), a faithful translation; no change needed. DW's sentence 'conseillère principale du gouverneur de province qui a présidé la cérémonie' can be read as either Murekatete or the governor having presided over the ceremony; the governor is not named. The page also says the official launch was carried out in Goma by the parallel administration installed by the rebels.
src: Chantal Murekatete, cadre du M23 et conseillère principale du gouverneur de province qui a présidé la cérémonie, assure que

la session spéciale des examens d'Etat pour les élèves autodidactes du secondaire, c'est-à-dire des candidats libres, s'est tenue ce mardi 25 mars dans les zones contrôlées par les rebelles du M23, dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu.

r7-CMD-WZ-001.s: The Sentry reported that Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (also known as Abwakasi) leads operations along the Lubero-Bapere-Manguredjipa axis, with headquarters in Lohoa and positions across Batike, Baredje and Bapukara.
r7-CMD-WZ-001.a: ADF (Abwakasi group), as The Sentry names it
r7-CMD-WZ-001.n: Corroborates the GoE placement of Abwakasi's unit in Lubero (existing claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007/-008) with a second, independent NGO source and adds the headquarters (Lohoa) and named positions. The Sentry's map caption dates deployment areas 'as of October 2025'; the excerpt itself carries no date, so the date is the report date.
r7-CMD-WZ-001.vn: Verbatim on the PDF (p.7). Present-tense post and positions are The Sentry's; date is the report date, precision month is correct. The Sentry's accompanying map shows 'ADF deployment areas as of October 2025'; the sentence itself is undated.
src: Ahmad Mahmood Hassan (also known as Abwakasi) leads operations along the Lubero-Bapere-Manguredjipa axis,54 with headquarters in Lohoa and positions across Batike, Baredje, and Bapukara.

r7-CMD-WZ-002.s: The Sentry reported that Abwakasi reportedly commands around 600 individuals, including roughly 250 combatants since June 2024.
r7-CMD-WZ-002.x: The Sentry: about 600 individuals under Abwakasi, of whom roughly 250 combatants since June 2024
r7-CMD-WZ-002.n: The Sentry says 'reportedly'; no source for the figure in the excerpt (footnote 58 not retrieved). Figure is for the whole ADF Abwakasi group, including non-combatants.
r7-CMD-WZ-002.vn: Verbatim (p.8); hedge kept in the statement. Grade C because the figure is hedged and its basis (fn 58) was not checked. The Sentry hedges the figure with 'reportedly'; the hedge must stay. The figure includes non-combatants (abducted civilians and dependents, per the preceding sentence of the report).
src: Abwakasi reportedly commands around 600 individuals, including roughly 250 combatants since June 2024,58

r7-CMD-WZ-003.s: The Sentry listed Meya Sebagala (Mzee Mayor) among key ADF leaders present along Baluku at Madina camp, citing its interviews with military intelligence, civil society representatives and local researchers in eastern DRC in January 2026.
r7-CMD-WZ-003.l: Madina camp (Mambasa territory, Ituri per The Sentry)
r7-CMD-WZ-003.a: ADF (Seka Baluku group), as The Sentry names it
r7-CMD-WZ-003.n: Footnote text. Location is in Ituri (outside Phase 1 geography), recorded because the GoE (existing claims r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007/-008) links Meya's unit to ADF mass-casualty attacks including in Lubero/Beni. The Sentry spells the second leader 'Kasibante (Defender)'; Actualite.cd on 2026-03-24 reports the army saying 'Difenda Kasibandi' was killed - this page does not say whether these are the same person; not inferred.
r7-CMD-WZ-003.vn: Footnote text verified (p.~19). Location corrected: The Sentry says 'near the Ituri River', not 'Ituri' province; province stays 'other'. Outside the Phase 1 provinces (province 'other'). The Sentry spells 'Kasibante (Defender)'; Actualite.cd relays an FARDC claim that 'Difenda Kasibandi' was killed. No source here says they are the same person.
src: Key ADF leaders present along Baluku at Madina camp include Mehdi (Panisha), Kasibante (Defender), and Meya Sebagala (Mzee Mayor). See: The Sentry interviews with military intelligence, civil society representatives, and local researchers in eastern DRC, January 2026.

r7-CMD-WZ-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that since June 2024 Bapere (Lubero) has hosted two ADF groups, including the one led by Abwakasi, which it described as known for its harsh and deadly methods.
r7-CMD-WZ-004.n: Outlet's own sentence following a traditional chief's remarks; date is the publication date of the article.
r7-CMD-WZ-004.vn: Verbatim; outlet's own narration paragraph. Single clause, single source. Elsewhere in the article, Actualite.cd attributes its identification of the Bapere ADF to security and customary sources in Bapere.
src: Depuis Juin 2024, Bapere accueille deux groupes ADF, dont celui conduit par Abwakasi, réputé pour ses méthodes dures et meurtrières.

r7-CMD-WZ-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the FARDC announced on Tuesday 24 March that Difenda Kasibandi, one of the leaders of the ADF, had been killed in a joint FARDC-UPDF operation at Asangwa, on the outskirts of the Lindi river, on the boundary between Lubero and Mambasa territories. In its own narration, the outlet said the operation targeted a group of Islamists led by ADF chief Abouakas.
r7-CMD-WZ-005.l: Asangwa, near the Lindi river, boundary of Lubero and Mambasa territories
r7-CMD-WZ-005.a: ADF (group led by 'Abouakas'); FARDC-UPDF joint operation
r7-CMD-WZ-005.n: Army claim relayed by the outlet; no independent confirmation found. The article spells the ADF chief 'Abouakas' (elsewhere 'Abwakasi'); this page does not itself equate the two spellings in the excerpt. The page also spells the victim 'Kisibandi' once. Whether 'Difenda Kasibandi' is the 'Muhammad Kasibante, alias Difenda or Defender' named by the UN Group of Experts (existing claim r1-UCD-OTHER-AG-007) is not stated in the cited excerpts and is not inferred. The excerpt gives the announcement date, not the date of the operation (the article says the exact date of the hostages' release was not communicated).
r7-CMD-WZ-005.vn: Draft put the 'Abouakas' clause under the FARDC announcement; on the page it is the outlet's narration. Separated, and the death attributed to the army. Draft also gave territory Lubero alone, which the source does not say. The death is an FARDC claim, not an established fact. The page spells the name 'Kisibandi' once, and calls the ADF chief 'Abouakas' (elsewhere 'Abwakasi'). The operation date was not given; 24 March is the announcement date. The site is on the North Kivu/Ituri boundary.
src: Difenda Kasibandi, un des leaders des islamistes des Forces démocratiques alliées (ADF) a été éliminé lors d’une opération conjointe FARDC-UPDF à Asangwa, dans les périphéries de la rivière Lindi, à la limite entre les territoires de Lubero et de Mambasa, ont annoncé ce mardi 24 mars, les Forces Armées de la République Démocratique du Congo.

L’opération militaire a ciblé un groupe des islamistes conduits par le chef des ADF, Abouakas, l'un des principaux idéologues du mouvement qui a récemment dirigé des attaques sanglantes contre la population civile dans le secteur des Bapere (Lubero).

r7-CMD-WZ-006.s: RFI said that the Wazalendo groups at Uvira are led by known and feared militia chiefs, citing among them the former FARDC member René Itongwa, the former soldier and CNPSC leader William Amuri Yakutumba, sanctioned by the UN, and John Makanaki Kasimbira, whom it described as long installed in the hills overlooking Uvira and very hostile to General Olivier Gasita, deputy commander of the 33rd military region.
r7-CMD-WZ-006.l: Uvira and the hills above it
r7-CMD-WZ-006.a: Wazalendo groups (CNPSC of Yakutumba; groups of Itongwa and Makanaki Kasimbira), as RFI names them
r7-CMD-WZ-006.n: RFI analysis (8 September 2025), cited through a pressafrik.com copy credited 'RFI'; rfi.fr itself returned no text to the page fetcher and was not worked around. Corroborates existing claims on Makanaki (r1-UV-2025Q1-020, r1-UV-2025Q2-001) with a major-wire source and adds Gasita as deputy commander of the 33rd military region (FARDC) as the Wazalendo target. Existing claim r1-UV-2025Q2-001 spells him 'René Makanaki' (Actualite.cd): spellings differ across outlets.
r7-CMD-WZ-006.vn: Confirmed: the pressafrik copy ends with an 'RFI' credit and date, so the origin is RFI. The 'led by known militia chiefs' clause rests on the page sentence before the excerpt (an excerpt gap). Fixed the 'which/whom' wording. RFI calls Gasita 'deputy commander of the 33rd military region'; Kivu Morning Post (4 Sept 2025) says he was appointed to head intelligence supervision in the 33rd military region. The two sources give different posts.
src: Il y a par exemple l’ancien FARDC René Itongwa, ou encore l’ex-militaire et leader de la CNPSC William Amuri Yakutumba, sanctionné par l’ONU.

Il y a aussi John Makanaki Kasimbira, installé depuis longtemps dans les collines qui surplombent Uvira et très hostile au général Olivier Gasita, commandant adjoint de la 33ème région militaire, qui accumule les frustrations du mouvement « ville morte ».

r7-CMD-WZ-007.s: In an analysis of the cohabitation of FARDC and Wazalendo at Uvira, RFI said that Wazalendo and FARDC do not always obey the same hierarchy and that the Wazalendo are groups organised in quasi-autonomous entities, each answering directly to its chief.
r7-CMD-WZ-007.n: Analytical statement by RFI, not a finding by a monitor. Same page and caveats as the preceding RFI claim.
r7-CMD-WZ-007.vn: Verbatim; this is RFI analysis, and the copy credits RFI.
src: Mais la réalité, c’est que Wazalendo et FARDC n’obéissent pas toujours à la même hiérarchie. La situation est aussi délicate, parce que ces Wazalendo connaissent le terrain par cœur. Ce sont des groupes organisés en entités quasi-autonomes, chacun répondant directement à son chef.

r7-CMD-WZ-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, in a viral video, denounced General Gasita, saying: 'Here in Uvira, we refuse this disorder of sending us foreign faces, people who do not look like Congolese. If they have their Rwandan commanders, we will not accept them here in Uvira.'
r7-CMD-WZ-008.a: Wazalendo (general 'Muzalendo' Makanaki Kasimbira, as the outlet names him)
r7-CMD-WZ-008.n: Statement by a self-styled general reported by a local outlet; the video date is not given, so the date is approximate (report date). Recorded as the commander's own account and attributed; the remark about 'Rwandan commanders' is his allegation, not a finding. Rank is the outlet's wording ('général'), not an FARDC rank.
r7-CMD-WZ-008.vn: Verbatim; the 'general' title is the outlet's wording. The remark about 'Rwandan commanders' is the speaker's allegation. Kivu Morning Post describes Gasita's new post as head of intelligence supervision in the 33rd military region, while RFI calls him deputy commander.
src: Ici à Uvira, nous refusons ce désordre de nous envoyer des visages étrangers, des personnes qui ne ressemblent pas aux Congolais. S’ils ont leurs commandants rwandais, nous ne les accepterons pas ici à Uvira,” a déclaré le général Muzalendo Makanaki Kasimbira, dans une vidéo virale, dénonçant le général Gasita.

r7-CMD-WZ-009.s: Tumaini Africa News reported that the RAD provincial coordinator for South Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompanied by representatives of the VDP Wazalendo, expressed gratitude to President Tshisekedi and the central government for a 325 US dollar incentive payment called 'effort de guerre', in a press briefing held in Kalundu commune, Uvira city.
r7-CMD-WZ-009.a: RAD (Réserve armée de la défense), South Kivu; VDP Wazalendo
r7-CMD-WZ-009.x: Tumaini Africa News: 325 US dollars per the 'effort de guerre' payment
r7-CMD-WZ-009.n: Page date 20 Feb 2026 (publication); the briefing is described only as held on an unstated day. Single outlet (Tumaini Africa News, a Congolese online outlet); the page carries no dateline of the briefing.
r7-CMD-WZ-009.vn: Statement verified. Date precision changed from 'day' to 'approximate': the page gives only its publication date (20/02/2026 08:21), not the day of the briefing. 2026-10-29: date_precision edited: QA 0.4 (A4): the event date is a month only (2026-02, reported 2026-02-20); precision was 'day'
src: Le coordinateur provincial de la Réserve armée de la défense (RAD), sud-Kivu, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, accompagné des représentants des Volontaires pour la défense de la patrie (VDP) Wazalendo, a exprimé sa reconnaissance au Président de la République, Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, ainsi qu’au gouvernement central, pour l’octroi d’une prime d’encouragement de 325 dollars américains, dénommée « effort de guerre ».
Cette déclaration a été faite lors d’un point de presse tenu dans la commune de Kalundu, dans la ville d’Uvira, en présence de plusieurs journalistes.

r7-CMD-WZ-010.s: Tumaini Africa News reported that the 'self-proclaimed lieutenant general' Makanaki said, in the same press briefing at Uvira, that the incentive payment was a pleasant surprise and a real comfort for the Wazalendo.
r7-CMD-WZ-010.n: The page prints only 'Makanaki'; it does not give his first names, so identity with Makanaki Kasimbira John (other claims) is not stated by this source. Rank is self-proclaimed, as the outlet says.
r7-CMD-WZ-010.vn: Verified. Date precision changed to approximate, as for claim 8. The briefing context comes from the page paragraph before the excerpt.
src: Le lieutenant général autoproclamé Makanaki a souligné que cet acte constitue une agréable surprise et un réel réconfort pour les Wazalendo, « car cela touche directement leur cœur ».

r7-CMD-WZ-011.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the RAD provincial coordinator, Alexis Mwamba Dunia, announced on Thursday 22 January 2026 security measures for Uvira: at a press conference he formally banned carrying firearms and bladed weapons in urban areas and the erection of illegal roadblocks by self-defence groups, demanded the immediate withdrawal of the Wazalendo from the city centre, and said that urban security now fell exclusively under the PNC and the Military Police; the outlet added that the RAD was setting up a special unit to secure the city.
r7-CMD-WZ-011.a: RAD (Réserve Armée de la Défense), South Kivu; Wazalendo
r7-CMD-WZ-011.n: Single local outlet; the Wazalendo chain-of-command point is that a RAD coordinator, not an FARDC commander, is the one issuing orders to Wazalendo here. Whether the Wazalendo withdrew was not checked in this unit. The outlet adds that Wazalendo were accused of pillage and attacks on civilians including Banyamulenge (not cited here).
r7-CMD-WZ-011.vn: All clauses verbatim on the page; 22 January 2026 was a Thursday.
src: Le coordonnateur provincial de la Réserve Armée de la Défense (RAD), Alexis Mwamba Dunia, a annoncé jeudi 22 janvier 2026 une série de mesures sécuritaires pour rétablir l’ordre public dans la ville d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.

Lors d’une conférence de presse, il a interdit formellement le port d’armes à feu et d’armes blanches en milieu urbain, ainsi que l’érection de barrières routières illégales par des groupes d’autodéfense.

Alexis Mwamba exige également le retrait immédiat des Wazalendo du centre-ville, précisant que leur redéploiement doit se faire vers les zones montagneuses où l’ennemi est signalé. Selon lui, la sécurité en milieu urbain relève désormais exclusivement de la Police nationale congolaise (PNC) et de la Police militaire (PM).
Dans ce cadre, la RAD met en place une unité spéciale chargée de sécuriser et d’assainir la ville.

r7-CMD-WZ-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that in April 2025 the national defence minister had announced at Uvira that the local Wazalendo fighters supporting the army in defending the city now depended exclusively on the national coordinator of the Réserve armée de défense (RAD), General Padiri Bulenda.
r7-CMD-WZ-012.a: RAD national coordinator (General Padiri Bulenda); Wazalendo of Uvira
r7-CMD-WZ-012.n: Same outlet as existing claim r1-UV-2025Q2-006 (Radio Okapi, April 2025), so not an independent origin; it is a later retrospective that restates the tie and gives Bulenda's rank and post.
r7-CMD-WZ-012.vn: Verbatim. Same outlet as the existing April 2025 claim the researcher cites, so it is not independent; it adds Padiri Bulenda's rank and post. Retrospective (16 May 2026) on an April 2025 announcement; the minister is not named in the passage.
src: En avril 2025, le ministre de la Défense nationale avait annoncé à Uvira (Sud-Kivu) que les combattants locaux Wazalendo, qui appuyaient l’armée dans la défense de cette cité, dépendaient désormais exclusivement du coordonnateur national de la Réserve armée de défense (RAD), le général Padiri Bulenda.

r7-CMD-WZ-013.s: Bunia Actualité reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Évariste Kakule Somo, called on the VDP, known as Wazalendo, to show more discipline in a meeting on Friday in his liaison office in Butembo, and that John Maangayiko, spokesperson of the Wazalendo of Grand Nord-Kivu, spoke in the presence of the FARDC operations commander in the area, Brigadier General Joseph Mugisa.
r7-CMD-WZ-013.a: VDP/Wazalendo (Grand Nord-Kivu front); FARDC operations command
r7-CMD-WZ-013.n: Date computed from weekday ('vendredi') and publication date 11 January 2026. Corroborates the existing tie of Joseph Mugisa (existing claims r1-UCD-FARDC-WZ-010/-012) and of the spokesperson (r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-020, spelled 'John Mangaiko' by Kivu Morning Post; spellings differ). The page also says two Wazalendo factions clashed at Butembo on Sunday 4 January (see existing claims on Tango Fort).
r7-CMD-WZ-013.vn: Verbatim. Location corrected: the page does not place Butembo in Lubero territory. Grade lowered to C because this is a single local outlet and I could not check the corroborating existing claims (the packet was missing). 'Friday' before the 11 January 2026 publication (a Sunday) points to 9 January 2026; the date is derived, not printed.
ent: Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie
src: Le gouverneur militaire du Nord-Kivu, le général-major Évariste Kakule Somo, a appelé vendredi les Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie (VDP), dits Wazalendo, à plus de discipline, lors d’une rencontre tenue dans son bureau de liaison à Butembo, dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.

« Nous nous engageons à respecter strictement les consignes du gouvernement », a déclaré John Maangayiko, porte-parole des Wazalendo au Grand Nord-Kivu, à l’issue de l’audience. Il s’exprimait en présence du commandant des opérations militaires des FARDC dans la zone, le général de brigade Joseph Mugisa.

r7-CMD-WZ-014.s: The Agence Congolaise de Presse (ACP), the state news agency, reported from a Ministry of the Interior workshop at Uvira that Willian Amuri Yakutumba, whom ACP described as coordinator of the 'Wazalendo' in South Kivu province, said that not all armed persons are Wazalendo and that the Wazalendo must be distinguished from other armed groups or individuals in South Kivu; ACP also described Alexis Dunia as 'also coordinator of wazalendo'.
r7-CMD-WZ-014.a: Wazalendo of South Kivu (coordinators Willian Amuri Yakutumba and Alexis Dunia, as ACP names them)
r7-CMD-WZ-014.n: State news agency (partisan_drc_government): cited for what it says of titles, not for the facts. The agency gives both Yakutumba and Alexis Dunia the title of Wazalendo coordinator, whereas the RAD sources (Tumaini Africa News, Kivu Morning Post) give Alexis Mwamba Dunia the title of RAD provincial coordinator. Existing claims (HRW r1-UC-FARDC-028; Afrikarabia r1-UV-2025Q3-014) name deputy Justin Bitakwira as coordinator of the Wazalendo in South Kivu: titles differ by source and date; not reconciled here. Dateline Uvira 23 September 2026 (workshop opened 21 September).
r7-CMD-WZ-014.vn: The draft had Yakutumba saying that Dunia was 'also coordinator'. On the page this is ACP's own description of Dunia, so it is now attributed to ACP. Date changed from 23 September (day) to the workshop range, because the agency's weekday and day count do not agree. Titles are the state agency's wording. ACP calls Dunia 'aussi coordinateur de wazalendo' while Tumaini and Kivu Morning Post call Alexis Mwamba Dunia RAD provincial coordinator. ACP's dates conflict: the plea is dated 'mercredi' and 'the second day', but the workshop opened 21 September (a Monday), so the date is given as a range. ACP spells 'Willian'.
src: Les participants à un atelier organisé par le ministère de l’Intérieur à Uvira, dans la province du Sud -Kivu (Est de la République démocratique du Congo), ont plaidé, mercredi, lors de la deuxième journée des travaux, pour une meilleure compréhension des «Wazalendo»

Toutes les personnes armées ne sont pas de « wazalendo ».Il est nécessaire de bien distinguer les wazalendo des autres groupes ou individus armés opérant dans la province du Sud-Kivu », a déclaré M. Willian Amuri Yakutumba, coordonnateur des « Wazalendo » dans la province du Sud-Kivu.
De son côté, M. Alexis Dunia, aussi coordinateur de wazalendo,a indiqué que la restauration de l’autorité de l’Etat ne se limite pas à la reprise ou à la sécurisation d’un territoire

r7-CMD-WZ-015.s: Amnesty International said that the top commander of the CMC-FDP is Dominique “Domi” Kamanzi Ndaruhutse, whom the European Union sanctioned in July 2024, and that he has fought with various Nyatura groups for more than 10 years and, according to the UN group of experts on DRC, collaborated with the FDLR, particularly in Rutshuru’s Bwito area.
r7-CMD-WZ-015.l: Rutshuru territory (CMC-FDP operates primarily in the Bukombo area)
r7-CMD-WZ-015.a: CMC-FDP (Collectif des mouvements pour le changement - Forces de défense du peuple), as Amnesty names it
r7-CMD-WZ-015.n: Post (top commander) is Amnesty's wording as of its 25 June 2026 release; the EU listing (July 2024) is pre-window and appears only inside the cited sentence. The collaboration with the FDLR is attributed by Amnesty to the UN Group of Experts. The CMC-FDP's own response is recorded in existing claims (r1-POL-2026-012, r1-SV-2026-027). The page is the Amnesty International UK copy of the release; the Amnesty USA copy returned no text to the page fetcher.
r7-CMD-WZ-015.vn: Both passages verbatim on the Amnesty UK copy. The FDLR collaboration stays attributed to the UN Group of Experts. Amnesty describes the CMC-FDP as a member of the Wazalendo coalition.
src: In July 2024, the European Union sanctioned CMC-FDP’s top commander, Dominique “Domi” Kamanzi Ndaruhutse for “committing acts that constitute serious human rights violations and abuses.”

He has fought with various Nyatura (Kinyarwanda for “hit hard”) groups for more than 10 years and has, according to the UN group of experts on DRC, collaborated with the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), particularly in Rutshuru’s Bwito area.

r7-CMD-WZ-016.s: Amnesty International said that the FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition, and that the DRC's finance minister told the National Assembly's Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$4 million per month.
r7-CMD-WZ-016.l: Kinshasa (National Assembly Defence and Security Committee)
r7-CMD-WZ-016.a: DRC government (finance minister, not named in the excerpt); FARDC
r7-CMD-WZ-016.x: Amnesty International (reporting the finance minister): US$ 4 million per month paid to Wazalendo groups
r7-CMD-WZ-016.n: Second-hand: Amnesty reports what the minister said to the committee; the minister is unnamed in the excerpt. The first sentence ('FARDC supports the armed groups...') is Amnesty's own assertion, in the context of the CMC-FDP. No primary record of the committee testimony was retrieved in this unit.
r7-CMD-WZ-016.vn: Verbatim. Removed the 'Kinshasa' location and territory, which the source does not print. Normalised the figure to the page's 'US$4 million'. Second-hand: no primary record of the minister's testimony was retrieved, and the minister is not named.
src: FARDC supports the armed groups financially and with weapons and ammunition. The DRC’s finance minister told the National Assembly’s Defence and Security Committee in December 2025 that the state pays Wazalendo groups US$ 4 million per month .

r7-E-FIZ-001.s: BBC News Gahuza reported, citing residents, that the Twirwaneho armed group took the Point-Zero area in Fizi territory after heavy fighting on Wednesday and Thursday.
r7-E-FIZ-001.l: Point-Zero, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-001.a: Twirwaneho (as BBC names it, working with M23)
r7-E-FIZ-001.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page (month 'Ukwa mbere' = January). Date computed from weekdays and publication date 17 January 2026 (a Saturday): Wednesday 14 and Thursday 15 January; the capture itself is reported by the page as known on Friday 16 January. Corroborates REC-0586 (16 January). The page also relays that Congolese media (Actualite) said Twirwaneho with AFC/M23 took the area on Friday.
r7-E-FIZ-001.vn: Exact excerpt; translation faithful (the capitalised-word flag is only English renderings of place names and 'BBC'). Same event as the unit's mid-January 2026 Point-Zero capture; page dated 17 Ukwa mbere 2026. BBC's headline puts 'took' in quotation marks; the page also relays Actualité saying Twirwaneho with AFC/M23 took the area on Friday, and a Minembwe resident saying 'on Friday we heard that Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zero'. BBC could not reach the FARDC or Twirwaneho spokespeople.
src: Umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa Twirwaneho muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo wafashe 'agace k'ingenzi' mu bya gisirikare ka Point-Zero muri teritwari ya Fizi mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo nyuma y'imirwano ikomeye yabaye ku wa gatatu no ku wa kane, nk'uko abahaturiye babibwiye BBC.

r7-E-FIZ-002.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media confirmed government forces with Wazalendo had pushed Twirwaneho fighters out of Point-Zéro on Thursday, an area they had held for nearly two weeks; BBC said it asked the FARDC and Twirwaneho sides and neither had replied.
r7-E-FIZ-002.l: Point-Zéro, Fizi territory (Fizi highlands), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-002.a: FARDC with Wazalendo (as BBC names them) against Twirwaneho
r7-E-FIZ-002.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page; credits Reuters for the photo only (the page text credits 'Ahavuye isanamu, Reuters'). Date computed from 'kuri uyu wa kane' (this Thursday) and publication date 29 January 2026 (a Thursday). Corroborates REC-0587/REC-0601 (FARDC-FDNB retake 29 January). Party statements: BBC states neither FARDC nor Twirwaneho answered its questions at publication.
r7-E-FIZ-002.vn: Excerpt exact and translation faithful. Graded C, not B: the retake rests on unnamed Congolese media relayed by BBC (BBC did not confirm it, and its resident source hedged), and those media may be the same origin as the records it corroborates (REC-0587/0601), so not shown independent. BBC's own resident source hedged: FARDC and Wazalendo 'bashobora kuba koko bafashe Point-Zéro, nubwo nta gihamya ntakuka turabona' (may indeed have taken Point-Zéro, though we have no firm proof yet).
src: Ibinyamakuru bimwe muri DR Congo byemeje ko ingabo za leta zifatanyije na Wazalendo bakuye abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho kuri Point-Zéro kuri uyu wa kane, agace bari bamaze hafi ibyumweru bibiri bafashe. BBC yabajije uruhande rwa FARDC n'urwa Twirwaneho kuri ibi ariko ntacyo impande zombi zasubije kugeza ubu.

r7-E-FIZ-003.s: DW Swahili reported that the FARDC spokesperson for the Sokola 2 operations in South Kivu, Luteni (Lieutenant) Reagan Mbuyi, said the aircraft brought down came from Rwanda, that 'one of those helicopters from Rwanda, we shot it down', and that 13 rebel fighters of the group DW prints as Tugwaného and of M23 AFC had surrendered to the FARDC.
r7-E-FIZ-003.l: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-003.n: Party statement (FARDC) relayed by DW; the shoot-down and surrenders are the army's claim only. DW's spelling 'Tugwaného' for Twirwaneho kept as printed. The Rwandan government's reaction was not on the page. Speaker as printed 'Luteni Reagan Mbuyi' (other outlets print Mbuyi Reagan). Related: REC-0619 (April 2026 Burundian deployment) and REC-0621.
r7-E-FIZ-003.vn: Statement narrowed to the excerpts: 'Twirwaneho' replaced by DW's printed 'Tugwaného' (no excerpt prints 'Twirwaneho'); helicopter quote kept as the speaker's words. Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Army claim only; DW's headline states the shoot-down as fact. No Rwandan response on the page. In the same quote the spokesperson also claimed Minembwe centre was held by the army ('kituo mji wa Minembwe ni mali yetu').
src: Moja ya helikopta hizo kutoka Rwanda, tuliitungua helikopta hiyo na kufuatia operesheni hiyo, kulikuwa na wapiganaji wa waasi 13 wa kundi la Tugwaného na M23 AFC waliojisalimisha kwa FARDC.
Msemaji wa jeshi la FARDC kwenye operesheni za kijeshi kwa jina ma Sokola 2 katika jimbo la kivu kusini, Luteni Reagan Mbuyi amesema ndege iliyoangushwa ilitokea Rwanda

r7-E-FIZ-004.s: DW Swahili reported that, despite the army saying the situation had calmed, local sources in the war zone said fighting began again that day in the early morning at Mikenge and neighbouring areas.
r7-E-FIZ-004.l: Mikenge and surroundings, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory / Minembwe highlands, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-004.a: FARDC (the army's 'calm' account) versus local sources at the front; the excerpt names no side in the renewed fighting
r7-E-FIZ-004.n: Contradicts the FARDC spokesperson's 'calm' account in the same DW article. The page gives the time in Swahili clock ('saa kumi na moja na dakika arobaini na tano alfajiri', which converts to about 05:45 local time); the statement says only 'at dawn' to avoid a conversion error. The excerpt_en renders the Swahili hours literally.
r7-E-FIZ-004.vn: Same article, same day as the FARDC spokesperson's 'calm' claim (claim 2), so the counterclaim is about the same event. The stored excerpt_en rendered the Swahili clock literally ('eleven forty-five'), which an English reader takes as 11:45; Swahili 11:45 alfajiri is 05:45. Actor narrowed: DW's next sentence names the fighters as 'Twighaneho na Red_Ntabara' (its spellings), not 'Red-Tabara', and the excerpt itself names no side. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-FIZ claim 3)
src: Licha ya jeshi kusema kuwa hali imekuwa shwari, vyanzo vya ndani kwenye eneo la vita vimesema, mapigano yalianza tena hii leo saa kumi na moja na dakika arobaini na tano alfajiri huko Mikenge na katika maeneo jirani.

r7-E-FIZ-005.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Mufashi, a civil-society leader in the Minembwe area, said that besides essential goods no longer reaching residents, international aid organisations that used to take medicines to the area were now not allowed to get there.
r7-E-FIZ-005.l: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-005.a: not stated by the speaker in this passage (the protest targeted government and Burundian forces)
r7-E-FIZ-005.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page published 5 November 2025; protest date computed from 'ku wa kabiri' (Tuesday) and publication date. Single named civil-society source; BBC says it tried to get a response from the South Kivu government and army on the road closures without success. Adds a Kirundi/Kinyarwanda-press origin to REC-0186 and REC-0202.
r7-E-FIZ-005.vn: Original statement said the article prints only 'Mufashi'; it prints 'Santos Mufashi' once, but outside the stored excerpt, so the first name is left out of the statement (only names a surviving excerpt prints). Dropped the protest/Uvira clause (claim 5 carries it) and the actor, which the excerpt does not attribute. Speaker's account only; he does not say who bars the aid groups. The page prints his full name as Santos Mufashi; BBC says it could not reach the South Kivu government or the army on the road closures. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Mufashi avuga ko uretse ibyangombwa nkenerwa bitakibageraho, n'imiryango mpuzamahanga ifasha yajyanaga imiti muri ako gace ubu itemerewe kuhagera.
Santos Mufashi ukuriye imiryango ya sosiyete sivile muri ako gace

r7-E-FIZ-006.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Tuesday residents of Minembwe protested against what they called the closure of all roads linking them to Uvira, which they attributed to government and Burundian forces.
r7-E-FIZ-006.l: Minembwe, Fizi territory (Hauts Plateaux), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-006.a: government forces and Burundian forces (as the protesters allege)
r7-E-FIZ-006.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page. Date computed from 'ku wa kabiri' and publication date 5 November 2025 (Wednesday). Corroborates the protest reported by SOS Medias Burundi on 6 November 2025 and REC-0202.
r7-E-FIZ-006.vn: Exact excerpt; translation faithful; attribution to government and Burundian forces stays the protesters'. Page dated 5 November 2025 (Wednesday), so Tuesday is 4 November.
src: Ku wa kabiri mu gace ka Minembwe k'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo habaye imyigaragambyo y'abaturage bamagana 'gufungwa kw'amayira yose' abahuza n'umujyi wa Uvira ahava ibya nkenerwa mu buzima bwabo, bavuga ko bikorwa n'ingabo za leta n'iz'u Burundi.

r7-E-FIZ-007.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Burundian army admitted it had closed the roads, aiming to 'protect Uvira and the Burundian border', and asked residents in Minembwe to 'separate themselves from the enemies' there.
r7-E-FIZ-007.l: Roads from Minembwe toward Uvira, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-007.a: Burundian army (FDNB) as reported by BBC
r7-E-FIZ-007.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page, dated 25 November 2025. The page does not give the date or channel of the Burundian army statement, only that it 'admitted' it ('caremeye'). Note: a BBC Gahuza page of 12 August 2025 (already cited in the edition) reports the Burundian army spokesperson saying there was no Burundian soldier at Minembwe; the two statements differ in scope (presence at Minembwe versus closing roads) and are not reconciled on the page.
r7-E-FIZ-007.vn: Exact excerpt; 'caremeye' = admitted/acknowledged, faithfully rendered. Party statement relayed by BBC, which interviewed the spokesperson. The same page quotes Brig. Gen. Gaspard Baratuza, Burundian army spokesperson, in an interview with BBC. A BBC Gahuza page of 17 January 2026 says that at the time of the November protest the Burundian army spokesperson told BBC there were no Burundian soldiers in that area (they were at Muramvya, Mugeti and Majembwe). The two accounts are not reconciled.
src: Igisirikare c'Uburundi caremeye ko ari co cazibiye aya mayira mu ntumbero yo "gukingira Uvira n'urubibe rw'Uburundi", kigasaba abanyagihugu bari i Minembwe "kuvavanura n'abansi" bariyo.

r7-E-FIZ-008.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Twirwaneho group announced it controlled Minembwe and its surroundings and, for the first time, confirmed it had allied itself with AFC/M23, according to a person in Minembwe.
r7-E-FIZ-008.l: Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-008.n: Kirundi-language BBC Gahuza page. Twirwaneho communique dated 'ku wa kabiri nijoro' (Tuesday night) = 25 February 2025 (computed from weekday and the 26 February publication date). Corroborates REC-0130 and REC-0132. Party statements: BBC reports FARDC and the government did not answer its questions at publication; a government statement on the Minembwe capture was not on this page.
r7-E-FIZ-008.vn: Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Statement keeps the announcement as Twirwaneho's; it is not stated as BBC's own finding. The page adds that some reports said FARDC retook some positions in Tuesday's fighting, 'gusa nta ruhande rurayemeza' (no side has confirmed), and that 'Ibi leta ntacyo irabivugaho' (the government has said nothing on this). BBC's second excerpt: the army and government had not answered its questions.
src: Umutwe wa Twirwaneho ukorera i Mulenge mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo watangaje ko ugenzura agace ka Minembwe n'inkengero zayo, kandi "ku nshuro ya mbere" wemeza ko wifatanyije na AFC/M23, nk'uko umwe mu bari i Minembwe abivuga.
BBC yagerageje kuvugisha igisirikare n'uruhande rwa leta ku bivugwa na Twirwaneho n'abari i Minembwe ariko kugeza ubu ntibasubije ibibazo babajijwe.

r7-E-FIZ-009.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho took Point-Zéro on the morning of 16 January 2026, a day after taking other key points in Fizi territory including Baruta hill and shooting down a drone, and that Twirwaneho's leadership said the DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo and FDLR forces fled toward Mulima and Mutambala.
r7-E-FIZ-009.l: Point-Zéro, Baruta hill and Isumo, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-009.a: Twirwaneho (MRDP-Twirwaneho); the page names the opposing coalition as DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo and FDLR forces
r7-E-FIZ-009.n: Kinyarwanda-language Rwandan outlet (Umuryango.rw), which the project treats as state-aligned on contested facts; the capture, the flight of the other side and the FDLR presence are Twirwaneho's account relayed by the outlet. The FDLR attribution is the outlet's/Twirwaneho's wording only. Corroborates REC-0586 with a place-level detail (Baruta, Isumo, Mulima, Mutambala).
r7-E-FIZ-009.vn: Both excerpts exact on the retained copy (the live site refuses the fetch, HTTP 406); translations faithful. The statement already attributes the capture to the outlet and the flight claim to Twirwaneho's leadership. Partisan Rwandan outlet: the capture and the presence of FDLR are the outlet's and Twirwaneho's account (the page calls FDLR 'umutwe w'iterabwoba', a terrorist group). Byline Angeline Mukangenzi, 16 January 2026. The timing broadly agrees with BBC Gahuza (claim 0: capture known on Friday 16 January).
src: Twirwaneho yafashe Point-Zéro mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 16 Mutarama 2026, nyuma y’umunsi umwe ifashe ibindi by’ingenzi muri teritwari ya Fizi birimo umusozi wa Baruta, ikanahanura drone y’ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC.

Ubuyobozi bwa Twirwaneho bwatangaje ko ubwo ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, Wazalendo na FDLR byari bimaze kwamburwa Point-Zéro, umusozi wa Baruta no ku Isumo, byahunze byerekeza mu gace ka Mulima na Mutambala.

r7-E-FIZ-010.s: BTN Rwanda reported that FARDC launched an air strike in Minembwe, and that politician Moïse Nyarugabo said the attack was launched on a camp in the Mikenke area on the morning of 12 December 2025.
r7-E-FIZ-010.l: Mikenke (Mikenge) camp, Minembwe area, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-010.a: FARDC (air strike), as alleged by Nyarugabo
r7-E-FIZ-010.n: Single Rwandan outlet (BTN Rwanda) relaying a Congolese politician's statement; no casualty figure on the page. The page gives the strike date as 12 December 2025 in the text; its dateline reads only partly in the extraction. Relates to REC-0224 (12 December fighting and shelling at Rusanguku and Bilalombili) and REC-0230 (13 December MRDP/AFC-M23 allegation). Speaker is a Banyamulenge politician; treat as an allegation.
r7-E-FIZ-010.vn: Nyarugabo's excerpt says only that 'this attack' hit the camp. The FARDC and warplane attribution is BTN's own narration (its headline and first paragraph), not Nyarugabo's words, so the statement now credits each part to whoever said it. The first clause rests on the page's first paragraph and the title, not the stored excerpt. Partisan Rwandan outlet. The page gives no casualty figure and does not say what kind of camp ('inkambi') it was. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Umunyapolitiki Moïse Nyarugabo yatangaje ko iki gitero cyagabwe mu nkambi iri mu gace ka Mikenke mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 12 Ukuboza 2025, mu gihe ingabo za RDC n’iz’u Burundi zikomeje kugorwa n’urugamba.
Ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) zagabye igitero cy’indege y’intambara mu gice cya Minembwe

r7-E-FIZ-011.s: BTN Rwanda reported that the MRDP-Twirwaneho group said that closing the paths residents of Minembwe use to reach markets and clinics was meant to kill them because of their Banyamulenge ethnicity.
r7-E-FIZ-011.l: Minembwe area, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-011.a: DRC and Burundian forces (as alleged by MRDP-Twirwaneho)
r7-E-FIZ-011.n: Attributed allegation of MRDP-Twirwaneho only (partisan); the same page says DRC and Burundian forces had long closed those paths, accusing residents of working with enemies. Relates to REC-0186 and REC-0202.
r7-E-FIZ-011.vn: Statement faithful and attributed. The stored excerpt_en turned 'ugaragaza ko' (argues, asserts) into 'shows', which reads as if the claim were proven; also 'urwanirira' = fights for. Corrected. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-FIZ claim 10)
src: Umutwe wa MRDP-Twirwaneho urwanirira abatuye muri Minembwe ugaragaza ko gufunga inzira abahatuye banyuramo bajya ku masoko no ku mavuriro bigamije kubica, bazira ubwoko bwabo kuko abenshi muri bo ari Abanyamulenge.

r7-E-FIZ-012.s: Kigali Shows reported that Colonel Joseph Nganzo Olikwa Tipi, deputy commander of the 12th Brigade of the FARDC at Minembwe, was killed at Mikenke on Tuesday 3 March 2026 in fighting between government forces with allied groups and Twirwaneho with AFC/M23; it said FARDC leadership had not publicly commented.
r7-E-FIZ-012.a: Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 (as the outlet describes the opposing side)
r7-E-FIZ-012.n: Single Kinyarwanda outlet (Kigali Shows, a Rwandan entertainment/news site whose headline is partisan: 'M23 killed ... colonel who had persecuted Banyamulenge'). The death is unconfirmed by FARDC at publication. The page also says the colonel was under EU sanctions; that sanction detail is not repeated here. Related to REC-0534 (FARDC retake of Mikenge 1-2 March) and REC-0609. A combatant; no individual responsibility implied.
r7-E-FIZ-012.vn: All four excerpts exact; translations faithful. Page dated 4 March 2026; 3 March 2026 was a Tuesday. The capitalised-word flag on excerpt_en is only English renderings. Single partisan Rwandan outlet. Its headline says 'M23 killed' the colonel and calls him one 'who had persecuted Banyamulenge'. The page says he was 'reportedly' ('bivugwa') killed in an ambush by a sniper while commanding a FARDC unit called 'Hiboux'. Unconfirmed by FARDC.
src: Colonel Joseph Nganzo Olikwa Tipi, umwe mu basirikare bakuru b’Ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC), yiciwe mu mirwano ikomeje guhuza ingabo za Leta n’imitwe iyirwanya mu bice bya Minembwe, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo.
Uyu musirikare wari umuyobozi wungirije wa Brigade ya 12 ikorera muri Minembwe, yanabaye kandi umuyobozi wa Brigade ya 212 ya FARDC mu bihe byashize.
Yaguye mu gace ka Mikenke ku wa Kabiri tariki ya 3 Werurwe 2026, ahari kubera imirwano ikomeye hagati y’ingabo za Leta zifatanyije n’imitwe ziyishyigikiye, n’ihuriro rigizwe na Twirwaneho na AFC/M23.
Kugeza ubu, ubuyobozi bwa FARDC ntiburagira icyo butangaza ku mugaragaro ku rupfu rwa Colonel Nganzo, mu gihe imirwano muri Minembwe igikomeje gufata indi ntera hagati y’impande zihanganye.

r7-E-FIZ-013.s: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that Burundian army non-commissioned officer Ferdinand Nyabenda, nicknamed Bikorwa, fell three months earlier at Rugezi in Fizi territory and that his family was not informed.
