r7-E-FIZ-013.n: Burundian independent radio (RPA) in French on a Kirundi-service site; date is approximate: 'il y a trois mois' relative to the 19 September 2025 page date (about June 2025). Single source quoting a neighbour; the army did not confirm. Relates to REC-0167 (clashes at Rugezi, about 4-9 June 2025) and REC-0160.
r7-E-FIZ-013.vn: Excerpt exact. The 'family not informed' clause is on the page next to the excerpt and in the title, not in the stored excerpt. Single source (RPA, an independent Burundian radio) quoting a neighbour; the army did not confirm the death. Page dated 19 September 2025, so 'three months ago' is about June 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Ferdinand Nyabenda, surnommé Bikorwa, sous-officier de l’armée burundaise, est tombé il y a trois mois dans la localité de Rugezi, en territoire de Fizi.
Durant toute cette période, sa famille ignorait cette tragédie.

r7-E-FIZ-014.s: UN News (Swahili) reported that OCHA, in a statement quoting its humanitarian partners, said that since the middle of July fighting in the Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga areas had caused more than 48,000 people to leave their homes.
r7-E-FIZ-014.l: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories (highlands), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-014.a: not attributed by the source (fighting between FARDC and armed groups including M23, per OCHA sources)
r7-E-FIZ-014.x: OCHA via UN News Swahili: more than 48,000 displaced since mid-July 2026
r7-E-FIZ-014.n: UN News Swahili relays an OCHA update dated around 4 August 2026. Figure 48,000 is OCHA's; REC-1280 carries a later figure of 53,000 (Fizi and Nundu health zones) and REC-0555 an earlier early-July flight. Combined area (Uvira, Fizi, Mwenga), not Fizi alone.
r7-E-FIZ-014.vn: Excerpt exact; translation faithful. Added that OCHA was quoting its humanitarian partners, as the excerpt says. The figure covers Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga together.
src: OCHA kupitia taarifa iliyochapishwa kwenye wavuti wake, imenukuu washirika wake wa kiutu wakisema kuwa tangu katikati ya mwezi uliopita wa Julai, mapigano katika maeneo ya Uvira, Fizi na Mwenga yamesababisha zaidi ya watu 48,000 kuyahama makazi yao.

r7-E-FIZ-015.s: UN News (Swahili), citing OCHA, reported that the health sector in the affected areas was badly affected by the destruction of health facilities and the departure of health workers, and that since January more than 80 people wounded by fighting and explosive remnants of war had been unable to get the treatment they needed.
r7-E-FIZ-015.l: Highland areas of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-015.x: OCHA via UN News Swahili: more than 80 wounded since January unable to get needed treatment
r7-E-FIZ-015.n: Date is the UN News publication date (4 August 2026); the OCHA text does not give a single incident date. The page does not say who destroyed the facilities. Complements REC-0555 (disrupted supply routes and medical supplies) and REC-1280.
r7-E-FIZ-015.vn: The excerpt says 'affected areas', not 'highland areas' ('highland' comes only from the page's first paragraph), so 'highland' was removed. Otherwise faithful; the health passage sits in OCHA's list of impacts. The page does not say who destroyed the health facilities.
src: Sekta ya afya imeathirika vibaya kwa kiwango kikubwa kutokana na uharibifu wa vituo vya afya na kuondoka kwa wahudumu wa afya katika maeneo yaliyoathirika. Tangu mwezi Januari, zaidi ya watu 80 waliojeruhiwa kutokana na mapigano na mabaki ya vilipuzi vya kivita wameshindwa kupata matibabu wanayohitaji.

OCHA kupitia taarifa iliyochapishwa kwenye wavuti wake, imenukuu washirika wake wa kiutu wakisema kuwa tangu katikati ya mwezi uliopita wa Julai, mapigano katika maeneo ya Uvira, Fizi na Mwenga yamesababisha zaidi ya watu 48,000 kuyahama makazi yao.

r7-E-FIZ-016.s: DW Swahili reported that Jacques Alimasi, described as the supervisor (Msimamizi) of the Fizi territory civil-society organisation, said fighting continued in Fizi, citing the previous day in Point zero village and also the villages of Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and villages around Minembwe, and that killings were increasing.
r7-E-FIZ-016.l: Point Zero, Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe and surroundings, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-016.n: Single civil-society voice quoted by DW on 19 February 2026, a day after Angola's ceasefire call took effect; 'jana' (yesterday) places the Point Zero fighting on 18 February 2026. No casualty count or perpetrator given; 'killings' is the speaker's word. Related: REC-0606 (5 February Point Zero fighting), REC-0609.
r7-E-FIZ-016.vn: 'Msimamizi' is supervisor or administrator, not 'head', so the title is now given as DW prints it. 'Point zero' is spelled as printed. Both excerpts exact; translations faithful. Page dated 19 February 2026, so 'jana' (yesterday) is 18 February. No perpetrator or casualty count given.
src: Jacques Alimasi ni Msimamizi wa Shirika la raia wa Wilaya ya Fizi, ameelezea hali ya mapigano na wasiwasi katika vijiji kadhaa vya wilaya ya Fizi

Tunaendelea kushuhudia mapigano katika wilaya ya Fizi, mfano ni jana huko katika kijiji cha Point zero nahata katika vijiji vingine vya Rusanguku, Tuwetuwe, Mikenge, Minembwe na vijiji vya kandokando ya Minembwe, Mauaji yanazidi kufanyika

r7-E-FIZ-017.s: Minembwe Capital News (a Banyamulenge community outlet) reported that on Thursday 22 May 2025 the headquarters of the Mikenke hospitals was moved to Gipupu; it said the reason was not clearly known but that the administration described it as security reasons.
r7-E-FIZ-017.l: Mikenke (Mikenge) general hospital, Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, moved to Gipupu (Kipupu), South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-017.a: not attributed by the source (relocation for security reasons per the administration, as reported)
r7-E-FIZ-017.n: Banyamulenge community outlet (partisan) in Kinyarwanda, single source. The page also says the area where the hospital was relocated is controlled by Wazalendo, FDLR and the national army with Burundian forces, while Mikenke is held by Twirwaneho and M23 since February 2025 (the outlet's account); and that the hospitals are supported by MDM/PIN according to some staff. Not in the edition: REC-0468 covers looting of the Itombwe referral hospital in March 2025; REC-0546/0627 and REC-0534 cover 2026 hospital events at Mikenge.
r7-E-FIZ-017.vn: Exact excerpt; translation faithful; the statement keeps the outlet's hedges. Partisan community outlet; the account rests on 'information from those areas'. The page places Mikenke in Itombwe sector, Mwenga territory, and says the receiving area (Gipupu, Mibunda) is held by Wazalendo, FDLR and FARDC with Burundian forces (the outlet's account).
src: Uyu munsi ku wa kane tariki ya 22/05/2025, amakuru ava muri ibyo bice avuga ko kwaribwo habaye kwimura icyicaro gikuru cy’ibi bitaro bya Mikenke, aho cyimurirwa mu Gipupu hatari mu ntera ndende uvuye aha n’ubundi byahoraga. Icyatumye haba kwimura iki cyicyaro cy’ibi bitaro ntikizwi neza, ariko mubyo ubuyobozi bwasobanuye bavuga ko ari impamvu z’umutekano.

r7-E-FIZ-018.s: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to sources at Lusenda camp, the police commissioner in charge of the camp, Masumbuko Lutombo, personally directs recruitment operations aimed mainly at young Burundian refugees, to integrate them into the Wazalendo armed groups.
r7-E-FIZ-018.l: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-018.a: Masumbuko Lutombo, police commissioner of the camp (as alleged by refugees and sources quoted by RPA); recruiting for Wazalendo groups
r7-E-FIZ-018.n: Single Burundian radio source (RPA, French text on a site that also carries Kirundi bulletins); unnamed sources; allegation not confirmed by the Congolese police or UNHCR on the page. The page says recruitment began after humanitarian organisations suspended food assistance. Earlier 2025 reports of refugee recruitment are in REC-0169.
r7-E-FIZ-018.vn: Exact excerpt; the attribution to sources is kept. Page dated 25 July 2026. Allegation from unnamed sources; no response from the Congolese police or UNHCR on the page. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
src: Selon des sources à Lusenda, le commissaire de police en charge du camp, Masumbuko Lutombo, dirige personnellement les opérations de recrutement visant principalement les jeunes réfugiés burundais, afin de les intégrer aux groupes armés Wazalendo.

r7-E-FIZ-019.s: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that at Lusenda in South Kivu the sick had had no access to medicines for six months; it said IDAV, a partner of the UN refugee agency (HCR), indicated that stocks of medicines were at Kalemie and being forwarded.
r7-E-FIZ-019.l: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-019.x: RPA: six months without medicines at Lusenda
r7-E-FIZ-019.n: Single Burundian radio source quoting refugees; no UNHCR statement on the page. The cause is described as a long supply gap, not an attack. Complements the Fizi territory health-supply records (REC-0171, REC-0203).
r7-E-FIZ-019.vn: 'UNHCR' replaced by the source's 'HCR'. The source says 'À Lusenda', not 'at Lusenda camp', so the wording follows the excerpt. Both excerpts exact. Page dated 23 March 2026. The page says UNHCR's DRC office, when contacted, promised to respond soon. It describes a supply gap, not an attack.
src: À Lusenda, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, cela fait déjà six mois que les malades n’ont plus accès aux médicaments.
L’organisation IDAV, partenaire du Haut-Commissariat des Nations unies pour les réfugiés (HCR), a indiqué que des stocks de médicaments se trouvent à Kalemie et sont en cours d’acheminement.

r7-E-FIZ-020.s: Radio Publique Africaine (RPA, Burundi) reported that, according to a source among the refugees at Lusenda camp, some women were engaging in prostitution to feed their children amid famine in the camp.
r7-E-FIZ-020.l: Lusenda refugee camp, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-020.n: Reported by RPA from an unnamed refugee source; recorded as survival-related sexual exploitation context, not as an allegation of rape or of a named perpetrator. The same page says some boys join armed groups (Wazalendo) and girls marry early. Date is the page date.
r7-E-FIZ-020.vn: Exact excerpt; the famine context is in the title and the page. Survival-related sexual exploitation context from one unnamed refugee source; not an allegation of rape. Page dated 18 July 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Certaines femmes se livrent à la prostitution pour pouvoir nourrir leurs enfants, déplore une source parmi les réfugiés.
La crise alimentaire entraîne également la dislocation de plusieurs familles.

r7-E-FIZ-021.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Twirwaneho spokesperson Kamasa Ndakize Welcome announced on 5 August 2025 that attacks by FDLR, FARDC and another group, Mai Mai Ngomanzito, began at Irumba and Rugezi in the south of Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho confirmed Burundian forces took no part in that day's attacks.
r7-E-FIZ-021.l: Irumba and Rugezi, south of Minembwe, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-E-FIZ-021.a: FDLR, FARDC and Mai Mai Ngomanzito (as alleged by Twirwaneho); Burundian forces said by Twirwaneho not to have taken part that day
r7-E-FIZ-021.n: Partisan (Twirwaneho) statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet in Kinyarwanda. Differs from REC-0188 (MRDP-Twirwaneho communique of 6 August alleging FARDC, FDLR and the Burundian army attacked Kipupu, Bilalo Mbili, Lulenge and Mikenge): here Twirwaneho says Burundian forces were not involved in the 5 August attacks at Irumba and Rugezi. The two statements concern different villages and days and are not reconciled by the source. The page also relays a Twirwaneho claim made the previous week that FDLR fighters were being trained in Burundi; not recorded here.
r7-E-FIZ-021.vn: Both excerpts exact on the retained copy (the live site refuses the fetch, HTTP 406); translations faithful. Byline Isimbi Estella, 6 August 2025. Partisan statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the quoted statement calls FDLR 'abajenosideri' and the war 'intambara ya jenoside', which is Twirwaneho's wording. It differs from REC-0188 (6 August communique naming the Burundian army), which concerns other villages; the source does not reconcile them.
src: Umuvugizi wa Twirwaneho, Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, ku wa 5 Kanama 2025 yatangaje ko ibitero bya FDLR, FARDC n’undi mutwe wa Mai Mai Ngomanzito, byatangiriye muri Irumba na Rugezi mu majyepfo ya Minembwe.
Twirwaneho yemeje ko Ingabo z’u Burundi zitagize uruhare mu bitero by’uwo munsi, isaba ko ziva burundu mu mugambi wo kurimbura Abanyamulenge kandi zikawuvamo ku mugaragaro.

r7-E-GOMA-001.s: Bwiza reported, citing 'various reports' coming from Goma, that the drone attack launched on Goma by the forces of the DRC government was aimed at, among others, former president Joseph Kabila Kabange; it said the attack of 11 March struck the mainly residential Himbi area near Lake Kivu, where residents said they heard two explosions at dawn.
r7-E-GOMA-001.a: Forces of the DRC government, as Bwiza states
r7-E-GOMA-001.x: Bwiza: two explosions heard by residents; no casualty figure in the excerpts
r7-E-GOMA-001.n: Corroborates REC-0874 (Himbi drone strike) from a Kinyarwanda-language Rwandan outlet (partisan on contested facts); the target (Kabila) is the outlet's account of 'various reports', not independently confirmed. The article also gives a chronology that the DRC government received information on 10 March that Kabila was in the area.
r7-E-GOMA-001.vn: Both excerpts are exact. Removed 'Wednesday' (only in the page sentence 'kuri uyu wa Gatatu tariki ya 11 Werurwe', outside the excerpt: excerpt gap). Page date Wednesday 11 March 2026 checked (weekday correct). Same page also gives a toll of three including Karine Buisset ('Kugeza ubu abantu batatu barimo Umufaransakazi Karine Buisset wakoreraga UNICEF ni bo byamenyekanye ko biciwe muri kiriya gitero'), which matches claim 31 (Umuryango.rw) but both are Rwandan outlets; see claim 31 discrepancy note. Bwiza's 'Amakuru atandukanye ... aremeza' = 'various reports ... affirm' — the outlet presents it as confirmed; statement keeps it attributed. Rwandan outlet; the target (Kabila, and per the same page Makenga, Nangaa and Bisimwa, all with 'bivugwa' = it is said) is Bwiza's account of unnamed reports, not established. Bwiza dates the strike to Wednesday 11 March at about 'saa kumi n'igice' (Kinyarwanda clock, about 04:30) and says the DRC government had made no statement.
src: igitero cya drone ingabo za Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo zagabye mu mujyi wa Goma, cyari kigambiriye abarimo Joseph Kabila Kabange wahoze ari Perezida wa kiriya gihugu.

tariki ya 11 Werurwe, ni bwo i Goma hagabwe igitero cya drone. Ni igitero cyagabwe mu gace kiganjemo ingo z'abaturage ka Himbi, hafi y'ikiyaga cya Kivu. Abatuye muri aka gace bavuga ko mu rucyerera bumvise iturika inshuro ebyiri

r7-E-GOMA-002.s: Umuryango.rw reported that on Thursday 7 May Congolese government forces launched a drone attack at Muja in Nyiragongo territory, where AFC/M23 soldiers were, that the explosion was heard in Goma city, and that, in the outlet's words, no one was killed or injured.
r7-E-GOMA-002.a: Forces of the DRC government (FARDC), per Umuryango.rw; targeted AFC/M23 soldiers
r7-E-GOMA-002.x: Umuryango.rw: no one killed or wounded
r7-E-GOMA-002.n: Rwandan outlet, not independently sourced; no FARDC account found in this round. Date: page is dated Friday 8 May 2026 and says Thursday 7 May. 'Mu ma saa saba' in Kinyarwanda clock = about 13:00. Not in known_records (nearest are REC-0888 and REC-0889 on 24 May 2026).
r7-E-GOMA-002.vn: Excerpts exact. Page dated Friday 08 May 2026; Thursday 7 May 2026 checked (weekday correct). 'Mu ma saa saba y'igicamunsi' = about 1 p.m., translation correct. Wire-style credit to Bwiza set as originating source. Umuryango.rw credits the story to Bwiza ('Src: Bwiza' at the foot of the page; excerpt gap). Both are Rwandan outlets. The same page relays Lawrence Kanyuka (on X) that a government drone strike the same Thursday at Kalenga, Masisi, killed civilians: a lead, not a claim here.
src: Ingabo za Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ku wa Kane tariki ya 7 Gicurasi zagabye igitero cya drone mu bice bya Muja ho muri Teritwari ya Nyiragongo, ahari abasirikare ba AFC/M23. Mu ma saa saba y’igicamunsi cyo ku wa Kane ni bwo icyo gitero cyabaye, ndetse urusaku rw’igisasu yarashe rwumvikanye mu mujyi wa Goma.
Iyo drone yaturutse mu bice bya Rugari yari igambiriye kurasa ku basirikare ba AFC/M23 bari ku burinzi, gusa ku bw’amahirwe ntawe yigeze yica cyangwa ngo imukomeretse.

r7-E-GOMA-003.s: BBC Gahuza reported, citing members of Rutshuru civil society, that heavy fighting on Saturday and Sunday between M23 and Wazalendo fighters at Nyanzale (Rutshuru territory) left civilians dead and others fleeing; civil society member Kambele said he had learned of at least three civilians dead near Nyanzale, and BBC wrote that Congolese media reported that a child was among those who died in the Sunday evening fighting.
r7-E-GOMA-003.l: Nyanzale and Kiyeye, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r7-E-GOMA-003.a: M23 and Wazalendo, as BBC Gahuza names them
r7-E-GOMA-003.x: BBC Gahuza: Kambele, named by BBC Gahuza as of Rutshuru civil society, knew of at least three civilians dead near Nyanzale and said the numbers of dead and displaced were not known; Congolese media said a child was among the dead
r7-E-GOMA-003.n: New: no known record covers Nyanzale/Kiyeye fighting on 21-22 June 2025 (BBC page dated 23 June 2025 gives Saturday and Sunday; dates computed from weekdays and publication date). Same page says M23 had made no statement; CMC statement condemning M23 bombardment of Nyarubande, Burambo, Muhanga, Kihondo-centre and Kiyeye on Saturday, relayed from Radio Okapi (originating source Radio Okapi for that part).
r7-E-GOMA-003.vn: Excerpts exact and support every clause; deaths stay attributed to civil society and Congolese media. BBC is a credible non-partisan origin: B. Page dated 23 June 2025 (Monday): Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 June 2025, computed. The page names the speaker 'Emile Kambele'. Same page: fighting began on Saturday at Kiyeye (Wazalendo-held); Radio Okapi relayed a CMC statement condemning M23 shelling of Nyarubande, Burambo, Muhanga, Kihondo-centre and Kiyeye; M23 had made no statement.
src: Imirwano 'ikomeye' ku wa gatandatu no ku cyumweru yashyamiranyije inyeshyamba za M23 n'abarwanyi ba Wazalendo muri teritwari ya Rutsuru mu gace ka Nyanzale mu ntara ya Kivu ya Ruguru ituma hari abasivile bahasiga ubuzima abandi barahunga, nk'uko abo muri sosiyete sivile ya Rutshuru babivuga.

Kambele yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango ko batazi neza imibare y'abantu bapfuye n'abavuye mu byabo bahunga iyi mirwano, gusa ko we yamenye "nibura abasivile batatu bapfuye" hafi ya Nyanzale. Ibinyamakuru muri DR Congo bivuga ko mu bapfuye kubera imirwano yo ku cyumweru nimugoroba harimo umwana.

r7-E-GOMA-004.s: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said the new Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, is 'a lie' with 'no foundation'; in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka it said the HRW and UN allegations are politically motivated, and that HRW deliberately avoided mentioning armed groups it says work with Kinshasa, including FDLR, Nyatura, PARECO and Wazalendo.
r7-E-GOMA-004.x: HRW (as relayed by BBC Gahuza): at least 140 civilians killed, mostly Hutu
r7-E-GOMA-004.n: Counterclaim to REC-0345 (Binza killings, HRW report of 20 Aug 2025). The M23 statement is dated by BBC to 7 August in an earlier communiqué plus this reaction; BBC page published 21 Aug 2025. Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said.
r7-E-GOMA-004.vn: All four excerpts exact (byline Didier Bikorimana, 21 Aug 2025). Grade B for the fact of the statement as reported by BBC. Partisan statement, cited only as what AFC/M23 said. Same page: M23 had already denied the allegations in a document of 7 August 2025; Rwanda told BBC Newshour 'RDF nta ho ihuriye' (RDF has nothing to do with it); DRC FM Thérèse Kayikwamba also responded. Counterclaim to the Binza killings (REC-0345).
src: Umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa AFC/M23 urwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo uvuga ko raporo nshya y'umuryango uharanira uburenganzira bwa muntu Human Rights Watch (HRW) iwushinja gukora itsembatsemba ku basivile biganjemo Abahutu, ari "ikinyoma" kandi ko '"nta shingiro" ifite.
Raporo ya HRW yatangajwe ku wa gatatu ishinja inyeshyamba za M23 kwica abasivile nibura 140 biganjemo Abahutu
Itangazo rya M23, ryasohowe n'umuvugizi wayo Lawrence Kanyuka, rivuga ko ibi birego bya HRW na ONU bishingiye ku mpamvu za politike

M23 ivuga ko muri raporo yayo HRW yirinze "ku bushake" kuvuga indi mitwe yitwaje intwaro ikorera mu gace ka parike y'igihugu ya Virunga, ivuga ko ikorana na leta ya Kinshasa, irimo FDLR, Nyatura, PARECO na Wazalendo.

r7-E-GOMA-005.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that a report prepared by the Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) of the UN human rights office said all parties failed to protect civilians adequately during the fighting, in particular when M23 and RDF took the city of Goma at the end of January 2025, and during attacks on schools and hospitals.
r7-E-GOMA-005.l: Goma, North Kivu (and attacks on schools and hospitals, place not specified)
r7-E-GOMA-005.a: M23 and RDF (capture of Goma); the report says all parties failed to protect civilians
r7-E-GOMA-005.n: Independent Swahili-language UN News relay of the OHCHR FFM report (5 Sept 2025). The excerpt does not say which hospitals or which party attacked them; it is a general statement. Cited to add a Swahili UN origin for the Goma hospital incidents (REC-0256, REC-0289), not to attribute them.
r7-E-GOMA-005.vn: Removed the release date '5 September 2025', which no excerpt prints (page: 'iliyotolewa Ijumaa tarehe 5 Septemba 2025', outside the excerpts: excerpt gap). 'pande zote' = 'all parties' (statement said 'the parties'). UN fact-finding report: A. General finding: the excerpt names no hospital and no party responsible for the attacks on schools and hospitals. Do not use it to attribute the Goma hospital incidents (REC-0256, REC-0289). 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 4)
src: Inaweka wazi jinsi pande zote zilivyoshindwa kulinda raia ipasavyo wakati wa mapigano, hasa wakati M23 na RDF walipochukua mji wa Goma mwishoni mwa mwezi Januari mwaka huu wa 2025, na pia wakati wa mashambulizi dhidi ya shule na hospitali.
Ripoti hii imeandaliwa na Ujumbe wa Kutafuta Ukweli (FFM) wa Ofisi ya Haki za Binadamu ya Umoja wa Mataifa, kwa agizo la Baraza la Haki za Binadamu la Umoja wa Mataifa.

r7-E-GOMA-006.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN human rights office Fact-Finding Mission (FFM) report said M23 members committed sexual violence, mainly gang rape, and other forms of sexual violence including sexual slavery; women and girls were mainly targeted, but men, boys and people UN News Kiswahili calls 'watu wa jinsia moja' (literally 'people of the same sex') were also victims, including in detention.
r7-E-GOMA-006.l: M23-controlled areas of North Kivu and South Kivu
r7-E-GOMA-006.a: M23 members, as the OHCHR FFM report is relayed by UN News
r7-E-GOMA-006.n: Swahili UN News relay of OHCHR FFM report; place not stated in excerpt beyond 'M23-controlled' areas covered by the report. Wording of the last category in the Swahili ('watu wa jinsia moja') is translated literally.
r7-E-GOMA-006.vn: Excerpt exact. The draft's 'people of diverse sexual characteristics' was an interpretation, not a translation; narrowed to the Swahili wording. No place in the excerpt beyond the report's scope. The Swahili 'watu wa jinsia moja' literally means 'people of the same sex'; it probably renders the report's reference to sexual and gender minorities, but the English wording should be checked against the FFM report itself. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 5)
src: Pia, wanachama wa M23 walifanya ukatili wa kijinsia, hasa ubakaji wa makundi, na aina nyingine za ukatili wa kijinsia, ikiwemo utumwa wa ngono. Wanawake na wasichana walilengwa zaidi, lakini wanaume, wavulana na watu wa jinsia moja pia walikuwa wahanga, ikiwemo wakiwa kizuizini.
Ripoti hii imeandaliwa na Ujumbe wa Kutafuta Ukweli (FFM) wa Ofisi ya Haki za Binadamu ya Umoja wa Mataifa, kwa agizo la Baraza la Haki za Binadamu la Umoja wa Mataifa.

r7-E-GOMA-007.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that the OHCHR Fact-Finding Mission found a pattern of widespread sexual violence, especially rape and gang rape of women and girls, and looting by FARDC and Wazalendo members as they withdrew from the front line in January and February.
r7-E-GOMA-007.l: North Kivu and South Kivu front-line withdrawal areas (not specified in the excerpt)
r7-E-GOMA-007.a: FARDC and Wazalendo members, per OHCHR FFM report as relayed
r7-E-GOMA-007.n: Relates to REC-0253 (looting by retreating FARDC/Wazalendo at Goma) but the excerpt does not name Goma; verifier should confirm whether the same events.
r7-E-GOMA-007.vn: Excerpt exact and matches the statement. UN fact-finding report: A. The excerpt names no place; do not merge with REC-0253 (looting at Goma) without a source placing these acts at Goma. The page adds a quote that perpetrators acted 'in large groups and in many places at the same time'. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 6)
src: FFM imebaini mfumo wa matumizi yaliyoenea ya ukatili wa kijinsia, hasa ubakaji na ubakaji wa makundi dhidi ya wanawake na wasichana, na uporaji uliofanywa na wanachama wa FARDC na Wazalendo walipokuwa wakirudi kutoka mstari wa mbele mnamo mwezi Januari na Februari.
Ripoti hii imeandaliwa na Ujumbe wa Kutafuta Ukweli (FFM) wa Ofisi ya Haki za Binadamu ya Umoja wa Mataifa, kwa agizo la Baraza la Haki za Binadamu la Umoja wa Mataifa.

r7-E-GOMA-008.s: Umuryango.rw reported that in the night of 21 to 22 July 2025 Wazalendo fighters, suspected to have come from Virunga Park, attacked the Mugunga area and Rusayo groupement, that gunfire was heard for about three hours, and that AFC/M23 pushed the Wazalendo fighters back.
r7-E-GOMA-008.l: Mugunga and Rusayo groupement, west of Goma, North Kivu
r7-E-GOMA-008.a: Wazalendo fighters (attackers) and AFC/M23 (defenders), per Umuryango.rw
r7-E-GOMA-008.x: Umuryango.rw: gunfire lasted about three hours; no casualty figure in the excerpts
r7-E-GOMA-008.n: New event: no known record for an attack on Mugunga/Rusayo in July 2025 (nearest REC-0299 of 11 April 2025 and Group of Experts annex for 11-12 April). Rwandan outlet (page intro places the attack west of Goma) relaying AFC/M23 account; no FARDC/Wazalendo statement found yet. Same story carried by igihe.com and umusarenews.com (not retrievable/used).
r7-E-GOMA-008.vn: Excerpts exact (byline ISIMBI Estella, Wednesday 23 Jul 2025). 'bikekwa' kept as 'suspected'. Source type corrected to partisan Rwandan outlet; C. Rwandan outlet giving the AFC/M23 side; no Wazalendo or FARDC account. The page says residents of Ndosho and Kyeshero heard the gunfire and places the attack west of Goma.
src: Mu ijoro ryo ku wa 21 rishyira uwa 22 Nyakanga 2025, abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bikekwa ko baturutse muri Pariki ya Virunga bagabye igitero mu gace ka Mugunga ndetse no muri gurupoma ya Rusayo.
Muri iryo joro humvikanye urusaku rw’amasasu rwamaze amasaha agera kuri atatu, ubwo AFC/M23 yashakishaga abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bashakaga guhungabanya umutekano wa Goma.
ariko muri iryo joro AFC/M23 yashoboye gusubiza inyuma abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bose.

r7-E-GOMA-009.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Manzi Willy, whom it described as the governor of North Kivu appointed by AFC/M23, said on 22 July that their fighters continue to destroy everything that could disturb the security of Goma, and that when AFC/M23 took Goma the opposing forces had hidden guns, ammunition and bombs among the population, which the alliance uncovers day by day.
r7-E-GOMA-009.n: The page names the AFC/M23 governor as 'Manzi Willy'; other sources in this edition name the de facto governor differently (e.g. Bahati Musanga Erasto, REC-0880 area) so the name is as printed by Umuryango.rw and may be an error; flag for verifier.
r7-E-GOMA-009.vn: Excerpts exact. Narrowed the title to the outlet's description and translated 'ribitahura' as 'uncovers'. Year 2025 from the page date (Wednesday 23 Jul 2025). DISCREPANCY: Umuryango.rw (22 July 2025) calls Manzi Willy the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu, while Umuryango.rw itself (claim 13 of this unit, 9 April 2026) and other edition records name Bahati Musanga Erasto as that governor. The title may be an outlet error; the name and title are recorded as printed.
src: Guverineri w’intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’iri huriro, Manzi Willy, tariki ya 22 Nyakanga yatangaje ko abarwanyi babo bakomeje gusenya ibintu byose bishobora guhungabanya umutekano w’uyu mujyi.
Manzi yasobanuye ko ubwo AFC/M23 yafataga Goma, ingabo byari bihanganye zahishe mu baturage imbunda, amasasu, amabombe n’ibindi bishobora kwica, kandi ko umunsi ku wundi iri huriro ribitahura.

r7-E-GOMA-010.s: Bwiza reported that residents of Buramba village (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory) continue to complain of insecurity caused by Wazalendo and FDLR rebels who harass them, and that, it is said, those often harassed are accused of working with AFC/M23; citing Kivu Morning Post, it said these armed rebels also attack users of the Kiwanja-Ishasha road at places such as Katoro, near Katwiguru, and Cabafu, where the latest attack took place on Sunday 8 March 2026.
r7-E-GOMA-010.l: Buramba (Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom) and Kiwanja-Ishasha road (Katoro, near Katwiguru; Cabafu), Rutshuru territory
r7-E-GOMA-010.a: Wazalendo and FDLR fighters, as Bwiza reports
r7-E-GOMA-010.x: No casualty figures in the excerpts
r7-E-GOMA-010.n: New: no known record for Buramba/Cabafu harassment (REC-0875 is a different incident on the Kanyabayonga-Kiwanja road on 18 March 2026). Bwiza is Rwandan and says it takes the road-attack information from Kivu Morning Post (second excerpt); that those targeted are accused of working with AFC/M23 is Bwiza's unattributed 'biravugwa' (it is said). Date is the latest attack date given; the harassment is ongoing.
r7-E-GOMA-010.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date ('10 March 2026'), which no excerpt prints; the hedge 'Biravugwa' had been dropped in the draft statement and is restored. Page dated Tuesday 10 March 2026; Sunday 8 March 2026 checked (weekday correct). Rwandan outlet; the road attacks are credited to Kivu Morning Post. 'Biravugwa' (it is said) kept as a hedge. The page also quotes an unnamed resident on looting and abductions by armed Wazalendo and FDLR (excerpt gap: 'by’umwihariko gusahura no gushimuta bikorwa n’abantu bitwaje intwaro ba wazalendo na FDLR').
src: Abatuye mu Mudugudu wa Buramba, muri Gurupoma ya Binza, Sheferi ya Bwisha, muri Teritwari ya Rutshuru, bakomeje gutaka bivovotera umutekano mucye uterwa n’inyeshyamba za wazalendo na FDLR zikomeje kubahohotera. Biravugwa ko abahohoterwa kenshi bashinjwa gukorana na AFC/M23.

Hejuru yo gucengera mu baturage mu masaha y’ijoro nk’uko tubikesha Kivu Morning Post, izi nyeshyamba zitwaje intwaro zinatera abakoresha umuhanda Kiwanja-Ishasha, nk’ahitwa Katoro, hafi ya Katwiguru, ndetse n’ahitwa Cabafu, aho igitero giheruka cyabaye ku Cyumweru, itariki 8 Werurwe 2026.

r7-E-GOMA-011.s: Bwiza, relaying Radio Okapi, reported that heavy fighting took place all morning on Monday 12 January between AFC/M23 fighters and CMC Wazalendo in many villages of Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru territory, that no toll had been announced, and that the fighting started at Bumbasha, a few kilometres from Mweso, before spreading to Karambi and Chahemba, sending hundreds of residents fleeing to nearby villages and to Mweso centre.
r7-E-GOMA-011.l: Bumbasha, Karambi, Chahemba (Bukombo groupement, Rutshuru), near Mweso
r7-E-GOMA-011.x: Bwiza (relaying Radio Okapi): no toll announced; hundreds of residents fled
r7-E-GOMA-011.n: Kinyarwanda relay of Radio Okapi (originating source Radio Okapi); existing records REC-0862/REC-0865 are Radio Okapi-based, so this is a language relay, not an independent origin.
r7-E-GOMA-011.vn: Excerpts exact; Bwiza credits Radio Okapi ('dukesha iyi nkuru'). Page dated Tuesday 13 January 2026; Monday 12 January 2026 checked. Grade rests on the Radio Okapi origin, which corroborates existing records. Kinyarwanda relay of Radio Okapi; not independent of the Radio Okapi-based records (REC-0862, REC-0865). The page adds that the displaced sheltered in churches and schools.
src: Imirwano ikaze yabaye mu gitondo cyose cyo kuwa Mbere, itariki ya 12 Mutarama, hagati y’abarwanyi ba AFC / M23 n’inyeshyamba za Wazalendo zo mu mutwe wa CMC mu midugudu myinshi yo muri Gurupoma ya Bukombo muri Teritwari ya Rutshuru (Kivu y'Amajyaruguru). Nta mibare y'abiciwe muri iyi mirwano yatangajwe.

Amakuru aturuka muri ako gace agera kuri Radio Okapi, dukesha iyi nkuru, avuga ko imirwano yatangiriye i Bumbasha, ku birometero bike uvuye i Mweso, mbere yo gukwira Karambi na Chahemba. Aya makuru avuga ko imirwano yatumye abaturage babarirwa mu magana bahungira mu midugudu baturanye ndetse no muri centre ya Mweso

r7-E-GOMA-012.s: Umunota reported that heavy fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and Wazalendo fighters of the Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC) took place from dawn on Monday, mainly at Munguli in Kihondo groupement and at Kikuro in Tongo groupement, according to information from the area.
r7-E-GOMA-012.l: Munguli (Kihondo groupement) and Kikuro (Tongo groupement), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r7-E-GOMA-012.x: No casualty figure in the excerpts
r7-E-GOMA-012.n: New: no known record for fighting in Bwito on 28-30 June 2025. The page gives no byline or agency credit; the wording ('information from the area') suggests relayed local reporting, probably Radio Okapi, but the page does not say so. Monday is 30 June per the page ('ku wa 30 Kamena'). Umunota is a Rwandan outlet.
r7-E-GOMA-012.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed '1 July 2025', '30 June' and 'Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory', which the excerpt does not print (all are on the page outside it). Date 30 June 2025 is from the page sentence outside the excerpt ('ubwo Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo yizihizaga isabukuru y’imyaka 65 imaze ibonye ubwigenge ku wa 30 Kamena', Bwito chiefdom): excerpt gap. Page dated 1 July 2025; 30 June 2025 was a Monday. Rwandan outlet with no byline or credit; the page adds that gunfire was heard from 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' (about 6 a.m.).
ent: Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC)
src: Iyi mirwano ikomeye yabaye kuva mu museke wo ku wa mbere, hagati y’abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 n’abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bo muri Collectif des mouvements pour le changement (CMC). Amakuru aturuka muri ako gace avuga ko iyi mirwano yabereye cyane cyane i Munguli, muri Gurupoma ya Kihondo, no muri Kikuro, muri Gurupoma ya Tongo.

r7-E-GOMA-013.s: Umunota reported that on Saturday and Sunday heavy fighting took place at Birambizo and Karambi in Bukombo groupement and in Kihondo groupement, that according to information from the area it made hundreds of residents flee their homes, and that on Sunday at least six houses were burned in Karambi town and its surroundings.
r7-E-GOMA-013.l: Birambizo and Karambi (Bukombo groupement) and Kihondo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory
r7-E-GOMA-013.a: not attributed by the source (the same article describes fighting between AFC/M23 and CMC Wazalendo)
r7-E-GOMA-013.x: Umunota: at least six houses burned in Karambi and surroundings on Sunday; hundreds of residents fled
r7-E-GOMA-013.n: Date computed from weekdays and publication date (Saturday 28 June, Sunday 29 June 2025). No perpetrator named for the burning.
r7-E-GOMA-013.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '1 July 2025', which the excerpt does not print. No perpetrator named for the burning. Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 June 2025 computed from the page date (1 July 2025) and its reference to Monday 30 June.
src: Ku wa gatandatu no ku Cyumweru, uduce twa Birambizo na Karambi, muri Gurupoma ya Bukombo, no muri Gurupoma ya Kihondo, niho habaye imirwano ikaze. Nk’uko amakuru aturuka muri ako gace abitangaza, iyi mirwano yatumye abaturage babarirwa mu magana bahunga ingo zabo. Ku cyumweru, byibuze amazu atandatu yatwitse mu mujyi wa Karambi no mu turere tuyikikije.

r7-E-GOMA-014.s: Umuryango.rw reported that an announcement of 9 April 2026 by the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré mayor of Goma in place of Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who was made head of Lubero territory, and named Nshimiyimana Juvénal, formerly in charge of mobilisation and recruitment of new fighters in AFC/M23, deputy mayor of Goma.
r7-E-GOMA-014.n: Corroborates REC-0881 and Kivu Morning Post claims r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009/010; Umuryango.rw dates the announcement 9 April 2026 whereas those claims date it 8 April: one-day discrepancy for the verifier. Rwandan outlet; appointments are AFC/M23 de facto acts.
r7-E-GOMA-014.vn: Excerpts exact (page dated Thursday 09 Apr 2026). Corroborates REC-0881 with the date discrepancy above. DISCREPANCY: Umuryango.rw dates the announcement 9 April 2026; Kivu Morning Post claims r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009/010 (REC-0881) date it 8 April 2026. The page also spells the new mayor 'Kasuba Ngabo' in a photo caption and names Katembo Isevisya and Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy burgomasters.
src: Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Bahati Musanga Erasto, yahinduye ubuyobozi bw’Umujyi wa Goma. Itangazo ryo ku wa 9 Mata 2026 rigaragaza ko Kisuba Ngabo Désiré yagizwe Meya wa Goma, asimbuye Julien Katembo Ndalieni wagizwe Umuyobozi wa teritwari ya Lubero.
Nshimiyimana Juvénal wari Umuyobozi ushinzwe ubukangurambaga no gushaka abarwanyi bashya muri AFC/M23 yagizwe Visi Meya w’Umujyi wa Goma.

r7-E-GOMA-015.s: Umuryango.rw reported that on 11 May CADECO, a bank opened by AFC/M23 after the Congolese government closed banks in the areas the group controls, opened two counters in Goma at a ceremony led by the AFC/M23 deputy governor of North Kivu for economy and finance, Shadrack Amani.
r7-E-GOMA-015.n: New de facto governance item (no CADECO record in the edition). Date: the article is dated 13 May 2026 and says '11 Gicurasi' (11 May), year taken from the page date. Rwandan outlet reporting the AFC/M23 account; the article's first sentence (bank opened last year) is not in the excerpt.
r7-E-GOMA-015.vn: Excerpts exact and support the statement. Rwandan outlet: C. Year 2026 from the page date (Wednesday 13 May 2026). The page also names the board chair Kabasha Amani and director general Javan Dusabe Sangano, and says branches were planned in Rutshuru, Masisi and Minova centres (lead).
src: Banki ya CADECO yafunguwe na AFC/M23 nyuma y’uko Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo yari imaze gufunga amabanki yo mu bice uriya mutwe ugenzura, yatangiye gutanga Serivisi z’imari ku batuye mu mujyi wa Goma.
Ku wa 11 Gicurasi ni bwo CADECO yafunguye ‘guichets’ ebyiri mu mujyi wa Goma, mu muhango wayobowe na Visi-Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru ushinzwe ubukungu n’imari, Shadrack Amani.

r7-E-GOMA-016.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that OCHA had reported that armed men raided at least two hospitals in Goma, the capital of North Kivu, and abducted several patients.
r7-E-GOMA-016.l: At least two hospitals in Goma, North Kivu
r7-E-GOMA-016.a: Armed men (watu wenye silaha), as OCHA is quoted
r7-E-GOMA-016.x: OCHA via UN News: at least two hospitals raided; 'several' patients abducted
r7-E-GOMA-016.n: Swahili UN News relay of an OCHA report; corroborates the raids on Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho hospitals (REC-0286) without naming them. Date computed from 'Monday this week' (page published Tuesday 4 March 2025): Monday 3 March 2025; the raids themselves were earlier. The page text carries typographic artefacts in places but not in the excerpt.
r7-E-GOMA-016.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed '4 March 2025' and 'Monday of that week', which the excerpt does not print. Single UN agency report relayed, not an investigation: B rather than A. Source language is Swahili, not Kinyarwanda. OCHA's report is dated by the page to 'Jumatatu wiki hii' (Monday this week), i.e. Monday 3 March 2025 for a page dated Tuesday 4 March 2025 (excerpt gap); the raids themselves were earlier. Hospitals are not named; likely the Heal Africa and CBCA Ndosho raids (REC-0286) but the excerpt does not say so.
src: OCHA iliripoti kuwa watu wenye silaha walivamia angalau hospitali mbili katika mji mkuu wa Kivu Kaskazini, Goma, na kuwateka nyara wagonjwa kadhaa.

r7-E-GOMA-017.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that on Sunday 8 February 2026 AFC-M23 presented 7,532 new commandos who had finished military training at Tchanzu (Rutshuru, North Kivu), a ceremony it described as marking a new stage in the structure of the ARC (Jeshi la Mapinduzi la Kongo), the armed wing of the movement led by General Sultani Makenga.
r7-E-GOMA-017.l: Tchanzu training centre, Rutshuru, North Kivu
r7-E-GOMA-017.a: AFC-M23 / Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC), under General Sultani Makenga, per SOS Médias Burundi
r7-E-GOMA-017.n: New: same site as REC-0312 (Tchanzu graduation of 1 Oct 2025) but a different cohort and date; no record of the 8 Feb 2026 ceremony. Burundian independent outlet; the figure is AFC-M23's own presentation as relayed; SOS Médias Burundi gives no named original source. Whether the trainees were volunteers or conscripts is not addressed in the excerpts.
r7-E-GOMA-017.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the dateline 'from Goma on 10 February 2026', which no excerpt prints. Kept ARC wording as printed. Source language is Swahili, not Kinyarwanda. The figure of 7,532 is AFC-M23's presentation as relayed; no independent count. The page has the dateline 'Goma, Februari 10, 2026' and is dated 12 February 2026. Whether 'inayoongozwa na' (led by) qualifies the movement or its armed wing is ambiguous in the Swahili. Different cohort from REC-0312 (Tchanzu, 1 Oct 2025). 8 February 2026 was a Sunday (checked).
src: Jumapili, Februari 8, 2026, Muungano wa Mto Congo-M23 (AFC-M23), muungano wa waasi unaoendelea mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo (DRC), uliwasilisha makomandoo wapya 7,532 ambao walikuwa wamemaliza mafunzo yao ya kijeshi huko Tchanzu (Wilaya ya Rutshuru, Kivu Kaskazini).
Sherehe hii inaashiria hatua mpya katika muundo wa Jeshi la Mapinduzi la Kongo (ARC), mrengo wenye silaha wa harakati inayoongozwa na Jenerali Sultani Makenga.

r7-E-GOMA-018.s: SOS Médias Burundi quoted Major General Sultani Makenga, AFC-M23 military coordinator, as saying to the new troops: 'From today you have become soldiers of the ARC, an army that emerged to liberate the people, our country is run by incompetent people living in Kinshasa'.
r7-E-GOMA-018.n: Partisan statement cited only for what Makenga is reported to have said; the date of the speech is the ceremony date of 8 February 2026 given in the same article.
r7-E-GOMA-018.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed 'at Tchanzu on 8 February 2026' from the statement because this source's excerpt does not print it; date field kept from the article. Partisan speech cited only as what Makenga said. Speech at the Tchanzu graduation ceremony; the date (Sunday 8 February 2026) and place are in another sentence of the same article, not in this excerpt (excerpt gap: 'Jumapili, Februari 8, 2026, ... huko Tchanzu (Wilaya ya Rutshuru, Kivu Kaskazini)'). 'wazembe' can also be rendered 'negligent' or 'lazy'.
src: “Kuanzia leo mmekuwa askari wa ARC, jeshi lililojitokeza kuwakomboa wananchi, nchi yetu inaendeshwa na watu wazembe wanaoishi Kinshasa,” alisema Meja Jenerali Sultani Makenga, Mratibu wa Kijeshi wa AFC-M23.

r7-E-GOMA-019.s: DW Kiswahili reported that by the end of May hundreds of men were sitting on black volcanic gravel in the streets of Murambi, north of Goma, guarded by M23 fighters; that some Goma residents said people were arrested for minor reasons such as wearing dirty clothes or not shaving, many being gathered in a sports ground then turned into an open prison; and that those not cleared by evidence considered credible were taken to private places of detention.
r7-E-GOMA-019.l: Murambi (north of Goma) and a sports ground used as an open prison, Goma
r7-E-GOMA-019.a: M23 fighters, as DW Kiswahili states
r7-E-GOMA-019.x: DW Kiswahili: 'hundreds of men' at Murambi
r7-E-GOMA-019.n: DW Kiswahili one-year-on feature (byline Sylivanus Karemera); it quotes AFP once for an unrelated resident account and may draw on AFP and NGO reporting more widely, but does not credit an agency for these passages. 'End of May' is taken as 2025 from the article's chronology; the stadium is not named in the Swahili ('uwanja wa michezo'); REC-0292 identifies Stade de l'Unité for March 2025, so treat the link as tentative.
r7-E-GOMA-019.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '27 January 2026', which no excerpt prints. Source language is Swahili. DW feature (byline Sylivanus Karemera, 27 January 2026) that quotes AFP for one resident; parts may draw on AFP without credit. 'May' is placed in 2025 by the article's chronology (capture in January 2025, Uvira offensive in December). The sports ground is unnamed; REC-0292 (Stade de l'Unité, March 2025) may be the same site but the month differs: tentative link only.
src: Kufikia mwishoni mwa mwezi Mei, mamia ya wanaume walikuwa wameketi kwenye changarawe nyeusi ya volkano katika mitaa ya Murambi, kaskazini mwa Goma, wakilindwa na wapiganaji wa M23.

Baadhi ya wakazi mji wa Goma walisema watu wengine walikamatwa kwa sababu ndogo tu kama vile, kuvaa nguo chafu au kutonyoa ndevu, wengi walikusanywa paamoja katika uwanja wa michezo ambao wakati huo uligeuzwa gereza la wazi.
Wale ambao hawakuthibitishwa na ushahidi uliochukuliwa kuwa wa kuaminika walipelekwa katika vizuizi vya faragha.

r7-E-GOMA-020.s: DW Kiswahili reported that Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said residents of Goma continue to face suffering.
r7-E-GOMA-020.n: Only a paraphrase of Muyaya's remark with no date or channel; kept as a statement lead. Partisan: cited only for what the spokesperson said.
r7-E-GOMA-020.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. Undated paraphrase with no channel given, in a feature dated 27 January 2026; a statement lead only.
src: Msemaji wa serikali ya Kongo Patrick Muyaya alisema wakaazi wa Goma wanaendelea kukabiliwa na mateso.

r7-E-GOMA-021.s: DW Kiswahili reported that civilians and former government fighters were forcibly registered, and that M23 announced it had gained 7,000 new members by September.
r7-E-GOMA-021.x: DW Kiswahili: M23 said 7,000 new members by September
r7-E-GOMA-021.n: Brief line in a feature without attribution beyond M23's own announcement of the figure; the place of the forced registration is implied by the article (Goma) rather than stated in the sentence.
r7-E-GOMA-021.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date and 'in Goma', which the sentence does not state. The sentence names no place; the article is about Goma. September is 2025 by the article's chronology. The 7,000 figure is M23's; compare the 7,532 commandos AFC-M23 presented at Tchanzu on 8 February 2026 (claim 16), a different date and count.
src: Raia na wapiganaji wa zamani wa serikali walisajiliwa kwa nguvu. M23 ilitangaza kuwa ilikuwa imewapata wanachama wapya 7,000 kufikia mwezi Septemba.

r7-E-GOMA-022.s: DW Kiswahili reported that in October the group began appointing its own magistrates, but that observers said the rebels' court system was not fair.
r7-E-GOMA-022.n: Date 'October' as in the article's chronology (year 2025 implied); REC-1195 records the integration of 378 magistrates on 3 November 2025, so the dates differ in month. The unnamed 'observers' are not identified.
r7-E-GOMA-022.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. DISCREPANCY (month): DW places the start of M23 magistrate appointments in October (2025 by the article's chronology), while REC-1195 records the integration of 378 magistrates on 3 November 2025. The observers are not named.
src: Mnamo Oktoba, kundi hilo lilianza kuteua mahakimu wake, lakini wadadisi walisema mfumo wa mahakama za waasi hao haukuwa na haki.

r7-E-GOMA-023.s: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 said the more than 2,500 people who died in the recent fighting in Goma were government soldiers (FARDC) and Wazalendo; that Bertrand Bisimwa, one of the leaders of M23, said no family in Goma was in mourning because of those dead; and that he said the bodies removed from the streets and buried were those of FARDC soldiers and their collaborators, including Wazalendo, FDLR, European mercenaries and Burundian forces, who died in battle.
r7-E-GOMA-023.x: M23 (via BBC Gahuza): more than 2,500 dead, said to be FARDC and Wazalendo
r7-E-GOMA-023.n: Counterclaim to the casualty accounts for the fight for Goma (REC-0250 and Kinshasa's account). BBC notes that it is hard to know the truth of what the state side and Rwanda/M23 say about the dead. Partisan statement cited only for what M23 said.
r7-E-GOMA-023.vn: Excerpts exact (page 5 Feb 2025). Removed the publication date; 'M23 leader' narrowed to 'one of M23's leaders' (umwe mu bakuru); the figures field dropped the UN and Muyaya figures, which are not in this claim's excerpts (they belong to claims 23 and 25). Partisan statement cited only as what M23 said. BBC writes that neither OCHA nor the Red Cross confirm whether the bodies buried were civilians or soldiers. DISCREPANCY within M23's own accounts: more than 2,500 dead said to be FARDC/Wazalendo here (5 Feb 2025) vs Kanyuka's M23 report that only 874 fighters died in the fight for Goma (claim 24, 3 June 2025); compare OCHA/UN figures (claim 23) and Muyaya's (claim 25).
src: Umutwe wa M23 watangaje ko abantu bapfuye mu mirwano iheruka i Goma barenga 2,500 ari abasirikare ba leta (FARDC) na Wazalendo.
Bertrand Bisimwa umwe mu bakuru b'umutwe wa M23 yatangaje ko "nta muryango w'i Goma uri mu kiriyo kubera aba bapfuye".

Yavuze ko imirambo yahoze mu mihanda i Goma, yahavanywe igahambwa ari "iy'abasirikare ba FARDC n'abakorana na bo", yavuzemo Wazalendo, FDLR, abacanshuro b'i Burayi n'ingabo z'u Burundi, yemeza ko baguye ku rugamba.

r7-E-GOMA-024.s: BBC Gahuza reported that the UN humanitarian office OCHA-RDC said at least 2,000 bodies had already been buried and about 900 others were in the morgues of various hospitals in Goma, and that the UN said on Monday that at least 900 people had been killed and more than 2,800 wounded in the fighting, with hospitals still struggling to treat all the wounded.
r7-E-GOMA-024.x: OCHA-RDC (via BBC Gahuza): at least 2,000 bodies buried, about 900 in hospital morgues; UN: at least 900 killed and more than 2,800 wounded
r7-E-GOMA-024.n: Figures per source, not merged: BBC notes that neither the UN nor the Red Cross confirm whether the bodies buried were civilians or soldiers. 'Monday' is 3 February 2025 by the page date (computed).
r7-E-GOMA-024.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date, which no excerpt prints. Figures per source, not merged; the 900 in morgues (OCHA-RDC) and the 900 killed (UN) are separate figures. BBC adds that neither the UN office nor the Red Cross confirm whether the dead were civilians or soldiers. 'Monday' = 3 February 2025 (page dated 5 February 2025).
src: Ishami rya ONU rishinzwe ubutabazi, OCHA-RDC, rivuga ko imirambo nibura 2,000 yamaze guhambwa kandi ko indi igera kuri 900 iri mu buruhukiro bw'ibitaro bitandukanye i Goma.
ONU ku wa mbere yatangaje ko abantu nibura 900 bishwe naho abarenga 2,800 barakomeretse kubera iyo mirwano, kandi ko ibitaro bikigowe no kubasha kuvura izo nkomere zose.

r7-E-GOMA-025.s: BBC Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replying on X to the Human Rights Watch report, said that report and the recent Amnesty International report are 'propaganda tools working for the Kinshasa authorities', and cited a report published by M23 the previous week saying that only 874 fighters died in the fighting to take Goma.
r7-E-GOMA-025.x: Kanyuka (via BBC Gahuza): only 874 fighters died in the fighting to take Goma, per an M23 report
r7-E-GOMA-025.n: Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said; the X post itself was not fetched (BBC relays it).
r7-E-GOMA-025.vn: Excerpts exact (page 3 June 2025). Removed the publication date; figures field dropped the HRW figure, which is not in this claim's excerpts. Partisan statement cited only as what M23 said; the X post itself was not retained. DISCREPANCY with claim 22: M23 said in February 2025 that more than 2,500 dead were FARDC/Wazalendo. HRW told BBC it had asked Kanyuka about its findings and received no reply.
src: Mu gusubiza ku birego biri muri raporo ya HRW umuvugizi wa M23 Lawrence Kanyuka yanditse ubutumwa kuri X avuga ko iyo raporo, hamwe n'iya Amnesty International iheruka gusohoka, ari "ibikoresho by'icengezamatwara bikorera ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa".
Kanyuka yatangaje kandi raporo yasohowe na M23 mu cyumweru gishize ivuga ko mu mirwano yo gufata umujyi wa Goma hapfuye abantu 874 b'abarwanyi gusa.

r7-E-GOMA-026.s: BBC Gahuza reported that Patrick Muyaya, spokesperson of the Kinshasa government, had recently said that more than 2,000 bodies were still in the streets of Goma needing burial, and that he accused Rwandan forces and M23 of killing civilians in the recent fighting in Goma and its surroundings.
r7-E-GOMA-026.x: Muyaya (via BBC Gahuza): more than 2,000 bodies in the streets
r7-E-GOMA-026.n: Government account, partisan on attribution; BBC gives no date for Muyaya's remark (before 5 Feb 2025).
r7-E-GOMA-026.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date, which the excerpt does not print. Government account; BBC gives no date for Muyaya's remark (before 5 February 2025).
src: Patrick Muyaya, umuvugizi wa leta ya Kinshasa aheruka gutangaza ko imirambo irenga 2,000 ikiri mu mihanda i Goma ikeneye guhambwa. Yashinje ingabo z' Rwanda na M23 ubwicanyi ku basivile mu mirwano iheruka i Goma no mu nkengero zayo.

r7-E-GOMA-027.s: BBC Gahuza reported that a Human Rights Watch report said M23 killed at least 21 civilians in Goma in February whose deaths it could confirm, with evidence of many more; that on 22 February at least three pickup trucks carrying M23 fighters went to different parts of Goma and the fighters killed seven people in Katindo, with 11 more bodies including a boy found later near a construction site; that the next day the fighters rounded people up to force them into M23 and killed three who tried to escape; and that three health workers told HRW more than 50 bodies were removed from the Kasika area between 22 and 23 February.
r7-E-GOMA-027.l: Katindo and other Goma neighbourhoods (Camp Katindo, Avenue du Commandant Belge, Avenue Kasika, Avenue Mulongwe)
r7-E-GOMA-027.a: M23 fighters, per Human Rights Watch
r7-E-GOMA-027.x: HRW (via BBC Gahuza): at least 21 civilians confirmed killed; 7 at Katindo plus 11 bodies found later (including a boy); 3 killed trying to escape; three health workers told HRW over 50 bodies were removed from Kasika between 22 and 23 February
r7-E-GOMA-027.n: Kinyarwanda relay of the HRW report of 3 June 2025 (originating source HRW). Corroborates the UN Group of Experts claims on the Katindo killings of 22 February 2025 (r2-G-DOC-446-018/019).
r7-E-GOMA-027.vn: All four excerpts exact. Removed the publication date; added the Kasika clause from source 3, which the draft cited but did not state. Kept B: a relay of an NGO investigation through a single outlet. Relay of the HRW report of 3 June 2025. 'Seven' and 'three' are printed in the Kinyarwanda excerpts as words (barindwi, eshatu, batatu). The page lists Camp Katindo, Avenue du Commandant Belge, Avenue Kasika and Avenue Mulongwe among the sites. Corroborates the Group of Experts claims on the Katindo killings of 22 February 2025 (r2-G-DOC-446-018/019).
src: Umutwe wa M23 wishe abasivile nibura 21 i Goma mu kwezi kwa Gashyantare(2), nk'uko bivugwa na raporo ya Human Rights Watch (HRW) yasohotse uyu munsi, ivuga ko abo ari abo wemeza neza, ko hari ibimenyetso ko hari n'abandi benshi bishwe.

Raporo ya HRW ivuga ko tariki 22 Gashyantare (2) nibura imodoka eshatu za 'pickup' zirimo abarwanyi ba M23 zagiye mu bice bitandukanye bya Goma, abarwanyi bazirimo bakica abantu barindwi mu gace ka Katindo, ko nyuma habonetse indi mirambo 11 irimo umwana w'umuhungu hafi y'ahantu harimo kubakwa.
Iyi raporo ivuga ko ku munsi wakurikiyeho, aba barwanyi bakusanyije abantu "bagamije kubinjiza ku ngufu" muri M23, maze bakica batatu bagerageje gucika.
HRW ivuga ko abakozi batatu bo kwa muganga bayibwiye ko hari imirambo irenga 50 yakuwe mu gace ka Kasika hagati ya tariki 22 na 23 Gashyantare

r7-E-GOMA-028.s: BBC Gahuza reported that displacement camps on the outskirts of Goma, which had held hundreds of thousands of people, were bare ground after M23 fighters took the city; an independent journalist in Goma who visited the Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara camps said almost all the tents were down; it was not clearly known whether the remaining displaced people had gone home voluntarily or by force; and Dany Kalume of Goma civil society said many had returned to areas of Rutshuru and Masisi controlled by M23 and that M23 had provided vehicles the previous week to take back those remaining in some of the camps.
r7-E-GOMA-028.l: Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara displacement camps, outskirts of Goma
r7-E-GOMA-028.a: M23, as BBC Gahuza and the civil society source describe
r7-E-GOMA-028.x: BBC Gahuza: camps 'used to hold hundreds of thousands' of people (excerpt)
r7-E-GOMA-028.n: Corroborates REC-0282 (forced dismantling of IDP camps around Goma, January and February 2025) with a Kinyarwanda BBC source that explicitly says it is unclear whether the returns were voluntary. The figures of 300,000-400,000 are from aid groups cited in the same article (not excerpted).
r7-E-GOMA-028.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date '3 February 2025', which no excerpt prints; added Kalume's Rutshuru/Masisi returns, which his excerpt states. BBC states it is unclear whether returns were voluntary or forced; do not present this as forced return. Aid groups cited on the page put the pre-fighting population of Kanyaruchinya and Lushagara at 300,000-400,000 (outside the excerpts).
src: Inkambi z'impunzi zari ziri ku nkengero z'umujyi wa Goma zahoze zirimo abantu ibihumbi amagana ubu ni imbuga gusa nyuma y'ifatwa ry'uyu mujyi wigaruriwe n'abarwanyi ba M23.
Umwe mu banyamakuru wigenga ukorera i Goma wasuye inkambi za Kanyaruchinya na Lushagara yabwiye BBC ko yasanze amahema hafi yose muri izi nkambi ari hasi.
Ntibizwi neza niba impunzi zari zisigaye muri izi nkambi zaratashye ku bushake cyangwa ku gahato.

Dany Kalume, umwe mu bagize sosiyete sivile ya Goma yabwiye BBC ko benshi mu bari batuye muri izi nkambi basubiye mu ngo zabo mu duce twa Rutshuru na Masisi tugenzurwa na M23, ko mu cyumweru gishize M23 yatanze imodoka zo gucyura abari basigaye muri zimwe muri izo nkambi.

r7-E-GOMA-029.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that the UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, Mary Lawlor, said she had received credible reports of human rights defenders held incommunicado, forcibly disappeared and tortured in Rutshuru and Masisi, North Kivu, and that about six defenders were reported to have disappeared after trying to flee Goma after the city was taken by M23.
r7-E-GOMA-029.a: not attributed in this passage (the report concerns M23-controlled areas)
r7-E-GOMA-029.x: Lawlor (via UN News): about six defenders reported disappeared after trying to flee Goma
r7-E-GOMA-029.n: Swahili UN News relay of a Geneva statement by the UN Special Rapporteur (OHCHR special procedures). The passage does not say who held or tortured the defenders. Names of defenders are not given.
r7-E-GOMA-029.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date. A Special Rapporteur's statement on reports received is not a documented investigation: B rather than A. The passage does not say who held, disappeared or tortured the defenders. Statement given in Geneva; page dated 5 March 2025.
src: Mtaalamu huyo amesema amepokea ripoti za kuaminika za watetezi wa haki za binadamu kushikiliwa bila mawasiliano, kutoweshwa kwa nguvu, na kuteswa huko Rutshuru na Masisi, Kivu Kaskazini, huku takribani watetezi sita wa haki za binadamu wakiripotiwa kutoweka baada ya kujaribu kutoroka Goma baada ya jiji hilo kuchukuliwa na M23.
anayehusika na hali ya watetezi wa haki za binadamu, Mary Lawlor leo ametoa wito wa msaada wa dharura na wa vitendo kwa watetezi wa haki za binadamu katika eneo hilo.

r7-E-GOMA-030.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that Mary Lawlor, UN Special Rapporteur on human rights defenders, said a defender had recently told her that M23 rebels had drawn up a list of human rights defenders to be arrested in the areas they controlled.
r7-E-GOMA-030.a: M23, as alleged by a defender quoted by the Special Rapporteur
r7-E-GOMA-030.n: Single-source allegation relayed by the Special Rapporteur from an unnamed defender; not a finding. Cited as an allegation only. M23 response not found in this round.
r7-E-GOMA-030.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the publication date. The underlying allegation rests on one anonymous source: C. An allegation from one unnamed defender, relayed by the Special Rapporteur; not a finding. No M23 response found.
src: amesema Lawlor na kuongeza kuwa watu hao wanaishi kwa hofu na hatari ni halisi na kwama hivi karibuni, mtetezi mmoja alimpa taarifa kuwa waasi wa M23 wameandaa orodha ya watetezi wa haki za binadamu watakaokamatwa katika maeneo waliyoyadhibiti.
anayehusika na hali ya watetezi wa haki za binadamu, Mary Lawlor leo ametoa wito wa msaada wa dharura na wa vitendo kwa watetezi wa haki za binadamu katika eneo hilo.

r7-E-GOMA-031.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa told residents of Goma that, a year after the city's administration was installed, everything was now in order, that the war in the city was completely over, and that what remained was to continue development and to liberate all of Congo.
r7-E-GOMA-031.n: Partisan statement cited only for what Nangaa is reported to have said, by a Rwandan outlet. Date: 'Friday 06 Feb 2026' as printed by the page.
r7-E-GOMA-031.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed 'on Friday 6 February 2026', which no excerpt prints. Date from the page sentence outside the excerpts: 'Corneille Nangaa yabitangaje kuri uyu wa Gatanu tariki 06 Gashyantare 2026' (Friday 6 February 2026, weekday correct): excerpt gap. Partisan statement by a Rwandan outlet.
src: Umuhuzabikorwa w’Ihuriro AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa yabwiye abaturage bo mu Mujyi wa Goma ko nyuma y’umwaka hashyizweho ubuyobozi bw’uyu mujyi, ubu ibintu byose byamaze kujya ku murongo igisigaye ari ugukomeza urugendo rw’iterambere ndetse no kubohora Congo yose.
Muri iki kiganiro, Nangaa yagiranye n’abaturage b’i Goma, yababwiye ko intambara muri uyu Mujyi yarangiye burundu

r7-E-GOMA-032.s: Umuryango.rw reported that in the early morning of 11 March drones of the DRC army fired on residents' homes in the Himbi area, killing three civilians including the Frenchwoman Karine Buisset, who worked for UNICEF.
r7-E-GOMA-032.a: DRC army (ingabo za RDC), as Umuryango.rw states
r7-E-GOMA-032.x: Umuryango.rw: three civilians killed, including UNICEF worker Karine Buisset
r7-E-GOMA-032.n: Corroborates REC-0874 and Group of Experts/UN News claims (r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/004, r1-GOE-026) on the death of UNICEF staff member Karine Buisset. The toll of three civilians is Umuryango.rw's (a Rwandan outlet aligned with the AFC/M23 account) and is not in the other claims I saw; treat as a single-source figure. The excerpt's 'Mu masaa kumi y’urukerera' follows the Kinyarwanda clock (about 04:00), not 10:00; the translation is literal.
r7-E-GOMA-032.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the publication date '12 March 2026', which the excerpt does not print. Translation corrected: 'saa kumi' in Kinyarwanda time is about 4 a.m., not 'ten'. DISCREPANCY: the toll of three civilians (Umuryango.rw; also Bwiza, claim 0 page) is not in the existing records on this strike (REC-0874; r1-ATR-NK-2026-003/004; r1-GOE-026). Both are Rwandan outlets and the attribution to DRC army drones is theirs. Time: about 04:00 (Umuryango.rw) / about 04:30 (Bwiza), not 10:00. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-GOMA claim 31)
src: Mu masaa kumi y’urukerera rwo ku wa 11 Werurwe, drones z’ingabo za RDC zarashe ingo z’abaturage mu gace ka Himbi, zica abasivili batatu barimo Umufaransakazi wakoreraga ishami ry’Umuryango w’Abibumbye ryita ku bana (UNICEF), Karine Buisset.

r7-E-GOMA-033.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 condemned the attack and said it was not right for the international community to keep silent while the DRC government deliberately violates the ceasefire agreement signed in Doha, Qatar.
r7-E-GOMA-033.n: Partisan statement cited only for what AFC/M23 said; the page does not give the channel or the signatory.
r7-E-GOMA-033.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed '12 March 2026' and '11 March drone attack on Goma', which the excerpt does not print. 'The attack' is the 11 March 2026 drone strike on Himbi, Goma (previous sentence of the page, outside the excerpt). The page gives no date, channel or signatory for the AFC/M23 condemnation; reported 12 March 2026.
src: AFC/M23 yamaganye iki gitero, igaragaza ko bidakwiye ko umuryango mpuzamahanga ukomeza guceceka mu gihe Leta ya RDC irenga nkana ku masezerano y’agahenge yasinyiwe i Doha muri Qatar.

r7-E-GOMA-034.s: Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 12 March 2026 many Goma residents gathered in a protest against the drone attack launched on the city by the forces of the DRC, asking AFC/M23 to liberate the whole country, after an invitation from civil society, and that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the protesters asked AFC/M23 to remove Félix Tshisekedi's government throughout the DRC.
r7-E-GOMA-034.a: Goma residents (protesters), as Umuryango.rw describes; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
r7-E-GOMA-034.n: Rwandan outlet; the protest is described as called after an invitation from civil society (not in the excerpts). Whether the gathering was spontaneous or organised is not established; the page says it followed an invitation from civil society. Kanyuka's remark is partisan.
r7-E-GOMA-034.vn: Excerpts exact. Corrected 'Felix' to 'Félix' as printed; added the civil-society invitation from the page (excerpt gap) because it bears on whether the protest was organised. Excerpt gap: the civil-society invitation is in the page sentence 'Nyuma yo kwakira ubutumire bwa sosiyete sivile, mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 12 Werurwe abaturage benshi b’i Goma bahagaritse ibikorwa byabo', not in the stored excerpt. Whether attendance was voluntary is not established; a protest in an AFC/M23-held city reported by a Rwandan outlet and relayed by the AFC/M23 spokesperson. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 12 Werurwe 2026, abaturage benshi batuye i Goma bahuriye mu myigaragambyo yamagana igitero cya drones ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo zagabye muri uyu mujyi, basaba ihuriro AFC/M23 kubohora iki gihugu cyose.
Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko abigaragambya basabye “AFC/M23 gukura ubutegetsi bwa Félix Tshisekedi muri RDC yose”
Nyuma yo kwakira ubutumire bwa sosiyete sivile, mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 12 Werurwe abaturage benshi b’i Goma bahagaritse ibikorwa byabo

r7-E-GOMA-035.s: Umuryango.rw reported that on the morning of 22 December 2025 residents of Goma and neighbouring areas took part in a protest against AFC/M23's withdrawal from the city of Uvira, and that AFC/M23 fighters had left Uvira on 17 and 18 December after about a week there.
r7-E-GOMA-035.n: Goma-side political event related to the Uvira withdrawal (Uvira is another unit's area). Rwandan outlet; whether the protest was organised is not stated in the excerpts.
r7-E-GOMA-035.vn: Excerpts exact (page dated Monday 22 Dec 2025). Statement matches. Rwandan outlet. The page quotes a placard rejecting the return of FARDC, Wazalendo, Burundian forces and mercenaries to Uvira, and says AFC/M23 withdrew at the request of the United States; relevant to the Uvira unit.
src: Abatuye mu mujyi wa Goma no mu bice bihana imbibi mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo babyukiye mu myigaragambyo yamagana kuva mu mujyi wa Uvira kw’abarwanyi b’ihuriro AFC/M23. Iyi myigaragambyo yabaye mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 22 Ukuboza 2025.
Tariki ya 17 n’iya 18 Ukuboza, abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bavuye mu mujyi wa Uvira bari bamazemo icyumweru.

r7-E-IGIHE-001.s: Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said, in reaction to a Human Rights Watch report, that 'the RDF is not AFC/M23' and that any proper investigation requires impartiality, access to where events happen, solid evidence, respect for the law and not announcing conclusions in advance or putting calls for sanctions first, according to Igihe.
r7-E-IGIHE-001.l: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
r7-E-IGIHE-001.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet relaying its own government's statement; Rwanda's position that it has no forces in eastern DRC conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings (e.g. over 8,000 RDF troops, see existing claims r1-UC-RDF-010). The HRW report concerned is the 10 June 2026 report (78 pages per Igihe). Igihe p01 says the message was posted 'this Thursday' (11 June 2026); p02 (12 June) says posted on X.
r7-E-IGIHE-001.vn: Both Igihe pages print the quote; translation checked (accurate). Capitalised-word flag is the Rwanda/u Rwanda rendering; no correction needed. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. Rwanda's denial of RDF involvement conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings recorded elsewhere. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Yakomeje yibutsa uyu muryango ko ntaho ingabo z’u Rwanda zihuriye na AFC/M23. Ati “Bikwiriye gusobanuka neza, RDF ntabwo ari AFC/M23. Iperereza ryose rikozwe neza risaba kutabogama, kugera aho ibintu bibera, ibimenyetso simusiga, kubahiriza amategeko ndetse no kudatangaza imyanzuro mbere y’igihe, cyangwa ngo ushyire imbere gusaba ibihano.”

“It should be clear that the RDF is not AFC/M23,” Makolo said. “Any serious investigation requires impartiality, access, forensic rigour, due process, and not conclusions announced in advance, or bombastic calls for sanctions.”
Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda, Yolande Makolo, yanenze raporo iherutse gushyirwa hanze n’Umuryango Human Rights Watch

r7-E-IGIHE-002.s: Igihe reported that Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X, dismissed the Human Rights Watch report as part of a 30-year pattern of anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, and 'sanctions first and investigation later'.
r7-E-IGIHE-002.l: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
r7-E-IGIHE-002.n: Same statement as E-IGIHE-a-001; Makolo's own words are the quoted English text in p02; p01 paraphrases.
r7-E-IGIHE-002.vn: Quote verbatim in p02; p01 paraphrases the same; translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: In a statement posted on X, Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo dismissed the report as part of a long-standing pattern in HRW's reporting on Rwanda. “Human Rights Watch on Rwanda is a 30-year pattern: anonymous claims, no site visits or forensics, sanctions first and investigation later,” Makolo wrote.

Yagaragaje ko kuva mu myaka 30 ishize uyu muryango waranzwe n’imyitwarire ihora yisubiramo iyo bigeze ku Rwanda irimo kudatangaza imyirondoro y’abo ikesha amakuru, kutigerera ahabera ibyo uvuga, kutagira ibimenyetso simusiga ndetse no gushyira imbere ibihano.

r7-E-IGIHE-003.s: According to Igihe, Makolo said that HRW itself had stated that Kinshasa arms, supports and works closely with the FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army, which she said made HRW unable to take on an impartial investigation.
r7-E-IGIHE-003.l: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
r7-E-IGIHE-003.n: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. The Kinyarwanda phrase 'izingiyeho intambara n'akaga ku kiremwamuntu' is translated closely but is awkward in the original. Existing claims record UN/HRW findings on FARDC cooperation with FDLR and Wazalendo separately.
r7-E-IGIHE-003.vn: Quote printed in p01; p02 paraphrases the same list. Translation adequate; "izingiyeho intambara n’akaga ku kiremwamuntu" rendered loosely but not in the statement. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 2)
src: Ati “Muri raporo yayo iheruka, HRW ntabwo ishobora gufata inshingano (zo gukora iperereza ritabogamye) mu gihe yirengagiza bimwe mu byo yitangarije: Kinshasa iha intwaro, igatera inkunga ndetse igakorana bya hafi na FDLR, Wazalendo, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga n’igisirikare cy’u Burundi, byose bifatwa nk’ingabo cyangwa imitwe yitwaje intwaro izingiyeho intambara n’akaga ku kiremwamuntu mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC.”

r7-E-IGIHE-004.s: Igihe reported that the Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda said that no HRW investigator set foot at the places named in the report, and that there were no visits, no exhumations for investigation and no laboratory tests.
r7-E-IGIHE-004.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
r7-E-IGIHE-004.n: Rwandan government claim about HRW methodology, not a finding. HRW's own methods are described in HRW's report (interviews with 102 former detainees per existing claim r1-SV-2026-031).
r7-E-IGIHE-004.vn: Both pages print it; translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. HRW describes its own methods in its report.
src: Ibiro by’Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma byatangaje ko nta mukozi n’umwe wa HRW wageze aho ibivugwa byabereye. Biti “Nta muntu ushinzwe gukora iperereza wakandagije ikirenge cye ahantu iyi raporo ivuga. Nta kuhasura byigeze bibaho, nta gutaburura imirambo hagamijwe iperereza ndetse nta bizamini by’abahanga byo muri laboratwari byigeze bikorwa.
According to Kigali, no investigators visited the locations where the alleged abuses occurred, no exhumations were conducted and no forensic examinations were undertaken.

r7-E-IGIHE-005.s: According to Kigali, as reported by Igihe, HRW's own report acknowledges that the Congolese army has supported armed groups opposed to M23, including the FDLR.
r7-E-IGIHE-005.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
r7-E-IGIHE-005.n: Rwandan government characterisation of the HRW report; not independently checked against the report. Date is the Igihe article date (12 June 2026).
r7-E-IGIHE-005.vn: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. Rwanda's characterisation of the HRW report; not checked against the report.
src: According to Kigali, HRW's own report acknowledges that the Congolese army has supported armed groups opposed to M23, including the FDLR, a militia formed by perpetrators of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.

r7-E-IGIHE-006.s: Igihe reported that the Rwandan statement cited passages in the HRW report saying that Congolese authorities armed, financed and coordinated operations with Wazalendo militias and that government support for such groups contributed to human rights violations.
r7-E-IGIHE-006.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
r7-E-IGIHE-006.n: Rwandan government characterisation of the HRW report; not checked against the report.
r7-E-IGIHE-006.vn: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: The statement also cited passages in the report saying Congolese authorities armed, financed and coordinated operations with Wazalendo militias and that government support for such groups contributed to human rights violations.

r7-E-IGIHE-007.s: Igihe wrote that the HRW report also states that the Congolese army and those allied with it carried out acts of abuse, killing, rape and unlawful detention in the outskirts of Goma.
r7-E-IGIHE-007.a: Congolese army and its allies (as Igihe summarises HRW)
r7-E-IGIHE-007.n: This is Igihe's own summary of what the 10 June 2026 HRW report says; the incident dates are not stated by Igihe (date given is the report publication date). To be checked against the HRW report itself. Included because it concerns sexual violence alleged against FARDC and allies.
r7-E-IGIHE-007.vn: Verbatim on p01; translation accurate ("guhohotera abantu" = mistreating/abusing people). Grade C: secondhand partisan paraphrase. Igihe's paraphrase of the 10 June 2026 HRW report, placed within its account of the Rwandan government statement (the English edition says the statement "cited passages in the report"). Incident dates not given; check against the HRW report itself.
src: Ikindi uyu muryango ugaragaza ni uko Ingabo za RDC n’abo bafatanyije bakoze ibikorwa byo guhohotera abantu, kwica, gufata ku ngufu no gufunga abantu bitemewe mu nkengero za Goma.

r7-E-IGIHE-008.s: According to Igihe, the Rwandan government said HRW claims to have satellite images showing killings 'carried out by Rwandan forces and M23', with features resembling graves, but that HRW cannot confirm whether they are graves or other objects.
r7-E-IGIHE-008.n: Rwandan government characterisation of the HRW report's use of satellite imagery. Useful lead: HRW satellite imagery of alleged graves.
r7-E-IGIHE-008.vn: p01 carries the full clause; p02 the general point. Translation accurate. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: Guverinoma yagaragaje ko HRW ivuga ko ifite amashusho yafashwe na satellite agaragaza ubwicanyi “bwakozwe n’ingabo z’u Rwanda na M23”, agaragaza ibimeze nk’imva zashyinguwemo abapfuye, ariko ko idashora guhamya niba ari imva koko cyangwa ibindi bintu bijya kumera nka zo.
The statement also criticised HRW for presenting allegations as established facts while acknowledging uncertainty in sections of the report dealing with legal assessments and satellite imagery.

r7-E-IGIHE-009.s: Rwanda's Office of the Government Spokesperson said, according to Igihe, that 'alleged M23 conduct cannot be treated as RDF conduct' and accused HRW of 'selective accountability', saying it focused primarily on Rwanda and M23 and paid insufficient attention to abuses by Congolese government forces and their allies.
r7-E-IGIHE-009.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
