r7-E-IGIHE-009.n: Rwandan government statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-009.vn: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: Rwanda faulted HRW's attempt to treat the RDF and M23 as a single actor. “Alleged M23 conduct cannot be treated as RDF conduct,” the statement said. The government accused HRW of applying “selective accountability” by focusing primarily on Rwanda and M23 while paying insufficient attention to abuses committed by Congolese government forces and their allies.

r7-E-IGIHE-010.s: Igihe reported that a 78-page HRW report published on 10 June alleges that Rwandan military forces and the M23 rebel movement carried out large-scale forced recruitment and abusive detention of captured combatants and civilians in North and South Kivu between mid-2024 and December 2025.
r7-E-IGIHE-010.a: Rwandan military forces and M23 (alleged by HRW, as described by Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-010.n: Igihe's description of the HRW report (corroborates existence and scope of the HRW report already recorded; Igihe is partisan and this is not independent evidence of the underlying facts). HRW period begins mid-2024; only the part from 1 January 2025 falls in the edition window. In p01 Igihe describes the same report as covering deaths, unlawful detention and forced recruitment of civilians.
r7-E-IGIHE-010.vn: Verbatim on p02; the existence of the HRW report is not contested; the allegations remain HRW's. Igihe's description of the HRW report; the alleged period begins mid-2024, only the part from 1 January 2025 is in the edition window.
src: The response follows the publication of a 78-page HRW report on June 10, which alleges that Rwandan military forces and the M23 rebel movement carried out large-scale forced recruitment and abusive detention of captured combatants and civilians in North and South Kivu provinces between mid-2024 and December 2025.

r7-E-IGIHE-011.s: Makolo said, according to Igihe, that the sustainable solution to the conflict is to implement the Washington agreement and impartial mediation aimed at ending the war and promoting regional cooperation; the English edition quotes her as saying the Washington peace accords remain 'the path forward'.
r7-E-IGIHE-011.n: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-011.vn: Both pages print it; translation accurate ("kubahiriza" = respecting/implementing). Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: Makolo yavuze ko umuti urambye kuri iki kibazo ari ukubahiriza amasezerano ya Washington, n’ubuhuza butabogamye, hagamijwe kurangiza intambara no kwimakaza ubufatanye bw’akarere.
Makolo added that the Washington peace accords remain “the path forward” for addressing insecurity in eastern DRC through dialogue, accountability and regional cooperation.

r7-E-IGIHE-012.s: Igihe reported that Rwanda's statement highlighted the FDLR as a key security threat and accused HRW of failing to adequately examine its role and its links to Congolese government forces.
r7-E-IGIHE-012.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
r7-E-IGIHE-012.n: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-012.vn: Verbatim on p02. Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding.
src: On the FDLR, Rwanda highlighted the militia as a key security threat and accused HRW of failing to adequately examine its role and links to Congolese government forces.

r7-E-IGIHE-013.s: Igihe reported that the Rwandan Office of the Government Spokesperson said HRW had not named the Congolese or Wazalendo individuals for whom it was calling for sanctions, and quoted it as saying 'HRW strongly condemns Rwanda and M23, while the support Kinshasa gives to violent armed groups is described in a deceptive/vague way'.
r7-E-IGIHE-013.a: Government of Rwanda (Office of the Government Spokesperson)
r7-E-IGIHE-013.n: The Kinyarwanda 'by’amahushuka' is translated 'in a deceptive way' (literally 'deceptively/with deception'); meaning in context is that the support is described misleadingly or vaguely. Party statement.
r7-E-IGIHE-013.vn: Verbatim on p01. "by’amahushuka" is closer to "superficially/in passing" than "deceptively"; the statement already hedges "deceptive/vague". Rwandan government statement relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned); a party account, not a finding. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 12)
src: Bagaragaza kandi ko uyu muryango nta na hamwe wigeze uvuga amazina y’Abanye-Congo cyangwa abo muri Wazalendo usabira ibihano. Biti “HRW ijora bikomeye u Rwanda na M23, mu gihe ubufasha Kinshasa iha imitwe yitwaje intwaro igira urugomo buvugwaho by’amahushuka.”

r7-E-IGIHE-014.s: Igihe reported that in May 2026 AFC/M23 accused Human Rights Watch of defaming it, publishing falsehoods and ignoring the truth, in response to an HRW report released on 14 May that accuses its fighters of killing civilians in Uvira city, raping women and abducting people between December 2025 and January 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-014.a: AFC/M23 (statement); HRW allegation against AFC/M23 fighters
r7-E-IGIHE-014.n: Placeholder: excerpt anchor corrected below if needed. Igihe gives the HRW report date as 14 May; its article of 14 May (p03) says 13 May. Existing claims r1-SV-2026-008 and r2-G-UV-SVHC-010 record AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka's 15 May reply (via Actualite.cd).
r7-E-IGIHE-014.vn: Both passages verbatim on p01. Translation corrected: the "it works in line with the DRC government" clause refers to HRW. AFC/M23 statement as relayed by Igihe. Igihe dates the HRW report 14 May here; its 14 May article (p03) says 13 May. AFC/M23 reply also recorded via other outlets. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 13)
src: Uretse u Rwanda, muri Gicurasi 2026, Ihuriro AFC/M23 ryashinje Human Rights Watch kuriharabika, gutangaza ibinyoma no kwirengagiza ukuri, mu buryo bushimangira ko ukorera mu murongo w’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo.

Ryatanze ubu butumwa risubiza raporo ya HRW yasohotse ku wa 14 Gicurasi, ishinja abarwanyi baryo kwicira abasivili mu Mujyi wa Uvira, gufata abagore ku ngufu no gushimuta abantu hagati y’Ukuboza 2025 na Mutarama 2026.

r7-E-IGIHE-015.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said the DRC army continues to work with the FDLR, which HRW does not want to address in its reports, and that HRW's bias makes the organisation lose credibility.
r7-E-IGIHE-015.n: Party statement relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-015.vn: Verbatim on p01; translation accurate. AFC/M23 statement as relayed by Igihe (partisan).
src: Iri huriro ryagaragaje ko ingabo za RDC zikomeje gukorana n’umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR washinzwe n’abagize uruhare muri Jenoside yakorewe Abatutsi mu 1994, ariko ko HRW idashaka kubivugaho muri raporo zayo. AFC/M23 yatangaje ko kubogama HRW yagaragaje muri raporo yayo gutuma uyu muryango utakarizwa icyizere mu buryo bukomeye, ibituma ibyo utangaza bidahabwa agaciro.

r7-E-IGIHE-016.s: Igihe reported that Rwandan Government Spokesperson Yolande Makolo said on X on 14 May 2026 that 'HRW has a way of working and Rwanda is always its yardstick showing it has worked well'.
r7-E-IGIHE-016.l: Kigali (statement on X); subject: eastern DRC
r7-E-IGIHE-016.n: Corroborates existing claim r7-L-RW-002 (Umuryango.rw) on the same X post. Igihe is partisan; this is evidence of what Makolo said, not of the facts.
r7-E-IGIHE-016.vn: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Existing list in packet is empty, so the corroboration target could not be checked here. Party statement relayed by Igihe.
src: Ubutumwe bwa Makolo bwanyuze ku rubuga X kuri uyu wa 14 Gicurasi 2026, bugira buti “HRW ifite uburyo ikora kandi u Rwanda ruhora ari igipimo cyayo kigaragaza ko yakoze neza.”

r7-E-IGIHE-017.s: Igihe reported that Makolo was criticising an HRW report released on 13 May that accuses Rwandan forces and M23 fighters of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in Uvira city from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-017.a: Rwandan forces and M23 fighters (alleged by HRW, as described by Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-017.n: Igihe's description of the HRW Uvira report; the report date is 13 May here but 14 May in Igihe's p01 and in other sources (BBC claim r2-G-UV-SVHC-011 dated 14 May). HRW's own findings are recorded in existing claims (e.g. r1-HC-2026-001, r1-HC-2026-003).
r7-E-IGIHE-017.vn: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Igihe's description of the HRW Uvira report. Igihe dates the report 13 May here but 14 May in its 11 June article; discrepancy left as stated.
src: Makolo yanengaga raporo HRW yashyize hanze ku wa 13 Gicurasi, ishinja ingabo z’u Rwanda n’abarwanyi b’umutwe witwaje intwaro wa M23 kwica abasivili, kubashimuta no gufata ku ngufu abagore mu Mujyi wa Uvira, kuva tariki ya 10 Ukuboza 2025 kugeza ku ya 17 Mutarama 2026.

r7-E-IGIHE-018.s: Igihe reported that the Rwandan government has often told the international community that none of its troops are in eastern DRC and that it only put defensive measures on the border.
r7-E-IGIHE-018.n: Rwanda's position as relayed by Igihe. It conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings that RDF troops were deployed in eastern DRC (see existing claims r1-UC-RDF-010, r1-GOE-005). Surfaced as a discrepancy, not resolved.
r7-E-IGIHE-018.vn: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. Rwanda's position as relayed by Igihe; it conflicts with UN Group of Experts findings that RDF troops were deployed in eastern DRC.
src: Ni kenshi Leta y’u Rwanda yagaragarije umuryango mpuzamahanga ko nta ngabo zarwo ziri mu burasirazuba bwa RDC, isobanura ko icyo rwakoze ari ugushyira ingamba z’ubwirinzi ku mupaka kugira ngo ibibazo byo muri iki gihugu cy’abaturanyi bitarugeramo.

r7-E-IGIHE-019.s: Igihe wrote that in January 2025 armed units including the FDLR fired into Rubavu town while fighting M23 in Goma, and that many of the shells fired were neutralised by Rwandan forces.
r7-E-IGIHE-019.a: armed forces including the FDLR (per Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-019.n: Single Rwandan state-aligned source; the attribution to FDLR rather than FARDC or others is Igihe's. Date given only as January 2025.
r7-E-IGIHE-019.vn: "Ibisasu byinshi mu byarashwe" means "many of the shells fired", not "most"; narrowed. Igihe's own narration (Rwandan state-aligned); attribution of the fire to FDLR-including units is Igihe's. Exact dates not given. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 18)
src: Muri Mutarama 2025, imitwe y’ingabo irimo FDLR yarashe mu Mujyi wa Rubavu ubwo yari ihanganiye na M23 mu Mujyi wa Goma. Ibisasu byinshi mu byarashwe byapfubijwe n’ingabo z’u Rwanda

r7-E-IGIHE-020.s: Igihe wrote that HRW explained that those it interviewed included Burundian and DRC officials including soldiers, and argued that this makes the report highly doubtful because they are the ones fighting M23 in areas including Uvira.
r7-E-IGIHE-020.n: The argument is Igihe's, not a party statement; the factual element (HRW interviewed Burundian and Congolese officials including soldiers) should be checked against the HRW report methodology.
r7-E-IGIHE-020.vn: Verbatim on p03; translation accurate. The argument is Igihe's editorial; the factual element should be checked against the HRW report methodology.
src: HRW yasobanuye ko mu bo waganiriye na bo harimo abayobozi bo mu Burundi na RDC barimo n’abasirikare, ibituma raporo yawo ishidikanywaho cyane kubera ko abo ni bo bahanganye n’abarwanyi ba M23 mu bice birimo Uvira.

r7-E-IGIHE-021.s: Igihe reported that the DRC army coalition was accused of shooting at a civilian plane carrying medicines and food to Minembwe commune on the morning of 27 August 2026; MRDP-Twirwaneho officer Colonel Fidèle Rugabo said the plane was hit by a shell from a gun on the ground as it reached the Bikuba area.
r7-E-IGIHE-021.a: DRC army coalition (accused, per Twirwaneho via Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-021.n: Single partisan Rwandan source relaying Twirwaneho. Independent reports (ReelActu, LSi Africa, Kivu Morning Post, 27-28 Aug 2026) confirm a plane was shot down near Minembwe but give conflicting accounts of its cargo and origin: see E-IGIHE-a-023 to 027. LSi puts the site at Bikuba, Fizi territory. No independent confirmation of civilian or military nature (ReelActu). Records for the downing: none found in project data at time of search. A search snippet mentions a similar earlier incident on 30 June (Instagram, unverified lead only).
r7-E-IGIHE-021.vn: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. "Civilian" and "medicines" are the Twirwaneho account as Igihe relays it; statement keeps "was accused". Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
src: Ihuriro ry’ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo ryashinjwe kurasa indege ya gisivili yari ijyanye imiti n’ibiribwa muri Komini Minembwe mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 27 Kanama 2026. Umwe mu bofisiye b’umutwe wa MRDP-Twirwaneho ugenzura Minembwe, Colonel Fidèle Rugabo, yatangaje ko iyi ndege yarashwe n’igisasu cy’imbunda yari ku butaka ubwo yari igeze mu gace ka Bikuba.

r7-E-IGIHE-022.s: Colonel Fidèle Rugabo of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe: 'MRDP strongly condemned the shooting down of a civilian plane that was carrying medicines and food'.
r7-E-IGIHE-022.n: Party statement. ReelActu (27 Aug) separately quotes 'Rugabo Fidèle' accusing the FARDC and calling it a 'provocation'.
r7-E-IGIHE-022.vn: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. Party statement (MRDP-Twirwaneho) relayed by Igihe. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
src: Col Rugabo yagize ati “MRDP yamaganiye kure ihanurwa ry’indege ya gisivili yari itwaye imiti n’ibiribwa.”

r7-E-IGIHE-023.s: ReelActu reported that a plane was shot down on Thursday near the Minembwe aerodrome in the Fizi highlands, during the mission of the expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (MCVE+), and that the circumstances of its destruction and the nature of its cargo were the subject of opposing versions.
r7-E-IGIHE-023.a: not attributed by the source (versions conflict)
r7-E-IGIHE-023.n: Independent Congolese outlet (ReelActu, journalist Ghislain Watongoka, 27 Aug 2026 14:20); corroborates the Igihe account that a plane was shot down. 'Thursday' is 27 August 2026 per the page date.
r7-E-IGIHE-023.vn: Both excerpts verbatim on the retained ReelActu page (byline Ghislain Watongoka, 27 Aug 2026 14:20). Downing also reported by LSi Africa and Kivu Morning Post; grade B kept conservatively. LSi Africa places the hit at Bikuba, about thirty kilometres from the Minembwe aerodrome; ReelActu says near the aerodrome. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
src: Un avion a été abattu jeudi près de l'aérodrome de Minembwe, dans les hauts plateaux du territoire de Fizi (Sud-Kivu). L'incident est survenu alors que la mission du Mécanisme conjoint de vérification élargi (MCVE+), composée d'experts de l'ONU, de la RDC et du Rwanda, poursuit ses opérations de contrôle du cessez-le-feu prévu par les accords de Doha.
Les circonstances de la destruction de l'appareil et la nature de sa cargaison font l'objet de versions opposées.

r7-E-IGIHE-024.s: ReelActu reported that Rugabo Fidèle, a member of the Twirwaneho-M23 coalition, publicly confirmed the destruction of the plane and accused the FARDC of shooting down 'a civil aircraft carrying medicines and food', calling the incident a 'provocation' that came two days after the MCVE+ team left Minembwe.
r7-E-IGIHE-024.n: Party statement as reported by an independent outlet. Note the interval: ReelActu says two days after the MCVE+ team left; LSi Africa says three days after a MCVE+ mission, and Igihe says EJVM+ visited Minembwe on 25 August.
r7-E-IGIHE-024.vn: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Party statement. Interval after the MCVE+ visit differs: two days after the team left (ReelActu), three days after the mission (LSi), the day after (Kivu Morning Post); Igihe dates the EJVM+ visit 25 August.
src: De son côté, Rugabo Fidèle, membre influent de la coalition Twirwaneho-M23, a confirmé publiquement la destruction de l’avion. Dans une déclaration, il accuse les FARDC d’avoir abattu « un avion civil transportant des médicaments et des aliments » et qualifie l’incident de « provocation » intervenue deux jours après le départ de l’équipe du MCVE+ de Minembwe.

r7-E-IGIHE-025.s: ReelActu reported that Congolese security sources maintain the plane was carrying out a resupply mission for rebel positions in the highlands.
r7-E-IGIHE-025.n: Anonymous Congolese security sources, relayed by ReelActu; the opposing account to Twirwaneho's 'civil aircraft carrying medicines'.
r7-E-IGIHE-025.vn: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Anonymous security sources. Accounts of the 27 August 2026 Minembwe plane downing conflict: Twirwaneho/AFC/M23 say a civilian aircraft carrying medicines and food; the Fizi administrator (LSi Africa) says it came from Rwanda carrying soldiers; Congolese security sources (ReelActu) say a rebel resupply flight; no independent confirmation of its nature (ReelActu, LSi).
src: Des sources sécuritaires congolaises soutiennent qu’il effectuait une mission de ravitaillement au profit des positions rebelles dans les hauts plateaux.

r7-E-IGIHE-026.s: ReelActu reported that no independent source had confirmed whether the plane was civil or military, or its exact cargo, and that the Congolese authorities had not yet published a communiqué detailing the circumstances of the operation.
r7-E-IGIHE-026.a: Congolese authorities (no statement found as of the article)
r7-E-IGIHE-026.n: Records the absence of a Kinshasa/FARDC communiqué as of 27 Aug 2026 per ReelActu (see gap party_statements).
r7-E-IGIHE-026.vn: Verbatim on retained ReelActu page. Status as of ReelActu's 27 August 14:20 article.
src: À ce stade, aucune source indépendante n’a confirmé si l’appareil était civil ou militaire, ni le contenu exact de sa cargaison. Les autorités congolaises n’ont pas encore publié de communiqué détaillant les circonstances de l’opération.

r7-E-IGIHE-027.s: LSi Africa reported that Fizi territory administrator Sammy Kalonji Badibanga said the plane came from Rwanda and was carrying soldiers, equipment and food, while sources linked to Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 described it as a civil aircraft linking Bukavu to Minembwe with medicines and equipment on board and two crew members.
r7-E-IGIHE-027.a: Fizi territory administrator (DRC authority) vs Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 sources
r7-E-IGIHE-027.n: Two opposing accounts recorded side by side by an independent outlet. LSi adds that no verifiable element makes it possible to attribute the missile to the Wazalendo, the Burundian forces or another component, and places the hit 'dans la matinée à Bikuba, dans le territoire de Fizi' (page text). Its dateline places the aerodrome distance at about thirty kilometres. Rwanda has not been found commenting on the claim that the plane came from Rwanda.
r7-E-IGIHE-027.vn: Verbatim on retained LSi Africa page. LSi also says no verifiable element allows attribution of the projectile to Wazalendo, Burundian forces or another component. ReelActu spells the administrator "Samy Kalonji".
src: Des sources liées aux Twirwaneho-AFC/M23 présentent l’appareil comme un avion civil reliant Bukavu à Minembwe, avec des médicaments et du matériel à bord. Elles évoquent deux membres d’équipage. L’administrateur du territoire de Fizi, Sammy Kalonji Badibanga, livre une autre version. Il affirme que l’avion venait du Rwanda et transportait des militaires, du matériel ainsi que des vivres.

r7-E-IGIHE-028.s: Kivu Morning Post wrote that a civil plane carrying medicines was shot down near Minembwe on Thursday, and that the Fizi territory administrator 'under the Kinshasa regime' claimed the attack, saying the plane had been shot down by the FARDC.
r7-E-IGIHE-028.n: Kivu Morning Post (28 Aug 2026) wording conflicts with LSi Africa's account of the same administrator's statement (plane came from Rwanda carrying soldiers); the two are not reconciled. KMP's framing 'régime de Kinshasa' and 'revendiqué' is the outlet's own.
r7-E-IGIHE-028.vn: Verbatim on retained KMP page (28 Aug 2026, La Rédaction). Grade C: single outlet, framing aligned with one party. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based and uses AFC/M23 framing ("régime de Kinshasa"); its "civil plane carrying medicines" is unattributed narration. Its account of the administrator conflicts with LSi Africa's; not reconciled.
src: Jeudi, un avion civil transportant des médicaments a été abattu près de Minembwe. Un incident survenu au lendemain d’une mission de vérification du cessez-le-feu. L’administrateur du territoire de Fizi sous le régime de Kinshasa a revendiqué l’attaque, affirmant que l’avion avait été abattu par les FARDC.

r7-E-IGIHE-029.s: Igihe reported that the plane was shot down after the international body in charge of ceasefire monitoring (EJVM+) visited Minembwe on 25 August and assessed the effects of the attacks.
r7-E-IGIHE-029.n: ReelActu says the MCVE+ mission was deployed in Minembwe (Bashimukaku Sud) from 24 August; Igihe says the visit was on 25 August. Different start dates reported.
r7-E-IGIHE-029.vn: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. ReelActu says the MCVE+ mission was deployed in Minembwe (Bashimukaku Sud) from 24 August; Igihe says the visit was on 25 August.
src: Iyi ndege ihanuwe nyuma y’aho ku wa 25 Kanama, urwego mpuzamahanga ruhuriweho rushinzwe kugenzura iyubahirizwa ry’agahenge (EJVM+) rusuye Minembwe, rukagenzura ingaruka z’ibitero byahagabwe.

r7-E-IGIHE-030.s: According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces began attacking Point-Zero, Nyaruhinga and Mukoko in Minembwe at about seven in the morning and that the DRC coalition was using combat drones and heavy weapons.
r7-E-IGIHE-030.a: DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-E-IGIHE-030.n: Party statement relayed by Igihe. Compare Kivu Morning Post of 28 Aug 2026 (existing claim r1-SKS-2026Q3-001) for Kanyuka's later statement.
r7-E-IGIHE-030.vn: Verbatim on p04; "mu masaa moya y'igitondo" = around 7 a.m., correct. AFC/M23 statement relayed by Igihe (27 Aug). Kivu Morning Post quotes a Kanyuka statement on intensified attacks on Point Zéro from 04:00 on 28 August.
src: Umuvugizi w’ihuriro AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, Wazalendo, FDLR n’abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga, byatangiye kugaba ibitero muri Point-Zero, Nyaruhinga na Mukoko muri Minembwe mu masaa moya y’igitondo. Kanyuka yasobanuye ko muri ibi bitero, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC riri kwifashisha drones z’intambara ndetse n’imbunda ziremereye

r7-E-IGIHE-031.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 also accused the DRC government forces of attacks in areas of Walungu territory in South Kivu, including Nzibira, Kishadu and Chulwe, and in Katoyi in Masisi territory.
r7-E-IGIHE-031.a: DRC government forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-E-IGIHE-031.n: Party allegation relayed by Igihe. Existing record REC-1265 covers displacement from Nzibira after fighting in Walungu (20-27 Aug).
r7-E-IGIHE-031.vn: Verbatim on p04; translation accurate. AFC/M23 allegation relayed by Igihe.
src: AFC/M23 kandi yashinje ingabo za Leta ya RDC kugaba ibitero mu bice byo muri Teritwari ya Walungu mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, birimo Nzibira, Kishadu na Chulwe ndetse na Katoyi muri Teritwari ya Masisi.

r7-E-IGIHE-032.s: Igihe, citing the SOS Médias website of the Burundians, reported that the Kamenge military hospital alone was housing 87 wounded Burundian soldiers.
r7-E-IGIHE-032.a: Burundian soldiers wounded in fighting with AFC/M23
r7-E-IGIHE-032.x: 87 wounded Burundian soldiers at Kamenge military hospital (Igihe, citing SOS Médias)
r7-E-IGIHE-032.n: Relays SOS Médias Burundi (original article of 8 Dec 2025 cited in E-IGIHE-a-033). Related earlier claim for Jan 2025: r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-006.
r7-E-IGIHE-032.vn: Statement verbatim-supported on p05; figures field narrowed to the 87 Igihe prints (the "100" came from SOS, not this excerpt). Relay of SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec 2025, recorded separately); not independent of it.
src: Urubuga SOS Medias rw’Abarundi rwatangaje ko mu bitaro bya gisirikare bya Kamenge byonyine, bicumbikiye inkomere 87 z’abasirikare b’u Burundi.

r7-E-IGIHE-033.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, in recent days, more than a hundred wounded had been reported, 87 of them admitted to the Kamenge military hospital, north of Bujumbura, and that Burundian authorities were keeping silent about the real losses.
r7-E-IGIHE-033.a: Burundian soldiers wounded in fighting with M23/AFC
r7-E-IGIHE-033.x: more than a hundred ("plus d’une centaine") wounded reported in recent days; 87 admitted to Kamenge military hospital
r7-E-IGIHE-033.n: Original reporting by SOS Médias Burundi's own reporters at the hospital (independent of Igihe).
r7-E-IGIHE-033.vn: Verbatim on retained SOS page (Adam Ntwari, 8 Dec 2025). Figures field rewritten in the source's words: the page prints "centaine", not "100". SOS Médias Burundi is an exile Burundian outlet critical of the Burundian government; no official Burundian figure was given.
src: Rien que ces derniers jours, plus d’une centaine de blessés ont été signalés, dont 87 admis à l’hôpital militaire de Kamenge, au nord de Bujumbura. Tandis que les autorités burundaises gardent le silence sur les pertes réelles

r7-E-IGIHE-034.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported, quoting a journalist at the Kamenge military hospital, that lack of beds forced some patients to share the same bed and that 'a single bed can accommodate up to three patients' because the two emergency wards were full.
r7-E-IGIHE-034.n: Hospital overcrowding affecting wounded Burundian soldiers in Bujumbura (hospital capacity); patients are military, not civilians, so not recorded as civilian access to health care.
r7-E-IGIHE-034.vn: Verbatim on retained SOS page. Patients are wounded soldiers, not civilians.
src: Le manque de lits oblige certains patients à partager le même couchage : « Les deux salles d’urgence sont pleines. Un seul lit peut accueillir jusqu’à trois patients », rapporte un autre journaliste.

r7-E-IGIHE-035.s: Igihe reported that other wounded had been sent to other hospitals including Tanganyika Care Polyclinic, and that many Bujumbura hospitals were severely overcrowded, with up to three patients on one bed.
r7-E-IGIHE-035.x: up to three patients per bed (Igihe and SOS Médias)
r7-E-IGIHE-035.n: Igihe, partly relaying SOS Médias Burundi (SOS names Tanganyika Care Polyclinic and up to three patients per bed).
r7-E-IGIHE-035.vn: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. SOS Médias (the apparent origin) reports the bed-sharing at Kamenge's two emergency wards only; Igihe generalises it to many Bujumbura hospitals.
src: Izindi nkomere zoherejwe mu bindi bitaro birimo Tanganyika Care Polyclinic. Ibitaro byinshi by’i Bujumbura biracucitse cyane kubera iki kibazo, aho igitanda kiri guhuriraho abarwayi bagera kuri batatu.

r7-E-IGIHE-036.s: Igihe reported, on the basis of unspecified information ('hari amakuru avuga'), that because of defeat the Burundian army leadership had asked its soldiers to return home quickly to avoid losing more lives in the war in the DRC.
r7-E-IGIHE-036.n: Unattributed rumour in a partisan outlet; hedged 'hari amakuru avuga' = 'there is information saying'. Other sources say a large part of Burundian troops withdrew in December 2025 (REC-0231).
r7-E-IGIHE-036.vn: Verbatim on p05; hedge preserved. Hedged in the source ("hari amakuru avuga" = there is information saying); unattributed.
src: Hari amakuru avuga ko kubera gutsindwa, ubuyobozi bw’igisirikare cy’u Burundi bwasabye abasirikare bacyo gutaha bwangu mu rwego rwo kwirinda ko ubuzima bwabo bwakomeza gutikirira mu ntambara yo muri RDC.

r7-E-IGIHE-037.s: Igihe reported that from the morning of 8 December 2025 many Burundian troops, Imbonerakure and Wazalendo were fleeing from Uvira city to Bujumbura, and that residents who saw them said they looked exhausted.
r7-E-IGIHE-037.n: Date conflict to surface: other sources date the fall of Uvira to the night of 9 to 10 December 2025 (REC-0113; SOS Médias dateline 10 Dec: city fell night of 9 December). Igihe describes flight from Uvira on 8 December, before the city was taken. Not reconciled.
r7-E-IGIHE-037.vn: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. Date conflict: other sources date the fall of Uvira to the night of 9-10 December 2025; Igihe describes flight from Uvira on 8 December. Not reconciled.
src: Kuva mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 8 Ukuboza 2025, ingabo nyinshi z’u Burundi, Imbonerakure na Wazalendo ziri guhungira i Bujumbura ziturutse mu mujyi wa Uvira. Abaturage bababonye bavuga ko basaga n’abananiwe cyane.

r7-E-IGIHE-038.s: Igihe reported that the Burundian army sent many soldiers to the border to receive those fleeing, to keep calm, and that those coming from the DRC were being disarmed before continuing to where they were lodged.
src: Igisirikare cy’u Burundi cyohereje ku mupaka abasirikare benshi kugira ngo bakire abahunga mu rwego rwo kubungabunga ituze. Abari kuva muri RDC bari kwamburwa intwaro mbere yo gukomereza aho bacumbika.

r7-E-IGIHE-039.s: Igihe reported that Burundian, DRC and Wazalendo forces were being overpowered because they had lost many areas, and that AFC/M23 fighters who left Kamanyola the previous week had reached Sange, about 30 kilometres towards Uvira city.
r7-E-IGIHE-039.n: Compare REC-0212 (M23 reported advancing to Luberizi, Luvungi, 6 Dec) and REC-0214 (7 Dec Sange explosion). Igihe says AFC/M23 left Kamanyola 'last week' (week before 8 Dec); Kamanyola had been under AFC/M23 since February 2025.
r7-E-IGIHE-039.vn: Verbatim on p05; translation accurate. Igihe narration (Rwandan state-aligned).
src: Ingabo z’u Burundi, iza RDC na Wazalendo biri kurushwa imbaraga, kuko byambuwe ibice byinshi. Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bavuye muri santere ya Kamanyola mu cyumweru gishize, ubu bageze mu gace ka Sange kari mu ntera y’ibilometero 30 berekeza mu mujyi wa Uvira.

r7-E-IGIHE-040.s: Igihe reported that Burundi had sent nearly 20 thousand soldiers ('ibihumbi 20') to South Kivu, many of whom went to areas around Minembwe in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories, closing the routes by which Banyamulenge went to markets and clinics.
r7-E-IGIHE-040.l: Minembwe area (Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories)
r7-E-IGIHE-040.x: Igihe: nearly 20 thousand Burundian soldiers sent to South Kivu
r7-E-IGIHE-040.n: Allegation by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet (the same allegation is made by Twirwaneho, see E-IGIHE-a-062); existing records REC-0202 and claim r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034 (OCHA warned of difficulties accessing food and healthcare in Minembwe) record the blockade independently. Troop figure is the same as Rwanda's statement of 10 Dec 2025 (r1-ST-RW-007).
r7-E-IGIHE-040.vn: Verbatim on p05; "hafi ibihumbi 20" = nearly 20,000, correct. Allegation by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; Twirwaneho makes the same allegation. Troop figure unverified.
src: U Burundi bwohereje abasirikare hafi ibihumbi 20 muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo. Inyinshi zagiye mu bice bikikije Minembwe muri teritwari ya Uvira, Fizi na Mwenga, zifunga inzira Abanyamulenge banyuragamo bajya ku masoko no ku mavuriro.

r7-E-IGIHE-041.s: Igihe reported that it is said ('biravugwa') that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani, commander of the eighth battalion of the Burundian forces fighting in eastern DRC, was shot dead by AFC/M23; the news began circulating on the evening of 5 December 2025, with reports that he fell in fighting at Luvungi that killed many other Burundian soldiers fighting beside the FARDC.
r7-E-IGIHE-041.n: Hedged ('biravugwa', 'bivugwa') in the source. Corroborated independently by Congovirtuel (existing claim r1-SKS-2025Q4-018) and SOS Médias Burundi (E-IGIHE-a-044).
r7-E-IGIHE-041.vn: Both excerpts verbatim on p06; hedges preserved; translation accurate. Death reported, hedged by Igihe ("biravugwa", "bivugwa"); neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed it as of 6 Dec 2025 (Igihe). SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec) also lists him among the dead.
src: Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani wari umuyobozi wa batayo ya munani y'Ingabo z'u Burundi ziri kurwanira mu Burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, biravugwa ko yishwe arashwe n'umutwe wa AFC/M23.

Ni amakuru yatangiye gucicikana ku mugoroba wo kuri uyu wa 5 Ukuboza 2025, aho bivugwa ko yaguye mu mirwano yahitanye n'abandi basirikare benshi b'u Burundi mu gace ka Luvungi, barwana ku ruhande rw'ingabo za RDC, FARDC, bahanganye na AFC/M23.

r7-E-IGIHE-042.s: Igihe reported that Pacifique Nininahazwe, head of FOCODE, said on X that Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani (SS1564), commander of the eighth battalion of Burundian forces in the DRC (TAFOC), was shot dead the previous night with his three guards, and that he was the highest-ranking FDNB soldier killed in this war.
r7-E-IGIHE-042.n: Nininahazwe is a Burundian human-rights activist (FOCODE), not a party; his X statement is the originating claim. 'Last night' relative to 5 Dec evening: date approximate. The three guards are unnamed.
r7-E-IGIHE-042.vn: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. The three guards are not named. Death reported, hedged by Igihe ("biravugwa", "bivugwa"); neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed it as of 6 Dec 2025 (Igihe). SOS Médias Burundi (8 Dec) also lists him among the dead. Nininahazwe is a Burundian human-rights activist (FOCODE).
src: Pacifique Nininahazwe, wabitangarije ku rukuta rwe rwa X. Yagize ati "Lieutenant Colonel Athanase Minani (SS1564), Umuyobozi wa batayo ya munani y'ingabo z'u Burundi muri RDC (TAFOC), yishwe arashwe mu ijoro ryakeye (n'abarinzi be batatu), mu mirwano ikomeje muri RDC."
Yakomeje avuga ko "ni we musirikare ufite ipeti ryo hejuru mu gisirikare cy'u Burundi (FDNB) wiciwe muri iyi ntambara."

r7-E-IGIHE-043.s: Igihe reported that Lt Col Minani was formerly of the old Burundian army (Ex FAB) and had been promoted to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel in July of the year of writing.
r7-E-IGIHE-043.n: Corroborates the Congovirtuel detail (former FAB officer). 'This year' = 2025 (article dated 6 Dec 2025).
r7-E-IGIHE-043.vn: Verbatim on p06. "This year" = 2025 per the article date (6 Dec 2025).
src: Lt Col Minani yahoze mu ngabo za kera z'u Burundi (Ex FAB), akaba yarazamuwe mu ntera agahabwa ipeti rya Lieutenant Colonel muri Nyakanga uyu mwaka.

r7-E-IGIHE-044.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that among the Burundian soldiers killed since 1 December in the localities of Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi and Sange was Lieutenant-Colonel Athanase Minani, the highest-ranking Burundian officer killed since the start of the official intervention in the DRC.
r7-E-IGIHE-044.l: Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi, Sange (Uvira territory)
r7-E-IGIHE-044.n: SOS Médias Burundi's original text (8 Dec 2025). The page also says the Burundian authorities were silent on real losses. Independent of Igihe; consistent with Congovirtuel (r1-SKS-2025Q4-018).
r7-E-IGIHE-044.vn: Verbatim on retained SOS page (Adam Ntwari, 8 Dec 2025). No official Burundian confirmation recorded on the page ("Aucune communication officielle n’a été faite" refers to Sange deaths).
src: Depuis le 1er décembre, de nombreux militaires burundais ont été tués dans les localités de Lubarika, Mitambili, Katogota, Luvungi et Sange, où les affrontements sont particulièrement violents. Parmi les victimes figure le lieutenant-colonel Athanase Minani, le plus haut gradé burundais tué depuis le début de l’intervention officielle en RDC.

r7-E-IGIHE-045.s: Igihe reported that neither the Burundian army nor AFC/M23 had confirmed the death of the senior Burundian soldier (Lt Col Minani).
r7-E-IGIHE-045.n: Absence of confirmation as of the article date. No search was run by this agent for later statements (see gap).
r7-E-IGIHE-045.vn: Verbatim on p06. As of the article date (6 Dec 2025).
src: Yaba igisirikare cy'u Burundi cyangwa AFC/M23 bahanganiye muri RDC, nta ruhande na rumwe ruremeza amakuru y'urupfu rw'uyu musirikare ukomeye w'u Burundi.

r7-E-IGIHE-046.s: Igihe wrote that information reaching it said AFC/M23 had learned that DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were about to attack it at Kamanyola and decided to fire first; a person close to AFC/M23's top leadership told it that the explosions heard on the morning of 2 December were fired by AFC/M23 fighters and had seriously shaken the DRC government coalition.
r7-E-IGIHE-046.a: AFC/M23 (per a person close to its leadership)
r7-E-IGIHE-046.n: Anonymous partisan account; the other side's version is that AFC/M23 started the clashes (see SOS Médias claim r1-SKC-2025H2-007 on exchanges of fire at Katogota/Kamanyola on 2 December).
r7-E-IGIHE-046.vn: The pre-emption account is Igihe's "reliable information", not the person close to the leadership; split the attribution. Translation accurate. Anonymous partisan account of who fired first; the opposing account is that AFC/M23 started the clashes.
src: Amakuru yizewe agera kuri IGIHE avuga ko AFC/M23 yamenye ko ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi na Wazalendo bigiye kuyigabaho ibitero muri Kamanyola, ifata icyemezo cyo kubitanga kurasa.

Umuntu wa hafi y’ubuyobozi bukuru bwa AFC/M23 yasobanuye ko ibisasu byumvikanye mu gitondo cya tariki ya 2 Ukuboza byarashwe n’abarwanyi babo, kandi ko byahungabanyije bikomeye ihuriro rya Leta ya RDC.

r7-E-IGIHE-047.s: Igihe reported that, on the same day as the explosions it dates to the morning of 2 December, DRC and Burundian forces fired on Kamanyola centre, held by AFC/M23 for nearly 10 months, with shells destroying civilian homes and infrastructure; three civilians died and others were injured.
r7-E-IGIHE-047.x: three civilians ("abaturage batatu") died; others injured (number not given)
r7-E-IGIHE-047.n: Single partisan source; see REC-0209 (SOS Médias: exchange of fire around Katogota and Kamanyola, five civilians wounded) and REC-0211.
r7-E-IGIHE-047.vn: Supported on p06. Replacement quote extended to the preceding sentence so the "2 December" date is printed; figures field written in the source's words. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; casualty figure unverified. Other reports of the 2 December exchanges give different civilian casualty figures.
src: Umuntu wa hafi y’ubuyobozi bukuru bwa AFC/M23 yasobanuye ko ibisasu byumvikanye mu gitondo cya tariki ya 2 Ukuboza byarashwe n’abarwanyi babo, kandi ko byahungabanyije bikomeye ihuriro rya Leta ya RDC. Uwo munsi, ingabo za RDC n’iz’u Burundi na zo zarashe muri santere ya Kamanyola imaze amezi hafi 10 igenzura na AFC/M23, ibisasu byazo bisenya inzu z’abaturage n’ibikorwaremezo. Hapfuye abaturage batatu, abandi barakomereka.

r7-E-IGIHE-048.s: Igihe reported that since the morning of 5 December 2025 DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces were attacking areas of Uvira territory including Katogota, Kamanyola and Luvungi groupement, and that shells falling on Luvungi made many residents flee to areas such as Sange, Runingu, Ndolera and Uvira city.
r7-E-IGIHE-048.a: DRC, Burundian and Wazalendo forces (per Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-048.n: Single partisan source; compare REC-0212 and REC-0211.
r7-E-IGIHE-048.vn: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; Igihe attributes the attacks to the government coalition.
src: Kuva mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 5 Ukuboza 2025, Ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi na Wazalendo ziri kugaba ibitero mu bice byo muri Teritwari ya Uvira birimo Katogota, Kamanyola no muri Gurupoma ya Luvungi.
Ibisasu byaguye muri Santere ya Luvungi byatumye abaturage benshi bahunga berekeza mu bindi bice byo muri Uvira bitari kuberamo imirwano nka Sange, Runingu, Ndolera no mu Mujyi wa Uvira.

r7-E-IGIHE-049.s: Bertrand Bisimwa, Deputy Leader of AFC/M23 in charge of political activities, said, according to Igihe, that Burundian forces inside Burundi were shelling heavily populated areas of Kamanyola, Katogota and Luvungi, causing the deaths of innocent people including children and destroying houses, schools, churches and markets.
r7-E-IGIHE-049.l: Kamanyola, Katogota, Luvungi (Uvira territory); shelling alleged from Burundian territory
r7-E-IGIHE-049.n: Party statement; date approximate ('this morning' in an article published at 00:28 on 6 Dec 2025, so probably 5 Dec). Cross-border shelling allegation. See REC-0211 and UN Group of Experts claim r1-GOE-005.
r7-E-IGIHE-049.vn: Verbatim on p06; translation accurate. AFC/M23 allegation of cross-border shelling; "this morning" in an article dated 6 Dec 00:28, so probably 5 Dec. No casualty figures given.
src: Umuyobozi Wungirije wa AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, Bertrand Bisimwa, yatangaje ko ingabo z’Abarundi ziri mu Burundi ziri kurasa muri Kamanyola, Katogota na Luvungi. Ati “Muri iki gitondo, ingabo z’u Burundi ziri mu Burundi ziri gusuka ibisasu mu bice bituwe cyane muri Kamanyola, Katogota na Luvungi, zigateza imfu z’inzirakarengane zirimo abana, zigasenya inzu, amashuri, insengero n’amasoko.”

r7-E-IGIHE-050.s: Igihe reported that the fighting continued after Rwanda and the DRC signed a peace agreement on 4 December 2025, which AFC/M23 said does not concern it.
r7-E-IGIHE-050.n: Party position as relayed by Igihe; the place of signature is not stated in this excerpt.
r7-E-IGIHE-050.vn: Verbatim on p06. AFC/M23 position as relayed by Igihe.
src: Iyi mirwano ikomeje mu gihe ku wa 4 Ukuboza 2025, u Rwanda na RDC byashyize umukono ku masezerano y'amahoro, ibintu AFC/M23 yavuze ko ibyo biganiro n'ayo masezerano bitayireba.

r7-E-IGIHE-051.s: Igihe reported that earlier in the week of the article, DRC media outlets reported that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas it listed as Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese and relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, and that the move was prompted by pressure from the United States government.
r7-E-IGIHE-051.l: Lubero territory: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga
r7-E-IGIHE-051.n: Reports of a pull-back that AFC/M23 denied (E-IGIHE-a-052). Igihe lists the areas as 'territories'. Compare Anadolu/Radio Okapi account of 23 March 2026 (r1-NKN-2026H1-002, REC-1008).
r7-E-IGIHE-051.vn: Verbatim on p07 (English edition). Igihe relays unnamed Congolese media reports; the US-pressure motive is what those reports "suggested". AFC/M23 denied a withdrawal. Igihe calls the localities "territories"; only Lubero is a territory.
src: Earlier this week, media outlets in DRC began reporting that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas in the Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, and Kipese territories, relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba, and Kanyabayonga. These reports suggested that the move was prompted by pressure from the United States government on AFC/M23.

r7-E-IGIHE-052.s: According to Igihe, North Kivu Governor Erasto Bahati (AFC/M23 administration) dismissed the reports of withdrawal in a statement, saying the activities along the front were regular troop rotations within AFC/M23 and that the rumours were fuelled by social media and the Kinshasa government.
r7-E-IGIHE-052.n: Governor Bahati is the AFC/M23-appointed governor of North Kivu. Statement date is the Igihe article date (29 March 2026); the statement itself may be a day or two earlier.
r7-E-IGIHE-052.vn: Supported verbatim on p07; reworded only for clarity (the draft said "said ... that the reports were dismissed"). Bahati is the AFC/M23-appointed governor. Statement date is the Igihe article date (29 March 2026); the statement may be earlier.
src: In a statement released by the Governor of North Kivu Province, Erasto Bahati, these reports were dismissed, with the governor clarifying that what is happening is simply a routine rotation of troops.
"The leadership of North Kivu Province reassures all citizens that the activities occurring along the battlefront are part of the regular military troop rotations within AFC/M23."

"It is completely different from the rumors fueled by social media and the Kinshasa government, which aim to confuse and frighten people who are living in peace and security. AFC/M23 remains committed to protecting all citizens from harm, regardless of its origin."

r7-E-IGIHE-053.s: Igihe reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye said in an interview with Jeune Afrique published on 10 May 2026 that the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings with the DRC was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi's borders, alleging that M23 operates with Rwanda's backing.
r7-E-IGIHE-053.n: Interview relayed by Igihe, which frames the remarks as 'false' in its own text. Jeune Afrique original not checked by this agent; compare existing Burundian border-closure records (REC-0115, REC-0020).
r7-E-IGIHE-053.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: In an interview with Jeune Afrique published on May 10, 2026, Ndayishimiye discussed the closure of the Gatumba and Vugizo border crossings between Burundi and DR Congo on the South Kivu side. He claimed the decision was linked to the proximity of M23 fighters near Burundi’s borders, alleging that the group operates with Rwanda’s backing.

r7-E-IGIHE-054.s: According to Igihe, Ndayishimiye said that Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders a security concern and expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure to end the tensions.
r7-E-IGIHE-054.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: According to Ndayishimiye, Burundi considers the presence of M23 fighters near its borders as a security concern, although he expressed hope that the Washington peace agreement would increase pressure aimed at ending the tensions.

r7-E-IGIHE-055.s: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to the DRC to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself, under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi's operational zone.
r7-E-IGIHE-055.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: Ndayishimiye maintained that Burundian troops were sent to DR Congo to assist Congolese forces against their enemies rather than to defend Burundi itself. He explained that the deployment was carried out under regional arrangements that assigned South Kivu as Burundi’s operational zone.

r7-E-IGIHE-056.s: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye argued that fighting continued despite regional efforts because some countries failed to contain the conflict, and that only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.
r7-E-IGIHE-056.n: Interview relayed by Igihe; relevant to command and control of Burundian troops (FDNB under FARDC directives).
r7-E-IGIHE-056.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: He further argued that despite efforts by regional actors, fighting continued because some countries failed to contain the conflict. According to him, only Uganda and Burundi remained actively engaged, with Burundian troops operating under the directives of the Congolese army.

r7-E-IGIHE-057.s: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as terrorist, and that Rwanda has consistently denied this, insisting it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.
r7-E-IGIHE-057.a: Government of Burundi (Ndayishimiye); Government of Rwanda (denial)
r7-E-IGIHE-057.n: The Rwandan denial is stated by Igihe as background, not as a fresh statement.
r7-E-IGIHE-057.vn: Verbatim on p08. Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked. The Rwandan denial is Igihe background, not a new statement.
src: The Burundian leader also repeated accusations that Rwanda supports RED Tabara, a group Burundi describes as a terrorist organization responsible for attacks inside the country. Rwanda has consistently denied the allegations, insisting that it does not support any group seeking to destabilize Burundi.

r7-E-IGIHE-058.s: Igihe reported that, asked about Rwanda's accusation that Burundi collaborates with the FDLR, Ndayishimiye said he had asked President Paul Kagame for intelligence on FDLR positions and that Burundi would attack the group if given such information.
r7-E-IGIHE-058.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: In response, Ndayishimiye argued that he had previously asked President Paul Kagame to provide intelligence on FDLR positions, insisting that Burundi would attack the group if such information were made available.

r7-E-IGIHE-059.s: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with the FDLR, but argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups.
r7-E-IGIHE-059.n: Significant if accurate: a head of state acknowledging FARDC-FDLR cooperation. Relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; check against the Jeune Afrique original.
r7-E-IGIHE-059.vn: Verbatim on p08. Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked. The acknowledgement of FARDC-FDLR cooperation rests on Igihe's paraphrase only; check the Jeune Afrique original before relying on it.
src: When asked how Burundian troops could avoid cooperating with FDLR while operating alongside FARDC, which has repeatedly been accused of collaborating with the group, Ndayishimiye acknowledged that Congolese forces work with FDLR. However, he argued that Burundian troops operate separately under Congolese command structures and do not mix with those groups

r7-E-IGIHE-060.s: Igihe reported that Ndayishimiye proposed coordinated military action by Rwanda, the DRC, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups in the region, saying this could reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.
r7-E-IGIHE-060.vn: Verbatim on p08 (Igihe English edition, 11 May 2026). Ndayishimiye's Jeune Afrique interview (published 10 May 2026, journalist Romain Gras) as paraphrased by Igihe's English edition, which calls his remarks "false" in its own framing; the Jeune Afrique original was not checked.
src: He proposed coordinated military action involving Rwanda, DR Congo, Burundi and Uganda against armed groups operating in the region, saying such cooperation could help reassure Rwanda about its security concerns.

r7-E-IGIHE-061.s: Igihe reported that Burundi had deployed more than 20,000 troops to South Kivu under bilateral agreements with the DRC, and that the deployment was reduced in early December 2025 after M23 fighters captured several areas in the Ruzizi Plain and the city of Uvira.
r7-E-IGIHE-061.x: Igihe: more than 20,000 Burundian troops deployed to South Kivu
r7-E-IGIHE-061.n: Igihe background text. Corroborates REC-0231 and the Rwandan government figure (r1-ST-RW-007).
r7-E-IGIHE-061.vn: Verbatim on p08. Igihe background narration; troop figure not officially confirmed by Burundi.
src: Under bilateral agreements signed between Burundi and DR Congo in 2022 and 2023, Burundi deployed more than 20,000 troops to South Kivu. The deployment was reduced in early December 2025 after M23 fighters captured several areas in the Ruzizi Plain and the city of Uvira.

r7-E-IGIHE-062.s: Igihe described TAFOC as the Burundian bilateral contingent in the DRC, which began operations in South Kivu in 2022 alongside Congolese forces against armed groups including RED Tabara, FOREBU, FNL and Twirwaneho.
r7-E-IGIHE-062.n: Background on a unit name (TAFOC) used by Burundian forces in the DRC; start in 2022 is outside the edition window, so the claim is dated to the Igihe article and used only to identify the unit. Minani is described by Nininahazwe as a TAFOC battalion commander (E-IGIHE-a-042).
r7-E-IGIHE-062.vn: Verbatim on p08. Igihe background used only to identify the TAFOC unit; the 2022 start is before the edition window.
src: The bilateral contingent, known as TAFOC, began operations in South Kivu in 2022 alongside Congolese forces against armed groups including RED Tabara, FOREBU, FNL and Twirwaneho.

r7-E-IGIHE-063.s: Igihe, relaying an AFC/M23 communiqué, reported that seven people died, three were seriously injured and one lightly injured on Saturday 12 September 2026 when an explosive device, which the communiqué describes as planted by those AFC/M23 called enemies, went off at Jomba, Gikoro, Rugunga village in Rutshuru, after a child found it in a field and began handling it.
r7-E-IGIHE-063.x: seven ("barindwi") dead, three ("batatu") seriously injured, one ("umwe") lightly injured (Igihe, relaying AFC/M23)
r7-E-IGIHE-063.n: AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet. Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd (existing claim r1-NKS-2026Q3-006) report the same blast with differing details. Igihe calls Rutshuru a 'province' (it is a territory). The child who found the device is not named and his status (killed or injured) is not stated.
r7-E-IGIHE-063.vn: All three passages verbatim on p09; translations accurate. Figures field written as the words the source prints (the excerpts give no digits). AFC/M23 communiqué as relayed by Igihe; other outlets report the same blast with differing details. Igihe uses Rwandan administrative terms (Umurenge/sector, Ntara/province) for Rutshuru. The child is not named and the child's fate is not stated.
src: Abantu barindwi bapfuye abandi batatu barakomereka bikomeye, mu gihe undi umwe yagize ibikomere byoroheje nyuma y’igisasu cyatezwe n’abo AFC/M23 yise abanzi mu gace ka Jomba, mu Murenge wa Gikoro, mu Mudugudu wa Rugunga, mu Ntara ya Rutshuru.
Ibi byabaye ku wa Gatandatu, tariki ya 12 Nzeri 2026, nyuma y’uko umwana wavumbuye igisasu mu murima atabizi yatangiye kugikorakora, bikaza kurangira gituritse.
Itangazo rya AFC/M23 rivuga ko abakomeretse bahise bajyanwa ku Bitaro Bikuru bya Rugunga muri Teritwari ya Rutshuru.

r7-E-IGIHE-064.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 expressed deep sorrow, condoled with the families, and asked residents of liberated areas to follow instructions on avoiding explosives still in the ground, not to touch, move or try to dismantle anything they suspect may be a bomb.
r7-E-IGIHE-064.n: Party communiqué as relayed by Igihe.
r7-E-IGIHE-064.vn: Verbatim on p09; translation accurate. Party communiqué; "liberated areas" is AFC/M23's term.
src: Umutwe wa AFC-M23 wavuze ko wababajwe cyane n’iki gitero, unihanganisha imiryango yabuze ababo ndetse n’inshuti z’abahitanywe n’iturika ry’iki gisasu.

AFC-M23 yasabye abaturage bari mu bice byabohowe gukurikiza amabwiriza yatanzwe ajyanye no kwirinda ibiturika bikiri mu butaka. Yasabye kandi abaturage kwirinda gukorakora, kwimura cyangwa kugerageza gusenya ikintu bakeka ko gishobora kuba igisasu, haba mu murima, mu rugo cyangwa ku muhanda

r7-E-IGIHE-065.s: Igihe reported that DRC soldiers and fighters of the Wazalendo alliance exchanged fire in Uvira city overnight, with heavy gunfire (AK-47 and machine guns) heard from eight in the evening on 5 September 2025, because of a disagreement.
r7-E-IGIHE-065.n: Single partisan source; casualties not mentioned. Related events: Wazalendo protests against General Gasita in Uvira from 2 September (REC-0093), and deaths from demonstrations (REC-0097).
r7-E-IGIHE-065.vn: Verbatim on p10; "masaa mbiri y'ijoro" = 8 p.m., correct. Single Rwandan state-aligned source; no casualties reported.
src: Ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo n’abarwanyi b'Ihuriro ry’imitwe yitwaje intwaro rya Wazalendo baraye barasaniye mu Mujyi wa Uvira mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo kubera kutumvikana. Amasasu menshi muri uyu mujyi wegereye Ikiyaga cya Tanganyika yumvikanye kuva mu masaa Mbiri y’ijoro ryo ku wa 5 Nzeri 2025. Hifashishwaga imbunda zirimo Ak-47 na machine gun.

r7-E-IGIHE-066.s: Igihe reported, on unspecified information ('amakuru avuga'), that the Wazalendo fighters who exchanged fire with the DRC army belonged to the armed group led by 'Général' John Makanaki, which has operated in South Kivu for a long time.
r7-E-IGIHE-066.a: Wazalendo group led by 'Général' John Makanaki
r7-E-IGIHE-066.n: Hedged ('amakuru avuga'). Name 'John Makanaki' as printed; other sources print Makanaki Kasimbira John / René Makanaki (existing claims r7-CMD-WZ-008, r1-UV-2025Q2-001).
r7-E-IGIHE-066.vn: Verbatim on p10; hedge preserved. Hedged in the source ("amakuru avuga" = information says). Name printed "John Makanaki"; other sources print other forms.
src: Amakuru avuga ko abarwanyi ba Wazalendo barasanye n’ingabo za RDC ari abo mu mutwe witwaje intwaro uyoborwa na ‘Général’ John Makanaki bamaze igihe kirekire bakorera muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo.

r7-E-IGIHE-067.s: Igihe reported that since 2 September 2025 Wazalendo had been in a major protest in Uvira demanding that DRC Brig Gen Gasita Olivier leave the city because, they claimed, he is Rwandan, doubting his nationality because he is a Munyamulenge; Wazalendo closed the main road, halting all economic activity.
r7-E-IGIHE-067.n: Corroborates REC-0093 (demonstrations against Gasita). The ethnic basis of the demand (Munyamulenge identity) is relevant to discrimination.
r7-E-IGIHE-067.vn: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. "ngo" hedge preserved ("they claimed").
src: Kuva tariki ya 2 Nzeri 2025, Wazalendo bari mu myigaragambyo ikomeye muri Uvira, isaba ko umusirikare wa RDC, Brig Gen. Gasita Olivier, ava muri uyu mujyi kuko ngo ni Umunyarwanda. Bashidikanya ku bwenegihugu bwe bashingiye ku kuba ari Umunyamulenge.

Ubuzima bwarahagaze muri uyu mujyi kuko Wazalendo yafunze umuhanda munini waho, ihagarika ibikorwa byose abaturage bakesha imibereho n’iterambere. Bavuze ko bazahagarika imyigaragambyo mu gihe ubuyobozi buzaba bukuye Brig Gen Gasita aha hantu.

r7-E-IGIHE-068.s: Igihe reported that on 5 September 2025 the acting mayor of Uvira, Kifara Kapenda Kik'v, led a meeting to calm tensions attended by Wazalendo leaders including Makanaki and 'Général' William Amur Yakutumba, but it achieved nothing as the protest continued.
r7-E-IGIHE-068.n: Radio Okapi (existing claim r1-UV-2025Q3-017) calls Kifara Kapenda the deputy mayor of Uvira; Igihe says 'Meya w'agateganyo' (acting mayor). Name spelled as Igihe prints it.
r7-E-IGIHE-068.vn: Verbatim on p10. Igihe says acting mayor ("Meya w'agateganyo"); Radio Okapi calls him deputy mayor. Name spelled as Igihe prints it.
src: Ku wa 5 Nzeri 2025, Meya w’agateganyo w’uyu mujyi, Kifara Kapenda Kik’v, yayoboye inama yari igamije guhosha umwuka mubi, yitabiriwe n’abayobozi bo muri Wazalendo barimo Makanaki na 'Général' William Amur Yakutumba ariko nta musaruro yagezeho kuko imyigaragambyo yakomeje.

r7-E-IGIHE-069.s: Wazalendo leader William Yakutumba said at the meeting held in Uvira, according to Igihe: 'That leader who was sent here, called Gen Gasita, we do not want him here in Uvira'.
r7-E-IGIHE-069.n: Party statement. Name printed 'William Amur Yakutumba' elsewhere on the page.
r7-E-IGIHE-069.vn: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Party statement relayed by Igihe.
src: Muri iyi nama yumvikanyemo urusaku rwinshi rwa Wazalendo, Yakutumba yagize ati "Uwo muyobozi woherejwe hano, yitwa Gen Gasita, ntitumushaka hano muri Uvira."

r7-E-IGIHE-070.s: Igihe reported that Yakutumba insisted Brig Gen Gasita must leave Uvira, and that Makanaki said that if the soldier had not left by 8 September his fighters would close the DRC-Burundi border and the Uvira port on Lake Tanganyika.
r7-E-IGIHE-070.n: Threat to close the border and port (a civilian-supply and humanitarian concern). Party statement.
r7-E-IGIHE-070.vn: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Threat, as relayed by Igihe.
src: Yakutumba yashimangiye ko Brig Gen Gasita agomba kuva muri Uvira, Makanaki agaragaza ko nibigera tariki ya 8 Nzeri uyu musirikare ataragenda, abarwanyi be bazafunga umupaka wa RDC n’u Burundi n’icyambu cya Uvira ku Kiyaga cya Tanganyika.

r7-E-IGIHE-071.s: FARDC spokesperson Maj Gen Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, according to Igihe, had asked Wazalendo to accept Brig Gen Gasita, explaining that he had not betrayed the country and had been appointed by the Head of State; the fighters refused and asked for his replacement.
r7-E-IGIHE-071.n: Corroborates existing claims r1-UV-2025Q3-031 and r1-UV-2025Q3-032 (Ekenge's statements). Date of the statement not given by Igihe (before 6 Sept 2025).
r7-E-IGIHE-071.vn: Verbatim on p10; translation accurate. Igihe does not date Ekenge's appeal (pluperfect "yari yasabye"; before 6 Sept 2025).
src: Umuvugizi w'Ingabo za RDC, Gen Maj. Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, yari yasabye Wazalendo kwemera kwakira Brig Gen Gasita, abasobanurira ko uyu musirikare atigeze agambanira igihugu kandi ko yashyizweho n'Umukuru w'Igihugu ariko aba barwanyi babyanze, bagasaba ko asimbuzwa.

r7-E-IGIHE-072.s: Igihe reported that on the morning of 25 September 2025 various media reported that M23 had deployed additional troops and weapons in Lubero territory to strengthen control over Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera and Kirumba.
r7-E-IGIHE-072.l: Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera, Kirumba (Lubero territory)
r7-E-IGIHE-072.n: Igihe wrongly says Lubero is 'located in South Kivu Province' (it is in North Kivu); the places named are in Lubero territory. Corroborates Actualite.cd (r4-G-LOCAL-NK-002, vehicles shuttling Kirumba-Katondi).
r7-E-IGIHE-072.vn: Verbatim on p11 (English edition, 26 Sep 2025). Igihe wrongly places Lubero territory in South Kivu; it is in North Kivu. Igihe relays unnamed media reports.
src: More than eight months later, on the morning of September 25, 2025, various media outlets reported that M23 had deployed additional troops and weapons in this territory to strengthen its control over areas such as Kipese, Katondi, Munyakandomi, Vulera, and Kirumba.

r7-E-IGIHE-073.s: Igihe reported that in February 2025 M23 captured the Kitsombiro area in Lubero after intense clashes with the FARDC.
r7-E-IGIHE-073.n: Corroborates REC-0973 (Kipese and Katondi taken after the fall of Kitsumbiro). Igihe spells Kitsombiro; Kivu Morning Post spells Kitsumbiro.
r7-E-IGIHE-073.vn: Verbatim on p11. Spelled "Kitsombiro" by Igihe; other outlets print "Kitsumbiro". Igihe background narration.
src: In February 2025, M23 captured the area of Kitsombiro in Lubero after intense clashes with the DRC’s armed forces (FARDC).

r7-E-IGIHE-074.s: Igihe reported that M23 had also reinforced its forces in the localities of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa, which it read as signalling plans to extend control to other parts of what it called South Kivu Province.
r7-E-IGIHE-074.n: Igihe does not say which territory Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa are in; the interpretation ('plans to expand') is Igihe's. Place names as printed.
r7-E-IGIHE-074.vn: Verbatim on p11; narrowed so the interpretation and the mislabelled province are Igihe's. Igihe wrongly places Lubero territory in South Kivu; it is in North Kivu. The territory of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa is not stated; the "plans to expand" reading is Igihe's.
src: M23 has not only increased its presence in Lubero but has also bolstered its forces in the localities of Rusamambu and Bukumbirwa, signaling plans to expand its control to other parts of South Kivu Province.

r7-E-IGIHE-075.s: Igihe reported that the group had recruited 7,437 new fighters who had undergone six months of military training at the Rumangabo base in North Kivu, including former FARDC soldiers and Wazalendo members who joined M23 after the capture of Goma and Bukavu.
r7-E-IGIHE-075.x: Igihe: 7,437 new fighters; six months of training at Rumangabo
r7-E-IGIHE-075.n: Corroborates the figure of 7,437 'commandos' whose pass-out AFC/M23 publicised on 14 September 2025 (UN Group of Experts, r1-UC-M23-018, REC-0311). The claim that former FARDC and Wazalendo joined is Igihe's.
r7-E-IGIHE-075.vn: Verbatim on p11. Igihe narration; the figure matches the 7,437 recruits AFC/M23 publicised in September 2025. The composition of the recruits is Igihe's claim.
src: In recent days, the group recruited 7,437 new fighters who had undergone six months of military training at the Rumangabo military base in North Kivu Province. These recruits include former FARDC soldiers as well as members of the Wazalendo coalition who joined M23 after capturing cities such as Goma and Bukavu.

r7-E-IGIHE-076.s: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on Thursday 3 April 2025, according to Igihe, that the group had repositioned its forces in Walikale and surroundings, and warned that if Kinshasa regime forces persisted in provocations or attacked civilians in liberated areas or AFC/M23 positions, the goodwill gesture would be cancelled and 'we will eliminate the threat at its source'.
r7-E-IGIHE-076.n: Party statement; the page is the English text on fr.igihe.com. Corroborates REC-0400 (announced AFC/M23 withdrawal from Walikale and reactions). UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-075) attributes the early April withdrawal to FARDC airstrikes, a different cause.
r7-E-IGIHE-076.vn: Verbatim on p12 ("Walikale and its surroundings" is in the quoted statement). AFC/M23 statement relayed by Igihe (4 April 2025). The UN Group of Experts gives a different cause for the early-April withdrawal.
src: In a statement released on Thursday, April 3, 2025, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka affirmed that the rebel group had repositioned its forces in the region. He warned, however, that any aggression from Kinshasa would trigger an immediate response.

"If the forces of the Kinshasa regime persist in their provocations or attack civilians in the liberated areas as well as our positions, the gesture of goodwill undertaken will be immediately cancelled, and we will eliminate the threat at its source," Kanyuka said.

r7-E-IGIHE-077.s: Igihe reported that M23 took control of Walikale on 19 March 2025, notably seizing the Kigoma airstrip, after conquering several surrounding localities including Ngora, Kisima and Mubanda.
r7-E-IGIHE-077.l: Walikale; Kigoma airstrip; Ngora, Kisima, Mubanda
r7-E-IGIHE-077.n: Corroborates REC-0395 (UN Secretary-General: M23 took control of Walikale town on 19 March 2025 and withdrew shortly afterwards).
r7-E-IGIHE-077.vn: Verbatim on p12. Igihe background narration; consistent with UN reporting that M23 took Walikale town on 19 March 2025.
src: The M23 took control of Walikale on March 19, 2025, notably seizing the Kigoma airstrip, after conquering several surrounding localities, including Ngora, Kisima and Mubanda.

r7-E-IGIHE-078.s: Igihe reported that after taking Walikale the rebel group announced its withdrawal, describing it as 'a choice aimed at creating a climate conducive to political dialogue', and called on local authorities and residents to guarantee security in the region.
r7-E-IGIHE-078.n: Date of the withdrawal announcement not given in the excerpt; Igihe refers elsewhere in the article to the AFC/M23 press release of Sunday 23 March 2025.
r7-E-IGIHE-078.vn: Verbatim on p12. Announcement date not given in the excerpt; Igihe refers to an AFC/M23 press release of Sunday 23 March 2025.
src: Subsequently, the rebel group announced its withdrawal, describing this decision as "a choice aimed at creating a climate conducive to political dialogue". Despite this withdrawal, the M23 called on local authorities and residents to guarantee security in the region.

r7-E-IGIHE-079.s: Igihe reported that the Congolese government and the M23 were to begin direct talks on 9 April 2025 in Doha, Qatar, the first direct negotiation between the two parties since the rebels took two provincial capitals.
r7-E-IGIHE-079.a: Government of the DRC; M23; Qatar (mediator)
r7-E-IGIHE-079.n: Forward-looking report (published 4 April 2025), not confirmation that the talks took place on that day.
r7-E-IGIHE-079.vn: Verbatim on p12. Forward-looking (published 4 April 2025); not confirmation the talks began that day.
src: Furthermore, the Congolese government and the M23 rebels are to begin direct talks on April 9, 2025 in Doha, the capital of Qatar, as part of ongoing efforts to restore peace. This meeting will mark the first direct negotiation between the two parties since the rebels took control of two provincial capitals in eastern Congo.

r7-E-IGIHE-080.s: Igihe reported that a meeting initially planned in Angola on 18 March was abruptly cancelled after M23 withdrew in protest against European Union sanctions on its leaders, and that diplomatic efforts resumed after an unexpected mid-March meeting between Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame in Doha.
r7-E-IGIHE-080.a: M23; Angola; Qatar; Presidents Tshisekedi and Kagame
r7-E-IGIHE-080.n: Background reported by Igihe on mediation; no Kivu location. Statement-level context only.
r7-E-IGIHE-080.vn: Verbatim on p12; removed the year "2025" from the statement because the excerpt does not print it (date field keeps 2025-03-18). Igihe background on mediation (article of 4 April 2025; the year is the article's).
src: A meeting initially planned in Angola on March 18 was abruptly cancelled after the M23 withdrew in protest against the sanctions imposed by the European Union on its leaders. However, diplomatic efforts resumed following an unexpected meeting in mid-March between Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi and his counterpart Paul Kagame in Doha.

r7-E-IGIHE-081.s: Igihe reported that the AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Bahati Musanga Erasto, changed the leadership of Goma city, and that a notice of 9 April 2026 named Kisuba Ngabo Désiré, until then deputy mayor, mayor of Goma, replacing Julien Katembo Ndalieni, who became head of Lubero territory.
r7-E-IGIHE-081.n: Date conflict: Kivu Morning Post (existing claim r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-009) dates the reshuffle 8 April 2026, Igihe cites a notice of 9 April 2026. Name spellings differ: Igihe 'Kisuba Ngabo Désiré', 'Julien Katembo Ndalieni'; KMP 'Désiré Kisuba Ngabo', 'Julienne Katembo Ndalieni'. Printed as Igihe prints them.
r7-E-IGIHE-081.vn: Both passages verbatim on p13; translations accurate. Igihe cites a notice of 9 April 2026; another outlet dates the reshuffle 8 April 2026. Spellings as Igihe prints them (its photo caption prints "Kasuba Ngabo"); other outlets print variants.
src: Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Bahati Musanga Erasto, yahinduye ubuyobozi bw’Umujyi wa Goma.

Itangazo ryo ku wa 9 Mata 2026 rigaragaza ko Kisuba Ngabo Désiré yagizwe Meya wa Goma, asimbuye Julien Katembo Ndalieni wagizwe Umuyobozi wa teritwari ya Lubero. Kisuba yari asanzwe ari Visi Meya w’uyu mujyi.

r7-E-IGIHE-082.s: Igihe reported that Nshimiyimana Juvénal, who had been in charge of mobilisation and recruiting new fighters in AFC/M23, was named deputy mayor of Goma.
r7-E-IGIHE-082.n: New detail on a de facto official's earlier role (recruitment), relevant to forced-recruitment leads (REC-0304). Kivu Morning Post prints the name 'Juvénal Nshimimana' (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-010).
r7-E-IGIHE-082.vn: Verbatim on p13; "gushaka abarwanyi bashya" = recruiting new fighters, correct. Name as Igihe prints it; another outlet prints "Juvénal Nshimimana".
src: Nshimiyimana Juvénal wari Umuyobozi ushinzwe ubukangurambaga no gushaka abarwanyi bashya muri AFC/M23 yagizwe Visi Meya w’Umujyi wa Goma.

r7-E-IGIHE-083.s: Igihe reported that, in the same reshuffle, Katembo Isevisya, who had been in the Lubero territory leadership, and Radjabu Kwizera Elie were given deputy burgomaster posts, Radjabu Kwizera Elie as deputy burgomaster of Karisimbi commune.
r7-E-IGIHE-083.n: The Kinyarwanda sentence is garbled in the source ('Komite yahawe Burugumesitiri wungirije'); translated literally. KMP (r1-UCD-M23-ADMIN-010) says Katembo Isevisya became deputy bourgmestre.
r7-E-IGIHE-083.vn: Verbatim on p13; statement does not go beyond the text. The source sentence is garbled ("Komite yahawe Burugumesitiri wungirije", probably a typo for a commune); which commune Katembo Isevisya serves is not clear from Igihe.
src: Komite yahawe Burugumesitiri wungirije, Katembo Isevisya wari mu buyobozi bwa teritwari ya Lubero, Radjabu Kwizera Elie agirwa Burugumesitiri wungirije wa Komini Karisimbi.

r7-E-IGIHE-084.s: Katembo said in an interview with Igihe in January 2026 that Goma was now safe and that all activities, including trade, were going better than before.
r7-E-IGIHE-084.a: AFC/M23 de facto authority in Goma
r7-E-IGIHE-084.n: Only 'Katembo' is printed in the sentence; the article elsewhere names Julien Katembo Ndalieni as the replaced mayor. Party claim; contradicts reports of insecurity in Goma recorded by UN and NGOs.
r7-E-IGIHE-084.vn: Verbatim on p13; translation accurate. Only "Katembo" is printed in this sentence (in context, apparently the outgoing mayor Julien Katembo Ndalieni). De facto official's claim; conflicts with UN and NGO reports of insecurity in Goma.
src: Mu kiganiro Katembo yagiranye na IGIHE muri Mutarama 2026, yatangaje ko ubu Goma itekanye, kandi ko ibikorerwamo byose birimo ubucuruzi bigenda neza kurusha uko byahoze.

r7-E-IGIHE-085.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 took the city of Goma on 27 January 2025 and then installed new officials to bring it back on track in security, welfare and infrastructure projects.
r7-E-IGIHE-085.n: Corroborates REC-0247 (capture of Goma by AFC/M23 and RDF, 26-29 January 2025). Igihe gives AFC/M23 alone.
r7-E-IGIHE-085.vn: Verbatim on p13. Igihe narration; it names AFC/M23 alone (other sources record RDF participation).
src: AFC/M23 yafashe umujyi wa Goma tariki ya 27 Mutarama 2025. Yashyizeho abayobozi bashya kugira ngo bayifashe kuwusubiza ku murongo mu rwego rw’umutekano, imibereho y’abaturage, banakurikirane imishinga yo kubaka ibikorwaremezo.

r7-E-IGIHE-086.s: Igihe reported that MDRP-Twirwaneho had for days been saying that many Burundian troops were deployed around Minembwe, including Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya and Mwenga, to starve the Banyamulenge by closing the roads they use to go to buy supplies.
r7-E-IGIHE-086.l: Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya, Mwenga (around Minembwe)
r7-E-IGIHE-086.n: Party allegation relayed by a partisan outlet; corroborates existing records on the Minembwe blockade (REC-0202). 'MDRP' (printed so here) is the same group elsewhere printed MRDP-Twirwaneho.
r7-E-IGIHE-086.vn: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned). The intent to starve is Twirwaneho's allegation. Igihe prints "MDRP" here, elsewhere "MRDP".
src: Umutwe wa MDRP-Twirwaneho umaze iminsi ugaragaza ko ingabo nyinshi z’u Burundi zoherejwe mu bice bikikije Minembwe birimo Mikenke, Point-Zéro, Makombo, Mikalati, Gipupu, Murambya na Mwenga kugira ngo wicishe inzara Abanyamulenge zikoresheje uburyo bwo gufunga inzira banyuramo bajya guhaha.

r7-E-IGIHE-087.s: Igihe reported that during heavy fighting in the Ruzizi Plain since the start of the previous week many Burundian troops left areas they controlled such as Sange, Runingo, Kiliba and Uvira town, fleeing along with the DRC forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.
r7-E-IGIHE-087.a: Burundian troops, DRC forces, Wazalendo, FDLR (fleeing); AFC/M23 advancing
r7-E-IGIHE-087.n: Corroborates REC-0231 (large part of Burundian soldiers withdrew) and REC-0113 (Uvira taken). The mention of the FDLR among those fleeing is Igihe's.
r7-E-IGIHE-087.vn: Verbatim on p14. Igihe narration; the presence of FDLR among those fleeing is Igihe's claim.
src: Mu rugamba rukomeye rwabereye mu Kibaya cya Rusizi kuva mu ntangiriro z’icyumweru gishize, ingabo nyinshi z’u Burundi zavuye mu bice zagenzuraga nka Sange, Runingo, Kiliba no mu Mujyi wa Uvira, zihungana n’iza RDC, Wazalendo na FDLR.

r7-E-IGIHE-088.s: Igihe reported ('bivugwa') that the Burundian troops left these areas on an order from their top command because they had lost many soldiers in the war, including one of their leaders, Lt Col Athanase Minani, and that many were taken prisoner.
r7-E-IGIHE-088.n: Hedged ('Bivugwa'). Claim that many were captured (as prisoners of war) is not corroborated elsewhere in this pass; see M23's earlier presentation of captured Burundian soldiers (not in this file).
r7-E-IGIHE-088.vn: Verbatim on p14; hedge preserved. Hedged ("bivugwa" = it is said). The claim that many were captured is uncorroborated here.
src: Bivugwa ko Ingabo z’u Burundi zavuye muri ibi bice hashingiwe ku ibwiriza zahawe n’ubuyobozi bukuru bwazo, kuko zatakarije abasirikare benshi mu ntambara barimo umwe mu bayobozi babo, Lt Col Athanase Minani, benshi bafatwa mpiri.

r7-E-IGIHE-089.s: Igihe reported that Wazalendo groups affirm that some Burundian soldiers fled with them into the Itombwe forest, where they were going to regroup to attack various areas controlled by AFC/M23.
r7-E-IGIHE-089.n: Party statement ('Wazalendo groups') relayed by a partisan outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-089.vn: Verbatim on p14. Unnamed Wazalendo groups as relayed by Igihe.
src: Imitwe ya Wazalendo ihamya ko hari abasirikare b’u Burundi bahunganye na yo mu ishyamba rya Itombwe, aho bagiye kwisuganyiriza kugira ngo bazatere ibice bitandukanye bigenzurwa na AFC/M23.
