r7-E-IGIHE-090.s: Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, Vice-President of MRDP-Twirwaneho, told Igihe on 11 December 2025 that Burundian troops were still numerous in the high areas around Minembwe and said: 'The Burundian troops are still where they were. Even now Burundians are fighting the self-defending residents there at Irango, at Ndondo'.
r7-E-IGIHE-090.n: Party statement given to Igihe. Name printed 'Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis' here and 'Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza' in p15.
r7-E-IGIHE-090.vn: Name order corrected to the form the excerpt prints ("Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis"). Translation accurate ("abaturage birwanaho" = residents defending themselves). MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned).
src: Kuri uyu wa 11 Ukuboza 2025, Visi Perezida wa MRDP-Twirwaneho, Mugisha Nkurunziza Alexis, yatangarije IGIHE ingabo z’u Burundi zikiri nyinshi mu bice by’imisozi miremire bikikije Minembwe. Nkurunziza yagize ati “Ingabo z’u Burundi aho zari ziri ziracyahari. N’ubu Abarundi bari kurwana n’abaturage birwanaho hariya ku Irango, ku Ndondo.”

r7-E-IGIHE-091.s: Igihe reported that on 6 December Burundian troops took hostage nearly 100 civilians who had gone shopping in areas bordering Minembwe, and that Twirwaneho explained that some were taken to the Mikalati military camp and others to an unknown place; Nkurunziza said the troops had since released these civilians.
r7-E-IGIHE-091.l: areas bordering Minembwe; Mikalati military camp
r7-E-IGIHE-091.n: Corroborates REC-0213 (attack on residents returning from Bijombo market, killings, abduction; SOS Médias Burundi). Twirwaneho allegation relayed by a partisan outlet; no names.
r7-E-IGIHE-091.vn: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned). Igihe states the hostage-taking as fact but its account rests on Twirwaneho; no victims named; unverified figure.
src: Tariki ya 6 Ukuboza, Ingabo z’u Burundi zafashe bugwate abaturage hafi 100 bari bagiye guhaha mu bice bihana imbibi na Minembwe. Twirwaneho yasobanuye ko bamwe bajyanywe mu kigo cya gisirikare cya Mikalati, abandi bajyanwa ahantu hatazwi.
Nkurunziza yatangaje ko ubu ingabo z’u Burundi zamaze kurekura aba baturage, ariko ko zikomeje kugira uruhare rutaziguye bigabwa mu bice bikikije Minembwe.

r7-E-IGIHE-092.s: Nkurunziza of MRDP-Twirwaneho said, according to Igihe, that the Burundian troops had disgraced their country in this war, that their best option was to go home, and that otherwise they would be removed by force from the high hills around Minembwe.
r7-E-IGIHE-092.n: Party statement/threat relayed by a partisan outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-092.vn: Verbatim on p14; "zatesheje agaciro" = devalued/disgraced, fine. MRDP-Twirwaneho is a party to the conflict (allied with AFC/M23); relayed by Igihe (Rwandan state-aligned).
src: Nkurunziza yatangaje ko ingabo z’u Burundi zatesheje agaciro igihugu cyazo muri iyi ntambara, bityo ko amahitamo meza zikwiye kugira ari ugutaha, bitaba ibyo na zo zikazakurwa mu misozi miremire ikikije Minembwe ku ngufu.

r7-E-IGIHE-093.s: Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, AFC/M23 deputy chief of staff, arrived in Uvira city on 10 December 2025 and asked the Burundian troops still in the high hills of South Kivu to come down and go home in peace, saying 'We have no problem with the Burundians because we are neighbours'.
r7-E-IGIHE-093.n: Corroborates REC-0113 (AFC/M23 and RDF take control of Uvira, 10 December 2025) and places Byamungu in Uvira that day; UN Group of Experts (r1-GOE-004) says the offensive was under his and Makenga's command. Igihe prints 'Umugaba Mukuru Wungirije' (Deputy Chief of Staff).
r7-E-IGIHE-093.vn: Verbatim on p14; translation accurate. AFC/M23 commander's statement relayed by Igihe; places Byamungu in Uvira on 10 December 2025.
src: Ubwo Umugaba Mukuru Wungirije wa AFC/M23, Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu yageraga mu Mujyi wa Uvira ku wa 10 Ukuboza 2025, yasabye ingabo z’u Burundi zikiri mu misozi miremire yo muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo ko zamanuka, zigataha mu mahoro.

Brig Gen Byamungu yagize ati “Abari mu misozi itandukanye, turabasaba kumanuka, bambuke umupaka, basubire iwabo amahoro. Nta kibazo dufitanye n’Abarundi kubera ko turi abaturanyi, twahoze turi abaturanyi

r7-E-IGIHE-094.s: Igihe reported that FARDC's military spokesperson in South Kivu, Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said in a communiqué that FARDC had been controlling Minembwe since the night of 17 June 2026, that Twirwaneho fighters were fleeing towards Walungu territory, and that FARDC had captured many MRDP-Twirwaneho and M23 fighters, weapons, ammunition and other military equipment.
r7-E-IGIHE-094.n: FARDC claim relayed by a partisan outlet, contested by Twirwaneho (E-IGIHE-a-095). Existing claims: r1-SKS-2026Q2-005 (Actualite.cd, Kalonji said FARDC had since the evening of Tuesday 16 June retaken positions), REC-0634, REC-0635, REC-0637.
r7-E-IGIHE-094.vn: Verbatim on p15; translation accurate. No figures for captured fighters. Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June.
src: Itangazo ryasohowe n’Umuvugizi w’igisirikare cya RDC muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo, Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, rivuga ko kiri kugenzura Minembwe kuva mu ijoro ryo ku wa 17 Kamena 2026, abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho bahunga berekeza muri Teritwari ya Walungu.
Lt Kalonji kandi yatangaje ko ingabo za RDC zafashe abarwanyi benshi ba MRDP-Twirwaneho na M23, intwaro, amasasu n’ibindi bikoresho bya gisirikare byinshi.

r7-E-IGIHE-095.s: Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho Vice-President Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza said the claim that DRC forces had taken Minembwe was false, and that Col Fidèle Rugabo affirmed that the group still controls Minembwe, saying 'The lies are many. Up to now we are still in Minembwe... Long live M23'.
r7-E-IGIHE-095.n: Party statements given to Igihe; the second is a direct quote. Counterclaim to the FARDC communiqué of E-IGIHE-a-094. UN Secretary-General later (July) recorded Twirwaneho and M23 regaining Point Zero (REC-0642).
r7-E-IGIHE-095.vn: Verbatim on p15; translation accurate. Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June. Party statements given to Igihe.
src: Kuri uyu wa 18 Kamena, IGIHE yavuganye na Visi Perezida wa MRDP-Twirwaneho ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, dipolomasi n’imiyoborere, Alexis Mugisha Nkurunziza, avuga ko ibivugwa ko ingabo za RDC zafashe Minembwe ari ibinyoma. Umwe mu bofisiye bakuru ba MRDP-Twirwaneho, Col Fidèle Rugabo, yashimangiye ko Minembwe ikigenzurwa n’uyu mutwe
Col Rugabo yagize ati "Ibinyoma ni byinshi. Kugeza ubu turacyari muri Minembwe. MRDP irakomeza irwanire abaturage bacu. Harakabaho M23."

r7-E-IGIHE-096.s: Igihe reported that MRDP-Twirwaneho President Dr Freddy Kaniki Rukema told journalists at a press conference in Goma on 18 June that DRC government forces had intensified attacks in Minembwe, that attacks on civilians there had increased and that the international community knew but was doing nothing; asked whether Minembwe had been taken, he said they had not done it and would not.
r7-E-IGIHE-096.n: Party statement at a press conference in Goma (AFC/M23-held city). Second excerpt is the answer to the journalist's question about Minembwe having been taken.
r7-E-IGIHE-096.vn: Verbatim on p15; removed the year "2026" from the statement because the excerpt prints only "18 Kamena" (date field keeps 2026-06-18). Contested control of Minembwe in June 2026: FARDC claimed it (Lt Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji); MRDP-Twirwaneho denied it. Another outlet quotes Kalonji dating the FARDC advance from the evening of 16 June. Party statement at a press conference in AFC/M23-held Goma.
src: Perezida wa MRDP-Twirwaneho, Dr. Freddy Kaniki Rukema, yabwiye abanyamakuru bateraniye mu kiganiro cyabereye mu Mujyi wa Goma kuri uyu wa 18 Kamena ko ingabo za Leta ya RDC zakajije ibitero muri Minembwe. Dr. Kaniki yatangaje ko ibitero biri kugabwa ku basivili muri Minembwe byakajije umurego, kandi ko umuryango mpuzamahanga ubizi ariko ntacyo uri kubikoraho.
Ntekereza ko bifuza ko baba babikoze. Ntibabikoze kandi ntibazabikora. Ibyo ubyandike ku rutare, ntibizahinduka.

r7-E-IGIHE-097.s: Igihe reported, citing reliable information from South Kivu, that despite the difficult mountainous terrain M23 fighters had reached Minembwe to join Twirwaneho in protecting the security of residents.
r7-E-IGIHE-097.n: Unnamed 'reliable information' in a partisan outlet; presence of M23 fighters in Minembwe is relevant to the Rwanda/M23 linkage question. UN Secretary-General (REC-0642) records Twirwaneho and M23 operating together near Minembwe in July.
r7-E-IGIHE-097.vn: Verbatim on p15. Anonymous "reliable information" in a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the protective purpose is the source's framing.
src: Amakuru yizewe ava muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo ahamya ko nubwo inzira zagoranye kuko iki gice ari icy’imisozi miremire, abarwanyi b’umutwe wa M23 bageze muri Minembwe bajya kwifatanya na Twirwaneho kurinda umutekano w’abahatuye.

r7-E-IGIHE-098.s: Igihe reported that Burundian troops had also reached the front to help the DRC forces take Minembwe commune, but that available information says they had recently lost many soldiers, some of whose bodies were loaded onto a truck and taken to Bujumbura.
r7-E-IGIHE-098.n: Unattributed claim ('amakuru ahari avuga'); no figures. Compare SOS Médias Burundi reports on repatriation of bodies (r1 / REC-0210 context).
r7-E-IGIHE-098.vn: Verbatim on p15; hedge preserved. Hedged and unattributed ("amakuru ahari avuga" = available information says); no figures.
src: Ingabo z’u Burundi na zo zageze ku rugamba kugira ngo zifashe iza RDC gufata iyi Komini ariko amakuru ahari avuga ko ziherutse kuhatakariza abasirikare benshi, imirambo imwe muri yo ipakirwa mu ikamyo, ijyanwa i Bujumbura.

r7-E-IGIHE-099.s: Igihe reported that on 25 December 2025 Wazalendo fighters appeared in Makobola centre (Fizi territory) saying they had driven AFC/M23 out, and that their spokesperson, named Winston Makufuli, said 'People should remain calm, we have taken Makobola back. We thank President Félix Tshisekedi who sent FARDC troops to protect our country's security'.
r7-E-IGIHE-099.n: Party claim relayed by Igihe; contested by Igihe's own reporting (E-IGIHE-a-100). Corroborates Umuryango's account (existing claim r7-E-UV-038 on AFC/M23 leaving Makobola on 25 December). Records: AFC/M23 had occupied Makobola 2 on 13-14 Dec (REC-0229).
r7-E-IGIHE-099.vn: Verbatim on p16; translation accurate. Accounts of AFC/M23's departure from Makobola differ: Wazalendo say they drove it out; Igihe's "reliable information" and a resident say it left without fighting.
src: Ku wa 25 Ukuboza 2025, iyi santere yagaragayemo abarwanyi bo mu ihuriro Wazalendo rishyigikiwe n’ubutegetsi bwa RDC, bemeza ko bakuye AFC/M23 muri iyi santere.

Umuvugizi w’abarwanyi bagaragaye muri Makobola witwa Winston Makufuli yagize ati “Abaturage bakomeze batuze, Makobola twayisubije. Turashimira Perezida Félix Tshisekedi wohereje ingabo za FARDC kugira ngo zirinde umutekano w’igihugu cyacu.”

r7-E-IGIHE-100.s: Igihe reported, on 'reliable information' and a resident's account, that AFC/M23 left Makobola without fighting, as 25 December was calm and residents were celebrating Christmas; a Makobola resident said that in the afternoon ("saa munani z'amanywa") they saw the fighters heading towards Uvira with their luggage and that FARDC and Wazalendo arrived a few minutes later.
r7-E-IGIHE-100.n: Unnamed resident and 'reliable information' in a partisan outlet; AFC/M23 had said it withdrew from Uvira by 18 December (E-IGIHE-a-102), so its presence heading to Uvira on 25 December is unexplained. Umuryango (r7-E-UV-038) says fighters were attacked as they left.
r7-E-IGIHE-100.vn: Verbatim on p16. Replaced the numeral "2 p.m." (not printed) with the source's own time expression. Accounts of AFC/M23's departure from Makobola differ: Wazalendo say they drove it out; Igihe's "reliable information" and a resident say it left without fighting. "Saa munani z'amanywa" is 2 p.m. in Kinyarwanda time reckoning. AFC/M23 said it had left Uvira by 18 December, so its fighters heading to Uvira on 25 December is not explained.
src: Nubwo Makufuli yatangaje ko ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryakuye AFC/M23 muri Makobola, amakuru yizewe ahamya ko AFC/M23 yahavuye nta mirwano ibaye kuko ku wa 25 Ukuboza hari hatuje, abaturage bizihiza Noheli.
Umuturage wo muri Makobola yagize ati "Saa munani z’amanywa ni bwo twababonye berekeza muri Uvira bafite imizigo yabo. Nyuma y’iminota mike, twabonye FARDC na Wazalendo bahagera.”

r7-E-IGIHE-101.s: Igihe reported that on 24 December there was heavy fighting in various parts of Makobola centre, caused by drone and heavy-weapon attacks launched by DRC forces and Wazalendo, at Makobola 1, Makobola 2, Kiringi, Kirambi and elsewhere, causing many residents to flee to safer areas including Uvira city.
r7-E-IGIHE-101.n: Single partisan source; related earlier fighting: REC-0236 (Bangwi and Makobola, 21 December).
r7-E-IGIHE-101.vn: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). Single Rwandan state-aligned source; attribution of the attacks to DRC forces and Wazalendo is Igihe's.
src: Ku wa 24 Ukuboza, mu duce dutandukanye tw’iyi santere habaye imirwano ikomeye yatewe n’ibitero bya drones n’intwaro ziremereye byatangijwe n’ingabo za RDC na Wazalendo. Iyi mirwano yabereye muri Makobola 1, Makobola 2, Kiringi, Kirambi n’ahandi yatumye abaturage benshi bahungira mu bice bitekanye birimo umujyi wa Uvira uri mu majyaruguru.

r7-E-IGIHE-102.s: Igihe reported that on the morning of 26 December DRC forces and Wazalendo fired on Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, by Uvira city, using war drones.
r7-E-IGIHE-102.n: The word 'ahaherera' in the original is translated 'adjoining' (uncertain). Umuryango (existing claim r7-E-UV-037) reports the same Kalundu attack, adding two AFC/M23 boats were hit. No casualty figures here.
r7-E-IGIHE-102.vn: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). "adjacent to" softened to "by". Single Rwandan state-aligned source; no casualty figures. "ahaherera ku mujyi wa Uvira" read as "by/at the edge of Uvira city". 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 101)
src: Mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 26 Ukuboza, Ingabo za RDC na Wazalendo byarashe ku cyambu cya Kalundu kiri ku Kiyaga cya Tanganyika, ahaherera ku mujyi wa Uvira, bikoresheje drones z’intambara.

r7-E-IGIHE-103.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 affirms that by 18 December all its fighters had left Uvira city, to build confidence in the Doha talks with the DRC government.
r7-E-IGIHE-103.n: AFC/M23's claim (partisan). The UN Group of Experts (r1-UC-RDF-011, REC-0005) says AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026, a month later; Ebuteli dates it 16 January. Discrepancy surfaced, not resolved. See REC-0127 (AFC/M23 announces unilateral withdrawal, competing statements).
r7-E-IGIHE-103.vn: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). AFC/M23's claim. The UN Group of Experts says AFC/M23 and RDF troops withdrew from Uvira on 18 January 2026; discrepancy surfaced, not resolved.
src: AFC/M23 yemeza ko tariki ya 18 Ukuboza abarwanyi bayo bose bari bamaze kuva mu Mujyi wa Uvira, mu kubaka icyizere mu biganiro biyihuriza na Leta ya RDC i Doha muri Qatar, kugira ngo impande zombi zigere ku masezerano y’amahoro.

r7-E-IGIHE-104.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 delegates returned to the Doha talks on 12 December, but the DRC government refused to send its delegates there, complaining that the alliance's fighters had taken Uvira city on 9 December.
r7-E-IGIHE-104.n: Igihe puts the taking of Uvira on 9 December; UN Group of Experts and others say 10 December (REC-0113; SOS Médias: night of 9 to 10 December). No DRC government statement found by this agent.
r7-E-IGIHE-104.vn: Removed the year from the statement because the excerpt prints only day and month (the date field keeps the year from the 26 Dec 2025 article). Igihe puts the taking of Uvira on 9 December; other sources give 10 December (night of 9-10). No DRC government statement checked.
src: Intumwa za AFC/M23 zasubiye mu biganiro i Doha tariki ya 12 Ukuboza, ariko Leta ya RDC yanze koherezayo intumwa zayo, yinubira ko abarwanyi b’iri huriro bafashe umujyi wa Uvira tariki ya 9 Ukuboza.

r7-E-IGIHE-105.s: Igihe reported that Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, President of the Council of Ministers of Togo and the mediator appointed by the African Union, made a visit of a few hours to Kinshasa on 22 December to discuss the war in eastern DRC.
r7-E-IGIHE-105.vn: Verbatim on p16; translation accurate. Mediator activity; Igihe report.
src: Perezida w’Inama y’Abaminisitiri ya Togo akaba n’umuhuza washyizweho n’Umuryango wa Afurika Yunze Ubumwe (AU), Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, yagiriye uruzinduko rw’amasaha make i Kinshasa tariki ya 22 Ukuboza, rwari rugamije kuganira ku ntambara yo mu burasirazuba bwa RDC.

r7-E-IGIHE-106.s: Igihe reported that Point-Zéro was captured by AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho fighters in the middle of the night of 4 July 2026, after heavy fighting against DRC forces allied with Burundian forces, Wazalendo and the FDLR.
r7-E-IGIHE-106.n: Corroborates REC-0553 and REC-0642 (UN Secretary-General: Twirwaneho and M23 regained control of Point Zero). FARDC announced a 'repli stratégique' (r6-F-FIZ-012).
r7-E-IGIHE-106.vn: Verbatim on p17; translation accurate. Capture date as Igihe states it ("mu gicuku cyo ku wa 4 Nyakanga 2026"); other records may give different dates for the Point-Zéro capture, not reconciled here. FDLR involvement is Igihe's claim.
src: Point-Zéro yafashwe n’abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 na MRDP-Twirwaneho mu gicuku cyo ku wa 4 Nyakanga 2026, nyuma y’imirwano ikomeye yabahanganishije n’ingabo za RDC zifatanyije n’iz’u Burundi, Wazalendo na FDLR.

r7-E-IGIHE-107.s: Igihe reported that in January 2026 Twirwaneho fighters had captured Point-Zéro and used it to block attacks that had long been launched on Minembwe, but were dislodged by DRC government forces using drones and warplanes.
r7-E-IGIHE-107.n: Compare Umuryango.rw (r7-E-FIZ-009): Twirwaneho took Point-Zéro on 16 January 2026. No record yet for the January capture or the subsequent loss.
r7-E-IGIHE-107.vn: Verbatim on p17. Igihe does not give exact dates for the January capture or loss; another outlet dates the capture 16 January 2026.
src: No muri Mutarama 2026, abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho bari bafashe Point-Zéro, bayifashisha mu gukumira ibitero byari bimaze igihe kirekire bigabwa kuri Minembwe, ariko bahakurwa n’ingabo za Leta ya RDC zifashishaga drones n’indege z’intambara.

r7-E-IGIHE-108.s: Azarias Ruberwa said, according to Igihe, that there is a serious humanitarian problem around Point-Zéro and Minembwe because attacks are launched as if the area were uninhabited, adding that he feared people might be displaced permanently.
r7-E-IGIHE-108.n: Commentary by a politician from Minembwe; not a party statement. The original contains a typo ('kgukomera').
r7-E-IGIHE-108.vn: Verbatim on p17. "kuhacika" can mean "vanish from there"; translation corrected. Ruberwa (former DRC Vice-President, from Minembwe) is quoted without a date or venue; the article also cites Jeune Afrique, so the quote may be relayed from there. Date is the Igihe article date. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 107)
src: Azarias Ruberwa yavuze ko ikibazo cy’ubutabazi muri ako gace kiri kgukomera kurushaho, kuko ibitero bigabwa nk’aho ari ahantu hadatuwe. Ati "Hari ikibazo gikomeye cy’ubutabazi. Bararwana nk’aho aka gace kadatuwemo n’abantu. Usibye ubwicanyi, mfite impungenge z’uko abantu bashobora kuhacika. Hari igihe abantu bashobora kurambirwa bakagenda burundu."

r7-E-IGIHE-109.s: Igihe reported that AFC/M23 said that as long as DRC government forces continue to fire blindly at areas it controls, including Point-Zéro, without regard for civilians living there, it will continue to fight for them and protect its positions.
r7-E-IGIHE-109.n: Party statement relayed by a partisan outlet.
r7-E-IGIHE-109.vn: Verbatim on p17; translation accurate. Party statement relayed by Igihe; undated.
src: AFC/M23 yatangaje ko mu gihe ingabo za Leta ya RDC zikomeje kurasa buhumyi mu bice igenzura birimo Point-Zéro, zititaye ku basivili bahatuye, izakomeza kubarwanirira, inarinda ibirindiro byayo.

r7-E-IGIHE-110.s: Igihe reported that in recent days the alliance of forces supporting the DRC government launched drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Point Zéro, trying to retake it and continuing into the centre of Minembwe, but that Twirwaneho and AFC/M23 fighters held firm.
r7-E-IGIHE-110.a: Forces supporting the DRC government (alleged); AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (defending)
r7-E-IGIHE-110.n: Compare Actualite.cd on clashes at Point Zéro and Nyaruhinga on 30 September (REC-0661) and the 28 and 31 August reports (REC-0559, REC-0657).
r7-E-IGIHE-110.vn: Verbatim on p17. Igihe narration; dates not given ("mu minsi ya vuba" = in recent days, before 25 Sept 2026).
src: Mu minsi ya vuba, ihuriro ry’ingabo zishyigikiye Leta ya RDC zagabye ibitero bya drones n’intwaro ziremereye muri Point Zéro, bishaka kuyisubiza, bigakomereza rwagati muri Minembwe ariko abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho na AFC/M23 bazibereye ibamba.

r7-E-IGIHE-111.s: According to Igihe, AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 10 October 2026 that forces including those of the DRC, FDLR, Maï-Maï groups, foreign mercenaries and Burundian soldiers launched drone attacks on the night of 9 October 2026 ("saa yine z'ijoro", about 10 p.m.) on Point Zéro village and surroundings, and similar attacks later that night ("saa saba z'ijoro" of 9 into 10 October) at Rugezi and surroundings in Minembwe; he said the attacks on inhabited areas caused deaths and mass flight.
r7-E-IGIHE-111.a: DRC forces, FDLR, Mai-Mai groups, foreign mercenaries and Burundian soldiers (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-E-IGIHE-111.x: no toll given (Igihe: AFC/M23 had not published the number of dead, wounded or displaced)
r7-E-IGIHE-111.n: Party allegation; AFC/M23 had not published a toll (p18: 'ntiratangaza umubare w'abiciwe'). Times: 'saa yine z'ijoro' = 10 p.m., 'saa saba z'ijoro' = 1 a.m. Compare Radio Maendeleo/SOS Médias on FRN claims at Rugezi in October 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-111.vn: Verbatim on p18; translations accurate. Replaced "1 a.m." (numeral not printed) with the source's time expression and spelled Maï-Maï as printed. AFC/M23 allegation; no toll published (Igihe: AFC/M23 had not given the number of dead, injured or displaced). "Saa saba z'ijoro" is 1 a.m. in Kinyarwanda time reckoning.
src: Kuri uyu wa 10 Ukwakira 2026, Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko izi ngabo zirimo iza RDC, FDLR, imitwe ya Maï-Maï, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga ndetse n’abasirikare b’u Burundi.

Kanyuka yavuze ko ahagana saa yine z’ijoro ryo ku wa 9 Ukwakira 2026, izi ngabo zagabye ibitero by’indege zitagira abapilote, zirasa mu mudugudu wa Point Zéro no mu bice biwukikije. Yavuze ko ahagana saa saba z’ijoro ryo ku wa 9 rishyira ku wa 10 Ukwakira, ibitero nk’ibyo byagabwe muri Rugezi no mu bice bihakikije, na ho muri Minembwe.
Kanyuka yatangaje ko ibi bitero byagabwe mu duce dutuwe n’abaturage byateje impfu, benshi barahunga ndetse byongera ubukana bw’ikibazo cy’ubutabazi kimaze igihe muri iki gice.

r7-E-IGIHE-112.s: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that from the early hours of 20 April 2026 the coalition of DRC government forces launched a suicide-drone attack on the Mikenke area in Minembwe commune.
r7-E-IGIHE-112.a: AFC/M23 (spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka); alleged perpetrator: ihuriro ry'ingabo za Leta ya RDC (DRC government forces coalition)
r7-E-IGIHE-112.n: Party account only; Igihe is Rwandan state-aligned and does not say where Kanyuka spoke. 'Saa cyenda y'urukerera' is Kinyarwanda clock reckoning (about 03:00). Related existing records: FARDC said on 19 April that AFC/M23 drones hit its positions at Mikenge and Kakenge (REC-0621); Kanyuka's 25-26 April statement (REC-0622). No FARDC reply to the 20 April claim found in this page.
r7-E-IGIHE-112.vn: Page carries the sentence verbatim; attributed to Kanyuka. Capitalised-word flag is DRC/RDC rendering; translation clarified for the clock time. Party account (AFC/M23) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; no FARDC reply on this page. 'Saa cyenda' is Kinyarwanda clock time, about 03:00. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 111)
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko guhera mu masaa cyenda y’urukerera rwo kuri uyu wa 20 Mata 2026, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryagabye igitero cya drones z’ubwiyahuzi mu gace ka Mikenke muri Komini Minembwe.

r7-E-IGIHE-113.s: AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that at 5:30 government coalition forces also attacked the densely populated area of Mitimingi in Masisi territory, causing much damage and making many families flee; Igihe places this in its account of attacks on 20 April 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-113.a: AFC/M23 (spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka); alleged perpetrator: 'izi ngabo' (the DRC government forces coalition)
r7-E-IGIHE-113.n: No casualty figure given. 'Izi ngabo' refers back to the previous sentence (DRC government coalition). Igihe's lede claims the shelling 'is taking the lives of many civilians' in its own voice; the excerpt does not support a toll.
r7-E-IGIHE-113.vn: Flagged figures (20, 2026, M23) were outside the excerpt; replacement quote now spans the contiguous preceding sentence that prints them. Statement narrowed so the date is Igihe's context, not part of Kanyuka's quote. Party account only. Igihe does not say whether '5:30' is clock time or Kinyarwanda reckoning (which would be 11:30); the date 20 April comes from the preceding sentence. No casualty figure given; Igihe's own lede asserting civilian deaths is not supported by any quoted figure. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: integrator: full translation of the replaced excerpt (the earlier excerpt_en covered only its last sentences)
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko guhera mu masaa cyenda y’urukerera rwo kuri uyu wa 20 Mata 2026, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryagabye igitero cya drones z’ubwiyahuzi mu gace ka Mikenke muri Komini Minembwe. Kanyuka yagize ati "Saa 5:30, izi ngabo zanagabye igitero ku gace gatuwe cyane ka Mitimingi muri teritwari ya Masisi, hangirika byinshi, imiryango myinshi irahunga."

r7-E-IGIHE-114.s: Igihe reported that in the night of 18 to 19 April 2026 the DRC government forces coalition launched heavy-weapon and suicide-drone attacks on areas including Kalingi and Bidegu in Minembwe and on Mitimingi and neighbouring areas.
r7-E-IGIHE-114.l: Kalingi, Bidegu (Minembwe commune, South Kivu); Mitimingi (Masisi, North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-114.a: ihuriro ry'ingabo za Leta ya RDC (DRC government forces coalition), as Igihe names it
r7-E-IGIHE-114.n: The sentence is stated in Igihe's own voice but sits between Kanyuka's statements and is almost certainly AFC/M23-sourced; no source named. Compare FARDC's own 19 April statement (REC-0621), which says AFC/M23 drones struck FARDC positions at Mikenge and Kakenge.
r7-E-IGIHE-114.vn: Supported verbatim; attribution kept to Igihe. Translation adequate. Igihe's own voice, sitting between quotes of AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka and probably sourced to AFC/M23; no independent confirmation. The statement's year 2026 is the article's (published 20 April 2026).
src: Mu ijoro ryo ku wa 18 rishyira uwa 19 Mata, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC ryagabye ibitero by’imbunda ziremereye na drones z’ubwiyahuzi mu duce turimo Kalingi na Bidegu muri Minembwe na Mitimingi no mu bice bihana imbibi.

r7-E-IGIHE-115.s: AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 continues to point to repeated, deliberate breaches of the ceasefire by the Kinshasa government and that it is fully ready to defend civilians and to set up a proper security space to protect the population.
r7-E-IGIHE-115.l: Minembwe and Masisi (South and North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-115.n: Party statement; the date is the article date (20 April 2026) and Igihe does not say when Kanyuka spoke.
r7-E-IGIHE-115.vn: 'Kugaragaza' is 'to show/point out', not 'document'; softened. Full name (Lawrence Kanyuka) is printed earlier on the page; kept to the surname the excerpt prints. Party statement; Igihe does not say when or where Kanyuka said it (article dated 20 April 2026).
src: Kanyuka yagize ati "AFC/M23 ikomeje kugaragaza ukurenga ku gahenge kenshi, gukorwa nkana na Leta ya Kinshasa. Ishimangira ko yiteguye rwose kurwanirira abasivili no gushyiraho umwanya ukwiye w’umutekano kugira ngo turinde abaturage intambara dushozwaho na Leta."

r7-E-IGIHE-116.s: Igihe reported that the DRC government and AFC/M23 had agreed that the work of an international body to monitor compliance with the ceasefire in North Kivu and South Kivu would start soon, and that the agreement launching the body's activities was signed in Switzerland on 14 April.
r7-E-IGIHE-116.l: Switzerland (talks); body covers North Kivu and South Kivu
r7-E-IGIHE-116.n: Independently documented elsewhere in the project: the UN Group of Experts places the Doha-process talks in Montreux between 13 and 17 April 2026 (claim r2-G-DOC-466-046) and a joint statement of 19 April exists (r1-ST-MED-2026-008); neither is linked to a record. Igihe is cited only for the 14 April signing date and the 'monitoring body starts soon' wording.
r7-E-IGIHE-116.vn: Supported verbatim, but sole source is partisan_rwanda: grade lowered B to C per the rule for Igihe without an independent origin on the claim itself. Single partisan (Rwandan state-aligned) source on this claim; other project records (UN Group of Experts, joint statement) cover the Switzerland talks but are not cited here. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 115)
src: Leta ya RDC ikomeje kugaba ibitero nyuma y’aho yo na AFC/M23 byumvikanye ko imirimo y’urwego mpuzamahanga ruzajya rugenzura iyubahirizwa ry’agahenge mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru na Kivu y’Amajyepfo, itangira vuba.

Amasezerano atangiza ibikorwa by’uru rwego yasinyiwe mu Busuwisi tariki ya 14 Mata, ubwo impande zombi zari zikomeje ibiganiro by’amahoro byibandaga ahanini ku korohereza abari mu bikorwa byo gutabara abagizweho ingaruka n’intambara.

r7-E-IGIHE-117.s: AFC/M23 told Congolese and the international community, according to Igihe, that the Kinshasa government was putting war first, while Igihe reported that DRC forces were still launching drone and heavy-weapon attacks on Minembwe and Masisi while the talks that began on 13 April were under way.
r7-E-IGIHE-117.a: AFC/M23; DRC government forces (as Igihe names them)
r7-E-IGIHE-117.n: The first sentence is in Igihe's own voice and the second is AFC/M23's position; the page does not say who first reported the attacks.
r7-E-IGIHE-117.vn: Both sentences verbatim on the page; attribution split correctly. The attacks are asserted in Igihe's own voice (Rwandan state-aligned), the 'war first' line is AFC/M23's position; no independent confirmation.
src: Ubwo ibi biganiro byatangiye tariki ya 13 Mata byari bikomeje, Leta ya RDC yari ikigaba ibitero bya drones n’intwaro ziremereye muri Minembwe na Masisi. AFC/M23 yamenyesheje Abanye-Congo n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko Leta ishyize imbere intambara.

r7-E-IGIHE-118.s: AFC/M23 said, according to Igihe, that no residents of Minembwe commune would be killed again by the government forces coalition because the war there was over; AFC/M23 deputy leader for political affairs, diplomacy and governance Bertand Bisimwa (as Igihe spells the name) delivered the message to Minembwe residents.
r7-E-IGIHE-118.n: Existing claim r1-ST-M23-2026-014 (Umuryango) carries the same announcement under REC-0642. Date: Igihe says the leaders' celebration in Minembwe was on 8 July; the address date itself is not stated.
r7-E-IGIHE-118.vn: 'Bertrand' is not printed anywhere on the page (Igihe prints 'Bertand'); removed the unprinted spelling. Otherwise verbatim. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe (article of 11 July 2026); Igihe gives 8 July as the day of the celebration in Minembwe but not the exact date of the address.
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ryatangaje ko nta baturage bo muri Komini ya Minembwe bazongera kwicwa n’ihuriro ry’Ingabo za Leta kuko intambara yaho yarangiye.

Umuyobozi wungirije wa AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, dipolomasi n’imiyoborere, Bertand Bisimwa, yagejeje ubu butumwa ku baturage ba Minembwe nyuma y’aho ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, FDLR na Wazalendo byambuwe ibice birimo Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu na Rwitsankuku.

r7-E-IGIHE-119.s: Igihe reported that the DRC, Burundian, FDLR and Wazalendo forces were dispossessed of areas including Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu and Rwitsankuku, and that once these areas were taken senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them.
r7-E-IGIHE-119.l: Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu, Rwitsankuku (Minembwe area, South Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-119.a: AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho (as Igihe presents the capture)
r7-E-IGIHE-119.n: Igihe says 'byambuwe' (were dispossessed of) without naming the taker in that sentence; the second passage says the areas 'having been taken' were visited by AFC/M23 leaders. Compare the Radio Okapi account of a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' from Point Zéro (r6-F-FIZ-012, REC-0642). Igihe's own dated account of Point-Zéro on 4 July is in the p33 claims.
r7-E-IGIHE-119.vn: Removed the article date (11), which no excerpt prints; otherwise supported. Territorial claim in the voice of Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; the sentence does not name who took the areas or when. Other project sources describe a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' from Point Zéro; Igihe's own p33 article dates Point-Zéro's fall to 4 July.
src: Umuyobozi wungirije wa AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, dipolomasi n’imiyoborere, Bertand Bisimwa, yagejeje ubu butumwa ku baturage ba Minembwe nyuma y’aho ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, FDLR na Wazalendo byambuwe ibice birimo Point-Zéro, Mikenke, Kalingi, Ilundu na Rwitsankuku.

Ibi bice bimaze gufatwa, abayobozi bakuru muri AFC/M23 barimo Bisimwa, Dr. Freddy Kaniki ushinzwe ubukungu n’imari muri iri huriro akanaba Perezida wa MRDP Twirwaneho n’Umugaba Mukuru wungirije wa M23, Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, barabisuye.

r7-E-IGIHE-120.s: Igihe reported that once the Minembwe-area positions were taken, senior AFC/M23 leaders visited them, including Bisimwa, Dr. Freddy Kaniki (in charge of economy and finance in the alliance and President of MRDP Twirwaneho) and Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu (Deputy Commander-in-Chief of M23); it also states that 8 July was a day of songs of thanks for the residents of Minembwe.
r7-E-IGIHE-120.n: Roles as Igihe prints them. The visit date is not given precisely; 8 July is the date of the celebration. Photo captions on the page also place Kanyuka and 'PC Mavugo' of MRDP-Twirwaneho in Minembwe.
r7-E-IGIHE-120.vn: Full first name 'Bertand' is not in either excerpt; narrowed to 'Bisimwa'. Otherwise verbatim. Roles as Igihe prints them. The visit date is not stated; 8 July is the date of the celebration. Photo captions also place Lawrence Kanyuka and 'PC Mavugo' of MRDP-Twirwaneho in Minembwe and Byamungu at Point-Zéro. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 119)
src: Ibi bice bimaze gufatwa, abayobozi bakuru muri AFC/M23 barimo Bisimwa, Dr. Freddy Kaniki ushinzwe ubukungu n’imari muri iri huriro akanaba Perezida wa MRDP Twirwaneho n’Umugaba Mukuru wungirije wa M23, Brig Gen Bernard Byamungu, barabisuye.
Tariki ya 8 Nyakanga wari umunsi w’indirimbo z’amashimwe ku batuye muri Minembwe, ziherekejwe n’imbyino z’igisirimba.

r7-E-IGIHE-121.s: AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertand Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 fighters from many parts of the country and MRDP Twirwaneho had united to stop what he described as a plan by the DRC government forces to wipe out Congolese because of their ethnic origin.
r7-E-IGIHE-121.a: AFC/M23 (Bertand Bisimwa); alleged: ingabo za Leta ya RDC (DRC government forces)
r7-E-IGIHE-121.n: Allegation of intent by a party leader; no evidence cited in the article. 'Kurimbura' rendered 'wipe out'; no legal label is applied.
r7-E-IGIHE-121.vn: Verbatim; 'kurimbura Abanye-Congo zibahora ubwoko bwabo' = wipe out Congolese because of their ethnicity. Attributed. Allegation of intent by a party leader (AFC/M23) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; no evidence cited.
src: Bisimwa yatangaje ko abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bakomoka mu bice byinshi by’igihugu n’aba MRDP Twirwaneho zunze ubumwe kugira ngo zihagarike umugambi w’ingabo za Leta ya RDC zifite umugambi wo kurimbura Abanye-Congo zibahora ubwoko bwabo.

r7-E-IGIHE-122.s: The AFC/M23-appointed Governor of North Kivu, Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, asked residents of the Binza groupement (Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, near the Ugandan border) to distance themselves from the FDLR, telling them its founders had shed innocent blood in Rwanda, according to Igihe.
r7-E-IGIHE-122.l: Binza groupement, Bwisha chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-122.n: 'Terrorist group' is Igihe's/the speaker's wording, not ours. The exact date of the visit is not given; article dated 26 Feb 2026. REC-0869 covers a tour of the neighbouring Bwito chiefdom from 12 Feb 2026.

src: Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, yasabye abaturage kwitandukanya n’umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR, abamenyesha ko abawushinze bamennye amaraso y’inzirakarengane mu Rwanda.

Ubu butumwa yabuhaye abatuye muri Sheferi ya Bwisha, Gurupoma ya Binza, muri teritwari ya Rutshuru, hafi y’umupaka wa Uganda, ubwo yabasuraga, aherekejwe n’abandi bayobozi bo ku rwego rwa politiki n’urw’umutekano.

r7-E-IGIHE-123.s: Igihe quoted Governor Bahati as saying FDLR members are thieves who spend their days deceiving residents, robbing them and raping women and girls. No date, place, victim or incident is given.
r7-E-IGIHE-123.l: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu), general allegation
r7-E-IGIHE-123.a: Allegation by AFC/M23 governor against FDLR
r7-E-IGIHE-123.n: Generalised accusation by a party official; a lead only. 'Gusambanya ku gahato' translated as 'to rape by force'. No incident, victim count or date. Not an established finding.
r7-E-IGIHE-123.vn: 'AFC/M23' (flagged 23) is not in the excerpt; moved the affiliation to the note. 'Gusambanya ku gahato' = rape (force). Generalised accusation by an AFC/M23-appointed governor (identified at the top of the article), relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; a lead only, no incident, victim or date.
src: Guverineri Bahati yavuze ko abagize FDLR ari ibisambo by’inda mbi, byirirwa bishuka abaturage, bikabambura, bigasambanya abagore n’abakobwa ku gahato.

r7-E-IGIHE-124.s: Igihe quoted governor Bahati as saying, of the FDLR ('those bandits'), that what they can do is ambush vehicles, loot, and kill those inside; the passage gives no date, place or incident.
r7-E-IGIHE-124.a: Allegation by AFC/M23 governor against FDLR
r7-E-IGIHE-124.n: The speaker is Governor Bahati by context (the preceding sentences of the article); the 'Ati' attribution carries over. Generalised accusation, no incident.
r7-E-IGIHE-124.vn: Speaker is clear: 'Ati' directly follows 'Guverineri Bahati yavuze...'. Replacement quote spans the two contiguous sentences so the name is printed; AFC/M23 moved out of the statement (flagged 23). src: Guverineri Bahati yavuze ko abagize FDLR ari ibisambo by’inda mbi, byirirwa bishuka abaturage, bikabambura, bigasambanya abagore n’abakobwa ku gahato. Ati “Ariya mabandi ntazigera agira igihugu nk’uko tugifite uku, icyo bashoboye ni ukujya batega ibico imodoka, bagasahura, abazirimo bakabica, ari na wo muvumo ubariho.”

r7-E-IGIHE-125.s: Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, the provincial governor appointed by AFC/M23, said, according to Igihe, of the FDLR, that 'we know well that they are still in the forests, and we will not cease to fight them until we defeat them.'
r7-E-IGIHE-125.n: Speaker identified by the article's context (quote from the speech by Governor Bahati). The sentence in the excerpt is itself the continuation of a quoted speech, so the attribution is contextual.
r7-E-IGIHE-125.vn: Rendered as 'we' (the speaker's word) rather than 'AFC/M23 knows'; replacement quote spans the contiguous opening paragraphs so the speaker and affiliation are printed. Speaker is Bahati by context: the quote follows the paragraph on his Binza visit. 'They' is the FDLR by context. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe.
src: Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, Col Bahati Musanga Erasto, yasabye abaturage kwitandukanya n’umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR, abamenyesha ko abawushinze bamennye amaraso y’inzirakarengane mu Rwanda. Ubu butumwa yabuhaye abatuye muri Sheferi ya Bwisha, Gurupoma ya Binza, muri teritwari ya Rutshuru, hafi y’umupaka wa Uganda, ubwo yabasuraga, aherekejwe n’abandi bayobozi bo ku rwego rwa politiki n’urw’umutekano. Ati “Bariho umuvumo w’Imana, ntibazabasha no kugera ku nzozi zabo zo gutaha bagafata igihugu baturutsemo, kuko bakivuyemo bamennye amaraso y’inzirakarengane, bageze na hano bakomeza kuyamena, ni byo biri kubakurikirana, ubu bariho amaraso afite urubanza. Turabizi neza ko bakiri mu mashyamba, kandi ntituzahwema kubarwanya kugeza tubatsinze.”

r7-E-IGIHE-126.s: Igihe reported that Governor Bahati indicated that if FDLR fighters were not supported by some of the residents who take them food in the forests, they would leave it and hand themselves over to AFC/M23, which would hand them to Rwanda.
r7-E-IGIHE-126.n: Describes an announced handover pathway (AFC/M23 to Rwanda) for FDLR fighters; useful lead on repatriation/transfers. No individual case named.
r7-E-IGIHE-126.vn: Verbatim; replacement quote spans the contiguous sentences that name Bahati. The speaker is Bahati by context ('Yagaragaje' continues his remarks). Party statement; describes an announced AFC/M23-to-Rwanda handover pathway, no individual case.
src: Guverineri Bahati yavuze ko abagize FDLR ari ibisambo by’inda mbi, byirirwa bishuka abaturage, bikabambura, bigasambanya abagore n’abakobwa ku gahato. Ati “Ariya mabandi ntazigera agira igihugu nk’uko tugifite uku, icyo bashoboye ni ukujya batega ibico imodoka, bagasahura, abazirimo bakabica, ari na wo muvumo ubariho.” Yagaragaje ko abarwanyi ba FDLR baramutse badashyigikiwe na bamwe mu baturage babajyanira ibyo kurya mu mashyamba, bayivanamo bakishyikiriza AFC/M23, ikabashyikiriza u Rwanda.

r7-E-IGIHE-127.s: Igihe reported that in November 2025 the vice-president of Rwanda's national demobilisation and reintegration commission (RDRC), Maj Gen (Rtd) Jacques Nziza, explained that in 10 months Rwanda had received more than 200 FDLR fighters.
r7-E-IGIHE-127.l: Rwanda (receiving FDLR fighters from eastern DRC)
r7-E-IGIHE-127.x: Igihe, citing RDRC: more than 200 FDLR fighters received in 10 months
r7-E-IGIHE-127.n: Rwandan official figure as relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the 10-month window is not anchored to dates in the passage.
r7-E-IGIHE-127.vn: Verbatim on the page; figures and name match. Rwandan official figure relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; the 10-month window is not anchored to dates.
src: Mu Ugushyingo 2025, Visi Perezida wa Komisiyo y’Igihugu Ishinzwe Gusezerera no Gusubiza mu buzima busanzwe abari abarwanyi (RDRC), Maj Gen (Rtd) Jacques Nziza, yasobanuye ko mu mezi 10, u Rwanda rwakiriye abarwanyi barenga 200 ba FDLR.

r7-E-IGIHE-128.s: Igihe reported, citing a UN report it does not name, that FDLR fighters captured and repatriated to Rwanda since AFC/M23 took Goma in January 2025 are far more numerous than those who returned while the DRC government controlled the area.
r7-E-IGIHE-128.l: Areas under AFC/M23 control in North Kivu; Rwanda
r7-E-IGIHE-128.n: The UN report is not named or dated; the claim should be checked against the Group of Experts reports before use. No figure given.
r7-E-IGIHE-128.vn: Verbatim; attribution to an unnamed UN report kept as Igihe's claim. Igihe cites an unnamed, undated UN report; check against the UN Group of Experts reports before use. No figure given.
src: Raporo y’Umuryango w’Abibumbye igaragaza ko abarwanyi ba FDLR bafashwe, bagacyurwa mu Rwanda kuva AFC/M23 yafata umujyi wa Goma muri Mutarama 2025, ari benshi cyane ugereranyije n’abatashye mu gihe Leta ya RDC yahagenzuraga.

r7-E-IGIHE-129.s: AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa criticised the United Nations on X, according to Igihe, after the UN sanctioned several AFC/M23 leaders, saying it had been misled and was driven by emotion, and that sanctioning only the side that respects its peace commitments showed the UN had lost its way.
r7-E-IGIHE-129.n: Igihe does not link or date the X post. The article's original post is not cited by URL; per project rules, cite the outlet and treat the post as a lead only. Related existing claims on the listing: r1-UC-M23-033/-034/-035 (no record).
r7-E-IGIHE-129.vn: Verbatim; attribution correct. Party statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe (article of 19 July 2026); the X post is not linked or dated. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 128)
src: Umuyobozi wungirije w’Ihuriro AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibikorwa bya politiki, dipolomasi n’imiyoborere, Bertrand Bisimwa, yanenze Umuryango w’Abibumbye uheruka gufatira ibihano bamwe mu bayobozi b’iryo huriro, agaragaza ko wavangiwe kandi uyoborwa n’amarangamutima.
Yabigarutseho yifashishije konti ye ya X aho yagaragaje ko gufatira ibihano uruhande rumwe kandi runubahiriza ibyo rusabwa mu rugendo rw’amahoro bishimangira ko Loni yataye umurongo.

r7-E-IGIHE-130.s: Bisimwa said, according to Igihe, that putting pressure on people affected by ethnic discrimination to leave their land is a grave mistake that will have consequences.
r7-E-IGIHE-130.n: Speaker is Bisimwa by the article's context; the excerpt starts at the verb 'Yagaragaje' (he showed).
r7-E-IGIHE-130.vn: Verbatim; replacement quote extends to the contiguous sentences that name Bisimwa. Speaker is Bisimwa by context (the paragraph continues his remarks and the next sentence names him). Party statement relayed by Igihe; not stated whether this was on X.
src: Yagaragaje ko gushyira igitutu ku bagizweho ingaruka n’ibikorwa by’ivangura bishingiye ku moko ngo bave ku butaka bwabo ari ikosa rikomeye kandi rizagira ingaruka. Yerekanye ko ibyo bishobora kugira ingaruka ku kuba impande zihanganye zakomeza gukaza umurego, kwiyongera no kurushaho gukomere kw’ibikorwa by’urugomo n’ihohoterwa no kudindira ku rugendo rugamije kugera ku mahoro. Bisimwa yavuze ko politiki ishingiye ku rwango no ku ivangura, n'iyo yashyigikirwa n'Isi yose, idashobora na rimwe gutsinda ubutabera n'amahoro arambye.

r7-E-IGIHE-131.s: Igihe reported that the UN had recently imposed sanctions on AFC/M23 coordinator Corneille Nangaa, on Col Nzenze Imani, described as in charge of intelligence and military operations in the alliance, and on Brig Gen Charles Sematama, who leads Twirwaneho in Minembwe commune; Igihe wrote that Sematama was sanctioned for leading a group accused of "killing civilians, recruiting children into the army and engaging in activities that disturb the peace and security of the population."
r7-E-IGIHE-131.l: UN Security Council (listing); persons active in North and South Kivu
r7-E-IGIHE-131.a: UN Security Council (as Igihe names it); Corneille Nangaa; Col Nzenze Imani; Brig Gen Charles Sematama
r7-E-IGIHE-131.n: The listing is independently documented in existing claims (r1-UC-M23-033, -035 7sur7.cd citing a UN communiqué of 14 July 2026; r4-G-LOCAL/SECO r4-G-CMD-LEGAL-001); none is linked to a record. Igihe's wording 'Col Nzenze Imani' differs from OFAC's 'John Imani Nzenze' (r1-UC-M23-004). The quoted grounds for Sematama are Igihe's rendering, in Kinyarwanda, of the UN listing grounds.
r7-E-IGIHE-131.vn: Sole source is Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; grade lowered B to C (the independent UN-listing claims are separate). Statement extended with source 1, which the original did not use. Igihe's name order 'Col Nzenze Imani' differs from OFAC's 'John Imani Nzenze' in other project claims. The listing grounds are Igihe's Kinyarwanda rendering of the UN text, not the UN text itself. The page adds that the Security Council was presided by the DRC from July 2026.
src: Ibihano Bisimwa yavugaga ni ibyo Loni iheruka gufatira Umuhuzabikorwa wa AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, Col Nzenze Imani ushinzwe iperereza n’ibikorwa bya gisirikare muri iri huriro na Brig Gen Charles Sematama uyobora umutwe wa Twirwaneho ukorera muri Komini Minembwe.
Brig Gen Sematama we akazira kuyobora umutwe ushinjwa "kwica abasivili, kwinjiza abana mu gisirikare no kujya mu bikorwa bihungabanya amahoro n’umutekano by’abaturage."

r7-E-IGIHE-132.s: AFC/M23 deputy leader and MRDP-Twirwaneho President Freddy Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that forces supporting the DRC government had again besieged Minembwe commune in South Kivu.
r7-E-IGIHE-132.a: AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho (Freddy Kaniki); alleged: DRC government-supporting forces
r7-E-IGIHE-132.n: Party statement. The Group of Experts independently describes Minembwe as encircled by FARDC and allied forces since mid-2025 (r1-GOE-020, REC-0620), and also that MRDP/Twirwaneho prevented civilians from leaving (REC-0183). Kinshasa's reply to this 21 Sept claim not found in this page.
r7-E-IGIHE-132.vn: Verbatim; the 21 September date comes from the next sentence of the page (claim 132). Party statement (AFC/M23 / MRDP-Twirwaneho) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe, article of 22 September 2026; no Kinshasa reply on this page.
src: Umuyobozi wungirije wa AFC/M23 akaba na Perezida wa MRDP-Twirwaneho, Freddy Kaniki, yavuze ko ingabo zishyigikiye ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi zongeye kugota Komini Minembwe mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo.

r7-E-IGIHE-133.s: Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that Minembwe was in a serious security situation and that the DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenary forces had chosen to breach the ceasefire agreement adopted at the Doha talks.
r7-E-IGIHE-133.a: AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho (Freddy Kaniki); alleged: DRC, Burundian, Wazalendo, FDLR forces and 'abacanshuro b’abanyamahahanga' (foreign mercenaries)
r7-E-IGIHE-133.n: Party allegation naming Burundian forces and 'foreign mercenaries'. Igihe spells 'abanyamahahanga' as printed. Related fighting on 27 and 30 Sept is in REC-0570/REC-0661.
r7-E-IGIHE-133.vn: Verbatim; date and parties match. Party allegation naming Burundian forces and 'foreign mercenaries' ('abacanshuro b’abanyamahahanga', as printed); relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 132)
src: Mu ijoro ryo ku wa 21 Nzeri 2026, Kaniki yatangaje ko Minembwe iri mu bihe bikomeye by’umutekano, agaragaza ko ingabo za Leta ya RDC, iz’u Burundi, Wazalendo, FDLR n’abacanshuro b’abanyamahahanga byahisemo kurenga ku masezerano y’agahenge yemejwe mu biganiro bya Doha.

r7-E-IGIHE-134.s: Kaniki said, according to Igihe, that residents of Minembwe had their routes closed to them for going to seek health care, for bringing food and for going to markets, contrary to the Doha resolutions.
r7-E-IGIHE-134.a: AFC/M23 and MRDP-Twirwaneho (Freddy Kaniki); alleged: government coalition forces besieging Minembwe
r7-E-IGIHE-134.n: Party allegation; no facility, patient or date of blockade specified. Independent context: UN Group of Experts on limits to movement and aid at Minembwe (REC-0620) and OCHA warnings on access to food and care (r1-UC-BI-FDLR-034); the GoE also reports that Twirwaneho itself restricted civilians leaving (REC-0183), so both-direction restrictions are on record.
r7-E-IGIHE-134.vn: Verbatim; translation smoothed. Party allegation; no facility, patient or date of closure given. Igihe adds in its own voice that the movement of residents was hampered by the attacks. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 133)
src: Kaniki yavuze ko abaturage bo muri Minembwe bafungiwe inzira banyuramo bajya kwivuza, banyuzamo ibiribwa ndetse bajya ku masoko; bihabanye n’imyanzuro yafatiwe mu biganiro bya Doha.

r7-E-IGIHE-135.s: Kaniki called on the international community, according to Igihe, to act before a serious humanitarian problem arises, saying AFC/M23 continues to support the political path but will not keep watching Minembwe residents being put in danger.
r7-E-IGIHE-135.n: Igihe also quotes Kaniki calling the situation a 'red line' (umurongo utukura). 'Amahanga' translated 'foreign countries / the international community'.
r7-E-IGIHE-135.vn: Verbatim; replacement quote spans the contiguous sentences naming Kaniki. Speaker is Kaniki by context ('Uyu muyobozi', this leader). Party statement relayed by Igihe. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: integrator: full translation of the replaced excerpt (the earlier excerpt_en covered only its last sentences)
src: Kaniki yavuze ko abaturage bo muri Minembwe bafungiwe inzira banyuramo bajya kwivuza, banyuzamo ibiribwa ndetse bajya ku masoko; bihabanye n’imyanzuro yafatiwe mu biganiro bya Doha. Yagize ati “Ibi ntibigomba gufatwa nk’ibisanzwe. Iki ni igihe cyo gufata icyemezo gikomeye. Uyu ni umurongo utukura.” Uyu muyobozi yavuze ko amahanga akwiye kugira icyo akora mbere y’uko habaho ikibazo gikomeye cy’ubutabazi, avuga ko AFC/M23 ikomeje gushyigikira inzira ya politiki ariko ko itazakomeza kurebera abaturage ba Minembwe bashyirwa mu kaga.

r7-E-IGIHE-136.s: Igihe reported that in early July 2026 AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho fighters had restored security in Minembwe by driving the DRC government forces coalition out of surrounding areas including Point-Zéro, and that the government forces were now launching strong attacks around Minembwe, including Point-Zéro, intending to retake them.
r7-E-IGIHE-136.l: Point-Zéro and areas around Minembwe (South Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-136.a: DRC government forces coalition (attacking); AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (holding), as Igihe describes
r7-E-IGIHE-136.n: Control claim stated in Igihe's own voice (no named source). Cross-check: Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd and Kivu Morning Post claims on fighting at Point Zéro on 28 Aug, 27 Sept and 30 Sept 2026 (REC-0559, REC-0657, REC-0570, REC-0661).
r7-E-IGIHE-136.vn: Both passages verbatim; attribution to Igihe kept. Control claims in the voice of Rwandan state-aligned Igihe, no named source; 'now' is the article's 22 September 2026. Other project sources (Radio Okapi, Actualite.cd, Kivu Morning Post) report fighting at Point Zéro in late August and late September 2026.
src: Muri iki gihe, ingabo za Leta ya RDC ziri kugaba ibitero bikomeye mu bice bikikije Minembwe birimo Point-Zéro, zifite intego yo kubyisubiza.

Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 na Twirwaneho bari barashoboye kugarura umutekano muri Minembwe mu ntangiriro za Nyakanga 2026 ubwo birukanaga ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya RDC mu bice bihakikije birimo Point-Zéro.

r7-E-IGIHE-137.s: Igihe reported that five people were killed in an attack in the night of 25 to 26 October 2026 at Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory; Euphrem Kabasha, Rutshuru territory administrator appointed by the FRN, said it was carried out by the FDLR together with the Nyatura CMC FDP of Gashegu Héritier and Mbitezi.
r7-E-IGIHE-137.l: Kabizo, Tongo groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-137.a: Euphrem Kabasha (Rutshuru territory administrator appointed by the FRN) as the source of the attribution
r7-E-IGIHE-137.x: Igihe, quoting Kabasha: five people killed; time given as 'saa saba z’ijoro' in the lede and 'ahagana saa 1:30' in the quote
r7-E-IGIHE-137.n: Same origin (Kabasha) as the existing Kivu Morning Post claim r1-UCD-NK-FARDC-WZ-017 (REC-0922), so no independent second origin. Attribution differs: Kivu Morning Post's headline/lede attributes the attack to 'Wazalendo CMC' (its piece, 26 Oct 2026), Igihe to the FDLR together with Nyatura CMC FDP; Igihe also names the FDLR as the author in its headline. Competing account on the same area: Wazalendo ambush of an FRN convoy near Kabizo and Katovu (REC-0921). A Serper search (fr, 24-29 Oct 2026) found no further independent outlet. No victim names printed. 'Kabizo yongeye kugabwaho' = Kabizo attacked 'again'.
r7-E-IGIHE-137.vn: Verbatim; the toll and attribution are Kabasha's (a de facto FRN/AFC-aligned administrator) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe. Attribution conflict: Kivu Morning Post (same origin, Kabasha) attributes the 26 October attack to 'Wazalendo CMC'; Igihe quotes Kabasha attributing it to the FDLR with Nyatura CMC FDP. Each stays as its source states. Same origin, so not independent. Time: lede 'saa saba z'ijoro' (about 01:00) vs quote 'saa 1:30'. No victim names printed. Kabizo was attacked 'again'. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 136)
src: Umuyobozi wa Teritwari ya Rutshuru washyizweho n’umutwe wa FRN, Euphrem Kabasha, yavuze ko iki gitero cyagabwe mu gace ka Kabizo kari muri Gurupoma ya Tongo muri Sheferi ya Bwito, mu masaa saba z’ijoro.

Yagize ati “Mu ijoro ryo ku wa 25 rishyira ku wa 26 Ukwakira, ahagana saa 1:30, Kabizo yongeye kugabwaho igitero cyahitanye abantu, cyagabwe na FDLR ifatanyije na Nyatura CMC FDP ya Gashegu Héritier na Mbitezi. Cyibasiye abaturage, abantu batanu baricwa.”

r7-E-IGIHE-138.s: Igihe reported that the fighting in Rutshuru territory had stopped farming activity in the areas of Kabizo and Katovu.
r7-E-IGIHE-138.l: Kabizo and Katovu, Rutshuru territory (North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-138.n: Igihe's own statement; compare the Kivu Morning Post/Cable CD reports of farmers deserting fields on 26 October 2026 after the convoy ambush (REC-0921).
r7-E-IGIHE-138.vn: Verbatim. Igihe's own statement, no named source (article of 26 October 2026).
src: Iki gitero kigabwe mu gihe umutekano muri Rutshuru ukomeje kuzamba, aho imirwano yatumye n’ibikorwa by’ubuhinzi bihagarara mu duce twa Kabizo na Katovu.

r7-E-IGIHE-139.s: Twirwaneho officer Col Fidèle Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that at 'saa cyenda z’urukerera' on 18 September 2026 DRC, Burundian, FDLR, P5 and Wazalendo forces attacked residents at Mukoko and Nyaruhinga, and that 'the enemy is being beaten like a drum'.
r7-E-IGIHE-139.a: MRDP Twirwaneho (Col Fidèle Rugabo); alleged: ingabo za RDC, iz'u Burundi, FDLR, P5 na Wazalendo
r7-E-IGIHE-139.n: Party account. 'P5' is printed without explanation (a Wazalendo-linked group name in other sources; not explained by Igihe). Time 'saa cyenda z'urukerera' = about 03:00 on the Kinyarwanda clock. FARDC/Kinshasa reply not found in this page.
r7-E-IGIHE-139.vn: Verbatim; clock time clarified in translation. Party account (MRDP Twirwaneho) relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; 'P5' not explained on the page. No FARDC reply here. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 138) 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 138)
src: Col Fidèle Rugabo uri mu bofisiye ba Twirwaneho yatangaje ko saa cyenda z’urukerera rwo ku wa 18 Nzeri 2026, ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, FDLR, P5 na Wazalendo byateye abaturage muri Mukoko na Nyaruhinga.
Yagize ati "Umwanzi mu cyerekezo cya Mukoko yateye abaturage saa cyenda z’urukerera. Umwanzi akaba arimo gukubitwa nk’ingoma."

src: Umutwe wa AFC/ M23 urwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, wahakanye amakuru avuga ko watangiye gukura abarwanyi mu bice bimwe byo mu Burasirazuba bw’igihugu ugenzura.
Mu itangazo ryashyizwe hanze na Guverineri w’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, Erasto Bahati, yahakanye iby’aya makuru, avuga ko ikiri kuba ari ugusimbuza ingabo.

Iri tangazo rivuga ko “Ubuyobozi bw’Intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru burahumuriza abatuye intara yose ko ibikorwa biri kuba ku mirongo y’urugamba ari gahunda isanzwe yo gusimbuza mu gisirikare cya AFC/M23.”
Ibi bitandukanye n’ibihuha byatijwe umurindi n’imbuga nkoranyambaga by’ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, bigamije gushyira abantu mu rujijo no gutera ubwoba ababayeho mu mahoro n’umutekano.

r7-E-IGIHE-165.s: Igihe reported that at the end of the week Congolese newspapers had begun writing that AFC/M23 was withdrawing fighters from areas of Lubero territory (Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese) and relocating them to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga; AFC/M23 denied this.
r7-E-IGIHE-165.l: Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi, Kipese; Alimbongo, Kirumba, Kanyabayonga (Lubero territory, North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-165.a: AFC/M23 (reported movement); Congolese media (source of the report)
r7-E-IGIHE-165.n: Igihe relays Congolese press and then AFC/M23's denial (see the denial claim). The 'US pressure' attribution is in the next sentence of the page (not cited). Radio Okapi, Anadolu and the North Kivu governor (REC-1008) independently reported a pull-back, so the claim is contested rather than denied by all sources; 'change: contested' reflects that.
r7-E-IGIHE-165.vn: Fixed a stray ', ;'. The denial clause was not in this claim's excerpt; replacement quote now spans the contiguous opening sentence that carries it. Igihe relays the Congolese press and AFC/M23's denial; the page adds that the press attributed the move to US pressure. Other project sources report a pull-back, so the movement is contested.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/ M23 urwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, wahakanye amakuru avuga ko watangiye gukura abarwanyi mu bice bimwe byo mu Burasirazuba bw’igihugu ugenzura. Mu mpera z’iki cyumweru nibwo ibinyamakuru byo muri RDC byatangiye kwandika ko AFC/M23 iri gukura abarwanyi mu bice byo muri Teritwari ya Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi na Kipese, bakimurirwa muri Alimbongo, Kirumba na Kanyabayonga.

src: Ubwo butumwa yatanze ku wa 21 Gashyantare 2025, abuherekesha ifoto ya Col Rukunda, Lt Col Ngoma yavuze ko abibwira ko bazatsemba Abanyamulenge bari muri RDC bibeshya, kandi ko vuba aba Banye-Congo bazabohorwa, bidegembye mu gihugu cyabo.
Nyuma y’urupfu rwa Col Rukunda alias Makanika, Umuvugizi wa M23 mu rwego rwa gisirikare, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, yasezeranyije Abanyamulenge kubabohora.

Orchestrator: reworded two words (Congolese, Igihe's) that promote flagged as unprinted; meaning unchanged. src: Yibukije Perelman ko ku 26 Kamena 2026, Umujyanama wa Perezida Trump mu bijyanye n’ubufatanye na Afurika, Massad Boulos, yabwiye Akanama k’Umuryango w’Abibumbye gashinzwe umutekano ko Leta ya RDC itigeze isenya FDLR byibura mu bice igenzura, agaragaza ko impamvu u Rwanda ari rwo rukomeje guhanwa itumvikana.

r7-E-IGIHE-179.s: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that DRC forces had also launched attacks on various areas controlled by AFC/M23 and MRDP Twirwaneho, killing many civilians, and asked how many civilians must die before it is understood that the DRC should respect the ceasefire.
r7-E-IGIHE-179.l: areas held by AFC/M23 and Twirwaneho (South and North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-179.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet reporting a Rwandan minister; a BBC News Gahuza report of the same France 24 interview exists (r7-L-RW-003, no record). 'Twirwanehomuri' is printed as one word in Igihe (typo for 'Twirwaneho muri'). No incident, place or toll named in the passage.
r7-E-IGIHE-179.vn: Verbatim. Rwandan foreign minister's statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe from a France 24 interview (article of 29 June 2026); the France 24 original was not checked. No incident, place or toll named. 'Twirwanehomuri' is an Igihe typo for 'Twirwaneho muri'.
src: Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yagaragaje ko ingabo za RDC zanagabye igitero mu bice bitandukanye bigenzurwa n’ihuriro AFC/M23 n’umutwe wa MRDP Twirwanehomuri, zica abasivili benshi, abaza ati “None ni abasivili bangahe bagomba gupfa kugira ngo twumve ko RDC ikwiye kubahiriza agahenge?”

r7-E-IGIHE-180.s: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US sanctions on Gasabo Refinery, its head and other mining companies on 25 June could bring no solution between Rwanda and the DRC and were biased, adding that sanctions are not a mediator's role.
r7-E-IGIHE-180.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet reporting a Rwandan minister; a BBC News Gahuza report of the same France 24 interview exists (r7-L-RW-003, no record). The sanctions themselves (OFAC, 25 June 2026) are not documented in this note; excerpt ends mid-quotation. Excerpt is 55 words.
r7-E-IGIHE-180.vn: Verbatim. Rwandan foreign minister's statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe from a France 24 interview (article of 29 June 2026); the France 24 original was not checked. The US sanctions of 25 June on Gasabo Refinery are described by Igihe, not documented here.
src: Ku bihano Amerika yafatiye Gasabo Refinery, umuyobozi wayo n’izindi sosiyete z’ubucukuzi bw’amabuye y’agaciro tariki ya 25 Kamena, Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yagaragaje ko nta gisubizo bishobora kuzana hagati y’u Rwanda na RDC. Yagize ati “Mbere na mbere, ibi bihano birabogamye. Bibogamira ku ruhande rumwe kandi nta musaruro byatanga. Gutanga ibihano si inshingano y’umuhuza.

r7-E-IGIHE-181.s: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the effects of bias had begun to show because DRC forces had stepped up attacks on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe commune and on AFC/M23 positions, since President Tshisekedi saw that the US would not penalise him.
r7-E-IGIHE-181.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet reporting a Rwandan minister; a BBC News Gahuza report of the same France 24 interview exists (r7-L-RW-003, no record). The subject of 'Yagaragaje' is Nduhungirehe by context. The excerpt prints 'Banyamulenge' (translated). Related: AFC/M23 and FARDC accounts of strikes around Minembwe (REC-0622, REC-0601).
r7-E-IGIHE-181.vn: Verbatim; replacement quote spans the contiguous preceding quote that names Nduhungirehe. Rwandan foreign minister's statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe from a France 24 interview (article of 29 June 2026); the France 24 original was not checked. Speaker is Nduhungirehe by context ('Yagaragaje' follows his quotes).
src: Yagize ati “Mbere na mbere, ibi bihano birabogamye. Bibogamira ku ruhande rumwe kandi nta musaruro byatanga. Gutanga ibihano si inshingano y’umuhuza. Niba umuhuza abona ko gufata ibihano ari ngombwa, kubifatira uruhande rumwe byoshya urundi.” Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yakomeje ati “Ariko ku rundi ruhande, tubwira umuhuza wa Amerika ko twagiranye amasezerano n’uruhande rwitwa RDC, rwemeye guhagarika imirwano no gusenya FDLR. Amahoro ntiyaboneka mu gihe uruhande rumwe ari rwo rwubahiriza ibyo rusabwa mu masezerano.” Yagaragaje ko ingaruka zo kubogama zatangiye kugaragara kuko ingabo za RDC zenyegeje ibitero ku Banyamulenge muri Komini Minembwe no ku birindiro bya AFC/M23 kubera ko Perezida Félix Tshisekedi yabonye ko Amerika ntacyo imutwara.

r7-E-IGIHE-182.s: Nduhungirehe said, according to Igihe, that the US had set no deadline for Rwanda to lift its defensive measures and that Rwanda itself had offered an idea of how both sides could speed up implementation of the Washington agreement; Igihe adds that Rubio told legislators he was confident Rwanda would lift them by mid-July 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-182.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet reporting a Rwandan minister; a BBC News Gahuza report of the same France 24 interview exists (r7-L-RW-003, no record). 'Ingamba z'ubwirinzi' (defensive measures) is the Rwandan government's term for its military posture/deployments; the passage does not define it. Nduhungirehe's own words 'nta gihe ntarengwa cyatanzwe na Amerika' (the US gave no deadline) are in the next sentence of the page, not in this excerpt.
r7-E-IGIHE-182.vn: The 'no deadline' clause was outside the excerpt; replacement quote extends to the contiguous next sentence. Rwandan foreign minister's statement relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe from a France 24 interview (article of 29 June 2026); the France 24 original was not checked. Rubio's statement is relayed second-hand; 'ingamba z'ubwirinzi' (defensive measures) is the Rwandan government's term, not defined here.
src: Muri icyo kiganiro n’abadepite, Minisitiri Rubio yababwiye ko afite icyizere ko hagati muri Nyakanga 2026, u Rwanda ruzaba rwakuyeho ingamba z’ubwirinzi rwashyizeho. Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yasobanuye ko ibyo byashingiye ku gitekerezo u Rwanda rwatanze. Ati “Icya mbere, nta gihe ntarengwa cyatanzwe na Amerika. Ni twebwe u Rwanda, mu rwego rwo kwihutisha ishyirwa mu bikorwa amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington agamije amahoro n’iterambere, twatanze igitekerezo cy’uburyo impande zombi zakwihutisha gushyira mu bikorwa ibyo ziyemeje.”

r7-E-IGIHE-183.s: Igihe reported that on 2 March 2026 the United States imposed sanctions on the Rwandan army and its officials, accusing them of violating the Washington peace agreement.
r7-E-IGIHE-183.n: Independently documented: US Treasury (OFAC) announcement of 2 March 2026 sanctioning the RDF and four senior officials (claim r1-POL-2026-001, no record linked). Igihe is cited only as a Rwandan outlet's confirmation.
r7-E-IGIHE-183.vn: Sole source is Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; grade lowered B to C. Statement verbatim. Igihe's own voice; the 2 March 2026 US sanctions on the RDF are documented independently (US Treasury) in another project claim, not cited here.
src: Tariki ya 2 Werurwe 2026, Amerika yafatiye ibihano ingabo z’u Rwanda n’abayobozi bazo, izishinja kurenga ku masezerano y’amahoro ya Washington.

r7-E-IGIHE-184.s: Twirwaneho officer Col Fidele Rugabo announced, according to Igihe, that Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi and Rubemba at 'saa munani y’igicuku' on 4 July 2026, ending military operations at Point-Zéro at 'saa munani n’iminota 35'.
r7-E-IGIHE-184.l: Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi, Rubemba (Fizi/Mwenga highlands, South Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-184.a: MRDP-Twirwaneho (Col Fidele Rugabo); FARDC, FDNB, FDLR and Wazalendo (dislodged, per Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-184.n: Independently documented by SOS Médias Burundi (r1-UV-2026Q3-003, REC-0553) and Radio Okapi, which reports a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' from Point Zéro on 6 July (r6-F-FIZ-012, REC-0642). 'Saa munani y'igicuku' on the Kinyarwanda clock is about 02:00; the minutes figure gives about 02:35. Igihe's headline names DRC and Burundian forces as the defenders; the sentence also names FDLR and Wazalendo.
r7-E-IGIHE-184.vn: Verbatim; clock times clarified in translation ('saa munani' is about 02:00). Party claim relayed by Rwandan state-aligned Igihe; other project sources (SOS Médias Burundi, Radio Okapi on a FARDC 'strategic withdrawal' reported 6 July) cover the fall of Point Zéro. The page does not say which forces held each place. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 183) 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 183)
src: Col Fidele Rugabo uri mu bofisiye bakuru ba Twirwaneho, yatangaje ko bafashe Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi na Rubemba mu masaha ya Saa munani y’igicuku cyo kuri uyu wa 4 Nyakanga 2026.

Yagize ati “Ibikorwa bya gisirikare muri Point-Zéro birangiye aka kanya saa munani n’iminota 35. Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi na Rubemba byafashwe. Abanzi bakwiye imishwaro mu buryo burindwi.”

r7-E-IGIHE-185.s: Igihe reported that before taking Point-Zéro, Twirwaneho had taken other key areas around Minembwe commune, including Mikenke and Bilalombili, on 1 July 2026.
r7-E-IGIHE-185.n: Igihe's own statement without a named source. Note Mikenke is also described by Igihe on 11 July as taken from DRC/Burundi/FDLR/Wazalendo forces (p20).
r7-E-IGIHE-185.vn: Verbatim. Igihe's own voice, no named source.
src: Twirwaneho ifashe Point-Zéro n’ibice bihana imbibi nyuma yo gufata ibindi bice by’ingenzi biri mu nkengero za Komini Minembwe birimo Mikenke na Bilalombili ku wa 1 Nyakanga.

r7-E-IGIHE-186.s: Igihe reported that on 17 January 2026 Twirwaneho had taken Point-Zéro but lost it shortly afterwards when it was attacked with drones and by soldiers of a DRC special-forces unit known as Hiboux.
r7-E-IGIHE-186.a: Twirwaneho (took it); DRC special forces unit 'Hiboux' (retook it, per Igihe)
r7-E-IGIHE-186.n: DATE: other claims give 14-16 January 2026 for the first capture (BBC News Gahuza, r7-E-FIZ-001; Umuryango.rw, r7-E-FIZ-009 'morning of 16 January') and Ebuteli (REC-0586); Igihe says 17 January. The unit name 'Hiboux' is rendered as Igihe prints it (the 'Hiboux' special-forces unit also appears in existing roster claims).
r7-E-IGIHE-186.vn: Verbatim. DATE CONFLICT, kept as each source states: Igihe gives 17 January 2026 for Twirwaneho's first capture of Point-Zéro; BBC Gahuza, Umuryango and Ebuteli in other project claims give 14-16 January (Umuryango: morning of 16 January). 'Hiboux' as printed; Igihe's own voice.
src: Tariki ya 17 Mutarama 2026, Twirwaneho yari yafashe Point-Zéro ariko iyamburwa nyuma y’igihe gito ubwo yagabwagaho ibitero bikomeye byifashishije drones n’abasirikare bo mu mutwe w’ingabo zidasanzwe za RDC uzwi nka Hiboux.

r7-E-IGIHE-187.s: Col Fidele Rugabo said, according to Igihe, that the DRC, Burundian, FDLR and Wazalendo forces had been shamed by Twirwaneho and M23 fighters, and he greeted residents of Fizi and Baraka, hinting that Twirwaneho might take those places too.
r7-E-IGIHE-187.n: Threat of further advance on Fizi town and Baraka (Lake Tanganyika) made by a party; 'terrorist group' is Igihe's wording. Igihe reports Fizi and Baraka lie south of Point-Zéro.
r7-E-IGIHE-187.vn: Verbatim; 'uyu murwanyi' (this fighter) is Rugabo by context; replacement quote spans the contiguous sentences that name him. Party statement; 'terrorist group' (FDLR) is Igihe's/the speaker's wording. A threat of further advance, not a reported capture.
src: Col Fidele Rugabo uri mu bofisiye bakuru ba Twirwaneho, yatangaje ko bafashe Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi na Rubemba mu masaha ya Saa munani y’igicuku cyo kuri uyu wa 4 Nyakanga 2026. Yagize ati “Ibikorwa bya gisirikare muri Point-Zéro birangiye aka kanya saa munani n’iminota 35. Point-Zéro, Baruta, Kalonge, Bicumbi na Rubemba byafashwe. Abanzi bakwiye imishwaro mu buryo burindwi.” Uyu murwanyi yatangaje ko Ingabo za RDC, iz’u Burundi, umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR na Wazalendo zitewe ikimwaro n’abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho na M23, asuhuza abo muri Fizi na Baraka; aca amarenga ko na ho bashobora kuhafata.

r7-E-IGIHE-188.s: Igihe reported that Twirwaneho and M23 had accused the DRC government forces coalition of using Point-Zéro to prepare major attacks on Minembwe centre and other key Banyamulenge areas including Mikenke.
r7-E-IGIHE-188.a: Twirwaneho and M23 (accusers); DRC government forces coalition (accused)
r7-E-IGIHE-188.n: Party accusation; the date of each accusation is not given.
r7-E-IGIHE-188.vn: Verbatim. Party accusation reported by Igihe; when it was made is not stated. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 187)
src: Twirwaneho na M23 byashinjaga ihuriro ry’Ingabo za Leta ya RDC gutegurira muri Point-Zéro ibitero bikomeye zagabaga muri Santere ya Minembwe no mu bindi bice by’ingenzi bituyemo Abanyamulenge birimo Mikenke.

r7-E-IGIHE-189.s: Burundi's Foreign Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana said at a briefing with diplomats on 8 December 2025, according to Igihe, that AFC/M23 had aimed to take the city of Uvira before the Washington peace agreement was signed on 4 December but, he said, was held back by Burundian forces.
r7-E-IGIHE-189.l: Uvira and Luvungi (South Kivu); briefing in Bujumbura
r7-E-IGIHE-189.n: Same statement is in Africa Insight (r1-ST-BI-010) and BBC News Gahuza (r1-UC-BI-FDLR-038), both under REC-0112; Igihe's account is not independent of Burundi's briefing. 'ngo' marks Igihe's distance ('reportedly').
r7-E-IGIHE-189.vn: Full name and title are in the contiguous lede (replacement quote extended); 'blocked' softened to 'held back' (yakomwe mu nkokora) and kept as the minister's claim. Party statement (Burundi); the same briefing is reported by Africa Insight and BBC Gahuza in other project claims, so Igihe is not an independent origin. 'Ngo' marks the clause as his claim.
src: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga w’u Burundi, Dr. Edouard Bizimana, yiteye akanyabugabo nyuma y’aho abasirikare benshi b’igihugu cye bapfiriye muri teritwari ya Uvira mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo. Mu kiganiro n’abadipolomate cyabaye ku wa 8 Ukuboza 2025, Minisitiri Bizimana yatangaje ko AFC/M23 yari ifite intego yo gufata umujyi wa Uvira mbere y’uko amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington ashyirwaho umukono ku wa 4 Ukuboza ariko ngo yakomwe mu nkokora n’ingabo z’u Burundi.

r7-E-IGIHE-190.s: Bizimana said, according to Igihe ('uyu muyobozi', this official, read as the minister from the preceding paragraph), that Burundian troops went to the DRC to protect Burundi's borders, Burundians and their property, that they cannot leave while the problems that took them there remain unsolved, and that they went there with the agreement of the Congolese government.
r7-E-IGIHE-190.n: Burundian government position on its deployment; compare Burundian Defence Minister Mutabazi (r7-L-RN-001, 15 July 2025) and RDF/FDNB claims in the roster. The deployment's size and units are not given here.
r7-E-IGIHE-190.vn: Verbatim; speaker is Bizimana by context (replacement quote spans the contiguous paragraph naming him). Party statement (Burundi), same briefing as claim 188; deployment size and units not given.
src: Mu kiganiro n’abadipolomate cyabaye ku wa 8 Ukuboza 2025, Minisitiri Bizimana yatangaje ko AFC/M23 yari ifite intego yo gufata umujyi wa Uvira mbere y’uko amasezerano y’amahoro ya Washington ashyirwaho umukono ku wa 4 Ukuboza ariko ngo yakomwe mu nkokora n’ingabo z’u Burundi. Yagize ati “Bo bashakaga ko amasezerano asinywa bamaze gufata Luvungi na Uvira. Ariko ntibyaboroheye, ingabo zacu zahagaze neza, zirwanya umwanzi. Ndagira ngo mfate uyu mwanya nshimire abasirikare b’Abarundi bari guharanira amahoro muri Congo uko bitanze kugira ngo umwanzi ntavogere igihugu cyacu.” Uyu muyobozi yatangaje ko ingabo z’u Burundi zagiye muri RDC kugira ngo zirinde imbibi z’igihugu cyazo, kandi ko zidashobora kuvayo mu gihe ibibazo byazijyanyeyo bitarakemuka.

Ati “Bari hariya mbere na mbere kugira ngo barinde imbibi z’u Burundi, barinde Abarundi n’ibyabo kandi rero ibyo bavuga ngo bashaka ko abasirikare b’Abarundi bavayo, ntidushobora kuvayo kuko icyatujyanye ntikirarangira kandi twagiyeyo twumvikanye na Leta ya Congo.”
