r7-E-IGIHE-191.s: AFC/M23 military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma said on 6 December, according to Igihe, 'Those who crossed over have learned a lesson', that 'Congo is not Cibitoke, nor Ngozi or their Bujumbura', and that they come to AFC/M23's home where it is fighting for the truth.
r7-E-IGIHE-191.l: n/a (statement); Burundian forces in South Kivu
r7-E-IGIHE-191.a: AFC/M23 (Lt Col Willy Ngoma); addressed to Burundian forces
r7-E-IGIHE-191.n: Addressed to Burundian forces by implication ('those who crossed over', Cibitoke, Ngozi, Bujumbura are Burundian places); the excerpt does not name Burundian forces. Channel of the original statement is not given.
r7-E-IGIHE-191.vn: Verbatim. Party statement (AFC/M23); addressed to Burundian forces by implication (Cibitoke, Ngozi, Bujumbura are in Burundi). Channel not given. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 190)
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 mu rwego rwa gisirikare, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, tariki ya 6 Ukuboza yagize ati “Abambutse babonye isomo. Basanze abagabo turi maso kandi tuzaba maso. Congo ntabwo ari Cibitoke, ntabwo ari Ngozi cyangwa Bujumbura yabo, oya. Baradusanga iwacu, turwanirira ukuri, kandi bazabibona.”

r7-E-IGIHE-192.s: Igihe reported that within a week the Burundian army, working with DRC forces, Wazalendo and FDLR, had been dispossessed of many areas of South Kivu including Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere and Sange; a photo caption says AFC/M23 fighters coming from Kamanyola were now approaching the city of Uvira.
r7-E-IGIHE-192.l: Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere, Sange (Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-192.a: AFC/M23 (advancing); Burundian army, FARDC, Wazalendo, FDLR (dispossessed), as Igihe presents it
r7-E-IGIHE-192.n: Igihe's own overview, dated by the article (9 Dec 2025). Cross-check the individual captures: Radio Maendeleo/Radio Okapi/Group of Experts on Luvungi, Katogota and Sange (REC-0212, REC-0215, REC-0216, REC-0528). Igihe names Burundian forces as having been dislodged; contested elsewhere (Burundian communiqués and FDNB statements in the roster).
r7-E-IGIHE-192.vn: Verbatim; source 1 is a photo caption. Igihe's own overview (article of 9 December 2025); the advancing force is not named in the first sentence. Individual captures are covered by Radio Maendeleo, Radio Okapi and the UN Group of Experts in other project claims.
src: Mu gihe kitarenze icyumweru, ingabo z’u Burundi ziri gukorana n’iza RDC, imitwe ya Wazalendo na FDLR, byambuwe ibice byinshi byo muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo birimo Katogota, Rurambo, Luberizi, Luvungi, Mutalule, Bwegera, Nyakabere na Sange.
Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 baturutse muri Kamanyola, ubu bari gusatira umujyi wa Uvira

r7-E-IGIHE-193.s: Igihe reported that 4 December 2025 was a very bad day for Burundian forces, as many were killed in an AFC/M23 attack and more than 100 were taken prisoner, and that Lt Col Athanase Minani was killed then.
r7-E-IGIHE-193.x: Igihe: more than 100 taken prisoner ('abarenga 100 bafatwa mpiri'); number killed not given ('abenshi', many)
r7-E-IGIHE-193.n: Igihe does not say who 'them' (bo) are beyond the preceding Burundian forces. The killing of Lt Col Minani is independently reported by Congovirtuel (r1-SKS-2025Q4-018, REC-0210). The 100+ prisoners figure is not confirmed elsewhere here; the FDNB spokesperson denied captures in January 2025 (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-005) in a different context.
r7-E-IGIHE-193.vn: Verbatim; name as printed. Igihe's own voice, no named source; 'them' is the Burundian forces of the preceding sentences. The 100+ prisoners figure is unconfirmed. Igihe's p06 article reports Minani's death as hedged ('biravugwa'); here it is stated flatly. Congovirtuel separately reports his death (other project claim). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 192)
src: Tariki ya 4 Ukuboza yabaye umunsi mubi cyane kuri bo kuko abenshi biciwe mu gitero cya AFC/M23, abarenga 100 bafatwa mpiri. Ni bwo bapfushije Lt Col Athanase Minani.

r7-E-IGIHE-194.s: Igihe reported that many Bujumbura hospitals received bodies and wounded Burundian soldiers, and, citing 'the SOS website', that the military hospital at Kamenge alone received 87 wounded, with others taken to other clinics including Tanganyika Care Polyclinic.
r7-E-IGIHE-194.l: Bujumbura (Burundi): Kamenge military hospital; Tanganyika Care Polyclinic
r7-E-IGIHE-194.x: Igihe, citing SOS: 87 wounded received at the Kamenge military hospital alone
r7-E-IGIHE-194.n: Relays SOS Médias Burundi ('urubuga SOS'); the SOS original was not located. Compare SOS's January 2025 Kamenge figures (81 injured, 19 dead, REC-1166). Casualties are soldiers, not civilians.
r7-E-IGIHE-194.vn: 'SOS Médias Burundi' is not printed on the page (it says 'urubuga SOS'); the name moved to originating_source. Statement reordered so only the 87 figure is credited to SOS. The 87 figure is relayed from SOS Médias Burundi (8 December 2025 per the unit's corroboration note); the SOS original was not checked here. Casualties are soldiers.
src: Ibitaro byinshi by’i Bujumbura byakiriye imirambo n’inkomere z’abasirikare b’u Burundi. Ibya gisirikare bya Kamenge byonyine byakiriye inkomere 87 nk’uko byasobanuwe n’urubuga SOS, izindi zijyanwa mu yandi mavuriro arimo Tanganyika Care Polyclinic.

r7-E-IGIHE-195.s: Igihe reported ('Amakuru avuga' = reports say) that after losing Sange on 8 December 2025 Burundian soldiers were ordered to leave Uvira city quickly, though it was not known whether to regroup or not to return; DRC soldiers, Wazalendo, Imbonerakure and many civilians followed them.
r7-E-IGIHE-195.n: Hedged and unattributed ('Amakuru avuga'). Imbonerakure (the Burundian ruling-party youth wing) are named as accompanying the withdrawal. Compare SOS Médias Burundi on a large part of Burundian soldiers withdrawing in December 2025 (r1-UCD-RDF-FDNB-003) and the AFC/M23 announced withdrawal from Uvira (REC-0127).
r7-E-IGIHE-195.vn: Verbatim; hedge preserved. Hedged and unattributed ('amakuru avuga', reports say). The year 2025 is the article's (9 December 2025).
src: Amakuru avuga ko nyuma yo kwamburwa santere ya Sange ku wa 8 Ukuboza, abasirikare b’u Burundi bahawe ibwiriza ryo kuva mu mujyi wa Uvira bwangu, gusa ikitaramenyekana ni niba byakozwe kugira ngo bajye kwisuganya cyangwa se niba badateze gusubirayo.
Abasirikare b’u Burundi ntibahunze bonyine, kuko aba RDC na Wazalendo, Imbonerakure n’abasivili benshi babakurikiye.

r7-E-IGIHE-196.s: Igihe reported that Bizimana asserted AFC/M23's aim was to take Uvira before Christmas, and that as of 8 December 2025 AFC/M23 fighters were within 30 kilometres of Uvira city.
r7-E-IGIHE-196.x: Igihe: AFC/M23 within 30 km of Uvira city as of 8 December 2025
r7-E-IGIHE-196.n: The 30 km figure is Igihe's; Uvira was taken, according to other claims, around 10 December 2025 (r7-L-RW-005, r7-L-RN-002, REC-0127).
r7-E-IGIHE-196.vn: Verbatim. The 30 km figure is Igihe's own; the Christmas aim is the Burundian minister's claim. Igihe adds its own gloss that AFC/M23 appeared set to reach that aim soon.
src: Kugeza tariki ya 8 Ukuboza 2025, abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bari mu ntera y’ibilometero 30 bagana mu mujyi wa Uvira. Minisitiri Bizimana ahamya ko bafite intego yo gufata uyu mujyi mbere ya Noheli,

r7-E-IGIHE-197.s: Igihe reported that most of the Burundians who remained in the DRC were concentrated in areas around Minembwe in Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories.
r7-E-IGIHE-197.l: Around Minembwe: Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga territories (South Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-197.n: 'Abarundi' (Burundians) is read in context as Burundian troops, per the preceding paragraph; the excerpt does not say 'troops'. Igihe's own assertion.
r7-E-IGIHE-197.vn: Verbatim. Igihe's own assertion; 'Abarundi' (Burundians) read as Burundian troops from the preceding paragraph, which the excerpt does not say. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 196)
src: Abarundi benshi basigaye muri RDC biganje mu bice bikikije Minembwe muri teritwari ya Uvira, Fizi na Mwenga.

r7-E-IGIHE-198.s: Igihe reported that M23 had taken the Kitsombiro centre in Lubero territory after heavy fighting against DRC forces on the morning of 19 February 2025, and that Kitsombiro is 25 kilometres from the Lubero centre.
r7-E-IGIHE-198.n: No other source on Kitsombiro for 19 February 2025 was found among existing claims; the earliest are Actualite.cd on 24 Feb-2 Mar and 20 March 2025 (M23 holding Kanyabayonga to Kitsombiro, REC-0982). Treat the exact capture date as unconfirmed.
r7-E-IGIHE-198.vn: Verbatim. Igihe's own voice; no independent source in the project dates the Kitsombiro capture to 19 February 2025 (Actualite.cd places M23 there from late February/March 2025). Treat the date as single-source.
src: Umutwe witwaje intwaro wa M23 wafashe santere ya Kitsombiro iherereye muri teritwari ya Lubero, intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo.
Yafashwe nyuma y’imirwano ikomeye yahanganishije ingabo za RDC na M23 mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa 19 Gashyantare 2025.
Santere ya Kitsombiro iri mu ntera y’ibilometero 25 werekeza muri santere ya Lubero.

r7-E-IGIHE-199.s: Igihe reported ('amakuru avuga', 'haravugwa') that, according to news from Lubero, DRC forces tried to use heavy guns and helicopters to stop M23 fighters without success, and that soldiers who fled the fighting were reportedly arrested by the army's military-conduct branch.
r7-E-IGIHE-199.n: Hedged, unsourced local reports. 'Ishami ... rishinzwe imyitwarire' (branch responsible for conduct/discipline) is rendered as 'military-conduct branch'; the exact FARDC body is not named. Igihe also says many civilians fled to safer areas (next sentence, not cited).
r7-E-IGIHE-199.vn: Verbatim; hedges kept. Hedged, unsourced local reports ('amakuru avuga', 'haravugwa'); the FARDC body ('ishami rishinzwe imyitwarire', the branch responsible for discipline) is not named. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 198)
src: Amakuru ava muri Lubero avuga ko ingabo za RDC zagerageje gukoresha imbunda ziremereye na kajugujugu, mu gukumira abarwanyi ba M23 ariko biba iby’ubusa. Haravugwa abasirikare bahunze urugamba, batabwa muri yombi n’ishami ry’igisirikare cya RDC rishinzwe imyitwarire.

r7-E-IGIHE-200.s: Igihe reported that M23 already controlled other areas of Lubero territory, including Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba and Matembe, which it said it had taken at the end of 2024.
r7-E-IGIHE-200.l: Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba, Matembe (Lubero territory, North Kivu)
r7-E-IGIHE-200.n: The capture (late 2024) is out of window; recorded only as the position held on 19 February 2025.
r7-E-IGIHE-200.vn: Verbatim. Position held as of the article (19 February 2025); the captures themselves (end of 2024) are outside the window. Igihe's own voice.
src: Umutwe wa M23 usanzwe igenzura ibindi bice byo muri Lubero, birimo Alimbongo, Kanyabayonga, Kayna, Kirumba ndetse na Matembe, wafashe mu mpera z'umwaka wa 2024.

r7-E-IGIHE-201.s: A FARDC captain shot dead Lungele Mbiso, coordinator of the communication cell of South Kivu governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the afternoon of 5 July 2025, according to Actualite.cd (citing local civil society); Igihe reports the same killing in Uvira territory.
r7-E-IGIHE-201.n: Actualite.cd (6 July 2025) is the independent Congolese source, fetched with tools/page_text.py; it also sources the account to local civil society. Motive not stated by either outlet. Social-media reposts of the same story exist (Facebook/X); not cited. The captain is unnamed in both.
r7-E-IGIHE-201.vn: Actualite.cd page re-fetched and read: supports the killing, date, rank and roles. Removed the '1 killed' figure (no numeral printed) and used the governor's name as printed ('Jean Jacques Purusi'). Grade B on one credible non-partisan origin. Excerpt gap: the clause 'Actualite.cd cites local civil society' rests on the page passage 'Selon la société civile locale, l'incident a eu lieu aux environs de 15h', not the stored excerpt. Motive not stated by either outlet; the captain is unnamed. Actualite.cd adds the killing was on avenue Kasavubu around 15:00, not far from the governorate. Igihe's account (7 July) repeats Actualite.cd's details and is probably not an independent origin. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 200) 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Umusirikare wa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo ufite ipeti rya Captain yishe umuyobozi mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo washyizweho na Leta. Uyu muyobozi ushinzwe itumanaho mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo,Lungele Mbiso, yishwe arasiwe muri teritwari ya Uvira tariki ya 5 Nyakanga 2025.
Un capitaine des FARDC a abattu l'après-midi du 05 juillet 2025 le coordonnateur de la cellule de communication du gouverneur Jean Jacques Purusi monsieur Lungele Mbiso.
Selon la société civile locale, l'incident a eu lieu aux environs de 15h

r7-E-IGIHE-202.s: Uvira youth leader Kiza Tiniko said, according to Actualite.cd and Igihe, that angry residents lynched (beat to death) the captain who had killed the governor's communication coordinator; Actualite.cd adds, citing several other sources, that the soldier threw away his weapon before being chased by the population, and Igihe adds, citing news from Uvira, that he threw away the gun he had used to shoot Lungele out of fear of being prosecuted.
r7-E-IGIHE-202.a: Uvira residents (crowd); victim a FARDC captain
r7-E-IGIHE-202.n: Victim is a soldier killed by a crowd; categorised under the nearest available category (the perpetrators are civilians). Igihe's 'threw away the gun out of fear' is stated without attribution ('Amakuru ava muri Uvira'); Actualite.cd says only that he threw away his weapon before being pursued by the population. Igihe puts Kiza Tiniko's time at 'saa cyenda n'iminota 20' (15:20), matching Actualite.cd.
r7-E-IGIHE-202.vn: Actualite.cd page read: it supports the lynching and the discarded weapon (replacement quote spans the contiguous passage). Removed the '1' figure; 'Mbiso' is not in this claim's excerpts, so the victim of the first killing is described by role. Motive kept as Igihe's. Excerpt gap: the clause that the soldier threw away his weapon before being chased (Actualite.cd, citing several other sources) rests on the page passage 'le militaire dont il est question a jeté son arme avant d'être poursuivi par la population', given as source 2's replacement quote, not the stored excerpt. The victim of this incident is the unnamed captain, killed by a crowd. The 'fear of prosecution' motive is Igihe's alone, from unnamed 'news from Uvira'. Igihe and Actualite.cd share one origin for the lynching (Kiza Tiniko). 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-IGIHE claim 201) 2026-10-29: source 2 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Umuyobozi wa sosiyete sivile ihuza urubyiruko rwo muri Uvira, Kiza Tiniko, yasobanuye ko abaturage na bo bakubise uyu musirikare kugeza apfuye.
Amakuru ava muri Uvira asobanura ko mbere y’uko uyu musirikare yicwa, yataye imbunda yarasishije Lungele bitewe n’ubwoba bw’uko yashoboraga gukurikiranwa.

" Il y a un capitaine qui a tué le coordonnateur de la cellule de communication du gouverneur aux environs de 15h20. En colère, la population a lynché ce militaire et est aussi mort ", explique Kiza Tiniko, président des jeunes d'Uvira.
le militaire dont il est question a jeté son arme avant d'être poursuivi par la population

r7-E-IGIHE-203.s: Igihe reported that the office of the government-appointed South Kivu governor, Jean-Jacques Purusi, relocated to Uvira in February 2025 once AFC/M23 had taken Bukavu.
r7-E-IGIHE-203.a: South Kivu provincial government (Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi)
r7-E-IGIHE-203.n: Independently documented by Radio Okapi (24 Feb 2025, communication cell of the governor, REC-0064).
r7-E-IGIHE-203.vn: Verbatim. Igihe's own voice; the year is the article's context (published 7 July 2025). Actualite.cd's page also says Uvira became the provincial capital after AFC/M23 took Bukavu, and Radio Okapi documents the move in another project claim.
src: Mu mujyi wa Uvira ni ho himukiye ibiro bya Guverineri w’intara washyizweho na Leta, Jean-Jacques Purusi, muri Gashyantare ubwo ihuriro AFC/M23 ryari rimaze gufata umujyi wa Bukavu.

r7-E-NKN-001.s: DW Swahili reported, according to Samuel Kagheni, described as one of the civil-society leaders in the village, that on Saturday the ADF attacked the village of Ngohi Vuyinga in Lubero territory (North Kivu); 9 people were killed and many others lost their homes after their houses were burned.
r7-E-NKN-001.a: ADF (as stated in the DW text)
r7-E-NKN-001.x: DW (citing Samuel Kagheni): 9 killed, many others displaced by burned houses
r7-E-NKN-001.n: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday') and DW publication date 10 March 2025 (Monday). No known record for Ngohi Vuyinga (claim_search found none). The toll 9 is DW's/Kagheni's first count; the page says the toll may rise because many people were unaccounted for. Other outlets (not fetched) give 11 killed; not used.
r7-E-NKN-001.vn: Excerpt and page (DW, datePublished 2025-03-10) support every clause; translation checked. Single origin (local civil-society leader via DW). Date derived from 'Saturday' (Jumamosi) and DW's page date of 10 March 2025; the page says the toll may rise as many people were unaccounted for.
src: Siku ya Jumamosi kundi la ADF lilikishambulia kijiji cha Ngohi Vuyinga katika eneo la Lubero, jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini, watu 9 waliuwawa na wengine wengi kupoteza makaazi yao baada ya nyumba zao kuchomwa moto, hii ikiwa ni kulingana na Samuel Kagheni moja ya viongozi wa mashirika ya kiraia katika kijiji hicho.

r7-E-NKN-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that about ten militiamen were killed in violent clashes between the night of Monday 3 March and the morning of Tuesday 4 March in Butembo, and that, according to civil society in Kimemi, the fighting pitted two Wazalendo militia groups against each other. It said an interim report indicated ten militiamen killed and several wounded, treated in health structures in the area.
r7-E-NKN-002.l: Butembo (Kimemi neighbourhood, Mont Tabor and Mavina area), Butembo city
r7-E-NKN-002.x: SOS Médias Burundi: about ten militiamen killed (interim), several wounded; BBC Gahuza (citing RFI): about ten dead per NGOs, six per an army spokesman (see separate claim)
r7-E-NKN-002.n: Page dated 7 March 2025 (URL date); French original dated 5 March. Second independent origin: BBC Gahuza (in Kirundi) citing RFI, see next claim. SOS Médias Burundi notes no official comment had been recorded from the authorities.
r7-E-NKN-002.vn: Page checked; translation correct. SOS Médias is a non-partisan outlet for this conflict; one origin, consistent with BBC Gahuza/RFI. BBC Gahuza (claim 3) gives six dead per an army spokesman and up to ten per associations; figures not merged. The page notes no official comment from the authorities had been recorded.
src: Takriban wanamgambo kumi waliuawa wakati wa mapigano makali yaliyotokea kati ya usiku wa Jumatatu Machi 3 na asubuhi ya Jumanne Machi 4 huko Butembo, katika jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini mashariki mwa Kongo. Kulingana na mashirika ya kiraia huko Kimemi, mojawapo ya vitongoji vya jiji hilo, mapigano haya yalipinga makundi mawili ya wanamgambo wa Wazalendo.
Ripoti ya muda inaonyesha wanamgambo kumi waliuawa na kadhaa kujeruhiwa, kutibiwa katika miundo ya afya katika kanda.

r7-E-NKN-003.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) quoted a resident on social media as saying that four dead bodies were discovered 'this morning', that they 'would be' young militiamen from the Mavina group, and that they had been tied up before being hanged (the verb used, kunyongwa, can also mean strangled).
r7-E-NKN-003.l: near the Université Catholique du Graben (UCG) campus, Butembo
r7-E-NKN-003.a: not stated by the source (the resident names the presumed victims' group, not the perpetrators)
r7-E-NKN-003.x: resident quoted on social media: four bodies
r7-E-NKN-003.n: Single unnamed resident quoted from social media; hedged ('wangekuwa' = 'would be'). The excerpt ends at 'mitandao ya kijamii'; the verb 'kunyongwa' is translated 'hanged' (could also be read 'strangled'). Reviewer: translation of kunyongwa to be confirmed.
r7-E-NKN-003.vn: Removed 'on the morning after the clashes' (the quote says only 'this morning') and the inferred perpetrator (Tabor-based group): the page says the Mavina group attacked the Tabor group but does not say who killed these four. kunyongwa is ambiguous (hang/strangle); noted. Single unnamed resident relayed from social media; hedged ('wangekuwa'). 'This morning' is relative to the undated post; the page places the bodies near the UCG area after the 3-4 March clashes. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKN claim 2)
src: “Miili minne iliyokufa iligunduliwa asubuhi ya leo. Hawa wangekuwa wanamgambo vijana kutoka kundi la Mavina. Walikuwa wamefungwa kabla ya kunyongwa,” anashuhudia mkazi mmoja kwenye mitandao ya kijamii

r7-E-NKN-004.s: BBC Gahuza (Kirundi), relaying RFI, reported that news from Butembo said about ten people died in clashes between two groups of Wazalendo fighters, which broke out on 3 March and lasted several hours in the Kimemi hills of the city; it added that an army spokesman in the area said in a video that six dead were known, while non-political associations said up to ten died on both sides.
r7-E-NKN-004.x: BBC Gahuza: about ten dead per local associations ('up to ten on both sides'); six known dead per an army spokesman in a video
r7-E-NKN-004.n: Kirundi-language text (March = 'Ntwarante'; translation by the agent, reviewer should confirm). The figures differ by speaker (six per army spokesman vs ten per associations); not merged. Same event as the SOS Médias Burundi claim; two outlets, SOS and BBC/RFI, are likely independent in sourcing.
r7-E-NKN-004.vn: Kirundi translation checked (Ntwarante = March; 'amasaha atari make' = several hours; 'Amashirahamwe adaharanira ivyicaro vya poritike' = non-political associations). RFI is cited only for the date/duration sentence; the first sentence is BBC's own. Six dead per an army spokesman vs up to ten per non-political associations; kept separate.
src: Amakuru ava mu gisagara ca Butembo c'intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru avuga ko abantu hafi cumi bapfuye mu mishamirano yadutse hagati y'imirwi ibiri y'abarwanyi ba Wazalendo. Nk'uko bivugwa n'ikinyamakuru RFI, iyi mishamirano yadutse ku wa 3 Ntwarante (3), ikaba yamaze amasaha atari make ku mitumba ya Kimemi muri ico gisagara.

umuvugizi w'igisirikare muri ako karere avuga, aho muri videwo yacishije ku mbuga hwaniro amenyesha ko bazi batandatu bapfuye. Amashirahamwe adaharanira ivyicaro vya poritike yoyo avuga ko hapfuye abashika cumi ku mpande zompi.

r7-E-NKN-005.s: Vatican News (Swahili), citing local sources of the pontifical charity Aid to the Church in Need (given as ACS), reported that more than 70 bodies were found in a Protestant church at Maiba, North Kivu; it said the killings took place between 12 and 15 February 2025 at the hands of ADF fighters who entered the village and abducted about 100 people.
r7-E-NKN-005.a: ADF, per the ACN source quoted by Vatican News
r7-E-NKN-005.x: Vatican News citing ACN source: more than 70 bodies; about 100 abducted
r7-E-NKN-005.n: Adds an independent (church-network) origin and a 12-15 February killing window and 'about 100 abducted' to REC-1243 (abduction night of 11-12 Feb, bodies found 14-15 Feb). ACN's source is anonymised for security per the page. The page itself says the victims included women, children and elderly people.
r7-E-NKN-005.vn: Page (dated 24 Feb 2025) checked; figures and dates match. 'Terrorist Islamic group' wording is the outlet's and is not carried into the statement. ACN's source is anonymous for security reasons, per the page.
src: Kwa mujibu wa vyanzo vya ndani kutoka Shirika la Kipapa la Makanisa Hitaji,(ACS), linabainisha kuwa: “Zaidi ya miili 70 imepatikana katika Kanisa la Kiprotestanti huko Maiba,Kivu Kaskazini, iliyosambaratishwa na ghasia kutokana na makundi ya waasi.”

Mauaji hayo yalifanyika kati ya tarehe 12 na 15 Februari 2025 mikononi mwa waasi wa Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), kundi la kigaidi la Kiislamu lenye asili ya Uganda, ambao waliingia kijijini hapo na kuwateka takriban watu 100.

r7-E-NKN-006.s: UN News Kiswahili, relaying a MONUSCO statement released in Kinshasa, reported that ADF attacks between 13 and 19 November 2025 in parts of Lubero (Bapere and Baswagha areas) killed 89 civilians, including 20 women, with the number of children not yet known.
r7-E-NKN-006.x: MONUSCO (via UN News Kiswahili): 89 civilians killed, including 20 women; number of children not yet known
r7-E-NKN-006.n: Swahili UN News copy of the MONUSCO release (also published in English on the MONUSCO site). Corroborates the toll in REC-0941.
r7-E-NKN-006.vn: Matches page (dated 21 Nov 2025). Swahili copy of a MONUSCO release; same origin as the English MONUSCO statement, so not independent of it.
src: umelaani vikali mashambulizi makubwa yaliyofanywa na kundi lenye silaha la Allied Democratic Forces ADF kati ya tarehe 13 na 19 Novemba 2025 katika baadhi ya maeneo ya Lubero, jimboni Kivu Kaskazini na kukatili maisha ya raia wengi.

Taarifa zilizokusanywa na MONUSCO na kutolewa leo mjini Kinshasa zinaonesha kwamba mashambulizi hayo yaliyofanywa katika utawala wa Bapere na Baswagha yamesababisha vifo vya raia 89, wakiwemo wanawake 20 na idadi ya watoto bado haijulikani.

r7-E-NKN-007.s: UN News Kiswahili, relaying MONUSCO, reported that in the village of Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, at least 17 civilians, including women who were receiving care in the maternity ward, were killed inside a health centre run by the Catholic Church, and that four wards with patients caught fire during the attack.
r7-E-NKN-007.l: Byambwe, 60 km west of Lubero, Lubero territory
r7-E-NKN-007.x: MONUSCO via UN News Kiswahili: at least 17 civilians killed in the health centre
r7-E-NKN-007.n: The excerpt does not itself name ADF or the night of 14-15 November; both come from the same release's opening sentence (13-19 Nov ADF attacks in Lubero). Corroborates REC-0942.
r7-E-NKN-007.vn: Matches page. MONUSCO origin, not independent of the English release. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Katika kijiji cha Byambwe, kilichoko kilomita 60 magharibi mwa Lubero, angalau raia 17 wakiwemo wanawake waliokuwa wakipatiwa huduma katika wodi ya uzazi waliuawa ndani ya kituo cha afya kinachoendeshwa na Kanisa Katoliki. Wakati wa shambulizi hilo, wodi nne zenye wagonjwa ziliwaka moto.

Taarifa zilizokusanywa na MONUSCO na kutolewa leo mjini Kinshasa zinaonesha kwamba mashambulizi hayo yaliyofanywa katika utawala wa Bapere na Baswagha yamesababisha vifo vya raia 89, wakiwemo wanawake 20 na idadi ya watoto bado haijulikani.

umelaani vikali mashambulizi makubwa yaliyofanywa na kundi lenye silaha la Allied Democratic Forces ADF kati ya tarehe 13 na 19 Novemba 2025 katika baadhi ya maeneo ya Lubero, jimboni Kivu Kaskazini na kukatili maisha ya raia wengi.

r7-E-NKN-008.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that MONUSCO strongly condemned recent attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Beni and Lubero, North Kivu, between 9 and 16 August 2025, which caused the deaths of about 52 civilians including women and children.
r7-E-NKN-008.x: MONUSCO via UN News Kiswahili: about 52 civilians killed, including women and children
r7-E-NKN-008.n: Swahili copy of the MONUSCO statement already cited elsewhere in English (reliefweb); added here as a Swahili-language corroboration only. The page adds that the attacks were accompanied by abductions, looting and destruction of property.
r7-E-NKN-008.vn: Matches page (dated 19 Aug 2025: statement released 19 August in Kinshasa). Swahili copy of a MONUSCO statement already cited in English; same origin.
src: Umoja wa Mataifa kupitia Ujumbe wake wa kulinda amani nchini Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Congo, (MONUSCO) umelaani vikali mashambulio ya hivi karibuni yaliyofanywa na Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) katika mikoa ya Beni na Lubero, Kaskazini mwa Kivu kati ya tarehe 9 na 16 ya mwezi huu wa Agosti. Mashambulio haya yamesababisha vifo vya raia takribani 52 wakiwemo wanawake na watoto,

r7-E-NKN-009.s: DW Swahili reported that a government official in the area, Macaire Sivikunula, said the attack happened 'last night' in the village of Ntoyo in Lubero territory, and that Lubero military administrator Colonel Alain Kiwewa told Reuters the number killed was about 60 and might rise because some people had not yet been found.
r7-E-NKN-009.x: DW (quoting Col. Alain Kiwewa to Reuters): about 60 killed, may rise
r7-E-NKN-009.n: Early (day-after) figure of about 60; later counts in known records are higher (e.g., 64 buried of 89 in a Radio Okapi report cited elsewhere). 'Last night' is relative to DW's page date 9 September 2025, hence the night of 8-9 September. Names the two local officials by role (Sivikunula: government official in the area; Kiwewa: Lubero military administrator) for the statements-by-local-authorities requirement.
r7-E-NKN-009.vn: Page (dated 9 Sep 2025) checked; translation correct. DW's own headline says 50 and its lead 'more than 50' (machete attack during a funeral); the official figure quoted is about 60. Not merged.
src: Afisa wa serikali katika eneo hilo Macaire Sivikunula amesema shambulio hilo limetokea jana usiku katika kijiji cha Ntoyo, kilichopo katika eneo la Lubero, jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini. Msimamizi wa kijeshi wa Lubero Kanali Alain Kiwewa, ameliambia shirika la habari la Reuters kwamba, idadi ya watu waliouawa ni takriban watu 60 na huenda ikaongezeka kwani baadhi ya watu bado hawajapatikana.

r7-E-NKN-010.s: TRT Afrika Swahili reported that suspected ADF rebels killed 19 civilians in a night attack in eastern DRC, according to two local officials. Alain Kiwewa, military administrator of Lubero, said the attack, believed to have been carried out by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), took place in the village of Mukondo in North Kivu and that the toll could rise; a local pastor who declined to be named said the attackers wore uniforms resembling those of the Congolese army and attacked people with guns, knives and clubs.
r7-E-NKN-010.x: two local officials (via Reuters/TRT): 19 civilians killed; toll may rise
r7-E-NKN-010.n: The TRT page carries no date in its text; the date (Monday 13 October 2025) is from the search listing and confirmed by Radio Okapi and Actualite.cd items of 13 and 14 October 2025 about 19 civilians killed at Mukondo (seen in search results, not fetched). Wire copy: the page's picture credit is Reuters and the French TRT copy cites Reuters. Attack date computed from 'Monday' official statement; the attack was 'night' before. Not in known_records (claim_search 'Mukondo' found none).
r7-E-NKN-010.vn: Fixed garbled opening ('TRT ... suspected') and dropped the weekday not used in the excerpt's English rendering; kept 'suspected/believed'. The text carries no wire credit (only a Reuters photo credit), so the origin is left as TRT rather than inferred as Reuters. The page also quotes civil-society leader Espoir Kambale: 19 killed, 8 wounded, 26 houses burned (not in the excerpts).
src: Washukiwa wa waasi wa ADF wamewaua raia 19 katika shambulio la usiku huko mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Congo (DRC), maafisa wawili wa eneo hilo walisema Jumatatu, hali inayozidi kuzorotesha usalama katika eneo hilo lenye utajiri wa madini.

Shambulio hilo, linalodhaniwa kufanywa na kundi la Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), lilitokea katika kijiji cha Mukondo kilichopo mkoa wa Kivu Kaskazini, alisema Alain Kiwewa, msimamizi wa kijeshi wa eneo la Lubero ambako Mukondo iko, akiongeza kuwa idadi ya vifo inaweza kuongezeka.

Washambuliaji huko Mukondo walivaa sare zinazofanana na zile za jeshi la Kongo, jambo lililowaruhusu kuingia kijijini bila kushukiwa. Kisha waliwashambulia watu kwa kutumia bunduki, visu, na marungu, alisema mchungaji wa eneo hilo ambaye alikataa kutaja jina lake kwa sababu za kiusalama.

r7-E-NKN-011.s: DW Swahili reported that 10 people were killed in eastern DRC by extremist rebels linked to the group calling itself the Islamic State (IS), and that these ADF rebels attacked the village of Makoko in Lubero territory, North Kivu, 'yesterday'; it said, as stated by David Sikuli, a member of parliament for the province, that at the time there were no Congolese soldiers in the village, only fighters known as Wazalendo.
r7-E-NKN-011.a: ADF (as stated in the DW text)
r7-E-NKN-011.n: Differs from REC-0951 (Muhangi, about thirty killed, 15 January 2025) in place name (Makoko vs Muhangi) and toll (10 vs about 30); may be a separate attack the same day, or a variant name and count. DW page dated 16 January 2025, 'yesterday' = 15 January. DW's lead sentence says 'extremist rebels linked to IS' and the next paragraph names the ADF.
r7-E-NKN-011.vn: 'ADF-linked rebels' changed to the page's wording (lead: rebels linked to IS; next paragraph: 'those ADF rebels'). 'mbunge wa jimbo hilo' = MP of that province (jimbo is used for the province in the same sentence), not 'the area's MP'. 'jana' relative to DW datePublished 2025-01-16 gives 15 January. DW's Makoko figure (10 killed, 15 January 2025) differs in place and toll from the Muhangi record (about 30); it may be a separate attack. Kept separate, not merged. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKN claim 10)
src: Watu 10 wameuawa mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo na waasi wenye itikadi kali wenye mafungamano na kundi la kigaidi linalojiita Dola la Kiislamu (IS).

Waasi hao wa ADF walishambulia jana kijiji cha Makoko katika eneo la Lubero, Jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini. Wakati wa mashambulizi hayo, hakukuwa na askari wa Kongo katika kijiji hicho, ispokuwa wapiganaji wanaojulikana kama Wazalendo, ambao mara kadhaa wamekua wakishirikiana na vikosi vya Kongo. Hayo yameelezwa na mbunge wa jimbo hilo David Sikuli,

r7-E-NKN-012.s: BBC Swahili reported that a six-year-old girl who was being treated for Ebola was abducted from a health facility in eastern DRC: armed people stormed a clinic near the town of Butembo in North Kivu and took the child with her mother. Dr. Lubambo Maboko Gaston, the province's Ebola response manager, told Reuters that the two had not yet been found and made an urgent call to the abductors.
r7-E-NKN-012.l: clinic near Butembo, Butembo / Lubero area
r7-E-NKN-012.x: one six-year-old girl with Ebola and her mother taken
r7-E-NKN-012.n: Exact date of the abduction is not in the BBC Swahili entry (live-page entry dated 17 June 2026). A TRT Afrika French copy of Reuters (listed in search results with a wrong date) says the clinic was stormed 'late Monday' and a provincial notice seen by Reuters did not identify the attackers; Monday before 17 June is 15 June, but that date is not in the cited excerpt. Reuters is the originating wire. Page also notes the DRC government had not issued an official statement on the abduction at publication time. Not in known_records (claim_search 'six-year-old', 'Ebola clinic Butembo' found none).
r7-E-NKN-012.vn: Live-page entry located (firstPublished 2026-06-17); text matches; Gaston's quote is credited to Reuters. Victim is a minor and is not named by the source. The BBC entry (17 June 2026) does not give the date of the abduction.
src: Mamlaka za afya nchini Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasi ya Congo zimo katika hali ya taharuki baada ya msichana wa miaka sita aliyekuwa akipatiwa matibabu ya Ebola, kutekwa nyara kutoka kituo cha afya mashariki mwa nchi hiyo. Watu wenye silaha walivamia kliniki moja karibu na mji wa Butembo, jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini, na kumchukua mtoto huyo pamoja na mama yake

Dkt. Lubambo Maboko Gaston, meneja wa kukabiliana na mlipuko wa Ebola katika jimbo hilo, ametoa wito wa dharura kwa watekaji na familia hiyo. "Hadi sasa bado hatujawapata watu hao wawili. Tunatoa wito rasmi kwao kwenda haraka iwezekanavyo katika kituo cha matibabu ya Ebola," Dkt. Gaston aliliambia shirika la habari la Reuters.

r7-E-NKN-013.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that a new series of attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) caused mourning in the Beni area of North Kivu, and that between the night of Saturday 30 May and Sunday 31 May 2026, about 17 civilians were killed in several coordinated attacks on the Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes in the Beni area, according to local sources and civil-society actors.
r7-E-NKN-013.l: Vemba-Katota and Vemba-Masulukwede axes, east of Ngadi, near Beni
r7-E-NKN-013.a: ADF (identified as ADF fighters by residents, per the page)
r7-E-NKN-013.x: SOS Médias Burundi: about 17 civilians killed
r7-E-NKN-013.n: Toll differs slightly from REC-1211 (at least 16, night of 30 to 31 May). The page also says seven bodies were found on the Vemba-Katota road on Sunday morning and four more in the forest on the Vemba-Masulukwede road, and that several people were missing, some believed abducted. The headline says 'at least 17'. The 'ADF' attribution is in a later sentence (not in the excerpt); reviewer may narrow.
r7-E-NKN-013.vn: Page (Goma dateline 1 June 2026, URL 5 June) checked; 'yanayohusishwa na' = attributed to, preserved. Text says 'about 17', headline and later text 'at least 17'; the related record gives at least 16. Kept as the source's figure.
src: Msururu mpya wa mashambulizi yanayohusishwa na waasi wa Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) yamesababisha maombolezo katika eneo la Beni katika jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini

Kati ya usiku wa Jumamosi, Mei 30, na Jumapili, Mei 31, 2026, takriban raia 17 waliuawa katika mashambulizi kadhaa yaliyoratibiwa kwenye shoka za Vemba-Katota na Vemba-Masulukwede, kulingana na vyanzo vya ndani na watendaji wa mashirika ya kiraia.

r7-E-NKN-014.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that in the Butembo and Beni health zones, as well as Kisangani, doctors, nurses, laboratory technicians and community health workers were refusing to return to work, demanding payment of their salaries and hazard allowances.
r7-E-NKN-014.n: Context claim on civilian access to care during the 2026 Ebola outbreak; the strike is by health workers over unpaid pay, not an attack. The excerpt does not itself print the date 18 July (the dateline 'Julai 18, 2026' is elsewhere on the page). Single outlet.
r7-E-NKN-014.vn: Excerpt matches the page lead (Goma dateline 18 July 2026); translation correct ('bado wanakataa' = still refuse). Strike context, not an attack.
src: Katika maeneo ya afya ya Butembo na Beni, mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo (DRC), pamoja na Kisangani, kaskazini mashariki mwa nchi, madaktari, wauguzi, mafundi wa maabara, na wahudumu wa afya ya jamii bado wanakataa kurejea kazini. Wanadai kulipwa mishahara yao na marupurupu ya hatari

r7-E-NKN-015.s: BBC Swahili reported that the trial of about sixty FARDC deserter soldiers and two female accomplices opened on the day of the entry before the Butembo military tribunal sitting at Musienene; local journalist Seros Muyisa, present at the hearing, told the BBC the accused were charged with fleeing the enemy, theft, rape, extortion and other offences in the areas of Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene.
r7-E-NKN-015.l: Musienene (Butembo military tribunal); offences alleged in Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu and Musienene
r7-E-NKN-015.x: about sixty soldiers and two women accused (BBC Swahili); BBC Gahuza: about sixty accused
r7-E-NKN-015.n: The BBC Swahili live-page entry's headline says 'wahukumiwa' (sentenced) but its text says the case 'opened today'; the BBC Gahuza version says the trial began on Monday (24 February) and was later updated with convictions (next claim). Day discrepancy: 'today' (25 Feb, Tuesday) vs 'Monday' (24 Feb). The rape charge is an allegation in the charge sheet as reported by the journalist, not a finding. Related to but distinct from REC-0928/0929 (June-July 2025 hearings at Lubero-centre).
r7-E-NKN-015.vn: Entry found on the live page under 25 February 2025; quotes verbatim; 'wanashtakiwa' = are charged/prosecuted. The entry's text says 'sixty' and its headline 'about 60' ('Takriban ... 60') and 'wahukumiwa' (sentenced), while the text says the case opened that day. BBC Gahuza says the trial began on Monday (24 Feb); this entry says 'today' (25 Feb). Kept separate. Rape is a charge, not a finding.
src: Kesi dhidi ya wanajeshi sitini watoro wa vikosi vya jeshi la Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Congo (FARDC) na washirika wawili wa kike imefunguliwa leo. Watuhumiwa hao walifikishwa katika mahakama ya kijeshi ya Butembo mjini Musienene, katika mkoa wa Kivu Kaskazini.

"Watuhumiwa wanashtakiwa na mahakama ya kijeshi ya Butembo kwa kumkimbia adui, wizi, ubakaji, unyang'anyi na makosa mengine katika maeneo ya Lubero-Centre, Kimbulu na Musienene," Seros Muyisa, mwandishi wa habari wa eneo hilo ambaye alikuwepo katika kikao hicho, aliiambia BBC.

r7-E-NKN-016.s: BBC Gahuza (Kirundi) reported in an update that 55 of the soldiers accused of offences including fleeing the battlefield and looting were convicted and sentenced to death, and that the trial of about 60 FARDC soldiers began on Monday in the city of Butembo.
r7-E-NKN-016.x: BBC Gahuza: about 60 accused; 55 convicted and sentenced to death (update)
r7-E-NKN-016.n: Kirundi text; translation by the agent, reviewer to confirm ('guhunga' = flee; 'gusahura' = loot; 'ibikorwa by'ubugizi bwa nabi' = criminal acts). The excerpt does not mention rape; the rape charge is in the BBC Swahili claim. Date of the update is not stated (page dated 25 February 2025). Conflict: Monday (24 Feb) here vs 'today' (25 Feb) in BBC Swahili.
r7-E-NKN-016.vn: Translation checked: 'barabihamijwe, bakatirwa urwo gupfa' = found guilty, sentenced to death; 'ku wa mbere' = Monday. Page datePublished 2025-02-25. Day discrepancy with BBC Swahili ('today', 25 Feb) kept; the update's own date is not stated. The page's quote from Seros Muyisa also lists rape ('gufata ku ngufu') among the charges.
src: Ivugurura: Abasirikare 55 mu baregwaga ibyaha birimo guhunga urugamba no gusahura barabihamijwe, bakatirwa urwo gupfa. Urubanza rw'aba basirikare b'ingabo za FARDC bagera kuri 60 bashinjwa guta urugamba bagahunga bagakora ibikorwa by'ubugizi bwa nabi rwatangiye kuburanishwa ku wa mbere mu mujyi wa Butembo w'intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru muri DR Congo.

r7-E-NKN-017.s: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported, citing DRC media and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, that the defecting groups were Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M) group, who were said to have joined AFC/M23 on 9 March 2025.
r7-E-NKN-017.l: North Kivu (Lubero territory, per record REC-0981)
r7-E-NKN-017.a: Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP); part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua; NDC-R/M; AFC/M23
r7-E-NKN-017.n: Tanzanian outlet relaying DRC media (the page itself cites Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd elsewhere); 'juzi' = the day before yesterday relative to the page date, Tuesday 11 March 2025. Names the signatory of the defection statement and the three groups. The statement was reported as 'said to have joined', not confirmed by the page.
r7-E-NKN-017.vn: Excerpt matches the page (dated 11 March 2025); 'vinadaiwa' (alleged) preserved as 'said to have joined'; 'juzi' gives 9 March, matching the date printed.
src: Kwa mujibu wa vyombo vya habari nchini DRC, taarifa iliyosainiwa na kiongozi wa wazalendo, Shukuru Bulenda, vikundi hivyo vilivyoasi ni pamoja na Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), sehemu ya Mai-Mai Kifuafua na kikundi cha Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M). Vikundi hivyo, vinadaiwa kujiunga na AFC/M23, juzi Machi 9, 2025.

r7-E-NKN-018.s: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 captured the town of Kasugho on 2 March 2025 and left on 7 March, heading for Bunyatenge, a gold-mining area six hours from Kasugho.
r7-E-NKN-018.n: Adds the capture date (2 March) and the departure date (7 March) and destination (Bunyatenge) to REC-0976 (M23 withdraws from Kasugho, Katoyo and Kagheri, night of 6 to 7 March). The 'M23' wording is the page's; the sentence is not itself attributed on the page, which cites Kivu Morning Post for the previous sentence.
r7-E-NKN-018.vn: Excerpt matches page. Origin corrected to the outlet, since the sentence itself carries no attribution. The page does not attribute this sentence; the preceding paragraph cites Kivu Morning Post.
src: M23 imekuwa ikijaribu kuzunguka ngome za FARDC katika mji wa Lubero tangu mwishoni mwa Februari bila mafanikio. M23 iliuteka Mji wa Kasugho Machi 2, 2025, kabla ya kuondoka Machi 7 na kuelekea Bunyatenge, eneo lenye machimbo ya dhahabu lililo umbali wa saa sita kutoka Kasugho nchini humo.

r7-E-NKN-019.s: UN News Kiswahili reported, citing OCHA, that violence increased on 2 May in the Lubero area, forcing about 30,000 people to flee their homes.
r7-E-NKN-019.x: OCHA via UN News Kiswahili: about 30,000 people displaced
r7-E-NKN-019.n: Gives the displacement figure for the 2 May 2025 fighting around Lunyasenge (REC-1246). The excerpt itself does not name the fighting parties; the page's wider context is the M23/FARDC conflict and WFP aid via Beni. The article also reports WFP intends to use relief supplies stored in warehouses in Beni to assist about 140,000 people in the Lubero area.
r7-E-NKN-019.vn: Matches the page (dated 7 May 2025). The parties are not named in the sentence; actor correctly left unattributed.
src: Vurugu ziliongezeka tarehe 2 Mei katika eneo la Lubero, na kulazimisha takriban watu 30,000 kukimbia makazi yao, kwa mujibu wa ofisi ya Umoja wa Mataifa ya kuratibu misaada ya kibinadamu na masuala ya dharura OCHA

r7-E-NKN-020.s: DW (French) reported that the Butembo human-rights network Redho said it recorded 280 sexual-violence cases brought to justice in the city of Butembo in 2025, in a report made public in mid-March; Redho coordinator Muhindo Wasingya said the slowness of judicial procedures favours out-of-court settlements between families.
r7-E-NKN-020.x: Redho (via DW): 280 sexual-violence crimes brought to justice in Butembo in 2025 (complaints filed only)
r7-E-NKN-020.n: French-language DW item (10 April 2026) found while sweeping for Swahili; used as locator for a statistic. The page notes that the figure counts complaints filed only and that women's-rights activists link the rise to the ongoing conflict. Redho's name for its coordinator is spelled 'Muhindo Wasingya' on this page; Radio Moto items cited in other records spell 'Wasivinywa'. Single local NGO origin relayed by DW. Date range is the 2025 calendar year; report published mid-March (2026).
r7-E-NKN-020.vn: Page (dated 10 April 2026) checked; French matches; name spelled as printed. Count covers complaints filed only, per the page.
src: Dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo, les cas de violences sexuelles continuent d'augmenter.

Rien que pour la ville de Butembo, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, le Réseau pour les droits de l'Homme, le Redho, dit avoir enregistré, en 2025, 280 crimes de ce genre qui ont été portés devant la justice, dans un rapport rendu public à la mi-mars.
Muhindo Wasingya, le coordonnateur du Redho, s'inquiète notamment de la lenteur des procédures judiciaires qui favorise le recours à des accords à l'amiable entre les familles.

r7-E-NKW-001.s: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 had continued its attacks in eastern Congo and entered the town of Walikale, two days after Presidents Tshisekedi of Congo and Kagame of Rwanda called for a ceasefire following their meeting in Qatar.
r7-E-NKW-001.n: Independent Swahili-language corroboration of the entry into Walikale (known record dates the taking to 19 March). DW page date 20.03.2025 confirmed on page. Article byline Bakari Ubena.
r7-E-NKW-001.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date 20.03.2025 confirmed on the snapshot; same event as REC-0395 (Walikale town, 19-20 March 2025). DW page dated 20 March 2025 (byline Bakari Ubena); REC-0395 dates the taking of Walikale to 19 March.
src: M23 imeendeleza mashambulizi mashariki mwa Kongo na kuingia katika mji wa Walikale, siku mbili baada ya marais Tshisekedi wa Kongo na Kagame wa Rwanda kutoa wito wa kusitisha mapigano kufuatia mkutano wao huko Qatar.

r7-E-NKW-002.s: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the AFC/M23 alliance said, in a statement published on X, that it had decided to withdraw its forces from Walikale town and from the neighbouring areas.
r7-E-NKW-002.n: Reports a party statement (AFC/M23, via X as relayed by DW); DW is not partisan. The announcement is of intent; DW 24 March page and the DW 4 April page say the withdrawal had not yet occurred / then occurred.
r7-E-NKW-002.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). The page ends 'Vyanzo: RTRE/AFP', so the copy is credited to Reuters and AFP. Same event as REC-0400 (22-24 March 2025). Announcement of intent only; DW of 4 April 2025 reports the withdrawal took place then.
src: Muungano wa makundi ya waasi wa AFC/M23 umesema katika taarifa yake iliyochapishwa kwenye jukwaa la X, kwamba umeamua kuviondoa vikosi vyake kutoka kwenye mji wa Walikale na pia kutoka kwenye maeneo ya jirani ya mji huo.

r7-E-NKW-003.s: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that the Congolese Foreign Minister Therese Kayikwamba Wagner told journalists that the government was waiting eagerly to see whether M23 would really withdraw from the town of Walikale.
r7-E-NKW-003.n: Kinshasa reaction to the announced withdrawal (record REC-0400 covers reactions).
r7-E-NKW-003.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Wire credit RTRE/AFP at the end of the page. Kinshasa reaction belongs to REC-0400.
src: Waziri wa Mambo ya Nje wa Kongo Therese Kayikwamba Wagner, amewaambia waandishi wa Habari kwamba serikali inasubiri kwa hamu kuona kama kweli M23 watajiondoa kutoka kwenye mji wa Walikale

r7-E-NKW-004.s: Deutsche Welle Swahili reported that M23 rebels had withdrawn from the strategic town of Walikale, describing the move as a gesture of goodwill before peace talks; confirming the departure, Congolese army spokesperson Sylvain Ekenge said on Friday that his soldiers had witnessed it.
r7-E-NKW-004.n: Second, Swahili-language origin for the early-April withdrawal. Weekday only ("Ijumaa"); date computed from weekday and publication date (4 April 2025 was a Friday).
r7-E-NKW-004.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date 04.04.2025 (a Friday) confirmed; same event as REC-0402 (AFC/M23 withdrawal from Walikale, April 2025). Both sources are the same page.
src: Akithibitisha kuondoka kwa M23, msemaji wa jeshi la Kongo Sylvain Ekenge siku ya Ijumaa alisema kwamba wanajeshi wake wameshuhudia kuondoa kwao.
Waasi wa kundi la M23 katika mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kongo wamejiondoa kutoka mji wa kimkakati wa Walikale, wakielezea hatua hiyo kama ishara ya nia njema kabla ya mazungumzo ya amani.

r7-E-NKW-005.s: Taarifa Rwanda (Kinyarwanda edition) said that, in a communique issued on Monday 28 September, the organisation Forces vives de Masisi said many residents had been killed or wounded and others had fled their villages, some of them killed by drone strikes; it quoted civil society member Télesphore Mithondeke as saying that a drone attack at Kaleta-Bitoyi, in Ufamandu II, killed a woman and a child, and that fighting at Burungu in Bashali killed eight residents.
r7-E-NKW-005.l: Kaleta-Bitoyi (Ufamandu II) and Burungu (Bashali), Masisi territory
r7-E-NKW-005.a: drone strikes and fighting between AFC/M23, FARDC and Wazalendo (attribution of the drone strikes not stated in the excerpts)
r7-E-NKW-005.x: Mithondeke (via Taarifa): a woman and a child killed by a drone at Kaleta-Bitoyi; eight residents killed at Burungu
r7-E-NKW-005.n: Taarifa is a Rwanda-based outlet; it relays civil-society statements and cites Radio Okapi. Corroborates the 28 Sept air strike on Kaleta/Bitoyi (REC-0743) and the Burungu toll (REC-0740, eight civilians killed). Also says the army had not responded at the time of Radio Okapi publication. Page date 29 Sept 2026 confirmed. The statement date is that of the communique.
r7-E-NKW-005.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Taarifa is on the project's partisan list: source_type corrected to partisan_rwanda_government and grade C. Page 'Last updated: September 29, 2026' confirmed. Matches REC-0743 (Kaleta/Bitoyi air strike, 28 Sept 2026) and REC-0740 (Burungu, eight killed, about 26 Sept 2026). Rwanda-based outlet; the page cites Radio Okapi and appears to retell its report, so it is probably not independent of the Radio Okapi-based records.
src: Télesphore Mithondeke, ukora muri sosiyete sivile muri Masisi, yasabye ko hakorwa iperereza kugira ngo hamenyekane ababigizemo uruhare, anasaba impande zose ziri mu mirwano kubahiriza amategeko mpuzamahanga arengera abasivili mu gihe cy’intambara. Mithondeke yavuze ko mu gace ka Kaleta-Bitoyi, ahitwa Ufamandu II, igitero cya drone cyahitanye umugore n’umwana.

Mu itangazo ryasohowe ku wa Mbere tariki ya 28 Nzeri(9), umuryango uharanira inyungu z’abaturage wa Forces vives de Masisi wavuze ko hari abaturage benshi bishwe cyangwa bagakomereka, abandi bagahunga imidugudu yabo. Uyu muryango wavuze ko bamwe mu baturage bishwe n’ibitero by’indege zitagira abapilote (drones) zitwarwamo ibisasu
Mithondeke kandi yavuze ko imirwano yabereye i Burungu ahitwa Bashali, yahitanye abaturage umunani.

r7-E-NKW-006.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that AFC/M23 denied Amnesty International's allegations that it killed and abused small-scale miners and took gold and coltan to Rwanda; in a statement it issued in Goma on Tuesday, AFC/M23 said Amnesty had not provided solid evidence that could be examined.
r7-E-NKW-006.n: AFC/M23 reply to the Amnesty briefing of 21 September 2026 (REC-0727, REC-0728). BBC Gahuza live page dated 23 Ukw'icenda (September) 2026; statement "ejo ku wa kabiri" = Tuesday; date computed from weekday and publication date (22 September 2026). Grade B is for what AFC/M23 said, not for the underlying allegations.
r7-E-NKW-006.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page dated 23 Ukw'icenda 2026 (Wednesday); 'ejo ku wa kabiri' = yesterday, Tuesday = 22 September 2026. Reply to the Amnesty briefing in REC-0727/REC-0728. Grade B is for what AFC/M23 said, not for the allegations.
src: Umuhari AFC/M23 wahakanye ivyagiriji vya Amnesty International bivuga ko wishe kandi ugahohotera abacukuzi bato bato, ukanatwara inzahabu na coltan mu Rwanda. Mw’itangazo yasohoye i Goma ejo ku wa kabiri, AFC/M23 yavuze ko Amnesty itatanze ivyemezo bifadika bishobora gusuzumwa.

r7-E-NKW-007.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that, in a report published on Monday, Amnesty had accused the movement of killings, ill-treatment of people ('ugukubagura abantu'), detention without legal procedure, forced labour and forcible recruitment into armed groups, and said these happened at the Rubaya coltan site in North Kivu and at the Lomera gold mines in South Kivu.
r7-E-NKW-007.l: Rubaya (Masisi, North Kivu) and Lomera (South Kivu)
r7-E-NKW-007.n: Second-language retelling of Amnesty (primary: Amnesty). Translation of "ugukubagura" is "beating" (uncertain verb form). Amnesty publication date derived from "the day before" the page date; known records give 21 September 2026.
r7-E-NKW-007.vn: 'ku munsi wa mbere uheze' means 'last Monday', not 'the previous day'; with the page dated Wednesday 23 September 2026, Monday is 21 September, matching the Amnesty date in REC-0727/0728. Translation corrected in extra. Relation changed from corroborates to adds_detail because BBC relays Amnesty itself (same origin). Publication date removed from the statement. The movement is AFC/M23, the subject of the BBC entry. Retelling of Amnesty International's report; not an independent corroboration of it. 'ugukubagura' is rendered as ill-treatment; the researcher's 'beating' is uncertain. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 6)
src: Mu cegeranyo casohotse ku munsi wa mbere uheze, Amnesty yari yagirije uwo muhari ibirego vy'ubwicanyi, ugukubagura abantu, ukubapfunga ata mategeko akurikijwe, ukubakoresha ku nguvu no kubinjiza mu mirwi y’abarwanyi ku nguvu. Iryo shirahamwe ryavuze ko ivyo vyabereye ahacukurwa coltan i Rubaya muri Kivu ya Ruguru no ku birombwe vy’inzahabu vya Lomera muri Kivu y’Epfo.

r7-E-NKW-008.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 authorities in eastern DRC said more than 200 people had died after a mine collapsed in the mineral-rich town of Rubaya.
r7-E-NKW-008.x: BBC Gahuza: more than 200 dead, per M23 authorities
r7-E-NKW-008.n: BBC Gahuza (Kinyarwanda edition; published 31 Ukwa mbere 2026, updated 1 Ukwa kabiri). Known record REC-0685 gives at least 226 (Actualite.cd); this source says more than 200 per M23 authorities.
r7-E-NKW-008.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed the 226 figure from 'figures' (no excerpt prints it). BBC page 'Yatangajwe 31 Ukwa mbere 2026' confirmed. REC-0685 gives at least 226 (confirmed by the AFC/M23-appointed governorate); BBC's 'more than 200' comes from the same party, so it is not an independent count.
src: Abategetsi bo mu nyeshyamba za M23 mu burasirazuba bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DRC) bavuga ko abantu barenga 200 bapfuye nyuma yuko ikirombe gicukurwamo amabuye y'agaciro gihirimye mu mujyi wa Rubaya ukungahaye ku mabuye y'agaciro.

r7-E-NKW-009.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Lumumba Kambere Muyisa, spokesperson of the governor of North Kivu province, told the media that the upper parts of the mine had fallen into the mine on Wednesday because of heavy rain.
r7-E-NKW-009.a: AFC/M23-appointed provincial administration (as described by BBC: "M23 authorities")
r7-E-NKW-009.n: Weekday only ("ku wa gatatu"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Wednesday before Saturday 31 Jan 2026 = 28 Jan). BBC places him among "M23 authorities" in the preceding sentence; the page does not say so in this sentence.
r7-E-NKW-009.vn: Excerpt supports the statement; translation checked. Same event as REC-0685. The governor is the AFC/M23-appointed Erasto Bahati Musanga (per the same page).
src: Lumumba Kambere Muyisa, umuvugizi wa guverineri w'intara ya Kivu ya Ruguru, yabwiye ibitangazamakuru ko ibice byo hejuru by'icyo kirombe byahubukiye mu kirombe ku wa gatatu kubera imvura nyinshi

r7-E-NKW-010.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government, in a statement on the Rubaya mine collapse, said that in June 2025 more than 300 civilians had died at Rubaya in a similar way, and that a ministerial order of February 2025 had banned mining in the Rubaya zone.
r7-E-NKW-010.x: DRC government: more than 300 civilians dead, June 2025
r7-E-NKW-010.n: A June 2025 mass-casualty event at Rubaya is mentioned only in this government statement as relayed by BBC; not otherwise verified here. Kinshasa is a party. Figure of 300 is the government's. Check against r2-G-LOCAL-004 (7sur7: 300 young people arrested, 28-29 June 2025), which is a different event (arrests).
r7-E-NKW-010.vn: Excerpt supports the statement. Grade raised to B: BBC is a credible origin for what the government said; the underlying toll remains unverified (noted). The June 2025 toll is Kinshasa's claim in a statement about the January 2026 collapse; not verified elsewhere here. Not the same event as REC-0420 (arrests at Rubaya, 28 June-3 July 2025).
src: Leta ya DRC yavuze ko guhera muri Gashyantare (2) mu 2025, iteka rya minisitiri ryategetse ko akarere k'ubucukuzi bw'amabuye y'agaciro ka Rubaya katemerewe gucukurwamo kuko nta buryo bw'umutekano na bucye buhari ku bacukuzi, yibutsa ko no muri Kamena (6) mu 2025 abasivile barenga 300 bapfuye i Rubaya mu buryo nk'ubwo.

r7-E-NKW-011.s: Bwiza (Rwanda), relaying information reaching Actualite.cd, reported that on Tuesday 20 October, at Ntoto, capital of the Waloa Uroba groupement in Walikale territory, a soldier and a civilian were killed by bullets when two units of the FARDC turned on each other, and that another soldier and a civilian were seriously wounded; it said the head of the Waloa Uroba groupement, Barthélemy Mulengezi Luc, explained that the incident occurred when a group of soldiers coming from the front tried to cross Ntoto.
r7-E-NKW-011.a: FARDC soldiers (two FARDC units, including Military Police)
r7-E-NKW-011.x: Bwiza/Actualite.cd: one soldier and one civilian killed; another soldier and a civilian seriously wounded
r7-E-NKW-011.n: Known record REC-0750 (about 20 Oct 2026, Ntoto, "Waloa Loanda") gives two dead; Bwiza prints the groupement as "Waloa Uroba". Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet (partisan); the content relays Actualite.cd and Congolese officials. Page date 20 Oktoba 2026 confirmed on page. Military Police role stated in the Bwiza text, not in the excerpts.
r7-E-NKW-011.vn: Date 20 October and Tuesday are in the excerpt; page dated Jumanne 20 Oktoba 2026 confirmed. Removed 'citing' wording that went beyond the page and the Military Police role (not in the excerpts). Rwandan outlet relaying Actualite.cd: grade C, not independent of the Actualite.cd-based record. Bwiza prints the groupement as 'Waloa Uroba' here but 'Waloa Loanda' in its 27 October article; REC-0750 has Waloa Loanda.
src: Kuri uyu wa Kabiri, itariki ya 20 Ukwakira, ahitwa Ntoto, umurwa mukuru wa Gurupoma ya Waloa Uroba, muri Teritwari ya Walikale mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, umusirikare n’umusivili bishwe n’amasasu ubwo imitwe ibiri y’Ingabo za Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) yasubiranagamo.

Amakuru agera kuri ACTUALITE.CD avuga ko undi musirikare n’umusivili na bo bakomeretse bikabije. Umuyobozi wa Gurupoma ya Waloa Uroba, Barthélemy Mulengezi Luc, yasobanuye ko ibyabaye byabaye igihe itsinda ry'abasirikare bari baturutse ku rugamba bagerageza kwambuka Ntoto.

r7-E-NKW-012.s: Bwiza (Rwanda) reported that 54 soldiers of the 3415th regiment of the FARDC began to be tried before the Goma Military Court, sitting specially in Walikale, from Monday 26 October, and that they are accused of offences including murder, abandoning their duties, wasting ammunition and military equipment, and refusing to obey orders; according to Major Dieudonné Kasereka, in charge of communications in the 34th military region, the soldiers were arrested on 20 October after the events at Ntoto, in the Waloa Loanda area.
r7-E-NKW-012.a: FARDC 3415th regiment soldiers; Major Dieudonné Kasereka, communications officer, 34th military region
r7-E-NKW-012.n: Adds charges, the arrest date and the army source to REC-0752 (trial of 54 soldiers of the 3415th) and REC-0750 (Ntoto). Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet; the facts are relayed Congolese army statements.
r7-E-NKW-012.vn: 'charged with' changed to 'accused of' (bashinjwa); attribution to Kasereka limited to the arrest, which is all S2 credits to him; trial and accusations are Bwiza's narration. 'guta imirimo yabo' rendered 'abandoning their duties' rather than 'desertion'. Publication date removed; date set to trial start 26 October 2026 (Monday, matches). Page dated Kuwa Kabiri 27 Ukwakira 2026 confirmed. 'bashinjwa' = 'are accused of'; the source does not state formal charges. The verdict was expected in early November.
src: Abasirikare 54 bo muri régiment ya 3415 y’Ingabo za Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) batangiye kuburanishwa imbere y’Urukiko rwa Gisirikare rwa Goma, ruteraniye mu buryo bwihariye i Walikale, muri Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, kuva ku wa Mbere, itariki ya 26 Ukwakira.

Aba basirikare bashinjwa ibyaha birimo ubwicanyi, guta imirimo yabo, gusesagura amasasu n’ibikoresho bya gisirikare, ndetse no kwanga kumvira amategeko. ‎Biteganyijwe ko umwanzuro w’urukiko uzasohoka mu ntangiriro z’ukwezi k’Ugushyingo.

Nk’uko byatangajwe na Major Dieudonné Kasereka, ushinzwe itumanaho mu Karere ka 34 ka Gisirikare, aba basirikare batawe muri yombi ku wa 20 Ukwakira nyuma y’ibyabereye i Ntoto, mu gace ka Waloa Loanda, hafi y’umupaka na Teritwari ya Masisi.

r7-E-NKW-013.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that around 'saa saba' in the night of 19 to 20 October (the seventh hour of the night, about one in the morning), Wazalendo groups attacked AFC/M23 at Nyabiondo and heavy fighting began; it placed the Nyabiondo centre in Masisi territory, North Kivu.
r7-E-NKW-013.n: Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Monday 20, Oct 2025" confirmed. "saa saba y'ijoro" read as about 01:00. Corroborates REC-0447 (19 Oct 2025, Nyabiondo).
r7-E-NKW-013.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed the digit '1' (not printed); the clock reading is spelled out. Page 'Monday 20, Oct 2025' confirmed. Same place and night as REC-0447 (19 Oct 2025, Nyabiondo). Partisan Rwandan outlet: C. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 12)
src: Ihuriro rya AFC/M23 na Wazalendo ishyigikiwe n’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo biri mu mirwano ikomeye muri santere ya Nyabiondo iherereye muri teritwari ya Masisi, intara ya Kivu y’Amajyaruguru.
Mu masaa saba y’ijoro ryo ku wa 19 rishyira uwa 20 Ukwakira, imitwe ya Wazalendo yagabye igitero kuri AFC/M23 muri Nyabiondo, hatangira imirwano ikomeye.

r7-E-NKW-014.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that on the evening of 18 October aircraft of the DRC army fired on AFC/M23 positions at Mpeti and Buhaya in Walikale, and that AFC/M23 deputy leader Bertrand Bisimwa condemned the attack, recalling that the DRC government was violating the agreement the two sides made in Doha, Qatar.
r7-E-NKW-014.a: FARDC aircraft (per Umuryango.rw); AFC/M23 deputy head Bertrand Bisimwa (condemnation)
r7-E-NKW-014.n: Rwandan partisan outlet relaying an AFC/M23 position; no independent confirmation seen here. Not in known records for 18 Oct 2025 (checked list).
r7-E-NKW-014.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page date Monday 20 Oct 2025 confirmed; no known record for 18 Oct 2025 at Mpeti/Buhaya. Partisan outlet: C.
src: Ku mugoroba wa tariki ya 18 Ukwakira, indege z’ingabo za RDC zarashe ku birindiro bya AFC/M23 muri Mpeti na Buhaya muri Walikale. Umuyobozi wungirije wa AFC/M23, Bertrand Bisimwa, yamaganye iki gitero, yibutsa ko Leta ya RDC iri kurenga ku masezerano impande zombi zagiranye ubwo zari i Doha muri Qatar.

r7-E-NKW-015.s: Ijambo.net (Rwanda) reported that M23 took the trading centre of Mubi in Walikale territory on Friday 21 March, with reports saying it took it without fighting because the government forces had already fled it; it said the centre lies about 36 kilometres from Walikale-Centre on the road to Kisangani.
r7-E-NKW-015.n: Ijambo.net is a Rwanda-based outlet (Yirunga Ltd, Rubavu); treated as not independent of Rwandan narrative. Page "Published: 2025-03-22 11:09:56 CAT" confirmed. Related to REC-0398/REC-0399 (looting at Mubi on 20-21 March, army fall-back toward Mubi) but not the same fact; first control claim for Mubi.
r7-E-NKW-015.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). The hedge 'amakuru akavuga' covers both 'without fighting' and the flight of government forces; statement now keeps both inside it. Ijambo.net is on the partisan list: source_type corrected. Page 'Published: 2025-03-22' confirmed; 21 March 2025 is a Friday.
src: Umutwe wa M23 wigaruriye Centre y’ubucuruzi ya Mubi yo muri Teritwari ya Walikale,
M23 yayigaruriye ku wa Gatanu tariki ya 21 Werurwe, amakuru akavuga ko yayifashe itarwanye kuko mbere yo kuyigeramo ihuriro ry’Ingabo za Leta ryari ryamaze kuyihunga.
Iyi Centre iherereye mu bilometero bibarirwa muri 36 uvuye i Walikale-Centre, ku muhanda ujya mu mujyi wa Kisangani.

r7-E-NKW-016.s: BBC Swahili reported that, in a statement issued on Sunday 23 March 2025, Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the government welcomed the news that FARDC and Wazalendo military activities would also be suspended.
r7-E-NKW-016.n: Rwanda's account of the M23 announced withdrawal (REC-0400 covers reactions). Entry is on a BBC Swahili live page that carries multiple items; the entry is dated 23 Machi 2025 on the page. The live page was archived on 25 March per search metadata; entry date used.
r7-E-NKW-016.vn: Entry dated 23 Machi 2025 on the live page; 23 March 2025 is a Sunday. Excerpt supports the statement.
src: Katika taarifa iliyotolewa Jumapili Machi 23, msemaji wa serikali Yolande Makolo alisema kwamba wamepokea vyema habari kwamba shughuli za kijeshi za jeshi la FARDC na kundi la Wazalendo linalowaunga mkono yatasitishwa pia.

r7-E-NKW-017.s: BBC News Swahili reported that the Congolese army had stepped up its campaign to get FDLR rebels to surrender to Congolese authorities or to MONUSCO peacekeepers, and that police and army officers had been using loudspeakers in the Walikale area of North Kivu to urge them to surrender; it said the operation was also in the Pinga area, on the Masisi border, where some FDLR groups are said to be camped.
r7-E-NKW-017.n: BBC Swahili live-page entry dated 8 Novemba 2025 (photo credit AFP; text unattributed). Context for REC-0697/REC-0698 (FDLR at Pinga 2026) one year earlier. Kinshasa army campaign; no FDLR response (page says FDLR had made no statement on the peace plan).
r7-E-NKW-017.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Live-page entry dated 8 Novemba 2025 confirmed (photo credit AFP; no text credit).
src: Jeshi la Jamhuri ya demokrasi ya Congo limeimarisha kampeni yake ya kutaka waasi wa Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), kutoka Rwanda linaloendesha shughuli zake nchini DRC, kujisalimisha kwa mamlaka za Congo au kwa walinda amani wa Umoja wa Mataifa (MONUSCO).
Maafisa wa polisi na jeshi la FRDC wamekuwa wakitumia vipaza sauti katika eneo la Walikale, jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini, kuwahimiza waasi hao wajisalimishe.
Oparesheni hiyo pia katika eneo la Pinga, mpakani mwa Masisi, ambako kunatajwa kuwa baadhi ya makundi ya FDLR yanapiga kambi huko.

r7-E-NKW-018.s: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that M23 launched surprise attacks that broke through government forces' strongholds near the capital of the Masisi district and ended up capturing the Nyabiondo area and several neighbouring villages, from 'the day before yesterday, March 9, 2025'.
r7-E-NKW-018.l: Nyabiondo and neighbouring villages, Masisi territory
r7-E-NKW-018.n: Tanzanian daily; article is a summary of local-media reporting (page cites Kivu Morning Post and Actualite.cd elsewhere) and does not name the origin of the Nyabiondo sentence. Page date Jumanne, Machi 11, 2025 confirmed. Corroborates r2-G-NKW-MASISI-001 / REC-0388.
r7-E-NKW-018.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Jumanne, Machi 11, 2025' confirmed; same event as REC-0388. Mwananchi's article is a compilation credited 'with the help of agencies'; the origin of this sentence is not named.
src: M23 ilianzisha mashambulizi ya kushtukiza yaliyovunja ngome za vikosi vya serikali karibu na mji mkuu wa wilaya ya Masisi na kuishia kuteka eneo la Nyabiondo na vijiji kadhaa jirani, kuanzia juzi Machi 9, 2025.

r7-E-NKW-019.s: Mwananchi (Tanzania) reported that, according to media in the DRC and a statement signed by the Wazalendo leader Shukuru Bulenda, the groups that defected included Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), part of Mai-Mai Kifuafua and the Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M), and that these groups were alleged to have joined AFC/M23 on March 9, 2025.
r7-E-NKW-019.l: North Kivu (location not stated in the excerpt)
r7-E-NKW-019.a: Wazalendo groups (FPP-AP, Mai-Mai Kifuafua part, NDC-R/M) allegedly joining AFC/M23
r7-E-NKW-019.n: Related to REC-0387 (FCR allegiance to AFC/M23, 7 March 2025, different group named); Mwananchi names other groups and the date 9 March. Secondhand; other Wazalendo groups could have denied. No denial searched here.
r7-E-NKW-019.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Different group and date from REC-0387 (FCR, 7 March 2025): new_related_event kept. The Mwananchi sentence is garbled; it is unclear whether Bulenda's statement announced the defection or listed the groups. The hedge 'vinadaiwa' (alleged) is kept.
src: Kwa mujibu wa vyombo vya habari nchini DRC, taarifa iliyosainiwa na kiongozi wa wazalendo, Shukuru Bulenda, vikundi hivyo vilivyoasi ni pamoja na Mai-Mai Kabidon (FPP-AP), sehemu ya Mai-Mai Kifuafua na kikundi cha Nduma Defense of Congo-Renovated (NDC-R/M). Vikundi hivyo, vinadaiwa kujiunga na AFC/M23, juzi Machi 9, 2025.

r7-E-NKW-020.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Thursday the areas of the Nyamaboko 1 groupements in Masisi 'became the hotbed of terrifying fighting', according to Voltaire Batundi, head of Masisi civil society, and that the fighting, which began in the morning and lasted almost all day, made thousands of people leave their homes and flee.
r7-E-NKW-020.a: M23 vs FARDC and Wazalendo (fighting); no perpetrator for displacement
r7-E-NKW-020.x: Voltaire Batundi (Masisi civil society) via BBC: thousands displaced
r7-E-NKW-020.n: BBC Gahuza page "Yatangajwe 14 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025" (14 November 2025). Weekday only ("ku wa kane"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Thursday 13 November 2025). Neighbouring known records: REC-0455 (12 Nov), REC-0456 (15 Nov). Toll "thousands" is civil society's figure.
r7-E-NKW-020.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Yatangajwe 14 Ukw'icumi na rimwe 2025' (Friday) confirmed; Thursday = 13 November 2025, between REC-0455 (12 Nov) and REC-0456 (15 Nov).
src: Ku wa kane uduce twa 'groupement' za Nyamaboko1 muri Masisi "twabaye isibaniro ry'imirwano iteye ubwoba" nk'uko Voltaire Batundi ukuriye sosiyete sivile ya Masisi yabibwiye BBC. Iyo mirwano yatangiye kuva mu gitondo imara hafi umunsi wose mu bice bitandukanye, yatumye abantu babarirwa mu bihumbi bava mu ngo zabo barahunga

r7-E-NKW-021.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that some Congolese media said that on Thursday the M23 took the Kazinga area in Masisi, but that this information had not been confirmed by any of the warring sides.
r7-E-NKW-021.a: M23 (as reported by some Congolese media)
r7-E-NKW-021.n: Unconfirmed claim as BBC states. Weekday only; date computed from weekday and publication date (Thursday 13 November 2025). Kazinga also appears in REC-0460 (health centre looting, Nov-Dec 2025) and REC-0732 (Sept 2026).
r7-E-NKW-021.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source).
src: Bimwe mu binyamakuru muri Congo bivuga ko ku wa kane umutwe wa M23 wafashe agace ka Kazinga muri Masisi, gusa aya makuru ntaremezwa n'uruhande urwo ari rwo rwose muri izi zirwana.

r7-E-NKW-022.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that on Thursday 26 February 2026, at about 16:15, combined forces, especially those of the FDLR, entered the JTN tea area at Mweso and shot 19 cows, of which 15 died immediately and 4 were seriously wounded.
r7-E-NKW-022.l: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
r7-E-NKW-022.a: combined forces "mainly of the FDLR", per AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
r7-E-NKW-022.n: AFC/M23 allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Friday 27, Feb 2026" confirmed. The page itself says AFC/M23 had not issued a communique on it. Clock time printed as "16:15" with a garbled Kinyarwanda expression. No Kinshasa/FARDC response found.
r7-E-NKW-022.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Removed 'on X' (in the page but not in an excerpt). Kinyarwanda time 'saa kumi na cumi n'itanu z'amanywa' = 16:15, as printed. 26 Feb 2026 is a Thursday. Relation corrected from counterclaim to new (it is an allegation, not a reply to a record; no record for Mweso/JTN); category corrected to looting_or_destruction. Party allegation; the headline blames FARDC while the quoted account names combined forces 'especially FDLR'. No FARDC response found.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko FARDC iri gukora ibyaha by’intambara kuko iri kurasa abaturage idasize n’amatungo yabo.

Kanyuka yavuze ko ku wa Kane, tariki ya 26 Gashyantare 2026, ahagana saa kumi na Cumi n’Itanu z’amanywa (16:15), ingabo zishyize hamwe, cyane cyane iz’omutwe wa FDLR, zinjiye mu gice cy’icyayi cya JTN giherereye i Mweso.” Akomeza agira ati ” Mu bikorwa by’ubugome bukabije, abo barwanyi barashe inka 19, aho 15 zapfuye ako kanya naho 4 zigakomereka bikabije.

r7-E-NKW-023.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the fighters fired bursts of bullets at a 19-year-old girl called Wamahoro, from Kitchanga, who died immediately.
r7-E-NKW-023.l: JTN tea estate, Mweso, Masisi territory
r7-E-NKW-023.a: combined forces "mainly of the FDLR", per AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka
r7-E-NKW-023.n: Names the victim as printed by Umuryango.rw. The sentence is within the quotation attributed to Kanyuka. AFC/M23 allegation, no independent confirmation seen.
r7-E-NKW-023.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Name spelled as printed. Relation corrected from counterclaim to new; category to attack_on_civilians. Part of the same Kanyuka account as the JTN/Mweso cattle shooting of 26 February 2026; no independent confirmation.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko FARDC iri gukora ibyaha by’intambara kuko iri kurasa abaturage idasize n’amatungo yabo.
Icyababaje kurushaho, ni uko barashe amasasu y’urufaya ku mukobwa w’imyaka 19 witwa Wamahoro, ukomoka i Kitchanga, akaba yahise yitaba Imana ako kanya.”

r7-E-NKW-024.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that women it interviewed on September 21, 2025 in MPATI, in the Bashali chiefdom of Masisi territory, recounted brutal acts committed by NYATURA and CMC-FDP militiamen; a resident identified as M. N. said 'almost all the women here were raped during the war' and that she herself had suffered brutal acts at the hands of the men of Jenerali Guidon. The excerpts do not date the acts.
r7-E-NKW-024.a: NYATURA and Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement – Vikosi vya Ulinzi vya Watu (CMC-FDP) militiamen, per the women interviewed
