r7-E-NKW-024.x: SOS Médias Burundi: more than 70 victims in total per the chief of Mpati (period not stated for the total; chief's rate refers to April-October 2024)
r7-E-NKW-024.n: Local testimony reported by SOS Médias Burundi (Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 30 September 2025, dateline Goma 29 September 2025). The dates of the incidents are NOT stated: the page's chief of Mpati (Safari Mbarushimana Jean de Dieu) gives a figure of at least three women a day for April-October 2024 and "more than 70" victims in total, which falls before the project window and is not used here; the claim rests on the interviews of 21 September 2025. Witnesses are given by initials only and one is a 17-year-old ("S. O., 17"), not listed. Attribution of "General Guidon" men: Guidon Shimiray Mwissa is the NDC-R leader per other records.
r7-E-NKW-024.vn: Removed the dateline day and the 70/2024 figures (no excerpt prints them; the 2024 period is pre-window). Added M. N.'s attribution to 'General Guidon's men', which the excerpt prints and which differs from the NYATURA/CMC-FDP attribution. M. N.'s status narrowed: she says she was 'tortured by brutal acts' and does not say in the excerpt that she was raped. Page date 30 Septemba 2025, dateline Goma 29 September 2025. Window caution: the acts are undated. Elsewhere on the page the chief of Mpati dates the rapes he counts to April-October 2024, and residents say the violence stopped when M23 took control of Mpati, so the acts may predate 1 January 2025. Only the interviews (21 September 2025) are inside the window. The page also quotes a 17-year-old (initials S. O.), not listed because no excerpt prints her.
src: Mji wa MPATI, ulioko katika eneo la kichifu la Bashali, eneo la Masisi,

Wanawake waliohojiwa na SOS Media Burundi mnamo Septemba 21, 2025, walisimulia vitendo vya kinyama vilivyofanywa na wanamgambo wa NYATURA na Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement – Vikosi vya Ulinzi vya Watu (CMC-FDP).
M. N., mkazi wa MPATI, alishuhudia: “Takriban wanawake wote hapa walibakwa wakati wa vita. Mimi mwenyewe niliteswa na vitendo vya kinyama mikononi mwa wanaume wa Jenerali Guidon.

r7-E-NKW-025.s: Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that Rwandan President Kagame said that in the areas M23 controls, it does well in combating FDLR and other criminal groups, but that in Masisi, Walikale and other areas controlled by FARDC, FDLR is still found there, cooperating with government forces.
r7-E-NKW-025.n: Rwanda's own position as reported by a Rwandan outlet (party statement, not evidence of the fact). Context: REC-0697 (Pinga, FARDC helicopter delivery to FDLR-FOCA, reported) and REC-0698 (FARDC operation against FDLR around Pinga-Walikale, 29 March 2026). The occasion of the remarks is not stated in the excerpt.
r7-E-NKW-025.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page '3 April 2026 at 17:27' confirmed. Party statement (Rwanda) reported by a Rwandan outlet; not evidence of the facts asserted.
src: Perezida Kagame yavuze ko mu turere M23 igenzura, ikora neza mu guhangana na FDLR n'indi mitwe y'abagizi ba nabi, ariko mu turere twa Masisi, Walikale n’ahandi ingabo za FARDC zigenzura, FDLR iracyahaboneka aho ifatanya n'ingabo za Guverinoma.

r7-E-NKW-026.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that an air strike attributed to the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) killed about seven civilians and wounded more than 40 others on Friday, January 2, 2026, at Masisi-Center.
r7-E-NKW-026.a: FARDC (air strike attributed to FARDC, per SOS Médias Burundi)
r7-E-NKW-026.x: about seven civilians killed, more than 40 wounded (SOS Médias Burundi)
r7-E-NKW-026.n: Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 4 January 2026 confirmed. Known record REC-0681 (2 January 2026 drone strike on Masisi-centre). The page reports a drone; time of day not used (clock expression ambiguous in the Swahili translation). Attribution to FARDC is "alleged/attributed" per the page; no Kinshasa response seen on this page.
r7-E-NKW-026.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Figures field changed to words as printed. Page dateline 'Goma, Januari 4, 2026' confirmed; same event as REC-0681. The page says witnesses put it at 'saa 1:00 usiku' local time (Swahili clock: about 7 p.m.) and that a drone 'reportedly' dropped the device on a building housing a small War Child base; not used in the statement.
src: Shambulio la anga lililohusishwa na Wanajeshi wa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo (FARDC) liliua takriban raia saba na kuwajeruhi wengine zaidi ya 40 mnamo Ijumaa, Januari 2, 2026, Masisi-Center,

r7-E-NKW-027.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that, according to Doctors Without Borders (MSF), 42 people, most of them wounded in the attack, were currently admitted to the Masisi General Referral Hospital.
r7-E-NKW-027.a: not applicable (hospital admissions after a strike attributed to FARDC)
r7-E-NKW-027.x: MSF (via SOS Médias Burundi): 42 people admitted
r7-E-NKW-027.n: MSF figure as relayed by SOS Médias Burundi (MSF primary source not cited on page). Adds the hospital burden to REC-0681. No attack on the hospital is alleged here.
r7-E-NKW-027.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). 'kwa sasa wamelazwa' = 'are currently admitted', so 'then admitted' changed.
src: Kwa mujibu wa Shirika la Madaktari Wasio na Mipaka (MSF), watu 42 ambao wengi wao walijeruhiwa katika shambulio hilo kwa sasa wamelazwa katika Hospitali Kuu ya Rufaa ya Masisi.

r7-E-NKW-028.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that MONUSCO condemned on Saturday 3 January 2026 the drone strike of the previous day at Masisi-Center.
r7-E-NKW-028.n: Context statement (mediator/UN, not a party). Known record REC-0681.
r7-E-NKW-028.vn: Excerpt prints the date (Saturday, January 3, 2026, a Saturday) and the condemnation; single clause, single source.
src: Ujumbe wa Umoja wa Mataifa wa Kutuliza Utulivu katika Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo (MONUSCO) umelaani Jumamosi, Januari 3, 2026, shambulio la ndege zisizo na rubani lililotokea siku iliyotangulia huko Masisi-Center.

r7-E-NKW-029.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported, in a dispatch datelined Goma 27 November 2025, that heavy fighting broke out at dawn on Thursday between M23 rebels and local Wazalendo militiamen at the village of Kibati, in the Luberike grouping of Walikale territory.
r7-E-NKW-029.n: Burundian independent outlet; page headline date 30 November 2025, dateline "Goma, Novemba 27, 2025"; weekday "Alhamisi" = Thursday 27 November 2025 (date computed from weekday and dateline). The page says it was the fourth Wazalendo attack on Kibati in a few weeks. Neighbouring known records: REC-0450 (27-29 Oct 2025), REC-0459 (25 Nov 2025).
r7-E-NKW-029.vn: Excerpts support each clause; page headline date 30 November 2025, dateline 27 November 2025 (a Thursday).
src: SOS Médias Burundi Goma, Novemba 27, 2025 – Mapigano makali yalizuka alfajiri siku ya Alhamisi kati ya waasi wa M23, wenye mfungamano na Muungano wa Kongo River Alliance (AFC), vuguvugu la kisiasa na kijeshi linaloipinga Kinshasa, na wanamgambo wa ndani wa Wazalendo, wanaoungwa mkono na mamlaka ya Kongo.
Makabiliano hayo yalifanyika katika kijiji cha Kibati, katika kundi la Luberike, eneo la Walikale, jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini.

r7-E-NKW-030.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that the FARDC used their air force to strike AFC/M23 positions at Kibati (Walikale) and Kasopo (Masisi), and that no official casualty figures were available.
r7-E-NKW-030.a: FARDC air force (per SOS Médias Burundi)
r7-E-NKW-030.n: The page gives no date for the strikes other than the dispatch dateline; the time of day given on the page uses an ambiguous clock expression and is not used. Related to REC-0457 (21 Nov 2025 Sukhoi bombing at Kibanda near Kasopo).
r7-E-NKW-030.vn: Excerpts support the statement; date normalised to the month (original value '2025-11 (reported 2025-11-27)' is not a date). Possibly related to REC-0457 (21 Nov 2025 Sukhoi strike near Kasopo), not shown to be the same. Time given on the page ('saa 9:00 asubuhi') is ambiguous between Swahili and Western clocks and is not used.
src: FARDC (Vikosi vya Wanajeshi vya Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo) walitumia jeshi lao la anga kushambulia nyadhifa za AFC/M23 huko Kibati (Walikale) na Kasopo (Masisi).
Hakuna takwimu rasmi za majeruhi zinazopatikana, kwani eneo hilo linabaki kuwa gumu kufikiwa.

r7-E-NKW-031.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said M23 rebels had retaken the town of Masisi on the afternoon of Thursday, after he had announced in the morning of the same day that government forces had retaken it on Wednesday.
r7-E-NKW-031.n: BBC Gahuza page "Yatangajwe 9 Ukwa mbere 2025" confirmed. Kinshasa (FARDC) account; qualifies REC-0368 (reported FARDC-Wazalendo recapture of Masisi-Centre, 8 January): per the same spokesperson, the recapture was reversed on 9 January. Weekdays given on the page ("ku wa gatatu", "uno wa kane") match 8 and 9 January 2025.
r7-E-NKW-031.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Added 'afternoon' ('ku muhingamo'), which the excerpt_en dropped; translation corrected. Page 'Yatangajwe 9 Ukwa mbere 2025' (Thursday) confirmed. Qualifies REC-0368 (reported recapture, 8 January). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 30)
src: Umuvugizi w'igisirikare ca Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC), Jenerali Majoro Sylvain Ekenge amenyesha ko inyeshamba za M23 zisubije igisagara ca Masisi ku muhingamo w'uno wa kane , inyuma y'aho mu gatondo ko kuri uno musi nyene amenyeshereje ko ingabo za reta zari zakigaruye ejo ku wa gatatu.

r7-E-NKW-032.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge said government forces were doing well there and were the ones controlling the whole town of Ngungu and its surroundings.
r7-E-NKW-032.n: Party account (FARDC); no independent confirmation on the page. Ngungu also named in the UN GoE conversion of villages into towns (r2-G-DOC-858-059, August 2025).
r7-E-NKW-032.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Party claim of control; no independent confirmation on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-NKW claim 31)
src: Umuvugizi w'igisirikare ca Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC), Jenerali Majoro Sylvain Ekenge amenyesha ko inyeshamba za M23 zisubije igisagara ca Masisi ku muhingamo w'uno wa kane , inyuma y'aho mu gatondo ko kuri uno musi nyene amenyeshereje ko ingabo za reta zari zakigaruye ejo ku wa gatatu.
Jenerali Majoro Ekenge avuga ko ingabo za reta zivyifatamwo neza, kandi ko ari zo zigenzura igisagara cose ca Ngungu no mu micungararo yaco.

r7-E-NKW-033.s: BBC News Swahili reported that the M23 rebellion, backed by Rwanda, took control of the town of Masisi, an important town in eastern DRC, on Saturday, and that the DRC army had pulled back, saying it was avoiding losing more lives in the town of Masisi.
r7-E-NKW-033.n: Weekday only ("Jumamosi"); date computed from weekday and publication date (Saturday 4 January 2025, matches REC-0366). Page "Iliyochapishwa 7 Januari 2025" confirmed. The text relays AFP and Reuters (MP Alexis Bahunga quoted to AFP elsewhere on the page).
r7-E-NKW-033.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Page 'Iliyochapishwa 7 Januari 2025' confirmed; 4 January 2025 was a Saturday. REC-0366 rests on BBC News Afrique; this BBC Swahili page is likely the same BBC newsroom origin, so it is not independent corroboration.
src: Uasi wa kundi la M23, linaloungwa mkono na Rwanda, ulichukua udhibiti wa mji wa Masisi, mji muhimu mashariki mwa Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Congo, Jumamosi.
Wakati huo huo, jeshi la DRC limerudi nyuma, likisema linaepuka kupoteza maisha zaidi katika mji wa Masisi.

r7-E-NKW-034.s: BBC News Swahili reported that Alexis Bahunga, a member of parliament of North Kivu province, told AFP that it was with great sadness that he learned of the capture of the Masisi centre by M23, and that he asked the government to take steps to restore government authority across the whole area.
r7-E-NKW-034.a: Alexis Bahunga, member of parliament for North Kivu province
r7-E-NKW-034.n: A local elected official (not the executive). Quote credited by BBC to AFP: originating source AFP.
r7-E-NKW-034.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Reaction to the capture in REC-0366: relation changed from new_related_event to adds_detail. 'mbunge wa jimbo' can mean either a national MP elected in the province or a provincial deputy.
src: "Ni kwa masikitiko makubwa kufahamu kuhusu kutekwa kwa kituo cha Masisi na M23," Alexis Bahunga, mbunge wa jimbo la Kivu Kaskazini, aliliambia shirika la habari la AFP. "Tunaiomba serikali kuchukua hatua zinazolenga kurejesha mamlaka ya serikali katika eneo lote," aliongeza.

r7-E-NKW-035.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said FDLR fighters, together with Wazalendo, killed 10 residents in Masisi and Walikale territories; AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the attack was launched in the Malemo and Kalembe area, on the Masisi-Walikale border, in the night of 24 May 2026, and that in Malemo they killed three civilians, wounded six and abducted the local leader, whose fate was still unknown.
r7-E-NKW-035.a: FDLR together with Wazalendo, per AFC/M23 (Umuryango.rw headline)
r7-E-NKW-035.x: AFC/M23 (via Umuryango.rw): 10 residents killed in Masisi and Walikale; at Malemo three civilians killed, six wounded, the local leader abducted
r7-E-NKW-035.n: AFC/M23 account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date "Monday 25, May 2026" confirmed. The "10 residents" total is AFC/M23's; the page itself breaks out only three killed and six wounded at Malemo. Known record REC-0706 (night of 24-25 May 2026, Wazalendo attack on AFC/M23 positions at Kalembe, civilians killed). The word "terrorist" is the outlet's wording of AFC/M23's label, not adopted here. No Kinshasa/FARDC reply seen.
r7-E-NKW-035.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Figures written as the excerpts print them (words for three/six). Same place and night as REC-0706 (Kalembe, 24-25 May 2026). Party allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet; 'terrorist' is the outlet's/AFC/M23's label and is not adopted. No Kinshasa reply found.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yatangaje ko iki gitero cyagabwe mu gace ka Malemo na Kalembe ku rugabano rwa Masisi na Walikale mu ijoro ryo ku wa 24 Gicurasi 2026.
Kanyuka yagize ati “Muri Malemo bishe abasivili batatu, bakomeretsa batandatu, banashimuta umuyobozi waho, ubu kugeza uyu munsi ibyamubayeho ntibiramenyekana.”

Ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ryatangaje ko abarwanyi b’umutwe w’iterabwoba wa FDLR bari kumwe na Wazalendo, biciye muri Teritwari ya Masisi na Walikale abaturage 10.

r7-E-NKW-036.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwanda) reported that AFC/M23 said that after leaving those areas, FDLR and Wazalendo heavily looted the Bweru area, taking 11 cows belonging to residents and many pigs.
r7-E-NKW-036.x: AFC/M23: 11 cows and many pigs taken
r7-E-NKW-036.n: AFC/M23 allegation via Rwandan outlet (partisan). Date: night of 24 May is that of the attack, the looting is said to follow it.
r7-E-NKW-036.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source).
src: AFC/M23 yatangaje ko nyuma yo kuva muri utu duce, FDLR na Wazalendo muri utu duce, byasahuye bikomeye agace ka Bweru, bitwara inka 11 z’abaturage ndetse n’ingurube nyinshi.

r7-E-NKW-037.s: UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported on 10 September 2026 that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said government forces launched attacks at dawn on Thursday 10 September 2026 in areas including Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and their surroundings, and that, posting on X, he said the fighting was continuing and many residents had fled.
r7-E-NKW-037.l: Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje and Kibati and surroundings (Masisi and Walikale)
r7-E-NKW-037.n: AFC/M23 account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (partisan); page date September 10, 2026 confirmed. Corroborates REC-0734 (10 Sept 2026 offensive on AFC-M23 positions, Kibati) and REC-0733 (8 Sept Malemo). The Kinshasa account of the same day is in the existing records (Radio Okapi).
r7-E-NKW-037.vn: Excerpts print every date and place; page 'September 10, 2026' confirmed; 10 Sept 2026 is a Thursday. Party account, partisan relay: C. Same day and Kibati as REC-0734.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yavuze ko ingabo za Leta ya RDC zagabye ibitero mu rukerera rwo ku wa Kane, tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026, mu bice birimo Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje na Kibati n’ahabikikije.
Mu butumwa yanyujije ku rubuga rwa X, Kanyuka yavuze ko imirwano yari igikomeje ubwo yatangazaga aya makuru, ndetse ko abaturage benshi bahunze ingo zabo.

r7-E-NKW-038.s: UMUSEKE (Rwanda) reported that the AFC/M23 spokesperson said the escalation of fighting affected residents' security and could hinder aid work, and that aid organisations and their staff could not reach residents affected by the attacks.
r7-E-NKW-038.n: Party claim of humanitarian access denial attributed to Kinshasa-side attacks; no independent confirmation on the page. "Yavuze" refers to Kanyuka in the preceding sentence (excerpt starts at the claim; attribution to Kanyuka comes from the surrounding paragraph).
r7-E-NKW-038.vn: Excerpts support both clauses; S1 'Yavuze' follows S0's speaker on the page.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 yavuze ko uku gukaza imirwano kwagize ingaruka ku mutekano w’abaturage ndetse ko bishobora no kubangamira ibikorwa by’ubutabazi.
Yavuze ko imiryango itanga ubutabazi n’abakozi bayo batabasha kugera ku baturage bagizweho ingaruka n’ibitero by’ingabo za Leta ya Congo n’abafatanyabikorwa bayo.

r7-E-NKW-039.s: Rwanda Tribune (Rwanda) reported that information from the area said AFC/M23 had taken Mindjendje hill, in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba groupement; it said fighting on Thursday 10 September 2026 began in the morning and continued in areas near the border of Walikale and Masisi, and that residents said the fighting was heavy and drones were used.
r7-E-NKW-039.l: Mindjendje hill, Banakindi, Kisimba groupement (Walikale-Masisi border)
r7-E-NKW-039.n: Rwandan outlet (partisan) citing unnamed local information; "Last updated: September 11, 2026 6:35 am" on page. Precedes REC-0741 (about 27 Sept 2026, FARDC retaking positions around Mindjendje), which implies the position changed hands; this claim records only the 10 September claim of capture.
r7-E-NKW-039.vn: Removed the 'last updated' day (11 not in an excerpt). The page does not tie the capture explicitly to the 10 September fighting; the statement now reports the two separately. Precedes REC-0741 (FARDC retaking positions around Mindjendje, about 27 Sept 2026).
src: Amakuru aturuka muri ako gace avuga ko AFC/M23 yigaruriye umusozi wa Mindjendje, uherereye mu gace ka Banakindi, muri groupement ya Kisimba.

Imirwano yabereye kuri uyu wa Kane, tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026, yatangiye mu gitondo, ikomereza mu bice biri hafi y’umupaka w’uturere twa Walikale na Masisi. Abaturage bo muri ako gace bavuga ko imirwano yari ikomeye, ndetse hakaba harakoreshejwe n’indege zitagira abapilote.

r7-E-NKW-040.s: Bwiza (Rwanda, English edition), relaying Actualite.cd, reported that various reports from the Waloa Loanda groupement in Walikale territory indicated that a large number of armed individuals, believed to be FDLR rebels, were disturbing security in Mishipo, in the Makungurano area; that, according to several sources, a man claiming to be a general, known as Mutayonga and said to be from Masisi territory, had been in Mishipo for several days with around 100 armed men; that reports suggested the group's leader told residents to vacate the area, claiming he had bought the land; and that, according to information received by Actualite.cd, the alleged FDLR fighters had been firing shots to intimidate the population.
r7-E-NKW-040.l: Mishipo, Makungurano area, Waloa Loanda groupement, Walikale territory
r7-E-NKW-040.a: armed individuals believed to be FDLR rebels, led by a man known as Mutayonga (per local reports)
r7-E-NKW-040.n: Rwandan outlet republishing Actualite.cd material (the page says "According to information received by Actualite.cd"); page date "Tuesday, July 8, 2025" confirmed. Alleged FDLR attribution rests on "believed to be", not established. Not checked against Actualite.cd original (French). Status: intimidation and an eviction demand; no casualties reported on the page.
r7-E-NKW-040.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement (no excerpt prints it; the source date is shown with the source). Kept the 'reports suggest' hedge on the eviction demand and added the S3 clause the claim cited but did not state. Page 'Tuesday, July 8, 2025' confirmed. FDLR attribution is 'believed to be'/'alleged' in the source. No casualties reported.
src: Various reports from the Waloa Loanda groupement (in Walikale Territory , North Kivu) indicate that a large number of armed individuals , believed to be FDLR rebels , are disturbing security in Mishipo , in the Makungurano area.

According to several sources, a man claiming to be a general , known as Mutayonga and said to be from Masisi Territory , has been in Mishipo for several days, accompanied by around 100 armed men , carrying both heavy and light weapons .
reports suggest that in a meeting with locals, the group's leader told residents to vacate the area , claiming that he had bought the land
According to information received by Actualite.cd , since the group’s arrival, the alleged FDLR fighters have been firing shots to intimidate the population

r7-E-SKN-001.s: Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that heavy fighting with heavy weapons between AFC/M23 fighters and the Wazalendo and FARDC coalition began, from 'saa saba z'amanywa' (the Kinyarwanda daytime hour count), on Thursday 3 September 2026 at Chinono, an area linking Ziralo and Mubuku in Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe territory; it cited local civil society as saying the fighting made many residents flee.
r7-E-SKN-001.l: Chinono, between Ziralo and Mubuku groupements, Buhavu chiefdom, Kalehe
r7-E-SKN-001.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo and FARDC coalition (as the source names them)
r7-E-SKN-001.n: Single Rwandan outlet relaying Kivu Morning Post (originating_source); not in known_records (claim_search 'Chinono' returns nothing). Hour is printed in Kinyarwanda clock style ('saa saba z'amanywa', i.e. the seventh hour of the day, 13:00 by the usual conversion); the statement keeps the printed form. Bwiza is Rwanda-based; treat as relay.
r7-E-SKN-001.vn: Page (Bwiza, byline Denis Nsengiyumva, dated 4 Sept 2026) prints both passages; it credits Kivu Morning Post for the account. 3 Sept 2026 is a Thursday. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 0)
src: Imirwano ikaze yakoreshejwemo intwaro ziremereye yahuje kuva saa saba z’amanywa kuri uyu wa Kane ushize, itariki ya 3 Nzeri 2026, abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 n’ihuriro rya Wazalendo na FARDC ahitwa Chinono muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo. Iyo mirwano nk’uko tubikesha urubuga rwa Kivu Morning Post, yabereye mu gace ka Chinono gahuza uduce twa Ziralo na Mubuku muri Sheferi ya Buhavu, Teritwari ya Kalehe,

Nk’uko bitangazwa n’imiryango itegamiye kuri leta (sosiyete sivile) yo muri ako gace, iyi mirwano yatumye abaturage benshi bahunga. Bamwe berekeza i Ramba muri Gurupoma ya Mubuku, mu gihe abandi bahungiye mu mashyamba.

r7-E-SKN-002.s: Bwiza, citing Kivu Morning Post, reported that other fighting in the same area took place on Wednesday 2 September 2026 when the coalition attacked the village of Lomera in Kabare territory, and that an AFC/M23 communiqué said the attack killed people and made many residents flee.
r7-E-SKN-002.a: the Wazalendo-FARDC coalition (as the page refers back to it); casualty claim from an AFC/M23 communiqué
r7-E-SKN-002.n: AFC/M23 account relayed; no toll given. Related to REC-1073 (Lomera, September 2026, Amnesty: four men detained by M23) and the 2025 Lomera mining suspension records, but a different event. Contradiction to check: none. Date 'Wednesday, 2 September' printed with day and month in the page (kuwa Gatatu, itariki 2 Nzeri).
r7-E-SKN-002.vn: Statement supported. Actor corrected: 'ihuriro ry'izo ngabo zirwanira ubutegetsi' refers back to the Wazalendo-FARDC alliance named earlier on the page ('forces fighting for the government'), not to unnamed 'forces fighting for power'. The deaths rest only on the AFC/M23 communiqué; no toll. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 1)
src: Indi mirwano muri icyo gice yabaye kuwa Gatatu, itariki 2 Nzeri, ubwo ihuriro ry’izo ngabo zirwanira ubutegetsi zateraga Umudugudu wa Lomera, muri Teritwari ya Kabare. Ihuriro AFC/M23 mu itangazo ryashyize ahagaragara ryavuze ko icyo gitero cyahitanye abantu ndetse gituma abaturage bahunga ku bwinshi.

r7-E-SKN-003.s: Bwiza (byline Bénjamin BABOU) reported that AFC/M23 had taken Tushunguti, in Ziralo groupement, Kalehe territory, after heavy fighting with FARDC and armed groups supporting it, and that information from the area said AFC/M23 fighters had driven out Wazalendo and others on the Kinshasa side.
r7-E-SKN-003.n: Page is dated 2 September 2026 and does not say on which day the capture happened (date given is the report date; 'approximate'). The page also cites a Critical Threats report for 18-19 August captures (digest, not cited here) and says fighting resumed at Tushunguti on 17 August. Compare REC-1043/1044/1045 (Tushunguti April-May 2026) and REC-1254/1257 (Aug 2026). Control claim: Tushunguti held by AFC/M23 as of 2 Sept 2026 per Bwiza.
r7-E-SKN-003.vn: Statement supported (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, dated 2 Sept 2026). Date corrected to a report date: the page does not give the day of capture and itself cites a Critical Threats report that AFC/M23 took Tushunguti on 18 August 2026 ('Raporo ya Critical Threats ivuga ko ku wa 18 Kanama AFC/M23 yafashe Tushunguti'), so the capture may predate 2 September. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. The page also cites Critical Threats for a capture of Tushunguti on 18 August 2026; the day of the capture it reports is not given.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 wafashe agace ka Tushunguti gaherereye muri Groupement ya Ziralo, muri Teritwari ya Kalehe mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, nyuma y’imirwano ikomeye n’ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) n’imitwe yitwaje intwaro iyishyigikiye.
Amakuru ava muri ako gace avuga ko abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bashoboye kwirukana abarwanyi ba Wazalendo n’abandi bari ku ruhande rwa Leta ya Kinshasa, maze bigarurira Tushunguti.

r7-E-SKN-004.s: Bwiza reported, citing information from the area, that FARDC supported by Wazalendo fighters retook the centre of Numbi in Kalehe territory on Tuesday 6 October 2026 after it had been controlled by M23 rebels for several months; it added that, according to some information, M23 fighters had fallen back to Numbi on Monday after losing positions at Shanje, Gasenda and the hills of Bukumba.
r7-E-SKN-004.n: Corroborates REC-1080 (Numbi retaken by FARDC and Wazalendo, 6 Oct 2026) and the Shanje/Lumbishi/Numbi entries REC-1081 and REC-1083 from a Kinyarwanda outlet (Bwiza, Rwanda-based; source of 'amakuru aturuka mu gace' not named). Adds the names Gasenda and the Bukumba hills as positions the source says M23 lost on the previous days. Bwiza also published (later, per its own related-links) that AFC/M23 retook Lumbishi and Numbi hours after Wazalendo took them; not fetched.
r7-E-SKN-004.vn: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 6 Oct 2026). Bwiza's sources are unnamed local information. Same day Bwiza published that AFC/M23 retook Numbi within hours (claim 25). Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
src: Ingabo za Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC), zifashijwe n'abarwanyi ba Wazalendo, zongeye kwigarurira centre ya Numbi kuri uyu wa Kabiri, itariki ya 6 Ukwakira 2026, muri Teritwari ya Kalehe muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo, nyuma y'amezi menshi hagenzurwa n'inyeshyamba za M23, nk'uko amakuru aturuka mu gace abivuga.
Nk'uko amakuru amwe abivuga, abarwanyi ba M23 bari basubiye inyma basubira muri Numbi kuwa Mbere nyuma yo gutakaza ibirindiro cyane cyane i Shanje, Gasenda, n'udusozi twa Bukumba.

r7-E-SKN-005.s: Bwiza reported that, according to information announced by the AFC/M23 alliance, forces fighting for Kinshasa, chiefly FDLR members, began destruction at Shanje and its surroundings (Kalehe territory) on Wednesday 7 October 2026 from 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo', burning many civilian houses and the market; the AFC/M23 communiqué said further information on damage and casualties would be published later.
r7-E-SKN-005.n: Party account (AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet); cite only for what AFC/M23 said. Concerns REC-1084 (Shanje shops burned, night of 6-7 Oct 2026, Radio Maendeleo citing returnees, no perpetrator attributed in that record). Time discrepancy between outlets: Bwiza prints the start as 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo', Umuryango prints 'saa Kumi n'igice' (no a.m./p.m. qualifier) for what it says Lawrence Kanyuka stated (see companion claim); on the usual Kinyarwanda conversion the two read 10:30 and 04:30 and cannot both be right if converted, so the printed forms are kept. Do not read the burning as established; no independent attribution to FDLR found in this unit.
r7-E-SKN-005.vn: All three passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 7 Oct 2026, published 06:34; title 'FDLR iravugwaho' = 'FDLR is alleged'). The first sentence is in Bwiza's voice but the page states the information comes from the AFC/M23 communiqué; party account only. Same event as REC-1084 (Shanje burning, 6-7 Oct 2026). Hour discrepancy: Bwiza prints 'saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo' (10:30 a.m. on the Kinyarwanda clock) but published this piece at 06:34 on 7 October, so 10:30 that morning cannot be right as converted; Umuryango prints Kanyuka's start time as 'saa Kumi n'igice' (04:30 or 16:30). Both may render 4:30 a.m.; unresolved. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 4)
src: Amakuru atangazwa n’Ihuriro AFC/M23 aravuga ko amazu menshi y'abasivili yatwitse hamwe n'isoko ryaho,

Kuri uyu wa Gatatu, itariki ya 7 Ukwakira 2026, guhera saa yine n'igice za mu gitondo, ihuriro ry’ingabo zirwanira ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, cyane cyane abagize umutwe wa FDLR, zakoze ibikorwa byo gusenya mu gace ka Shanje no mu nkengero zaho muri Teritwari ya Kalehe.
Ihuriro AFC/M23 mu itangazo ryashyize ahagaragara ryavuze ko amakuru y’inyongera ku bijyanye n’ibyangiritse ndetse n’ababa baguye muri ibi bikorwa bizatangazwa nyuma.

r7-E-SKN-006.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a message on 7 October 2026 that attacks by forces supporting the Kinshasa government, including FDLR fighters, in the Shanje area of Kalehe territory had destroyed civilian houses and the market, and that details of the damage and of any dead or wounded would be published later.
r7-E-SKN-006.a: AFC/M23 spokesperson (accusing FDLR and Kinshasa-aligned forces)
r7-E-SKN-006.n: Party statement relayed by Rwandan outlet Umuryango.rw (page loaded via browser UA). Statement kind: social-media/message as reported. Time of start differs from Bwiza's report of the same communiqué (see companion claim). Concerns REC-1084.
r7-E-SKN-006.vn: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 7 Oct 2026; read from the retained copy, the live site refuses plain requests). Party statement only. Same event as REC-1084 and claim 4. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 5)
src: Ihuriro rya AFC/M23 rivuga ko ingabo zishyigikiye ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, zirimo abarwanyi ba FDLR, zagabye ibitero mu bice bya Shanje no mu nkengero zaho, muri Teritwari ya Kalehe, Kivu y’Amajyepfo.

Mu butumwa bwatanzwe ku wa 7 Ukwakira 2026, Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yavuze ko ibyo bitero byatangiye guhera saa Kumi n’igice, avuga ko byagize ingaruka ku baturage n’ibikorwa byabo. Kanyuka yavuze ko mu byangijwe harimo amazu y’abasivili ndetse n’isoko,
Yatangaje ko amakuru arambuye ku buso bw’ibyangijwe ndetse n’umubare w’abantu bashobora kuba barapfuye cyangwa bagakomereka azatangazwa nyuma.

r7-E-SKN-007.s: DW Kiswahili (Iddi Ssessanga) reported that a woman, whose name DW said had been changed for her safety, told DW that three soldiers broke into her home and one of them tried to rape her; DW said the incident took place in February in Kavumu village, 30 km from Bukavu.
r7-E-SKN-007.l: Kavumu village, about 30 km from Bukavu, Kabare
r7-E-SKN-007.a: three soldiers (not further identified by the source)
r7-E-SKN-007.n: Corroborates REC-0776 (attempted rape during break-in by three soldiers, Kavumu, February 2025) from an independent outlet that spoke to the survivor (name changed by DW, so not listed). The page does not say which army the soldiers belonged to; the same article says community groups blame the Congolese army and Wazalendo for sexual violence in northern South Kivu villages (see companion claim).
r7-E-SKN-007.vn: Both passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Iddi Ssessanga, 2 July 2025). The survivor's name on the page, 'Riziki', is a pseudonym DW says it changed, so it is not listed as a name. The soldiers' army is not stated. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: ambaye aliileza DW jinsi askari watatu walivovamia nyumba yake na mmoja wao kujaribu kumbaka.
Tukio hilo lilitokea Februari katika kijiji cha Kavumu, kilomita 30 kutoka Bukavu.
Miongoni mwa waathirika ni Riziki (jina limebadilishwa kwa usalama wake), ambaye aliileza DW jinsi askari watatu walivovamia nyumba yake na mmoja wao kujaribu kumbaka.

r7-E-SKN-008.s: DW Kiswahili reported that, in villages of northern South Kivu that it describes as having become war zones during the fighting of January and February, women and children suffered rape and sexual violence by armed men, and that community groups and activists blamed the Congolese army and Wazalendo fighters (from North Kivu) for taking part.
r7-E-SKN-008.l: Villages in northern South Kivu along Lake Kivu (Kalehe and Kabare area, as the article frames the M23 advance on Bukavu)
r7-E-SKN-008.a: Congolese army and Wazalendo fighters, as blamed by community groups and activists
r7-E-SKN-008.n: Adds a second origin (community groups and activists, as relayed by DW) for the attribution in REC-0763 / REC-0765 (sexual violence by FARDC and Wazalendo in Kalehe and between Kalehe and Kavumu, Jan-Feb 2025). The article names no village except Kavumu and no number; place given only as 'villages in the north of South Kivu'.
r7-E-SKN-008.vn: Narrowed: the page dates the M23 advance that turned villages into war zones to 'between January and February'; it does not itself date the rapes, so the statement now ties them to that period of fighting rather than stating their dates as fact. The year is the page's (2 July 2025). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Katika vijiji vya kaskazini mwa jimbo la Kivu Kusini, wanawake na watoto walikumbwa na vitendo vya ubakaji na ukatili wa kingono kutoka kwa wanaume waliokuwa na silaha.
Makundi ya kijamii na wanaharakati wanalilaumu jeshi la Kongo pamoja na wapiganaji wa kundi la Wazalendo (kutoka Kivu Kaskazini) kushiriki katika matukio haya.
kuligeuza vijiji kadhaa kando ya Ziwa Kivu kuwa maeneo ya vita kati ya Januari na Februari

r7-E-SKN-009.s: DW Kiswahili reported that in areas taken by M23, such as Bukavu and Goma, witnesses had reported a rise in rape, mostly of married women and girls, and that some women were forced to have sex to obtain certain services; it said many survivors do not report out of fear or shame.
r7-E-SKN-009.a: not attributed by the source beyond 'areas taken by M23'
r7-E-SKN-009.n: General statement attributed to unnamed witnesses; no date, place within Bukavu or perpetrator given. The page does not attribute the acts to M23 itself; it only places them in M23-held areas.
r7-E-SKN-009.vn: Passage on the page (DW Kiswahili, 2 July 2025). Unnamed witnesses; no perpetrator named beyond the place being M23-held. 'wake za watu' = married women.
src: Katika maeneo yaliyotekwa na M23, kama Bukavu na Goma, mashuhuda wameripoti ongezeko la ubakaji – hasa dhidi ya wake za watu na wasichana – ambapo baadhi ya wanawake hulazimishwa kufanya ngono ili kupata huduma fulani. Waathirika wengi hawaripoti kutokana na hofu au aibu.

r7-E-SKN-010.s: DW Kiswahili, citing MSF, reported that in the north of South Kivu MSF had attended to nearly 700 victims since the start of the year.
r7-E-SKN-010.x: DW citing MSF: nearly 700 victims treated in northern South Kivu since the start of 2025
r7-E-SKN-010.n: Relays MSF figures (originating_source MSF); complements REC-0773 (MSF survivors assisted, Kalehe and Uvira regions, Jan-June 2025); the DW wording says 'north of South Kivu' and does not name Kalehe.
r7-E-SKN-010.vn: Supported. 'wahanga' is 'victims', not 'survivors'; wording aligned. Relays MSF; the year is the page's (2 July 2025).
src: Kaskazini mwa Kivu Kusini, MSF imewahudumia karibu wahanga 700 tangu mwanzo wa mwaka.

r7-E-SKN-011.s: DW Kiswahili (Mitima DeLachance) reported that hundreds of Catholic women marched in South Kivu on the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women, representing 44 parishes of the Bukavu archdiocese, and that the march was held at the Olame centre because public demonstrations had been banned by the new authorities of Bukavu city.
r7-E-SKN-011.a: new authorities of Bukavu city (AFC/M23 administration, as the source implies)
r7-E-SKN-011.n: Reports a ban on public demonstrations by 'watawala wapya' (new rulers) of Bukavu; the page does not name the ban's issuer or date. The march was about sexual violence used as a weapon of war and digital harassment.
r7-E-SKN-011.vn: All passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Mitima DeLachance, 25 Nov 2025). The page does not name who issued the ban or when.
src: Tarehe 25 Novemba ni Siku ya Kimataifa ya Kutokomeza Ukatili dhidi ya Wanawake. Nchini Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo, mamia ya wanawake wa dhehebu la kikatoliki waliandamana Kivu Kusini kudai kukomeshwa ukatili huo.
Wanawake hao waliowakilisha parokia 44 za dayosisi kuu ya Bukavu, walifanya gwaride la amani kupinga unyanyasaji wa kidijitali na unyanyasaji wa kingono unaotumika kama silaha ya vita.
Kwa kuwa maandamano ya umma yamepigwa marufuku na watawala wapya wa jiji la Bukavu, gwaride hili liliandaliwa katika kiwanja cha kituo cha Olame, kikiwa mojawapo ya miundo ya dayosisi ya Bukavu.

r7-E-SKN-012.s: DW Kiswahili reported that before AFC/M23 took Bukavu in February, soldiers of the Congolese army had already been convicted of sexual violence against women in several villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that when AFC-M23 arrived in Bukavu the accused fled, together with judges and lawyers.
r7-E-SKN-012.l: Villages of Kabare and Kalehe territories; Bukavu
r7-E-SKN-012.a: soldiers of the Congolese army (convicted, per DW)
r7-E-SKN-012.n: Corroborates REC-0767 (Bukavu court sentences soldiers for murder and rape, 14 Feb 2025) and REC-0768/0769 (escape of detainees, convicted SGBV prisoners) from Swahili-language DW; no names or dates in this passage.
r7-E-SKN-012.vn: Passage on the DW Kiswahili page (25 Nov 2025). 'wamehukumiwa' = had been sentenced; 'washtakiwa' = the accused, as translated.
src: Kabla ya AFC/M23 kuuteka mji wa Bukavu mnamo Februari, askari wa jeshi la Kongo walikuwa tayari wamehukumiwa kwa ukatili wa kijinsia dhidi ya wanawake katika vijiji kadhaa vya wilaya za Kabare na Kalehe. AFC-M23 walipofika Bukavu, washtakiwa walikimbia, pamoja na majaji na mawakili.

r7-E-SKN-013.s: DW Kiswahili reported that, after AFC/M23 reached Bukavu, rape cases were later witnessed although they were dismissed by AFC/M23; it quoted women's rights defender Nono Mwavita as saying women's security has not improved.
r7-E-SKN-013.n: The article does not say who raised the cases, how many, or in what words AFC/M23 rejected them: a denial reported at second hand by DW. Pairs with the 'new' claim on rises in rape in Bukavu and with REC-0859 (climate of fear nine months after the capture).
r7-E-SKN-013.vn: Both passages on the DW page (25 Nov 2025). The denial is reported at second hand; no wording, date or number.
src: Lakini pia baadae visa vya ubakaji vilishuhudiwa licha yakuwa vilitupiliwa mbali na AFC/M23.
Nono Mwavita ni Mtetezi wa haki za wanawake, anasema usalama wa mwanamke bado haujaimarika na anatoa wito kwa pande zote kwenye migogoro kulinda wanawake na watoto.

r7-E-SKN-014.s: Bwiza reported a communiqué of Lawrence Kanyuka, whom it called FRN spokesperson, saying that on Monday 26 October 2026 at about 4:00 a.m. the Kinshasa-backed forces attacked Mitimbili and Munanira in Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu territory, after attacks on Kuwihene, Rugezi and Point Zéro in the Minembwe area the previous night using kamikaze drones and 120mm and 82mm mortars.
r7-E-SKN-014.l: Mitimbili and Munanira, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu
r7-E-SKN-014.a: joint forces supporting Kinshasa (as alleged in the communiqué)
r7-E-SKN-014.n: Party account only (the spokesperson is printed as 'Umuvugizi wa FRN, Lawrence Kanyuka'; the unit's other records call Kanyuka AFC/M23 spokesperson: FRN is printed as the source has it, not resolved here). Relates to REC-0580 (26-27 Oct: FARDC claims to retake Mitimbili) and REC-0574 (12 Oct Mitimbili). Minembwe parts belong to unit E-FIZ. Do not read the attack claims as established.
r7-E-SKN-014.vn: All passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 26 Oct 2026, published 14:43). Party account. Bwiza prints 'Umuvugizi wa FRN' and 'Murenge wa Kaziba' (murenge = sector; Kaziba is a chiefdom in the DRC system); printed labels kept. Related to REC-0580. Bwiza calls Kanyuka 'FRN spokesperson' here; BBC Gahuza headlines on the same site describe FRN as an armed movement led by Joseph Kabila. The label is kept as printed.
src: Nk'uko bigaragara mu itangazo ryashyizwe ahagaraga n'Umuvugizi wa FRN, Lawrence Kanyuka, "mu ijoro ryo ku wa 25 rishyira ku wa 26 Ukwakira 2026, ingabo zifatanyije zishyigikiye ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa zongereye ibitero zigaba Kuwihene, Rugezi, Point Zéro n’inkengero zaho mu karere ka Minembwe.
Iri tangazo rivuga ko ibi bitero byakozwe hifashishijwe indege zitagira abapilote zikoreshwa nk’ibisasu (kamikaze drones) hamwe n’intwaro ziremereye, zirimo za mortier 120mm na 82mm.

Mu gitondo cyo ku wa Mbere, itariki ya 26 Ukwakira 2026, ahagana saa kumi za mu gitondo (4:00 a.m.), izo ngabo n'ubundi zagabye ibitero ahitwa Mitimbili na Munanira, mu Murenge wa Kaziba muri Teritwari ya Walungu, muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo," ibi ni ibikomeza gutangazwa muri iryo tangazo.

r7-E-SKN-015.s: Bwiza reported that on Monday 12 October 2026 fighting between AFC/M23 fighters and FARDC supported by Wazalendo was reported in Kaziba chiefdom, and that, according to information from the area reaching Bwiza, it restarted at 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' on the Mitimbili hills in Muhumba groupement, east of Kaziba near the border with Bafulero chiefdom; it added that a second battle at Mwera in Butuzi groupement was reported on social network X.
r7-E-SKN-015.l: Mitimbili hills, Muhumba groupement, Kaziba chiefdom, Walungu; Mwera, Butuzi groupement
r7-E-SKN-015.n: Corroborates REC-0574 (resumption of clashes on the Mitimbili hills, 12 Oct 2026) from a Kinyarwanda outlet; adds Mwera (Butuzi groupement) as a second reported front, sourced by Bwiza only to posts on X (a lead, not verified). Bwiza prints the hour as 'saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo' (twelfth hour of the day on the Kinyarwanda clock, i.e. 06:00 by the usual conversion; kept as printed).
r7-E-SKN-015.vn: All passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 12 Oct 2026, published 07:19, consistent with a 06:00 start). The Mwera front rests on social-media posts only. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 14)
src: Kuri uyu wa Mbere, itariki ya 12 Ukwakira 2026, haravugwa imirwano mishya, iri kubera muri Sheferi ya Kaziba, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, hagati y’abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 na FARDC ishyigikiwe na Wazalendo.

Nk’uko amakuru aturuka muri ako gace agera kuri Bwiza abitangaza, imirwano yongeye gutangira saa kumi n'ebyiri za mu gitondo ku dusozi twa Mitimbili, muri Gurupoma ya Muhumba, mu burasirazuba bwa Kaziba, hafi y'umupaka na Sheferi ya Bafulero.
Urundi rugamba rwa kabiri ruri kubera ahitwa muri Mwera, muri Gurupoma ya Butuzi groupement, nkuko bigaragara mu yandi makuru agaragara ku rubuga nkoranyambaga rwa X.

r7-E-SKN-016.s: Umuryango.rw reported that the Wazalendo alliance, backed by the DRC government, expelled students and teachers from schools in Kabare and Walungu territories of South Kivu, that the expulsions began on 9 September 2025, and that videos on social media showed people fleeing while Wazalendo fighters told them studying or teaching meant nothing to them.
r7-E-SKN-016.l: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
r7-E-SKN-016.n: Corroborates REC-0847 (9 Sept 2025, armed men presenting themselves as Wazalendo empty schools in Kabare territory) from a Rwanda-based outlet that relies on social-media videos and does not give its own eyewitness source; extends the area to Walungu territory. Umuryango.rw is Rwandan and its framing is partisan towards AFC/M23; the facts rest on videos it describes, which this unit did not see.
r7-E-SKN-016.vn: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline JABO Blaise Patience, 11 Sept 2025; retained copy). Rests on videos the outlet describes. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
src: Ihuriro ry’imitwe yitwaje intwaro rya Wazalendo rishyigikiwe n’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo ryirukanye abanyeshuri n’abarimu mu mashuri yo muri teritwari ya Kabare na Walungu mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo.
Ibikorwa byo gusohora abanyeshuri n’abarimu mu mashuri byatangiye tariki ya 9 Nzeri 2025.
Amashusho yakwirakwiye ku mbuga nkoranyambaga agaragaza bose bahunga, abarwanyi bo muri Wazalendo bababwira ko kwiga cyangwa kwigisha kwabo ntacyo bibabwiye.

r7-E-SKN-017.s: Umuryango.rw reported that, in videos circulating on social media, one Wazalendo fighter was heard speaking Swahili and saying that students found studying would be killed, and another told students everyone should go home and that whoever went to school would die.
r7-E-SKN-017.l: Schools in Kabare and Walungu territories
r7-E-SKN-017.a: Wazalendo (as heard in videos described by the outlet)
r7-E-SKN-017.n: Threats as described by the outlet from videos it did not link; not independently verified here. Pairs with the school expulsions claim and with REC-0847. Quote translated from the Kinyarwanda rendering the outlet prints.
r7-E-SKN-017.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 11 Sept 2025). Quotes are the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering of videos it did not link.
src: Umwe muri Wazalendo yumvikanye avuga mu rurimi rw’Igiswahili, ati “Abanyeshuri dusanga bari kwiga turabica. Ndabivuze, nta mishyikirano irabaho.
Undi murwanyi yagize ati “Abanyeshuri bose, umuntu wese ajye iwabo kandi urajya ku ishuri arapfa.

r7-E-SKN-018.s: Umuryango.rw reported that the AFC/M23 alliance condemned the silence of the international community, aid organisations and human rights defenders while Wazalendo continued actions depriving residents of their rights, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said, citing the Wazalendo statements, that 'these words push people into killings and war crimes'.
r7-E-SKN-018.n: Party statement (AFC/M23 spokesperson as reported by a Rwanda-based outlet); the legal phrase 'war crimes' ('ibyaha by’intambara') is Kanyuka's, quoted with attribution, not a finding. Statement kind: statement as reported; no date of utterance given beyond the article date.
r7-E-SKN-018.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 11 Sept 2025). 'War crimes' is Kanyuka's phrase, quoted with attribution.
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa RDC ryamaganye uguceceka k’umuryango mpuzamahanga, imiryango y’ubutabazi n’abaharanira uburenganzira bw’ikiremwamuntu mu gihe Wazalendo ikomeje ibikorwa byambura abaturage uburenganzira bwabo.
Umuvugizi w’iri huriro, Lawrence Kanyuka, yashingiye ku magambo yavuzwe na Wazalendo, agira ati “Aya magambo ashora abantu mu bwicanyi n’ibyaha by’intambara agamije gusenya ahazaza h’abana bacu.”

r7-E-SKN-019.s: DW Kiswahili reported that local civil society organisations spoke of the deaths of at least seven people, including five civilians, and of wounded people being treated at Kavumu health facilities, after Wazalendo tried for a few minutes to take Kavumu airport before M23 forces drove them out.
r7-E-SKN-019.x: Civil society (via DW): at least seven dead, including five civilians; wounded treated at Kavumu health facilities
r7-E-SKN-019.n: Adds a toll to REC-0812 (Wazalendo temporarily retake Kavumu airport, 13 April 2025): civil society sources cited by DW say at least 7 dead including 5 civilians. Date: the article is dated 14 April 2025 and describes calm after the violence; the incident date is taken from REC-0812, not from this page.
r7-E-SKN-019.vn: Statement supported (DW Kiswahili, 14 April 2025). Date corrected: this page does not date the Kavumu attack (13 April came from REC-0812, not from this source); the claim is dated by its report.
src: Mashirika ya kiraia ya eneo hilo yanazungumzia kuhusu vifo vya watu wasiopunguwa saba wakiwemo raia watano na watu waliojeruhiwa wanaotibiwa katika vituo vya afya vya Kavumu. Wapiganaji hao wa Wazalendo walijaribu kuuteka uwanja wa ndege wa Kavumu kwa dakika chache kabla ya kutimuliwa kwa nguvu na vikosi vya M23.

r7-E-SKN-020.s: DW Kiswahili reported that further heavy fighting between M23 and Wazalendo took place 'yesterday, Sunday' at Burhale in Walungu district, where vehicles and houses suspected of sheltering M23 were burned by Wazalendo in an area called Mashango.
r7-E-SKN-020.n: Date computed from weekday and publication date (article dated 14 April 2025, 'jana Jumapili' = Sunday 13 April 2025). Not in known_records at Mashango (REC-0477 is Burhale, 18 March 2025). Single source; no toll.
r7-E-SKN-020.vn: Passage on the DW page dated 14 April 2025 (a Monday), so 'jana Jumapili' is 13 April 2025. Single source, no toll.
src: Mapigano mengine makali kati ya M23 na Wazalendo yalitokea jana Jumapili huko Burhale katika wilaya ya Walungu ambapo magari na nyumba zinazoshukiwa kuwahifadhi M23 zilichomwa moto na Wazalendo katika eneo linaloitwa Mashango.

r7-E-SKN-021.s: DW Kiswahili (Tatu Karema) reported that witnesses said heavy fighting had taken place since early morning at Kasheke village after other heavy fighting there and in the villages of Lemera and Bushaku and in some villages of Kabare and Kalehe, and that civil society sources estimated that nearly 12 villages were under Wazalendo control, which M23 had not confirmed.
r7-E-SKN-021.l: Kasheke, Lemera, Bushaku and other villages, Kalehe and Kabare
r7-E-SKN-021.x: Civil society (via DW): nearly 12 villages under Wazalendo control; M23 not confirming
r7-E-SKN-021.n: Corroborates REC-0810/REC-0811 (9 April: Wazalendo recover Shanje, Bushaku 1, Bushaku 2, Nyawaronga) with a second origin (civil society sources and witnesses cited by DW). 'Nearly 12 villages' is a civil-society estimate, unconfirmed by M23, as DW says. The day of the Kasheke fighting is not given; date is the report date.
r7-E-SKN-021.vn: Both passages on the DW Kiswahili page (byline Tatu Karema, 11 April 2025). 'Nearly 12 villages' is a civil-society estimate.
src: Mashuhuda wanasema mapambano makali yamefanyika tangu mapema asubuhi katika kijiji cha Kasheke baada ya mapambano mengine makali kutokea hapo na katika vijiji vya Lemera, Bushaku na kwenye baadhi ya vijiji vya wilaya za Kabare na Kalehe.
Vyanzo vya mashirika ya kiraia vilikadiria kuwa karibu vijiji 12 vimekuwa chini ya udhibiti wa Wazalendo, habari ambayo haijathibitishwa na M23.

r7-E-SKN-022.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that M23 rebels took the town of Nzibira in Walungu territory on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday' after first shelling army positions, according to witnesses, and it cited Radio Okapi for fighting in surrounding villages including Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo.
r7-E-SKN-022.l: Nzibira, Walungu; surrounding villages Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza, Kalongo
r7-E-SKN-022.a: M23 (as the source names it); FARDC with allied groups
r7-E-SKN-022.n: Adds the capture date to REC-0506 (which is dated 26-29 Sept 2025): BBC (22 Sept) says the town was taken on the evening of 'yesterday, Sunday' (21 Sept; date computed from weekday and publication date), and r1-SKC-2025H2-017 (Radio Okapi) says FARDC counter-attacked on 29 Sept 'a week after' the occupation. Possible date discrepancy with REC-0506 for the reviewer. Page is in Kirundi although filed on BBC's 'Gahuza' service; relays Radio Okapi (UN-supported) and witnesses.
r7-E-SKN-022.vn: All passages on the page (BBC News Gahuza, published 22 Sept 2025; body in Kirundi). 'ku mugoroba w'ejo ku wa Mungu' = yesterday, Sunday evening = 21 Sept 2025. Date discrepancy with REC-0506 (26-29 Sept 2025) to surface.
src: Amakuru ava muri Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DR Congo) avuga ko inyeshamba z'umuhari M23 uvugwa ko ufashwe mu mugongo n'Urwanda zigaruriye igisagara gikomeye ca Nzibira kiri mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo.

Ababibonye bavuga ko inyeshamba zabanje gucucagira ibisasu ibirindiro vy'ingabo za reta zikoresheje vya bimodoka vy'intambara bitamenwa n'amasasu asanzwe, imbere y'uko zifata iki gisagara ku mugoroba w'ejo ku wa Mungu.

Radio Okapi ifashwe mu mugongo n'ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu ONU, ikorera muri Congo, isubiramwo ababibonye bavuga ko intambara zabaye urutavanako mu bigwati bitari bike vyo mu micungararo y'ico gisagara harimwo Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza na Kalongo.

r7-E-SKN-023.s: Umuryango.rw reported that fighting between AFC/M23 and FARDC and allied groups intensified on Sunday 21 September 2025 in Walungu territory and ended with M23 defeating the government army and Wazalendo fighters and taking Nzibira, with the heaviest fighting at Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza and Kalongo, as Radio Okapi reported.
r7-E-SKN-023.n: Corroborates BBC Gahuza on the date (day 21 September 2025 is printed here) and the localities; both relay Radio Okapi, so they are not independent of one another or of the Radio Okapi account already in the edition. Rwanda-based outlet; framing partisan towards AFC/M23. Relevant to the date given in REC-0506 (26-29 September).
r7-E-SKN-023.vn: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISHIMWE Jean de Dieu, 22 Sept 2025; retained copy). The localities are relayed from Radio Okapi; graded on its own sources (a partisan Rwanda-based outlet). Agrees with BBC Gahuza on 21 Sept. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Imirwano ku mpande zombi yarushijeho gukomera ku Cyumweru tariki 21 Nzeri 2025, ariko birangira M23 itsinsuye ingabo za Leta n’abarwanyi ba Wazalendo.
Imirwano ikomeye yabereye mu duce twa Cisaza, Cibanda, Muyange, Karhuliza na Kalongo nk’uko Radio Okapi yabitangaje.
Abarwanyi b’ihuriro AFC/M23 bafashe Umujyi wa Nzibira uherereye muri Teritwari ya Walungu

r7-E-SKN-024.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the AFC/M23 group accused the DRC government army of 'excessively severe' drone attacks 'in areas inhabited by civilians' at Lumbishi, Kalehe territory, on Monday, and that Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué that the CH-4 drone attacks 'destroyed many things and caused many civilians to flee'.
r7-E-SKN-024.a: DRC government army (FARDC) drones, as alleged by AFC/M23
r7-E-SKN-024.n: Party allegation (AFC/M23) reported by BBC with Kinshasa's denial (see companion claim); no toll given. Date: the page is dated 4 May 2026 and says 'this Monday' (4 May 2026 is a Monday). Not in known_records (no Lumbishi record for May 2026). Page is in Kirundi.
r7-E-SKN-024.vn: Narrowed: the page does not call Kanyuka 'spokesperson' here, and the article body is Kinyarwanda (the Gahuza site carries both languages), not Kirundi. Page published 4 May 2026, a Monday. Party allegation.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 urashinja igisirikare cya leta ya DR Congo kugaba ibitero "by'ubukana burenze" gikoresheje za 'drones' "mu duce dutuwe n'abaturage" i Lumbishi muri teritwari ya Karehe mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo kuri uyu wa mbere.
Mu itangazo, Lawrence Kanyuka yavuze ko ibitero byo kuri uyu wa mbere byifashishije indege za 'drones' za CH-4 "byangije ibintu byinshi kandi bigateza guhunga kw'abaturage benshi b'abasivile".

r7-E-SKN-025.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Jacques Kongolo, adviser to President Félix Tshisekedi, told BBC on Monday that the government side was not the one violating the ceasefire agreements, and quoted him as saying that the other side uses Rwandan drones to shoot at them and then lies that it was the government side that fired.
r7-E-SKN-025.n: Kinshasa's response to the AFC/M23 drone allegation at Lumbishi, as printed by BBC; Kongolo's words are a party claim about Rwanda's role that this unit did not verify.
r7-E-SKN-025.vn: Supported; only the language label removed (the article body is Kinyarwanda, not Kirundi). Party statement as told to BBC.
src: Jacques Kongolo, umujyanama wa Perezida Félix Tshisekedi yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango kuri uyu wa mbere ko uruhande rwa leta atari rwo ruhonyora amasezerano y'agahenge. Komeza usome Kongolo yagize ati: "[Nibo] Bakoresha amadrones y'u Rwanda mu kuturasa bagahita babeshya ngo ni twe twarashe".

r7-E-SKN-026.s: Bwiza reported that the Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu and Numbi areas of Kalehe territory were retaken by AFC/M23 fighters a few hours after Wazalendo had taken them, and that on Tuesday 6 October 2026 the Kinshasa-aligned coalition, chiefly Wazalendo and FDLR, had taken Shanje town, the Gasenda area and the Bukumba hills.
r7-E-SKN-026.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo and FDLR (as the source names them)
r7-E-SKN-026.n: Contradicts the end-state in REC-1080 / REC-1081 (Numbi, Shanje, Lumbishi reported retaken by FARDC and Wazalendo on 5-6 Oct; Radio Maendeleo on 20 Oct says a counter-offensive allowed troops to retake): Bwiza says AFC/M23 retook Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu and Numbi within hours, and attributes the 6 Oct capture to Wazalendo and FDLR (the Radio Okapi/Maendeleo-based records say FARDC with Wazalendo). Control claims from a Rwanda-based outlet that does not name its source for the retaking; the page is dated 7 Oct 2026 and does not give the hour of the retaking. Treat 'contested'.
r7-E-SKN-026.vn: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated 7 Oct 2026, 11:31). Same event as REC-1080/1081 (Kalehe, 5-7 Oct 2026); it contradicts their end state and their attribution (FARDC with Wazalendo vs Wazalendo and FDLR). Bwiza names no source for the retaking. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
src: Ibice bya Lumbishi, Shanje, Kavumu na Numbi muri Teritwari ya Kalehe, mu Ntara ya Kivu y'Amajyepfo byongeye kwigarurirwa n'abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 nyuma y’amasaha make Wazalendo zihigaruriye.

Kuwa Kabiri, itariki 6 Ukwakira 2026, nibwo ihuriro ry'ingabo zirwanira ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, cyane cyane inyeshyamba za Wazalendo na FDLR, ryari ryafashe Umujyi wa Shanje, agace ka Gasenda n'udusozi twa Bukumba, muri Teritwari ya Kalehe.

r7-E-SKN-027.s: Bwiza reported, citing unnamed 'new information', that about 60 houses, including kiosks, were burned in Shanje centre and cattle were looted, including two herds said to belong to Gen. Gabriel Amisi Kumba, known as Tango Four.
r7-E-SKN-027.a: not attributed in this sentence; the same article attributes destruction at Shanje on 7 October to FDLR-dominated Wazalendo, citing an AFC/M23 communiqué
r7-E-SKN-027.x: Bwiza (unnamed 'new information'): about 60 houses incl. kiosks burned at Shanje centre
r7-E-SKN-027.n: Adds a house count (about 60) and a looting detail to REC-1084 (Shanje, almost all shops burned, night of 6-7 Oct 2026). Source of the figure not named; the herds' owner is a claim by 'new information', not verified. The article ties the destruction to FDLR via the AFC/M23 communiqué (see other claims); no independent attribution.
r7-E-SKN-027.vn: Passage on the page (Bwiza, 7 Oct 2026). Unnamed source; 'bivugwa ko' (it is said) hedge kept as 'said to belong'.
src: Amakuru mashya aravuga ko amazu agera kuri 60, harimo na za kiosque, yatwitse muri centre ya Shanje, ndetse haba no gusahura no kwiba inka, harimo n'amashyo abiri y'inka, bivugwa ko ari aya Gen. Gabriel Amisi Kumba, uzwi ku izina rya Tango Four.

r7-E-SKN-028.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Tuesday 11 August 2026 that the Kinshasa government's forces, including FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army (FDNB), had launched general attacks from 05:00 with heavy weapons on densely populated parts of Kalehe territory, including Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, with some residents killed and injured.
r7-E-SKN-028.l: Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi and Gafufura, Kalehe
r7-E-SKN-028.a: FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and FDNB (Burundi), as alleged by AFC/M23
r7-E-SKN-028.n: Party account only (AFC/M23). It adds an allegation of Burundian army (FDNB) participation that no other record in this unit's scope carries for Kalehe in August 2026; no denial from Burundi or Kinshasa on this specific allegation was found in this unit's searches (see gap party_statements). Concerns REC-1066, REC-1067 and REC-1252 (army says it foiled M23 attacks, 11-12 Aug 2026). Bwiza notes the post came after days of calm and after the July fighting at Minembwe. Kanyuka's text quoted on the page names the same places.
r7-E-SKN-028.vn: All passages on the page (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, 11 Aug 2026, 14:40). The page says AFC/M23 made the accusation 'kuri uyu wa Kabiri tariki ya 11 Kanama 2026'. Party account only.
src: Umuvugizi w'uyu mutwe, Lawrence Kanyuka, yifashishije urubuga nkoranyambaga rwa X yatangaje ko biriya bitero byibasiye ahantu hatuwe cyane byagabwe n'Ingabo za Leta ya RDC, FARDC, umutwe wa FDLR, imitwe yitwaje intwaro ya Wazalendo, abacanshuro b'abanyamahanga ndetse n'Ingabo z'u Burundi, FDNB.

Kuri uyu wa Kabiri tariki ya 11 Kanama 2026, guhera saa 05:00 za mu gitondo, ihuriro ry'ingabo z'ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, zirimo FARDC, FDLR, imitwe ya Wazalendo, abacanshuro b'abanyamahanga ndetse n'Ingabo z'u Burundi (FDNB), ryagabye ibitero rusange zikoresheje imbunda ziremereye mu bice byinshi bituwe cyane bya Teritwari ya Kalehe, birimo Chambombo, Cyangugu, Kaziba ya Rumbishi, Kwisimbi na Gafufura.
AFC/M23 yavuze ko ibyo bitero byagize ingaruka ku baturage, aho bamwe bishwe abandi bagakomereka, mu gihe imitungo yangiritse ndetse n'imiryango imwe ikava mu byayo ihunga.

r7-E-SKN-029.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 announced that on 17 August 2026 FARDC, FDLR and other armed groups working with the Kinshasa government launched simultaneous attacks (the spokesperson listing also FDLR, Wazalendo groups, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army FDNB among the attackers) in places including Kalehe territory (Katare, Tushunguti, Nyamugari and Kivoka) and on the Minembwe line, with AFC-M23 saying 120mm mortars and KT-6 drones were used and that the attacks killed civilians and destroyed homes and schools.
r7-E-SKN-029.a: FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and FDNB, as listed by AFC/M23 (the page names FDNB in the list)
r7-E-SKN-029.n: Party account only. Bwiza's piece on Tushunguti (2 Sept 2026) also says fighting resumed at Tushunguti, Katare, Nyamugari and Kivoka on 17 August 2026; no independent source for civilian deaths found in this unit. Kanyuka is named on the page as the person who said the list of attackers included FDNB; the passage structure is ambiguous about who exactly announced which part, so the statement attributes to 'AFC/M23' and cites the spokesperson only as the page does.
r7-E-SKN-029.vn: All passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 17 Aug 2026; retained copy). Party account only. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 28)
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo ryatangaje ko ku wa 17 Kanama 2026, ingabo za FARDC, umurwe wa FDLR n’indi mitwe yitwaje intwaro ikorana na Guverinoma ya Kinshasa yagabye ibitero icyarimwe mu bice bitandukanye, birimo ibyo muri Teritwari ya Kalehe no ku murongo wa Minembwe.

Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka yavuze ko uyu mutwe wavuze ko muri ibyo bitero harimo Ingabo za Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, FARDC, FDLR, imitwe ya Wazalendo, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga ndetse n’Ingabo z’u Burundi, FDNB.
AFC-M23 yatangaje ko guhera saa Moya n’iminota 50, ibitero byagabwe icyarimwe mu bice ituwe cyane bya Katare, Tushunguti, Nyamugari na Kivoka, byose biri muri Teritwari ya Kalehe.
AFC-M23 yavuze ko muri ibyo bitero hakoreshejwe ibisasu bya mortier bya milimetero 120 ndetse n’indege zitagira abapilote zo mu bwoko bwa KT-6.
AFC-M23 ivuga ko ibyo bitero byahitanye ubuzima bw’abasivili, bisenya inzu, amashuri n’ibindi bikorwaremezo by’abasivili, ndetse bigatuma imiryango yose iva mu byabo.

r7-E-SKN-030.s: Umuseke, crediting Radio Maendeleo, reported that a large fire broke out on the morning of Thursday 10 September 2026 on Avenue Kasheke 3 in the Buholo-Kasha area of Bagira commune, Bukavu, damaging two schools (Mogo primary school and a school called Furaha), with at least 27 bodies counted by 15:00 on provisional figures; the page quotes the Buholo-Kasha area head Patrice Mugaruka Buduge as saying the fire started at about 8:00 a.m.
r7-E-SKN-030.l: Avenue Kasheke 3, Buholo-Kasha, Bagira commune, Bukavu
r7-E-SKN-030.a: fire; cause not stated by the source
r7-E-SKN-030.x: Umuseke citing Radio Maendeleo: at least 27 bodies counted by 15:00 (provisional)
r7-E-SKN-030.n: CONFLICTS with REC-1074 and r1-ST-DRC-2026-004 (Actualite.cd: two schools in Kadutu commune, Cimpunda) and with the AFC/M23 account (24 dead, Tshimpunda area, Kadutu commune, fire in the early afternoon; separate claim): this relay of Radio Maendeleo gives Bagira commune, Buholo-Kasha, Avenue Kasheke 3, schools Mogo and Furaha, at least 27 dead (provisional), start about 8:00 a.m. The place names differ and could be different spellings or different parts of one event; this unit cannot resolve it. Umuseke is a Rwandan outlet relaying a Bukavu radio (originating_source Radio Maendeleo); original not fetched.
r7-E-SKN-030.vn: All passages on the page (Umuseke, byline Ange Eric Hatangimana, 10 Sept 2026). The page credits the whole story to Radio Maendeleo ('Radio Maendeleo dukesha iyi nkuru'). Same event as REC-1074; place, schools, toll and hour conflict with the Actualite.cd record and the AFC/M23 account (claim 30). Radio Maendeleo's own report not seen, so kept at C. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Iyi nkongi y’umuriro ukomeye yadutse mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa Kane, tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026, kuri Avenue Kasheke 3 mu gace ka Buholo – Kasha, muri Komini ya Bagira.
Inyubako zibasiwe n’umuriro harimo amashuri abiri, ishuri ribanza rya Mogo n’iryitwa Furaha.

Kugeza ku isaha ya saa cyenda z’amanywa (15:00) zo ku wa Kane, tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026, imirambo nibura 27 yari imaze kubarurwa mbere yo kujyanwa mu buruhukiro bw’imirambo (morgue) hakoreshejwe imodoka z’imbangukiragutabara.

Umuriro wadutse ahagana saa mbiri za mu gitondo (8:00 a.m.), kandi mu gihe kitageze ku isaha imwe, ubukana bw’ibyangiritse bwari bumaze kugaragara, nk’uko byatangajwe na Patrice Mugaruka Buduge, umuyobozi w’agace ka Buholo-Kasha.

r7-E-SKN-031.s: Bwiza reported that the AFC-M23 alliance announced that 24 children and students, 19 girls and five boys, died in a fire that struck houses in the Tshimpunda area of Kadutu commune, Bukavu, and that spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a communiqué of Thursday 10 September 2026 that the fire happened in the first hours after noon.
r7-E-SKN-031.a: fire; cause under investigation per AFC-M23
r7-E-SKN-031.x: AFC-M23: 24 dead (19 girls, five boys), 29 injured, 21 critical (17 at Kadutu General Hospital, four at Bukavu Provincial General Hospital)
r7-E-SKN-031.n: Party statement (AFC/M23 administers Bukavu; the communiqué is relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet). Toll, location (Tshimpunda/Kadutu), school names (Mosala, Nongo) and time (after noon) differ from the Umuseke/Radio Maendeleo account (27 dead, Buholo-Kasha, Bagira, Mogo and Furaha schools, from about 8:00) and from REC-1074; kept as separate claims, none resolved. Health-care note: the communiqué names the hospitals receiving the 29 injured.
r7-E-SKN-031.vn: Passages on the page (Bwiza, byline Bénjamin BABOU, 10 Sept 2026, 19:26). Party statement by the de facto administration. Same event as REC-1074 and claim 29; conflicting details recorded separately.
src: Ihuriro AFC-M23 ryatangaje ko abana n'abanyeshuri 24, barimo abakobwa 19 n’abahungu batanu, ari bo bapfiriye mu nkongi y’umuriro yibasiye amazu yo mu gace ka Tshimpunda ho muri Komini ya Kadutu, mu Mujyi wa Bukavu.
Umuvugizi w'iri huriro, Lawrence Kanyuka, mu itangazo yasohoye kuri uyu wa Kane tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026 yavuze ko iyo nkongi yabaye mu masaha ya mbere ya nyuma ya saa sita.
Ibyangijwe n’inkongi birimo Ishuri Ribanza rya Mosala riri muri Komini ya Kadutu ndetse n'Ishuri Ribanza rya Nongo riri muri Komini ya Bagira.

AFC-M23 yatangaje ko usibye abantu 24 bapfuye, abandi 29 barimo kuvurirwa mu bitaro bitandukanye byo mu Mujyi wa Bukavu nyuma yo gukomereka. Muri abo barwayi, 21 bari mu bitaro by'indembe, aho 17 bari mu Bitaro Bikuru bya Kadutu, mu gihe abandi bane bari ku Bitaro Bikuru by’Intara ya Bukavu.

r7-E-SKN-032.s: Umuseke (byline Ndekezi Johnson) reported that AFC/M23 fighters took Idjwi island, in Lake Kivu, South Kivu, and that since the evening of 12 March 2025 the island had been controlled by M23; it quoted one journalist on the island as saying government soldiers fled before M23 fighters set foot there.
r7-E-SKN-032.n: New control change not in known_records (REC-0779 is the RDF base on Idjwi, REC-0819 Mugote market 12 May 2025). Rwanda-based outlet; the claim that soldiers fled rests on one unnamed journalist. Date is the evening of 12 March 2025 as printed.
r7-E-SKN-032.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuseke, byline NDEKEZI JOHNSON, 13 March 2025). Single Rwanda-based outlet; the flight of soldiers rests on one unnamed journalist.
src: Kuva ku mugoroba wo ku wa 12 Werurwe 2025, iki kirwa gikora ku bihugu bibiri aribyo Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo n’u Rwanda kiragenzurwa na M23.
Umwe mu banyamakuru bakorera kuri icyo kirwa avuga ko abasirikare ba Leta bahunze mbere y’uko abarwanyi ba M23 bakandagiza ikirenge kuri icyo kirwa.

r7-E-SKN-033.s: Umuseke reported that on arriving at Idjwi AFC/M23 first gave a broadcast on the island's radio, Obuguma, before meeting residents, and that Mustapha Maomboleo, head of Idjwi territory, said the broadcast was meant to reassure the island's residents.
r7-E-SKN-033.n: Spelling 'Mustapha Maomboleo' as printed by Umuseke; BBC Swahili (5 March 2025) prints the same administrator as 'Mustafa Mamboleo'. Whether he was an AFC/M23 appointee or the previous state administrator is not stated by the page. Date is the page date.
r7-E-SKN-033.vn: Passage on the page (Umuseke, 13 March 2025). The page does not say whether the territory head was a state or AFC/M23 appointee.
src: AFC/M23 ikigera ku Idjwi yabanje gutanga ikiganiro kuri radiyo yo kuri iki kirwa yitwa Obuguma mbere yo gukorana inama n’abaturage. Mustapha Maomboleo, umuyobozi wa teritwari ya Idjwi, yavuze ko icyo kiganiro cyari kigamije guhumuriza abatuye icyo kirwa.

r7-E-SKN-034.s: BBC News Swahili reported that, according to the United Nations, at least 42,000 people were living in temporary camps on Idjwi island, while locals estimated there might be as many as 60,000 displaced people living on the island.
r7-E-SKN-034.x: UN via BBC: at least 42,000 in temporary camps; locals: as many as 60,000 displaced on Idjwi
r7-E-SKN-034.n: Figures per source, not merged: UN (via BBC) at least 42,000 in temporary camps; locals up to 60,000 displaced. Page is dated 5 March 2025, before the reported M23 takeover of the island (12 March 2025).
r7-E-SKN-034.vn: Passage on the page (BBC News Swahili, byline Marina Daras and Catherine Heathwood, published 5 March 2025). 'wakimbizi' here are displaced Congolese (the page speaks of 'Wakongo waliokimbia makazi yao').
src: Kwa mujibu wa Umoja wa Mataifa, kuna angalau watu 42,000 wanaoishi katika kambi za muda, lakini hakuna rekodi rasmi kwa wale waliokolewa na familia za wenyeji. Wenyeji wanakadiria kuwa kunaweza kuwa na wakimbizi wengi kama 60,000 wanaoishi Idjwi.

r7-E-SKN-035.s: BBC News Swahili reported that Idjwi island had only one main hospital and few vehicles, that it was often impossible for people in remote areas to get treatment, and quoted local radio director Yves Minani as saying that sometimes they must walk 10 km with a patient on a stretcher and that patients sometimes die on the way.
r7-E-SKN-035.a: not applicable (structural access barrier, no actor)
r7-E-SKN-035.n: Geographic and resource barrier to care described by a local radio director, not an attack or denial by an armed actor; included because the brief asks for civilian access to health care. 'Yves Minani' is described elsewhere on the page as an entrepreneur and director of a local radio station. Pre-dates the M23 takeover of the island.
r7-E-SKN-035.vn: Passages on the page (BBC News Swahili, 5 March 2025). The excerpt prints only 'Yves'; the full name and role are printed elsewhere on the page (quoted in clause_support). Structural access barrier, no armed actor. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Kuna hospitali kuu moja tu, na kuna magari machache tu, mara nyingi haiwezekani kwa wale walio katika maeneo ya mbali kupata matibabu. "Wakati mwingine tunalazimika kutembea kilomita 10 na mgonjwa kwenye machela," anasema Yves. "Wakati mwingine wanakufa njiani kwa sababu hatuwezi kufika kwa haraka vya kutosha.
anasema Yves Minani, mjasiriamali na mkurugenzi wa kituo cha redio cha ndani

r7-E-SKN-036.s: Ijambo (Chief editor Yves Iyaremye) reported that M23 said the FARDC used a Sukhoï 25 warplane to bomb inhabited areas of Kalehe territory, killing 10 people and wounding 25, and that M23 political spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué, put the attack on Thursday 13 February 2025.
r7-E-SKN-036.a: FARDC Sukhoï 25 aircraft, as alleged by M23
r7-E-SKN-036.n: Party allegation (M23) relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet; the page itself says FARDC had not yet given its side. No other source for the Kalehe bombing toll found in the edition (claim_search 'Sukhoi' and 'Kalehe' show no 13 Feb 2025 record). Related to REC-0786 (fall of Kalehe, 12 Feb 2025), REC-0775 (bombing of mpox treatment centres at Kalehe/Minova/Miti-Murhesa, reported 24 Feb 2025). Published 2025-02-14 08:04 CAT per the page.
r7-E-SKN-036.vn: Both passages on the page (Ijambo, author Yves Iyaremye, Chief Editor, published 2025-02-14 08:04 CAT). The page says FARDC had not yet given its side. Party allegation only.
src: Umutwe wa M23 watangaje ko igisirikare cya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) cyakoresheje indege y’intambara yo mu bwoko bwa Sukhoï 25, ikarasa ibisasu mu bice bituwemo n’abaturage muri Teritwari ya Kalehe, bigahitana abantu 10 mu gihe abandi 25 bakomeretse.
Mu itangazo ryashyizwe ahagaragara n’umuvugizi wa M23 ushinzwe ibya politiki, Lawrence Kanyuka, yemeje ko icyo gitero cyabaye kuri Kane, tariki 13 Gashyantare 2025

r7-E-SKN-037.s: Ijambo reported that M23 said the bombing destroyed Kalehe General Hospital, which usually received many patients in the area, and many houses of residents.
r7-E-SKN-037.l: Kalehe General Hospital (Ibitaro Bikuru bya Kalehe), Kalehe
r7-E-SKN-037.n: M23 allegation only; extent of damage ('destroyed') is M23's wording and is unverified; no independent source found in this unit. Day of the attack comes from the paired claim (Thursday 13 February 2025 per the communiqué); the page itself places this sentence right after the toll.
r7-E-SKN-037.vn: Passage on the page (Ijambo, 14 Feb 2025). M23 allegation only; extent unverified.
src: M23 ivuga ko iki gitero cyasenye Ibitaro Bikuru bya Kalehe, byari bisanzwe byakira abarwayi benshi muri aka gace, ndetse n’amazu menshi y’abaturage.

r7-E-SKN-038.s: Ijambo reported that M23 said it took Kalehe-Centre to stop the violence reported in Bukavu city, where it accused FARDC and its helpers, including FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo, of killing residents, looting their property and committing serious violence against women.
r7-E-SKN-038.l: Kalehe-Centre (taken Wednesday 12 February 2025, per the page); Bukavu (alleged violence)
r7-E-SKN-038.a: M23 accusing FARDC, FDLR, Burundian soldiers and Wazalendo
r7-E-SKN-038.n: M23's stated justification and accusation (party statement, relayed). The page says the capture of Kalehe-Centre took place on Wednesday 12 February 2025 ('ku wa Gatatu, tariki 12 Gashyantare 2025'). The allegation of sexual violence in Bukavu before the city's fall is not substantiated in this source. FARDC response: the page says FARDC had not yet publicly stated its side.
r7-E-SKN-038.vn: Passage on the page (Ijambo, 14 Feb 2025); the page dates the capture of Kalehe-Centre to Wednesday 12 February 2025. Party justification only.
src: M23 ivuga ko yafashe aka gace kugira ngo ihagarike ihohoterwa rivugwa mu Mujyi wa Bukavu, aho ishinja FARDC n’abayifasha barimo FDLR, abasirikare b’u Burundi na Wazalendo, kuba barishe abaturage, bagasahura imitungo yabo, ndetse bagakora ihohoterwa rikabije ku bagore.
