r7-E-SKN-039.s: BBC News Gahuza reported on the capture of Kalehe centre by M23, quoting an unnamed Kalehe civil-society leader who said that since the evening of Wednesday M23 fighters were in Kalehe centre, the main town of Kalehe territory.
r7-E-SKN-039.n: Corroborates REC-0786 (fall of Kalehe, 12 Feb 2025) with an independent origin (BBC's own call to a civil-society leader). Date computed from weekday ('wednesday') and publication date 13 Feb 2025 (a Thursday).
r7-E-SKN-039.vn: Passage on the page (BBC News Gahuza, published 13 Feb 2025, a Thursday); 'ku wa gatatu' = Wednesday 12 Feb 2025.
src: Umwe mu bakuriye sosiyete civile ya Kalehe utifuje gutangazwa, yabwiye BBC ko kuva ku mugoroba wo ku wa gatatu Kalehe centre - umujyi mukuru wa teritwari ya Karehe - irimo abarwanyi ba M23.

r7-E-SKN-040.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Wednesday the provincial army command said that M23 attacked army positions at Kalehe Centre and Ihusi, quoting it as saying 'these attacks caused the loss of many civilian lives', and that the army says Rwandan troops fight alongside M23, which both sides deny; M23 had said nothing yet on the army's statement.
r7-E-SKN-040.n: FARDC account relayed by BBC (the original FARDC statement not seen). The BBC sentence is garbled in the original; the translation follows its wording. 'Many civilian lives' lost is a FARDC assertion, with no figure. Pairs with the M23 account (Ijambo, 14 Feb) of a Sukhoi bombing on 13 Feb: the two accounts blame each other.
r7-E-SKN-040.vn: Both passages on the page (BBC News Gahuza, 13 Feb 2025). FARDC account relayed by BBC; no figure.
src: Ku wa gatatu, igisirikare cya leta muri iyi ntara cyatangaje ko M23 mu gikorwa cyo kurenga ku gahenge kasabwe n'inama y'i Dar es Salaam, M23 yateye ibirindiro by'ingabo muri Kalehe Centre na Ihusi ko "ibyo bitero byateye kubura ubuzima bw'abasivile benshi".
Uruhande rwa M23 ntacyo ruratangaza ku byavuzwe n'ingabo za leta zivuga ko ari ingabo z'u Rwanda zifatanya na M23 – ibyo izi mpande zombi zo zihakana.

r7-E-SKN-041.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting that began on Tuesday and grew on Wednesday made residents flee in various directions, including to islands in Lake Kivu and the large island of Idjwi, and others south towards Bukavu, according to a Kalehe civil-society member who told BBC.
r7-E-SKN-041.l: Kalehe territory (to Idjwi, lake islands and Bukavu)
r7-E-SKN-041.n: Dates computed from weekdays and the publication date (13 Feb 2025). No numbers given. Adds a flight route (to Idjwi) not in known_records.
r7-E-SKN-041.vn: Passage on the page (BBC News Gahuza, 13 Feb 2025). Raised to B: BBC's own source, non-partisan, not contested.
src: Imirwano yatangiye ku wa kabiri igakomera ku wa gatatu yatumye abaturage bo muri utu duce bahungira mu byerekezo bitandukanye birimo kuri bimwe mu birwa byo mu kiyaga cya Kivu no ku kirwa kinini cya Idjwi, abandi berekeje mu majyepfo bagana i Bukavu, nk'uko umwe mu bagize sosiyete civile ya Kalehe yabibwiye BBC.

r7-E-SKN-042.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked Kavumu in Kabare territory on the morning of Sunday 13 April, that videos on social media showed fighters with DRC flags in Kavumu centre heading for the airport that M23 had taken two months earlier, and that, according to information, after a short fight M23 retook all of Kavumu; it added that information reaching BWIZA said many Wazalendo were killed, including the leader of the attack.
r7-E-SKN-042.n: M23-side account relayed by a Rwanda-based outlet that credits BWIZA; losses to Wazalendo are not independently confirmed here. Complements REC-0812 (Wazalendo temporarily retake Kavumu airport, 13 Apr 2025) and the DW Kiswahili claim (at least seven dead including five civilians, per civil society). The page also says many others were captured by M23 (not cited here: the sentence is garbled). The page is dated Monday 14 April 2025.
r7-E-SKN-042.vn: Supported (Umuryango.rw, byline ISHIMWE Jean de Dieu, 14 April 2025; retained copy). Only the stray trailing comma removed and the retaking attributed to 'information' as printed ('Amakuru avuga'). The Wazalendo losses rest on BWIZA's unnamed information; DW's civil-society toll (claim 18) is different. Rwanda-based outlet; contested facts are recorded only as what it (or the party it relays) says.
src: Mu gitondo cyo ku Cyumweru tariki ya 13 Mata ni bwo abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bagabye ibitero mu gace ka Kavumu ko muri Teritwari ya Kabare, mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo.

Amashusho yakwirakwijwe ku mbuga nkoranyambaga yerekana izi nyeshyamba zari zifite amabendera ya RDC ziri muri Centre ya Kavumu ndetse zigana ku kibuga cy’indege cyo muri aka gace M23 yigaruriye mu mezi abiri ashize.

Amakuru avuga ko nyuma y’uko y’imirwano yamaze akanya gato M23 yahise yisubiza Kavumu yose. Ni imirwano amakuru agera ku bitangazamakuru bya BWIZA yemeza ko yiciwemo Wazalendo benshi, barimo n’uwari uyoboye igitero cyo ku Cyumweru.

r7-E-SKN-043.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 fighters denied information spreading on social media from Burundians that they had been dispossessed of Kavumu airport in South Kivu, and that AFC/M23-Twirwaneho said the circulating information was false and urged people to beware of rumours, saying 'Wazalendo and FARDC have no strength'.
r7-E-SKN-043.l: Kavumu airport, Kabare (about 25 km from Bukavu, per the page)
r7-E-SKN-043.a: AFC/M23 (and Twirwaneho as named on the page)
r7-E-SKN-043.n: Corroborates REC-0853 (AFC/M23 denies losing control of Kavumu airport, 27 Oct 2025) with the party's wording; the control assertion itself is from UMUSEKE 'reliable information' per this page, i.e. the same origin as the existing record, so not independent. Party statement only; the claim of an FARDC/Wazalendo/FDLR takeover is, per this page, a social-media rumour by pro-government Burundians, which this unit did not trace.
r7-E-SKN-043.vn: Narrowed: the excerpt says the claims were spread 'by Burundians' ('n'Abarundi'); 'mostly' belongs to a different rumour on the page (about Nangaa) and is removed. Umuryango.rw, byline Brenda MIZERO, 27 Oct 2025. Party statement; same event as REC-0853.
src: Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 banyomoje amakuru akomeje gusakazwa ku mbuga nkoranyambaga n’Abarundi, avuga ko bambuwe ikibuga cy’indege cya Kavumu giherereye mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo mu Burasirazuba bwa RDC.
Ni mu gihe kandi AFC/M23-Twirwaneho ivuga ko amakuru ari gukwirakwizwa ko yambuwe Kavumu ari ibinyoma, isaba abantu kwitondera ibihuha. Yagize ati: “Wazalendo na FARDC nta mbaraga bafite.”

r7-E-SKN-044.s: Bwiza reported that on the morning of Sunday 22 February [2026] security kept deteriorating in Kavumu, Kabare territory, after fighting the previous Saturday, and that a local resident said the fighting began after a Wazalendo fighter was taken to a health centre and could be heard from Katana to Kavumu.
r7-E-SKN-044.a: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo working with FARDC
r7-E-SKN-044.n: Corroborates REC-1033 (clashes at Kavumu and along the Katana-Kavumu axis, 21 Feb 2026) from a Rwanda-based outlet. The year is not printed in the excerpt; the page header gives Sunday 22 February 2026. The resident's claim that the fighting began after a Wazalendo fighter was taken to a health centre is a single anonymous testimony; whether the health centre was attacked is not stated.
r7-E-SKN-044.vn: Both passages on the page (Bwiza, dated Sunday 22 February 2026, 08:28). Bwiza credits ACTUALITE.CD for its account ('inkuru dukesha ACTUALITE.CD'). Single anonymous testimony for the trigger.
src: Umutekano wakomeje kwangirika mu gitondo cyo kuri iki Cyumweru, itariki ya 22 Gashyantare, i Kavumu, muri Teritwari ya Kabare, muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo nyuma y'imirwano yahiriwe kuri uyu wa Gatandatu ushize.

Umuturage wo muri ako gace yagize ati: "Imirwano yatangiye nyuma y'uko umurwanyi wa Wazalendo ajyanwe mu kigo nderabuzima. Nyuma y'amasaha make, imirwano yatangiye. Kuva Katana kugera Kavumu, twumvaga urusaku rw'amasasu".

r7-E-SKN-045.s: Bwiza reported that on Wednesday 30 July heavy fighting took place in Kamakombe village, Kabare territory, between M23 and a Wazalendo group, that it reportedly began on Tuesday at Mbayo village in Bugorhe groupement after M23 was reportedly reinforced at Kavumu airport, and that civil-society representatives said AFC/M23 rebels set out to drive the group out of Kamakombe on Wednesday morning.
r7-E-SKN-045.l: Kamakombe and Mbayo villages, Bugorhe groupement, Kabare
r7-E-SKN-045.a: M23; Wazalendo group (MDLC / RRADRDC as the page names it)
r7-E-SKN-045.n: Corroborates REC-0837 (29-30 July 2025, Mbayo and Kamakombe, Bugorhe) and REC-0838 (2 Aug). Year not printed in the text; the search index dates the page 30 July 2025 and the details match REC-0837. Names the Wazalendo group as Mouvement décisif de la libération du Congo (MDLC / RRADRDC) in another sentence of the page.
r7-E-SKN-045.vn: Supported (Bwiza, dated Wednesday 30 July 2025). Hedge restored: the page puts the reinforcement under 'ngo' (reportedly) as well as the start under 'bivugwa ko'.
src: Kuri uyu wa Gatatu, itariki ya 30 Nyakanga, imirwano ikaze yabereye mu Mudugudu wa Kamakombe, muri Teritwari ya Kabare (Kivu y'Amajyefo), hagati y'inyeshyamba za M23 n'umutwe wa Wazalendo ukorera muri ako karere.
Iyi mirwano bivugwa ko yatangiriye ku wa Kabiri mu Mudugudu wa Mbayo, uherereye muri Gurupoma ya Bugorhe, nyuma y’uko ngo umutwe wa M23 wongerewe ingufu ku kibuga cy’indege cya Kavumu.

Abahagarariye sosiyete sivili baremeza ko nyuma y’umunsi w’ibitero bikaze ndetse n’ibitero byo gusubiza, inyeshyamba za AFC/M23 zazindutse zishaka kwirukana uwo mutwe i Kamakombe mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa Gatatu.

r7-E-SKN-046.s: Umuryango.rw reported that, according to residents, armed men suspected to include government soldiers and Wazalendo caused fear over the weekend in Bukavu and its outskirts and in Kavumu and Katana in Kabare territory, where they were accused of looting and killing civilians, and that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi confirmed that about seven civilians were killed at Kavumu.
r7-E-SKN-046.l: Bukavu; Kavumu and Katana, Kabare territory
r7-E-SKN-046.a: armed men suspected to include government soldiers and Wazalendo, per residents; the governor said it could not be confirmed that they were soldiers
r7-E-SKN-046.x: Governor Purusi: about seven civilians killed at Kavumu; civil society (separate claim): more than nine; Kabare official quoted by RFI: nine dead
r7-E-SKN-046.n: Corroborates and dates REC-0765 (looting, killings and sexual violence attributed to retreating FARDC soldiers between Kalehe and Kavumu, 6-8 Feb 2025) with a governor's confirmation of about seven civilian deaths at Kavumu; dates computed from 'weekend' and the page date Monday 10 Feb 2025. No sexual violence is mentioned in these passages. The page repeats RFI for one quote and reads like a relay of a larger report; byline credit of the wire is not printed.
r7-E-SKN-046.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline Joseph Iradukunda, Monday 10 Feb 2025; retained copy). Downgraded to C: the only source is a Rwanda-based outlet whose text appears to relay BBC ('yabwiye BBC') without credit; origin unconfirmed.
src: Abantu bitwaje intwaro, bikekwa ko barimo n’abasirikare ba leta na Wazalendo, bateye impagarara mu mpera z’icyumweru mu mujyi wa Bukavu n’inkengero zawo no mu duce twa Kavumu, Katana muri teritwari ya Kabare muri DR Congo, aho bashinjwa gusahura no kwica abasivile, nk’uko bivugwa n’abaturage.
Guverineri Jean-Jacques Purusi wa Kivu y’Epfo yatanze ubutumwa bwo guhumuriza rubanda. Yemeje ko i Kavumu hishwe abasivile bagera kuri barindwi, avuga ko ababikoze bagomba kubiryozwa.

r7-E-SKN-047.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi of South Kivu, speaking about the violence at Kavumu and nearby, said that it was not possible to confirm that those responsible were government soldiers and that they could be bandits who take advantage of the situation to buy weapons and frighten the population; he said it happened as troops at the front were being replaced by new teams.
r7-E-SKN-047.a: South Kivu provincial governor (Jean-Jacques Purusi) on the perpetrators
r7-E-SKN-047.n: State authority's account: attributes the killings to armed men whose affiliation is not confirmed, possibly bandits; contrasts with residents and civil society who blame government forces and Wazalendo (see companion claims). The governor also says a security meeting decided those responsible must be sought and punished. Date computed from 'weekend' and the page date.
r7-E-SKN-047.vn: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). State authority's account. Downgraded to C for the same reason as claim 45. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 46)
src: Guverineri Jean-Jacques Purusi wa Kivu y’Epfo yatanze ubutumwa bwo guhumuriza rubanda.

Guverineri Purusi yumvikanye avuga ko abakoze ibyo "ntawakwemeza ko ari abasirikare ba leta" ati: "Birashoboka ko ari amabandi afatira ku buryo ibintu bimeze akagura intwaro agatangira gutera ubwoba rubanda.

Ku byabaye i Kavumu no hafi yaho, Guverineri Purusi avuga ko byabaye ubwo habaga guhindura abari ku rugamba hakoherezwa amatsinda mashya, "kuko abakoze cyane bagomba gusimburwa". Ati: "Bava i Karehe kugera i Kavumu hari bamwe bakoze urwo rugomo,

r7-E-SKN-048.s: Umuryango.rw reported that civil-society members issued a statement saying more than nine people were killed in these acts, that people were looted and others wounded, and that they blamed government forces and Wazalendo; it quoted Maitre Pascal Mupenda, a Kabare official, via RFI, as saying nine dead were being counted and that the soldiers should leave.
r7-E-SKN-048.a: government forces and Wazalendo, as blamed by civil society
r7-E-SKN-048.x: Civil society: more than nine killed; Pascal Mupenda (Kabare, via RFI): nine dead; governor: about seven (separate claim)
r7-E-SKN-048.n: Figures per source, not merged: governor about seven civilians killed at Kavumu; civil society more than nine; Kabare official nine. The second excerpt names Pascal Mupenda with the title as printed ('Maitre'); his words are a quote relayed from RFI.
r7-E-SKN-048.vn: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). Figures per source (governor about seven; civil society more than nine; Mupenda nine). Downgraded to C (partisan relay, origin unconfirmed). 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Abagize sosiyete sivile basohoye itangazo bavuga ko ibi bikorwa muri rusange byiciwemo abantu barenga icyenda, abantu bagasahurwa, abandi bagakomereka. Bashinja ingabo za leta na Wazalendo.

Radio RFI isubiramo Maitre Pascal Mupenda umwe mu bategetsi b’i Kabare agira ati: "Kubera iki abasirikare bagakwiye kuturinda ari bo ubu bari kuduteza umutekano mucye? Birababaje kuba ubu tubarura abantu icyenda bapfuye.
Turifuza ko abo basirikare bose bagenda.

r7-E-SKN-049.s: Umuryango.rw reported that on Saturday armed men fired into the air in Bukavu city before entering shops and small markets and looting, as Bukavu residents showed on social media.
r7-E-SKN-049.n: Date computed from 'Saturday' and the page date (Monday 10 Feb 2025). Source is residents' social-media posts as described by the outlet; no number of shops or victims.
r7-E-SKN-049.vn: Passage on the page (Umuryango.rw, Monday 10 Feb 2025), so Saturday is 8 Feb 2025.
src: Ku wa gatandatu, abantu bitwaje intwaro barashe amasasu mu kirere mu mujyi wa Bukavu mbere yo kwinjira mu maduka n’amasoko mato mato bagasahura, nk’uko abatuye i Bukavu babigaragaje ku mbuga nkoranyambaga.

r7-E-SKN-050.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Kinshasa government spokesman Patrick Muyaya told Top Congo FM on Sunday that M23, which he called the Rwandan army, had approached and taken Nyabibwe and that all further attacks launched from Nyabibwe had been thwarted, and that rumours reaching Bukavu of M23 being 10 or 15 km away were false as they were in fact more than 100 km away.
r7-E-SKN-050.n: Government statement (Patrick Muyaya, via Top Congo FM as relayed by Umuryango.rw; originating_source Top Congo FM). Concerns REC-0784 (capture of Nyabibwe, 5-6 Feb 2025) and the later advance to Bukavu (16 Feb), which proved the rumours' distance claim wrong within a week. Date computed from 'Sunday' and the page date; the weekend interview date is not otherwise given.
r7-E-SKN-050.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 10 Feb 2025). Government statement relayed from Top Congo FM. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-SKN claim 49)
src: Ku cyumweru, Patrick Muyaya uvugira leta ya Kinshasa abajijwe uko ibintu bimeze yabwiye ikinyamakuru Top Congo FM ko, mu minsi yashize M23 – yita ingabo z’u Rwanda – yasatiriye igafata Nyabibwe, ati: "Guhera Nyabibwe hari ibindi bitero bakoze byo gusatira bavuye i Nyabibwe ariko byose byaburijwemo."
Ibyo rero byakurikiwe n’ibihuha byageze muri Kivu y’Epfo (i Bukavu) aho bamwe bavugaga ngo bari muri 10 cyangwa 15km ariko mu by’ukuri bari muri kilometero zirenga 100".

r7-E-SKN-051.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on 28 August 2025 that since the night of Wednesday 27 August 2025 an alliance of Kinshasa's forces, which he listed as FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, mercenaries, Imbonerakure and the Burundian army, had been shelling densely populated areas of Minembwe (Mikenke) and Kalehe (Katana, Kavumu, Katasomwa, Nyabibwe) with CH-4 drones and heavy weapons.
r7-E-SKN-051.a: FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, mercenaries, Imbonerakure and Burundian army, as alleged by AFC/M23
r7-E-SKN-051.n: Party account only; allegation of Imbonerakure and Burundian army participation in the Kalehe/Kabare area is AFC/M23's. The page lists Katana and Kavumu under Kalehe in the quote although they are in Kabare territory; reproduced as printed. No casualty figure given here. Compare REC-0846 (25 Aug 2025 clashes in the Kalehe highlands) and REC-0781/0782 (Lomera suspensions).
r7-E-SKN-051.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 28 Aug 2025; retained copy). Party account; Katana and Kavumu are listed under Kalehe in the quote as printed.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, kuri uyu wa 28 Kanama 2025 yasobanuye ko ibi bitero bya drones za CH-4 n’intwaro ziremereye byagabwe mu gace ka Mikenke mu misozi ya Minembwe ituyemo Abanyamulenge no mu bice bigize teritwari ya Kalehe.

Ati “Kuva mu ijoro ryo ku wa Gatatu tariki ya 27 Kanama 2025, ihuriro ry’ingabo za Leta ya Kinshasa (FARDC, FDLR, Mai Mai Wazalendo, abacancuro, Imbonerakure n’ingabo z’u Burundi, riri kurasa nta kuvangura ibice bituwe cyane muri Minembwe (Mikenke) na Kalehe (Katana, Kavumu, Katasomwa, Nyabibwe) no mu bice bihana imbibi, rikoresheje drones za CH-4 zigaba ibitero n’intwaro ziremereye. Ibitero birakomeje.”

r7-E-SKN-052.s: Umuryango.rw reported that fighting at Nyangezi and Lurhala in Walungu territory began on 17 June 2025 and that, according to information from Nyangezi, about 45 km from Bukavu, many residents fled the trading centre on the morning of 18 June; it quoted a resident as saying the fighting started the day before and reached Weza.
r7-E-SKN-052.a: AFC/M23; Wazalendo (the article frames the fighting as between them)
r7-E-SKN-052.n: No Nyangezi record for June 2025 in known_records (REC-0482 is Nyangezi, about 18 April 2025). Rwanda-based outlet; sources are unnamed 'information from the area' and a resident quote. No casualty figure.
r7-E-SKN-052.vn: Passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, byline ISIMBI Estella, 19 June 2025; retained copy). Unnamed sources. 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Mu gace ka Nyangezi na Lurhala muri teritwari ya Walungu mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, imirwano yatangiye tariki ya 17 Kamena 2025, abaturage bashya ubwoba bitewe n’intwaro ziremereye zifashishijwe.
Amakuru aturuka muri Nyangezi, mu bilometero bigera kuri 45 uvuye mu mujyi wa Bukavu, avuga ko mu gitondo cyo ku wa 18 Kamena, abaturage benshi bahunze santere yaho mu rwego rwo gukiza ubuzima bwabo.
Umuturage yagize ati “Turi guhunga. Imirwano yatangiye ejo, igera muri Weza.

r7-E-SKN-053.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Wazalendo fighters attacked AFC/M23 positions at Katana, Mumosho and Chirunga in Kabare territory on the morning of 18 June, with residents explaining that Wazalendo tried to dislodge AFC/M23 from these areas.
r7-E-SKN-053.n: Corroborates REC-0828 (17-18 June 2025: Cirunga, Mumosho, Katana) and adds the 'attempt to dislodge' framing from residents; same-day Kalehe residents reportedly heard gunfire (not cited). Year taken from the page date (19 June 2025).
r7-E-SKN-053.vn: Both passages on the page (Umuryango.rw, 19 June 2025).
src: Abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bagabye ibitero ku birindiro bya AFC/M23 muri Katana, Mumosho na Chirunga muri teritwari ya Kabare mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, mu gitondo cyo ku wa 18 Kamena.
Abaturage basobanuye ko Wazalendo yageragezaga gukura AFC/M23 muri utu duce.

r7-E-SKN-054.s: Bwiza (English edition, byline Fred Karege) reported that on 20 May 2025 the DRC National Commission for Monitoring the Implementation of the Addis Ababa Agreement released a report detailing serious crimes against civilians in Goma and Bukavu between January and April 2025 during the occupation by AFC-M23, presented at the National Museum in Kinshasa by the commission's coordinator Alphonse Ntumba Lwaba.
r7-E-SKN-054.n: Government-side statement (a Congolese state commission's report) known only through this Rwandan outlet's summary; the report itself (over 100 pages per Bwiza) was not located in this unit, so its allegations are not recorded here. The legal labels the page mentions ('war crimes', 'crimes against humanity') are the commission's/ministers' wording as relayed and are not adopted. No existing record covers this report (claim_search: no match). Suggest a follow-up to find the report text (Congolese government sites).
r7-E-SKN-054.vn: Both passages on the page (Bwiza English edition, byline Fred Karege, 21 May 2025). source_type corrected: the outlet is Rwanda-based media reporting a DRC state commission, not a DRC-government publication; the report itself was not seen.
ent: National Commission for Monitoring the Implementation of the Addis Ababa Agreement
src: On May 20, 2025, the National Commission for Monitoring the Implementation of the Addis Ababa Agreement in Ethiopia released a comprehensive report detailing serious crimes committed against civilians in Goma and Bukavu between January and April 2025, during the occupation by AFC-M23 rebels.
The report, unveiled at the National Museum in Kinshasa, was presented by Alphonse Ntumba Lwaba, the commission's coordinator,

r7-E-UV-001.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that, in Uvira city, local civil society organisations were reporting that about 12 civilians had been killed by armed groups since 18 January, and quoted UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric saying about 2,400 people had fled Uvira towards Kamanyola.
r7-E-UV-001.a: armed groups (makundi yaliyojihami), as the source words it
r7-E-UV-001.x: UN News Kiswahili (civil society as cited): about 12 civilians killed since 18 January 2026; UN spokesperson: about 2,400 people fled Uvira towards Kamanyola
r7-E-UV-001.n: Kiswahili UN News relay of the UN spokesperson noon briefing; the 12-killed figure is attributed by the page to local civil society, not verified by the UN. Date is the page date (23 Jan 2026). Note destination of the 2,400 is Kamanyola, not Burundi.
r7-E-UV-001.vn: Both excerpts on the page. The 12-killed figure is the page's report of local civil society, not a UN finding; the 2,400 figure is Dujarric's quote. Statement keeps that split.
src: Huko mjini Uvira jimboni Kivu Kusini, mashirika ya kiraia ya eneo hilo yanaripoti kuwa takribani raia 12 wameuawa na makundi yaliyojihami tangu tarehe 18 mwezi huu wa Januari.

“Na kutokana na hofu ya kuendelea kwa vurugu hizo, takriban watu 2,400 wamekimbia mji wa Uvira kuelekea Kamanyola, ambako wamehifadhiwa na wenyeji wao, na wengine wakiwa kwenye vituo vya pamoja wakitafuta usalama,” amesema Dujarric

r7-E-UV-002.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that, according to Radio Okapi, calm returned to Uvira on Monday after clashes on Sunday between FARDC and Wazalendo in which 12 people, civilians and soldiers, died; Serge Kigwati, who heads civil society there, confirmed that the clashes arose because Wazalendo tried to disarm FARDC soldiers who had fled Bukavu and the FARDC refused.
r7-E-UV-002.x: BBC Gahuza citing Radio Okapi: 12 killed, civilians and soldiers
r7-E-UV-002.n: The 12-dead figure is relayed from Radio Okapi (already in r1-UV-2025Q1-001), so not independent; the added value is the Kinyarwanda account and the civil-society explanation of the cause. Date computed from weekday: the page is dated 18 February 2025 and says the clashes were 'on Sunday', i.e. 16 February 2025. An anonymous resident quoted by BBC said Wazalendo asked for equipment and FARDC refused it, which led to the clash.
r7-E-UV-002.vn: Supported. Page dated 18 Feb 2025 (Tuesday); 'ku cyumweru' = Sunday 16 Feb. Toll relays Radio Okapi (already in the store per research notes), so not independent of it. The 12-dead toll is Radio Okapi's, relayed by BBC Gahuza; not an independent count.
src: Ituze ryagarutse ku wa mbere mu mujyi wa Uvira mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo nyuma y'imirwano yabaye ku cyumweru yiciwemo abantu 12, abasivile n'abasirikare, nk'uko bivugwa na Radio Okapi.

Serge Kigwati ukuriye sosiyete civile muri ako gace nawe yemeje ko imirwano muri Uvira yatewe no kuba Wazalendo barashatse kwambura intwaro abasirikare ba FARDC bahunze bava i Bukavu. Maze FARDC babyanga bikavamo kurasana.

r7-E-UV-003.s: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that, as Wazalendo and some FARDC soldiers returned to Uvira on Sunday, several incidents of looting occurred in warehouses near Kalundu port, in several government offices and in some people's homes, especially those of members of the Banyamulenge community.
r7-E-UV-003.l: Warehouses near Kalundu port, government offices and homes, Uvira city
r7-E-UV-003.a: not attributed by the source (written in the context of the Wazalendo return)
r7-E-UV-003.n: The article, dated 19 January 2026, says 'Sunday' (18 January 2026); date computed from the page's own statement that Wazalendo and FARDC returned on Sunday, one day after the AFC/M23 withdrawal. The source does not name who looted.
r7-E-UV-003.vn: Excerpt on page; the Sunday return is in the article's lede (page-only for that clause). Looters not named by DW. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Wakati huo huo, matukio kadhaa ya uporaji yametokea katika maghala karibu na bandari ya Kalundu, katika ofisi kadhaa za serikali, na pia katika baadhi ya nyumba za watu, hasa zile za wanajamii wa Banyamulenge.
Wapiganaji wa kundi la Wazalendo na baadhi ya wanajeshi wa Kongo, FARDC wamerejea katika mji wa Uvira Jumapili

r7-E-UV-004.s: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that in the evening FARDC soldiers removed several Banyamulenge families who feared for their safety in Uvira and took them to a safe place.
r7-E-UV-004.n: Single media source; day computed from the article's sequence (Sunday return of Wazalendo/FARDC, 'in the evening'). The destination is not given.
r7-E-UV-004.vn: Excerpt on page and supports the statement. Regraded C to B: DW is a credible non-partisan outlet, as in claim 2 from the same article. Day is inferred from sequence, so the date is approximate. DW does not say on which day ('in the evening' follows the account of the Sunday 18 January return) or where the families were taken.
src: Majira ya jioni, askari wa jeshi la Kongo waliziondoa familia kadhaa za Banyamulenge ambazo zilihofia usalama wao katika mji wa Uvira na kuwapeleka mahali salama.

r7-E-UV-005.s: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, in a press release, warned that some AFC/M23 fighters were allegedly hiding in Uvira to cause chaos and blame the Wazalendo and the Congolese army, and confirmed that AFC/M23 had withdrawn to the Sange area although they were supposed to withdraw to Kamanyola.
r7-E-UV-005.n: Statement as relayed by DW Kiswahili (author Mitima DeLachance); the press release itself was not seen.
r7-E-UV-005.vn: Supported; statement keeps 'allegedly' (wanaodaiwa). Date is the DW article date, not the release date.
src: Katika taarifa kwa vyombo vya habari, gavana wa Kivu Kusini chini ya utawala wa Kinshasa Jean-Jacques Purusi ameonya kuwepo kwa baadhi ya wapiganaji wa AFC/M23 wanaodaiwa kujificha katika mji wa Uvira ili kuleta fujo na kuwalaumu Wazalendo na jeshi la Kongo. Hata hivyo, Purusi amethibitisha kwamba AFC/M23 wamejiondoa hadi kwenye maeneo ya Sange licha yakuwa walitakiwa kujiondoa hadi Kamanyola.

r7-E-UV-006.s: Deutsche Welle Kiswahili reported that Corneille Nangaa, AFC/M23 coordinator, said on X that AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira in good faith and that he was appalled by acts of reprisal, looting of public property, targeted killings and the forced displacement of the Tutsi Banyamulenge community.
r7-E-UV-006.n: Party statement (partisan) relayed by DW; the X post was not opened. The date is the DW article date; the post date is not given.
r7-E-UV-006.vn: Party statement correctly attributed. Post date not given.
src: Kwenye akaunti yake ya mtandao wa kijamii X, Corneille Nangaa, mratibu wa AFC/M23, alisema kuwa AFC/M23 ilijiondoa Uvira kwa nia njema. Nangaa ameeleza kwamba anachukizwa na vitendo vya kujilipizia kisasi, uporaji wa mali ya umma, mauaji yaliyolengwa, na kulazimishwa kuhama kwa jamii ya Watutsi ya Banyamulenge.

r7-E-UV-007.s: Umuseke (a Rwandan online outlet) reported that the FARDC and the Wazalendo, usual partners in fighting the M23, shot at each other openly on Thursday 1 May, with fighting starting at about saa kumi n'imwe in the morning at Kasenga and spreading quickly to surrounding areas, and that residents of Kakombe said gunfire continued on Friday and that they had no choice but to flee.
r7-E-UV-007.n: Umuseke is a privately owned Rwandan outlet; Rwandan media are treated as partisan on contested facts. The page is dated 2 May 2025; Thursday 1 May is stated by the page. Complements REC-0077 (Kasenga and Kakombe clashes) with the time sequence and the Kakombe residents' account. The same page claims Burundian soldiers deployed to protect Uvira declined to get involved (see separate claim).
r7-E-UV-007.vn: Narrowed to the excerpts: the 'brewing for almost a week' and the mid-morning pause / afternoon resumption clauses sit only elsewhere on the page. excerpt_en mistranslated the start time as 'the eleventh hour of the morning'; saa kumi n'imwe z'igitondo is about 05:00. Parties named in the page title. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 6)
src: Byafashe indi ntera ku wa Kane, tariki ya 1 Gicurasi, ubwo aba basanzwe ari abafatanyabikorwa mu kurwanya M23 bahisemo kurasana mu buryo bweruye. Iyo mirwano yatangiye ahagana saa kumi n’imwe z’igitondo, itangirira ahitwa i Kasenga, mbere yo gukwira mu bice bihakikije mu gihe gito.
Abatuye ahitwa Kakombe bavuga ko urusaku rw’amasasu rwakomeje kumvikana kuri uyu wa Gatanu, bakemeza ko ku bwabo nta yandi mahitamo bafite uretse guhunga.

r7-E-UV-008.s: Umuseke reported that Burundian soldiers deployed to protect the town of Uvira refused to get involved in the FARDC-Wazalendo fighting, and that the Wazalendo said some FARDC soldiers had prepared a boat to take them to Kalemie if M23 fighters attacked Uvira.
r7-E-UV-008.a: Burundian soldiers (as the outlet words it: 'Abasirikare b’Abarundi'); Wazalendo; FARDC
r7-E-UV-008.n: Partisan-leaning Rwandan outlet; the characterisation of Burundian soldiers' motives and 'the war they were pushed into for President Ndayishimiye's interests' is the outlet's own wording and is not independently verified. Month precision only because the claims are undated within the article (published 2 May 2025).
r7-E-UV-008.vn: Both excerpts on page; claim attributed to the outlet. Refers to the 1-2 May 2025 fighting. The Burundian soldiers' refusal is Umuseke's own unsourced narration, from a Rwandan outlet hostile to Burundi's role; its comment on their motives is not carried.
src: Wazalendo ivuga ko hari abasirikare ba FARDC bateguye ubwato bugomba kubambutsa bubajyana i Kalemie, mu gihe abarwanyi ba M23 baba bateye umujyi wa Uvira.
Abasirikare b’Abarundi boherejwe kurinda umujyi wa Uvira banze kwivanga muri iyi mirwano, basa n’abarambiwe iyi ntambara bashowemo ku nyungu za Perezida Ndayishimiye.

r7-E-UV-009.s: Kigali Today (Rwanda) reported that residents of Uvira said that since AFC/M23 left, groups of young criminals backed by the Wazalendo broke into and looted the homes and churches of Banyamulenge and other Kinyarwanda speakers, and that the Impuzamashyirahamwe Iharanira Uburenganzira bwa Muntu (DPC) issued a letter on 18 January 2026 raising concern for the safety of Uvira residents, especially Banyamulenge.
r7-E-UV-009.a: young criminals supported by Wazalendo, according to residents quoted by the outlet
r7-E-UV-009.n: Kigali Today is a Rwandan outlet aligned with the Rwandan state and is partisan on Uvira (Kigali's stated line backs the Banyamulenge and AFC/M23); cite for what residents and the DPC said, not for the facts. Date 18 January 2026 is the DPC letter date; the looting dates per other sources 18-20 January. The page says AFC/M23 left Uvira 'on Saturday 17 January 2026'.
r7-E-UV-009.vn: Supported and attributed (residents; DPC). Kigali Today is partisan on this; grade C.
src: Abatuye umujyi wa Uvira uherereye muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo, bavuga ko kuva AFC/M23 yawuvamo, insoresore z’abagizi ba nabi bashyigikiwe n’umutwe wa Wazalendo, bigabije inzu n’insengero by’Abanyamulenge n’abandi bavuga ururimi rw’Ikinyarwanda, barabasahura, barabasenyera ndetse hagira uwitambika akagirirwa nabi cyane.

Impuzamashyirahamwe Iharanira Uburenganzira bwa Muntu (DPC), yasohoye urwandiko ku ya 18 Mutarama 2026, rugaragaza impungenge ifite ku mutekano w’abatuye muri Uvira, cyane cyane Abanyamulenge, kubera ko uwo mujyi utarimo ubuyobozi nyuma yaho AFC/M23 iwuviriyemo, bigatuma wibasirwa n’ubugizi bwa nabi.

r7-E-UV-010.s: SOS Médias Burundi (Swahili edition) reported that Colonel Fureko, a Banyamulenge and a recently integrated Wazalendo officer, was arrested on Saturday 8 November at Lemera, Uvira territory, while travelling to Mulenge, that former colleagues accused him of links to M23 and Twirwaneho, and that according to several sources Fureko and eight young Banyamulenge with him were beaten, wounded and stripped of their weapons and uniforms.
r7-E-UV-010.l: Lemera, Uvira territory, South Kivu (travelling towards Mulenge)
r7-E-UV-010.a: not stated by the source; his former colleagues ('Wenzake wa zamani') accuse him of M23 and Twirwaneho links
r7-E-UV-010.x: SOS Médias Burundi: Fureko and eight young Banyamulenge
r7-E-UV-010.n: Single Swahili-edition article by SOS Médias Burundi (dateline Bukavu, 10 Nov 2025); no existing claim mentions Fureko. The page itself says relatives and residents of Lemera and Kitoga denounce unjustified abuse, and that some Banyamulenge accuse him of leading Mai-Mai attacks at Kahololo (not cited here). 'Fureko' printed as a single name with rank Kanali (colonel).
r7-E-UV-010.vn: Statement supported unchanged. Actor corrected: the draft said 'former colleagues in the Wazalendo' arrested him; the page names no arresting party, only that former colleagues accuse him. Name printed as 'Fureko'. The page does not say who arrested him. It adds that he and his companions were held in a cell at Luvungi pending investigation, and that some Banyamulenge accuse him of leading Mai-Mai attacks at Kahololo.
src: Kanali Fureko, mwanachama wa jamii ya Banyamulenge na afisa aliyejumuishwa hivi majuzi katika wanamgambo wa eneo la Wazalendo, wakiungwa mkono na mamlaka ya Kongo, alikamatwa Jumamosi hii, Novemba 8, huko Lemera, katika eneo la Uvira, alipokuwa akisafiri kwenda Mulenge, pia katika eneo la Uvira, jimbo la Kivu Kusini.

Wenzake wa zamani wanamtuhumu kuwa na uhusiano na kundi la waasi la M23 na wapiganaji wa Twirwaneho, ambao pia wanaundwa na vijana wa Banyamulenge. Kwa mujibu wa vyanzo kadhaa vya habari, Fureko na vijana wanane wa Banyamulenge aliokuwa nao walipigwa, kujeruhiwa na kuvuliwa silaha na sare zao na kusababisha taharuki mkoani humo.

r7-E-UV-011.s: Mwananchi reported, without naming a source for this passage, that Wazalendo fighters had had to stand firm to defend the town of Uvira against M23 fighters after FARDC soldiers were alleged to have fled the fighting, with others taking canoes to escape to Kalemie.
r7-E-UV-011.n: Mwananchi is a Tanzanian daily; the sentence cited is the outlet's own summary after paraphrasing Reuters on FARDC desertions (its Reuters attribution concerns Lubero and desertions in general; the Uvira sentence itself has no named source). Treat as weak corroboration of REC-0049.
r7-E-UV-011.vn: Origin corrected: the page cites Reuters only for FARDC desertions near Lubero; the Uvira sentence is the outlet's own and unattributed, so 'partly based on Reuters' and the Reuters origin are removed. 'mitumbwi' = canoes.
src: Wapiganaji wa kikosi cha Wazalendo wamelazimika kusimama kidete kutetea Mji wa Uvira dhidi ya wapiganaji wa M23, baada ya askari wa FARDC kudaiwa kutoroka mapigano, huku wengine wakidandia mitumbwi na kutorokea Kalemie nchini humo.

r7-E-UV-012.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi edition) reported that on the third day nobody could move around the town because of looting by armed people, including of the stores of charitable organisations, and quoted a statement posted on X by MSF saying that, unable to move around the town, medical teams and other aid workers were in danger, and that hospitals in the area kept receiving wounded people every day, including ordinary civilians.
r7-E-UV-012.a: armed people (abantu bafise ibirwanisho), not otherwise identified in the cited passages
r7-E-UV-012.n: The BBC Gahuza page is dated 20 Feb 2025 (updated 21 Feb); 'the third day' is counted from the start of unrest per the article's context and is not given as a date, so the date field is the publication date. Both MSF and the looting passages are relays of reporting already in the edition (MSF statements of Feb 2025 are in r1-UV-2025Q1-011 and others). The sentence on stolen NGO stores is the outlet's own text with no named source.
r7-E-UV-012.vn: 'irageramiwe' means 'are endangered/at risk', not 'are blocked'; translation and statement corrected. The 'third day' is not dated by the page (published 20 Feb 2025). MSF statement already in the store per research notes, so not independent. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 11)
src: Ku munsi wa gatatu, nta muntu yashobora gucaruka muri uwo muji kubera ubusuma bwakozwe n'abantu bafise ibirwanisho, aho bivye n'ibigega vy'amashirahamwe y'abagiraneza.

Ishirahamwe ry'abaganga batagira imbibe -MSF, ritanga infashanyo zo kwa muganga, ryateye akamo risaba ko abanyagihugu bokingirwa, kandi n'ubufasha bukabashikira. "Tudashobora kugenda mu muji, imigwi y'abaganga n'abajejwe ubundi bufasha irageramiwe. Ibitaro mu karere, bikomeza kwakira abakomeretse buri munsi, harimwo n'abanyagihugu basanzwe". Niko ivuga mw'itangazo ryashizwe ku rubuga rwabo rwa X.

r7-E-UV-013.s: Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that on Wednesday 31 December 2025 the DRC government, through its Communications Minister and spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, accused the Rwandan forces in a statement of attacks in the Kamanyola-Uvira areas 'with bombs and kamikaze drones' that, it said, killed more than 1,500 people and displaced about 500,000.
r7-E-UV-013.a: Rwandan forces (Ingabo z'u Rwanda), as accused by the DRC government
r7-E-UV-013.x: DRC government (Muyaya, as relayed by Bwiza): more than 1,500 killed; about 500,000 displaced
r7-E-UV-013.n: Statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet (Bwiza), partisan on this issue; the communiqué itself was not opened. Bwiza adds that Muyaya showed no proof and said his information came from civil society, humanitarian organisations and some state bodies (outlet's own comment and a summary of Muyaya's sourcing). Related existing claims: r1-UV-2026Q1-014 (Muyaya, 1,500 dead, 19-20 Jan 2026) - check whether the 1,500 figure there is the same.
r7-E-UV-013.vn: Supported; the hedge 'ngo' is kept as 'it said'. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet, which adds that Muyaya showed no proof and cited civil society, humanitarian organisations and some state bodies. The communiqué itself was not seen.
src: Ku wa Gatatu tariki ya 31 Ukuboza 2025, ni bwo RDC biciye muri Minisitiri wayo w'Itumanaho akanaba Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma yayo yashinje Ingabo z'u Rwanda ibyo birego.

Minisitiri Patrick Muyaya mu itangazo yasohoye, kandi yashinje Ingabo z'u Rwanda kugaba ibitero mu bice bya Kamanyola-Uvira "zikoresheje amabombe na drone za Kamikaze", ngo byicirwamo abarenga 1,500 na ho ababarirwa mu 500,000 bava mu byabo.

r7-E-UV-014.s: Bwiza reported that Patrick Muyaya also accused the Rwandan forces of sending three battalions of soldiers into the highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, saying they were disguised as Twirwaneho fighters.
r7-E-UV-014.l: Highlands of Uvira, Fizi and Mwenga, South Kivu
r7-E-UV-014.a: Rwandan forces, as accused by the DRC government
r7-E-UV-014.x: DRC government (Muyaya, as relayed by Bwiza): three battalions
r7-E-UV-014.n: Partisan Rwandan outlet relaying the DRC statement of 31 December 2025; the sentence 'Uyu mugabo' refers to Minister Muyaya per the preceding sentence of the article.
r7-E-UV-014.vn: Supported; 'Uyu mugabo' refers to Muyaya in the preceding paragraph. The page adds Muyaya said the aim was to extend the war into Fizi and then Kalemie (not carried).
src: Uyu mugabo kandi yashinje Ingabo z'u Rwanda kohereza batayo eshatu z'abasirikare mu misozi miremire ya Uvira, Fizi na Mwenga, akavuga ko ziyoberanyije zikigira abarwanyi ba Twirwaneho.

r7-E-UV-015.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, through its spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, replied that what the Kinshasa government said was propaganda and lies intended to mislead the public.
r7-E-UV-015.l: Uvira territory and Kamanyola axis, South Kivu
r7-E-UV-015.n: Party statement as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; date is the Bwiza publication date (2 January 2026), the reply's own date is not stated.
r7-E-UV-015.vn: The 'rejected the territory allegations in Muyaya's statement' clause is only in the following quote on the page, not in the excerpt, so it is narrowed out (lesson 1). Same event as claim 12: it is the reply to the 31 Dec statement. The page also quotes AFC/M23 rejecting 'the allegations of seizing territory made by Mr Patrick Muyaya in his statement of 31 December 2025'.
src: AFC/M23 biciye mu muvugizi wayo, Lawrence Kanyuka, yasubije ko ibivugwa na Leta ya Kinshasa ari icengezamatwara n'ibinyoma bigamije kuyobya rubanda.

r7-E-UV-016.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said the killings of civilians in South Kivu during the previous month's fighting came from air attacks and shells fired by Kinshasa's forces including FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries and Burundi's national army, in areas including Kamanyola, Luvungi and Sange, with 8 killed and 55 wounded in Kamanyola alone.
r7-E-UV-016.l: Kamanyola, Luvungi, Sange and surroundings, Ruzizi plain
r7-E-UV-016.a: FARDC, FDLR, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, foreign mercenaries, Burundi national army (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-E-UV-016.x: AFC/M23 (as relayed by Bwiza): 8 killed and 55 wounded in Kamanyola alone
r7-E-UV-016.n: Partisan account (AFC/M23) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; 'last month' is relative to the 2 January 2026 article, i.e. December 2025. Compare with REC-0209 (5 civilians wounded around Katogota and Kamanyola) and REC-0211 (rockets from Kamanyola, cross-border shelling).
r7-E-UV-016.vn: Supported party account. The '23' flag is 'AFC/M23', which the title prints. The 8 killed / 55 wounded figures for Kamanyola match those of the Kamanyola head and a Saint-Joseph Hospital doctor relayed by Umuryango (claims 21-22); both reach the edition through Rwandan outlets and may share an origin.
src: Iri huriro risobanura ko ubwicanyi bwibasiye abaturage bo muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo mu gihe cy'imirwano yo mu kwezi gushize, bukomoka ku bitero by’indege n’ibisasu byarashwe n’ingabo z’ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa zirimo FARDC, FDLR, imitwe ya Mai-Mai Wazalendo, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga, n’ingabo z’igihugu z’u Burundi.
Ni ibitero byibasiye uduce dutuwe cyane twa Kamanyola, Luvungi, Sange, no mu nkengero zatwo, bihitana abantu 8 abandi 55 barakomereka muri Kamanyola gusa.

r7-E-UV-017.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 said that, in areas that government forces had tried to retake including Uvira and Makobola, those forces carried out 'acts of rape and organised looting'.
r7-E-UV-017.a: government forces (Ingabo za Leta), as alleged by AFC/M23
r7-E-UV-017.n: Allegation by a party to the conflict (AFC/M23) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; it is not independently verified and conflicts with the attribution of rapes at Uvira to M23/RDF in REC-0122/REC-0024. The article does not give dates or a count. The time frame (December 2025 to early January 2026) is inferred from the article's reply to the 31 December 2025 statement; mark as approximate.
r7-E-UV-017.vn: Excerpt supports the attributed allegation; 'ngo' (reportedly) is carried by 'AFC/M23 said'. Unverified allegation by a party to the conflict; no date, place detail or count. HRW (claim 41) attributes rapes in Uvira to M23 and Rwandan soldiers.
src: Mu duce Ingabo za Leta ngo zashatse gusubiramo harimo umujyi wa Uvira n'uwa Makobola, aho izo ngabo zanakoreye "ibikorwa byo gusambanya abagore ku ngufu no gusahura ku buryo buteguwe."

r7-E-UV-018.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 accused government forces of having fired heavy and light weapons on residents who were holding a peaceful demonstration on 22 December.
r7-E-UV-018.l: not stated in the cited passage
r7-E-UV-018.a: government forces (ingabo za Leta), as alleged by AFC/M23
r7-E-UV-018.n: Party allegation relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the place of the demonstration is not given in the passage. Not verified.
r7-E-UV-018.vn: Supported party allegation; the page does not say where the 22 December demonstration was.
src: AFC/M23 kandi yashinje ingabo za Leta kuba zariraye mu baturage bari mu myigaragambyo y'amahoro yo ku wa 22 Ukuboza zikabarasaho zikoresheje imbunda nini n'izoroheje, ku buryo byashyize ubuzima bw’abaturage mu kaga gakomeye kandi bikaba ari ukurenga ku burenganzira bwabo bw’ibanze.

r7-E-UV-019.s: Umuseke (a Rwandan outlet), in a correction, reported that fighters of the Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), led by Joseph Kabila, had taken the Kadezi area, which it said is distinct from Kawezi as had continued to be reported, and that the Kadezi hills lie 70 kilometres from the town of Uvira; it said news of the capture had circulated on social media from the morning of Monday 26 October 2026.
r7-E-UV-019.l: Kadezi hills (between the Kaziba and Lubarika hills), about 70 km from Uvira city
r7-E-UV-019.a: FRN (Front pour la Refondation de la Nation), described as led by Joseph Kabila and formerly AFC/M23
r7-E-UV-019.x: Umuseke: Kadezi hills 70 km from the town of Uvira
r7-E-UV-019.n: Rwandan outlet, treat as partisan; the claim rests on social-media videos and unnamed sites and was not confirmed by the DRC army in the page. Conflict with the edition: records REC-0679 and claims r1-UV-2026Q4-017/-019/-023 (Radio Okapi, Taarifa, Radio Maendeleo) concern Kawizi (Kahwizi), about 8-10 km from Uvira, where rumours of capture were denied by FARDC/civil society; Umuseke says the capture was of Kadezi hills 70 km away, not Kawizi. The earlier URL of the same article ('ingabo-za-kabila-zigeze-mu-bilometero-10-ugana-uvira', 'Kabila's forces reached 10 km from Uvira') redirects to this corrected text, so the earlier '10 km' claim appears to have been withdrawn by the outlet.
r7-E-UV-019.vn: Relation changed from contradicts to new_related_event: the correction says the place taken was Kadezi, 70 km away, not Kawezi; it does not contradict the Kawizi denials (it agrees Kawezi was not the place taken), so it is not the same event as the Kawizi rumour records. Figures field had 8-10 km numbers from other outlets that no excerpt prints; removed. 'about 70 km' -> '70 kilometres' as printed. Rests on social-media videos and unnamed sites; not confirmed by FARDC in the page. The article's original URL ('...zigeze-mu-bilometero-10-ugana-uvira', 'reached 10 km from Uvira') now carries this corrected text.
ent: Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)
src: Abarwanyi bo mu mutwe wa Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN), uyobowe na Joseph Kabila, bigaruriye agace ka Kadezi bitandukanye na Kawezi nk’uko byakomeje kuvugwa, n’ubwo utu duce tujya kwitiranwa kandi tukaba turi muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo ariko turatandukanye.
Imisozi ya Kadezi iherereye ku ntera ya kilometero 70 uvuye mu mujyi wa Uvira, mu Ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo muri Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC).
Amakuru yo gufatwa kwa kariya gace yacicikanye ku mbuga nkoranyambaga kuva mu gitondo cyo kuri uyu wa Mbere tariki ya 26 Ukwakira, 2026.

r7-E-UV-020.s: Analysons Kongo reported (dateline Uvira, 17 September 2026), citing The Great Lakes Eye, which cited an anonymous Burundian colonel, that twelve Burundian soldiers were allegedly killed by their own comrades after trying to leave their positions on the Bijombo front, in the night of 10 September at Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory; it said the FDNB had issued no communiqué confirming or denying the information.
r7-E-UV-020.l: Kiliba Haut, Kagando groupement, Uvira territory (Bijombo front)
r7-E-UV-020.a: Burundian soldiers (FDNB), allegedly killed by their own comrades
r7-E-UV-020.x: Analysons Kongo citing The Great Lakes Eye: twelve Burundian soldiers
r7-E-UV-020.n: Single anonymous source relayed twice; unconfirmed, the outlet itself calls it unconfirmed ('si elle était confirmée'). Swahili-language posts on Instagram/Facebook repeat it but are not citable. The original The Great Lakes Eye article was not located. French source used because no Kirundi/Swahili/Kinyarwanda web page carrying the text was fetchable; flagged for a Burundian official statement (FDNB: none found).
r7-E-UV-020.vn: All three passages on the page; the conditional (auraient, se seraient) is kept as 'allegedly'. Unconfirmed: one anonymous source, relayed twice; the outlet itself writes 'si elle était confirmée'.
ent: Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB)
src: Uvira, 17 septembre 2026 — Douze militaires burundais auraient été tués par leurs propres camarades après avoir tenté de quitter leurs positions sur le front de Bijombo, dans le territoire d’Uvira, au Sud-Kivu.

Selon The Great Lakes Eye , qui cite un colonel burundais s’exprimant sous couvert d’anonymat, les faits se seraient produits dans la nuit du 10 septembre à Kiliba Haut , dans le groupement de Kagando.
La Force de défense nationale du Burundi (FDNB) n’a, à ce jour, publié aucun communiqué confirmant ou démentant ces informations.

r7-E-UV-021.s: Rwanda Tribune reported that fighting began in the early hours of Saturday 10 October 2026 and that, according to residents, at around 'saa yine' in the morning fighters said to belong to the AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara alliance attacked positions of the Wazalendo groups Binjigi and Masango, which repelled the attack, with fighting continuing towards Magunda; it said that as of writing no official statement had explained how the fighting ended or whether there were dead or wounded.
r7-E-UV-021.l: Bijombo and Masango hills, Magunda direction, Uvira territory
r7-E-UV-021.a: AFC/M23, Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara (alleged attackers); Wazalendo groups Binjigi and Masango
r7-E-UV-021.n: Rwandan outlet (Rwanda Tribune), partisan-leaning; relays unnamed residents and social media. Page dated 11 October 2026 (last updated 12:52). 'saa yine' is Kinyarwanda clock reckoning (about 10:00); left unconverted. The same page names Wazalendo of 'MRDP-Twirwaneho led by General Masheke Radi' trying to push back the attackers, which is unclear and was not used.
r7-E-UV-021.vn: The 'not verified by independent bodies' clause was not in any excerpt (page only); replaced by the no-official-statement clause that source 2 carries, and moved to the note. The draft blended the 'saa yine' time with the date from a separate sentence; now split. The page says the information on the attackers and the course of the fighting had not been verified by independent bodies.
src: Amakuru aturuka muri ako gace avuga ko imirwano yatangiye mu rukerera rwo ku wa Gatandatu, tariki ya 10 Ukwakira 2026,

Amakuru yatanzwe n’abaturage bo muri ako karere avuga ko ahagana saa yine za mu gitondo, abarwanyi bivugwa ko bari mu ihuriro rya AFC/M23, Twirwaneho na Red-Tabara bagabye igitero ku birindiro by’abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bo mu matsinda ya Binjigi na Masango. Ayo makuru avuga ko abarwanyi ba Wazalendo bashoboye gusubiza inyuma icyo gitero, ariko imirwano igakomeza mu cyerekezo cya Magunda.
Kugeza igihe iyi nkuru yandikwaga, nta tangazo ryemewe ryari ryatangajwe risobanura uko imirwano yarangiye, niba hari abayiguyemo cyangwa abakomeretse, ndetse n’ibyangiritse ku mitungo y’abaturage.

r7-E-UV-022.s: Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the head of Kamanyola, Hassan Shabani, said that from 2 to 4 December about 150 shells fired from Burundi hit Kamanyola, killing eight residents; that a doctor at Saint-Joseph Hospital in Kamanyola said that while Burundian forces were firing on the town they received 55 wounded, including 27 seriously wounded who were sent to Bukavu general hospital; and that a resident whose wife and two children were killed told CTGL that a shell fell on their house and four people died.
r7-E-UV-022.a: Burundian forces (Ingabo z’u Burundi), as alleged by the Kamanyola authority and a resident
r7-E-UV-022.x: Hassan Shabani: about 150 shells, eight residents killed; Saint-Joseph Hospital doctor: 55 wounded received, 27 of them seriously; resident (via CTGL): four people killed when a shell hit his house
r7-E-UV-022.n: Rwandan outlet (Umuryango); testimony relayed from CTGL. Page states that Kamanyola, in Walungu territory, is controlled by AFC/M23, so the 'head of Kamanyola' appears to be a de facto (AFC/M23-installed) authority, but the page does not say so. Existing record REC-0211 reports rockets from Kamanyola and cross-border shelling; the Burundian army's own account is separate (REC-0217 etc.). Burundian official position on this shelling: not seen in this source. Resident quoted unnamed, with the line 'Abantu bane barapfuye. Abanjye ni umugore wanjye, abana babiri n’umuturanyi wari hano' (four people dead) which differs from the head's count of eight in total.
r7-E-UV-022.vn: Figures field used digits ('8') no excerpt prints; rewritten in the excerpts' terms. 'zirimo 27 ... zoherezwa' reads most naturally as the 27 seriously wounded being sent to Bukavu, not all 55; statement narrowed accordingly. excerpt_en for source 2 was a summary, not a translation; corrected. Kamanyola was under AFC/M23 control (per the page), so the 'head of Kamanyola' is presumably an AFC/M23-installed authority; the page does not say so. The resident's testimony is relayed from CTGL, not gathered by Umuryango. The same eight killed and 55 wounded appear in AFC/M23's own statement (claim 15). 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 21)
src: Umuyobozi wa Kamanyola, Hassan Shabani, yatangaje ko kuva tariki ya 2 kugeza ku ya 4 Ukuboza, muri iyi santere hatewe ibisasu bigera ku 150 byaturutse mu Burundi, byica abaturage umunani.

Umuganga mu Bitaro bya Saint-Joseph muri Kamanyola yatangaje ko ubwo Ingabo z’u Burundi zarasaga muri iyi santere, bakiriye inkomere 55, zirimo 27 zari zakomeretse cyane, zoherezwa mu Btaro bikuru bya Bukavu kugira ngo zihabwe ubuvuzi bwisumbuyeho.

Umuturage wiciwe umugore n’abana babiri yatangarije urubuga CTGL (Conspiracy Tracker Great Lakes) ko mu gihe Ingabo z’u Burundi zarasaga muri Kamanyola, babuze uko bahunga kuko nta buryo bwo kubibafashamo bari bafite. Ati "Ntitwagize amahirwe yo guhunga kuko nta buryo twari dufite. Twasabwe kuguma mu nzu. Ni uko igisasu cyaje, kigwa ku nzu yacu. Abantu bane barapfuye.

r7-E-UV-023.s: Umuryango reported that Kamanyola head Hassan Shabani said that in the shelling of 2-4 December schools, civilians' houses and the hospital were hit, with eight people dead.
r7-E-UV-023.a: Burundian forces (Ingabo z’u Burundi), as alleged by Hassan Shabani
r7-E-UV-023.n: The word 'ibitaro' in the quotation is plural/generic ('hospital(s)'); the page does not name which hospital. Single-source allegation by a local authority relayed by a Rwandan outlet. The doctor at Saint-Joseph Hospital in Kamanyola gives patient figures in the preceding claim but does not say that hospital was hit.
r7-E-UV-023.vn: Statement supported; figures field rewritten without the unprinted digit. 'ibitaro' may be singular or plural; no hospital is named.
src: Umuyobozi wa Kamanyola, Hassan Shabani, yatangaje ko kuva tariki ya 2 kugeza ku ya 4 Ukuboza, muri iyi santere hatewe ibisasu bigera ku 150 byaturutse mu Burundi, byica abaturage umunani.
Amashuri yararashwe, inzu z’abasivili zararashwe, ibitaro byarashwe, abantu umunani barapfuye.

r7-E-UV-024.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that a 12-year-old boy died of gunfire and at least nine other people were wounded during a protest in Uvira on Monday, and that the FARDC spokesperson in the area, Lt. Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said the child was killed when the army tried to stop protesters entering the main military office in the town.
r7-E-UV-024.l: Uvira city (main military headquarters), South Kivu
r7-E-UV-024.a: not stated; the FARDC spokesperson said the child was killed when the army tried to stop protesters entering the main military office
r7-E-UV-024.x: BBC Gahuza: a 12-year-old boy killed, at least nine wounded
r7-E-UV-024.n: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere', Monday) and the page date of 9 September 2025 (Monday 8 September). BBC states the account as the FARDC spokesperson's; the page also relays the governor's figure (separate claim). Existing: r1-UV-2025Q3-024 (Radio Okapi: 1 dead, 9 wounded) and r1-UV-2025Q3-023 (SOS Médias Burundi: at least 5 killed).
r7-E-UV-024.vn: Statement supported. Figures field credited the toll to the FARDC spokesperson, but it is BBC's own narration; the spokesperson does not say soldiers shot the child, so the actor field is narrowed. Digits replaced by the printed words. The page text is Kinyarwanda, though tagged 'rn'. Toll differs by source: BBC Gahuza one boy killed and at least nine wounded; governor Purusi via AP three dead and five wounded (claim 24).
src: Umwana w'umuhungu w'imyaka 12 yapfuye arashwe, abantu nibura icyenda na bo barakomereka mu myigaragambyo yabayemo guhangana hagati y'abasirikare n'abigaragambya ku wa mbere mu mujyi wa Uvira mu ntara ya Kivu y'Epfo ya DR Congo.

Umuvugizi w'igisirikare cya FARDC muri ako gace, Lt. Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji yatangaje ko uwo mwana yishwe ubwo igisirikare cyagerageza kubuza abigaragambya kwinjira mu biro bikuru bya gisirikare muri uyu mujyi.

r7-E-UV-025.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Associated Press, repeating South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, said the dead in the Uvira protest were three people, with five wounded.
r7-E-UV-025.a: not attributed (protest of Wazalendo-backed demonstrators against Brig Gen Gasita)
r7-E-UV-025.x: AP citing governor Jean-Jacques Purusi (via BBC Gahuza): three dead, five wounded
r7-E-UV-025.n: Conflicting toll: governor/AP 3 dead 5 wounded versus FARDC spokesperson 1 dead 9+ wounded (Radio Okapi and BBC Gahuza) versus SOS Médias Burundi at least 5 dead; see REC-0097 (three wounded died on 4 September) for earlier deaths in the same demonstrations. Date computed from weekday and page date.
r7-E-UV-025.vn: Same protest as claim 23 ('iyi myigaragambyo', Monday 8 Sep 2025): the contradiction is genuine (three dead vs one). Figures field carried other sources' tolls in digits no excerpt prints; narrowed to this source.
src: Ibiro ntaramakuru Associated Press bisubiramo guverineri Jean-Jacques Purusi w'iyi ntara igice kigenzurwa na leta avuga ko abapfuye muri iyi myigaragambyo ari abantu batatu, abandi batanu ko bakomeretse.

r7-E-UV-026.s: Bwiza (a Rwandan outlet) reported that the DRC government had cut internet in the town of Uvira a few days after its forces returned, and that the DRC government had said nothing on the matter, while reports said President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi gave the order.
r7-E-UV-026.l: Uvira city and surroundings, South Kivu
r7-E-UV-026.n: Single Rwandan outlet, partisan on this; no Kinshasa statement found in the page. Not yet corroborated by an independent source in this search (searched: 'internet Uvira' in the edition returned nothing). A telecom shutdown affects health-care access and reporting but the page does not say so.
r7-E-UV-026.vn: Supported and attributed. Single Rwandan outlet; the Tshisekedi order rests on unnamed 'reports'. No independent confirmation of the shutdown.
src: Leta ya Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, yakupye internet mu mujyi wa Uvira uherereye mu ntara ya Kivu y'Amajyepfo, nyuma y'iminsi mike ingabo zayo ziwugarutsemo.

Leta ya Congo Kinshasa ntacyo iratangaza ku makuru yo gukupa internet muri Uvira cyangwa ngo isobanure icyatumye ifata kiriya cyemezo. Amakuru icyakora avuga ko Perezida Félix Antoine Tshisekedi ari we watanze itegeko ry'uko internet ivanwaho.

r7-E-UV-027.s: Bwiza reported that Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23 and deputy coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo, said on X that the Kinshasa government's decision to cut internet in Uvira aimed to hide the bad acts its forces were committing there.
r7-E-UV-027.n: Party statement as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the X post was not opened; quoted phrase is the outlet's translation into Kinyarwanda of the post (the original language of the post is not stated). Date is the Bwiza article date.
src: Perezida wa M23 akanaba umuhuzabikorwa wungirije w'ihuriro Alliance Fleuve Congo, Bertrand Bisimwa, abinyujije ku rubuga rwe rwa X yatangaje ko icyemezo cya Leta ya Kinshasa cyo gukupa internet muri Uvira kigamije guhisha amabi ingabo zayo zikomeje gukorera muri uriya mujyi.

r7-E-UV-028.s: Bwiza reported that the UN Group of Experts on Congo report said the assault on Uvira was led directly by AFC/M23 military leaders Gen. Sultani Makenga and Bernard Byamungu, and that Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, former Rwandan army chief of staff, 'played a major role in coordinating' the operation.
r7-E-UV-028.a: AFC/M23 (Makenga, Byamungu); James Kabarebe (Rwanda), as named by the UN Group of Experts
r7-E-UV-028.n: Relay by a Rwandan outlet of a UN Group of Experts report; the existing claim r1-UC-M23-001 (Actualite.cd) carries the same. Bwiza also notes (not cited) that Rwanda's foreign ministry rejected the US OFAC sanctions on Kabarebe as baseless. The page is dated 1 July 2026, the date of the article not of the report.
r7-E-UV-028.vn: Supported; relay of the UN GoE, not independent of the existing GoE claim. Kept at B because the report itself was not opened. Relay of a UN Group of Experts report (not seen directly); same origin as the existing claim carrying the report.
src: Raporo y'Itsinda ry'Impuguke z'Umuryango w'Abibumbye kuri Congo, yashinje Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe wahoze ari Umugaba Mukuru w'Ingabo z'u Rwanda kugira uruhare rukomeye mu ihuzwa ry'igitero cya AFC/M23 cyafashe umujyi wa Uvira mu ntara ya Kivu y'Amajyepfo.

Iyo raporo ivuga ko igitero cyagabwe kuri Uvira cyari kiyobowe mu buryo butaziguye na ba Gen. Sultani Makenga na Bernard Byamungu, abayobozi ba gisirikare ba AFC/M23. Ariko yongeraho ko Gen (Rtd) Kabarebe "yagize uruhare rukomeye mu guhuza" icyo gikorwa cya gisirikare.

r7-E-UV-029.s: Bwiza reported that houses of Tutsi in Uvira were attacked by residents led by Wazalendo fighters who had returned to the town and looted everything, particularly in Tutsi homes, and that other reports said a church considered to be mostly Tutsi was looted that Sunday morning.
r7-E-UV-029.a: residents led by Wazalendo fighters, per Bwiza
r7-E-UV-029.n: Rwandan outlet (Bwiza), partisan; written the same day (18 January 2026, 15:22). Video on social media is mentioned but not described reliably; 'Abatutsi' is the outlet's term, other sources say Banyamulenge.
src: Inzu z'Abatutsi mu Mujyi wa Uvira, mu Ntara ya Kivu y'Amajyepfo, zagabweho ibitero n'abaturage, bayobowe n'abarwanyi ba Wazalendo basubiye muri uyu mujyi basahura buri kintu cyane cyane mu nzu z'Abatutsi.
Andi makuru avuga ko hari Itorero rifatwa nk'iryiganjemo Abatutsi ryasahuwe muri iki gitondo cyo ku Cyumweru.

r7-E-UV-030.s: Bwiza reported that it was said five civilians had died in Uvira after the Wazalendo and FARDC returned, though the outlet said it could not confirm this.
r7-E-UV-030.n: Unconfirmed figure from a Rwandan outlet on the day of the return; compare UN News Kiswahili (about 12 civilians killed since 18 January per local civil society, 23 January) and REC-0010.
r7-E-UV-030.vn: Supported; the outlet's own hedge ('tutabasha kubyemeza') is kept.
src: Biravugwa ndetse ko Abasivili batanu bapfuye nubwo tutabasha kubyemeza. Ibi biravugwa nyuma y'uko inyeshyamba za Wazalendo zifatanya n’Ingabo za Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (FARDC) zisubiye mu Mujyi wa Uvira, muri Kivu y'Amajyepfo,

r7-E-UV-031.s: Bwiza reported that the Banyamulenge organisation Amohoro Peace Association issued a statement saying Banyamulenge were in danger, that Uvira was heading into a humanitarian emergency, and that after AFC/M23's withdrawal under United States pressure Banyamulenge civilians were being hunted while Wazalendo groups were targeting, killing and looting the homes of people called 'Banyarwanda'.
r7-E-UV-031.a: Wazalendo, as alleged by Amohoro Peace Association
r7-E-UV-031.n: Community-association statement (partisan on the conflict) as relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the association's own page was not opened.
r7-E-UV-031.vn: Supported; community association statement relayed by a partisan outlet.
src: Ishyirahamwe Amohoro Peace Association ry'Abanyamulenge ryasohoye itangazo rivuga ko Abanyamulenge bari mu kaga. "Uvira iragana mu bihe byihutirwa by'ubutabazi. Nyuma yo kugenda ku gahato kwa AFC/M23 ku gitutu cya Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika, abasivili b'Abanyamulenge barimo guhigwa, mu gihe imitwe yitwara gisirikare ya Wazalendo yibasiye, ikica, ikanasahura amazu y’abantu bise "Banyarwanda," ijambo ryakoreshejwe kenshi mu kwibasira abatutsi Banyamulenge.

r7-E-UV-032.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the DRC government said it had ordered its troops not to confront the M23 as it advanced in Uvira, and explained that it wanted to avoid civilians losing their lives there.
r7-E-UV-032.n: Statement as reported by BBC Gahuza (original BBC wording in English in the same story family: not checked). The page does not name the government source or give the date or channel of the statement. The same page says the larger part of Congolese forces left Uvira although residents say fighting continues.
r7-E-UV-032.vn: Supported; BBC does not name the government speaker or channel.
src: Reta ya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo ivuga ko yategetse ingabo zayo kutivuna umuhari uyigwanya wa M23 mu gihe uriko uratera intambwe zikomeye mu gisagara ca Uvira, akarere ka nyuma gakomeye kari gasigaye katarafatwa mu buseruko bw'ico gihugu. Reta ya Congo isigura ko yashatse kwirinda ko abasivire bahasiga ubuzima.

r7-E-UV-033.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a statement on X that for more than three months AFC/M23 had denounced hate speech, attacks on citizens because of their appearance, and killings 'in the liberated areas' of M23 carried out by fighters allied with the Kinshasa government and its accomplice Burundi, and that the town of Uvira was now 'liberated'.
r7-E-UV-033.n: Party statement (partisan), relayed by BBC; the X post itself was not opened. Compare r1-UV-2025Q4-003 (BBC English) and r1-UV-2025Q4-021 (SOS Médias Burundi).
r7-E-UV-033.vn: Kirundi 'yiyamirije' (kwiyamiriza) means 'denounced/protested against', not 'endured'; translation and statement corrected. Regraded B to C: the content is a party's claim (the fact that Kanyuka posted it is well attested by BBC, but the claim records his allegations). Same X post as the BBC English claim in the store per research notes. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 32)
src: Mw'itangazo ryaciye ku rubuga rwa X rwa Lawrence Kanyuka, umuvugizi w'uwo murwi, avuga ko amenyesha abantu bose ko kuva mu mezi arenga atatu, AFC/M23 yiyamirije amajambo abiba urwanko, ibitero vyibasira abenegihugu kubera uko bavutse basa, n'ubwicanyi bukorerwa "mu turere twabohowe" na M23 bukozwe n'abarwanyi bafashanya na reta ya Kinshasa na somambike wabo, ari we Uburundi.
Ati: "Uyu musi, iyi nkeke yakuweho kandi turemeza ko igisagara ca Uvira ubu cabohowe. Turahimiriza abenegihugu gusubira mu bikorwa vyabo mu mutekano ntangere: AFC/M23 irahari kugira ngo ibakingire."

r7-E-UV-034.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Olivier Muhasha, one of the journalists in Uvira, told it that morning that the fighters had reportedly entered only two quarters, Kavimvira and Kagenge, while the others were in the hands of the government army and the Wazalendo, and that Uvira has 14 quarters.
r7-E-UV-034.l: Kavimvira and Kagenge quarters, Uvira city
r7-E-UV-034.x: BBC Gahuza (journalist Olivier Muhasha): the fighters reportedly in two of Uvira's 14 quarters
r7-E-UV-034.n: Qualifies the 10 December capture record (REC-0113/0218: 'AFC/M23 and Rwandan forces take control of Uvira'): on the morning of 10 December a journalist on the spot told BBC that the fighters held two quarters only. Same BBC page notes the information was not confirmed. The page text misspells 'Muhasha'; name copied as printed. The 'Kagenge' spelling is as printed (the edition elsewhere may use Kagenge/Kalimabenge variants).
r7-E-UV-034.vn: 'boba binjiye' is the Kirundi reportative conditional ('had reportedly entered'); the hedge was dropped in the draft and the translation. Figures field used digits '2' no excerpt prints. 'These fighters' = M23 per the preceding sentence. 'The fighters' are the M23 fighters named in the preceding sentence of the page, which BBC says had reportedly entered the town (unconfirmed). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (E-UV claim 33) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Ariko, Olivier Muhasha, umwe mu banyamakuru bari mu muji wa Uvira, yabwiye BBC Gahuzamiryango muri aka gatondo ko aba barwanyi boba binjiye mu makaritiye abiri gusa, Kavimvira na Kagenge, ayandi nayo akaba ari mu minwe y'igisirikare ca reta n'abarwanyi ba Wazalendo. Uvira igizwe n'amakaritiye 14.
hari amakuru ataremezwa neza avuga ko abarwanyi ba M23 boba binjiye

r7-E-UV-035.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi told Radio Okapi on Tuesday that Uvira was controlled by government troops, denying rumours that M23 rebels had entered the town.
r7-E-UV-035.n: Date computed from weekday ('ejo ku wa kabiri' = yesterday, Tuesday) and the page date of 10 December 2025, i.e. Tuesday 9 December. Existing claim r1-UV-2025Q4-003 has the BBC English version of the 10 December governor statement.
r7-E-UV-035.vn: Supported; page dated 10 Dec 2025, 'ejo ku wa kabiri' = Tuesday 9 Dec. Relay of Radio Okapi.
src: Hagati aho, mu gihe buramatari w'intara ya Kivu y'Epfo, Jean-Jacques Purusi, ejo ku wa kabiri yabwiye Radio Okapi yo muri Congo ko Uvira yagenzurwa n'ingabo za reta akabeshuza ibihuha vyavuga ko inyeshamba za M23 zoba zari zinjiye muri iki gisagara

r7-E-UV-036.s: Umuryango (a Rwandan outlet) reported that AFC/M23 shot down a FARDC Sukhoi-25 combat aircraft that had been used to attack it; according to information from South Kivu, the aircraft was hit in the air over Kalundu port, Uvira territory, at about saa saba in the afternoon of 26 December 2025 and fell into Lake Tanganyika, and two people aboard were said to have died.
r7-E-UV-036.x: Umuryango: two people aboard said to have died
r7-E-UV-036.n: Rwandan outlet, treat as partisan; no FARDC or Kinshasa statement on the aircraft was found in this source, and no independent confirmation seen (not searched further for lack of budget). The page also says it was the second Su-25 the DRC army lost, the first having been captured at Goma in late January 2025, and says Twirwaneho claimed to have shot down a helicopter carrying white mercenaries on 6 December (not cited). 'saa saba' is Kinyarwanda clock reckoning (about 13:00); left unconverted. Existing record REC-0128 covers the AFC/M23 covert presence in Uvira after the 15-16 Dec announcement.
r7-E-UV-036.vn: Supported and attributed to the outlet. Single Rwandan outlet; no FARDC or independent confirmation of the shoot-down.
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 rirwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo ryahanuye indege y’intambara yo mu bwoko bwa Sukhoi-25 yifashishwaga n’igisirikare cy’iki gihugu (FARDC) mu kurigabaho ibitero.

Amakuru aturuka mu ntara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo yemeza ko iyi ndege yarasiwe mu kirere cyo ku cyambu cya Kalundu muri teritwari ya Uvira, intara ya Kivu y’Amajyepfo, mu ma Saa Saba y’amanywa yo kuri uyu wa 26 Ukuboza 2025, igwa mu kiyaga cya Tanganyika.
Bivugwa ko abantu babiri bari bayirimo baguye muri Tanganyika, barapfa.

r7-E-UV-037.s: Umuryango reported that DRC forces attacked Kalundu port on Lake Tanganyika, where two AFC/M23 boats were said to have been hit and the fighters aboard died, and that DRC army combat drones hit AFC/M23 bases including one at Kala, Uvira territory, at the former MONUSCO base.
r7-E-UV-037.l: Kalundu port and Kala, Uvira territory
r7-E-UV-037.a: DRC forces (Ingabo za RDC) and Wazalendo; AFC/M23 boats and bases
r7-E-UV-037.n: Single partisan Rwandan source; unverified casualty claim ('bivugwa', reportedly).
r7-E-UV-037.vn: Supported; the page places the attacks on the day of publication (26 Dec 2025, 'kuva mu gitondo cy'uyu munsi').
src: Ingabo za RDC zagabye igitero ku cyambu cya Kalundu kiri ku kiyaga cya Tanganyika ku ruhande rw’umujyi wa Uvira, abo bivugwa ko ubwato bubiri bwa AFC/M23 bwarashwe, abarwanyi bari baburimo bahasiga ubuzima.
Drones z’intambara z’ingabo za RDC kandi zarashe ibigo bya AFC/M23 birimo icya Kala muri teritwari ya Uvira, ahahoze ikigo cy’ingabo ziri mu butumwa bw’amahoro bw’Umuryango w’Abibumbye (MONUSCO).

r7-E-UV-038.s: Umuryango reported that AFC/M23 fighters left Makobola in the afternoon of 25 December 2025 and were then attacked, and that DRC forces and Wazalendo went to take control of Makobola, as residents there confirmed.
r7-E-UV-038.n: Partisan Rwandan outlet; complements Radio Okapi/Actualite.cd claims of 13-23 Dec 2025 on Makobola (r2-G-SKS-FIZI-008 etc.). Igihe (Rwanda) also carried 'Fizi: AFC/M23 yavuye muri Makobola' on 26 December 2025 but its page could not be fetched. Makobola is in Fizi territory, shown here because the edition links it to the Uvira offensive (REC-0218).
r7-E-UV-038.vn: Supported. Makobola is in Fizi territory.
src: Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bagabweho ibi bitero nyuma yo kuva muri santere ya Makobola ku gicamunsi cyo ku wa 25 Ukuboza. Ingabo za RDC na Wazalendo byahise bijya kuhagenzura nk’uko abaturage baho babyemeza.

r7-E-UV-039.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that fighting on Tuesday between Wazalendo and FARDC in Uvira left people dead and created tension according to the town's authorities, that DRC media said about eight people had died, that part of the fighting took place in the Kavimvira area near the Burundi border, and that Radio RFI said it began over a disagreement between Wazalendo and FARDC on the entry of people coming from Burundi.
r7-E-UV-039.l: Uvira city, including Kavimvira near the Burundi border
r7-E-UV-039.x: BBC Gahuza citing unnamed DRC media: about eight dead
r7-E-UV-039.n: Date computed from weekday ('Tuesday') and the page date of 27 August 2025 (Wednesday), i.e. Tuesday 26 August. Death toll is 'about eight' per unnamed DRC media as relayed by BBC; the edition's REC-0092 does not give a toll; the BBC page does not give a source for civilian versus military dead. Compare REC-0090 (25 August, Mulongwe, clash over vehicles) for a different stated cause.
r7-E-UV-039.vn: Statement supported; figures field rewritten without the unprinted digit. Page dated Wed 27 Aug 2025, so Tuesday = 26 Aug.
src: Imirwano ku wa kabiri hagati y'imitwe ya Wazalendo n'ingabo za FARDC mu mujyi wa Uvira yatumye abantu bahasiga ubuzima kandi itera impagarara nk'uko abategetsi b'uyu mujyi babivuga. Ibinyamakuru muri DR Congo bivuga ko abantu bagera ku munani bapfuye.

Imwe mu mirwano hagati y'impande zombi yabereye mu gace ka Kavimvira kari hafi y'umupaka n'u Burundi. Radio RFI ivuga ko yavuye ku kutumvikana hagati ya Wazalendo na FARDC ku kwinjira kw'abantu bavuye mu Burundi.

r7-E-UV-040.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that, in an official statement on the events, the provincial governor asked the Wazalendo and the government army to 'take measures to avoid falling into the enemy's trap', saying the enemy was spreading false information that he had surrounded the town of Uvira, and that Governor Jean Jacques Purusi, on the government side, convened an 'extraordinary meeting' with representatives of the army, religious leaders, youth and women, customary authorities and the leaders of the "Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie" or Wazalendo.
r7-E-UV-040.n: Relayed by BBC Gahuza from the provincial government; the date is approximate (statement issued around 26-27 August 2025). Extends r1-UV-2025Q3-007 (SOS Médias Burundi on the spokesperson Luganywa relaying Purusi's condemnation).
r7-E-UV-040.vn: The draft's 'statement from the government of the part of South Kivu controlled by the government' is not what the excerpt says ('itangazo ry'ubutegetsi' = a statement by the authorities; the governor is 'of this province'); narrowed. Name spelled 'Jean Jacques Purusi' as this page prints it.
ent: Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie
src: Mu itangazo ry'ubutegetsi rivuga ku byabaye, rivuga ko Guverineri w'iyi ntara asaba Wazalendo n'ingabo za leta "gufata ingamba zo kwirinda kugwa mu mutego w'umwanzi" avuga ko uwo mwanzi "akwiza amakuru atari yo ko yagose umujyi wa Uvira, kandi bidafite ishingiro".

Kubera iki kibazo, Guverineri w'iyi ntara Jean Jacques Purusi, ku ruhande rwa leta, yatumije "inama idasanzwe" imuhuza n'abahagarariye ingabo, abakuriye amadini, urubyiruko n'abagore, abategetsi gakondo, hamwe n'abakuriye abitwa "Volontaires pour la Défense de la Patrie" cyangwa Wazalendo.
