r7-E-UV-041.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said its researchers found evidence that 53 civilians (46 men, one woman and five boys) were summarily killed in attacks on residents' homes in different parts of Uvira after the Rwanda-backed fighters took the town in December, and that HRW visited three sites said to hold mass graves, one of them in a place permanently guarded by UN peacekeepers.
r7-E-UV-041.a: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers, as alleged by HRW
r7-E-UV-041.x: HRW (via BBC Gahuza): 53 civilians killed without trial (46 men, one woman, five boys); three alleged mass-grave sites visited
r7-E-UV-041.n: Kirundi-language BBC version of the HRW report of 14 May 2026 (the BBC English story is already in the edition; this is not an independent origin). Note the page itself states that the BBC could not get a response from M23 or Rwanda. Page date 14 May 2026 ('Ukwa gatanu 2026'). The date range is the occupation period as given elsewhere in the edition (the page says M23 left in January).
r7-E-UV-041.vn: Statement supported. Figures used digits '1' and '5' no excerpt prints; rewritten. Regraded B to A: origin is a documented HRW investigation (rubric A), though relayed by BBC and not independent of the HRW/BBC English claims in the store.
src: Ishirahamwe Human Rights Watch (HRW) rivuga ko abatohoza baryo babonye ibimenyetso vyerekana ko abasivile 53 bishwe ata rubanza — abagabo 46, umugore umwe hamwe n'abahungu batanu — mu bitero vyakorewe ku mazu y'abanyagihugu mu bice bitandukanye vy'igisagara inyuma y'uko abo barwanyi, bashigikiwe n'Urwanda, bafashe Uvira mu kwezi kwa Kigarama (12).

Abatohoza bayo kandi baragendeye ibibanza bitatu bivugwa ko birimwo ibinogo rusangi vyatawemwo abantu i Uvira, harimwo kimwe kiri ahantu hahora hacunzwe n'abasirikare ba ONU bashinzwe kugarukana amahoro.

r7-E-UV-042.s: BBC News Gahuza (Kirundi) reported that Human Rights Watch said it investigated and documented eight cases of rape alleged against the M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers during their occupation of Uvira, and quoted a woman who said they stripped her, tied her hands behind her back with her clothes and raped her, and that her husband was shot dead when he tried to help her.
r7-E-UV-042.a: M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers, as alleged by HRW
r7-E-UV-042.x: HRW (via BBC Gahuza): eight cases of rape documented
r7-E-UV-042.n: The page carries a content warning on sexual violence; the survivor is not named and no name is searched for. Kirundi version of the HRW findings (same origin as the BBC English and HRW pages already in the edition). Compare AFC/M23's counter-allegation (Bwiza) that government forces committed rapes at Uvira/Makobola. The government's own report of 14,400 rapes (r1-UV-2026Q1-037) and the health actors' 1,100 cases (REC-0025) differ in order of magnitude and method.
r7-E-UV-042.vn: Supported; 'abo barwanyi' = the M23 fighters named in the page title and lede. Regraded B to A on the HRW origin; not independent of the HRW claims in the store. No survivor named.
src: HRW ivuga ko yatohoje kandi yandika ivyaha umunani vy'ugusambanya abagore ku nguvu, vyagirizwa abo barwanyi hamwe n'abasirikare b'Urwanda mu gihe bari bigaruriye ico gisagara.

Umugore umwe yavuze ati: "Baranyambuye impuzu zose, bambohera amaboko inyuma bakoresheje impuzu zanje, hanyuma baransambanya ku nguvu," Yongeyeko ko igihe umugabo wiwe yagerageza kumutabara, yarashwe agapfa.

r7-E-UV-043.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda had continued to deny backing M23 or deploying its soldiers in eastern DRC, and that M23 and the Rwandan government did not respond to the BBC's request for comment on HRW's findings on Uvira.
r7-E-UV-043.n: This records 'no statement found' from M23 and Rwanda in this source at publication. The Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo replied separately to HRW (Igihe, 'RDF si AFC/M23', page not fetchable by the helper); see gaps. The excerpt's 'ruhakana' sentence is BBC's own summary of Rwanda's long-standing position, not a dated statement.
r7-E-UV-043.vn: Supported. Source 1's originating_source corrected from Human Rights Watch to BBC: the no-reply line concerns BBC's own request. The page also says HRW wrote to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders in April and got no reply.
src: Urwanda rwagumye ruhakana ko rushigikiye M23 canke ko abasirikare barwo barungitswe mu buseruko bwa RD Congo, igihugu kirangwamwo amabuye y'agaciro menshi . Ariko HRW ivuga ko benshi mu bo yabajije bavuze ko babonye amahano yakozwe n'abasirikare b'Urwanda bambaye umwambaro ubaranga hamwe n'abarwanyi ba M23.
M23 na Reta y'Urwanda ntibarishura ubusabe bwa BBC bwo kugira ico bavuze.

r7-E-UV-044.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that on Saturday night Burundi's foreign minister Edouard Bizimana wrote on X that it was important to stress Qatar's bad role in using its word and money to stop the United States from acting, and in the same post accused Rwanda of continuing to seize areas in eastern DR Congo contrary to the Washington agreement without the United States doing anything.
r7-E-UV-044.l: eastern DRC (statement about the Uvira-period conflict)
r7-E-UV-044.n: Date computed from weekday ('Saturday night') and the page date of 4 January 2026 (Sunday), so Saturday 3 January. BBC adds that Bizimana later deleted the post; the post itself was not opened. The statement is about the wider conflict after the Uvira capture (the page says the M23 took Uvira the previous month and said it left), not an Uvira incident.
r7-E-UV-044.vn: Supported; page dated Sunday 4 Jan 2026, so 'Saturday night' = 3 Jan. BBC reports Bizimana later deleted the post.
src: Ni nyuma y'uko ku wa gatandatu nijoro Minisitiri Edouard Bizimana yanditse ku rubuga X ko ari "ingenzi gushimangira uruhare rubi rwa Qatar mu gukoresha ijambo ryayo n'amafaranga ikabuza Amerika kugira icyo ikora".
Mu nyandiko ye Bizimana yashinjaga u Rwanda "gukomeza gufata uturere mu burasirazuba bwa DR Congo" binyuranyije n'amasezerano ya Washington ariko Amerika ntigire icyo ibikoraho.

r7-E-UV-045.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, in what it described as correcting his foreign minister, said on X that Burundi had always praised Qatar's 'important role' in mediation on the DRC and that it was necessary to clarify 'whatever was not clearly understood and the wrong words' about Qatar's role.
r7-E-UV-045.n: Mediator-related statement (Qatar) by Burundi's head of state; not Uvira-specific. Page notes Qatar's Al-Khulaifi thanked Ndayishimiye for the clarification.
src: Mu gisa no gukosora ibyavuzwe na Minisitiri we w'ububanyi n'amahanga, Perezida Evariste Ndayishimiye w'u Burundi yatangaje ko igihugu cye 'igihe cyose cyashimiye 'uruhare rw'ingenzi' rwa Qatar mu buhuza ku kibazo cya Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo.

Bizimana iyi nyandiko ye yaje kuyisiba, ariko nyuma yo gukomeza guhanahanwa no gutangwaho ibitekerezo n'abantu batandukanye, byatumye kuri iki cyumweru nimugoroba Perezida Ndayishimiye asa n'uyigarukaho. Atavuze ko ari ubutumwa bwa Bizimana arimo kuvugaho, Ndayishimiye yanditse ku rubuga X ko ari ngombwa gusobanura "ikitumvikanye neza cyose n'imvugo itari yo ku ruhare rwa Qatar mu iterambere no kubaka amahoro".

r7-E-UV-046.s: UN News Kiswahili reported that, in South Kivu, about 20 civilians had been killed and 10 wounded since 23 March in fighting in the Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, and quoted the UN spokesperson saying that destruction of homes and livestock had forced many families to flee while access to food and health services remained limited.
r7-E-UV-046.l: Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga areas, South Kivu
r7-E-UV-046.a: armed groups (makundi yaliyojihami), as the UN page words it
r7-E-UV-046.x: UN (via UN News Kiswahili): about 20 civilians killed and 10 wounded since 23 March in Uvira, Kalehe and Mwenga
r7-E-UV-046.n: Briefing of 2 April 2026 at UN headquarters (page text: 'tarehe 2 Aprili'). The figures are not broken down by area (Uvira, Kalehe, Mwenga); Kalehe and Mwenga are outside the Uvira unit.
r7-E-UV-046.vn: The spokesperson's name and the 'citing humanitarian agencies' attribution sit only in an earlier paragraph of the page, not the excerpt; narrowed to 'the UN spokesperson' as the excerpt says. Figures supported. The figures are not broken down by area; Kalehe and Mwenga are outside Uvira. The page spells the spokesperson 'Stephen Dujarric'.
src: Katika jimbo la Kivu Kusini, takribani raia 20 wameuawa na wengine 10 wamejeruhiwa tangu Machi 23 katika mapigano yaliyotokea maeneo ya Uvira, Kalehe na Mwenga. “Uharibifu wa makazi na mifugo umelazimisha familia nyingi kukimbia, huku upatikanaji wa chakula na huduma za afya ukiendelea kuwa mdogo,” ameeleza Msemaji huyo wa Umoja wa Mataifa.

r7-L-DRC-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in reaction to Amnesty International's June 2026 report accusing the CMC-FDP armed group of serious abuses in Rutshuru, the CMC-FDP spokesperson categorically rejected the accusations and said that no official complaint had been filed before the movement's internal disciplinary or judicial bodies.
r7-L-DRC-001.n: Spokesperson not named by the page. Only the CMC-FDP reacted on this page; no statement by the government or FARDC on the Amnesty report found on it. CMC-FDP is a Wazalendo coalition member (party statement, not fact).
r7-L-DRC-001.vn: Excerpt exact and supports every clause; report date 25 June 2026 printed on the page. Translation checked (flag benign: capitalised 'In'). B: one credible non-partisan outlet reporting that the statement was made. Party statement (CMC-FDP, a Wazalendo-affiliated group): the claim is that its spokesperson said this, not that it is true. src: En réaction, le porte-parole du CMC-FDP rejette catégoriquement ces accusations. Il affirme qu’aucune plainte officielle n’a été déposée devant les instances disciplinaires ou judiciaires internes du mouvement, contestant ainsi les conclusions du rapport.

L’organisation Amnesty International accuse le groupe armé Collectif des Mouvements pour le Changement Forces de Défense du Peuple (CMC-FDP) d’être impliqué dans de graves violations des droits humains dans le groupement de Bukombo, en chefferie de Bwito, territoire de Rutshuru (Nord-Kivu). Dans un rapport publié jeudi 25 juin 2026

r7-L-DRC-002.s: DW Swahili reported that Minister of Information and government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya accused the M23 of continuing the war and called their announcement of leaving Uvira 'upotoshaji' (a distortion/misinformation), saying it was a ploy to disrupt the mediator, the United States.
r7-L-DRC-002.n: Relevant to D-018 (day AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira): this is Kinshasa's account on 17 Dec 2025 that the withdrawal was not real. Page date taken from the page (17.12.2025). Remainder of the Muyaya quote on the page is in Swahili translation of his remarks; wording is DW's rendering.
r7-L-DRC-002.vn: Both excerpts exact; page dated 17.12.2025 (byline Byobe Malenga). Swahili translations checked: 'kumvuruga' = to confuse/disrupt, 'upotoshaji' = distortion/misinformation; correct. Flags benign (M23 read as a number; capitalised English words). Both sources are the same page, so one origin: B. Muyaya's words are DW's Swahili rendering; the original-language wording was not seen. Kinshasa's account of the M23 announcement, not a finding that M23 stayed. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Waziri wa Habari na Msemaji wa Serikali, Patrick Muyaya amewashutumu waasi hao kwa kuendeleza vita, siku chache tu baada ya kusaini makubaliano ya amani na kulitaja tangazo lao la kuondoka kama upotoshaji.
Ni dhahiri huu ni ujanja wa kumvuruga mpatanishi ambaye ni Marekani, aliyejitolea kuchukua hatua, kwa sababu ni wazi kuwa kilichotokea Uvira hakikubaliki.
Serikali ya Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo imelikataa tangazo la waasi wa M23 kwamba wanajiondoa kwenye mji wa Uvira ulioko Kivu Kusini.

r7-L-DRC-003.s: Ouragan.cd reported a communiqué published on 6 March by Deputy Prime Minister for the Interior Jacquemain Shabani. In the article's account, Kigali deployed its troops on 28 February and on 3 and 4 March in the Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals to take away patients, most of them Congolese soldiers, and their carers, and some of them were executed. The article then attributes to the Interior Ministry communiqué the statement that the Rwandan army and its M23 auxiliaries carried out incursions into Goma hospitals, taking about a hundred patients and carers, among them Congolese soldiers, and that they were summarily executed.
r7-L-DRC-003.l: Goma, North Kivu (Ndosho and CBCA Virunga hospitals)
r7-L-DRC-003.a: DRC government (Ministry of the Interior) accusing Rwandan forces (RDF) and M23
r7-L-DRC-003.x: Kinshasa communiqué (as reported by Ouragan.cd): 'une centaine de malades et garde-malades' taken; dates 28 February, 3 and 4 March
r7-L-DRC-003.n: Answers r1/HC-2025#3 (Kinshasa statement on the 28 Feb hospital removals) and D-011 (date and number of patients): this is Kinshasa's account (partisan, 'party says'): 28 Feb, 3 and 4 March; 'une centaine'; hospitals named Ndosho and CBCA Virunga (Heal Africa not named). The communiqué's first passage says 'certains d'entre eux' were executed; the later passage says 'Ils ont sommairement été exécutés' (all), an internal inconsistency in the outlet's wording. Ouragan.cd page is a media relay of the communiqué; the communiqué text itself was not seen.
r7-L-DRC-003.vn: All excerpts exact. Original statement merged the two passages and presented the 28 Feb-4 Mar passage as communiqué wording; corrected to say which passage the article attributes to the communiqué and to keep both execution wordings. 'Rwandan forces' replaced by the page's own 'Kigali'/'Rwandan army'. Year dropped from the statement (no excerpt prints it; page date 7 March 2025). Translations checked; flags benign. Kinshasa's account (party says). The relayed text is internally inconsistent: one passage says 'some of them' were executed, the passage attributed to the communiqué says 'they were summarily executed'. The communiqué itself was not seen; the 28 Feb / 3-4 March passage is the outlet's rendering and is not in quotation marks.
src: indique, dans un communiqué publié le 6 mars, par le vice-Premier ministre de l’Intérieur, Jacquemain Shabani.

Pire que tout, Kigali a déployé ses troupes le 28 février, les 3 et 4 mars derniers, dans les hôpitaux de Ndosho et CBCA Virunga pour enlever des malades, dont la plupart des militaires congolais et leurs garde-malades. Malheureusement, certains d’entre eux ont été sauvagement exécutés

L’armée rwandaise et ses supplétifs du M23 ont effectué une série d’incursions dans les hôpitaux de Goma en enlevant une centaine de malades et garde-malades, parmi lesquels des soldats de la RDC. Ils ont sommairement été exécutés, ajoute le communiqué du ministère de l’Intérieur.

r7-L-DRC-004.s: Actualite.cd reported that DRC Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba presented on 7 April a report on violations allegedly committed by AFC/M23 during the occupation of Uvira and its surroundings with Rwandan support; the government said it had counted more than 14 400 women raped, and the page gives two different figures for people killed, which it does not reconcile (see note).
r7-L-DRC-004.a: DRC government (Ministry of Human Rights) accusing AFC/M23
r7-L-DRC-004.x: Government, as reported by Actualite.cd: more than 14 400 women raped. Death toll: two different figures on the same page (see note); none chosen.
r7-L-DRC-004.n: Government (partisan) figures, 'party says'. The same page prints 'plus de 15 000 personnes tuées' (report summary) and, in the minister's quoted words, 'Plus de 1 500 morts' - a discrepancy inside the outlet's text that cannot be resolved from the page (possible typo); both are recorded, not merged. Relevant to D-025 (mass-grave body counts) and to the sexual-violence picture at Uvira; the very large rape figure is the government's own and is not independently corroborated here.
r7-L-DRC-004.vn: Excerpts exact. The original statement gave only the 15 000 figure while the page also prints 1 500 in the minister's own quoted words: a silent choice. Narrowed: the death toll moves to the note with both figures verbatim (the 1 500 passage is on the page but in no stored excerpt, so it cannot go in the statement). Figures field narrowed to numbers an excerpt prints. Weekday and date (Tuesday 7 April) are printed. Conditional 'qu’auraient commis' kept as 'allegedly'. Government (party) figures. The same Actualite.cd page prints two death tolls for the same report: 'plus de 15 000 personnes tuées' (outlet's summary) and 'Plus de 1 500 morts' (the minister's quoted words). Both are shown as printed; neither is chosen. The rape figure is the government's own and is not independently corroborated here. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 3) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Après des travaux de documentation, le ministre des droits humains, Samuel Mbemba a dévoilé mardi 7 avril, le rapport sur les actes de violations qu’auraient commis les rebelles de l'AFC/M23 lors de l’occupation de la ville d’Uvira et ses environs, dans la province du Sud-Kivu, avec le soutien du Rwanda.

Le rapport répertorie plus de 15 000 personnes tuées directement dans les offensives armées des rebelles, et d’autres par manque d’accès aux soins. Le gouvernement dit avoir dénombré plus 14 400 femmes violées dans ces atrocités
Plus de 1 500 morts, victimes directes des offensives armées et du manque d’accès aux soins.

r7-L-DRC-005.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese government said it had found several mass graves after the AFC/M23 left Uvira: three graves at Mayi Moto holding 115 bodies according to the government, one at Kilomani with 31 bodies, one at Kala and two at Rutembo.
r7-L-DRC-005.l: Mayi Moto, Kilomani, Kala, Rutembo (Uvira area), South Kivu
r7-L-DRC-005.a: DRC government (Ministry of Human Rights) accusing AFC/M23
r7-L-DRC-005.x: Government as reported by Actualite.cd: 115 bodies in three graves at Mayi Moto; 31 bodies at Kilomani; Kala (one grave) and Rutembo (two graves) with no count given
r7-L-DRC-005.n: For D-025 (number of bodies in the Uvira mass graves): government count per Actualite.cd. The page links the discovery to the AFC/M23 departure and says 'Comme Human Rights Watch' also found graves; the date of the minister's presentation (7 April 2026) is used as the statement date.
r7-L-DRC-005.vn: Excerpt exact; figures 115 and 31 match. 'M23' flag benign. The 'after AFC/M23 left Uvira' clause is on the page (quoted) but not in the excerpt: expect an excerpt-gap warning. Translation tightened ('avaient permis l'ensevelissement' = had been used to bury). Government count (party says); the page does not say who dug the graves or who the dead were. The clause on the AFC/M23 departure rests on a page passage outside the stored excerpt. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 4) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Les trois fosses découvertes à Mayi Moto, avaient permis l'ensevelissement de 115 cadavres, d’après le gouvernement. Une autre, trouvée à Kilomani contient 31 corps humains entassés. Une autre encore a été trouvée à Kala et deux autres fosses communes à Rutembo.
Comme Human Rights Watch, le gouvernement congolais a lui aussi débusqué plusieurs fosses communes après le départ des rebelles de l’AFC/M23 de la ville stratégique d’Uvira et ses environs.

r7-L-DRC-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, speaking on Radio Okapi's Dialogue entre Congolais on Tuesday 20 January, confirmed that life had resumed in Uvira after the AFC/M23 withdrawal and that loyalist forces now controlled the city; he announced the imminent restoration of State authority.
r7-L-DRC-006.n: Relevant to D-021 (day provincial authorities returned to Uvira): on 20 Jan the governor said the provincial government 'devrait s'installer officiellement à Uvira dans les prochains jours'; his own arrival is dated 23 Jan 2026 by UNE.CD and Kivutimes (see next claim).
r7-L-DRC-006.vn: Excerpt exact; 20 January 2026 was a Tuesday, consistent with page date 21/01/2026. The 'life resumed / AFC/M23 withdrawal' and 'State authority' clauses are on the page outside the excerpt (excerpt-gap warning expected). Flags benign. Provincial government's statement; the claim is that the governor said it. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a confirmé cette information lors de son passage, mardi 20 janvier, au cours de l'émission Dialogue entre Congolais sur Radio Okapi. Le chef de l'exécutif provincial a rassuré sur la situation sécuritaire de cette cité stratégique du Sud-Kivu, confirmant que les forces loyalistes contrôlent désormais la ville.

La vie a repris son cours normal dans la ville d’Uvira, après le retrait des troupes rebelles de l’AFC/M23, soutenues par l’armée rwandaise. Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a confirmé cette information lors de son passage, mardi 20 janvier, au cours de l'émission Dialogue entre Congolais sur Radio Okapi.
Jean-Jacques Purusi a également annoncé le rétablissement imminent de l'autorité de l'État dans cette partie du pays.

r7-L-DRC-007.s: UNE.CD reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi returned on Friday 23 January 2026 to Uvira, the provisional seat of provincial institutions, after the withdrawal of the AFC-M23; it said he, his provincial government and other officials had fallen back to Fizi-Baraka after the fall of Uvira on 10 December 2025. Kivutimes, reporting the same arrival, said instead that the provincial authority had been forced to flee to Bujumbura, in Burundi.
r7-L-DRC-007.n: D-021: both outlets give 23 January 2026 for the governor's return. They differ on where the authorities had gone: UNE.CD says Fizi-Baraka; Kivutimes says the provincial authority fled to Bujumbura. Kivutimes also reports the governor visited the Kalundu port 'après les actes de pillages qui ont été perpétrés par les rebelles avant le retrait' (outlet narration, not a governor statement) and later returned to Bujumbura the same afternoon (relevant to D-020, who looted Uvira).
r7-L-DRC-007.vn: All excerpts exact; 23 January 2026 was a Friday. The original statement rested only on UNE.CD while citing Kivutimes; corrected to say which clause rests on which outlet and to surface the Fizi-Baraka/Bujumbura discrepancy. B: two local outlets agree on the date of arrival, disagree on the earlier whereabouts. Discrepancy: UNE.CD says the provincial authorities fell back to Fizi-Baraka; Kivutimes says they fled to Bujumbura (Kivutimes also says the governor returned to Bujumbura the same afternoon). Both date the arrival to Friday 23 January 2026. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 6)
src: Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a regagné, ce vendredi 23 janvier 2026, la ville d’Uvira, siège provisoire des institutions provinciales, après le retrait des éléments de l’AFC-M23 qui occupaient la zone.

Pour rappel, Jean-Jacques Purusi, les membres de son gouvernement provincial ainsi que plusieurs animateurs des institutions du Sud-Kivu s’étaient repliés à Fizi-Baraka après la chute de la ville d’Uvira, le 10 décembre 2025.

Cette arrivée intervient quelques jours après le retrait des rebelles dans la ville occupée pendant quelques jours alors que l’autorité province a été contraint de prendre fuite pour Bujumbura,la capitale économique de la République du Burundi.

r7-L-DRC-008.s: JamboRDC reported that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, speaking to the press on Saturday 6 September, called on the residents of Uvira to stay calm and not to give in to enemy manipulation, after protests by Wazalendo and citizen movements demanding the departure of General Olivier Gasita.
r7-L-DRC-008.n: Answers r1/UV-2025Q3#3 only in part: this is the army spokesperson (Ekenge), not the government spokesperson Muyaya; no direct Muyaya statement on the Uvira unrest was found. The page also says the protesters accuse Gasita of links to the M23 and of taking part in the capture of Bukavu, 'allégations que réfutent l'armée'. The page itself shows the protests were by Wazalendo; Wazalendo leadership's own statement is not on this page. JamboRDC is a Bukavu/South Kivu local outlet (location not stated on the page; not asserted).
r7-L-DRC-008.vn: Excerpts exact; 6 September 2025 was a Saturday. 'Olivier Gasita' and the press-briefing clause are printed on the page outside the excerpts (quoted above). Translations checked. FARDC statement; the claim is that its spokesperson said this. JamboRDC names the officer 'Olivier Gasita'; MediaCongo Press (claim 8) prints 'Sylvain Gasita'. Not harmonised. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Le porte-parole des Forces armées congolaises (FARDC), le général major Sylvain Ekenge a appelé ce samedi 6 septembre, les habitants d’Uvira (Sud-Kivu) au calme et à ne pas céder à la manipulation de l’ennemi.
Sylvain Ekenge accuse les rebelles et leurs alliés de vouloir instrumentaliser certains Wazalendo pour créer des tensions communautaires et déstabiliser la paix dans la région.
Devant la presse ce samedi, le porte-parole des FARDC a dénoncé les tentatives de manipulation autour de la nomination du général Olivier Gasita
Il a lancé ce message suite à une série de manifestations organisées par les Wazalendo et certains mouvements citoyens qui exigent le départ du général Olivier Gasita

r7-L-DRC-009.s: MediaCongo Press reported that National Assembly president Vital Kamerhe announced on Monday 8 September 2025, after an inter-institutional meeting chaired by the head of state, that President Tshisekedi had decided to send a government mission to Uvira after protests against the appointment of General Gasita as head of military intelligence in the area.
r7-L-DRC-009.a: DRC government / Presidency (relayed by National Assembly president)
r7-L-DRC-009.n: Kamerhe's statement is already known to the project (target r1/UV-2025Q3#3 cites it); this adds a second outlet and the outlet's line that the government and FARDC reaffirmed confidence in Gasita (the outlet's own wording, no speaker). The page names him 'général Sylvain Gasita' in the lead and 'général Olivier Gasita' is the name printed by JamboRDC; the page-level name is not harmonised here. No Muyaya statement found.
r7-L-DRC-009.vn: Excerpts exact; 8 September 2025 was a Monday. The decision clause rests on the lead paragraph (quoted). Source 1 (government and FARDC reaffirm confidence) is outlet narration with no speaker and is not used in the statement. The page names the officer 'Sylvain Gasita'; JamboRDC (claim 7) prints 'Olivier Gasita'. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: C’est le président de l’Assemblée nationale, Vital Kamerhe, qui l’a annoncé lundi 8 septembre 2025, à l’issue d’une réunion interinstitutionnelle présidée par le chef de l’État.
De son côté, le gouvernement et les FARDC réaffirment leur confiance au général Gasita, qui bénéficie du soutien direct du président Tshisekedi.

Le président de la République, Félix Tshisekedi, a décidé de dépêcher une mission gouvernementale à Uvira, après les manifestations contre la nomination du général Sylvain Gasita comme chef du renseignement militaire dans cette partie du pays.

« Concernant la crise sécuritaire dans l’Est de la République, le chef de l’État est préoccupé par la situation et cherche des solutions à travers une mission gouvernementale qui sera envoyée à Uvira », a-t-il déclaré.

r7-L-DRC-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, reacting at a press briefing to recent Human Rights Watch and Global Witness reports on the security, humanitarian and natural-resources situation in AFC/M23-held areas, said the publications were not a surprise to the Congolese authorities and that Kinshasa was acting on a judicial front and an economic front.
r7-L-DRC-010.n: The page does not say which HRW report is meant ('récents rapports'); the HRW report on arbitrary detention, killings and forced recruitment in M23-held areas was published 10 June 2026 (cited elsewhere in the project) and HRW's Uvira report on 14 May 2026, but this page does not name either, so the link to the sexual-violence reports (r1/SV-2026#1) is NOT established. Briefing date not stated; article date used. Kinshasa's own wording (party says).
r7-L-DRC-010.vn: Excerpts exact; page dated Sunday 21/06/2026. Checked the researcher's caution: the statement names no specific report and claims only what the page says. The description of the reports is the outlet's narration (quoted). Kinshasa's own wording: party says. The page does not name or date the HRW report(s) meant ('récents rapports'); it mentions HRW's documentation of forced recruitment of children. Do not link this statement to a specific HRW report (e.g. on sexual violence) on this page's evidence. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Réagissant à ces rapports lors d’un briefing de presse coanimé avec son collègue de la Santé publique, Hygiène et Prévoyance sociale, Samuel Roger Kamba, le porte-parole du gouvernement, Patrick Muyaya, a indiqué que ces publications ne constituaient pas une surprise pour les autorités congolaises.
Selon lui, Kinshasa agit notamment sur "un front judiciaire et un front économique".

face aux accusations contenues dans les récents rapports de Human Rights Watch et Global Witness concernant la situation sécuritaire, humanitaire et l’exploitation des ressources naturelles dans les zones sous contrôle de la rébellion de l’AFC/M23 dans l’Est de la RDC.

r7-L-DRC-011.s: Radio Okapi reported that government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya, after the creation of the FRN, said that the former head of state's choice to take up arms was an attack on the Republic and the constitutional order.
r7-L-DRC-011.l: Kinshasa (national statement on the FRN), other

Earlier BBC page said the government had not commented; this is a later statement. The same page says Muyaya spoke in a video on Sunday 18 October. Radio Okapi (21 Oct 2026, 'Dialogue entre Congolais') also aired a Muyaya interview on the FRN; only the programme summary is on the page, not his words.
r7-L-DRC-011.vn: Excerpt exact and supports the quote. The excerpt prints neither 'Muyaya', 'Joseph Kabila', 'FRN' nor '18'; the title prints 'Patrick Muyaya' and 'FRN', so the statement keeps those and drops 'Joseph Kabila' and the date (page passages quoted in clause_support). ent: Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN)
src: Le porte-parole du gouvernement estime que le choix de l’ancien chef de l’État de prendre les armes constitue une attaque contre les institutions et l’ordre constitutionnel. « Le choix qu’il fait de prendre les armes, c’est de s’attaquer à la République et à l’ordre constitutionnel », affirme-t-il.

Le porte-parole du gouvernement congolais, Patrick Muyaya, appelle les leaders de la Coalition Article 64 (C64), à clarifier leur position après la création du Front pour la refondation de la nation (FRN), dirigé par l’ancien président Joseph Kabila.
Dans une vidéo diffusée dimanche 18 octobre sur les réseaux sociaux, Patrick Muyaya interpelle les responsables de cette plateforme de l’opposition

r7-L-DRC-012.s: Radio Okapi reported that, according to parliamentary sources, head of state Félix Tshisekedi told members of parliament and senators of the presidential majority that the emergence of the FRN was in no way a surprise to him.
r7-L-DRC-012.n: Second-hand (unnamed parliamentary sources); a closed meeting, no transcript. Answers target r1/UC-M23#3.
r7-L-DRC-012.vn: Excerpt exact. Excerpt prints neither the president's name, FRN, 24 nor Kinshasa; the title prints 'Félix Tshisekedi' and 'FRN', so those stay and the date/place move to the date field and note. C: anonymous relay. a été au centre des échanges entre le président de la République, Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, et les députés ainsi que sénateurs de la majorité présidentielle, samedi 24 octobre à Kinshasa.

r7-L-DRC-013.s: Radio Okapi reported that the wife of local notable Rugamba and their five children (one boy and four girls) were killed by armed men who attacked their home at Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, on the night of Thursday to Friday 3 July [2026], and that the Congolese army and the AFC/M23 each blamed the other.
r7-L-DRC-013.l: Kabizo (Butare locality), Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r7-L-DRC-013.a: Armed men; FARDC and AFC/M23 accuse each other
r7-L-DRC-013.x: Radio Okapi: six killed (wife of notable Rugamba and five children)
r7-L-DRC-013.n: The page is dated 4 July 2026 and gives 21:30 on Thursday 2 July (butare locality) per local sources; no victim is named, only the notable's surname. Related to target r3/G-CTR#0 (Kabizo), but a different event from the 25-26 Oct 2026 Kabizo attack named there.
r7-L-DRC-013.vn: Excerpt exact; page dated Saturday 04/07/2026, so 3 July 2026 was the Friday. Statement kept as written (the bracketed year is the researcher's marked insertion; place names are quoted from the page in clause_support). Graded B, up from C: the killing is Radio Okapi's own report (one credible non-partisan origin); attribution remains contested and is stated as such. Perpetrators unidentified; each party blames the other (see the FARDC and AFC/M23 accounts). No victim is named; Rugamba is the notable whose family was killed, not a listed victim. A different event from the 25-26 October 2026 Kabizo attack. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-DRC claim 12) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: L’épouse du notable local Rugamba et ses cinq enfants – un garçon et quatre filles – ont été tués lors de l’attaque de leur domicile par des hommes armés, dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi 3 juillet. L’armée congolaise et le mouvement rebelle AFC/M23, qui contrôle la zone, s’accusent mutuellement d’être responsables de cette tuerie.
Le meurtre de six membres d’une même famille dans l’agglomération de Kabizo, dans la chefferie de Bwito, territoire de Rutshuru, suscite de vives réactions.

r7-L-DRC-014.s: Radio Okapi reported that the spokesperson of the 34th military region, Major Dieudonné Kasereka, rejected the AFC/M23's version of the Kabizo killings and denounced a disinformation campaign meant, in his words, to conceal abuses committed by RDF/AFC-M23 elements.
r7-L-DRC-014.l: Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r7-L-DRC-014.n: FARDC account only; party statement, not fact. Kasereka also cites a 12 June killing of nine people at Rusamambu and Kanoune (Walikale) which the page does not source further.
r7-L-DRC-014.vn: Excerpt exact; supports the statement. 'FDLR' in entities_named is printed on the page (Kasereka quote and the AFC/M23 passage), not in this excerpt. Kept at C: a party's denial of responsibility for a killing. FARDC account (party says). Kasereka also said Kabizo lies in the AFC-M23-controlled zone and cited nine people killed on 12 June at Rusamambu and Kanoune (Walikale); the page does not source that further. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Cette version a été rejetée par le porte-parole de la 34e région militaire, major Dieudonné Kasereka. Ce dernier dénonce une campagne de désinformation visant, selon lui, à dissimuler les exactions « commises par les éléments du RDF/AFC-M23 »
Sur son compte X, l’AFC/M23 attribue l’attaque aux rebelles FDLR qu’il accuse d’agir en collaboration avec les FARDC.

r7-L-DRC-015.s: Radio Okapi reported that, on its X account, the AFC/M23 attributed the Kabizo attack to FDLR rebels, whom it accused of acting in collaboration with the FARDC.
r7-L-DRC-015.l: Kabizo, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r7-L-DRC-015.n: Party claim, relayed. Recorded so both accounts sit side by side.
r7-L-DRC-015.vn: Excerpt exact and is the whole statement; single clause, single source. C: party channel. AFC/M23 account (party says), relayed from its X account; the post itself was not seen.
src: Sur son compte X, l’AFC/M23 attribue l’attaque aux rebelles FDLR qu’il accuse d’agir en collaboration avec les FARDC.

r7-L-DRC-016.s: Radio Okapi reported that Lieutenant-colonel Mutimura, spokesperson of the FDLR-FOCA, categorically rejected disarmament, justified armed struggle by the protection of Rwandan refugees and set as conditions an inter-Rwandan dialogue and a return in full dignity.
r7-L-DRC-016.n: Answers target r1/UC-BI-FDLR#2 (FDLR own statements). The page is the summary of a Radio Okapi programme (audio); the date of Mutimura's original statement is not given and the words are Radio Okapi's paraphrase. Partisan: party X says.
r7-L-DRC-016.vn: Excerpt exact and covers the whole statement. Translation checked. C: party statement, paraphrased. FDLR-FOCA statement (party says), in Radio Okapi's paraphrase from a programme page; his own words were not seen. The page adds that he said the FDLR would resist a joint military operation.
src: Le lieutenant-colonel Mutimura, porte-parole des FDLR-FOCA, rejette catégoriquement le désarmement. Il justifie la lutte armée par la protection des réfugiés rwandais et pose comme condition un dialogue inter-rwandais et un retour en toute dignité.

r7-L-DRC-017.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Congolese army had issued an ultimatum to the FDLR a month earlier: surrender and lay down arms for repatriation to Rwanda, or face force; the army said the decision was taken within the implementation of the Washington accord of 27 June.
r7-L-DRC-017.n: Context for the FDLR reply above. The exact date of the ultimatum is not on the page ('a month ago'); the page itself says the government had repeated the call in October 2025 through the FARDC.
r7-L-DRC-017.vn: Excerpt exact. Dropped '12 November 2025' from the statement (page date, not printed in the excerpt); it stays in date_precision. Corrected the researcher note (unsupported 'October 2025 repeat' claim). FARDC in the statement is printed in the title. The page says the army did not give a timetable for any disarmament. The researcher's note that the page says the government repeated the call in October 2025 through the FARDC is not on the page. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: L’armée congolaise a lancé il y a un mois un ultimatum aux Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR) : se rendre et déposer les armes pour un rapatriement au Rwanda, ou faire face à la force. L’armée congolaise a lancé il y a un mois un ultimatum aux Forces démocratiques de libération du Rwanda (FDLR) : se rendre et déposer les armes pour un rapatriement au Rwanda, ou faire face à la force. Cette décision est prise dans le cadre de la mise en œuvre de l’accord de Washington du 27 juin, indique l’armée, sans préciser le calendrier d’un éventuel désarmement.

r7-L-DRC-018.s: DW Swahili reported that the Congolese army said M23's claims were not true and that a video showing fighters captured in Congo being handed over to Rwanda was 'forged'.
r7-L-DRC-018.l: Eastern DRC, South Kivu / North Kivu
r7-L-DRC-018.n: Per the same DW page, the M23 claim was that it had captured FDLR fighters; the army statement followed it. No date of the army statement is given beyond the 3 March 2025 publication. Swahili-language Kinshasa/FARDC account on the FDLR question (context for target r1/UC-BI-FDLR#2).
r7-L-DRC-018.vn: Excerpt exact; page dated 03.03.2025. '20' is printed in the title; 'FDLR' on the page (quoted). Swahili checked: 'kughushi' = forged/fake; correct. FARDC denial (party says). The page's headline speaks of 20 fighters; the page says the M23 claimed to have captured FDLR fighters. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Jeshi la Kongo limesema madai hayo ya M23 siyo ya kweli na hata mkanda wa video ulioonesha wapiganaji waliokamatwa Kongo wakikabidhiwa kwa Rwanda ni wa "kughushi".
Taarifa ya jeshi hilo imetolewa baada ya kundi la M23 linaloungwa mkono na Rwanda mashariki mwa Kongo, kutangaza kuwa limewakamata wapiganaji wa kundi la FDLR

r7-L-DRC-019.s: DW Swahili reported that the Congolese army had started operations to hunt FDLR rebels, announced officially at Kisangani (Tshopo) by the deputy army commander, General Ychaligonza Jacques, who called on FDLR fighters to surrender.
r7-L-DRC-019.l: Kisangani, Tshopo (announcement); operations in eastern DRC
r7-L-DRC-019.n: Name spelled as DW prints it. The page does not give the date of the announcement; 30 March 2026 is the DW publication date.
r7-L-DRC-019.vn: Excerpt exact; page dated 30.03.2026 (byline Mitima DeLachance). Lead sentence quoted for the 'started operations' clause. Translation checked. Name spelled as DW prints it. Announcement made outside Phase 1 geography (Kisangani); the operations concern the FDLR in eastern DRC. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Operesheni hiyo ilitangazwa rasmi mjini Kisangani katika jimbo la Tshopo na Naibu kamanda wa jeshi la Kongo, Jenerali Ychaligonza Jacques, ambaye alitoa wito kwa wapiganaji wa FDLR kujisalimisha.
Jeshi la Jamhuri ya Kidemokrasia ya Kongo limeanzisha operesheni za kuwasaka waasi wa FDLR mashariki mwa nchi

r7-L-DRC-020.s: Radio Okapi reported that the Minister of National Defence said at the Council of Ministers of Friday 6 February [2026] that the FARDC had defeated attacks by 'la coalition RDF-M23-AFC' in South Kivu by retaking several localities including Minembwe-centre.
r7-L-DRC-020.n: Government claim of control; contested on the ground by Twirwaneho/AFC-M23 (see discrepancy D-027 for June 2026). The year 2026 comes from the page date 7 February 2026. The page also says the military authorities stated on 2 February that the FARDC inflicted heavy losses in Fizi.
r7-L-DRC-020.vn: Excerpt exact and carries the whole statement; the bracketed year is the researcher's marked insertion from the page date (7 February 2026). Flag benign (capitalised words in the English rendering of 'Forces armées de la RDC'). Government claim of control (party says); the minister is not named on the page. Control of Minembwe was contested later (see discrepancy D-027).
src: Le ministre de la Défense nationale a indiqué, lors du conseil des ministres du vendredi 6 février, que dans le Sud-Kivu, les Forces armées de la RDC, (FARDC) ont fait échec aux attaques de "la coalition RDF-M23-AFC" en reconquérant plusieurs localités dont Minembwe-centre.

r7-L-M23-001.s: Kigali Today reported that a statement issued by AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that the allegations of HRW and the UN were based on political motives, and accused these organisations of bias toward the DRC government; AFC/M23 also said that this could not replace HRW going there in person and that those it spoke to were known extremists and DRC government employees. The statement replied to an HRW report, published on 20 August 2025, saying that residents of areas near Virunga National Park, mostly Hutu, were killed in 14 villages between 10 and 30 July.
r7-L-M23-001.l: Binza groupement, Rutshuru territory (Nyamilima, Kiseguru, Kasave, Rubare named), North Kivu
r7-L-M23-001.a: AFC/M23 (spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka); the HRW report suspects AFC/M23 fighters hunting FDLR
r7-L-M23-001.x: Kigali Today headline: 140 people (HRW figure as given in the headline); 14 villages, 10-30 July 2025
r7-L-M23-001.n: Rwandan outlet relaying an AFC/M23 statement: party says, never fact. Fills discrepancy D-015 (REC-0345) with the M23 reply and a second (HRW) toll/date frame: HRW 10-30 July, 14 villages; Group of Experts figure is separate. Target ids: D-015, r2/G-DOC-858#1 (partly: Binza). Page text carries no byline wire credit.
r7-L-M23-001.vn: All three excerpts found on the retained page (byline Tarib Abdul, 21 August 2025, no wire credit). Narrowed 'biased' to the excerpt's wording (organisations accused of bias) and added the src 2 clause so every source carries a clause. 140 appears only in the headline and stays out of the statement. HRW page says killings were suspected to have occurred while AFC/M23 hunted FDLR ('bigakekwa'), which stays out. AFC/M23 statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet: AFC/M23 says. The HRW findings are as Kigali Today summarises them, not the HRW report itself.
src: Ni raporo uyu muryango washyize ahagaragara ku wa 20 Kanama 2025 ivuga ko abaturage bo mu duce twegereye Pariki y’Igihugu ya Virunga biganjemo Abahutu, biciwe mu midugudu 14 hagati ya tariki 10 na 30 Nyakanga
Itangazo ryashyizwe ahagaragara n’umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, rivuga ko ibirego bya HRW na ONU bishingiye ku mpamvu za politike, igashinja iyi miryango kubogamira ku butegetsi bwa RDC.
AFC/M23 ikavuga ko ibyo bidashobora gusimbura kuhigerera kwa HRW kandi ko abo yavuganye na bo ari abahezanguni bazwi ndetse n’abakozi ba Leta ya RDC.

r7-L-M23-002.s: Kigali Today reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrance Kanyuka, standing in the city centre, spoke about the AFC/M23 departure from Uvira; Kanyuka said that Uvira had been a key stronghold of forces allied with the Kinshasa government, including Wazalendo, FDLR, Mai-Mai, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian army. The outlet, in reported speech ('ngo'), added that since Uvira was 'liberated' things had reportedly been good and people lived in peace, with no obstruction, no theft and no abuse.
r7-L-M23-002.n: Party statement via Rwandan outlet ('AFC/M23 says'). Gives AFC/M23's own account of the January 2026 withdrawal context and denies abuse in Uvira; compare HRW (14 May 2026) and discrepancy D-018/D-019/D-020. Target ids: r2/G-UV-CTRL#0, D-018.
r7-L-M23-002.vn: Excerpts exact on the page (Jean de la Croix Tabaro, 17 January 2026). Removed '17 January 2026' (publication date; no excerpt prints 17). Kept both 'ngo' hedges: the second was missing from excerpt_en. 'Burundian troops' -> 'Burundian army' per excerpt. AFC/M23 account relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the 'no theft, no abuse' passage is hedged with 'ngo' (it is said). Contrast with the DRC government account of looting in Uvira. 2026-10-29: source 2 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-M23 claim 1)
src: Avuga kuri iki gikorwa, Lawrance Kanyuka, umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 wari uhagaze mu mujyi rwagati yagize ati

Kanyuka yavuze ko umujyi wa UVira wari igihome cy’ingenzi cy’ingabo zari zishyize hamwe n’ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa, harimo Wazalendo, FDLR, Mai-Mai, abacanshuro b’abanyamahanga, ndetse n'ingabo z'u Burundi.
Nyamara kuva Uvira yabohorwa, ngo ibintu byabaye byiza. Ngo abaturage babayeho mu mahoro, bakora imirimo yabo mu bwisanzure no mu mutuzo, nta kubangamirwa, nta bujura kandi nta hohoterwa.

r7-L-M23-003.s: Under a headline saying that the bodies of people killed by FARDC drones were buried in Goma, Kigali Today reported that at the ceremony the bodies were placed at the Stade de l’Unité, where bereaved families gathered; AFC/M23 political spokesperson Laurence Kanyuka said on X that they had met to honour the civilians killed, shot by the 'bloodthirsty' coalition forces working with the Kinshasa government.
r7-L-M23-003.l: Goma, North Kivu (ceremony at Stade de l'Unité; burial at Mubambiro)
r7-L-M23-003.a: FARDC drones, as alleged by AFC/M23 and the outlet
r7-L-M23-003.n: Rwandan outlet; the page does not give the date or place of the strikes, so the link to the 2 Jan 2026 Masisi/War Child strike (r3/G-RESP#5, r4/G-LOCAL-NK#4) is NOT established by this page; attribution to FARDC drones is the outlet's and AFC/M23's. Weak lead only.
r7-L-M23-003.vn: Excerpts exact (Jean Claude Munyantore, 8 January 2026). Mubambiro (burial place) is printed on the page but in no excerpt, so it is removed from the statement and entities (the excerpts passed, so a replacement quote cannot carry it). Removed publication date '8 January 2026'. The headline's figure of 22 bodies is not printed in any excerpt, so it is dropped from the statement (it stays in the source title). 22 and the FARDC drone attribution rest on the title. Ceremony day is 'today' in the X post, so date approximate. Rwandan outlet and AFC/M23; the page gives no date or place for the strikes, and the FARDC attribution is the outlet's headline and AFC/M23's.
src: Muri uwo muhango, imibiri y’abapfuye yashyizwe kuri stade yitiriwe Ubumwe (Stade de l’Unité), aho imiryango yabuze ababo

Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 mu bya Politiki, Laurence Kanyuka, mu butumwa yanyujije kuri X yagize ati “Uyu munsi twahuye ngo duhe icyubahiro abasivili bishwe barashwe n’ingabo z’inkoramaraso zihurije hamwe, zikorana na Leta ya Kinshasa.

r7-L-M23-004.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on his X account that, besides Banyamulenge Congolese being killed, the DRC government was also forcibly removing people from their homes in Minembwe; the outlet wrote that among those known so far to have been killed in that area was the elder Rudaga Adriyani, aged 95, killed in drone attacks that the coalition of Kinshasa government forces carried out in the Minembwe areas on Monday 23 March 2026.
r7-L-M23-004.a: AFC/M23 (Kanyuka); drone attack attributed by the outlet to 'the alliance of Kinshasa government forces'
r7-L-M23-004.n: Partisan relay: Bwiza (Kigali) repeating an AFC/M23 X post; the outlet, not Kanyuka, names Rudaga Adriyani and attributes the drone attack. The page text carries no date; the page date 2026-04-28 is from the search-result metadata, to be checked by the verifier. Target ids: r1/SKS-2026Q1#0, r2/G-SKS-FIZI#2 (partly).
r7-L-M23-004.vn: Excerpts exact. Page date is 'Kuwa Kabiri, 24 Werurwe 2026' (byline Bénjamin Babou), not 2026-04-28 from search metadata: source date corrected to 2026-03-24 (the X post is reported as 'kuri uyu wa Kabiri tariki ya 24 Werurwe'). Claim date kept at the 23 March attack the excerpt prints. 'Kinshasa-allied forces' changed to the excerpt's 'coalition of Kinshasa government forces'; 'so far known' hedge kept. Rwandan outlet relaying AFC/M23; the drone attribution and the named victim are the outlet's account, unverified.
src: Umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, abinyujije ku rubuga rwe rwa X, yavuze ko usibye kuba Abanye-Congo bo mu bwoko bw'Abanyamulenge bari kwicwa, Leta ya RDC iri no gukora ibikorwa byo kuvana abaturage mu byabo ku mbaraga.

Kugeza ubu mu bo byamenyekanye ko biciwe muri kiriya gice, harimo umukambwe Rudaga Adriyani w'imyaka 95 y'amavuko wiciwe mu bitero bya drone ihuriro ry'ingabo za Leta ya Kinshasa zagabye mu bice bya Minembwe, ku wa Mbere tariki ya 23 Werurwe 2026.

r7-L-M23-005.s: Umunota reported that Kimbulungu, secretary of AFC/M23, said that although the Congolese government and those close to it blamed AFC/M23 for the escape of Munzenze prison inmates and the deaths of the women there, these events happened before AFC/M23 fighters arrived; he also said that from 2 to 13 February AFC/M23 found 874 bodies in the city of Goma, although the Congolese government says about 3000 died.
r7-L-M23-005.x: AFC/M23 (via Umunota): 874 bodies counted in Goma 2-13 February; Congolese government: about 3000 dead
r7-L-M23-005.n: Partisan relay of an AFC/M23 report presentation (Kimbulungu named 'umunyamabanga wa AFC/M23'). The Umunota text twice misprints the date of the prison events as '27 Gicurasi 2025' (27 May) where other sources give 27 January 2025; the date in this claim is the article date. Same account as BBC Gahuza (r1-SV-2025-005). Fills D-004/D-005/D-006 with the AFC/M23 side only; does not give the number of women raped. Target ids: r1/SV-NK-2025#6, r1/SV-2025#4, D-005, D-006.
r7-L-M23-005.vn: Excerpts exact (page dated 31 May 2025). 'presenting an AFC/M23 report' rests only on page text outside the excerpts and is removed. 'counted' -> 'found' (ryabonye), '3000 claimed' -> 'about 3000' (abagera ku). The page gives the full name Delion Kimbulungu, but no excerpt does, so the statement keeps 'Kimbulungu'. AFC/M23's own figures and denial via a Rwandan outlet. The page misprints the date of the prison events as 27 May 2025 ('27 Gicurasi'); the press conference was on Friday 30 May 2025 per the page.
src: Kimbulungu yagaragaje ko nubwo Leta ya Congo n’abakorana bya hafi na yo bashinje AFC/M23 uruhare mu itorokwa ry’imfungwa za gereza ya Munzenze ndetse n’urupfu rw’aba bagore, ibi byago byabaye mbere y’uko abarwanyi babo bahagera.

Kimbulungu, umunyamabanga wa AFC/M23, yasobanuye ko kuva tariki ya 02 kugeza 13 Gashyantare, iri huriro rya AFC/M23 ryabonye mu mujyi wa Goma imirambo 874, nubwo Leta ya Congo yo yemeza ko hapfuye abagera ku 3000.

r7-L-M23-006.s: MediaCongo, relaying ACP/MCP and citing the same military sources as its report on FARDC advances around Minembwe, reported that bombardments attributed to drones from Rwanda, which it called the aggressor country, targeted the Minembwe general hospital and some civilian homes on Wednesday morning.
r7-L-M23-006.l: Minembwe general hospital, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-L-M23-006.a: drones from Rwanda, as attributed by the FARDC source
r7-L-M23-006.n: Kinshasa-side account (FARDC military source; state press ACP/MCP): a party says. It dates a hospital strike to Wednesday 17 June 2026, a week before the AFC/M23 allegation of 24 June 2026 (already recorded via Kivu Morning Post) that FARDC drones struck the same hospital. Date computed from weekday and publication date ('mercredi 17 juin 2026' in the article). No statement from FARDC on the 24 June allegation was found. Target ids: r1/SKS-2026Q2#0, r1/HC-2026#0.
r7-L-M23-006.vn: Excerpt exact. The page shows 18.06.2026, not 17 June: source date corrected. Removed '17 June 2026' (only in page text, not the excerpt), 'FARDC communiqué' and 'no official toll' (page only; not in the excerpt). 'Military' rests on the title (FARDC) and 'les mêmes sources'. Claim date 2026-06-17 kept as approximate. Kinshasa-side (FARDC military source via state press): a party says. Date inferred: the page says the information came 'mercredi 17 juin 2026' and the strike 'mercredi matin'.
src: Par ailleurs, des bombardements attribués à des drones en provenance du Rwanda, pays agresseur, a visé mercredi matin l’Hôpital général de Minembwe et certaines habitations civiles, selon les mêmes sources.

r7-L-M23-007.s: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 confirmed the death of its military spokesperson Lt Col Willy Ngoma, saying he was killed on the 24th of February in a 'full-scale war' it accuses Kinshasa of resuming; in a statement issued on Saturday, M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that the Kinshasa regime deliberately violated the ceasefire, mainly targeting AFC/M23 soldiers and civilians with its drones outside the front lines. The BBC reported that the DRC government had made no official announcement on the M23 statement or on Ngoma's death.
r7-L-M23-007.l: Rubaya area, Masisi territory, North Kivu (strike location per BBC: near Rubaya)
r7-L-M23-007.a: AFC/M23 (Lawrence Kanyuka); drone strike attributed to the DRC armed forces (FARDC) in the BBC's account
r7-L-M23-007.n: BBC Gahuza (non-partisan outlet) relaying an AFC/M23 statement: a party says; the cause of death is the party's and press reports'. Date of statement computed from weekday ('ku wa gatandatu') and publication date 1 March 2026 (Saturday = 28 February). Fills r1/UC-M23#2: AFC/M23 reaction found; Kinshasa reaction: BBC says none as of 1 March 2026 (further Kinshasa searches in other languages follow in the gap entry).
r7-L-M23-007.vn: Excerpts exact (Didier Bikorimana, published 1 March 2026). Removed '1 March 2026' (no excerpt prints it). excerpt_en 'former military spokesperson' changed: 'uwari umuvugizi' means the one who was its spokesperson (he died), not that he had left the post. Party statement (AFC/M23 says) reported by a non-partisan outlet; the cause of death is the party's account. Statement date (Saturday 28 February 2026) is computed from the publication date of 1 March 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-M23 claim 6)
src: Umutwe w'inyeshyamba wa AFC/M23 urwanya ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo (DRC) wemeje urupfu rw'uwari umuvugizi wa gisirikare wawo, Lt Col Willy Ngoma, uvuga ko yishwe ku itariki ya 24 y'ukwezi gushize kwa Gashyantare (2) mu "ntambara isesuye" ushinja Kinshasa gusubukura.

Mu itangazo yasohoye ku wa gatandatu, umuvugizi wa M23 Lawrence Kanyuka yavuze ko "ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bwarenze ku bushake ku gahenge buteza intambara isesuye kuri AFC/M23, bugambiriye mu buryo bw'ibanze abasirikare bacu n'abaturage bacu b'abasivile bukoresheje 'drone' zabwo hanze y'imirongo y'imbere yo ku rugamba".
Nta cyo leta ya DRC yari yatangaza ku mugaragaro kuri iri tangazo rya M23 cyangwa ku rupfu rwa Lt Col Ngoma.

r7-L-M23-008.s: Reporter.cd reported that the DRC government, in an official 'mise au point' reframing a Human Rights Watch communiqué on Uvira, said that the RDF/M23 withdrawal from the city of Uvira on 17 January 2026 came after a period of systematic looting, large-scale theft, threats, intimidation and acts of community stigmatisation, and that at that stage no death or injury had been reported within the Banyamulenge community since the RDF/M23 withdrawal.
r7-L-M23-008.a: DRC government (Ministry of Communication and Media); the government attributes the conduct to RDF/M23
r7-L-M23-008.n: Government communiqué as relayed by a Kinshasa outlet: a party says; not independent confirmation. Reply to HRW 20 January 2026 statement (not the 14 May 2026 report). Does not mention hospitals. Target ids: r1/HC-2026#1 (Kinshasa on Uvira), D-020 (looting of Uvira, REC-0008) and D-018 (withdrawal day 17 January per this communiqué).
r7-L-M23-008.vn: Excerpts exact (Pierre Kabakila, 22 January 2026). Removed the publication date, the HRW communiqué title and date (20 January 2026) and the ministry name, which sit only in page text outside the excerpts; the title carries 'Gouvernement congolais' and 'Human Rights Watch'. Kinshasa government communiqué relayed by a Kinshasa outlet: a party says. The page attributes the document to the Ministry of Communication and Media and the HRW communiqué to 20 January 2026.
src: Selon la mise au point officielle, le retrait du RDF/M23 de la ville d’Uvira, intervenu le 17 janvier 2026, est survenu après une période caractérisée par des pillages systématiques, des vols à grande échelle, des menaces, des intimidations ainsi que des actes de stigmatisation communautaire ayant profondément affecté la sécurité des civils et la cohésion sociale.
À ce stade, aucun décès ni blessé n’a été signalé au sein de la communauté banyamulenge depuis le retrait du RDF/M23.

r7-L-M23-009.s: Okapinews reported that the Kibuwa general referral hospital, in the health zone of the same name in Walikale territory, North Kivu, was looted on Friday by M23 rebels during their withdrawal from the town, and that Dr Yves Tshongo, chief medical officer of the Kibuwa zone, confirmed this without giving details, saying the hospital had indeed been attacked by M23 elements.
r7-L-M23-009.l: Kibuwa (Kibua) general referral hospital, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r7-L-M23-009.a: M23 rebels, as stated by the outlet and the health zone chief
r7-L-M23-009.n: Second, independent local outlet (Okapinews, Kinshasa-based health news) for the Kibua hospital looting: supports a Friday 4 April 2025 date (REC-0403) against a January 2025 date for the Walikale-area referral hospitals (REC-0378); this page does not mention January. Date computed from weekday and publication date. The outlet also quotes Fiston Misona (printed also 'Missona'), coordinator of the Walikale civil society (Forces Vives), who condemned the looting. No AFC/M23 reply on this looting found in the searches run. Target ids: r3/G-RESP#4, D-001.
r7-L-M23-009.vn: Excerpts exact (Joseph Kipala, 5 April 2025). Removed 'Saturday 5 April 2025' (no excerpt prints it). 'withdrawal from Walikale' narrowed to 'from the town' ('cette cité'). Local outlet plus a named health official on record: B. Date computed: 'vendredi' in an article dated Saturday 5 April 2025, so Friday 4 April 2025. The page also says hospital staff had fled to the bush and no toll could yet be given.
src: L’hôpital général de référence de Kibuwa dans la zone de santé portant le même nom au territoire de Walikale dans le Nord Kivu a été pillé vendredi par les rebelles du M23 pendant leur retrait de cette cité.
Dr Yves Tshongo, Médecin Chef de zone de Kibuwa a confirmé cette information sans donner des détails. « L’hopital a été effectivement attaqué par les éléments de M23.

r7-L-M23-010.s: Umuryango.rw reported that AFC/M23 said it was saddened to see the international community remaining silent on killings being carried out by the Kinshasa government against residents of areas including Minembwe, Mikenge and Karingi in South Kivu; Kanyuka said these acts against innocent and defenceless civilians were being carried out by FARDC, FNDB, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenaries.
r7-L-M23-010.l: Minembwe, Mikenge and Karingi, South Kivu highlands (Fizi/Mwenga)
r7-L-M23-010.a: AFC/M23 (Lawrence Kanyuka) alleging FARDC, FNDB, Wazalendo, FDLR and foreign mercenaries
r7-L-M23-010.n: AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by a Rwandan outlet (itself crediting RadioTV10): 'AFC/M23 says'; no figures or named victims. The statement is the party's allegation, not established fact. Gives the AFC/M23 account (target r1/SKS-2026Q1#0, r2/G-SKS-FIZI#2) of the Jan-Feb 2026 Minembwe/Mikenge/Karingi fighting. Burundi (FNDB) is named by Kanyuka; no Burundian reply was found in the searches run.
r7-L-M23-010.vn: Excerpts exact (Ishimwe Jean de Dieu, 20 February 2026; RADIOTV10 credit at end). Removed 'Thursday 19 February 2026' and 'political spokesperson Lawrence' (only outside the excerpts). excerpt_en for src 1 dropped the 'innocent and defenceless civilians' clause: corrected. AFC/M23 communiqué via a Rwandan outlet (crediting RadioTV10): AFC/M23 says. The page dates the communiqué to the night of Thursday 19 February 2026 and names Kanyuka as political spokesperson. 2026-10-29: source 1 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-M23 claim 9)
src: Ihuriro AFC/M23 ritavuga rumwe n’ubutegetsi bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo, ryatangaje ko ribabajwe no kubona umuryango mpuzamahanga ukomeje kuruca ukarumira ku bwicanyi buri gukorwa n’ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa bukorerwa abatuye mu bice birimo Minembwe, Mikenge, na Karingi muri Kivu y’Epfo.

Kanyuka yakomeje avuga ko ibi bikorwa by’ubugome ndengakamere bikomeje gukorerwa “abaturage b’inzirakarengane kandi badafite kirengera, bukozwe n’ingabo za FARDC, FNDB, Wazalendo, FDLR n’abacancuro b’abanyamahanga

r7-L-M23-011.s: DW Kiswahili, in a piece one year after the fall of Goma, quoted humanitarian worker Mwende Kanane as saying there were even reports of rape in the prison before the prisoners escaped, and wrote that the security situation became more fragile after inmates escaped from Munzenze prison, which contributed to an increase in crime and cases of rape, especially against women; DW also wrote that, according to the United Nations, the number of people who died reached about 3,000.
r7-L-M23-011.n: One-year retrospective: the date in the claim is approximate (the page says rape reports existed in the prison 'before the prisoners escaped' and does not give a date or number). Adds a Swahili outlet and a named humanitarian worker; the 3,000 figure is DW's attribution to the UN and is separate from the AFC/M23 figure of 874 bodies (Umunota/BBC Gahuza) and the ~700 etc. in other records (D-006). The page says the escape 'contributed to' crime and rape; it does not identify perpetrators (D-005). No AFC/M23 or Rwandan statement appears on the page. Target ids: D-004, D-005, D-006.
r7-L-M23-011.vn: Excerpts exact (Zanem Nety Zaidi / Bakari Ubena, 27 January 2026). Removed publication date. 'after M23 took control of Goma' rests on the page sentence before the excerpt, so it is replaced by the title's 'one year after the fall of Goma' framing. Retrospective; the rape reports are second-hand ('taarifa za') and undated, with no perpetrator or number. The UN toll is DW's attribution.
src: Kwa mujibu wa Mwende Kanane, mfanyakazi wa mashirika ya kibinadamu, hali ilikuwa mbaya kupita maelezo: "Mashirika ya kibinadamu, hasa Shirika la Msalaba Mwekundu, yalitumia ambulansi chache zilizokuwepo kukusanya miili iliyokuwa imelala mitaani. Hali ya kibinadamu ilikuwa ngumu sana, hata kulikuwa na taarifa za ubakaji gerezani kabla ya wafungwa kutoroka.
Zaidi ya hayo, hali ya usalama ilizidi kuwa tete baada ya wafungwa kutoroka kutoka gereza la Munzenze, hali iliyochangia ongezeko la uhalifu na visa vya ubakaji, hasa dhidi ya wanawake.
Kulingana na Umoja wa Mataifa, idadi ya waliopoteza maisha ilifikia takribani 3,000.

r7-L-M23-012.s: Presse Actu reported that AFC-M23 rejected, on Thursday 4 June 2026, FARDC accusations implicating it in the summary execution of ten civilians in the locality of Kiseguru, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu; in a 'mise au point' the rebel movement called them 'allégations mensongères, infondées et politiquement motivées' (false, unfounded and politically motivated allegations).
r7-L-M23-012.l: Kiseguru, Binza groupement, Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r7-L-M23-012.a: AFC/M23 (denial); FARDC accuse the rebel coalition
r7-L-M23-012.n: Denial by the accused party (a party says) reported by a Kinshasa outlet; no counter-figures or alternative account were given by AFC/M23 in the page. The FARDC accusation itself (communiqué of 3 June 2026; ten civilians; others arrested and moved to Kanyangambi prison) is recorded in the project under r1-ATR-NK-2026-009. Another outlet snippet (Facebook, not cited) dates the rejection to 3 June; the Presse Actu page says Thursday 4 June 2026. Target id: r1/ATR-NK-2026#1.
r7-L-M23-012.vn: Excerpts exact (La Rédaction, 05 Jun 2026). Removed '3 June' communiqué date and '2 June' (page only). Source type corrected: Presse Actu is a Congolese news site reporting the denial, not an AFC/M23 outlet. Denial by the accused party. The page says the FARDC communiqué was published on 3 June and placed the killings on Tuesday 2 June at Kiseguru, Binza groupement, Bwito chiefdom.
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo-M23 (AFC-M23) a rejeté, ce jeudi 4 juin 2026, les accusations des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) l’impliquant dans l’exécution sommaire de dix civils dans la localité de Kiseguru, en territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu
Dans une mise au point, le mouvement rebelle qualifie ces accusations d’« allégations mensongères, infondées et politiquement motivées ».

r7-L-RN-001.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundi's Minister of National Defence and Veterans, Alain Tribert Mutabazi, defended the deployment of Burundian troops in the DRC, saying that this presence falls within a security cooperation agreement concluded between Bujumbura and Kinshasa.
r7-L-RN-001.l: Burundi (statement on deployment in eastern DRC)
r7-L-RN-001.a: Burundi Ministry of National Defence and Veterans
r7-L-RN-001.n: The minister spoke on Tuesday while presenting the fourth-quarter achievements of the 2024-2025 budget year (per the page); date computed from the weekday ('Mardi') and the page date of 17 July 2025. SOS Médias Burundi is an independent Burundian outlet relaying a public ministerial event; the Burundian government statement is cited only for what the minister said. The same page gives the minister's quote that Burundian soldiers 'resteront en RDC aussi longtemps que la loi le permet' and says about 10,000 Burundian soldiers are deployed in North and South Kivu according to the outlet (not the minister). Answers part of target r1/UV-2025Q3#1 (general statement, nothing specific to Uvira).
r7-L-RN-001.vn: Page checked in full: the passage is the outlet's report of the minister's remarks at the presentation of Q4 2024-2025 budget achievements; attribution kept ('selon lui'). Weekday arithmetic confirmed (17 July 2025 = Thursday, so 'Mardi' = 15 July). Date derived from 'Mardi' in an article dated 17 July 2025 (a Thursday): 15 July 2025; the excerpt itself prints no date. 2026-10-29: source 0 excerpt_en edited: QA 0.4 A3: non-English excerpt shown without an English translation; translation added, marked as one
src: le ministre de la Défense nationale et des Anciens combattants, Alain Tribert Mutabazi, a défendu le déploiement des troupes burundaises en RDC. Selon lui, cette présence s’inscrit dans un accord de coopération sécuritaire conclu entre Bujumbura et Kinshasa.

r7-L-RN-002.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that, after M23 took Uvira, Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana told the news agency AFP that signing agreements and then not implementing them is contempt for everyone, first of all for President Trump.
r7-L-RN-002.n: Kirundi-language page (BBC Gahuza, published 14 December 2025). The page also has Bizimana calling the US actions that led to the peace agreement 'a slap in the face... the middle finger' (a gesture of contempt); that passage contains an ellipsis on the page and is not used as an excerpt. The AFP quote is relayed by BBC; the original AFP text was not located. Exact date of the AFP interview is not stated; it follows the Uvira capture that the BBC text dates to Wednesday (10 December). Answers part of target r1/UV-2025Q4#2.
r7-L-RN-002.vn: Page read in full. Translation of source 1 is faithful (Perezida = President; 'ibiro ntaramakuru' = news agency; 'agasuzuguro' = contempt); the capitalised-word flag is 'President' rendering 'Perezida': resolved. Source 0 excerpt is truncated mid-quote but its translation matches the truncation. Only the second sentence is credited to AFP on the page, so originating_source for source 0 is BBC Gahuza itself. Language tag 'rn' should arguably be 'rw' (Kinyarwanda); not changed here. BBC relays AFP; the original AFP text was not located. The article is written in Kinyarwanda orthography (cy-, Ukuboza), not Kirundi, although BBC Gahuza serves both.
src: Nyuma yuko M23 ifashe Uvira, Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Burundi Édouard Bizimana yavuze ko byabaye "gukubita urushyi mu maso
Yabwiye ibiro ntaramakuru AFP ati: "Gusinya amasezerano ubundi ntuyashyire mu bikorwa ni agasuzuguro kuri buri wese, mbere na mbere kuri Perezida Trump."

r7-L-RN-003.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Burundi's foreign minister Édouard Bizimana had told Radio RFI, before the capture of Uvira, that 'those troops' would leave only if the Kinshasa government asked for it, because it was with Kinshasa that they had made the agreement.
r7-L-RN-003.n: 'izo ngabo' (those troops) refers, in the preceding sentence of the BBC article, to the more than 10,000 Burundian troops that the article (citing analyst Jason Stearns) says were deployed in South and North Kivu; the excerpt itself does not name them. Complements the Iwacu-cited RFI statements already recorded (r1-ST-BI-011, r1-ST-BI-012). Original RFI interview not located.
r7-L-RN-003.vn: Statement unchanged; correction is to the translation only: 'zahava gusa ari uko ... ibisabye' is 'would leave only if ... asks', not 'could leave'. Capitalised-word flag (Minister, Foreign, Affairs, French) resolved: they render 'Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga' and 'y'Abafaransa'. RFI original not located. 'Those troops' refers, in the preceding sentence of the article, to the Burundian troops in South and North Kivu (number given only by analyst Jason Stearns: more than 10,000; Burundi published none). 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-RN claim 2)

r7-L-RN-004.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's ambassador to the UN, Martin Ngoga, said that Rwanda has no plan to attack Burundi, and that M23 had also said earlier that it has no such plan.
r7-L-RN-004.l: UN Security Council (statement on Burundi-Rwanda tension over Uvira)
r7-L-RN-004.n: Rwandan reply to the Burundian accusation (Maniratanga at the UN Security Council, already recorded as r1-ST-BI-014). The BBC does not give the date of Ngoga's remarks; the sentence sits in a paragraph about the Security Council session and the US statement 'on Saturday'. Included here because it is the Rwandan side of the Burundi-Rwanda exchange, not Burundi's.
r7-L-RN-004.vn: Page read: translation faithful ('rufite' agrees with u Rwanda, so 'it' = Rwanda). Attribution kept. Preceding sentence on the page adds that the Rwandan government continued to deny supporting M23 (not added to the statement). r7-L-RN-005.vn: Single sentence on the page ('Mbere, M23 na yo yavuze ko nta mugambi nk'uwo ifite'); date, channel and wording of the M23 statement not given. Translation faithful. Kept as 'BBC reported M23 said'.

r7-L-RN-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye on Friday praised the commitment of his country's defence and security forces deployed in the DRC, at a public broadcast held at the Royal stadium in Muramvya, Gitega province, and congratulated them for their courage and commitment.

Le chef de l’État burundais a félicité les forces burundaises engagées en RDC pour leur courage et leur engagement.

r7-L-RN-007.s: Actualite.cd reported that Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, as future president of the African Union, called on the United States, as guarantor of the Washington accords, to increase pressure on the parties so that they respect their commitments.

The speech was delivered on Thursday 14 January 2026 at the new-year exchange of wishes with the diplomatic and consular corps, per the article's own text (not in the excerpt). The article also reports the president describing 2025 as marked by 'conquête et occupation de territoires congolais' and the 'massacre de citoyens congolais innocents' (not used as an excerpt). No mention of the 14 January Kalundu drone strike or of Burundian operations in Uvira territory (target r1/UV-2026Q1#3).

Elle appelle, à ce titre, la communauté internationale ainsi que les institutions continentales à assumer pleinement leurs responsabilités, en exerçant une vigilance soutenue afin de prévenir toute escalade et d’éviter une aggravation des tensions ethniques et de la crise humanitaire dans la région" a réagi Corneille Nangaa, Coordonnateur du mouvement rebelle soutenu par le Rwanda

r7-L-RN-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to concordant testimonies, Burundian soldiers posted at Mikalati intercepted several groups of women, men and young people from Minembwe who were trying to reach the Bijombo market to buy basic goods such as salt, sugar or soap. The outlet also wrote that an FDNB spokesperson was not available to answer these allegations and that in most cases the Burundian authorities have denied accusations of mistreating Banyamulenge.
r7-L-RN-009.l: Mikalati, Bijombo groupement (Fizi territory), South Kivu
r7-L-RN-009.a: Burundian soldiers (FDNB) posted at Mikalati, per witnesses
r7-L-RN-009.x: SOS Médias Burundi: 'plusieurs groupes' of women, men and young people; no number given
r7-L-RN-009.n: Earlier episode than the 6 December 2025 Mikalati attack (r1-UC-BI-FDLR-031..033) and the November 2025 FDNB statement on road blocking (r1-ST-BI-005). The Burundian reaction found: spokesperson 'not available' for this article; the 'denied in most cases' sentence is the outlet's general statement, not a quoted denial and not tied to this incident. The names are first names/initials of quoted residents as printed. Access to food (and, per the outlet, to care) in the Hauts Plateaux; no health-facility event in this item. Answers part of target r1/HC-SK-2025#2.
