src: Selon des témoignages concordants, les militaires burundais postés à Mikalati ont intercepté plusieurs groupes — des femmes, des hommes et des jeunes — qui tentaient de rejoindre le marché pour acheter des produits de première nécessité tels que le sel, le sucre ou le savon.

Un porte-parole de la Force de Défense Nationale du Burundi (FDNB) n’était pas disponible pour répondre à ces allégations. Cependant, dans la plupart des cas, les autorités burundaises ont nié les accusations selon lesquelles l’armée burundaise et des membres de la ligue des jeunes du CNDD-FDD, le parti au pouvoir, qui les accompagnent parfois en RDC, malmèneraient les Banyamulenge.
Ils veulent qu’on meure sans sel, ni sucre, ni huile », témoigne Espérance, une commerçante de Minembwe refoulée le week-end dernier.
Comment vivre sans sel ni savon ? », déplore Éric M., un autre habitant.

Le week-end dernier, plusieurs habitants de Minembwe, principalement issus de la communauté Banyamulenge, ont été refoulés par des soldats burundais alors qu’ils se rendaient au marché de Bijombo, dans le groupement du même nom, territoire de Fizi.

r7-L-RN-010.s: La Libre reported that Kinshasa's troops, supported notably by Wazalendo militias and by Burundian army personnel, were forced to turn back when they were less than two kilometres from Minembwe airport; it wrote that several accounts from Congolese rebel circles and from Burundian ranks mention a large number killed in these clashes near Minembwe, with all figures between 100 and 150 Burundians in one morning, and that since the start of the Burundian intervention Bujumbura has published no 'credible' official figure.
r7-L-RN-010.a: FARDC, Wazalendo and Burundian army (coalition); AFC/M23 and allies (opponents, not named in the excerpts)
r7-L-RN-010.x: La Libre: 'between 100 and 150 Burundians in one morning' (accounts from rebel circles and Burundian ranks); no official Burundian figure
r7-L-RN-010.n: Paywalled article (marked 'réservé aux abonnés'; the text was retrievable by the helper). Burundian losses rest on anonymous testimony (including one former Burundian soldier) and are unverified. The article dates the turn-back 'three weeks' after President Tshisekedi's announcement in Houston of the retaking of Minembwe; the exact date is not given (the existing register places the Minembwe clashes in June 2026, see D-027 and the 9 June 2026 losses in target r1/SKC-2026H1#3). The 'no credible official figure' sentence is La Libre's own statement, so no Burundian government statement on these losses was found in this article. Authors' byline: Hubert Leclercq.
r7-L-RN-010.vn: Page read (paywall text retrievable; byline Hubert Leclercq; photo credit AFP only, text not wire copy). The 'no credible official figure' sentence is the journalist's narration. Translations faithful; capitalised-word flags (Kinshasa's, Wazalendo, Congolese, Burundian, DRC) are renderings of words in the excerpts: resolved. Casualty figures rest on unnamed testimony from rebel circles and Burundian ranks as reported by La Libre (Hubert Leclercq); unverified. The turn-back is dated only 'three weeks' after Tshisekedi's Houston announcement.
src: Les troupes de Kinshasa, soutenues notamment par les milices wazalendos et les effectifs de l'armée burundaise, ont été contraintes de rebrousser chemin alors qu'elles étaient à moins de deux kilomètres de l'aéroport de Minembwe.

Plusieurs témoignages venus des milieux rebelles congolais mais aussi des rangs burundais évoquent un nombre important de tués dans ces affrontements près de Minembwe. Tous les chiffres oscillent entre 100 et 150 Burundais en une matinée.
Depuis le début de l'intervention militaire burundaise en RDC, à la demande de Kinshasa, en 2022, aucun chiffre officiel "crédible" n'a été publié par Bujumbura.

r7-L-RN-011.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Kagame, a contingent of more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers was said to be operating in several provinces, notably Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale and Kisangani, and that he accused Burundi of regular strikes against civilians, notably at Minembwe; the outlet wrote that at the time of publication the Burundian authorities had not reacted.
r7-L-RN-011.l: Uvira, Minembwe and other places in the DRC, as listed by Kagame
r7-L-RN-011.x: Kagame (via Kivu Morning Post): more than twenty thousand Burundian soldiers
r7-L-RN-011.n: Rwandan statement ('Kagame says'), not an established fact; the figure of 20,000 is Kagame's as relayed by the outlet. The page says the remarks were made at the swearing-in of new members of Kagame's cabinet, without a date; Anadolu (r1-UV-2025Q4-019) dates the remarks to Thursday 11 December 2025. The second excerpt is the outlet's statement that Burundi had not reacted at publication; later Burundian replies were searched for and not found (see gap for r1/UV-2025Q4#2).
r7-L-RN-011.vn: Page read. The French conditional 'opérerait' (reported, unconfirmed) was rendered as an indicative 'is currently operating'; translation and statement corrected to keep the hedge. Capitalised-word flags ('According', 'Kigali' context, 'Rwandan') resolved as renderings. The page gives the occasion (swearing-in of new cabinet members) but no date. Kagame's figure and allegations, not established facts. The outlet lists Uvira and Minembwe among 'provinces' as Kagame is reported to have said. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (L-RN claim 10)
src: Selon Kagame, un contingent de plus de vingt mille soldats burundais opérerait actuellement dans plusieurs provinces, notamment Uvira, Minembwe, Kalemie, Kindu, Walikale et Kisangani. Il accuse également le Burundi de frappes régulières contre les civils, notamment à Minembwe, et déplore le silence de la communauté internationale.

Le président rwandais critique enfin le « réflexe systématique » d’accuser Kigali de tous les incidents dans l’Est congolais. Au moment de la publication, les autorités burundaises n’avaient pas réagi.

r7-L-RN-012.s: Radio Isanganiro, in a 'vrai ou faux' item on an online claim about Congolese officials moving their families from Uvira to Bujumbura and about Burundian soldiers in camps in Burundi, wrote that the Burundian army has never published such information and that reliable international media have never published information on the number of troops Burundi has, abroad or at home.
r7-L-RN-012.a: Radio Isanganiro (Burundi private radio) commenting on the Burundian army
r7-L-RN-012.n: Not a statement by the Burundian army or government: a Burundian private radio (Bujumbura; broadcasts in Kirundi, Swahili, French) saying the army has published no such figures. Useful as a Kirundi-language confirmation, as of June 2025, that no FDNB statement on troop numbers or on the Uvira area was found (target r1/UV-2025Q2#1). 'nk'ayo' (such) refers to the preceding online claim of fewer than 5,000 soldiers in Burundian camps, which the item rejects as unfounded.
r7-L-RN-012.vn: Page read (Kirundi, 'Vrai ou Faux' section, 18/06/2025). Translation of the excerpt is faithful; statement narrowed from 'figures' to 'information' ('amakuru ku gitigiri' = information on the number). Capitalised-word flags (Burundian, Burundi) resolved as renderings. Not a statement by the Burundian army or government: a private Burundian radio's fact-check. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration) 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Igisirikare c’Uburundi nticigeze gitangaza amakuru nk’ayo kandi n’ibinyamakuru mpuzamakungu vyizewe ntibirigera bitangaza amakuru ku gitigiri c’ingabo Uburundi bufise, iziri hanze n’iziri mu gihugu.

Nk’akarorero urubuga rwiyita “Ukuri Kunywanisha Online TV” bavugako abategetsi mu gisirikare ca Congo bari muri Uvira hamwe n’abandi bategetsi hamwe n’abagwizatunga bariko bahungira mu Burundi mu gisagara ca Bujumbura.
Baravuga kandi ko mu makambi y’igisirikare c’Uburundi ari ku butaka bw’Uburundi ata basirikare bashika ibihumbi bitanu (5000) bahari kuko bose bari kugwana mu buseruko bwa Congo.

r7-L-RW-001.s: Ijambo.net reported that the Government of Rwanda, in a statement issued on Monday 2 March 2026, rejected the sanctions the United States had imposed on some senior RDF officers, saying they were biased and aimed at presenting a picture contrary to the truth about the long-running insecurity in eastern DRC. The outlet reported that the US named Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen Ruki Karusisi, Gen Mubarakh Muganga and Brig Gen Stanislas Gashugi, and that Rwanda said the US had ignored drone and ground attacks by DRC forces that it said continued despite the agreement to stop fighting and killed many civilians.
r7-L-RW-001.n: Kinyarwanda account of the Rwandan government communiqué of 2 March 2026 (the existing claim r1-UC-RDF-017 carries the AP/Reuters version of Makolo's statement). Ijambo.net is a Rwandan online outlet (Rubavu); the page has no wire credit. Per the page, Rwanda says the sanctions were one-sided while both sides were in peace talks; this adds Rwanda's own counter-allegation about drone attacks, recorded here as Rwanda's account only. Answers targets r1/POL-2026#0, r4/G-CMD-LEGAL#3, r1/UV-2026Q1#2.
r7-L-RW-001.vn: Page read in full (byline Yves Iyaremye; no wire credit). Translations faithful: 'yamaganye' = rejected/condemned, 'bibogamye' = biased, 'bigahitana ubuzima bw'abasivili benshi' = kill many civilians. Capitalised-word flags (United States of America, Rwanda Defence Force, Democratic Republic of Congo, Monday, March, America) are renderings of 'Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika', 'Ingabo z'u Rwanda', 'Mbere', 'Werurwe': resolved. Source 0 excerpt joins two adjacent paragraphs; both on the page.
src: Guverinoma y’u Rwanda yamaganye ibihano Leta Zunze Ubumwe za Amerika zafatiye bamwe mu bayobozi bakuru b’Ingabo z’u Rwanda (RDF), ivuga ko bibogamye kandi bigamije kugaragaza isura ihabanye n’ukuri ku bibazo by’umutekano muke bimaze igihe mu Burasirazuba bwa Repubulika Iharanira Demokarasi ya Congo (RDC). Ni mu itangazo Guverinoma y’u Rwanda yasohoye kuri uyu wa Mbere, tariki ya 2 Werurwe 2026
Kuri uyu wa Mbere ni bwo Amerika yatangaje ko yafatiye ibihano abasirikare bakuru ba RDF barimo Maj Gen Vincent Nyakarundi, Maj. Gen Ruki Karusisi, Gen Mubarakh Muganga na Brig Gen Stanislas Gashugi.

U Rwanda rugaragaza ko Amerika yirengagije ibitero bya ‘drones’ n’ibyo ku butaka bikomeje kugabwa n’Ingabo za RDC, binyuranyije n’amasezerano yo guhagarika imirwano, kandi bigahitana ubuzima bw’abasivili benshi.

r7-L-RW-002.s: Umuryango.rw (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, in a post on X on 14 May 2026, criticised Human Rights Watch, writing (in the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering) that HRW has its way of working and Rwanda is always its measure showing that it has worked well. The outlet described the HRW report of 13 May as accusing Rwandan soldiers and fighters of the armed group M23 of killing civilians, abducting them and raping women in the city of Uvira from 10 December 2025 to 17 January 2026.
r7-L-RW-002.l: Uvira (the HRW report's subject); statement made online
r7-L-RW-002.n: Rwandan state-aligned outlet; the post is Makolo's, relayed by the outlet (the X post itself was not fetched). The same outlet's text goes on to say that Rwanda has repeatedly told the international community it has no troops in eastern DRC; that is the outlet's wording, not recorded as Makolo's. The igihe.com version (igihe.com/mu-rwanda/article/rdf-si-afc-m23-yolande-makolo-kuri-human-rights-watch, 11 June per search listing, and the mobile copy) could not be fetched by the helper (via=none), so it was not cited and no workaround was tried. HRW's own wording of the allegations is in existing claims (e.g. r2-G-UV-SVHC-011, REC-0002/REC-0003). No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply to HRW's April letter found beyond this post. Answers targets r1/SV-2026#1, r2/G-UV-SVHC#2, r3/G-RESP#6, r1/UV-2025Q4#3, r5/G-DISC2#2 for Rwanda.
r7-L-RW-002.vn: Retained page read (byline ISIMBI Estella, 15 May 2026). Translation faithful ('igipimo' = yardstick/measure). The outlet's own later sentences (Rwanda has no troops in eastern DRC; HRW unreliable) are its narration and correctly not credited to Makolo. Capitalised-word flags ('Government', 'Rwandan') resolved as renderings. Makolo's X post was not fetched; the wording is the outlet's Kinyarwanda rendering.
src: Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda, Yolande Makolo, yagaragaje ko umuryango Human Rights Watch uharanira uburenganzira bw’ikiremwamuntu utavuze ku Rwanda, akazi kawo katagaragara. Ubutumwe bwa Makolo bwanyuze ku rubuga X kuri uyu wa 14 Gicurasi 2026, bugira buti “HRW ifite uburyo ikora kandi u Rwanda ruhora ari igipimo cyayo kigaragaza ko yakoze neza.”

Makolo yanengaga raporo HRW yashyize hanze ku wa 13 Gicurasi, ishinja ingabo z’u Rwanda n’abarwanyi b’umutwe witwaje intwaro wa M23 kwica abasivili, kubashimuta no gufata ku ngufu abagore mu Mujyi wa Uvira, kuva tariki ya 10 Ukuboza 2025 kugeza ku ya 17 Mutarama 2026.

r7-L-RW-003.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, in a France 24 interview broadcast on Monday, wondered why Rwanda 'alone' is being sanctioned although the US-led peace agreement signed in December 2025 concerns both sides, and said of the sanctions: 'Those sanctions first of all are unfair to us, they concern one side and are not productive.'
r7-L-RW-003.l: Kigali (statement); sanctions concern the eastern DRC conflict
r7-L-RW-003.n: Date computed from weekday ('ku wa mbere') and the publication date 30 June 2026 (a Monday is 29 June 2026). The article is about the US sanctions announced 'last Thursday' on Rwandan mining companies (Gasabo Gold Refinery and others) and their officials; the excerpts above do not name them, so the statement says 'sanctions'. BBC adds that the DRC government welcomed the sanctions (Muyaya on X); not recorded here. BBC calls this Rwanda's first explicit public statement on those sanctions. Answers r4/G-CMD-LEGAL#3 in part (Rwanda on US designations); the 2 March 2026 reply is in the Ijambo.net claim.
r7-L-RW-003.vn: Page read (byline Didier Bikorimana, 30 June 2026). 30 June 2026 is a Tuesday, so 'ku wa mbere' = 29 June. Translations faithful ('biraturenganya' = are unjust to us). Capitalised-word flags are renderings (Minister, Foreign Affairs, America, President, December): resolved. Kinyarwanda article, tagged rw correctly.
src: Mu kiganiro yagiranye na televiziyo France 24 cyatangajwe ku wa mbere, Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Rwanda Olivier Nduhungirehe yibajije impamvu u Rwanda "rwonyine" ari rwo rufatirwa ibihano, mu gihe amasezerano y'amahoro – yayobowe n'Amerika yashyizweho umukono mu Kuboza (12) mu 2025 hagati ya Perezida w'u Rwanda Paul Kagame na Perezida wa DRC Félix Tshisekedi – areba impande zombi.
Minisitiri Nduhungirehe yongeyeho ati: "Biriya bihano mbere na mbere biraturenganya, bireba uruhande rumwe kandi ntibitanga umusaruro.

r7-L-RW-004.s: A Rwandan broadcaster's website reported that Rwanda's Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Olivier Nduhungirehe, writing on X, disputed remarks by US adviser Massad Boulos by saying AFC/M23 had completed its withdrawal from Uvira weeks before the US imposed sanctions on the RDF; the outlet reported him saying AFC/M23 began leaving Uvira on 16 December 2025 and completed its withdrawal on 17 January 2026, and that the Congolese army later returned to the city alongside Burundian forces, the FDLR and Wazalendo armed groups.
r7-L-RW-004.n: Rwandan outlet reporting a post on X (the post itself was not fetched); the exact post date is not given on the page, the outlet is dated 27 September 2026 (a Kinyarwanda copy at thenewsjam.rw is dated 26 September 2026). The dates given are Nduhungirehe's, not independently verified; they bear on discrepancy D-018 (day AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira; REC-0005, REC-0591) and D-019. The page also quotes Boulos as saying the sanctions followed the Uvira offensive; that is a US statement as reported. Answers r2/G-UV-CTRL#0 and r1/UV-2026Q1#2 for Rwanda.
r7-L-RW-004.vn: Page read; English original, no translation issue. Boulos's own quoted remark on the page ('Sanctions on Rwanda were a direct result of the invasion of Uvira...') is context, not added. Withdrawal dates are Nduhungirehe's, not independently verified; the X post itself was not fetched.
src: Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Olivier Nduhungirehe said AFC/M23 had completed its withdrawal from Uvira weeks before the United States imposed sanctions on the Rwanda Defence Force. Writing on X, Nduhungirehe disputed remarks made by US Senior Adviser for Africa Massad Boulos during an interview with France 24.

Nduhungirehe responded that AFC/M23, which he described as a Congolese movement, began leaving Uvira on December 16, 2025, and completed its withdrawal on January 17, 2026. He said the Congolese army later returned to the city alongside Burundian forces, the FDLR and Wazalendo armed groups.

r7-L-RW-005.s: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame, asked about the capture of Uvira on 10 December (six days after the Washington agreement) and US pressure, said that 'they' wanted to convince people there was a link between the capture of Uvira and the Washington agreement and that it was a way of rejecting the agreement, 'That is not true at all', and added that whether or not the Washington agreement was signed, 'the capture of Uvira was necessary'.
r7-L-RW-005.n: Kagame's wording is 'gufatwa kwa Uvira' (the capture/taking of Uvira) without naming who captured it; the question frames it as an M23 capture on 10 December 2025. The second sentence cited is a later sentence of the same answer (not contiguous with the first). Statement attributed to Kagame via a Rwandan outlet's translation of the Jeune Afrique interview. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.
r7-L-RW-005.vn: Page read; Q/A labels 'Jeune Afrique:' / 'Paul Kagame:' are printed. Translations faithful ('byari ngombwa' = was necessary; 'Ibyo si ukuri na gato' = that is not true at all). Flags ('American', 'President') resolved as renderings of 'Amerika', 'Perezida'. Kagame's words reach us as Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a French-language Jeune Afrique interview; the French original was not checked. The interview took place 'last month' (March 2026) at Village Urugwiro, per the page.
src: Paul Kagame: Oya. Ni ibindi. Bashakaga kwemeza abantu ko hari isano hagati yo gufatwa kwa Uvira n’amasezerano ya Washington, kandi ko gufatwa kwa Uvira kwari uburyo bwo kwanga ayo masezerano. Ibyo si ukuri na gato.
Amasezerano ya Washington asinywa, cyangwa n'iyo adasinywa, gufatwa kwa Uvira byari ngombwa.

Jeune Afrique: Gufata Uvira ku itariki ya 10 Ukuboza, iminsi itandatu nyuma y’amasezerano ya Washington, haba ari ho haturutse igitutu cya Amerika, ubutegetsi bwa Trump bugahera aho bubafatira ibihano? Ubyumva gute?
Mu kiganiro cyihariye yahaye Jeune Afrique, Perezida Kagame yabwiye Kinshasa, Washington n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko bagomba gukora inshingano zabo.

r7-L-RW-006.s: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame, asked whether he agreed with the reading that Rwandan troops are on eastern DRC soil after Rwanda's ambassador in Washington said on 22 January that Rwanda has 'security cooperation with AFC/M23', answered 'Yes, of course', and said that defensive measures mean protecting Rwanda and its borders from threats, including using military equipment and sending troops on the ground, and that if guarding the border requires dealing with the problem 5, 10 or 20 kilometres back, it is a defensive measure.
r7-L-RW-006.n: The page's question (not in the excerpt) cites the Rwandan ambassador in Washington saying on 22 January that Rwanda has 'security cooperation with AFC/M23', which many understood as RDF troops on eastern DRC soil. The answer does not say where the 5-20 km is measured from (the page's own words: 'inyuma', 'behind/back'). Recorded as Kagame's statement only; compare the UN Group of Experts findings on RDF deployments in existing claims. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.
r7-L-RW-006.vn: Statement supported by source 0 as written. The question that gives 'Yes, of course' its meaning is on the page but not in any stored excerpt, so it is recorded in the note for an excerpt extension rather than added to the statement. Translation faithful ('Nta gihabanye' = there is no contradiction). Source 1 (generic intro sentence) supports only the interview's framing. Context the stored excerpts do not carry (excerpt gap; extend with source_edits.py add_excerpt): on the page the 'Yes, of course' answers the interviewer's question: 'Ku itariki ya 22 Mutarama, ambasaderi wanyu muri Washington yavuze ko u Rwanda rufite « ubufatanye mu mutekano na AFC/M23 », abantu benshi babyumvise nk’aho ingabo z’u Rwanda ziri ku butaka bw'Uburasirazuba bwa RDC. Murabyemera?' (On 22 January your ambassador in Washington said Rwanda has 'security cooperation with AFC/M23', which many understood as Rwandan troops being on eastern DRC soil. Do you agree?). As printed in a Kinyarwanda translation of a French interview; French original not checked. The answer does not say where the 5-20 km is measured from. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension: the interviewer's question that 'Yes, of course' answers (verifier excerpt gap) 2026-10-29: statement edited: interviewer's question restored after the excerpt was extended to carry it (verifier excerpt gap)
src: Paul Kagame: Yego, birumvikana. Ingamba z’ubwirinzi ni ukuvuga kurinda igihugu cyacu n’imipaka yacu ku bidutera akaga, harimo gukoresha ibikoresho bya gisirikare, kohereza ingabo ku butaka cyangwa ibindi. Nta gihabanye. Niba zirinze umupaka wacu kandi bisaba guhangana n’ikibazo kuri kilometero 5, 10 cyangwa 20 inyuma, ni ingamba z’ubwirinzi.
Mu kiganiro cyihariye yahaye Jeune Afrique, Perezida Kagame yabwiye Kinshasa, Washington n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko bagomba gukora inshingano zabo.

Ku itariki ya 22 Mutarama, ambasaderi wanyu muri Washington yavuze ko u Rwanda rufite « ubufatanye mu mutekano na AFC/M23 », abantu benshi babyumvise nk’aho ingabo z’u Rwanda ziri ku butaka bw'Uburasirazuba bwa RDC. Murabyemera? Paul Kagame: Yego, birumvikana.

r7-L-RW-007.s: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that, asked about repeated reports that M23 has violated human rights and forcibly put people into the army since taking Goma in January 2025, Paul Kagame answered that he would accept that allegation if told that Goma has more peace than before M23 went there, and said things are now better than before and that Goma and Bukavu are doing well.
r7-L-RW-007.n: Kagame's answer is a general rejection by comparison; it does not address any specific incident, and no figures are given. The first excerpt is the interviewer's question as printed by the outlet. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.
r7-L-RW-007.vn: Page read; labels printed. Translations faithful. Flag ('President') resolved. A general rejection by comparison; addresses no specific incident. Translation chain as for the other Jeune Afrique claims.
src: Jeune Afrique: Kuva M23 yafata Goma muri Mutarama 2025, kenshi bavuze ko yica uburenganzira bwa muntu kandi igashyira abantu mu gisirikare ku ngufu

Paul Kagame: Nakwemera icyo kirego uramutse umbwiye ko i Goma hari amahoro kurusha mbere y'uko M23 ihajya. Ubu ibintu bimeze neza kuruta mbere. Buri wese ashobora kugereranya: Goma na Bukavu bimeze neza.
Mu kiganiro cyihariye yahaye Jeune Afrique, Perezida Kagame yabwiye Kinshasa, Washington n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko bagomba gukora inshingano zabo.

r7-L-RW-008.s: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame said that M23 is not a Rwandan group but a Congolese group that came to be called AFC/M23, which also includes former president Joseph Kabila.
r7-L-RW-008.n: Kagame's answer to a question on the 2 March 2026 US sanctions. Kagame's claim about Kabila's membership of AFC/M23 is as printed by the outlet; for Kinshasa's contrary framing and the later FRN, see other claims. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.
r7-L-RW-008.vn: Page read; answer is labelled 'Paul Kagame:' and follows the question on the 2 March US sanctions. Translation faithful ('unabarizwamo' = also counts among its members). Flags ('First', 'Rwandan', 'Congolese', 'President') resolved as renderings.
src: Paul Kagame: Mbere na mbere, banza wumve uwo tuvugaho. M23 si umutwe w’u Rwanda, ahubwo ni umutwe w’Abanyekongo waje kwitwa AFC/M23, ukaba unabarizwamo uwahoze ari Perezida Joseph Kabila.
Mu kiganiro cyihariye yahaye Jeune Afrique, Perezida Kagame yabwiye Kinshasa, Washington n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko bagomba gukora inshingano zabo.

r7-L-RW-009.s: Kigali Today's Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview reports that Paul Kagame said that in areas M23 holds it works well in confronting 'these criminals', but in the territories of Masisi, Walikale and elsewhere where FARDC operate, the FDLR are still present in cooperation with the government.
r7-L-RW-009.n: Kagame's allegation about FARDC-FDLR cooperation, with no named unit, date or place beyond the territories; the DRC's contrary position is in other claims. Kigali Today (Rwandan, government-friendly outlet) publishes a Kinyarwanda version of a Jeune Afrique interview; the page says the interview was held 'last month' at Village Urugwiro (so March 2026), and gives its own date of 3 April 2026. The Kinyarwanda is the outlet's rendering; the original French was not fetched. Jeune Afrique's question introduces the 2 March 2026 US sanctions; see the Ijambo.net and BBC claims.
r7-L-RW-009.vn: Narrowed: the excerpt runs together a line that is probably the interviewer's question (mislabelled 'Paul Kagame:' on the page, immediately after another 'Paul Kagame:' answer) with Kagame's answer. Only the answer is kept. Translation of the answer faithful. Flag resolved. On the page the sentence 'Mu gihe guverinoma ya Kongo yagaragaje ubushake bwo guhagarika ibikorwa bya FDLR, ibisubizo bigeze he?' carries a second consecutive 'Paul Kagame:' label but reads as the interviewer's question; it is not credited to Kagame here. An allegation by Kagame with no unit, date or place beyond the territories.
src: Paul Kagame: Mu gihe guverinoma ya Kongo yagaragaje ubushake bwo guhagarika ibikorwa bya FDLR, ibisubizo bigeze he? Mu turere M23 ifite, ikora neza mu guhangana n’aba bagizi ba nabi, ariko mu turere twa Masisi, Walikale n’ahandi FARDC zikora, FDLR ziracyariho mu bufatanye na guverinoma.
Mu kiganiro cyihariye yahaye Jeune Afrique, Perezida Kagame yabwiye Kinshasa, Washington n’umuryango mpuzamahanga ko bagomba gukora inshingano zabo.

r7-L-RW-010.s: Umunota.com (Rwandan outlet) reported that Rwanda's Foreign Minister, Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, said in an RBA interview on the evening of 10 December 2025 that Rwanda is not the one to answer for ceasefire violations, but the FDLR and Burundian troops, who he said have a plan to destabilise Rwanda's security.
r7-L-RW-010.n: Rwandan outlet relaying a state broadcaster (RBA) interview. The article's closing lines say the interview followed AFC/M23's announcement that it had taken Uvira and international pressure on Rwanda, and that Rwanda denies the accusation. Answers r1/UC-BI-FDLR#1 (Rwandan response to the Burundian accusation of 8 December 2025), r2/G-UV-CTRL#0 and r1/UV-2025Q4#2 (Rwanda side).
r7-L-RW-010.vn: Retained page read (byline Raymond Tuyishimire, 11 Dec 2025). Translation faithful ('rubazwa' = is to be held to account). Flags (Minister, Foreign Affairs, Cooperation, Burundian, December) resolved as renderings; 'Ubutwererane' = (International) Cooperation.
src: Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga n’Ubutwererane w’u Rwanda ,Amb Olivier Jean Patrick Nduhungirehe, yatangaje ko u Rwanda atari rwo rubazwa ibyo kwica agahenge ahubwo FDLR n’ingabo z’u Burundi bifite umugambi wo guhungabanya umutekano warwo. Ni mu kiganiro Amb Nduhungirehe yagiranye na RBA ku mugoroba wo kuwa 10 Ukuboza 2025

r7-L-RW-011.s: Umunota.com reported that Foreign Minister Nduhungirehe, in the same RBA interview, said that Burundian soldiers in South Kivu had now reached twenty thousand, a problem he said Rwanda has raised repeatedly, and alleged that they prevent the Banyamulenge from leaving their areas so as to starve them.
r7-L-RW-011.x: Nduhungirehe: Burundian soldiers 'now reached twenty thousand' in South Kivu (no other figure on the page)
r7-L-RW-011.n: Figure and allegation are Nduhungirehe's, as reported; no independent figure for Burundian troop numbers is given on the page. The word 'batangatanze' in the quote could not be translated with confidence and is left untranslated. For other sources on FDNB numbers see the Group of Experts claims already in the file.
r7-L-RW-011.vn: Statement said the troops 'hold' the Banyamulenge areas, which translates the untranslatable 'batangatanze' by guess; narrowed to what the excerpt clearly says ('bakababuza gusohoka kugira ngo babicishe inzara' = preventing them from going out so as to starve them). Translation otherwise faithful; flags resolved as renderings. Figure and allegation are Nduhungirehe's. The verb 'batangatanze' is uncertain (possibly a misspelling); later in the same article he says the troops 'zibasira abanyamurenge, zikabagota, zikabicisha inzara' (attack the Banyamulenge, encircle them, starve them).

A Burundian government statement relayed by a Rwandan outlet, so recorded as 'Burundi says' only; the Burundian original was not fetched. Context for target r1/UC-BI-FDLR#1.

src: Ubwo ku wa mbere w’iki cyumweru, Minisitiri w’Ububanyi n’Amahanga w’u Burundi, Bizimana Edouard , yagiranaga ikiganiro n’abahagarariye ibihugu byabo mu Burundi, yavuze ko u Rwanda rwateye ibirindiro by’ingabo zabo ziri muri RDcongo ndetse ko ngo rufite umugambi wo kubatera bityo bazirwanaho.

r7-L-RW-013.s: Umunota.com reported that Muyaya, in a message posted on X, said that all the attacks launched on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe were launched by M23 together with Rwanda.
r7-L-RW-013.a: Muyaya (named by the outlet by surname only, without title)
r7-L-RW-013.n: The outlet gives no date for Muyaya's post (before the 3 April 2026 article) and does not print his title; The page prints only the surname 'Muyaya'; BBC Gahuza (30 June 2026) identifies Patrick Muyaya as the DRC government spokesperson, and the DRC party attribution here rests on that. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet; the post was not fetched. The page also says Banyamulenge in Minembwe, Fizi, Uvira and Itombwe report attacks by FARDC with Wazalendo, FDLR and Burundian troops, and drone strikes in Minembwe killing civilians and cattle (outlet's own text, not recorded as fact). Answers r1/SKS-2026Q1#0 for Rwanda.
r7-L-RW-013.vn: Actor corrected: the source names only 'Muyaya'; the party attribution 'Government of the DRC (spokesperson)' was inferred from a different page, which the rules forbid. Statement and translation otherwise faithful. Known only through a Rwandan outlet replying to it; Muyaya's post was not fetched and is undated on the page. The page prints only the surname; that this is the DRC government spokesperson is an inference from another source and should be confirmed from the post itself.
src: Ibi Yolande Makolo yabitangaje asubiza ubutumwa Muyaya yanyujije kurubuga rwa X, aho yavuze ko ibitero byose byagabwe ku Banyamulenge muri Minembwe byagabwe na M23 ifatanyije n’u Rwanda.

r7-L-RW-014.n: Makolo's wording is a rhetorical charge and names no specific incident; 'genocide' appears only inside the attributed quotation. Relayed by a Rwandan outlet. Answers r1/SKS-2026Q1#0 (Rwanda on the Minembwe fighting) in part.

src: Makolo yagaragaje ko imvugo za Muyaya ari amayeri yo gushaka kwegeka ibyaha bya FARDC kuri M23. Yagize ati “Gushinja abandi ibyo mukora aho uwakoze ibyaha abyegeka ku wabikorewe. ubusanzwe bikoreshwa mu gushishikariza abantu ubugizi bwa nabi cyangwa Jenoside.

r7-L-RW-016.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that the Rwandan government had not yet said anything publicly about the new EU sanctions (on Generals Ruki Karusisi, Eugène Nkubito and Pascal Muhizi), but that regarding the earlier sanctions by the United Kingdom, America and Canada, Rwandan officials say those sanctions do not help resolve the war in DR Congo and undermine Africa's effort to seek a peaceful solution.

r7-L-RW-016.vn: Page read. r7-L-RW-017.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Oscar Balinda said that gold and coltan mined in the east of the DRC pass through Rwanda but only in transit to foreign markets; that he said the Amnesty report was the same as others published by organisations he said are paid by the Kinshasa government to tarnish the name of AFC/M23, and the outlet wrote that he gave no evidence for this; and that Amnesty said AFC/M23 had not answered its questions, while AFC/M23 denies that Amnesty ever approached it.
r7-L-RW-017.n: Balinda's account of the Amnesty International report (published 21 September 2026 per BBC's '21 Nyakanga (9)', i.e. month 9; the umuryango.rw copy wrongly prints July). No Rwandan government reply to the Amnesty report found; BBC says it sought Kinshasa's comment and got none. Answers r2/G-NKW-MASISI#0 and r2/G-UNDOCS#1 for AFC/M23.

src: Umuvugizi w'umuhari wa AFC/M23, Oscar Balinda, avuga ko inzahabu na coltan bicukurwa mu buseruko bwa Repubulika ya Demokarasi ya Congo bica mu Rwanda ariko ko bihaca gusa biriko birajanwa ku masoko yo hanze.
Yavuze ko ico cegeranyo ari co kimwe n’ibindi bisohorwa n’amashirahamwe Balinda yavuze ko ahembwa na reta y’i Kinshasa kugira acafuze izina rya AFC/M23. Nta cemezo yatanze kuri ivyo yavuze.
Igihe ico cegeranyo cashirwa ahabona, Amnesty yavuze ko AFC/M23 batari bishuye ibibazo yari yababajije mu gukora ico cegeranyo. AFC/M23 yo irahakana ko Amnesty itigeze ibarondera.

r7-L-RW-018.s: A Rwandan broadcaster's website reported that Rwandan Foreign Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe, speaking to AFP in Moscow on 28 October 2026, defended Rwanda against accusations over the conflict in eastern DRC, saying the country should not be blamed for political and security problems that require Congolese solutions; he said Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever, and rejected Kinshasa's description of former Congolese president Joseph Kabila as a Rwandan proxy.
r7-L-RW-018.n: Rwandan outlet summarising an AFP interview; the AFP original was not fetched. Per the page, the Kabila accusation followed his decision to join forces with M23 'earlier in October' (AFP, as cited). Relevant to r1/UV-2026Q4#3 (Rwanda on FRN/Kabila claims, Oct 2026); no Rwandan statement specific to Uvira or the FRN's Uvira claims was found.
r7-L-RW-018.vn: Page read; English, no translation issue. Page credits the interview to AFP ('Speaking to AFP', 'According to AFP'). RadioTV10's summary of an AFP interview; the AFP original was not fetched. The first clause is the outlet's paraphrase.
src: Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe defended Rwanda against accusations over the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, saying the country should not be blamed for political and security problems that require Congolese solutions.

Speaking to AFP on the sidelines of the Russia-Africa Summit in Moscow on October 28, Nduhungirehe described the political and security situation in DR Congo as primarily a Congolese matter. “Rwanda must not be held as a scapegoat for what is happening in Congo forever,” he said.
Nduhungirehe also rejected Kinshasa’s description of former Congolese president Joseph Kabila as a Rwandan proxy.

r7-S2-M23A-001.s: BBC Gahuza reported, citing its Kinshasa correspondent, that the Congolese army (FARDC) confirmed it had carried out strikes on Rubaya centre on Tuesday that 'killed' AFC/M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma.
r7-S2-M23A-001.n: Resolves part of target r1/UC-M23#2: FARDC (not the civilian government) confirmed the strike. The same article says M23 had not yet officially confirmed the death. BBC Gahuza of 1 March 2026 (earlier round) said the government had made no official comment. Article date taken from search result (25 Feb 2026); body says 'Tuesday' (24 Feb 2026).
r7-S2-M23A-001.vn: Verbatim on the BBC Gahuza page, which prints 'Yatangajwe 25 Ukwa kabiri 2026' (25 February 2026); Tuesday = 24 February 2026. The same article says M23 had not officially confirmed Ngoma's death ('Umutwe wa M23 nturemeza kumugaragaro urupfu rwa Willy Ngoma'), while unnamed AFC/M23 insiders said he was killed in a FARDC drone strike.
src: Igisirikare cya DR Congo (FARDC) cyemeje ko cyakoze ibitero muri centre ya Rubaya mu burasirazuba bw'iki gihugu ku wa kabiri "kigahitana" Willy Ngoma umuvugizi w'umutwe wa AFC/M23, nk'uko umunyamakuru wa BBC i Kinshasa abivuga.

r7-S2-M23A-002.s: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka wrote on X at about 5 a.m. on Tuesday that the drone attacks 'fired blindly' at the Rubaya area 'killing innocent civilians', calling it a 'crime against humanity and a war crime'.

src: Gusa mu gitondo ahagana saa kumi n'imwe ku wa kabiri, umuvugizi wa AFC/M23, Lawrence Kanyuka, yanditse ubutumwa ku rubuga X avuga ko ibitero bya 'drones' "byarashe buhumyi" agace ka Rubaya "byica abasivile b'inzirakarengane", abyita "icyaha ku nyoko muntu n'icyaha cy'intambara".

src: Mu itangazo, AFC/M23 yavuze ko “ubugome nk’ubu ku ndege ya gisivile itwaye imfashanyo ari ubunyamaswa budasanzwe” kandi ko byasibye amahirwe yo kugeza ku baturage ibyo bakeneye mu gihe “bamaze imyaka bagoswe batagera ku isoko.”

src: Dans un communiqué, l’ AFC-M23 a accusé les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa d’avoir lancé des attaques simultanées à l’artillerie lourde contre plusieurs zones densément peuplées du territoire de Kalehe, notamment Rumbishi, Chambombo, Cyamatare et Gasovu.

« Ces bombardements ont causé plusieurs pertes en vies humaines et contraint de nombreux civils à fuir leurs habitations, provoquant ainsi de nouveaux déplacements forcés de populations », a déploré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’ AFC-M23.
Pour l’heure, l’armée congolaise n’a pas encore réagi.

src: Des affrontements ont repris ce mardi 31 mars 2026 dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo.
