“Axe Lubero : les villages de Kabesebese et Mutondi sont également sous le feu des attaques, qui se poursuivent activement.

r7-S2-M23A-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23, in a message on X by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accused the FARDC and allied Wazalendo of looting, targeted violence and hate speech in Uvira after the AFC/M23 withdrawal, and said that loyalist forces had also multiplied attacks on its positions in the Fizi highlands and that there had been recent clashes at Kipese (Lubero) and Kasoko (Masisi).
r7-S2-M23A-007.a: FARDC, Mai-Mai Wazalendo, Burundi National Defence Force and unidentified armed elements (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-007.n: Party says. Mentions of Kipese (Lubero) and Kasoko (Masisi) relate to targets r1/NKN-2026H1#1 and r1/NKW-2026H1#1 (January 2026 clashes, AFC/M23 line). Uvira allegations are AFC/M23's and are not established.
r7-S2-M23A-007.vn: Supported by excerpts and page. KMP says the FARDC announced they retook Uvira on Sunday 18 January 2026 after the AFC/M23 withdrawal. The 'after the withdrawal' clause rests on the page, in the conditional ('se serait dégradée'). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo / Mouvement du 23 Mars (AFC/M23) a accusé les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et leurs alliés Wazalendo d’être responsables de pillages, de violences ciblées et de la propagation de discours de haine à Uvira, dans l’est de la RDC.
Dans un message publié sur le réseau social X, son porte-parole, Lawrence Kanyuka, affirme que ces exactions visent particulièrement des civils banyamulenge

L’AFC/M23 affirme également que les forces loyalistes ont multiplié les attaques contre ses positions dans les Hauts-Plateaux de Fizi, en violation du cessez-le-feu, et évoque d’autres affrontements récents à Kipese, dans le territoire de Lubero, ainsi qu’à Kasoko, en territoire de Masisi.
Selon l’AFC/M23, la situation se serait dégradée immédiatement après son retrait d’Uvira.

r7-S2-M23A-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka accused coalition forces of Kinshasa, the FDLR, Wazalendo militias, foreign mercenaries and the Burundian National Defence Force of intensifying operations on several fronts on Sunday 13 September 2026, and said attacks on Walikale territory began around 14:00 against Minjenje and Kibati, with ground and air operations including drones and heavy artillery.
r7-S2-M23A-008.l: Minjenje and Kibati, Walikale, North Kivu; Minembwe area (Mukoko, Rugezi, Point Zéro), South Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-008.a: FARDC coalition, FDLR, Wazalendo, mercenaries and the Burundian National Defence Force (as alleged by AFC-M23)
r7-S2-M23A-008.n: Party says. Gives AFC/M23's own account of Kibati (Walikale) fighting in Sept 2026 for target r1/NKW-2026H2#0; the Minembwe-area villages (Mukoko, Rugezi, Point Zéro) are on the same page and relate to SKS-2026 targets. Article dated 14 Sep 2026 for 'Sunday 13 September 2026'.
r7-S2-M23A-008.vn: Verbatim on the KMP page of 14 Sep 2026.
src: De nouveaux combats ont été signalés dimanche 13 septembre 2026 dans plusieurs zones du Sud-Kivu et du Nord-Kivu entre l’AFC-M23 et l’armée congolaise, alliée aux Wazalendo.

Dans son communiqué, Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23, accuse les forces coalisées de Kinshasa, les FDLR, les milices Wazalendo, des mercenaires étrangers ainsi que la Force de défense nationale du Burundi d’avoir intensifié leurs opérations sur plusieurs fronts.

Dans le territoire de Walikale, au Nord-Kivu, Lawrence Kanyuka affirme que les attaques ont débuté vers 14h00 contre Minjenje et Kibati. Il fait état d’opérations terrestres et aériennes, menées notamment avec des drones et de l’artillerie lourde.

r7-S2-M23A-009.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué, AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the whole of May 2026 was marked by intensified land and air offensives by the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' against densely populated areas and its positions, notably at Minembwe, Masisi, Numbi and Walikale, and that any attack would now receive a proportionate response; the outlet added that other fighting was reported on the Kibati axis, on the border of Walikale and Masisi territories, with AFC-M23 accusing the army of attacking its areas with heavy artillery.
r7-S2-M23A-009.a: FARDC and allies (as alleged by AFC-M23)
r7-S2-M23A-009.n: Party says. AFC/M23 line for target r1/NKW-2026H1#1 (Kibati/Buhimba offensives). The 3 June 2026 Kivu Morning Post article (https://kivumorningpost.com/2026/06/03/nord-kivu-lafc-m23-denonce-des-bombardements-et-des-offensives-contre-des-zones-civiles-a-minembwe/) carries a further AFC-M23 communiqué on repeated strikes on Gakenke, Bidegu and Mikenge (Minembwe highlands) on 2-3 June, citing KT-6 combat drones, and says violent fighting was reported at Kibati and Buhimba; not recorded as a separate claim.
r7-S2-M23A-009.vn: Removed 'on 2 June 2026' from the Kibati clause (no excerpt prints the day; the claim date carries it) and used the excerpt's 'any attack would now' wording. The page also states, in the outlet's own voice, that on Tuesday 2 June 2026 the Congolese army intensified air strikes on Bidegu, Gakenke and Mikenkeh with kamikaze drones and KT-6.
src: Selon Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23, toute attaque recevra désormais une réponse proportionnée et les forces du mouvement éloigneront la menace au-delà de leurs positions de départ.

L’ensemble du mois de mai 2026 a été marqué par une intensification préoccupante des offensives terrestres et aériennes menées par les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa contre des zones densément peuplées ainsi que contre nos positions sur plusieurs axes, notamment à Minembwe, Masisi, Numbi et Walikale”

D’autres combats sont signalés sur l’axe Kibati et dans les zones environnantes, situées à la frontière des territoires de Walikale et de Masisi. L’AFC-M23 accuse l’armée congolaise d’avoir attaqué ses zones en utilisant de l’artillerie lourde.

r7-S2-M23A-010.s: Ijambo reported that AFC/M23 appointed new authorities for North Kivu and Goma city in a statement posted on X by Laurence Kanyuka, AFC/M23 political spokesperson, naming Bahati Musanga Joseph governor of North Kivu, with Manzi Ngarambe Willy as vice-governor for politics, administration and legal affairs.
r7-S2-M23A-010.n: Party says (de facto appointments). The page prints the year '2024' for the statement date, which is a typo: the page itself refers to the capture of Goma 'in recent weeks' and the search result dates the page 6 Feb 2025, so date is given as 2025-02-05. igihe.com (same story, 5 Feb 2025 per search result) could not be fetched by the checker (via=none). Target r1/NKS-2025Q1#7: appointments of governor/vice-governors found; mayor, airport/bank closures and weapons ultimatum not found in this source.
r7-S2-M23A-010.vn: Verbatim on the Ijambo page ('Published: 2025-02-06 08:41:05 CAT'). Rwandan outlet relaying an AFC/M23 appointment: C. The page prints the statement date as '5 Gashyantare 2024', an evident typo: the page is published 2025-02-06 and refers to the capture of Goma in recent weeks. Name discrepancy to note: Ijambo prints the governor as 'Bahati Musanga Joseph', while AP (Jan 2026) has 'Erasto Musanga' and Into Rwanda (Mar 2026) 'Erasto Bahati'; whether these are the same person is not established by this page.
src: Ibyo byatangajwe mu itangazo ryashyizwe kuri X na Laurence Kanyuka, Umuvugizi w’umutwe wa AFC/M23 mu bya politiki, ku itariki 5 Gashyantare 2024.
M23 yagize Bahati Musanga Joseph Guverineri wa Kivu y’Amajyaruguru, aho azungirizwa na Manzi Ngarambe Willy , wagizwe Visi-Guverineri ushinzwe ibijyanye na politiki, ubuyobozi, n’amategeko.

r7-S2-M23A-011.s: BBC Gahuza reported that AFC/M23 said a Human Rights Watch report accusing it of killing at least 140 civilians, mostly Hutu, in the previous month was 'a lie and distortion of the truth', that it had already rejected the allegations as 'unfounded' in a document of 7 August, and that a statement issued by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the HRW and UN allegations were politically motivated and biased towards the 'incapable' Kinshasa government.
r7-S2-M23A-011.l: villages near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru, North Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-011.a: AFC/M23 (reply); HRW and UN allegations attributed to M23 with RDF support
r7-S2-M23A-011.x: HRW (as reported by BBC): at least 140 civilians killed, mostly Hutu
r7-S2-M23A-011.n: Party says (AFC/M23 reply to the HRW report of 20 Aug 2025). This concerns the July 2025 killings in villages near Virunga NP (Rutshuru), i.e. later than the Bwito Bambo/Tongo killings named in the target r1/NKS-2025Q2#0; recorded because it is the AFC/M23 denial on a similar allegation set; the Rwandan government's reply is in the next claim. Page date from the page itself (21 Ukw'umunani 2025 = 21 August 2025).
r7-S2-M23A-011.vn: Verbatim on the BBC page ('Yatangajwe 21 Ukw'umunani 2025'). Fixed originating_source for source 0, which is BBC's summary of the HRW report, not the AFC/M23 document.
src: Raporo ya HRW yatangajwe ku wa gatatu ishinja inyeshyamba za M23 kwica abasivile nibura 140 biganjemo Abahutu mu kwezi gushize
Ariko M23 ivuga ko isanzwe yarahakanye ibi "birego bidafite ishingiro" mu nyandiko yayo yo ku itariki ya 7 y'uku kwezi kwa Kanama (8).

Itangazo rya M23, ryasohowe n'umuvugizi wayo Lawrence Kanyuka, rivuga ko ibi birego bya HRW na ONU bishingiye ku mpamvu za politike, ikanashinja iyi miryango kubogamira ku "butegetsi bw'abadashoboye na busa" bwa Kinshasa.

M23 yanzura ivuga ko iyi raporo ya HRW ari "ikinyoma no kugoreka ukuri", ikaba ari n'"igikoresho cy'icengezamatwara" cy'ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa kigamije "guharabika AFC/M23 irwanira kubohora abantu bayo".

r7-S2-M23A-012.s: BBC Gahuza reported that the Rwandan government said, in a statement given to BBC Newshour, that the RDF has 'nothing to do with' the killings alleged in Human Rights Watch's report, that 'M23 is not controlled by Rwanda' and that M23 should be asked about these matters.
r7-S2-M23A-012.l: villages near Virunga National Park, Rutshuru, North Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-012.n: Rwanda's reply, relevant to the 'Rwanda' party of r1/NKS-2025Q2#0 (listed with Rwanda and AFC/M23). Date computed from 'on Wednesday' and publication date 21 Aug 2025 (Wednesday 20 Aug 2025); date computed from weekday and publication date.
r7-S2-M23A-012.vn: Verbatim; statement given directly to the BBC. Wednesday = 20 August 2025.
src: Mbere, leta y'u Rwanda yahakanye ibyo birego bya ONU, ndetse mu itangazo ku wa gatatu yahaye ikiganiro Newshour cya BBC yavuze ko "RDF nta ho ihuriye" n'ibi bivugwa ko byagezweho mu iperereza rya HRW. Iryo tangazo rigira riti: "M23 ntabwo igenzurwa n'u Rwanda ndetse ibi bibazo bikwiye kuba ari bo [M23] bibazwa."

r7-S2-M23A-013.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, in a communiqué on his X account, accused the FARDC of attacks on its positions and said that at least three civilians were killed and five others injured in a FARDC strike at Kamanyola.
r7-S2-M23A-013.x: AFC/M23: at least 3 civilians killed, 5 injured (Kamanyola)
r7-S2-M23A-013.n: Party says. AFC/M23 account of the Oct-Dec 2025 Kamanyola/Walungu clashes (target r1/SKC-2025H2#1). The same page carries the FARDC 33rd military region account (next claim).
r7-S2-M23A-013.vn: Verbatim. Figure flag '3' is a false positive ('trois' in the excerpt).
src: Dans un communiqué sur son compte X, Lawrence Kanyuka porte parole de l’AFC-M23 a accusé les FARDC d’attaques contre leurs positions. Il a indiqué qu’au moins trois civils ont été tués et 5 autres blessés lors d’une frappe des FARDC à Kamanyola.

r7-S2-M23A-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that the 33rd military region of the FARDC, based at Uvira, said it had stopped attacks by AFC-M23 fighters, and that the region's spokesperson Captain Sylvain Bijanu said these 'enemies of peace' had also attacked its positions at Rugezi and Ngungu (Minembwe), Kaziba (Walungu), Kasika (Mwenga) and Civanga-Hombo (Kalehe).
r7-S2-M23A-014.l: Katogota-Luvungi axis (Uvira); Rugezi and Ngungu (Minembwe, Fizi); Kaziba (Walungu); Kasika (Mwenga); Civanga-Hombo (Kalehe)
r7-S2-M23A-014.n: Kinshasa/FARDC account of the same day's clashes (target r1/SKC-2025H2#1 asks for FARDC on these clashes). Party says.
r7-S2-M23A-014.vn: Removed the day '2 December 2025' (no excerpt prints it; the claim date carries it) and kept the spokesperson's own words 'enemies of peace'. Fighting broke out early on Tuesday 2 December 2025 per the page; the commander, Brig. Gen. Ilunga Kabamba Jean-Jacques, said the AFC-M23 attacked FARDC positions on the Katogota-Luvungi axis.
src: La 33ème région militaire des Forces armées congolaise basée à Uvira a affirmé avoir stopper les attaques des combattants de l’AFC-M23.

“Comme si cela ne suffisait pas, ces ennemis de la paix ont également attaqué nos positions dans les localités de Rugezi et Ngungu à Minembwe dans les hauts plateaux de Fizi, à Kaziba en territoire de Walungu, à Kasika à Mwenga mais également à Civanga-Hombo en territoire de Kalehe”
a renchérit , Le porte-parole de la 33ème région militaire, Le Capitaine Sylvain Bijanu.

r7-S2-M23A-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a statement on X, the AFC/M23 spokesperson said the 'Kinshasa regime, through its coalition forces' launched generalised attacks on several axes targeting civilian populations on Tuesday 7 April 2026, with attacks, per the movement, spreading from 06:50 to Lumbishi, Katale and Tushunguti in Kalehe territory where civilian areas were also hit.
r7-S2-M23A-015.l: Lumbishi, Katale, Tushunguti (Kalehe); Mikenge (Minembwe highlands), South Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-015.a: FARDC and coalition forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-015.n: Party says. AFC/M23's account for the Kalehe fighting of 6-7 April 2026 (target r1/SKN-2026Q2#0); the same page also reports the AFC/M23 statement on drone strikes on Mikenge from 06:45. Fetched page does not carry a FARDC reply. The AFC/M23 capture of Tushunguti is reported by the outlet separately (2026-04-08), already cited elsewhere or not fetched here.
r7-S2-M23A-015.vn: Verbatim on the KMP page of 7 Apr 2026.
src: De nouveaux affrontements ont été signalés mardi 7 avril 2026 dans la matinée entre les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) et les combattants de l’AFC/M23 dans plusieurs villages du Sud-Kivu.
Ces combats touchent Mikenge, sur les hauts plateaux de Minembwe, et plusieurs villages du territoire de Kalehe, selon Lawrence Kanyuka, chef du département de communication de l’AFC/M23.

Dans une déclaration publiée sur son compte X, le porte-parole de l’AFC/M23 affirme que « le régime de Kinshasa, à travers ses forces coalisées, a déclenché des attaques généralisées sur plusieurs axes, visant des populations civiles ».
Le mouvement ajoute que les attaques se sont étendues à partir de 6h50 aux localités de Lumbishi, Katale et Tushunguti, dans le territoire de Kalehe, où des zones civiles ont également été atteintes.

r7-S2-M23A-016.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Monday 24 March 2025 that, contrary to the communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025, the FARDC and their coalition forces had not withdrawn their attack drones from Walikale; he said this delayed the repositioning of AFC/M23 forces in the area and was a major obstacle to respect for the ceasefire.
r7-S2-M23A-016.a: FARDC and coalition forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-016.n: Party says. This is the AFC/M23 allegation named in target r1/NKW-2025H1#3. The same page says that the FARDC had earlier taken note of the withdrawal and pledged to avoid offensive action; no Kinshasa reply to the 24 March allegation appears on this page.
r7-S2-M23A-016.vn: Verbatim on the KMP page of 24 Mar 2025. Discrepancy on the page: the outlet refers to the Congolese army's announcement of 'le samedi précédent' while Kanyuka cites a communiqué of Sunday 23 March 2025. The page also says the FARDC had taken note of the withdrawal and pledged to avoid offensive action.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23, a confirmé cette présence, expliquant qu’elle est due à la présence continue des avions d’attaque des FARDC dans la région

« Contrairement à ce qui avait été indiqué dans le communiqué du dimanche 23 mars 2025, les FARDC et leurs forces coalisées n’ont pas retiré leurs drones d’attaque de Walikale. Cette situation retarde le repositionnement des forces de l’AFC/M23 dans la zone.
Il convient de souligner que cet acte constitue un obstacle majeur au respect du cessez-le-feu et compromet ainsi les initiatives de paix en cours », a déclaré Kanyuka sur X ce lundi 24 mars.

r7-S2-M23A-017.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC/M23, in a communiqué signed by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, accused the Congolese authorities of continuing 'offensive military manoeuvres', citing troop and materiel movements at Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga and Uvira, and said two military ships carrying more than 1 125 fighters of the 'coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime' docked at Uvira on Sunday 10 August from Kalemie.
r7-S2-M23A-017.l: Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga and Uvira (South Kivu / Walikale area)
r7-S2-M23A-017.a: FARDC and coalition forces (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-017.x: AFC/M23: more than 1 125 fighters landed at Uvira
r7-S2-M23A-017.n: Party says; the communiqué's date is 'Monday' before the 12 Aug 2025 page (11 Aug 2025, computed from weekday and publication date). Contextual to the Kalehe/Kabare/Mwenga ceasefire-violation accusations (targets r1/SKN-2025Q3#2, r1/SKC-2025H2#1) but does not name Kasheke or Kamakombe.
r7-S2-M23A-017.vn: Supported; the 'offensive manoeuvres' clause is in the article's opening line on the page. KMP reports the ship landing in the conditional ('auraient accosté'): an AFC/M23 allegation only. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Dans un communiqué signé par son porte-parole, Lawrence Kanyuka, le mouvement politico militaire cite plusieurs zones où auraient été observés « d’importants mouvements de troupes et de matériel militaire » , notamment Nzimbira, Mwenga, Bunyakiri, Kibuwa, Pinga et Uvira. L’AFC/M23 affirme que ces déploiements empruntent différents axes, dont Kindu–Shabunda, Kinshasa–Bujumbura, Kisangani–Walikale et Kalemie–Uvira.
Selon le groupe armé, deux navires militaires transportant plus de 1 125 combattants des « forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa » auraient accosté à Uvira dimanche 10 août en provenance de Kalemie.
L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC/M23) a accusé lundi les autorités congolaises de poursuivre « des manœuvres militaires offensives »

r7-S2-M23A-018.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, in a statement issued by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that around 22:00 on the night of Sunday 24 May 2026 FDLR fighters supported by Wazalendo attacked the villages of Malemo and Kalembe between Masisi and Walikale; Kanyuka said seven civilians were killed and three seriously injured at Malemo, and three killed, nine injured and a village chief abducted at Kalembe, and that the fighters looted 11 cows and many pigs at Bweru.
r7-S2-M23A-018.l: Malemo and Kalembe (and Bweru), between Masisi and Walikale, North Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-018.a: FDLR fighters supported by Wazalendo (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-018.x: AFC/M23: Malemo 7 civilians killed, 3 seriously injured; Kalembe 3 killed, 9 injured, 1 village chief abducted (name not given); Bweru: 11 cows looted
r7-S2-M23A-018.n: Party says (AFC/M23 communiqué relayed by Rwandan outlet Bwiza, which carries the byline Benjamin Babou). Page header date (29 Oct 2026) is the site's current date; the article date is 'Kuwa Mbere, 25 Gicurasi 2026' (Monday 25 May 2026). This is the AFC/M23 account of the Kalembe attack named in target r1/NKW-2026H1#1; no FARDC account on this page. The village chief's name is not given. Clock time: 'saa yine z'ijoro' (Kinyarwanda count, night) is about 22:00.
r7-S2-M23A-018.vn: All figures are printed in words in the excerpts (barindwi=7, batatu=3, icyenda=9); flags are digit/word mismatches. Rwandan outlet relaying a party statement: C. 'saa yine z'ijoro' is the fourth hour of the night count, about 22:00. Page date confirmed from the article itself: 'Kuwa Mbere, 25 Gicurasi 2026' (the 29 Oct 2026 header is the site's current date).
src: AFC/M23 mu itangazo ryasohowe n'umuvugizi wayo, Lawrence Kanyuka, yavuze ko ibyo bitero byabaye mu ijoro ryo ku Cyumweru tariki ya 24 Gicurasi 2026, ahagana saa yine z’ijoro.

Ku wa 24 Gicurasi 2026 ahagana saa yine z’ijoro, itsinda rinini ry’abarwanyi ba FDLR rifashijwe n’imitwe ya Wazalendo ryagabye igitero gikomeye kandi cyateguwe ku midugudu ya Malemo na Kalembe iri hagati ya Masisi na Walikale.

Kanyuka yavuze ko muri Malemo abaturage barindwi bishwe, abandi batatu bagakomereka bikomeye. Muri Kalembe ho yavuze ko abandi bantu batatu bishwe, icyenda bagakomereka, ndetse hakanashimutwa umukuru w’umudugudu.
Nk’uko byatangajwe na Lawrence Kanyuka, mbere yo kuva muri ako gace abo barwanyi banasahuye abaturage bo mu mudugudu wa Bweru, batwara inka 11 n’ingurube nyinshi.

r7-S2-M23A-019.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X on Thursday 10 September 2026 that, from 05:00, forces of the Kinshasa government and the groups supporting them intensified attacks on populated areas on the edges of Masisi and Walikale (Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje, Kibati and surroundings), that at about 07:00 they attacked Buhimba (Masisi) with ground forces using 82 mm mortars and 12.7 mm machine guns, and that aid organisations and their staff had difficulty reaching affected residents.
r7-S2-M23A-019.l: Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje, Kibati, Buhimba, Masisi and Walikale, North Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-019.a: forces of the Kinshasa government and allied groups (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-019.n: Party says (relayed by Rwandan outlet Bwiza; page text is Kinyarwanda with a Swahili-language template). AFC/M23's own account of the September 2026 fighting at Kibati/Buhimba (target r1/NKW-2026H2#0, which asks for AFC/M23's own account of Kibati captures; no Katoy/Humura account found yet). Complements the Kivu Morning Post claim of 13 Sept 2026.
r7-S2-M23A-019.vn: Verbatim; page dated 'Alhamisi, 10 Septemba 2026 saa 09:44' (Thursday). '12,7' printed with a comma. The page writes the times as 'saa 05:00' and 'saa 07:00' in digits; read as clock times (morning), consistent with the article's posting time of 09:44.
src: Lawrence Kanyuka, umuvugizi wa AFC/M23 ushinzwe ibya politiki, ni we watangaje aya makuru kuri X kuri uyu wa Kane tariki ya 10 Nzeri 2026.

Yavuze ko guhera saa 05:00, ingabo za Leta ya Kinshasa n’imitwe izifasha urugamba bakajije ibitero ku bice bituwe cyane biri ku nkengero za Masisi na Walikale. Mu duce yagaragaje harimo Ihula, Malemo, Minjenje, Kibati no mu nkengero zatwo.

Kanyuka kandi yavuze ko ahagana saa 07:00, izo ngabo zagabye igitero kuri Buhimba no mu nkengero zayo, muri Teritwari ya Masisi. Yavuze ko icyo gitero cyari kiyobowe n’ingabo zo ku butaka, zifashishije za mortier za milimetero 82 ndetse n’imbunda za mitrailleuse za milimetero 12,7.
Kanyuka yavuze ko imiryango itanga ubutabazi n’abakozi bayo bafite ingorane zo kugera ku baturage bugarijwe n’ingaruka z’imirwano, kubera umutekano muke uri mu bice byibasiwe.

r7-S2-M23A-020.s: Bwiza reported, citing reliable information reaching it, that AFC/M23 fighters regained control of Remeka in Masisi territory after a commando operation on the night of Wednesday 23 September 2026, and that the capture was also confirmed by Ngarambe Manzi Willy, whom the outlet calls the Deputy Governor of North Kivu Province, in a message on X.
r7-S2-M23A-020.a: AFC/M23 (as reported by Bwiza); de facto deputy governor Ngarambe Manzi Willy
r7-S2-M23A-020.n: Party says (Rwandan outlet Bwiza, 'reliable information reaching BWIZA'). De facto AFC/M23 administration official confirms retaking of Remeka after the FARDC/Wazalendo/FDLR/Burundian capture of 15-16 September 2026, per the same page (which cites Actualite.cd and Critical Threats; those are not used here). Gives AFC/M23's own account for the Remeka element of target r1/NKW-2026H2#0. Article dated Thursday 24 September 2026 (page header); the excerpt gives the commando operation on the night of 23 September.
r7-S2-M23A-020.vn: Attributed the capture to the outlet's unnamed information and the 'Deputy Governor' title to the outlet, since he is an AFC/M23-appointed official, not Kinshasa's. Ngarambe Manzi Willy holds the post under the AFC/M23 administration (Ijambo, Feb 2025, reports his appointment by M23 as vice-governor). Rwandan outlet; capture not independently confirmed here. Page dated Thursday 24 September 2026. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Abarwanyi ba AFC/M23 bongeye kugenzura agace ka Remeka gaherereye muri Teritwari ya Masisi, nyuma ya Operasiyo ya gikomando yakozwe n’abarwanyi b’uyu mutwe mu ijoro ryo ku wa Gatatu tariki ya 23 Nzeri 2026.
Ifatwa ryako kandi ryanemejwe na Guverineri wungirije w'Intara ya Kivu y'Amajyaruguru, Ngarambe Manzi Willy, mu butumwa yanyujije ku rubuga rwe rwa X.
Amakuru yizewe agera kuri BWIZA avuga ko muri iryo joro abakomando ba AFC/M23 bagabye igitero

r7-S2-M23A-021.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, through spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that an attack at 18:30 on Sunday 29 March, when the coalition of DRC government forces entered the densely populated centre of Shanji, killed people it named as Shadai Ndagije, Bisengi Mpenze, Gitinywa Etienne, Gashimye Hitimana, Daniel Hategeka, Ndayambaje Muhire and Iradukunda Nsanzumuhire, and injured more than 20 others.
r7-S2-M23A-021.a: coalition of forces fighting on the side of the DRC government (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-021.n: Party says (AFC/M23 statement relayed by Rwandan outlet Bwiza, byline Benjamin Babou, article dated Monday 30 March 2026). This is the AFC/M23 direct statement on the Shanje incident of 29-30 March 2026 sought by target r1/SKN-2026Q1#1. Names are as printed by the page and as AFC/M23 gave them; being named is not a finding of individual responsibility. The same page carries AFC/M23's allegation of kamikaze drone attacks on Gakenke and Mikenke (Minembwe) on 29-30 March. No FARDC or Wazalendo reply on this page.
r7-S2-M23A-021.vn: Removed the number 'seven' (printed only in the outlet's lead, not in an excerpt) and the spelling 'Shanje'; the names and 'more than 20' are verbatim. The outlet's lead gives the toll as seven ('Abantu barindwi'); the excerpt lists seven names. Spelling on the page is 'Shanji' (Shanje in other sources), Kalehe territory. Page dated Monday 30 March 2026.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 biciye mu muvugizi wawo, Lawrence Kanyuka, watangaje ko igitero cyiciwemo bariya bantu cyabaye ku Cyumweru tariki ya 29 Werurwe saa 18:30, ubwo ihuriro ry'ingabo za Leta ya RDC zacengeraga muri Centre ituwe n'abaturage benshi ya Shanji.

Abishwe nk'uko AFC/M23 ibivuga, barimo Shadai Ndagije, Bisengi Mpenze, Gitinywa Etienne, Gashimye Hitimana, Daniel Hategeka, Ndayambaje Muhire na Iradukunda Nsanzumuhire. Igitero cyiciwemo aba bantu kandi cyanakomerekeyemo abandi barenga 20 nk'uko uriya mutwe ubivuga.

r7-S2-M23A-022.s: Bwiza reported that, since Monday 23 March, AFC/M23 had started withdrawing troops from areas it controlled in Lubero territory, including Kipese, Munyakondomi, Ivatama, Ilambula, Luseke and Musimba, and that information from inside AFC/M23 said the group took the decision to pull out of areas it had controlled for more than a year as a confidence-building measure toward resolving the conflict peacefully.
r7-S2-M23A-022.l: Kipese, Munyakondomi, Ivatama, Ilambula, Luseke, Musimba (Lubero), North Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-022.n: Rwandan outlet Bwiza (article dated Wednesday 25 March 2026); the withdrawal date is the page's 'Monday 23 March'. No on-the-record AFC/M23 communiqué on the withdrawal was found on this page: the stated reason comes from unnamed sources inside AFC/M23. Relates to target r1/NKN-2026H1#1 (late-March 2026 withdrawal from Kipese/Lunyasenge).
r7-S2-M23A-022.vn: Verbatim on Bwiza (Wednesday 25 March 2026). Rwandan outlet and unnamed party sources: C. Discrepancy to surface: five days later (Into Rwanda, 30 March 2026) the AFC/M23-appointed North Kivu governor called the movements a routine troop rotation and dismissed reports of a pull-back. Bwiza adds the group kept troops only at Katondi.
src: Umutwe wa AFC/M23 kuva ku wa Mbere tariki ya 23 Werurwe, watangiye kuvana ingabo zawo mu bice bitandukanye wagenzuraga byo muri Teritwari ya Lubero, mu ntara ya Kivu y'Amajyaruguru.
Uduce byamenyekanye ko uriya mutwe wamaze kuvanamo ingabo turimo Kipese, Munyakondomi, Ivatama, Ilambula, Luseke na Musimba.

Amakuru aturuka imbere muri AFC/M23, avuga ko uriya mutwe wafashe icyemezo cyo kuvana ingabo zawo muri turiya duce wari umaze umwaka urenga ugenzura, nk'ingamba irema icyizere cy'uko ugishyize imbere "gukemuka amakimbirane yo mu burasirazuba bwa Congo Kinshasa mu mahoro".

r7-S2-M23A-023.s: Bwiza reported that AFC/M23, in a statement by spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, said that on Sunday 28 June 2026 at around 01:00 the coalition of forces of the Kinshasa government burned many civilian houses at Lumbishi (Kalehe) after organised looting, and that entire families perished in the fire.
r7-S2-M23A-023.a: coalition of forces of the Kinshasa government (as alleged by AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-023.x: No toll given: 'entire families perished in the fire' (AFC/M23)
r7-S2-M23A-023.n: Party says; AFC/M23 allegation of burning and looting by Kinshasa-aligned forces; relayed by Rwandan outlet Bwiza (byline Denis Nsengiyumva; article Monday 29 June 2026). Not established; no FARDC reply on the page. Related to the AFC/M23 account of Kalehe (targets r1/SKN-2026Q2#0 and r1/SKN-2026Q3#2). Quote punctuation in source E2 is as printed.
r7-S2-M23A-023.vn: Verbatim. The hedge 'ngo' in source 0 is carried by 'According to' in the excerpt_en and by the statement's attribution. AFC/M23 allegation; no toll and no FARDC reply on the page. Page dated Monday 29 June 2026.
src: Nk'uko byatangajwe na AFC/M23 mu itangazo ry'Umuvugizi Lawrence Kanyuka, ngo ni igitero cyateguwe kandi gikoranwa ubugome ndengakamere.

Kuri iki Cyumweru, itariki ya 28 Kamena 2026, ahagana mu ma saa 1h00 ', ihuriro ry’ingabo z’ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa zatwitse amazu menshi y’abasivili i Lumbishi nyuma yo kwishora mu busahuzi bwakozwe mu buryo bwateguwe."
Imiryango yose yatikiriye mu muriro muri iki gitero cyakoranwe ubugome burengeje urugero".

r7-S2-M23A-024.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, in a communiqué published on Tuesday 25 February 2025, AFC/M23 said that several villages of Minembwe, notably Irundu and Nyarujoka, were bombed that day, and alerted to a rise in persecution of the Banyamulenge community in Uvira city, which it said took the form of arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances and other repression; the outlet added that the Congolese authorities had not officially reacted to the accusations.
r7-S2-M23A-024.l: Irundu and Nyarujoka (Minembwe highlands); Uvira (city), South Kivu
r7-S2-M23A-024.a: not attributed in the excerpts (AFC/M23 alleges bombardment and persecution by the authorities)
r7-S2-M23A-024.n: Party says (AFC/M23 communiqué of 25 Feb 2025 relayed by Kivu Morning Post, page dated 26 Feb 2025). Gives AFC/M23's line on Minembwe in the days around the Twirwaneho takeover (target r1/SKS-2025Q1#0, which asks for Kinshasa/FARDC on the Twirwaneho capture of Minembwe/Mikenge and lists AFC/M23 as the party searched). The Kinshasa non-reaction is the outlet's statement, not a search finding.
r7-S2-M23A-024.vn: All clauses on the KMP page of 26 Feb 2025 ('that day' from the communiqué quote on the page). 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Dans un communiqué publié ce mardi 25 février 2025, l’AFC/M23 affirme que plusieurs villages de Minembwe, notamment Irundu et Nyarujoka, ont été la cible de bombardements.

En parallèle, le M23 alerte sur une recrudescence des persécutions contre la communauté Banyamulenge dans la ville d’Uvira. Elle affirme que ces actes se traduisent par des arrestations arbitraires, des disparitions forcées et d’autres formes de répression.
Jusqu’à présent, les autorités congolaises n’ont pas officiellement réagi à ces accusations.
« Le 25 février 2025, plusieurs villages de Minembwe, notamment Irundu et Nyarujoka, ont été bombardés

r7-S2-M23A-025.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 said on Sunday 11 October 2026 that the Congolese armed forces and their allies had intensified offensives against civilians in North and South Kivu, and that, according to spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, at 06:15 those forces intensified ground offensives towards Kuwihene on the Rugezi axis in the Minembwe region, with FDLR elements on the front line alongside foreign mercenaries, causing deaths and mass displacement of civilians.
r7-S2-M23A-025.l: Kuwihene, Rugezi axis, Minembwe region (South Kivu); Kacyayi, Kumungoti and Marangara (Masisi, North Kivu)
r7-S2-M23A-025.a: Congolese armed forces and allies, with FDLR elements and foreign mercenaries (as alleged by AFC-M23)
r7-S2-M23A-025.n: Party says. AFC/M23 line for target r1/SKS-2026Q4#0 (Oct 2026 Minembwe/Fizi fighting; the target's 11 Oct drone allegation south of Minembwe and Rwanda/Burundi reactions are not addressed here) and general Oct 2026 context for the North Kivu targets (Masisi villages Kacyayi, Kumungoti, Marangara). The page says FARDC, allied to the Burundian army and Wazalendo, had intensified attacks for over a month (outlet's own text).
r7-S2-M23A-025.vn: Verbatim on the KMP page of 12 Oct 2026.
src: L’Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC-M23) a déploré, dimanche 11 octobre 2026, des attaques généralisées des Forces armées congolaises et de leurs alliés, les accusant d’avoir intensifié les offensives contre les civils dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et du Sud-Kivu.

« Le même dimanche, à 6 h 15, ces forces ont intensifié leurs offensives terrestres en direction de Kuwihene et de ses environs, sur l’axe de Rugezi, dans la région de Minembwe, en déployant en première ligne des éléments des FDLR, aux côtés de mercenaires étrangers.

Ces attaques, menées au moyen d’assauts terrestres et de tirs d’armes lourdes, entraînent des pertes en vies humaines et provoquent des déplacements massifs de populations civiles », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23.

r7-S2-M23A-026.s: Radio Okapi reported that, in a communiqué published on 26 July 2025, FARDC spokesperson Maj. Gen. Sylvain Ekenge called 'unfounded' the MRDP-Twirwaneho claims that FDLR elements trained in Burundi had infiltrated to commit targeted massacres of Banyamulenge, described them as an attempt at manipulation, and said the FARDC held verified information on a planned massacre at Minembwe involving Twirwaneho in collaboration with Red Tabara.
r7-S2-M23A-026.a: FARDC (statement); MRDP-Twirwaneho and Red Tabara (alleged by FARDC)
r7-S2-M23A-026.n: Party says (FARDC communiqué as reported by Radio Okapi). Adjacent to target r1/SKS-2025Q3#0 (it answers Twirwaneho's 25 July infiltration alert, not the 9 July air-strike allegation; KMP of 9 July 2025, already cited elsewhere, says the government had not reacted to that). Burundi's government is not quoted. Statement context from the same page: Twirwaneho alleged FDLR elements trained and equipped in Burundi.
r7-S2-M23A-026.vn: Verbatim on Radio Okapi (27 Jul 2025). excerpt_en for source 0 dropped the conditional 'auraient infiltré'; correction supplied. Radio Okapi adds that, per the communiqué, the plan would aim to provoke an international outcry and blame the Congolese and Burundian governments. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (S2-M23A claim 25)
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont fermement rejeté les accusations du groupe armé MRDP-Twirwaneho, actif dans les Hauts plateaux de Fizi, qui affirme que des éléments des FDLR formés au Burundi auraient infiltré le pays pour commettre des massacres ciblés contre les populations banyamulenge.

Dans un communiqué publié le 26 juillet, le général-major Sylvain Ekenge, porte-parole des FARDC, qualifie ces allégations de « non fondées » et les considère comme une tentative de manipulation visant à déstabiliser l’opinion publique et à saboter les efforts de paix en cours, notamment ceux des processus de Washington et de Doha.

A l’inverse, les FARDC affirment détenir des informations vérifiées sur un projet de massacre planifié à Minembwe (Sud-Kivu), impliquant le groupe Twirwaneho en collaboration avec Red Tabara, un autre groupe armé actif dans la région.

r7-S2-M23A-027.s: Bwiza reported that M23 rebels took control of Katogota, about 80 km north of Uvira, on the Thursday before publication, and that M23 had so far neither confirmed nor denied its presence there, while videos circulating on social media showed armed men claiming to belong to M23 in the area.
r7-S2-M23A-027.n: Rwandan outlet Bwiza (byline Fred Karege, Friday 9 May 2025). Documents that, as of 9 May 2025, AFC/M23 had made no statement on Katogota (target r1/SKS-2025Q2#0 asks for AFC-M23 on Rugezi/Katogota). Date computed from weekday and publication date. The Rugezi fighting (Wazalendo Biloze Bishambuke group vs Twirwaneho) is outlet text. Used mainly as evidence of non-statement; the capture is by M23 per the outlet.
r7-S2-M23A-027.vn: Verbatim; the video clause is on the page just after the excerpt. Rwandan outlet: C. Page dated 'Vendredi 9 mai 2025'; the Thursday is 8 May 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Ces violences surviennent alors que, jeudi , les rebelles du M23 ont pris le contrôle de Katogota , une localité située à environ 80 km au nord de la ville d'Uvira . Jusqu’à présent, le M23 n’a ni confirmé ni démenti sa présence à Katogota
mais des vidéos circulant sur les réseaux sociaux depuis jeudi montrent des hommes armés affirmant appartenir au M23 dans cette zone.

r7-S2-M23B-001.s: The Associated Press reported that M23 claimed that the attack of 2 January in the Masisi territory, which it said targeted its military positions, was carried out by the FARDC and their allies, and that the rebel group said all the victims are civilians, a claim questioned by at least one expert.
r7-S2-M23B-001.l: Masisi territory (Masisi), North Kivu; symbolic burial held at the Unity Stadium, Goma
r7-S2-M23B-001.a: M23 (AFC/M23 administration); attack attributed by M23 to the FARDC and their allies
r7-S2-M23B-001.n: AP copy on thecanadianpressnews.ca; apnews.com original could not be fetched by the helper. Page says 'The FARDC has not commented on the attack' (supports Kinshasa-silence gap for G-RESP#5). Date is the funeral date (Thursday 8 January 2026), attack 2 January. War Child is not named on this page.
r7-S2-M23B-001.vn: Page (AP copy, byline Ruth Alonga, The Associated Press, Jan 8, 2026) supports all clauses. Removed the year '2026' from the strike date because the excerpt prints only 'Jan. 2'; the claim date carries the year. AP adds that the FARDC had not commented on the attack, and that Ebuteli researcher Stewart Muhindo called the figure of 22 civilians killed 'greatly exaggerated'.
src: M23 claimed that the attack, which targeted their military positions in the Masisi territory on Jan. 2, was carried out by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and their allies. The rebel group said all the victims are civilians, a claim questioned by at least one expert

r7-S2-M23B-002.s: The Associated Press reported that the administrator of the Masisi territory, Emmanuel Ndizeye, said at the ceremony that the area had been hit by 'a series of bombings', and that the bodies transferred to Goma came only from areas accessible by road.
r7-S2-M23B-002.l: Goma (Unity Stadium), North Kivu; strikes in Masisi territory
r7-S2-M23B-002.a: Masisi territory administrator (speaking at an M23 ceremony)
r7-S2-M23B-002.n: Party statement relayed by AP. The page does not label Ndizeye's affiliation in that sentence; it says the ceremony was held in the presence of M23 administration officials.
r7-S2-M23B-002.vn: Verbatim on the AP page; party-side official speaking at an M23 ceremony. AP does not state who appointed Ndizeye; the ceremony was held in the presence of M23 administration officials.
src: The administrator of the Masisi territory, Emmanuel Ndizeye, said during the ceremony that the area had been hit by “a series of bombings.” He specified that the bodies transferred to Goma came only from areas accessible by road.

r7-S2-M23B-003.s: The Associated Press reported that Erasto Musanga, named as the governor of North Kivu by the M23 administration, accused President Félix Tshisekedi of being responsible for the violence, saying 'Even as we speak, Tshisekedi is killing more people', and threatened legal action through the M23's own justice system.
r7-S2-M23B-003.vn: Verbatim on the AP page. Party statement.
src: Erasto Musanga, named as the governor of North Kivu by the M23 administration, accused Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi of being responsible for the violence. “Even as we speak, Tshisekedi is killing more people,” he said, threatening legal action through the M23's own justice system.

r7-S2-M23B-004.s: The Associated Press reported that Patrick Muyaya, the spokesperson for the Congolese government, said in a post on X that the funeral held on Thursday was 'the height of indecency and inhumanity'.
r7-S2-M23B-004.l: Goma, North Kivu (statement made in Kinshasa)
r7-S2-M23B-004.n: Kinshasa reply, found incidentally while searching for the AFC/M23 account; it replies to the funeral, not the strike itself. Date computed from 'Thursday' and publication date 8 Jan 2026.
r7-S2-M23B-004.vn: Supported; reworded 'the M23's funeral' to 'the funeral held on Thursday' to clear the figure flag ('23' from 'M23' not printed in the excerpt). AP also quotes Muyaya blaming Rwanda and the M23 for the crimes; the funeral was the M23's ceremony of 8 January 2026 in Goma.
src: Patrick Muyaya, the spokesperson for the Congolese government, said in a post on X that Thursday's funeral was “the height of indecency and inhumanity.”

r7-S2-M23B-005.s: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that in the night of 21 to 22 October 2026 the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime intensified their bombardments of the densely populated zone of Rugezi, in the Minembwe region, using kamikaze drones and heavy artillery fire, and that the bombardments were continuing.
r7-S2-M23B-005.l: Rugezi, Minembwe region, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-005.a: FRN (the former AFC/M23) accusing 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa'
r7-S2-M23B-005.n: Primary post from the FRN spokesperson's X account (the page header gives his title). FRN is the coalition announced 12 Oct 2026 replacing AFC/M23 as Kabila-led front; the project already holds KMP's relay of the same communiqué (r1-ST-DRC-2026-009/-010). Party account, not established fact; no independent confirmation of the strike on this page.
r7-S2-M23B-005.vn: Verbatim in the retained X post (9:19 AM, Oct 22, 2026); the account's bio names Kanyuka as FRN spokesperson. Same origin as the existing KMP relay, so not independent of it. FRN (formerly AFC/M23) allegation; not independently confirmed.
src: Dans la nuit du 21 au 22 octobre 2026, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont intensifié leurs bombardements contre la zone densément peuplée de Rugezi, dans la région de Minembwe. Ces attaques ont été menées au moyen de drones kamikaze et de tirs a l'artillerie lourde. Les bombardements se poursuivent à l’heure actuelle.

r7-S2-M23B-006.s: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that the Kinshasa regime had entered a decisive phase of its military preparations and was preparing a large-scale offensive mobilising land forces, air assets and heavy artillery simultaneously, reinforcing troops and military equipment at Luvungi and Lubarika.
r7-S2-M23B-006.l: Luvungi, Lubarika and the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-006.a: FRN accusing the Kinshasa regime and Burundian troops
r7-S2-M23B-006.n: Same post as the Rugezi claim. FRN allegation; no independent confirmation on this page. Existing KMP relay: r1-ST-DRC-2026-009/-010.
r7-S2-M23B-006.vn: Verbatim in the retained X post. FRN allegation.
src: Le régime de Kinshasa est entre dans une phase décisive de ses préparatifs militaires et se prépare à déclencher une offensive de grande envergure mobilisant simultanément des forces terrestres, des moyens aériens et de l’artillerie lourde. Il renforce des troupes et des équipements militaires à Luvungi et à Lubarika.

r7-S2-M23B-007.s: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that there were movements of Burundian troops crossing the Ruzizi river towards the Ruzizi plain, joining other elements gathered at the established headquarters, and that foreign mercenaries were also part of the military set-up.
r7-S2-M23B-007.l: Luvungi, Lubarika and the Ruzizi plain, Uvira territory, South Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-007.a: FRN alleging Burundian troops and 'mercenaires étrangers' on the Kinshasa side
r7-S2-M23B-007.n: Same post as the Rugezi claim; the sentence begins 'Parallèlement, des mouvements de troupes Burundaises…' (verb missing in the original). FRN allegation only; Burundi's government reply not found (see gap UV-2026Q4#3/ST-DRC-2026#0 notes).
r7-S2-M23B-007.vn: Verbatim in the retained X post. excerpt_en flag is a false positive (sentence-initial 'Foreign'); the translation matches the excerpt.
src: des mouvements de troupes Burundaises franchissant la rivière Ruzizi en direction de la plaine de la Ruzizi. Ces troupes rejoignent d’autres éléments regroupés au quartier général établi. Les mercenaires étrangers font aussi partie de ce dispositif militaire.

r7-S2-M23B-008.s: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in a post on his X account that Brigadier General François Kamanzi, commander of operations of the 12th military region in Kongo-Central, had joined the 'Lions de Sarambwe' within the Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC), having chosen to break with the Kinshasa regime whose daily attacks, the post says, deliberately target civilian populations.
r7-S2-M23B-008.l: 12th military region, Kongo-Central (statement issued by FRN in eastern DRC)
r7-S2-M23B-008.a: FRN / ARC ('Lions de Sarambwe'); FARDC officer François Kamanzi
r7-S2-M23B-008.n: Primary post (time 5:31 PM, Oct 27, 2026 as shown on the page). Party announcement of a defection, not confirmed by FARDC on this page. Existing relays: r1-UV-2026Q4-034 (BBC Gahuza), r3-G-CTR-010, r1-UCD-M23-COMMAND-022.
r7-S2-M23B-008.vn: Verbatim in the retained X post (5:31 PM, Oct 27, 2026). excerpt_en flag: capitalisation of a translated title only; translation is faithful. FRN announcement of a defection; no FARDC confirmation found.
src: Nous confirmons qu’à ce jour, le général de brigade François KAMANZI, commandant des opérations de la 12ᵉ Région militaire au Kongo-Central, a rejoint les rangs des Lions de Sarambwe, au sein de l’Armée révolutionnaire congolaise (ARC). Ce haut gradé a choisi de rompre avec le régime de Kinshasa, dont les attaques quotidiennes prennent délibérément pour cible les populations civiles.

r7-S2-M23B-009.s: FRN spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said in the same post that two other officers had also joined the FRN's ranks, that their identities would be made public in the coming days, and encouraged other FARDC members and all Congolese to join the FRN.
r7-S2-M23B-009.l: statement issued by FRN in eastern DRC
r7-S2-M23B-009.n: Same post as previous claim. Party assertion; no FARDC reply on this page.
r7-S2-M23B-009.vn: Verbatim in the retained X post.
ent: Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)
src: nous annonçons que deux autres officiers ont également rejoint nos rangs. Leurs identités seront rendues publiques dans les prochains jours. Nous encourageons les autres membres des FARDC, ainsi que l’ensemble des Congolais, à rejoindre le Front pour la Refondation de la Nation (FRN)

r7-S2-M23B-010.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said on X that the movement strongly rejects the Human Rights Watch report as 'very biased' (ibogamye cyane), selective, containing untruths and not matching realities on the ground.
r7-S2-M23B-010.l: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
r7-S2-M23B-010.a: AFC/M23 (spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka) replying to Human Rights Watch
r7-S2-M23B-010.n: Party reply relayed by BBC Gahuza; the X post itself (x.com/LawrenceKanyuka/status/2066897082070253961, search snippet titled 'RESPONSE OF THE ALLIANCE FLEUVE CONGO-MOUVEMENT DU 23 MARS (AFC-M23) TO THE HUMAN RIGHTS WATCH REPORT') failed to load in the helper, so only the BBC relay is cited. The page's date is 'Yatangajwe 10 Ukwa gatandatu 2026'. Not previously in the project (the Rwanda reply is r3-G-RESP-005).
r7-S2-M23B-010.vn: Verbatim on the BBC Gahuza page, published 'Yatangajwe 10 Ukwa gatandatu 2026' (10 June 2026). The 'HRW report' is the report the article is about ('Raporo nshya ya HRW' in the title). Party statement relayed by BBC.
src: Umuvugizi wa M23 Lawrence Kanyuka yatangaje ku rubuga nkoranyambaga rwa X ko uyu mutwe wamaganye ukomeje iyo raporo "ibogamye cyane", "ihitamo bamwe, irimo ibitari ukuri kandi idahuye n'ukuri kw'ibibera ku rubuga".

r7-S2-M23B-011.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Kanyuka added that the HRW report again focuses almost entirely on AFC/M23 while greatly downplaying or ignoring the very serious abuses committed by the combined forces of the Kinshasa regime, and that this approach raises serious questions about the neutrality and credibility of its conclusions.
r7-S2-M23B-011.l: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
r7-S2-M23B-011.a: AFC/M23 (spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka) replying to Human Rights Watch
r7-S2-M23B-011.n: Same BBC Gahuza page. Party reply.
r7-S2-M23B-011.vn: Verbatim on the BBC Gahuza page; translation faithful.
src: Yongeyeho ati: "Ku yindi nshuro, uyu muryango uribanda hafi ya hose kuri AFC/M23, mu gihe ugabanya cyane cyangwa wirengagiza amahonyora akomeye cyane akorwa n'ingabo zishyize hamwe z'ubutegetsi bwa Kinshasa." Kanyuka avuga ko ubwo buryo bw'imikorere bwa HRW butera kwibaza "ibibazo bikomeye ku kutabogama no ku kwizerwa kw'imyanzuro yayo" muri iyo raporo.

r7-S2-M23B-012.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that M23 firmly denies 'these allegations', which in the article refer to the abduction of young men and boys and their military training, and that Kanyuka said its mobilisation activities are carried out openly, without hiding them, and 'voluntarily'.
r7-S2-M23B-012.l: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
r7-S2-M23B-012.n: 'Ibi birego' (these allegations) refers back to the preceding sentence of the BBC article (HRW says M23 abducted young men and boys from homes, schools and churches, subjected them to propaganda and gave them military training). The excerpt cannot include that sentence within the 60-word limit.
r7-S2-M23B-012.vn: Replaced the editorial parenthesis with a plain clause tied to the page's preceding sentence; otherwise supported. The article attributes the abduction finding to HRW ('HRW ivuga ko...'); the clause on what 'these allegations' refers to rests on the preceding sentence of the page, not the stored excerpt. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: M23 ihakana ibi birego yivuye inyuma ndetse Kanyuka yavuze ko ibikorwa by'ubukangurambaga byayo ibikorera ku mugaragaro nta kubihisha kandi ko ubwo bukangurambaga bukorwa "ku bushake".
umutwe wa M23 waguye ibikorwa ukajya ushimuta abasore n'abahungu ubakuye mu ngo, mu mashuri no mu nsengero, ukabakorera icengezamatwara ndetse ukabaha imyitozo ya gisirikare.

r7-S2-M23B-013.s: BBC News Gahuza reported that Rwanda's foreign minister Olivier Nduhungirehe replied to BBC Gahuzamiryango by WhatsApp that the Rwandan government does not respond to HRW reports of this kind, saying 'Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW.' (Nothing. We never respond to HRW.)
r7-S2-M23B-013.l: eastern DRC (HRW report covering Rumangabo and Tshanzu camps); statement published via X
r7-S2-M23B-013.a: Government of Rwanda replying to Human Rights Watch
r7-S2-M23B-013.n: Rwandan reply found incidentally; the Rwandan government later published a written response (r3-G-RESP-005, ogs.gov.rw), so 'does not respond' was not its final position. Date: article date 10 June 2026.
r7-S2-M23B-013.vn: Direct reply to the BBC, verbatim on the page. Grade B: a credible outlet's own exchange establishes that the statement was made; content is Rwanda's position only. The Rwandan government later published a written response to the report (held in the project as r3-G-RESP-005), so this was not its final position.
src: Minisitiri w'ububanyi n'amahanga w'u Rwanda Olivier Nduhungirehe yasubije BBC Gahuzamiryango mu butumwa bwo kuri WhatsApp ko leta y'u Rwanda idasubiza kuri raporo nk'izi za HRW. Yagize ati: "Ntacyo. Ntitujya dusubiza HRW."

r7-S2-M23B-014.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that AFC-M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said that from 14:00 on Thursday 10 September 2026 until late at night the coalition forces of the Kinshasa regime continued indiscriminate bombardments with kamikaze drones against Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma in the Minembwe region.
r7-S2-M23B-014.l: Point-Zéro and Nyamabuguma, Minembwe region, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-014.a: AFC-M23 accusing 'les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa'
r7-S2-M23B-014.n: Party statement; KMP article dated 11 Sep 2026 (the opening lines say bombardments of the army were reported 'ce matin, vendredi 11 septembre 2026'). The article also says Kanyuka characterised the strikes with legal labels; not repeated here. No casualty figure.
r7-S2-M23B-014.vn: Verbatim on the KMP page (byline La Rédaction; 'ce matin, vendredi 11 septembre 2026'). Party allegation; legal labels on the page not repeated.
src: « Depuis 14h00 hier, jeudi 10 septembre 2026, et jusqu’à tard dans la nuit, les forces coalisées du régime de Kinshasa ont poursuivi leurs bombardements indiscriminés contre Point-Zéro et Nyamabuguma, dans la région de Minembwe, au moyen de drones kamikazes », a déclaré Lawrence Kanyuka, porte-parole de l’AFC-M23.

r7-S2-M23B-015.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to Twirwaneho spokesperson colonel Fidèle Rugabo, two battalions, 'dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises' (the wording is ambiguous: including that of the Hiboux and of Burundian forces), had been deployed on the Rurambo axis, and that on the Bijombo axis four battalions of the FARDC and of the Burundian army, with elements of the P5 and Wazalendo, were visible towards Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati and Kajoka.
r7-S2-M23B-015.l: Rurambo and Bijombo axes (Kirungwa, Munanira, Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati, Kajoka), Uvira/Fizi highlands, South Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-015.a: Twirwaneho (spokesperson Fidèle Rugabo) alleging FARDC, Burundian army, P5 and Wazalendo deployments
r7-S2-M23B-015.x: Twirwaneho: two battalions on the Rurambo axis; four battalions on the Bijombo axis
r7-S2-M23B-015.n: Twirwaneho communiqué of Thursday (10 Sept 2026) as relayed by KMP; the article's wording is 'deux bataillons, dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises' (ambiguous). Burundian government reply not found. Existing related claim: r1-UV-2026Q3-008 (SOS Médias Burundi, 31 Aug).
r7-S2-M23B-015.vn: originating_source was wrong (Kanyuka); the passage is Twirwaneho's spokesperson in a Thursday communiqué. Removed '(ally of AFC-M23)' from the statement (not in the excerpt; figure flag '23'), kept the ambiguous French wording visible. KMP describes Twirwaneho as allied to the AFC-M23 ('le Twirwaneho, allié à l’AFC-M23'). The communiqué was issued on the Thursday (10 September 2026) per the page. Party allegation, not confirmed.
src: Selon le colonel Fidèle Rugabo, porte-parole du Twirwaneho, deux bataillons, dont celui des Hiboux et des forces burundaises, ont été déployés sur l’axe Rurambo. Sur l’axe Bijombo, quatre bataillons des FARDC et de l’armée burundaise, ainsi que des éléments du P5 et des Wazalendo, ont été visibles vers Kirungwa, Munanira et Gataka, Zikambitse-Marimba, Rubarati et Kajoka.

r7-S2-M23B-016.s: Into Rwanda reported that a statement released by Erasto Bahati, whom it calls the Governor of North Kivu Province, dismissed reports of an AFC/M23 pull-back, saying that what is happening is a routine rotation of troops, and quoted the statement as saying the activities along the battlefront are part of the regular military troop rotations within AFC/M23.
r7-S2-M23B-016.l: Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese areas; Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, North Kivu
r7-S2-M23B-016.a: AFC/M23 (North Kivu governor in the M23 administration)
r7-S2-M23B-016.n: Rwandan outlet (state-aligned media are partisan on contested facts); cited only for what the AFC/M23 governor's statement said. 'Governor Erasto Bahati' is probably the person other sources call Bahati Musanga Erasto / Erasto Musanga (not stated on this page). The page names the reports being denied: withdrawal from Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese, relocating to Alimbongo, Kirumba and Kanyabayonga, allegedly under US pressure. Igihe's Kinyarwanda item could not be fetched; Instagram/Facebook posts of 29 Mar 2026 ('AFC/M23 yahakanye ibyo kuva mu bice bimwe yafashe') were leads only.
r7-S2-M23B-016.vn: Rwandan outlet relaying a party statement: 'AFC/M23 says', grade C. Narrowed the 'Lubero' wording and made the governor title the outlet's, since he is the AFC/M23-appointed official. Bahati holds the post under the AFC/M23 administration, not the Kinshasa government. Into Rwanda (30 March 2026) says the reports appeared 'earlier this week'; the statement's own date is not given, so the date is approximate (on or before 30 March 2026). The reports named withdrawals from Lubero, Lunyasenge, Bukununu, Musiya, Katondi and Kipese. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: the Governor of North Kivu Province, Erasto Bahati, these reports were dismissed, with the governor clarifying that what is happening is simply a routine rotation of troops. The statement read: “The leadership of North Kivu Province reassures all citizens that the activities occurring along the battlefront are part of the regular military troop rotations within AFC/M23.”
has denied reports claiming they are pulling fighters from various regions in eastern DRC under their control.

r7-S2-M23B-017.s: A pro-government Rwandan outlet reported that on Wednesday, 2 July 2025, the Rwandan government spokesperson Makolo Yolande set out Rwanda's position on the report of the group of UN experts (whom the outlet calls 'so-called' experts), and that she criticised the group for what the outlet calls lies in the report aimed at distorting the truth.
r7-S2-M23B-017.l: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
r7-S2-M23B-017.n: Partisan Rwandan outlet; the outlet's wording 'abiyita Impuguke' ('so-called experts') is the outlet's own. The page does not give the report number; the report is the Group of Experts' final report (S/2025/446 per the project's target r2/G-DOC-446). The primary X post was not fetched. Rwanda's government reply is to the Group of Experts report, not to the AFC/M23 allegations; AFC/M23's own reply to the Katindo findings was not found.
r7-S2-M23B-017.vn: Removed the outlet name (figure flag '250') and 'via her X account' (not in the excerpt); made the 'lies' and 'so-called' framing the outlet's, as the excerpt is the outlet's narration. The page says she spoke through her X account ('Abinyujije kurubuga rwe rwa X'); the X post itself was not retained. The report is the UN Group of Experts' final report of mid-2025.
src: Kuri uyu wa Gatatu ku itariki ya 02 Nyakanga 2025, umuvugizi wa guverinoma y’u Rwanda,Makolo Yolande yagaragaje aho u Rwanda ruhagaze kuri raporo y’itsinda ry’abiyita Impuguke z’Umuryango w’Abibumbye, aho yanenze iryo tsinda ku binyoma byaranze iyo raporo hagamijwe kugoreka ukuri.

r7-S2-M23B-018.s: The outlet (pro-government) reported that Makolo Yolande said the UN experts' report confirms that the FDLR is helped by the Congolese government, but that the experts deliberately discount the concerns of Rwanda that led to the putting in place of defensive measures.
r7-S2-M23B-018.l: Kigali (statement on the eastern DRC conflict)
r7-S2-M23B-018.n: Same page as the previous claim. Partisan outlet; Rwanda says; not established fact.
r7-S2-M23B-018.vn: Removed the outlet name (figure flag '250'); 'ifashwa' rendered as 'helped' (the excerpt_en's own word) rather than 'supported'. Rwanda says; not established fact.
src: aho yagaragaje ko iyo raporo ishimangira ko FDLR ifashwa na leta ya Congo ariko ko abo biyita impuguke z’Umuryango w’abibumbye bigiza nkana maze bagatesha agaciro impungenge z’u Rwanda zatumye hashyirwaho ingamba z’ubwirinzi.

r7-S2-M23B-019.s: JamboRDC reported that in a mise au point published on Tuesday, signed by Bertrand Bisimwa, deputy coordinator of the AFC/M23, the movement said it rejects 'formally and as a whole' the accusations in Amnesty International's report on the Rubaya and Lomera mining sites, which it judges 'not established and insufficiently substantiated'.
r7-S2-M23B-019.l: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
r7-S2-M23B-019.n: Fills the gap for r2/G-NKW-MASISI#0 and r2/G-UNDOCS#1 (Amnesty itself said M23 had not responded; the reply came the day after publication). Page date 24/09/2026. The AFC/M23 mise au point itself was not located on a party channel; JamboRDC is a local outlet relaying it. A Kinyarwanda video post (YouTube) and Swahili posts also reported the denial (leads only). Rwanda's reply to Amnesty not found.
r7-S2-M23B-019.vn: Verbatim on JamboRDC (La Rédaction, 24/09/2026); title names Rubaya and Lomera. 2026-10-29: source 0 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Dans une mise au point publiée mardi 22 septembre 2026, le mouvement affirme rejeter « formellement et dans leur ensemble » les accusations contenues dans le rapport d’Amnesty International, qu’il juge « non établies et insuffisamment étayées ». Signé par Bertrand Bisimwa, coordonnateur adjoint de l’AFC/M23,
Dans son enquête publiée lundi 21 septembre, Amnesty International affirme avoir documenté plusieurs violations présumées dans les deux sites miniers contrôlés par le M23.

r7-S2-M23B-020.s: JamboRDC reported that the AFC/M23 said each case alleged by Amnesty should establish the reality of the alleged facts, their date and place, the identity of the alleged perpetrators and any link with the AFC/M23 and its chain of command, and that 'an accusation does not in itself constitute proof'.
r7-S2-M23B-020.l: Rubaya mining site (Masisi territory, North Kivu) and Lomera (Kabare territory, South Kivu)
r7-S2-M23B-020.n: Same page and statement as the previous claim.
src: Le mouvement estime que chaque cas devrait notamment permettre d’établir la réalité des faits allégués, leur date et leur lieu, l’identité des auteurs présumés ainsi que leur éventuel lien avec l’AFC/M23 et sa chaîne de commandement. « Une accusation ne constitue pas, à elle seule, une preuve, » soutient le mouvement.

r7-S2-RN-001.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Burundian authorities presented 13 people to journalists on 9 October, a majority of them Banyamulenge refugees, whom the authorities accused of espionage for Rwanda and for armed groups active in eastern RDC; Pierre Nkurikiye said the suspects collaborated with armed groups active in the region, including the AFC/M23, Red-Tabara and Twirwaneho.
r7-S2-RN-001.l: Bujumbura (Burundi); the armed groups named operate in eastern DRC
r7-S2-RN-001.a: Burundian authorities; Pierre Nkurikiye (as reported by SOS Médias Burundi)
r7-S2-RN-001.n: Burundian official account of its own arrests; the allegations are not independently verified. The page states that relatives and congregants contest the accusations. Adjacent to, not a reply to, FRN's October 2026 troop-crossing allegation (target r1/ST-DRC-2026#0). The page also names the suspects (including pastors); those names are not in the excerpts and are not listed here.
r7-S2-RN-001.vn: Page (retained, dated 11 octobre 2026, byline Adam Ntwari) prints both excerpts. Narrowed: the accusations are explicitly the authorities' ('whom the authorities accused'); 'namely' changed to 'including' (source: 'notamment', not exhaustive); weekday removed; 'DRC' replaced by 'RDC' as the excerpt prints it. excerpt_en flags are false positives (Friday/vendredi, Congolese Tutsi/tutsi congolaise): translations are faithful. Page also names three pastors among those presented (in the 'Des pasteurs parmi les personnes présentées' section); not in any excerpt, so not listed in victims_named; lead for a later pass under policy v1. Burundi's ministry account of its own arrests, relayed by one outlet; not independently verified. The same page reports that relatives and congregants contest the accusations, and that journalists were not allowed to ask questions allowing independent verification.
src: Les autorités burundaises ont présenté vendredi 9 octobre à des journalistes triés sur le volet 13 personnes, dont une majorité de réfugiés banyamulenge, accusées d’espionnage au profit du Rwanda et de groupes armés actifs dans l’est de la République démocratique du Congo (RDC).

Pierre Nkurikiye affirme que les suspects collaboraient avec des groupes armés actifs dans la région, notamment l’AFC/M23, Red-Tabara, un groupe armé burundais basé dans l’est de la RDC, et Twirwaneho, un groupe armé composé majoritairement de combattants issus de la minorité tutsi congolaise banyamulenge.

r7-S2-RN-002.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, on the occasion of the presentation of the suspects, the spokesperson of the ministry in charge of security, Pierre Nkurikiye, called on Burundians to monitor the Banyamulenge and to stop renting houses to them.
r7-S2-RN-002.a: Pierre Nkurikiye, as reported by SOS Médias Burundi
r7-S2-RN-002.n: Single-outlet report of an official call; relevant to the position of Banyamulenge in Burundi, not a finding about Kivu fighting. The presentation was on 9 October 2026 and concerned 13 suspects (see the companion claim).
r7-S2-RN-002.vn: Excerpt is verbatim on the retained page (11 octobre 2026) and carries the whole statement, attributed to the speaker. Page also prints the direct quote (see note). excerpt_en faithful ('Security'/'Sécurité' capitalisation only). Single-outlet report. The page also quotes him directly: « Il faut surveiller leurs déplacements et ne plus leur louer de maisons, surtout ici à Bujumbura ».
src: À cette occasion, le porte-parole du ministère en charge de la Sécurité, Pierre Nkurikiye, a appelé les Burundais à surveiller les Banyamulenge et à ne plus leur louer de maisons.

r7-S2-RN-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that Burundi's permanent representative to the UN, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, in his presentation on Friday 12 December 2025, accused Rwanda of having favoured the taking of Uvira in violation of the Washington accords and resolution 2773, and quoted him as saying Burundi was particularly concerned by cross-border attacks, including artillery and drones, some of which reached localities of Burundian territory.
r7-S2-RN-003.a: Burundi (government) via Zéphyrin Maniratanga; Rwanda as the party accused
r7-S2-RN-003.n: Party account (Burundi): Rwanda's role and the civilian casualties are Burundi's assertions. Possible overlap with r1-ST-BI-014 (another Maniratanga statement); check at promotion. Outside the Sept-Oct 2026 window of target r1/ST-DRC-2026#4. The page names the council briefing as on MONUSCO (not the special session).
r7-S2-RN-003.vn: Statement unchanged; actor narrowed (the speaker accuses Rwanda; AFC/M23 is named only in Actualite.cd's narration, not by him). Retained page dated 14/12/2025, byline Clément MUAMBA; both excerpts verbatim. Not a duplicate of r1-ST-BI-014: that claim rests on a different article (16 Dec 2025) about a 'special session' with an undated Tshibitoke-bombardment assertion; this claim covers different assertions (Uvira, Washington accords, resolution 2773, cross-border attacks) with an exact date. They may come from the same council meeting; the editor may link them. excerpt_en faithful (Friday/United Nations flags are capitalisation only). Party account (Burundi). Actualite.cd places the remarks at the Security Council briefing on MONUSCO.
src: Dans son exposé, vendredi 12 décembre 2025, le représentant permanent du Burundi auprès des Nations unies, Zéphyrin Maniratanga, a dénoncé l’attitude qu’il qualifie de belliqueuse du Rwanda, l’accusant d’avoir favorisé la prise de la ville d’Uvira en violation des accords de Washington et de la résolution 2773.

Le Burundi souhaite dénoncer la violation répétée de la résolution 2773, illustrée par la prise d’Uvira par l’armée rwandaise. Ces opérations ont entraîné de nombreuses victimes civiles. Nous sommes particulièrement préoccupés par les attaques transfrontalières, y compris l’usage de l’artillerie, de drones et d’autres moyens létaux, dont certains ont atteint des localités du territoire burundais.

r7-S2-RW-001.s: UMUSEKE reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said the RDC government cannot pursue the process of halting the fighting while it is itself the one starting the war; she was replying to Patrick Muyaya, minister of information, who had explained that President Tshisekedi said Rwanda was violating the agreements by launching attacks in South Kivu. UMUSEKE also reported that Makolo stressed that Rwanda has nothing to do with the fighting continuing in South Kivu.
r7-S2-RW-001.n: Rwandan outlet relaying the government spokesperson: recorded as what Rwanda said, not as fact. Page date 10 Dec 2025 08:39; the date of the underlying statement is not given. Serves the Uvira Q4 2025 Rwanda statement gap (r1/UV-2025Q4#2).
r7-S2-RW-001.vn: Excerpts exact and page date 'December 10, 2025 8:39 am' confirmed. 'gashozantambara' means the instigator/starter of war, and 'kandi' is 'while/and yet', not 'because': the draft's 'because it was the one waging war' and 'oversee a ceasefire process' narrowed to the excerpt's wording. Capitalisation flag: 'DRC' renders 'RDC', 'Congolese' renders 'Congo'; legitimate translation, case fixed in excerpt_en. Rwandan outlet relaying the Rwandan government spokesperson: what Rwanda says, not a finding. The date of the underlying statement is not given; page dated December 10, 2025. 2026-10-29: source 0 supporting_excerpt edited: verifier translation correction (S2-RW claim 0)
src: Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma, Yolande Makolo, yavuze ko Leta ya RDC idashobora gukurikirana inzira yo guhagarika imirwano kandi ari yo gashozantambara. Yasubizaga Minisitiri w’Itangazamakuru Patrick Muyaya, wasobanuraga ko Perezida Tshisekedi yavuze ko u Rwanda rurenga ku masezerano rugaba ibitero muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo.
Yolande Makolo yamaganye amagambo y’abayobozi ba Congo bavanga ibibazo bibiri bitandukanye, ashimangira ko u Rwanda ntaho ruhuriye n’imirwano ikomeje muri Kivu y’Amajyepfo.

r7-S2-RW-002.s: Umuryango.rw reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo said Kayikwamba's message was meant to mislead and that the DRC government should not hide its failure to protect Congolese from its own army and armed groups, and quoted her saying that it is not Rwandans who are killing in Beni, Ituri, Kwamouth, Goma, Minembwe or Uvira.
r7-S2-RW-002.l: Beni, Ituri, Kwamouth, Goma, Minembwe, Uvira (as listed by the speaker)
r7-S2-RW-002.n: Rwandan outlet relaying the government spokesperson (party says). The excerpt starts at "Yolande Makolo" (the sentence opens "Umuvugizi wa Guverinoma y’u Rwanda,"). Per the page, the statement replies to an interview by DRC foreign minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner with Deutsche Welle. Date computed from the page date only (Saturday 17 May 2025). Serves r1/UV-2025Q2#2 (Rwanda on Uvira, Q2 2025) and r1/NKS-2025Q2#0.
r7-S2-RW-002.vn: Excerpt exact; page byline 'Yanditswe na: Angeline MUKANGENZI Kuwa: Saturday 17, May 2025' confirms date. Translation faithful ('yagaragaje' = showed/pointed out; 'bibasirwa n’ingabo zayo' = targeted by its army). Capitalisation flag: DRC/Congolese/She render RDC/Abanye-Congo; legitimate. r7-S2-RW-003.s: Umuryango.rw reported that the Government of Rwanda said that reports of the UN human rights office (OHCHR) in the DRC show that armed groups, the FARDC and the FDLR are the ones raping civilians.
r7-S2-RW-003.a: Government of Rwanda; alleges armed groups, FARDC and FDLR
r7-S2-RW-003.n: Rwandan outlet paraphrasing the government; party says only. Rwanda's characterisation of OHCHR reports is not verified here. Serves the Rwanda sexual-violence statement gaps (r3/G-RESP#1, r1/SV-2025#4) only loosely: it is a general statement, not about Munzenze.
r7-S2-RW-003.vn: Excerpt exact, same page and date (17 May 2025). 'zihamya' = confirm/attest; 'show' acceptable and attributed to the Government of Rwanda via the outlet. No hedge words in the excerpt. Capitalisation flag: Government/Rwanda/DRC/United Nations render Guverinoma/Rwanda/RDC/Umuryango w’Abibumbye; legitimate. Umuryango.rw's paraphrase of the Rwandan government's position; Rwanda's reading of OHCHR reports is not verified here and does not refer to a specific incident.
