r7-S2-RW-004.s: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a "response" to the Human Rights Watch report of 14 May 2026, saying that the 14 May report claimed that the M23 and Rwandan forces, and no longer the Wazalendo, were the principal threat to the civilians covered in HRW's January 2026 statement, and that the conduct of the FARDC and Wazalendo in Uvira and the surrounding territory had not been the subject of a comparable 23-page investigative report.
r7-S2-RW-004.n: Party's own website: what Rwanda says, not fact. The response page itself carries no date line; 15 May 2026 comes from the OGS library listing (third source). BBC Afrique (15 May 2026, bbc.com/afrique/articles/cj4pw07x02yo) said the Rwandan government and M23 had not yet answered a BBC request for comment and that HRW wrote to the Rwandan government and M23 leaders in April and received no reply. This response fills the gap "HRW says none received" for r1/HC-2026#1 with a post-publication Rwandan reply. The response does not address the HRW sexual-violence findings directly.
r7-S2-RW-004.vn: All excerpts exact on the retained pages; listing confirms 'Friday, 15 May, 2026'. Statement keeps HRW's report as characterised by Rwanda ('claimed'). Rwandan government's own website: what Rwanda says about an HRW report. The response page carries no date; 15 May 2026 is the OGS library listing date.
src: Four months later, on 14 May 2026, HRW published a report claiming that it was instead the M23 and Rwandan forces, and no longer the Wazalendo, who were the principal threat to the same civilians it had reported on in its January 2026 statement.

The conduct of the Congolese armed forces (FARDC) and of the Wazalendo militias in Uvira and the surrounding territory has not been the subject of a comparable 23-page investigative report, despite a documented record across 2025 and 2026
Rwanda’s Response to the Human Rights Watch Report of 14 May 2026 Friday, 15 May, 2026

r7-S2-RW-005.s: The Office of the Government Spokesperson of Rwanda published a response to a post by Muyaya and to an HRW report, saying that nowhere in the HRW document is Rwanda attributed responsibility for the mass graves, and that the same report documents summary executions and sexual violence by the FARDC and Wazalendo against South Kivu populations before and during their withdrawal from Uvira.
r7-S2-RW-005.a: Government of Rwanda (OGS); alleges FARDC and Wazalendo
r7-S2-RW-005.n: Party's own website; what Rwanda says about an HRW report (the page cites HRW of April 1, 2026), not a finding. The response page carries no date line; 14 May 2026 is the OGS library listing date (third source). Serves r1/UV-2026Q3#1 (Rwanda on Uvira mass-grave allegations, earlier round noted Sept 2026) as an earlier Rwandan statement on the same allegation, and r1/HC-2026#1.
r7-S2-RW-005.vn: Excerpts exact; listing confirms 'Thursday, 14 May, 2026'. Page identifies the report as 'HRW April 1, 2026 Report'. Allegations remain attributed to Rwanda. Rwandan government's own website characterising the HRW report of 1 April 2026 (per the page); not a finding. The page has no date line; 14 May 2026 is the OGS listing date. The same two sentences also appear in the Ministry of Defence fact-check dated 24 April 2026.
src: Nowhere in this document is Rwanda attributed responsibility for the mass graves. The report itself acknowledges that it is “difficult to know exactly who is buried in all the graves, when they were buried, and how they died.”

What this same report clearly documents is that the FARDC and the Wazalendo committed serious abuses against the populations of South Kivu, including summary executions and sexual violence, before and during their withdrawal from Uvira.
Rwanda’s Response to Muyaya’s post and HRW Report Thursday, 14 May, 2026

r7-S2-RW-006.s: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that Jean-Jacques Purusi accused Rwanda and the AFC/M23 of being responsible for the massacres in Uvira, pointing to mass graves, and responding that since the AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira the city has been in chaos, with killings, looting and sexual violence in several neighbourhoods.
r7-S2-RW-006.a: Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Defence website)
r7-S2-RW-006.n: Party's own government site: what Rwanda says. The page heading names Jean-Jacques Purusi (Governor of South Kivu) and Patrick Muyaya and a briefing dated 02 April 2026; publication date 24 April 2026 per the OGS listing and the page. Serves r1/UV-2026Q3#1 (Rwanda on Uvira mass-grave allegations) and r1/ATR-SK-2026#2 loosely.
r7-S2-RW-006.vn: Excerpt exact; page shows '24 April 2026' under the heading. Same event and place. Rwandan government website: what Rwanda says. It answers a briefing by South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi and Patrick Muyaya dated 02 April 2026; the page attributes the post-withdrawal violence mainly to VDP/Wazalendo, citing SOS Médias Burundi.
src: Jean-Jacques Purusi accused Rwanda and the AFC/M23 of being responsible for the massacres in Uvira, pointing to the discovery of mass graves reportedly containing hundreds of bodies. Fact: Since the AFC/M23 withdrew from Uvira, the city has been plunged into chaos. Killings, looting, and sexual violence have erupted in several neighborhoods.

r7-S2-RW-007.s: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" stating that in the High Plateaus of South Kivu the Banyamulenge have faced systematic attacks by a coalition of Maï-Maï groups operating in collaboration with the FARDC, involving killings, rape, the burning of villages, mass theft of cattle and "even drone strikes by the Congolese government".
r7-S2-RW-007.l: High Plateaus of South Kivu (Hauts Plateaux), incl. Minembwe area
r7-S2-RW-007.a: Government of Rwanda (Ministry of Defence website); alleges Maï-Maï groups, FARDC, Congolese government drones
r7-S2-RW-007.n: Party's own government site. The fact-check answers DRC foreign minister Kayikwamba's Al Jazeera interview (title says 13 November 2025). Date is the interview date given in the page title; the publication date of the fact-check is not shown on the page. General statement on drone strikes in the highlands: it does not address the later Mulima or Fizi strikes of 2026 (r1/SKS-2026Q3#0, r1/ATR-SK-2026#2).
r7-S2-RW-007.vn: Excerpt exact. The draft used the interview date (13 Nov 2025) as the claim and source date and said the page shows no publication date; the retained page prints '24 April 2026' directly under the title (the same date as the MoD South Kivu fact-check and the OGS listing of several fact-checks). Date corrected to 2026-04-24; the interview date is kept in the note only (the excerpt does not print it). Rwandan government website: what Rwanda says. The page, titled as a fact-check of DRC foreign minister Kayikwamba's Al Jazeera interview of 13 November 2025, is dated 24 April 2026.
src: In the High Plateaus of South Kivu, the Banyamulenge community has been under siege for years, facing systematic attacks carried out by a coalition of Maï-Maï groups operating in collaboration with the FARDC. These attacks involve killings, rape, the burning of villages, mass theft of cattle, and even drone strikes by the Congolese government.

r7-S2-RW-008.s: Bwiza reported that Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo, on X, accused Muyaya of continuing to turn the day of remembrance for the victims of the Gatumba killings into a platform for spreading messages against Rwanda; Bwiza reported that Muyaya had also accused Rwanda of having links with M23 and with the Twirwaneho and Red-Tabara groups.
r7-S2-RW-008.n: Bwiza is a Kinyarwanda/French outlet; the X post itself was not opened. Related to the Rwanda/Twirwaneho allegation context of Aug 2026 (r1/UV-2026Q3#1); not about a specific incident. Second excerpt gives Muyaya's accusation, which the page attributes to him.
r7-S2-RW-008.vn: Excerpts exact; byline 'By Bénjamin BABOU • Ku Cyumweru, 16 Kanama 2026' confirms Sunday 16 Aug 2026. 'yashinje' = accused, so 'said' changed to 'accused'; 'kugira aho ruhuriye na' = having links/a connection with. The pronoun subject of 'Yanashinje' is Muyaya per the preceding sentence on the page (given in replacement_quotes). Capitalisation flag on source 1 is the pronoun 'He'; legitimate. Rwanda-based outlet relaying an exchange on X; the X posts were not opened. The exchange followed remarks by Tito Rutaremara at the 22nd Gatumba commemoration in Kigali on 13 August (per the page). 2026-10-29: source 1 sources.append edited: excerpt extension for a clause supported only by the retained page (r7 integration)
src: Yolande Makolo yifashishije urubuga rwa X, yashinje Muyaya kuba akomeje guhindura umunsi wo kwibuka abazize ubwicanyi bwo mu Gatumba urubuga rwo gukwirakwizamo ubutumwa burwanya u Rwanda.
Yanashinje u Rwanda kugira aho ruhuriye na M23 ndetse n’imitwe ya Twirwaneho na Red-Tabara, avuga ko ibyo bikorwa biri mu mugambi wo guhungabanya ubusugire bw’igihugu cye.

Muyaya yavuze ko kuba Rutaremara yarasabye urubyiruko rw’Abanyamulenge gufata intwaro ari ikimenyetso cy’uko u Rwanda rugira uruhare mu bibazo by’umutekano muke bikomeje kugaragara mu Burasirazuba bwa Congo.

r7-S2-RW-009.s: The Rwandan Ministry of Defence website published a "fact-checking" responding to Jean-Jacques Purusi's accusation that the AFC/M23 slaughtered Banyamulenge cattle to frame the FARDC, stating that multiple recent reports describe drone strikes affecting the Minembwe area in South Kivu that hit civilians and property, including injuries and deaths.

r7-S2-RW-009.n: Party's own government site. The page (not the excerpt) names villages Gakenke, Ilundu and Kiziba and links DW and RNA News reports; it does not name who flew the drones. Does not address the 25 April 2026 FARDC claim of a downed Rwandan UAV at Point Zéro (r1/ST-M23-2026#0).
r7-S2-RW-009.vn: Excerpt exact; page dated 24 April 2026. Statement matches the excerpt. Rwandan government website: what Rwanda says. It does not name who operated the drones; elsewhere on the page it says drones struck Gakenke, Ilundu and Kiziba, citing RNA News and DW.
src: Jean-Jacques Purusi accused the AFC/M23 of slaughtering Banyamulenge cattle to frame the FARDC. Fact: Multiple recent reports describe drone strikes affecting the Minembwe area in South Kivu that hit civilians and property, including injuries and deaths.

src: On 25 January 2025, the High Representative of the Union for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy issued a statement on behalf of the Union expressing its deep concern at the latest escalation of the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), as aggravated by the renewed offensive of the M23 armed group supported by the Rwanda Defence Force (RDF). (3) The RDF’s unauthorised presence in the DRC constitutes a violation of that country’s territorial integrity and sustains the armed conflict, instability and insecurity in the region.

r8-EU-509-002.s: Council Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/509 of 17 March 2025 states that revenues from the illegal extraction and trafficking of natural resources from eastern DRC are used to fund, among others, the M23, and adds nine persons and one entity to the EU's DRC sanctions list (Annex Ia to Regulation (EC) No 1183/2005).

src: Gasabo Gold Refinery Place of establishment: Kigali, Rwanda The Gasabo Gold Refinery, based in Kigali, began its refining activities on 1 June 2022 following the closure of Aldango Gold Refinery. The illegal extraction and trafficking of natural resources from eastern DRC, such as gold, contributes to the escalation of the conflict. The transit of gold through the only gold refinery in Rwanda, Gasabo Gold Refinery, contributes to the illicit export via Rwanda of illegally extracted gold.

r9-V-FU-001.s: The New Humanitarian reported that a civil society activist in Uvira said that for three months the state was completely absent in the city, that there were abuses, and that people were whipped, arrested and some died in detention; the article ties this to a militia-led policing force that residents said carried out arbitrary arrests.
r9-V-FU-001.a: Wazalendo (pro-government militias), as described by residents to The New Humanitarian
r9-V-FU-001.n: Anonymous civil society activist; no dates or names of detainees. Article says more than a dozen Uvira residents spoke to the outlet. Independent context: HRW 15 Sep 2025 on Wazalendo and army threats to civilians in Uvira (already cited elsewhere).
r9-V-FU-001.vn: Retained user copy (fetch_failed for the script) prints the passage verbatim; replacement quote extended to include the residents' account of a militia-led policing force. src: Still more reported a militia-led policing force that has carried out arbitrary arrests and other abuses. “For three months, the state was completely absent in Uvira. An alternative was necessary to keep the city standing at the time, but there were abuses,” said a civil society activist. “People were whipped, arrested, some died in detention.”

The article does not date the attack.

r9-V-FU-002.n: Single anonymous testimony; date not stated. The woman is not named.

src: A Banyamulenge woman who has lived in Uvira her entire life said she was attacked by six Wazalendo fighters — three in plain clothes and three in uniforms — while fetching water at a tap. She said the attackers called them “Rwandans”. “They beat me with sticks over and over, until I couldn't even scream anymore,” she said.

r9-V-FU-003.s: The New Humanitarian reported that demonstrations organised against Gasita in Uvira turned violent when Congolese military forces fired on unarmed protesters, killing at least one person and wounding several others, including children.
r9-V-FU-003.a: Congolese military forces (FARDC), as stated by the outlet
r9-V-FU-003.x: The New Humanitarian: at least one killed, several wounded including children (other outlets in the store give higher tolls)
r9-V-FU-003.n: The article gives the month ('in September') and the appointment of General Olivier Gasita but no day for the shooting. Lower toll than SOS Medias Burundi (5 dead), Kivu Morning Post (Wazalendo spokesperson: 12 dead) and HRW (an 8-year-old boy killed, at least nine wounded) already in the store; record as a discrepancy, not a conflict of fact.
r9-V-FU-003.vn: Retained user copy prints the passage; replacement quote extended to the September/Gasita sentence that dates the protests. Outlet's own narration from a credible non-partisan origin: B. The outlet gives the month (September 2025) but no day. Its toll (at least one killed) is lower than other outlets' tolls already in the store; a discrepancy to surface, not resolve.
src: Also in September, around two weeks after the funeral incident, there were major tensions following the appointment of General Olivier Gasita – who is also a Banyamulenge – to command military operations in Uvira. Wazalendo fighters, Wazalendo fighters, who see Gasita as responsible for the fall of Bukavu and suspected him – without providing evidence – of M23 ties, paralysed the city for eight days by setting up roadblocks, closing the border into Burundi, and shutting shops and schools. The fighters also organised demonstrations against Gasita – who ultimately left the city – which turned violent when Congolese military forces fired on unarmed protesters, killing at least one person and wounding several others, including children.

r9-V-FU-004.s: The New Humanitarian reported that the self-proclaimed Wazalendo police chief for South Kivu, General Kimanuka Musasa Nyambwe Nungisa, denied that the militias have implemented a taxation system and said they came to defend Uvira when authorities and security services fled.
r9-V-FU-004.n: Reply to residents' and a port official's accounts that Wazalendo collect a 'contribution to the resistance'. Title 'General' and 'self-proclaimed' as printed by the outlet.
r9-V-FU-004.vn: Retained user copy prints the passage verbatim. The claim records that he made the denial (a party's statement reported by a credible outlet), not that the denial is true: B.
src: The self‑proclaimed Wazalendo police chief for South Kivu, General Kimanuka Musasa Nyambwe Nungisa, denied the militias have implemented a taxation system and said they simply came to defend Uvira when authorities and security services fled.

r9-V-FU-005.s: The New Humanitarian reported that the Congolese army carried out raids in search of alleged M23 collaborators, mainly in hotels across Uvira, and that these operations led to arbitrary arrests and contributed to a climate of fear, particularly among Banyamulenge.
r9-V-FU-005.a: Congolese army (FARDC), as stated by the outlet
r9-V-FU-005.n: Outlet's own characterisation; no dates, numbers or names.

src: For its part, the Congolese army has carried out raids in search of alleged M23 collaborators, mainly in hotels across the city. These operations have led to arbitrary arrests and contributed to a climate of fear, particularly among Banyamulenge.

r9-V-FU-006.s: The New Humanitarian, in an article about Uvira, reported that in September Wazalendo fighters disrupted the funeral of an army colonel, a Tutsi officer from the region, and his wife (both had died in a plane crash), accusing the relatives of collaborating with Rwanda, and that witnesses reported Wazalendo militants declaring that no 'Rwandan' should be buried on Congolese soil. The article does not state where the funeral took place or name the colonel.

Month discrepancy to be surfaced, not resolved here. The same passage reports an 8-year-old boy killed by gunfire/shelling nearby (per a neighbour); it is not made a separate claim because the excerpt is limited to the funeral.

src: Tensions escalated in September when Wazalendo fighters disrupted the funeral of an army colonel – a Tutsi officer from the region – and his wife (both had died in a plane crash), accusing the deceased’s relatives of collaborating with Rwanda. Witnesses reported Wazalendo militants declaring, “No ‘Rwandan’ should be buried here on Congolese soil”

r9-V-FU-007.s: Foxtime.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi officially announced the discovery of at least 344 bodies in three mass graves in the city of Uvira and its outskirts, brought to light after the withdrawal of the AFC/M23.

r9-V-FU-007.a: South Kivu provincial government (Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi); the outlet's framing attributes the killings to AFC/M23
r9-V-FU-007.x: Foxtime.cd: at least 344 bodies in three mass graves
r9-V-FU-007.n: Page text carries no absolute date ('2 mois ago'). The date 2026-09-11 comes from the Friends of the Congo Substack (dated 11 Sep 2026, says Purusi spoke on Top Congo FM), which could not be fetched as page text and is a lead only. The 344 figure is a government count; neither Foxtime nor the Substack says who dug up or counted the bodies or how they died. AFC/M23 spokesperson Kanyuka earlier (Reuters, Feb 2026) said he knew of no such graves (already in the store). Possible relation to REC-0023 and REC-0648. Earlier tolls already in the store: 31 + 141 = 172 bodies in two graves (Reuters via BBC Gahuza, Feb 2026) and 210 in three graves (Radio Okapi, 3 Apr 2026).

The 344 figure is a government count; the page does not say who dug up or counted the bodies or how the people died. Earlier tolls in the store are lower (172 in two graves, Feb 2026; 210 in three graves, Apr 2026).

r9-V-FU-008.s: Foxtime.cd reported that the military judiciary has already opened investigations directly targeting the commanders and leaders of the AFC/M23 coalition to formally establish responsibility for what the outlet called 'this barbarity', in its article on the Uvira mass graves.

Let me remind you that in South Kivu we witnessed the invasion of Uvira, which, according to us, was organized under Kigali's direct command. Bombs were used. Kamikaze drones were used indiscriminately against peaceful civilians.

src: Le porte parole évoque parallèlement la présence de combattants du Front national de libération (FNL) et de Résistance pour un État de Droit (Red Tabara) à Minembwe.
L’entretien radiophonique accordé par le porte parole des Forces de défense du Burundi, le général Gaspard Baratuza à la BBC Gahuza

r9-V-NK1-001.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that, according to the communication cell of the North Kivu governorate, the operating theatre of the Sake Afya referral health centre (CSR) in Masisi territory had been ransacked and vandalised during the latest clashes in the area, making surgical interventions almost impossible; the article does not say who damaged it. It reported that the vice-governor of North Kivu, Schadrack Amani, of the Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN), handed over medical equipment for the centre's maternity and operating theatre on Tuesday 27 October 2026.
r9-V-NK1-001.l: Sake Afya referral health centre (Centre de Santé de Référence Sake Afya), Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-001.a: FRN North Kivu governorate (communication cell), as reported
r9-V-NK1-001.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-01. The pro-AFC/M23 post alleges looting by Wazalendo before the FRN took Sake; this page attributes the damage to no one and says only 'derniers affrontements' per the governorate (a de facto authority, so the damage account is that party's). The page calls Amani 'vice-gouverneur' in the first paragraph and 'gouverneur' in a later one. Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based outlet now operating under FRN control (note for the reviewer). Date is the handover date; the damage date is not given.
r9-V-NK1-001.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the inserted '(FRN-run)' label for the governorate, which the page does not print as such (it names the vice-governor as FRN); 'the governorate's vice-governor' changed to 'vice-governor of North Kivu' as printed. The note's claim that the page later calls Amani 'gouverneur' was not seen in the retained text. Flag on source 1 excerpt_en is the capitalised 'Tuesday/North Kivu' translation; translation matches the excerpt. The damage account is the governorate's (a de facto authority under the FRN, per the page's naming of the vice-governor's affiliation). The date is the handover date; the damage date is not given. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.
ent: Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN)
src: Selon la cellule de communication du Gouvernorat, le bloc opératoire de Sake Afya avait été saccagé et vandalisé lors des derniers affrontements qui ont secoué la zone, rendant les interventions chirurgicales quasi impossibles.
Le don a été remis hier, mardi 27 octobre 2026, par le vice-gouverneur du Nord-Kivu, Schadrack Amani, du Front pour la refondation de la Nation (FRN).

r9-V-NK1-002.s: Insecurity Insight's October 2025 DRC incident-monitoring brief listed, as a publicly reported and unverified incident, that on 27 October 2025 the Sake Afia health centre in Bikali neighbourhood, Sake town, Masisi territory, was stormed by armed men dressed in military uniforms who took everything before fleeing during a night attack on the area.
r9-V-NK1-002.l: Sake Afia health centre, Bikali neighbourhood, Sake, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-002.a: armed men in military uniforms (as the brief states)
r9-V-NK1-002.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-01 (related, not the same incident: the post concerns looting of the operating theatre by Wazalendo at an unstated date). 'Sake Afia' is the brief's spelling of Sake Afya. The brief says its incidents are publicly reported and not verified; it does not name its underlying source for this item. Source date: the PDF is stored under a January 2026 upload path (exact publication day not on the page), so 2026-01-01 is a placeholder for 2026-01.
r9-V-NK1-002.vn: Excerpt exact in the PDF (North Kivu section). Statement matches, including the unverified caveat printed on the page. Grade lowered from B to C: the brief compiles publicly reported, unverified incidents and gives no underlying source. Source date placeholder must be corrected to month precision (2026-01) via source_edits; no day is printed. Insecurity Insight states its listed incidents have not been verified through ground investigations, and does not name its source for this item. Source publication date: January 2026 (month only; 2026-01-01 is a placeholder).
src: 27 October 2025: In Bikali neighbourhood, Sake town, Masisi territory, the Sake Afia health centre was stormed by armed men dressed in military uniforms who took everything before fleeing during a night attack on the area.

r9-V-NK1-003.s: Kinpressactu reported that the human rights organisation Dynamique Génération Consciente (DYGENEC-RDC) raised an alert on Monday 12 October 2026 that four young fishermen had reportedly been found dead in Lake Kivu at Goma and a fifth was missing, and denounced alleged executions involving armed elements of the AFC/M23. According to DYGENEC-RDC, the four were Ombeni Dunia Patrick, Chrispin Cuma, Ishara Bunaza and Emmanuel Cikuru, and their bodies were taken to the morgue of the Goma general hospital; the fifth, Adili Banza Julien, had not been found. DYGENEC-RDC said colleagues of the victims told it the five men had reportedly been tied up and thrown into Lake Kivu on the night of Saturday 10 to Sunday 11 October 2026, and that two more bodies had reportedly been found on Monday morning at the Étoile du Kivu boat port. Kinpressactu said these elements, the alleged circumstances of the deaths and the alleged involvement of armed elements required independent verification.
r9-V-NK1-003.l: Lake Kivu shore, Goma (Étoile du Kivu boat port), North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-003.a: AFC/M23 armed elements (as alleged by DYGENEC-RDC)
r9-V-NK1-003.x: per DYGENEC-RDC via Kinpressactu: four bodies found, one fisherman missing, two further bodies reportedly found on the Monday morning; four bodies taken to the Goma general hospital morgue
r9-V-NK1-003.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-05. Pro-DRC posts relay DYGENEC-RDC; this claim is DYGENEC's account as carried by Kinpressactu (Kinshasa). The fifth name is 'Adili Banza Julien' on this page; the posts print 'Adili Banza Jules' (beto.cd also prints Julien). Another account (CongoRassure) reports one body, named Crispin Chuma, found on the Sunday morning (see next claim); Kinpressactu itself says the cases may not all be the same series. No AFC/M23 or urban-authority statement was found (beto.cd of 12 Oct 2026 says none had been reported).
r9-V-NK1-003.vn: Excerpts exact. Restored the conditionals the page uses ('auraient été retrouvés', 'auraient été ligotés', 'auraient été découverts'); victim statuses changed from 'killed' to 'found dead (per DYGENEC-RDC)' since the deaths' cause is DYGENEC's allegation; added the page's morgue detail with its passage. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words (DYGENEC names) and the translations match the excerpts. An advocacy organisation's unverified account; Kinpressactu itself says the circumstances and responsibility are not established and that the CongoRassure case (Crispin Chuma) may not be part of the same series. Spellings Chrispin Cuma (DYGENEC) and Crispin Chuma (CongoRassure) are kept as printed.
src: L’alerte a été rapportée le lundi 12 octobre 2026 par la Dynamique Génération Consciente (DYGENEC-RDC), une organisation de défense des droits humains, qui dénonce des faits présumés d’exécutions impliquant des éléments armés de l’AFC/M23.

Selon la DYGENEC-RDC, les quatre victimes retrouvées sont identifiées comme suit : Ombeni Dunia Patrick, originaire de Masisi ; Chrispin Cuma, originaire d’Idjwi ; Ishara Bunaza, originaire de Buzi Bulenga ; Emmanuel Cikuru, également originaire d’Idjwi.
Le cinquième pêcheur, identifié comme Adili Banza Julien, n’avait toujours pas été retrouvé dans les eaux du lac Kivu au moment de la publication de l’alerte.

La DYGENEC-RDC affirme avoir recueilli auprès de collègues des victimes des informations selon lesquelles les cinq hommes auraient été ligotés avant d’être jetés dans le lac Kivu, dans la nuit du samedi 10 au dimanche 11 octobre 2026. L’organisation indique également que deux corps supplémentaires auraient été découverts lundi matin au port du bateau Étoile du Kivu.

r9-V-NK1-004.s: CongoRassure reported that the body of a young man in his thirties, identified as Crispin Chuma, resident of the Les Volcans quarter in Goma commune, was pulled from Lake Kivu at the Goma port on the morning of Sunday 11 October, with, according to local sources, his feet and hands tied and marks of strangulation and torture. According to testimony gathered on the spot, he had been returning home on Saturday evening around 20:30 with two friends, singing a song deemed hostile to the M23/AFC rebellion; pursued by armed men assimilated to the M23, his two friends reportedly fled, while Crispin Chuma was reportedly arrested and taken to an unknown destination, and his body was found floating the next morning.
r9-V-NK1-004.l: Goma port, Lake Kivu, Goma, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-004.a: armed men assimilated to the M23 (as reported by witnesses)
r9-V-NK1-004.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-05 (possibly the same series as the DYGENEC list, where the name is spelled 'Chrispin Cuma'; Kinpressactu says the information does not confirm that all reported cases are the same). CongoRassure is a local outlet; Jules Ngeleza, president of the Goma communal youth council, is quoted denouncing 'un énième cas'. The two Chuma/Cuma spellings are kept as each source prints them.
r9-V-NK1-004.vn: Excerpts exact. The draft dropped the conditionals ('seraient parvenus', 'aurait été interpellé') and stated he 'was pursued ... and was seized'; the page says the friends were pursued and he was reportedly arrested and taken to an unknown destination. Corrected 'M23 rebellion' to 'M23/AFC rebellion' as printed. Status 'killed' changed to 'found dead'. Single local outlet relaying local sources and witnesses; the arrest is reported in the conditional and the page does not say who took him.
src: Le corps sans vie d'un jeune homme d'une trentaine d'années a été repêché ce dimanche 11 octobre matin dans les eaux du lac Kivu, au niveau du port de Goma. La victime a été identifiée comme Crispin Chuma, résident du Quartier « Les Volcans », en Commune de Goma.
Selon des sources locales, son corps présentait les pieds et les mains ligotés et des traces d'étranglement et de torture.
D'après des témoignages recueillis sur place, l'infortuné rentrait à son domicile samedi soir vers 20h30 avec deux de ses amis en scandant une chanson jugée hostile à la rébellion du M23/AFC.

Poursuivis par des hommes armés assimilés au M23, ses deux amis seraient parvenus à prendre fuite. Crispin Chuma, lui, aurait été interpellé et conduit vers une destination inconnue. Son corps a été retrouvé flottant le lendemain matin.

r9-V-NK1-005.s: The Committee to Protect Journalists reported that on 19 September 2025, intelligence agents with the M23 and AFC rebel groups detained Ricardo Olenga, a reporter with the privately owned Radio Kako FM, at their Goma office, according to local media and two journalists who spoke to CPJ anonymously; it said the groups detained him for sharing a video that discussed alleged abuses by the two groups, that he is accused of spreading false news, and, according to those sources, that he was transferred on 23 October to Goma's Munzenze central prison. CPJ said its request for comment to M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma received no response.
r9-V-NK1-005.l: Goma, North Kivu (AFC/M23 intelligence office; Munzenze central prison)
r9-V-NK1-005.a: M23 and AFC intelligence agents (as CPJ reports)
r9-V-NK1-005.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-07. Posts of 20 Oct 2025 allege detention since 19 Sept 2025 without visits for publishing a video of a mother protesting her child's detention; CPJ confirms the arrest, the video and the accusation of false news. Other Congolese reports (Mashariki RDC, 20 Sept 2025) give the arrest day as 'samedi 19 septembre 2025'; 19 Sept 2025 was a Friday, so the weekday in that report is inconsistent and the date 19 Sept is taken from CPJ and RSF. Mashariki RDC (Bukavu-area local outlet, not cited) has the same arrest report.
r9-V-NK1-005.vn: Excerpts exact; year 2025 printed in the dateline (source 1). Narrowed attribution of the Munzenze transfer to 'those sources' as the page does, rather than CPJ's own statement.
src: On September 19, intelligence agents with the M23 and AFC rebel groups detained Olenga, a reporter with the privately owned Radio Kako FM broadcaster, at their Goma office, according to local media and two journalists who spoke with CPJ, on condition of anonymity for fear of retaliation.

Kinshasa, October 30, 2025—The M23 and Congo River Alliance (AFC) rebel groups must ensure the immediate and unconditional release of journalist Ricardo Olenga, detained for over a month in the eastern city of Goma, in North Kivu, the Committee to Protect Journalists said Thursday.

The groups detained Olenga for sharing a video that discussed alleged abuses by the two armed groups — he is accused of spreading false news. On October 23, the journalist was transferred to Goma’s Munzenze central prison, those sources said.
CPJ’s request for comment sent to M23 spokesperson Willy Ngoma via messaging app in late October received no response.

r9-V-NK1-006.s: Reporters Without Borders (RSF), in a March 2026 report on journalists in the Great Lakes region, said Ricardo Olenga, a Kako FM radio contributor, was arrested by the M23 in Goma on 19 September 2025 and detained until 17 November in unsanitary conditions, after the station's YouTube channel and TikTok account broadcast a video in which a member of the public deplored conditions since the M23 takeover.
r9-V-NK1-006.x: detention of about two months (19 September to 17 November 2025), per RSF
r9-V-NK1-006.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-07. Gives the release date (17 Nov 2025), which the 2026-06-06 post (not cited) implies. RSF's text does not mention the alleged order to dispose of two prisoners' bodies at Lac Vert; that allegation (Olenga's testimony as relayed by a pro-DRC account) was not found in any fetched page. Actualite.cd (28 Mar 2026) also lists Olenga as detained nearly two months in 2025 (spelled 'Kalo FM'); not cited.
r9-V-NK1-006.vn: Excerpt exact in the PDF (report dated March 2026 on its cover page). Statement matches; RSF attributes the arrest to 'the M23' only, as the claim does. AFP credits in the PDF are photo credits, not for this entry.
src: Ricardo Olenga: September 2025 – Goma (North Kivu). Kako FM radio contributor. - Arrested by the M23 in Goma on 19 September 2025, and detained until 17 November in unsanitary conditions. - The reason: the radio station's YouTube channel and TikTok account had broadcast a video in which a member of the public deplored conditions since the M23 takeover.

r9-V-NK1-007.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that Bulenda Siliro, 74, an avenue chief in the Lac Vert quarter of Goma, was killed on Tuesday 16 September after being kidnapped with his son; the Lac Vert quarter chief, Dedesi Mitima, told the outlet the kidnapping took place between 12 and 13 September, that the family paid the full ransom but only the son was released (reaching Mugunga on the morning of 17 September), and that Bulenda Siliro was shot dead anyway.
r9-V-NK1-007.l: Lac Vert quarter, Goma, North Kivu (son released at Mugunga)
r9-V-NK1-007.x: ransom paid in full, amount not stated
r9-V-NK1-007.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-08 (the post is a Kivu Morning Post item). Single local source; no perpetrator named. The article also mentions an earlier killing in the same quarter (Mbangu Shabanyere Germain, youth president) with no date. RSF's report mentions a different journalist case involving 'the suspicious disappearance of a community chief, blamed on the M23'; not shown to be this one. Kivu Morning Post is Goma-based.
r9-V-NK1-007.vn: Excerpts exact; statement matches the page, including attribution to the quarter chief. 16 September 2025 was a Tuesday, consistent with the article date. excerpt_en flags are capitalised words (Lac Vert / Kivumorningpost); translations match. Single local outlet; no perpetrator named (the page says only 'ravisseurs'). Year from the article date (17 September 2025).
src: Bulenda Siliro, âgé de 74 ans et chef d’avenue dans le quartier LacVert, en ville de Goma, a été tué le mardi 16 septembre après avoir été enlevé avec son fils.

La famille avait payé une rançon pour leur libération, mais seul le garçon a été relâché, rejoignant Mugunga le matin du 17 septembre à 6h, après un passage par Kimoka, a rapporté Dedesi Mitima, chef de quartier du Lac Vert, lors d’un entretien avec Kivumorningpost.

Selon Dedesi Mitima, le kidnapping a eu lieu entre le 12 et le 13 septembre. La rançon exigée par les ravisseurs a été entièrement fournie par la famille, mais malgré cela, Bulenda Siliro a été abattu.

r9-V-NK1-008.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that a group of at least ten men escaped mob justice on Wednesday 17 September 2025 in the Kalinda quarter of Mulekera commune, Beni city, after residents suspected and apprehended them; according to its sources the men, all from Ituri, were assimilated to M23-AFC rebels. It said the Congolese National Police intervened to save them and that the Mulekera mayor, Commissaire supérieur principal Ngongo Mayanga Dieudonné, said the competent services were questioning the suspects. Challenge Info quoted Ngongo Mayanga as saying it could not yet be confirmed whether they were rebels and that investigations were under way.
r9-V-NK1-008.l: Kalinda quarter, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-008.a: residents of Kalinda (mob); Congolese National Police intervened
r9-V-NK1-008.x: Kivu Morning Post: at least 10 men; Challenge Info: 10 men
r9-V-NK1-008.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-08 (second item in the post; the Goma killing is a separate claim). Two local outlets agree. A second Kivu Morning Post article of the same date says the suspects were released after being questioned (headline: 'libérés après identification par les autorités'); another KMP item says the governor condemned the assault on persons assimilated to the M23. Not cited.
r9-V-NK1-008.vn: Excerpts exact; two local outlets independently report the event. Narrowed 'told Challenge Info' to 'Challenge Info quoted' (the page says 'a-t-il déclaré', not that he spoke to the outlet); the police intervention is KMP's narration and is now attributed to the outlet, not the mayor.
src: Un groupe d’au moins 10 hommes a échappé à une justice populaire après avoir été suspecté et appréhendé par la population ce mercredi 17 septembre 2025 au quartier Kalinda, en commune de Mulekera, dans la ville de Beni (Nord-Kivu). Selon nos sources, ces hommes, venus tous de l’Ituri, province voisine, étaient assimilés aux rebelles du M23-AFC.

La police nationale congolaise est intervenue pour sauver ces vies. Le commissaire supérieur principal Ngongo Mayanga Dieudonné, bourgmestre de Mulekera, précise que les services compétents sont déjà en train d’auditionner les suspects.

Le commissaire supérieur Ngongo Mayanga a précisé que les services de sécurité procèdent actuellement à l’identification et à l’audition des suspects, ainsi que du propriétaire de la maison qu’ils occupaient en location. « Pour l’instant, nous ne pouvons pas confirmer s’ils sont des rebelles ou non. Les enquêtes sont en cours », a-t-il déclaré.

r9-V-NK1-009.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local sources, that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura, chief of Kiziba 2 village in Nyiragongo territory, was killed in the night from Monday to Tuesday 11 February with all the members of his family: armed bandits entered his home and opened fire, killing the chief, his wife and his three children, a boy and two girls. It said the perpetrators were not known and that civil society actors in Nyiragongo suspected a settling of scores resembling a targeted assassination. A second outlet, whose Kiziba II article is the second source cited here, reported that Kimanuka Musekura Prosper, chief of Kiziba II village in Mudja groupement, was killed in the night of Monday 10 to Tuesday 11 February 2025 with his wife and three children by heavily armed unknown persons, named the children as his son Benjamin and his daughters Sifa and Iragi, and said the five bodies were taken to a local morgue.
r9-V-NK1-009.l: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-009.a: armed bandits / unidentified heavily armed men (as the sources say)
r9-V-NK1-009.x: Radio Okapi: village chief, wife and three children killed; 7sur7.cd: village chief and wife and three children, five bodies taken to a morgue
r9-V-NK1-009.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-09. The post spells the village 'Kibiza II' and the daughter 'Safi'; the outlets print 'Kiziba 2/II' and 'Sifa'. Two outlets agree on wife and three children; Actualite.cd's account (next claim) counts four dead and does not mention the wife. Date: night 10-11 Feb 2025, within days after M23's capture of Goma; the area was then under M23 control, but no source attributes the killing to any armed group. The 7sur7 excerpt is cited as two passages of the same page.
r9-V-NK1-009.vn: Excerpts exact. The draft merged the two outlets' dates ('Monday 10 ... 2025' is 7sur7's wording; Radio Okapi prints 'lundi à ce mardi 11 février'); each date now sits with its outlet, and 'settling of scores' restored. The figure flag '7' is from the outlet name 7sur7.cd, not a figure. Two independent outlets (Radio Okapi, 7sur7.cd) agree on the killing of the chief, wife and three children: grade A. Note Actualite.cd (claim 9) counts four dead without the wife.
src: Le chef du village Kiziba 2, Prosper Kimanuka Musekura a été tué la nuit de lundi à ce mardi 11 février avec tous les membres de sa famille dans les environs de Goma. Les faits ont eu lieu dans le village même de Kiziba 2, au territoire de Nyiragongo, rapportent des sources locales.

Des bandits armés se sont introduits dans son domicile et ont ouvert le feu sur tous les membres de la famille. Le chef du village, sa femme et ses trois enfants, un garçon et deux filles, ont tous été tués.
Si les auteurs de ce meurtre ne sont pas connus, les acteurs de la société civile dans le territoire de Nyiragongo pensent à un règlement de compte qui ressemble à un assassinat ciblé.

Le chef du village Kiziba II dans le groupement Mudja en territoire de Nyiragongo (Nord-Kivu), Kimanuka Musekura Prosper, a été tué dans la nuit du lundi 10 à ce mardi 11 février 2025 avec sa femme et ses trois enfants par des inconnus lourdement armés.
à savoir son fils Benjamin et ses deux filles Sifa et Iragi. Les cinq corps ont été conduits dans une morgue de la place

r9-V-NK1-010.s: Actualite.cd reported that the chief of Kiziba 2 village in Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, was killed with his three children in the night of Monday to Tuesday 11 February 2025; according to its sources unidentified armed bandits entered the victims' home around 1:00 and fired on them. A relative speaking anonymously said four people had been killed for reasons not yet elucidated, that no one could say who committed the act, and that Prosper Kimanuka Musekura was among the dead.
r9-V-NK1-010.l: Kiziba 2 village, Mudja groupement, Nyiragongo territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-010.a: unidentified armed bandits (as the source says)
r9-V-NK1-010.x: Actualite.cd: four people killed (chief and three children); Radio Okapi and a second outlet: the chief's wife was also killed (five dead)
r9-V-NK1-010.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-09. Differs from Radio Okapi and 7sur7.cd on the wife (not mentioned here; the quoted relative says four dead). Kept as a separate claim for that reason.
r9-V-NK1-010.vn: Excerpts exact; the 2025 year is from the article's date line (mar 11/02/2025). Statement matches; the relative's anonymity is printed on the page. Actualite.cd counts four dead (chief and three children) and does not mention the wife; Radio Okapi and 7sur7.cd say five, including the wife. The page also notes Nyiragongo had been occupied by 'M23/RDF' since late January 2025 but attributes the killing to no one.
src: Le chef du village Kiziba 2 dans le groupement Mudja, dans le territoire de Nyiragongo (Nord-Kivu), a été tué dans la nuit de lundi à ce mardi 11 février, avec ses trois enfants.
Selon nos sources, des bandits armés non identifiés jusque-là, ont fait irruption dans le domicile des victimes, aux environs de 1h00 et ont tiré sur ces citoyens, avant de se retirer.

Malheureusement, ils ont tiré sur le chef Prosper Kimanuka Musekura qui est décédé. Ils ont tiré ensuite sur ses trois enfants dont deux filles et un garçon. Donc, ça fait quatre personnes qui viennent d'être lâchement tuées pour des raisons non encore élucidées. On ne sait pas dire avec exactitude qui a commis cet acte ignoble.

r9-V-NK1-011.s: Actualite.cd reported that four people were killed and several wounded in an armed attack on a pharmacy in the Katoyi quarter of Goma on the evening of Friday 16 May 2025, around 19:00 on Makengele avenue near the Katindo mosque; it said men in uniform, not yet identified, burst in and opened fire, killing the pharmacist and three of his customers, and took an unspecified sum of money and telephones. A resident of Maranatha avenue told the outlet the shooting was around 19:27.
r9-V-NK1-011.l: Makengele avenue, Katoyi quarter, near Katindo mosque (Maranatha avenue), Goma, North Kivu
r9-V-NK1-011.a: men in uniform, not yet identified (as the source says)
r9-V-NK1-011.x: Actualite.cd: four killed (the pharmacist and three customers), several wounded
r9-V-NK1-011.n: Video-lead cluster C-NK-10. Matches the posts (19:27, four dead, pharmacist and clients) though the outlet places it in Katoyi on Makengele avenue near the Katindo mosque rather than at the mosque entrance in Maranatha. No group is named; the page says only that Goma is 'sous occupation de l'AFC/M23'. A pharmacist was among those killed; the pharmacy is a private shop, not a hospital, so this is not coded as an attack on a health facility. No second outlet found.
r9-V-NK1-011.vn: Excerpts exact; statement matches the page (including 'men in uniform, not yet identified'; no group named). Grade B: one credible national outlet with its own resident witness, per the rubric's 'one credible non-partisan origin'.
src: ven 16/05/2025 - 20:26 Quatre personnes sont tuées et plusieurs autres blessées lors d'une attaque armée perpétrée dans la soirée de ce vendredi contre une pharmacie au quartier Katoyi, à Goma (Nord-Kivu). Le drame s’est produit aux environs de 19h00 sur l’avenue Makengele, à proximité de la mosquée de Katindo.

Des hommes en uniforme, non encore identifiés, ont fait irruption dans une pharmacie ouvrant le feu sur les personnes qui s’y trouvaient. Le pharmacien et trois de ses clients ont été tués sur le coup. Plusieurs autres ont été blessés, tandis que les assaillants ont emporté une somme d’argent non précisée ainsi que des téléphones.
« C’était vers 19h27. On a entendu des rafales de balles. Après, on a appris que tous ceux qui étaient à l’intérieur de la pharmacie avaient été tués »

r9-V-NK1-012.s: Enquete.cd reported that a 25-year-old man, missing since his arrest on 4 September 2025 in Goma, had been found dead and buried, according to information given to his relatives on 8 August. According to the testimony relayed by civil society actor and human rights defender Jules Ngeleza, Chubaka Buhendwa Josué Maroy had been arrested on alleged accusations of collaborating with the FDLR, and his arrest was reportedly carried out on the order of Sultani Makenga, military head of the M23. The outlet said the family said it learned of his death and burial from a security officer of the movement.
r9-V-NK1-012.a: M23 (as alleged by relatives and civil society)
r9-V-NK1-012.n: Found while searching C-NK-11/12 (Goma, Sept 2025 arrests and later body discoveries); not one of the cluster incidents. Allegation by relatives and a civil-society actor; the M23 response was not found. The same article says that in June 2026 two bodies were found in Lake Kivu amid residents' allegations of executions, and that the Goma communal youth council denounced bodies and abductions in June 2026.
r9-V-NK1-012.vn: Excerpts exact. Removed the year in '8 August 2026' (the excerpt prints only '8 août dernier'; the article is dated 10 August 2026), kept the conditional 'reportedly', and attributed the family's account as the page does. Allegation by relatives and a civil society actor; the order by Sultani Makenga is reported in the conditional. No M23 response found.
src: Un jeune homme de 25 ans, porté disparu depuis son arrestation le 4 septembre 2025 à Goma, a été retrouvé mort et inhumé, selon des informations communiquées à ses proches le 8 août dernier.

D’après le témoignage relayé par Jules Ngeleza, acteur de la société civile et défenseur des droits humains, Chubaka Buhendwa Josué Maroy avait été arrêté pour des accusations présumées de collaboration avec les FDLR. Son arrestation aurait été effectuée sur ordre de Sultani Makenga, responsable militaire du M23.

r9-V-NK2-001.s: Challenge Info reported that an agent in charge of dignified and safe burials in the Ebola response was violently assaulted on Wednesday 19 August 2026 in the city of Beni while recovering the body of a person presumed to have died of Ebola; Enquête News (enquetenews.info) reported that the agent of the response team against the Bundibugyo strain of Ebola was assaulted at Kasanga-Tuha, Beni, and, according to testimonies, would have been confronted by youths present at the place of death; DW summarised that a response agent had been violently assaulted in Beni.
r9-V-NK2-001.l: Kasanga-Tuha neighbourhood (Kasanga Tuha), Beni city, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-001.a: youths present at the place of death (as reported by Enquête News); not otherwise attributed
r9-V-NK2-001.x: Challenge Info: one agent assaulted; Enquête News: one agent assaulted, circumstances and state of health not yet established
r9-V-NK2-001.n: Cluster C-NK-02 (video lead; posts not cited). Date of the Beni assault is printed in the Challenge Info and Enquête News texts (Wednesday 19 August 2026). The post said around 19/20 August. No existing claim on Ebola response attacks in Beni found with claim_search.
r9-V-NK2-001.vn: All three pages print what is attributed; Challenge Info page also prints 'récupérer le corps d’une personne présumée décédée d’Ebola'. Enquête News keeps the conditional ('aurait été pris à partie').
src: Un agent chargé de l’enterrement digne et sécurisé des dépouilles dans le cadre de la riposte contre Ebola a été violemment agressé ce mercredi 19 août 2026 dans la ville de Beni, au Nord-Kivu.

Selon les témoignages , l’agent intervenait sur le lieu après décès d’un patient pour l’évacuation de la dépouille conformément aux mesures prévues dans le cadre de la riposte contre Ebola. Alors qu’il accomplissait son intervention, il aurait été pris à partie par des jeunes présents sur le lieu du décès.
Un agent de l’équipe de la riposte contre la souche BUNDIBUGYO de l’épidémie d’Ebola a été agressé mercredi 19 août 2026 dernier au quartier Kasanga-Tuha, à Beni, au Nord-Kivu.

Ces derniers jours, plusieurs incidents ont visé les équipes de santé, notamment la violente agression d'un agent de la riposte à Beni et l'attaque d'une équipe lors d'un enterrement dans le Haut-Uélé.

r9-V-NK2-002.s: Kivu Morning Post reported that on 19 August 2026 at about 09:00 a Red Cross team deployed for awareness and intervention activities in the Kasanga Tuha neighbourhood, Mulekera commune, Beni, was confronted by the population, who according to witnesses accused the humanitarian team amid a high number of reported deaths; a Red Cross agent identified as Querrin was assaulted but reportedly came out "sain et sauf", and the toll also lists three other victims receiving care at the Beni General Referral Hospital.
r9-V-NK2-002.l: Kasanga Tuha, Mulekera commune, Beni city, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-002.x: Kivu Morning Post: one Red Cross agent assaulted, "three other victims" at Beni General Referral Hospital
r9-V-NK2-002.n: Same neighbourhood and date as the Challenge Info / Enquête News assault (possibly the same incident described differently: Red Cross team vs. burial agent). Not merged. Kivu Morning Post is a Goma-based outlet.
r9-V-NK2-002.vn: Every clause on the page; name 'Querrin' printed; possibly the same incident as claim 0 told differently, kept separate.
ent: Hôpital Général de Référence de Beni
src: La journée du mercredi 19 août 2026 a été fortement perturbée dans le quartier Kasanga Tuha, en commune de Mulekera à Beni, au Nord-Kivu.

Vers 09h00, une équipe de la Croix-Rouge déployée pour des activités de sensibilisation et d’intervention a été prise à partie par la population. Selon des témoins sur place, les habitants, inquiets et en colère face au nombre élevé de morts signalés, ont accusé l’équipe humanitaire.

Un agent de la Croix-Rouge, identifié sous le nom de Querrin, a été agressé au cours de l’incident. D’après les premières informations, il est sorti « sain et sauf ». Le bilan fait également état de trois autres victimes. Elles poursuivent actuellement des soins à l’Hôpital Général de Référence de Beni.

r9-V-NK2-003.s: Enquête.cd reported that youths attacked and stoned on Monday 24 August a morgue of a health facility in Beni, North Kivu, before forcibly extracting a body, at a time when the DRC faces an Ebola epidemic; RTEE Kivu reported that a group of youths forced their way on Monday 24 August 2026 into the morgue of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni and took away a body, and that according to first information they reportedly removed it without respecting the planned sanitary formalities.
r9-V-NK2-003.l: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-003.x: Enquête.cd: one body removed; RTEE Kivu: one body removed
r9-V-NK2-003.n: Cluster C-NK-03. The post date (24 August 2026) matches both outlets. Dr Katembo Ngalika (ACP) says this was the third attack on this morgue since the outbreak began; see the following claim. Local outlets: RTEE Kivu (Beni), Enquête.cd.
r9-V-NK2-003.vn: RTEE prints the 'sans respecter les formalités sanitaires' clause as conditional on first information ('auraient'); narrowed to keep the hedge.
src: Des jeunes ont attaqué et caillassé lundi 24 août une morgue d’une structure sanitaire à Beni, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, avant d’en extraire de force un corps.
L’incident intervient alors que la République démocratique du Congo fait face à une épidémie d’Ebola qui continue de mobiliser les autorités sanitaires.
Un groupe de jeunes s’est introduit de force, lundi 24 août 2026, dans la morgue du Centre médical Ruwenzori, à Beni, avant d’emporter une dépouille.

r9-V-NK2-004.s: ACP (Agence Congolaise de Presse) reported that Dr Katembo Ngalika, medical director of the Centre médical Ruwenzori in Beni, said that youths came with brutality, broke doors and windows, and that the two people in the morgue were intimidated and beaten, and that the youths took the body in violation of the response norms; he said it was the third attack on this morgue since the start of the Ebola epidemic in the region and that no particular security arrangement had been put around the clinic despite alerts.
r9-V-NK2-004.l: Centre médical Ruwenzori, Beni city, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-004.x: ACP quoting Dr Katembo Ngalika: two people present in the morgue intimidated and beaten; third attack on this morgue since the outbreak began
r9-V-NK2-004.n: ACP is the Congolese state press agency; the account is the facility director's. Adds to the previous claim (same event).
r9-V-NK2-004.vn: Statement unchanged; excerpts extended so that the 'violation des normes de la riposte' and 'absence de dispositif sécuritaire' clauses rest on stored text. Director's own account via state agency ACP.
src: « Nous avons été déçus. Ils sont venus avec brutalité. Ils ont cassé les portes, les vitres et, comme il n’y avait que deux personnes à la morgue, elles ont été intimidées et frappées.

a déclaré le Dr Katembo Ngalika, médecin directeur du Centre médical Ruwenzori. Selon ce responsable médical, il s’agit de la troisième attaque enregistrée contre la morgue de cette structure depuis le début de l’épidémie de la maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) dans la région.

r9-V-NK2-005.s: Enquête.cd reported that the military governor of North Kivu, Major General Evariste Somo Kakule, had recently warned that anyone who obstructed Ebola response operations or attacked the agents mobilised would be severely punished.
r9-V-NK2-005.a: Government of the DRC (North Kivu military governor)
r9-V-NK2-005.n: Relayed warning; date not given in the excerpt.
r9-V-NK2-005.vn: Excerpt carries the whole statement; date of the warning not given ('récemment').
src: Le gouverneur militaire du Nord-Kivu, le général-major Evariste Somo Kakule, avait récemment averti que toute personne qui entraverait les opérations de riposte contre Ebola ou s’en prendrait aux agents mobilisés serait sévèrement sanctionnée.

r9-V-NK2-006.s: Radio Okapi reported that a viral video shows Beni youths armed with bladed weapons manhandling Ebola response agents, one victim being a woman seen receiving blows from sticks.
r9-V-NK2-006.a: youths of Beni (as shown in a video described by Radio Okapi)
r9-V-NK2-006.n: Describes a video as reported by Radio Okapi; date of the incident not given; related precedent to the August incidents.
r9-V-NK2-006.vn: Removed the publication date added to the statement (not in the excerpt); incident date unknown.
src: Une vidéo, devenue virale, montre des jeunes de Beni, munis d'armes blanches, en train de molester des agents commis à la riposte contre Ebola. Une des victimes est une dame qu'on aperçoit en train de recevoir des coups de bâtons d'une violence aveugle.

r9-V-NK2-007.s: La Voix de l'UCG (lavoixdelucg.cd) reported that, according to Dr Kalima Nzanzu, president of the cell of doctors of the Grand Nord, pillaging in some hospitals, displacement of health staff and abandonment of patients, notably those with mental disorders, made an alarming picture; he said many doctors who worked in referral health centres and hospitals were now displaced in Butembo without work, that these centres were closed and, though deserted, had been pillaged, and he named the centres of Luofu and Muhangi and said the situation at Alimbongo was even more critical.
r9-V-NK2-007.l: Luofu, Muhangi, Alimbongo (Lubero territory) and Butembo, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-007.a: ADF and M23 conflict (as framed by the source); pillagers not identified
r9-V-NK2-007.n: Cluster C-NK-04. The original report dates from 23 January 2025 (statement made at a medical day held on a Sunday in Butembo); the video-lead post of 10 February 2025 repeats it. Same author (Georges Kisando) as the X post. Related existing records REC-0951 and REC-1242 concern the 15 January 2025 ADF killing at Muhangi and fighting at Luofu, not the health structures. No independent second outlet fetched (rtvh.net page blocked/empty; MSF 16 Jan 2025 on Lubero not fetched).
r9-V-NK2-007.vn: Removed the publication date from the statement; S1 extended to the doctor's opening sentence (the 'many doctors from referral centres' clause). Statement given at a medical day in Butembo 'ce dimanche' (page, 23 January 2025). Perpetrators of the pillaging not named. The pillagers are not identified; the outlet frames the crisis as caused by ADF massacres and the M23 war.
src: Pillages dans certains hôpitaux, déplacement du personnel soignant, et abandon des patients, notamment ceux souffrant de troubles mentaux, constituent un tableau alarmant, selon le Dr Kalima Nzanzu, président de la cellule des médecins du Grand Nord.
Ces centres sont désormais fermés, et ces médecins se retrouvent pratiquement en déplacement dans la ville de Butembo, sans emploi. En outre, ces centres, bien que désertés, ont été pillés.
On peut citer les centres de Luofu et de Muhangi. Quant à Alimbongo, la situation est encore plus critique.

r9-V-NK2-008.s: Radio Okapi reported, citing local humanitarian organisations, that at least ten people were abducted, two others killed and several goods pillaged between Tuesday and Wednesday 24 June in Rutshuru territory, in at least six localities; on Wednesday morning at least seven people were abducted between 9h and 10h on the Kibirizi–Rwindi (at Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu road axes, among them three motorcycle-taxi drivers and their clients, and the attackers also took at least eighteen packages of fish from Vitshumbi; the perpetrators of these abductions remained unknown.
r9-V-NK2-008.l: Kibirizi–Rwindi axis (Butindiri) and Kibirizi–Kibingu axis, Rutshuru territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-008.x: Radio Okapi: at least 10 abducted and 2 killed across six localities between Tuesday and Wednesday; at least 7 abducted on the two axes on Wednesday morning, including three motorcycle-taxi drivers; at least 18 packages of fish taken
r9-V-NK2-008.n: Cluster C-NK-13. The pro-AFC/M23 post attributes the abductions to FDLR, FARDC and Wazalendo and mentions ransom releases; Radio Okapi attributes them to nobody and does not mention ransom. The date of the weekday (Wednesday 24 June) is stated by the article ("mardi et mercredi 24 juin"). Existing records REC-0900 (Bwito, July-August 2026) and r1-NKS-2025Q4-007 (19 Dec 2025 on the same axis) are different incidents.
r9-V-NK2-008.vn: Removed the year the excerpt does not print; 'perpetrators unknown' narrowed to the abductions as the page says ('auteurs de ces enlèvements'). The two killed are, per the page, a woman and child hit by stray bullets in AFC-M23/FDLR clashes (not in excerpts, so not stated).
src: Au moins dix personnes ont été enlevées, deux autres tuées et plusieurs biens pillés entre mardi et mercredi 24 juin dans le territoire de Rutshuru, au Nord-Kivu, à la suite d’une série d’incidents sécuritaires signalés dans au moins six localités.

Selon des organisations humanitaires locales, ces événements incluent des braquages routiers, des incursions armées et des affrontements entre groupes armés, aggravant une situation sécuritaire déjà préoccupante.

Ces organisations rapportent que mercredi matin, au moins sept personnes ont été enlevées entre 9h et 10h locales sur les axes routiers Kibirizi–Rwindi (au niveau de Butindiri) et Kibirizi–Kibingu. Parmi les victimes figurent trois conducteurs de moto-taxi et leurs clients.
Les assaillants ont également emporté au moins dix-huit colis de poissons en provenance de Vitshumbi. Les auteurs de ces enlèvements restent inconnus à ce stade.

r9-V-NK2-009.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that the mining town of Rubaya (Masisi territory) was hit on the night of Saturday 23 to Sunday 24 May 2026 by several explosions attributed by residents to military aircraft; a first strike allegedly targeted a hotel facility known as Rubaya's Guest House, causing several injuries and significant property damage according to local sources, and a second strike allegedly hit an outlying grazing area, destroying several homes and causing livestock losses; local civil society denounced shelling affecting inhabited areas far from the front lines.
r9-V-NK2-009.a: military aircraft (attribution by residents; not further specified by the source)
r9-V-NK2-009.x: SOS Médias Burundi: "several injuries" at the guest house; no death toll printed
r9-V-NK2-009.n: Cluster C-NK-14. ALREADY RECORDED: r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi, 25 May 2026: strike around 00:15 on a guest house in Rubaya, origin undetermined, claimed by no party). This claim adds injuries, the second strike and civil-society reaction. The pro-AFC/M23 claim of 189 civilians killed is NOT supported by either source (no death toll printed). SOS Médias also notes the AFC/M23 statement of 24 May named Rumangabo, Minembwe and Kalehe (not Rubaya) and that no Congolese official response had been published; "The information advanced by the various parties could not be independently verified."
r9-V-NK2-009.vn: Excerpts carry every clause with the source's hedges ('allegedly', 'according to local sources'); no toll printed (the 189 figure from the lead is unsupported). Adds to r1-ATR-NK-2026-006 (Radio Okapi), not a duplicate.
src: the mining town of Rubaya was hit on the night of Saturday 23 to Sunday 24 May 2026 by several explosions attributed by residents to military aircraft, in a context of resurgence of fighting between the FARDCM/23. A first strike allegedly targeted a hotel facility known as Rubaya’s Guest House, causing several injuries and significant property damage, according to local sources.

A second strike would then hit an outlying grazing area, causing the destruction of several homes and livestock losses. The local civil society denounces shelling affecting inhabited areas far from the front lines

r9-V-NK2-010.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that in a statement issued on 24 May the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu, claiming that Rumangabo (Rutshuru) and the Virunga National Park eco-guards camp were targeted by CH-4 drones, and recalling bombings in Minembwe and Kalehe causing civilian casualties; the AFC/M23 described the operations as "war crimes". SOS Médias added that at the time of publication no official response from the Congolese authorities had been made public and that the information could not be independently verified.
r9-V-NK2-010.a: AFC/M23 (statement); accused: DRC Armed Forces and allies
r9-V-NK2-010.n: AFC/M23 party account. Overlaps r1-NKS-2026Q2-007 (Kivu Morning Post, Kanyuka statement on Rumangabo); this is an additional independent relay and records the absence of an official Kinshasa response as of 27 May 2026.
r9-V-NK2-010.vn: Party account kept as 'AFC/M23 accused/claims'; 'war crimes' is the party's quoted wording. Different relay from r1-NKS-2026Q2-007, adds Minembwe/Kalehe and the no-response note.
src: In a statement issued on May 24, the AFC/M23 accused the DRC Armed Forces and their allies of conducting a series of air strikes in North Kivu and South Kivu. The movement claims that Rumangabo, in Rutshuru territory, as well as the camp of the eco-guards of the Virunga National Park, were allegedly targeted by CH-4 fighter drones.

It also recalls bombings in several towns of Minembwe and Kalehe, causing civilian casualties and material destruction. The AFC/M23 describes these operations as “war crimes” and accuses the Congolese government of targeting inhabited areas.

At the time of publication, no official response from the Congolese authorities had been made public regarding these allegations. The information advanced by the various parties could not be independently verified.

r9-V-NK2-011.s: Radio Elimu UOR (Butembo) reported that presumed ADF carried out a deadly incursion in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May 2026 in Beni territory and that local civil society spoke of 24 people killed in the villages Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi and Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku locality, Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni-Mbau sector), according to KINOS KATUO; the vice-president of civil society in Oïcha commune, Samuel MAHAMBA, said 19 bodies had been counted at the morgue and feared the toll would rise; Enquête.cd reported at least 24 civilians killed in an attack attributed to the ADF, with bodies taken to the Oïcha morgue and others missing.
r9-V-NK2-011.l: Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi, Mangambo (Babila-Bakaiku, Batangi-Mbau), Beni territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-011.x: Radio Elimu UOR (civil society): 24 killed, 19 bodies counted at the morgue; Enquête.cd: at least 24 civilians killed (provisional); existing record r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008 (Radio Okapi): at least 26
r9-V-NK2-011.n: Cluster C-NK-15. ALREADY RECORDED in r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008 (Radio Okapi, at least 26 killed, night of Tuesday to Wednesday 6 May, same farming blocks). The video-lead post says "night of 6-7 May"; the sources say the night of 5-6 May (Enquête.cd prints "la nuit du mercredi 6 mai"). The 24 figure is the civil-society count; 26 includes 2 killed at Katerrain the previous night per Radio Elimu. Radio Elimu adds that presumed ADF were also accused of killing two inhabitants of Katerrain on the night of 4-5 May ("26 morts en 2 jours"), not used in the statement.
r9-V-NK2-011.vn: Date and 'présumés ADF' are printed on the Radio Elimu page, not in the stored excerpt: S0 extended. Fear of a rising toll moved to a quote. Tolls kept per source (24 / 19 at the morgue / at least 24); Radio Okapi's 26 in r4-G-LOCAL-NK-008 is not merged (Radio Elimu's own 26 adds two killed at Katerrain on 4-5 May).
src: La société civile parle de 24 personnes tuées par l’ennemi. L’information nous est livrée par le Président de la Société civile à Mamove et environs en territoire de Beni. Selon KINOS KATUO, l’ennemi a opéré dans les villages Manzungu, Musangwa, Wasafi et Mangambo en localité Babila-Bakaiku, groupement Batangi-Mbau, secteur de Beni-Mbau.

Samuel MAHAMBA, vice-Président de la Société civile, forces vives, en commune de Oïcha, fait constater que la plupart des victimes sont des citoyens qui habitaient le chef-lieu du territoire de Beni. « Nous venons de compter 19 corps déposés à la morgue.

Au moins 24 civils ont été tués dans la nuit du mercredi 6 mai 2026 lors d’une nouvelle attaque attribuée aux rebelles des Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) dans le territoire de Beni, au Nord-Kivu, selon des sources locales et des membres de la société civile.

Des responsables locaux indiquent que plusieurs corps ont déjà été acheminés à la morgue d’Oïcha, chef-lieu du territoire de Beni. Le bilan reste toutefois provisoire, car plusieurs personnes sont encore portées disparues, laissant craindre une augmentation du nombre de victimes dans les prochaines heures.

r9-V-NK2-012.s: 24News Agency reported that an attack attributed to ADF fighters in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 simultaneously targeted the Matete, Kitoho and Mamuli neighbourhoods of Mbau (Beni territory), killing at least sixteen civilians, burning houses and motorcycles and carrying off an undetermined number of people; at Matete the victims were surprised while taking part in a wake (veillée mortuaire), the attackers burned a hut and three motorcycles before killing people, and the toll in that neighbourhood reached nine; at least seven were killed at Kitoho.
r9-V-NK2-012.l: Matete, Kitoho, Mamuli neighbourhoods, Mbau, Batangi-Mbau, Beni territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-012.x: 24News Agency: at least 16 killed (9 at Matete, at least 7 at Kitoho); undetermined number taken away. Actualite.cd (4 June): 21 killed after further bodies found. Congo Quotidien / Guardian: about 10 provisional
r9-V-NK2-012.n: Cluster C-NK-16. The video-lead post (survivors) says ADF infiltrated a mourning gathering with weapons hidden in mats and killed about ten; 24News confirms the wake at Matete and a toll of at least 16 (9 at Matete); the detail about weapons hidden in mats was NOT found in any fetched source. Not previously recorded (claim_search on Mbau for May-June 2026 returned nothing). 24News Agency is a Congolese online outlet; the byline is Gires Kasongo.
r9-V-NK2-012.vn: Excerpts carry every clause; 'attributed to' ADF kept. Weapons-in-mats detail from the lead not found and not included.
src: une nouvelle attaque attribuée aux combattants de l’ADF dans la nuit du mardi au mercredi 3 juin 2026. Les assaillants ont simultanément pris pour cible les quartiers Matete, Kitoho et Mamuli, où ils ont tué au moins seize civils, incendié des maisons ainsi que des motos, et emporté un nombre encore indéterminé de personnes.

Au quartier Matete, les victimes ont été surprises alors qu’elles participaient à une veillée mortuaire. Les assaillants ont incendié une paillote et trois motos avant de tuer des personnes. Trois corps ont été retrouvés sur les lieux de l’attaque, tandis que d’autres dépouilles ont été découvertes par la suite, portant à neuf le bilan dans ce quartier.
À Kitoho, au moins sept personnes ont été tuées, des maisons incendiées et une moto réduite en cendres.

r9-V-NK2-013.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to details given by local civil society on Thursday 4 June, the toll of the Mbau attack had risen from 16 to 21 dead after four bodies were found towards Kingeste and a fifth near Ngite, with several other civilians still missing; the page adds that in three days the ADF had killed more than 40 people in attacks on the city and territory of Beni and had taken several civilians hostage.
r9-V-NK2-013.l: Mbau (Kingeste, Ngite), Beni territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-013.x: Actualite.cd (local civil society): 21 dead (up from 16); more than 40 killed in three days across Beni city and territory
r9-V-NK2-013.n: Updated toll for the same event as the 24News claim.
r9-V-NK2-013.vn: Removed the publication date added as 'reported on 4 June 2026'; the civil society update is dated 'jeudi 4 juin' in the excerpt.
src: Les précisions fournies par la société civile locale ce jeudi 4 juin indiquent que quatre des corps découverts ont été localisés vers la zone de Kingeste, tandis que le cinquième a été retrouvé près de Ngite. Ce qui fait grimper le bilan de 16 à 21 morts alors que plusieurs autres civils restent disparus.

En trois jours, les ADF ont tué plus de 40 personnes dans les attaques contre la ville et le territoire de Beni. Les assaillants ont également pris en otage plusieurs civils qui demeurent en captivité

r9-V-NK2-014.s: Congo Quotidien reported that an attack attributed to ADF rebels in the night of Tuesday to Wednesday 3 June 2026 hit the localities of Matété, Mamuli and Kitoho (Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory), causing the death of about ten people according to a provisional toll from local civil society; The Guardian wrote that at least 10 people were massacred in raids on those three villages and that the ADF has been blamed.
r9-V-NK2-014.l: Matété, Mamuli, Kitoho (Mbau), Batangi-Mbau groupement, Beni territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-014.x: Congo Quotidien: about ten dead (provisional, civil society); The Guardian: at least 10 massacred
r9-V-NK2-014.n: The Guardian byline is Prosper Heri Ngorora in Goma; the Guardian page does not carry a wire credit. Early provisional toll; superseded by the 16 and 21 figures (see other Mbau claims).
r9-V-NK2-014.vn: Punctuation fixed; tolls kept per source (about ten, provisional, civil society; at least 10, Guardian).
src: Une attaque attribuée aux rebelles ADF a frappé trois villages du territoire de Beni, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, dans la nuit du mardi au mercredi 3 juin 2026.

Les localités de Matété, Mamuli et Kitoho, situées dans le groupement Batangi-Mbau, ont été la cible d’une incursion simultanée qui a causé la mort d’une dizaine de personnes, selon un bilan provisoire communiqué par la société civile locale.

At least 10 people were massacred in raids on three villages around the city of Beni, in North Kivu, in the early hours of Wednesday morning. The Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), a militia affiliated to Islamic State , has been blamed for the attacks on the villages of Matété, Mamuli and Kitoho in eastern DRC.

r9-V-NK2-015.s: The Guardian reported that just before midnight on Saturday the militia entered Beni, where people were beheaded and others shot, causing widespread panic and sending hundreds of people running into the bush; more than 20 men, women and children were reported killed and dozens missing, according to witnesses.
r9-V-NK2-015.d: 2026-05-30 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
r9-V-NK2-015.a: the militia (identified elsewhere in the article as the ADF)
r9-V-NK2-015.x: The Guardian: more than 20 killed and dozens missing according to witnesses
r9-V-NK2-015.n: Related event found while searching Mbau. 24News Agency (3 June) places the Beni city (Ngadi) massacres three days before Mbau; SOS Médias Burundi (1 June 2026, seen in results, not fetched) reported at least 17 civilians killed in under 24 hours. The "Saturday" is computed from the Guardian's publication date (Thursday 4 June 2026). No existing record found with claim_search.
r9-V-NK2-015.vn: Removed the article date the statement had added; the excerpt says only 'Saturday'. Ngandi appears on the page (not in the statement). The Guardian names the ADF elsewhere on the page; a resident calls it 'an attack carried out by the ADF'.
src: Just before midnight on Saturday, the militia entered Beni, which has been under DRC military administration since 2021. People were beheaded and others shot in the attack, which caused widespread panic and sent hundreds of people running from their homes into the bush.
More than 20 men, women and children, were reported killed and dozens missing, according to witnesses.

r9-V-NK2-016.s: The Guardian reported that the military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after the Saturday attacks.
r9-V-NK2-016.d: 2026-06-02 (date computed from weekday and publication date)
r9-V-NK2-016.n: Health-care context: insecurity (ADF attack on Beni city) linked to patients leaving Ebola treatment centres.
src: The military governor of North Kivu said in a statement on Tuesday that three patients confirmed to have Ebola had fled treatment centres in Beni after Saturday’s attacks.

r9-V-NK2-017.s: Labeur (labeur.info) reported that the Consortium International pour les Droits de l’Homme au Congo (CIDHC), in a report made public on Monday 4 May 2026, said it had documented civilians killed without investigation, citizens beaten to humiliation, and men and women arrested without warrant, detained without trial and released on payment; according to the CIDHC, at Walo Uruba (in the Kiraku locality) and at Shempunu, populations were allegedly beaten, locked up and forced to pay money on the pretext of not having shown a "salongo" token.
r9-V-NK2-017.l: Walo Uruba (Kiraku locality) and Shempunu, Walikale territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK2-017.a: not named by the source (the CIDHC report, as relayed, blames abuse of administrative authority)
r9-V-NK2-017.n: Cluster C-NK-21. Allegation by an NGO (CIDHC) about government-held Walikale; the pro-AFC/M23 post relayed it. The post spelled the locality "Walowa Uroba"; the page prints "Walo Uruba". The Goma-presentation detail and the name Jean-Paul Ngahangondi were not found on any fetched page. Kivu7.net and newsdrc.com versions could not be fetched. No response from authorities found.
r9-V-NK2-017.vn: Statement supported; actor field corrected: the page names no perpetrator for these acts and does not say 'armed men in government-held Walikale' (the report says 'L’autorité administrative est utilisée pour fabriquer une faute').
ent: Consortium International pour les Droits de l’Homme au Congo
src: Le Consortium International pour les Droits de l’Homme au Congo (CIDHC) alerte sur le piétinement de l’État de droit et les violations des droits humains dans le territoire de Walikale, en province du Nord-Kivu.
Dans son rapport, rendu public ce lundi 04 mai 2026, le CIDHC affirme qu’un système organisé de violence, d’extorsion et d’impunité fonctionne au grand jour dans cette entité.

Le consortium indique avoir documenté plusieurs cas, notamment : des civils tués sans enquêtes ; des citoyens battus jusqu’à l’humiliation ; des hommes et femmes arrêtés sans mandat, puis détenus sans jugement, avant d’être libérés moyennant paiement.
