r9-V-NK3-009.s: Imvahonshya (Rwanda) reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, confirmed on social media that an FDLR fighter known as Yoweri, nicknamed Tokyo, had been captured in fighting in Masisi; the outlet said news of his capture began circulating on social media on Friday 24 October 2025, when he was said to have been captured by AFC/M23 fighters.
r9-V-NK3-009.n: Cluster C-NK-23. Rwandan outlet (Imvahonshya); cited only for what the AFC/M23 official said. No independent (non-Rwandan, non-AFC/M23) report found; no Kinshasa or FDLR reaction found. The Igihe English page could not be fetched (page_text via=none).
r9-V-NK3-009.vn: Excerpts and page match; attribution to Manzi and to social-media reports kept as printed; 'FDLR' is in the page title. Rwandan state-aligned outlet relaying an AFC/M23 official; the capture is AFC/M23's account. The date is when news of the capture began circulating, not the capture date. No independent, Kinshasa or FDLR account found.
src: Visi Guverineri wa Kivu y’Amajyaruguru washyizweho n’umutwe wa AFC/M23 Willy Manzi, yemeje ayo makuru ashimangira ko iyo ndwanyi yafatiwe ku rugamba i Masisi.

Amakuru y’uwo murwanyi uzwi ku izina rya Yoweri wamamaye nka Tokyo, yatangiye gukwirakwira ku mbuga nkoranyambaga ku wa Gatanu tariki ya 24 Ukwakira 2025, aho bivugwa ko yafashwe n’abarwanyi ba AFC/M23.

r9-V-NK3-010.s: Imvahonshya reported that Willy Manzi, the North Kivu deputy governor appointed by AFC/M23, said on social media that Yoweri, alias Tokyo, together with others including Jean-Marie of the Nyatura group, Tiger and Ignace Dunia, had committed terrible crimes including rape, killings and the burning of countless houses; this is an allegation by an AFC/M23 official.
r9-V-NK3-010.l: Masisi, North Kivu (place of alleged crimes not stated in the quote)
r9-V-NK3-010.n: Cluster C-NK-23. Unverified allegation by a party official; no dates, places or victims given. Umuseke (below) adds that the same allegations of rape, killing and burning of homes, especially against Tutsi in Burungu and Kibarizo in October 2023, were made by the outlet itself (pre-2025, not used).
r9-V-NK3-010.vn: Statement kept; date changed to the window in which the statement was made (news circulated from 24 Oct; article 26 Oct), since the page does not date Manzi's post. Unverified allegation by an AFC/M23 official, relayed by a Rwandan state-aligned outlet; no date, place or victim is given for the alleged crimes. The '23' flag is from 'AFC/M23'.
src: Afatanyije n’abandi barimo Jean-Marie wo mu mutwe wa Nyatura, Tiger na Ignace Dunia, uyu mugabo yakoze ibyaha biteye ubwoba birimo gufata ku ngufu, ubwicanyi, no gutwika inzu zitagira ingano.

r9-V-NK3-011.s: Umuseke (Rwanda) reported that an AFC/M23 fighter, Col. Samuel Nsabimana Mwendangabo, said Tokyo had been shot in the leg and then captured, and that he would first be treated; the colonel said he was captured 'aho bita i Muzimu'.
r9-V-NK3-011.x: one fighter captured, wounded in the leg
r9-V-NK3-011.n: Cluster C-NK-23. Rwandan outlet; statement attributed to the AFC/M23 officer. The same page says some residents disagreed that he should be treated, and that AFC/M23 had not yet said what it would do with him ('Kugeza ubu ntacyo AFC/M23 iravuga izakoresha uyu mugabo'). Pro-AFC/M23 video post carried the same alias.
r9-V-NK3-011.vn: Statement supported; date changed from the publication date to the month, since the capture date is not stated. AFC/M23 officer's account via a Rwandan outlet. Umuseke places the capture in Masisi territory 'this week' (its own narration: 'Tokyo yafatiwe muri Teritwari ya Masisi muri Kivu ya Ruguru'); it also says AFC/M23 had not said what it would do with him.
src: Cyakora umurwanyi wa AFC/M23 witwa Col. Samuel Nsabimana Mwendangabo yavuze ko uyu Tokyo yarashwe akaguru, ubundi baramufata, kandi babanza kumuvura
Bamufatiye aho bita i Muzimu, ntabwo tumwica,

r9-V-NK3-012.s: Dépêche.cd reported that FARDC military intelligence services announced in Beni the interception of a truck carrying several sacks of hemp and that, according to the Congolese army, the cargo allegedly belonged to an AFC-M23 commander identified as Zimurinda Innocent, based in Rutshuru territory.
r9-V-NK3-012.a: FARDC; AFC-M23 commander named by the army
r9-V-NK3-012.n: Cluster C-NK-24. The post (20 May) spelled the name 'Zimuhinda', said the driver named the owner, and said the commander was RDF/M23; the page spells it 'Zimurinda Innocent', does not mention Goma or the driver, and attributes the ownership claim to the army. Date: page dated 19 May 2026 and says 'mardi' (19 May 2026 is a Tuesday). No AFC/M23 reaction found.
r9-V-NK3-012.vn: Narrowed: the announcement is credited on the page to the military intelligence services, not to the Sukola 1 spokesperson; conditional 'appartiendrait' kept as 'allegedly'. The FARDC's allegation only ('appartiendrait'); no AFC/M23 reaction found. Existing r1-UCD-M23-BRIGADES-012 names a Colonel Innocent Zimurinda in the AFC/M23 command; identity not established by this page.
src: Par ailleurs, les services de renseignements militaires ont annoncé l’interception d’un camion transportant plusieurs sacs de chanvre. Selon l’armée congolaise, cette cargaison appartiendrait à un commandant de l’AFC-M23 identifié comme Zimurinda Innocent, basé dans le territoire de Rutshuru.

r9-V-NK3-013.s: Dépêche.cd reported that the FARDC presented in Beni, on Tuesday, 'plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l'AFC-M23', among them Byamungu Zembezembe Jean-Pierre, from South Kivu, arrested in the Matongé district in central Beni; Matofali Bushu Arsène, described by the army as a member of the armed group FFPP/AP of Kabido; and a young woman, Kavira Léa, whom the military authorities say was recruited by Katembo Ndalieni, former mayor of Goma under the rebel administration.
r9-V-NK3-013.n: Cluster C-NK-24. Reported only from the army's presentation; no independent check of the accusations; no court or defence account found. The post spoke of 'alleged Rwandan spies'; the page speaks of alleged AFC-M23 collaborators. The article also mentions Paluku Kisaka Yereyere and Mapenzi Mike as contacts alleged by the army, and gives a long army description of Byamungu Zembezembe (Uvira 2023 candidate); not used in the statement.
r9-V-NK3-013.vn: Statement extended to the two other presented people listed in victims_named (each printed in an excerpt); the 'unverified' caveat moved to the note; spelling 'Matongé' as printed. The FARDC's account of a presentation of detainees: the accusations are the army's and unverified; no court, defence or AFC/M23 account found. Being named is not a finding of responsibility.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont présenté, mardi à Beni, dans la province du Nord-Kivu, plusieurs personnes accusées de collaborer avec les rebelles de l’AFC-M23.
Parmi les personnes présentées figure Byamungu Zembezembe Jean-Pierre, originaire du Sud-Kivu et interpellé dans le quartier Matongé, au centre-ville de Beni.
Un autre suspect présenté à la presse est Matofali Bushu Arsène, décrit par l’armée comme membre du groupe armé FFPP/AP de Kabido.

Une jeune femme, Kavira Léa, a également été présentée. Les autorités militaires affirment qu’elle aurait été recrutée par Katembo Ndalieni, ancien maire de Goma sous l’administration rebelle et actuel administrateur de Lubero pour le compte du mouvement AFC-M23.

r9-V-NK3-014.s: Actualite.cd reported that at least two civilians died on Friday 3 January 2025 in bombardments that hit homes in the Renga district of the Bweremana agglomeration, Masisi, and three others were wounded by shrapnel in Kashenda district; according to local civil society, the bombs were launched by the M23 from the lines of fighting against local 'wazalendo' fighters.
r9-V-NK3-014.l: Renga and Kashenda districts, Bweremana, Masisi territory, North Kivu
r9-V-NK3-014.x: Actualite.cd: au moins deux civils morts; trois autres personnes blessées at Kashenda
r9-V-NK3-014.n: Cluster C-NK-29: the post (3 Jan) said M23-Wazalendo fighting on Ndumba hills near Bweremana and residents carrying two bodies of bomb victims; Actualite.cd corroborates. The 'at least two killed' is the outlet's figure; the quoted civil-society president speaks of two women killed and three injured at Renga plus 'three wounded' at Kashenda. Journal's own phrase: M23 'coalition M23/RDF' is used in the same article for 2 Jan assaults.
r9-V-NK3-014.vn: Both excerpts on the page; statement keeps the toll as 'at least two' and the M23 attribution as civil society's. The attribution to the M23 is local civil society's, as the outlet reports it. The quoted civil-society president speaks of two women killed at Renga.
src: Au moins deux civils ont trouvé la mort ce vendredi 3 janvier 2025, dans des bombardements qui ont touché des habitations au quartier Renga, dans l’agglomération de Bweremana, en territoire de Masisi (Nord-Kivu). Trois autres personnes ont été blessées par des éclats au quartier Kashenda, toujours à Bweremana.
Selon la société civile locale, ces bombes ont été lancées par le M23 à partir des lignes des combats contre les combattants locaux « wazalendo » qui s’affrontent depuis tôt le matin.

r9-V-NK3-015.s: Actualite.cd reported, citing the president of Bweremana civil society, that the M23 launched simultaneous attacks from 5 a.m. on wazalendo positions on several hills overlooking the Bweremana-Minova axis, including Ndumba, Kashingamutwe and Kabase.
r9-V-NK3-015.l: Ndumba, Kashingamutwe, Kabase hills, Bweremana-Minova axis, Masisi, North Kivu
r9-V-NK3-015.n: Cluster C-NK-29. Single local civil-society source relayed by Actualite.cd. 'Selon la même source' refers to Flory Musanganya, named in the preceding sentence of the page.
r9-V-NK3-015.vn: The speaker's name is not printed in the stored excerpt ('Selon la même source'), so the statement names his role; the page passage naming him is in clause_support. Single local civil-society source; the speaker (Flory Musanganya) is named in the sentence before the excerpt.
src: Selon la même source, le M23 a lancé depuis 5h du matin des attaques simultanées sur des positions des wazalendo sur plusieurs collines surplombant l'axe Bweremana-Minova dont Ndumba, Kashingamutwe, Kabase.

r9-V-NK3-016.s: Ouragan.cd reported that, on the margins of the 61st session of the UN Human Rights Council, DRC Human Rights Minister Samuel Mbemba said at the rostrum that he counted more than 17 000 documented serious human rights violations, nearly 15 000 deaths and about eight million displaced.
r9-V-NK3-016.x: Ouragan.cd (reporting Mbemba): plus de 17 000 violations graves documentées; près de 15 000 morts; environ huit millions de déplacés
r9-V-NK3-016.n: Cluster C-X-04: the post (28 Feb) said '17 015 morts en 12 mois', 'un viol toutes les 4 minutes', '30 000 esclaves modernes à Rubaya'. This article gives different headline figures (over 17,000 violations, nearly 15,000 deaths) and does not mention the rape frequency or Rubaya in the passage checked; the figures are not reconciled (discrepancy). The article's date line is 6 March 2026; the exact day of the speech is not stated. Earlier DRC government figures by Mbemba are in r1-UV-2026Q1-037 and r2-G-UV-CTRL-017.
r9-V-NK3-016.vn: Both excerpts on the page; statement adds nothing beyond them. Government figures as reported by Ouragan.cd; they cover eastern DRC (not only the Kivus) and differ from the figures in the social-media post that led to this search. The speech date is not given; the article is dated 6 March 2026.
src: Les chiffres sont accablants. A la tribune, le ministre Samuel Mbemba a dénombré plus de 17 000 violations graves de droits de l’homme documentées, près de 15 000 morts et environ huit millions de déplacés.
En marge de la 61e session du Conseil des droits de l’homme des Nations unies , le ministre congolais des Droits humains, Samuel Mbemba , a haussé le ton.

r9-V-NK3-017.s: ChimpReports reported that the Tanzania People's Defence Forces (TPDF) said, in a statement by Col. Ilonda, that following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on 24 and 28 January 2025 it had lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries and were receiving treatment in Goma, and that all TPDF troops deployed in the DRC remain safe.
r9-V-NK3-017.x: TPDF: two soldiers lost, four others injured; no captures mentioned
r9-V-NK3-017.n: Cluster C-NK-28. The post (30 Jan) claimed 16 Tanzanian soldiers were captured by M23 'yesterday'. The TPDF statement (made 'Sunday', published 3 Feb 2025; date computed from weekday and publication date) reports two dead and four injured and says its troops 'remain safe', and does not mention captures; it does not explicitly deny captures. ChimpReports is a Ugandan outlet relaying the TPDF statement.
r9-V-NK3-017.vn: The excerpts print 'Col. Ilonda' only; first name 'Gaudentius' (on the page) moved out of the statement to clause_support. ChimpReports (published 3 Feb 2025) says Tanzania confirmed 'Sunday'; the date 2 Feb is computed from that. The statement does not mention any captured soldiers and does not deny captures; it does not name the attackers (ChimpReports' narration says M23).
src: Following consecutive attacks in the Sake and Goma areas on January 24 and 28, 2025, TPDF has lost two of its soldiers while four others sustained injuries. The injured personnel are currently receiving treatment in Goma,” said Col. Ilonda.
Col. Ilonda assured that all TPDF troops deployed in the DRC remain safe and are continuing with their peacekeeping duties as directed by SADC.

r9-V-NK3-018.s: 7sur7.cd reported that on 20 February the cemetery of Musigiko, in Kabare territory, South Kivu, was the burial place of 18 people who died in the fighting during the M23's capture of Bukavu, their bodies placed in body bags and laid in a mass grave in Bukavu; it said John Kashinzwe, Red Cross provincial secretary in South Kivu, specified the remains had been recovered from various places in the city, and that the Red Cross with the ICRC had earlier announced collecting 26 bodies.
r9-V-NK3-018.l: Musigiko cemetery, Kabare territory, and Bukavu, South Kivu
r9-V-NK3-018.x: 7sur7.cd: 18 personnes inhumées; 26 corps recueillis (Red Cross/ICRC, earlier announcement)
r9-V-NK3-018.n: Cluster Q-10 (existing REC-0793/0794: children killed 16 Feb, executions). The page has a minor internal inconsistency (cemetery in Kabare territory, grave 'à Bukavu'). This claim adds the burial and Red Cross collection figures; it does not link the 18 dead to the six children or to any perpetrator.
r9-V-NK3-018.vn: Both excerpts on the page; statement matches; the '7' flag is from the outlet name 7sur7.cd. The page places the cemetery in Kabare territory but the grave 'à Bukavu'. It does not identify who killed the 18 or whether they were civilians or combatants.
src: Le 20 février, le cimetière de Musigiko, situé dans le territoire de Kabare au Sud-Kivu, a été le lieu d'inhumation de 18 personnes ayant perdu la vie lors des affrontements survenus lors de la prise de la ville de Bukavu par les rebelles du M23. Les corps, placés dans des sacs mortuaires, ont été déposés dans une fosse commune à Bukavu.

John Kashinzwe, secrétaire provincial de la Croix-Rouge au Sud-Kivu, a précisé que ces dépouilles avaient été récupérées dans divers endroits de la ville avant d'être inhumées. La Croix-Rouge, en collaboration avec le Comité international de la Croix-Rouge (CICR), avait précédemment annoncé avoir recueilli 26 corps dans différents quartiers de Bukavu après la prise de la ville par le M23.

r9-V-NK3-019.s: CongoRassure reported that several FARDC soldiers captured at the fall of Goma had escaped from the military camp of Rumangabo, Rutshuru territory, where the M23 held them; according to testimonies it gathered, many of them reportedly died through summary executions, torture or forced labour, and one escapee said they were captured on 26 and 27 January 2025 in Goma and that 'beaucoup de nos frères d'armes ont été tués'.
r9-V-NK3-019.n: Cluster Q-07. Existing: REC-0305/0306/0879 (UN Group of Experts and HRW on Rumangabo). This adds a local outlet's account of an escape by FARDC soldiers captured in Goma; unnamed testimony, no numbers. The page continues that after fleeing the soldiers took refuge with the Wazalendo CMC/FDP group (name of leader on the page not used).
r9-V-NK3-019.vn: Statement supported by the page (first clause from the article's lead sentence); date changed from the publication date to the month reported, as the escape date is not given. Unnamed testimony relayed by a local outlet; no numbers. The escape date is not stated; the article is dated 16 August 2025. Context: UN Group of Experts and HRW reporting on Rumangabo is already in the store.
src: Beaucoup d’entre eux auraient péri, victimes d’exécutions sommaires, de tortures ou encore de travaux forcés imposés par les rebelles.

« Nous avons été capturés les 26 et 27 janvier 2025 à Goma lors des combats. Après une détention à Rutshuru, nous avons été transférés à Rumangabo. Là, beaucoup de nos frères d’armes ont été tués, d’autres réduits à l’esclavage.

r9-V-SK1-001.s: Deutsche Welle reported that a resident of Minembwe, speaking of drone bombardments, said that even the Minembwe general referral hospital and some health centres had been targeted, and quoted him as saying that the paediatric block had been bombed 'yesterday' and that the Ilundu health centre, next to the airfield, had been bombed too.
r9-V-SK1-001.l: Ilundu health centre, near Minembwe airfield (Minembwe), Fizi
r9-V-SK1-001.a: not attributed by the source (the resident speaks of drone bombardments)
r9-V-SK1-001.n: Lead from cluster C-SK-01 (pro-AFC/M23 post on a video filmed 22-27 July 2026). The post's further allegations (women giving birth unassisted, Methodist church hit) were not found in any fetched independent page. DW quotes one unnamed resident; the date of the bombing is 'hier' relative to the interview, so approximately late June 2026. Not the same as REC-0547 (7 June killings) or REC-0607 (church, March). DW is not a party source.
r9-V-SK1-001.vn: Excerpt verified on retained DW page (byline Jean-Noël Ba-Mweze, 25/06/2026). Statement matches the resident's quoted account and stays attributed. Single anonymous witness: C. One unnamed resident quoted by DW; no perpetrator named; the bombing date is 'yesterday' relative to an undated interview in an article published 25 June 2026. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The quote also says the paediatric block was bombed 'yesterday', a health-care detail the statement left out; added it, still attributed to the one unnamed resident and with no perpetrator. A search found PoliScoop (25 June 2026) asserting 'Les drones du régime de Kinshasa frappent l'hôpital général de Minembwe et le service pédiatrique' (a Kigali-aligned framing, usable only as that outlet's claim) and voixdespeuple.com relaying DW; neither is an independent witness. No FARDC response found.
src: cet habitant de Minembwe, qui évoque les bombardements de drones. Ilaffirme que même l’hôpital général de référence de Minembwe et certains centres de santé ont été pris pour cibles : "Le bloc de pédiatrie a été bombardé hier. Il y a le centre de santé Ilundu qui a été bombardé aussi, à côté de l’aérodrome.

r9-V-SK1-002.s: Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said in an RFI interview that he could share images in which Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones and carry out attacks using the medical equipment of an ambulance; he called it a serious and substantiated accusation and said: "It is a war crime."
r9-V-SK1-002.a: Government of the DRC (Patrick Muyaya) accusing Rwanda
r9-V-SK1-002.n: Party statement only (DRC government accusing Rwanda); RFI reproduces the interview, the minister did not show the images in the excerpt. The excerpt's setting is Minembwe ('Sur Minembwe, on en parle beaucoup'); the ambulance is not tied by name to Minembwe hospital in the excerpt. The legal label 'war crime' is the minister's, quoted. Cluster C-SK-02 posts allege FARDC drone footage and the Minembwe hospital ambulance; those details are not confirmed by any fetched page. No Rwandan or AFC/M23 reply found.
r9-V-SK1-002.vn: Excerpt exact on retained RFI page (published 01/07/2026). Narrowed to make the Minembwe context explicit (it is the question/answer setting, not an incident tie) and to quote the 'war crime' label rather than paraphrase it, per the vocabulary rule. Party statement (DRC government accusing Rwanda). The images were not shown in the interview text; the legal label is the minister's own, quoted. The interviewer's question concerned continued bombardment of the Minembwe area by the Congolese army and its allies. The answer was given in reply to a question about Minembwe ('Sur Minembwe, on en parle beaucoup, mais il se passe des choses inacceptables à Minembwe.').
src: Je pourrais vous partager des images sur lesquelles le Rwanda utilise les ambulances pour transporter des drones et faire des attaques en partant de l'utilisation des matériels médicaux d'une ambulance. C'est une accusation grave. C'est une accusation qui est étayée. C'est un crime de guerre.

r9-V-SK1-003.s: Mediacongo reported that, speaking to the press, the Congolese government spokesperson said Rwanda uses ambulances to transport drones intended to carry out attacks on civilians in South Kivu, and that he described these practices as war crimes.
r9-V-SK1-003.a: Government of the DRC (government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya) accusing Rwanda
r9-V-SK1-003.n: Section is 'Publireportages' on mediacongo.net, so it may be sponsored or relayed content; date 10 July taken from the search listing, to be checked by the reviewer. Government allegation only.
r9-V-SK1-003.vn: Page read in full: section 'Publireportages', end credit 'Chrioni Kibungu Ouragan / MCP, via mediacongo.net', editorialising partisan tone. Date confirmed on page (10.07.2026), not just the listing. Outlet verb 'révèle' neutralised to 'said'; origin credited to Ouragan; labelled partisan. Not independent evidence of the ambulance allegation (same government source). Published in mediacongo.net's Publireportages section and credited at the end to Chrioni Kibungu of Ouragan ('Ouragan / MCP, via mediacongo.net'); the speaker is Patrick Muyaya. Publireportage-section relay of a strongly pro-Kinshasa article (it calls the Rwandan government a 'gangster' regime in its own voice); usable only as 'the DRC government spokesperson says'. Same speaker and allegation as the RFI interview of 1 July; the article places it at a press briefing ('Face à la presse'), so it may be a separate occasion. The page date 10.07.2026 is printed on the page. The same page calls Sukola 2 Sud spokesperson Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji 'sous-lieutenant', whereas Actualite.cd calls him lieutenant-colonel.
src: Le porte-parole du gouvernement congolais révèle que le Rwanda utilise des ambulances pour transporter des drones destinés à mener des attaques contre les civils au Sud-Kivu. Il a qualifié ces pratiques de crimes de guerre.

r9-V-SK1-004.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th rapid-intervention brigade, was killed on Saturday 1 February 2025 in fighting with the M23 at Nyabibwe in Kalehe territory; military sources told the outlet he was shot by snipers after his men fled.
r9-V-SK1-004.n: Lead from cluster C-SK-03. Posts allege he was killed by comrades-in-arms (FARDC/Wazalendo) after anti-Tutsi media campaigns; that account was found only in social posts and not in any fetched page. Place variants: Nyabibwe, Mukwija (Radio Okapi), Mukwiza, Mukwidja. Excerpt is SOS Médias Burundi's own text; 'ce samedi' = 1 February 2025 as printed.
r9-V-SK1-004.vn: Excerpt exact on retained page; every clause carried by the page; the sniper account stays attributed to military sources. B: credible outlet, corroborated on the death by the FARDC communiqué (claims 4, 5). Place differs between outlets: Nyabibwe (SOS Médias Burundi), Mukwija (Radio Okapi). The allegation in social posts that he was killed by his own side is not in any fetched page.
src: Le colonel Alexis Rugabisha a été tué ce samedi 1er février 2025. Il est mort dans les combats entre l’armée congolaise et les rebelles du M23 dans la localité de Nyabibwe. C’est sur le territoire de Kalehe en province du Sud-Kivu à l’est du Congo. (SOS Médias Burundi) L’officier des FARDC ( Forces Armées de la République démocratique du Congo) commandait la 12e brigade d’intervention rapide. Des sources militaires ont confirmé à SOS Médias Burundi que le colonel Rugabisha a été abattu lors des hostilités entre l’armée congolaise et ses alliés et les rebelles du M23. « Ses hommes ont fui et il est resté avec très peu de soldats avec lui. Des tireurs d’élite en ont profité.

r9-V-SK1-005.s: Radio Okapi reported that Colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in clashes between the FARDC and the M23 at Mukwija in Kalehe territory, and that FARDC spokesperson Major General Sylvain Ekenge, in a communiqué published on Sunday 2 February 2025, praised his bravery and called his death an inestimable loss for the army and the nation.
r9-V-SK1-005.n: The FARDC account: killed in combat against M23. Radio Okapi names the place Mukwija; SOS Médias Burundi says Nyabibwe; actualite.cd (below) says the colonel led a counter-offensive from Nyabibwe towards Minova. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué Sunday 2 February; actualite.cd says 'samedi' (a discrepancy within the sources).
r9-V-SK1-005.vn: Attribution fixed: on the page the place (Mukwija) and the circumstances are Radio Okapi's own narration; the communiqué as reported only praises his bravery and calls the death an inestimable loss. The draft put the place in the spokesperson's mouth. Radio Okapi dates the communiqué Sunday 2 February 2025; Actualite.cd (published 2 February) says the army announced it on Saturday. Place: Mukwija (Radio Okapi) vs Nyabibwe (SOS Médias Burundi, Actualite.cd).
src: Le colonel Alexis Rugabisha, commandant de la 12ᵉ brigade des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo, a été tué lors des affrontements entre les FARDC et les rebelles du M23 à Mukwija, dans le territoire de Kalehe au Sud-Kivu. Le porte-parole des FARDC, le général major Sylvain Ekenge a, dans un communiqué publié ce dimanche 2 février 2025, salué la bravoure du colonel Rugabisha.

r9-V-SK1-006.s: Actualite.cd reported that the Congolese army announced in a communiqué that Colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commander of the FARDC 12th brigade, was killed in combat against the Rwandan army and the M23 in Kalehe territory; according to spokesperson Major General Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, he fell 'armes à la main' after leading a counter-offensive that pushed the M23 back from Nyabibwe towards the surroundings of Minova.
r9-V-SK1-006.n: Same FARDC communiqué as V-SK1-005, reported by a second outlet; do not count as independent of it. The FARDC attributes the death to the Rwandan army and the M23; the 'killed by comrades' allegation in the lead posts is not repeated by any fetched page.
r9-V-SK1-006.vn: Excerpt exact on retained page (dim 02/02/2025 - 16:22); all clauses stay attributed to the army/spokesperson as on the page. Same FARDC communiqué as claim 4 (Radio Okapi); not an independent origin for the circumstances. The attribution to 'the Rwandan army' is the FARDC's.
src: Le colonel Rugabisha Alexis, commandant de la 12ᵉ brigade des Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC), a été tué au combat contre l’armée rwandaise et ses alliés du Mouvement du 23 Mars (M23) dans le territoire de Kalehe, au Sud-Kivu, a annoncé samedi l’armée congolaise dans un communiqué. D’après le porte-parole des FARDC, le général-major Ekenge Bomusa Efomi Sylvain, le colonel Rugabisha est tombé “armes à la main” après avoir conduit une contre-offensive qui a repoussé les rebelles du M23 de Nyabibwe jusqu’aux environs de Minova.

r9-V-SK1-007.s: Radio Maendeleo reported that notables of northern Kabare territory denounced cases of abductions and intimidation at the Kavumu commercial centre that were pushing many young people and heads of families to leave their homes; the same report said gunfire had been heard for over a month and that deaths by bullets and injuries had been reported.
r9-V-SK1-007.l: Kavumu commercial centre, Bugorhe grouping, Kabare, South Kivu
r9-V-SK1-007.a: not attributed by the source (some sources cite clashes between AFC/M23 elements and Wazalendo groups, others say the origin of shooting is unknown)
r9-V-SK1-007.n: Lead from cluster C-SK-07 (post of about 3 August 2026 alleging youths taken away by M23-RDF and bodies of young people in Kavumu centre). Radio Maendeleo (Bukavu community radio) reports abductions and intimidation at Kavumu in general terms, attributing them to no one; no page found reports bodies of young people found in Kavumu centre on that day. 'Selon des sources locales' type reporting; one named notable (David Chikuru) appears in an audio element, not quoted in the text.
r9-V-SK1-007.vn: Page read in full (Last updated 2026/08/01). Statement is covered by the page; the gunfire and casualty clauses sit outside the stored excerpt (excerpt gap, quotes supplied in clause_support). Abductions are not attributed to any party. The same report says some sources cite clashes between AFC/M23 elements and Wazalendo while others say the origin of the shooting is unknown. No report of bodies of young people (the social-media lead) was found.
src: Face à cette situation, des notables de la région appellent les autorités à prendre des mesures urgentes afin de rétablir la sécurité et de rassurer la population. L’un d’eux, David Chikuru, revient sur cette situation dans cet élément. Ces acteurs dénoncent également des cas d’enlèvements et d’intimidations qui poussent de nombreux jeunes et chefs de famille à quitter leurs domiciles par crainte pour leur sécurité.

r9-V-SK1-008.s: Enquete.cd reported that, according to testimonies gathered on site, several residents of the Buliriko quarter of Kavumu, in Kabare territory, left their homes for Buhandahanda and Nzinzi, and that families said they feared a worsening situation after the installation on Saturday of a military camp attributed to AFC/M23 fighters.
r9-V-SK1-008.l: Buliriko quarter, Kavumu, Kabare, South Kivu
r9-V-SK1-008.a: AFC/M23 (camp attributed to its fighters, per the source)
r9-V-SK1-008.n: Related event at Kavumu on the dates of cluster C-SK-07; it does not report abductions or bodies. The article says no official communication had been made on the population movements or on the origin of detonations heard that morning. 'Saturday' = 1 August 2026, computed from the 2 August publication date (a Sunday per the article).
r9-V-SK1-008.vn: Both excerpts exact on retained page (2 August 2026); statement keeps the source's hedges. The camp is 'attributed to' AFC/M23 fighters; the article says no official communication had been made on the movements or the origin of the detonations.
src: Selon des témoignages recueillis sur place, plusieurs habitants ont quitté leurs domiciles pour se réfugier vers les localités de Buhandahanda et de Nzinzi.
Les familles disent craindre une dégradation de la situation après l’installation, samedi, d’un camp militaire attribué aux combattants de l’AFC/M23 dans le secteur.

r9-V-SK1-009.s: Bwiza reported that FDNB spokesperson Brigadier General Gaspard Baratuza told journalists on Tuesday 29 September 2026 that Maj. Nitunga Jérémie and Capt Kanjori Félicien were arrested by the DRC state on 21 August 2026 and are held at the FARDC headquarters in Baraka, where they were arrested after being found with telephones, and that it is suspected they may have been used 'in improper activities or in giving certain information'.
r9-V-SK1-009.a: DRC state / FARDC (as stated by the FDNB spokesperson)
r9-V-SK1-009.n: Adds detail to existing r1-ST-BI-021 (BBC Gahuza, same press conference, which has the confirmation and the denial of Kinshasa detention) and r1-UV-2026Q3-009 (SOS Médias Burundi): date of arrest 21 August 2026, place of detention (FARDC headquarters at Baraka), and the reason the spokesperson gave. Bwiza is a Rwandan outlet relaying the Burundian army press conference; the cluster post (Kirundi, 1 Oct 2026) matches. FARDC/Congolese government account of the arrests not found.
r9-V-SK1-009.vn: Excerpts exact on retained page (byline Bénjamin BABOU, 29 Nzeri 2026). Restored the source's hedge ('may have been used'), the rank titles as printed, and the place of detention (FARDC HQ, Baraka). Not independent of the existing press-conference claims. Burundian army's account relayed by a Rwandan outlet (Bwiza); same press conference as the existing BBC Gahuza claim. The suspicion is hedged in the source ('bigakekwa ko bashobora kuba...': it is suspected they may have been). No FARDC/Kinshasa account found.
src: Byemejwe n'umuvugizi wa FDNB, Général de Brigade Gaspard Baratuza, ubwo kuri uyu Kabiri tariki ya 29 Nzeri 2026 yagiranaga ikiganiro n’abanyamakuru.

Baratuza wasubizaga ikibazo cyabajijwe ku makuru yavugaga ko abo basirikare b’Abarundi bafungiye i Kinshasa, yasobanuye ko abo basirikare babiri, Maj. Nitunga Jérémie na Capt Kanjori Félicien batawe muri yombi na Leta ya RDC tariki ya 21 Kanama 2026. Yavuze ko bafungiye i Baraka, aho bafatiwe nyuma yo gusanganwa telefoni, bigakekwa ko bashobora kuba barakoreshwaga "mu bikorwa bidakwiye cyangwa mu gutanga amakuru runaka
Baratuza yemeje kandi ko abo basirikare bafungiye ku cyicaro gikuru cy’Ingabo za FARDC i Baraka, aho bari bakikorwaho iperereza kugira ngo hamenyekane neza ibyo bakurikiranweho.

r9-V-SK1-010.s: PoliScoop reported, according to accounts shared by Burundian sources, that two Burundian army officers held in eastern DRC since August had been repatriated to Burundi; it also reported that Major Jeremie Nitunga and Captain Felicien Kanjori had been arrested on 21 August in Baraka and detained by the FARDC and allied groups operating in the area.
r9-V-SK1-010.x: two officers detained since 21 August (per the source)
r9-V-SK1-010.n: Single small outlet relying on unnamed Burundian sources; the repatriation is not confirmed by any official Burundian or Congolese statement I found. Page carries an English text and a French text; the English text is cited. Spelling in the source omits accents.
r9-V-SK1-010.vn: Text verified on retained page (English and French versions). Split the attribution: only the repatriation is sourced to Burundian accounts; the arrest details are the outlet's narration. Date marked as 'by' the publication date since the repatriation date is not stated. Added the outlet's own caveat that neither government gave an account. Small online outlet (byline 'PoliScoop', 5 October 2026) relying on unnamed Burundian sources; repatriation date not given and not confirmed by any official statement. Its framing echoes Kigali's positions. The outlet adds that neither Bujumbura nor Kinshasa had offered a detailed public account of the detention or the terms of the release.
src: Two Burundian army officers who had been held in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo since August have been repatriated to Burundi, according to accounts shared by Burundian sources. Major Jeremie Nitunga and Captain Felicien Kanjori were arrested on 21 August in Baraka, a town in South Kivu on the western shore of Lake Tanganyika, and detained by the Congolese armed forces, the FARDC, and allied groups operating in the area.

r9-V-SK2-001.s: SOS Médias Burundi reported that, according to an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter it contacted, at least 17 Burundian soldiers were killed in the fighting at Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, and the fighter said: 'We captured one, along with their radios and their rifles.'
r9-V-SK2-001.l: Rugezi and Kabanju, Fizi territory, South Kivu
r9-V-SK2-001.x: SOS Médias Burundi (citing an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter): at least 17 Burundian soldiers killed; one captured
r9-V-SK2-001.n: Video-lead cluster C-SK-09. Same article as existing r1-SKS-2025Q2-009 (REC-0160) but that claim does not record the capture. Posts allege a named female Burundian soldier captured around 22-30 April; this article is dated 15 April, concerns 12 April, and names no captured person, so it does not confirm the posts' details. Twirwaneho is a party; account is the party's own. The article dates the clashes to Saturday 12 April.
r9-V-SK2-001.vn: Excerpt exact on retained page (15 avril 2025, byline David Yemba). Removed the meta-sentence about what the article does not say from the statement (moved to note); kept attribution to the fighter. Same article as existing r1-SKS-2025Q2-009, so not an independent origin; it adds the capture detail. Party's own claim (an anonymous Twirwaneho fighter); the article dates the clashes to Saturday 12 April and names no captured person, gives no sex or rank. It does not confirm the social-media posts about a named female soldier captured in late April.
src: Selon un combattant Twirwaneho contacté par SOS Médias Burundi, au moins 17 militaires burundais ont été tués au cours de ces affrontements. « Il y a beaucoup de soldats burundais qui sont morts dans les combats. Nous en avons capturé un, ainsi que leurs radios et leurs fusils », a déclaré ce combattant, sous couvert d’anonymat.

r9-V-SK2-002.s: Actualite.cd reported that the spokesperson of operation Sukola 2 Sud South Kivu, Lieutenant-Colonel Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, said that following the FARDC response against what he called the 'terrorist coalition RDF and its allies M23, Twirwaneho and Red Tabara' in the Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi, the FARDC had neutralised 23 rebels, 11 others had surrendered and several weapons were recovered.
r9-V-SK2-002.l: Hauts Plateaux of Uvira and Fizi (spokesperson's words); the article places the recaptured Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati in the Mwenga highlands, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
r9-V-SK2-002.a: FARDC (Sukola 2 Sud), as the spokesperson says
r9-V-SK2-002.n: Found while searching video-lead cluster C-SK-15 (Itombwe, 'M23 Red Tabara' arrests, ~8 Aug 2026). It does not report the arrests; it is a related FARDC claim of fighting against Red Tabara in the Hauts Plateaux from 28 August. Party account (FARDC); no AFC/M23 or Twirwaneho response found.
r9-V-SK2-002.vn: Excerpt exact on retained page (jeu 03/09/2026). Statement wording fine; location corrected: the draft placed Masango etc. in the Uvira/Fizi highlands, but the page puts them in the Mwenga highlands (Itombwe sector). Party (FARDC) figures, unverified. The article's lead places Masango, Ruhua and Rubarati in the Hauts Plateaux of Mwenga, Itombwe sector, not Uvira/Fizi. Rank discrepancy: Mediacongo (10 July 2026) calls him 'sous-lieutenant'.
src: Selon le porte-parole de l’opération Sukola 2 Sud Sud-Kivu, le lieutenant-colonel Reagan Mbuyi Kalonji, cette avancée résulte d’une riposte militaire menée dans ces zones. « À la suite de notre riposte contre la coalition terroriste RDF et ses alliés du M23, Twirwaneho et Red Tabara, dans les Hauts Plateaux d’Uvira et de Fizi, les FARDC ont neutralisé 23 rebelles, 11 autres se sont rendus et plusieurs armes ont été récupérées », a-t-il déclaré.

r9-V-SK2-003.s: Actualite.cd reported that, according to the army, a mass grave was discovered at Masango, where civilians killed during the occupation of the town by the M23/Twirwaneho/Red Tabara rebel forces, supported by Rwanda, are said to be buried.
r9-V-SK2-003.l: Masango, Hauts Plateaux of Mwenga, Itombwe sector, South Kivu
r9-V-SK2-003.n: Army allegation only; no independent verification found. Not from a video lead; found during C-SK-15 searches. Other Masango claims exist (UN GoE camps; SOS Medias Burundi 23 Aug).
r9-V-SK2-003.vn: Excerpt exact. The whole sentence, including the discovery, is attributed to the army; the draft attributed only the burial part. Location corrected from Uvira territory to the Mwenga highlands (Itombwe sector) as the page states; date made 'reported' since the discovery date is not given. Army allegation only (sentence ends 'selon l'armée'; burial is conditional, 'seraient enterrés'); no number of bodies, no names, no independent verification, no AFC/M23 or Twirwaneho response found.
src: Par ailleurs, une fosse commune a été découverte à Masango, où seraient enterrés des civils tués lors de l’occupation de cette agglomération par les forces rebelles M23/Twirwaneho/Red Tabara, soutenues par le Rwanda, selon l’armée.

r9-V-UV2-001.s: Radio Okapi reported that the FARDC presented to the press in Kinshasa on Saturday 3 January seven people it described as Rwandan soldiers and eight civilians, nationals of countries of the sub-region, and that Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said these suspects had been apprehended far from the borders during military operations in North and South Kivu.
r9-V-UV2-001.l: Kinshasa (presentation of the captives); capture sites in North and South Kivu, not specified
r9-V-UV2-001.a: FARDC (detaining party); the seven are described by the FARDC as Rwandan soldiers
r9-V-UV2-001.x: Radio Okapi (FARDC account): seven Rwandan soldiers and eight civilians presented
r9-V-UV2-001.n: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Party account: nationality and status of the captives are as claimed by the FARDC and not independently verified. Radio Okapi does not name Uvira as the capture site (compare the Liberal Info claim, which does). No response from Rwanda found. Not in the verified claims at drafting (claim_search 'sept militaires rwandais', 'Hazukay').
r9-V-UV2-001.vn: Both excerpts are on the page (published sam, 03/01/2026). Dropped the publication year and the quotation marks around 'suspects' clause; numbers written as the page words (sept, huit). Rank title kept as printed; role omitted from the statement because the two outlets name the service differently. The nationality and status of the captives are the FARDC's account; no independent identification and no Rwandan response found. Radio Okapi names Hazukay as deputy commander of the FARDC 'Service de commandement et d'information'; Liberal Info writes 'Service de communication et d'information'. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The FARDC is a party; Radio Okapi relays its presentation, and the captives' identity as Rwandan soldiers is the FARDC's account. Amended to attribute it. A search found Grands Lacs News (3 Jan 2026) headlining 'Kigali dément' (lead for a Rwandan denial; body not read) and quoting Hazukay that a major and a captain of the RDF were among them. Grade B fits the event of the presentation, not the identities.
src: Les Forces armées de la RDC (FARDC) a présenté, samedi 3 janvier, sept militaires rwandais et huit civils, ressortissants des pays de la sous-région, devant la presse, à Kinshasa.
Lieutenant-colonel Mak Hazukay a précisé que ces suspects ont été appréhendés loin des frontières lors des opérations militaires menées au Nord et Sud-Kivu.

r9-V-UV2-002.s: Liberal Info reported that on Saturday the FARDC presented at the Collège des Hautes Études de Stratégie et de Défense (CHESD) in Kinshasa seven people described as soldiers of the Rwandan defence forces (RDF) and eight civilians, including Burundian and Tanzanian nationals, whom Liberal Info described as 'captured in the city of Uvira'; the identification of the seven as RDF soldiers is the FARDC's account.
r9-V-UV2-002.l: Uvira (city), South Kivu (capture, per Liberal Info); Kinshasa (presentation)
r9-V-UV2-002.a: FARDC (detaining party); the seven are described as RDF soldiers
r9-V-UV2-002.x: Liberal Info (FARDC account): seven RDF soldiers and eight civilians
r9-V-UV2-002.n: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Date computed from 'samedi' and the 3 January 2026 page date. Conflicts on place with Radio Okapi (captures 'au Nord et Sud-Kivu', no town named); the same Liberal Info page later says the arrests came in operations 'dans le territoire d'Uvira'. Single outlet, FARDC account.
r9-V-UV2-002.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the page-date clause (a number no excerpt prints) and made explicit that 'captured in the city of Uvira' is the outlet's narration of the FARDC presentation, not an established capture site. Place of capture conflicts: Liberal Info's lead says 'dans la ville d'Uvira', the same page later reports the officer as saying the arrests came in operations 'dans le territoire d'Uvira', and Radio Okapi quotes him as saying 'au Nord et Sud-Kivu'. The 'Saturday' is 3 January 2026 by the page date (Publié le 3 janvier 2026). Identities are the FARDC's account. 2026-10-29: statement edited: red-team rt-r9-2: The FARDC is a party and the identification of the seven as RDF soldiers is its account; the statement gave it in Liberal Info's voice as fact. Amended to attribute the identification. A search found Grands Lacs News headlining the same presentation 'Kigali dément' (body not read; lead for a Rwandan denial) and quoting Hazukay that the captives were taken 'sur le théâtre des opérations dans les provinces du Nord-Kivu et Sud-Kivu', which again contradicts Liberal Info's 'capturés dans la ville d’Uvira'.
src: Les Forces armées de la République démocratique du Congo (FARDC) ont présenté, samedi, au siège du Collège des Hautes Études de Stratégie et de Défense (CHESD) à Kinshasa, sept (7) soldats des Forces de défense rwandaises (RDF) ainsi que huit (8) civils, parmi lesquels des ressortissants burundais et tanzaniens, capturés dans la ville d’Uvira, dans la province du Sud-Kivu

r9-V-UV2-003.s: Radio Okapi reported that FARDC Lieutenant-Colonel Mak Hazukay said, at the press presentation in Kinshasa, that the occupation of Uvira, far from Rwanda's borders, proves that the defensive-measures reason advanced by Kigali is 'un pire mensonge'.
r9-V-UV2-003.l: Kinshasa (press conference) concerning Uvira, South Kivu
r9-V-UV2-003.n: Video-lead cluster C-UV-10. Party statement (Kinshasa). Rwanda's response to the presentation: none found.
r9-V-UV2-003.vn: Excerpt exact on the Radio Okapi page; the 'a-t-il déploré' closes a quote the page attributes to Lt-Col Mak Hazukay (named in the preceding paragraph). Single clause, single source; attribution and wording match. Party statement (FARDC). 'L'occupation aujourd'hui d'Uvira' refers to the AFC/M23 occupation at the time of the briefing. Rwanda's response: none found.
src: capturés pendant les opérations militaires menées au Nord et Sud-Kivu. L’occupation aujourd’hui d’Uvira se trouvant loin de ses frontières prouve que la raison des mesures défensives avancées par Kigali est un pire mensonge », a-t-il déploré.

r9-V-UV2-004.s: Opinion Info and Actualite.cd reported that South Kivu governor Jean-Jacques Purusi, at a press briefing with Patrick Muyaya on Thursday 2 April 2026, said about 210 bodies had been found in three mass graves (Actualite.cd: at least 210); Opinion Info quotes him as saying Human Rights Watch had just detected more than 61 mass graves and that 31 mass graves had been found in only three municipalities, and names the three graves as Kamvivira, Kilomoni and Kimanga.
r9-V-UV2-004.x: Purusi per Opinion Info: about 210 bodies in three mass graves (Kamvivira, Kilomoni, Kimanga); more than 61 mass graves detected by HRW; 31 mass graves in three municipalities. Per Actualite.cd: at least 210 bodies
r9-V-UV2-004.n: Video-lead cluster Q-01 (REC-0023 holds the earlier Feb 2026 counts: 31+141 bodies per BBC Gahuza/Reuters, 151 per the provincial communiqué of 28 Feb). The 210 / 61 figures and the 2 April briefing are not in the verified claims at drafting. Figures differ across government statements: 151 (28 Feb communiqué), 171-172 (late Feb press), 210 (2 Apr). Third grave site is Kimanga here; Kavimvira and Kilomoni in earlier counts. The '61' is the governor's attribution to HRW; HRW's own count is not in these excerpts. The '344 bodies' of Sept 2026 (foxtime.cd, listing dated 11 Sept 2026) could not be fetched by the checker: see gaps.
r9-V-UV2-004.vn: Both excerpts exact. The raw statement credited both outlets with the 61 and 31 figures and the grave names, which only Opinion Info prints; split clause by clause, removed the publication dates (not in the excerpts), recorded the Actualite.cd wording difference. Governor's figures, not independently counted. The '61' is in Opinion Info's quote only: Actualite.cd quotes Purusi as saying HRW showed 'des dizaines des fausses communes', and quotes him dating the discovery of the three graves to 20 February (spelled Kavinvira, Kilomoni, Kimanga). Opinion Info calls Muyaya the government spokesperson; Actualite.cd calls him minister of communication. Earlier government counts differ (151, 171-172; see REC-0023).
src: « Human Rights Watch vient de détecter plus de 61 fosses communes. Et nous avons découvert 31 fosses communes seulement dans trois municipalités. Il y a des crimes de masse », a-t-il déclaré, soulignant qu’environ 210 corps inertes ont été retrouvés dans trois fosses communes à Kamvivira, Kilomoni et Kimanga.

avec au moins 210 corps. Ces chiffres ont été révélés jeudi 2 avril 2026 par le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, lors d’un briefing de presse tenu avec le ministre de la Communication et des Médias, Patrick Muyaya.

r9-V-UV2-005.s: African Facts reported that the group of James Bitolo, with other Biloze Bishamuke militiamen and Maï maï fighters, then attacked and pillaged the evangelical church where the funeral of Colonel Gisore took place, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying he was among those arrested in the church, that they shot at them, and that they stole crates of drinks, vehicles, medical equipment and telephones; African Facts wrote that videos and other testimonies it consulted corroborate the attack.
r9-V-UV2-005.a: as African Facts attributes it: group of James Bitolo, Biloze Bishamuke militiamen and Maï maï fighters
r9-V-UV2-005.n: Video-lead cluster Q-02 (a pro-M23 account posted this article). Existing REC-0091 / claim r2-G-UV-CTRL-002 (SOS Médias Burundi) dates the burial to Monday 25 August 2025; African Facts gives no funeral date, so date is month-level here. African Facts is a fact-checking outlet; the PDF is a copy hosted on francegenocidetutsi.org (the africanfacts.org original page was not fetchable). The medical equipment was taken from a church funeral gathering, not a health facility. The South Kivu government's account is a separate claim.
r9-V-UV2-005.vn: Excerpts exact in the retained PDF; byline, date and the 'président de la mutualité' passage are on the same page. Attribution is correct (outlet's narration for the perpetrators, Ntabaye's quote for the arrests, shooting and theft). Month-level date is right because the church attack has no day printed. Read from a PDF copy hosted by francegenocidetutsi.org (third-party advocacy archive), credited to African Facts; the original page could not be reached. The article dates Colonel Gisore's funeral to 25 August 2025 and places this attack 'ensuite', after the shooting that followed the funeral; no exact day is given for the church attack. The medical equipment was taken from a funeral gathering, not a health facility. Perpetrators as African Facts names them; Ntabaye's quote says only 'ils'.
src: Le groupe de James Bitolo, en compagnie d’autres miliciens Biloze Bishamuke et de combattants Maï maï, va ensuite attaquer et piller l’église évangélique où ont eu lieu les obsèques du colonel Gisore. « Moi même j’étais là, parmi les gens qui ont été arrêtés dans l’Église. Ils nous tiraient dessus.

Puis ils ont dérobé les caisses de boissons prévues pour la levée de deuil ainsi que des véhicules, des équipements médicaux, des téléphones, etc. », raconte Muyoboke Ntabaye. Des vidéos que nous avons consultées et d’autres témoignages corroborent la réalité de cette attaque.

r9-V-UV2-006.s: African Facts reported that, in a communiqué issued 'le jour même', the South Kivu government spokesperson summed up the events as a 'petite paralysie des activités dans Mulongwe' that would have caused no damage (conditional, as the article words it), and 'condamne les organisateurs des cérémonies funéraires'; the article adds that he also condemned messages aimed at tearing the social fabric between communities and spoke of a media war waged by the rebels.
r9-V-UV2-006.n: Video-lead cluster Q-02. Party account (provincial government) relayed by African Facts, which presents it critically. 'Le jour même' refers to the day of the events in the preceding paragraphs; the exact day is not printed in the excerpt.
r9-V-UV2-006.vn: Excerpt exact. Removed the bracketed gloss '(the Wazalendo disturbance around the funeral of Colonel Gisore)', which the excerpt does not say; kept 'n'aurait causé' as a conditional; added the communiqué's other condemnations that the same paragraph reports, so the party's account is not cut to its most damaging lines (those clauses rest on the page, not the stored excerpt). The provincial government's communiqué is known here only through African Facts, which presents it critically; the communiqué was not found or read. 'Le jour même' follows the article's account of the 25 August 2025 funeral events, but the communiqué's exact date is not printed. The spokesperson is not named.
src: Dans un communiqué diffusé le jour même, le porte-parole du gouvernement du Sud-Kivu résume les événements à une « petite paralysie des activités dans Mulongwe » qui n’aurait causé aucun dégât et « condamne les organisateurs des cérémonies funéraires ».

r9-V-UV2-007.s: African Facts reported that soldiers and militiamen had reportedly acted together 'hier matin' in the Nyabianda quarter, and quoted Muyoboke Ntabaye, president of the Banyamulenge mutuality of Uvira, as saying that soldiers, maï maï and persons in police uniform began the cordon at 5:00 and it lasted until 13:00, that more than fifteen members of his community were arrested without valid reason, and that some were taken to the cells of the Wazalendo militias instead of government buildings; the article also quotes him describing waking up in a cordon in the quarter 'deNamyanda' where many Banyamulenge live.
r9-V-UV2-007.l: Nyabianda / Namyanda quarter, Uvira (city), South Kivu (both spellings as printed)
r9-V-UV2-007.a: as Ntabaye states: soldiers, maï maï and persons in police uniform
r9-V-UV2-007.x: African Facts quoting Ntabaye: more than fifteen people arrested
r9-V-UV2-007.n: Video-lead cluster Q-02. Date computed from 'hier' and the article date 20 September 2025. Single-source account by a community leader; the page's own spelling 'deNamyanda' kept. No FARDC or government response to the cordon found. Existing claims r1-UV-2025Q3-020/-021 (SOS Médias Burundi) record the Mutualité's other complaints (beatings at Kabindula, water denial, abduction of a soldier and a policeman).
r9-V-UV2-007.vn: Excerpts exact. The raw statement put 'yesterday morning' and Nyabianda in Ntabaye's mouth; on the page they are African Facts' own narration, in the conditional ('se seraient ... entendus et auraient agi ensemble'). Re-attributed and removed the publication date (a number no excerpt prints). Single community-leader account relayed by African Facts from a PDF copy hosted by francegenocidetutsi.org. The date 19 September 2025 is computed from 'hier' and the article date (20/09/2025); the article's opening also says that nine days after the 10 September audio message soldiers and militiamen were patrolling some quarters. Nyabianda and 'deNamyanda' are both as printed and may be the same quarter. No FARDC, police or government response found.
src: Les militaires, les maï maï et des personnes en tenue de policiers ont commencé le bouclage à 5h00 et cela a duré jusqu’à 13h00. Beaucoup de membres de notre communauté, plus de quinze personnes, ont été arrêtées sans motif valable. Certaines personnes ont été amenées dans les cachots des milices Wazalendo au lieu des bâtiments gouvernementaux.

Ce matin nous nous sommes réveillés en plein bouclage dans le quartier deNamyanda où vivent beaucoup de gens de la communauté Banyamulenge », relatait hier Muyoboke Ntabaye, président de la mutualité des Banyamulenge d’Uvira.
